english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Pin'ilʋgʋn la Wina'am da maal agɔl nɛ teŋ.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Si'el da ka' teŋ la nii, ka zin'ig la wʋsa da an yɔɔg-yɔɔg, lik ma'aa da pɛ'ɛl, ka Wina'am Siig da laannɛ giligid ku'om la zug.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka li an nyain.” Ka li sid nie nyain.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am nyɛ ka nɛɛsim la an sʋm ka o bak nɛɛsim la ka kɛ lik.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am buol nɛɛsim la ye, “Nintaŋ” ka buol lik la ye, “Yʋ'ʋŋ.” Ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb ka bɛog nie, linɛ da an yiiga dabisir.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka si'el bɛɛ an lammiri bɛŋ ku'okanɛ bɛɛ agɔl la nɛ ku'okanɛ bɛ teŋir la.”

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am buol bʋnlammir dinɛ bɛɛ agɔl la ye, “Saŋgbauŋ.” Ka yʋ'ʋŋ da sɔb ka bɛog nie dabayi' daare la.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka ku'okanɛ bɛ saŋgbauŋ la teŋir la la'as zin'ig yinne, ka kɛ ka li teŋir la nie.” Ka li sid niŋ ala.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am buol zin'ikanɛ nie ka kʋdig la ye, “Teŋ,” ka buol ku'om la ye, “Atɛuk.” Ka Wina'am nyɛ ka li an sʋm.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka bʋmbʋʋda buudi wʋsa bul teŋinɛ yina. Bʋmbʋʋdbanɛ du'ad bielim nɛ tiis buudi wʋsa banɛ wan wala ka mɔr biili.” Ka li sid niŋ ala.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ka teŋ la pɛ'ɛl nɛ zʋʋd nɛ tiis. Ka bʋmbʋʋda wʋsa du'a li buudi. Ka Wina'am nyɛ ka li an sʋm.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb ka bɛog nie daba atan' daare la.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka bugum bɛɛ agɔl dinɛ na bak nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ ka an zanbin linɛ pa'an sɛɛung nɛ ʋʋn, nɛ dabisa nɛ yʋma.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka kɛ ka bugum bɛ saŋgbauŋ la ni dinɛ na tis teŋgbauŋ la nɛɛsim.” Ka li sid niŋ ala.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Wina'am da maal nɛ bugum kanda ayi'. Bugum tita'ar la da tisid nɛɛsim nintaŋ ka bugum si'asiŋ la tisid nɛɛsim yʋ'ʋŋ. O da lɛm maal nwadbibis.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Wina'am da maali ba niŋ saŋgbana la ni ye ba tis teŋgbauŋ la nɛɛsim

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: ka sʋ'oe nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ ka wɛlig nɛɛsim yi likin. Ka Wina'am nyɛ ka li an sʋm.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Ka yʋ'ʋŋ da sɔb ka bɛog nie daba anaasi daare la.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka ku'om la mɔr zimi nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ bɛ ku'omin wʋsa, ka kɛ ka niis buudi wʋsa ian'ad agɔla.”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am maal bʋnvʋbɛda banɛ bɛɛ atɛukʋn la, nɛ zimi nɛ ba buudi nɛ niis nɛ ba buudi. Ka Wina'am nyɛ ka li an sʋm.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am niŋi ba zug bareka ka yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka zimi la wiaki pɛ'ɛl atɛuk la ka kɛ ka niis la mɛ wiaki pɛ'ɛl teŋgbauŋ la.”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Ka yʋ'ʋŋ da sɔb ka bɛog nie daba anu daare la.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka teŋgbauŋ la mɔr bʋnvʋya nɛ li buudi wʋsa, yin bʋnkɔnbid nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ vuud teŋin nɛ sian'arin bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa nɛ ba buudi.” Ka li da niŋ ala.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Wina'am da maal sian'arin bʋnkɔnbid la nɛ ba buudi, nɛ yin bʋnkɔnbid nɛ ba buudi nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ vuud teŋin la wʋsa nɛ ba buudi. Ka Wina'am nyɛ ka li an sʋm.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka ti maal ninsaal nwɛnɛ ti mɛŋi an si'em la, ka kɛ ka o sʋ'oe zimi linɛ bɛ ku'omin la, nɛ niis banɛ ian'ada agɔla nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ bɛ teŋgbauŋʋn la, hali nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ vuud teŋin la wʋsa.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Ala ka Wina'am da maal ninsaal nwɛnɛ o mɛŋi an si'em la. Dau nɛ pu'a ka o da maal.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am niŋi ba zug bareka ka yɛl ye, “Du'am nɔbigi pɛ'ɛli teŋgbauŋ la, ka sʋ'oe teŋ la, nɛ zimi banɛ bɛɛ atɛukʋn, nɛ niis banɛ bɛɛ agɔl, nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ wʋsa ken teŋin la.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: M tis bʋnkɔnbid banɛ bɛ teŋin la nɛ niis banɛ bɛɛ agɔl nɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ ken teŋin hali nɛ linɛ wʋsa mɔr vʋm nɛ mɔma'asa ye li aan ba diib.” Ka li da niŋ ala.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Wina'am da nyɛ on maal si'el la wʋsa ka li an sʋm. Ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb ka bɛog nie daba ayuobʋ daare la.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Ala ka Wina'am da maal agɔl nɛ teŋ, nɛ bʋn linɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa naae.

english_verse: By the seventh day God had finished his work, and so he rested.
translation_verse: Ka daba ayɔpɔi la daar o da naae o tʋʋma la wʋsa ka vʋ'ʋs daakan la.

english_verse: God blessed the seventh day and made it special, because on that day he rested from his work.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am niŋ daba ayɔpɔi la daar zug bareka ka kɛ ka li an kasi, bɔzugɔ on da maal agɔl nɛ teŋi naae la daakan ka o da vʋ'ʋs. Wina'am da maal dau nɛ pu'a si'em

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Agɔl nɛ teŋ maaligʋ da pin'il si'em nwa'. Zugsɔb Wina'am da maal agɔl nɛ teŋ la,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: tiis nɛ mɔɔd wʋsa da nam pʋ yi teŋ la zugɔ, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb Wina'am da nam pʋ kɛ ka saa ni teŋ la zugɔ, ka ninsaal mɛ da nan kae na kua teŋ la.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Amaa ku'om da bunnɛ wʋ'ʋgid teŋ la.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am gbin'e tanni ya'ab dau ka vʋ'ʋs o mɛŋ vʋ'ʋsʋm niŋ o nyɔnya ni, ka dau la lieb ninsaal ka vʋ'ʋsid.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am maal lɔmbɔn'ɔg Eden teŋin la lɛbid ya-nya'aŋ baba, ka nɔk dau kanɛ ka o maal la niŋ anina.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am kɛ ka tiis nɛ ba buudi yii nɔbigi pɛ'ɛl lɔmbɔn'ɔg la. Tiis la da vɛnl ka an sʋ'ʋŋa nɛ diib. Ka nyɔvʋr tiig nɛ tikanɛ kɛt ka nid baŋid dinɛ an sʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛdi bakid da zi'e lɔmbɔn'ɔg la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Ka Kɔldatita'ar naan Eden pʋʋgin zɔt ka li ku'om dɔn'ɔsid lɔmbɔn'ɔg la. Li da pʋdignɛ zin'isa anaasi.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Yiiga kɔldaug la anɛ Pison. Kɔldaug kan pʋbidnɛ giligid Havila teŋ la ka sanlima bɛɛ ani.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Kɔldaug linɛ paas ayi' la anɛ Gihon. Lin da pʋbidnɛ giligid Kus teŋ la.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Linɛ paas atan' la anɛ Tigiris ka mɛ pʋbidi dɔl Asuor teŋ nya'aŋ. Ka linɛ paas anaasi an Efiritis.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am nɔk dau la niŋ Eden lɔmbɔn'ɔg la ni ye o tʋm ka gɔsidi li.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am bas dau nɔɔr ye, “Fʋ tun'e di tiis wala banɛ bɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la wʋsa,

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: amaa mid ka fʋ di tikanɛ kɛt ka fʋ baŋid linɛ an sʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛd la! Fʋ ya'a dii li fʋ na kpi.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛl ye, “Li ka' sʋ'ʋm ye dau bɛɛ o kɔn'ɔɔ. M na maal sʋŋid onɛ zemis nɛ o tis o.”

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am kɛ ka dau la gbis, ka o yis dau la sapirig ka maali lɛbis on yis lɔsi'a la.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Anina ka Zugsɔb Wina'am nɔk on yis sapirsi'a la maal pu'a mɔr na tis dau la.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Ka dau la yɛl ye, “Ɛnhee, kɔnbkaŋa anɛ mam kɔnbir ka niŋgbiŋ la mɛ an mam niŋgbiŋ. M na buol o ye pu'a, bɔzugɔ o yinɛ man dau la san'an na.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Dinzug, dau na bas o ba' nɛ o ma ka la'as nɛ o pu'a ka babayi' la na lieb niŋgbiŋ yinne.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Dau la nɛ o pu'a la da anɛ biel, ka mɛ pʋ zɔt nyannɛ.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Waaf la da anɛ zam sɔb hali gaad bʋnkɔnbid banɛ wʋsa ka Zugsɔb Wina'am da maal la. O da bu'os pu'a la ye, “Li an sida ye Wina'am yɛl ye ya da di tisi'a wala lɔmbɔn'ɔg nwa' nii?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la lɛbis waaf la ye, “Ti tun'e di tiwala lɔmbɔn'ɔg nwa' ni,

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: amaa Wina'am ye ti mid ka ti di tikanɛ bɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔg la teŋsʋk la wala, ye ti pʋn da si'isi lii, ka ti ya'a niŋ ala ti na kpi.”

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Wina'am mi' ye ya ya'a di wala la ya nini na nie ka ya nwɛnɛ on Wina'am nɛ, ka mi' sʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛdi bakid.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la da nyɛ ka tiig la wala an sʋm, nar nɛ diib ka lɛn vɛnli o nini ni, ka an linɛ na tis o baŋir la, o da pun'oe di ka zaŋ sieba tis o sid ka o mɛ di.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Anina ka ba nini nie ka ba gɔsi nyɛ ka ba zi'e biel, ka ba ans kekaŋ vaandi maali sɔɔn lusi ba nyan.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Zaam da ma'ae ka ba wʋm Zugsɔb Wina'am dammir lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la, ba da zɔɔ keŋ su'a tiis gbina ni.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am buol dau la, ka ye, “Fʋ bɛ yaanɛ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M wʋmi fʋ dammir ka dabiem kpɛn'ɛm bɔzugɔ m pa'a anɛ biel, lin ka m su'a m mɛŋ.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am lɛbis o ye, “Anɔ'ɔn yɛlif ye fʋ anɛ biellɛ? Fʋ maal bɔ? Fʋ zan'asi m nɔɔr nɛ ka di tikanɛ wala ka m daa kpa'asidif ye mid ka fʋ dii li la nɛ bɛɛ?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Ka dau la lɛbis ye, “Pu'a kan ka fʋ tisim la, onɛ tisim tiig la wal ka m di.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛl pu'a la ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka fʋ maal ala?” Ka pu'a la ye, “Waaf la pan'asim ka m di.”

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛl waaf la ye, “Fʋn maal nwa' la zug, kaanb bɛ'ɛd na bɛɛ fʋ zug bʋnkɔnbid buudi wʋsa sʋʋgin! Fʋ na vuudi fʋ pʋʋr zug, ka dit titan, hali ti paae fʋ nyɔvʋr bɛn.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Ka dataadʋg na bɛ fʋn nɛ pu'a la sʋʋgin, ka lɛm bɛ fʋ biis nɛ pu'a la biis sʋʋgin. Ka o na mɛdigi fʋ zug ka fʋn mɛ na dum o nɔbkpansinkpan'ar.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛl pu'a la ye, “Fʋ ya'a nɔk pʋʋg m na kɛ ka fʋ nyɛ tɔɔg hali fʋ du'am daar. Fʋ ya'a ti ye fʋ du'a biis, li na zabid hali, la'an nɛ wala fʋ ya'amlɛog na bɛɛ fʋ sid san'an, ka o mɛ sʋ'ʋf.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl Dau la ye, “Fʋn siaki fʋ pu'a nɔɔr ka di tiwal kanɛ ka m digil nɔɔr ye fʋ da di la, kaanb bɛ'ɛd bɛ teŋ la zugʋ fʋ yɛla. Fʋ na namis hali ka paam diibi di, hali ti paae fʋ nyɔvʋr bɛn.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Gɔn'ɔs nɛ mɔyaalis na yi teŋ la zug, ka fʋ na dit tiis wala nɛ mɔbiili.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: Ɔnsir na yiif ka fʋ nyaan paam diibi di, hali ti paae fʋn na lɛb teŋin daasi'er, bɔzugɔ li anɛ anina ka fʋ yina. Fʋ anɛ titan, ka na lɛb titanin.”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Adam da pʋd o pu'a la yʋ'ʋr ye Hawa, bɔzugɔ onɛ an saalib wʋsa ma.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am nɔk bʋnkɔnbid gbana maal fuudi yɛɛl Adam nɛ o pu'a.

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛl ye, “Ninsaal la yʋ'ʋn nwɛnɛ tinam nɛ, ka mi' sʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛdi bakid. Li pʋ sʋ'ʋm ye o pun'oe nyɔvʋr tiig la wala di ka vʋe saŋa wʋsaa.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am kad o yis Eden lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la, ye o keŋ kua teŋgbauŋ kanɛ ka o yi la na.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Ka o kad dau la yis ka kɛ ka Kerubnam sieba gur Eden lɔmbɔn'ɔg la za'anɔɔr. Ka zaŋ sʋ'ʋg dinɛ dit tuon nɛ nya'aŋ ka li ian'ad pil-pil ka giligid zin'ig la wʋsa gu'ud suor kanɛ ken nyɔvʋr tiigin la.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Adam da digin nɛ o pu'a Hawa ka o nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ ka ba pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Kain. Ka Hawa ye, “Nɛ Wina'am paŋ ka m du'a dau.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka o lɛn du'a o pitʋ Abɛl n paas. Abɛl da gʋ'ʋnnɛ kɔnbid, ka Kain mɛ an kpaad.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Ka saŋa ti paae ye ba maal maannɛ tis Wina'am la, Kain da nɔk o zʋʋd la sieba na tis Zugsɔb la,

translation_verse: Sidim Bɔn'ɔg kanɛ ka ba da tʋ'ʋs tanp la da pɛ'ɛl nɛ bʋmbu'azulima ka kotaal bɛ li pʋʋgin, ka Sodom nɛ Gomora na'anam la da zɔt la, ba nidib sieba da lu nɛ bʋmbu'ad la ni, ka banɛ kpɛlim la zɔɔ dʋ zuoya la zug.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Na'anama anaasi la da faaɛn Sodom nɛ Gomora la'ad nɛ ba disʋma wʋsa mɔri keŋ.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Ba da la'am nɔk Abram pitʋ biig Lot nɛ o la'ad wʋsa mɔri keŋ, bɔzugɔ o da bɛnɛ Sodom teŋin.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Ka dau sɔ' yi tanpin la zɔɔ mɔr labaari kena tis Abram onɛ an Hibiru nid la. Abram yir da kpi'enɛ Mamir onɛ an Ammon nid la tititada. Mamir nɛ o pitib banɛ an Anɛr nɛ Esikol da mɔri nɔnaar nɛ Abram.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Abram n da wʋm ye ba gban'e Lot n keŋ la, o da buol o yidim ka ba la'as kɔbistan' nɛ pii nɛ anii (

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la ka Abram pʋdig o dap la ka ba zab nɛ ba ka kadi ba mɔri paae Hoba dinɛ bɛ Damaskus tempʋʋg datiuŋ baba la.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: O da paam la'ad la wʋsa faaɛn ka mɔr o pitʋ biig Lot nɛ o la'ad wʋsa, nɛ pu'ab wʋsa nɛ nidib la wʋsa lɛb na. Melkizedek niŋ Abram zug albareka

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Abram n da zabi nyaŋ Kedolma na'ab nɛ na'abanɛ wʋsa da la'as nɛ o ka lɛbid na la, Sodom Na'ab da yina sia'al o Seave Bɔn'ɔg zin'igin.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Ka Melkizedek onɛ an Salem Na'ab la mɔr diib nɛ daam yina. O da anɛ Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la maanmaan.

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: Ka o niŋ Abram bareka yɛt ye, “Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa, ka maal agɔl nɛ teŋ la niŋim Abram zug albareka.

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Ka bareka mɛ bɛ nɛ Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la, bɔzugɔ o nɔki fʋ dataasi niŋi fʋ nu'usin.” Ka Abram da yis la'abanɛ ka o fan' la wʋsa yinne piiga pʋʋgin tis o.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Ka Sodom Na'ab yɛl Abram ye, “Zaŋim nidib la tisim ka sʋ'oe la'ad la.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Amaa Abram yɛl Sodom Na'ab la ye, “Mam ʋki m nu'usi tis Zugsɔb Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa ka maal agɔl nɛ teŋ la, pɔɔ zi'el

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: ye m kʋ di'e si'eli yii fʋ san'anɛ, baa li ya'a anɛ gum bɛɛ ta'adir nwiiga. M pʋ bɔɔd ye fʋ ti yɛl bɛog daar ye fʋnɛ kɛ ka mam Abram lieb bʋmmɔra.

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Ayei, mam kʋ di'e si'ela, ya'a ka' dikanɛ ka m nidib la di laa. Amaa kɛl ka Anɛr nɛ Esikol nɛ Mamir banɛ dɔllimi keŋ zaba la paami ba pʋʋr.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa nya'aŋ ka Abram wʋm Zugsɔb pian'ad zaansʋŋin, ye, “Abram, da zɔt dabiem! Ka m na gurif ka yɛltɔɔg kʋ paae fɔ, ka na tisif yʋ'ʋtita'ar.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Ka Abram yɛl ye, “Naa, m Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔba! Bɔ ka fʋ ye fʋ tisim, ka m ka' biig la? Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ ye o dii m faar la, ka'anɛ Eliezer onɛ yi Damaskus la naa?”

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Ka Abram lɛn yɛl ye, “Fʋ pʋ tisim biisɛ, dinzugɔ sankpan'as onɛ bɛ m yin la na dii m faar.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis o ye, “Ayei, dau kaŋa kʋ dii fʋ faarɛ, amaa fʋ mɛŋ biribiŋ du'adiŋi na dii fʋ faar.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Ka o kɛ ka o yi paalʋ ka yɛl o ye, “Gɔsim saŋgbana la ni ka kaal nwadbibis la! Fʋ sid na nyaŋi kaali baa?” Ka lɛn yɛl o ye, “Ala ka fʋ yaas mɛ na zu'oe.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Ka Abram da niŋ Zugsɔb yadda, ka Zugsɔb gɛlig ka yɛl ye o anɛ pʋpielim sɔb o tuon.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, “Manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ mɔri fʋ yi Ur Kaldea teŋin kɛn teŋ kaŋa na ye fʋ sʋ'oe li.”

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Amaa Abram yɛl ye, “Naa, m Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔba! M na niŋ wala ka baŋ ye mam na sʋ'oe li?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl o ye, “Mɔr na'asa'a, nɛ bʋnya'aŋ, nɛ pɛrabanɛ an yʋma atan', tan' nɛ sian'arin dawan nɛ na'adawan na.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Ka Abram mɔri li wʋsa na ka kɔdigi ba buak pʋsʋk pʋsʋkʋ digili ba ka ba ya'ad taaba, amaa o pʋ buak dawana la.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Ka zʋʋnd da sig na ye ba di ni'im la, ka Abram kadi ba.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Ka winnigi da lut la, gbɛɛm da zɛɛg Abram ka o gbis ka zin'ig la lieb lik biridi ka dabiem kpɛn' o.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Zʋmaaŋ kanɛ paas anaasi la ni, fʋ biis na ti lɛb kpɛla na, bɔzugɔ Amor dim tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la nam pʋ paae li bɛnnɛ.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Ka winnigi da li ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb la, Abram nyɛ ka bugum nɛ nyɔ'ɔs dɔl bʋnkɔnbbu'ama la teŋsʋki gaad.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Daakan la ka Zugsɔb la maal nɔnaar nɛ Abram ye, “M na kɛ ka fʋ yaas sʋ'oe teŋgbauŋ nwa' wʋsa, lin yi Egipt teŋ titɔndig la paae Efiritis kɔldatita'ar la nɛ

english_verse: They will possess the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
translation_verse: Ken dim sʋ'ʋlim la, nɛ Kenas dim nɛ Kadmon dim

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: nɛ Hitti dim nɛ Perizi dim nɛ Refa dim

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: nɛ Amor dim nɛ Keenan dim nɛ Girgas dim nɛ Jebus dim la wʋsa.”

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Abram pu'a Sarai da nam pʋ du'a biiga. Amaa o da mɔr yammʋg onɛ an Egipt pu'asadir ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Haga.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Ka o digin nɛ o ka o nɔk pʋʋg. Haga da nyɛ ka o mɔr pʋʋg la ka pin'ili nɛ'ɛsid Sarai.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Ka Sarai yɛl Abram ye, “Nɛ'ɛskaŋa wʋsa yinɛ fʋ san'an na! Manɛ nɔki m yammʋgi tisif, ka on yʋ'ʋn nyɛ ka o mɔr pʋʋg la o pʋ lɛn na'asid mam ya'asa. Zugsɔb la na gaŋ onɛ mɔr bʋʋd mam nɛ fʋn sʋʋgin!”

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Ka Abram yɛl Sara ye, “Fʋ yammʋg la bɛnɛ fʋ nu'usin. Maalim o fʋn na maal si'em!” Ka Sara namis Haga hali ka o zɔ ka bas o.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak da nyɛ Haga ka o bɛ mɔɔgin zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om bun, ka li kpi'e suokanɛ ken Seur la.

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: Ka maliak la yɛl o ye, “Haga onɛ an Sarai yammʋga, fʋ yi yaanɛ na, ka wa'ae yaanɛ?” Ka o gandig ye, “M zɔtnɛ yiti m zugdaan Sarai san'an.”

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb maliak la yɛl o ye, “Ayei! Lɛm Sarai san'an ka siak o nɔɔr!”

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn yɛl o ye, “Fʋn mɔr pʋsi'a nannanna la, fʋ na du'a biribiŋ ka pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Isimael, Zugsɔb la nyɛ fʋ namisʋg la zug.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: Biig la na gɔɔnd nwɛnɛ wɛog bʋŋ nɛ ka kisig sɔ' wʋsa, ka sɔ' wʋsa mɛ na kisig o, ka on nɛ o ba'abiis na an dataas nɛ taaba.”

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Ka Haga pʋd Wina'am onɛ pian' tis o la yʋ'ʋr ye, “Fʋnɛ an Wina'am onɛ nyɛtim” Ka yɛl ye, “M sid nyɛ Wina'am ka nan kpɛn vʋe!”

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Lin ka ba buon bulig la ye Berlahairoi la. Li nan kpɛm bɛ Kades nɛ Bered teŋsʋk hali ti paae zina.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: M na maal nɔnaar man nɛ fʋn teŋsʋk, ka fʋ yaas na nɔbigi zu'oe hali ti galis.”

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Ka Abram vanbin teŋin na'as o, ka Wina'am yɛl o ye,

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Ba kʋ lɛm buonnɛ fʋ yʋ'ʋr ye Abram ya'asa, fʋ yʋ'ʋr na anɛ Abraham, bɔzugɔ m na kɛ ka fʋ lieb buudi bɛdegʋ yaab.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Man na tisif du'am bɛdegʋ ka fʋ na lieb buudi kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb yaab, ka na'anam na yii fʋ san'an na.

english_verse: I will always keep the promise I have made to you and your descendants, because I am your God and their God.
translation_verse: Man na kɛ ka m nɔnaar kanɛ ka m maal man nɛ fʋn teŋsʋk la bɛ saŋa kanɛ ka' naarɛ, hali ti paae fʋ yaas banɛ na dɔlli fʋ nya'aŋ na. Man na an fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas wʋsa Wina'am.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: M na nɔk Keenan teŋ la wʋsa tis fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ, ka na aan ba Wina'am.”

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Asɛɛ ka ya kpɛn' baŋʋ ka li lieb nɔnaar kanɛ bɛ mam nɛ fʋn sʋʋgin.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Biribiŋ kanɛ wʋsa pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋʋ, yanam yisim o buudi la ni, bɔzugɔ o ki'is man nɔnaar la nɛ.”

english_verse: Abraham, from now on your wife's name will be Sarah instead of Sarai.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am lɛn yɛl Abraham ye, “Da lɛm buonnɛ fʋ pu'a la ye Sarai, yʋ'ʋn buolim o ye, ‘Sara.’

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: Man na niŋ o bareka ka o na du'a biribiŋi tisif. M mɛ na niŋ o bareka ka o lieb buudi bɛdegʋ yaab. Ka buudi na'anam na yii o san'an na.”

english_verse: Then he asked God, “Why not let Ishmael inherit what you have promised me?”
translation_verse: Ka Abraham yɛl Wina'am ye, “Li ya'a anɛ Isimael n ye o di'e albareka kaŋa.”

english_verse: But God answered: No! You and Sarah will have a son. His name will be Isaac, and I will make an everlasting promise to him and his descendants.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am lɛbis o ye, “Ayei! Fʋ pu'a Sara na du'a biribiŋi tisif, ka fʋ na pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Isaak. Ka m na maali m nɔnaar nɛ on nɛ o yaas ka li bɛ saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: M wʋm fʋn sɔsim si'eli zaŋi keŋ Isimael yɛla la; gɔsima, m na niŋ o zug bareka ka o du'a biis bɛdegʋ ka tuongatib pii nɛ ayi' na yi o san'an na. M na kɛ ka o lieb teŋ tita'ar sɔb.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: Amaa li anɛ fʋ biig Isaak onɛ ka Sara na du'a yʋʋm anwana win la na paam mam nɔnaar bareka la.”

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Wina'am nɛ Abraham sɔnsig la da naae la, o da bas Abraham ka gaad.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb da nie o mɛŋi tis Abraham titita'ar dinɛ bɛ Mamir teŋin la, saŋkanɛ ka o da zin' o fuud sʋgʋr za'anɔɔrin nintaŋ tisʋʋs saŋa la.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Ka Abraham ʋk o zugʋ gɔs ka nyɛ ka dapa atan' zi'e yamma. Ka on nyɛɛ ba la, o duoe nɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ zɔɔ tʋ'ʋsi ba ka su'uni o zugʋ na'asi ba,

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: ka yɛli ba ye, “M zugdaana, ya ya'a na siak, yanam da gaadɛ ka bie m yin na nu ku'om!

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Zi'enimi ka ba mɔr ku'om bi'ela na ka ya wabisi ya nɔba, ka zin'in tikaŋa gbinnin vʋ'ʋs,

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: ka m tisi ya diib ka ya di ka paam paŋi gaad. Bɔzugɔ ya tis nɛ man onɛ aan ya sankpan'as la girima ka yii m yin na.” Ka ba lɛbis o ye, “Tɔ'! Maalim ala.”

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”
translation_verse: Ka Abraham duoe tɔ'ɔtɔ kpɛn' Sara san'an fuug sʋgʋrin, ka yɛl o ye o duom tɔ'ɔtɔ mak zɔ'ɔm kuriba atan' maal bodobodo,

english_verse: After saying this, he rushed off to his herd of cattle and picked out one of the best calves, which his servant quickly prepared.
translation_verse: ka gaadi keŋ niigi la ni gaŋ na'apɔlsʋŋ ka yɛl o dasaŋ ye o kʋʋm maal.

english_verse: He then served his guests some yogurt and milk together with the meat. While they were eating, he stood near them under the tree,
translation_verse: Ka o mɔr bin'ispielig nɛ bin'isgbisidim nɛ ni'im sɛn'ɛda la na pʋdigi tis saam la ka ba dit; ka Abraham zi'e tiig la gbinnin gu'usid.

english_verse: and they asked, “Where's your wife Sarah?” “She is right there in the tent,” Abraham answered.
translation_verse: Ka ba bu'os o ye, “Fʋ pu'a Sara bɛ yaanɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “O bɛ fuug sʋgʋrin la sa.”

english_verse: Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was well past the age for having children.
translation_verse: Ka Abraham nɛ o pu'a Sara da kʋdig ka Sara tʋʋg du'am.

english_verse: So she laughed and said to herself, “Now that I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really know such happiness?”
translation_verse: Ka o la' o sʋʋnrin sa ka yɛl ye, “Li na niŋ wala ka mam pu'anya'aŋ kʋdkaŋa lɛn du'a ya'asɛ? Ka m zugdaan mɛ kʋdigi anwana la?”

english_verse: The Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh? Does she doubt that she can have a child in her old age?
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Abraham ye, “Bɔ ka Sara la', ka yɛl ye on pu'anya'aŋ kʋdkaŋa kʋ nyaŋi du'a?

english_verse: I am the Lord! There is nothing too difficult for me. I'll come back next year at the time I promised, and Sarah will already have a son.”
translation_verse: Si'el bɛɛ tɔi tis Zugsɔb laa? Man ti ye m lɛb yʋʋm anwana win na la, ka Sara na mɔr biribiŋ.”

english_verse: Sarah was so frightened that she lied and said, “I didn't laugh.” “Yes, you did!” he answered. Abraham Prays for Sodom
translation_verse: Dabiem da kpɛn' Sara ka o ki'is ye on pʋ la'aa, amaa ka o ye, “Asida, fʋ la'aya!”

english_verse: When the three men got ready to leave, they looked down toward Sodom, and Abraham walked part of the way with them.
translation_verse: Ka dap la duoe kennɛ kpa'ad Sodom, ka Abraham zi'eli ba suor. Abraham sɔs Wina'am Sodom teŋ yɛla

english_verse: The Lord said to himself, “I should tell Abraham what I am going to do,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Man na su'a dinɛ ka m ye m maal la nɛ Abraham?

english_verse: since his family will become a great and powerful nation that will be a blessing to all the other nations on earth.

translation_verse: Ka Abraham ye, “Tɔ', m pɔya.”

english_verse: One day, Abraham told Abimelech, “Some of your servants have taken over one of my wells.”
translation_verse: Ka Abraham fabili tis Na'ab Abimelek bulig kanɛ ka Na'ab yammis la faaɛn la yɛla.

english_verse: “This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Man zi' onɛ tʋm nwaa, fʋ mɛ pʋ yɛli ma. Zina ma'aa ka m wʋm.”

english_verse: Abraham gave Abimelech some sheep and cattle, then the two men made a peace treaty.
translation_verse: Ka Abraham mɔr pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi na tis Na'ab Abimelek ka babayi' la maal nɔnaar nɛ taaba.

english_verse: Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep,
translation_verse: Ka Abraham yis pɛsa'as ayɔpɔi o pɛ'ɛs la ni zi'eli ba kɔn'.

english_verse: and Abimelech asked, “Why have you done this?”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Abimelek bu'os o ye, “Fʋ gaans pɛsa'as ayɔpɔi la ye fʋ maal bɔ?”

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: Ka Abraham lɛbis ye, “M bɔɔd ye fʋ di'e pɛsa'as ayɔpɔi la ka li pa'al ye manɛ tu bulig la.”

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Alazug ka ba buon zin'ig la ye Beerseba bɔzugɔ anina ka nidib ayi' nwa' pɔɔ tis taaba.

english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Nɔnaar la nya'aŋ la ka Abimelek nɛ Fikol onɛ an o soogianam kpɛɛm la lɛbi kul Filistia sʋ'ʋlimin.

english_verse: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and worshiped the eternal Lord God.
translation_verse: Abraham da sɛ tima'asir Beerseba teŋin ka pʋ'ʋs Wina'am Kanɛ Ka' Naar la.

english_verse: Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him. Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
translation_verse: Ka lina wʋsa nya'aŋ ka Wina'am gban'e ye o kpans Abraham yadda niŋiri gɔs, ka buol o ye, “Abraham!” Ka Abraham siak ye, “Naa! Manɛ nwa'.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl ye, “Nɔkimi fʋ biyimmir Isaak onɛ ka fʋ nɔŋ la mɔri keŋ Moria teŋin ka m na pa'alif zuokanɛ ka fʋ na nɔk o maal nyu'or maannɛ tis mam.”

english_verse: So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la Abraham da isigi nɔk o yammis ayi' nɛ o biig Isaak ka bɔ daad linɛ na maal maan la ka ban' o buŋi gban'e suori ken zin'ikanɛ ka Wina'am yɛl o la.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: Abraham da keŋi daba atan', ka daba atan' daar la o da ʋk o zugʋ gɔsi nyɛ zin'ig la ka li bɛ lallisa.

english_verse: He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
translation_verse: Ka Abraham yɛl o yammis la ye, “Kpɛlimmi kpɛla nɛ bʋŋ la, ka mam nɛ biig la keŋi pʋ'ʋs ka lɛb na.”

english_verse: Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along,
translation_verse: Ka Abraham nɔk daad linɛ na maal maan la ziil o biig Isaak ka o mɛŋ mɔr sʋ'ʋg nɛ bugum, ka babayi' la dɔl taaba ken.

english_verse: Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?” “My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.” The two of them walked on, and
translation_verse: Ka Abraham lɛbis ye, “M biiga, Wina'am na gɔs pɛ'og kanɛ na maal maan la yɛla.” Ka babayi' la dɔl taaba keŋ.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: Ban da paae zin'ikan ka Wina'am pa'ali ba la, ka Abraham mɛ' maan bimbim ka kɔ' daadi pa'ali li zugin, ka lɔɔ o biig Isaak n pa'al daad linɛ bɛ bimbim la zug.

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: Ka tiɛn o nu'ugʋ nɔk sʋ'ʋg ye o kɔdig biig la maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb maliak naan saazugʋ buol o ye, “Abraham, Abraham!” Ka o siak ye, “Naa! Manɛ nwa'.”

english_verse: “Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
translation_verse: Ka maliak la ye, “Digilim sʋ'ʋg la, ka da si'is biig la. Nannanna, m baŋ ye fʋ sid zɔt man Wina'am, fʋn pʋ mɔŋimi fʋ biyimmir la.”

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in the bushes. So he took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.
translation_verse: Ka Abraham gɔs mɔɔgin la nyɛ pɛraug ka gɛnda vil o iila zi'el. Ka o keŋ nɔk pɛraug la maal maan la ka bas o biig la.

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Ka Abraham pʋd zin'ig la ye Zugsɔb Na Bɔɔ Tis. Ka lin yi saŋkan la paae zina nidib yɛt ye, “Zugsɔb zuorin la o na bɔɔ tis.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak da lɛm buol Abraham ya'as

english_verse: You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise,
translation_verse: ka yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb yɛlif ye, ‘Fʋn siak ka pʋ mɔŋimi fʋ biyimmir la zugɔ, m pɔya ye

english_verse: “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live.
translation_verse: m na niŋi fʋ zug bareka bɛdegʋ, ka kɛ ka fʋ yaas na ti zu'oe bɛdegʋ wʋʋ nwadbibis banɛ bɛɛ agɔla bɛɛ titanbin'isʋg kanɛ bɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la; ba na nyaŋi ba bi'emnam wʋsa ka faaɛn ba tɛɛns.

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: Fʋ yaas la ma'asim zug dunia buudi wʋsa na paam bareka, fʋn siak mam nɔɔr la yɛla.’”

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: Ka Abraham lɛb o yammis la san'an ka ba dɔl taaba lɛb Beerseba n zin'in anina bi'ela.

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Ka Nahor pu'abil onɛ yʋ'ʋri da buon Reuma mɛ da du'a biribis anaasi, ka ba yʋda anɛ Teba nɛ Gaham nɛ Tahas nɛ Maaka.

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: “M anɛ saan teŋ nwa' pʋʋgin. Linzug, kuosimi paalʋ tisi nɛ m ka li na an zin'ikanɛ ka m mummi m kum.”

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Ti zugdaana, wʋmma! Fʋ anɛ Wina'am na'abiig ka bɛ nɛ ti kpɛla, gɔsimi ti yaad zin'igin wʋsa ka fʋn bɔɔd ye fʋ mumi fʋ kum zin'isi'a wʋsa fʋn mum! Ti sɔ' kʋ kadif ye fʋ da mum kum yaadin nwaa.”

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: ka yɛli ba ye, “Ya ya'a siaki m nɔɔr ye m mumi m kum la, m na sɔsi ya ka ya bɛlim Zohar biig Efiron n tisim,

english_verse: to sell me Machpelah Cave at the end of his field. I'll pay what it's worth, and all of you can be witnesses.”
translation_verse: ka o nɔk Makipiela tampinlɛuŋ kanɛ bɛɛ o pɔɔg nɔɔrin la tisim. Ka o ya'a siak on kuos o paalʋ la tisim ka m yɔ ka di'e li ka li an zin'ikanɛ ka m na mumi m kum ya teŋ nwa' ni.”

english_verse: “Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl ye, “Ayei, kɛlisima! Mam nɔk paalʋ la nɛ tampinlɛuŋ kanɛ bɛ li pʋʋgin la tisif zaalim m buudi la nifin. Kem mumi fʋ kum!”

english_verse: Once again, Abraham bowed down
translation_verse: Ka Abraham lɛn igin teŋin nidib la tuon

english_verse: and said to Ephron, “In front of these witnesses, I offer you the full price, so I can bury my wife. Please accept my offer.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl Efiron ba nifin ye, “M ba', kɛlisima! M bɔɔd ye fʋ kuos paalʋ la tisim ka di'e li ligidi, ka m na nyaŋi mumi m kum anina.”

english_verse: “But sir,” the man replied, “the property is worth only
translation_verse: “M zugdaana, kɛlisima! Paalʋ la ligidi anɛ anzurifa kɔbisnaasi (

english_verse: So Abraham buried his wife Sarah in Machpelah Cave that was in the field
translation_verse: Ka li nya'aŋ ka Abraham mum o pu'a Sara Makipiela tampinlɛuŋʋn, dinɛ kpi'e Mamir, linɛ an Hebron teŋi bɛ Keenan teŋgbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Abraham was now a very old man. The Lord had made him rich, and he was successful in everything he did.
translation_verse: Abraham yʋ'ʋn da kʋdig nɛ hali, ka Zugsɔb la niŋ o zug albareka si'el wʋsa ni.

english_verse: One day, Abraham called in his most trusted servant and said to him, “Solemnly promise me
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o sankpan'as kpɛɛm onɛ gɔsid o yir la'ad wʋsa la ye, “Nɔkimi fʋ nu'ugʋ si'isi m gbɛr,

english_verse: in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: ka m kɛ ka fʋ pɔ Zugsɔb onɛ an arezana nɛ dunia Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr zug, ye fʋ kʋ li'a Keenan dim banɛ ka man nɛ ban la'am bɛ la pu'asadire tisim biig la.

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ na keŋi m mɛŋ teŋin nɛ m mɛŋ du'adibin bɔ pu'a na tisim biig Isaak.”

english_verse: But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
translation_verse: Ka sankpan'as la bu'os o ye, “Ka m ya'a keŋ ka pu'a la pʋ siak ye o dɔllim ka ti lɛb kpɛla na, mam mɔri fʋ biig la lɛb fʋn yi teŋ si'a kena laa?”

english_verse: “No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what.
translation_verse: Ka Abraham yɛl ye, “Mid ka fʋ mɔri m biig la lɛb anina!”

english_verse: The Lord who rules heaven brought me here from the land where I was born and promised that he would give this land to my descendants forever. When you go back there, the Lord will send his angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son.
translation_verse: Ka ye, “Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ an arezana Wina'am, ka mɔrimi yii m saam yin nɛ m du'adib teŋin kɛn kpɛla na ka pɔɔ zi'eli m ye, o na nɔk teŋ kaŋa tisim yaas la; Wina'am kan na kɛ ka o maliak dɔlli fʋ keŋ ka fʋ bɔ pu'a anina na tisim biig la.

english_verse: If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.”
translation_verse: Pu'a la ya'a zan'as ka pʋ dɔlli fʋ kenaa, fʋn yisi fʋ mɛŋ nɔpɔɔr kanɛ ka fʋ pɔɔ zi'el la pʋʋgin. Amaa mid ka fʋ dɔlli m biig la keŋ!”

english_verse: So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
translation_verse: Ka sankpan'as la duoe gban'e Abraham gbɛr, ka pɔ nɔɔrɛ zi'el yɛl kaŋa zug.

english_verse: Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
translation_verse: Ka sankpan'as la nɔk o zugdaan la yʋgʋma piiga, ka nɔk la'asʋma o zugdaan la san'an mɔri keŋ. O da yii keŋ Aram Naharam gaadi keŋ paae tempʋkanɛ ka Nahor da zin' la.

english_verse: When he got there, he let the camels rest near the well outside the city. It was late afternoon, the time when the women came out for water.
translation_verse: Ka o kɛ ka yʋgʋma la igini kpi'en nɛ bulig, teŋ la yiŋ. Li da anɛ zaam, saŋkanɛ ka pu'ab ken kɔlʋgin wikid ku'om la.

english_verse: The servant prayed: You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today.
translation_verse: Ani ka o sɔs Wina'am ye, “Wina'am onɛ aan m zugdaan Abraham Wina'am, kɛl ka si'el wʋsa niŋ sʋ'ʋŋa zina tisim, ka li na an bareka tisim zugdaan la.

english_verse: The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water,
translation_verse: Gɔsima, m zi'enɛ buligin nwa', ka teŋ la pu'asada na yina wik ku'om.

english_verse: and I'll ask one of them for a drink. If she gives me a drink and then offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen and that you have kept your promise to my master.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka m ya'a yɛl bipuŋ sɔ' ye, ‘M bɛlimnɛ, tisim ku'om nɛ nwam ka m nu, ka o na yɛl ye, “Di'em nu, ka kɛ ka m tisi fʋ yʋgʋma la ka ba nu mɛn.” Kɛl ka bipuŋ kan na an onɛ ka fʋ gaŋ ye fʋ tisi fʋ tʋmtʋm Isaak. Nɛ' ka m na baŋ ye fʋ pa'ali fʋ nɔŋilim nɛ m zugdaan la.’”

english_verse: Abraham's servant ran to her and said, “Please let me have a drink of water.”
translation_verse: Ka sankpan'as la tʋ'ʋs o tɔ'ɔtɔ ka yɛl o ye, “M bɛlimnɛ, tisim ku'om bi'ela.”

english_verse: “I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank.
translation_verse: Ka o tʋk yʋʋr la tɔ'ɔtɔ n zanl o nu'usin ka yɛl ye, “Di'em nu, m zugdaana;” ka tis o ku'om la.

english_verse: After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted.
translation_verse: Ka o kpa'ae ku'om la tɔ'ɔtɔ niŋ linɛ ka ba maal ka bʋnkɔnbid nuudi li pʋʋgin la, ka zɔɔ lɛb buligin la wik ku'om na. O da wiknɛ ala hali ka li ti siak yʋgʋma la wʋsa.

english_verse: Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
translation_verse: Ka dau la gɔsid o kii ka pʋ yɛl si'ela bɔzugɔ, o bɔɔd ye o baŋ ye Zugsɔb la maal o ken la sʋm bɛɛ?

english_verse: The servant had brought along an expensive gold ring and two large gold bracelets. When Rebekah had finished bringing the water, he gave her the ring for her nose and the bracelets for her arms.
translation_verse: Yʋgʋma la nuu naae la, ka o yis sanlim baŋ kanɛ ga'an nyɔnya ni nɛ sanlim baans ayi' banɛ pid nu'usin tis o,

english_verse: Then he said, “Please tell me who your father is. Does he have room in his house for me and my men to spend the night?”
translation_verse: ka bu'os o ye, “Fʋ aan anɔ'ɔn pu'ayua? M bɛlimnɛ, dɔɔg bɛɛ fʋ saam yin la ka m na gbɛɛn?”

english_verse: She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M anɛ Betuel pu'ayua, ka Nahor nɛ Milika aan m yaanam.”

english_verse: We have a place where you and your men can stay, and we also have enough straw and feed for your camels.”
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛl ye, “Ti mɔr yaama bɛdegʋ linɛ ka yʋgʋma la na ɔnb, dɔɔg mɛ bɛ ka fʋ na gbɛn.”

english_verse: Then the servant bowed his head and prayed,
translation_verse: Ka dau la igin teŋin zun'e Zugsɔb la,

english_verse: “I thank you, Lord God of my master Abraham! You have led me to his relatives and kept your promise to him.”
translation_verse: n yɛt ye, “Na'asi bɛ nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan m zugdaan Abraham Wina'am la, o nan kpɛn dɔlli m zugdaan la nɛ pʋpielim nɛ sida. O mɔrimi keŋi paae m zugdaan la du'adibin!”

english_verse: Rebekah ran straight home and told her family everything.
translation_verse: Ka pu'asadir la zɔɔ kuli yɛl o ma yidim linɛ niŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well.
translation_verse: Rebɛka da mɔr taʋn ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Laban, ka on da nyɛ sanlim baŋ linɛ bɛ Rebɛka nyɔɔrin nɛ baŋ banɛ pid o nu'ugin la, ka wʋm dau la yɛl o si'em la, o yii keŋ dau la san'an nyɛɛ o, ka o nan zi'e kpi'e nɛ yʋgʋma la bulig la baba.

english_verse: Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
translation_verse: On paae la, ka yɛl dau la ye, “Kem na ka fʋ anɛ onɛ ka Zugsɔb tisif bareka! Bɔ ka fʋ zi'e yiŋ kpɛla? M maal dɔkanɛ ka fʋ na gbɛn nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka yʋgʋma la na digin.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet.
translation_verse: Ka dau la dɔl Laban keŋ yin la ka ba yidigi ba la'ad la, ka tis yʋgʋma la yaama ka mɛ gbin'e ku'om na tis dau la nɛ o nidib ka ba pie ba nɔba.

english_verse: After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.” “Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
translation_verse: Ba daa mɔr diib na tisi ba ka o ye, “M ya'a pʋ yɛli ya man kɛn si'el yɛla la na, m kʋ di si'ela.” Ka Laban lɛbis ye, “Ka yɛlimi ti!”

english_verse: The servant explained: I am Abraham's servant.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “M anɛ Abraham sankpan'as.

english_verse: The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la niŋi m zugdaan la bareka ka o mɔr kpan'am hali. Zugsɔb la tis o pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi nɛ anzurifa nɛ sanlima. O mɔr sankpan'as dap nɛ sankpan'as pu'ab nɛ yʋgʋma nɛ bʋmis.

english_verse: Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything.
translation_verse: M zugdaan la pu'a Sara da du'a biribiŋi tis o saŋkanɛ ka o da kʋdig, ka o zaŋ on mɔr si'el wʋsa tis biig la.

english_verse: I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan.
translation_verse: M zugdaan la kɛnɛ ka m pɔ nɔɔr ye m kʋ bɔ pu'a Keenan dim pu'asada la nii tis o biribiŋ la.

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for my son from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: O yɛlim ye m kemi o saam yidimin, nɛ banɛ aan o dɔɔg nidibin la bɔ pu'a na tis o biig la.”

english_verse: I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
translation_verse: Ka m bu'osim zugdaan la ye, “Ka m ya'a keŋ ka pu'a la pʋ siak ye o dɔllimi lɛb na?”

english_verse: My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb kanɛ ka m dɔl la na tʋm o maliak ka o dɔlli fʋ keŋ ka kɛ ka fʋ ken la niŋ sʋ'ʋŋa tisif, ka fʋ na nyɛ pu'a m mɛŋ dɔɔg nɛ m saam yidimin tisim biig la.

english_verse: But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ ya'a keŋi m dɔɔg dimin la ka ba zan'as ka pʋ kɛ ka pu'a la dɔlli fɔ, fʋ yisi fʋ mɛŋ nɔɔr kanɛ ka fʋ pɔɔ zi'el la pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son
translation_verse: “Ka man kpɛn paae buligin la zina na la, m sɔsi m zugdaan Abraham Zugsɔb Wina'am la ye, ‘Maalim yɛlkanɛ zug ka m kɛn zina nwa' na la tisim.

english_verse: while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, m zi'enɛ bulkaŋa nwa' nɔɔrin kpɛla, pu'asadir ya'a kena ka m yɛl o ye o tisim ku'om nwammin ka m nu

english_verse: If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
translation_verse: ka o ya'a yɛlim ye, “Di'em nu, ka m mɛ wiki tisi fʋ yʋgʋma la,” kɛl ka on sɔb na an onɛ ka Zugsɔb la gaŋ ye o tisim zugdaan biig la.’

english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Man ti sɔs Wina'am m sʋʋnrin naae la, ka Rebɛka buk yʋʋri kenna. Ka o paae na sig buligin la wik ku'om na ka m yɛl o ye, ‘M bɛlimnɛ tisim ku'om ka m nu.’

english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: Ka o tʋk yʋʋr la zanl o nu'ugin ka yɛl ye, ‘Di'em nu, m zugdaana, ka m wiki tis yʋgʋma la.’ Ka gbin'e ku'om la tisim ka m nu, ka o wiki tis yʋgʋma la ka ba nu mɛn.

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Ka m bu'os o ye, ‘Fʋ aan anɔ'ɔn pu'ayua?’ Ka o lɛbis ye, ‘M anɛ Betuel pu'ayua ka m yaanam an Nahor nɛ Milika.’ Ka m nɔk nyɔnya ni baŋi ga'al o nyɔnya ka pid o nu'us baans.

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: Ka m igin teŋin zun'e Zugsɔb onɛ aan m zugdaan Abraham Wina'am onɛ dɔlisim sʋ'ʋŋa ka m nyɛɛm zugdaan ba'abiig yaaŋi tis o biig la.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
translation_verse: Alazug, ya ya'a na niŋi m zugdaan la lin nar si'em nɛ linɛ an pʋpielim, yanam yɛlimim; ya'a lɛn ka' ala yanam mɛ yɛlim, ka m baŋ mam na niŋ si'em.”

english_verse: Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter.
translation_verse: Ka Laban nɛ Betuel lɛbis ye, “Nɛ' yinɛ Zugsɔb la san'an na, ti kʋ nyaŋi yɛlif si'ela.

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”
translation_verse: Rebɛka nwa', mɔr o kuli tisi fʋ zugdaan biig la ka o lieb o pu'a wʋʋ Zugsɔb la zi'el si'em la.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant bowed down and thanked the Lord.
translation_verse: Abraham sankpan'as la wʋm ban yɛl si'em la, ka igin teŋin Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
translation_verse: Ka yis sanlima nɛ anzurifa la'ad, nɛ fuudi tis Rebɛka, ka mɛ nɔk la'ad ka li ligidi zu'oe tis Rebɛka taʋn la nɛ o ma.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: Ka on nɛ nimbanɛ dɔl o kena la yʋ'ʋn di ka nu, ka gbɛɛn ani. Bɛogʋ nie la ka o yɛl ye, “M na sɔs suori lɛbi m zugdaan la san'an.”

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Rebɛka taʋn nɛ o ma lɛbis ye, “Kɛl ka bipuŋ la nan kpɛlimmi ti san'an wʋʋ dabpiiga ka ya nyaan kul.”

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o yɛli ba ye, “Da vi'idini m suorɛ! Zugsɔb la sadigim maali m ken la ka li an sʋ'ʋŋa la, m na sɔs suor ka lɛbi yɛli m zugdaan.” Ban mɔr Isaak pu'a na tis o si'em

english_verse: They answered, “Let's ask Rebekah what she wants to do.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Kɛl ka ti buol bipuŋ la mɛŋi bu'os o gɔs.”

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ka ba buol Rebɛka bu'os o ye, “Fʋ na dɔl dau kaŋa keŋɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn!”

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ala ka ba zi'el Rebɛka suor nɛ o biyuol nɛ Abraham sankpan'as la nɛ banɛ dɔl o keŋ la.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka ba kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis Rebɛka ye, “Ti taʋn, fʋ na wiak tusa-tusa! Fʋ yaas na nyaŋi ba dataasi faaɛn ba tɛɛns.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Ani ka Rebɛka nɛ o pu'asadtaaba la ban' ba yʋgʋma dɔl dau la ka ba kul.

english_verse: At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Ka Isaak onɛ yiri da bɛ Negef teŋgbauŋʋn la, da yi Berlahairoi baba kena.

english_verse: One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?” “He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
translation_verse: ka bu'os sankpan'as la ye, “Dau kanɛ yi sian'arin kenna tʋ'ʋsidi ti la aan anɔ'ɔnɛ?” Ka sankpan'as la lɛbis ye, “O anɛ m zugdaan.” Ka Rebɛka nɔk fubili lus o mɛŋ.

english_verse: The servant told Isaac everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Ani ka Sankpan'as la yɛl Isaak on maal si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: Isaac took Rebekah into the tent where his mother had lived before she died, and Rebekah became his wife. He loved her and was comforted over the loss of his mother.
translation_verse: Isaak da mɔr Rebɛka kpɛn'ɛs o ma Sara fuug sʋgʋrin, ka dii o ka o lieb o pu'a ka o da nɔŋ o. Ka li kɛ ka o sʋʋnr bʋk ka o pʋ lɛn tɛn'ɛsidi o ma Sara kum la yɛla nɛ sʋnsa'aŋɔ.

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: Ketura da du'a Zimran nɛ Joksan nɛ Medan nɛ Midian nɛ Isibak nɛ Sua.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Joksan da du'a biis ayi' ka ba yʋda buon Seeba nɛ Dedan. Ka Dedan biis an Asiria dim nɛ Letusii dim nɛ Leum dim.

english_verse: Midian also had five sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah.
translation_verse: Midian biis da anɛ Efa nɛ Efer nɛ Hanok nɛ Abida nɛ Eldaa. Bama wʋsa da anɛ Ketura yaas.

english_verse: While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac. The Death of Abraham
translation_verse: amaa on da nam vʋe la o da yis arezak la sieba tis o pu'abibis la biis ka kɛ ka ba yi Isaak san'anɛ lɛb tembanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la.

english_verse: Abraham died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Abraham da kʋdignɛ hali paae o yʋma bɛn ka nyaan kpii paae o yaanam.

english_verse: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him east of Hebron in Machpelah Cave that was part of the field Abraham had bought from Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite. Abraham was buried there beside his wife Sarah.
translation_verse: Pɔkan ka Abraham da da' yi Hitti dim ni la. Anina ka ba da mum Abraham nɛ o pu'a Sara.

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Abraham kum nya'aŋ la Wina'am da niŋ Isaak zug bareka, ka o zin'inɛ kpi'enɛ Berlahairoi buligin la. Abraham yaas yɛla (

english_verse: Ishmael was the son of Abraham and Hagar, the slave woman of Sarah.
translation_verse: Nwa' pa'an Abraham biig Isimael yaas yɛla: Sara yammʋg Haga onɛ da an Egipt nid la da du'a Isimael n tis Abraham.

english_verse: Ishmael had twelve sons, in this order: Nebaioth, Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
translation_verse: Isimael biis la yʋda nwana: Nebaiof ka Isimael du'a yiiga, ka onɛ tia'al la an Kedar nɛ Adibiel nɛ Mibsam

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: nɛ Misima nɛ Duma nɛ Masa

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: nɛ Hadar nɛ Tema nɛ Jetur nɛ Nafis nɛ Kedema.

english_verse: Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
translation_verse: Bama da an Isimael biis pii nɛ ayi' la, banɛ da aan ba buudi la tuongatib ka ba da zaŋi ba yʋda pʋd tɛɛns pii nɛ ayi' banɛ ka ba da mɛ' la.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: O yaas mɛ da zin'inɛ Havila nɛ Seur tɛɛns banɛ kpi'e Egipt titɔndig lɛbisid Asuor baba. Ba da lal nɛ ba du'adib la wʋsa.

english_verse: when he died. The Birth of Esau and Jacob
translation_verse: ) ka nyaan kʋdigi paae o bɛn ka maal ka'alim.

english_verse: Isaac was the son of Abraham,
translation_verse: Nwa' pa'an Abraham biig Isaak yaas yɛla: Abraham da anɛ Isaak saam.

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak da sɔs Zugsɔb n tis o pu'a la bɔzugɔ o da anɛ kʋndu'ar. Ka Zugsɔb gandigi o sɔsʋg, ka o pu'a Rebɛka nɔk liiba pʋʋg.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Ka biis la mɔɔd nɛ taaba o pʋʋgin la ka o bu'os ye, “Bɔɔ nwa' maan mam?” Ka ba keŋ Zugsɔb la san'an ye ba baŋ yɛl la gbin.

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl o ye, “Buudi ayi' bɛɛ fʋ pʋʋgin la, Nidiba ayi' ka fʋ ye fʋ du'a. Fʋ ya'a du'a ba, ba na pʋdig kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb. Ka yinne la na mɔr paŋi gat o tiraan, ka kpɛɛm la na lieb o pitʋ la tʋmtʋm.”

english_verse: the first baby was covered with red hair, so he was named Esau.
translation_verse: ka onɛ yi yiiga na la mu'oe ka o niŋgbina wʋsa mɔr kɔnbilʋg nwɛnɛ kɔnbʋg gbauŋ nɛ, ka ba pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Esau.

english_verse: The second baby grabbed on to his brother's heel, so they named him Jacob. Isaac was
translation_verse: Ka onɛ dɔl la gban'e Esau nɔbkpansinkpan'ar. Ka ba pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Jakob. Saŋkan ka Rebɛka du'a liiba la, Isaak yʋma da anɛ pisyuobʋ.

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Ka biis la nɔbig ka Esau lieb tɔn'ɔsi gɔɔnd mɔɔgin tɔn'ɔsid nɛ nimmua. Ka Jakob mɛ an ninkanɛ an baanlimm, ka bɛ yin saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak da bɔɔd mɔɔgin ni'im pamm, ka li kɛ ka o nɔŋ Esau on kʋʋd ni'im na tisid o la zug, amaa ka Rebɛka mɛ nɔŋ Jakob.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka Jakob dʋgid o zɛɛnd ka Esau yii keŋ mɔɔgin tɔn'ɔsi lɛb na, ka o kɔ'ɔm zabid hali.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl Jakob ye, “Tɔ'ɔtɔ! Tisimi fʋ dikanɛ mu'oe wii nwa' la, ka m vibidnɛ!”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “Sell me your rights as the first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “Asɛɛ ka fʋ siak ye din yi nannanna ken, fʋ kuosi fʋ kpɛuŋ faar la tisim.”

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Ka Esau lɛbis ye, “Gɔsima, m kpiidnɛ, ka kpɛuŋ faar la sʋm an bɔɔ tisi ma?”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “Promise me your birthrights, here and now!” And that's what Esau did.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl o ye, “Asɛɛ fʋ pɔɔ zi'el yiiga.” Ka o sid pɔɔ zi'el ka kuosi o kpi'euŋ faar la tis Jakob.

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob tis o bodobodo nɛ zɛɛnd la. Ka o di ka nu ka duoe keŋ o ken. Esau niŋnɛ ala ka o ba' kae o kpi'euŋ faar la yɛla.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Kɔ'ɔm da lu teŋin la nwɛnɛ kɔ'ɔm kanɛ da lu Abraham saŋa la nɛ, ka Isaak keŋ Na'ab Abimelek onɛ an Filistia dim Na'ab ka bɛ Gera teŋin la san'an.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl o ye, “Da keŋ Egipt teŋinɛ, bɛ teŋ kan ka m yɛl ye fʋ bɛ la.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Bɛ kpɛla bi'ela ka m na bɛ nɛf ka niŋif bareka. Fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas ka m na nɔk tɛɛns nwa' wʋsa tis, ka mam da kaanb si'em tis Abraham la na nan kpɛn zi'e ala.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka fʋ yaas zu'oe wʋʋ nwadbibisi an si'em bɛ saŋgbana ni la, ka m na tisi ba teŋ la wʋsa. Fʋ yaas ma'asim zug ka dunia nwa' tɛɛns wʋsa na nyɛ bareka.

english_verse: Isaac moved to Gerar
translation_verse: Ka Isaak nan kpɛn zin' Gera teŋin.

english_verse: with his beautiful wife Rebekah. He was afraid that someone might kill him to get her, and so he told everyone that Rebekah was his sister.
translation_verse: Ka teŋ la dap bu'os o pu'a la yɛla ka o ye, “O anɛ m taʋn,” bɔzugɔ o da zɔtnɛ dabiem nɛ on na yɛl ye, “O anɛ m pu'a.” O da tɛn'ɛs ye dap la na kʋʋ o Rebɛka zug, bɔzugɔ Rebɛka vɛnlnɛ hali.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Isaak n da bɛ teŋ la nii yuug la, Na'ab Abimelek onɛ an Filistia dim na'ab la gɔs nɛ takoro ni ka nyɛ ka Isaak di'emid nɛ Rebɛka.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la buol Isaak ka yɛl o ye, “O anɛ fʋ pu'a, ka bɔzug ka fʋ ye o anɛ fʋ taʋn?” Ka Isaak lɛbis ye, “M tɛn'ɛs ye m ya'a yɛl ye o anɛ m pu'a, ba na kʋʋmi o zug.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Ka Abimelek bu'os o ye, “Tʋʋm bɔɔ nwa' ka fʋ tʋm tisi ti nwa'? Dap la yinne tun'e digin nɛ fʋ pu'a la ka li pa'al ye fʋnɛ mɔr taal na tisi ti.”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Ka o tis nidib la wʋsa nɔɔr ye, “On wʋsa namis dau kaŋa bɛɛ o pu'a la, m na kɛ ka ba kʋʋ o.”

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: Ka Isaak kua teŋin la yʋʋm kan la m bun nɔɔr kɔbiga bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb da niŋ o bareka.

english_verse: and Isaac was so successful that he became very rich.
translation_verse: Ka o paam arezak bɛdegʋ ka o arezak la nɔbig hali ka o ti lieb bʋndaan.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: O da mɔr kɔnbid nɛ niigi nɛ yammis hali bɛdegʋ, ka lizug ka Filistia dim la yʋ'ʋn mɔr fufum.

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.
translation_verse: Ka bulis ban wʋsa ka o saam Abraham yammis la da tu la, Filistia dim la pin' ba nɛ titan.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Abimelek yɛl Isaak ye, “Duom tɔɔm ka basi ti, ka fʋ paŋ yʋ'ʋn gati ti nɛ.”

english_verse: Isaac left and settled in Gerar Valley,
translation_verse: Ka Isaak duoe laligi keŋ zin' Gera bɔn'ɔgin.

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak gaae bulbanɛ ka ba da tu o saam Abraham saŋa ka Filistia dim la pin' ba o kum nya'aŋ la. O da tis bulis la yʋ'ʋbanɛ ka o saam Abraham da pʋn buonnɛ ba la.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Isaak yammis la da tu bulsi'a bɔn'ɔgin nyɛ ku'oma'asig.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Ka Gera na'akemnib zab nɛ Isaak na'akemnib ka yɛl ye ku'om la anɛ bam bʋn, ka o pʋd bulig la ye Esek, ka li anɛ ban da zab nɛ o la zug.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Ka ba tu bulig yinne ya'as ka ba zab nɛ ba ya'as, ka o pʋd o li ye Sitna.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn keŋ tuonnɛ tu bulig ka sɔ' pʋ lɛn zabi li zugɔ, ka o pʋd bulkan ye Rehobof; ka yɛl ye, “Nannanna Zugsɔb yalig paalʋ tisi ti, ka ti na an sʋm ka keŋ tuon teŋ kaŋa pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Ka o yi anina keŋ Beerseba.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan ka Zugsɔb nie o mɛŋi tis o ka yɛl ye, “Manɛ aan fʋ saam Abraham Wina'am la. Da zɔt dabiem ka m bɛ nɛf. M na niŋi fʋ zug bareka ka fʋ yaas na nɔbig ka li anɛ m tʋmtʋm Abraham zug.”

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak mɛ' maan bimbim anina ka buol Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋri pʋ'ʋsid o. Anina ka o kpa' o Fuug Sʋgʋr ka o yammis tu bulig.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Abimelek yi Gera kɛɛn o san'an na, ka dɔl o na'ayikpɛɛm onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Ahuzaf nɛ o soogia kpɛɛm Fikol.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Ka Isaak bu'osi ba ye, “Bɔ ka ya kennɛ m san'an na? Ka' yanamɛ kisigim ka kadimi yisi ya teŋin la?”
