english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Asida ti baŋ ye Zugsɔb la bɛ nɛf. Alazug ka ti bɔɔd ye tinam nɛ fʋn maal nɔɔr yinne. Kɛl ka tinam nɛ fʋ naal nɔnaar

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: ka lin anɛ ye fʋ kʋ maali ti bɛ'ɛdɛ nwɛnɛ tinamɛ daa pʋ maalif bɛ'ɛd si'em la asɛɛ sʋ'ʋm ma'aa, ka ye fʋ yim nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm la. Ti mi' ye Zugsɔb la sid niŋif bareka nannanna.”

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak nyaan maal diib nɛ bʋnnuuda tisi ba ka ba di ka nu.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka ba kaanbi zi'el taaba. Ka Isaak zi'eli ba suor ka ba kul ka o kpɛlim nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Daakan la ka Isaak yammis kena yɛl o ye, “Bulig la ka ti tuud la, ti paae ku'om.”

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Ka o pʋd bulig la yʋ'ʋr ye Siiba. Lin yi saŋkan sa paae zina tempʋʋg la yʋ'ʋr anɛ Beerseba.

english_verse: But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_verse: Pu'a bama da san'am Isaak nɛ Rebɛka sʋnf hali.

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Isaak da kʋdignɛ ka o nini pʋ lɛn nyɛt sʋ'ʋŋaa. O da buol o bikpɛɛm Esau ka yɛl o ye, “M biiga!” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Naa, manɛ nwa'!”

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak ye, “M kʋdigya ka mɛ zi' daakan ka m na kpii.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: Duom nɔki fʋ tɔn'ɔsʋg la'ad dinɛ an tiraug nɛ piema la, kpɛn' sian'arin kʋ bʋnkɔnbʋg na

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: maal dikanɛ malis ka m nɔŋ la tisim ka m di, ka kaanb albareka tisif ka nyaan kpi.”

english_verse: Rebekah had been listening, and as soon as Esau left to go hunting,
translation_verse: Rebɛka da kɛlisidnɛ Isaak n pian'adi tisid o biig Esau la. Esau da yii kpɛn' sian'arin ye o kʋ bʋnkɔnbʋgʋ lɛb na la,

english_verse: she said to Jacob, “I heard your father tell Esau
translation_verse: ka Rebɛka yɛl o biig Jakob ye, “Gɔsima, m wʋm ka fʋ saam yɛli fʋ bier Esau

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: ye o kem sian'arinɛ kʋ bʋnkɔnbʋg na maal dikanɛ malisi tis o, ka o di ka niŋ o zug albareka Zugsɔb la tuon ka nyaan kpi.

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: Tɔ', m biiga, wʋm sʋ'ʋŋa ka maal mam ye m yɛlif si'el la.

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Yim keŋ kɔnbidin la gaŋ bʋpaalis ayi' mɔr na ka m maal dimalisiŋ nwɛnɛ on bɔɔd si'em la

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: mɔri keŋi tis o, ka o di ka kaanb albareka la tisif ka nyaan kpi.”

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl o ma Rebɛka ye, “Amaa m bier Esau anɛ dau kanɛ mɔr kɔnbilʋg ka mam pʋ mɔra.

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: Ka m saam ya'a si'isim ka baŋ ye li anɛ manɛ, li kʋ nwɛnɛ m bɔɔd ye m pan'as o nɛɛ? Ka li ya'a niŋ ala, o na pɔ nɔɔri niŋim ka ka' albareka.”

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Ka o ma la yɛl o ye, “M biiga kɛl ka kaanb bɛ'ɛd la dɔl mam. Tʋm mam yɛl si'em la; kem mɔri ba na tisim.”

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: Ka o keŋ gban'e ba na tis o. Ka o maal dikanɛ malis wʋʋ o saam la bɔɔd si'em la.

english_verse: She also covered the smooth part of his hands and neck with goatskins
translation_verse: ka lɛn nɔk bʋʋs la gbana ligil o nu'us nɛ o niŋgɔɔnr zin'ikanɛ ka' kɔnbilʋg la.

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: Ka yʋ'ʋn nɔk dimalisiŋ nɛ bodobodo la tis Jakob.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Ka o mɔri kpɛn' o saam la san'an ka pʋ'ʋs o ye, “Sɔnsiga!” Ka o siak ye, “Nambaa, m biiga. Fʋ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ?”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛbis o saam ye, “Manɛ fʋ bikpɛɛm Esau. M maal fʋn yɛlim si'em la. Duom di, ka kaanb albareka niŋim zug.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak bu'os o biig la ye, “Fʋ niŋ wala paami li tɔ'ɔtɔ ala m biiga?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb Wina'am la sʋŋim.”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Ka Isaak yɛl Jakob ye, “M biiga, li'elim na ka m si'isi fʋ gɔs ka baŋ ye fʋ sid anɛ Esau bɛɛ ka' Esau.”

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob li'el na ka o saam si'is o ka yɛl ye, “Kʋkɔr la anɛ Jakob kʋkɔr, amaa nu'us la anɛ Esau nu'us.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “Are you really my son Esau?” “Yes, I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os ye, “Ka fʋ sid anɛ m biig Esau?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn!”

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “M biiga, mɔr diib la na ka m di ka niŋi fʋ zug albareka.” Ka Jakob mɔr diib la keŋ tis o ka o di, ka o tis o daam ka o nu.

english_verse: Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.”
translation_verse: Ka o saam Isaak yɛl o ye, “M biiga kem na kuakim.”

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Ka o kena kuak o. Ka Isaak n wʋm o fuud la nyuug la, o da niŋ o zug albareka ka yɛl ye, “M biig la nyuug nwɛnɛ pɔkanɛ ka Zugsɔb niŋi li bareka nɛ.

english_verse: God will bless you, my son, with dew from heaven and with fertile fields, rich with grain and grapes.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ Wina'am na kɛ ka mɛligim lii fʋ pɔɔdin, ka kɛ ka fʋ pɔɔd mɔr kʋ'ʋlʋm pamm, ka fʋ zʋʋd nɛ daam maal bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Tɛɛns wʋsa nidib na tʋm tisif. Ba na igini fʋ tuonnɛ na'asif. Fʋ na an zugdaan fʋ ba'abiis wʋsa tuon ka fʋ mabiis na igini fʋ tuon. Onɛ pɔ bɛ'ɛd wʋsa tisif, bɛ'ɛd na dɔl o. Ka onɛ niŋi fʋ zug bareka, albareka na dɔl o.”

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Isaak n da niŋ Jakob zug albareka naae ka o duoe yi la, li da pʋ yuugɛ ka o bier Esau mɛ yi tɔn'ɔsʋgʋ paae na.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Ka mɛ maal dikanɛ malisi mɔri kena tis o saam la. Ka yɛl o ye, “M ba', duom di diib la, ka niŋim zug bareka!”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ka o saam Isaak bu'os o ye, “Fʋ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “M anɛ Esau fʋ bikpɛɛm la.”

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Ka Isaak kirid gba-gba-gba ka yɛl ye, “Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ la tɔn'ɔsi kena maal diib na tisim la? M di'e di ka niŋ o zug bareka ka fʋ mɛ nan kpɛn kpɛn'ɛd na la. O mɛ sid na nyɛ albareka.”

english_verse: Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
translation_verse: Amaa o lɛbis ye, “Fʋ pitʋ la kennɛ na pan'asim ka di'e fʋ albareka la.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Ka Esau yɛl ye, “Ya'a an sida, bi'esʋg kae ka ba pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Jakob ka li gbin an ‘Zam sɔb la!’ Nɔɔra ayi' nwa' ka o zam mam. O da faanm kpɛuŋ faar ka nannanna ka o lɛn faaɛn m albareka!” Ka o bu'os o saam la ye, “Fʋ pʋ kɛ albareka baa bi'ela digil mam mɛnɛ?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Isaak lɛbis o ye, “M kɛnɛ ka o aan fʋ zugdaan ka kɛ ka o ba'abiis wʋsa aan o yammis, ka o na mɔr zʋʋd nɛ daam wʋsa. M biiga, bɔ ka m ye m lɛm maali tisi fɔ?”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Ka Esau lɛn yɛl o ye, “M ba', fʋn mɔri albareka yinne ma'aanɛ? Aba, kʋdim niŋim man zug bareka mɛn; m ba'!” Ka o kaas bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Ka o saam Isaak yɛl o ye, “Fʋ bɛllim zin'ig na lal nɛ pɔɔd banɛ mɔr kʋ'ʋlʋm, ka mɛligim pʋn kʋ luu anina.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Fʋ na mɔr sʋ'ʋgʋ zabid ka na an onɛ tʋmmi tisid Jakob. Amaa saŋa kenna ka fʋ kʋ lɛn siaki aan o yammʋgɔ ka na sʋ'oe fʋ mɛŋ.”

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ka Esau kisig Jakob, ka li anɛ o saamme daa niŋ albareka si'a niŋ o la zug. O da tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin sa ye, “M saam ya'a kpi ka ti maal o kʋʋri naae m na kʋʋ m pitʋ Jakob!”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Rebɛka da wʋm linɛ ka Esau yɛl la, ka o buol o bipit Jakob la na yɛl o ye, “Fʋ bier gban'anɛ ye o kʋʋf.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ m biiga, maalim man ye m yɛlif si'em nwa', duom zɔɔ keŋi m taʋn Laban san'an Haran teŋin.

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: Bɛɛ anina ti paae saŋkanɛ ka fʋ bier la sʋnf na ma'ae.

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: Fʋ bier ya'a ti tam fʋn tʋm si'em tis o la ka o sʋnf ma'ae, m na tʋm yɛlif ka fʋ kul na. Ya wʋsa ya'a kpi daar yinne, li nyɔɔd an bɔ?”

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Ka Rebɛka yɛl Isaak ye, “M ya'am yinɛ Hitti dim biis banɛ ka Esau di la. Jakob mɛ ya'a lɛn di pu'ab buud kaŋa ni, m ya'a kpi sɔn'oe!”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Ka Isaak buol Jakob ka kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis o ka sa'al o ye, “Da di pu'a yi Keenan buudi la nii.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Mɛ Laban anɛ fʋ ansiba? Kem Padanaram fʋ ma saam Betuel san'an n di pu'a yi Laban biisin la.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Wina'am Onɛ Galis la na niŋi fʋ zug bareka ka kɛ ka fʋ du'am nɔbig ka fʋ yaas na ti an buudi bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: O na niŋ fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas zug albareka wʋʋ on da niŋi fʋ yaab Abraham zug si'em la. Ala ka fʋ na sʋ'oe teŋ kanɛ ka fʋ an saanne li pʋʋgin la, teŋ kanɛ ka Wina'am zaŋi tis Abraham la.”

english_verse: Isaac then sent Jacob to stay with Rebekah's brother Laban, the son of Bethuel the Aramean. Esau Marries the Daughter of Ishmael
translation_verse: Ka Isaak kɛ ka Jakob keŋ Padanaram paae Laban onɛ saamme an Betuel ka o an Aram teŋ nid, ka o taʋn an Rebɛka onɛ an Jakob nɛ Esau ma la san'an.

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Esau da wʋm ye Isaak niŋ Jakob zug albareka ka kɛ ka o keŋ Padanaram teŋin ye o di pu'a, ka mɛ wʋm ye o yɛl o ye, “Mit ka fʋ di pu'a Keenan dimin la,”

english_verse: and that he had obeyed his father and mother.
translation_verse: ka Jakob sid siak o saam nɛ o ma nɔɔr ka keŋ Padanaram teŋin la,

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Esau yʋ'ʋn da baŋ ye o saam sʋnf pʋ malis nɛ on di Keenan dim pu'ab la.

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: Alazug, o da duoe keŋ Isimael onɛ an Abraham biig la san'an dii o bipuŋ Mahalaf onɛ taʋn da an Nebaiof la paas pu'a banɛ ka o pʋn dɛŋi di sa la. Jakob n zaansim Betel teŋin la yɛla

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Jakob n da yi Beerseba wa'ae Haran teŋin la,

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: o da paae zin'isi'a ka winnig li, ka o zin'inɛ anina. O da nɔk kugir linɛ bɛɛ anina la yinne digil ka kʋk o zug.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: O da zaansim nyɛ dadʋg ka li ti' dunia ni keŋ ba'al arezana ni, ka Wina'am maliaknam dɔlisidi lii dʋt ka sigid.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: Anina ka Zugsɔb la zi'enɛ o baba ka yɛl ye, “Manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ yaab Abraham Wina'am, nɛ Isaak Wina'am la. M na zaŋ teŋ kanɛ ka fʋ dig la tis fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: Fʋ yaas na zu'oe nwɛnɛ titanbin'isʋg nɛ, ka fʋ sʋ'ʋlim na yaligi keŋ ya-tuona, nɛ ya-nya'aŋ, la'an nɛ datiuŋ nɛ dagɔbʋg wʋsa. Ka fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas la zug ka dunia nidib wʋsa na nyɛ bareka.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: M na bɛ nɛf ka gurif fʋn keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa, ka na mɔri fʋ lɛb teŋ kaŋa ni na. M kʋ basi fɔɔ, asɛɛ m ti maal man pɔɔ zi'el si'em la wʋsa.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Jakob da nie gbɛɛmin ka ye, “Sida, Zugsɔb la sid bɛ kpɛla ka mam pʋ baŋɛ.”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Dabiem da mɔr o nɛ, ka o yɛl ye, “Zin'ikaŋa anɛ dabiem zin'ig! Li anɛ Wina'am Yir, ka lɛn an arezana za'anɔɔr.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da bɔɔd nier la, ka Jakob nɔk kugkanɛ ka o sa kʋk la ba'a zi'el sappi nwɛnɛ zan'antɔlig nɛ, ka nɔk kpaam kpa'ae niŋi li zug.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Before that it had been named Luz.
translation_verse: O da pʋd zin'ig la yʋ'ʋr Betel. Amaa teŋ la yʋ'ʋr da dɛŋi buon ye Luz.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Ani ka Jakob zi'el nɔkaŋa ye, “Wina'am ya'a bɛ nɛ m ka gurimi m ken nwa' pʋʋgin, ka tisim diib nɛ fuud,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: ka lɛm mɔrim laafi lɛbi m saam yir, Zugsɔb la sid na aan m Wina'am.

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: Kugkanɛ ka m ba' zi'el nwɛnɛ zan'antɔlig nwa' na lieb Wina'am pʋ'ʋsʋg zin'ig, ka on tisim si'el wʋsa, m na pʋdig piiga ka tis o yinne.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Ka Jakob keŋ paae teŋ kanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Anina ka o nyɛ ka bulig bɛ mɔɔgin ka pɛ'ɛs dig gum-gum kpi'e bulig la zin'is atan'. Bulkan la ni ka ba wiid ku'om tisid pɛ'ɛs la. Ka kugtita'ar ligil bulig la nɔɔr.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Ban da ɛɛnti niŋ si'em nwa', kɔnbid la wʋsa ya'a la'as na naae, kɔnbkemnib la biligidnɛ kugir la yis bulig la nɔɔrin ka kɔnbid la nu. Ka ba ya'a nuu naae, kɔnbkemnib la na lɛm bilig kugir la lɛbisi ligil bulig la nɔɔr.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob bu'os kɔnbkemnib la ye; “M pitiba, yanam yi yaanɛ na?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Tinam yinɛ Haran teŋin na.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛm bu'osi ba ye, “Ya mi' Laban onɛ an Nahor yaaŋ laa?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, ti mi' o.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob bu'osi ba ye, “O mɔr laafi?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Laafi bɛɛ o. Gɔsima, o bipuŋ Rakɛl nwana dɔl o kɔnbidi kenna.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Ka o ye, “Gɔsimiya, nintaŋ la nam bɛ, saŋa pʋ paae ye ya la'asi kad kɔnbid la kulɛ; kɛl ka ba nu ku'om ka ya mɔri ba lɛb yaama zin'igin.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ayei, ti kʋ nyaŋɛ, ya'a ka' ye kɔnbkemnib la wʋsa kena ka ti la'asi bilig kugir la yis bulig la nɔɔrin ka nyaan kɛ ka kɔnbid la nu ku'om.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Ban nam sɔnsid la ka Rakɛl mɛ paad na nɛ o saam kɔnbid, bɔzugɔ onɛ da kem kɔnbid la.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob n nyɛ Rakɛl onɛ aan o ansib Laban pu'ayua la nɛ Laban kɔnbid la, o keŋ nɛ bilig kugir la yis bulig la nɔɔrin ka kɛ ka o ansib kɔnbid la nu.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob pʋ'ʋs Rakɛl sʋ'ʋŋa ka o sʋnf ma'ae hali ka o pin'ili kaasid sumalisim zug.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Ka yɛl Rakɛl ye o anɛ o saam nid, ka an Rebɛka biig. Ka pu'asadir la zɔɔ kuli yɛl o saam la.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Laban n wʋm o ansiŋ Jakob yɛla la o duoe yina zɔɔ tʋ'ʋs o. Ka bibig o ka pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa ka mɔr o kul yin. Anina ka Jakob yɛl Laban o ken labaar wʋsa,

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: ka Laban yɛl ye, “Asida fʋ anɛ mam ziim!” Jakob da bɛɛ o san'an paae nwadig yinne. Jakob nɛ o pu'ab yɛla

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Ka Laban yʋ'ʋn yɛl o ye, “Li pʋ nar ye fʋ tʋmmi tisidim zaalim fʋn aan m nid la zugɔ; yɛlim fʋn na di'e si'el.”

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Jakob ya'am da kpɛn' Rakɛl ka o ye, “M na tʋm yʋma ayɔpɔi tisif ka di'e fʋ biig Rakɛl onɛ an Lea pitʋ la.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Ka Laban lɛbis ye, “Li an sʋ'ʋŋa ye m zaŋ o tis fʋ gaad mam na tis dau sɔ'. Zin'inim kpɛla tʋm tisim.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob tʋm yʋma ayɔpɔi Rakɛl yɛla, ka li nwɛnɛ dabisa bi'ela nɛ, on nɔŋ o la zug.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl Laban ye, “M saŋa la naae ya, nɔkim m pu'a tisim!”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Ka Laban buol nimbanɛ bɛ zin'ikan la wʋsa ka maal di'ema tisi ba.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Amaa yʋ'ʋŋi da sɔb la, o da nɔknɛ o bipuŋ kpɛɛm la kɛ ka o kpɛn' Jakob dɔɔgin.

english_verse: Laban also gave Zilpah to Leah as her servant woman.
translation_verse: Ka Laban nɔk o sankpan'asnam yinne onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Zilipa tis o bipuŋ la ye o lieb o tʋmtʋm pu'ak.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Ka bɛogʋ da nie la Jakob da baŋ ye li anɛ Lea ka tans Laban ye, “Bɔɔ la ka fʋ maalim wala? M tʋm tisif nɛ Rakɛl zug, bɛɛ ka' ala? Ka bɔ ka fʋ pan'asi ma?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Ka Laban lɛbis ye, “Li ka' tinam malʋŋ ye fʋ nɔk biigi tis sid ka o bier zin'iya.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Kʋdim maalim bipuŋ kaŋa pu'adiir malʋŋ la naae, ka m na tisi fʋ o pitʋ la, ka fʋ lɛn tʋm yʋma ayɔpɔi ya'asi yɔ.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob mɛ digin nɛ Rakɛl ka nɔŋ Rakɛl n gaad Lea, ka lɛn tʋm yʋma ayɔpɔi tis Laban. Jakob biis yɛla

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da nyɛ ka ba pʋ nɔŋ Lea la ka o yɔ'ɔg o du'am amaa Rakɛl on da anɛ kʋndu'ar.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Ka Lea nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ ka pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Reuben, bɔzugɔ o da yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la nyɛɛm namisʋg; nannanna m sid na nɔŋim.”

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn nɔk pʋʋg ya'as du'a biribiŋ ka yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb baŋ ye ba pʋ nɔŋi ma ka tisim oŋa ya'as.” Ka pʋd on ye Simeon.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ ka ye, “Nannanna m sid na la'as nɛ mam, bɔzugɔ m du'a biribis atan' tis o.” Ka pʋd on yʋ'ʋr ye Levi.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ka lɛn nɔk pʋʋg ya'asi du'a biribiŋ ka ye, “Saŋkaŋa m pian' Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr!” Ka pʋd on yʋ'ʋr ye Juda. Ka pʋ lɛn du'a ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Rakɛl n da nyɛ ka on nɛ Jakob pʋ du'ad biis la o da nɛnni o bier la nɛ, ka yɛl Jakob ye, “Tisim biis ka ya'a ka' ala, m na kpi!”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob sʋʋnr pɛlig ka o bu'os o ye, “Manɛ an Wina'am kɛ ka fʋ pʋ du'a biisɛ?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M tʋmtʋm pu'ak Biliha nwa', dim o ka o du'a biisi tisim, ka anina ka m yʋ'ʋr mɛ saa na pʋdig.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: ka o tʋk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Ka Rakɛl ye, “Wina'am tisim bʋʋd; o wʋmi m fabʋlʋg ka tisim biribiŋ!” Ka dinzug ka o pʋd o ye Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Rakɛl tʋmtʋm pu'ak Biliha da lɛn nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋi tis Jakob ya'as,

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: ka Rakɛl ye, “M mɔ nɛ m bier la ka paam nyaŋir!” Ka o pʋd on ye Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Lea nyɛ ka o gu'oe du'am la ka o mɛ nɔk o tʋmtʋm pu'ak Zilipa tis Jakob ye o lieb o pu'a.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Ka Lea tʋmtʋm pu'ak Zilipa du'a biribiŋi tis Jakob.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Ka Lea yɛl ye, “Li anɛ zusʋŋ!” Ka pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Gad.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: ka Lea ye, “M sʋʋnr ma'aya. M pu'a taab na buon mam ye sumalisim sɔb!” Ka pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Aser.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Ka li ti paae ki bunib saŋa ka Reuben keŋ pɔɔgin ka nyɛ du'am tiim nya'a mɔr na tis o ma Lea, ka Rakɛl yɛl o ye, “M bierɛ, nɔkimi fʋ biig du'am tiim nya'a la tisim.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Ka Lea lɛbis o ye, “Fʋn faanm sidi m san'an la pʋ siakɛ, ka fʋ lɛn ye fʋ faanm du'am tiim pɛ'ɛsɛɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Tɔ'! Fʋn ya'a na siaki tisim ti-nya'a la, mam mɛ na siak ka Jakob kpɛn' fʋ san'an yʋ'ʋŋ kaŋa nwa'.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Zaam da ma'aya ka Jakob yi pɔɔgine kunna ka Lea yii tʋ'ʋs o ka yɛl o ye, “Asɛɛ fʋ digin nɛ m yʋ'ʋŋa bɔzugɔ m nɔki m biig du'am ti-nya'a la tiaki m nintaa dabisir la ye fʋ kpɛn' man san'an na.” Ka o da digin nɛ o yʋ'ʋŋ kan,

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: ka Wina'am wʋm Lea sɔsʋg ka o nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ onɛ pɛ'ɛsi anu n tis Jakob.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Ka Lea yɛl ye, “M nɔki m tʋmtʋm pu'ak la tisim sid ka Wina'am yɔɔm linzug!” Ka o pʋd o ye Isaka.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Ka Lea yɛl ye, “Wina'am tisim bʋnsʋŋ hali. Nannanna m sid na tisim girima bɔzugɔ m du'a biribis ayuobʋ tis o!” Ka pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Zebulun.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka o du'a bipuŋ ka pʋd on ye Daina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: ka o nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ ka ye, “Wina'am yisim nyannin!”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Ka o pʋd o ye Josef. Ka yɛl ye, “Wina'am paasim biribiŋ ya'as!” Jakob n kɛ ka o kɔnbid zu'oe si'em

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka Jakob yɛl Laban ye, “Basim ka m lɛbi kul m mɛŋ teŋin.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Nɔkimi m pu'ab nɛ m bibanɛ yɛla ka m tʋm tisif la tisim ka m kul. Fʋ mɛŋ mi' mam tʋm tʋʋm si'a tisif.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛbis o ye, “Fʋ mɛŋ mi' mam tʋm tisif ka gɔsi fʋ bʋnkɔnbid sʋ'ʋŋa si'em.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Fʋn da mɔr bi'ela ka m kena ka ba yʋ'ʋn nɔbig bɛdegʋ, ka Zugsɔb niŋi fʋ zug bareka zin'is wʋsa, man paae kpɛla hali nɛ zina. Amaa bʋndaar ka m na tʋm si'eli tisim mɛŋ yidima?”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye m tisi fɔ?” Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “Da tisim si'ela, amaa fʋ ya'a na maal bʋnkaŋa ma'aa tisim, m na keŋ gɔsi fʋ kɔnbid la ka guri ba ya'as.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka m keŋi fʋ kɔnbidin la zina gaans pɛpʋpɔnra la ba kɔn', nɛ pɛbil sabilis, nɛ bʋpʋpɔnra la ba kɔn', ka ba na aan m yɔɔd.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog sa fʋ ya'a ti kena ye fʋ vɛɛnsi gɔs m bʋnkɔnbban ka fʋ tisim la, m na an sida sɔb; ka bʋnkɔnbʋg kanɛ ka' pʋpɔnrʋg bɛɛ sabilig la fʋ na baŋ ye m zu nɛ.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Ka Laban yɛl ye, “Tɔ', m siakya!”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Daakan la ka o yis bʋraad nɛ bʋnya'as banɛ an pʋpɔnra la ka lɛn gɛndig pielim, nɛ pɛrasabilis la, nɔki ba tis o biis ye ba gur.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: O da kɛnɛ ka o biis la mɔri ba keŋ lalli wʋʋ daba atan' ken, ka basi ba anina, ka Jakob on nan kpɛn gɔsid Laban kɔnbbanɛ kpɛlim la.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Amaa Jakob da nwaae tiis sieba wila pigisi li pa'ad la sieba ka bas sieba ka li an pʋpɔnra-pʋpɔnra

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: ka nɔki li sɛɛl zin'ibanɛ ka kɔnbbanɛ bɔɔd dʋʋb la kenna ye ba nu ku'om ka li sɛɛ ba tuon.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ wʋsa ka kɔnbnya'aŋ sʋma ti siak dʋʋb, Jakob da ɛɛn nɔk nɛ dapʋpɔnra la sɛ, ka ba gɔsidi li ka dʋt.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Amaa li ya'a anɛ kɔnbnya'as banɛ tadig la siak dʋʋb o pʋ sɛɛd daad la. Ka lin kɛ ka bʋnkɔnbid banɛ tadig la an Laban din ka banɛ kpi'em la lieb on din.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Di da niŋnɛ ala ka Jakob lieb arezak daan hali. O da mɔr kɔnbid bɛdegʋ nɛ yammis nɛ yʋgʋma nɛ bʋmis.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Di da kena ka Jakob wʋm ye Laban biribis la yɛt ye, “Jakob zu nɛ ti saam bʋn wʋsa, o kpan'am la wʋsa da anɛ ti saam din.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob nyɛ ka Laban bɛllim zaŋi ken o san'an pʋ lɛn nwɛnɛ lin da an si'em la.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Jakob ye, “Lɛmmi fʋ saam teŋin nɛ fʋ nidibin, ka m na bɛ nɛf.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Ka Jakob tʋm buol Rakɛl nɛ Lea ye ba kem o san'an mɔɔgin zin'ikanɛ ka o bʋnkɔnbid la bɛ la.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “M nyɛ ka ya saam bɛllim zaŋi ken mam san'an pʋ lɛn nwɛnɛ lin da an si'em, amaa m saam Wina'am la bɛ nɛ mam.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Ya mi' man tʋm nɛ m paŋ si'em tisi ya saam la.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Amaa ya saam zam mam hali ka tiaki m yɔɔd nɔɔr piiga. Amaa Wina'am pʋ kɛ ka o san'am mam.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: O ya'a ye, ‘Pɛpʋpɔnra la na anɛ fʋ bʋn,’ ba wʋsa da du'adi pɛpʋpɔnra, ka o mɛ ya'a da ye, ‘Pɛlasalasa la na anɛ fʋ bʋn,’ ba wʋsa du'adi lasa-lasa.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Ala ka Wina'am nɔki ya saam bʋnkɔnbid la tis mam.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: Kɔnbid la dʋʋb saŋa ka m da zaansim nyɛ ka bʋraad banɛ dʋt bʋnya'as la da anɛ bʋmpʋpɔnra nɛ lasa-lasa.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am maliak buolim zaansʋŋin la ye, ‘Jakob!’ Ka m siak ye, ‘Naa, manɛ nwa'!’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Ka o ye, ‘Gɔsima, bʋraad banɛ dʋt la wʋsa anɛ pʋpɔnra, nɛ lasa-lasa. Man nyɛ Laban n maannif si'em la zug ka m niŋ ala.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Manɛ an Betel teŋin Wina'am la, zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ da nɔk kugiri ba'a zi'el ka bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ ka pɔ nɔɔri tisim la. Nannanna basim teŋ kaŋa ka lɛbi fʋ nidib teŋin.’”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Ayei! O pʋ gɔs ka tinam anɛ saammaa? O pʋ kuosi ti nɛ ka di'e dinɛ ka ba yɔɔ ti yɛla la dii naae?

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Sida arezak kanɛ ka Wina'am nɔki yii ti saam san'an la anɛ tinam nɛ ti biis din. Dinzugɔ tʋm dinɛ wʋsa ka Wina'am yɛlif.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Ka Jakob duoe nɔk o pu'ab la nɛ o biis la ban'al yʋgʋma.

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: Ka kad bʋnkɔnbid la galis tuon, nɛ la'abanɛ ka o paam Padanaram teŋin la lɛbid Keenan, o saam Isaak san'an.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Laban n, da gaad ye o kies o pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid la, ka Rakɛl zuu o saam Laban yir wina.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Jakob da nɔk on mɔr si'el wʋsa n zɔɔ lɔ'ɔŋ Efiritis kɔldaug la kennɛ kpa'ad Gilead linɛ an zuoya teŋ la.

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Daba atan' daar ka ba nyaan yɛl Laban ye Jakob zɔya.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Ka o duoe la'as o ba'abiis ka ba kad Jakob bugiri keŋ daba ayɔpɔi ka paae o Gilead linɛ an zuoya teŋin la.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Ka Laban onɛ an Aram nid la yʋ'ʋn da nyɛ zaansʋŋʋn yʋ'ʋŋ ka Wina'am yɛl o ye, “Gu'usimi fʋ mɛŋ! Mid ka fʋ pian' linɛ an sʋm bɛɛ bɛ'ɛdi tis Jakob!”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Ka Laban yʋ'ʋn keŋ paae Jakob san'an. Ka Jakob ti' o sʋga Gilead zuoya teŋin, ka Laban nɛ o nidib la mɛ paae na ti' ba sʋga anina mɛn.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Ka Laban yɛl Jakob ye, “Bɔɔ la ka fʋ tʋm? Fʋ pan'asimi mɔri m pu'ayuos la zɔ wʋʋ tanpin ka ba gban'e ba nɛ.

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ pan'asim ka su'a zɔ? Bɔɔ maal ka fʋ pʋ yɛlim ka m kɛ ka fʋ keŋ nɛ sumalisim, nɛ yʋʋma, ka siyada nwɛ'ɛd ka wiis piebida?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Fʋ pʋ kɛ ka m kaanbi tisim yaas nɛ m pu'ayuos la ka kɛɛsi ba sʋ'ʋŋa. Fʋ tʋmnɛ yalim tʋʋma!

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: M mɔr suori na tun'e san'amif, amaa yʋ'ʋŋin ka fʋ saam Wina'am la sa yɛlim ye, ‘Gu'usim ka da pian' bɛ'ɛd bɛɛ sʋm tis Jakob la.’

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Ya'a an sida, m mi' ye fʋ bɔɔd nɛ fʋ sʋʋnr wʋsa ye fʋ kuli fʋ saam yir. Ka bɔzug kimm ka fʋ zuu m wina?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛbis Laban ye, “Dabiem zug ka m zɔ, bɔzugɔ m tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ na faaɛn fʋ pu'ayuos la nɛ paŋ.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ ya'a nyɛ ka sɔ' mɔri fʋ wina la, o sɔb na kpi! Vɛɛnsimi ti, ti du'adib la wʋsa nifin ka gɔs ye fʋ si'el bɛɛ m san'anɛɛ. Fʋ ya'a nyɛ si'el fʋn nɔkim.” Jakob da nam pʋ baŋ ye Rakɛl zu wina la.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Ka Laban kpɛn' Jakob dɔɔgin la, nɛ Lea dɔɔgin, nɛ ba tʋmtʋm pu'ab dɔɔdin la ka pʋ nyɛɛ. Ka o gaadi kpɛn' Rakɛl dɔɔgin la mɛn.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Li saŋa ka Rakɛl pʋn nɔk wina la niŋ o yʋgʋm ga'arin ka zin' li zug, ka Laban iee zin'ig wʋsa dɔɔg la pʋʋgin ka pʋ nyɛ si'ela.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Ka Rakɛl yɛl o saam ye, “M ba', da kɛ ka fʋ sʋʋnr duoe man zin' fʋ tuon la zugɔ, ka m kʋ nyaŋi duoe bɔzugɔ m paami m pier.” Ka Laban iee-iee dɔɔgin la wʋsa ka pʋ nyɛ wina la.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Ka Jakob sʋʋnr pɛlig ka o tans Laban ka bu'os o ye, “Taal bɔ kimm ka m tʋm? Bɛɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɔ ka m tʋm ka fʋ kad mam paae kpɛla na?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Nannanna fʋn gɔsi m la'adin la wʋsa la, fʋ lauk bɔ ka fʋ nyɛ? Fʋ ya'a nyɛ lauk si'a, fʋn mɔri li na digili fʋ nidib nɛ mam nidib la tuon ka ba tisi ti babayi' la onɛ mɔr bʋʋd!

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: M nam mɔr ni'imi kɛɛn fʋ san'an na ye kɔnbid la yinne ka bʋnkɔnbbɛ'og gban'e. Hali baa li ya'a niŋ ala, m gban'adnɛ m mɛŋ pɛ'ogʋ yɔɔ li sam. Ka ba ya'a zu kɔnbʋg yʋ'ʋŋ bɛɛ nintaŋ fʋ yɛt ye m yɔɔmi li sam.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: M bɛllim da an si'em la, ka nintaŋ nwɛ'ɛdim ka waad kʋʋdim ka gbɛɛm yii m nini ni.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: M yaanam Wina'am onɛ an Abraham Wina'am nɛ Isaak Wina'am ya'a ka'anɛ m san'anɛ, bi'esʋg kae ye fʋ naan kadin mam ka m keŋ nɛ nu'uzaalisɛ. Amaa Zugsɔb la nyɛ m namisʋg la zug, nɛ man tʋm nimmua siem la, din ka o sa zɛrigif yʋ'ʋŋin man zug la.”

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Laban lɛbis o ye, “Pu'ab la anɛ mam pu'ayuos, ba biis la mɛ anɛ man din, ka bʋnkɔnbid la anɛ man din mɛn. Fʋn nyɛt si'el la wʋsa anɛ mam bʋn. La'an nɛ wala, m na lɛn nyaŋi niŋ bɔ nɛ m pu'ayuos nwa' nɛ ba biis banɛ ka ba du'a la?

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Kɛl ka mam nɛ fʋ maal nɔnaar, ka li an kasɛt man nɛ fʋ teŋsʋk.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Ka Jakob nɔk kugiri ba'a zi'el sappi ye li an kasɛt kugir,

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: ka yɛl o nidib la ye, “La'asimi kuga na!” Ka ba la'as kuga dʋ'ʋs dʋʋr. Ka ba wʋsa la'as taaba kuga la baba di diib.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban da pʋd o li yʋ'ʋr ye Jegar Sahaduta, ka Jakob mɛ buoli li o mɛŋ pian'adin ye Galeed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Laban da yɛl ye, “Dʋʋr kaŋa anɛ kasɛt mam nɛ fʋn sʋʋgin.” Linzug ka ba da buon zin'ig la ye Galeed.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Li yʋ'ʋr yinne mɛ an Misipa, bɔzugɔ o yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la na gɔs man nɛ fʋ ti wɛligir nwa' pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Laban da lɛn yɛl ye, “Fʋ ya'a pʋ maali m biis la sʋ'ʋŋa, bɛɛ fʋ tɔɔmnɛ di pu'a sieba, la'an nɛ man ka' anina la, baŋim ye Wina'am anɛ kasɛt man nɛ fʋ sʋʋgin.”

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Kuga dʋʋr la nɛ tiɛnr kugir nwa' anɛ kasɛti pa'an ye mam kʋ lɔ'ɔŋi kɛɛn fʋ san'an na daami fɔ, ka fʋ mɛ kʋ lɔ'ɔŋi li kɛn mam san'an na daami ma.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Onɛ an Abraham Wina'am nɛ Nahor Wina'am, nɛ ba yaanam Wina'am la, na pa'al onɛ mɔr bʋʋd man nɛ fʋn sʋʋgin.” Ka Jakob mɛ pɔɔ o saam Isaak yʋ'ʋr zug ka siak nɔzi'elʋg la.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: O da maal maan zuoya teŋin la ka buol o nidib ka ba di. Ba da dii naae ka gbɛɛn anina.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Ka di yim bɛogʋn asuba ka Laban kuak o yaas nɛ o pu'ayuos la pʋ'ʋsi ba sʋ'ʋŋa ka kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tisi ba ka lɛbi kul.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yii ani ken ka Wina'am maliaknam sia'al o.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob n nyɛ ba la o yɛl ye, “Kpɛla anɛ Wina'am nidib la la'asʋg zin'ig!” Ka pʋd zin'ikan la ye Mahanam.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Jakob da pʋn dɛŋi tʋm nidib Esau san'an Seir teŋin dinɛ bɛ Edom sʋ'ʋlim la.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: O da yɛli ba ye, “M bɔɔd ye ya keŋi paae m bier Esau san'an pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa tisim, ka yɛl o ye, ‘Fʋ tʋmtʋm Jakob da bɛnɛ Laban san'an yuug hali nɛ zina.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: M mɔr niigi nɛ bʋmis, nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ bʋʋs, nɛ yamdaad nɛ yampu'ab. M tʋmnɛ fʋ san'an na ye fʋ zɔɔ m nimbaanlig.’”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Banɛ ka Jakob tʋmi ba la da lɛb na n yɛl ye, “Ti keŋi paae fʋ bier Esau san'an, ka o mɛ bɛ suori kenna ye o nyɛɛf; o mɔri dap kɔbisnaasi kenna.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Dabiem nɛ ya'am nwa'ar da kɛ ka Jakob pʋdig nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la zin'is ayi', nɛ kɔnbid nɛ niigi nɛ yʋgʋma la wʋsa.

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: O da tɛn'ɛs ye, “Esau ya'a kena zabid nɛ zin'ig yinne, banɛ nan kpɛlim la na zɔɔ pɔns.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob sɔs Wina'am ye, “Wina'am kanɛ aan m yaab Abraham Wina'am ka aan m saam Isaak Wina'am, Zugsɔba, fʋ yɛl ye m lɛmmi m teŋin nɛ m nidibin ka fʋ na kɛ ka m yɛla ken tuon.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: M sɔsidif ye fʋ faaɛn mam yisi m bier Esau nu'usin, bɔzugɔ dabiem mɔrim nɛ ye o na kena zab nɛ m ka pu'alim man nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis la wʋsa.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ yɛl ye fʋ na tʋm tʋʋm sʋma tisim, ka kɛ ka m yaas an wʋʋ atɛuk titanbin'isʋg nɛ, linɛ ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kaalɛ.”

english_verse: After Jacob had spent the night there, he chose some animals as gifts for Esau:
translation_verse: Jakob da gbɛɛn anina yʋ'ʋŋ kan la nie bɛog, ka yis on mɔr si'el la sieba ye o tʋm tis o bier Esau.

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye o tʋmtʋm Jakob bɛ nya'aŋi kenna. O da tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin sa ye, “M ya'a kɛ ka ba zaŋ piini nwa' gaad tuon di na bʋgʋli m bier la sʋʋnr ka m ya'a paae, o kʋ niŋim si'ela.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Alazug ka Jakob buol zin'ikan ye Peniel. Ka yɛl ye, “Bɔzugɔ m nyɛ Wina'am nindaa nɛ m nif ka nan kpɛn vʋe!”

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Ka yɛl onɛ tia'al la, nɛ atan' sɔb, nɛ banɛ dɔl la wʋsa, ye ba ya'a tʋ'ʋs Esau ban yɛl o ala mɛn,

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Jakob piini la da gaad tuon ka o mɛŋ gbɛɛn anina daakan la. Jakob n mɔ nɛ Wina'am si'em

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Dau la ti baŋ ka o kʋ nyaŋ o la, o da si'isnɛ Jakob kpiilʋg ka kɛ ka li kpirig.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Ka dau la yɛl o ye, “Kɛl ka m keŋ, ka bɛog nie ya.” Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “M kʋ basif ka fʋ keŋɛ asɛɛ ka fʋ niŋi m zug bareka.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka dau la bu'os o ye, “Fʋ yʋ'ʋrɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Jakob.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Ka dau la ye, “Fʋ yʋ'ʋr kʋ lɛm buon ye Jakob ya'asɛ, amaa Israel, bɔzugɔ fʋ mɔ nɛ fʋ Wina'am nɛ dap ka nyaŋ.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl ye, “M sɔsidif nɛ, yɛlimi fʋ yʋ'ʋr!” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ka bɔ ka fʋ bu'osidi m yʋ'ʋrɛ?” Ka niŋ o zug bareka anina.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Ka winnigi da dʋt na la ka o gaad Peniel ka kpɛ'ɛsid; o kpiilʋg la zug.

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”

translation_verse: Jakob piini la da gaad tuon ka o mɛŋ gbɛɛn anina daakan la. Jakob n mɔ nɛ Wina'am si'em

translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl ye, “M sɔsidif nɛ, yɛlimi fʋ yʋ'ʋr!” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ka bɔ ka fʋ bu'osidi m yʋ'ʋrɛ?” Ka niŋ o zug bareka anina.

translation_verse: Ka winnigi da dʋt na la ka o gaad Peniel ka kpɛ'ɛsid; o kpiilʋg la zug.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yii ani ken ka Wina'am maliaknam sia'al o.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob n nyɛ ba la o yɛl ye, “Kpɛla anɛ Wina'am nidib la la'asʋg zin'ig!” Ka pʋd zin'ikan la ye Mahanam.

translation_verse: Jakob da pʋn dɛŋi tʋm nidib Esau san'an Seir teŋin dinɛ bɛ Edom sʋ'ʋlim la.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: O da yɛli ba ye, “M bɔɔd ye ya keŋi paae m bier Esau san'an pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa tisim, ka yɛl o ye, ‘Fʋ tʋmtʋm Jakob da bɛnɛ Laban san'an yuug hali nɛ zina.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: M mɔr niigi nɛ bʋmis, nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ bʋʋs, nɛ yamdaad nɛ yampu'ab. M tʋmnɛ fʋ san'an na ye fʋ zɔɔ m nimbaanlig.’”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Banɛ ka Jakob tʋmi ba la da lɛb na n yɛl ye, “Ti keŋi paae fʋ bier Esau san'an, ka o mɛ bɛ suori kenna ye o nyɛɛf; o mɔri dap kɔbisnaasi kenna.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Dabiem nɛ ya'am nwa'ar da kɛ ka Jakob pʋdig nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la zin'is ayi', nɛ kɔnbid nɛ niigi nɛ yʋgʋma la wʋsa.

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: O da tɛn'ɛs ye, “Esau ya'a kena zabid nɛ zin'ig yinne, banɛ nan kpɛlim la na zɔɔ pɔns.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob sɔs Wina'am ye, “Wina'am kanɛ aan m yaab Abraham Wina'am ka aan m saam Isaak Wina'am, Zugsɔba, fʋ yɛl ye m lɛmmi m teŋin nɛ m nidibin ka fʋ na kɛ ka m yɛla ken tuon.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: M sɔsidif ye fʋ faaɛn mam yisi m bier Esau nu'usin, bɔzugɔ dabiem mɔrim nɛ ye o na kena zab nɛ m ka pu'alim man nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis la wʋsa.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ yɛl ye fʋ na tʋm tʋʋm sʋma tisim, ka kɛ ka m yaas an wʋʋ atɛuk titanbin'isʋg nɛ, linɛ ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kaalɛ.”

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: Ka kɛ ka tʋmtʋm pu'ab la nɛ ba biis la gaad tuon ka Lea nɛ o biis dɔl ka Rakɛl nɛ o biig Josef kpɛlim nya'aŋ.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Ka o mɛŋ gaad tuonnɛ igin teŋin nɔɔra ayɔpɔi ka nyaan paae o bier la.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Ka Esau zɔ tɔ'ɔtɔ tʋ'ʋs o na ka kuak o ka nɔk o nu'usi vil o niŋgɔɔnr ka pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa; ka ba wʋsa kum.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Ka Esau gɔs ka nyɛ pu'ab nɛ biis la, ka bu'os o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnamɛ nwana dɔlli fɔ?” Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “Bibama ka Wina'am nɔki tisim, m bierɛ.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Ka tʋmtʋm pu'ab nɛ ba biis la yʋ'ʋn paae na igin teŋin.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Ka Lea nɛ o biis mɛ kena igin teŋin, ka li nya'aŋ ka Josef nɛ Rakɛl mɛ paae na igin teŋin.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Ka Esau bu'os ye, “Ka bʋnkɔnbid banɛ wʋsa ka m tʋ'ʋsi ba suorin la gbin an bɔ?” Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “M zugdaana, m mɔri ba na ye m tisif ka fʋ di suguru.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Ka Esau yɛl ye, “Mam pʋn mɔr linɛ siakim. Kɛl ka fʋn mɔr si'el la nan kpɛn aan fʋ din.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “Ayei, m bɛlimnɛ, fʋ sʋnf ya'a sid ma'ae nɛ mam, fʋn di'em m piini nwa'. Mam nyɛɛ fʋ nindaa la li nwɛnɛ m nyɛnɛ Wina'am nɛ, ka li anɛ fʋn di'em sʋ'ʋŋa la zug.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: M bɛlimnɛ, di'em piini linɛ ka m mɔr na la; Wina'am sʋŋim ka m paam linɛ siakim.” Ka Jakob muk hali, ka Esau ti gʋ'ʋŋi siak ka di'e la'ad la.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Ka Esau yɛl ye, “Ti kem! M na dɔllif.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Amaa Jakob lɛbis ye, “Ayei, m zugdaana! Fʋ mi' ye biis la nam pɔɔd, ka li mɛ sʋm ye m gɔsid pɛ'ɛs nɛ na'abanɛ nan mu'asidi ba biis la. Ti ya'a ye ti mugusi ba keŋ baa daar yinne, bʋnkɔnbid la na kpi wʋsa.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: M bierɛ, fʋn gaadim tuon ka mam mɛ kpɛlim nya'aŋi dɔl bʋnkɔnbid la bi'el-bi'el, nɛ biis la, hali nɛ tinamɛ na paae fʋ san'an Seir teŋin na.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Ka Esau lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Ya'a aan ala, fʋn kɛl ka m basim dap sieba ka ba sʋŋif ka gurif.” Ka Jakob ye, “M bierɛ, m pʋ'ʋs ya, amaa li sia'al ya.”

english_verse: So Esau left for Edom.
translation_verse: Ka Esau gban'e o suori lɛb Seir teŋin.

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Ka Jakob mɛ gaadi keŋ Sukot teŋin. Anina o da mɛ' yir nɛ gariki kpɛn'ɛs o bʋnkɔnbid la, dinzug ka ba buon zin'ig kan la ye Sukof la.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Jakob n yi Padanaram la nya'aŋ la o da paae Sekɛm tempʋʋgin dinɛ bɛ Keenan sʋ'ʋlimin la nɛ laafi. Ka yi kpikpɛŋ bi'ela n zin'in anina.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Jakob da da' paalʋ Hamor onɛ da an Sekɛm saam la san'an anzurifa kɔbiga. O da ti' sʋga anina zin'in.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Anina ka o mɛ' maan bimbim ka buoli li yʋ'ʋr ye El Elohe Israel.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Lea da du'a bipuŋ sɔ' tis Jakob ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Daina. Daar yinne ka Daina da yii keŋ ye o pʋ'ʋs teŋ la pu'a sieba.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Hamor da anɛ Hivi buudi ka di teŋ la na'am, ka o biribiŋ Sekɛm nyɛ Daina ka o ya'am kpɛn' o ka o san'am o.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Ka o ya'am wʋsa kpɛn' Daina, onɛ an Jakob bipuŋ la, ka o nɔŋ pu'asadir la hali ka pian' nɛ kʋkɔmalisiŋi tis o.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Ka Sekɛm yɛl o saam Hamor ye, “Li'am pu'a kaŋa tisim ka m dii o.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ ka Jakob wʋm ye Sekɛm bibig o biig Daina la, o biis da nan bɛ nɛ mɔɔgin kem niigi. Ka o sin baanlimm gur biis la ka ba kul na.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Jakob biis yi mɔɔgini paae na ka wʋm dinɛ maal la, ka li daami ba ka ba sʋʋnr pɛlig bɔzugɔ Sekɛm diis nɛ Israel nyan on san'am Jakob pu'ayua la, li pʋ sʋm ye nɛ' maali nɛ.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Hamor yɛli ba ye, “M biig Sekɛm sʋʋnr kpɛn' fʋ bipuŋ la nɛ hali. M sɔsidif ye fʋ tis o ka o lieb o pu'a.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Kɛl ka ti di taaba biis. Tisimi ti ya pu'asada la ka tinam mɛ tisi ya ti pu'asada.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Ya na tun'e zin' teŋin la nɛ ti, ka nyaŋi tɔlim bɛɛ da' paalʋ ka li na aan ya din.”

english_verse: Shechem added, “Do this favor for me, and I'll give whatever you want.
translation_verse: Ka Sekɛm mɛ da bɛɛ ani ka yɛl Daina saam nɛ o tanp ye, “Siakimi ka m na tisi ya linɛ wʋsa ka ya bɔɔd.

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Amaa Sekɛm daa san'ami ba taʋn Daina la zug, Jakob biis la da ma' lɛbis on nɛ o saam Hamor

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: ye, “Tinam kʋ nyaŋi tʋm tʋʋm kaŋa; ti kʋ nyaŋi nɔki ti taʋn tis dau kanɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋ; lin aan ti kisʋg la zug.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Yɛl yinne ma'aa na kɛ ka ti siak. Ka li anɛ ye asɛɛ ka ya siaki lieb wʋʋ tinam ka kpɛn'ɛsi ya dap la wʋsa baŋʋ.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a niŋ ala ti na nɔki ti tanpi tisi ya, ka mɛ nɔki ya tanp la, ka ti na bɛ ya san'an ka tinam nɛ yanam na an buudi yinne.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a pʋ siak ye ya kpɛn' baŋʋ, tinam na nɔki ti taʋn keŋ.”

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Ka ban yɛl si'em la an sʋ'ʋŋa tis Hamor nɛ o biig Sekɛm.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Dasaŋ la da pʋ gu'usɛ ka kpɛn' baŋʋ tɔ'ɔtɔ bɔzugɔ, o ya'am da kpɛn' Daina nɛ hali. O mɛ da anɛ onɛ ka o yidim wʋsa tisid o na'asi.

english_verse: The two men met with the other leaders of their city and told them:
translation_verse: Ka Hamor nɛ o biig Sekɛm keŋ tempʋʋg la za'anɔɔrin ka pian' tis o nidib la ye,

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Dap la anɛ ti zuanam. Kɛl ka ba bɛɛ ti teŋin la ka tɔlim, bɔzugɔ teŋ la paalʋ zu'oya ka ba tun'e bɛ. Ti na tun'e dii ba bipumis la ka bam mɛ dii ti bipumis.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Amaa linɛ na kɛ ka dap nwa' siaki bɛ nɛ ti anɛ ye asɛɛ ka ti dap la wʋsa kpɛn' baŋʋ wʋʋ ban nɛ.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Yanamɛ nyɛ nwa', ba bʋnkɔnbid nɛ ba la'ad wʋsa kʋ lieb tinam bʋnnɛɛ? Kɛl ka ti siak ka ba bɛ kpɛla.”

english_verse: Every grown man followed this advice and got circumcised. Dinah's Brothers Take Revenge
translation_verse: Ka dap banɛ wʋsa yi za'anɔɔrin la ka wʋm Hamor nɛ Sekɛm yɛl si'el la siak ka ba kpɛn'ɛs dap wʋsa baŋʋ.

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Ka daba atan' nya'aŋ ka ba wʋsa digi ka li zabidi ba, ka Jakob biribis ayi' Simeon nɛ Levi, banɛ an Daina mabiis la, nɔki ba sʋ'ʋsi keŋi niŋ dap la kʋʋb diin, kʋʋ ba wʋsa.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da kʋ Hamor nɛ Sekɛm wʋsa ka yisi ba taʋn Daina Sekɛm yin la mɔri kul.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob biis la kena nyɛ ka ba wʋsa kpi la, ka ba vaae teŋ la la'ad la wʋsa, ban san'ami ba taʋn la zug.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Ka biis la kadi ba bʋnkɔnbid banɛ an niigi, nɛ bʋmis nɛ pɛ'ɛs la ka faaɛn linɛ wʋsa bɛ tempʋʋgin nɛ pɔɔdin la.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: Ba da vaae ba areza'as nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis nɛ bʋn linɛ bɛɛ ba yaan wʋsa.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl Simeon nɛ Levi ye, “Ya bɔnɛ yɛli tisim. Keenan dim nɛ Perizi dim banɛ bɛ kpɛla la kisig mam. Ti mɛ pʋ zu'oe, ba ya'a la'as taaba ye ba zab nɛ ti, ba na kʋ mam nɛ m yidim la wʋsa.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Fʋn nyɛ la li an sʋm ye o maali ti taʋn la wʋʋ pu'agɔɔndirɛɛ?”

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Kɛlli ka ti duoe lɛb Betel ka mɛ' maan bimbimi tis Wina'am onɛ ka m bɛ yɛla ni ka o sʋŋim hali ka bɛ nɛ m zin'ikanɛ wʋsa ka m keŋ la.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Ka ba vaae bada nɛ wina la nɛ tʋblɛma la wʋsa tis Jakob ka o nɔki pin' titita'ar gbinnin Sekɛm tempʋʋgin.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Ka ba yii lɛbid ka Wina'am dabiem kpɛn' tempʋʋg la dim wʋsa, ka ba pʋ kadi baa.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Anina ka o mɛ' maan bimbim ka buol zin'ig la ye El Betel, bɔzugɔ anina ka Wina'am da nie o mɛŋi pa'al o, on da zɔti yiti o bier san'an la.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Debora onɛ an Rakɛl biyuol la da kpi, ka ba mum o titita'ar kanɛ bɛ Betel la gbinnin, ka ba pʋd zin'ig la ye Allon-Bakuf.

english_verse: After Jacob came back to the land of Canaan, God appeared to him again. This time he gave Jacob a new name and blessed him by saying: I am God All-Powerful, and from now on your name will be Israel instead of Jacob. You will have many children. Your descendants will become nations, and some of the men in your family will even be kings.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am lɛn yɛl o ye, “Manɛ an Wina'am Onɛ Galis la. Du'ami biis ka nɔbigi bɛdegʋ. Fʋ na wiak buudi bɛdegʋ hali ka ba lieb tembɛda. Na'anam na yii fʋ tuŋʋn na.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Teŋ kan ka m da tis Abraham nɛ Isaak la, m mɛ na nɔki li tis fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas banɛ dɔlli fʋ nya'aŋ la.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yʋ'ʋn nɔk kugiri ba'a zi'el sappi, zin'ikanɛ ka Wina'am pian' tis o la, ka bu'oe daam nɛ malʋŋ kpaam niŋi li zug,

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: ka buol zin'ikanɛ ka Wina'am pian' tis o la ye Betel. Rakɛl kum yɛla

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Ka ba keŋ bi'ela yi Betel ka nam pʋ paae Efirata teŋin naa ka Rakɛl sa'ae ka li wʋm o hali.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Ka saŋkanɛ ka li wʋm o hali la, ka pu'adu'as la yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem ka ɔŋa mɛ anɛ biribiŋ.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ka on bɔɔd kum la ka pʋd o biribiŋ la yʋ'ʋr ye Ben-Oni. Amaa ka o saam da pʋd o ye Benjamin.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ka Rakɛl kpi ka ba mum o suor linɛ ken Efirata teŋin kpikpɛŋ, ani ka ba buon Betilehem nannanna la.

english_verse: Jacob set up a tombstone over her grave, and it is still there.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob nɔk kugiri ba'a zi'el sappi o yaʋg zug, ka li nan kpɛm bɛ zina pa'an Rakɛl yaʋg la zin'ig.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Ka Israel lɛn keŋ bi'ela paae Migdaleda teŋin zin'in. Jakob biis yɛla (

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Israel n da bɛ teŋ kan la, ka Reuben digin nɛ o saam pu'abil Biliha ka Israel wʋmi li yɛla. Jakob da mɔr biribis pii nɛ ayi':

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob kuli o saam Isaak san'an Mamir linɛ kpi'e nɛ Kiriaf Ariba teŋin linɛ an Hebron, zin'ikanɛ ka Abraham nɛ Isaak da zin' la.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Esau da dii o pu'ab la ka ba an Keenan dim. O da di Ada onɛ saamme an Elon onɛ an Hitti nid la, nɛ Oholibama ka on mɛ an Ana pu'ayua ka an Zibeon yaaŋ onɛ an Hivi nid.

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: Ka o da di Basemaf ya'as, onɛ an Isimael pu'ayua ka an Nebaiof taʋn.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: ka Oholibama du'a Jeus nɛ Jalam nɛ Kora. Bama da an Esau biis banɛ ka o da du'a Keenan sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Esau da nɔk o pu'ab nɛ o biis nɛ o yidim wʋsa nɛ o niigi nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa, la'an nɛ la'abanɛ ka o paam Keenan teŋin la wʋsa, duoe keŋ teŋ kanɛ lal nɛ o pitʋ Jakob.

english_verse: He did this because the land was too crowded and could not support him and his brother with their flocks and herds.
translation_verse: Ba la'ad la da zu'oe nɛ galis ka ba kʋ nyaŋi la'am bɛɛ. Ban da bɛ teŋ si'a la da pɔɔd ka pʋ siaki babayi' la, ba bʋnkɔnbid la zu'oe la zug.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Ala ka Esau , da keŋ zin' Seir zuoya teŋin la.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Esau yaas banɛ da an na'anam la nwa': Elifaz da an Esau bikpɛŋ ka o biis banɛ da di na'am la anɛ: Teman nɛ Omar nɛ Zefo nɛ Kenas

english_verse: Korah, Gatam, and Amalek. These and Esau's other descendants lived in the land of Edom.
translation_verse: nɛ Kora nɛ Gatam nɛ Amalek. Bama da aan o yaas banɛ an na'anam Edom sʋ'ʋlimin la ka yi Elifaz tuŋʋn na ka an Ada yaas.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Esau pu'a Oholibama biis banɛ da di na'am nwa': Jeus nɛ Jalam nɛ Kora. Bama da an na'anamɛ yi Esau pu'a Oholibama onɛ an Ana pu'ayua la tuŋʋn na.

english_verse: All of these clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom.
translation_verse: Bama da an Esau biribis, banɛ da aan ba na'anam. Seir yaas yɛla (

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Seir, onɛ an Hor nid la, da dɛŋi bɛ Seir teŋin la, ka o biribis an Lotani nɛ Soobal nɛ Zibeon nɛ Ana

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotani biribis nwa': Hori nɛ Hemam. Timna da anɛ Lotani taʋn.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Soobal biribis da anɛ: Alivan nɛ Manahaf nɛ Ebal nɛ Siefo nɛ Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibeon biribis da anɛ: Aya nɛ Ana. Ana kaŋa da bɛ sian'arin kemmi o saam Zibeon bʋmis ka nyɛ ka ku'otʋʋlʋg tans teŋin yit na la.

english_verse: Anah's children were Dishon and Oholibamah.
translation_verse: Ana biisi nwa': Diseon nɛ Oholibama onɛ da na Ana pu'ayua la.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
