translation_verse: Diseon biis da anɛ: Hemdan nɛ Esiban nɛ Itiran nɛ Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezer biribis da anɛ: Bilihan nɛ Zaavan nɛ Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Disean biis da anɛ: Uz nɛ Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Bama da an Hor dim na'anam: Lotani nɛ Soobal nɛ Zibeon nɛ Ana.

english_verse: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, and they lived in the land of Seir.
translation_verse: Diseon nɛ Ezer nɛ Disean. Bama da an Hor dim na'anam wʋʋ ba dɔɔdi an si'em, Seir teŋin la.

english_verse: Before there were kings in Israel, the following kings ruled Edom one after another: Bela son of Beor from Dinhabah; Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah; Husham from the land of Teman; Hadad son of Bedad from Avith ; Samlah from Masrekah; Shaul from the city of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River; Baalhanan son of Achbor; Hadar from the city of Pau .
translation_verse: Baal-Hanan onɛ an Akibo biig la da kpi la, Hada da di'e o zin'igi di na'am la, ka o tempʋʋg la yʋ'ʋr buon Pau, ka o pu'a yʋ'ʋr buon Mehetabɛl ka o ma yʋ'ʋr buon Matired onɛ mɛ an Mezahab pu'ayua.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Na'anam banɛ da yi Esau tuŋʋn na la nwa', li pa'annɛ ba yʋda nɛ ba dɔɔd nɛ ban yi sʋ'ʋlim si'a na. Ba da anɛ: Timna nɛ Aliva nɛ Jetef

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: nɛ Oholibama nɛ Ela nɛ Pinon

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: nɛ Kena nɛ Teman nɛ Mibzar

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: nɛ Magdiel nɛ Iram. Bama da an Edom na'anamɛ dɔlis wʋʋ ba wʋsa da zin' teŋ-teŋ si'em la, sɔ' wʋsa nɛ o sʋ'ʋlim. Esau, onɛ an Edom, buudi wʋsa yaab la, yɛla la.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Jakob da zin'inɛ o saamme da zin'in teŋ si'a, Keenan teŋin la.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Ka dau la lɛbis ye, “Ba tɔɔm ya. M pa'a wʋm ka ba yɛt ye, ‘Kɛlli ka ti keŋ Dotan teŋin.’” Josef da duoe kad o bieya la bugir ka nyɛɛ ba ka ba kpi'e Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Israel da nɔŋ Josef n gaadi o biis la wʋsa, bɔzugɔ o da du'a o nɛ saŋkanɛ ka o da kʋdig. Ka o da sɛn fukanɛ bɛɛ li kɔn' ka vɛnl hali tis o.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: O bieya la da nyɛ ka ba saam nɔŋ o gaadi ba wʋsa la, ba da kisig o nɛ, ka pʋ bɔɔd o yɛla.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Ka Josef ti zaansim ka tu'as zaansʋŋ la tis o bieya la ka ba da maligim kisig o hali.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: O da yɛli ba ye, “Kɛlisimi zaansʋŋ kanɛ ka m zaansim.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Man zaansim nɛ, ka ti bɔbid mui bɔn'ɔgin, ka mam mui bɔbir la duoe zi'e sappi, ka yanam mui bɔba la la'asi giligi li ka igini li tuon.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: O bieya la da yɛl o ye, “Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ na sʋ'oe tinamaa?” Ka maligim kisig o hali, o zaansʋŋ la nɛ on yɛl si'el la zug.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn zaansim ya'as ka yɛl o bieya la ye, “Kɛlisimi, mam lɛn zaansim nɛ ya'as, ka winnig nɛ nwadig nɛ nwadbibis pii nɛ yinne la'asi igini man tuon.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Ka mɛ yɛl o saam wʋʋ on yɛl o bieya si'em la, ka o saam tans o ka yɛl ye, “Zaansʋŋ bɔ buudi la ka fʋ zaansim? Mam nɛ fʋ ma nɛ fʋ bieya la sid na kena igin fʋn tuonnɛ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: O bieya la da mɔr o nɛ fufum, amaa ka o saam la mɔr nɛ' wʋsa o pʋtɛn'ɛrin. Josef bieya kuos o si'em

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: O bieya la da keŋ zin'ikanɛ kpi'e Sekɛm tempʋʋgin la ye ba kemi ba saam pɛ'ɛs anina.

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Ka Israel yɛl Josef ye, “Gɔsima! Fʋ bieya la keŋ ye ba kem pɛ'ɛs la Sekɛm baba bɛɛ bɔ? Kem na ka m tʋmi fʋ ba san'an.” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Tɔ', m wʋm ya.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o ye, “Kem gɔs ye ban nɛ pɛ'ɛs la wʋsa mɔr laafi, ka lɛb na ka m wʋmi ba labaar.” Ka o tʋm o ka o yi Hebron bɔn'ɔgin la keŋ hali ti paae Sekɛm teŋin.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: Ka dau sɔ' da nyɛɛ o ka o giilimmi giligid karinyana la ni, ka bu'os o ye, “Fʋ ieed bɔ?”

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M ieednɛ m bieya, fʋ na pa'alim ban kemmi ba kɔnbid la zin'isi'aa?”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: Amaa ban da nyɛɛ o ka o nam pʋ paae ba san'an na la, ba sɔns nɛ taaba n gban'e ye ba kʋʋ o.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl taaba ye, “Zaansʋŋ sɔb la nwana kenna!

english_verse: pieces of silver they sold him to the Ishmaelites who took him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Kemi na ka ti kʋʋ o lɔs bulbama yinne ni, ka yɛl ye, bʋnkɔnbbɛ'ogʋ gban'e o ɔnb. Ala ka ti na gɔsi o zaansʋŋ la na niŋ si'em!”

english_verse: Reuben heard this and tried to protect Joseph from them. “Let's not kill him,” he said.
translation_verse: Reuben n da wʋm la, o da mɔ ye o faaɛn o ba nu'usin, ka yɛl ye, “Ti da kʋʋ o.”

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛli ba ye, “Ti da yis ziim. Lɔmminɛ o sian'arin bʋmbɔkin nwa', ka da si'isi nɛ o nɛ ya nu'ugɔ.” Reuben da yɛl nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ ye o faaɛn o yi ba nu'usin mɔri lɛbi tis o saam.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Josef n da paae o bieya san'an na la, ba da yɛɛg o fuvɛnliŋ kanɛ ka o yɛ la

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Ba yʋ'ʋn da zin' ye ba di diib, ka nyɛ Isimael nidib ka ba yi Gilead n gat ka mɔr yʋgʋma ka ziid zɛɛnd banɛ nyuusid nɛ nimmi'isʋg kpaam nɛ tudaari mɔri gati ken Egipt.

english_verse: So Judah said, “What will we gain if we kill our brother and hide his body?
translation_verse: Juda da yɛl bama la ye, “Ti ya'a kʋʋ ti pitʋ nwa' su'a di nyɔɔd an bɔ tisi ti?

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Reuben n da lɛb bʋmbɔkin la ka Josef kae la, o da aans o fuud sʋnsa'aŋ zug.

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: O da lɛb o ba'abiis la san'an yɛl ye, “Biig la kae, nannanna m lɛbid yaanɛ?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Ka ba nɔk Josef fuug la, ka kʋ bʋʋgi nɔk fuug la mi'is ziimin la.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: Ba da mɔr fuvɛnliŋ la lɛbi ba saam san'an yɛl o ye, “Ti pi'ig nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ, di'em gɔs ye li anɛ fʋ biig la fuugɔɔ?”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ka o baŋi li ka ye, “Li anɛ m biig la fuug! Bʋnkɔnbbɛ'ogʋ gban'e o, Josef sid aansnɛ zɔra-zɔra.”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Jakob da aaɛn o fuud sʋnsa'aŋ zug, ka yɛ bɔto fuug, ka kaas o biig la yɛla dabisa bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: O biribis nɛ bipumis wʋsa da la'asi bɛlim o, amaa ka o zan'as ka ye, “Ayei, m na kaasi ala ti paae m yaʋgʋn, m biig la zug!” Ala ka o saam la da kum o yɛla hali.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Midian dim la da kuos Josef Egipt teŋin tis Potifa onɛ an Faaro na'ayikpɛm la yinne. O da anɛ banɛ gur na'ab la tuongat.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Juda da bas o ba'abiis ka keŋi bɛ dau sɔ' san'an Adullam teŋin, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Hira.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Ani ka Juda nyɛ Keenan dau onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Sua la pu'ayua. O da dii o ka digin nɛ o,

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: ka o gban'e pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ ka ba pʋd o, o yʋ'ʋr ye Er.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn du'a biribiŋi pʋd o, o yʋ'ʋr ye Sela. O da du'a o nɛ Kezib teŋin.

english_verse: Later, Judah chose Tamar as a wife for Er, his oldest son.
translation_verse: Juda da bɔ pu'a tis Er onɛ aan o bikpɛɛm la. O yʋ'ʋri da buon Tamar.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Amaa Er, onɛ an Juda bikpɛɛm la, da anɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb Zugsɔb la tuon, alazug Zugsɔb la da kʋʋ o.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Juda da yɛl Onan ye, “Dimi fʋ bier pu'a la, ka maal pʋkɔndiir malima nwɛnɛ lin nar si'em ka li kɛ ka fʋ du'a biisi tisi fʋ bier ka o gbin da li'.”

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Amaa Onan n da baŋ ye o kʋ sʋ'oe biis la, o ɛɛnti digin nɛ pu'a la ka kpa'ae o daulim bas teŋ, linɛ na kɛ ka o kʋ du'a biisi tis o bier la.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: On da tʋm si'el la da anɛ bugus tʋʋma Zugsɔb la tuon. Ka o mɛ kʋʋ o.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Ka Juda da yɛl o bipu'a Tamar ye, “Lɛmmi fʋ saam yiri bɛ nɛ pʋkɔntim la ka m biig Sela ti nɔbig.” O da tɛn'ɛs ye, “Daasi'erɛ Sela na ti kpi wʋʋ o bieya la kpi si'em la.” Tamar da keŋ bɛɛ o saam yin.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Li da yuug ya hali ka Juda pu'a onɛ an Sua pu'ayua la nyaan kpi. Juda sʋnsa'aŋi da gaad la, o da keŋ Timna teŋin, ka o nidib la kiesid o pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid anina. O zua Hira onɛ an Adullam nid la da dɔl o keŋ.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl Tamar ye, “Fʋ dayaam dau la bɛ suori wa'ae Timna ye o kies o pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid la.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Ka o da yɛɛs o pʋkɔnfuud ka tiak fuudi yɛ ka viligi o zug nɛ fubili tiak o mɛŋ ka keŋ zin' Enaim za'anɔɔrin dinɛ bɛ Timna suorin la. Bɔzugɔ, o da nyɛ ka Sela bi', ka ba pʋ kɛ ka o kul o.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Juda nyɛɛ o la, ka tɛn'ɛs ye o anɛ pu'agɔɔndir, on lus o nindaa la zug,

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “M na tisif bʋpɔl m kɔnbid la pʋʋgin.” Ka o bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ na tisim ka li an kasɛt hali nɛ fʋn na ti mɔr bʋʋg la na tisi ma?”

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os o ye, “Ka bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye m tisif ka li an kasɛta?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Nɔkimi fʋ niŋgɔɔnr baŋ kanɛ ka fʋ yʋ'ʋr sɔbi niŋ anina la nɛ fʋ dansaar la tisim.” Ka o zaŋi tis o ka digin nɛ o. Ka o kpɛn gban'e pʋʋg.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Tamar n gaad la, o yɛɛg fukanɛ lus o zug la ka lɛbis o pʋkɔnfuud la yɛ ya'as.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Juda da tʋm o zua onɛ an Adullam nid la nɛ bʋpɔl ye o keŋ tis pu'a la ka di'e o la'abanɛ ka o yɛl nɔɔri zi'el la. Amaa ka o keŋ ka pʋ nyɛɛ o.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os dap banɛ bɛɛ anina la ye, “Teŋgban pu'agɔɔndir kanɛ zin' suor kpikpɛŋ Enaim teŋ za'anɔɔrin la bɛ ya?” Ka ba yɛl o ye, “Teŋgban pu'agɔɔndir ka' kpɛlaa.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛb Juda san'an yɛl o ye, “Mam pʋ nyɛɛ o, dinɛ lɛm paas la dap banɛ bɛɛ anina la ye, ‘Teŋgban pu'agɔɔndir ka' kpɛlaa.’”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Juda da yɛl ye, “On mɔr si'el la kɛl ka o mɔri keŋ; ya'a ka' ala, ba na la'adi ti. Li ya'a an sida, m pʋ pan'as o, bɔzugɔ m tʋm ya ye ba mɔr bʋpɔl la keŋi tis o ka pʋ nyɛɛ o.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Nwadis atan' nya'aŋ ka ba yɛl Juda ye, “Fʋ bipu'a Tamar kpɛn' nɛ dap bɔɔb ka ba'asi nɔk pʋʋg.” Juda da yɛl ye, “Mɔri nɛ o yina ka nyu'oe o nɛ bugum ka o kpi.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Ban mɔr Tamar n yina la, o tʋm labaari yɛl o dayaam dau la ye, “M mɔr nɛ pʋʋg ka li anɛ dau kanɛ sʋ'oe la'abama nwa' tisim.” Ka yɛl ye, “Gɔsim ye fʋ na baŋ la'abama an sɔ' bʋnnɛɛ? Li anɛ baŋ nɛ li nwiig, nɛ dansaar.”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Juda da baŋya ka ye, “O anɛ pʋpielim sɔbi gaad man. Mam pʋ zaŋ o tisim biig Sela ka o di la zugʋ kɛ ka pu'a la niŋim anwana la.” Juda da pʋ lɛn digin nɛ o ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: On da du'ad la, ka yinne yis o nu'ug na, ka pu'adu'as la nɔk gum zɛn'ugʋ lɔɔ o nu'ug la ka ye, “Oŋa yi yiiga na.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Amaa, on lɛbis o nu'ug la, ka yinne la yina, ka o ye, “Fʋn kɔɔ yi si'em nwanaa?” Ka pʋd o, o yʋ'ʋr ye Perez.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Ka liibir onɛ mɔr gum zɛn'ug o nu'ugin la yʋ'ʋn yina ka ba tis o yʋ'ʋr ye Zera.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Tɔ', ka ba da mɔr Josef n keŋ Egipt ka Potifa onɛ an Faaro na'ayikpɛɛm ka an banɛ gur Na'ab la tuongat la da' o Isimael dim banɛ mɔr o na la san'an.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: o zugdaan la da nyɛ ka Zugsɔb bɛ nɛ o, ka linɛ ka o tʋm wʋsa da kennɛ tuon sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: O sʋnf da ma'ae nɛ o hali ka o kɛ ka o gur o. Potifa da nɔk o yir wʋsa nɛ on mɔr si'el wʋsa yɛla niŋ o nu'usin ka o gɔti li.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: O da zaŋ on mɔr si'el wʋsa gu'ul Josef. Josef n da gɔsid si'el wʋsa la zug, o ba'a da lɛn kae o yir la yɛla nii, ya'a ka' on na di disi'a ma'aanɛ. Josef yʋ'ʋn da nɔb nɛ hali ka vɛnl.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Li da pʋ yuugɛ ka o zugdaan la pu'a ya'am kpɛn' o ka o yɛl o ye, “Kem na digin nɛ m!”

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Amaa o da zan'as ka yɛl o ye, “Gɔsima li ka' manɛ gɔsid si'el wʋsa yiraa? M zugdaan pʋ lɛn gɔsid si'el-si'el yiraa. Bɔzugɔ, o nɔki li wʋsa niŋi m nu'usin.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Sɔ' ka' yin kpɛla gat mam. M zugdaan la pʋ mɔŋim si'el si'ela, asɛɛ fʋn ma'aa, fʋn aan o pu'a la zug. M na niŋ wala maal bugisim kaŋa buudi, tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔgi m Wina'am?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ on da zan'as la, pu'a la da sin'igid Josef nɛ daar wʋsa, ka o mɛ da zan'as ye o kʋ digin nɛ o bɛɛ li'el o san'anɛ.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka o kpɛn' yin la ye o tʋm o tʋʋma, ka yammis la sɔ'ɔsɔ ka' yin la.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la gban'e o fuug ka yɛl ye, “Kem na digin nɛ m!” Ka Josef yɛɛg fuug la bas o nu'usin ka zɔɔ yi.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: pu'a la buol yin la yammis la wʋsa yɛli ba ye, “Gɔsimi ban mɔr Hibiru bikaŋa kena ye o ziemi ti si'em! O kpɛn' kpɛla na ye o digin nɛ mam; ka m kaas kuŋ,

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: ka on wʋm ka m kaas ye ba faanmim la, ka o zɔ ka bas o fuugʋ m nu'usin.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: O da nɔk fuug la digil ka o sid la ti kul na.

english_verse: Then she said, “That Hebrew slave of yours tried to rape me!
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o ye, “Hibiru yammʋg kanɛ ka fʋ mɔr na la kena ye o bibigim.

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Amaa on wʋm ka m kaas ye ba faanmim mɛ bas la, ka o zɔ ka bas o fuugʋ m nu'usin.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: ka o mɔr Josef n keŋ yɔ' zin'ikanɛ ka ba yɔɔd na'ab nimbanɛ da tʋm bɛ'ɛd la. Josef n da bɛ sanrega ni la,

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da bɛ nɛ o; ka onɛ gur sanrega la ya'am kpɛn' o.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Onɛ gur sanrega la da kɛ ka Josef sʋ'oe banɛ bɛ sanrega ni la, ka gɔsid linɛ wʋsa tʋm anina.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Onɛ gur sanrega la da pʋ lɛn gɔsid linɛ wʋsa ka o niŋ Josef nu'usin la, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la da bɛ nɛ o ka kɛ ka on maal si'el wʋsa ken tuon sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: O da nɔki ba yɔ' onɛ an banɛ gur na'ab la tuongat yin, dɔkanɛ ka ba da yɔ' Josef ani la mɛn.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Banɛ gur na'ab la tuongat da nɔki ba niŋ Josef nu'usin ka o gɔsidi ba. Ba da bɛɛ anina ka li yuug bi'ela.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Dapa ayi' nwa', onɛ kuobid na'ab daam nɛ onɛ sʋ'oe bodobodo yɛla la da zaansim yʋ'ʋŋ yinne, ka sɔ' wʋsa zaansʋŋ mɔri li gbine li kɔn'.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie ka Josef kɛɛn ba san'an na la, o da nyɛ ka ba nindaas zuŋ ka ba sʋnya san'am.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ti babayi' nwa' sa zaansimnɛ yʋ'ʋŋ, amaa sɔ' kae na pa'ali ti li gbinnɛ.” Ka Josef lɛbis ye, “Abaŋ zaansʋŋ gbin pʋ yit nɛ Wina'am ni naa? Yɛliminimɛ ya zaansʋŋ la!”

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: ka li mɔr wila atan' ka vanpɔla yina ka puum mɛ pu, ka li pʋ yuugɛ ka li wali bi'ig.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Ka nwam kanɛ ka m mɔri tisid Faaro daam la bɛɛ m nu'ugin ka m nɔk wala la nwiaki niŋ Faaro nwammin la, nɔki niŋ o nu'ugin.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl o ye, “Li gbinni nwa'. Wila atan' la anɛ daba atan'.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Daba atan' nwa' sʋʋgin, Faaro na yisif kpɛla ka kɛ ka fʋ lɛbi tʋmmi fʋ tʋʋma wʋʋ fʋn daa pʋn tʋm si'em la, ka fʋ na nɔk Faaro nwammi niŋ o nu'usin wʋʋ fʋn daa kuobid o daam si'em la.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Amaa si'el wʋsa ya'a keŋ sʋ'ʋŋa tisif, fʋn tɛnri m yɛla ka pa'al pʋpielim nɛ m, pian'ami m yɛla tis Faaro ka kɛ ka m yi sanrega nwa' ni.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Ba mukim nɛ ziimɛ yi Hibiru teŋin na, hali kpɛla nwa' m pʋ tʋm si'el dinɛ nar ye m bɛ bʋmbɔk kaŋa nii.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Onɛ an bodobodo maannib kpɛɛm la nyɛ ka Josef tu'as o tiraan la yɛla ka li malis la, o yɛl Josef ye, “Mam mɛ sa zaansimnɛ ka bodobodo pɛɛd atan' bɛɛ m zugin,

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: ka pɛ'ɛkanɛ bɛ zugin la, ka bodobodo buudi wʋsa linɛ an Faaro din bɛɛ di ni, amaa ka niis ɔnbid bodobodo la.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl ye, “Li gbinni nwa'. Pɛɛd atan' la anɛ daba atan'.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Dabisa atan' nwa' sʋʋgin, Faaro na yisif kpɛla ka fi'igi fʋ zug, ka yuluf tiig zug, ka niis dii fʋ niŋgbina la.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Daba atan' daar la da anɛ Faaro du'am tiɛnr dabisir, ka o maal di'ema nɛ ba ka dʋg diibi tisid o na'ayikpɛm. Ka o yis onɛ gɔsid o daam yɛla nɛ onɛ maan o bodobodo la sanrega ni na zi'eli ba o na'ayikpɛm la tuon.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: ka yul onɛ aan o bodobodo maannib kpɛɛm la nwɛnɛ Josef n da pa'ali ba zaansʋŋ la gbin si'em la.

english_verse: but the king's personal servant completely forgot about Joseph.
translation_verse: Amaa onɛ sʋ'oe daam yɛla la da tam Josef yɛla nɛ.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Yʋma ayi' nya'aŋ ka Faaro zaansim, ka o zi'e kɔldakanɛ ka ba buon Nail la nɔɔrin.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Ka niigi ayɔpɔi yi kɔldaugin la na nɔb hali saalim ɔnbid kɔlkantima.

english_verse: Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka niigi ayɔpɔi banɛ waŋim ka pʋ vɛnla yi kɔldaugin la na zi'e kpi'e na'abama la kɔldaug la nɔɔrin.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Ka banɛ waŋim ka pʋ vɛnl la vɔl na'abanɛ nɔbi saalim la. Ka Faaro daa yirigi nie gbɛɛmin.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbi gbis ya'as ka lɛn zaansim nyɛ kawɛnna ayɔpɔi ka ba bɛdim ka vɛnl sʋ'ʋŋa la'asi bɛ kawɛndaug yinne ni.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Ban nya'aŋ la ka kawɛnbaanlʋg ayɔpɔi mɛ yina ka sisi'em yi ya-nya'aŋ na nwɛ' ba ka ba ziank.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Ka kawɛnbaanlʋg la vɔl kawɛnbɛda la, ka Faaro nie gbɛɛmin nyɛ ka li an zaansʋŋ.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ nie la ka o sʋʋnr san'am, ka o tʋm buol ya'am dim nɛ banɛ tʋm nyalima Egipt teŋgbauŋʋn la wʋsa. Faaro da tu'asi ba o zaansʋŋ la yɛla amaa sɔ' da pʋ nyaŋi tu'as o zaansʋŋ la gbinnɛ.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Ani ka onɛ kuobid Faaro daam la yɛl ye, “Zina, m tiɛn gbɛlʋŋ kanɛ ka m maal la:

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Na'ab Faaro, fʋ sʋnfʋ da pɛlig nɛ fʋ yammis ka fʋ nɔk mam nɛ banɛ maan bodobodo kpɛɛm la keŋi yɔ sanrega ni banɛ gur na'ab tuongat la yin la,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: ti nidib ayi' la da zaansim yʋ'ʋŋ yinne ka zaansʋŋ wʋsa mɔri li gbin.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Hibiru dim dasaŋ da la'am bɛ nɛ ti anina, ka an banɛ gur Na'ab tuongat la sankpan'as. Ka ti tu'asi ti zaansima la tis o ka o pa'al sɔ' wʋsa zaansʋŋ gbin.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Ka si'el wʋsa sid maal nwɛnɛ on yɛli ti si'em la. Ba da lɛbis mam m tʋʋma ni ka yul dau kaŋa la tiig zug.” Josef pa'al Faaro zaansʋŋ la gbin

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Faaro da tʋm ye ba mɔr Josef na, ka ba yis o sanrega la ni tɔ'ɔtɔ mɔr o na. On pʋni o zug ka yɛɛ o fuudi naae la, o kɛn Faaro tuon na.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl Josef ye, “M zaansimnɛ ka sɔ' kae na nyaŋi tu'asimi li gbinnɛ, amaa m wʋmi fʋ yɛla ye, fʋ ya'a wʋm zaansʋŋ fʋ na nyaŋi tu'asi li gbin.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Josef da yɛl Faaro ye, “Man kʋ nyaŋi tu'asif zaansʋŋ la gbinnɛ, amaa Wina'am ma'aa na nyaŋi tu'as Faaro li gbin.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ani ka Faaro yɛl Josef ye, “M zaansʋŋ la pʋʋgin ka m nyɛ ka m zi'e Nail kɔldaug la nɔɔrin,

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Ka kɔldaug la pʋʋgin ka niigi ayɔpɔi yina nɔbi saalim bɛ kɔlkantima la sʋʋgin ɔnbid.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ la, ka niigi ayɔpɔi yina waŋim pʋ vɛnla ka banlig hali. Ya'a an sida, man nan zi' nyɛ niigi Egipt teŋin ka ba waŋim ka lɛr wʋʋ na'abama.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Amaa ban vɔli ba naae la nya'aŋ, sɔ' kʋ baŋ ye ba vɔl si'ela, ka nan kpɛn an wʋʋ ban aan si'em la. Ani ka m nie gbɛɛmin.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: M zaansʋŋin la ya'as, m nyɛ kawɛnna ayɔpɔi la'asi bɛ kawɛndaug yinne ni vɛnl ka mɔr bielim sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Ban yina la nya'aŋ ka kawɛnna ayɔpɔi mɛ yina banlig hali ka sisi'em da'ae yi ya-nya'aŋ na nwɛ' ba ka ba ziank.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Ka kawɛnbaanla la vɔl kawɛnsʋma ayɔpɔi la. Ka m zaŋi li yɛla tu'asi tisim tiim dim amaa sɔ' pʋ nyaŋi yɛli mɛ li gbinnɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Ani ka Josef yɛl Faaro ye, “Naa na'ab Faaro, fʋ zaansʋŋ la anɛ yinne ka li gbin mɛ an yinne. Wina'am nienɛ pa'alif on bɔɔd ye o maal si'em.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Na'asʋma ayɔpɔi la anɛ yʋma ayɔpɔi ka kawɛnsʋma ayɔpɔi la mɛ an yʋma ayɔpɔi. Li wʋsa anɛ yinne ka mɔr gbin yinne.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Na'awana ayɔpɔi banɛ pʋ vɛnl ka yina la zi'enɛ pa'al yʋma ayɔpɔi, ka kawɛnbaanla banɛ ka sisi'em yi ya-nya'aŋ na ʋki ba la pa'an yʋma ayɔpɔi mɛn. Ba pa'an ye kɔ'ɔm na bɛ yʋma ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Li kpɛn anɛ wʋʋ mam yɛlif si'em la. Wina'am pa'alif nɛ on bɔɔd ye o maal si'em.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Yʋma ayɔpɔi la, Egipt teŋin la wʋsa ba na nyɛ zʋʋd hali ka li zu'oe,

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Ba kʋ lɛn tɛnr tigir kanɛ daa bɛ teŋin la, bɔzugɔ, kɔ'ɔm kanɛ na dɔlli li nya'aŋ la na wʋm nidib hali.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ka dinɛ kɛ ka zaansʋŋ la kɛn Faaro san'an na zin'is ayi' la anɛ ye Wina'am pʋn dɛŋi gban'e li sa, ka na tʋmi li ka li kʋ lɛn yuugɛ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: “Nannanna, Na'ab Faaro, gaŋim dau onɛ mɔr ya'am ka mi' dinɛ an sʋm, ka kɛ ka o gɔsid Egipt teŋgbauŋ wʋsa.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Ka gaŋ ninsieba ka ba na di'esid diib nidib la san'an la'asid Egipt teŋin la wʋsa. Zin'is anu wʋsa pʋʋgin ba na di'e yinne, yʋma ayɔpɔi linɛ ka diib na bɛ bɛdegʋ la.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Ba di'esim diib la yʋʋm sʋma banɛ kenna la wʋsa, ka tis suor ka ba su'a diib la tempʋʋdin la ka li bɛ fʋn nu'usin, Na'aba.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Dikaŋa ye li dignɛ an teŋgbauŋ la bʋn. Ba na ti dii li nɛ yʋma ayɔpɔi linɛ na an kɔ'ɔm la saŋa Egipt teŋin la. Ala ka kɔ'ɔm kʋ san'am teŋgbauŋ la.” Ban dʋ'ʋs Josef Egipt teŋin si'em

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Gban'akaŋa da an sʋm tis Faaro nɛ o na'ayikpɛm la.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Faaro da bu'osi ba ye, “Ti na lɛn nyɛ sɔ' ka o nwɛnɛ dau kaŋa onɛ ka Wina'am Siig bɛɛ o nii?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Ani ka Faaro yɛl Josef ye, “Wina'am sadigim nie nɛ'ɛŋa pa'alif la, sɔ' kae na mɔr ya'am nɛ mi'ilim nwɛnɛ fʋnɛ.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Fʋ na sʋ'oe m na'ayir la gɔsid, ka m nidib la wʋsa na di'e fʋ nɔɔr zin'ig wʋsa. M na'am gbauŋ la zug ma'aa ka m na gatif.”

english_verse: You are now governor of all Egypt!”
translation_verse: Ala ka Faaro yɛl Josef ye, “M zaŋ Egipt teŋgbauŋ wʋsa niŋi fʋ nu'usin.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Ani ka Faaro pidig o nu'ubil baŋ dinɛ an o zanbin la pid Josef. O da bɔb o nɛ fupiel sʋma ka nɔk sanlim zɔnti kɔl o niŋgɔɔnr.

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: O da nɔk na'am tɛreko kanɛ paas ayi' ka widi tɛɛd la tis o ye o mɔri ken, ka kɛ ka sɔ' gaad tuonnɛ tansid ye, “Iginimi teŋin!” Ala ka Faaro kɛ ka Josef sʋ'oe Egipt teŋgbauŋ wʋsa.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Faaro da yɛl Josef ye, “Manɛ an Faaro, amaa ya'a ka' fʋn na tis nɔɔrɛ, sɔ' ka' suori niŋid si'el Egipt teŋin ya'asa.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Faaro da pʋd Josef yʋ'ʋr ye Zafenaf-Panea, ka nɔk Potifera, onɛ an Oon teŋin maanmaan la pu'ayua onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Asenat n tis o ka o di.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Yʋʋm sʋma ayɔpɔi la saŋa zʋʋd da maal sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Ka yʋma ayɔpɔi banɛ ka zʋʋd maal sʋ'ʋŋa Egipt teŋin la Josef da di'es zuudi su'a tempʋʋdin la. Tempʋʋg wʋsa o da su'ad zʋʋd dinɛ ka ba buni anina la.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Josef da su'a ki ka li zu'oe hali nwɛnɛ atɛuk titanbin'isʋg nɛ. Li da zu'oe nɛ galis ka o bas ka pʋ lɛn sɔbid on di'esid si'em, bɔzugɔ, li da zu'oe nɛ galis ka ba kʋ nyaŋi makɛ.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Josef da pʋd o bikpɛɛm la yʋ'ʋr ye Manase ka yɛl ye, “Wina'am kɛya ka m tami m namisʋg la wʋsa nɛ m saam yir yɛla.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Biribiŋ kanɛ paas ayi' la, o da pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Efiram, ka o yɛl ye, “Wina'am kɛ ka m paam du'am, teŋ kanɛ ka m nyɛ namisʋg la ni.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Yʋma ayɔpɔi banɛ ka diib da bɛ la da paae li bɛn,

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: ka yʋma ayɔpɔi dinɛ an kɔ'ɔm yʋma la pin'il wʋʋ Josef n yɛl si'em la. Kɔ'ɔm da lu tɛɛns wʋsa pʋʋgin, amaa Egipt teŋgbauŋ wʋsa da mɔr diib.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Kɔ'ɔm la da ti ye li wʋm Egipt dim la, ba da kaasi tis Faaro ye o tisi ba diib, amaa ka o da yɛl Egipt dim wʋsa ye, “Kemi Josef san'an, ka tʋm on yɛli ya ye ya niŋ si'em wʋsa.”

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Kɔ'ɔm la da yadig teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa la, Josef da yɔ'ɔg diib dɔɔd la kuos diibi tis Egipt dim bɔzugɔ kɔ'ɔmtita'ar da lu Egipt teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa zug.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Tɛɛns wʋsa nidib da kennɛ Egipt teŋin na da'ad diib Josef san'an bɔzugɔ kɔ'ɔmtita'ar la da lu nɛ dunia wʋsa.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Jakob n da baŋ ye diib bɛ Egipt teŋin la, o yɛl o biis ye, “Bɔ ka ya nan kpɛn zin' gɔsid taaba?”

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛli ba ye, “M wʋm ye diib bɛ Egipt teŋin, kem da'ae na ka ti di ka nyaŋi yi kumin.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Josef bieya piiga da keŋ Egipt teŋin ye ba da' diib.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Amaa Jakob da pʋ kɛ ka Josef pitʋ Benjamin dɔl o bieya la keŋɛ, bɔzugɔ o da zɔti dabiem ye o na ti nyɛ dɛŋ.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Lin niŋ si'em la ka Israel biis la mɛ da la'as nɛ banɛ keŋ ye ba da' diib la, bɔzugɔ, kɔ'ɔm la mɛ da li Keenan teŋin. Josef kpans o bieyanam piiga

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Josef n da an teŋ la gɔmena, onɛ kuosid diibi tisid nidib la wʋsa. Josef bieya la da paae la ba da vanbin o tuon ka ba nindaas kpa' teŋin.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ani ka o tiɛn on da zaansim ba yɛla la, ka yɛl ye, “Ya pigidnɛ teŋ la! Ya kena ye ya labisi gɔsi ti teŋ la zin'ikanɛ ka ti pʋ gura.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ayei, ti zugdaana, fʋ tʋmtʋmnib kena ye ti da' diib.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “Ayei, ya kena ye ya labisi gɔs teŋ la zin'ikanɛ ka ti pʋ gura.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ayei, ti zugdaana, ti da anɛ pii nɛ ayi', an dau yinne biisi bɛ Keenan teŋin. Kpaanr la kpɛlimnɛ ti saam san'an, amaa yinne lɛn kae.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Man na kpansi ya si'em nwa', m pɔ nɛ Na'ab Faaro yʋ'ʋr ye ya kʋ yi kpɛla kulɛ asɛɛ ka ya mɔri ya pitʋ onɛ an kpaanr la kɛn kpɛla na.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Tʋmmi ya nid yinne ka o keŋ mɔri ya pitʋ la na. Yanam banɛ kpɛlim la na bɛ sanrega ni, ala ka m na kpansi baŋ ye ya pian'ad la anɛ sida bɛɛ ziri. M yɛti ya nɛ sida ye, ya ya'a pʋ mɔr o naa, alaa ya sid anɛ banɛ kena ye ya labisi gɔs teŋ la.”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Ka o nɔki ba niŋ sanrega ni daba atan'.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Daba atan' la daar ka Josef yɛli ba ye, “Niŋimi na anwa ka ya na vʋe, bɔzugɔ mam anɛ onɛ zɔt Wina'am.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a sid anɛ sida dim, kɛlli ka ya nid yinne kpɛlim sanrega ni ka o taaba la mɔr diibi kuli tisi ya yidim banɛ kpiid kɔ'ɔm la.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Amaa asɛɛ ka ya mɔri ya pitbil la na, ka m baŋ ye ya anɛ sida dim ka lin na kɛ ka ya kʋ kpii.” Ka ba siak ye ba na niŋ ala. Simeon ba'abiis la kul ka o kpɛlim la yɛla

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl taaba ye, “Sida ti namisʋg la anɛ ti pitʋ la yɛla. Ti nyɛ on da namis si'em ka bɛlimi ti o nyɔvʋr yɛla, amaa ka ti zan'as ka pʋ kɛlisɛ; dinɛ kɛ ka namiskaŋa kennɛ ti zugin na.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Reuben da lɛbisi ba ye, “M da pʋ yɛli ya ye ya da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kaŋa tis biig la ka ya pʋ kɛligɛ? Nannanna, asɛɛ ka ti yɔɔ o ziim kanɛ da yi la sam.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Ba da pʋ baŋ ye Josef na wʋm ban pian'ad si'el la, bɔzugɔ sɔ' da di'esid pian'ad la.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: O da fɛndig o nindaa ba san'an ka kum, ka lɛn fɛndigi ba san'an na ka pian'ad nɛ ba ya'as. Ka o kɛ ka ba nɔk Simeon n yɔɔ ba nini ni.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Josef da tis nɔɔr ye o nidib la pɛ'ɛli ba bɔtnam la nɛ diib ka nɔk sɔ' wʋsa ligidi lɛbisi sʋʋ o bɔto la ni, ka tisi ba dinɛ ka ba na di suor zug. Ban maal nɛ' wʋsa tisi ba naae la,

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: ba da lɔɔ ba bʋmis nɛ ba diibi duoe yii kun.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Ba da paae zin'isi'a ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb ka ba zi'en, ka yinne yidigi o bɔto ye o gbin'e diib bi'ela tis o bʋŋ ka nyɛ ka o ligidi la bɛɛ o bɔto nɔɔrin.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o ba'abiis la ye, “Ba lɛbisi m ligidi m bɔto la ni.” Ka ba ya'am iank ka ba fɛndigi gɔsid taaba nɛ dabiem ka ye, “Yɛl bɔɔ nwa' ka Wina'am kɛ ka li paae ti?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Ban paae ba saam san'an Keenan teŋin la, ba tu'as o linɛ niŋi ba la wʋsa. Ba yɛl o ye,

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Ye ti da anɛ biribis pii nɛ ayi' an saam yinne biis. Yinne la lɛn kae ka kpaanr la kpɛlimmi ti saam san'an Keenan teŋin.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ka onɛ an zugdaani sʋ'oe teŋ la yɛli ti ye, ‘Man na niŋ si'em baŋ ye ya anɛ sida dimi nwa', basimini ya nid yinne kpɛla ka mɔr diib la kuli tisi ya yidim banɛ namisid nɛ kɔ'ɔm la.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka mɔri ya pitbil la na, ka m nyɛɛ o ka baŋ ye ya anɛ sida dim. Ani ka m na lɛbisi ya nid la tisi ya, ka ya yʋ'ʋn na nyaŋi kpiisid teŋin la.’”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Ka ban ti kpa'asid diib bɔtnamin la, ka sɔ' wʋsa ligidi lɔɔ bɛɛ o bɔto la pʋʋg. Ban nɛ ba saamme nyɛ ligidi la lɔɔ bɛɛ ani la, dabiem kpɛn' ba nɛ ka ba ya'am iank.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Ka ba saam Jakob yɛli ba ye, “Ya kɛya ka m kɔ'ɔŋi m biis. Josef lɛn kae, ka Simeon mɛ lɛn kae. Nannanna, ya lɛm bɔɔd ye ya mɔr Benjamin keŋ ya'as. Si'el wʋsa yʋ'ʋn anɛ bɛ'ɛdi tisim!”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Reuben yɛl o saam ye, “M ya'a pʋ mɔr o lɛb na tisi fɔ, fʋn kʋʋm man biribis ayi' la wʋsa. Nɔkim o niŋi m nu'usin ka mam na mɔr o lɛb na.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Amaa Jakob yɛl ye, “Mam biig la kʋ dɔlli ya keŋ aninaa. O bier kpiya ka on ma'aa kpɛlim. Ya ya'a mɔr o keŋ ka si'el ti niŋ o suor zug, m zuobpielim nwa' na sig yaʋgʋn nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Ka kɔ'ɔm la yʋ'ʋn mu'oe wii teŋ la zug.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Ban ti di dikanɛ ka ba mɔri yi Egipt la na naae la, ka ba saam yɛli ba ye, “Lɛm keŋi da' diib bi'ela na tisi ti.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: amaa fʋ ya'a kʋ kɛ ka o keŋɛ, li na tɔi bɔzugɔ, dau la yɛli ti ye, ‘Ya kʋ nyɛɛm nindaa, asɛɛ yanamɛ na dɔlli ya pitʋ la na.’”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Israel da bu'osi ba ye, “Bɔzug kimm ka yanam yɛl dau la ye ya mɔr pitʋ ka zi yɛl kaŋa kɛɛn m zugin na?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Dau la bu'osi ti nɛ ti mɛŋ nɛ ti yidim yɛla. O bu'osi ti ye, ‘Ya saam nam bɛɛ? Ya mɔr bier bɛɛ pitʋ ya'asɛɛ?’ Tinam lɛbis nɛ wʋʋ on bu'osi ti si'em la. Tinam ye ti niŋ wala baŋ ye o na yɛl ye ti mɔri ti pitʋ la kena?”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Ani ka Juda yɛl o saam Israel ye, “Kɛl ka biig la dɔl mam ka ti duoe keŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ ka lɛb na, ka tinam nɛ fʋn nɛ ti biis la vʋ'ʋg ka kɔ'ɔm da kʋʋ tii.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ na siaki zi'enɛ o nyɔvʋr yɛla. M ya'a ti pʋ mɔr biig la lɛb na zi'eli fʋ tuon kpɛla naa, fʋn gban'am mam, ka mam mɛŋ na zi taal la hali nɛ m nyɔvʋr bɛn.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Din an si'em la, ti ya'a pʋ yuuginɛɛ, anwaa ti keŋin nɔɔra ayi' ka lɛbin na.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Ani ka ba saam Israel yɛl ye, “Li ya'a aan ala, yanam niŋim anwa: Mɔri la'asʋma dinɛ bɛ teŋin la mɔri keŋ tis dau la ka li aan ya piini; nɔkimi kpaam linɛ an tiim bi'ela, nɛ siind bi'ela, bʋnnyubisa nɛ mir nɛ tiis walsʋma.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn nɔk anzurifa ligidi la zin'is ayi' mɔri keŋ, bɔzugɔ anzurifa linɛ ka ba daa nɔki niŋi ya bɔtnamin la anɛ ya nɔki lɛbisi tisi ba, ka daasi'erɛɛ ba daa yidig nɛ.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Dɔllini ya pitʋ la keŋi tɔ'ɔtɔ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Wina'am Onɛ Galis la na kɛ ka dau la zɔɔ ya nimbaanlig ka kɛ ka Simeon nɛ Benjamin dɔlli ya lɛb na. Aa tɔ, m ya'a na kɔ'ɔŋi m biis nwaa, m na kɔ'ɔŋi banɛ.” Josef maal o ba'abiis saauŋ

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Ba da duoe nɔk piini la, nɛ ki la ligidi zin'is ayi', ka dɔl Benjamin ka ba lɛb Egipt tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ nɔki ba mɛŋi pa'al Josef.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Josef n nyɛ ka Benjamin dɔlli ba la ka o yɛl onɛ gɔsid o yin la ye, “Dɔl dap bama keŋi m yin; kɔdigim bʋnkɔnbʋg ka ba maal diib; man nɛ ban na la'am di nintaŋa.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Dau la da niŋ wʋʋ Josef yɛl o si'em la, ka dɔl dap la keŋ Josef yin.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Dabiem da gban'e dap la nɛ ban da mɔri ba keŋ o yin la. Ba tɛn'ɛs ye, “Anzurifa ligidi dinɛ daa bɛɛ ti bɔtnamin la zug ka ba mɔri ti kɛn kpɛla na. O bɔɔd ye o zab nɛ ti nyaŋi ti ka faaɛn ti bʋmis la ka ti lieb o sankpan'asnam.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Ka ban dɔl Josef tʋmtʋm la paae Josef yir za'anɔɔrin la, ba da yɛl o ye,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Naa, tinamɛ daa dɛŋin kena ye ti da' diib la,

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: ka daa lɛbidi kun ka paae suor ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔbi ti ka sɔ' wʋsa yɔ'ɔg o bɔto nyɛ ka anzurifa ligidi kanɛ ka ti nɔki da' diib la nan kpɛn bɔbig ala bɛɛ ti bɔtnam nɔya ni. Din ka ti mɔri lɛb na.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Ti mɛ lɛm mɔr anzurifa ligidi na ye ti da' diib ya'as. Ti zi' onɛ daa nɔk ligidi la niŋi ti bɔtnamin laa.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “Li siakya, da zɔti dabiem, li anɛ ya Wina'am onɛ aan ya yaanam Wina'am la daa zaŋ ligidi la niŋi ya bɔtnamin la, manɛ daa di'e ya ligidi la.” Ka yʋ'ʋn dɔl Simeon yina tisi ba.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Tʋmtʋm la da dɔl dap la kpɛn' Josef yin, ka tisi ba ku'om ka ba pie ba nɔba ka tisi ba bʋmis la yaama ka ba ɔnb.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Ka ba ti'ebi ba piini la gur Josef n na ti lɛb nintaŋ na bɔzugɔ ba wʋm ye, ba na ti dii anina.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Josef n ti kul na la, ka ba nɔki ba piini linɛ ka ba mɔri kena la tis o, ka igini paae teŋin na'as o.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Ka o bu'osi ba niŋgbina an si'em, ka ye, “Ya saam onɛ an bʋnkʋdʋg ka ya daa yɛli mɛ o yɛla la an wala? O nan kpɛn vʋeyaa?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ti saam onɛ an fʋ sankpan'as la nan vʋe ka mɔr laafi.” Ka ba igin teŋin na'as o ya'as.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: On ti gɔsi nyɛɛ o pitʋ Benjamin, onɛ aan o mɛŋ mabiig la, ka bu'osi ba ye, “Ya pitʋ kanɛ an kpaanr onɛ ka ya daa yɛlim o yɛla la nwaa? M dakɔɔnrɛ, Wina'am pʋpielim na bɛ nɛf.”

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Josef sʋnf da san'am o pitʋ la zug, ka o yii su'a zin'isi'a kum. O da kpɛn' o dɔgbɛɛndigin kaasid anina.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: On ti kum naae ka pie o nindaa la, o da gban'e o mɛŋi yina ka ye, “Pʋdigimi diib la!”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Ka ba pʋdigi zi'el o tuon, ka zi'el o bieya la diibi ba tuon, ka zi'el Egipt nimbanɛ ka on nɛ ban dit la ba kɔn', bɔzugɔ Egipt dim da pʋ siakid ye ba la'asi di nɛ Hibiru nidiba, din aan ba kisʋg la zug.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Ba da kɛnɛ ka ba zin'in kpɛmmir Josef tuon. Kpɛɛm la da zin'in yiiga ka onɛ pa'a o zug la dɔl, ka ba tʋʋn ala hali ti paae onɛ an kpaanr la. Ka ba lidigi gɔsid taaba.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Ban da gbin'es diib Josef diib zin'igin la pʋdigi tisi ba la, Benjamin diib da zu'oe gaad sɔ' wʋsa din zin'is anu. Ka ba la'asi di ka nu nɛ o n tig.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ka zaŋi m anzurifa kɔp la niŋ biig la bɔto la nɔɔrin, lin nɛ o ligidi la wʋsa.” Ka o da niŋ nwɛnɛ Josef n yɛl o si'em la.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ka bɛkɛung ka ba nɔki ba bʋmisi yi.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Ban da nam pʋ lalig la, ka Josef yɛl o tʋmtʋm la ye, “Zɔm tɔ'ɔtɔ bɛn dap la, ka fʋ ya'a gban'e ba fʋn yɛlimi ba ye, ‘Bɔ ka ya nɔk bɛ'ɛdi lɛbis nɛ sʋm?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Li ka'anɛ kɔp kanɛ ka m yisɔb mɔri nuud ka mɔri gɔsid o bɛog yɛla la ka ya zuu? Ya tʋm bɛ'ɛd.’”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: On da gban'e ba la, o yɛli ba ala,

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ti zugdaana, bɔ ka fʋ yɛti ti anwa? Ti pɔya ye ti pʋ tʋm bʋnkaŋaa.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Fʋ mi' ye tinamɛ daa paae Keenan nyɛ ligidkanɛ bɛɛ ti bɔtnamin la, ti daa mɔri lɛbis na, ka wala ka ti na zu sanlima bɛɛ anzurifa fʋ yisɔb la yin nɛ?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a nyɛɛ ti sɔ' ka o mɔr kɔp la, fʋn kʋʋm o, ka kɛ ka tinam banɛ kpɛlim la liebi fʋ yisɔb la sankpan'asnam.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “Li an sʋm, m na maal nwɛnɛ yanamɛ yɛl si'em la, amaa onɛ bɔto ni ka m nyɛ kɔp la, on ma'aa na liebi m yisɔb la sankpan'as.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ka sɔ' wʋsa digil o bɔto ka yɔ'ɔgi li.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Ka Josef tʋmtʋm la pin'il kpɛɛm la bɔto la ni yiiga n paae ba wʋsa. Ka on da paae Benjamin bɔto la o nyɛ kɔp la anina.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Bʋnkaŋa da san'ami ba sʋnya pamm ka ba aansi ba fuudi li zug. Ka ba wʋsa zaŋi ba la'adi pa'ali ba bʋmis la zugʋ lɛb teŋin la.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Ka Juda nɛ o pitib la da paae anina la, Josef da nan bɛ nɛ yin. Ka ba igin o tuon,

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: ka o yɛli ba ye, “Ya maal bɔɔ la? Ya zi' ye m na nyaŋi su'a baŋɛɛ?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Ka Juda yɛl ye, “Ti zugdaana, ti ye ti yɛl ye bɔ? Ti na niŋ wala ka fʋ baŋ ye ti zi' li ti'irɛ? Wina'am yisi ti gbin. Ti wʋsa na anɛ fʋ sankpan'asnam, kas-kas anɛ onɛ bɔto ni ka kɔp la bɛ la.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛli ba ye, “M kʋ namisi ya wʋsa. Onɛ ka m kɔp la bɛɛ o bɔto ni la, on ma'aa na liebi m sankpan'as; ka yanam banɛ kpɛlim la na tun'e kuli ya saam yin nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.”

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ka Juda li'el o san'an na n yɛl o ye, “M zugdaana, dim suguru ka m tu'asif bi'ela. Da kɛ ka fʋ sʋnf duoe nɛ ma, baa fʋn zem nɛ Na'ab Faaro la.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: M zugdaana, fʋ daa bu'osi ti ye, ‘Ya saam la nan kpɛn vʋeya, ka ya mɔr ba'abiis sieba ka ba bɛɛ?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Ka ti lɛbis ye, ‘Ti saam anɛ bʋnkʋdʋg. O da kʋdignɛ ka nyaan du'a Benjamin. Ka Benjamin mabiig la mɛ kpinɛ. Ka Benjamin ma'aa vʋe ka ti ba' la nɔŋ o galis.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Fʋ yɛli ti ye ti mɔr o na ka fʋ mɛŋ nyɛɛ o nɛ fʋ nini,

english_verse: We told you that our father would die if Benjamin left him.
translation_verse: ka tinam yɛlif ye, ‘Benjamin ya'a kena ka bas o ba' la, o ba' la na kpi.’

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Ti zugdaana, fʋ daa yɛli ti ye asɛɛ ka ti dɔlli ti pitbil la na, ya'a ka' ala ti kʋ lɛn nyɛ fʋ nindaa.

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ tinamɛ daa kuli paae ti saam la san'an la, ti daa tu'as o fʋn pian' si'el la wʋsa tisi ti la.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Li pʋ yuugɛ ka ti saam yɛli ti ye, ‘Lɛm keŋi da' diib bi'ela na tisi ti.’

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Ka ti lɛbis o ye, ‘Ti kʋ nyaŋi keŋɛ. Ti ya'a na dɔlli ti pitbil la, ti na keŋ; amaa ti ya'a pʋ dɔl o keŋɛ, ti kʋ nyaŋi nyɛ dau la nindaa.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ka ti saam yɛli ti ye, ‘Ya mi' ye m pu'a da du'a biis ayi' tisim,

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: ka ba yinne bɔdig ka basim, ka m da yɛl ye bʋnkɔnbbɛ'ogʋ sid gban'e o ka aans o zɔra-zɔra; ka m pʋ lɛn nyɛɛ o hali nɛ zina.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Ka ya ya'a mɔr oŋa mɛ keŋ ka si'el ti niŋ o suor zug, m zuobpielim nwa' na sig yaʋgʋn nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.’

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ sid daa pɛsigi m mɛŋ ka pɛ'ɛŋ biig la m saam san'an, ka yɛl o ye m ya'a pʋ mɔr o lɛbis naa, taal la na dɔllim hali ti paae n nyɔvʋr bɛn.

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Dinzug, m sɔsidif ye fʋ kɛ ka man di'e biig la zi'esim kpɛlim kpɛla tʋmmi tisidif, ka biig la duoe dɔl o bieya kul o saam san'an.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Ayei, m zugdaana, m na niŋ wala kuli m saam san'an ka pʋ dɔl biig la keŋɛ? Da kɛ ka m nini nyɛ bʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ na paae m saam la.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Josef da pʋ lɛn nyaŋi gban'e o mɛŋ o ba'abiis la tuonnɛ, ka o tans ye o nidib la wʋsa yim ka kɛɛ o. Ka sɔ' lɛn ka' dɔɔgin la, ka o zaŋ o mɛŋi pa'ali ba ka ba baŋ on an sɔ'.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Ka Josef kaas hali, ka Egipt nidib nɛ banɛ bɛ Na'ayin la wʋsa wʋm.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Josef yɛl o ba'abiis la ye, “Mam anɛ Josef. M ba' la nan kpɛn vʋeyaa?” Amaa o ba'abiis la zi' ban ye ba lɛbis si'em tis oo, bɔzugɔ dabiem gban'e ba nɛ.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl o ba'abiis la ye, “Paaminɛ m tuon na.” Ka ban paae na la, o yɛli ba ye, “Mam anɛ ya ba'abiig Josef onɛ ka ya da kuosi tis Egipt dim la.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Da kɛ ka li daami ya ka ya sʋnya duod nɛ ya mɛŋ yanamɛ kuos mam tis kpɛla na la yɛla, bɔzugɔ Wina'am nɔk mam dɛŋi ya tuon na ye li faaɛn nidib vʋm.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Yʋma ayi' nwa' ka kɔ'ɔm sig teŋ nwa' zug na, ka li nan kpɛlim yʋma anu ka sɔ' kʋ kua bɛɛ bunɛ.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Amaa Wina'am nɔk mam dɛŋi ya tuon ye yanam nɛ ya yidim nyɛ faangir.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Li ka'anɛ yanamɛ kɛ ka mam bɛ kpɛla, li anɛ Wina'am zug. Onɛ kɛ ka m an wʋʋ Na'ab Faaro ba', ka sʋ'oe o yidim la wʋsa ka gɔsid Egipt teŋ wʋsa.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ zɔmi tɔ'ɔtɔ lɛbi m ba' san'an ka yɛl o ye, ‘Josef onɛ aan fʋ biig la yɛl ye Wina'am kɛ ka m an Egipt teŋ wʋsa zugdaan. Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ na ka da yuugɛ.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Fʋn nɛ fʋ biis, nɛ fʋ yaas nɛ fʋ bʋnkɔnbid nɛ fʋn mɔr si'el wʋsa na bɛ nɛ Gosen teŋin linɛ kpi'e nɛ mam la.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Mam na gɔsi fʋ yɛla, bɔzugɔ yʋma anu banɛ kenna la, kɔ'ɔm la na nan kpɛm bɛ ka fʋn nɛ fʋ yidim wʋsa ba'as yɔri.’”

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: “Yanam wʋsa nɛ m pitʋ Benjamin pʋn baŋ ye li anɛ mam mɛŋi pian'adi tisid ya.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Yɛlimi m ba' la na'asi lin ka m nyɛt Egipt kpɛla la, nɛ yanamɛ nyɛ si'el wʋsa nɛ ya mɛŋ nini, ka mɔri m ba' lɛb tɔ'ɔtɔ na.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Ka o pʋ'ʋs o ba'abiis la wʋsa sʋ'ʋŋa ka kaas pamm, lin nya'aŋ la ka on nɛ o ba'abiis la sɔns nɛ taaba.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Labaari da paae Faaro ye Josef ba'abiis kena la, Faaro nɛ o kpɛɛmnam sʋnf da malis nɛ,

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: ka Faaro yɛl Josef ye, “Yɛlimi fʋ ba'abiis la ye, ‘Lɔɔmini ya la'ad ka maal siri nɛ ya bʋmisi lɛb Keenan teŋin.

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: Ka mɔri ya saam nɛ ya yidim wʋsa lɛb mam san'an na. Mam na tisi ya zin'isʋŋ kpɛla ka ya di malisim teŋin la.’

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Mɛ yɛlimi ba ye ba niŋim anwa: ‘Nɔkimi tɛrekonamɛ lɛbi zii ya biis nɛ ya pu'ab ka dɔlli ya saam la kena.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Da kɛ ka yanamɛ mɔr si'el wʋsa la yɛla paki ya, bɔzugɔ m na tisi ya la'asʋma Egipt kpɛla ka li aan ya mɔrim.’”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Ka Israel biis la sid niŋ ala. Ka Josef nɔk tɛrekonam nɛ ba suorin diib tisi ba nwɛnɛ Faaro yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: O nɔk fuvɛnla tisi ba wʋsa, ka tis Benjamin anzurifa ligidi bɛdegʋ nɛ fuvɛnla zin'is anu.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Ka nɔk Egipt la'asʋma lɔ bʋmis piiga zug ka ba zii keŋ tis o ba' la ka lɛn kɛ ka bʋŋnya'as piiga zi diib ye o saam ya'a ti kena, on dit.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Ka o kɛɛsi ba ye ba kulim, ka yɛli ba ye ba da zab suorinɛ.

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Ka ba yi Egipt teŋin keŋ paae ba saam Jakob san'an, Keenan teŋin.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl o ye, “Josef nan kpɛn vʋe! Onɛ gɔsid Egipt teŋ la wʋsa.” Li da lidigi ba ba' la nɛ ka o pʋ niŋi ba yaddaa.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Amaa ban da yɛl o linɛ wʋsa ka Josef yɛl la, ka o mɛ nyɛ tɛreko banɛ ka ba mɔr na ye ba nɔk o lɛb la, ka o ya'am lɛb na ka o sʋnf kpi'em.

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “Li siakya! M yʋ'ʋn baŋya ye m biig Josef nan kpɛn vʋe. M na dɔlli keŋ nyɛɛ o ka nyaan kpi.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Alazug ka Israel da nɔk on sʋ'oe si'el wʋsa yii keŋ Egipt, ka on paae Beerseba teŋin la, o maal maannɛ tis o ba' Isaak Wina'am.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am pian' tis Jakob zaansʋŋin ka buol o ye, “Jakob, Jakob!” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Naa, manɛ nwa'!”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am yɛl o ye, “Mam anɛ Wina'am onɛ aan fʋ ba' Isaak Wina'am.” Ka lɛn yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem fʋn ken Egipt la zugɔ. M na kɛ ka fʋ buudi an bɛdegʋ anina.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: M na mɔri fʋ keŋ Egipt, ka lɛn mɔri fʋ lɛb na. Ka Josef mɛŋ na gban'af ka fʋ kpi.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Bama an banɛ ka Lea da du'a tis Jakob on da bɛ Padanaram la, paas nɛ o bipuŋ onɛ yʋ'ʋr buon Daina. O biis nɛ o yaas, biribis nɛ bipumis, da anɛ pistan' nɛ atan'.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Ka Faaro ya'a buoli ya bu'os ye, ‘Ya tʋʋma an bɔ?’

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Zilipa da du'a bibama n tis Jakob, onɛ ka Laban nɔk tis o pu'ayua Lea la. Ba wʋsa la'as taaba anɛ pii nɛ ayuobʋ.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Jakob nɛ Biliha onɛ ka Laban nɔki tis o pu'ayua Rakɛl la biis da la'as taaba anɛ ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: Sixty-six members of Jacob's family went to Egypt with him, not counting his daughters-in-law.
translation_verse: Nimbanɛ da an Jakob mɛŋ yaas ka dɔlli ba keŋ Egipt da anɛ pisyuobʋ nɛ ayuobʋ. O bipu'ab kal da pʋ paasɛ.

english_verse: Jacob's two grandsons who were born there made it a total of
translation_verse: Josef biis ayi' banɛ ka ba da du'a Egipt da paas, ka kal la la'as pisyɔpɔi. Josef di'e o saam Jakob Egipt teŋin

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Jakob da dɛŋi tʋm Juda ye o gaad tuonnɛ paae Josef san'an ka o pa'al o Gosen teŋ la suor, ka ba nyaan paae Gosen teŋin la.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Josef da nɔk o tɛreko keŋ Gosen teŋin ye o tʋ'ʋs o ba' Jakob, onɛ yʋ'ʋri lɛm buon Israel la. Ka Josef n da paae o ba' tuon la, o nɔk o nu'usi kuak o ba' la ka kaasi yuug hali.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Ka Israel yɛl Josef ye, “Nannanna m yʋ'ʋn na kpi, bɔzugɔ man nyɛɛf nɛ m nini, ka fʋ kpɛn vʋe la.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl o ba'abiis nɛ o ba' yidim la ye, “M na keŋ pian' tis Faaro ka yɛl o ye m ba'abiis nɛ m ba' yidim banɛ da bɛ Keenan la kena.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
