translation_verse: Ye, nidib la anɛ kɔnbkemnib ka gʋ'ʋn bʋnkɔnbid, ka ba mɔri ba kɔnbid nɛ ba niigi kena nɛ ban mɔr si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: Yanam lɛbisim o ye, ‘Ti gʋ'ʋnnɛ bʋnkɔnbid. Ti saamnam mɛ da gʋ'ʋnnɛ.’ Ya ya'a yɛl o ala, o na kɛ ka ya bɛ Gosen teŋin la.” Josef da bɔɔd ye ba yɛl nwa' tis Na'ab la bɔzugɔ Egipt nidib da kis onɛ gʋ'ʋn wʋsa.

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Ka Faaro bu'os Josef ba'abiis la ye, “Ya nu'ug tʋʋm an bɔ?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Naa! Ti anɛ kɔnbkemnib nwɛnɛ ti saamnamɛ da gʋ'ʋn si'em la.”

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da yɛl ye, “Na'aba, ti kena ye ti bɛ kpɛla saŋa bi'ela, kɔ'ɔm la bɛ Keenan ka ti bʋnkɔnbid kʋ nyɛ yaama la zug. Kɛl ka ti zin'in Gosen teŋin.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Faaro yɛl Josef ye, “Fʋ ba' nɛ fʋ ba'abiis la kɛɛn fʋ san'an na,

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: ka Egipt teŋgbauŋ paalʋ wʋsa bɛɛ fʋ nu'usin. Kɛl ka fʋ ba' nɛ fʋ ba'abiis la zin'in zin'ikanɛ an sʋm la. Kɛl ka ba zin'in Gosen teŋin, ka fʋ ya'a baŋ banɛ mi' bʋnkɔnbid tʋʋma sʋ'ʋŋa, fʋn kɛl ka ba gɔsidi m bʋnkɔnbid la tisim.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Ka Josef mɔr o saam Jakob na pa'al Na'ab Faaro. Ka Jakob da sɔs Wina'am albareka tis Faaro. On da naae la,

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Faaro bu'os o ye, “Fʋ yʋma aan ala?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I have lived only
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛbis ye, “M yʋma anɛ kɔbiga nɛ pistan' (

english_verse: years, and I have had to move from place to place. My parents and my grandparents also had to move from place to place. But they lived much longer, and their life was not as hard as mine.”
translation_verse: ). M giligidnɛ wʋʋ m saamnamɛ da giligid si'em la. M yʋma pʋ zu'oe paae m yaanam yʋma, ka lɛɛ kpi'emi tisim.”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob lɛn niŋ Faaro zug albareka ka nyaan yi.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Ka Josef nɔk o ba' nɛ o ba'abiis la ka ba zin'in zin'ikanɛ an sʋm hali Egipt teŋin. Li da anɛ Rameses sʋ'ʋlimin la nwɛnɛ Faaro pa'al si'em la.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Diibi da ka' la kɛ ka kɔ'ɔm la maligim paasid ka Egipt nɛ Keenan dim wʋsa namisid.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Ka Josef kuos dikanɛ ka ba digil la, ka la'as tɛɛns la ligidi wʋsa nɔki digil Na'ab Faaro yin.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Ka ligidii da pɔ'ɔg Egipt nɛ Keenan dim wʋsa la, Egipt dim wʋsa da kɛn Josef san'an na ka yɛl o ye, “Tisimi ti diib ka ti na kpi kɔ'ɔm! Ti dii ti ligidi la wʋsa naae.”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Josef da yɛli ba ye, “Mɔrini ya niigi la na tiak nɛ diib, yanamɛ ka' ligidi la zug.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Yʋʋm kan la da gaad la, ba da kɛn Josef san'an yʋʋm kanɛ dɔlli li nya'aŋ la na ka yɛl ye, “Ti zugdaana, ti kʋ su'a fɔ; ti ligidi naae nɛ ka bʋnkɔnbid lɛn kae. Ti pʋ mɔr si'ela ya'a kae ti mɛŋ nɛ ti pɔɔd la.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Da kɛ ka ti kpi kɔ'ɔm ka ti teŋ la san'am. Fʋ ya'a na tisi ti diib ka ti di, nɛ bʋmbʋʋda ka ti bʋd, ti na kuosi ti mɛŋ nɛ ti pɔɔd wʋsa tis na'ab la, ka lieb o sankpan'asnam.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Kɔ'ɔm la da mu'oenɛ hali, ka Josef ti ba'asi da' Egipt teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa tis Na'ab Faaro ka teŋ la wʋsa lieb o din,

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: O lɛɛ da pʋ da' maanmaannib la paalʋʋ, bɔzugɔ Faaro da tisid maanmaannib la ligidi ka ba mɔri da'ad diib ka pʋ kuosi ba paalʋ laa.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl nidib la ye, “Gɔsimiya, man sadigim da' yanam nɛ ya pɔɔd wʋsa tis Faaro la, asɛɛ ka ya di'e bʋmbʋʋda nwa' bʋd pɔɔd la.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a ti buni li, yanam pʋdigimi li zin'is anu nɔki yinne tis Faaro. Ka pʋdigir anaasi dinɛ kpɛlim la na an bʋmbʋʋda nɛ diibi tisi ya mɛŋ nɛ ya yidim.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl ye, “Fʋ faaɛn ti bas! Li ya'a tigi fʋ nini, ti na an sankpan'asnam tis Na'ab Faaro.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Ka Josef nɔki li ka li an nɔzi'elʋg hali nɛ zina ye sɔ' ya'a bun zʋʋdi pɛ'ɛl bɔto anu, yinne anɛ Faaro din. Maanmaannib la ma'aa paalʋ ka Faaro da pʋ di'ee.

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da zin'inɛ Egipt teŋ kanɛ buon Gosen sʋ'ʋlim la. Ba da paam kpan'am nɛ diib bɛdegʋ ka mɛ nɔbigi zu'oe hali.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Lin da paae o kum saŋa la, o buol o biig Josef ka yɛl o ye, “Fʋ ya'a nɔŋim, fʋn nɔkimi fʋ nu'ugi si'isi m gbɛr ka li pa'ali fʋ nimmua, ka kaanbi zi'el ye fʋ kʋ mumim Egipt kpɛla. Mumim zin'ikanɛ ka ba mumi m saamnam la.”

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl o ye, “Naa, m ba', m na niŋ ala.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob yɛl o ye, “Pɔɔm!” Ka Josef pɔɔ zi'el. Ka Jakob zaŋ o duori tik ka su'uni o zugʋ pian' Wina'am.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ka lina wʋsa nya'aŋ, ba daa ti yɛl Josef ye, “Fʋ ba' la ka' laafii.” Ka Josef duoe nɔk o biis ayi' la, Manase nɛ Efiram keŋ.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Ka ban da yɛl Jakob ye, “Fʋ biig Josef kena la,” ka o kpɛ'ɛŋ o mɛŋi duoe zin'in.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Jakob da yɛl Josef ye, “Wina'am Onɛ Galis la da nie o mɛŋi tis mam Luz teŋin linɛ bɛ Keenan la, ka tisim albareka,

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: ka yɛlim ye, ‘M na kɛ ka fʋ du'a biis bɛdegʋ ka ya kal zu'oe. M na kɛ ka fʋ paam yaas. Ka mɛ na zaŋ teŋ kaŋa wʋsa tisif ka li liebi fʋ din.’”

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: “Tɔ', fʋ biribis ayi' banɛ ka fʋ du'a Egipt ka man nyaan kena la anɛ mam mɛŋ biis. Ɛɛn, Efiram nɛ Manase na aan m biis, nwɛnɛ Reuben nɛ Simeon n aan m biis si'em la.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Bibanɛ ka fʋ na du'a ba nya'aŋ la na aan fʋ din, amaa ba faar na yinɛ Efiram nɛ Manase san'an na.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Man da yit Paddan teŋin lɛbid na la ka Rakɛl kpi suorin, ka li niŋim sʋnsa'aŋ. Li da pʋ lal nɛ Efirata teŋa. Ka m su'a o, suokanɛ ken Efirata teŋin la .”

english_verse: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Israel nini da pʋ nyɛt sʋ'ʋŋa ka li anɛ on kʋdig la zug. Ka Josef mɔri ba kɛɛn o tuon na, ka o ba' la kuaki ba ka pʋ'ʋsi ba sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Ka Israel yɛl Josef ye, “M da pʋ baŋ ye m na lɛn nyɛɛ fʋ nindaa ya'asa. Ka Wina'am siak ka m nyɛ fʋ biis gba!”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Ka Josef yʋ'ʋn vɛ'ɛg biis la zin' o saam nɔba zug ka igin o tuonnɛ vanbin teŋin.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Ka Josef nɔk biis ayi' la, ka Efiram bɛɛ o datiuŋ ka lɛɛ bɛɛ o saam Israel dagɔbʋg, ka Manase bɛɛ o dagɔbʋg ka lɛɛ bɛ Israel datiuŋ, ka mɔri ba ala li'el o ba' san'an na.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Amaa Israel nɔk o datiuŋ nu'ugʋ pa'al Efiram zug, la'an nɛ on an biig la; ka mɛ nɔk o dagɔbʋg nu'ugʋ lɔbi puugi pa'al Manase zug, la'an nɛ Manase an kpɛɛm la.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Ka o niŋ Josef albareka ka yɛl ye, “Wina'am onɛ ka m yaab Abraham nɛ m saam Isaak da dɔl la, Wina'am onɛ aan m kɔnbkem ka gurim hali ti paae zina la,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: ka kɛ ka o maliak kanɛ yis mam san'auŋʋn la, na niŋ biis nwa' zug bareka. Bama zug ka nidib na tiɛn m yʋ'ʋr, nɛ m yaab Abraham nɛ m saam Isaak yʋda. Ka mɛ kɛ ka ba nɔbig hali pɛ'ɛl teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Josef n nyɛ ka o ba' la nɔk o datiuŋ nu'ug la pa'al Efiram zug la, li da pʋ malis oo, ka o nɔk o ba' la nu'ug la ye o yis Efiram zugin la pa'al Manase zugin.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl o ba' ye, “Ayei m ba', kpɛɛm nwa'! Nɔkimi fʋ datiuŋʋ pa'al o zug!”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o ba' la yɛl o ye, “Mam mi', m biiga, m mi'. On mɛ na mɔr nidib ka lieb bɛdegʋ, amaa Efiram na gaad Manase, bɔzugɔ Efiram yaas na lieb buudi bɛdegʋ gaad o.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛli ba ye, “Saŋa na kena ka Israel nidib ya'a sɔs Wina'am albareka, ba na sɔsidi tisid taaba ka yɛt ye, ‘M sɔsid Wina'am ye o tisif albareka nwɛnɛ on da tis Efiram nɛ Manase albareka si'em la!’” Ala ka Jakob nɔk Efiram yʋ'ʋri niŋ tuon ka li pa'al ye onɛ gaad Manase.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Ka li nya'aŋ ka Jakob yɛl Josef ye, “M kʋ lɛn vʋe yuugɛ, amaa Wina'am na bɛ nɛf ka mɔri fʋ lɛbi fʋ yaanam teŋin.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Jakob da buol o biis la ka yɛli ba ye la'asimi na ka m yɛli ya yanamɛ na ti an si'em saŋa linɛ kenna la.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: Jakob biisɛ, la'asimi na ka kɛlisi; kɛlisimini ya ba' Israel, pian'ad!

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: Reuben, fʋnɛ aan m bikpɛɛm, fʋnɛ aan m kpi'euŋ nɛ onɛ ka m pɔnsi du'a. Fʋ anɛ onɛ mɔr girima nɛ paŋ.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Fʋ pʋ gban'adi fʋ mɛŋ sʋ'ʋŋa ka nwɛnɛ ku'okanɛ yɛŋim nɛ. Fʋ gbɛn nɛ mam pu'a san'ami m gadʋg. Linzug fʋ kʋ lɛn an girima sɔba.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simeon nɛ Levi anɛ mabiis nɛ taaba, ba lɛɛ mɔri ba zaba la'adi tʋ'ʋsid nidib.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: M kʋ zaŋi m nu'ugʋ kpɛn'ɛsi ba yɛla nii. M mɛ kʋ la'as nɛ baa, bɔzugɔ ba sʋnya da duoe ya ka ba kʋ nidib, ka kɛns lɔlis gada ka li ka' gbinnɛ.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: M nɔpɔɔr bɛɛ ba zug, ba sʋnya zabid hali ka pʋ ya'asid duor la zug. Ba sʋnkanɛ ɛɛnti duoe ka ba bɔɔd ninkʋʋsim la. M na widigi ba Jakob buudi ni bas ka widigi ba yaas Israel buudi la ni.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: “Juda, fʋ ba'abiis la na wɔ'ɔgif, ba na vanbini fʋ tuon fʋn na nyaŋidi fʋ dataas la zug.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Juda, fʋ anɛ gbigimbil onɛ kʋʋdi o ni'im ka lɛbid o gbɛɛnsigin. Fʋ anɛ ninzɔtir wʋʋ gbigim kʋdig nɛ ka sɔ' kʋ daami fɔ.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: O na nɔk o bʋŋʋ lɔ vain tiig, ka nɔk o bʋŋbili lɔ tikanɛ willi wal pamm. Daam na bug wʋʋ ku'om nɛ ka o mɔri pied fuud, tiwala daam na buk wʋʋ ku'om nɛ.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Fʋ nini na mu'oe gaad daam, ka fʋ nyina pɛligi gaad bin'isim.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Zebulun, fʋ na bɛ nɛ ku'om nɔɔrin ka tʋm anrima tʋʋma. Ka fʋ teŋ titɔndig na yaligi keŋ hali paae Sidon teŋin sa.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isaka, fʋ nwɛnɛ bʋŋ kanɛ mɔr paŋ nɛ, fʋ na tʋm ka pʋ gɛɛnda.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Fʋ na nwɛnɛ waafʋ dig suorin, ka na dum wief nɔbir, ka kɛ ka onɛ ban'ad o la lɛb nya'aŋi lu.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: “M Zugsɔba, mam gu'usidnɛ bɔɔdi fʋ faangir la.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: “Gad, nidib bɛdegʋ na zabi nyaŋif, amaa fʋn mɛ na tuligi zab nɛ ba wʋsa.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Aser, fʋ na mɔr disʋma ka na tis na'ab la dikanɛ sʋm nɛ o.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: Naftali, fʋ na nwɛnɛ walig kanɛ mɔr yɔlisim, ka du'ad bivɛnla hali.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: Josef, fʋ na nwɛnɛ tikanɛ bɛ ku'om nɔɔrin nɛ, ka wan walsʋma ka zaŋguom na gu' fʋ lɛbis.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Fʋ dataas zabid nɛf nɛ sʋnpɛɛn, ka dɔllif nɛ tiraad nɛ piema.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ kpɛn zi'enɛ kiŋ-kiŋ nɛ fʋ tiraug ka tʋ'ʋsidi zabidi ba nyaŋid, ka li anɛ Jakob Wina'am la zug, onɛ aan fʋ Kɔnbkem onɛ an Israel Tampiing la.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Fʋ saamnam Wina'am la na sʋ'ʋŋif, Wina'am Onɛ Galis la na niŋi fʋ zug bareka. O na tisif albareka linɛ an saa nɛ teŋin albareka linɛ an ma'asim nɛ kʋ'ʋlʋm, albareka linɛ an du'am nɛ biis nɛ bʋnkɔnbid bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Ɛɛn, fʋ saam albareka zu'oe gaad zʋʋd linɛ yit zuoya nɛ kʋkʋna banɛ da dɛŋin bɛ kʋdimin sa la ni. Albareka nwa' wʋsa na bɛ Josef zugin, on an tuongati o ba'abiisin la zug.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Benjamin, fʋ na nwɛnɛ zaŋku'ar kanɛ an bʋnzɔtire, kʋʋdi fʋ bi'emnam bɛogʋn nɛ zaam.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Bama an Israel dɔɔd pii nɛ ayi' la, ka ba saam Jakob da niŋ albareka niŋi ba yinne-yinne zug. O da tis sɔ' mɛkama o albareka linɛ nar nɛ o. Jakob kum yɛla

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Hitti nidib la san'an ka ba da da' pɔɔg nɛ li tampinlɛuŋ la. Mummi mam anina.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Jakob n da pa'ali ba on bɔɔd si'em naae la o da lɛbi digin ka kpɛm bas o mɛŋ.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Ka Josef luu bibig o ba' la ka kaas hali.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Ka sʋnsa'aŋ la nya'aŋ ka Josef yɛl na'ayikpɛm la ye, “Nɔkimi labakaŋa keŋ tis Na'ab la:

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: ‘M ba' la daa bɔɔd ye o kpi la, o daa kɛ ka m pɔ nɔɔr ye m na ti mum o yakanɛ ka o maali digil Keenan teŋin la. Dinzug kɛl ka m keŋ mumi m ba' la ka lɛb na.’”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro yɛl ye, “Kem mumi fʋ ba' la nwɛnɛ fʋn daa pɔ nɔɔr ye fʋ na niŋ si'em la.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Ban da paae Atad zieŋin linɛ bɛ Joodan kɔldaug nya'aŋ la, ba kpɛn' nɛ kukuma hali yuug. Ka Josef zaŋ daba ayɔpɔi kaas o saam kʋʋr nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Keenan dim la nyɛ ka nidib la maan sʋnsa'aŋ Atad zieŋin la, ba yɛl ye, “Gɔsimi, Egipt nidib la maan sʋnsa'aŋ si'em!” Lin ka ba buon zin'ig la ye Abɛl-Miziram.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Jakob biis la da maal nwɛnɛ on da pʋn yɛli ba si'em la

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: ka zaŋ o niŋgbiŋ la mɔri keŋ mum yaʋg kanɛ bɛ Makipiela pʋʋgin, Mamir nya'aŋ, paalʋ kanɛ ka Abraham da da' Efiron onɛ an Hitti dau san'an ye ba mummi ba kum anina la.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Josef n da mum o ba' la naae la, on nɛ o ba'abiis nɛ banɛ da dɔl o keŋi maal kʋʋr la da lɛb Egipt teŋin. Josef n kpɛmis o ba'abiis la sʋnya si'em

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Ba ba' la kum nya'aŋ la ka Josef ba'abiis la yɛl taaba ye, “Ka Josef ya'a nan kpɛn kisi ti ka bɔ suoya ye o lɛbisi ti bɛ'ɛd wʋʋ tinamɛ da maal o si'em la?”

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ‘Dimi fʋ bieya la suguru! Baa ban tʋmif bɛ'ɛd la, asɛɛ ka fʋ kɛɛ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi bas.’ Ti anɛ fʋ ba' la Wina'am yammis, dimi ti suguru!” Josef n da di'e labakaŋa la, o da kumya hali.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: O ba'abiis la da kena vanbin o tuon, ka yɛl o ye, “Tinamɛ nwa' fʋ tuon ka an fʋ sankpan'asnam.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛli ba ye, “Da zɔti dabiem, m kʋ nyaŋi nɔki m mɛŋi zi'el Wina'am zin'iginɛ.

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Yanam da gban'e nɛ bɛ'ɛd mam yɛla, amaa ka Wina'am lɛbigi li sʋm, ye li sʋŋ nidib bɛdegʋ, ka faaɛn ba yis kumin wʋʋ lin an si'em zina la.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Si'el kae ka ya na zɔt dabiem. Mam na gɔsi ya nɛ ya biis sʋ'ʋŋa.” Ka o pian' pian'asʋma tisi ba ka ba lɛbi kul nɛ sumalisim. Josef kum yɛla

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Josef nɛ o ba'abiis la da nan kpɛm bɛ nɛ Egipt teŋin. O da anɛ yʋma kɔbiga nɛ piiga (

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: O da vʋe yuug ka da nyɛ Efiram yaan-tan', ka da lɛn di'e Manase biig Makir biis la o nu'usin.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Ka yɛl o ba'abiis la ye, “M bɔɔd ye m kpinɛ, amaa Wina'am na ba'asi gɔsi ya sʋ'ʋŋa ka mɔri ya yi teŋ kaŋa ni ka ya kpɛn' teŋ kanɛ ka o da pɔ nɔɔri tis Abraham nɛ Isaak nɛ Jakob ye o na tisi ba la.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Ka Josef yɛl o nidib ye, “Pɔɔm tisi nɛ m ye Wina'am ya'a mɔri yaa lɛbi ya teŋin la ya na mɔri m niŋgbiŋ la keŋ.”

english_verse: So Joseph died in Egypt at the age of
translation_verse: Ka Josef n da paae yʋma kɔbiga nɛ piiga (

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Israel nidib da nɔbigid hali nɛ du'am pʋʋgin, ka mɔr paŋ ka zu'oe pɛ'ɛl teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Ka na'apaalig onɛ zi' Josef yɛla da di na'am Egipt teŋin.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: O da yɛl o nidib la ye, “Gɔsimiya, Israel dim la nɔbigidnɛ galisi gaadi ti.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛlli ka ti bɔ suoya namisi ba ka ba da nɔbigi gaadi tii. Ya'a ka' ala, zaba ya'a duoe, ba na la'as nɛ ti dataas la zab nɛ ti ka zɔɔ yi ti teŋin la.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Ka ba gaans tʋʋma zugdaannam ye ba gur Israel dim la ka kɛ ka ba tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema. Nimbama da kɛ ka Israel dim la mɛ tempʋbanɛ an Pittom nɛ Rameses ka li an na'ab la la'ad digilʋg zin'is ka Egipt dim nɔkidi ba la'adi niŋid ani.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Amaa la'an nɛ ban da maan si'em bɔɔd ye ba kal sie la, ba da nan kpɛn nɔbigidnɛ. Ka ba zɔt Israel dim la dabiem.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Ba da kɛ ka Israel dim la bɛllim tɔi hali ka ba nwɛ'ɛd tampiga ka tʋm pɔɔd tʋʋm kpi'ema bɛdegʋ dinɛ ka' na'anaa.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Egipt Na'ab la da buol Hibiru pu'adu'asnam banɛ yʋda an Sifra nɛ Pua la, yɛli ba ye,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Ya ya'a du'asid Hibiru pu'ab la ka nyɛ ka biig la an biribiŋ, yanam kʋʋm o; amaa o ya'a an bipuŋ, yanam da kʋʋ oo.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Amaa pu'adu'asnam la da zɔt Wina'am dabiem ka pʋ tʋm wʋʋ Egipt na'ab la yɛl si'em laa, ka bas biribis la.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Ka Egipt Na'ab la buol pu'adu'asnam la ka yɛli ba ye, “Bɔɔ nwa' ka ya tʋm? Ya niŋ wala bas biribis la ka pʋ kʋʋ ba?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Ka pu'adu'asnam la yɛl na'ab Faaro ye, “Hibiru pu'ab la pʋ nwɛnɛ Egipt pu'ab laa. Ba du'am pʋ tɔiya, ka tinamɛ ti ye ti baŋ la ka ba pʋn du'a sa.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Pu'adu'asnam la zɔt Wina'am dabiem la zug ka o kɛ ka ba zak yalig.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro yɛl o nidib la ye, “Bikanɛ wʋsa ka ba du'a o ka o an biribiŋ, yanam nɔkim o lɔb kɔldaugin, amaa o ya'a anɛ bipuŋ yanam basim o.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Levi dau di Levi dɔɔg pu'asadir

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: ka o pu'a la nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ. Ka on nyɛ ka o an vɛnliŋ la, o da nɔk o su'a nwadis atan'.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Amaa on da gɔs ka o kʋ lɛn nyaŋi su'a biig la, o da nɔk nɛ pɛog, ka nɔk kotaali bʋligi li. Ka nɔk biig la niŋ pɛog la pʋʋgin ka keŋ digil o Nail mu'ar nɔɔrin mɔɔd sʋʋgin.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Ka biig la taʋn zi'e lalli ka gɔsid dinɛ na maal o.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro bipuŋ sɔ' da sig mu'arin la ye o sʋ, ka banɛ gɔsid na'abiig la dɔl o dɛn'ɛnid mu'ar la nɔɔr. Ka o nyɛ ka pɛog bɛ mɔɔdin la ka o tʋm pu'asada banɛ gɔsid o la yinne ye o nɔk na.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'abiig la pibigi li ka nyɛ bilia ka o kaasid, ka o zɔ biig la nimbaanlig, ka yɛl ye, “Bikaŋa anɛ Hibiru dim biig yinne.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Ka biig la taʋn bu'os Na'ab Faaro bipuŋ la ye, “M keŋ bɔ Hibiru dim pu'ab la yinne na ka o ugus biig la tisi fɔɔ?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Ɛɛn, kem!” Ka biig la keŋ mɔr bilia la ma na.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Ka Faaro bipuŋ la yɛl o ye o nɔkim biig la ugusi tis o, ka o na yɔɔ o. Ka pu'a la nɔk biig la ugus o.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Ka biig la nɔbig, ka o mɔr o keŋ tis Na'ab Faaro bipuŋ la ka o lieb o biig. Ka o pʋd biig la yʋ'ʋr ye Moses. Moses zɔɔ keŋ Midian teŋin

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Moses n da nɔbig la, daar yinne ka o yii keŋ o nidibin la ka nyɛ ban namisidi ba si'em ba tʋʋma ni la. Ka mɛ nyɛ Egipt nid ka o bʋ'ʋd Hibiru dau sɔ' onɛ an Moses nidib la yinne.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Ka o gɔsi gɔs ka pʋ nyɛ sɔ' anina babaa, ka o nwɛ' Egipt nid la kʋʋ mum titanbin'isi ni.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Ka li yimbɛog ka o lɛn yi ka nyɛ ka Hibiru nidib ayi' zabid nɛ taaba ka o bu'os onɛ tʋm taal la ye, “Bɔɔ maal ka fʋ nwɛ'ɛdi fʋ mabiig onɛ an Hibiru nida?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Ka dau la yɛl o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ gaŋif ye fʋ an sariakat tinam sʋʋginɛ? Fʋ bɔɔd ye fʋ kʋ mam wʋʋ fʋn sa kʋ Egipt nid si'em laa?” Anina ka Moses ya'am iank ka o tɛn'ɛs ye, “Mam sa tʋm si'el la, nidib baŋ ya!”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro wʋm ka bɔɔd ye o kʋ Moses ka o baŋ ka zɔɔ yi Faaro san'an keŋ bɛ Midian teŋin zin' kpi'e nɛ bulig.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ka maanmaan sɔ' bɛ Midian teŋin ka mɔr pu'ayuos ayɔpɔi, ka ba keŋ buligin la ye ba wik ku'om tisi ba saam kɔnbid.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Ka kɔnbkem sieba kena kadi ba, amaa ka Moses sʋŋi ba ka ba paam ku'om nulis kɔnbid la.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Ka pu'asada la lɛbi ba saam san'an ka pʋ yuug la, ka o bu'osi ba ye, “Bɔɔ maal ka ya pʋ yuug zina?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Egipt dau sɔ' sʋŋi ti ka kɔnbkemnib la pʋ daami tii. O la'am wik nɛ ku'om la sʋŋi ti ka ti nulis kɔnbid la.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ka o bu'osi ba ye, “Ka o bɛ yaanɛ? Ka bɔ ka ya bas o ani? Kem buol o nɛ o na ka o paam si'eli di.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Ka Moses siak ye o na bɛ dau la yin; ka dau la nɔk o bipuŋ Zippora tis Moses ka o lieb o pu'a.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Ka Zippora du'a biribiŋ ka Moses pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye, Gersom, ka li pa'al ye, “M anɛ saan teŋzʋŋin.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Li da yuug ya hali ka Egipt Na'ab Faaro kpi. Ka Israel dim la paam namisʋg hali, ka kaasidi bɔɔd sʋŋir, bɔzugɔ ba da anɛ sankpan'asnam teŋ la ni, ka ba kaasig la paae Wina'am san'an.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am wʋmi ba kaasig, ka tiɛn on da kaanbi zi'el Abraham nɛ Isaak nɛ Jakob la.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am gɔs Israel dim la ka zɔɔ ba nimbaanlig.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Moses da kemnɛ o diem Jetro kɔnbid. Jetro da anɛ Midian maanmaan. O da kem kɔnbid la lalig hali keŋ paae Wina'am zuor linɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Horeb la.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Anina ka o nyɛ Wina'am maliak ka o nie o mɛŋ bugumini bɛ tituugin. Ka Moses nyɛ ka bugum la bɛ tituugin la dit ka li pʋ kanbida.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Ka Moses tɛn'ɛs ye, “M na keŋ gɔs nyalim kanɛ kɛ ka bugum bɛ tituugin dit ka li pʋ kanbid la.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la nyɛ ka o kenna ye o gɔs la, ka Wina'am buol tituugin la ye, “Moses, Moses!” Ka Moses siak ye, “Manɛ nwa'.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am ye, “Da li'el naa! Pidigimi fʋ ta'ada la, ka zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ zi'e la anɛ kasi.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “Manɛ aan fʋ yaanam Wina'am la, m anɛ Abraham Wina'am, nɛ Isaak Wina'am, nɛ Jakob Wina'am.” Ani ka Moses su'a o nindaa bɔzugɔ o da zɔtnɛ on na kpa' gɔs Wina'am.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “M sid nyɛɛm nidib la namisid Egipt si'em. M wʋmi ba kaasig ban namisidi ba la zug ka li yɛla daamim.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: M kena ye m faaɛn ba yi Egipt dim nu'usin mɔri ba keŋ teŋ kanɛ yalim, ka an sʋm, ka bin'isim nɛ siind pʋbid la. Teŋ kan ka Keenan dim nɛ Hitti dim nɛ Amor dim nɛ Perizi dim nɛ Hivi dim nɛ Jebus dim bɛ la.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Israel dim la fabʋlʋg paae mam na ka mam mɛ nyɛ Egipt dim la maannɛ ba si'em.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, kem ka m tʋmif nɛ Faaro san'an ye fʋ mɔr Israel dim la yi Egipt teŋin na.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Moses bu'os Wina'am ye, “Ka mam mɛ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ na keŋ Na'ab Faaro san'anɛ yis Israel dim la Egipt teŋinɛ?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am ye, “Man na bɛ nɛf. Ka lina na an zanbin ye manɛ tʋmif. Fʋ ya'a mɔri ba yina ya na pʋ'ʋs mam Wina'am zuokaŋa ni.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Ka Moses bu'os Wina'am ye, “Ka m ya'a keŋ yɛl Israel dim la ye, ‘Ya yaanam Wina'am la tʋm mam ya san'an na,’ ka ba bu'osim ye, ‘O yʋ'ʋrɛ?’ M ye m lɛbisi ba ye anɔ'ɔnɛ?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am lɛn yɛl Moses ye, “Yɛlim Israel dim la ye, Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba yaab Abraham Wina'am, nɛ Isaak Wina'am nɛ Jakob Wina'am la tʋmi mɛ ya san'an na. M yʋ'ʋkaŋa ye li bɛ nɛ saŋa wʋsa, ka zʋmaana wʋsa na zaŋi li ka tɛnri m yɛla saŋa linɛ ka' naarɛ.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kem la'as Israel kpɛɛmnam la, ka yɛli ba ye Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya yaanam Wina'am, Abraham Wina'am nɛ Isaak Wina'am nɛ Jakob Wina'am la, nie o mɛŋi pa'alif ka yɛlif ye o nyɛ Egipt dim la maannɛ ba si'em.

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: M kaanb ya ye, ‘M na mɔri ya yi namiskanɛ ka ya nyɛt Egipt teŋin la keŋ teŋ kanɛ ka Keenan dim nɛ Hitti dim nɛ Amor dim nɛ Perizi dim nɛ Hivi dim nɛ Jebus dim bɛ, ka bin'isim nɛ siind pʋbid la ni.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a ti tu'as ala, Israel kpɛɛmnam la na wʋm tisif, ka fʋn nɛ ban na keŋ Egipt na'ab Faaro san'an yɛl o ye, ‘Zugsɔb onɛ an Hibiru dim Wina'am la, yɛli ti ye ti nɔk daba atan' keŋ mɔɔgin maal malʋŋʋ tis on Zugsɔb Wina'am.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Amaa mam mi' ye Egipt na'ab la kʋ bas suor ka ya keŋi, asɛɛ ka si'el maal ka o nyɛ.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Ka m na tiɛn m nu'ug ka dam Egipt dim la nɛ nyalima banɛ ka m ye m tʋmmi ya san'an la; ka li nya'aŋ ka o na basi ya ka ya keŋ.

english_verse: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka Egipt dim gɔsi ya sʋ'ʋŋa, ka ya ya'a ti yi teŋin la m kʋ kɛ ka ya yinɛ nu'uzaalisɛ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Ya pu'a wʋsa na yɛl o kpi'a nɛ onɛ bɛɛ o yin wʋsa ka o na tis o anzurifa nɛ sanlima nɛ fuud; ka ya na zaŋi ziili o ya biribis nɛ ya bipumisi keŋ. Ala ka ya na paam la'ad Egipt dim la san'an.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Ka Moses lɛbis ye, “Ka ba ya'a pʋ siak bɛɛ kɛlisim pian'adɛ ka yɛl ye, ‘Zugsɔb la pʋ nie pa'ali ma?’”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Bɔɔ bɛɛ fʋ nu'ugin la?” Ka o ye, “Dansaar.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la ye, “Nɔkim bas teŋin!” Ka Moses nɔki bas teŋin, ka li kilim waaf ka o zɔ ka bas waaf la.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, “Nɔkimi fʋ nu'ugi gban'e o zʋʋr!” Ka Moses gban'e waaf la zʋʋr ka o lɛn kilim dansaar o nu'ugin.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la ye, “Ala ka ba na baŋ ka niŋ yadda ye man Zugsɔb, onɛ aan ba yaab Abraham nɛ Isaak nɛ Jakob Wina'am la nie o mɛŋi pa'alif.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb lɛn yɛl Moses ye, “Nɔkimi fʋ nu'ugʋ su gɛfa ni!” Ka Moses nɔki su, ka on yis na la, ka li nwa' kʋkɔm.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn yɛl o ye, “Lɛn nɔki fʋ nu'ug la su!” Ka Moses lɛn nɔk nu'ug la su, ka on yis na la, ka li lɛbi an wʋʋ o niŋgbina la an si'em la.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Amaa ba ya'a pʋ niŋ nwa' wʋsa yaddaa, fʋn kabigim ku'om Nail mu'arin la bu'oe bas teŋ kpi'emisin, ka ku'om la na kilim ziim teŋin la.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Ka Moses yɛl Zugsɔb la ye, “M Zugsɔba, kɛlisima! M biilimin sa man zi' pian'adɛ, hali la'an nɛ fʋn pian' tis man onɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la, m nɔɔr pʋ lakid sʋ'ʋŋaa.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ tis ninsaal nɔɔrɛ? Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ kɛt ka o an tʋbkpida bɛɛ gika? Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ tis o nini bɛɛ kɛt ka o an zʋnzɔŋa? Li ka'anɛ mam Zugsɔb laa?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, kem ka m na sʋ'ʋŋif ka fʋ pian', ka pa'alif fʋn na yɛl si'el.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Moses lɛbis ye, “M Zugsɔba, m bɛlimnɛ, tʋm sɔ' ka o tʋm tʋʋma la tisif.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb sʋʋnr duoe nɛ Moses, ka o ye, “Ka fʋ bier Aaron, onɛ an Levi Dɔɔg nid la? M mi' ye on mi' pian'ad sʋ'ʋŋa. Hali o bɛ suori kenna ye o tʋ'ʋsif. O ya'a nyɛɛf, o sʋnf na ma'ae.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: O na pian' tis nidib la tisif. Ka na aan fʋ nɔdi'es, ka li nwɛnɛ fʋnɛ an Wina'am tis o.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Mɔr dansaar la fʋ nu'ugin ka zaŋi li tʋm nyalima tʋʋma.” Moses n lɛb Egipt la yɛla

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Ka Moses lɛbi yɛl o diem Jetro ye, “Kɛl ka m lɛb Egipt n kaae m nidib la gɔs ye ba nan kpɛn vʋe bɛɛ?” Ka Jetro ye, “Kem, ka fʋ na paae sʋ'ʋŋa!”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Moses da bɛ Midian la, Zugsɔb da yɛl o ye, “Lɛm Egipt ka dap banɛ wʋsa da bɔɔd ye ba kʋʋf la kpiya.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɔk o pu'a nɛ o biisi ban'al bʋŋ zug, ka ba gban'e suori lɛbid Egipt; ka Wina'am dansaar la bɛɛ o nu'ugin.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye, “Fʋ ya'a paae Egipt, fʋn kpɛ'ɛŋi fʋ mɛŋ ka tʋm nyalim banɛ ka m ye fʋ tʋm la Na'ab Faaro san'an, amaa m na digilimi o sʋnf ka o kʋ kɛ ka nidib la yii.”

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Yɛlim Na'ab Faaro ye Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Israel anɛ m bikpɛɛm.”

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Ka m yɛtif ye, “Kɛl ka m bikpɛɛm la keŋ ka wɔ'ɔgim. Amaa fʋ zan'as nɛ ye o kʋ keŋɛ; dinzugɔ m na kʋʋ fʋ mɛŋ bikpɛɛm.”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Moses da kunna ka gbɛn zin'isi'a ka Zugsɔb la kena bɔɔd ye o kʋʋ o.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Zippora nɔk barigi kpɛn'ɛs o biribiŋ la baŋʋ, ka nɔk on nwaae si'el la keŋi si'is Moses nɔba ka yɛl o ye, “Fʋn aan m sid la zug ka zikaŋa yit!”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb bas Moses; ka pu'a la yɛl ye, “Fʋn aan m sid la zug ka ziim yit!” Ka li pa'al baŋʋ kpɛn'ɛb yɛla.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Aaron ye o kem mɔɔgin la tʋ'ʋs Moses. Ka o keŋ sia'al Moses Wina'am zuorin la, ka pʋ'ʋs o.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Ka Moses yɛl Aaron dinɛ wʋsa ka Zugsɔb tʋm o ye o keŋ yɛl, nɛ nyalim banɛ ka o ye o maal la.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɛ Aaron buol Israel kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: ka Aaron yɛli ba dinɛ ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses la wʋsa. Ka Moses maal nyalima la ka nidib la nyɛ,

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: ka niŋ yadda. Ka ban wʋm ye Zugsɔb la nyɛɛ ba namisʋg ka tiɛn ba yɛla ye o sʋŋi ba la, ba igini tis o girima.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka Moses nɛ Aaron keŋ yɛl Na'ab Faaro ye, “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, ‘Kɛl ka m nidib la keŋ maal malʋŋʋ tisim sian'anr sʋʋgin.’”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ an Zugsɔb la ka li kpa' tilas ye m wʋm tis o ka kɛ ka Israel dim keŋɛ? M zi' Zugsɔb la, ka mɛ kʋ kɛ ka Israel keŋɛ.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl ye, “Hibiru dim Wina'am la yɛl ye ti nɔkim daba atan' keŋ mɔɔgin maal malʋŋʋ tis on Zugsɔb Wina'am, ka ya'a ka' ala o na kɛ ka wiim li na bɛɛ kɛ ka ti kpi tanpin.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro lɛn yɛl ye, “Gɔsima, nidib la ka' bɛn teŋ nwa' pʋʋginɛ, ka fʋ yɛl ye ba basim tʋʋmaa?”

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Da lɛn tisid nidib la la'abanɛ ka ba mɔri maan tampiga la; kɛlli ka ba mɛŋ keŋ bɔɔ ba la'ad.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Amaa kɛl ka ba maal wʋʋ ban daa maan si'em la, da sie tampigbanɛ ka ba maan la kallɛ; ba anɛ gbanya'anam dinɛ kɛ ka ba fabin ka ye ban keŋ maal malʋŋʋ tisi ba Wina'am la.

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka tʋʋma la kpi'em tis dap la, ka ba na bɛɛ anina tʋm ka kʋ kɛlis ziri pian'adɛ.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Ka banɛ gɔsid tʋmtʋmnib la yɛl nidib la ye, “Na'ab Faaro yɛl si'eli nwa':

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: ‘M kʋ lɛn tisi ya la'abanɛ ka ya mɔri maan tampiga laa. Kem bɔɔe la'ad la zin'ikanɛ ka ya na nyɛ, amaa tʋʋma la pʋ ye li bu'oe baa bi'elaa.’”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Ka nidib la widig Egipt zin'ig wʋsa ieed la'ad la ye ba tʋm.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Nimbanɛ gɔsid tʋʋma la da mugusid nidib la ye, “Naami tʋʋma la daar wʋsa wʋʋ tinamɛ daa tisidi ya la'ad ka ya tʋm si'em la!”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ba da bʋ'ʋd Israel tʋmtʋmnib tuongatib la ka yɛt ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka ya pʋ tʋm ka li paae dabisbanɛ gaad la?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Israel nimbanɛ gaad tuonnɛ gɔsid tʋʋma la da keŋ fabili tis Na'ab Faaro ye, “Naa! Bɔɔ kɛ ka fʋ namisidi ti anwana?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Tinam pʋ paam la'abanɛ na maal tampiga laa, ka ba ye ti maalim tampiga ka bʋ'ʋdi ti, amaa li yinɛ fʋ mɛŋ nidib la san'an na.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro lɛbis ye, “Ya anɛ gbanya'anam! Ya'a ka' ala ya naan kʋ yɛlin ye m kɛl ka ya yi Egipt teŋinɛ keŋ maal malʋŋʋ tisi ya Zugsɔba.

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Lɛm mɛɛi! Ba pʋ ye ba tisi ya la'ad la, amaa la'an nɛ wala bɔɔmi la'ad la tʋm wʋʋ yanamɛ daa tʋm si'em la.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Na'ab Faaro n zan'as la, Israel tʋʋma tuongatib la baŋ ye ba bɛ nɛ yɛla ni.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Ka ban yi Na'ab Faaro yin la ba nyɛ ka Moses nɛ Aaron guri ba yiŋ,

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: ka tʋmtʋmnib tuongatib la yɛl Moses nɛ Aaron ye, “Zugsɔb na kadi ya sariabɛ'og! Yanamɛ zaŋ tinamɛ tugul Na'ab Faaro nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la! Ya tisi ba sʋ'ʋg ye ba kʋʋ ti.”

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Ka Moses lɛb Zugsɔb la san'an ka yɛl ye, “M Zugsɔba, bɔ ka fʋ basi fʋ nidib ka ba namisida? Ka bɔzugʋ kɛ ka fʋ tʋmim na?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Din yi daakanɛ ka m yɛl Na'ab Faaro labaar la, hali ti paae zina, o sʋʋnr pɛlig nɛ fʋ nidib la nɛ hali galis, ka fʋ nam pʋ maal si'eli pa'al ye fʋ na yisi baa.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye, “Nannanna fʋ na nyɛ mam na maal Faaro si'em. Mam mɔr paŋ tita'ar la zug, o na kɛ ka ba yi, asida mam mɔr paŋ tita'ar la zug, o na kadi ba yis o teŋin la.”

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am lɛn yɛl Moses ye, “Manɛ an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: M da nɔki m mɛŋi pa'al Abraham, nɛ Isaak, nɛ Jakob ye manɛ an Wina'am Onɛ Galis la, amaa m daa pʋ nie m yʋ'ʋr kanɛ buon ‘Zugsɔb’ la pa'ali baa.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: M lɛn kaanb ye m na tisi ba Keenan teŋ la, teŋ kanɛ ka ba da bɛ ka an saam la.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: M mɛ lɛn wʋm Israel dim banɛ ka Egipt dim namisidi ba la fabʋlʋg, ka tiɛn man da maal nɔnaar nɛ ba la yɛla.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, yɛlim Israel dim la ye, ‘Manɛ an Zugsɔb la, ka m na mɔri ya yis Egipt dim namisʋg pʋʋgin.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: M na nɔki ya ka ya aan m mɛŋ nidib, ka m na aan ya Wina'am; ka ya na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ mɔri ya yi Egipt dim namisʋgʋn la.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: M na mɔri ya keŋ teŋ kanɛ ka m kaanbi tis Abraham, nɛ Isaak, nɛ Jakob la, ka nɔki tisi ya ka li aan ya bʋn. Manɛ an Zugsɔb la.’”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Ka Moses pian' ala tis Israel dim la, ka ba pʋ siak Moses nɔɔrɛ, bɔzugɔ ba sʋnf da digilimnɛ ba tʋʋm kpi'ema la zug.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb pian' tis Moses ye,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Kem yɛl Egipt Na'ab Faaro ye o kɛ ka Israel dim la yii o teŋin la!”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ka Moses yɛl Zugsɔb ye, “Israel dim la ya'a pʋ siak mam nɔɔrɛ, Na'ab Faaro na niŋ wala wʋm tisi ma, ka m mɛ pʋ tun'e pian'ad la?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb pian' tis Moses nɛ Aaron ye, “M bɔɔd ye ya mɔr Israel dim la yi Egipt teŋin la. Kem yɛli Israel dim nɛ Egipt Na'ab Faaro nɛ'ɛŋa.” Moses tuŋ yɛla

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Banɛ da an Israel dim dɔɔd kpɛɛmnam la yʋda nwa': Israel bikpɛŋ Reuben biis da anɛ Hanok nɛ Pallu nɛ Heziron nɛ Karmi. Bama da an Reuben dɔɔg dim.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Simeon dɔɔg dimi nwa': Jemuel nɛ Jamin nɛ Ohad nɛ Jakin nɛ Zohar, nɛ Sauul onɛ maa da an Keenan nid la. Bama an Simeon dɔɔg dim.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Ka Gerson tuŋ dim mɛ an Libni nɛ Simie.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Merari tuŋ dim mɛ da anɛ Mahili nɛ Musi. Bama da an Levi dɔɔg la dim.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Izar tuŋ dim da anɛ Kora nɛ Nefeg nɛ Zikir.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Ka Uziel tuŋ dim an Misael nɛ Elizafan nɛ Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aaron da nɔknɛ Eliseba, Aminadab bipuŋ onɛ an Nason taʋn la, ka o lieb o pu'a, ka ba du'a Nadab nɛ Abihu nɛ Eleazar nɛ Itamar.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Eleazar onɛ an Aaron biig la da nɔk Putiel bipuŋ yinne ka o lieb o pu'a, ka ba du'a Finehas. Bama da an Levi Dɔɔg Dim la.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Li anɛ Aaron nɛ Moses kaŋa ka Zugsɔb da yɛli ba ye, “Yisimi Israel dim la ka ba dɔl taaba dɔɔg-dɔɔg yi Egipt teŋin na.”

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Li da anɛ Moses nɛ Aaron n pian' tis Egipt Na'ab Faaro ye o yis Israel dim teŋin la. Aaron di'es Moses pian'ad

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la da pian' tis Moses Egipt teŋin la,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: o da yɛl Moses ye, “Manɛ an Zugsɔb la. Yɛlim Egipt Na'ab Faaro man yɛlif si'el la wʋsa.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Moses yɛl Zugsɔb ye, “Mam pʋ tun'e pian'ada, ka Na'ab Faaro ye o niŋ wala wʋm tis mam?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye, “M na kɛ ka fʋ nwɛnɛ Wina'am nɛ tis Na'ab Faaro ka fʋ bier Aaron aan fʋ nɔdi'es.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Yɛlim mam yɛlif si'el la wʋsa tis Aaron, ka o yɛl Na'ab Faaro ka o kɛ ka Israel dim la yi.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Amaa Faaro kʋ wʋm tisi fɔ, dinɛ na kɛ ka m mɔri m nimbanɛ an Israel dim la yi Egipt teŋin ka ba dɔl taaba dɔɔg-dɔɔg. Ka Egipt teŋ dim na nyɛ namisʋg bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɛ Aaron tʋm wʋʋ Zugsɔb la yɛli ba si'em la.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Na'ab Faaro ya'a ti yɛli ya ye ya maalim nyalima, fʋn yɛlim Aaron ye o nɔkim o dansaari la lɔbi bas teŋ ka li na kilim waaf Faaro tuon.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɛ Aaron kpɛn' Na'ab Faaro san'an maal wʋʋ Zugsɔb la yɛli ba si'em la. Ka Aaron nɔk dansaar la lɔbi bas teŋ ka li kilim waaf, Faaro nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la tuon.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab Faaro mɛ da buol o Egipt tiim dim banɛ tʋm nyalima la ka ba mɛ tʋm ala.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Ka ba wʋsa mɛ nɔki ba dansaya lɔbi bas teŋ ka li kilim wiigi. Amaa ka Aaron dansaar la vɔli ba dansaya la wʋsa.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro sʋnf maligim digilim hali ka o pʋ wʋm tisi baa, wʋʋ Zugsɔb la pʋn yɛl si'em la. Ku'om kilim ziim la yɛla

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye, “Na'ab Faaro sʋnf digilimnɛ ka o zan'as ye nidib la kʋ yii.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Saa kem Faaro san'an bɛkɛung ka o saa na yii keŋ mu'arin la. Zi'enim Nail mu'ar la gbɛog ka mɔr dansaar kanɛ kilim waaf la fʋ nu'ugin ka o ya'a paae na

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: fʋn yɛl o ye, ‘Zugsɔb onɛ an Hibiru dim Wina'am la, tʋm mam fʋ san'an na ye m yɛlif ye asɛɛ fʋ kɛ ka m nidib la yii keŋ pʋ'ʋs mam mɔɔgin. Amaa hali nɛ anwa, fʋ pʋ wʋmma.’

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Alazug, Zugsɔb la yɛl ye ‘M na tʋm nwa' ka fʋ baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la. Gɔsima, m ye m san'amnɛ ku'okanɛ bɛ mu'a nɛ kɔlisin la wʋsa ka li kilim ziim.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Ka zimi banɛ bɛ mu'a nɛ kɔlisin la wʋsa na kpi, ka ku'om la na pun'oe, ka Egipt dim kʋ nyaŋi nu ku'om laa.’”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb da lɛn yɛl Moses ye, “Yɛlim Aaron ka o nɔk dansaar la ʋki tiesi kpa' Egipt ku'obanɛ an mu'a nɛ kɔlis nɛ bɛɛnna nɛ kɔldaad nɛ bulis wʋsa. Ka ziim na di'e Egipt teŋ wʋsa, la'an nɛ ba nwama nɛ dʋgid.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɛ Aaron maal wʋʋ Zugsɔb la yɛli ba si'em la, ka nɔk dansaar la ʋki tiesi kpa' ku'om la Faaro nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la nini ni, ka ku'om la kilim ziim.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka zimi banɛ bɛ ku'omin la wʋsa kpi, ka ku'om la wʋsa pun'oe, ka Egipt dim pʋ lɛn nuud ku'om kɔlis la nii. Bɔzugɔ Egipt teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa da anɛ ziim.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ka Egipt dim banɛ tʋm nyalima la mɛ maal ala, ka Na'ab Faaro sʋnf maligim digilim ka o pʋ wʋm tisi ba, wʋʋ Zugsɔb la pʋn yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Ka Faaro fɛndigi lɛbi kuli o yin ka li pʋ daami o sʋnf baa bi'elaa.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ka Egipt dim la tu bulisi kpi'el nɛ kɔlis la paam ku'om nuud, bɔzugɔ ba kʋ nyaŋi nu kɔlis la ku'om. Lɔmisi daam Egipt dim la yɛla

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Daba ayɔpɔi nya'aŋ Zugsɔb da san'am ku'om la.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye, “Kem Na'ab Faaro san'anɛ yɛl o ye, ‘Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛtif ye fʋ kɛ ka o nidib la yi teŋin la keŋ wɔ'ɔg o.’

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Ka ye, ‘Fʋ ya'a zan'as ye ba kʋ yii, m na kɛ ka lɔmis di'e teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Ka ku'om la wʋsa na an lɔmis. Ba na kpɛn' na'ayin la, kpɛn' fʋ dɔɔgin, nɛ fʋ digisigin. Ba mɛ na kpɛn' fʋ kpɛɛmnam yaan nɛ fʋ nidib wʋsa ya' pʋʋgin, hali ya za'ambɛmisin na an lɔmis.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka lɔmis la na dʋt fʋn nɛ kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa.’”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye o yɛlim Aaron ka o nɔk dansaar la tiesi kpa' ku'om zin'is wʋsa ka lɔmis na yina pɛ'ɛl Egipt teŋ la.

english_verse: Aaron obeyed, and suddenly frogs were everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka Aaron tiesi kpa' Egipt ku'om zin'is wʋsa ka lɔmis yina di'e teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Egipt dim banɛ tʋm nyalima mɛ maal ala ka lɔmis yina pɛ'ɛl teŋ la.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro buol Moses nɛ Aaron ye, “Sɔsimi Zugsɔb ka o kɛ ka lɔmis la yii m san'an, ka m na kɛ ka Israel dim la yii keŋ maal malʋŋʋ tis Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Ka Moses yɛl Na'ab Faaro ye, “Naa, Na'aba, tisimim saŋa kanɛ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye m sɔs Wina'am tis fʋn nɛ fʋ kpɛɛmnam nɛ fʋ nidib wʋsa, ka lɔmis la yi ka basi ya ka kɛ banɛ bɛ ku'omin la ma'aa.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro ye, “Bɛog.” Ka Moses ye, “Li na niŋ wʋʋ fʋn yɛl si'em la, ka fʋ baŋ ye ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la bɛ, ka sɔ' kae nwɛn oo.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Lɔmis la wʋsa na lɛb ku'omin la ka bas fʋn nɛ fʋ yidim, nɛ fʋ kpɛɛmnam, nɛ fʋ nidib la wʋsa.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɛ Aaron yi Na'ab Faaro san'an ka Moses da fabili tis Zugsɔb lɔmis la yɛla.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb wʋm o fabʋlʋg ka kɛ ka lɔmis la kpii ba yaan, nɛ ba za'asin, nɛ ba pɔɔdin nɛ zin'is wʋsa.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Ka ba vaae lɔmis la la'as dʋya-dʋya ka teŋ la pun'oe.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab Faaro nyɛ ka yɔlisim kena la, ka o digilimi o sʋnf ka pʋ lɛn siak ye o wʋm tis Moses nɛ Aaron, wʋʋ Zugsɔb la pʋn yɛl si'em la. Pɔ'ɔdi yi Egipt teŋin la yɛla

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye o yɛlim Aaron ka o nɔk o dansaar la nwɛ' teŋ la ka uusʋg duoe ka Egipt teŋ la wʋsa uusʋg na kilim pɔ'ɔd.

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Ka Aaron sid nɔk o dansaar la nwɛ' teŋin ka pɔ'ɔd yina niŋ nidib nɛ bʋnkɔnbid mi'ii. Ka Egipt teŋin wʋsa uusʋg lieb pɔ'ɔd.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Amaa ka ba banɛ tʋm nyalima la mak ye ba mɛ tʋm ala, ka maki gʋ'ʋŋ, ka pɔ'ɔd la dum nidib la nɛ bʋnkɔnbid.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ka banɛ tʋm nyalima la yɛl Na'ab Faaro ye, “Wina'am nu'ug bɛ yɛl kaŋa ni.” Amaa Na'ab Faaro sʋnf digilim nɛ ka o pʋ kɛlisɛ, wʋʋ Zugsɔb la pʋn yɛl si'em la. Pʋmpɔɔsi yi Egipt teŋin la yɛla

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb lɛn yɛl Moses ye, “Duom bɛogʋn keŋ Faaro san'an saŋkanɛ ka o ken mu'arin la, ka yɛl o ye, ‘Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, kɛl ka m nidib la yii keŋ pʋ'ʋsim.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a zan'as, m na tʋm pʋmpɔɔs na kad fʋn nɛ fʋ kpɛɛmnam, nɛ fʋ nidib wʋsa ya' na anɛ pʋmpɔɔs ma'aa, la'an nɛ teŋin la wʋsa.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb tʋm nwa', ka pʋmpɔɔs yina hali pɛ'ɛl Na'ab Faaro yir nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la ya', nɛ yir wʋsa Egipt tempʋʋgin; pʋmpɔɔs la da san'am teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro buol Moses nɛ Aaron ka ye, “Yim keŋ ka maali malʋŋʋ tisi ya Wina'am la teŋ kaŋa ni.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Amaa Moses lɛbis o ye, “Li pʋ tu'alɛ, bɔzugɔ kɔnbbanɛ ka ti ye ti maali tis Zugsɔb Wina'am la anɛ kisʋgʋ tis Egipt dim. Ka ti ya'a maal malʋŋ kanɛ kisi ba san'an, ba na lɔbi ti nɛ kuga.

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Ti na keŋnɛ mɔɔgin daba atan' maal malʋŋ la tisi ti Zugsɔb Wina'am wʋʋ on yɛli ti si'em la.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Faaro lɛbis ye, “M na kɛ ka ya keŋ mɔɔgin la maal malʋŋ la tisi ya Zugsɔb Wina'am la, amaa da laligi nyaa! Sɔsim Wina'am tisim!”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ka Moses lɛbis o ye, “Ti ya'a yi kpɛla, m na sɔs Zugsɔb la ka bɛog, pʋmpɔɔs la wʋsa saa na bas fʋn nɛ fʋ nidib la. Amaa mid ka fʋ ma', ka pʋmpɔɔs la gaad ka fʋ pʋ kɛ ka nidib la keŋi maal malʋŋʋ tis Zugsɔb laa.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Ka Moses yi ka bas Na'ab Faaro ka sɔs Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la maal wʋʋ Moses n sɔs si'em la, ka pʋmpɔɔs la bas Faaro nɛ o nidib la wʋsa ka yinne pʋ kpɛlim.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Faaro lɛn digilimi o sʋnf ka pʋ siak ye nidib la keŋɛ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Moses ye, “Kem yɛl Na'ab Faaro ye Zugsɔb onɛ an Hibiru dim Wina'am la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, ‘Kɛl ka m nidib banɛ an Israel dim la yii keŋi pʋ'ʋs mam.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb na kɛ ka ban'abɛ'ɛd gban'e ya bʋnkɔnbid banɛ an widi nɛ bʋmis nɛ yʋgʋma nɛ niigi nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ bʋʋs.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb na bak Israel bʋnkɔnbid nɛ Egipt dim bʋnkɔnbid, ka Israel bʋnkɔnbʋg baa yinne kʋ kpii.

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb tis saŋa ye li yimbɛog, on Zugsɔb na tʋm bʋnkaŋa teŋ la ni.’”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Ka li yimbɛog ka Zugsɔb sid tʋm wʋʋ on yɛl si'em la, ka Egipt dim bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa kpi, amaa Israel bʋnkɔnbʋg baa yinne pʋ kpii.
