english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Ba na la'as nɛ fʋ gɔsid zin'ikanɛ an La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋr la nɛ tʋʋm kanɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa, ka sɔ'ɔsɔ da li'el yanamɛ bɛ si'el la na.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Ya tʋʋma anɛ ye ya gɔt Kasi Zin'ig la nɛ maan daka la ka m sʋnpɛɛn da paae Israel dim la ya'asɛ.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋi gaŋi ya Levi taaba la Israel dim la sʋʋgin ka ba an wʋʋ piini tisi ya. M pɛsigi ba tis Zugsɔb la ye ba tʋm La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋrin la.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Amaa fʋn nɛ fʋ biis la ma'aa na tʋm maan la tʋʋma nɛ maan daka yɛla nɛ linɛ bɛ fuug linɛ bɛŋ la pʋʋgin. M tisif maan tʋʋma la nɛ ka li an piini. Ninkanɛ pʋ nar ye o li'el Fuug Sʋgʋr la ya'a li'el, yanam on kʋʋm o.”

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ba ni'im la na aan fʋ din, nwɛnɛ kugsir linɛ ka ba ɛɛn nyɔɔsim la, nɛ datiuŋ gbɛr la aan fʋ din si'em la.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Fʋ na sʋ'oe maan kanɛ an kasi ka ba pʋ nɔki nyu'oe nɛ bugum. Maan banɛ ka ba mɔr na wʋsa ka li an kasi la, li ya'a anɛ zʋʋd maan bɛɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɛɛ taal maana, li anɛ fʋn nɛ fʋ biis din.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Dimi li wʋʋ bʋn linɛ an kasi; dau wʋsa anɛ ye o dii li. Li anɛ tilas ye ya gɔsi li ka li an kasi.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Linɛ wʋsa ka ba yisi lii li kɔn' nyɔɔsʋŋ maan la ni mɛ na anɛ fʋ din. M nɔki li tis fʋn nɛ fʋ bipumis nɛ biribis saŋa wʋsa. Onɛ wʋsa bɛɛ fʋ yin la ka an nyain wʋʋ malʋŋ la bɔɔd si'em la tun'e dii li.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: Ban zaŋid olif kpavɛnliŋ si'a nɛ daam linɛ an sʋm nɛ zʋʋd linɛ ka ba tisid man Zugsɔb la nɛ bʋndɛɛnna wʋsa anɛ fʋ din.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Bʋndɛɛŋ linɛ wʋsa yi teŋgbauŋʋn la ka ba mɔri kɛn Zugsɔb la san'an na, anɛ fʋ din. Onɛ wʋsa bɛɛ fʋ yin la ka an nyain wʋʋ malʋŋ la bɔɔd si'em la tun'e dii li.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Linɛ wʋsa bɛ Israel teŋin ka ba pɛsigi tis Zugsɔb la anɛ fʋ din.”

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Linɛ wʋsa du'a yiiga ka an ninsaal nɛ bʋnkɔnbʋg wʋsa, ka ba pɛsigi li tis Zugsɔb la anɛ fʋ din. Amaa asɛɛ ka fʋ siak ka ba da' ninsaal bikpɛŋ bɛɛ bʋnkɔnbʋg kanɛ wʋsa ka malʋŋ la pʋʋgin ka o ka' nyain la bikpɛŋ.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Ba ya'a ti an wʋʋ nwadig la, asɛɛ ka fʋ kɛ ka ba da' ba wʋʋ lin nar ye ba da' ba si'em nɛ anzurifa gbila anu, ka li na an Wina'am Fuug Sʋgʋr ligidi, ka' daar wʋsa ligidi.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Amaa li ya'a an na'araug bɛɛ pɛ'og bɛɛ bʋʋg bikpɛŋ, yanam da siak ka ba da' baa, ban an kasi la zug. Ti'eliminɛ ba ziim misig maan daka la, ka nyu'oe kpaam la nɛ bugum ka li nyuug la na malisi tis Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: “Linɛ wʋsa ka ba yisi li kɔn' maan linɛ an kasi ka Israel dim kenna maannɛ tisid Zugsɔb la, m nɔki li tis fʋn nɛ fʋ biribis nɛ bipumis ka li na aan ya din saŋa wʋsa. Li anɛ nɔnaar kanɛ ka' bɛn ka Zugsɔb la maal nɛ fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas wʋsa.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Aaron ye, “Fʋ kʋ mɔr faar bɛɛ pʋʋr teŋ la nii; manɛ aan fʋ pʋʋr nɛ fʋ faar Israel dim la sʋʋgin.

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Manɛ tis Levi dɔɔg la bʋn linɛ bɛ Israel wʋsa pʋdigir piiga vaar yinne ye li aan ba faar ban tʋm tʋʋm si'a La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋrin la zug.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Li anɛ Levi buudi la na tʋm La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋr la tʋʋma ka zi taal kanɛ wʋsa tʋm tisi li. Nɛ' anɛ zi'elkanɛ na bɛ hali ti paae zʋmaʋŋ kanɛ na ti kena. Ba kʋ paam faar Israel dim la san'anɛ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim Levi dɔɔg dim la ye ba ya'a di'e pʋdigir yinne piiga pʋʋgin Israel dim la san'an, bam mɛ yisim ayinne pʋdigir piiga pʋʋgin tis Zugsɔb la ka li an maannɛ tis o.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Ya maan la na an wʋʋ ki ɛɛn yi zieŋin na la bɛɛ ban nwiakid daam zin'isi'a la.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Yɛlim Levi dɔɔg la ye, “Ya ya'a nɔk linɛ an sʋ'ʋm tis Zugsɔb la, li na nwɛnɛ ki yii ya zieŋin na, bɛɛ daam yi ban nwiakid zin'isi'a la na.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Yanam nɛ ya yidim na nyaŋi di linɛ kpɛlim la zin'ig wʋsa. Bɔzugɔ li anɛ yɔɔdi tisi ya, yanamɛ tʋm La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋrin la zug.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a tis Zugsɔb la linɛ nar la yiiga, ya kʋ kpɛn' taalin nɛ linɛ kpɛlim la; li na kɛ ka ya kʋ dian'a maana banɛ an kasi ka Israel dim maannɛ tisid Zugsɔb la; ala ka ya kʋ kpii.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la zi'el zi'elsi'a nwa': Yɛlim Israel dim la ye ba mɔr na'asa'azin'a kanɛ pʋ mɔr dɛŋŋa ka ba mɛ nan zi' nɔk o kuaa.

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: Nɔkim o tis Elieza onɛ an maanmaan la ka o kɛ ka ba zaŋi yii ya la'asʋg zin'ig la yiŋi kɔdig o, o nini ni.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Elieza onɛ an maanmaan la na nɔk o nu'ubili tin'e ziim la misig nɔɔra ayɔpɔi kpa' La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋr la tuon.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: O na zi'e gɔt ka ba nyu'oe naaf la gbauŋ nɛ ni'im nɛ ziim nɛ pʋt nɛ o pʋʋgin la'ad wʋsa ka li kanb.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Maanmaan la anɛ ye o nɔk na'aziinr dibir nɛ nyulinnyu'us nɛ pien zɛn'ugʋ lɔs bugum kanɛ dit naaf la ni.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ maanmaan la na pie o fuug ka sʋ ka yʋ'ʋn na tun'e lɛb la'asʋg la zin'igin, amaa o kʋ an nyainnɛ asɛɛ li ti paae zaam.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Dau kanɛ nyu'oe naaf la bugum la anɛ o pie o fuud ka sʋ, ka kʋ an nyainnɛ, asɛɛ li ti paae zaam.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Dau kanɛ an nyain na ku'ol tampɛligim la nɔki niŋ zin'ikanɛ an nyain ka bɛ la'asʋg zin'ig la yiŋ. Israel dim la na nɔki li digil ka lin an linɛ na niŋid ku'okanɛ ka sɔ' na pie o mɛŋ ka lieb nyain la ni; li anɛ linɛ piedi yisid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Onɛ mɛ ku'ol naaf la tampɛligim la mɛ anɛ ye o pie o fuug, on mɛ kʋ an nyainnɛ asɛɛ li ti paae zaam. Nɛ' na an zi'elʋg linɛ na bɛ saŋa wʋsa tis Israel dim nɛ saam banɛ bɛ nɛ ba la.

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋsa si'is kum na lieb dian'ad sɔb daba ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Li anɛ tilas ye o pie o mɛŋ nɛ ku'om la daba atan' nɛ daba ayɔpɔi daar, ka nyaan lieb nyain. Amaa o ya'a pʋ pie o mɛŋ daba atan' nɛ daba ayɔpɔi la daare, o kʋ lieb nyainnɛ.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋsa si'is kum ka pʋ pie o mɛŋa, o sɔb dian'anɛ Fuug Sʋgʋr la. Ba yisim on daana Israel buudi ni. Bɔzugɔ ba pʋ misig o ku'okanɛ kɛt ka nid liebid nyain la, o anɛ dian'ad sɔb; ka o dian'ad la na kpɛlim o mɛŋ zug.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Sɔ' ya'a kpi sʋgʋrin li zi'elʋgʋ nwa': Onɛ kpɛn' dɔɔgin la bɛɛ onɛ bɛ dɔɔg la pʋʋgin na kilim dian'ad sɔb daba ayɔpɔi;

english_verse: Any open jar in the tent is unclean.
translation_verse: lauk kanɛ wʋsa mɛ bɛ ani ka liŋ pʋ pibili li na lieb dian'ad lauk.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Sɔ' ya'a bɛ paalʋ ka si'is onɛ ka ba kʋʋ o nɛ sʋ'ʋg bɛɛ onɛ kpii a-daar-paaeya kum bɛɛ onɛ si'is ninsaal kɔnbir bɛɛ yaʋg, on sɔb na lieb dian'ad sɔb daba ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Dau kanɛ an nyain malʋŋ pʋʋgin na nɔk nyulinnyu'usi tʋm ku'omin la misig dɔɔg la, nɛ di la'ad wʋsa, nɛ nimbanɛ pʋn dɛŋi bɛɛ ani la wʋsa. O mɛ na misig onɛ wʋsa si'is ninsaal kɔnbir bɛɛ kum bɛɛ yaʋg la.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Onɛ an nyain la na misig onɛ ka' nyain la daba atan' nɛ ayɔpɔi la daar. Onɛ ka ba pie o ka o lieb nyain la na pie o fuug ka sʋ nɛ ku'om ka lieb nyain zakan nɔɔ.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Amaa onɛ lieb dian'ad sɔb ya'a pʋ siak ye o maal o mɛŋ nyainnɛ, li anɛ tilas ye ba yis o nidibin la, bɔzugɔ o dian'a Zugsɔb Fuug Sʋgʋr la. Ka ku'okanɛ kɛt ka ba liebid nyain la mɛ pʋ misig oo, ka o an dian'ad sɔb.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Lina na aan ba zi'elʋg saŋa wʋsa. “Onɛ nɔk ku'okanɛ na kɛ ka ba lieb nyain la misig, asɛɛ ka o mɛ pie o fuud, ka onɛ si'is ku'om la na kilim dian'ad sɔb asɛɛ li ti paae zaam.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Bʋn linɛ wʋsa ka onɛ ka' nyain la si'is na lieb dian'ad, ka onɛ mɛ si'isi li na lieb dian'ad sɔb asɛɛ li ti paae zaam.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Nwadkanɛ daa pin'in la ni Israel buudi la wʋsa da paae Zin mɔɔgin la zin'in Kades teŋin. Ani ka Miriam da kpi ka ba mum o.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa ku'om da kae ka nidib la na nuu, ka ba la'as taaba nyɔn Moses nɛ Aaron.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ba da zabid nɛ Moses ka yɛt ye, “Ti ya'a kpiin wʋʋ ti ba'abiis la daa kpi Zugsɔb la tuon si'em la naan sɔn'ɔn

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ mɔr Zugsɔb nidib la kɛn mɔɔgin kpɛla na, ye tinam nɛ ti bʋnkɔnbid la kpi kpɛla?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ mɔri ti yi Egipt teŋin kɛn zin'itɔɔg kaŋa ni na? Diib bɛɛ kekama kae, pomanganɛt nɛ bʋnnuuda mɛ kae. Ka ku'om mɛ kae nuuda.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Moses nɛ Aaron yi nidib la san'anɛ keŋ La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋr la za'anɔɔrini vanbin Zugsɔb la tuon, ka o girima sigi ba san'an na.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Nɔkimi fʋ dansaar la ka fʋn nɛ Aaron la'as nidib la wʋsa. Pian'am tis tampiing la ka ba nini nyɛ, ka li na kpa'ae ku'okanɛ bɛɛ li ni la wʋsa yis na. Fʋ na paam ku'om tampiingin la ka nidib la nɛ ba bʋnkɔnbid la wʋsa nu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Moses sid da nɔk dansaar la Zugsɔb la nini ni wʋʋ on yɛl o si'em la.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Ka Moses nɛ Aaron da la'as nidib la tampiing la tuon ka Moses yɛl nidib la ye, “Kɛlisimi yanam nyɔnyɔlʋg dima, li anɛ tilas ye ti kɛ ka ku'om yi tampiing kaŋa ni naa?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Ani ka Moses ʋk dansaar la nwɛ' tampiing la nɔɔr ayi' ka ku'om da tansi yina, ka nidib la nɛ ba bʋnkɔnbid la wʋsa nu.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses nɛ Aaron ye, “Yanamɛ pʋ niŋ mam yadda bɛɛ na'as mam wʋʋ onɛ an kasi Israel nidib tuon la, ya kʋ mɔr nidib la keŋi kpɛn' teŋ kanɛ ka m tisi ba laa.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Nɛ' da an Meriba teŋ ku'om, zin'ikanɛ ka Israel dim da zabid nɛ Zugsɔb ka o pa'ali ba ye o anɛ kasi la. Edom na'abi pʋ tis Israel dim suor la yɛla

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Ban da nam bɛ Kades la, Moses da tʋm nidib ye ba kem yɛl Edom na'ab ye; “Israel dim banɛ aan fʋ ba'abiis la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Fʋ mi' tɔɔg kanɛ paae ti la,

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: ti yaanam da keŋ Egipt teŋin ka ti da bɛɛ ani yʋma bɛdegʋ. Egipt dim la da namisi ti nɛ ti yaanam la,

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: amaa ti da kaasi tis Zugsɔb la, ka o wʋmi ti kukuma ka tʋm o maliak ka o yisi ti Egipt teŋin na.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Ti bɛlimnɛ, kɛl ka ti dɔlli fʋ teŋin la gaad. Ti kʋ buŋi ya vain tiis pɔɔdin bɛɛ nu ku'om bulsi'a nii. Ti ye ti dɔl nɛ Na'ab Suoraug la tituaa ka kʋ buŋi lɛb datiuŋ bɛɛ dagɔbʋga hali nɛ tinamɛ na ti yii fʋ teŋ la ni fas.’”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Amaa Edom na'ab da lɛbis ye, “Mid ka ya gaad kpɛla; ya ya'a zi' ka mak, ti na yina tʋ'ʋsi ya nɛ zaba.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Israel dim la da lɛbis ye, “Ti ye ti dɔl nɛ suoraug la, ka tinam bɛɛ ti bʋnkɔnbʋg ya'a nuu ya ku'osi'a wʋsa, ti na yɔɔ li sam. Ti kʋdim bɔɔd ye ti gaadnɛ nɔba; si'el pʋ lɛm paasɛ.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛn lɛbis ye, “Ya kʋ gaad kpɛla!” Edom na'ab da yina tʋ'ʋsi ba nɛ soogianam bɛdegʋ banɛ kpi'em.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Edom dimi da pʋ siak ye ba dɔlli ba san'anɛ gaad la zug, Israel dim la da fɛndigi tiak suor ka basi ba. Aaron kum yɛla

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Israel nidib la wʋsa da yi Kades teŋin keŋ paae zuokanɛ buon ye Hor la.

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aaron na maal ka'alim. O kʋ kpɛn' teŋ kanɛ ka m tis Israel dim la, bɔzugɔ ya nidib ayi' la wʋsa ki'isi m nɔɔr Meriba, ku'om la zin'igin.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Dɔl Aaron nɛ o biig Elieza dʋ zuokanɛ buon ye Hor la zugin.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Yɛɛgim Aaron fuug la yɛɛli o biig Elieza, bɔzugɔ Aaron na maal ka'alim; o ye o kpinɛ ani.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Moses da niŋ wʋʋ Zugsɔb la yɛl o si'em la. Ba da dʋ zuokanɛ buon Hor la zug nidib la wʋsa nini ni.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Moses da yɛɛg Aaron fuug la yɛɛli o biig Elieza. Aaron da kpii ani nɔɔ, zuor la zug. Ka Moses nɛ Elieza sig teŋin na.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim la wʋsa, da baŋ ye Aaron kpiya la ba da kum o yɛla dabisa pistan'.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Ba da naam Hor zuorin la dɔl suokanɛ ken Atɛuk Zɛn'ugʋn la, ye ba dɛn'ɛn Edom teŋ baba. Amaa nidib la sʋnf da duonɛ pamm suorin la

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: ka ba pian' zɛrig Wina'am nɛ Moses, n yɛt ye, “Bɔ ka ya mɔri ti yi Egipt teŋin kena ye ti kpi mɔɔgin kpɛla? Diib kae! Ku'om kae! Ka ti mɛ pʋ bɔɔd diyɔɔd banɛ bɛ la!”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Dinzug Zugsɔb la da tʋm wa'atɔɔdi ba san'an; ka ba dum nidib la ka Israel dim bɛdegʋ kpi.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Nidib la da kɛn Moses san'an na yɛl o ye, “Ti tʋm taal tinamɛ pian' zɛrig Zugsɔb nɛ fʋ la. Sɔsim Zugsɔb la ka o yis wiigi la ti san'an!” Ka Moses da sɔs Wina'am nidib la yɛla.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye, “Maalim waafʋ nɔki tabil daugʋ sɛɛl sappi, ka onɛ wʋsa ka waaf dum o tun'e gɔsi li ka vʋ'ʋg.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Moses da nɔk kʋntzɛn'ugʋ maal waafʋ ya'al daug zug. Ka onɛ wʋsa ka waaf da dum o ka o gɔdigi gɔsi li da vʋ'ʋgid nɛ. Moab suor la yɛla

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Israel dim la yʋ'ʋn da vurigi paae Obof teŋin.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Ba da naan ani paae Zered bɔn'ɔgin zi'en ani.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Ka yii ani keŋ la'as teŋ kanɛ bɛ Aanon kɔldaug la lɔm, sian'anr linɛ paae Ammon dim sʋ'ʋlim la ni. Aanon da anɛ Moab teŋ titɔndig, ka bɛ Moab nɛ Amor dim tɛɛns la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Linɛ kɛ ka gbauŋ kanɛ ka ba sɔb Zugsɔb zaba yɛla la yɛl ye, “Waheb linɛ bɛ Sufa teŋin nɛ li bɔn'ɔfaligin nɛ Aanon kɔldaug baba la

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: nɛ bɔn'ɔfalig linɛ zuligid hali ti paae Ar teŋin zin'ikanɛ lɛbid Moab titɔndigin la.”

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Ba da yii ani tʋgisi paae teŋ kanɛ buon Beer la, bulkanɛ ka Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye, “La'asim nidib la na ka m na tisi ba ku'om.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Ala ka Israel dim da yʋ'ʋm yʋʋm kaŋa yɛt ye, “Buliga bulim!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋmmi bulig kanɛ ka tuongatib tu, ka ninsʋma yaae la yɛla, banɛ zanl na'am dansaya nɛ duoya la.” Ka ba naam mɔɔgin la keŋ paae Matana teŋin,

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: yi Matana teŋin keŋ paae Nahaliel ka yi Nahaliel keŋ paae Bamof

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: ka yi Bamof keŋ paae bɔn'ɔg kanɛ bɛ Moab zuokanɛ buon Piisig sisɛrim la lɛbisid Jesimon pipirig la baba. Ban nyaŋ na'ab Sihon nɛ na'ab Og si'em

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Hesbon da anɛ Amor na'ab Sihon tempʋʋg, ka o da zab nɛ Moab na'akʋdʋg ka faaɛn o teŋ la ti paae Aanon kɔldaug la paas.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Israel dim la da tʋm nidib ye ba yɛl Amor dim na'ab onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Sihon la ye,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Ti bɛlimnɛ, kɛl ka ti dɔlli fʋ teŋin la gaad. Ti kʋ buŋi ya vain tiis pɔɔdin bɛɛ nu ku'om bulsi'a nii. Ti ye ti dɔl nɛ Na'ab Suoraug la tituaa hali nɛ tinamɛ na ti yii fʋ teŋin la.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Amaa Sihon da pʋ siak ye ba dɔl ani gaadɛ. O da la'as o zabzabidib la tʋ'ʋs Israel mɔɔgin la. On da paae Jahaz teŋin la, o da zab nɛ Israel ani.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Israel da nyaŋi ba, ka faaɛn teŋ la lin naam Aanon ti paae Yabok kɔldaug, hali ti paae Ammon dim teŋ titɔndig la bɔzugɔ, teŋ kan da kpi'em nɛ hali.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Israel dim da nyaŋ Amor dim tempʋʋs la wʋsa ka zin'in ani, la'an nɛ Hesbon teŋ nɛ linɛ gilig la wʋsa.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Linɛ kɛ ka onɛ siilim siiliŋ la yɛl ye, “Kem Hesbon na ka kɛ ka li maligim mɛ'; kɛl ka Sihon teŋ la lɛn lɛbi li zin'igin.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Bugum da naam Hesbon yina, bugum pielim yi Sihon teŋin na. Li da kanb Ar teŋ linɛ bɛ Moab la, nɛ banɛ sʋ'oe Aanon teŋ kʋkʋna la.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Yɛl paae ya, Moab dima! Ya paam san'auŋ yanam banɛ wɔ'ɔgid Kemos la! O nɔk o biribisi tis ka ba lieb wʋʋ banɛ zɔt nɛ ka o bipumis lieb wʋʋ yammis nɛ tis Sihon onɛ an Amor na'ab la.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Amaa nannanna tinam san'ami ba wʋsa; Hesbon san'amnɛ hali ti paae Dibon teŋin. Ti nwa'ae li hali paae Nofa teŋ kanɛ tiɛn hali ti paae Medeba la.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Alazug Israel dim da zin'in Amor dim la teŋin.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Moses n da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ labisi gɔs Jaza la nya'aŋ, Israel dim da zabi nyaŋ teŋ la nɛ li teŋkpɛmis la ka faaɛn li ka kad Amor dim banɛ bɛɛ ani la yis.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Ba yʋ'ʋn da fɛndigi nɔk suori kpa' Basan, ka Og onɛ an Basan na'ab la la'as o zabzabidibi tʋ'ʋsi ba Edire teŋin zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl Moses ye, “Da zɔɔ o dabiem, ka m gban'e ba tisi ya sa, on nɛ o zabzabidib la nɛ o teŋ la wʋsa. Maalim o wʋʋ fʋn da maal Sihon onɛ an Amor dim na'ab ka da sʋ'oe Hesbon teŋ si'em la.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ba da kʋ Na'ab Og nɛ o biis, nɛ o zabzabidib la wʋsa, ka sɔ' pʋ kpɛlim; ka da di'e o teŋ la sʋ'ʋg.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Israel dim la da keŋi paae Moab zin'ikanɛ an sassi ka bɛ Joodan lɔm lɛbisid Jeriko tempʋʋg la baba.

english_verse: When King Balak of Moab and his people heard how many Israelites there were and what they had done to the Amorites, he and the Moabites were terrified and panicked.
translation_verse: ka dabiem gban'e Moab dim bɔzugɔ ba da zu'oe nɛ hali. Ya'a an sida dabiem da gban'e Moab dim Israel nidib la yɛla.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Moab dim da yɛl Midian teŋ kpɛɛmnam ye, “Nimbama zu'oe si'em la, ba ye ba lɛlig nɛ si'el wʋsa linɛ giligi ti, wʋʋ niigi ɛɛn lɛlig mɔɔg si'em la.” Alazug Balak onɛ an Zippor biig, ka an Moab na'ab saŋkan la,

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: da tʋm buol Balaam onɛ an Beor biig, ka da bɛɛ o mɛŋ teŋin Petor linɛ kpi'e Efiritis kɔldaug la. Balak da yɛl o ye, “Ninsieba naam Egipt n yina pɛ'ɛl nɛ zin'ig la wʋsa, ka zin' kpi'e nɛ mam yammin-yammin.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Kem na pɔ nɔɔri tisi ba, bɔzugɔ ba paŋ gat mam; daasi'erɛɛ m na nyaŋi kadi ba yis teŋ kaŋa ni. Bɔzugɔ m mi' ye banɛ ka fʋ niŋi ba albareka la, sid mɔr albareka, ka banɛ ka fʋ pɔ nɔɔri tisi ba la, li sid na dɔlli ba.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Moab nɛ Midian kpɛɛmnam la da duoe ka nɔk ba'ad ligidi keŋ. Ban da paae Balaam san'an la, ba da yɛl o Balak n yɛl si'em.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Ka Balaam yɛli ba ye, “Gbɛɛmi kpɛla yʋ'ʋŋa, ka m na lɛb na yɛli ya Zugsɔb la tisim labasi'a.”

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Wina'am da kɛn Balaam san'an na bu'os o ye, “Nimbama aan anɔ'ɔnamɛ kɛɛn fʋ san'an na la?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Balaam da lɛbis Wina'am ye, “Balak onɛ an Zippor biig, ka an Moab na'ab la tʋmi ba nɛ labakaŋa na ye,

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: ‘Nimbanɛ yi Egipt na pɛ'ɛl zin'ig wʋsa kpɛla la, kem na pɔɔ niŋi ba tisim, ka daasi'erɛ li na sʋŋ ka m nyaŋi zab nɛ ba kadi ba yis kpɛla.’”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Amaa Wina'am da yɛl Balaam ye, “Da dɔlli ba keŋɛ. Mid ka fʋ pɔ nɔɔri niŋ nimbama, bɔzugɔ ba anɛ banɛ ka albareka bɛɛ ba ni.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Bɛog da nieya ka Balaam duoe yɛl Balak na'ayikpɛm la ye, “Lɛmmi nɛ ya mɛŋ teŋin, ka Zugsɔb la pʋ siak ye m dɔlli ya keŋɛ.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Dinzug Moab na'ayikpɛm la da lɛbi yɛl Balak ye, “Balaam pʋ siak ye o dɔlli ti kenaa.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Balak da tiaki tʋm kpɛɛm sieba, banɛ zu'oe ka mɔr girima gat yiiga dim la.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Ba da kɛn Balaam san'an na yɛl o ye, “Balak onɛ an Zippor biig la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Da kɛ ka si'el gidigif ka fʋ pʋ kena,

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: bɔzugɔ m na yɔɔf sʋ'ʋŋa, ka lɛm maal fʋn bɔɔd si'el wʋsa tisif. Kem na pɔ nɔɔri niŋ nidib la tisim.’”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Amaa Balaam da lɛbisi ba ye, “Hali baa Balak ya'a nɔk o na'ayir la wʋsa pɛ'ɛl nɛ anzurifa nɛ sanlima tisim, m kʋ nyaŋi zan'asi m Zugsɔb onɛ aan m Wina'am la zi'elʋg ka maal si'ela.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Zina gbɛɛmi kpɛla yʋ'ʋŋa wʋʋ ya taaba la daa niŋ si'em la, ka m bu'os Zugsɔb la gɔs on na yɛlim si'em.”

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la Wina'am da kɛn Balaam san'an na yɛl o ye, “Nimbama ya'a lɛn kena buolif, fʋn dɔlli ba keŋ; amaa maalim linɛ ka m yɛlif ye fʋ maal la ma'aa.” Balaam bʋŋ pian' tis o

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Balaam da duoe bɛogʋn lɔɔ o bʋŋʋ dɔl Moab na'ayikpɛm la keŋ.

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Amaa Wina'am sʋnf da duoe nɛ on keŋ la, ka Zugsɔb maliak kidigi zi'en suor la zug ye o geŋ o. Balaam da ban'adnɛ o bʋŋ, ka o yammis ayi' dɔl o.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Bʋŋ la da nyɛ Zugsɔb maliak la ka o zi'e suor la zug ka fuoe sʋ'ʋgʋ zanl o nu'ugin, ka o buŋi kpɛn' mɔɔgi gaad. Ka Balaam pin'ili bʋ'ʋd bʋŋ la ye o lɛb suor pʋʋg.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la da tɔlisi zi'en lɔmbɔn'ɔd ayi' banɛ ka ba mɛ' zaŋguoma ayi' bɛŋ, ka suobaanlig bɛɛ li teŋsʋk la.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Bʋŋ la n da nyɛ Zugsɔb maliak la, o da miee labin zaŋguom la urig Balaam nɔbir. Ka o lɛm bʋ' o ya'as.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la da lɛn vurigi tɔlis zi'en tuon zin'ikanɛ ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi fɛndig datiuŋ bɛɛ dagɔbʋga.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Bʋŋ la da lɛn nyɛ Zugsɔb maliak la, o da digin nɛ Balaam wʋsa teŋin, ka Balaam sʋnf duoe hali ka o vɔb bʋŋ la nɛ o dansaar.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb kɛ ka bʋŋ la ya'ae o nɔɔri pian' Balaam ye, “Bɔ kimm ka m maalif ka li kɛ ka fʋ bʋ'ʋm nɔɔr atan' sa?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Balaam da lɛbis o ye, “Fʋ mɔrim nɛ maan galim! M ya'a mɔrin sʋ'ʋgʋ m nu'ugin m naan kʋʋnif nannanna.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Bʋŋ la da lɛbis Balaam ye, “Man ka'anɛ fʋ mɛŋ bʋŋ onɛ ka fʋ ban'ad saŋa wʋsa ti paae zinaa? Fʋ nam mi' nyɛ ka m maal anwa tisi fɔɔ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ayei!”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɔ'ɔg Balaam nini ka o nyɛ maliak la zi'e suor la teŋsʋk ka fuoe sʋ'ʋgʋ zanl. Ka o igin ka vanbin teŋin.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la da bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bʋ' bʋŋ la nɔɔr atan' sa? M kena ye m giŋif bɔzugɔ ken la ka' sʋ'ʋm m nini nii.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Nɔɔr atan' ka bʋŋ la nyɛɛm ka yuk. Bʋŋ la ya'a pʋ yukinɛ, anwaa m kʋʋnif ka basin bʋŋ la.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Balaam da lɛbisi yɛl Zugsɔb maliak la ye, “M tʋm taal, m pa'a pʋ baŋ ye fʋ zi'enɛ suorin la ye fʋ geŋi ma. Nannanna li ya'a pʋ malisi fɔ m na lɛbi kul.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Ka maliak la lɛbisi yɛl Balaam ye, “Dɔl nidib la keŋ, amaa yɛlim nɛ man ye fʋ yɛl si'el ma'aa.” Ka Balaam dɔl Balak na'ayikpɛm la keŋ.

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Balak n da wʋm ye Balaam kenna la, o da yi ye o tʋ'ʋs o Moab teŋ si'a linɛ bɛ Aanon bɔn'ɔgin, o teŋ titɔndig bɛn la.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Balak da bu'os Balaam ye, “Mam pʋ tʋm ye ba kena buolif nɛ nimmua? Ka bɔ ka fʋ pʋ kɛn tʋʋlig-tʋʋlig na? Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye m kʋ nyaŋi yɔɔf bɛɛ?”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Ka Balaam dɔl Balak n keŋ Kiriaf Huzof teŋin.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Balak da kʋ niigi nɛ pɛ'ɛsi tɔnd ni'imi tis Balaam nɛ kpɛɛmnam banɛ bɛɛ o san'an la.

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la Balak da dɔl Balaam keŋ Bamof Baal, ani ka o nyɛ Israel dim la sieba.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam da yɛl Na'ab Balak ye, “Mɛɛmi maan bimbima ayɔpɔi kpɛla, ka mɔri na'araad ayɔpɔi nɛ pɛraad ayɔpɔi na tisim.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak da maal wʋʋ Balaam yɛl o si'em la, ka babayi' la kɔdig na'araug nɛ pɛraug bimbim wʋsa zugin.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Ka Balaam yɛl Balak ye, “Zi'enim kpi'enɛ fʋ maan la, ka m yi kpikpɛŋ ka daasi'erɛɛ Zugsɔb la na kɛɛn m san'an na. On nie si'el wʋsa pa'alim, m na yɛlif.” Ka yii dʋ zuor zug.

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Wina'am da sia'al o ani, ka Balaam yɛl ye, “Mam maal nɛ bimbima ayɔpɔi, ka kɔdig na'araug nɛ pɛraug bimbim wʋsa zugin.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la nɔk labaari niŋ Balaam nɔɔrin ka yɛl o ye, “Lɛm Balak san'an yɛl o labakaŋa.”

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: O da lɛbi nyɛ ka Balak nam zi'e kpi'e o maan la, on nɛ Moab na'ayikpɛm la wʋsa.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Ka Balaam yɛl labakaŋa ye, “Balak mɔrimi yi Aram teŋin na, Moab na'ab mɔrimi yi ya-nya'aŋ zuoya la ni na ka yɛlim ye, ‘Kem na pɔ nɔɔri niŋ Jakob zugin tisim; kem na, ka zan'as Israel dim.’

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Man ye m niŋ wala pɔ nɔɔri tis banɛ ka Wina'am pʋ pɔ nɔɔri tisɛ? Man ye m niŋ wala zan'as banɛ ka Zugsɔb la pʋ zan'asɛ?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: M naam tampiing la zugʋ nyɛɛ ba, zuor la zug, m bɛɛ ani ka nyɛti ba. M nyɛ nimbanɛ baki ba mɛŋ ka bɛɛ ba kɔn' nɛ buudsi'a wʋsa.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi kaal Jakob yaasɛ? Ba anɛ wʋʋ titanbin'isʋg nɛ! Bɛɛ anɔ'ɔn na gi'el Israel nidiba, hali baa ba pʋdigir anaasi? Kɛl ka m kpi pʋpiel kum, ka m naar nwɛnɛ pʋpiel nɛ!”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Balak da yɛl Balaam ye, “Fʋ maal bɔɔ la tis mam? M mɔrif na ye fʋ pɔ nɔɔri tisim dataas, amaa ka fʋ lɛɛ niŋidi ba zug albareka ma'aa!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M da pian' Zugsɔb la nɔk pian'asi'a niŋi m nɔɔrinɛ?”

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Ka Balak yɛl o ye, “Dɔllim ka ti keŋ zin'isi'a ya'as ka fʋ na nyɛɛ ba: fʋ na nyɛ nɛ ban bi'ela ka ka' ba wʋsaa. Ka ani ka fʋ na pɔ nɔɔri niŋi ba tisim.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: O da dɔl o keŋ Zofim paalʋ ni, Pisig zuor la zug, ka o lɛm mɛ' maan bimbima ayɔpɔi ani ka kɔdig na'araug nɛ pɛraug bimbim wʋsa zug.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Balaam da yɛl Balak ye, “Kpɛlim kpɛla zi'enɛ kpi'en nɛ fʋ maan la, ka m tʋ'ʋs o kpɛ'ɛsa.”

english_verse: The Lord appeared to Balaam and gave him another message, then he told him to go and tell Balak.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da tʋ'ʋs Balaam ka nɔk labaari niŋ o nɔɔrin, ka yɛl o ye, “Lɛm Balak san'anɛ tis o labakaŋa.”

english_verse: Balaam went back and saw him and his officials standing beside the offerings. Balak asked, “What did the Lord say?”
translation_verse: O da lɛbi keŋ nyɛɛ o ka o zi'e kpi'e o maan la, nɛ Moab na'ayikpɛm la wʋsa. Balak da bu'os o ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl ye bɔ?”

english_verse: God is no mere human! He doesn't tell lies or change his mind. God always keeps his promises.
translation_verse: Wina'am ka' ninsaal ka na ma' ziri, bɛɛ ninsaal biig ka na tiak o pʋtɛn'ɛrɛ. O nan mi' yɛl si'el ka pʋ tʋmi lii? Bɛɛ kaanb si'el ka pʋ niŋi li bunnɛ?

english_verse: “My command from God was to bless these people, and there's nothing I can do to change what he has done.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, ba tisim nɛ zi'elʋg ye m niŋ albareka niŋi ba zug. O pʋn niŋ albareka niŋi ba ka m kʋ nyaŋi tiaki li.

english_verse: Israel's king is the Lord God. He lives there with them and intends them no harm.
translation_verse: Zutɔɔg kae Jakob san'anɛ, sʋnsa'aŋ kae Israel dim san'anɛ. Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba Wina'am la bɛ nɛ ba; ba tansid nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye o anɛ na'ab ba teŋsʋk.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led Israel out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Wina'am mɔri ba yi Egipt teŋin na; ba paŋ nwɛnɛ wɛnaaf paŋ nɛ.

english_verse: No magic charms can work against them— just look what God has done for his people.
translation_verse: Ba'akɔlʋg sɔb kae na nyaŋi duoe zi'enɛ ba yɛlaa, sɔnpʋt kae na tun'e san'ami ba. Nidib yʋ'ʋn na gɔt Jakob nɛ Israel dim ka yɛt ye, ‘Gɔsim Zugsɔb la maal si'el!’

english_verse: They are like angry lions ready to attack; and they won't rest until their victim is gobbled up.”
translation_verse: Nidib la duonɛ wʋʋ gbigimnya'as nɛ: ba duoe ba mɛŋ wʋʋ gbigimi na nyɛ bʋnkɔnbʋg ka mɔ hali ti kʋʋ o ka nuu o ziim.”

english_verse: Balak shouted, “If you're not going to curse Israel, then at least don't bless them.”
translation_verse: Ka Balak yɛl Balaam ye, “Tɔ'! Fʋ ya'a kʋ pɔ nɔɔri niŋi ba, fʋn mɛ da niŋi ba zug bareka baa bi'elaa!”

english_verse: “I've already told you,” Balaam answered. “I will say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Third Message
translation_verse: Ka Balaam lɛbis ye, “M pʋn pʋ yɛlif ye li anɛ tilas ye m maal Zugsɔb la yɛl ye m maal si'elaa?”

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Come on, let's try another place. Maybe God will let you curse Israel from there.”
translation_verse: Ka Balak yɛl Balaam ye, “Kem na, ka m nɔki fʋ keŋ zin'isi'a ya'as. Ka daasi'erɛɛ li na malis Wina'am sʋnf ka o kɛ ka fʋ naam ani pɔ nɔɔri niŋi ba.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to Mount Peor overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ka Balak nɔk Balaam dʋ zuokanɛ buon Peor la ka linɛ kpa' Jesimon pipirig la.

english_verse: Balaam said, “Build seven altars here, then bring me seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Balaam da yɛl ye, “Mɛɛm maan bimbima ayɔpɔi kpɛla, ka lɔ na'araad ayɔpɔi nɛ pɛraad ayɔpɔi tisim.”

english_verse: After Balak had done what Balaam asked, he sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Balak da niŋ wʋʋ Balaam yɛl si'em la, ka o kʋ naaf nɛ pɛ'og bimbim wʋsa zugin.

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Balaam da baŋ ye li anɛ Zugsɔb la bɔɔdim ye o niŋ Israel dim zug albareka la, o da pʋ lɛm maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm wʋʋ on ɛɛnti niŋid si'em la, amaa o da fɛndig o nindaa kpa' sian'anr la baba

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: ka ʋk o nindaa nyɛ ka Israel dim la'as dɔɔg, dɔɔgʋ zi'e. Ka Wina'am Siig la da sig o zugin na,

english_verse: and Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: ka o tis o labaar la ye, “Balaam onɛ an Beor biig la pian'ʋkʋ nwa', on kanɛ nyɛt nyain la labaari nwa'.

english_verse: It comes from the Lord, the God All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋm Wina'am pian'ad la pian'ʋkʋ la, onɛ ka Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la nied yɛla pa'an o, onɛ vanbin nɛ onɛ nini yɔ'ɔg la yɛt ye,

english_verse: It's like a grove of palm trees or a garden beside a river. You are like tall aloe trees that the Lord has planted, or like cedars growing near water.
translation_verse: Ya nwɛnɛ bɔn'ɔfaligi yadigi yi paalʋ nɛ, ka nwɛnɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔgʋ na bɛ kɔlʋg nɔɔrin nɛ. Ya nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la na sɛ tivɛnliŋ nɛ, ka nwɛnɛ na'aziinri na bɛ bɛuŋ kpikpɛŋ nɛ.

english_verse: You and your descendants will prosper like an orchard beside a stream. Your king will rule with power and be a greater king than Agag the Amalekite.
translation_verse: Ku'om na pɛ'ɛli ba buati badig; ba bʋmbʋʋda na paam ku'om bɛdegʋ. Ba na'ab na mɔr kpi'euŋʋ gat Na'ab Agag: ba sʋ'ʋlim na nyɛ zʋn'or.

english_verse: With the strength of a wild ox, God led you out of Egypt. You will defeat your enemies, shooting them with arrows and crushing their bones.
translation_verse: Wina'am mɔri ba yi Egipt teŋin na; ba paŋ nwɛnɛ wɛnaaf paŋ nɛ. Ba san'amid tembanɛ kisi ba ka kɔɔdi ba kɔnba bur-bur, ka kʋnsidi ba nɛ ba kpana.

english_verse: Like a lion you lie down, resting after an attack. Who would dare disturb you? “Anyone who blesses you will be blessed; anyone who curses you will be cursed.”
translation_verse: Ba vanbnɛ teŋin nwɛnɛ gbigim nɛ. Ka nwɛnɛ gbigimnya'aŋ nɛ. Anɔ'ɔnɛ gɛɛm na daami ba? Israel, banɛ niŋif albareka na paam albareka, ka banɛ pɔ nɔɔri tisif paam nɔpɔɔr!’”

english_verse: When Balak heard this, he was so furious that he pounded his fist against his hand and said, “I called you here to place a curse on my enemies, and you've blessed them three times.
translation_verse: Ka Balak sʋnf duoe nɛ Balaam. Ka o nwɛ' nu'usi pisig ka ye, “Mam buolif ye fʋ pɔ nɔɔri tisim dataas la, amaa ka fʋ niŋi ba zug albareka nɔɔr atan' nwa' wʋsa!

english_verse: Leave now and go home! I told you I would pay you well, but since the Lord didn't let you do what I asked, you won't be paid.”
translation_verse: Nannanna duom kpɛla tɔ'ɔtɔ kuli fʋ yin! M daa yɛl ye m na yɔɔf bɛdegʋ, amaa Zugsɔb la kɛya ka fʋ kʋ nyɛ yɔɔd laa.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: ‘Hali baa Balak ya'a pɛ'ɛl o na'ayir la nɛ anzurifa nɛ sanlima nɔki tisim, m kʋ nyaŋi maal si'el nɛ m mɛŋ paŋa, li ya'a an sʋ'ʋm bɛɛ bɛ'ɛdɛ; m kʋ nyaŋi keŋ gaad Zugsɔb la tis nɔsi'a la, asɛɛ ka m yɛl Zugsɔb la yɛl si'el la nɔɔ.’

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Nannanna m lɛbid nɛ m mɛŋ nidibin, amaa kem na ka m yɛlif nidib nwa' na maali fʋ nidib la si'em dabisa banɛ kenna la.”

english_verse: Balaam said: “I am the son of Beor, and my words are true, so listen to my message!
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o labakaŋa ye, “Balaam onɛ anɛ Beor biig la pian'ʋkʋ la, nɛ onɛ nyɛt nyain la labaar.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋm Wina'am pian'ad la pian'ʋkʋ la, on ka Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la nied yɛla pa'an o. Onɛ vanbin, nɛ onɛ nini yɔ'ɔg la yɛt ye,

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: ‘M nyɛɛ o, amaa ka' nannannaa. M nyɛt o, amaa o ka' yamminɛ. Nwadbil na yi Jakob ni na, na'am dansaar na yi Israel na. O na nwa'ae Moab gbɛ'og ka nwa'as Sief yaas la wʋsa zut.

english_verse: Israel will conquer Edom and capture the land of that enemy nation.
translation_verse: O na sʋ'ʋg Edom teŋ la wʋsa: ka nyaŋ o dataas banɛ bɛ Seir teŋgbauŋʋn. Israel mɛ na nɔbig nɛ paŋ.

english_verse: The king of Israel will rule and destroy the survivors of every town there.
translation_verse: Tuongat na yi Jakob ni na, ka san'am linɛ kpɛlim bɛ tempʋʋgin la wʋsa.’”

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ka Balaam yʋ'ʋn fɛndigi gɔs Amalek dim la, ka yɛli ba yɛla ye, “Amalek da dɛŋ tɛɛns wʋsa tuon, amaa ba na ba'asi san'am saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.”

english_verse: “And this is what I saw about the Kenites: They think they're safe, living among the rocks,
translation_verse: Ka o yʋ'ʋn nyɛ Keen dim la ka yɛli ba ye, “Ya bɛllim zin'ig la nwɛnɛ zin'ikpi'euŋ nɛ, ka nwɛnɛ niis banɛ tɛɛdi ba tɛɛd tampinyɔ'ɔd pʋʋgin nɛ.

english_verse: but they will be wiped out when Assyria conquers them.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, Asiria dim la ya'a ti nyaŋi gban'e ya mɔri keŋ, yanam Keen dim na san'am.”

english_verse: Ships will come from Cyprus, bringing people who will invade the lands of Assyria and Eber. But finally, Cyprus itself will be ruined.”
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka anrintitada na naam Kitim teŋinɛ dɔl Atɛuk la suoya kena. Ba na nyaŋ Asiria la'an nɛ Ebɛr, amaa ban mɛ na ti paam san'auŋ.”

english_verse: After Balaam finished, he started home, and Balak also left.
translation_verse: Balaam da duoe lɛbi kul, ka Balak mɛ keŋ o ken.

english_verse: While the Israelites were camped at Acacia, some of the men had sex with Moabite women.
translation_verse: Israel dimi da nam bɛ Sittim teŋin la, ba dap la da pin'ili dig nɛ Moab buudi pu'ab la,

english_verse: These women then invited the men to ceremonies where sacrifices were offered to their gods. The men ate the meat from the sacrifices and worshiped the Moabite gods.
translation_verse: alazug, pu'ab la da ɛɛnti buonnɛ banɛ saŋa kanɛ ka ba maannɛ ba bada la. Nidib la da pin'ili dit ka iginidi pʋ'ʋsid bada la.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel because they had worshiped the god Baal Peor.
translation_verse: Alazug Israel dim da la'asi wɔ'ɔgid Baal Peor. Ka Zugsɔb sʋnf duoe nɛ ba hali.

english_verse: So he said to Moses, “Take the Israelite leaders who are responsible for this and have them killed in front of my sacred tent where everyone can see. Maybe then I will stop being angry with the Israelites.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb da yɛl Moses ye, “Yisim bama tuongatib la wʋsa kʋʋ ba dɛlig nintaŋ pieligin, ka li kɛ ka Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn yi Israel dim la zugin.”

english_verse: Moses told Israel's officials, “Each of you must put to death any of your men who worshiped Baal.”
translation_verse: Alazug Moses da buol Israel sariakatib la yɛli ba ye, “Sɔ' wʋsa kʋʋmi o nid onɛ wʋsa la'asi wɔ'ɔgid Baal Peor la.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Moses nɛ Israel nidib la wʋsa da zin' La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋr la za'anɔɔrini kaasidi li yɛla, ka Israel dau yinne mɔr Midian pu'a kena kpɛn' o yinne ba nini ni.

english_verse: Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron the priest, saw the couple and left the crowd. He found a spear
translation_verse: Ka Finehas onɛ da an Elieza biig ka an Aaron, onɛ da an maanmaan kpɛɛm yaaŋ la nyɛ la, o sʋnf da duoe nɛ hali, ka o duoe nidib la sʋʋgin la nɔk kpan

english_verse: and followed the man into his tent, where he ran the spear through the man and into the woman's stomach. The Lord immediately stopped punishing Israel with a deadly disease,
translation_verse: ka kad o hali ti kpɛn' dɔɔgin, ka ʋk kpan la kʋns dau la tɔlig pu'a la niŋgbiŋin. Alazug ban'akanɛ ka Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn da kɛ ka li gban'e Israel dim la da gu'oya.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye,

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”

translation_verse: Jair onɛ mɛ an Manase yaaŋ la da keŋi nyaŋ teŋkpɛmis la ka pʋd o li yʋ'ʋr ye Havof Jair.

english_verse: Nobah captured the town of Kenath with its villages and renamed it Nobah.
translation_verse: Ka Noba mɛ nyaŋ Kenaf nɛ tembanɛ gilig la ka pʋd o li ye Noba.

english_verse: As Israel traveled from Egypt under the command of Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Moses nɛ Aaron n da gaad Israel dim tuon ka ba yi Egipt teŋin gumm-gumm nwɛnɛ zabzabidib si'em la nwa'.

english_verse: Moses kept a list of the places they camped, just as the Lord had instructed. Here is the record of their journey:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da tis nɔɔr ka Moses sɔbi ba ken la yɛla si'em nwa'.

english_verse: Israel left the Egyptian city of Rameses on the fifteenth day of the first month. This was the day after the Lord had punished Egypt's gods by killing the first-born sons in every Egyptian family. So while the Egyptians were burying the bodies, they watched the Israelites proudly leave their country.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Egipt dim la nam bɛɛ ani mummi ba bikpɛɛmnam banɛ ka Zugsɔb da kʋ la. Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka tɔɔg sig ban nɛ ba bada la zugin na.

english_verse: After the Israelites left Rameses, they camped at Succoth,
translation_verse: Israel dim la da bas Rameses teŋin paae Sukot teŋinɛ la'asi digin ani.

english_verse: and from there, they moved their camp to Etham on the edge of the desert.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn naam Sukot n keŋ la'asi digin Etam kpi'en sian'anr la nɔɔrin.

english_verse: Then they turned back toward Pi-Hahiroth, east of Baal-Zephon, and camped near Migdol.
translation_verse: Ba da yi Etam, ka fɛndigi lɛb nya'aŋi keŋ lɛb Pihahirot lɛbisid ya-nya'aŋ Baal Zafon baba, diginɛ ani kpi'en nɛ Migdol teŋ la.

english_verse: They left Pi-Hahiroth, crossed the Red Sea, then walked three days into the Etham Desert and camped at Marah.
translation_verse: Ba da bas Pihahirot teŋ la ka lɔ'ɔŋ atɛuk la kpɛn' sian'arin. Ban da keŋ daba atan' Etam sian'arin la, ba da la'asi digin Mara teŋin.

english_verse: They left Elim and camped near the Red Sea,
translation_verse: Ba da duoe Elam teŋin la ka keŋ la'asi diginɛ kpi'en nɛ Atɛuk Zɛn'ug la.

english_verse: then turned east and camped along the western edge of the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn duoe Atɛuk Zɛn'ugʋn la keŋ la'asi digin Sin mɔɔgin la.

english_verse: From there they went to Dophkah, Alush, and Rephidim, where they had no water.
translation_verse: Ba da naam Alus n keŋ digin Refidim, zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om da kae ka nidib la na nuu.

english_verse: They left Rephidim and finally reached the Sinai Desert.
translation_verse: Ba da naam Refidim n keŋ la'asi digin Sinai mɔɔgin la.

english_verse: When they left Kadesh, they came to Mount Hor, on the border of Edom.
translation_verse: Ba da naam Kedes keŋ digin Hor zuorin, Edom teŋ titɔndigin.

english_verse: That's where the Lord commanded Aaron the priest to go to the top of the mountain. Aaron died there on the first day of the fifth month,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da tis nɔɔr ka Aaron onɛ da an maanmaan la dʋ Hor zuor la zug, zin'ikanɛ ka o da kpi nwadkanɛ paasid anu la pin'ilʋg daar, yʋʋm kanɛ paasid pisnaasi Israel dim la da yi Egipt na la.

english_verse: It was then that the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Southern Desert of Canaan, heard that Israel was headed that way.
translation_verse: Keenan dim na'ab onɛ da sʋ'oe Arad teŋ linɛ bɛ Negef teŋin la da wʋm ye Israel dim la kenna.

english_verse: and finally in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Ba da naam Abarim zuoya la ni keŋ digin Moab zin'ikanɛ an sassi ka kpi'e Joodan lɔm lɛbisid Jeriko tempʋʋg la baba.

english_verse: Their camp stretched from Beth-Jeshimoth to Acacia. The Lord's Command To Conquer Canaan
translation_verse: Ba da digin Moab teŋ kanɛ an sassi la Joodan kɔldaug gbɛog, lin naam Befijesimof ti paae Abɛl Sittim tɛɛns la bɛn.

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho, the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da pian' tis Moses Moab zin'ikanɛ an sassi ka bɛ Joodan lɔm lɛbisid Jeriko tempʋʋg la baba, yɛl o ye,

english_verse: to give the people of Israel this message: When you cross the Jordan River and enter Canaan,
translation_verse: “Pian'am tis Israel dim la ye, ‘Ya ya'a lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan n kpɛn' Keenan teŋin,

english_verse: you must force out the people living there. Destroy their idols and tear down their altars.
translation_verse: yanam on kad buudbanɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa yis ka san'ami ba bada banɛ ka ba kpi'a ka ya'ab la, nɛ ban maannɛ ba bada zin'isi'a la wʋsa.

english_verse: Then settle in the land—I have given it to you as your own.
translation_verse: Sʋ'ʋgimɛ teŋ la ka zin' ani, bɔzugɔ manɛ tisi ya teŋ la ye ya sʋ'ʋgi li.

english_verse: I will show you how to divide the land among the tribes, according to the number of clans in each one, so that the larger tribes will have more land than the smaller ones.
translation_verse: Maalimi bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm pʋdigi teŋ la dɔlis tuŋ wʋsa zem si'em. Banɛ zu'oe yanam on tisi ba ka li mɛ zu'oe, ka banɛ pɔɔd la yanam on tisi ba bi'ela mɛn. Ya ya'a maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la ka li gaŋ si'eli tis sɔ', li na aan o din. Ba na diti ba faar ka li dɔlli ba yaanam dɔɔd pʋʋri an si'em la.

english_verse: If you don't force out all the people there, they will be like splinters in your eyes and thorns in your back. They will always be trouble for you,
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a pʋ kad buudzʋna la yisɛ, banɛ ka ya bas la na kilim titanbin'isi ya nini ni nɛ gɔn'ɔsi ya niŋgbina ni. Ba na daami ya teŋ kanɛ ka ya ye ya zin'in la bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: and I will treat you as severely as I planned on treating them.
translation_verse: Ka man gban'e ye m niŋi ba si'em la, m tiaki niŋi ya.’”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel that their land in Canaan would have the following borders:
translation_verse: o yɛlim Israel dim la ye, “Ya ya'a kpɛn' Keenan, teŋ kanɛ ka m ye m tisi ya ka ya sʋ'oe li la, li na mɔr titɔndbama:

english_verse: The southern border will be the Zin Desert and the northwest part of Edom. This border will begin at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ya dagɔbʋg baba la na kpanb nɛ Zin sian'anr la dɔlis Edom teŋ titɔndig la. Li ya-nya'aŋ baba la na pin'il nɛ atɛuk linɛ buon ye Yaarim Tɛuk la naarin,

english_verse: It will go west from there, but will turn southward to include Scorpion Pass, the village of Zin, and the town of Kadesh-Barnea. From there, the border will continue to Hazar-Addar and on to Azmon.
translation_verse: lɔ'ɔŋi keŋ zin'ikanɛ buon Akirabim Suor la, gaadi paae Zin lɛb dagɔbʋg baba Kades Banɛa, ka gaadi paae Hazaradar lɔ'ɔŋi keŋ Azimon teŋin.

english_verse: It will run along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Zin'ikanɛ ka li yuki tɔ'ɔŋ kɔlbil linɛ bɛ Egipt teŋ titɔndigin la keŋ naae atɛukʋn la sa.

english_verse: The western border will be the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: “Ya-tuona baba titɔndig la na dɛn'ɛn Atɛuk Tita'ar nɔɔrin la. Ani na an titɔndig kan bɛn.

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean, then continue eastward to Mount Hor.
translation_verse: “Ya-datiuŋ baba titɔndig la na dɔlis ala naam atɛukʋn la paae Hor zuorin la tituaa.

english_verse: After that, it will run to Lebo-Hamath and across to Zedad, which is the northern edge of your land.
translation_verse: Ka mɛ naam Hor zuorin la paae Lebo-Hamat. Li na keŋ ala paae Zedad,

english_verse: From Zedad, the border will continue east to Ziphron and end at Hazar-Enan.
translation_verse: ka mɔr ala ti paae Zifiron ka naae Hazarenan teŋin. Nɛ' na an ya-datiuŋ la titɔndig bɛn.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin at Hazar-Enan in the north, then run south to Shepham,
translation_verse: “Ya-nya'aŋ titɔndig la na pin'il Hazarenan ti paae Siefam teŋin.

english_verse: and on down to Riblah on the east side of Ain. From there, it will go south to the eastern hills of Lake Galilee,
translation_verse: Titɔndig la na dɔl ala naam Siefam paae Dibila ya-nya'aŋ baba lɛbid Ayin teŋ baba ka keŋ ala zuligi paae Galile bɛuŋ linɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ baba la.

english_verse: then follow the Jordan River down to the north end of the Dead Sea. The land within those four borders will belong to you.
translation_verse: Titɔndig la na dɔlis ala zuligi keŋ Joodan kɔldaugin, dɔlis hali ti paae atɛuk linɛ buon ye Yaarim Tɛuk la. “Nɛ' na aan ya teŋ nɛ li titɔndisi gilig zin'ig wʋsa.”

english_verse: Then Moses told the people, “You will receive the land inside these borders. It will be yours, but the Lord has commanded you to divide it among the nine and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Moses da yɛl Israel dim la ye, “Maalimi bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm pʋdigi teŋ kaŋa sʋ'ʋgi li. Zugsɔb la tis nɔɔr ye ya nɔki tis dɔɔd awai nɛ pʋsʋk la,

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh have already been given their land
translation_verse: bɔzugɔ Reuben nɛ Gad dɔɔd nɛ Manase dɔɔg la pʋsʋk pʋn di'e ba faar sa, ka li dɔlisi ba wʋsa saamnam ya'.

english_verse: across from Jericho, east of the Jordan River.” The Leaders Who Will Divide the Land
translation_verse: Dɔɔd ayi' nɛ pʋsʋk bama pʋn di'e ba pʋʋr Joodan baba linɛ lɛbisid ya-nya'aŋ ka naan Jeriko teŋin lɛbid winnigi tansid zin'isi'a la.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye,

english_verse: “Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun will divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Elieza onɛ an maanmaan la nɛ Josua onɛ an Nun biig la na pʋdig teŋ la tisi ya.

english_verse: One leader from each tribe will help them,
translation_verse: Yisim tuongat yinne dɔɔg wʋsa sʋʋgin ka ba sʋŋi pʋdig teŋ la.

english_verse: These are the men the Lord commanded to help Eleazar and Joshua divide the land for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Dap bama ka Zugsɔb la da tisi ba nɔɔr ye ba pʋdig teŋ la tis Israel dim la Keenan teŋin la.

english_verse: to say to them: When you receive your tribal lands, you must give towns and pastures to the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim Israel dim la ye ba yisim teŋ kanɛ aan ba faar la tempʋsieba tis Levi dɔɔg la dim ka ba zin'in ani. Ka tisi ba sian'anr linɛ ka ba na kemmi ba bʋnkɔnbid.

english_verse: That way, the Levites will have towns to live in and pastures for their animals.
translation_verse: Lin na kɛ ka ba mɔr tɛɛns la zin' ka mɛ mɔr sian'anr linɛ gilig tɛɛns la ka ba niigi nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ bɛ wʋsa na ɔnbid ani.

english_verse: The pasture around each of these towns must be in the shape of a square, with the town itself in the center. The pasture is to measure
translation_verse: Teŋ la yiŋ la makimi wʋʋ nɔbir makir tusa atan', lɛbis ya-nya'aŋ nɛ ya-tuona nɛ dagɔbʋg nɛ datiuŋʋ gilig, ka tempʋʋg la bɛ teŋsʋk. Ba na nɔk zin'ibama ka li aan ba kɔnbid kem zin'ig.

english_verse: Six of the towns you give them will be Safe Towns where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection. But you will also give the Levites
translation_verse: Tembanɛ ka ya tis Levi dim la ni, tɛɛns ayuobʋ na lieb suak zin'is, ka sɔ' ya'a kʋ o tiraan on zɔɔ keŋ ani. Ka pɛ'ɛsi ba tɛɛns pisnaasi nɛ ayi' la'am pɛ'ɛs nɛ ba kɔnbid kem zin'is la.

english_verse: Since the towns for the Levites must come from Israel's own tribal lands, the larger tribes will give more towns than the smaller ones. The Safe Towns (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Tembanɛ ka ya ye ya tis Levi dɔɔg la yit Israel dim faar la ni la anɛ dɔɔg wʋsa na tis lin nar si'em. Nɔkimi bɛdegʋ yi banɛ mɔr bɛdegʋ ni, amaa ka lɛɛ nɔk bi'ela yi banɛ mɔr bi'ela la ni.” Tembanɛ an suak zin'is la yɛla

english_verse: by one of the victim's relatives. He will take revengefor his relative's death as soon as he finds you.
translation_verse: Li nar ye onɛ kpi la nid tan-tan na kʋʋ o yɔ sam la, o ya'a sia'al onɛ kʋʋ o nid la.

english_verse: There are to be six of these Safe Towns,
translation_verse: Tembama ayuobʋ la na liebi ya suak zin'is.

english_verse: The Lord then told Moses
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la da lɛn yɛl Moses ye,

english_verse: to tell the people of Israel: After you have crossed the Jordan River and are settled in Canaan,
translation_verse: “Yɛlim Israel dim la ye ba ya'a lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan n kpɛn' Keenan teŋin la

english_verse: choose Safe Towns, where a person who has accidentally killed someone can run for protection.
translation_verse: ban gaŋ teŋ sieba ka li lieb suak zin'is, ka sɔ' ya'a kʋʋ o tiraan ka li ka' ye o maal nɛ pɔn'ɔsim on zɔɔ keŋ ani.

english_verse: If the victim's relatives think it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of these Safe Towns for protection and not be killed before a trial is held.
translation_verse: Ani ka o na su'a ka ba kʋ kʋʋ o yɔ sam ka sariakatib la nam pʋ kad o saria.

english_verse: They will be places of protection for anyone who lives in Israel and accidentally kills someone. Laws about Murder and Accidental Killing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Tembama ayuobʋ la na an suak zin'igi tis Israel dim nɛ saam nɛ nimbanɛ wʋsa bɛɛ ba san'an, ka sɔ' ya'a kʋʋ o tiraan ka li ka' pɔn'ɔsim na tun'e zɔɔ keŋ su'a ani.

english_verse: Suppose you hit someone with a piece of iron or a large stone or a dangerous wooden tool. If that person dies, then you are a murderer and must be put to death
translation_verse: bɛɛ sɔ' ya'a zanl daug bʋn linɛ na nyaŋi kʋ nid, ka nɔki nwɛ' sɔ' ka o kpi, o mɛ anɛ ninkʋʋd, on sɔb li sʋm ye ba kʋʋ o mɛn.

english_verse: Or suppose you get angry and kill someone by pushing or hitting or by throwing something. You are a murderer and must be put to death by one of the victim's relatives.
translation_verse: bɛɛ o sʋnfʋ duoe ka o kunbil o nu'ugʋ nwɛ' o ka o kpi, o mɛ anɛ ninkʋʋd, on sɔb li sʋm ye ba kʋʋ o mɛn; onɛ kpi la nid tan-tan ya'a sia'al o, li anɛ ye o kʋʋ o.

english_verse: But if you are not angry and accidentally kill someone in any of these ways, the townspeople must hold a trial and decide if you are guilty.
translation_verse: banɛ kad saria la na pian' li yɛla onɛ kpi la nid tan-tan la nɛ onɛ kʋʋ o la san'an dɔl wʋʋ zi'elbama yɛl si'em la:

english_verse: If they decide that you are innocent, you will be protected from the victim's relative and sent to stay in one of the Safe Towns until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Banɛ la'as ye ba kad saria la na gur onɛ kʋ la sʋ'ʋŋa ka zii o lɛb suak teŋin, on daa zɔɔ keŋ si'el la. O na bɛɛ ani hali ka maanmaan onɛ ka ba bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam linɛ an kasi niŋ o zugin la ti kpi.

english_verse: and are killed by the victim's relative, he cannot be punished for killing you.
translation_verse: ka onɛ kpi la nid tan-tan nyɛɛ o teŋ la yiŋ, o tun'e kʋʋ o ka li ka' taalɛ.

english_verse: You must stay inside the town until the high priest dies; only then can you go back home.
translation_verse: Asɛɛ ninkʋʋd la bɛ suak zin'ig la, hali ka maanmaan kpɛɛm la ti kpi: li anɛ maanmaan kpɛɛm la ya'a ti kpi ka o nyaan lɛb o mɛŋ yin.

english_verse: The community of Israel must always obey these laws.
translation_verse: Yɛlbama na bɛ tis yanam nɛ zʋmaana banɛ na dɔlli ya nya'aŋ na, yanamɛ bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa.

english_verse: Death is the penalty for murder. But no one accused of murder can be put to death unless there are at least two witnesses to the crime.
translation_verse: Sɔ' ya'a kʋʋ o tiraan ka kasɛtib bɛ, li sʋm ye ba kʋʋ o mɛn. Amaa kasɛta dim la ya'a pʋ paae babayi' yanam mid ka ya kʋʋ o sɔba.

english_verse: You cannot give someone money to escape the death penalty; you must pay with your own life!
translation_verse: Da di'e yɔɔd onɛ kʋ nid ka li nar yɛ o kpi san'an ka bas oo. Bɔzugɔ li anɛ tilas ye o kpi.

english_verse: And if you have been proven innocent of murder and are living in a Safe Town, you cannot pay to go back home; you must stay there until the high priest dies.
translation_verse: Da di'e yɔɔd onɛ zɔɔ keŋ suak zin'igin ka tis o suor ye o lɛbi kuli o yin, ka maanmaan la nam pʋ kpii.

english_verse: One day the family leaders from the Gilead clan of the Manasseh tribe went to Moses and the other family leaders of Israel
translation_verse: Gilead onɛ da an Makir biig ka an Manase yaaŋ, ka Manase an Josef biig la dɔɔg kpɛɛmnam da kɛn Moses nɛ Israel kpɛɛm sieba san'an na.

english_verse: and said, “Sir, the Lord has said that he will show what land each tribe will receive as their own. And the Lord has commanded you to give the daughters of our relative Zelophehad the land that he would have received.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la da tisif nɔɔr ye fʋ maalim bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm pʋdig teŋ la tis Israel dim la, ka yɛlif ye fʋ nɔkimi ti ba'abiig Zelofehad faar la tis o bipumis la.

english_verse: But if they marry men from other tribes of Israel, the land they receive will become part of that tribe's inheritance and will no longer belong to us.
translation_verse: Ka gɔsima, li ya'a nwɛnɛ ba yinɛ kul dɔɔd sieba dap, ba na nɔk faar la tinam dɔɔgin la keŋ lɔ'ɔŋ dɔɔd banɛ ka ba kul la ni. Ka li pa'al ye tinam faar la sieba linɛ ka ba pʋdigi tisi ti la na gaad.

english_verse: Even when land is returned to its original owner in the Year of Celebration, we will not get back Zelophehad's land—it will belong to the tribe into which his daughters married.”
translation_verse: Israel dim yʋʋm pisnu malʋŋ di'ema saŋa ka si'el wʋsa lɛbidi li zin'igin la ya'a paae, ba faar la na keŋ paas nimbanɛ ka ba kul la san'an, ka ba nɔki ba mɔrim la yii ti yaanam faarin la.”

english_verse: So Moses told the people that the Lord had said: These men from the Manasseh tribe are right.
translation_verse: Ka nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la da yɛl si'em la, Moses da tis Israel dim la nɔkaŋa: “Josef yaas la yɛt si'el la anɛ sida.

english_verse: I will allow Zelophehad's daughters to marry anyone, as long as those men belong to one of the clans of the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tis nɔsi'a zaŋi ken Zelofehad bipumis la nwa': ‘Ba tun'e kul ban bɔɔd sɔ' wʋsa, o sɔb ya'a aan ba saam dɔɔg la nid.

english_verse: Tribal land must not be given to another tribe—it will remain the property of the tribe that received it.
translation_verse: Israel faar si'a kʋ naam dɔsi'a keŋ dɔsi'a, bɔzugɔ Israel nid wʋsa na mɔr faar kanɛ ka o di'e yii o yaanamin la.

english_verse: In the future, any daughter who inherits land must marry someone from her own tribe. Israel's tribal land is never to be passed from one tribe to another.
translation_verse: Faar si'a kʋ naam dɔɔg si'a lɔ'ɔŋ dɔɔg si'aa, bɔzugɔ Israel dɔɔg wʋsa anɛ ye ba kpɛm mɔr ban di'e faar si'a la.’”

english_verse: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah the daughters of Zelophehad obeyed the Lord and married their uncles' sons
translation_verse: Zelofehad biis la yʋda da anɛ Mahla nɛ Tiza nɛ Hogila nɛ Milika nɛ Noa; ka ba da kul nɛ ba saam ba'abiis la biribis.

english_verse: and remained part of the Manasseh tribe. So their land stayed in their father's clan.
translation_verse: Ala ka ba da kul sidib Manase onɛ an Josef biig la dɔɔgin, ka ba mɔrim la kpɛlimmi ba saam dɔɔg la ni.

english_verse: These are the laws that the Lord gave to Moses and the Israelites while they were camped in the lowlands of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Zi'elbama nɛ nɔbama ka Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses ye o tis Israel dim la Moab zin'ikanɛ an sassi ka bɛ Joodan lɔm lɛbisid Jeriko tempʋʋg baba la.

english_verse: Now, turn around and go back into the desert by way of Red Sea Road.
translation_verse: Amaa ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yanam, fɛndigim kpa' sian'anr la dɔl Atɛuk Zɛn'ug suor la.”

english_verse: People of Israel, when we were in our camp at Mount Sinai, the Lord our God told us: You have stayed here long enough.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am da yɛli ti Horeb zuorin la ye, ‘Ya yuug zuokaŋa zug hali; li sia'ala ala.

english_verse: Leave this place and go into the land that belongs to the Amorites and their neighbors the Canaanites. This land includes the Jordan River valley, the hill country, the western foothills, the Southern Desert, the Mediterranean seacoast, the Lebanon Mountains, and all the territory as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Duomini ya la'asʋg zin'igin la ka keŋ tuon zuor teŋ dinɛ an Amor dim sʋ'ʋlim la ni, nɛ nimbanɛ kpi'e nɛ banɛ bɛ Araba teŋin la nɛ zuoya teŋ nɛ kʋkʋna teŋ linɛ bɛ li tuon la nɛ Negef teŋ la nɛ teŋ kanɛ pʋ lal nɛ atɛuk nɔɔr la, la'an nɛ Keenan nɛ Lebanon tɛɛns wʋsa, hali ti paae Kɔldatita'ar dinɛ an Efiritis la.

english_verse: I give you this land, just as I promised your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Now you must go and take the land. Leaders Were Appointed (Exodus
translation_verse: Gɔsima, m zaŋ teŋ kaŋa tisi ya. Kem kpɛn' ka sʋ'ʋgini li, ka teŋ kan la ka mam Zugsɔb la, da pɔɔ zi'el ye m na tisi ya yaab Abraham nɛ Isaak nɛ Jakob nɛ ba yaas wʋsa banɛ na ti duoe ba nya'aŋ na la.’”
