english_verse: One day, Joshua was near Jericho when he saw a man standing some distance in front of him. The man was holding a sword, so Joshua walked up to him and asked, “Are you on our side or on our enemies' side?”
translation_verse: Josua da bɛ Jeriko tempʋʋg baba la, o da ʋk o nini gɔsi nyɛ dau sɔ' ka o mɔr zaba sʋ'ʋg o nu'uginɛ zi'e o tuon. Ka Josua keŋ paae o, ka yɛl o ye, “Fʋ anɛ ti nid bɛɛ ti zabdimtaas la yinne?”

english_verse: “Neither,” he answered. “I am here because I am the commander of the Lord's army.” Joshua fell to his knees and bowed down to the ground. “I am your servant,” he said. “Tell me what to do.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Ayei, m kena ye m gaad Zugsɔb tanp la tuon.” Ka Josua da igin teŋin na'as o ka yɛl ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, bɔ ka fʋ ye fʋ pa'ali ma?”

english_verse: “Take off your sandals,” the commander answered. “This is a holy place.” So Joshua took off his sandals.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Tanp Tuongat la lɛbis ye, “Pidigimi fʋ ta'ada la, ka fʋn zi'e si'el la anɛ kasi.” Ka Josua pidigi li.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Jericho had been locking the gates in their town wall because they were afraid of the Israelites. No one could go out or come in.
translation_verse: Jeriko tempʋʋg zaŋguom za'anɔya la da yɔnɛ kpar kiŋ-kiŋ Israel dim la yɛla. Sɔ'ɔsɔ da pʋ nyaŋidi yit bɛɛ kpɛn'ɛda.

english_verse: Take along the sacred chest and tell seven priests to walk in front of it, carrying trumpets. But on the seventh day, march slowly around the town seven times while the priests blow their trumpets.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka maanmaanniba ayɔpɔi mɔr na'atana bɛ Nɔnaar Daka la tuon. Ka daba ayɔpɔi daar la, ya na gilig teŋ la nɔɔr ayɔpɔi ka maanmaannib la piebidi ba na'atana la.

english_verse: Then the priests will blast on their trumpets, and everyone else will shout. The wall will fall down, and your soldiers can go straight in from every side.
translation_verse: Ka ya ya'a ti wʋm ka ba pieb na'atana la ka li yuug hali, ka sɔ' wʋsa wʋmi li, ba wʋsa kaasim kuŋ ka teŋ la zaŋguoma na lu, ka zabzabidib la wʋsa nyaŋi kpɛn' teŋin la.”

english_verse: Joshua called the priests together and said, “Take the chest and tell seven priests to carry trumpets and march ahead of it.”
translation_verse: Ka Josua buol maanmaannib la yɛli ba ye, “Zaŋimi Nɔnaar Daka la ka ya nidib ayɔpɔi bɛɛ li tuon ka mɔr na'atana.”

english_verse: They obeyed Joshua's orders and carried the chest once around the town before returning to camp for the night.
translation_verse: Ka o kɛ ka ba zaŋ Nɔnaar Daka la gilig teŋ la nɔɔr yinne ka lɛbi ba la'asʋg zin'igin la digin.

english_verse: On the seventh day, the army got up at daybreak. They marched slowly around Jericho the same as they had done for the past six days, except on this day they went around seven times.
translation_verse: Ka daba ayɔpɔi daar la ka ba isig bɛkɛungʋ keŋ gilig teŋ la nɔɔr ayɔpɔi. Dabiskaŋa ma'aa ka ba gilig nɔɔr ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: Then the priests blew the trumpets, and Joshua yelled: Get ready to shout! The Lord will let you capture this town.
translation_verse: Linɛ da paas ayɔpɔi la maanmaannib la da piebi ba na'atana la, ka Josua yɛl o nidib la ye, “Kuusimi, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la zaŋ teŋ la tisi ya!

english_verse: But you must destroy it and everything in it, to show that it now belongs to the Lord. The woman Rahab helped the spies we sent, so protect her and the others who are inside her house. But kill everyone else in the town.
translation_verse: San'ami teŋ la nɛ linɛ wʋsa bɛɛ ani ka li an maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la. Ya'a ka' Rahab onɛ an pu'agɔɔndir nɛ o yidim la ma'aa ka ya na basɛ, bɔzugɔ o daa su'a ti nimbanɛ daa keŋ labis ye ba vɛɛns teŋ la.

english_verse: The silver and gold and everything made of bronze and iron belong to the Lord and must be put in his treasury. Be careful to follow these instructions, because if you see something you want and take it, the Lord will destroy Israel. And it will be all your fault.
translation_verse: Ka linɛ wʋsa an sanlima nɛ anzurifa nɛ kʋnt anɛ Zugsɔb la din, li anɛ ye ya zaŋi li niŋ Zugsɔb la ligidi suak zin'igin.”

english_verse: The priests blew their trumpets again, and the soldiers shouted as loud as they could. The walls of Jericho fell flat. Then the soldiers rushed up the hill, went straight into the town, and captured it.
translation_verse: Maanmaannib la pieb na'atana la ka nidib la wʋm la, ba wʋsa maali tʋkpiidʋg ka zaŋguoma la lu. Ka zabzabidib la wʋsa paam suor zin'ig wʋsa kpɛn' teŋin la zabi nyaŋi li.

english_verse: After Jericho was destroyed, Joshua warned the people, “Someday a man will rebuild Jericho, but the Lord will put a curse on him, and the man's oldest son will die when he starts to build the town wall. And by the time he finishes the wall and puts gates in it, all his children will be dead.”
translation_verse: Saŋa kan la, Josua da yɛl nɔɔri zi'el ye, “Ninkanɛ wʋsa ye o maligim mɛ' Jeriko teŋ la, Zugsɔb la kaanb bɛ'ɛd bɛ ninkan zugin. Onɛ wʋsa ye o dɛŋi ɛɛnb teŋ la ɛɛnbir na kɔ'ɔŋ o biribiŋ kpɛɛm, ka onɛ mɛ ye o mɛɛ li za'anɔɔr la naae na kɔ'ɔŋ o bikpaanr.”

english_verse: The Lord helped Joshua in everything he did, and Joshua was famous everywhere in Canaan.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la da bɛ nɛ Josua ka o yʋ'ʋr yi teŋ la wʋsa ni.

english_verse: The Lord had said that everything in Jericho belonged to him. But Achan from the Judah tribe took some of the things from Jericho for himself. And so the Lord was angry with the Israelites, because one of them had disobeyed him.
translation_verse: Amaa Israel dim la da ki'is o nɔɔri zaŋi ken la'abanɛ an Zugsɔb din la. Akan onɛ da an Karmi biig ka Karmi an Zimiri biig ka on mɛ an Zera biig ka an Juda dɔɔg nid la da zu la'ad la sieba. Ka Zugsɔb sʋnf duoe nɛ Israel dim la.

english_verse: Joshua and the leaders of Israel tore their clothes and put dirt on their heads to show their sorrow. They lay facedown on the ground in front of the sacred chest until sunset.
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ Israel dim kpɛɛmnam la sʋʋnr san'am ka ba vanbin teŋ Zugsɔb la Nɔnaar Daka la tuon, ka digin ani ti paae zaam, ka bugu ba zut nɛ uusʋg ye li pa'ali ba sʋnsa'aŋ.

english_verse: Then Joshua said: Our Lord, did you bring us across the Jordan River just so the Amorites could destroy us? This wouldn't have happened if we had agreed to stay on the other side of the Jordan.
translation_verse: Ka Josua yɛl ye, “Zugsɔba, fʋnɛ sʋ'oe si'el wʋsa linɛ bɛ, bɔ ka fʋ mɔri ti lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la na? Fʋ ye fʋ zaŋi ti tis Amor dim la nɛ ka ba san'ami tii? Ti ya'a daa mi'in ka siaki kpɛlimin Joodan lɔ'ɔm la, li naan kʋ sɔn'ɔnɛɛ?

english_verse: I don't even know what to say to you, since Israel's army has turned and run from the enemy.
translation_verse: M Zugsɔba, m na yɛl ye bɔ, Israel dataas la yʋ'ʋn nyaŋi ba ka fɛndigi zɔ si'em la?

english_verse: Everyone will think you weren't strong enough to protect your people. Now the Canaanites and everyone else who lives in the land will surround us and wipe us out.
translation_verse: Keenan dim nɛ banɛ wʋsa bɛ teŋin la ya'a wʋmi li yɛla, ba na giligi ti kʋʋ ti wʋsa! Ka fʋ na niŋ wala gu' ka fʋ girima la kʋ yi?”

english_verse: The Lord answered: Stop lying there on the ground! Get up!
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbisi yɛl Josua ye, “Duom zi'en! Bɔ ka fʋ vanb teŋinɛ anwana?

english_verse: I said everything in Jericho belonged to me and had to be destroyed. But the Israelites have kept some of the things for themselves. They stole from me and hid what they took. Then they lied about it.
translation_verse: Israel tʋmnɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd ka ki'is man zi'el nɔsi'a ye ba dɔl la. Ba zaŋ la'abanɛ ka ba naan san'amin la ye li aan ba mɛŋ din. Ba zuu ba nɛ, ka ma' ye li anɛ ba mɛŋ din.

english_verse: What they stole was supposed to be destroyed, and now Israel itself must be destroyed. I cannot help you anymore until you do exactly what I have said. That's why Israel turns and runs from its enemies instead of standing up to them.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka Israel dim pʋ nyaŋi zab nɛ ba dataas la ka fɛndigi zɔ la. Ba zɔya ka li anɛ banɛ bɔ san'auŋʋ tisi ba mɛŋ. M kʋ lɛm bɛ nɛ ba ya'asɛ, ya'a ka' ba san'am la'abanɛ ka m yɛli ba ye ba da zaŋ laa.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel, “Tomorrow you will meet with the Lord your God, so make yourselves acceptable to worship him. The Lord says that you have taken things that should have been destroyed. You won't be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of those things.
translation_verse: “Duom maal nidib la ka ba an nyain. Yɛlimi ba ye ba maalimi ba mɛŋ nyain gur bɛkanɛ nied la; bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛt si'eli nwa': La'abanɛ ka m yɛli ba ye ba san'am bas la bɛɛ ba san'an. Ba kʋ nyaŋi zab nɛ ba dataas la, ya'a ka' ba yis la'ad la nɛ.

english_verse: “Tomorrow morning everyone must gather near the place of worship. You will come forward tribe by tribe, and the Lord will show which tribe is guilty. Next, the clans in that tribe must come forward, and the Lord will show which clan is guilty. The families in that clan must come, and the Lord will point out the guilty family. Finally, the men in that family must come,
translation_verse: Yɛlimi ba ye bɛog bɛogʋn ban yii zi'en dɔɔg-dɔɔg; ka dɔkanɛ ka m gaŋ la, dɔkan dim na yina zi'en tuŋ-tuŋ, ka tuŋ kanɛ ka m gaŋ la na yi tuon na zi'en yir-yir; ka yir kanɛ ka m gaŋ la na yi tuon na zi'en dau yinne-yinne.

english_verse: and the Lord will show who stole what should have been destroyed. That man must be put to death, his body burned, and his possessions thrown into the fire. He has done a terrible thing by breaking the sacred agreement that the Lord made with Israel.”
translation_verse: Ka ninkanɛ ka ba gban'e o ka o mɔr la'abanɛ ka ba zaŋi pɛsig la, ba na nyu'oe on nɛ o yidim nɛ on mɔr si'el wʋsa bugum. Bɔzugɔ o mɔr nyan tita'ari kɛn Israel dimin na, ka ki'isi m nɔɔr.”

english_verse: Joshua got up early the next morning and brought each tribe to the place of worship, where the Lord showed that the Judah tribe was guilty.
translation_verse: Ka Josua daa duoe bɛkɛung asuba ka kɛ ka Israel dim la yi tuon na dɔɔg-dɔɔg, ka ba da gaŋ Juda dɔɔg.

english_verse: Then Joshua brought the clans of Judah to the Lord, and the Lord showed that the Zerah clan was guilty. One by one he brought the leader of each family in the Zerah clan to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Zabdi's family was guilty.
translation_verse: Ka o mɔr Juda dim la yi tuon na ka ba gɔsi ba tuŋ-tuŋ, ka gaŋ Zera tuŋ. Ka o mɔr Zera tuŋ la yi tuon na, ka gɔsi ba yir-yir, ka gaŋ Zimiri yidim.

english_verse: Finally, Joshua brought each man in Zabdi's family to the Lord, and the Lord showed that Achan was the guilty one.
translation_verse: Ka o mɔr Zimiri yidimi yi tuon na ka ba gɔsi ba yinne-yinne ka gaŋ Akan onɛ an Karmi biig ka an Zimiri yaaŋ la.

english_verse: “Achan,” Joshua said, “the Lord God of Israel has decided that you are guilty. So tell me what you did, and don't try to hide anything.”
translation_verse: Ka Josua yɛl o ye, “M dakɔɔnrɛ, tisim Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la girima ka na'as o. Yɛlimim nannanna fʋn maal si'el; da su'a li nɛ mam.”

english_verse: “It's true,” Achan answered. “I sinned and disobeyed the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Akan lɛbis ye, “Asida, mam tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔg Israel Wina'am. Mam maal si'eli nwa':

english_verse: They brought them back and put them in front of the sacred chest, so Joshua and the rest of the Israelites could see them.
translation_verse: Ba da zaŋi ba yi Fuug Sʋgʋr la ni na ka mɔri keŋ Josua nɛ Israel dim la san'anɛ digil Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: Then everyone took Achan and the things he had stolen to Trouble Valley. They also took along his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys, and sheep, his tent, and everything else that belonged to him.
translation_verse: Josua nɛ Israel dim la da gban'e Akan ka zaŋ anzurifa nɛ fuug nɛ sanlima la nɛ Akan biribis nɛ bipumis nɛ o niigi nɛ bʋmis nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ o Fuug Sʋgʋr la nɛ o mɔrim wʋsa mɔri ba keŋ bɔn'ɔg linɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Akor Bɔn'ɔg la.

english_verse: Joshua said, “Achan, you caused us a lot of trouble. Now the Lord is paying you back with the same kind of trouble.” The people of Israel then stoned to death Achan and his family. They made a fire and burned the bodies, together with what Achan had stolen, and all his possessions.
translation_verse: Ka Josua bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ mɔr yɛl kaŋa kɛɛn ti san'an na? Zugsɔb la mɛ yʋ'ʋn na mɔr yɛla kɛɛn fʋ zugin na.” Ka nidib la wʋsa lɔb Akan n kʋʋ o, ka yʋ'ʋn lɔb o yidim la kʋʋ ba ka nyu'oe ba nɛ la'ad la wʋsa.

english_verse: They covered the remains with a big pile of rocks, which is still there. Then the Lord stopped being angry with Israel. That's how the place came to be called Trouble Valley.
translation_verse: Ba da zaŋ kuga diinl o ka li dʋ dʋʋr hali ka nan kpɛm bɛ zina. Lina kɛ ka ba buon zin'ikan la ye, Akor Bɔn'ɔg la. Ka Zugsɔb sʋnf nyaan yʋ'ʋn ma'ae.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't be afraid, and don't be discouraged by what happened at the town of Ai. Take the army and attack again. But first, order part of the army to set up an ambush on the other side of the town. I will help you defeat the king of Ai and his army, and you will capture the town and the land around it. Destroy Ai and kill its king as you did at Jericho. But you may keep the livestock and everything else you want.
translation_verse: Maalimi Ai nɛ ba na'ab la nwɛnɛ yanamɛ da maal Jeriko nɛ ba na'ab si'em la. Amaa nannanna, ya na tun'e zaŋi ba la'ad nɛ ba bʋnkɔbid la sʋ'oe. Kɛl ka zabzabidib la su'a mɔɔgin ka ti yina libig nidib la ka li lidigi ba.”

english_verse: Joshua quickly got the army ready to attack Ai. He chose
translation_verse: ka yɛli ba ye, “Su'ami teŋ la kpikpɛŋ, amaa ka lɛɛ da laligi na ala saa, ka maali siri guri.

english_verse: The rest of the army will come with me and attack near the gate. When the people of Ai come out to fight, we'll run away and let them chase us. They will think we are running from them just like the first time. But when we've let them chase us far enough away,
translation_verse: Ba na kadi ti yi teŋ la yiŋ ka ti pan'asi ba mɔri keŋ lallisa. Ka ba tɛn'ɛs ye ba nyaŋi ti nɛ ka ti zɔt nwɛnɛ ban daa niŋi ti si'em yiigin la.

english_verse: you come out of hiding. The Lord our God will help you capture the town.
translation_verse: Ka ya yʋ'ʋn na yii ya suak zin'igin la na kpɛn nyaŋi ba ka sʋ'ʋg teŋ la. Ya Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la na zaŋ teŋ la tisi ya.

english_verse: Then set it on fire, as the Lord has told us to do. Those are your orders,
translation_verse: Ka ya ya'a nyaŋ teŋ la yanam on nyu'omi li nɛ bugum nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la tisi ya nɔɔr ye ya tʋm si'em la. Nwa' ka m yɛti ya ye ya niŋ.”

english_verse: Early the next morning he got his troops ready to move out, and he and the other leaders of Israel led them to Ai.
translation_verse: Ka bɛogʋ nie la ka Josua duoe la'as zabzabidib la wʋsa ka on nɛ Israel kpɛɛmnam gaad tuonnɛ dɔlli ba keŋ Ai.

english_verse: They set up camp in full view of the town, across the valley to the north.
translation_verse: Ka o dɔl zabzabidib la keŋ li'el teŋ la ka ba la'as taaba digin tempʋʋg la ya-datiuŋ baba, ka bʋmbɔk bɛ ban nɛ Ai teŋsʋk.

english_verse: Now all his troops were in place. Part of the army was in the camp to the north of Ai, and the others were hiding to the west, ready to make a surprise attack. That night, Joshua went into the valley.
translation_verse: Ba da kɛ ka zabzabidib la ti'ebi zi'e ba zin'isin sʋ'ʋŋa. Bam da bɛnɛ ya-datiuŋ ka bam mɛ kpɛlim su'a teŋ la ya-tuona. Ka Josua mɛŋ da sigi gbɛn bʋmbɔkin la yʋ'ʋŋ kan la.

english_verse: Finally, the Lord told Joshua, “Point your sword at the town of Ai, because now I am going to help you defeat it!” As soon as Joshua pointed his sword at the town,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Josua ye, “Zaŋimi fʋ kpan la tiesi kpa' Ai tempʋʋg, ka man zaŋi lii tisif!” Ka Josua niŋ nwɛnɛ on yɛl o si'em la.

english_verse: the soldiers who had been hiding jumped up and ran into the town. They captured it and set it on fire.
translation_verse: Ka on kpɛn ʋk o nu'ug la, nimbanɛ su'a mɔɔgin la da yi tɔ'ɔtɔ na zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' teŋ la pʋʋgin nyaŋi li ka nyu'oe teŋ la bugum.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the other Israelite soldiers had come from the town and attacked the men of Ai from the rear. The Israelites captured the king of Ai and brought him to Joshua. They also chased the rest of the men of Ai into the desert and killed them. The Israelite army went back to Ai and killed everyone there.
translation_verse: Israel dim da kʋ Ai dim banɛ bɛ paalʋ la, nɛ banɛ zɔɔ keŋ sian'arin la, hali ka sɔ' pʋ kpɛlim; ba yʋ'ʋn da lɛb tempʋʋgin la san'ami li nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa.

english_verse: Joshua made sure every building in Ai was burned to the ground. He told his men to kill the king of Ai and hang his body on a tree. Then at sunset he told the Israelites to take down the body, throw it in the gateway of the town, and cover it with a big pile of rocks. translation_verse: O da nɔk Ai na'ab la yul tiig zug ka bas o ani ti paae zaamnɔɔr. Ka lin da sɔbid la, Josua da tis nɔɔr ye ba yisim o niŋgbiŋ la. english_verse: The people of Gibeon had also heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai.
translation_verse: Amaa Gibeon dimi da wʋm Josua niŋ Jeriko nɛ Ai tɛɛns si'em la,

english_verse: So they decided that some of their men should pretend to be messengers to Israel from a faraway country. The men put worn-out bags on their donkeys and found some old wineskins that had cracked and had been sewn back together.
translation_verse: ba da gban'e ye ba pan'as Israel dim la. Ba da gaans kpɛɛm sieba tʋmi ba ka nɔk bɔtkʋda nɛ daam waas banɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm lɔɔ ziili ba bʋmis ka li nwɛnɛ ba yinɛ lallisa na.

english_verse: Their sandals were old and patched, and their clothes were worn out. They even took along some dry and crumbly bread.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da yɛnɛ fukʋda, ka pid ta'adkʋda, ka zaŋ dipɔn'ɔsa paas.

english_verse: Then they went to the Israelite camp at Gilgal, where they said to Joshua and the men of Israel, “We have come from a country that is far from here. Please make a peace treaty with us.”
translation_verse: Ba da keŋ zin'ikanɛ ka Israel dim la la'as ka li bɛ Gilgal teŋin la, ka yɛl Josua nɛ Israel nidib la ye, “Ti yinɛ zin'ikanɛ lal hali na, ka bɔɔd ye ya maal nɔnaar nɛ ti.”

english_verse: We are your servants, and we live far from here. We came because the Lord your God is so famous. We heard what the Lord did in Egypt
translation_verse: Ka ba ma' yɛl o ye, “Ti yinɛ teŋ lalli na, bɔzugɔ ti wʋm Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la yɛla. Ti wʋm linɛ wʋsa ka o niŋ Egipt teŋin la,

english_verse: and what he did to those two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan: King Og of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, and King Sihon of Heshbon.
translation_verse: ka mɛ wʋm on niŋ si'em nɛ Amor teŋ na'anama ayi' banɛ bɛ Joodan kɔldaug nya'aŋ la, banɛ an Na'ab Sihon onɛ da bɛ Hesbon teŋin nɛ Na'ab Og onɛ da bɛ Asitarof teŋin la.

english_verse: Our leaders and everyone who lives in our country told us to meet with you and tell you that all of us are your servants. They said to ask you to make a peace treaty with our people. They told us to be sure and take along enough food for our journey.
translation_verse: Ti kpɛɛmnam nɛ nidib la wʋsa banɛ bɛɛ ti teŋin la yɛli ti ye ti ti'ebim nɛ diib ka kɛɛn ya san'an na, ka yɛli ya ye ti na tʋm tisi ya, ka ya maal nɔnaar nɛ ti.

english_verse: See this dry, crumbly bread of ours? It was hot out of the oven when we packed the food on the day we left our homes.
translation_verse: Gɔsimi ti diib la, tinamɛ daa ti'eb ka yi ye ti tʋ'ʋsi ya la, li daa nan tʋlnɛ. Amaa gɔsimi lin yʋ'ʋn kʋdig ka guunlim si'em.

english_verse: These cracked wineskins were new when we filled them, and our clothes and sandals are worn out because we have traveled so far.
translation_verse: Tinamɛ daa pɛ'ɛl daam waas nwa', ba daa anɛ bʋmpaala, amaa ba yʋ'ʋn aansnɛ. Ti fuud nɛ ti ta'ada mɛ kʋdig nɛ, ti suori wa'am la zug.”

english_verse: The Israelites tried some of the food, but they did not ask the Lord if he wanted them to make a treaty.
translation_verse: Ka Israel nidib la da siaki di'e ba diib bi'ela di ka pʋ bu'os Zugsɔb la li yɛlaa.

english_verse: So Joshua made a peace treaty with the messengers and promised that Israel would not kill their people. Israel's leaders swore that Israel would keep this promise.
translation_verse: Josua da naal nɔɔr nɛ ba ka ye o na kɛ ka ba bɛ nɛ ba nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm. Israel kpɛɛmnam la mɛ da bas nɔɔri tisi ba ye ba na dɔl ban kaanbi zi'el si'em la.

english_verse: A couple of days later, the Israelites found out that these people actually lived in the nearby towns of Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-Jearim. So the Israelites left the place where they had camped and arrived at the four towns two days later.
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim la duoe ye ba keŋ ie nidib la teŋ zin'ig, ka li nɔki ba daba atan' ka ba naan paae ba tempʋʋd la, tɛɛns la da anɛ Gibeon nɛ Kiefira nɛ Beerot nɛ Kiriaf Jiarim.

english_verse: But they did not attack the towns, because the Israelite leaders had sworn in the name of the Lord that they would let these people live. The Israelites complained about their leaders' decision not to attack,
translation_verse: Amaa Israel dim la da pʋ nyaŋi kʋʋ baa bɔzugɔ ba kpɛɛmnam la da maal nɔnaar nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr zug. Ka nidib la da nyɔnnɛ ba kpɛɛmnam la li yɛla.

english_verse: but the leaders reminded them, “We promised these people in the name of the Lord God of Israel that we would let them live, so we must not harm them. If we break our promise, God will punish us. We'll let them live, but we'll make them cut wood and carry water for our people.”
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛmnam la lɛn yɛl ye, “Ti na kɛ ka ba vʋe, amaa ba na nwaad daad ka ziid ku'om tisidi ti nidib la wʋsa.” Ala ka kpɛɛmnam la kaanbʋg la kpɛn zi'e.

english_verse: Joshua told some of his soldiers, “I want to meet with the Gibeonite leaders. Bring them here.” When the Gibeonites came, Joshua said, “You live close to us. Why did you lie by claiming you lived far away?
translation_verse: Josua da buol Gibeon dim la na ka yɛli ba ye, “Bɔ ka ya pan'asi ti ye yanam yinɛ lalli na, ka bɛ kpɛla yamminɛ?

english_verse: So now you are under a curse, and from now on your people will have to send workers to cut wood and carry water for the place of worship.”
translation_verse: Yanamɛ maal bʋnkaŋa la zug, nɔpɔɔr bɛɛ ya zug, lin zaŋ zina ken sa ya na nwaad daad ka ziid ku'om tisid Israel Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la.”

english_verse: The Gibeonites answered, “The Lord your God told his servant Moses that you were to kill everyone who lives here and take their land for yourselves. We were afraid you would kill us, and so we tricked you into making a peace treaty. But we agreed to be your servants,
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis o ye, “Linɛ kɛ ka ti maal anwa la anɛ ban da yɛli ti ye ya Zugsɔb Wina'am la da yɛl Moses ye o nɔkim teŋ kaŋa wʋsa tisi ya, ka san'am bʋnvʋr kanɛ wʋsa bɛɛ ani la. Ka ti vʋm zugʋ daa kɛ ka ti zɔɔ ya dabiem, linɛ kɛ ka ti maal nwa' la.

english_verse: Joshua did not let the Israelites kill the Gibeonites,
translation_verse: Alazug ka Josua da sʋŋi ba ka pʋ siak ka Israel dim la kʋʋ baa.

english_verse: but he did tell the Gibeonites that they would have to be servants of the nation of Israel. They would have to cut firewood and bring it for the priests to use for burning sacrifices on the Lord's altar, wherever the Lord decided the altar would be. The Gibeonites would also have to carry water for the priests. And that is still the work of the Gibeonites.
translation_verse: Amaa nɛ wala, o kɛ ka ba an yammisi nwaad daad ka ziid ku'om tisid Israel dim nɛ zin'ibanɛ ka Zugsɔb la gaŋ ye ba maan malima la. Ala ka ba aɛn hali ti paae zina.

english_verse: King Adonizedek of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured and destroyed the town of Ai, and then killed its king as he had done at Jericho. He also learned that the Gibeonites had signed a peace treaty with Israel.
translation_verse: Na'ab Adoni-Zedek onɛ an Jerusalem na'ab la da wʋm ye Josua nyaŋ Ai ka san'ami li wʋsa ka kʋʋ ba na'ab la nwɛnɛ on da tʋm Jeriko dim nɛ ba na'ab si'em la, ka mɛ wʋm ye Gibeon dim maal nɔnaar nɛ Israel dim ka zin' nɛ ba.

english_verse: This frightened Adonizedek and his people. They knew that Gibeon was a large town, as big as the towns that had kings, and even bigger than the town of Ai had been. And all of the men of Gibeon were warriors.
translation_verse: On wʋm si'em la da kɛnɛ ka dabiem kpɛn' on nɛ o nidib la bɔzugɔ, Gibeon da anɛ teŋ tita'ar nwɛnɛ teŋ titada banɛ mɔr na'anam si'em la. Li mɛ da zu'oe gaad Ai teŋ la ka ba nidib la wʋsa mɛ an zabzabidib.

english_verse: So Adonizedek sent messages to the kings of four other towns: King Hoham of Hebron, King Piram of Jarmuth, King Japhia of Lachish, and King Debir of Eglon. The messages said,
translation_verse: Alazug ka Adoni-Zedek onɛ an Jerusalem na'ab la da sɔs Hoham onɛ an Hebron na'ab nɛ Piram onɛ an Jarimuf na'ab nɛ Jafia onɛ an Lakis na'ab nɛ Debir onɛ an Eglon na'ab la

english_verse: “The Gibeonites have signed a peace treaty with Joshua and the Israelites. Come and help me attack Gibeon!”
translation_verse: ye, “Kemi na sʋŋinim ka m zab nɛ Gibeon dim, ka ba yɛl ye ba maal sumbʋgʋsʋm nɔnaar nɛ Josua nɛ Israel dim la.”

english_verse: the Gibeonites sent a message to the Israelite camp at Gilgal: “Joshua, please come and rescue us! The Amorite kings from the hill country have joined together and are attacking us. We are your servants, so don't let us down. Please hurry!”
translation_verse: Ka Gibeon nidib la da tʋm yɛl Josua nɛ banɛ da bɛ Gilgal teŋin la ye, “Da basi tinam banɛ aan fʋ yammis la! Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ na faaɛn ti. Sʋŋimi ti! Bɔzugɔ Ammon dim na'anam banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna zug la la'asi ba zabzabidib la wʋsa kena ye ba zab nɛ ti.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army, including his best warriors, left Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ka Josua duoe nɛ o zabzabidibi yi Gilgal, la'an nɛ banɛ mi' zaba sʋ'ʋŋa la wʋsa.

english_verse: “Joshua,” the Lord said, “don't be afraid of the Amorites. They will run away when you attack, and I will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Josua ye, “Da kɛ ka dabiem mɔri fɔ! Ka mam nɔki ba niŋi fʋ nu'usin. Hali ba sɔ' kae na nyaŋi zab nɛ fɔ.”

english_verse: Joshua marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon and made a surprise attack on the Amorite camp.
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ o nidib la yi Gilgal n keŋ yʋ'ʋŋ ka pʋ gbisɛ, hali ti libigi ba dataas la.

english_verse: The Lord made the enemy panic, and the Israelites started killing them right and left. They chased the Amorite troops up the road to Beth-Horon and kept on killing them, until they reached the towns of Azekah and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ban da nyɛ Israel dim la, Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka ba ya'am iank hali ka Israel zabzabidib la nyaŋi ba Gibeon teŋin la. Israel dim da kadi ba ka ba zɔɔ dɔl Befihoron, ka kʋʋ ba sieba hali ti paae Azeka nɛ Makeda.

english_verse: And while these troops were going down through Beth-Horon Pass, the Lord made huge hailstones fall on them all the way to Azekah. More of the enemy soldiers died from the hail than from the Israelite weapons.
translation_verse: Ban da zɔti yit Israel dim san'an la, Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka sakuga yi agɔla na luti ba zugin ban da nam bɛ Befihoron nɛ Azeka teŋsʋk la. Sakuga la da lu na kʋ ninsieba la da gaad nimbanɛ ka ba kʋ nɛ zaba sʋ'ʋraad la.

english_verse: The Lord was helping the Israelites defeat the Amorites that day. So about noon, Joshua prayed to the Lord loud enough for the Israelites to hear: “Our Lord, make the sun stop in the sky over Gibeon, and the moon stand still over Aijalon Valley.” So the sun and the moon stopped and stood still until Israel defeated its enemies. This poem can be found in The Book of Jashar. The sun stood still and didn't go down for about a whole day.
translation_verse: Ka winnig la sid zi'en anina yim kippi, ka nwadig la mɛ zi'en ani, hali ka ba ti nyaŋi yɔɔ ba dataas la sam. Bʋn linɛ da maal nwa' sɔb Jaser Gbauŋʋn. Winnig la da zi'en kippi ka pʋ luu hali ti paae dabismum bɛn.

english_verse: Never before and never since has the Lord done anything like that for someone who prayed. The Lord was really fighting for Israel.
translation_verse: Dabiskaŋa nwa' buudi nan zi' bɛɛ, ka mɛ kʋ maligim bɛ dabisa banɛ ken naa. Dabiskaŋa ka Zugsɔb sid da wʋm tis ninsaal. Ya'a an sida, Zugsɔb la da zabi tis Israel.

english_verse: After the battle, Joshua and the Israelites went back to their camp at Gilgal. Joshua Kills the Five Enemy Kings
translation_verse: Ka Josua da zaŋ zabzabidib la wʋsa lɛb Gilgal. Israel dim la zabi nyaŋ tɛɛns bɛdegʋ

english_verse: Joshua's soldiers told him, “The five kings have been found in a cave near Makkedah.”
translation_verse: Josua n da wʋm ye ba nyɛɛ ba ka ba su'a tampinlɛma ni la,

english_verse: Joshua answered, “Roll some big stones over the mouth of the cave and leave a few soldiers to guard it.
translation_verse: o da yɛl ye ba biligim kugtitada na ligili li nɔɔr la ka kɛ ka ninsieba guri li.

english_verse: But you and everyone else must keep going after the enemy troops, because they will be safe if they reach their walled towns. Don't let them get away! The Lord our God is helping us get rid of them.”
translation_verse: Ka ye, “Amaa da gu'oe ya dataas la kadibɔ, bɛɛ kɛ ka ba paae ba tɛɛns la kpɛn' ka pɔnsɛ, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la zaŋi ba niŋi ya nu'usin.”

english_verse: So Joshua and the Israelites almost wiped out the enemy soldiers. Only a few safely reached their walled towns.
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ Israel dim la kpɛn kʋʋ ba wʋsa ka ba bi'ela ma'aa nyaŋi zɔɔ paae ba tempʋbanɛ ka ba mɛ' guoma gilig la pɔns.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp at Makkedah, where Joshua was waiting for them. No one around there dared say anything bad about the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ka zabzabidib la wʋsa lɛb Josua san'an nɛ laafi, Makeda teŋin zin'ikanɛ ka ba la'asi bɛ ka zabid la, ka sɔ' pʋ lɛn ya'ae o nɔɔri yɛl Israel si'ela.

english_verse: Joshua told his soldiers, “Now, move the rocks from the entrance to the cave and bring those five kings to me.”
translation_verse: Josua yʋ'ʋn da yɛl ye, “Yɔ'ɔgimi tampinlɛma la nɔɔr, ka mɔri na'anam anu la na tisim.”

english_verse: The soldiers opened the entrance to the cave and brought out the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.
translation_verse: Ka ba yis na'anam la na tis o. Na'anam la daa anɛ: Jerusalem na'ab nɛ Hebron na'ab nɛ Jarimuf na'ab nɛ Lakis na'ab nɛ Eglon na'ab.

english_verse: After Joshua had called the army together, he forced the five kings to lie down on the ground. Then he called his officers forward and told them, “You fought these kings along with me, so put your feet on their necks.” The officers did this,
translation_verse: Ka ban da mɔr na'anam la kɛn Josua san'an na la, o da yɛl zabzabidib tuongatib la ye, “Kemi na zaŋi ya nɔba nɔɔ ba niŋgɔnya!” Ka ba sid kena zaŋi ba nɔba nɔɔ ba niŋgɔnya la.

english_verse: and Joshua continued, “Don't ever be afraid or discouraged. Be brave and strong. This is what the Lord will do to all your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka Josua yɛli ba ye, “Da zɔti dabiem, mɛ da kɛ ka ya giinla siɛn, zi'enimi sʋ'ʋŋa ka kpɛ'ɛŋi ya sʋnf, ka anwana ka Zugsɔb la na niŋidi ya dataas banɛ wʋsa na ti zabid nɛ ya la.”

english_verse: Joshua killed the five kings and told his men to hang each body on a tree. Then at sunset
translation_verse: Ka Josua da kʋ na'anam la ka zaŋi ba ya'al tiis anu zugin, ka basi ba ka ba bɛ tiis la zug hali ti paae zaamnɔɔr.

english_verse: he told some of his troops, “Take the bodies down and throw them into the cave where the kings were found. Cover the entrance to the cave with big rocks.” Joshua's troops obeyed his orders, and those rocks are still there. Joshua Continues the Fighting
translation_verse: Ka zaam ti ma'ae la, Josua da tis o nidib la nɔɔr ka ba zaŋi ba sigis na mɔri ba lɛbis tampinlɛma la ni, zin'ikanɛ ka ba da su'a la. Ka ba zaŋ kugtitada ligil tampinlɛma la nɔɔr la, hali ka li kpɛm bɛ zina.

english_verse: Joshua and his army left Makkedah and attacked the town of Libnah.
translation_verse: Josua nɛ Israel nidib la da yi Makeda teŋinɛ keŋ Libna tempʋʋgin zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: The Lord let them capture the town and its king, and they killed the king and everyone else, just as they had done at Jericho.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb zaŋ teŋ la dim nɛ ba na'ab la niŋ Israel dim nu'usin. Ka Josua kʋ nidib la wʋsa, ka sɔ' da pʋ lɛn kpɛlim ani vʋeya. O da niŋ na'ab la nwɛnɛ on da niŋ Jeriko na'ab si'em la.

english_verse: Joshua then led his army to Lachish, and they set up camp around the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ Israel nidib la da lɛn yi Libna keŋ Lakis tempʋʋgin; ba da la'asi ba zabzabidibi gilig teŋ la zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: and the next day the Lord let them capture the town. They killed everyone, as they had done at Libnah.
translation_verse: Daba ayi' daar la ka Zugsɔb la zaŋ Lakis n tisi ba. Ka Josua da kʋʋ ba wʋsa nwɛnɛ on da niŋ Libna dim si'em la.

english_verse: King Horam of Gezer arrived to help Lachish, but Joshua and his troops attacked and destroyed him and his army.
translation_verse: Horam onɛ da an Giza na'ab la, da kena zabidi sʋŋid Lakis dim la, la'an nɛ wala Josua da nyaŋi kʋʋ o nɛ o zabzabidib la wʋsa, hali ka sɔ' pʋ kpɛlim.

english_verse: From Lachish, Joshua took his troops to Eglon, where they set up camp surrounding the town. They attacked,
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ o nidib la lɛn yii keŋ Eglon tempʋʋginɛ la'as o zabzabidibi zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: captured it that same day, then killed everyone, as they had done at Lachish.
translation_verse: Daakan la ka ba tʋ'ʋs tanpi nyaŋi ba ka san'am banɛ wʋsa da bɛɛ anina la nwɛnɛ ban da niŋ Lakis dim si'em la.

english_verse: They captured the town and the nearby villages, then killed everyone, including the king. They destroyed Hebron in the same way they had destroyed Eglon.
translation_verse: Ba da nyaŋ teŋ la dim, ka kʋ sɔ' wʋsa; teŋ la dim nɛ ba na'ab nɛ ba teŋkpɛmis la nɛ banɛ wʋsa bɛɛ ani. Ba da san'ami li nwɛnɛ Eglon ka ba da san'am si'em la.

english_verse: Joshua and the Israelite army turned and attacked Debir.
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ Israel nidib la wʋsa yʋ'ʋn da fɛndigi zab nɛ Debir dim.

english_verse: They captured the town, and its nearby villages. Then they destroyed Debir and killed its king, together with everyone else, just as they had done with Hebron and Libnah.
translation_verse: Ba da nyaŋ tempʋʋg la nɛ li teŋkpɛmis la, nɛ teŋ la na'abi kʋʋ ba ka san'am si'el wʋsa linɛ bɛɛ ani la ka pʋ kɛ si'ela. Ba da niŋ ala nɛ Debir teŋ dim nɛ ba na'ab nwɛnɛ ban da niŋ Hebron nɛ Libna tɛɛns nɛ ba na'anam si'em la.

english_verse: Joshua captured towns everywhere in the land: In the central hill country and the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert and the region that slopes down toward the Dead Sea. Whenever he captured a town, he would kill the king and everyone else, as the Lord God of Israel had commanded.
translation_verse: Josua da nyaŋ tɛɛns la si'em la, la'an nɛ tembanɛ bɛ kʋkʋna ni la nɛ Negef nɛ zuoya kpikpɛmis nɛ zuoya teŋir nɛ ba na'anam wʋsa, ka sɔ' pʋ kpɛlim vʋeya; ka san'am bʋnvʋr wʋsa nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb, onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Joshua wiped out towns from Kadesh-Barnea to Gaza, everywhere in the region of Goshen, and as far north as Gibeon.
translation_verse: O da nyaŋi ba din pin'il Kades Banɛa ti paae Gaza nɛ Gosen teŋ la wʋsa ti paae Gibeon.

english_verse: King Jabin of Hazor heard about Joshua's victories, so he sent messages to many nearby kings and asked them to join him in fighting Israel. He sent these messages to King Jobab of Madon, the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,
translation_verse: Ka Jabin onɛ an Hazo teŋ na'ab la da wʋm Israel dimi zabi nyaŋi ba dataas si'em la, o da tʋm yɛl Jobab onɛ an Madon teŋ na'ab la nɛ na'anam banɛ bɛ Simiron nɛ Akisiaf la.

english_verse: the kings in the northern hill country and in the Jordan River valley south of Lake Galilee, and the kings in the foothills and in Naphath-Dor to the west.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn tʋm yɛl na'anam banɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ baba kʋkʋna la zug la, nɛ na'anam banɛ bɛ Araba bɔn'ɔgin linɛ bɛ Kinɛref teŋ la ya-tuona la, nɛ Sefela teŋgbauŋʋn la, nɛ Nafofidor teŋgbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: He sent messages to the Canaanite kings in the east and the west, to the Amorite, Hittite, Perizzite, and Jebusite kings in the hill country, and to the Hivite kings in the region of Mizpah, near the foot of Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: O mɛ da tʋm yɛl Keenan nimbanɛ kpi'e Joodan kɔldaug la, nɛ Amor dim nɛ Hitti dim nɛ Perizi dim nɛ Jebus dim banɛ bɛ teŋin la, la'an nɛ Hivi dim banɛ da zin' Hemon zuor linɛ bɛ Misipa teŋin la.

english_verse: The Lord told Joshua: Don't let them frighten you! I'll help you defeat them, and by this time tomorrow they will be dead. When you attack, the first thing you have to do is to cripple their horses. Then after the battle is over, burn their chariots.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Josua ye, “Da zɔti ba dabiem! Ka bɛog anwa saŋa, mam Zugsɔb na kʋʋ ba wʋsa tis Israel dim. Kɛnsimi ba widi la wʋsa gada ka nyu'oe ba tɛrekonam la nɛ bugum.”

english_verse: Joshua and his army made a surprise attack against the enemy camp at Merom Pond
translation_verse: Ka Josua nɛ o nidib la keŋ Merom kɔldaugin la libigi ba zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: and everyone else, then they set the town on fire.
translation_verse: Ba da kʋ sɔ' wʋsa, ka mɛ nyu'oe teŋ la, hali ka bʋnvʋr baa yinne pʋ lɛn kpɛlim.

english_verse: Joshua and his army took control of the northern and southern hill country, the foothills to the west, the Southern Desert, the whole region of Goshen, and the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Josua nɛ o zabzabidib la da nyaŋ tembanɛ wʋsa da bɛ kʋkʋna la ni, nɛ Negef nɛ Gosen tɛɛns la nɛ Araba, hali nɛ Israel teŋ zuoya zug nɛ li sisɛrim la wʋsa.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he wanted the towns in this region destroyed and their people killed without mercy. That's why the Lord made the people in the towns stubborn and determined to fight Israel. The only town that signed a peace treaty with Israel was the Hivite town of Gibeon. The Israelite army captured the rest of the towns in battle.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da digilimi ba sʋnf ka kɛ ka ba zab nɛ Israel dim, linɛ na kɛ ka ba nyaŋi ba, ka kʋʋ ba, ka li kʋ mɔr nimbaanliga, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la da yɛl Moses si'em la.

english_verse: During this same time, Joshua and his army killed the Anakim from the northern and southern hill country. They also destroyed the towns where the Anakim had lived, including Hebron, Debir, and Anab.
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa, Josua da keŋ san'am Anak buudbanɛ an nintitada bɛ kʋkʋna, linɛ bɛ Hebron nɛ Debir nɛ Anab nɛ kʋkʋna banɛ bɛ Juda nɛ Israel la. Josua da kpɛn san'ami ba nɛ, nɛ ba teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: There were not any Anakim left in the regions where the Israelites lived, although there were still some in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
translation_verse: Anak dim la nid sɔ' da pʋ lɛn kpɛlim Israel teŋ la nii, ya'a ka' Gaza nɛ Gaf nɛ Asdod tɛɛnsin la ka nidib kpɛlim bi'ela.

english_verse: That's how Joshua captured the land, just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Joshua divided it up among the tribes. Finally, there was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Josua da nyaŋ teŋ la wʋsa nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl Moses si'em la, ka zaŋi li tis Israel dim ka ba pʋdig, ka dɔɔg wʋsa paam o din. Ka nidib la zin'inɛ vʋ'ʋs, ka pʋ lɛn zab ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Before Moses died, he and the people of Israel had defeated two kings east of the Jordan River. These kings had ruled the region from the Arnon River gorge in the south to Mount Hermon in the north, including the eastern side of the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Israel nidib la da nyaŋi sʋ'oe teŋ la, ka zin'in Joodan nya'aŋ, lin zaŋ Aanon bɔn'ɔgin ti paae Araba bɔn'ɔgin nɛ Hemon zuor la tuon. Ba da nyaŋ na'anam ayi' anina.

english_verse: The first king that Moses and the Israelites defeated was an Amorite, King Sihon of Heshbon. The southern border of his kingdom ran down the middle of the Arnon River gorge, taking in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the gorge. The Jabbok River separated Sihon's kingdom from the Ammonites on the east. Then the Jabbok turned west and became his northern border, so his kingdom included the southern half of the region of Gilead.
translation_verse: Na'ab Sihon da bɛnɛ Hesbon tempʋʋgin. O sʋ'ʋlim la da anɛ Gilead teŋ la pʋsʋk, lin da yi Aroa tempʋʋgin, linɛ bɛ Aanon bɔn'ɔg nɔɔrin la, ka li bɛn dɔl kɔldaug la teŋsʋk la, hali ti paae Yabok bɔn'ɔg, linɛ an Amor dim sʋ'ʋlim titɔndig la.

english_verse: Next, Moses and the Israelites defeated King Og of Bashan, who lived in the town of Ashtaroth part of each year and in Edrei the rest of the year. Og was one of the last of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Ba da la'am nyaŋ Na'ab Og onɛ an Basan na'ab ka bɛ Asitarof nɛ Edire tempʋʋdin la. On ma'aa da kpɛlim Refa dimin la.

english_verse: His kingdom stretched north to Mount Hermon, east to the town of Salecah, and included the land of Bashan as far west as the borders of the kingdoms of Geshur and Maacah. He also ruled the northern half of Gilead.
translation_verse: Hemon zuor la da la'am bɛ nɛ o na'am sʋ'ʋlim la ni, nɛ Saleka, nɛ Basan wʋsa ti paae Gesur nɛ Maaka hali nɛ Gilead pʋsʋk la ti paae Sihon onɛ da an Hesbon na'ab la sʋ'ʋlim titɔndigin.

english_verse: Moses, the Lord's servant, had led the people of Israel in defeating Sihon and Og. Then Moses gave their land to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh.
translation_verse: Moses onɛ da an Zugsɔb tʋmtʋm la nɛ o nidib da nyaŋ na'anam ayi' nwa', ka zaŋi ba teŋ la tis Reuben dim nɛ Gad dim nɛ Manase dɔɔg la pʋsʋk ka li an ba sʋ'ʋlim.

english_verse: Later, Joshua and the Israelites defeated many kings west of the Jordan River, from Baal-Gad in Lebanon Valley in the north to Mount Halak near the country of Edom in the south. This region included the hill country and the foothills, the Jordan River valley and its western slopes, and the Southern Desert. Joshua and the Israelites took this land from the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. Joshua divided up the land among the tribes of Israel. The Israelites defeated the kings of the following towns west of the Jordan River:
translation_verse: Teŋ kanɛ ka ba pʋdig la mɛ la'am paas teŋ kanɛ bɛ kʋkʋna zug, nɛ zuoya teŋir la, nɛ Araba bɔn'ɔg la, nɛ kʋkʋna, nɛ pipiris, nɛ Negef la wʋsa. Teŋ kaŋa da anɛ Hitti dim nɛ Amor dim nɛ Keenan dim nɛ Perizi dim nɛ Hivi dim nɛ Jebus dim teŋ.

english_verse: Many years later, the Lord told Joshua: Now you are very old, but there is still a lot of land that Israel has not yet taken.
translation_verse: Josua yʋ'ʋn da kʋdigya, ka Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, fʋ yʋ'ʋn kʋdig nɛ, amaa tɛɛns bɛdegʋ nan kpɛm bɛ ka ya na sʋ'ʋg.

english_verse: Moses had already given land east of the Jordan River to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Moses onɛ da an Zugsɔb tʋmtʋm la da pʋn zaŋ teŋi tis Reuben nɛ Gad nɛ Manase dɔɔg la pʋsʋk. Li da bɛ nɛ Joodan kɔldaug la nya'aŋ.

english_verse: This region stretched north from the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, and included the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley. It covered the flatlands of Medeba north of Dibon,
translation_verse: Ba sʋ'ʋlim la da paae Aroa teŋ linɛ bɛ Aanon bɔn'ɔg nɔɔrin la, nɛ teŋ linɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔg la teŋsʋk, la'an nɛ paalʋ linɛ gilig Medeba tempʋʋg la ti paae Dibon teŋin,

english_verse: and took in the towns that had belonged to Sihon, the Amorite king of Heshbon. Some of these towns were as far east as the Ammonite border.
translation_verse: nɛ Amor dim Na'ab Sihon onɛ da zin' Hesbon tempʋʋgin ka sʋ'oe tɛɛns la keŋ paae Ammon dim sʋ'ʋlim la titɔndigin,

english_verse: However, the Israelites did not force the people of Geshur and Maacah to leave, and they still live there among the Israelites. Why Moses Did Not Give Land to the Levi Tribe
translation_verse: Amaa Israel dim la da pʋ kad Gesur dim bɛɛ Maaka dim la yisɛ, ka ba kpɛm bɛɛ ba teŋin la hali ti paae zina.

english_verse: Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord God of Israel had told them, “Instead of land, you will receive the sacrifices offered at my altar.” The Land Moses Gave to the Reuben Tribe
translation_verse: Ba da pʋ tis Levi dɔɔg la zin'isi'a ka li aan ba dinnɛ, bɔzugɔ maana banɛ ka ba nyu'odi tisid Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la aan ba faar nwɛnɛ on da kaanbi tisi ba si'em la.

english_verse: Moses gave land to each of the clans in the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Moses da zaŋ teŋ la zin'isi'a tis Reuben dɔɔg la ka li aan ba din.

english_verse: Their land started in the south at the town in the middle of the Arnon River valley, took in the town of Aroer on the northern edge of the valley, and went as far north as the flatlands around Medeba.
translation_verse: Ban sʋ'oe zin'isi'a la anɛ Aroa linɛ bɛ Aanon bɔn'ɔg nɔɔrin la, nɛ teŋ linɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔg la teŋsʋk la, la'an nɛ paalʋ linɛ gilig Medeba tempʋʋg la.

english_verse: The Amorite King Sihon had lived in Heshbon and had ruled the towns in the flatlands. Now Heshbon belonged to Reuben, and so did the following towns in the flatlands: Dibon, Bamoth-Baal, Beth-Baal-Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-Shahar on the hill in the valley, Beth-Peor, Slopes of Mount Pisgah, and Beth-Jeshimoth. Moses defeated Sihon and killed him and the Midianite chiefs who ruled parts of his kingdom for him. Their names were Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ zuoya banɛ bɛ Sihon sʋ'ʋlimin la, o da anɛ Amor dim na'ab ka bɛ Hesbon tempʋʋgin la. Moses da nyaŋ o, la'an nɛ Midian na'anam banɛ bɛ Evi nɛ Rekem nɛ Zur nɛ Hur nɛ Reba. Na'abama wʋsa da gɔsid teŋ la sʋŋid Na'ab Sihon.

english_verse: The Israelites also killed Balaam the son of Beor, who had been a fortuneteller.
translation_verse: Banɛ ka Israel da kʋ la yinne anɛ Balaam onɛ an Beor biig, ka da an ba'abʋgʋd la.

english_verse: This region with its towns and villages was the land for the Reuben tribe, and the Jordan River was its western border. The Land Moses Gave to the Gad Tribe
translation_verse: Reuben sʋ'ʋlim titɔndig da anɛ Joodan kɔldaug nɔɔr la. Tembama ka ba zaŋi tis Reuben dim ka li aan ba din.

english_verse: Moses also gave land to each of the clans in the Gad tribe.
translation_verse: Moses da lɛn zaŋ teŋ la zin'isi'a tis Gad dim ka ba mɛ sʋ'oe li.

english_verse: It included the town of Jazer, and in the Gilead region their territory took in the land and towns as far east as the town of Aroer just west of Rabbah. This was about half of the land that had once belonged to the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ka ban sʋ'oe zin'isi'a la la'am kpanb nɛ Jaza nɛ tɛɛns banɛ bɛ Gilead wʋsa, nɛ Ammon dim teŋ la pʋsʋk hali ti paae Aroa linɛ bɛ Rabba nya'aŋ la.

english_verse: The land given to Gad stretched from Heshbon in the south to Ramath-Mizpeh and Betonim in the north, and even further north to Mahanaim and Lidebor.
translation_verse: Ba teŋ la da pin'il nɛ Hesbon ti paae Ramafimisipe nɛ Betonim linɛ pin'il Mahanam ti paae Debir teŋ titɔndig la.

english_verse: Gad also received the eastern half of the Jordan River valley, which had been ruled by King Sihon of Heshbon. This territory stretched as far north as Lake Galilee, and included the towns of Beth-Haram, Beth-Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ tɛɛns banɛ da bɛ bɔn'ɔgin, wʋʋ Befiharam nɛ Befinimira nɛ Sukot nɛ Zaphon nɛ Na'ab Sihon, onɛ da an Hesbon na'ab la da sʋ'oe zin'ikanɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa, lin naan Joodan kɔldaug la ti paae Galile bɛuŋ la.

english_verse: These regions with their towns and villages were given to the Gad tribe. The Land Moses Gave to Half the Manasseh Tribe
translation_verse: Tembama ka ba zaŋi tis Gad dim la, ka li aan ba din.

english_verse: Moses gave land east of the Jordan River to half of the clans from the Manasseh tribe.
translation_verse: Moses da zaŋ teŋi tis Manase dɔɔg la pʋsʋk nidib ka ba sʋ'oe li.

english_verse: Their land started at Mahanaim and took in the region that King Og of Bashan had ruled, including Ashtaroth and Edrei, the two towns where he had lived. The villages where the Jair clan settled were part of Manasseh's land, and so was the northern half of the region of Gilead. The clans of this half of Manasseh had
translation_verse: Li paas Gilead teŋ la pʋsʋk la'an nɛ Asitarof nɛ Edire linɛ an Na'ab Og onɛ an Basan na'ab la na'am tempʋʋd. Ba da zaŋ nɛ nwa' wʋsa tis Makir onɛ da an Manase biig la tuŋ dim. Ba nidib la pʋsʋkʋ da di'e li.

english_verse: That was how Moses divided up the Moab Plains to the east of Jericho on the other side of the Jordan River, so these two and a half tribes would have land of their own.
translation_verse: Tembama wʋsa ka Moses da pʋdigi tisi ba saŋa kanɛ ka o da bɛ Moab teŋ kanɛ an sassi ka bɛ Joodan nya'aŋ, ka kpa'ad Jeriko tempʋʋg la.

english_verse: But Moses did not give any land to the Levi tribe, because the Lord had promised that he would always provide for them.
translation_verse: Amaa Moses da lɛɛ pʋ zaŋ teŋ la zin'isi'a tis Levi dɔɔg laa. O da yɛli ba ye Israel dim Wina'am la aan ba faar.

english_verse: One day while the Israelites were still camped at Gilgal, Caleb the son of Jephunneh went to talk with Joshua. Caleb belonged to the Kenaz clan, and many other people from the Judah tribe went with Caleb. He told Joshua: You know that back in Kadesh-Barnea the Lord talked to his prophet Moses about you and me.
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka ninsieba yi Juda dɔɔg la nii kɛn Josua san'an Gilgal teŋin na. Kaleb, onɛ an Jefune biig ka yi Kenas dimin la na da yɛl o ye, “Fʋ mi' Zugsɔb la da yɛl si'em tis Moses onɛ an Wina'am nid Kades Banɛa teŋin, ka li anɛ man nɛ fʋn yɛla.

english_verse: The other spies said things that made our people afraid, but I completely trusted the Lord God.
translation_verse: amaa m ba'abiis banɛ da dɔlli keŋ la kpɛn'ɛs nidib la dabiem. Ya'a kpɛlim mam, mam da dɔl Zugsɔb Wina'am la tituaa.

english_verse: The same day I came back, Moses told me, “Since you were faithful to the Lord God, I promise that the places where you went as a spy will belong to you and your descendants forever.”
translation_verse: Daakan la ka Moses da pɔɔ tisim, ye, ‘Keenan teŋgbauŋ kanɛ ka fʋ nɔbir nɔ wʋsa na anɛ fʋn nɛ fʋ yaas la din lin zaŋ zina ken sa, bɔzugɔ fʋ dɔl Zugsɔb Wina'am la nɛ fʋ sʋnf wʋsa.’

english_verse: I'm just as strong today as I was then, and I can still fight as well in battle.
translation_verse: ka nan kpɛm mɔr paŋ zina nwɛnɛ man da an si'em ka Moses tʋmim ka m keŋ la! M nan kpɛm mɔr paŋ kanɛ na yi zaba bɛɛ tʋm tʋʋm si'a wʋsa.

english_verse: So I'm asking you for the hill country that the Lord promised me that day. You were there. You heard the other spies talk about that part of the hill country and the large, walled towns where the Anakim live. But maybe the Lord will help me take their land, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Zaŋim teŋ kanɛ bɛ zuoya ni la tisim, teŋ kan ka Zugsɔb da kaanbi tisim daakan la. Ti da wʋm ye, gandaad buudbanɛ ka ba buon ye Anak dim la bɛɛ ani, ka mɛ' zaŋguom bɛda giligi ba tɛɛns la. Amaa Zugsɔb la na bɛ nɛ mam, ka m na nyaŋi kadi ba yis, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.”

english_verse: Joshua prayed that God would help Caleb, then he gave Hebron to Caleb and his descendants.
translation_verse: Ka Josua kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis Kaleb onɛ an Jefune biig la, ka zaŋ Hebron teŋ la tis o ka li aan o din.

english_verse: And Hebron still belongs to Caleb's descendants, because he was faithful to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: Hebron kpɛn anɛ Kaleb yaas teŋ hali ti paae zina bɔzugɔ, o da dɔl Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la nɛ o sʋnf wʋsa.

english_verse: Hebron used to be called Arba's Town, because Arba had been one of the greatest of the Anakim. There was peace in the land.
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ ka Hebron da nan ka' Kaleb din la, ba da buon teŋ la ye Kiriaf Ariba, . Ka teŋ la yʋ'ʋn digin baanlimm ka zaba kae.

english_verse: Judah's southern border started at the south end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ba titɔndig nwa' da pin'il nɛ Yaarim Tɛuk ya-dagɔbʋg baba,

english_verse: As it went west from there, it ran south of Scorpion Pass to Zin, and then came up from the south to Kadesh-Barnea. It continued past Hezron up to Addar, turned toward Karka,
translation_verse: ka naam Akirabim Suor la ti paae Zin, ka dɔl Kades Banɛa ya-dagɔbʋg keŋ sig Heziron paae Addar, ka gɔnligi keŋ Karka,

english_verse: and ran along to Azmon. After that, it followed the Egyptian Gorge and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. This was also Israel's southern border.
translation_verse: ka tʋgisi paae Azimon, dɔl kɔlbil linɛ bɛ Egipt teŋ titɔndigin la ti naae Atɛuk baba. Juda dim sʋ'ʋlim linɛ lɛbis ya-dagɔbʋg la bɛnnɛ la.

english_verse: Judah's eastern border ran the full length of the Dead Sea. The northern border started at the northern end of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Titɔndig kanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ baba la dɛn'ɛn nɛ Yaarim Tɛuk la hali ti paae Joodan kɔldaug la nɔɔrin. Ka ba titɔndig kanɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la da yii anina

english_verse: From there it went west up to Beth-Hoglah, continued north of Beth-Arabah, and went up to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: hali ti paae Befihogla, keŋ paae Bet Araba, ka tʋgisi paae Bohan Kugir .

english_verse: From there, it went to Trouble Valley and Debir, then turned north and went to Gilgal, which is on the north side of the valley across from Adummim Pass. It continued on to Enshemesh, Enrogel,
translation_verse: Titɔndig la da yi ani dɔl Akor Bɔn'ɔg la ti paae Debir ka gɔnligi kpa'ad ya-datiuŋ baba ti paae Gilgal, teŋ kanɛ kpa'ad Adumim Suor linɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔg ya-dagɔbʋg nɔɔrin la sa, ka yʋ'ʋn yi Ensemes kɔlisin la ti paae Enrogel;

english_verse: and up through Hinnom Valley on the land sloping south from Jerusalem. The city of Jerusalem itself belonged to the Jebusites. Next, the border went up to the top of the mountain on the west side of Hinnom Valley and at the north end of Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: ani ka li gaadi dɔl Hinnom Biis bɔn'ɔgin la, dɛn'ɛn Jebus dim tempʋʋg, linɛ an Jerusalem la, ya-dagɔbʋg baba, ka titɔndig la lɛn yi paae zuor kanɛ bɛ Hinnom bɔn'ɔg tuon, lɛbisid Refa Dim Bɔn'ɔg ya-datiuŋ la;

english_verse: At the top of the mountain it turned and went to Nephtoah Spring and then to the ruins on Mount Ephron. From there, it went to Baalah, which is now called Kiriath-Jearim.
translation_verse: ka yii ani keŋ Nefitoa kɔlisin dɔl tɛɛns banɛ bɛ Efiron zuorin la; ani ka li yii ti paae Baal, teŋ kanɛ ka ba buon zina ye Kiriaf Jiarim la;

english_verse: From Baalah the northern border curved west to Mount Seir and then ran along the northern ridge of Mount Jearim, where Chesalon is located. Then it went down to Beth-Shemesh and over to Timnah.
translation_verse: ka titɔndig la yii ani ken ya-tuona gɔnligi kpa'ad Edom zuoya teŋ la, ka yi Jiarim zuor , sigi ti paae Bet Semes nɛ Timna tɛɛnsin;

english_verse: Next, Caleb started a war with the town of Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Ka yii ani keŋ zab nɛ banɛ bɛ Debir tempʋʋgin la, .

english_verse: Joshua gave Caleb some land among the people of Judah, as God had told him to do. Caleb's share was Hebron, which at that time was known as Arba's Town, because Arba was the famous ancestor of the Anakim.
translation_verse: Ba da tis Kaleb onɛ an Jefune biig la zin'ikanɛ bɛ Juda dim sʋ'ʋlimin, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl Josua si'em la. O da di'e Hebron, teŋ kanɛ ka Ariba da sʋ'oe ka o saam an Anak la.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En-Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim.
translation_verse: Kaleb da kad Anak biis atan' la yis teŋ la ni; banɛ an Siesai nɛ Ahiman nɛ Talimai la.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdalgad, Dilan, Mizpeh, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmas, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth-Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah.
translation_verse: Ka Kaleb yɛl ye, “M na zaŋi m pu'ayua Akisa tis dau kanɛ wʋsa zabi nyaŋ Kiriaf Seefa ka o di.”

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: On da paae Ofniel yin la, daar yinne Akisa da yɛl o sid ye, “Asɛɛ fʋ yɛli m saam ka o tisif paalʋ.” Ka pu'a la da naanɛ o bʋŋ la zugʋ sig la, o saam Kaleb bu'os o ye, “Fʋ bɔɔd ye m maal bɔɔ tisi fɔ?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so I really need some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds, named Higher Pond and Lower Pond. Towns in Judah's Land
translation_verse: O da lɛbis ye, “Maalim si'el sʋ'ʋŋa tisim. Fʋn sadigim tisim paalʋ Negef teŋin la, mɛ tisim bulig.” Ka Kaleb tis o bulis ayi', linɛ bɛ zugin nɛ linɛ bɛ teŋir la.

english_verse: The following is a list of the towns in each region given to the Judah clans:
translation_verse: Tembama ka Juda nidib paam ka li aan ba bʋn.

english_verse: The first region was located in the Southern Desert along the border with Edom, and it had the following
translation_verse: nɛ Lebaof nɛ Silihim nɛ Ayin nɛ Rimmon. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns pisi nɛ awai, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The second region was located in the northern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: nɛ Siaaram nɛ Aditam nɛ Gedera nɛ Gederofam. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns pii nɛ anaasi, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The third region was located in the southern part of the lower foothills, and it had the following
translation_verse: nɛ Gederof nɛ Bet Dagon nɛ Naama nɛ Makeda. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns pii nɛ ayuobʋ, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The fourth region was located in the central part of the lower foothills, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah.
translation_verse: nɛ Kiela nɛ Akizib nɛ Maresa. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns awai, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The sixth region was in the southwestern part of the hill country, and it had the following eleven towns with their surrounding villages: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath-Sannah, which is now called Debir, Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh.
translation_verse: nɛ Gosen nɛ Holon nɛ Gilo. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns pii nɛ yinne, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The seventh region was located in the south-central part of Judah's hill country, and it had the following nine towns with their surrounding villages: Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth-Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath-Arba, which is now called Hebron, and Zior.
translation_verse: nɛ Humta nɛ Kiriaf Ariba, linɛ an Hebron la, nɛ Zior. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns awai, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The eighth region was located in the southeastern part of the hill country, and it had the following ten towns with their surrounding villages: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah.
translation_verse: nɛ Kain nɛ Gibea nɛ Timna. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns piiga, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The twelfth region was located in the desert along the Dead Sea, and it had the following six towns with their surrounding villages: Beth-Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, Salt Town, and En-Gedi. The Jebusites
translation_verse: nɛ Nibisan nɛ Yaarim Teŋ la nɛ Engedi. Tembama wʋsa la'as nɛ tɛɛns ayuobʋ, la'an nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the people of the Judah tribe could not capture the city and get rid of them. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Judah.
translation_verse: Amaa Juda dim la da pʋ nyaŋi yis Jebus dim banɛ da bɛ Jerusalem teŋin laa. Jebus dim la nan kpɛm bɛ Juda teŋin zina.

english_verse: The following is a description of the land that was divided among the clans of the Ephraim tribe. Their southern border started at Ataroth-Addar and went west to Upper Beth-Horon
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa da an Efiram dim pʋʋr, li da anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ: Ba sʋ'ʋlim la titɔndig linɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la da naanɛ Atarof Addar paae Zugin Befihoron

english_verse: Ephraim also had some towns and villages that were inside Manasseh's tribal land.
translation_verse: Li mɛ da la'am kpanb tempʋʋd nɛ ba teŋkpɛmis la wʋsa banɛ ka ba da gaŋi digil Efiram dim la yi Manase dim sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: Ephraim could not force the Canaanites out of Gezer, so there are still some Canaanites who live there among the Israelites. But now these Canaanites have to work as slaves for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ba da pʋ kad Keenan dim banɛ da bɛ Giza la. Hali ti paae zina Keenan dim nan kpɛn la'am zin' nɛ Efiram nidib amaa li anɛ tilasi tisi ba ye ba tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema tisi ba.

english_verse: The land of the Manasseh tribe went from its northern border with the Asher tribe south to Michmethath, which is to the east of Shechem. The southern border started there, but curved even farther south to include the people who lived around Tappuah Spring.
translation_verse: Manase sʋ'ʋlim la da pin'il nɛ Aser ti paae Mikmeta linɛ bɛ Sekɛm tempʋʋg nya'aŋ la. Titɔndig la yʋ'ʋn da keŋ paae ya-dagɔbʋg naanɛ ani keŋ kpanb nimbanɛ bɛ En Tapua teŋin la.

english_verse: Manasseh was supposed to have the following towns with their surrounding villages inside the borders of Issachar's and Asher's tribal lands: Beth-Shan, Ibleam, Endor, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor, which is also called Naphath.
translation_verse: Isaka nɛ Aser sʋ'ʋlim la sʋʋgin Manase mɛ da sʋ'oe Betsean nɛ Ibilam nɛ Dor nɛ Endo nɛ Taanak nɛ Megido la'an nɛ banɛ zin'ini giligi ba la.

english_verse: But the people of Manasseh could not capture these towns, so the Canaanites kept on living in them.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala Manase dim la da pʋ nyaŋi kad nimbanɛ bɛ tempʋʋsin la yis ka sʋ'ʋgi baa, bɔzugɔ Keenan dim la da gban'e ye asɛɛ ka ba zin'in sʋ'ʋlim kan la ni.

english_verse: When the Israelites grew stronger, they made the Canaanites in these towns work as their slaves, though they never did force them to leave. Joseph's Descendants Ask for More Land
translation_verse: Amaa Israel dim la da nɔbig hali ka mɔr kpi'euŋ la, ba da muk Keenan dim la ka ba tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema tisidi ba, amaa ka pʋ kadi ba yis teŋ la pʋʋgin nyainnɛ.

english_verse: One day the Joseph tribes came to Joshua and asked, “Why didn't you give us more land? The Lord has always been kind to us, and we have too many people for this small region.”
translation_verse: Josef nidib la da yɛl Josua ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka fʋ gaŋ zin'ig yinne ma'aa gbin'e paalʋ tisi ti ye li aan ti pʋʋrɛ? Ti nidib zu'oya ka Zugsɔb la mɛ niŋi ti zug bareka hali.”

english_verse: Joshua replied, “If there's not enough room for you in the hill country of Ephraim, then go into the forest that belonged to the Perizzites and the Rephaim. Clear out the trees and make more room for yourselves there.”
translation_verse: Ka Josua lɛbis ye, “Ya ya'a zu'oe ka Efiram teŋ kʋkʋna baba la pɔɔdi tisi ya, yanam on kem kpɛn' Perizi dim nɛ Refa dim mɔɔgin la kie vɔn'ɔdi paas.”

english_verse: “Even if we do that,” they answered, “there still won't be enough land for us in the hill country. And we can't move down into Jezreel Valley, because the Canaanites who live in Beth-Shan and in other parts of the valley have iron chariots.”
translation_verse: Josef nidib la da lɛbis ye, “Kʋkʋna teŋ la kʋ siaki ti, ka Keenan dim banɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔdin la wʋsa mɛ mɔr kʋnt zaba tɛrekonam. Ba sieba banɛ bɛ Betsean nɛ li teŋkpɛmis nɛ banɛ bɛ Jezireel bɔn'ɔgin la wʋsa mɛ mɔr tɛrekonam la.”

english_verse: “Your tribes do have a lot of people,” Joshua admitted. “I'll give you more land. Your tribes are powerful,
translation_verse: Amaa Josua da yɛl Josef yidim banɛ an Efiram nɛ Manase dim la ye, “Ya zu'oya ka mɔr kpi'euŋ; alazug, ya kʋ di'e pʋdigir yinne ma'aanɛ.

english_verse: so you can have the rest of the hill country, but it's a forest, and you'll have to cut down the trees and clear the land. You can also have Jezreel Valley. Even though the Canaanites there are strong and have iron chariots, you can force them to leave the valley.”
translation_verse: Ayei, kʋkʋna teŋ la na aan ya din, la'an nɛ linɛ an mɔɔg la, asɛɛ ka ya kie vɔn'ɔdi paas ka li wʋsa aan ya pʋʋr. La'an nɛ Keenan dim la mɔr kʋnt zaba tɛrekonam ka kpi'em la, ya na nyaŋi kadi ba yis.”

english_verse: After Israel had captured the land, they met at Shiloh and set up the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Israel nidib la wʋsa da la'as Siilo teŋin maal Fuug Sʋgʋri ti' ka li aan ba la'asʋg zin'ig. Teŋ la yʋ'ʋn da bɛnɛ ba nu'usin

english_verse: There were still seven tribes without any land,
translation_verse: amaa Israel dɔɔd ayɔpɔi da nam bɛ ka pʋ di'e ba pʋʋrɛ.

english_verse: Just before the men left camp, Joshua repeated their orders: “Explore the land and write a description of it. Then come back to Shiloh, and I will find out from the Lord how to divide the land.”
translation_verse: Nidib la da ye ba yii keŋ mak teŋ la, Josua da pa'ali ba ye, “Kem kaae giligi teŋ la ka sɔb lin an si'em, ka lɛbini m san'an na ka m maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm tisi ya Siilo teŋin kpɛla, Zugsɔb la tuon.”

english_verse: The men left and went across the land, dividing it into seven regions. They wrote down a description of each region, town by town, and returned to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Nidib la sid da yii keŋ kaae teŋ la. Ba da sɔb lin an si'em niŋ gbauŋʋn. Tempʋʋg wʋsa yinne-yinne ka ba da pʋdig zin'is ayɔpɔi, ka lɛb Josua san'an zin'ikanɛ ka ba la'as, Siilo teŋin la.

english_verse: Joshua found out from the Lord how to divide the land, and he told the tribes what the Lord had decided. Benjamin's Land
translation_verse: Josua yʋ'ʋn da maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm tisi ba Siilo teŋin, Zugsɔb la tuon, ka ani ka o pʋdig teŋ la tis Israel dim la ka li dɔl nɛ dɔɔg la an bɛn-bɛn si'em. Benjamin pʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: Benjamin was the first tribe chosen to receive land. The region for its clans lay between the Judah tribe on the south and the Joseph tribes on the north.
translation_verse: Bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la da gaŋnɛ Benjamin dɔɔg la, ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ. Ba pʋʋr la sʋ'ʋlim la da bɛnɛ Juda nɛ Josef dim la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: Benjamin's northern border started at the Jordan River and went up the ridge north of Jericho, then on west into the hill country as far as the Beth-Aven Desert.
translation_verse: Ba titɔndig linɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la da pin'il nɛ Joodan kɔldaugin la dɔlli yi ya-datiuŋʋ paae Jeriko zuligirin la gaad tuonnɛ dɔl kʋkʋna teŋ la yii ani paae Betaven sian'arin la;

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, Gibeah, Kiriath-Jearim, and Jerusalem, which is also called Jebusite Town. These regions are the tribal lands of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ka naan kʋkʋn kanɛ kpa' Befihoron ya-dagɔbʋg titɔndigin la gɔnligi lɛb ya-dagɔbʋgʋ dɔl teŋ la tuonnɛ yi Kiriaf Baal . Li da lɛb nɛ ya-tuona.

english_verse: Benjamin's southern border started at the edge of Kiriath-Jearim and went east to the ruins and on to Nephtoah Spring.
translation_verse: Li ya-dagɔbʋg baba la da pin'il Kiriaf Jiarim teŋ la kpikpɛŋ ya-tuona baba, ka titɔndig la keŋ yi Nefitoa kɔlisin la;

english_verse: From there it went to the bottom of the hill at the northern end of Rephaim Valley. The other side of this hill faces Hinnom Valley, which is on the land that slopes south from Jerusalem. The border went down through Hinnom Valley until it reached Enrogel.
translation_verse: ka li yʋ'ʋn dɔlis ala sig kʋkʋn la teŋiri kpa'ad Ben Hinnom bɔn'ɔfalig linɛ bɛ Refam bɔn'ɔg ya-datiuŋ la. Ka naan anina dɔlli yi Hinnom bɔn'ɔfaligin la dɛn'ɛn Jebus dim tempʋʋg la sisɛrim ti paae Enrogel.

english_verse: At Enrogel the border curved north and went to Enshemesh and on east to Geliloth, which is across the valley from Adummim Pass. Then it went down to the Monument of Bohan, who belonged to the Reuben tribe.
translation_verse: Ani ka li da gɔnligi lɛb datiuŋʋ keŋ Ensemes gaadi keŋ Gilgal, teŋ kanɛ kpa'ad Adumim Suor la, sigid Bohan Kugirin la. Bohan da anɛ Reuben biig;

english_verse: The border ran along the hillside north of Beth-Arabah, then down into the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: ani ka li da dɔl Bet Araba ya-datiuŋʋ gaadi zuligi sig Araba bɔn'ɔgin,

english_verse: Inside the valley it went south as far as the northern hillside of Beth-Hoglah. The last section of the border went from there to the northern end of the Dead Sea, at the mouth of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: ka tɔ'ɔŋ ala paae Befihogla keŋ yi Yaarim Tɛuk la hali ti paae Joodan kɔldaug la nɔɔrin. Ba ya-datiuŋ la titɔndigi la.

english_verse: The Jordan River itself was Benjamin's eastern border. These were the borders of Benjamin's tribal land, where the clans of Benjamin lived.
translation_verse: Joodan kɔldaug la da an ya-nya'aŋ la titɔndig. Titɔndis bama da pa'an Benjamin dim la pʋʋri an si'em bɛn-bɛn nɛ gilig wʋsa.

english_verse: Simeon was the second tribe chosen to receive land, and the region for its clans was inside Judah's borders.
translation_verse: Bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm linɛ pɛ'ɛs ayi' la da lu nɛ Simeon dim la zug, ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ. Ba pʋʋr da bɛ nɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlim la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: In one region of Simeon's tribal land there were the following
translation_verse: nɛ Bet Lebaof nɛ Siaruhen. Tempʋʋd pii nɛ atan' nɛ ba tembibis.

english_verse: and continued north to Gath-Hepher, Ethkazin, and Rimmonah, where it curved toward Neah
translation_verse: ka li kpɛn ken hali lɛbid ya-nya'aŋ Gaf Hifa nɛ Ef-Kaazin, li dɔlli yinɛ Rimmon gɔnligi kpa' Niya;

english_verse: In another region, Simeon had the following four towns with their surrounding villages: Enrimmon, Tachan, Ether, and Ashan.
translation_verse: Linɛ pɛ'ɛs anɛ Ayin nɛ Rimmon nɛ Eter nɛ Asean. Tempʋʋd anaasi nɛ ba tembibis,

english_verse: Simeon's land also included all the other towns and villages as far south as Baalath-Beer, which is also called Ramah of the South.
translation_verse: nɛ tembibis banɛ gilig tempʋbama wʋsa hali ti paae Baalaf Beer . Nɛ'ɛŋa da an Simeon dim la pʋʋr, ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ.

english_verse: Simeon's tribal land was actually inside Judah's territory. Judah had received too much land for the number of people in its tribe, so part of Judah's land was given to Simeon. Zebulun's Land
translation_verse: Simeon dim la da di'e ba faar nɛ Juda dim pʋʋr la pʋʋgin bɔzugɔ Juda pʋʋr la da zu'oe gaad lin nar ye ba di'e si'em. Alazug Simeon dim la da di'e ba faar la nɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlim la pʋʋgin. Zebulun pʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: and became the northern border. Then it curved south around Hannathon and went as far west as Iphtahel Valley.
translation_verse: ani ka titɔndig la gɔnligi yi tuonnɛ ken Hannaton n keŋ naae Ifitahel bɔn'ɔgin la.

english_verse: Zebulun had twelve towns with their surrounding villages. Some of these were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Jiralah, and Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Banɛ paas anɛ Kattaf nɛ Nahalal nɛ Simiron nɛ Idala nɛ Betilehem. Ba da anɛ tempʋʋd pii nɛ ayi' nɛ ba teŋkpɛmis.

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages: Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Debirath, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, En-Gannim, Enhaddah, Beth-Pazzez, Tabor, Shahazumah and Beth-Shemesh. Asher's Land
translation_verse: Tempʋbama nɛ ba tembibis la da anɛ Zebulun dim faar, ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ. Isaka pʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: Issachar was the fourth tribe chosen to receive land. The northern border for its clans went from Mount Tabor east to the Jordan River. Their land included the following
translation_verse: Tempʋbama nɛ ba tembibis la da anɛ Isaka dim faar ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ. Aser pʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: then east to Beth-Dagon. On the southeast, Asher shared a border with Zebulun along the Iphtahel Valley. On the eastern side their border ran north to Beth-Emek, went east of Cabul, and then on to Neiel,
translation_verse: Li da fɛndigi lɛb ya-nya'aŋ baba lɛbid Bet Dagon n paae Zebulun nɛ Ifitahel bɔn'ɔgin la, ka lɛb datiuŋ keŋ paae Bet Emek nɛ Neiel n gaadi dɔl Kabul lɛbid dagɔbʋg;

english_verse: Abdon, Rehob, Hammon, Kanah, and as far north as the city of Sidon.
translation_verse: ka keŋ dɔl Abidon nɛ Rehob nɛ Hamon nɛ Kana hali ti paae Sidon linɛ an teŋ tita'ar la.

english_verse: Then it turned west to become the northern border and went to Ramah and the fortress-city of Tyre. Near Tyre it turned toward Hosah and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. Asher had a total of
translation_verse: Tempʋbama nɛ ba tembibis la da anɛ Aser dim faar ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ. Naftali pʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: towns with their surrounding villages, including Mahalab, Achzib, Acco, Aphek, and Rehob. Naphtali's Land
translation_verse: hali ti paae Tabo nɛ Siahazuma nɛ Bet Semes keŋ naae Joodan kɔldaug nɔɔrin. Li da anɛ tempʋʋd pii nɛ ayuobʋ nɛ ba tembibis.

english_verse: The Naphtali clans received this region as their tribal land, and it included
translation_verse: Tempʋbama nɛ ba tembibis la da anɛ Naftali dim faar ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ. Dan pʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: The Israelites were still gathered in Shiloh in front of the sacred tent, when Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the family leaders of Israel finished giving out the land to the tribes. The Lord had told the people to give Joshua whatever town he wanted. So Joshua chose Timnath-Serah in the hill country of Ephraim, and the people gave it to him. Joshua went to Timnath-Serah, rebuilt it, and lived there.
translation_verse: Ka Eleazar onɛ an maanmaan la, nɛ Nun biig Josua nɛ Israel buudi la dɔɔd kpɛɛmnam da maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm pʋdig sʋ'ʋlim la tis taaba. Ba da niŋ ala nɛ Zugsɔb la tuon, La'asʋg Fuug Sʋgʋr linɛ da bɛ Siilo teŋin la za'anɔɔrin. Ala ka ba da maali pʋdig teŋ la naae.

english_verse: These Safe Towns were set up, so that if Israelites or even foreigners who lived in Israel accidentally killed someone, they could run to one of these towns. There they would be safe until a trial could be held, even if one of the victim's relatives came looking for revenge.
translation_verse: Israel nid wʋsa bɛɛ saan onɛ bɛ nɛ ba ya'a kʋ sɔ' ka li ka' pɔn'ɔsim, on sɔb na tun'e zɔɔ keŋ tembama ni ka banɛ kad o ye ba kʋʋ o yɔ sam la kʋ kʋʋ o. Li pʋ nar ye ba kʋ sɔ' ka pʋ kad o saria.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Joshua:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Josua ye

english_verse: When Moses was still alive, I commanded him to tell the Israelites about the Safe Towns. Now you tell them that it is time to set up these towns.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim Israel dim la ye ba gaŋ tembanɛ na an suak zin'is, nwɛnɛ man da pa'al Moses si'em la.

english_verse: If a person accidentally kills someone and the victim's relatives say it was murder, they might try to take revenge. Anyone accused of murder can run to one of the Safe Towns and be safe from the victim's relatives. The one needing protection will stand at the entrance to the town gate and explain to the town leaders what happened. Then the leaders will bring that person in and provide a place to live in their town.
translation_verse: O ya'a zɔɔ keŋ tembama yinne ni, o na zi'en teŋ la yaŋirin ka yɛl teŋ la kpɛɛmnam on tʋm si'el, ka ba di'e o kpɛn'ɛsi ba teŋin la ka bɔ zin'igi tis o ka o zin'in nɛ ba.

english_verse: One of the victim's relatives might come to the town, looking for revenge. But the town leaders must not simply hand over the person accused of murder. After all, the accused and the victim had been neighbors, not enemies.
translation_verse: Sɔ' ya'a dɔl o nya'aŋi paae na ye o kʋʋ o yɔ sam, ban da nɔk o tisɛ, bɔzugɔ o pʋ kʋʋ o kpi'a la pɔn'ɔsim-pɔn'ɔsim.

english_verse: The citizens of that Safe Town must come together and hold a trial. They may decide that the victim was killed accidentally and that the accused is not guilty of murder. Everyone found not guilty must still live in the Safe Town until the high priest dies. Then they can go back to their own towns and their homes that they had to leave behind.
translation_verse: O na bɛ teŋin la hali ti paae ban na ti tu'a antu'a la o nidib la tuon. O ya'a di bʋʋd, o na kpɛm bɛ ani ti paae saŋkanɛ ka maanmaan kpɛɛm la na kpi, ka o nyaan lɛb o mɛŋ teŋin.”

english_verse: The Israelites decided that the following three towns west of the Jordan River would be Safe Towns: Kedesh in Galilee in Naphtali's hill country, Shechem in Ephraim's hill country, and Kiriath-Arba in Judah's hill country. Kiriath-Arba is now called Hebron.
translation_verse: Alazug ba da gaŋ Kedes linɛ bɛ Galile kʋkʋna teŋ linɛ bɛ Naftali sʋ'ʋlimin la, nɛ Sekɛm linɛ bɛ Efiram kʋkʋna teŋ la nɛ Kiriaf Ariba linɛ bɛ Juda kʋkʋna teŋ la

english_verse: The Israelites had already decided on the following three towns east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the desert flatlands of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead, which was a town that belonged to Gad, and Golan in Bashan, which belonged to Manasseh.
translation_verse: lɛbisid Joodan kɔldaug lɔm, Jeriko teŋ nya'aŋ la. Ba da gaŋnɛ Bezer linɛ bɛ sian'arin Reuben dim paalʋ la ni, nɛ Ramot linɛ bɛ Gilead teŋgbauŋʋn ka an Gad dim sʋ'ʋlim la nɛ Golan linɛ bɛ Basan teŋgbauŋʋn ka an Manase dim sʋ'ʋlim la.

english_verse: While the Israelites were still camped at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, the family leaders of the Levi tribe went to speak to the priest Eleazar, Joshua, and the family leaders of the other Israelite tribes. The leaders of Levi said, “The Lord told Moses that you have to give us towns and provide pastures for our animals.”
translation_verse: Ba da kɛn Siilo linɛ bɛ Keenan teŋin la na yɛli ba ye, “Zugsɔb la da tis Moses nɔɔr ye ya tisi ti tempʋʋd ka ti zin' ani, nɛ sian'anr linɛ ka ti na kemmi ti niigi.”

english_verse: Since the Lord had said this, the leaders of the other Israelite tribes agreed to give some of the towns and pastures from their tribal lands to Levi.
translation_verse: Alazug, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl Moses si'em la, Israel dim la da tis Levi dim la tɛɛns nɛ sian'anr, linɛ an ba mɛŋ faar la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: The leaders asked the Lord to show them in what order the clans of Levi would be given towns, and which towns each clan would receive. The Kohath clans were first. The descendants of Aaron, Israel's first priest, were given
translation_verse: Yiiga bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la da gaŋnɛ Kohat dim la ka li anɛ tuŋ-tuŋ: Levi dim banɛ da an Aaron onɛ an maanmaan la yaas da paam tɛɛns pii nɛ atan' Juda dim sʋ'ʋlimin la, nɛ Simeon dim, nɛ Benjamin dim din la ni.

english_verse: The Lord had told Moses that he would show the Israelites which towns and pastures to give to the clans of Levi, and he did. Towns from Judah, Simeon, Benjamin
translation_verse: Alazug Israel dim da tis Levi dim la tembama nɛ sian'anr, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la da tis Moses nɔɔr si'em la.

english_verse: The descendants of Aaron from the Kohath clans of Levi were priests, and they were chosen to receive towns first. They were given
