translation_verse: Tɛɛns banɛ da an Aaron yaas din, banɛ an maanmaannib la wʋsa, da anɛ pii nɛ atan', la'an nɛ ba kɔnbid kemmʋg zin'ig.

english_verse: The clans of Levi that were descendants of Gershon received
translation_verse: Gerson tuŋ dim la tɛɛns wʋsa da anɛ pii nɛ atan' la'an nɛ ba kɔnbid kemmʋg zin'is.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb la da tis Israel dim paalʋ kanɛ ka o da pɔɔ zi'el ye o na tisi ba yaanam la wʋsa, ka ba sʋ'ʋgi li ka zin'inɛ ani.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da tisi ba vʋ'ʋsʋm, zin'ig wʋsa wʋʋ on da pɔ si'em zi'eli ba yaanam la. Ba dataas la baa yinne da pʋ nyaŋi zab nɛ ba, Zugsɔb la da nɔki ba dataas wʋsa niŋi ba nu'usin la zug.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da kaanb si'em tis Israel dim la baa yinne da pʋ gʋ'ʋŋɛ; li wʋsa da maal ya.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Josua da la'as Reuben dim la na nɛ Gad dim la nɛ Manase dim pʋsʋk la,

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Hali lin yuugi ti paae zina la, ya pʋ basi ya ba'abiis la, amaa ya tʋm tʋʋm kanɛ ka ya Zugsɔb Wina'am tisi ya ye ya tʋm la.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Nannanna ya Zugsɔb Wina'am la yʋ'ʋn tisi ya ba'abiis la vʋ'ʋsʋm wʋʋ on da zi'el nɔɔr si'em la. Lɛmmini ya yaan, teŋ kanɛ ka Moses onɛ an Zugsɔb tʋmtʋm la da tisi ya, Joodan kɔldaug gbɛkaŋa la.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Amaa, gu'usimi sʋ'ʋŋa ka siaki zi'ela banɛ ka Moses onɛ an Zugsɔb tʋmtʋm da tisi ya la, ye ya nɔŋi ya Zugsɔb Wina'am, ka dɔl o suoya la ka siak o zi'ela la wʋsa, ka gban'e o nu'us ayi', ka tʋmmi tisid o nɛ ya sʋnf wʋsa nɛ ya siig wʋsa.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Ka Israel dimi wʋm ye ba mɛ' bimbim Keenan titɔndig linɛ bɛ Gelilof teŋin kpi'e nɛ Joodan ka bɛ Israel dim baba la,

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Israel dim wʋsa da la'as taaba ye ba keŋ zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da tʋm Finehas onɛ an maanmaan ka an Eleazar biig la, ye o lɔ'ɔŋi paae Gilead teŋinɛ keŋ Reuben nɛ Gad nɛ Manase dim pʋsʋk la san'an.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Tuongatib yinne-yinne da yi dɔɔg piiga la wʋsa ni dɔl Finehas nya'aŋi keŋ.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Ba da keŋ paae Reuben nɛ Gad nɛ Manase dim la san'an Gilead teŋin yɛli ba ye,

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb nidib la wʋsa sʋnf san'amnɛ ka ba bu'osid taaba ye, ‘Bɔ ka ya tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kaŋa linɛ ka Israel Wina'am la kisa? Wala ka ya fɛndig Zugsɔb la san'an ka mɛ' bimbimi tisi ya mɛŋ ka zan'as o nɔɔr nannanna?

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ti da tʋm Peor baba ka Zugsɔb da tɛɛgi ti tʋbir la pʋ siak yanamɛ na zamis ya'am? Din keŋ paae zina ti nam pʋ pie tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ, la'an nɛ tinamɛ da namisi li yɛla la.

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Ya gban'e nɛ ye ya kʋ lɛn dɔl oo? Ya ya'a zan'as ka pʋ dɔl Zugsɔb la zinaa, bɛogɔ o sʋnf na pɛlig nɛ Israel dim wʋsa.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Teŋ kanɛ ka ya bɛ la ya'a an bɛ'ɛd, yanam kem Zugsɔb la teŋin na, zin'ikanɛ ka o Fuug Sʋgʋr bɛ la, ka tinam nɛ yanam pʋdigi ti paalʋ la. Amaa da zan'asi Zugsɔb la nɔɔr bɛɛ ya zan'as tinam nɔɔr ka mɛ' bimbimi tisi ya mɛŋ ka li ya'a ka'anɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am bimbim la ma'aanɛ.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Ya pʋ tɛnraa? Zera yaaŋ Akan onɛ da zan'as Zugsɔb la da tis nɔɔr ye ba san'am teŋ la la'ad wʋsa la, Israel dim wʋsa da namisi li zug. Li ka' on ma'aa da kpi o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la zugɔ.’”

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb la an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb! Zugsɔb onɛ an Wina'am Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la, onɛ mi'. Kɛl ka Israel dim baŋ ye, nɛ' ya'a anɛ ti zan'as nɛ Zugsɔb la nɔɔr bɛɛ ti tʋbiri zian'asi tis Zugsɔb la, yanam da basi ti zinaa.

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Ti ya'a mɛnɛ ti mɛŋ bimbim ye ti fɛndig ka bas Zugsɔb la ka yuki maannɛ ti mɛŋ maana li zug, ka li anɛ linɛ nyu'od bugum, bɛɛ zʋʋd maan, bɛɛ taaba la'asʋg maan la buudi wʋsa, Zugsɔb la mɛŋ on tɛɛgimi ti tʋbir.

english_verse: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la kɛ ka Joodan an titɔndig tinam nɛ yanam teŋsʋk yanam Reuben nɛ Gad dima, ya ka' pʋʋr Zugsɔb la san'anɛ!’ Alazug ya yaas pa'ati kɛ ka tinam yaas pʋ lɛn zɔt Zugsɔb laa.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Linzug ka ti yɛl ye, ti na la'asi mɛ' bimbim, ka li ka'anɛ maan kanɛ nyu'od bugum bɛɛ maan sieba zugɔ,

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders were pleased when they heard the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh explain why they had built the altar. Then Phinehas told them, “Today we know that the Lord is helping us. You have not been unfaithful to him, and this means that the Lord will not be angry with us.”
translation_verse: Finehas da yɛli ba ye, “Zina ti baŋ ya ye Zugsɔb la sid bɛ nɛ ti, bɔzugɔ ya pʋ tʋm biriku'an tʋʋmaa, amaa ka faaɛn ti yi Zugsɔb la tʋbtɛkir la pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Finehas nɛ tuongatib la ban da zin'in nɛ Reuben nɛ Gad dim Gilead teŋin naae la, ba da lɛb Keenan teŋin na ye ba yɛli tis Israel dim la.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Ba sʋnf da malis nɛ ban wʋm labasi'a la, ka na'as Wina'am yʋ'ʋr, ka bas ban gban'e ye ba keŋ zab ka san'am Reuben dim nɛ Gad dimi bɛ teŋ si'a la.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Reuben nɛ Gad dim da pʋd bimbim la yʋ'ʋr ye, Li anɛ Kasɛta tinam nɛ yanam sʋʋgin ye Zugsɔb la anɛ Wina'am.

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da tis Israel dim vʋ'ʋsʋm ba dataas banɛ giligi ba la nya'aŋ la, li da yuug ya hali ka Josua yʋ'ʋn da kʋdig pamm.

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: Alazug ka o da la'as Israel dim wʋsa, ba kpɛɛmnam nɛ bʋnkʋd nɛ tuongatib nɛ sariakatib nɛ kpi'emnamɛ yɛli ba ye, “Mam yʋ'ʋn kʋdig nɛ hali.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Yanam mɛŋ nyɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la kpɛn' ya zug ka maal tembanɛ giligi ya la si'em ya yɛla; li da anɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la zabi tisi ya.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la mɛŋi na kadi ba yis, ka bas suori tisi ya ka ya sʋ'ʋg teŋ la wʋʋ on da kaanbi zi'eli ya si'em la.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Kpɛ'ɛŋimini ya mɛŋ, ka gu'usi ka siaki linɛ wʋsa sɔb Moses zi'ela gbauŋʋn la, ka da fɛndigi lɛbi datiuŋ bɛɛ dagɔbʋga.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Da nɔki ya mɛŋi la'asi nɛ nimbanɛ na kpɛlim bɛ nɛ ya tembanɛ ka ya la'am bɛ la. Da buonnɛ ba bada la yʋda bɔɔd sʋŋirɛ, bɛɛ pɔɔd nɛ ba yʋ'ʋrɛ. Da dɔlli nɛ ba bɛɛ igini ba tuonnɛ.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Amaa li anɛ ya gban'e Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la kiŋ-kiŋ nwɛnɛ yanamɛ da mɔr o si'em ti paae zina la.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la gaad tuonnɛ kad buudtitada nɛ teŋ kpi'ema nidib. Hali ti paae zina sɔ' nan zi' nyaŋi zab nɛ ya.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Ya nid yinne na nyaŋi kadi ba tusir bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la zabidi tisidi ya wʋʋ on da zi'el nɔɔr si'em la.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: “Alazug gu'usimi sʋ'ʋŋa ka nɔŋi Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a niŋ ala, yanam on baŋim ye Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la kʋ lɛn gaad tuonnɛ kad tɛɛns la dim ka tisi ya suorɛ. Ba lɛɛ na lieb bɛndisi bɛndi ya ka lieb sisanbisi fiebi ya nya'aŋ, nɛ gɔn'ɔsi kunsidi ya nini hali ka ya ti bɔdig teŋ sʋŋ kaŋa linɛ ka Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la tisi ya la.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Tɔ', nannanna m kum saŋa paaeya. Ya mi' nɛ ya sʋʋnr nɛ ya siig wʋsa ye Zugsɔb la kaanb bareka sieba tisi ya la baa yinne pʋ lu teŋa. Li wʋsa niŋnɛ wʋʋ on kaanb si'em la.

english_verse: Yes, when the Lord makes a promise, he does what he has promised. But when he makes a threat, he will also do what he has threatened. The Lord is our God. He gave us this wonderful land and made an agreement with us that we would worship only him. But if you worship other gods, it will make the Lord furious. He will start getting rid of you, and soon not one of you will be left in this good land that he has given you.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a san'ami ya Zugsɔb Wina'am nɔnaar linɛ ka o zi'eli tisi ya la, ka keŋ maal winsieba iginidi ba tuon, Zugsɔb la sʋnpɛɛn na la'aŋi ya wʋʋ bugum nɛ, ka ya na bɔdig tɔ'ɔtɔ teŋ sʋŋ kanɛ ka o tisi ya la zug.”

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Josua da la'as Israel buudi dim la wʋsa Sekɛm teŋin. O da buol tuongatib nɛ kpɛɛmnam nɛ sariakatib nɛ kpi'emnam ka ba kɛn Wina'am tuon na.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Josua da yɛl nidib la wʋsa ye, “Zugsɔb Onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Kʋdimin sa, ya yaanam, la'an nɛ Tera onɛ da an Abraham nɛ Nahor saam la, da zin'inɛ kɔldaug kanɛ buon Efiritis la nya'aŋ ka pʋ'ʋsid winsieba.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Amaa m da yisi ya yaab Abraham teŋ kanɛ bɛ kɔldaug la nya'aŋi mɔr o kpɛn' Keenan teŋinɛ dɔl o giligi li wʋsa ka kɛ ka o paam yaas bɛdegʋ. M da kɛ ka o du'a Isaak,

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: ka Isaak mɛ du'a Jakob nɛ Esau. M da nɔk Edom teŋi tis Esau, zin'ikanɛ ka zuoya bɛ la, amaa Jakob nɛ o biis da keŋnɛ Egipt teŋin.

english_verse: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Man da yisi ya yaanam Egipt teŋin la, ba da paae Atɛuk Zɛn'ugʋn na ka Egipt dim la kadi ba bugir nɛ zaba tɛrekonam nɛ banɛ ban'ad widi zabid la paae ani.

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: Amaa ba da kaasi buol Zugsɔb la bɔɔd sʋŋir, ka o kɛ ka lik kɛn ban nɛ Egipt dim la teŋsʋk na. O da kɛ ka Atɛuk la ku'om la dii ba. Ka ya nyɛ nɛ ya mɛŋ nini man tʋm Egipt dim la tʋʋm si'a. Ka ya gilig sian'arin la yuug pamm.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: “‘M da mɔri ya keŋ paae Amor dim banɛ bɛ Joodan nya'aŋ la. Ba da zab nɛ ya ka m kɛ ka ya nyaŋi ba. Man Wina'am da san'ami ba ka tisi ya suor ka ya sʋ'ʋgi ba teŋ la.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka Balak onɛ an Zippor biig ka da lɛn an Moab dim na'ab la da ti'eb ye o zab nɛ Israel dim. O da tʋm buol Balaam onɛ an Beor biig la ye o kena pɔ nɔɔri niŋi ba.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Amaa m da pʋ siaki tis Balaam, ka o lɛɛ da niŋi ya bareka; ka m faaɛn ya yii Balak nu'usin.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: “‘Ya da lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la keŋ paae Jeriko teŋin. Jeriko teŋ nidib da zab nɛ ya nwɛnɛ Amor dim nɛ Perizi dim nɛ Keenan dim nɛ Hitti dim nɛ Girgas dim nɛ Hivi dim nɛ Jebus dim la da niŋ si'em la, amaa m da kɛ ka ya nyaŋi ba.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: M da kɛ ka tangbɛɛnlnam sigi ba sʋʋgin na kadi ba ka ba zɔ ka ya nyaan paae. Ka mɛ niŋ ala nɛ Ammon dim na'anam ayi' la. Li da ka'anɛ ya mɛŋ zaba sʋ'ʋg bɛɛ tiraug ka ya da nyaŋi ba.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Manɛ tisi ya teŋ linɛ ka ya pʋ namisi li yɛllɛ nɛ tempʋʋd banɛ ka ya pʋ mɛɛ, ka ya bɛɛ ani ka dit vain nɛ olif pɔɔd la nyɔɔd ka lɛɛ pʋ sɛɛ ba.’

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Nannanna tisimi Zugsɔb la girima ka dɔlli nɛ o nɛ sida. Basimi bada banɛ ka ya yaanam da dɔl kɔldaug la nya'aŋ nɛ Egipt teŋin la ka dɔl Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a tɛn'ɛs ye Zugsɔb la dɔllim ka' sʋ'ʋm tisi ya, yanam on gaŋim zina onɛ ka ya na dɔl. Ya ya'a na gaŋnɛ ya yaanamɛ da dɔl ba'asieba kɔldaug nya'aŋ la bɛɛ Amor dim, banɛ ka ya bɛɛ ba teŋin la wina, yanam gaŋimi. Amaa ya'a kpɛlimnɛ man nɛ m yidim, tinam na dɔl Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Nidib la da lɛbis ye, “Win da kɛ ka ti bas Zugsɔb la dɔllim ka dɔl winsieba!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Li da anɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am la mɛŋi yisi ti Egipt teŋin, zin'ikanɛ ka ti da an yammis la, ka maal tʋʋmnyalima ka ti nini nyɛ. O da guri ti, ti suor la ken pʋʋgin, la'an nɛ tinamɛ da dɔl teŋ sieba gaad la, ka yisi ti nidib la wʋsa nu'usin.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la kad tɛɛns la dim, la'an nɛ Amor dim banɛ da bɛ teŋin la. Tinam mɛ na dɔl Zugsɔb la, bɔzugɔ o anɛ ti Wina'am.”

english_verse: Joshua said: The Lord is fearsome; he is the one true God, and I don't think you are able to worship and obey him in the ways he demands. You would have to be completely faithful, and if you sin or rebel, he won't let you get away with it.
translation_verse: Amaa Josua da yɛl nidib la ye, “Ayei, ya kʋ nyaŋi dɔl Zugsɔb la. O anɛ Wina'am onɛ an kasi; o anɛ Wina'am onɛ mɔr fufum. O kʋ tami ya ki'isʋg nɛ ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la yɛllɛ.

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a zan'as Zugsɔb la ka dɔl buudzʋna bada, o na fɛndig ka kɛ ka san'auŋ paae ya ka ya kpi'ilim, la'an nɛ on dɛŋi an sʋ'ʋm tisi ya la.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Amaa nidib la da yɛl Josua ye, “Ayei! Tinam na dɔl Zugsɔb la!”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ka Josua yɛl nidib la ye, “Yanam mɛŋ di kasɛti tisi ya mɛŋ ye ya gaŋnɛ ye ya na dɔl Zugsɔb la.” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, tinam mɛŋi aan ti kasɛtib!”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Josua da yɛli ba ye, “Nannanna yʋ'ʋn lɔmmi buudzʋna bada linɛ bɛɛ ya san'an la bas, ka pɛligi ya sʋnya tis Zugsɔb, Israel Wina'am la!”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la yɛl Josua ye, “Tinam na dɔl Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am la ka siak o nɔɔr.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Daakan la Josua da maal nɔnaari tis nidib la, ka gban'e gban'ar nɛ ba, ka tisi ba zi'ela, Sekɛm teŋin la.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Josua da sɔbi li niŋ Wina'am wada gbauŋ la pʋʋgin, ka lɛn nɔk kugtita'ari ba'a li zi'el sappi titita'ar gbinnin, kpi'el Zugsɔb mɛŋ zin'ikanɛ an kasi la ni.

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: O da yɛl nidib la ye, “Gɔsimi! Kugkaŋa ye li anɛ kasɛti guri ya. Li wʋm Zugsɔb la pian'abanɛ ka o yɛli ti la wʋsa. Li na zi'enɛ di kasɛt, ya ya'a ka' sida dim Wina'am san'anɛ.” Ban mum sieba teŋin la

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Josua da kɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa lɛb o faari bɛ zin'isi'a.

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛnam nya'aŋ la, Josua onɛ an Nun biig ka lɛn an Zugsɔb tʋmtʋm la da anɛ yʋma kɔbiga nɛ piiga ka nyaan kpi.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ka ba mum o zin'ikanɛ ka o sʋ'oe ka li bɛ Timnaf Sera linɛ bɛ Efiram dinɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la, lɛbisid Gaas zuor la ya-datiuŋ.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Israel da dɔl Zugsɔb la sʋ'ʋŋa Josua vʋm saŋa la wʋsa, nɛ kpɛɛmnam banɛ da bɛ ka Josua nan kae ka mi' bʋn linɛ wʋsa ka Zugsɔb la tʋm tis Israel dim la.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Josef kɔnba linɛ ka Israel dim da zii mɔri yi Egipt teŋin na la mɛn, ba da mɔri li keŋ Sekɛm teŋinɛ mum zin'ikanɛ ka Jakob da nɔk anzurifa ligidi kɔbiga da' Hamor, onɛ saamme an Sekɛm la biis la san'an. Teŋ kaŋa da lieb Josef yaas la faar.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Ka Eleazar onɛ an Aaron biig la mɛ kpi ka ba mum o Gibea teŋin, zin'ikanɛ bɛ Efiram linɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ, ka ba da gaŋi li tis o biig Finehas la.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Josua da kpi la nya'aŋ, Israel dim da bu'os Zugsɔb la ye, “Anɔ'ɔnamɛ na gaad tuon yiiga zab nɛ Keenan dim la tisi ti?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da lɛbis ye, “Juda dim la na gaad tuon. M zaŋ teŋ la niŋi ba nu'usin.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Ka Juda dim la yɛl Simeon dim banɛ aan ba mabiis la ye, “Kemi na la'as nɛ ti keŋ sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ ka ba tisi ti la ni ka ti zab nɛ Keenan dim la ka tinam mɛ na kɛɛn ya teŋin la na zabi sʋŋi ya.” Ala ka Simeon dim la da dɔlli ba ka ba keŋ.

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Ka ba zabi nyaŋ Keenan dim la keŋ paae ba nimbanɛ bɛ Hebron, zin'ikanɛ ka ba da dɛŋin buon ye, Kiriaf Ariba la, ka nyaŋ nidib atan' banɛ yʋda buon ye Siesai nɛ Ahiman nɛ Talimai la.

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Adoni-Bezek da zɔya, amaa ka ba kad o hali gban'e o ka fi'is o nu'uraad nɛ o nɔbraad.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Ka Juda nidib duoe zab nɛ Jerusalem mɛ nyaŋ ka kʋ nidib la wʋsa ka nyu'oe teŋ la nɛ bugum.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Din nya'aŋ la ka Juda nidib keŋ zab nɛ Keenan dim banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna teŋin la nɛ Negef nɛ kʋkʋna sisɛrim la.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Ka yii ani zabi keŋ paae nimbanɛ bɛ Debir teŋin ka ba da dɛŋin buon ye, Kiriaf Seefa la.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Ka Kaleb yɛl ye, “M na zaŋi m pu'ayua Akisa tis dau kanɛ wʋsa zabi nyaŋ Kiriaf Seefa ka o di.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Ofniel onɛ an Kenas biig la da duoe zabi nyaŋ. Kenas da anɛ Kaleb pitʋ; ala ka Kaleb zaŋ o pu'ayua Akisa tis o ka o dii o.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: On da paae Ofniel yin la, daar yinne Akisa da yɛl o sid la ye, “Asɛɛ fʋ yɛli m saam ka o tisif paalʋ.” Ka pu'a la da naanɛ o bʋŋ la zugʋ sig la ka o saam Kaleb bu'os o ye, “Fʋ bɔɔd ye m maal bɔɔ tisi fɔ?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: O da lɛbis ye, “Tisim bʋn linɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa; fʋn sadigim tisim paalʋ Negef teŋin la, mɛ tisim bulig.” Ka Kaleb tis o bulis ayi', ka yinne bɛ teŋ la zugin ka yinne bɛ teŋir.

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ken dau kanɛ da an Moses diem la yaasi da yi tempʋkanɛ ka ba buon Kpʋkparis Teŋ la la'as nɛ Juda dim ye ba keŋ Juda Sian'ar linɛ bɛ Negef la zin'ini kpi'en nɛ Arad teŋ la.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Ani ka Juda dim keŋ la'as nɛ Simeon dim banɛ aan ba mabiis la zab nɛ Keenan dim banɛ bɛ Zefaf teŋin la san'am tempʋʋg la wʋsa. Dinzug ka ba da buon zin'ikan ye Horma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da bɛ nɛ Juda dim la, ka ba sʋ'ʋg kʋkʋna teŋ la wʋsa, amaa ba da pʋ nyaŋi kad nimbanɛ bɛ zin'ikanɛ ka paalʋ la dig sassi la, bɔzugɔ ba da mɔr widi tɛrekonam banɛ mɔr paŋ la zabid.

english_verse: The tribe of Judah gave the town of Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had told them to do. Caleb defeated the three Anakim clans and took over the town. The Benjamin Tribe Does Not Capture Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ba da zaŋ Hebron n tis Kaleb nwɛnɛ Moses n da zi'el si'em la, ka o kad Anak biribis atan' la yis anina.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Benjamin nidib la da pʋ nyaŋi kad Jebus dim banɛ da bɛ Jerusalem la, amaa Jebus dim la da kpɛn zin' nɛ ba Jerusalem teŋin la hali ti paae zina.

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Ba da tʋm nidib ye ba labisi kaae Betel teŋ kanɛ ka ba da dɛŋi buon ye Luz la.

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Ban da keŋ ye ba kaae teŋ la, ba da nyɛ dau ka o yit teŋ la pʋʋgin na ka ba yɛl o ye, “Pa'alimi ti tinamɛ na niŋ si'em kpɛn' teŋ la pʋʋgin ka ti na maalif sʋ'ʋŋa.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: O da pa'ali ba ka ba kpɛn' zabi kʋ teŋ la nidib ka bas dau la nɛ o yidim wʋsa.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Ala ka o da yii keŋ Hitti dim teŋin mɛ' tempʋʋg ka zaŋ o yʋ'ʋri pʋdi li ye Luz, ka yʋ'ʋr la kpɛm bɛɛ ala paae zina.

english_verse: Canaanites lived in the towns of Beth-Shan, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and all the villages nearby. The Canaanites were determined to stay, and the Manasseh tribe never did get rid of them. But later on, when the Israelites grew more powerful, they made slaves of the Canaanites.
translation_verse: Amaa Israel dimi yʋ'ʋn da paam paŋ la, ba da mugus Keenan dim la nɛ tʋʋm kpi'ema amaa ka pʋ kpɛn kadi ba yis nyainnɛ.

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Efiram dim mɛ da pʋ kad Keenan dim banɛ bɛ Giza la, amaa Keenan dim la da kpɛn la'am bɛ nɛ ba.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zebulun dim mɛ da pʋ kad Keenan dim banɛ bɛ Kitrun bɛɛ Nahalol la, ba da kpɛm bɛ nɛ ba; amaa ba da mugusi ka ba tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema tisidi ba.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Ka nɛ' zug Aser nidib la da la'am bɛnɛ nɛ Keenan dim banɛ bɛ teŋin la.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Naftali dim da pʋ kad banɛ bɛ Bet Semes bɛɛ Bet Anaf tɛɛnsin la, amaa ba da la'as nɛ Keenan dim banɛ bɛ teŋin la; ka li nya'aŋ ba da mugus banɛ bɛ Bet Semes nɛ Bet Anaf la ye ba tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema tisi ba.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amor dim la da kpɛn gu'ud Dan dimi keŋ paae kʋkʋna teŋ la ni, ka pʋ tisidi ba suor ka ba yit paalʋ zin'ikanɛ an nyain la nii.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amor dim la mɛ da mɔɔd ye ba kpɛn sʋ'ʋg Heres zuor la, nɛ Aijalon nɛ Saalibim tɛɛns la; amaa li nya'aŋ ka Josef yaas da nyɛ paŋ ka mugusi ba ye ba tʋm tʋʋm kpi'ema tisi ba.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Alazug ka Amor dim sʋ'ʋlim titɔndig da yi Akirabim keŋ paae Sela hali ka tʋʋg ani.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la Maliak da yi Gilgal teŋin kɛn Bokim na, yɛl ye, “M mɔri ya yi Egipt teŋin na, ka mɔri ya kɛn teŋ kanɛ ka m da pɔ nɔɔri zi'eli ya yaanam la na; ka yɛl ye, ‘M kʋ san'am nɔnaar kanɛ ka m da maal nɛ ya la.

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: Da la'asi ya mɛŋ nɛ teŋ la nidiba. San'amini ba malʋŋ bimbima la bas.’ Amaa ya pʋ siaki m nɔɔrɛ. Bɔ ka ya maal ala?

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Dinzug, nannanna m yɛti ya ye, ‘M kʋ kadi ba yisi ya san'anɛ; ba na an gɔn'ɔsi ya lʋga ni, ka ba wina la na an bɛndisi bɛndi ya.’”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Ala ka ba pʋd zin'ikan la ye Bokim. Anina ka ba da maal maana tis Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ka ba mum o zin'ikanɛ an o paalʋ ka aan o faar la, ka li bɛ Timnaf Heres linɛ bɛ Efiram dinɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la, lɛbisid Gaas zuor la ya-datiuŋ baba la. Zʋmaaŋ kanɛ an bugusim dim la yɛla

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Zʋmaaŋ kan la nidib wʋsa da maal ka'alim naae la nya'aŋ, zʋmaʋŋ si'a da duoe na ka zi' Zugsɔb la bɛɛ on maal si'el wʋsa tis Israel dim la.

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Israel dim ya'a da yi saŋsi'a wʋsa ye ba zab, Zugsɔb la pʋ tisidi ba suor ka ba nyaŋid nwɛnɛ on da pɔɔ zi'el si'em la. Ba da bɛnɛ namisʋg pʋʋgin. Wina'am n gaŋ banɛ na mɔr yɔlisim na la yɛla

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Ala ka Zugsɔb la gaans tuongatibi tisi ba ka ba faaɛn ba, ba bi'emnam nu'usin.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala ba da pʋ kɛlisidi ba tuongatib la nɔɔrɛ, amaa ka zɔti dɔl winsieba ka zun'odi ba. Ban da pʋ nwɛnɛ ba saamnama, ba da fɛndignɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ ka basi ba saamnamɛ da dɔl suosieba la, suokanɛ ka Zugsɔb la tis nɔɔr ye ba siaki dɔl la.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la ya'a da ɛɛnti tisi ba tuongat, o na bɛnɛ nɛ tuongat la ka faaɛn ba yisi ba dataas nu'usin tuongat la nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa la wʋsa; li anɛ Zugsɔb la da zɔti ba nimbaanlig ban da unsid nɛ tɔɔg ba dataas la da mugusidi ba ka namisidi ba la.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Amaa tuongat la ya'a da kpi, nidib la da fɛndignɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛd hali gaadi ba yaanamɛ da dɔl winsieba ka zun'odi ba la. Ba da zan'as ye ba kʋ basi ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nɛ ba tʋbzian'asim la.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Dinzug ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ Israel dim la ka o yɛl ye, “Israel dimi san'am nɔnaar kanɛ ka m da digili ba yaanam ka ba pʋ kɛlis man la zug,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: m kʋ lɛn kad buudbanɛ ka Josua da kad ka kpi la.

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka ba mak Israel dimi gɔs ye ba na kpɛn dɔl Zugsɔb la suor nwɛnɛ ba yaanamɛ da dɔllim si'em la”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka buudbanɛ bɛɛ anina la kpɛlim; o da pʋ kɛ ka Josua nyaŋi kadi ba vuguri n yisɛ.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: O da maal nɛ'ɛŋa ye o pa'al Israel yaas banɛ da nan zi' tanp nwɛ'ɛb la tanp nwɛ'ɛb suor.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Buudbanɛ da kpɛlim la anɛ; Filistia dim na'anam anu la, nɛ Keenan dim wʋsa nɛ Sidon dim nɛ Hivi dim banɛ bɛ Lebanon kʋkʋna din yi Baal Hemon zuorin paae Lebo-Hamat la.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ba da kpɛlim anina ye ba mak Israel dim la gɔs ye ba na di'e Zugsɔb la nɔzi'elʋg dinɛ ka o da tis Moses ye o tisi ba yaanam laa?

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: Israel dim da nɔk buudzʋna la pu'ayuosi tisi ba biribis ka nɔki ba mɛŋ bipumisi tisi ba biribis mɛn. Ka maannɛ ba wina nɛ ba teŋgbana la. Tuongat Ofniel n zabi nyaŋ Mesopotamia la yɛla

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon; ba da tami ba Zugsɔb Wina'am la yɛla ka zun'od teŋgbana banɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Baal nɛ Asera la.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ hali ka o kuosi ba tis Kusanrisiatam onɛ an Aram Naharam na'ab la, ka Israel dim da tʋm yʋma anii tis o.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Amaa ban da kaasi buol Zugsɔb la, o da gaŋ onɛ na faaɛn ba, onɛ da an Ofniel onɛ an Kenas biig la, Kenas da anɛ Kaleb pitʋ.

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Israel dim la da lɛn tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon, ka li zug kɛ ka Zugsɔb la da tis Eglon onɛ an Moab na'ab la paŋ ka o nyaŋ Israel dim la.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Eglon da la'as nɛ Ammon dim nɛ Amalek dimi zab nɛ Israel dim, ka faaɛn kpʋkparis Teŋ la.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Ehud n da tis yɔɔd la naae la, o da zi'el banɛ zi yɔɔd la kena la suor.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and the Lord chose Ehud from the Benjamin tribe to rescue them. They put Ehud in charge of taking the taxes to King Eglon, but before Ehud went, he made a double-edged dagger. Ehud was left-handed, so he strapped the dagger to his right thigh, where it was hidden under his robes.
translation_verse: Ehud da maal zaba sʋ'ʋbil kanɛ dit tuon nɛ nya'aŋ wʋsa, ka li wa'alim zemis nɛ o gbɛr, ka o sʋʋ li tɛɛngʋn n lɔɔ li o datiuŋ gbɛrin ka lusi li nɛ o fuug.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la kpɛlim zin' o kɔn'ɔkɔn' girimbisa la zug, na'am zin'ikanɛ ka o ɛɛnti zin' walʋsʋg saŋa la. Ehud da li'el o ka yɛl ye, “M mɔr labaar Wina'am san'an ye m yɛlif.” Na'ab la duoe o na'am gbauŋʋn la,

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: Ehud da zaŋi o dagɔbʋgʋ fuoe sʋ'ʋg la bɛɛ o datiuŋ gbɛrin la kʋns na'ab la pʋʋr.

english_verse: that even the handle was buried in his fat. Ehud left the dagger there. Then after closing and locking the doors to the room, he climbed through a window onto the porch
translation_verse: Ka Ehud yi za'ambɛŋin na ka yɔ' za'anɔya banɛ dʋt girimbisa la zug la ka kpari ba.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: On gaad la nya'aŋ, ka yammis la kena nyɛ ka girimbisa la za'anɔya kpar. Ka ba yɛl ye, “Daasi'erɛ o bɛnɛ bangida ni.”

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Ka ba gu'usid hali ka li ti kena mɔr nyan, amaa on da yuug ka pʋ yɔ'ɔg za'anɔya la ka ba zaŋ saafi na yɔ'ɔsi ba. Ani ka ba nyɛɛ ba zugdaan la kpii dig teŋin.

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Ban nan gu'usid la, ka Ehud niaki dɔl bada la bɛ si'el la su'a gaadi paae Seira teŋ.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “Dɔlli man nya'aŋ! Zugsɔb la zaŋ Moab dim banɛ aan ya dataas la niŋi ya nu'usin.” Ka ba dɔl o keŋ sʋ'ʋg ban lɔ'ɔŋid Joodan zin'isi'a ken Moab teŋin la, ka pʋ tis suor ka sɔ' na nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋ anina.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Din yi dabiskan la daar ka Moab yʋ'ʋn tʋmmi tisid Israel dim ka di'edi ba nɔɔr; ka teŋ la digin nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm paae yʋma pisnii. Tuongat Seamiga n faaɛn Israel dim si'em

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Ehud nya'aŋ la, Seamiga onɛ an Anaf biig la da zaŋ nɛ balaar kanɛ ka ba mɔri kem niigi kʋ Filistia dim kɔbisyuobʋ. Onɛ mɛ da faaɛn Israel dim la bas.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ehud kum nya'aŋ la, Israel nidib da lɛn tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon

english_verse: So the Lord let the Canaanite King Jabin of Hazor conquer Israel. Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, lived in Harosheth-Ha-Goiim.
translation_verse: ka o nɔki ba niŋ Jabin onɛ an Keenan na'ab ka zin' Hazo teŋin la nu'usin. O soogianam kpɛɛm da anɛ Sisera. O da bɛ nɛ Harosief-Hagoyim teŋin,

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Ka Sisera lɛn yɛl ye, “Zi'enim za'anɔɔrin la, ka sɔ' ya'a kena bu'osif ye fʋ pʋ nyɛ sɔ' kpɛlaa, fʋn yɛlim ye ayei.”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Debora onɛ an Wina'am nɔdi'espu'ak, ka an Lapidof pu'a la da an Israel dim tuongat saŋkan la.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: O da maal antu'a zin'ig kpʋkparig gbinnin ka ba buon ye, Debora Kpʋkparig ka li bɛ Rama nɛ Betel tɛɛns la teŋsʋk, ka an kʋkʋna teŋ linɛ bɛ Efiram sʋ'ʋlimin la. Israel dim da ken o san'an na ka o maannɛ ba pian'adi tisidi ba.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: O da tʋm buol Barak onɛ an Abinoam biig ka yi Kades Naftali teŋin la yɛl o ye, “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la tisif nɔɔr. Kem Naftali nɛ Zebulun tɛɛns la nii bɔ dap tusa piiga ka ya dɔl Tabo zuor suor la.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: M na pan'as Sisera, onɛ an Jabin soogianam kpɛɛm la, on nɛ o zaba tɛrekonam nɛ zabzabidib la wʋsa ka ba keŋ Kison kɔlʋgin la. M na nɔki ba niŋi fʋ nu'usin.”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Ka Debora yɛl ye, “Li an sʋ'ʋŋa, m na dɔlli fʋ keŋ. Amaa fʋn niŋid si'em la, na'asi la kʋ aan fʋ dinɛ: Zugsɔb la na zaŋ Sisera niŋ pu'a nu'ugin.” Ka duoe dɔl Barak n keŋ Kedes teŋin la.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Saŋkan ka Heber onɛ an Ken nid la da bas Ken dim sieba banɛ an Hobab onɛ da an Moses dakiig yaas la, ka keŋ ti' o fuug sʋgʋri kpi'el nɛ titita'ar dinɛ bɛ Zaananim ka pʋ lal nɛ Kedes la. Ba nyaŋ Sisera ka kʋʋ o

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl Sisera ye Barak Abinoam biig la gaadi keŋ dʋ Tabo zuor la,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Debora da yɛl Barak ye, “Kem! Zina an dabiskanɛ ka Zugsɔb la na zaŋ Sisera niŋi fʋ nu'usin. Hali Zugsɔb la pʋn gaadi fʋ tuon sa” Barak da sig Tabo zuor la teŋir, ka dap tusa piiga la dɔl o nya'aŋ.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Barak n da ken tuon la, Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka ba zabi nyaŋ Sisera nɛ o tɛrekonam nɛ o soogianam wʋsa, ka Sisera bas o tɛreko la ka zɔ nɛ nɔba.

english_verse: Barak's forces went after Sisera's chariots and army as far as Harosheth-Ha-Goiim. Sisera's entire army was wiped out.
translation_verse: Amaa Barak da kati dɔl tɛrekonam nɛ soogianam la paae Harosief-Hagoyim. Zabzabidib la wʋsa da kpinɛ tanpin; dau baa yinne da pʋ kpɛlim.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, Sisera da zɔ nɛ nɔba paae kpɛn' Jael onɛ an Heber pu'a la sʋgʋrin. Heber da anɛ Ken nid, bɔzugɔ o zugdaan Hazo Na'ab Jabin da maal zuod nɛ Heber dɔɔg dim la.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Jael da yii tʋ'ʋs Sisera ka yɛl o ye, “M zugdaana, kpɛn'ɛm na, da zɔt dabiem!” Ka o kpɛn' o sʋgʋrin la, ka o nɔk fuudi pil o.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Ka Sisera yɛl o ye, “Ku'onuudi mɔrim, nɔkim ku'om tisim ka m nu.” Ka o yɔ'ɔg bin'isim dinɛ ka ba maali su gan'arin la tis o ye o nu, lɛbis fuud la pil o.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Amaa Jael da zaŋ kpa'ar linɛ ka ba mɔri ba'ad Fuug Sʋgʋr la nɛ zan'ari keŋ o san'an baanlimm ka o gɛn hali digi gbisid, ka o nɔk kpa'ar la kpa' o gbɛ'ɛlaa tɔlig teŋin, ka o kpi.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Ka Barak bɛn Sisera paae na, ka Jael yina tʋ'ʋs o ka yɛl ye, “Kem na ka m na pa'alif dau kanɛ ka fʋ ieed la!” Ka o dɔl o kpɛn', ka Sisera kpii digi ka kpa'ar kpa' o gbɛ'ɛlaa tɔlig teŋ.

english_verse: That same day God defeated the Canaanite King Jabin while the Israelites looked on, and his army was no longer powerful enough to attack the Israelites.
translation_verse: Daakan la Wina'am da kɛ ka Israel dim nyaŋ Jabin Keenan dim na'ab la.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim maligim paam paŋi nyaŋ Keenan dim na'ab Jabin hali nɛ ban ti san'am o naae.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Daakan la ka Debora nɛ Barak onɛ an Abinoam biig la, da yʋ'ʋm yʋʋm kaŋa:

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: “Israel na'abiis gaad tuon, nidib la siaki pɛsigi ba mɛŋ. Wɔ'ɔgim Zugsɔb la!

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, fʋn da yi Seir teŋin ka dɔlisi keŋ Edom sʋ'ʋlimin la, teŋ da damya, ka agɔla kpa'ae ku'om, ka saŋgbana kpa'ae saku'om sigis na.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Siamega onɛ an Anaf biig la saŋa la, nɛ Jael saŋa la, Nidib da bas suoraad la ka dɔl suobuga.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Nidib da pʋ lɛn zu'oe teŋkpɛmisin ya'asa, hali ti paae saŋkanɛ ka man Debora duoe na, m da duoe zi'enɛ lieb Israel dim ma.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Israel dimi da gaŋ win paala saŋsi'a la, ka tanp da nwɛ'ɛd tɛɛns za'anɔya ni; ba zabzabidib banɛ an tusa pisnaasi la sʋʋgin, ba nid baa yinne da pʋ mɔr kpan bɛɛ gbanti'edʋgɔ.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: M nyɔɔg bɛ nɛ Israel na'abiis nɛ banɛ siaki pɛsigi ba mɛŋ la ni. Wɔ'ɔgimi Zugsɔb la!

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Yanam banɛ ban'ad bʋmpielis, ka zin' ga'ar dinɛ ka ba maal nɛ fusʋma zug la, hali nɛ yanam banɛ ken nɔba la wʋsa.

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Kɛlisimi banɛ la'as kɔlisin la yʋ'ʋm si'em. Ba yʋ'ʋmnɛ Zugsɔb pʋpielim tʋʋma la yɛla; O zabzabidib banɛ an pʋpielim dim Israel dimin la. Ka Zugsɔb nidib la yii keŋ tempʋʋg la za'anɔya ni.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Duom zi'en, duom zi'en, Debora. Duom zi'en, duom zi'enɛ yʋ'ʋm yʋʋma! Duom zi'en fʋn Barak onɛ an Abinoam biiga, Duom dɔl banɛ ka fʋ zabi nyaŋ la keŋ.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Ka nimbanɛ kpɛlim la sigi kɛn kpɛɛmnam la san'an na; Zugsɔb nidib la sigi paae m san'an na ye ba zab.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Sieba yinɛ Efiram na sig bɔn'ɔgin la, dɔlli yi Amalek teŋin; ‘Benjamin dim la dɔlli fʋ nidib la nya'aŋ!’ Kpɛɛmnam yi Makir dɔɔdin sig na, ba anɛ banɛ yi Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin la ka ziid zabzabidib kpɛɛm la dansaar.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Isaka tuongatib la bɛ Debora ni; Sida, Isaka dɔl Barak nya'aŋ, ka ba keŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ paae bɔn'ɔgin la. Amaa Reuben teŋ sʋ'ʋlimin la ba tɛn'ɛsidnɛ pʋtɛnda ayi', yi'.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka ya la'as nɛ banɛ kem kɔnbid ka ya tʋba wʋm kɔnbkemnib wiis piebʋgɔ? Reuben teŋ sʋ'ʋlimin la ba sid da tɛn'ɛsid pʋtɛnda ayi', yi'.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gilead dim kpɛlim Joodan kɔldaug la nya'aŋ. Ka bɔ ka Dan on nan kpɛm bɛ anrima la ni? Aser dim kpɛlim atɛuk la nɔɔrin, ka bɛ zin'ikanɛ ka anrima dɔlli sigid ku'omin la.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Zebulun nɛ Naftali nidib la kuosi ba nyɔvʋya, ka dɔl zaba zin'ikanɛ an kʋkʋna zug la.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Ani ka na'anam la yina zab; Keenan na'anam zab Taanak teŋin, zin'ikanɛ kpi'e Megido ku'om la, amaa ba pʋ nyaŋi faaɛn anzurifa bɛɛ ligidii.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Nwadbibis zab agɔl, ban bɛɛ agɔla ken la, ka zab nɛ Sisera.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kison kɔldaug la dii ba mɔri keŋ, Kison kɔldaug la anɛ kɔldakʋdʋg. M na keŋ tuon nɛ paŋ!

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Widi la kena dɛɛd nɛ paŋ; ka ba tafɛɛd la dammid parigid-parigid.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la yɛl ye, ‘Nɔpɔɔr bɛ Meroz teŋ la zug! Pɔɔm nɔpɔbɛ'ɛdi niŋ nidib la. Bɔzugɔ ba pʋ kena sʋŋ Zugsɔb la, ba sid pʋ sʋŋi zab nɛ banɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ la.’

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Jael anɛ pu'a kanɛ yʋ'ʋri mɔr albareka pu'ab sʋʋgin, o anɛ Heber onɛ an Ken nid la pu'a, O yʋ'ʋr dʋti gat pu'ab banɛ bɛ sʋga ni la wʋsa.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Dau la sɔs nɛ ku'om, ka o tis o bin'isim, lakanɛ nar nɛ ninsʋma la ka o zaŋi niŋ bin'isgbisidim tis o.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: O da zaŋ sʋgʋr kpa'ar nu'ug yinne ni, ka zaŋ tʋmtʋmnib zan'ar o datiuŋ nu'ugin keŋ nwɛ' Sisera zugʋ nwa'ae, ka kpa' o gbɛ'ɛlaa la, ka li buak.

english_verse: Sisera sank to his knees and fell dead at her feet.
translation_verse: Ka o lii o nɔba ni, o nɔba ni ka o da li; ka on li si'el la, ani ka o kpi.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sisera ma gɔsid takoro ni, o gɔsid takoro la vɔnya ni gu'usid ye o na lɛb na, ka yɛt ye ‘Bɔɔ niŋ ka o zaba tɛrekonam la nam pʋ kena? Bɔ ka tɛrekonam banɛ zu'oe hali la yuugɛ?’

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: ‘Anwaa o la'asid nɛ la'abanɛ ka ba zabi faaɛn la pʋdigid ka dau woo di'ed pu'asadir yinne bɛɛ ayi', yi', ka Sisera na paam fubanɛ pɔnri vɛnl, ka mɔr fubanɛ vɛnl pamm na tis mam.’

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: Zugsɔba! Kɛl ka fʋ bi'emnam wʋsa bɔdig ala! Amaa kɛl ka banɛ nɔŋif la nwɛnɛ winnigi tansid na nɛ paŋ si'em la.” Ka teŋ la da mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm paae yʋma pisnaasi.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Israel nidib da lɛn tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon, ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka ba namis yʋma ayɔpɔi Midian dim nu'usin.

english_verse: The Midianites were so cruel that many Israelites ran to the mountains and hid in caves.
translation_verse: Midian dim la da mugusidi ba nɛ hali, ka ba gʋ'ʋŋi maali ba sʋga kʋkʋna ni nɛ tampinlɛma ni nɛ ba kpi'euŋ zin'isin.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ wʋsa ka Israel nidib maali ba pɔɔd, Midian dim nɛ Amalek dim nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la da kpɛn'ɛdnɛ teŋ la nii faandi ba zʋʋd la nɛ paŋ.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Ba da kpɛn' na nɛ ba bʋnkɔnbid nɛ ba sʋga la'adi pɛ'ɛl teŋ la wʋʋ na'azɔmnam nɛ. Fʋ da kʋ nyaŋi kaal ban nɛ ba yʋgʋma laa. Ba da zin'in teŋin la hali ka san'am teŋ la la'ad wʋsa.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da kaasi buol Zugsɔb la Midian dim la da namisidi ba la zug,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: M yɛli ya ye, “Manɛ aan ya Zugsɔb Wina'am la, da pʋ'ʋsi Amor dim banɛ ka ya bɛɛ ba teŋin la wina la.” Amaa ya pʋ wʋm tisi ma.’” Zugsɔb maliak n da keŋ Gideon san'an si'em

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la Maliak da keŋ zin'in titita'ar gbinnin, ka tiig la bɛ Ofra teŋin. Joas onɛ an Abieza dim nid la da sʋ'oe li. Zin'ikan la ka Joas biig Gideon zɔ Midian dim la ka keŋi su'a bʋmbɔk kanɛ ka ba nwiakid tiwala daam la bʋ'ʋd o ki.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak da nie o mɛŋi pa'al Gideon ka yɛl o ye, “Zugsɔb bɛ nɛf, fʋn kanɛ an zabzabida amɛŋa!”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Amaa Gideon da lɛbis o ye, “Ka Zugsɔb la ya'a bɛ nɛ ti, wala ka nwa' maannɛ ti? Ka o nyalima la bɛ yaanɛ? Ti yaanam da yɛli ti ye, ‘Zugsɔb la tʋm nyalima mɔri ti yi Egipt na.’ Amaa nannanna Zugsɔb la basi ti ka kɛ ka ti lu Midian dim nu'usin.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la fɛndigi yɛl o ye, “Kem nɛ paŋ kanɛ ka fʋ mɔr la faaɛn Israel Midian dim nu'ugin. Ka' manɛ tʋmi fɔɔ?”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Amaa Gideon da lɛbis Zugsɔb la ye, “M ye m niŋ wala faaɛn Israel dim la? Tinam tuŋ la an tadimnam Manase dɔɔg ni, ka mam mɛ an tadimbʋʋg m saam zak la ni.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “M na bɛ nɛf ka fʋ na kʋ Midian dim la vuguri wʋʋ fʋn na kʋ nid yinne nɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Gideon yɛl ye, “M ya'a paae fʋ ya'am, fʋn maal zanbinnɛ pa'alim ye fʋnɛ pian'adi tisidim.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: M bɛlimnɛ, da keŋɛ ka m keŋ mɔr piini na tisif.” Ka Zugsɔb la ye, “M na gurif ka fʋ lɛb na.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Ka Gideon kul yinnɛ kʋ bʋʋg ka nɔk zɔ'ɔm dinɛ nam pʋ gɛndig danbinnɛ maal bodobodo, ka dʋg ni'im la niŋ laan, ka kpa'ae biim la niŋ dʋkʋnɛ mɔri kena tis Zugsɔb maliak la, tiig la gbinnin.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am maliak la yɛl o ye, “Nɔkim ni'im la nɛ bodobodo la zi'el tampiing la zug, ka kpa'ae biim la pu'al!” Ka Gideon maal ala.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb maliak la nɔk dansaar kanɛ bɛɛ o nu'ugin la si'is ni'im nɛ bodobodo dinɛ pʋ gɛndig danbin la. Ka bugum yi tampiingin la na di ni'im nɛ bodobodo la wʋsa. Ka Zugsɔb maliak la kpɛn mɛlim ani.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Gideon n baŋ ye li anɛ Zugsɔb maliak la, ka yɛl ye, “Woo! M Zugsɔb Wina'am! Man nyɛ fʋn Zugsɔb maliak la nɛ m nini nwa!”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem. Mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm! Bɔzugɔ fʋ kʋ kpii.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Ka Gideon mɛ' bimbim anina tis Zugsɔb la, ka pʋdi li ye, Zugsɔb la anɛ Sumbʋgʋsʋm Daan. Ka li kpɛm bɛ Ofra linɛ bɛ Abieza dim sʋ'ʋlimin la hali nɛ zina. Gideon n nwa'ae Baal ba'ar si'em

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la ka Zugsɔb yɛl o ye, “Gba'ami fʋ saam na'arapɔl, kanɛ paas ayi' ka an yʋma ayɔpɔi la fʋ saam na'abaukʋn la nɛ na'araug kanɛ bi', ka nwa'ae bimbim kanɛ ka fʋ saam mɔri maan Baal ba'ar la, ka kɔ'ɔg o Asera ba'ar daug la bas.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Ka mɛ' bimbim kanɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa tis Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la kʋkʋn kaŋa zug. Ka nɔk na'arapɔl kanɛ ka fʋ kʋʋ paas ayi' la pa'al Asera ba'ar daug kanɛ ka fʋ kɔ' la zugʋ nyu'oe ka li an nyu'or maan.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Ka Gideon yis o yammis piiga keŋ maal Zugsɔb la ye o maal si'em la. Amaa on da zɔt o yidim dabiem nɛ teŋ la dim la zug, o pʋ maal nintaŋa, o da maalnɛ yʋ'ʋŋ.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka teŋ la nidib yina nyɛ ka Baal bimbim la nwa'ae ka ba'ar Asera daug la mɛ kɔ', ka nyɛ ka ba nɔk na'arapɔl la maal malʋŋ.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Ka ba bu'os taaba ye, “Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ maal nwa'?” Ka ban vɛɛnsi gɔs la ba yɛl ye, “Gideon onɛ an Joas biig la tʋmi li.”

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Ka teŋ la dap yɛl Joas ye, “Mɔri fʋ biig la yis na! Asɛɛ ka o kpi, bɔzugɔ o nwa'ae Baal bimbim, ka kɔ'ɔg Asera ba'ar daug!”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Amaa Joas da lɛbis nimbanɛ sʋʋnri duoe ka ba gilig o la ye, “Ya ye ya sʋŋnɛ Baal ba'arɛ? Ya bɔɔd ye ya faaɛn o nɛɛ? Ayei! Onɛ wʋsa ye o zabi sʋŋ o na kpi bɛkanɛ nied nwa'! Baal ya'a sid anɛ ba'ar kanɛ mɔr paŋ, on faanm o mɛŋ, bɔzugɔ, li anɛ o bimbim ka ba nwa'ae.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Ka lin yi daakan, ba da yʋ'ʋn buon Gideon ye Jerubaal; ka li gbin an ye, “Kɛl ka Ba'ar la Zab nɛ o” bɔzugɔ onɛ nwa'ae ba'ar la bimbim.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka banɛ an Midian dim nɛ Amalek dim nɛ banɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la wʋsa da la'as taaba lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la gu' Jezireel bɔn'ɔgin la.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Siig da sig Gideon san'an ka o pieb na'atannɛ buol Abieza dim la, ye ba dɔl o.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ka lɛm mɔɔl labaari tis Manase dim wʋsa ye ba yim tanp nɛ banɛ an Aser nɛ Zebulun nɛ Naftali dim wʋsa, ka ba wʋsa mɛ yii kidigi ba.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: m na nɔk gungumi digil zieŋin. Ka mɛligim ya'a lu gungum la zugin ka teŋ la wʋsa an kpi'emis, m na baŋ ye fʋ na faaɛn Israel ka li yinɛ man nu'ugin, nwɛnɛ fʋn yɛl si'em la.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Ka li sid maal ala. Ka Gideon duoe bɛkɛung alifa nɔk gungum la nwiak, ka mɛligim ku'om la yina pɛ'ɛl nwam.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Ka Gideon lɛn yɛl Wina'am ye, “Da kɛ ka fʋ sʋʋnr pɛlig nɛ ma; kɛl ka m lɛm mak bʋn yinne gɔs. Kɛl ka m lɛn nɔk gungum la maki gɔs. Nannanna kɛl ka gungum la an kpi'emis ka mɛligim luu gilig teŋ la wʋsa ni.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la ka Wina'am tʋm ala, ka gungum la ma'aa an kpi'emis ka teŋ la pɛ'ɛl nɛ mɛligim.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Jerubaal, onɛ an Gideon la nɛ o nidib da duoe bɛogʋn keŋ gu' Harod buligin la. Ka Midian dim la mɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔkanɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ ka kpi'e zuokanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Moreh la baba.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Gideon ye, “Nimbanɛ ka fʋ mɔri ye ba zab Midian dim la zu'oe nɛ galis. Li na kɛ ka Israel dim ti nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg ye ba mɛŋ paŋ ka ba nyaŋ zaba la.

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Mɔɔlim tis nidib la ye, onɛ zɔt dabiem on lɛm ka bas Gilead zuor la.” Ka nidib tusa pisi nɛ ayi' lɛb. Ka kɛ tusa piiga.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Ka fʋ ya'a zɔt dabiem, fʋn kem sig zin'ikanɛ ka ba bɛ la ni, fʋn nɛ fʋ tʋmtʋm Pura.

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Zugsɔb yɛl Gideon ye, “Ba nan kpɛn zu'oe nɛ. Mɔri ba sig ku'omin la ka m na sie ba kal la tisif. Ka onɛ wʋsa ka m ye o da keŋ zaba la on da keŋɛ, ka onɛ wʋsa ka m ye o kem, on kem.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Ka Gideon mɔri ba sig ku'omin la, ka Zugsɔb yɛl o ye, “Bakim banɛ nuud ku'om la wʋʋ baa liasid si'em la ka kɛ banɛ igi nuud la.”

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Nidib kɔbistan' daa kabisidnɛ nuud, ka banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa igi nuud.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb yɛl Gideon ye, “Nidib kɔbistan' banɛ kabisid ku'om la nuud la, ban ka m ye m nɔk ka ya nyaŋ Midian dim la. Kɛl ka banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa lɛbi kul.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la, Zugsɔb la da yɛl Gideon ye, “Duom keŋ zab nɛ nidib la, ka mam tisi ya nyaŋir.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: Ya na wʋm ban yɛt si'el la wʋsa ka ya na nyɛ sʋnkpi'euŋʋ zab nɛ ba.” Ka Gideon nɛ o tʋmtʋm Pura keŋ hali paae zin'ikanɛ ka ba dataas la'as ye ba zab nɛ ba la.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Midian nidib nɛ Amalek nidib nɛ buudbanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la wʋsa da zu'oe nwɛnɛ na'azɔmnam nɛ, ba da mɔr yʋgʋma ka ba zu'oe nwɛnɛ kɔlʋgin titanbin'isʋg nɛ.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Gideon n paae anina la, o wʋm ka dau sɔ' pian'ad o tiraan on zaansim si'em. O yɛl ye on zaansim nɛ ka bodobodo gbil biligi sigi ba gbɛɛnb zin'igin la na nwɛ' Fuug Sʋgʋr yinne. Ka Fuug Sʋgʋr la lu teŋinɛ san'am.

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ka o zua la lɛbis ye, “Li ka' si'el si'ela, li anɛ Israel nid onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Gideon ka o saam an Joas la sʋ'ʋraugʋ la, Wina'am zaŋ Midian dimi niŋ o nu'usin, ka o nyaŋ zabzabidib la.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Gideon n wʋm dau la zaansʋŋ la nɛ li gbinnɛ an si'em la, o igin o duma zug, ka wɔ'ɔg Zugsɔb la, ka duoe lɛb Israel dim la san'an ka yɛli ba ye, “Duomi ka Zugsɔb la nɔk Midian dim la niŋi ti nu'usin!”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Ka mam nɛ m nidib la ya'a piebi ti na'atana la, yanam mɛ piebi ya na'atana la ka dʋ'ʋsi ya kʋkɔya yɛt ye, “Li anɛ Zugsɔb nɛ Gideon din!”

english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
