translation_verse: Gideon nɛ o nidib kɔbig la da paae zaba la zin'igin, ka li anɛ yʋ'ʋŋ tisʋʋs, saŋkan ka nimbanɛ ka ba tiak la yina ye ba gur za'anɔɔr la. Ka Gideon nɛ o nidib la kpɛm piebi ba na'atana la, ka nwa'ae ba yʋya banɛ ka ba zaŋ bugum niŋi li pʋʋgin la,

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: ka banɛ an pʋdigir ayi' kpɛlim la mɛ niŋ ala mɛn. Ba wʋsa da zanl bugum mɔɔg la nɛ ba dagɔbʋg nu'usin ka zanl na'atana la ba datiuŋ nu'usin ka tansid agɔla, gɔla yɛt ye, “Zugsɔb la nɛ Gideon zaba sʋ'ʋraug!”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Ka sɔ' wʋsa zi'enɛ gilig zaba zin'ig la. Ka ba dataas banɛ an Midian dim la wʋsa zɔt ka kaasid.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Ka nidib kɔbistan' la wʋsa piebi ba na'atana la, ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka ba dataas la tulig taaba. Ba da zɔɔ kpa' nɛ Zaretan hali ti paae Bet Sitta, teŋ kanɛ bɛ Abɛl Mehola kpi'e Tabaf la.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Ba da buol Israel nimbanɛ an Naftali dɔɔg nɛ Aser dɔɔg nɛ Manase dɔɔg dim la ka ba yina kad Midian dim la.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Ka Gideon tʋm nidib Efiram linɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la ye ba yɛli ba ye ba yim na gu' Midian dim la zin'ikanɛ ka ba na lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la, hali ti paae Bet Bara. Ka ba buol Efiram dim la ka ba yina gu' zin'ibanɛ bɛ Joodan la, hali ti paae Bet Bara.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Ba da gban'e Midian na'anama ayi' banɛ yʋda da an Oreb nɛ Zeeb la. Ba da kʋ Oreb nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba buon ye Oreb Tampiing la zug, ka kʋ Zeeb bʋmbɔk kanɛ ka ba nwiakid tiwala daam ka ba buon ye Zeeb Daam Bʋmbɔk la ni. Ba da kad Midian dim la lalig sa, ka mɔr Oreb nɛ Zeeb zut na tis Gideon saŋkanɛ ka o da bɛ Joodan kɔldaug baba la.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Efiram dim la yʋ'ʋn da bu'os Gideon ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ maali ti wala? Fʋn daa keŋ ye fʋ zab nɛ Midian dim la, bɔ ka fʋ daa pʋ buoli ti?” Ka zɛrig o hali.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Amaa o lɛbisi ba ye, “Bɔ ka man tʋm ka li na nyaŋi mak nɛ yanama? Hali yanam Efiram dimi tʋm si'el bi'ela la pʋ gaad tinam Abieza dimi tʋm si'el la wʋsa?

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Wina'am zaŋ Oreb nɛ Zeeb, banɛ an Midian tuongatib la, niŋi ya nu'usin. Bɔ ka man nyaŋi tʋm ka li zem nɛ ya?” Ani ka ba sʋʋnr la lɛbi bʋk.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: O da yɛl Sukot teŋ dim la ye, “Nɔkimi diibi tisim zabzabidib la, ka ba gɛnnɛ, ka man nan katnɛ Zeba nɛ Zalmunna banɛ an Midian na'anam la.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Amaa Sukot kpɛɛmnam la yɛl o ye, “Fʋ nam pʋ gban'e Zeba nɛ Zalmunna fʋ nu'usinɛ, ka bɔzug ka ti na tisi fʋ zabzabidib la diibɔ?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Ka Gideon lɛbis ye, “Nɛ' zug, Zugsɔb la ya'a ti zaŋ Zeba nɛ Zalmunna niŋi m nu'usin, m na aansi ya niŋgbina nɛ zaaŋ gɔn'ɔs nɛ gɔn'ɔs banɛ bɛ pipirigin la!”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Ka yii ani gaadi paae Peniel teŋin sɔsi ba mɛn, amaa ka ba lɛbis o nwɛnɛ Sukot dim la yɛl o si'em la.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl Peniel dim la ye, “M ya'a ti nyaŋ ka lɛb na, m na nwa'ae ya girimbisa la.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Ka Gideon lɛb na yɛl Sukot dim la ye, “Zeba nɛ Zalmunna nwana, banɛ yɛla ka ya pa'asim nɛ man ka yɛl ye, ‘Fʋ dɛŋi gban'e Zeba nɛ Zalmunna fʋ nu'usinɛɛ, ka bɔzug ka ti na tisi fʋ zabzabidib banɛ gɛn la diibɔ?’”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Gideon da dɔlisidnɛ banɛ kem kɔnbid suoya, Noba nɛ Jogbeha tɛɛns la nya'aŋ, ka libig Midian dim zabzabidib la.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Zeba nɛ Zalmunna, banɛ an Midian na'anama ayi' la, da zɔnɛ, amaa o da kadi ba hali gban'e ba, ka ba zabzabidib la wʋsa zɔɔ widig.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Gideon onɛ an Joas biig la da yi zaba la nii lɛb na, ka dɔl zin'ikanɛ buon Heres Suor la.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Ani ka o gban'e dasaŋ onɛ yi Sukot na, ka kɛ ka o sɔb teŋ la kpɛɛmnam nɛ ba tuongatib la yʋda tis o; nidib pisyɔpɔi nɛ ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: O da gban'e teŋ la kpɛɛmnam ka nɔk zaaŋ nɛ gɔn'ɔs banɛ bɛ pipirisin la namisi ba pa'ali ba ya'am.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: O mɛ da nwa'ae Peniel girimbisa la, ka kʋ teŋ la nidib wʋsa.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Ka bu'os Zeba nɛ Zalmunna ye, “Nimbɔ buudi ka ya daa kʋ Tabo zuorin la?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ba daa nwɛnɛ fʋ nɛ, sɔ' wʋsa daa nwɛnɛ na'abiig nɛ.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Ka Gideon lɛbis ye, “Bama daa anɛ man ba'abiis, ba anɛ mam mɛŋ ma pʋʋgin biis. Nɛ Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zugɔɔ, ya ya'a daa pʋ kʋʋnɛ baa, mam mɛ kʋ kʋʋ yaa.”

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Ka o fɛndigi kpa' Jeta, onɛ an o bikpɛɛm la, yɛl o ye, “Kʋʋmi ba!” Amaa Jeta pʋ fuoe o sʋ'ʋgɔ bɔzugɔ, o da anɛ biribiŋ bil ka zɔt dabiem.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Ka Zeba nɛ Zalmunna yɛl o ye, “Kem na tʋmi li fʋ mɛŋ. Dau la an si'em la o paŋ mɛ anɛ ala.” Ka Gideon yi tuon na kʋʋ ba, ka yisi ba yʋgʋma la baans banɛ bɛɛ ba niŋgɔnya ni la. Teŋ la da anɛ baanlimm Gideon tuon gaadʋg saŋa

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Israel dim da yɛl Gideon ye, “Dim na'am ka sʋ'oe ti, fʋn nɛ fʋ biig nɛ fʋ yaaŋ la wʋsa bɔzugɔ, fʋ faaɛn ti Midian dim nu'usin.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Amaa Gideon da yɛli ba ye, “Man kʋ aan ya na'ab bɛɛ m biig aan ya na'aba. Zugsɔb la na aan ya na'ab.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Ka yɛli ba ye, “M mɔr sɔsʋg yinne ye m sɔs nɛ ya, sɔ' wʋsa tisim tʋblɛm banɛ ka ya faaɛn pʋdig la.” .

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Ba da lɛbis ye, “Ti sʋnya malis nɛ tinamɛ na zaŋi tisif.” Ka ba zaŋ fuugʋ yadig ka sɔ' wʋsa yis tʋblɛm banɛ ka ba faaɛn pʋdig la nii lɔb fuugin la.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ka o pu'abil onɛ da bɛ Sekɛm la mɛ da du'a biribiŋi tis o, ka o pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Abimelek.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Gideon da kʋdignɛ hali paae o bɛn ka kpi, ka ba mum o, o ba' Joas yaʋgʋn, Ofra teŋin linɛ bɛ Abieza dim sʋ'ʋlimin la. Daamʋgʋ duoe Gideon kum nya'aŋ la yɛla

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Gideon kum nya'aŋ la, li pʋ yuugɛ ka Israel dim lieb wʋʋ pu'agɔɔnda nɛ, lɛm pʋ'ʋsid Baal dinɛ an teŋgban la. Ba da maalnɛ Baal Berit n zi'el ka o aan ba ba'ar

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: ka tami ba Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ faaɛn ba, ba bi'emnam nu'usin zin'ig wʋsa la yɛla.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da pʋ tʋm sʋm tis Jerubaal yidima, hali la'an nɛ on da tʋm tʋʋm sʋŋ si'a tisi ba la.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: “O da bu'os Sekɛm nidib wʋsa ye, ‘Bɔɔ an sʋm tisi ya, Jerubaal biis pisyɔpɔi la na sʋ'ʋgi ya bɛɛ ya bɔɔdnɛ dau yinne ma'anɛ? Tɛnri ye man anɛ ya ziim.’”

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl nɛ'ɛŋa tis Sekɛm nidib la, ba wʋsa da siak ye ba na dɔl Abimelek, bɔzugɔ ba da yɛl ye, “O anɛ ti sizua.”

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: O da keŋ Ofra linɛ aan o saam Jerubaal teŋin la zaŋ o ba'abiis pisyɔpɔi la wʋsa kʋ tampiing yinne zug. Amaa Jotam, onɛ an Jerubaal kpaanr la da zɔɔ su'a.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Sekɛm nɛ Bet Milo nidib la wʋsa da la'as Sekɛm titita'ar kanɛ kpi'e nɛ kugir kanɛ ba'a zi'e sappi la nii diis Abimelek na'am.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl Jotam nɛ'ɛŋa la, o da dʋ Gerizim zuor zug ka tansi agɔla yɛli ba ye, “Kɛlisimi, Sekɛm nidiba, ka Wina'am mɛ na kɛlisi tisi ya.

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka tiis yina la'as taaba ye ba diisi ba na'ab. Ba yɛl Olif tiig ye, ‘Aan ti na'ab!’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Amaa Olif tiig la lɛbis ye, ‘M basim m kpaam maalʋg, dinɛ ka ba mɔri na'asid wina nɛ saalib la, ka kena di tiis na'am?’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Ka ba mɛ yɛl Akekaŋ ye, ‘Kem na aan ti na'ab!’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Amaa Akekaŋ da lɛbis ye, ‘M basim m wala dinɛ an sʋm, ka malis hali la walib, ka di tiis na'am?’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Tiis la yʋ'ʋn da yɛl vain tiig ye, ‘Kem na dii ti na'am!’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Amaa ka vain tiig da lɛbis ye, ‘M basim daam maalʋg, dinɛ kpɛmisid wina nɛ ninsaalib la ka di tiis na'am?’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Li naar wʋsa, tiis la da yɛl Agun'a ye, ‘Kem na aan ti na'ab!’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Ka Agun'a da lɛbisi yɛl tiis la ye, ‘Ya ya'a sid bɔɔd ye ya bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋi m zugin ka diisim na'am ka m aan ya na'ab, yanam kem na su'a man ma'asimin! Amaa ya'a ka' ala, bugum on yi man Agun'a san'an na kanb na'aziinr tiis banɛ bɛ Lebanon kʋkʋna zug la wʋsa.’

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Amaa zina ya duoe zi'e m saam nɛ o yidim yɛla, kʋʋ o biribis pisyɔpɔi tampiing yinne zug, ka zaŋ Abimelek onɛ aan o sankpan'aspu'ak biigi diis o Sekɛm dim na'ab, on aan ya sizua la zug.

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: Ka ya ya'a maalnɛ dinɛ mɔr na'asi nɛ dinɛ dɔl suori tisin Jerubaal nɛ o yidim zina, yanam mɔri sumalisim zaŋi keŋ Abimelek san'an ka on mɛ mɔr sumalisim yanam zug.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Amaa li ya'a ka' alaa, kɛl ka bugum yi Abimelek san'an na di Sekɛm nɛ Bet Milo nidib, ka kɛ ka bugum yi Sekɛm nɛ Bet Milo nidibin na di Abimelek!”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Ka Jotam zɔɔ keŋ Beer n su'a, ka kpɛlim anina bɔzugɔ, o da zɔti Abimelek. Abimelek nɛ Sekɛm dim namisʋg yɛla

english_verse: Abimelech had been a military commander of Israel for three years,
translation_verse: Abimelek n da sʋ'ʋg Israel dim yʋma atan' la nya'aŋ,

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Ban da yi o nya'aŋ la, Sekɛm nidib la da kɛnɛ ka ninsieba su'a kʋkʋna zugʋ faand onɛ wʋsa dɔl zin'ikan la. Ka ba keŋ yɛl Abimelek.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Gaal onɛ an Ebɛd biig la da duoe nɛ o ba'abiisi keŋ Sekɛm, ka teŋ la nidib zaŋi ba ti'iri niŋ o san'an.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ban da yii keŋ pɔɔdinɛ la'as tiwala dinɛ ka ba mɔri nwiakidi maan daam la, ba da maal malʋŋʋ ba Win dɔɔgin la. Ban da bɛɛ ani dit ka nuud la, ba da pɔ nɔɔri tis Abimelek.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Ka Gaal onɛ an Ebɛd biig la yɛl ye, “Abimelek aan anɔ'ɔnɛ, ka Sekɛm mɛ aan anɔ'ɔn ka tinam na siak o nɔɔrɛ? O ka'anɛ Jerubaal biiga, ka ka' Zebul n an o nya'andɔlla? Tʋm tisi Hamor onɛ an Sekɛm saam la nidib. Abimelek lɛɛ aan anɔ'ɔn ka ti na tʋm tis o?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Nimbama ya'a siakin man nɔɔr, man naan yisin o; man naan yɛlin Abimelek ye, ‘Buolimi fʋ zabzabidib la wʋsa ka ba yina!’”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Zebul onɛ an teŋ la gɔmena da wʋm Gaal n yɛl si'em la, o sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ hali.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ yʋ'ʋŋ ya'a sɔb, fʋn nɛ fʋ nidib la yim paalʋ diginɛ guri ba.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Bɛog ya'a ti nie ka winnig dʋt la, dɛŋim duoe tʋ'ʋs tempʋʋgin la. Gaal nɛ o nidib la ya'a yina tʋ'ʋsif, fʋ nu'ugʋ gban'e si'el wʋsa fʋn maalimi ba fʋn bɔɔd si'em.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Ala ka Abimelek nɛ o zabzabidib la wʋsa yi yʋ'ʋŋʋ keŋ zin'ikanɛ kpi'e Sekɛm la pʋdig zin'is anaasi su'a.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Gaal da yina zi'e tempʋʋg la za'anɔɔrin, ka Abimelek nɛ o soogianam la mɛ kpɛn yii ba suak zin'igin la na.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Gaal da nyɛɛ ba ka yɛl Zebul ye, “Gɔsima, nidibi yi zuor la zugʋ sigid na la.” Zebul da lɛbis ye, “Fʋ yidig nɛ nɔk zuor la ma'asim maal nidib.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Amaa Gaal da lɛm pian' ya'as ye, “Gɔsima, nidibi yii kpɛn'ɛd teŋ la teŋsʋk la na, ka sieba naam ba'akɔn tiig la baba kenna la.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Amaa Zebul da yɛl o ye, “Fʋ pian'abɛdʋg la bɛ yaanɛ nannanna, fʋn kanɛ yɛl ye, ‘Abimelek aan anɔ'ɔn ka ti na tʋm tis o la?’ Ka' nimbanɛ ka fʋ la'ad la nwaa? Yim keŋ zab nɛ ba!”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ala ka Gaal gaad Sekɛm nidib la tuon ka ba zab nɛ Abimelek.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Ka Abimelek kad o ka o zɔ, ka sieba zɔ ka o kadi ba ka ba lii pu'alim suorin hali ti paae za'anɔɔr la kpɛn'ɛb zin'ig.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Abimelek da kpɛlim nɛ Aruma, ka Zebul kad Gaal nɛ o ba'abiis la yis Sekɛm.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la, Sekɛm nidib la da yi paalʋ, ka ba keŋ yɛl Abimelek.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Ka o da zaŋ o nidib la yina pʋdigi ba zin'is atan' su'a gur; on ti nyɛ ka nidib la yit tempʋʋgin la na la ka o duoe zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Ka Abimelek nɛ o nimbanɛ pʋdig zin'is atan' la zin'ig yinne zɔɔ keŋ paae teŋ la za'anɔɔrini zi'en anina. Ka zin'is ayi' banɛ kpɛlim la zɔɔ keŋ banɛ bɛ paalʋ la kʋʋ ba.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Daakan la wʋsa, Abimelek da zabnɛ kpɛn' tempʋʋgin hali ti nyaŋi kʋ nidib la wʋsa. Ka san'am tempʋʋg la ka zaŋ yaarim zu'asi li.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Ban da wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la, Sekɛm nimbanɛ bɛ suak zin'ikanɛ wa'am hali ka mɔr paŋ la da duoe keŋ El Berit pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg zin'ikanɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ la ni.

english_verse: but Abimelech found out where they were.
translation_verse: Abimelek n da wʋm ye ba la'asi anina la

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: on nɛ o nidib la wʋsa da duoe dʋ Zalmon zuor la zug. Ka o zaŋ lieŋe nwaae tiis wila buki o biankimpiiung zug ka yɛl banɛ dɔl o la ye, “Tɔ'ɔtɔ, niŋimi wʋʋ yanamɛ nyɛ ka m niŋ si'em la.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Nidib la wʋsa da nwaae tiis wila dɔl Abimelek. Ka ba la'asi ba vi' girimbisa la za'anɔɔrin, n lud nidib la lɛbis pʋʋgin, ka nyu'oe li nɛ bugum. Nidib banɛ da bɛ pʋʋgin la da paae wʋʋ tusir, pu'ab nɛ dap, ka ba wʋsa kpi.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Ka din nya'aŋ ka Abimelek keŋ Tebɛz tempʋʋginɛ gilig zin'ig la nyaŋi ba.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Teŋ la pʋʋgin, girimbisa kanɛ mɔr paŋ hali da bɛɛ ani, ka teŋ la nidib dap nɛ pu'ab wʋsa zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' ani. Ba da yɔ' nɛ ba mɛŋi lɛbis pʋʋgin ka dʋʋ agɔla.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Ka Abimelek keŋ paae fɔɔndi kpɛn'ɛd girimbisa la ni. Amaa on ti paad za'anɔɔrin la ye o nyu'oe li nɛ bugum la,

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: ka pu'a naan saazugʋ zaŋ nɛɛri bas o zugin, nwa'ae o zug la.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ka o buol onɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la tɔ'ɔtɔ ye, “Fuomi fʋ sʋ'ʋg la kʋʋm, ka ba da yɛl ye, ‘Pu'a kʋ o!’” Ka o tʋmtʋm la zaŋ o sʋ'ʋgʋ kʋns o ka o kpi.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Israel dim la nyɛ ka Abimelek kpi la, ba da lɛbi kuli ba yaan.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Li anɛ Wina'am da yɔ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka Abimelek tʋm tis o saam, n kʋ o ba'abiis pisyɔpɔi la.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Wina'am mɛ kɛ ya ka Sekɛm dim yɔɔ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la sam. Jotam onɛ an Jerubaal biig la nɔpɔɔr la da paae ba.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abimelek saŋa la gaad la, Tola onɛ da an Pua biig ka an Dodo yaaŋ la da duoe ye o faaɛn Israel dim. O da yinɛ Isaka tuŋʋn na, ka bɛ Siamir kʋkʋna teŋ linɛ an Efiram la sʋ'ʋlimin.

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Onɛ da dɔl o nya'aŋ da anɛ Jair onɛ yi Gilead sʋ'ʋlimin la na. O da gaad Israel dim tuon yʋma pisi nɛ ayi'.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Jair n da kpi la, ba da mum o nɛ Kamon teŋin. Jefita yɛla

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: o sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ ba. Ka o zaŋi ba niŋ Filistia dim nɛ Ammon dim la nu'usin.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Nidib banɛ bɛ Gilead la tuongatib da yɛl taaba ye, “Onɛ tʋ'ʋs yiiga zab nɛ Ammon dim la na an zugdaani sʋ'oe banɛ bɛ Gilead la wʋsa.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ammon dim la mɛ da lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la ye ba zab nɛ Juda nɛ Benjamin nɛ Efiram dim. Israel da bɛnɛ mugus tita'arin.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim kaasi tis Zugsɔb la ye, “Ti tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔgif, tinamɛ bas fʋn kanɛ aan ti Wina'am, ka dɔl Baal la zug.”

english_verse: The Lord answered: In the past when you came crying to me for help, I rescued you. At one time or another I've rescued you from the Egyptians, the Amorites, the Ammonites, the Philistines, the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites.
translation_verse: nɛ Sidon dim nɛ Amalek dim nɛ Maon dimi da mugusidi ya ka ya kaasi tisim ye m sʋŋi ya la, m da pʋ faaɛn yaa?

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Ya ya'a ti bɛ yɛla pʋʋgin, yanam kem kaasi tis wina banɛ ka ya gaŋ la; kɛlli ka ba faaɛn ya!”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim yɛl Zugsɔb la ye, “Ti sid tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. Maalimi ti dinɛ wʋsa ka fʋ tɛn'ɛs ka li tu'al, amaa faaɛn mɛ ti nannanna.”

english_verse: Then the Israelites got rid of the idols of the foreign gods, and they began worshiping only the Lord. Finally, there came a time when the Lord could no longer stand to see them suffer. The Ammonites Invade Gilead
translation_verse: Ka ba zaŋ win zʋna banɛ bɛɛ ba san'an la bas ka dɔl Zugsɔb la. Ka o pʋ lɛn siak ye Israel dim nyɛ namisʋg la ya'asɛ.

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Ba da buol Ammon dim ye ba yina zab, ka ba la'as Gilead teŋin; ka Israel dim la mɛ la'as taaba Misipa tempʋʋgin.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: yɛl o ye, “Kem na aan ti tuongat, ka ti nyaŋi zab nɛ Ammon dim la.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Jefita da yɛli ba ye, “Ya da pʋ kisigim ka kadimi yisi m ba' yinnee? Bɔ ka yɛl paae ya ka ya lɛn kennɛ m san'an na?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Ka Gilead kpɛɛmnam la yɛl o ye, “La'an nɛ din kʋdim an si'em wʋsa, tinam lɛbidnɛ fʋ san'an nannanna na. Kem na paasi ti ka ti zab nɛ Ammon dim la, ka fʋnɛ yʋ'ʋn na an zugdaani sʋ'oe onɛ wʋsa bɛ Gilead teŋin.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Jefita da lɛbis ye, “Ya'a nwɛnɛ ya dɔllim nɛ lɛb ye ti zab nɛ Ammon dim la ka Zugsɔb la zaŋi ba niŋi m nu'uginɛ, m sid na an ya zugdaana?”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Ka Gilead kpɛɛmnam la lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb la aan ti kasɛt, ti sid na maal fʋn yɛl si'em la.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Ka Jefita yʋ'ʋn dɔl Gilead kpɛɛmnam la ka nidib la da kɛ ka o gaadi ba tuonnɛ sʋ'oe ba zaba yɛla. O da paae Misipa teŋin ka lɛn tiɛn on pian' si'el la, Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Ani ka Jefita tʋm o tʋmtʋmnib Ammon na'ab san'an bu'os o ye, “Bɔɔ bɛ tinam nɛ fʋ sʋʋgin ka fʋ zabid nɛ ti teŋgbauŋɔ?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Ka Ammon dim na'ab la lɛbis labaari tis banɛ ka ba tʋm la ye, “Saŋkan ka Israel dim da yi Egipt teŋin na la, ba da faaɛn man teŋ, lin yi Aanon bɔn'ɔgin keŋ Yabok kɔldaugine mɔri ti paae Joodan kɔldaug. Nannanna lɛbisimi li baanlimm!”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Jefita da lɛn lɛbis labaari tʋm yɛl Ammon dim na'ab la, ye

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: “Man Jefita yɛt si'eli nwa' ye, Israel dim pʋ faaɛn Moab teŋ bɛɛ Ammon dim teŋa.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Amaa ban da yi Egipt teŋin na la, Israel dim da dɔl sian'arinɛ yi Atɛuk Zɛn'ugʋn ti paae Kades.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Ani ka Israel dim tʋm labaari yɛl Edom na'ab ye, ‘Tisimi ti suor ka ti dɔlli fʋ teŋgbauŋ la sʋ'ʋlimin gaad.’ Amaa ka Edom na'ab la pʋ kɛligɛ. Ba da tʋm yɛl Moab dim na'ab, ka o mɛ zan'as. Ani ka Israel kpɛlim Kades teŋin.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Ka ba luaki dɔl sian'arin kaae gilig Edom nɛ Moab tɛɛns la, dɔlli yi Moab teŋ nya'aŋi keŋ la'as taaba Aanon bɔn'ɔg la lɔm. Ba da pʋ kpɛn' Moab teŋinɛ, Aanon bɔn'ɔg la da aan ba titɔndig.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Israel tʋm labaari yɛl Sihon onɛ an Amor dim na'ab, ka sʋ'oe Hesbon teŋ la, ye o kɛl ka ti dɔl o teŋgbauŋʋn la gaadi keŋi ti mɛŋ zin'igin.

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Sihon da pʋ siak ye ba dɔl o sʋ'ʋlimin gaadɛ bɔzugɔ o da pʋ niŋ Israel dim la yadda. O da la'as o zabzabidib Jahaz teŋin zab nɛ Israel dim.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel dim Wina'am la, da zaŋ Sihon nɛ o nidib la wʋsa niŋ Israel dim nu'usin ka ba nyaŋi ba. Israel da faaɛn Amor dim banɛ bɛɛ anina la wʋsa teŋi

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: sʋ'ʋgi li wʋsa din yi Aanon n ti paae Yabok nɛ din yi sian'arin la ti paae Joodan kɔldaug.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Nannanna, Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel dim Wina'am la sadigim kad Amor dimi yis teŋin la ka tis o nidib Israel dim la, suobɔ ka fʋ ye fʋ dɔlis ka lɛn di'e teŋ la?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Fʋ kʋ zaŋ dinɛ ka fʋ win Kemos tisif laa? Dinɛ wʋsa ka ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la tisi ti la, ti na sʋ'ʋgi li.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Fʋ an sʋm gat Balak onɛ da an Zippor biig ka an Moab dim na'ab laa? O nam mi' nwa'as nɛ Israel, bɛɛ o zab nɛ baa?

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Mam pʋ tʋmif bɛ'ɛdɛ, amaa fʋnɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛdi tis man, ka ieed man nɛ zaba. Kɛl ka Zugsɔb, onɛ an sariakat la gban'e linɛ an sida zina nwa', Israel nɛ Ammon dim antu'a la ni.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Amaa Ammon dim na'ab la pʋ kɛlis Jefita tʋm labasi'a tis o laa.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Anina ka Zugsɔb Siig la kɛn Jefita san'an na. Ka o gilig Gilead nɛ Manase ka gaadi paae Misipa dinɛ bɛ Gilead teŋin la, ka yi anina tɔlisi kpa' Ammon dimi la'as zin'isi'a la.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Jefita da zi'el nɔɔri tis Zugsɔb la ye, “Fʋ ya'a zaŋ Ammon dim la niŋi m nu'ugin,

english_verse: and come home safely, I will sacrifice to you whoever comes out to meet me first.”
translation_verse: ka m ti nyaŋ ka lɛb na, bʋnkanɛ wʋsa dɛŋi yii m yir za'anɔɔrin na tʋ'ʋsim la na anɛ Zugsɔb la din, ka m na zaŋi maal maannɛ nyu'oe tis Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Ani ka Jefita duoe keŋ zab nɛ Ammon dim, ka Zugsɔb la zaŋi ba niŋ o nu'usin.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Jefita n da lɛbi kunnɛ o yin Misipa teŋin la, o pu'ayua da kɛ ka ba nwɛ' kɔna ka o wa'a yina tʋ'ʋs o. O da anɛ bipuŋ yimmir. Ya'a ka' on ma'anɛ, o da pʋ lɛm mɔr biribiŋ bɛɛ bipuŋa.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: On da nyɛɛ o la, o da aans o fuud sʋnsa'aŋ zug ka kaas ye, “Oi, m biiga! Fʋ kɛya ka m sʋnf wʋsa san'am ka malisim lɛn kae, bɔzugɔ m yɛl nɔɔri tis Zugsɔb la ka kʋ nyaŋi san'ami lii!”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: O da lɛbis ye, “M saama, fʋ zaŋi fʋ pian'ʋkʋ tis Zugsɔb la. Zugsɔb la sadigim yɔɔ fʋ bi'emnam Ammon dim la samme tisif la maalim man nwɛnɛ fʋn pɔɔ zi'el si'em la.

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Amaa bʋn yinne ka m bɔɔd ye m sɔsif; tisim nwadis ayi' ka man nɛ m zuanam gɔn kʋkʋna ni nɛ kukuma man kʋ kul sid la zug.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: O saam la da lɛbis o ye, “Ka kem!” Ka bas o ka o keŋ nwadis ayi'. On nɛ o bipuŋ taaba da keŋ kʋkʋna la ni gɔɔnd ka kum on kʋ kul sid la yɛla.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Nwadis ayi' la nya'aŋ, o da lɛn lɛb o saam san'an na ka o niŋ o nwɛnɛ on da pɔ nɔɔri zi'el si'em la. Bipuŋ la da nan zi' dau. Nɛ'ɛŋa da lieb Israel dim malʋŋ

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: ye yʋʋm wʋsa Israel pu'asada wʋsa na yi daba anaasi tiɛn Jefita onɛ an Gilead nid la pu'ayua la yɛla.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Efiram dim la da buoli ba zabzabidibi lɔ'ɔŋi keŋ Zafon ka yɛl Jefita ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ keŋ zab nɛ Ammon dim ka pʋ buoli ti ka ti la'am keŋɛ? Ti na nyu'oe fʋn nɛ fʋ yir la wʋsa!”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Jefita da lɛbisi ba ye, “Man nɛ m nidib la wʋsa daa nyɛ zabtita'ar nɛ Ammon dim, la'an nɛ wala man daa buoli ya ka ya pʋ kena faanmi ba nu'usinɛ.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Man daa nyɛ ka ya pʋ bɔɔd ye ya sʋŋim la, m daa kuosi m nyɔɔri lɔ'ɔŋ titɔndig la zab nɛ Ammon dim, ka Zugsɔb la tisim paŋ ka m nyaŋi ba. Nannanna bɔzug ka ya kɛn zina na ye ya zab nɛ ma?”

english_verse: But the men from Ephraim said, “You people of Gilead are nothing more than refugees from Ephraim. You even live on land that belongs to the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh.” So Jephthah called together the army of Gilead, then they attacked and defeated the army from Ephraim.
translation_verse: Alazug ka Jefita buol Gilead sʋ'ʋlim dimi la'asi ba zab nɛ Efiram dɔɔg dim. Gilead dim da nyaŋi ba, bɔzugɔ Efiram dim da yɛl ye, “Yanam Gilead dim anɛ banɛ ka Efiram nɛ Manase dɔɔd dim yisi ya bas.”

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Gilead dim da nyaŋi ba ka gu' ban da lɔ'ɔŋid Joodan kɔldaug la zin'isi'a la paae Efiram, ka Efiram teŋ nid ya'a zɔɔ yi zaba ni m paae na ka yɛli ba ye, “Kɛlli ka m lɔ'ɔŋ kpɛ'!” Gilead dim bu'osid o nɛ ye, “Fʋ anɛ Efiram dɔɔg nidaa?” O ya'a lɛbis ye, “Ayei!”

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: Ba na yɛl o ye, “Tɔ', yɛlim ye ‘shibbolef.’” O ya'a yɛl ye, “sibbolef”, on kʋ nyaŋi buol pian'ʋk la sʋ'ʋŋa la zug, ba na gban'e o kʋ Joodan suoya la ni. Efiram dim tusa pisnaasi nɛ ayi' da kpi saŋkan la. Jefita nɛ Ibizan nɛ Elon nɛ Abidon yɛla

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Jefita da gur Israel teŋ nɛ yʋma ayuobʋ. Jefita onɛ an Gilead teŋ nid la da kpiya ka ba mum o Gilead teŋin.

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ka on nya'aŋ la, Ibizan onɛ yi Betilehem la da an Israel tuongat.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Ibizan n da kpi la, ba da mum o nɛ Betilehem teŋin.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Ka on nya'aŋ ka Elon onɛ an Zebulun dɔɔg nid la da lieb Israel dim tuongat yʋʋm piiga.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Elon n da kpi la, ba da mum o nɛ Aijalon teŋin Zebulun teŋgbauŋʋn.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Israel dim da lɛn tʋm bɛ'ɛd ya'as Zugsɔb la nifin, ka Zugsɔb la zaŋi ba niŋ Filistia dim nu'usin yʋʋma pisnaasi.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Zora dim dau sɔ' da bɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Manoa, o da anɛ Dan dɔɔg nid, o pu'a da anɛ kʋndu'ar ka pʋ mɔr biiga.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: bɔzugɔ fʋ na tʋk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ, ka o zug kʋ pʋn nɛ bariga bɔzugɔ biig la ye o anɛ Naazir ninkanɛ ka Wina'am na gaŋ o, o du'am saŋa, ka o na pin'ili faaɛn Israel dim Filistia dim nu'usin ka tisi ba yɔlisim.”

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la keŋ o sid san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Wina'am nid kɛɛn m san'an na. O nwɛnɛ Wina'am maliak nɛ, ka o gɔsig la mɔr dabiem. Mam pʋ bu'os o on yi si'el naa, ka o mɛ pʋ yɛl man o yʋ'ʋrɛ.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Amaa o yɛl man ye, ‘Fʋ na tʋk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ. Alazugɔ, nannanna, da lɛn nu daam buudi wʋsa ka mɛ da di bʋnkanɛ kisa bɔzugɔ biig la ye o anɛ Naazir nid Wina'am san'an din yii o du'am saŋa ti paae o kum daar.’” Manoa winsɔsʋg yɛla

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Ani Manoa da sɔs Zugsɔb ye, “M Zugsɔba, m bɛlimnɛ, kɛl ka Wina'am dau kanɛ ka fʋ daa tʋm o na la lɛb na ya'asi pa'ali ti tinamɛ na ti mɔr biribiŋ kanɛ ka ti ye ti du'a la si'em.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Wina'am da wʋm tis Manoa, ka Wina'am maliak la lɛn lɛb pu'a la san'an na, saŋkanɛ ka o da yii bɛ pɔɔgin la; amaa o sid Manoa da ka' anina.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Pu'a la da zɔ tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ yɛl o sid ye, “Dau kanɛ daa nie o mɛŋi m san'an daakaŋa la lɛb na.”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Manoa da duoe dɔl o pu'a la keŋ, ka on paae dau la san'an la o yɛl dau la ye, “Fʋnɛ daa pian' tisim pu'a laa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Manɛ la.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Manoa da bu'os o ye, “Fʋ pian'ad la ya'a ti niŋ amɛŋa, biig la bɛllim suor nɛ o tʋʋma na ti an wala?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la da lɛbis ye, “Asɛɛ ka fʋ pu'a la dɔlis man yɛl o si'em la wʋsa.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: O kʋ di daam tiig la wala, bɛɛ o nu daam buudi wʋsa bɛɛ di dikanɛ kisa, asɛɛ o niŋ man yɛl o ye o dɔlis si'el la wʋsa.”

english_verse: “Please,” Manoah said, “stay here with us for just a little while, and we'll fix a young goat for you to eat.”
translation_verse: Manoa da yɛl Zugsɔb maliak la ye, “Ti bɔɔd ye fʋ kpɛlim ka ti kʋ bʋpɔlli maali dʋgi tisif.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la da lɛbis ye, “La'an nɛ yanamɛ giŋim la, m kʋ dii ya diib la baa bi'ela. Amaa maalimi maannɛ nyu'oe tis Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Manoa bu'os Zugsɔb maliak la ye, “Fʋ yʋ'ʋrɛ, ka fʋ pian'ad la ya'a ti lieb amɛŋa ka ti na'asi fɔ?”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bu'osidi m yʋ'ʋrɛ? Li tʋʋgi ya ya'am baŋir bɛn.”

english_verse: So Manoah took a young goat over to a large rock he had chosen for an altar, and he built a fire on the rock. Then he killed the goat, and offered it with some grain as a sacrifice to the Lord. But then an amazing thing happened.
translation_verse: Ani ka Manoa zaŋ bʋpaalig nɛ kii maal maan tampiing zugʋ tis Zugsɔb la. Ka Zugsɔb la tʋm tʋʋmnyalima ka Manoa nɛ o pu'a nyɛ. Saŋkanɛ ka ba da nan zi'e gɔsid,

english_verse: The fire blazed up toward the sky, and the Lord's angel went up toward heaven in the fire. Manoah and his wife bowed down low when they saw what happened.
translation_verse: ka bugum la dit maan la bimbim la zugʋ dʋti agɔla la, Zugsɔb maliak la da dɔl bugum la dʋ. Manoa nɛ o pu'a la da nyɛɛ li la, ba da sʋn'ʋni ba nindaa kpa' teŋin.

english_verse: Although the angel didn't appear to them again, they realized he was one of the Lord's angels.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak la da pʋ lɛn nie o mɛŋ ya'asi tis Manoa nɛ o pu'a la. Manoa yʋ'ʋn da baŋ ye o anɛ Zugsɔb maliak.

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: O da yɛl o pu'a la ye, “Ti na kpi, tinamɛ nyɛ Wina'am la!”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Amaa o pu'a lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb la ya'a gban'an ye o kʋʋ ti, o naan kʋ di'en piinkanɛ ka ti maal maannɛ tis o la, hali ka pa'ali ti nɛ'ɛnam bɛɛ o yɛli ti nɛ'ɛnama.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Pu'a la da du'a biribiŋ ka pʋd o, o yʋ'ʋr ye Samson. Biig la da nɔbig ya, ka Zugsɔb la niŋ o zug albareka.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Siig la da pin'ili mɔr o ken on da bɛ Mahane Dan teŋin, linɛ bɛ Zora nɛ Esitaol teŋsʋk la.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Samson da duoe keŋ Timna teŋin ka nyɛ Filistia dim pu'asadir ani.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: On da lɛbi kul la, o da yɛl o saam nɛ o ma ye, “M nyɛ Filistia dim pu'asadir Timna teŋin; li'aminɛ o tisim ka m dii o.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: O ba' nɛ o ma da lɛbis o ye, “Pu'a kanɛ narif ka' fʋ sizuopin la bɛɛ ti nidibin la wʋsa? Li anɛ tilas ye fʋ keŋ Filistia dim banɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋ la ni di pu'a?” Amaa Samson da lɛbis ye, “Li'aminɛ o tisim! Onɛ an onɛ nar nɛ man.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: O saam nɛ o ma da pʋ baŋ ye nɛ' yinɛ Zugsɔb onɛ bɔɔd ye o maal suori zab nɛ Filistia dim la san'an na; bɔzugɔ saŋkan la banɛ da sʋ'oe Israel dim la. Samson n kʋ gbigim la yɛla

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Samson da keŋ Timna, on nɛ o saam nɛ o ma. Ban da paad Timna teŋ dim tiis pɔɔdin la, gbigimpɔl da duoe anina kaasidi kpa'ad o na.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Siig da sig o san'an na nɛ paŋ ka o tɔɔns gbigim la nɛ o nu'us nwɛnɛ bʋbil ka o gban'e tɔɔnsid nɛ. Amaa o da pʋ yɛl o saam bɛɛ o ma on niŋ si'ela.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Ani ka o keŋ nyɛ pu'a la sɔns nɛ o, ka o ya'am kpɛn' o.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Ka lin nya'aŋ ka o da lɛbid ye o dii o pu'a la, ka bie nyɛ gbigim kpiiluŋ la, ka siins bɛ gbigim kpiiluŋin la ka siind mɛ bɛ.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Ka o tʋm baae siind la ken ka dit. On da lɛb o saam nɛ o ma san'an la, o da tisi ba ka ba mɛ di. Amaa o da pʋ yɛli ba ye o taab siind la nɛ gbigim kpiiluŋʋ nɛ.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: O saam la da keŋ ye o nyɛ pu'a la, ka Samson maal diibi la'as nidib ka ba di, nwɛnɛ ba malʋŋ la zi'el ye pu'a paal sid maal si'em la.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Ban da nyɛɛ o la, ba da zaŋ o taaba pistan' tis o.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: Ya ya'a kʋ nyaŋi yɛli li gbinnɛ, asɛɛ ka ya tis man banaas pistan' nɛ fusieba pistan'.” Ba da yɛl o ye, “Yɛlimi ti fʋ bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la ka ti wʋm!”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbisi ba ye, “Onɛ dit la ni, ka si'el yina ye ba di; onɛ an paŋ sɔb la pʋʋgin ka ba nyɛ bʋmmalisiŋ.” Li da mɔri paae daba atan' ka ba pʋ nyaŋi baŋi li gbinnɛ,

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: daba anaasi daar la, ba da yɛl Samson pu'a ye, “Bɛlisimi fʋ sid la ka o yɛli ti o bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la gbin, ya'a ka' alaa, ti na nyu'oe fʋn nɛ fʋ saam la yir wʋsa ka ya kpi. Ya buoli ti na ye ya faaɛn tii?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Ani ka Samson pu'a bibig o ka kum, ka gɛn'ɛdi yɛt ye, “Fʋ kis mam nɛ! Fʋ pʋ nɔŋi ma. Fʋ zaŋ bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm tisim nidib ka pʋ yɛl man bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la gbinnɛ.” Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Mam pʋ nyaŋi yɛli m saam bɛɛ m ma li gbinnɛ. Bɔzug ka m na pa'ali fʋ li gbinnɛ?”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: O pu'a la da kaas daba ayɔpɔi diib di'ema la saŋa la wʋsa. Alazug daba ayɔpɔi la daar o da gʋ'ʋŋ ka yɛl o, bɔzugɔ o da daam o nɛ galis. Pu'a la mɛ da yɛl o nidib la bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm la gbin.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Winnig da nam pʋ lii ka teŋ la nidib la'as o san'an na yɛl o ye, “Bɔɔ malisi gat siindɛ? Bɔɔ mɔr paŋi gat gbigimɛ?” Samson da yɛli ba ye, “Oi! Ya nɔki m na'asa'a la kuod! Ya ya'a daa pʋ pan'asi nɛ m sabua laa, Ya naan kʋ baŋinɛ li gbinnɛ.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Ba da zaŋ o pu'a la tis onɛ da aan o zua o pu'a diir malʋŋʋn la.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Man mi' sʋ'ʋŋa ye fʋ pʋ bɔɔd o, din ka m zaŋ o tisi fʋ zua. O pitʋ la pʋ vɛnli gat oo? Tiakim nɔk on la.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Samson da yɛli ba ye, “Nannanna m sid mɔr suori na paam Filistia dim la. M sid na maali ba bɛ'ɛd.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: O da zaŋ bugum vian'as mɔɔd la bʋnkɔnbid la zʋya ni, ka kadi ba kpɛn'ɛs Filistia dim ki pɔɔdin. Ka ba kpɛn' nyu'oe pɔɔd la nɛ linɛ ka ba buni digil la la'an nɛ olif tiis nɛ vain tiis pɔɔd la wʋsa.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da bu'os ye, “Anɔ'ɔn tʋm nɛ'?” Ka ba yɛli ba ye, “Li anɛ Samson, onɛ an Timna dim dau la diem, bɔzugɔ ba daa zaŋ o pu'a la tis o zua.” Alazug Filistia dim la da keŋ nyu'oe pu'a la nɛ o saam la wʋsaa kʋ.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Samson da yɛli ba ye, “Yanamɛ sadigim tʋm si'em la, man kʋ basɛ, asɛɛ ka m ti yɔ sam!”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: O da tʋ'ʋsi ba nɛ zaba hali ka dabiem bɛ, n kʋʋ ba bɛdegʋ. O da duoe keŋ Etam kpɛn' tampinyɔkin bɛɛ anina. Samson n kʋ Filistia dim tusir la yɛla

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da keŋ la'as taaba Juda teŋin yadig hali li'el Lehi teŋ la.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Juda nidib da bu'osi ba ye, “Bɔ ka ya kena ye ya zab nɛ ti?” Ba da lɛbis ye, “Ti kena ye ti gban'e Samson n lɔɔ niŋ o wʋʋ on niŋ tinam si'em la.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Ani ka nidib tusa atan' yi Juda keŋ Etam tampinyɔkin la yɛl Samson ye, “Fʋ zi' ye Filistia dim la sʋ'oe tii? Bɔ ka fʋ maali ti wala?” Ka o lɛbisi ba ye, “M maali banɛ ban maalim si'em la lɛbis.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl o ye, “Ti kɛnɛ na ye ti lɔɔ fʋ zaŋi tis Filistia dim la.” Ka Samson da lɛbisi ba ye, “Pɔɔmi ye ya kʋ kʋʋmi ya mɛŋa!”

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: On da li'en Lehi teŋ la, Filistia dim da tansid agɔla gɔla kennɛ o san'an na. Zugsɔb Siig la da kɛɛn o san'an na nɛ paŋ. Nwiis banɛ bɛɛ o nu'usin la da nwɛnɛ li anɛ gum nɛ tɔnsi o nu'usin la li.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Anina ka Samson yɛl ye, “Bʋŋ yier ka m zaŋi kʋʋ ba digil kuda-kuda! Bʋŋ yier ka m nɔki kʋ nidib tusir.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: On pian' naae la o lɔb kɔnbir la bas; ka ba buon zin'ikan la ye Ramaf Lehi.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Ku'onuud yʋ'ʋn da mɔr o nɛ, ka o kaasi buon Zugsɔb la ye, “M Zugsɔba! Fʋnɛ tisim nyaŋ kaŋa, ka li sʋm ye m kpiid ku'onuud ka li banɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋ la nu'usinɛ?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Ani ka Wina'am kɛ ka ku'om tans teŋin la na; ka Samson nu, ka o paŋ lɛb na ka o kpɛ'ɛŋ. Ala ka ba buon ku'om la yit si'el la ye Een-Hakkore. Li nan kpɛm bɛ Lehi teŋin la.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Samson da gur Israel teŋ la nɛ yʋʋm pisi, Filistia dim saŋa la.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl Gaza nidib la ye, “Samson bɛ kpɛla!” Alazug ba da gur o teŋ la za'anɔɔrin. Yʋ'ʋŋ kan wʋsa ba da pʋ vurigɛ ka yɛt ye bɛog ya'a nie ba na kʋ o.

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Lina nya'aŋ, ka o nyɛ pu'a sɔ' ya'as Sorek bɔn'ɔgin la bɔɔd. Pu'a la yʋ'ʋri da buon Delila.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la da kɛɛn o san'an na yɛl o ye, “Fʋ ya'a na nyaŋi bɛlis o ka o pa'ali fʋ o yɛlsu'adir dinɛ aan o paŋ tita'ar la, nɛ tinamɛ na niŋ si'em nyaŋ o ka lɔɔ o. Ti wʋsa yinne-yinne na tisif anzurifa gbila tusir nɛ kɔbig-kɔbig.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Delila da yɛl Samson ye, “Yɛlimi fʋ paŋ tita'ar la yɛlsu'adir la an si'em, nɛ sɔ' na niŋ si'em lɔɔf ka nyaŋif.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samson da lɛbis ye, “Sɔ' ya'a lɔɔm nɛ tiraug nwiis ayɔpɔi banɛ an bʋmma'asa ka nam pʋ kʋdigɛ, m na lieb tadim nwɛnɛ sɔ' wʋsa an si'em la.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Ka dap kena su'a dɔɔgin la, ka pu'a la tansi buol o ye, “Samson, Filistia dim la paae fʋ san'an na!” Amaa ka o kɛns nwiis la nwɛnɛ gum gaarigi na li'el bugum nɛ. Ala ka ba da pʋ baŋ yɛlsu'adir linɛ tisid o paŋ la.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Anina ka Delila yɛl Samson ye, “Fʋ buolim nɛ zɔlʋg ka ma'am! Nannanna kem na yɛlim ban na niŋ si'em lɔɔf.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o ye, “Sɔ' ya'a lɔɔm sʋ'ʋŋa nɛ nwipaala dinɛ ka ba nam pʋ nɔki li lɔɔ si'el si'ela, m na lieb tadim nwɛnɛ sɔ' wʋsa an si'em la.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Alazug Delila da zaŋ nwipaala lɔɔ o, ka dap kena su'a dɔɔgin la, ka o tansi buon o ye, “Samson, Filistia dim la paae fʋ san'an na!” Amaa ka o kɛns nwiis la o nu'usin nwɛnɛ gum gaarig nɛ.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Delila da lɛn yɛl Samson ye, “Hali nɛ nwa', fʋ nan kpɛm buonim nɛ zɔlʋg ka ma'adim. Yɛlim ban na niŋ si'em ka lɔɔf!” Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Fʋ ya'a pan'ami m zuobid la ayɔpɔi kpɛn'ɛs sʋlʋgini ʋg nɛ pien la naae ka kpa' li nɛ kpada, m na lieb tadim nwɛnɛ sɔ' wʋsa an si'em la.” Alazug o da bɛ gbɛɛmin ka Delila gban'e o zuobid la pan'ami li ayɔpɔi nɔki naal gumme ʋg nɛ pien,

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: ka kpa' nɛ kpada. Ka lɛn tansi buol o ya'as ye, “Samson, Filistia dim la paae fʋ san'an na!” Ka o nie gbɛɛmin ka tɛɛg kpada la vuoɛn nɛ gum la nɛ sʋlʋg dinɛ ka ba nɔki ʋg piena la wʋsa. Delila n namis Samson la yɛla

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Delila yɛl o ye, “Fʋ na niŋ wala yɛl ye fʋ nɔŋim, ka kʋ pie fʋ pʋʋgʋ tisi ma? Nɛ'ɛŋa paas nɔɔr atan' ka fʋ pan'asim ka pʋ yɛlimi fʋ paŋ tita'ar la yɛlsu'adir la gbinnɛ.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Muguskaŋa ka o da zi'e o zugin daar wʋsa ka o yaama ti yi.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ani ka o yɛl o si'el wʋsa, ye, “Barig nan zi' kpɛn' man zugʋ nɛ, bɔzugɔ m anɛ Naazir nid onɛ ka Wina'am gaŋ hali m du'am saŋa sa. M zug la ya'a pʋn, m paŋ la na yii m san'an ka m lieb tadim nwɛnɛ sɔ' wʋsa an si'em la.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Delila yʋ'ʋn da baŋ ye o yɛl o si'el wʋsa la, o da tʋm yɛl Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la ye, “Lɛmmi na ya'as, ka o yɛlim si'el wʋsa.” Ani ka Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la lɛb na ka zanl anzurifa ligidi la ba nu'usin.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Ka o kɛ ka o gbis o nɔba zug ka o buol dau ka o kena pʋni o zuobid ayɔpɔi dinɛ pan'am la. Delila yʋ'ʋn da nyaŋ o ka o paŋ la zɔ ka kɛɛ o.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Ani ka Filistia dim la nyaŋ o ka kpig o nini la wʋsa, ka mɔr o keŋ Gaza teŋin. Ka ba lɔɔ o nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug baans, ka kɛ ka o bɛ sanrega dɔɔgin la nɛ'ɛm ki tisidi ba.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Amaa ban da pʋn o la nya'aŋ, o zuobid la da lɛm pin'ili busid. Samson n yɔ sam O kumin si'em

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Filistia dim teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la da la'as ye ba maal maantita'ari tis Dagon onɛ aan ba win la, ka maal di'ema yɛt ye, “Ti win la zaŋ Samson onɛ aan ti bi'em la niŋi ti nu'usin!”

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Ba sʋnya da ma'ae hali galis la, ba da tansid ye, “Mɔri Samson n yina ka o di'em tisi ti!” Ka ba buol Samson ka o yi sanrega dɔɔgin la na di'em tisi ba. Ba da kɛ ka o zi'e zan'antɔlis ayi' la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Samson da yɛl biig onɛ mɔr o nu'ug la ye, “Kɛl ka m zi'en zin'ikanɛ ka m na nyaŋi babil zan'antɔlbanɛ ti'e pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la, ka zaŋi m mɛŋi dɛllim.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Anina ka Samson sɔs Zugsɔb la ye, “Zugsɔb onɛ gaad si'el wʋsa, tɛnri m yɛl. Wina'am, m sɔsidif nɛ kpɛmisimim yimmʋ ya'as, ka kɛ ka m nwɛ' yimmʋ ma'aa yɔ Filistia dim sam m nini ayi' nwa' yɛla.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Samson da paae gban'e zan'antɔlis ayi' banɛ bɛ sʋʋgin ka ti'e pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la mɔr la ka zaŋ o mɛŋi dɛlli ba, ka zaŋ o datiuŋ nu'ugʋ gban'e yinne ka o dagɔbʋg nu'ug mɛ gban'e yinne.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Ka Samson yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka m la'am kpi nɛ Filistia dim la!” Ka tɛbig nɛ o paŋ wʋsa ka pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg la li teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa zug. O da kʋ nidib bɛdegʋ o kum saŋa la, ka li gaad on da nan vʋe ka kʋ si'em la.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ani ka o bieya nɛ o pitib, o saamnam nɛ o yidim wʋsa keŋ yis o. Ba da mɔr o lɛb na mum o Zora nɛ Esitaol tɛɛnsin la teŋsʋk, o saam Manoa yaʋgʋn. O da an Israel tuongat nɛ yʋma pisi.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: La'an nɛ lin wʋsa, o da lɛbis anzurifa la tis o ma, ka o yis anzurifa ligidi la kɔbisyi' tis banɛ tʋm anzurifa tʋʋma la ka ba maal bada la, ka nɔki zi'el Maika yin.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Ka dau kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Maika la da mɔr teŋgbana zin'ig ka maal wina niŋ ani, ka sɛn dansik ka gaŋ o biig yinne ka o an maanmaan.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Israel da pʋ mɔr na'aba, sɔ' wʋsa da tʋm nɛ dinɛ malis o.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: O da bas teŋ kan la ka duoe ieed zin'ig ye o zin'in, ka keŋ paae Maika yin dinɛ bɛ Efiram kʋkʋna teŋin la.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Maika da bu'os o ye, “Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “M anɛ Levi dɔɔg nidi yi Betilehem Juda teŋin na, ka ieed zin'ig ye m zin'in.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Ani ka Maika yɛl o ye, “Bɛi nɛ man ka liebi m saam nɛ m maanmaan, ka m na tisif anzurifa ligidi piiga yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin, la'an nɛ fʋ fuud nɛ diib wʋsa.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Maika da zin'il Levi dɔɔg nid la ani, ka o lieb o maanmaan ka bɛɛ o yin la.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ka Maika yɛl ye, “Nannanna m mi' ye Zugsɔb la na sʋŋim, Levi nid nwa' sadigim liebi m maanmaan la.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Israel da pʋ mɔr na'aba, ka Dan dɔɔg dim la mɛ bɔɔd paalʋ dinɛ ka ba na zin'in ka li aan ba mɛŋ din, bɔzugɔ ba da nam pʋ la'as nɛ Israel dim buudi la ka na di faarɛ.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Alazug Dan dim la da tʋm zabzabidib anu ka ba yi Zora nɛ Esitaol keŋ ye ba labisi gɔs zin'ig la. Nimbama da zi'enɛ ba dɔɔd la wʋsa nɔba zug. Ba da yɛli ba ye, “Kem giligi teŋgbauŋ la gɔs.” Dap la da kpɛn' Efiram sʋ'ʋlim linɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la ti paae Maika yin na. Anina ka ba da gbɛn.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Ban da li'el Maika yin la ba da baŋ Levi nid la, ka kpɛn' anina bu'os o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ mɔrif kpɛla na? Ka fʋ tʋm bɔ kpɛla? Bɔ ka fʋ bɛ kpɛla?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: O da yɛli ba Maika maal si'em tis o, ka ye, “O nɔkim nɛ ye m aan o maanmaan.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl o ye, “Asɛɛ ka fʋ bu'os Wina'am gɔs ye ti ken la suor na an sʋ'ʋŋa tisi tii?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Ka Maanmaan la lɛbisi ba ye, “Kemi nɛ sumalisim. Zugsɔb la yɔ'ɔg suori tisi ya.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Alazug nidiba anu la da gaadi keŋ paae Lais teŋin na. Zin'ikan la ka ba da nyɛ nidib la bɛllim ka si'el pʋ daamidi baa, nwɛnɛ Sidon dim nɛ ka pʋ tɛn'ɛsid si'ela, ka mɔr sumalisim. Si'el-si'el da pʋ pansigi ba teŋin la, ba da mɔr kpan'am ya'as. Ba da bɛnɛ lalli nɛ Sidon dim la ka pʋ mɔr nɔnaar nɛ sɔ'ɔsɔ'ɔɔ.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Ban da lɛb Zora nɛ Esitaol tɛɛnsin la, ba ba'abiis la da bu'osi ba ye, “Ya keŋi gɔsi nyɛ ka li an wala?”
