english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Ya ya'a paae anina, ya na nyɛ nimbanɛ ka ba ba'a kae nɛ si'ela, nɛ teŋ kanɛ yalim ka Wina'am zaŋi niŋi ya nu'usin, teŋ kanɛ ka si'el-si'el pʋ pansigi ba.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Ani ka dap kɔbisyuobʋ banɛ an Dan dɔɔg nidib la bɔb nɛ zaba la'ad, ba da yinɛ Zora nɛ Esitaol tɛɛnsini keŋ.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Ban da yi suorin la ba da la'asi zi'en zin'ikanɛ kpi'e Kiriaf Jiarim teŋin linɛ bɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlimin la. Linɛ kɛ ka ba da buon zin'ikanɛ bɛ Kiriaf Jiarim teŋ ya-tuona la ye, Mahane Dan n ti paae zina la.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Ban yii anina la ba keŋ nɛ Efiram dinɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la keŋ paae Maika yin na. Bada nɛ maanmaan la yɛla

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Ani ka dap anu banɛ da keŋ kaae Lais teŋ la yɛli ba taaba la ye, “Ya mi' ye ya' bama nwa' ni yir yinne bɛɛ anina mɔr teŋgban nɛ winsieba banɛ bɛ yir wʋsa ni, nɛ ba'ar kanɛ ka ba kpi'a nɛ onɛ ka ba ya'abɛɛ? Nannanna ya mi' yanamɛ na niŋ si'em.”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis o ye, “An baanlimm! Da yɛl si'ela. Kem na dɔlli ti ka aan ti saam nɛ ti maanmaan. Li ka' sʋm nɛ fʋn na tʋm tis dɔɔg nɛ tuŋ yinne Israel teŋin gaad fʋn an dau yinne nɛ o yidim maanmaan naa?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Ani ka maanmaan la sʋnf ma'ae. Ka o zaŋ teŋgban la nɛ yin wina la wʋsa nɛ ba'ar kanɛ ka ba kpi'a la dɔl nidib la keŋ.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Ba da zaŋi ba bibibis la, nɛ ba bʋnkɔnbid nɛ ban sʋ'oe si'el wʋsa niŋi ba tuon, ka fɛndigi gaad.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Ban da yi Maika yinne lalig bi'ela la, nimbanɛ kpi'e Maika yin la da la'as taaba zɔɔ geŋ Dan dɔɔg nidib la sa'an.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Ban da tansi buoli ba la, Dan nidib la da fɛndigi yɛl Maika ye, “Fʋ labaar an bɔ ka fʋ buoli fʋ nidib ye fʋ zabɛ?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: O da lɛbisi ba ye, “Ya zaŋ wina banɛ ka m maal la, nɛ m maanmaanni mɔri keŋ. Bɔ ka m lɛm mɔr ya'asɛ? Bɔ ka ya bu'osidim ye m labaar an bɔ?”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Dan dɔɔg nidib la da lɛbis ye, “Da nwa'asid nɛ tii, ya'a ka' alaa, banɛ sʋnya dɛŋi pɛlig la na zab nɛ ya, ka fʋn nɛ fʋ yidim wʋsa na kɔ'ɔŋi ya nyɔvʋr.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Alazug Dan dɔɔg nidib la daa gaad; Maika n da nyɛ ka ba paŋ gat o la, ka o fɛndigi lɛbi kul. Dan dɔɔg dimi zab nɛ Lais teŋ dim banɛ zi' zaba ti'ir la yɛla

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Ba da zaŋi ba yaab Dan yʋ'ʋri pʋd teŋ la ye Dan Teŋ. Dan onɛ da an Jakob biig la, la'an nɛ ban da dɛŋi buon teŋ la yʋ'ʋr ye Lais la.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ ka Israel dim da nam pʋ mɔr na'aba la. Ka Levi dim nid onɛ bɛ teŋkpɛŋ lallisa Efiram kʋkʋna teŋin la da di pu'abil Betilehem teŋin linɛ bɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Amaa pu'a la da ka' sida sɔba. O da ginnɛ yuod, ka bas o sid la ka lɛb o saam yin Betilehem Juda sʋ'ʋlimin. Ka on da bɛɛ anina la nwadis anaasi la,

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: o sid da keŋ o san'an ye o bɛlis o ka o lɛb o san'an na. O da mɔr o tʋmtʋm nɛ bʋmis ayi' keŋ. Pu'a la da mɔr o keŋ o saam yin, ka o saam la nyɛɛ o la, ka di'e o nɛ sumalisim.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: O diem dau onɛ an o pu'a saam la da bɛllim o ye o kpɛlimmi ba san'an, ka o sid kpɛlim o san'an daba atan', dit ka nuud ka gbɛɛnd anina.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Daba anaasi daar la ba da dɛŋi duoe bɛogʋn ka o ti'eb ye o gaad, amaa o pu'a la saam la da yɛl o diem la ye ba kɛl ka nyɛ si'eli sʋʋgi ba nɔɔr, ka nyaan kul.

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Babayi' la da la'as taaba zin'in nɛ di ka nu. Din nya'aŋ la pu'a la saam la da yɛl ye, “M bɛlimnɛ, kʋdim siakim lɛm gbɛn yʋ'ʋŋa ka maal sumalisim!”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Dau la da duoe ye o kul la, o diem dau la da bɛllim o ka o gbɛn anina yʋ'ʋŋ kan la.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Daba anu daar la bɛkɛung ka o duoe ye o kul. Ka pu'a la saam la da yɛl ye, “Dimi diib ka gu'usi paae nintaŋ!” Ala ka babayi' la da la'asi di hali ti paae zaam.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Ani ka dau la nɛ o pu'abil nɛ o tʋmtʋm la duoe ye ba kul. Ka o diem dau la da yɛl ye, “M biiga, gɔsima, zaam kʋdim ma'ae nɛ la. Gbɛɛm kpɛla ka winnig bɔɔdi liigi la. Gbɛɛm ka maal sumalisim. Bɛog bɛkɛung fʋ tun'e gban'e fʋ suori kul.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Amaa, on pʋ bɔɔd ye o lɛm gbɛn yʋ'ʋŋ yinne paas la, dau la da bas ani ka kpa'ad Jebus teŋin , on nɛ o bʋmis ayi' banɛ ka o li'a ba la, nɛ o pu'abil la.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Ban da li'el Jebus ka yʋ'ʋŋ bɔɔd sɔb la, tʋmtʋm la da yɛl o zugdaan la ye, “Kɛl ka ti gbɛn Jebus dim tempʋʋgin kpɛla.”

english_verse: “No,” the Levite answered. “They aren't Israelites, and I refuse to spend the night there. We'll stop for the night at Gibeah,
translation_verse: O zugdaan la da lɛbis ye, “Ayei, ti kʋ keŋ teŋ zʋŋ banɛ nidibi ka' Israel dim la tempʋʋginɛ.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Ala ka ba da kpɛn ken, ka winnig ti kpɛn'ɛd, ban da li'en Gibea dinɛ bɛ Benjamin dɔɔg sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: Anina ka ba da zi'en ye ba gbɛn. Ba da keŋ zin'in tempʋʋgin la, amaa sɔ' da pʋ nɔki ba kpɛn'ɛs o yinne.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Zakan la bʋnkʋdʋg sɔ' da yi pɔɔginɛ kun na. O da anɛ Efiram linɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la nid, ka bɛ Gibea teŋin .

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: O da gɔsi nyɛ suoken la tempʋʋgin ka bu'os o ye, “Fʋ wa'ae yaanɛ? Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ti yinɛ suor zug Betilehem dinɛ bɛ Juda la, wa'ae teŋkpɛŋ kanɛ bɛ Efiram kʋkʋna teŋin la, anina ka m bɛ. M ɛɛnti bɛnɛ Betilehem teŋin Juda sʋ'ʋlimin la ka nannanna m kunnɛ yin. Sɔ' pʋ nɔkimi kpɛn' o yinne.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ti mɔr bʋmis la diib nɛ dinɛ ka ti na tɛ'ɛg ka ba digin, ka mɔri ti mɛŋ diib nɛ daam. Man nɛ m pu'a nɛ dasaŋ la pʋ bɔɔd si'el si'ela.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Bʋnkʋdʋg la da lɛbis ye, “Suor bɛ ka ya na kɛɛn m yin na. Kɛl ka m tisi ya dinɛ wʋsa ka ya bɔɔd. Amaa da digini suorin laa.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ala ka o dɔlli ba kuli o yin ka diis bʋmis la. Ban da pie ba nɔba naae la, ba da paam si'eli di ka nu.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Ban da nam maan sumalisim la, tempʋʋgin la nimbɛ'ɛd sieba da kena gilig yir la nwɛ'ɛd za'anɔɔr la, ka tansid bʋnkʋdʋg kanɛ an yidaan la ye, “Mɔr dau kanɛ kɛɛn fʋ yin la na ka ti digin nɛ o!”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Yisɔb la da yina yɛli ba ye, “Ayei, m zuanama, da tʋmmi dinɛ an zuziiga. Dau kaŋa sadigim an man saan la, da tʋmmi nyan tʋʋm kaŋa!

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Gɔsima, man pu'ayua onɛ nan zi' dau nwana, nɛ dau la pu'abil la, m na mɔri ba yi nannanna na tisi ya. Ya na tun'e digin nɛ ba ka maali ba yanamɛ bɔɔd si'el. Amaa ya'a kpɛlim dau kaŋa nwa', da tʋm o nyan tʋʋm kaŋa.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Amaa ba da pʋ kɛlis on yɛti ba si'el la, ka dau la gʋ'ʋŋi nɔk o pu'abil la tisi ba, ka ba bibig o san'am o yʋ'ʋŋ la wʋsa, ka bɛogʋ ti nied la ka ba nyaan bas o.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ nie naae la ka pu'a la lɛb yikanɛ ka o sid la bɛ la za'anɔɔrini digi teŋin hali ka winnig ti tans na.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: O sid la da duoe bɛogʋn yɔ'ɔg yir la za'anɔɔr ka yina ye o tɔlis tuon la, ka o pu'abil la lii digi yir la za'anɔɔrin ka o nu'us bɛ za'anɔɔrin la.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: O da yɛl o ye, “Duom ka ti keŋ!” Amaa o da pʋ ya'ae nɔɔrɛ. Ani ka dau la zaŋ o pa'al o bʋŋ zugʋ mɔri kul. Levi dau pu'abil ka ba kʋ ka o buudi sʋʋnr duoe

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: On paae yin la, o zaŋ nɛ sʋ'ʋgʋ nwaa o pu'a la zin'is pii nɛ ayi' ka nɔki tʋm tis Israel dɔɔd pii nɛ ayi' la bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋsa nyɛɛ li la yɛl ye, “Tʋʋm kaŋa nan zi' maal bɛɛ ti nyɛɛ li, din yi Israel dimi da yi Egipt teŋin na la. Tɛn'ɛsimini li! Gɔsimini li! Yɛlimi ti tinamɛ na niŋ si'em.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Ala ka Levi dɔɔg nid la, pu'a kanɛ ka ba kʋ la sid la, yɛl ye, “Man nɛ m pu'abili daa ken Gibea teŋin, Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin, ye ti gbɛn.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: M daa nwaansi m pu'abil la pʋdigi tis zin'ikanɛ wʋsa ka Israel dim bɛ ka li aan ba ba' sʋ'ʋlim la, bɔzugɔ nidib nwa' tʋm nɛ yɛlbɛ'ɛd nɛ dinɛ an nyan itʋŋ Israel teŋin.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Tɔ', yanam Israel dima, pian'am gban'e yanamɛ na kʋʋ li si'em.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Nidib la daa duoe vuguri yɛl ye, “Ti wʋsa kʋ kulɛ. Ayei, ti nid baa yinne kʋ kulɛ!

english_verse: Everyone agreed that Gibeah had to be punished.
translation_verse: Alazug Israel nidib la da duoe la'as taaba maal nɔɔr yinne zab nɛ teŋ la.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Israel dɔɔd la wʋsa da tʋm nidib Benjamin sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛnsin la wʋsa yɛt ye, “Yɛlpakir kanɛ maali ya sʋʋgin la gbin an bɔ?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: La'asim tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim banɛ bɛ Gibea nwa' la ka ti kʋʋ ba ka yis bɛ'ɛd Israel dim sʋʋgin!” Amaa Benjamin dim la da pʋ kɛlisi ba taaba banɛ an Israel dim la,

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: ka yii ba tempʋʋdin la la'as taaba Gibea teŋin ye ba zab nɛ Israel dim.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la ka Israel dim la'as taaba zin'ikanɛ pʋ lal nɛ Gibea la.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim yina ye ba zab nɛ Benjamin nidib la ka zi'enɛ ba zaba zi'esa ni Gibea teŋin ye ba zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Benjamin dim la da yi Gibea na zabi kʋ Israel dim tusa pisi nɛ ayi' dabiskan la.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: ka Finehas onɛ an Eleazar biig ka an Aaron yaaŋ la bɛɛ ani ka gɔsidi li tʋʋma). Israel dim da bu'os Zugsɔb la ye, “Ti lɛn lɛbi zab nɛ Benjamin nimbanɛ aan ti ba'abiis la, bɛɛ ti kɛla?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Kemi, bɛogɔ m na zaŋi ba niŋi ya nu'usin.”

english_verse: The Israelites surrounded Gibeah, but stayed where they could not be seen.
translation_verse: Ani ka Israel dim zaŋ zabzabidibi niŋi ba su'asa ni gilig Gibea.

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Alazug ba da naam Israel dim la tuonnɛ zɔti kpa'ad pipirigin, amaa ba da pʋ nyaŋi zɔɔ pɔnsɛ. Ka Israel dim la yi tempʋʋdin la na kʋʋ ba anina.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Ba da giligi ba ka kadi ba zɔɔ nyaŋi ba Gibea teŋ nɔɔrin dinɛ bɛ teŋ la nya'aŋ la.

english_verse: Twenty-five thousand soldiers of Benjamin died that day, all of them experienced warriors.
translation_verse: Dabiskan la Benjamin nidib la zabzabidib tusa pisi nɛ anu da kpi, ba wʋsa da anɛ banɛ mi' zaba sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da lɛb Benjamin teŋin kʋ nimbanɛ bɛ tempʋʋdin la wʋsa, la'an nɛ bʋnkɔnbid nɛ dinɛ wʋsa ka ba nif nyɛ. Ban da dɔlli yi teŋ sieba la wʋsa ba da nyu'oe ba nɛ bugum.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Israel dim da pʋn zi'el nɔɔr Misipa teŋin ye ba sɔ'ɔsɔ kʋ zaŋ o pu'ayua tis Benjamin dim dau sɔ' ka o dii.

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Nidib la da keŋ Betel teŋin zin' Wina'am tuonnɛ kaasid agɔla hali ti paae zaam yɛt ye,

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: “Zugsɔba, Israel dim Wina'am! Bɔɔ kɛ ka yɛl kaŋa tʋm Israel teŋinɛ? Bɔ ka zina nwa' ka Israel dɔɔg yinne bɔdigɛ?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ nie la ka nidib la isigi mɛ' bimbimi maal nyu'or maana nɛ taaba la'asʋg maana.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Israel dim la bu'os ye, “Israel buudi la wʋsa sʋʋgin, teŋ kanɛ nidibi pʋ la'as Zugsɔb la tuon na?” Ba da dɛŋi zi'el nɔɔr ye onɛ wʋsa pʋ la'as Zugsɔb la tuon Misipa teŋinɛ, ba na kʋʋ o.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim sʋnf da san'amnɛ ba ba'abiis banɛ an Benjamin dim la yɛla ka ba ye, “Zina Israel dɔɔg yinne yii ti kallin.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Ti na niŋ wala nyɛ pu'abi tis banɛ kpɛlim la; tinamɛ zi'el nɔɔr nɛ Zugsɔb la ye ti kʋ tisi ba ti pu'ayuos ka ba kuli ba la?”

english_verse: Again the Israelites asked, “Did any of the tribes stay away from the meeting at Mizpah?” After asking around, they discovered that no one had come from Jabesh in Gilead.
translation_verse: Li anɛ ban da kaal nidib la ka baŋ ye Jabis nimbanɛ yii Gilead la sɔ'ɔsɔ ka' anina.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Ani ka nidib la wʋsa da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ Benjamin dim la san'an, zin'ikanɛ an Rimmon tampiingin la, ye ba mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm nɛ ba.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Ala ka Benjamin nidib la da lɛb na, ka ba nɔk pu'asada banɛ ka ba da pʋ kʋ Jabis Gilead la na tisi ba ka ba di. Amaa ba da pʋ paae dap la wʋsaa.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Nidib la sʋnf da san'amnɛ Benjamin dim la, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la kɛ ka tɔ'ɔŋir kae Israel buudi la ni.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Ka la'asʋg la kpɛɛmnam la yɛl ye, “Benjamin dim pu'abi lɛn kae la, ti na niŋ wala paam pu'abi tis dap banɛ kpɛlim la?

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Benjamin nimbanɛ kpɛlim la sʋm ka ba mɔr banɛ na dii ba faar, ala ka Israel dɔsi'a kʋ bɔdig nyainnɛ.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Ti kʋ nyaŋi tisi ba ti pu'ayuos ye ba aan ba pu'aba, tinam Israel dimi sadigim digil nɔɔr la, nɔpɔɔr bɛ onɛ wʋsa tis Benjamin nid pu'a zug.

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Amaa gɔsima, li kʋ yuugɛ ka Zugsɔb la malʋŋ dinɛ an yʋʋm-yʋʋm la na maal Siilo teŋin. Li bɛnɛ Betel teŋ la datiuŋ baba suokanɛ yi Betel n ken Sekɛm la nya'aŋ, ka bɛ Lebona dagɔbʋg baba la.”

english_verse: The leaders told the men of Benjamin who still did not have wives: Go to Shiloh and hide in the vineyards near the festival.
translation_verse: Ala ka ba yɛl Benjamin nidib la ye, “Kem su'ae tiwanna pɔɔdin la,

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: ka Siilo pu'asada la ya'a ti yina ye ba la'asi wa'a, yanam zɔm yi pɔɔdin la na gban'e ba maali ya pu'abi mɔri ba kul Benjamin teŋin.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Ba saamnam bɛɛ ba tanp ya'a ti nyɔn nɛ ti, ti na yɛli ba ye, ‘Maalimi ti sʋm ka sʋŋi ba, bɔzugɔ zaba la saŋa la ti da pʋ nyɛ pu'abi tisi baa, ka yanam mɛ zi' li ti'irɛ, yanamɛ sadigim pʋ zaŋi ya pu'ayuosi tisi ba ye ba di la nɔpɔɔr la kʋ bɛɛ ya zugɔ.’”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Alazug Benjamin nidib la da niŋ ala, ka pu'asada la ya'a ɛɛnti wa'ad, dau woo gban'adnɛ pu'a mɔri kun. Ala ka ba da lɛbi ba mɛŋ sʋ'ʋlimin, ka lɛbisi mɛɛ ba tempʋʋd la bɛɛ ani.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Israel dim da bas zin'ikan la ka kul banɛ aan ba dɔɔg dimin, sɔ' wʋsa da keŋ o mɛŋ teŋin.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Israel dim da pʋ mɔr na'aba. Dinzug, sɔ' mɛkama da kʋdim tʋmnɛ o ya'am bɔɔdim.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Dau la yʋ'ʋri da aan Elimalek, ka o pu'a an Naomi. Ka o biribis la yʋda an Mahlon nɛ Kilion. Ba da anɛ Efirata dim, dinɛ pa'al ye ba anɛ Betilehem dinɛ bɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlim la teŋ nidib. Ba da keŋ Moab ye ba zin'in saŋa bi'ela.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Elimalek da kpiya ka kɛ Naomi pʋkɔɔnr nɛ o biribis ayi' la ma'aa.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Ka o biribis la da di Moab teŋin pu'asada. Yinne yʋ'ʋri da buon Orpa ka yinne la yʋ'ʋr mɛ buon Ruf. Ba da zin'in ani nwɛnɛ yʋʋm piiga,

english_verse: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Now Naomi had no husband or sons.
translation_verse: ka Mahlon nɛ Kilion wʋsa mɛ kpi, ka Naomi kpɛlim pʋkɔɔnr ka pʋ mɔr biiga.

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: ka Naomi yɛl o bipu'ab la ye, “Lɛm kulini ya du'adibin. Zugsɔb na kɛ ka o albareka la dɔlli ya nwɛnɛ yanamɛ maal mam nɛ banɛ kpi la sʋm si'em la.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na kɛ ka ya yinne-yinne paam sidibi kuli kpɛn' yir ka vʋ'ʋs.” Ka o kuaki ba ka kɛɛsi ba. Amaa o bipu'ab la pin'ili kum bɛdegʋ

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: ka ye, “Ayei, tinam pʋ bɔɔd ye ti basi fɔ, ti na dɔlli fʋ keŋi fʋ nidibin.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Ka Naomi lɛbis ye, “M biisɛ, li an sʋ'ʋŋa ye ya lɛb. Bɔ ka ya bɔɔd ye ya dɔlli ma? Ya tɛn'ɛs ye mam na lɛn nyaŋi du'a biribis ka ya kuli baa?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Lɛmmi kuli, bɔzugɔ m kʋdigi galis nɛ mam na nyaŋi kul sid ya'as. Baa m ya'a nyɛ sidi kul yʋ'ʋŋa du'a biribis,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: ya kʋ nyaŋi zin'in hali ka ba ti nɔbigɛ. Ya kʋ nyaŋi guri ba nɛ ban na ti siak pu'adiirɛ. Ayei, m biisɛ, ya mi' ye mam sʋnsa'aŋ gati ya sʋnsa'aŋi an si'em. Bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la kɛ ka yɛl kaŋa paae mam ka m sʋnf san'am hali.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛn kum bɛdegʋ. Ka Orpa kuak o sid ma la ka kɛɛs o ka lɛbi kul, amaa ka Ruf on zan'as ka tabin o nɛ nɔŋilim.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi yɛl o ye, “Ruf, fʋ sid kpɛɛm pu'a la lɛb o nidibin nɛ o wina banɛ ka o pʋ'ʋsid la ni. Fʋn mɛ lɛm dɔl o kul.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Ruf lɛbis ye, “Da yɛt mam ye m basimi fɔ. Kɛl ka m dɔllif. Fʋn wa'ae zin'isi'a la m na keŋ ani; zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ na bɛ la, m na bɛɛ ani. Fʋ nidib na an mam nidib, ka fʋ Wina'am aan m Wina'am.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ na kpi la, m mɛ na kpii ani ka ba na mumim ani. Zugsɔb kɛl ka sʋnsa'aŋ paae mam, m ya'a kɛ ka si'el wɛlig man nɛ fʋ ka ya'a ka' kum.”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Ka Naomi nyɛ ka Ruf bɔɔd ye o dɔl o nɛ o sʋnf wʋsa la, o da pʋ lɛm pian' si'ela.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Ka ba dɔl taaba paae Betilehem. Ka ban paae teŋin la, li da lidig teŋ la nidib wʋsa nɛ; ka pu'ab la yɛt ye, “Naomi nwa' bɛɛ?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛli ba ye, “Da lɛm buolinim ye Naomi, amaa buoliminim ye Mara, bɔzugɔ, Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la kɛ ka m bɛllim lieb tɔɔgʋ tisim.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: M da yi kpɛ' nɛ mɔrim bɛdegʋ, amaa Zugsɔb la kɛ ka m lɛb na nɛ nu'uzaalis. Bɔ ka ya buon man ye Naomi? Zugsɔb la tisim yɛlpakir. Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la kɛ ka zutɔɔg paam.”

english_verse: The barley harvest was just beginning when Naomi and Ruth, her Moabite daughter-in-law, arrived in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Li da niŋnɛ anwa ka Naomi nɛ o bipu'a yi Moab teŋin lɛbi kul na. Ba da paae Betilehem ka mui bunib nan pin'innɛ.

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Ban da nan tʋm saŋa bi'ela la ka Boaz yi Betilehem paae na, ka pʋ'ʋs banɛ bʋn ki la ye, “Zugsɔb na niŋi ya zug bareka!” Ka ba mɛ lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb na niŋi fʋ zug bareka.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Ka Boaz bu'os onɛ an bunib kpɛɛm la ye, “Pu'a kaŋa yi yaanɛ na?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛm la lɛbis ye, “Moab pu'a kanɛ dɔl Naomi lɛb na la, la.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: O yɛlim ye, ‘Fʋ na siak ka m wi'isi dɔl banɛ bʋn la nya'aŋa?’ O tʋmnɛ bɛogʋn sa ka keŋ ma'asim vʋ'ʋs bi'ela nwa'.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Ka Boaz yɛl Ruf ye, “M pu'ayua kɛlisim! Bɛ kpɛla wi'isim ka da lɛn keŋ zin'isi'a ya'asɛ. Dɔlli m pu'asada la nya'aŋi wi'isid.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Gɔsim dap la bɛ zin'isi'a ki'ed la, ka dɔl pu'asada la nya'aŋ; m yɛl dasam la ye ba da kadi fɔ. Ku'onuud mɛ ya'a ti mɔrif, fʋn kabigim ku'okanɛ ka dap la wiki zi'el la nu.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Ka Ruf igin ka o nindaa paae teŋin pʋ'ʋs o bɛdegʋ ka ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ na'as man anwa wʋsa, la'an nɛ man an saan la?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Ka Boaz lɛbis ye, “M pʋn wʋm fʋn tʋm sʋm si'em tisi fʋ sid ma la, lin yi fʋ sid kum saŋa ti paae zina, ka lɛn wʋm fʋn basi fʋ ba' nɛ fʋ ma nɛ fʋ teŋ ka kena zin'in nɛ nimbanɛ ka' fʋ buudii.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb na kɛ ka yɛlsʋm dɔllif, fʋ tʋʋm sʋŋ la zug. Israel Wina'am onɛ ka fʋ zaŋi fʋ mɛŋi niŋ o nu'ugin la na yɔɔf, fʋn maal sʋm la zug.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Ka Ruf lɛbis ye, “M zugdaana, fʋ na'asi m bɛdegʋ, fʋ pian'ad la kɛ ka m sʋnf ma'ae, baa mam pʋ zem nɛ fʋ tʋmtʋm yinne la.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Diib saŋa da paae ya ka Boaz yɛl Ruf ye, “Kem na di'e bodobodo nwa' gɛndig nɛ bʋnnuuda la di.” Dinzug, o da zin'in nɛ tʋmtʋmnib la, ka Boaz tis o kawɛnsɛn'ɛda. O da dii tig ka nya'al diib.

english_verse: When Ruth left to start picking up grain, Boaz told his men, “Don't stop her, even if she picks up grain from where it is stacked.
translation_verse: Ka on duoe pin'il wi'isʋg la Boaz yɛl dap la ye, “Kɛl ka o wi'is la'an nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ki bɔba la bɛ la ka da kad o.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Dinɛ paas, fuomi ki bɔba la nii digil ka o kena pi'isi paas ka da zɛrigi nɛ o.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Zaam da ma'ae la, Ruf da la'as o mui la bʋ' yɛlig ka li nwaas ye li pɛ'ɛl layalʋŋ.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Ka o zii lɛb teŋin la pa'al o sid ma la on paam si'em. O da lɛn tis o dikanɛ ka o di pɔɔgin ka li kpɛlim la.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Ka Naomi bu'os o ye, “Fʋ keŋ anɔ'ɔn pɔɔgine wi'is zina? Wina'am na niŋ o sɔb zug bareka.” Ka Ruf yɛl Naomi ye, on wi'is ki la sɔ' pɔɔgin la yʋ'ʋri buon Boaz.

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi yɛl ye, “Wina'am onɛ pʋ tammid o kaanbʋg banɛ vʋe nɛ banɛ kpi zug la na niŋ Boaz zug bareka!” Ka lɛn ye, “Dau kaŋa anɛ ti du'ad ka na nyaŋi dii ti faar.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Ka Ruf paas ye, “Dinɛ gaad wʋsa, o ye m dɔl o tʋmtʋmnib la wi'is ki la hali nɛ ki bunib la na ti naae.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi yɛl Ruf ye, “Fʋn wi'isidi dɔl pu'a banɛ bɛ Boaz pɔɔgin la an sʋm gaad fʋn na wi'is ninsieba pɔɔgin. Ya'a aan sɔ' pɔɔgin, ba na daamif.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Dinzug, Ruf da wi'isid nɛ dɔl tʋmtʋmnib la hali ka mui nɛ ki bunib la ti naae. Tʋʋma la naar nya'aŋ la, on nɛ o sid ma da kpɛm bɛ nɛ taaba.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka Naomi yɛl o bipu'a la ye, “M biiga, li kʋ an sʋm ka m bɔ sid sʋŋʋ tisif ka fʋ vʋ'ʋsɛ?

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Fʋ zi' ye Boaz onɛ ka fʋ dɔl o tʋmtʋm pu'ab la anɛ ti du'adaa? Gɔsima, o na yɛlig o mui la zieŋin zaama.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Sʋʋm ka lɔɔ fʋ zug ka zaŋ fusʋma la sɔɔn keŋ zieŋin la, amaa da kɛ ka o baŋ ye fʋ bɛɛ anii, asɛɛ ka o di ka nuu naae.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Ka o ya'a keŋ digin, fʋn kpa'am keŋ on dig zin'isi'a la, ka lak o fuug o nɔba babaa digin. Fʋ ya'a niŋ ala o na yɛlif fʋn na niŋ si'em.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Ka Ruf lɛbis ye, “Tɔ'; m na maal dinɛ wʋsa ka fʋ yɛl la.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Ka Ruf keŋ zieŋin la maal dinɛ wʋsa ka o sid ma la yɛl o ye o niŋ la.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Boaz n di ka nu naae ka li malis o hali la, o keŋ digin ki dʋʋr la kpikpɛŋ ye o gbis. Ka Ruf keŋ baanlimm lak fuug la o nɔba baba ka digin.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ tisʋʋs ka Boaz gbisi lɛbigi si'is o ka gɔsi nyɛ ka o dig o nɔba baba. Ka li lidig o,

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: ka o bu'os ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ la?” Ka Ruf lɛbis ye, “Li anɛ man Ruf, fʋ tʋmtʋm pu'ak la. Fʋn sadigim an onɛ na dii ti faar la, nɔkimi fʋ fuug la pilim.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Ka Boaz lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb na niŋi fʋ zug bareka. Fʋn tʋm tʋʋm sʋŋ si'el nwa' gaad fʋn dɛŋi maal si'em tis Naomi la, bɔzugɔ fʋ pʋ keŋ dɔl dasaŋ sɔ' onɛ an nɔŋdaan bɛɛ onɛ an kpan'am daana.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: M biiga, da zɔt dabiem, ka m na maali fʋ yɛla wʋsa. Fʋn bɔɔd si'el wʋsa m na tisif, bɔzugɔ sɔ' wʋsa baŋ ye fʋ anɛ pu'a sʋŋ.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Ya'a an sida, m anɛ onɛ na nyaŋi dii ya faar, amaa onɛ an fadit bɛɛ gaad man.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Diginim ka bɛog nie, ka o ya'a bɔɔd faar la, o na yɛl, amaa o ya'a pʋ bɔɔda, Wina'am kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zugɔ, mam na diif. Diginim ka bɛog nie.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Ka o digin o nɔba baba ka isigi duoe ka bɛog nam pʋ nie naae, ka Boaz yɛl o ye, “Da kɛ ka ba baŋ ye pu'a kɛn zieŋin nwa' naa.”

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Ka lɛn ye, “Nɔkimi fʋ fubil la yadig!” Ka on yadig fuug la ka Boaz mak mui nwama ayuobʋ tis o, ka o zii lɛb tempʋʋgin.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Ka paas ye, “Onɛ tisim mui nwama ayuobʋ nwa' ka ye, ‘Da lɛbi fʋ sid ma la ni nɛ nu'uzaalisɛ.’”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Ka Naomi ye, “M biiga, gu'usim, ka ti gɔs on na maal yɛl nwa' si'em, bɔzugɔ dau la kʋ vʋ'ʋsɛ asɛɛ ka o nyɛ yɛl la maalʋg.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Ka Boaz keŋ tempʋʋg za'anɔɔrini zin' ka fadit onɛ ka o sa yɛl o yɛla la kena gat. Ka Boaz buol o ye, “M zua, kem kpɛ' na zin'in!” Ka o keŋi zin'in.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Ka Boaz yɛl teŋ la kpɛɛmnam piiga ye ba zin'inim an kasɛtib.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Ka Boaz yɛl fadit la ye, “Naomi onɛ yi Moab teŋin lɛb na la kuosidi ti ba'abiig Elimalek paalʋ.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Ka man tɛn'ɛs ye m na mɔr yɛl nwa' paaf ka fʋ da' paalʋ la kpɛɛmnam nwa' tuon. Fʋ ya'a na nyaŋ, fʋn da'ami li. Amaa fʋ ya'a kʋ nyaŋɛ, fʋn yɛlim ka m baŋ. Bɔzugɔ sɔ' ka' suori na da' li ka ya'a ka' fʋnɛ, ka manɛ mɛ dɔlli fʋ nya'aŋ.” Ka o lɛbis ye, “M na da' li.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Dinzug ka Boaz ye, “Tɔ'; fʋ ya'a da' paalʋ la Naomi san'an, li anɛ tilas ye fʋ la'am sʋ'oe Ruf onɛ an Moab pu'a onɛ an pʋkɔɔnr la, ala ka paalʋ la na kpɛm bɛ onɛ kpi la nu'usin.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Anina ka fadit la ye, “Li ya'a aan ala, man kʋ nyaŋɛ. Fʋn ya'a na nyaŋ, fʋn da'am, bɔzugɔ m ya'a da' li m biis kʋ nyaŋi sʋ'oe lii, ka ba mɛŋ faar pʋdigir na tɔi.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka fadit la yɛl Boaz ye, “Fʋn mɛŋ da'ami li.” Ka pidig o ta'adir.

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Ka Boaz mɔɔli tis kpɛɛmnam nɛ kasɛtib la ye, “Zina zaŋi wa'ae la manɛ da' Elimalek nɛ Kilion nɛ Mahlon paalʋ la Naomi san'an.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Manɛ la'am sʋ'oe Ruf onɛ an Mahlon pʋkɔɔnr onɛ yi Moab teŋin la na. O na liebi m pu'a. Linɛ na kɛ ka onɛ kpi la yʋ'ʋr da bɔdig buudi la nii. Din ka m bɔɔd ye ya di kasɛt zina.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛmnam nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ za'anɔɔrin la yɛl ye, “Tinam anɛ kasɛtib. Zugsɔb la na kɛ ka pu'a kanɛ kpɛn'ɛdi fʋ yin la na an nwɛnɛ Rakɛl nɛ Lea banɛ da la'asi zi'el Israel buudi la. Fʋ na paam zi'esim Efirata teŋin ka mɛ nyɛ yʋ'ʋr Betilehem teŋin.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na tisif yaasi yi pu'a kaŋa san'an, ka fʋ yir la na nwɛnɛ Perez onɛ an Tama nɛ Juda biig la.” Boaz di Ruf

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Ka Boaz di Ruf ka digin nɛ o, ka Zugsɔb kɛ ka o nɔk pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Ka pu'ab la yɛl Naomi ye, “Zugsɔb di'em na'asi, on pʋ basif zaalim ka fʋ paam onɛ na di faar la. O na paam yʋ'ʋr Israel buudi ni.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Bikanɛ ka o du'a nwa' na tiaki fʋ bɛllim ka mɔrif hali nɛ fʋ kʋdigir. Fʋ bipu'a onɛ nɔŋif hali gaad fʋn na mɔrin biis ayɔpɔi la du'a yaaŋi tisif.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Ka Naomi nɔk biig la niŋ o nɔba zug yuol o.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Pu'abanɛ da bɛɛ ani la yɛl ye, “Naomi paam biribiŋ!” Ka ba pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye Obɛd. Obɛd mɛ da du'a Jese, ka Jese du'a Na'ab David. Perez yaas yɛla

english_verse: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
translation_verse: Obɛd mɛ da du'a Jese, ka Jese du'a Na'ab David.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Dau sɔ' da bɛ Ramataim teŋin an Zuf dɔɔg nidi yi kʋkʋna teŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Efiram la, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Elkana. O da anɛ Jeroham biig ka Jeroham mɛ an Elihu biig ka Elihu mɛ an Tohu biig ka Tohu mɛ an Zuf onɛ yi Efiram dɔɔgin la biig.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: O da mɔri pu'ab ayi'; yinne yʋ'ʋri da buon Hanna ka oŋa la an Penina. Penina da mɔr biis ka Hanna an kʋndu'ar.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Yʋʋm wʋsa Elkana nɛ o yidim da ɛɛnti keŋnɛ Siilo pʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la, ka maal maana anina. Eli biis ayi' banɛ yʋda da buon Hofini nɛ Finehas la da an maanmaannib saŋa kan la.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Elkana ya'a da maal o maan, o pʋdigid ni'im la nɛ tisid o pu'a Penina nɛ o biribis nɛ bipumis la wʋsa.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Amaa o da ɛɛn tis Hanna nɛ pʋdigir ayi', on nɔŋ o la zug, la'an nɛ Zugsɔb la da pʋ tis o du'am la.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da pʋ tis Hanna du'am la zug, o nintaa la da niŋid o bʋnsieba linɛ na duoe o sʋnf.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: O da maan o nɛ ala yʋʋm woo. Saŋkanɛ wʋsa ka Hanna dɔlli keŋ Zugsɔb la Pʋ'ʋsim Yin, o nintaa la na maal o siia hali ka Hanna sʋnf ti duoe ka o kaasi zan'as diib.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: O sid Elkana na bu'os o ye, “Hanna, bɔ ka fʋ kaasida? Bɔ ka fʋ zan'as diibɔ? Bɔ ka fʋ sʋnf san'am? Man an si'em tisif la pʋ gaad biis piigaa?”

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Ka Hanna kaanb kaanbʋgʋ, yɛt ye, “Zugsɔba, m anɛ fʋ sankpan'as, fʋ ya'a na gɔsim sʋnsa'aŋi zem si'em, ka tiɛn m yɛla ka da tam. Fʋ ya'a na tisim biribiŋ, m na nɔk o lɛbisi tisif ka o tʋm tisif nɛ o nyɔvʋr bɛn wʋsa ka ba kʋ pʋni o zugɔ.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Hanna da sɔsid Zugsɔb la nɛ o sʋʋnrin ka o nɔŋgban yʋmisid ka lɛɛ pʋ pian'ad ka li yita. Ka dinzug Eli da tɛn'ɛs ye o kʋʋl nɛ daam,

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bugi kena maan ala? Fʋ kʋ bas daam bugubɔɔ?”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Da tɛn'ɛs ye mam onɛ aan fʋ biig la anɛ pu'a yɔɔgɔ. Saŋa wʋsa mam sɔsidnɛ Zugsɔb la m sʋnsa'aŋ yɛla.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Ka Eli lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Kem nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm, Israel Wina'am la na tisif fʋn sɔs si'el la.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Ka Hanna ye, “Tɔ', m Ba'a, kɛl ka man onɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm pu'ak la nyɛ zugsʋŋʋ fʋ san'an.” Ka o yii lɛbi bɔ diibi di, ka tam sʋnsa'aŋ la yɛla ka o nindaa yʋ'ʋn an nyain.

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la ba da duoe pʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb la ka lɛbi ba yir dinɛ bɛ Ramataim la. Elkana daa digin nɛ o pu'a Hanna, ka Zugsɔb la tiɛn Hanna yɛla

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: ka li daa pʋ yuugɛ ka Hanna gban'e pʋʋgʋ du'a biribiŋ. Ka o pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye, Samuel bɔzugɔ o sɔs nɛ ka Zugsɔb tis o. Hanna pɛsig Samuel la yɛla

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Maan saŋa da lɛm paae ka Elkana nɛ o yidim keŋ ye ba maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la ka li kɛ ka o kaanbʋg la pɛ'ɛl.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Hanna da pʋ dɔlla, ka yɛl o sid la ye, “Biig la ya'a ti tuk bin'isir, m na mɔr o keŋ Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋrin la pɛsig o tis Wina'am ka o na bɛɛ anina saŋa wʋsa.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Ka o sid Elkana yɛl o ye, “Niŋim linɛ na an sʋm tisif. Kpɛlim kpɛla ti paae saŋkanɛ ka fʋ na tuk biig la bin'isir. Zugsɔb na kɛ ka o pian'ad la niŋ amɛŋa.” Ka pu'a la kpɛlim yinne ugus biig la hali nɛ on ti tuk biig la bin'isir.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Ka Samuel ma yɛl Eli ye, “Gaafara, m zugdaana, li anɛ sida ye manɛ an pu'a kanɛ da kɛn Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋrin na zi'e kpi'e fʋn da zin' si'el la sɔsid Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: M da sɔsid nɛ biig nwa' yɛla, ka Zugsɔb la sid gandigi m sɔsʋg ka tisim.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Zina m nɔkid o nɛ pɛsigidi tisid Zugsɔb la. O nyɔvʋr bɛn wʋsa o ye o anɛ Zugsɔb la din.” On naae la ka wɔ'ɔg Zugsɔb la anina.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Ka Hanna pʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb la yɛt ye, “M sʋnf malis nɛ Zugsɔb la. M mɛ tun'e duoe m zug agɔla yʋ'ʋs. M nɔɔr mɛ yʋ'ʋn kpi'emi m dataas tuon bɔzugɔ m pʋʋg pie Zugsɔb faangir la yɛla.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: Sɔ' kae an kasi wʋʋ Zugsɔb la, sɔ' lɛn kae nwɛnɛ fɔ; Tampinkpi'euŋ kae nwɛnɛ ti Wina'am la.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Da pian'ad nɛ nyɛɛsim saŋa wʋsaa, bɛɛ kɛ ka tita'alim pian'ad yiti ya nɔɔri nɛ. Zugsɔb Wina'am la an onɛ mi' si'el wʋsa. Onɛ mɛ makid sɔ' wʋsa tʋʋma.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Zabzabidib la tiraad wʋsa kɔya, amaa banɛ tadig la paam kpi'euŋ o san'an.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Banɛ da diti tigid la yʋ'ʋn kuosidi ba mɛŋ nɛ diib yɛla. Amaa banɛ ka kɔ'ɔm da mɔri ba la yʋ'ʋn tignɛ. Pu'a kanɛ da an kʋndu'ar la du'a biis ayɔpɔi; amaa pu'a kanɛ da mɔr biis bɛdegʋ la yʋ'ʋn zin'inɛ zaalim.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tun'e zi kum na, ka lɛn tun'e mɔr vʋm na. O tun'e sigis sɔ' yaʋgʋn ka lɛn vʋ'ʋg o.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tun'e kɛ ka nɔŋ bɛɛ arezak kena. O tun'e sief ka lɛn dʋ'ʋsif

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: onɛ ʋkid nɔŋ dim saazug, ka banɛ ka' si'el la mɛ paam si'el; ka kɛt ka ba nyaŋidi zin'inid nɛ na'abiis. Zugsɔb la sʋ'oe dunia ɛɛnbir wʋsa, ka nɔk teŋgbauŋ la sʋn'ʋli li zug.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: O na gur banɛ ka o gaŋ la, amaa bugusnam na an baanlimm likin. Sɔ' zi' nyaŋ nɛ o mɛŋ paŋa.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Banɛ ki'is Zugsɔb la na lieb zaalim, o na naan arezana nii zab nɛ ba; Zugsɔb la na kad saria ti paae dunia bɛn wʋsa. O na tis o na'ab la kpi'euŋ, o na gaŋ o ka dʋ'ʋs o yʋ'ʋr agɔla.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Ka Elkana lɛbi kul Rama teŋin, amaa biig la da kpɛlim Eli onɛ an maanmaan kpɛɛm la san'anɛ tʋmmi tisid Wina'am. Eli bibɛ'ɛdnam la yɛla

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la, maanmaannib la da niŋid nidib la si'em anɛ ye ba ya'a maal maan ka dʋg ni'im la ka li nam bɛ dʋkʋn, onɛ sʋŋid maanmaan la na nɔk dakanɛ an yiriba atan'

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: kʋns dʋk la pʋʋgin ka lin kʋnsi gban'e ni'im si'a wʋsa la ka ba yaae, ka li an maanmaan kpɛɛm la din. Anwa ka ba da maan Israel dim banɛ ken Siilo na maan maana la wʋsa.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Hali ba ya'a da ye ba nyu'oe ni'im kpaam la, onɛ sʋŋid maanmaan la na kena yɛl onɛ ye o maal maan la ye, “Tisim maanmaan la ni'im ka o sɛn'; o kʋ siaki di'e ni'im dʋgidaa fʋ san'anɛ asɛɛ ni'im kansa.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: O sɔb ya'a ye, “Kɛl ka ti naae malʋŋ bʋn la yiiga ka fʋ nyaan nɔk linɛ ka fʋ bɔɔd,” onɛ sʋŋid maanmaan la na lɛbis ye, “Ayei tisim nannanna, ya'a ka' alaa, m na nɔk nɛ paŋ!”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da nyɛ dasam la niŋid si'em la ka li anɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd tita'ar, bɔzugɔ ba da pʋ tisid maan kanɛ nyu'od bugum la girima. Samuel bɛ Siilo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Amaa Samuel da anɛ biig ka yɛ dansiki bɛ Wina'am tuonnɛ tʋm o tʋʋma.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Yʋʋm wʋsa o ma da sɛɛnd nɛ dansik ka on nɛ o sid ya'a ti keŋ ye ba maal yʋʋm-yʋʋm maan la ka o mɔri keŋ tis Samuel.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Yʋʋm wʋsa Eli da kaanbidnɛ kaanb sʋŋʋ tisid Elkana nɛ o pu'a la yɛt ye, “Zugsɔb la na tisi ya biig ka o lɛdig onɛ ka ya da sɔs ka o tisi ya ka ya lɛbisi tis o ye o tʋm o tʋʋma la.” Ka ba nyaan kul.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da zɔ Hanna nimbaanlig ka kɛ ka o du'a biribis atan' nɛ bipumis ayi'. Samuel on da bɛnɛ Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋrin la ti bi' Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: Eli was now very old, and he heard what his sons were doing to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Eli da yʋ'ʋn liebnɛ bʋnkʋdʋg, ka mɛ wʋm o biis la maan Israel dim la si'em. Ba da mɔri pu'a banɛ tʋm Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋr la za'anɔɔrin la digi.

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Ayei, m biisɛ; mam wʋm labasieba Zugsɔb la nidibin zaŋi kɛnɛ ya yɛla la ka' sʋm!

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Ninsaal ya'a tʋmm o ninsaal tiraan taal, Wina'am tun'e nwɛ' nu'ugʋ tis o; amaa ninsaal ya'a tʋm Zugsɔb la taalɛ, anɔ'ɔnɛ na nwɛ' nu'ugʋ tis o?” Amaa biis la da pʋ kɛlisi ba saam la sa'alʋgɔ, bɔzugɔ li da anɛ Wina'am mɛŋ bɔɔdim ye o kɛ ka ba kpi.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Samuel da nan kpɛn nɔbigid nɛ niŋgbiŋ, ka Zugsɔb la nɛ nidib wʋsa nɔŋ o yɛla. Eli yidim la yɛla nie paalʋ

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Saŋkan ka Zugsɔb la da tʋm Wina'am tʋmtʋm Eli san'an na yɛl o ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Ka' manɛ da nie m mɛŋi pa'ali fʋ saam yidim ban da nam bɛ Egipt Faaro nu'usin laa?

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: “Alazug, Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la, yɛli ya nyain ye, ‘Manɛ da kaanb ye fʋn nɛ fʋ saam tuŋ la wʋsa na an maanmaannib yʋma linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.’ Amaa Zugsɔb la lɛn yɛl ye kpan-kpan: ‘Banɛ na'asid man la m mɛ na na'asi ba, amaa banɛ ki'is mam la m mɛ na ki'isi ba.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, saŋa kenna ka mam na nwaae fʋn nɛ fʋ saam zak la paŋ giŋa, ka dau baa yinne kʋ kʋdig ka o zug pɛligɛ.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ka ya na paam mugusʋg man san'an, la'an nɛ mam na tʋm sʋ'ʋm tis Israel buudi la, yanam zak la sɔ' kʋ maligim lieb bʋnkʋdʋgɔ.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Onɛ yii fʋ zakin, ka m pʋ kad o maan daka la tʋʋma nii, o sɔb na bɛ amaa o tʋʋma na kɛ ka fʋ kaasid saŋa wʋsa ka ya ninta'am kɛ ka ya pʋ nyɛta ka nwɛnɛ zinzɔɔs nɛ. Ka kɛ ka fʋ sʋnf san'am ka fʋ yaas wʋsa na kpi kum kansa.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: “‘Dina na pa'al ye man yɛl si'el la na niŋa ala; fʋ biis ayi', Hofini nɛ Finehas na kpi daar yinne.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ na gaŋ maanmaan onɛ na an sida sɔb, onɛ na tʋm wʋʋ man gban'e si'em m pʋtɛn'ɛrin nɛ m sʋnfʋn la. M na maal o sɔb yir sʋ'ʋŋa ka on sɔb na tʋm nɛ na'akanɛ ka m gaŋ la saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ka banɛ wʋsa yʋ'ʋn kpɛlimmi fʋ zakin la na kenna igin o tuonnɛ sɔs anzurifa nɛ bodobodo zɔris ka bɛllim ye, “Gaŋimi ti ka ti sʋŋid maanmaan la ka paamid diibi dit.”’”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Eli nini da pʋ lɛn nyɛt sʋ'ʋŋa. Yʋ'ʋŋ yinne ka Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋr fitir bugum la nam pʋ kpiigɛ, ka Eli da dig o dig zin'ig ka Samuel mɛ da dig Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋrin la kpi'e Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la baba.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la buol Samuel ka o siak ye, “Wooi!”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Ka zɔɔ keŋ Eli san'anɛ yɛl ye, “Manɛ nwa', fʋnɛ buolɛɛ?” Ka Eli lɛbis o ye, “Mam pʋ buolɛ; lɛm digin!” Ka o sid lɛbi digin.

english_verse: Again the Lord called out Samuel's name. Samuel got up and went to Eli. “Here I am,” he said. “What do you want?” Eli told him, “Son, I didn't call you. Go back to sleep.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la buol ya'as ye, “Samuel!” Ka Samuel duoe keŋ Eli san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Manɛ nwa', fʋ buolim nɛɛ?” Eli lɛbis o ye, “M biiga, mam pʋ buolɛ, lɛm digin!”

english_verse: The Lord had not spoken to Samuel before, and Samuel did not recognize the voice.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Samuel da nan zi' Zugsɔb la, ka o mɛ da nan zi' nie o labaar la tis o.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da lɛm buol Samuel n pɛ'ɛs nɔɔra atan' ka Samuel duoe keŋ Eli san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Manɛ nwa', fʋnɛ buolɛɛ?” Ani ka Eli yʋ'ʋn baŋ ye li anɛ Zugsɔb la buon biig la.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Alazugɔ Eli da yɛl Samuel ye, “Kem digin ka o ya'a lɛm buol ya'as, fʋn on yɛlim ye, ‘Zugsɔba, pian'am ka man onɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as la kɛlisid.’” Ka Samuel sid lɛb o dig zin'igin la digin.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da lɛn sig na nɛ o girima buon nwɛnɛ on da dɛŋi buol si'em la ye, “Samuel! Samuel!” Ka Samuel siak ka ye, “Pian'am ka man onɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as la kɛlisid.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Samuel ye, “Gɔsima, m bɔɔd ye m maal si'el Israel dim san'an ka li lidig onɛ wʋsa wʋm.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ m da yɛl o ye m na kad o zak la saria saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ, tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka o mɛŋ mi' li yɛla la zug; o biis la tʋm nɛ linɛ an bɛ'ɛd ka o pʋ nyaŋi gu'oe baa.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Alazugɔ, m pɔnɛ tis Eli zak la ye, ‘Maan si'a bɛɛ suguru sɔsʋg kae na nyaŋi yis taal linɛ bɛɛ ani la.’”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samuel da digin ka bɛog nie ka o duoe yɔ'ɔg Zugsɔb la Pʋ'ʋsim Sʋgʋr la za'anɔya. O da zɔti dabiem nɛ on na yɛl Eli Wina'am nie si'eli pa'al o la.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Amaa Eli da buol o yɛl ye, “M biig Samuel!” Ka Samuel siak ye, “Manɛ nwa'!”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Ka Eli bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka o sa yɛli fɔ? Da su'adi ma! Fʋ ya'a su'a on yɛlif si'el la wʋsa nɛ mam, Wina'am kʋ kɛɛ fɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Samuel da yɛl o si'el wʋsa, ka pʋ su'aa. Ka Eli lɛbis ye, “Onɛ an Zugsɔb la; kɛl ka o tʋm linɛ ka o gɔs ka li nar la.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samuel n da nɔbigid la ka Zugsɔb la bɛ nɛ o, ka kɛ ka on kaanb si'el la wʋsa pʋ li teŋa.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Lin da zaŋ Israel dim wʋsa, pin'il Dan keŋ paae Beerseba, da siak ye Samuel sid anɛ Zugsɔb la nɔdi'es.

english_verse: The Lord often appeared to Samuel at Shiloh and told him what to say.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da pʋ gu'oe ka kpɛn ken tuonnɛ nɛɛn o mɛŋ Siilo, ani mɛn ka o da nɛɛn o mɛŋi pa'an Samuel o pian'ad pʋʋgin.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Samuel da pian'adi tisid Israel dim wʋsa ka ba kɛlisid o pian'ad. Saŋa da paae ya ye Israel dim la yii keŋ zab nɛ Filistia dim la. Israel dim la da la'as nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ba buon ye Ebɛnɛza, ka Filistia dim la mɛ la'as taaba Afek teŋin.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Dinzug ba da tʋm nidib Siilo ka ba mɔr Zugsɔb Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka zin' Kerubnama ayi' la teŋsʋk Nɔnaar Daka la zug na. Ka Eli biis ayi' la, Hofini nɛ Finehas da bɛɛ ani nɛ Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Zabzabidib la da lɛbi ba gbɛɛnb zin'igin ka Israel kpɛɛmnam la kena bu'os ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka Zugsɔb la basi ti ka ti dataas Filistia dim la nyaŋi ti zina wala? Kɛlli ka ti nɔki Zugsɔb la Nɔnaar Daka la yi Siilo kena ka li na faaɛn ti yisi ti dataas la nu'usin.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Ban da zi Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la paae la'asʋg zin'igin na la, Israel dim wʋsa da maal vuud pamm ka teŋ la mi'im.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Filistia dim la wʋm vuud la ka bu'os taaba ye, “Bɔ vuudi la yit Hibiru dim la'asʋg zin'igin la na?” Ban ti baŋ ye Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la paae la'asʋg zin'igin la,

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: dabiem da kpɛn' Filistia dim la ka ba yɛt ye, “Yɛl paae ti! Israel dim teŋgbana la kena bɛɛ ba san'an. Ti nan zi' nyɛ nɛ'ɛɛ.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Li na tɔi tisi ti. Anɔ'ɔnɛ na faaɛn ti yi teŋgban kpi'ema nwa' nu'usinɛ? Teŋgban banɛ da kɛ ka ban'anyalima gban'e Egipt dim pipirigin la.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Filistia dima gʋdigimini ya mɛŋ! Aaɛn dap, ya'a ka' ala Hibiru dim la na sʋ'oe ya wʋʋ yanamɛ da sʋ'oe ba si'em la. Kpɛ'ɛŋimini ya mɛŋ, ka zabi!”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Filistia dim da faaɛn Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la, ka Eli biis ayi' la, Hofini nɛ Finehas mɛ kpi. Eli kum yɛla

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Daakan nɔɔ ka Benjamin nid yi zab bɔn'ɔgin la na aans o fuud ka bug o zug nɛ titan sʋnsa'aŋ zug. Ka o duoe zɔɔ keŋ Siilo.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: On da zɔɔ paae na la, ka Eli zin' o kʋk zug suor kpikpɛŋi gɔsid, bɔzugɔ o ya'am da ian'adnɛ Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la yɛla. Dau la paae tempʋʋgin la naa yɛl linɛ maal la, ka teŋ la wʋsa da suak nɛ kaasig.

english_verse: “I escaped from the fighting today and ran here.” “Young man, what happened?” Eli asked.
translation_verse: Ka dau la yɛl Eli ye, “Man nan yinɛ zaba zin'igin la zina zɔɔ paae na.” Ka Eli bu'os ye, “M biiga, bɔɔ maalɛ?”

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
translation_verse: Ka dau kanɛ mɔr labaar la na yɛl ye, “Israel dim zɔnɛ ka Filistia dim la kʋ soogianam la bɛdegʋ. Fʋ biis ayi' la, Hofini nɛ Finehas mɛ kpiya. Filistia dim faaɛn Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la gaad.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: On yɛl ye ba faaɛn Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la, ka Eli kpɛn bik nɛ kʋk la li azampɛ'ɛl Siilo teŋ la za'anɔɔr la baba. Ka o niŋgɔɔnr kɔ'ɔg ka o kpi, bɔzugɔ o da anɛ bʋnkʋdʋg ka an nintɛbisʋg. O da an Israel dim tuongat nɛ yʋma pisnaasi.

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: O bipu'a onɛ an Finehas pu'a la da mɔri pʋʋg. Ka on wʋm labaar la ye Filistia dim faaɛn Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka ka o sid nɛ o dayaandau mɛ kpi la, o da sa'ae nɛ kpi'emis ka du'am la zabir da wʋm o hali.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: On da bɔɔd kum la ka pu'adu'asnam la yɛl o ye, “Da kɛ ka yɛla la kʋʋ fʋ giinlaa; gɔsima, fʋ du'a nɛ biribiŋ.” Amaa o da pʋ ya'ae o nɔɔr bɛɛ kɛlis ban yɛt si'el la.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da faaɛn Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la, ba da nɔki li yi Ebɛnɛza keŋ Asdod teŋin.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Ba da zi daka la keŋ kpɛn'ɛsi ba ba'ar linɛ ka ba buon Dagon la dɔɔgin zi'eli kpi'el ba'ar la.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la, ka Asdod dim yina nyɛɛ ba ba'ar linɛ buon Dagon la luu vanbin Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la tuon. Ka ba duoe li,

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: amaa bɛogʋ da lɛn nie la, ba yina nyɛnɛ ba ba'ar la lɛn luu vanb Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la tuon ya'as, ka o zug nɛ nu'us la kɔɔ dig za'anɔɔrin la, ka o niŋgbiŋ la ma'aa kpɛlim zi'e.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Linzug lin yi saŋkanɛ ti paae zina Dagon maanmaan, bɛɛ onɛ kpɛn'ɛd ba'ar la dɔɔgin wʋsa, pʋ nɔɔd za'anɔɔrin la.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋnf da pʋ malis nɛ Asdod teŋ nidib la nɛ zin'ibanɛ wʋsa kpi'e teŋ la. Ka o kɛ ka ba nyɛ san'auŋ nɛ tɔɔg ka natiŋkpi'emis gban'e ba.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Asdod dimi da nyɛ linɛ maan la, ka yɛl taaba ye, “Israel dim teŋgban daka la pʋ nar ye li bɛ nɛ ti kpɛla, bɔzugɔ li kɛnɛ ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf duod nɛ ti nɛ Dagon onɛ aan ti ba'ar la wʋsa.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Linzug ba da buol Filistia dim teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la wʋsa la'as ka bu'osi ba ye, “Ti na niŋ wala nɛ Israel dim teŋgban daka la?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Yisiminɛ li mɔri keŋ Gaf teŋin.” Ka ba sid yis Israel Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
