translation_verse: Dinzug ba da zaŋ Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la keŋ Ekron teŋin. Nɔnaar daka la da kpɛn'ɛd Ekron la, Ekron nidib da kaas kuŋʋ yɛt ye, “Ba mɔr Israel dim teŋgban daka la giligi paae kpɛla na ye ba kʋ tinam nɛ ti nidib la wʋsa.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Dinzug, ba da buol Filistia dim teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la wʋsa la'as ka yɛli ba ye, “Mɔri Israel teŋ dim win daka la lɛbisi li zin'igin, ya'a ka' ala li na kʋ tinam nɛ ti nidib la wʋsa!” Bɔzugɔ, kum da kʋʋd nɛ zin'ig wʋsa ka dabiem kpɛn' ba, ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf da duoe ka o namisi ba hali.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Banɛ da pʋ kpi la, natiŋkpi'emis da mɔdi ba, ka ba kaasid yɔɔg-yɔɔg.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la da bɛ Filistia sʋ'ʋlim nwadis ayɔpɔi la,

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da keŋ bu'osi ba teŋgban maannib nɛ ba'abʋgʋdib la ye, “Ti na niŋ Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la wala? Yɛlimi ti tinamɛ na niŋ si'em lɛbisi li, li zin'igin.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ya ya'a ye ya lɛbis Israel dim teŋgban daka la, yanam on da lɛbisi li zaalim, amaa mɔɔmi ka bɔɔe la'abanɛ ka ba na maal taal malʋŋʋ paasi. Ala ka ya na paam laafi, ka mɛ baŋ linɛ zugʋ kɛ ka o sʋnf pɛlig nɛ ya la.”

english_verse: “What should we send?” the Philistines asked. The priests and fortunetellers answered: There are five Philistine rulers, and they all have the same disease that you have.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da bu'os ye, “Taal maan la'abɔ ka ti na paasi keŋ tis o?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Zaŋimi sanlima maal natiŋkpi'emis anu, ka mɛ maal dayuus anu nwɛnɛ Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la kalli an si'em la. Bɔzugɔ tɔɔg la daa pʋ pansig teŋ sʋ'ʋdib bɛɛ tadim wʋsa.

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Maaliminɛ sanlima natiŋkpi'emis nɛ dayuus banɛ san'amidi ya teŋ la, ka nɔki li tis Israel dim teŋgban la, ka mɛ tis o girima, ka daasi'erɛɛ o na yis tɔɔg linɛ paadi ya nɛ ya bada nɛ ya teŋ la.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka ya digilimi ya sʋnya wʋʋ Egipt dim nɛ Faaro da niŋ si'em la? On da kɛ ka li wʋmi ba hali la, Faaro da pʋ bas suor ka ba yii?”

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: “Alazug, bɔɔmi niigi tɛreko paal nɛ na'abanɛ du'a ka ba nam pʋ niŋi ba yuasin nɛ, ka lɔɔ ba ta'al nɛ tɛreko la ka nɔki ba na'abibis la kpɛn'ɛs garikini lɔ.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Ka nɔki Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la pa'ali tɛreko la zug, ka lɛn nɔk daka yinne ka zaŋi ya taal malʋŋ la'ad la niŋi li pʋʋgin, ka nɔki pa'al tɛreko la pʋʋg ka kɛ ka li dɔlli li suor.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Amaa kpansimini li gɔsi; li ya'a kennɛ kpa'ad Israel teŋ linɛ ka ba buon Befisemes la, li pa'al ye li anɛ Zugsɔb la kɛ ka tɔɔg la paae ti. Amaa li ya'a pʋ niŋ ala, li pa'al ye ka' Zugsɔb la daa kɛ ka tɔɔg la kenaa, li yinɛ zin'isi'a kidig na.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Ka ba sid nɔk na'abanɛ aan ala lɔɔ ba ta'al nɛ tɛreko la ka yɔɔ ba biis la.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Ka nɔk Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la sʋn'ʋl tɛreko la zug nɛ sanlima banɛ ka ba zaŋi maal dayuus nɛ natiŋkpi'emis la.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Ka niigi la kpɛn kpa' keŋ Befisemes ka bʋʋn hali, ka pʋ bie lɛb suor la datiuŋ bɛɛ dagɔbʋgɔ. Ka Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la dɔl daka la nya'aŋ, hali ti paae Befisemes titɔndigin.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa Befisemes dim da bɛnɛ ba bɔn'ɔdin bʋn ki, ka ban ʋki ba nindaa nyɛ daka la ba da maan sumalisim.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filistia dim teŋ sʋ'ʋdiba anu la da bɛɛ ani ka nyɛ ban maal si'el la wʋsa ka nyaan lɛbi kul Ekron teŋin daakan nɔɔ.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Filistia dim banɛ da mɔr sanlima la kena maali ba taal malʋŋ la nwa': Asdod nɛ Gaza nɛ Askɛlon nɛ Gaf nɛ Ekron dim; ba da tis nɛ yinne-yinne.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Sanlim banɛ ka ba da maal wʋʋ dayuus la, ba da pʋdignɛ dɔlis Filistia dim teŋ nɛ li teŋ sʋ'ʋdibi an si'em teŋ bɛda la nɛ li tembibis la. Tampintita'ar linɛ ka ba da zaŋ Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la sʋn'ʋl la anɛ kasɛt hali ti paae zina. Li nan zi'e Josua pɔɔg la baba, Befisemes teŋin.

english_verse: Some of the men of Beth-Shemesh looked inside the sacred chest, and the Lord God killed
translation_verse: Amaa Befisemes nidib pisyɔpɔi da siki gɔs Nɔnaar Daka la pʋʋgin ka Zugsɔb la kʋʋ ba li zug. Nidib la da kaas nɛ hali, Zugsɔb la tɛɛgi ba tʋbir si'em la zug.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Ka Befisemes nidib la bu'os ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi zi'en Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ an kasi nwa' tuonnɛ? Ka ti na mɔr Daka la yi kpɛla, keŋ tisi anɔ'ɔnɛ?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Ka ba da tʋm nidib ka ba mɔr labaari keŋi tis Kiriaf Jiarim teŋ nidib la yɛli ba ye, “Filistia dim la lɛbis Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la na. Kemi na nɔkini li keŋi ya zin'igin la.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Ka Kiriaf Jiarim teŋ dim la da kena zaŋ Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la. Ba da mɔri li keŋi Abinadab yin linɛ bɛ kʋkʋna ni la, ka maal maan linɛ na kɛ ka o biig onɛ yʋ'ʋri da buon Eleazar gur Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la. Samuel nyaŋ Filistia dim

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Samuel da yɛl Israel dim wʋsa ye, “Ya ya'a sid bɔɔd ye ya lɛb Zugsɔb la san'an nɛ ya sʋnf wʋsa, yanam on basimi ya teŋzʋŋ bada nɛ wina nɛ Asitoref bada la'ad la wʋsa, ka pɛsigi ya mɛŋ wʋsa tis Zugsɔb la, ka tʋm tis on ma'aa. Ya ya'a niŋ ala, o na faaɛn ya yisi ya dataas Filistia dim la nu'usin.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim la sid basi ba bada banɛ an Baal nɛ Asitoref la, ka ti'e Zugsɔb la ma'aa.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Samuel yɛl ye, “La'asimi Israel dim wʋsa ka ba kɛn Misipa teŋin na, ka m nwɛ' Wina'am nu'ugʋ tisi ya.”

english_verse: The Israelites met together at Mizpah with Samuel as their leader. They drew water from the well and poured it out as an offering to the Lord. On that same day they went without eating to show their sorrow, and they confessed they had been unfaithful to the Lord. The Philistines Attack Israel
translation_verse: Ban da la'as Misipa na la ka wik ku'om bu'oe Zugsɔb la tuon. Daakan la ba da lɔ nɔɔr ka yɛl taal kanɛ ka ba tʋm ka li ka' sʋ'ʋm la wʋsa, ye, “Tinam tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon.” Samuel n da aan ba tuongat Misipa teŋin.

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Saŋkan ka Filistia dim la da wʋm ye Israel dim la'asi bɛ Misipa la, ba teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la da la'asi kena ye ba zab nɛ ba. Israel dim la da wʋm labaar la, dabiem da gban'e ba Filistia dim la yɛla.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl Samuel ye, “Da gu'oe fʋn sɔsid Zugsɔb Wina'am ti yɛla ye o faaɛn ti yis Filistia dim nu'usin la.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Samuel n da nam bɛɛ ani maan maan la, Filistia dim da mirid na ye ba zab nɛ ba. Amaa daakan la Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka satansʋg tans nɛ paŋ Filistia dim la san'an, ka dabietita'ar kpɛn' ba ka ba zɔ ka bas Israel dim la.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Israel dim dap la da yi Misipa teŋin tabinɛ ba gbin tɔ'ɔtɔ hali kʋʋ ba yinne-yinne sigi tʋʋg Befikaa teŋin sa.

english_verse: The Philistines were so badly beaten that it was quite a while before they attacked Israel again. After the battle, Samuel set up a monument between Mizpah and the rocky cliffs. He named it “Help Monument” to remind Israel how much the Lord had helped them. For as long as Samuel lived, the Lord helped Israel fight the Philistines.
translation_verse: Ba da nyaŋ Filistia dim la ka ba pʋ lɛn nyaŋi kpɛn' Israel sʋ'ʋlim daami ba ya'asa. Samuel nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa la wʋsa Zugsɔb la da zabidi nɛ Filistia dim la.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Ekron ken paae Gaf linɛ ka Filistia dim la da faaɛn Israel dim la san'an la, ba da lɛn di'e ba bʋn. Israel dim da faaɛn tembanɛ kpi'e ba wʋsa ya'as Filistia dim la nu'usin. Sumbʋgʋsʋm yʋ'ʋn da bɛ Israel dim nɛ Amor dim la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samuel da anɛ Israel dim sariakat o nyɔvʋr bɛn wʋsa.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Yʋʋm wʋsa, o da giligid nɛ, lin yi Betel keŋ paae Gilgal nɛ Misipa, kad Israel dim saria, zin'iban la wʋsa.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Amaa o da ɛɛn lɛbid Rama teŋin saŋa wʋsa, zin'ikanɛ ka o yir da bɛ la. Ani mɛn, o da kad Israel dim la saria. O da maal pʋ'ʋsim bimbim anii tis Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: O bikpɛŋ la yʋ'ʋri da buon Joel ka onɛ tia'al la yʋ'ʋr buon Abija. Ba da bɛnɛ Beerseba tʋm sariakadib tʋʋma ani.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Dinzug da kɛ ka Israel dim kpɛɛmnam la la'as taaba keŋ Samuel san'an Rama teŋin.

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl o ye, “Nannanna fʋ kʋdigya, ka fʋ biis la pʋ dɔl fʋn bɔɔd si'el la; alazugɔɔ gaŋim na'abi tisi ti ka o luu ti tuon, nwɛnɛ tembanɛ mɔr na'anam si'em la.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Amaa ban da yɛl ye, “Gaŋim na'abi tisi ti ka o luu ti tuon la,” li da pʋ malis Samuel sʋʋnrɛ; alazug Samuel da bu'os Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis o ye, “Siakim nidib la yɛlif si'el la wʋsa; li ka' fʋn ka ba zan'asɛ, amaa ba zan'as nɛ man kanɛ aan ba Na'ab la.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Ba da pʋn zan'asim daakanɛ ka ba pin'ili yi Egipt teŋin hali ti paae zina la. Ban kɛɛs mam bas ka dɔl ba'asieba la, ala nɔɔ ka ba maannif.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Siakim ban yɛtif si'el la; amaa sa'alimi ba sʋ'ʋŋa ka kɛ ka ba baŋ onɛ na aan ba na'ab la na tʋm si'em.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samuel da pian' tis nimbanɛ ye ba bɔɔdi ba mɛŋ na'ab la pa'ali ba Zugsɔb la yɛl o si'el la wʋsa.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: O yɛli ba ye, “Onɛ ye o aan ya na'ab la na tʋm si'em nwa': O na nɔki ya biribis la ka ba gɔsid o widi nɛ ba tɛrekonam la, ka o ya'a ken zin'isi'a wʋsa, ba sieba na gat o mɛŋ widi tɛreko la tuon.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: O na nɔki ya bipumis la ka ba sieba maan tudaar ka bam dʋgid bɛɛ sɛn'ɛd bodobodo.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: O na di'e ya pɔsʋma la nɛ ya vain tiis pɔɔd linɛ maan bʋnnuuda nɛ olif tiis linɛ vɛnl wʋsa ka nɔki tis banɛ tʋmmi tisid o la.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: O na kɛ ka ya pʋdigidi ya ki nɛ ya daam zin'is piiga ka o nɔk pʋdigir yinne tis o nayikpɛm nɛ banɛ tʋmmi tisid o la.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: O na di'e ya sankpan'as dap nɛ pu'ab nɛ ya niigi nɛ bʋmis wʋsa mɔri maan o mɛŋi bɔɔd si'el.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: O na di'e ya bʋnkɔnbid piiga pʋdigir yinne, hali ka ya mɛŋ lieb o yammis.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Dabiskan ya'a ti paae yanam mɛŋ na kaasidi bɔɔd yɔlisim yit na'akanɛ ka ya gaŋ la nu'usin, ka Zugsɔb la kʋ wʋm ka sʋŋi yaa.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: Li na kɛ ka ti mɛ nwɛnɛ tembanɛ kpi'enɛ ti mɔr na'anam ka ba luti ba tuon si'em la. Ka o na gati ti tuonnɛ zabidi ti zaba tisidi ti.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samuel da wʋm nidib la yɛl si'el wʋsa la, ka yɛl Zugsɔb ban yɛl si'el la nɔɔ.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da lɛbis ye, “Siakim tisi ba ka tisi ba na'ab.” Ka Samuel da yɛl Israel dim la ye ba wʋsa kulimi ba yaan.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Dau sɔ' da bɛɛ an Benjamin nid ka an ninvʋsʋŋ, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Kis. O saam da anɛ Abiel ka on saam mɛ an Zero ka on saam mɛ an Bekoraf ka on saam mɛ an Afia onɛ an Benjamin nid.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: O da mɔr biig ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Saul, ka sɔ' wʋsa nini da tig o ka o tiraan kae Israel nidibin la ya'asɛ, ka o wa'alim gaad sɔ' wʋsa.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Saŋkan la, Saul saam Kis bʋmis da bɔdig nɛ, ka o yɛl o biig Saul ye, “Dɔl yammis la yinne ka ya keŋ iee ba.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Ka o yii dɔl Efiram linɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la giligi keŋ Sialisa, amaa ba da pʋ nyɛɛ ba. Ba da keŋ hali ti kpɛn' Sia'alim sʋ'ʋlim, amaa bʋmis la da ka' anina. Ka ba gaadi keŋ yi Benjamin paalʋ titɔndigin, amaa ba da pʋ nyɛɛ ba.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Ban da paae Zuf sʋ'ʋlim la, ka Saul yɛl sankpan'as kanɛ dɔl o la ye, “Kɛl ka ti lɛb; ya'a ka' ala m saam na tam bʋmis la yɛla ka tinam yɛla yʋ'ʋn lɛbi pak o.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Ka sankpan'as la lɛbis ye, “Gɔsima! Wina'am nɔdi'es bɛ tempʋʋg kaŋa ni, ka ba tisid o girima hali. O ya'a yɛl si'el li sid niŋid nɛ. Ti kem o san'an nannanna, ka daasi'erɛɛ o na pa'ali ti tinamɛ na dɔl si'el.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Ka Saul bu'os sankpan'as la ye, “Ti ya'a keŋɛ, bɔ ka ti mɔri na tis o? Diib linɛ bɛɛ ti kɔlʋgin la naae ya. Ti pʋ mɔr piinsi'a na keŋ ka tis Wina'am nɔdi'es la.”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Ka sankpan'as la lɛn lɛbis ye, “Gɔsima! Mam mɔr anzurifa bi'ela kpɛla. M na nɔki tis Wina'am nɔdi'es la ka o pa'ali ti tinamɛ na dɔl si'el.”

english_verse: “Great!” Saul replied. “Let's go to the man who can see visions!” He said this because in those days God would answer questions by giving visions to prophets. Saul and his servant went to the town where the prophet lived.
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛl sankpan'as la ye, “Fʋ mɔya! Kem na ka ti keŋ!” Ba da sid keŋ Wina'am nɔdi'es la da bɛ teŋ si'a la.

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Ban da nan dʋt kʋkʋn la ye ba paae tempʋʋgin la, ba da sia'al pu'asada ka ba kenna ye ba wik ku'om, ka ba bu'osi ba ye, “Onɛ nyɛt la bɛ kpɛlaa?”

english_verse: “Yes, he is,” they replied. “He's in town today because there's going to be a sacrifice and a sacred meal at the place of worship. In fact, he's just ahead of you. Hurry
translation_verse: Ka ba ye, “Ɛɛn, o bɛ kpɛla! O bɛɛ ya tuon. Kemi tɔ'ɔtɔ ka o kennɛ ti teŋa zina na, bɔzugɔ nidib la mɔri ba maana bɛ maana zin'igin la.

english_verse: and you should find him right inside the town gate. He's on his way out to the place of worship to eat with the invited guests. They can't start eating until he blesses the sacrifice. If you go now, you should find him.”
translation_verse: Ya ya'a kpɛn' tempʋʋgin la tɔ'ɔtɔ, ya na nyɛɛ o ka o nyaan kpɛn' maan zin'igin di. Nidib la kʋ pin'il diibɔ asɛɛ ka o paae, bɔzugɔ onɛ ye o niŋ maan la zug bareka ka banɛ ka ba kaanb la nyaan di. Kemi nannanna ka ya na nyɛɛ o.”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Ba da keŋ tempʋʋgin la, ka ban da kpɛn'ɛd ani la, ba da nyɛ Samuel ka o dɔl ban bɛ zin'isi'a la ye o gaadi keŋ maan zin'igin la.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Ban saa na keŋ wʋʋ bɛog la, ka Zugsɔb la pʋn nie li yɛla pa'al Samuel ye,

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Bɛog anwa win la, mam na tʋm dau sɔ' ka o yi Benjamin teŋin kɛɛn fʋ san'an na. Nɔkim malʋŋ kpaam la bu'oe niŋ o zugin ka o liebi m nimbanɛ an Israel dim la tuongat. O na faanm nidib la yi Filistia dim la nu'ugin, ka gɔsi m nidib la bɔzugɔ ba kaasig paae mam na.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Samuel n da nyɛ Saul la, Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, “Dau kaŋa ka m sa yɛtif o yɛla la. Onɛ ye o guri m nidib la.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Saul n da keŋ paae Samuel san'an teŋ la za'anɔɔrin la, ka bu'os o ye, “M bɛlimnɛ, fʋ na pa'alim onɛ nyɛt la yinnee?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbis ye, “Manɛ an onɛ nyɛt la. Gaadim tuonnɛ keŋ maan zin'igin la, bɔzugɔ zina fʋ ye fʋ dinɛ nɛ mam, ka gbɛn ka bɛog bɛkɛung ka m yɛl linɛ wʋsa bɛɛ fʋ sʋʋnrin.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Ya'a an bʋmis banɛ bɔdig daba atan' zina la, da kɛ ka ba yɛla paki yaa; ka ba nyɛɛ ba. Anɔ'ɔn ka Israel dim ya'am wʋsa kpɛn' ka li ya'a ka' fʋ nɛ fʋ saam yidim la ma'aanɛ?”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Saul lɛbis ye, “Mam ka'anɛ Benjamin nid ka yi dɔkanɛ pɔɔd Israel buudi wʋsa ni na laa? Ka' tinam tuŋ la pɔɔdi gat Benjamin dim la wʋsa? Bɔ ka fʋ yɛtim nwa'?”

english_verse: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining room at the place of worship. About
translation_verse: Samuel da dɔl Saul nɛ sankpan'as la kpɛn' zɔŋŋin ka tisi ba zin'isʋma nimbɛda banɛ ka o kaanb la tuon. Nidib la kal da anɛ wʋʋ pistan'.

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Ka o nɔk gbɛmum la mɔr na digil Saul tuon. Ka Samuel yɛl ye, “Ban digilif si'eli nwa'. Ɔm ka fʋ zug ka ba yisi lii digili li kɔn' la'as kaŋa nwa' yɛla ka m nyaan buol nidib la.” Ka Saul di nɛ Samuel daakan.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Ban da naan maan zin'igin lɛb tempʋʋgin na la, Samuel da dɔl Saul n dʋʋ o dɔɔg zug ka ba sɔns.

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: Ba da dɛŋ isigir ka bɛog bɔɔd nier, ka Samuel buol Saul dɔɔg la zugʋ yɛl o ye, “Ti'ebim ka m kɛɛsi ya ka ya kul.” Saul n da ti'ebi naae la, ka on nɛ Samuel dɔl taaba yi.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Ban da yit tempʋʋgin la, Samuel yɛl Saul ye, “Yɛlimi fʋ sankpan'as la ka o gaadi ti tuon.” Ka sankpan'as la sid niŋ ala. Ka o mɛ yɛl Saul ye, “Fʋn zi'enim kpɛla bi'ela, ka m tisif labaar linɛ yi Wina'am san'an na.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Samuel da nɔk malʋŋ kpaam nɛ iili bu'oe niŋ Saul zugin ka pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa yɛt ye, “Zugsɔb la gaŋif ye fʋ gur o nimbanɛ aan o din la.”

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a bas mam kpɛla zina, fʋ na sia'al nidib ayi' Rakɛl yaʋg la baba, linɛ bɛ Zeliza kpi'e nɛ Benjamin titɔndig la. Ba na yɛlif ye ba nyɛ bʋmis banɛ ka ya daa ieed la. Nannanna bʋmis la yɛla pʋ lɛm paki fʋ saam ya'asɛ; yanam yɛla pak. O yʋ'ʋn bu'osid nɛ ye, “M na niŋ wala nɛ m biig nwa' yɛla”

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Fʋ na yii anina keŋ hali ti paae Tabo titita'arin la. Nidib atan' banɛ wa'ae Betel ye ba pʋ'ʋs Wina'am la na sia'alif ani. Yinne na tɛɛd bʋbibis atan', ka yinne mɛ mɔr bodobodo atan', ka onɛ kpɛlim la mɛ zanl daam nɛ gan'ar.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Ba na pʋ'ʋsif, ka tisif bodobodo ayi'. Da zan'asɛ, li sʋ'ʋm ye fʋ di'e lii ba san'an.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a di'e naae, fʋn on kem Gibea teŋ kanɛ ka ba buon ye, Wina'am din la, anina ka Filistia dim soogia sieba kena zin' gur la. Fʋ ya'a ti li'en tempʋʋg la, fʋ na sia'al nɔdi'esidib bɛdegʋ ka ba dɔl taaba naan malʋŋ zin'igin la yit na ka googinam nɛ siyada nɛ na'atana nɛ wiis gaadi ba tuonnɛ nwɛ'ɛd ka ba di'esid Wina'am pian'adi tisid nidib.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Siig la paŋ na sigi fʋ zugin na ka fʋn mɛ na la'as nɛ ba di'esid Wina'am pian'ad, ka mɛ na tiak ka lɛn ka' fʋn an sɔ' la ya'asɛ.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛnam wʋsa ya'a ti niŋ, fʋn tʋm fʋn gban'e si'el wʋsa, ka Wina'am la bɛ nɛf.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: “Gaadimi m tuonnɛ keŋ Gilgal, ka m na kɛɛn fʋ san'an na maal nyu'or maan nɛ taaba la'asʋg maan. Amaa asɛɛ fʋ gur daba ayɔpɔi ka m nyaan kena ka yɛlif fʋn ye fʋ tʋm si'el.” Saul na'am diib yɛla

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Saul da fɛndigi keŋ ka bas Samuel ka Wina'am da kɛɛn o san'an na tiak o sʋʋnr. Ka zanbin banɛ ka o yɛl ye li na niŋ la wʋsa niŋ daakan la.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Ban da paae Gibea la, nɔdi'esidib bɛdegʋ banɛ dɔl taaba da sia'al o; ka Wina'am Siig sig o zugin na nɛ paŋ. Ka o pɛ'ɛsi ba di'esid Wina'am pian'adi tisid nidib.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Nimbanɛ wʋsa da pʋn mi' o ka yʋ'ʋn nyɛɛ o ka o la'as nɛ nɔdi'esidib la mɛ di'esid Wina'am pian'adi tisid nidib la, ba da pin'ili bu'osid taaba ye, “Bɔɔ nwa' mɛ paae Kis biig la? Saul mɛ anɛ nɔdi'esidib la yinnee?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Dau sɔ' da bɛɛ ani ka bu'os ye, “Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ aan ba saama?” Ka li da lieb siiliŋ ye, “Saul mɛ yʋ'ʋn anɛ nɔdi'esidib la yinnee?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Saul n da gu'oe nɔdi'esʋg la, o da keŋ maan zin'igin la.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Ani la Saul saambil bu'os on nɛ o sankpan'as la ye, “Yaanɛ ka yanam keŋɛ?” Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Ti keŋ nɛ bʋmis la ieeb, amaa tinamɛ daa nam pʋ nyɛɛ ba la, ti daa keŋ Samuel san'an.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Saul saambil la da yɛl o ye, “Yɛlim mam Samuel n yɛli ya si'el.”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Ka Saul lɛbis o ye, “O yɛli ti ye ba nyɛ bʋmis la,” amaa o da pʋ yɛl o saambil la Samuel n yɛl o na'am la diib yɛla laa.

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Samuel da la'as Israel dim la wʋsa Zugsɔb tuon Misipa

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: ka yɛli ba ye, “Israel dim Wina'am la yɛl ye, ‘Manɛ yis yanam Israel dim la Egipt teŋin na ka faaɛn ya yis Egipt dim paŋ la pʋʋgin nɛ sʋ'ʋlim banɛ wʋsa da namisidi ya la.’

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Amaa ya zan'asi ya Wina'am onɛ faaɛn ya yisi ya tɔɔg nɛ sʋnsa'aŋin la ka yɛl ye, ‘Ayei, bɔɔm na'abi tisi ti.’ Alazugɔ nannanna mɔri nɛ ya dɔɔd nɛ tuŋ kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb la kɛn Zugsɔb la tuon na.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Samuel da buol dɔɔd la wʋsa yinne-yinne ye ba li'el na, Benjamin dɔɔg la ka ba da gaŋ.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Ka o yis Benjamin dɔɔg la tuon na, yis tuŋ-tuŋ: Matir tuŋ la ka ba da gaŋ. Li naar la wʋsa, Saul onɛ an Kis biig la ka ba da gaŋ. Amaa ban gɔs nidibin la, ba pʋ nyɛɛ o.

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛm bu'os Zugsɔb la ye, “Dau la on bɛ kpɛlaa?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, o su'a o mɛŋ la'ad la teŋsʋk.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Ba da keŋ yis o na zi'el nidibin la, ka o wa'alim gaadi ba wʋsa.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ka Samuel yɛl nidib la wʋsa ye, “Ya nyɛ dau kanɛ ka Zugsɔb la gaŋ laa? O tiraan kae nimbama wʋsa nii.” Ka nidib tans nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, “Na'aba! Wina'am na pɛligi fʋ zug!”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Samuel da tu'asi pa'ali ba na'am la suoya. O da sɔbi ba niŋ gbauŋʋn digil Zugsɔb la tuon, ka nyaan bas nidib la ka sɔ' wʋsa kul o yin.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Saul mɛ da lɛbi kul o yin linɛ bɛ Gibea teŋin la, ka dap banɛ sʋnfʋ da kpi'em ka Wina'am yɛlʋg bɛɛ ba sʋnfʋn dɔl o.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Amaa ninvʋyɔɔd la da yɛl ye, “Oŋa ye o niŋ wala sʋŋ tinama?” Ba da nɛ'ɛs o ka pʋ tis o piini. Amaa Saul da sin o nɔɔr ka pʋ yɛl si'ela.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Nahas onɛ an Ammon dim na'ab la da keŋ nɛ o zabzabidibi lɔbi gilig Jabis Gilead teŋ la. Jabis teŋ dim la da yɛl o ye, “Niŋim nɔɔr yinne nɛ ti, ka ti na siaki dɔllif.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Amaa Nahas onɛ an Ammon dau la lɛbis ye, “M na niŋ nɔɔr yinne nɛ ya, ya ya'a na siak ye m kpigi ya wʋsa datiuŋ nini ka li lieb nyannɛ tis Israel dim wʋsa.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Jabis kpɛɛmnam la da yɛl o ye, “Tisimi ti daba ayɔpɔi ka ti tʋm ka ba keŋ tis Israel dim labaar ka sɔ' ya'a pʋ kena faaɛn tii, ti na siaki dɔllif.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Banɛ ka ba da tʋm la mɔr labaar la paae Saul teŋ kanɛ ka ba buon ye, Gibea la yɛl nidib la, ba da nwɛ'ɛnɛ kuŋi kaasid agɔla.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Saŋkan ka Saul yi pɔɔginɛ kunna nɛ o niigi, ka bu'os ye, “Bɔɔ maal nidib la ka ba kaasida?” Ka ba yɛl o Jabis dim la yɛl si'el la wʋsa.

english_verse: Then the Spirit of God suddenly took control of Saul and made him furious.
translation_verse: Saul n da wʋm labaar la, Wina'am Siig da sig o zugin na nɛ paŋ ka o sʋnf duoe.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: O da nɔk lɔlis ayi' kʋʋ waansi ba ni'im la zɔra-zɔra tis ka ba giligi tis Israel dim wʋsa, ka yɛli ba ye, “Onɛ wʋsa pʋ yina dɔl Saul nɛ Samuel keŋ n zaba la, anwa ka m ye m maal o sɔb niigi.” Dinzug da kɛ ka ba zɔ Zugsɔb la dabiem ka ba wʋsa niŋ nɔɔr yinne.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl banɛ mɔr labaar la na ye, “Yɛlimi Jabis Gilead dim ye, ‘Bɛog, winnigi saa ye li bul saŋsi'a la, ka ya pʋn yi mugusʋg pʋʋgin.’” Ban da lɛb nɛ labakaŋa yɛl Jabis dim dap la, ba da mɔr sumpielim,

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl Ammon dim la ye, “Bɛog ti na mɔri ti mɛŋ na tisi ya, ka ya maal yanamɛ bɔɔd si'el.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la, Saul da pʋdig o nidib la zin'isa atan'. Bɛkɛung asuba, ka ba kɔɔ kpɛn' Ammon dim la teŋsʋk ba gbɛɛnb zin'igin la kɔti ba hali ka nintaŋ nyaan bul. Ban ka ba da pʋ paam la da widignɛ, ka sɔ' pʋ lɛn nyaŋi dɔl o tiraana. Ba siak ye Saul aan ba na'ab

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Nidib la da yʋ'ʋn bu'os Samuel ye, “Anɔ'ɔnamɛ daa bu'os ye Saul na nyaŋi aan ti na'ab la? Ba bɛ yaanɛ? Mɔri ba dima na ka ti kʋʋ ba!”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Amaa ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ kpiid zinaa. Bɔzugɔ zina ka Zugsɔb la faaɛn Israel dim la.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Samuel da yɛl nidib la ye, “Kemi na ka ti keŋi Gilgal n maligim diis na'am la anina.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Nidib la wʋsa da sid keŋ Gilgal n diis Saul na'am la Zugsɔb la tuon. Anina ka ba da maal taaba la'asʋg maana Zugsɔb la tuon, ka Saul nɛ Israel dim la wʋsa la'asi maal sumalistita'ar.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Samuel da yɛl Israel dim la ye, “Mam wʋmi ya pian'ad la wʋsa ka gaŋ Na'abi tisi ya.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Nannanna ya mɔr Na'ab onɛ aan ya tuongat. Ya'a kpɛlim mam, man anɛ bʋnkʋdʋg ka zug pɛlig, ka m biis la bɛ nɛ ya kpɛla. Mam daa anɛ ya tuongat m dasannimin sa kena paae zina.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Manɛ nwa' zi'e ya tuon. Yɛlimi sida, m ya'a maal sɔ' linɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm, yanam yɛliminim Zugsɔb la nɛ onɛ ka o gaŋ ka m zaŋ malʋŋ kpaam bu'oe niŋ o zug la tuon. Anɔ'ɔn lɔlig ka m di'e? Anɔ'ɔn bʋŋ ka m di'e? Anɔ'ɔn ka m filim? Anɔ'ɔn ka m wɛbigɛ? Anɔ'ɔn mi' da'am nɛ si'el ka m umi m nini ka di'e? M ya'a nam mi' niŋ bʋn bama yinne, yanam on yɛlimim, ka m na yɔɔ lɛbis.”

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la lɛbis ye, “Fʋ pʋ filim bɛɛ muki tii. Fʋ mɛ pʋ di'e si'eli yi sɔ' nu'uginɛɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbisi yɛli ba ye, “Zugsɔb la nɛ onɛ ka o gaŋ ye o an na'ab la di kasɛt zina, ye ya pʋ nyɛ man tʋm taal si'aa.” Ka nidib la lɛbis ye, “O sid di kasɛt.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel yʋ'ʋn yɛl nidib la ye, “Li anɛ Zugsɔb la da gaŋ Moses nɛ Aaron n yisi ya yaanam la Egipt teŋin.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Nannanna yʋ'ʋsɛɛ, zi'enimi kpɛla bɔzugɔ m bɔɔd ye m bu'osi ya nɛ Zugsɔb la tuon, zaŋi wa'ae tʋʋm sʋma banɛ ka o tʋm tisi ya yaanam la.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Jakob n da kpɛn' Egipt n naae la, ba da kaasi tis Zugsɔb la bɔɔd sʋŋir, ka Zugsɔb la tʋm Moses nɛ Aaron, banɛ da mɔri ya yaanam la yii paae kpɛla na ka ba zin'in la.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Amaa ba da tam Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba Wina'am la; ka o basi ba ka Sisera onɛ an Hazo zabzabidib tuongat la, nɛ Filistia dim nɛ Moab na'ab la wʋsa mɛ zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Ka ba kaasi tis Zugsɔb la, ka yɛl ye, ‘Ti tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd; ti zan'as Zugsɔb la ka dɔl Baal nɛ Asitoref banɛ an bada la. Amaa faanmi ti nannanna yii ti dataas la nu'usin ka ti na dɔllif.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da tʋm Jerubaal, nɛ Barak, nɛ Jefita nɛ Samuel n faaɛn ya yii ya dataas banɛ giligi ya la wʋsa nu'usin, ka ya na zin' ka dabiem kae.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Amaa yanamɛ da nyɛ Nahas Ammon dim na'ab ka o bɔɔd ye o tʋ'ʋsi ya nɛ zaba la, ya da yɛlim ye, ‘Ayei, ti bɔɔdi sɔ' ye o aan ti na'ab,’ la'an nɛ Zugsɔb Wina'am da aan ya na'ab la.

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Na'ab kanɛ ka ya gaŋ la nwa', onɛ ka yanam mɛŋ sɔs ye ya bɔɔd la, gɔsimi, Zugsɔb la sid gaŋ na'ab ye o guri ya.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Ya ya'a gi'igid Zugsɔb la, ka dɔl o, ka siakid o nɔɔr, ka pʋ ki'isid o zi'ela la; ka yanam nɛ ya na'ab la siaki dɔl Zugsɔb Wina'am, li na an sʋm tisi ya!

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a ki'isid o zi'ela la, o sʋnf na duoe nɛ ya wʋʋ ya yaanam la.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Nannanna aaɛn baanlimm, ka gɔsi Zugsɔb la ye o tʋm tʋʋm tita'asieba ka ya nini nyɛ!

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Ka' ki bunib saŋa nwaa? M na sɔs Zugsɔb la ka o kɛ ka satansʋg nɛ saa kena. Ka ya baŋ lin an bɛ'ɛd si'em yanamɛ daa yɛl Zugsɔb la ye ya bɔɔd na'ab la.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel sid da sɔs Zugsɔb la, ka daakan nɔɔ ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka satansʋg nɛ saa kena. Ka nidib la wʋsa pin'ili zɔt Zugsɔb la nɛ Samuel dabiem.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Nidib la wʋsa da yɛl Samuel ye, “Sɔsim Zugsɔb Wina'am la tis tinam banɛ aan fʋ yammis la ka ti da kpii. Bɔzugɔ ti zaŋ tinamɛ bɔɔd na'ab ka li an bɛ'ɛd la pɛ'ɛs bɛ'ɛd kanɛ pʋn bɛɛ ti ni la.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Samuel lɛbisi yɛli ba ye, “Da zɔti dabiem! Ya sid tʋm bɛ'ɛd kaŋa wʋsa; la'an nɛ wala da fɛndigi ka basi Zugsɔb la, amaa dɔlli nɛ o nɛ ya sʋnf wʋsa.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Da dɔlli bada banɛ ka' gbin la. Ba kʋ nyaŋi sʋŋi ya bɛɛ faaɛn ya, bɔzugɔ ba ka' gban'arɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋsʋŋ la zug, o kʋ kadi yaa basɛ, bɔzugɔ li malis o hali on kɛ ka ya lieb o mɛŋ nidib la.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim mam, win na yis, li na an yɛl kisʋg m ya'a zan'as ye m kʋ sɔs Zugsɔb la tisi ya. M mɛ na pa'ali ya linɛ an sʋm ka nar.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Amaa gu'usimi ka zɔɔe Zugsɔb la dabiem ka dɔlli nɛ o nɛ sida nɛ ya sʋnf wʋsa. Tɛn'ɛsimi tʋʋm sʋma banɛ ka o tʋm tisi ya la.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a zan'as ka nan tʋm linɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm, o na uus yanam nɛ ya na'ab la wʋsa lɔbi bas.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Israel dim wʋsa daa sid wʋm labaar la ye, “Saul tʋ'ʋsi zab nɛ Filistia dim bi'ela banɛ gur Geba la, ka nannanna ba sʋnf yʋ'ʋn duonɛ nɛ Israel.” Ba da la'as nidib la ye ba keŋ Saul san'an Gilgal teŋin.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Israel dap la da nyɛ ka zaba la mu'oe ka ba piridi ba soogianam la, ba da su'a tampinlɛma nɛ tʋtʋga ni nɛ bʋmbu'adin nɛ bulis pʋʋgin.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Hibiru dim sieba da lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan keŋ Gad nɛ Gilead tɛɛnsin. Saul da kpɛlim Gilgal, ka zabzabidib banɛ kpɛlim nɛ o la wʋsa kirid nɛ dabiem.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: O da kpɛlim ani daba ayɔpɔi, nwɛnɛ Samuel n zi'el si'em la, amaa Samuel da pʋ kɛn Gilgal na. Ka Saul nidib la yʋ'ʋn pin'ili widigid.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “Mɔri nyu'or maana nɛ taaba la'asʋg maana la na.” Ka Saul da maal malʋŋ kanɛ nyu'od la.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: On naae malʋŋ la ka Samuel mɛ paad, ka Saul yi ye o pʋ'ʋs o.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Ka Samuel bu'os o ye, “Fʋ bɔɔ wala?” Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Nidib la pin'ili widigidnɛ ka fʋ mɛ nam pʋ paae na wʋʋ fʋn daa zi'el saŋa la si'em la, ka Filistia dim la pin'ili la'asid Mikmas,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: ka mam zɔ ye Filistia dim la na paae na ka ti nam pʋ ie Zugsɔb la sʋŋirɛ. Linɛ kɛ ka li lieb tilasi tisim ye m maal maan la.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbis o ye, “Fʋ tʋm nɛ nwɛnɛ zɔlʋg nɛ! Bɔzugɔ, fʋ pʋ dɔl zi'elkanɛ ka fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am tisif la. Fʋ ya'a siakin zi'elʋg la fʋ naan sʋ'oe Israel yʋma dinɛ ka' bɛnnɛ,

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: amaa nannanna fʋ sʋ'ʋlim la kʋ maligim zi'enɛ; Zugsɔb la pʋn bɔ dau kanɛ ka o mɛŋ sʋnf bɔɔd ka gaŋ o ye o gaad o nidib la tuon, bɔzugɔ fʋ pʋ siaki dɔl Zugsɔb la zi'elʋgɔ.”

translation_verse: Samuel da bas Gilgal ka keŋ Gibea Benjamin sʋ'ʋlim la ni. Israel zaba la'ad pansig ya Ka Saul kaal dap banɛ bɛɛ o san'an la ka ba daa kpɛlim kɔbisyuobʋ.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Saul nɛ o biig Jonatan nɛ nimbanɛ da bɛɛ o san'an la wʋsa da zin'inɛ Geba linɛ kpi'e Gibea ka bɛ Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin la, ka Filistia dim la la'as Mikmas.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Ba da pʋ nyɛ baa nid yinne Israel pʋʋgin onɛ mi' kʋdubɔ. Bɔzugɔ Filistia dim la yɛl ye, “Ya'a ka' ala Israel dim la na maal sʋ'ʋs nɛ kpana!”

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Niigi kʋʋnr nɛ kʋnmɛŋa saasʋg da anɛ wʋʋ fʋn na pʋdigi ba la'af zin'isa atan' ka yis zin'is ayi' la yɔ, ka zin'ig yinne mɛ saasid kpana nɛ liemis nɛ gɔn'ɔg.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Alazug zaba la daare da paae la, Saul nɛ Jonatan soogianam la wʋsa sɔ' da pʋ mɔr zaba lauk o nu'uginɛ. Saul nɛ o biig Jonatan ma'aa da mɔr.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa Filistia dim la sieba yina keŋ suor linɛ dʋt kʋkʋna la paae Mikmas baba la zin' gur.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Tampiing yinne la da bɛnɛ ya-datiuŋʋ lɛbid Mikmas baba ka yinne bɛ ya-dagɔbʋgʋ lɛbid Geba baba.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Jonatan yɛl dasaŋ kanɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la ye, “Kem na ka ti keŋ yu'okɔn la san'an, ka daasi'erɛɛ Zugsɔb la na zabi tisi ti. Zugsɔb la ya'a gban'e ye o faaɛn o nidib la, si'el kae na geŋ o, baa ba an bɛdegʋ bɛɛ bi'ela.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Tʋmmi fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛre gban'e si'em wʋsa. Kem tuon ka m dɔl nɛ m sʋnf nɛ m paŋ wʋsa.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan lɛbis ye, “Alaa kem na ka ti lɔ'ɔŋi keŋ Filistia dap la san'an ka ba nyɛɛ ti.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Ba ya'a yɛli ti ye, ‘Zi'enimi yanamɛ bɛ si'el la ka ti kɛɛn ya san'an na,’ ti na zi'en ka kʋ keŋi ba san'anɛ.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Amaa ba ya'a yɛl ye, ‘Kemini ti san'an na,’ ti na keŋ, bɔzugɔ li anɛ zanbinnɛ pa'an ye Zugsɔb la nyaŋi baa tisi ti.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Ka ba tans Jonatan nɛ onɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la ye, “Kemi kpɛla na, ka ti pa'ali ya ya'am!” Jonatan da yɛl onɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la ye, “M ya'a dʋt, fʋn dɔllim; ka Zugsɔb la nyaŋi ba tis Israel.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan pin'ili dʋt zuokanɛ ka ba bɛɛ li zug la, igin nɛ nu'ug nɛ nɔba, ka o zaba la'aziid la dɔl o. Ka Filistia soogianam la lut Jonatan tuon, ka o la'aziid la kʋʋdi dɔl.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: nidib la ya'a diin dibanɛ ka ba dataas zɔ ka bas la, li naan aan wala? Waii! Ba naan kʋʋn Filistia dim la hali ka li gaad ala.”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Saul da la'as dap la wʋsa ka ba keŋ zaba la. Ba da nyɛ ka Filistia dim la zunnim ka kʋʋd taaba nɛ ba sʋ'ʋs.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Dabiem da kpɛn' soogia banɛ da bɛɛ ba la'asʋg zin'igin la nɛ banɛ bɛ yiŋ la nɛ banɛ gur la, hali nɛ banɛ yii keŋ ye ba zab la wʋsa. Ka teŋ la dam. Wina'am da kɛ ka dabiekaŋa kpɛn' ba.

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Saul n da nan kpɛm bɛ Gibea Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin la, ka daa pʋn kɛ ka ninsieba zi'e guri, ka ba gɔsi nyɛ ka soogianam la widigi zɔt yɔɔg-yɔɔg.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛl o nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la ye, “Gi'elim gɔsi ye anɔ'ɔnɛ kae kpɛla.” Ba da gi'eli nyɛ ka Jonatan nɛ onɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la kae.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Saul n da nam bɛɛ ni pian'adi tisid maanmaan kpɛɛm la, ba da wʋm Filistia dim la dammir nɛ tʋkpiidʋg la maligim ɔnsigid. Ka Saul yɛl maanmaan kpɛɛm la ye, “Ayei, kʋdim kɛl sa!”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hibiru dim banɛ da sʋŋid Filistia dim la da tiaki ba ya'am ka pin'ili zabidi sʋŋid Saul nɛ Jonatan.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Israel dim banɛ da su'a Efiram linɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la da wʋm ye Filistia dim bɛnɛ zɔɔgin la, ba da yina la'as taaba ku'ugi kpɛn' zaba la ni tʋʋlig-tʋʋlig.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Li da wʋm Israel dim dap daakan hali, bɔzugɔ Saul da pɔnɛ, ye sɔ' da di si'ela. Ye nɔpɔɔr bɛ onɛ lɛm si'el ka winnig nyaan lu, asɛɛ ka on ti nyaŋ o dataas la. Dinzug soogia sɔ' da pʋ lɛm si'ela.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Ban da tɔlis tuon la, ba nyɛ siindi yuodi yit tiyɔkin na, amaa ba sɔ' da pʋ tin'e niŋ o nɔɔrinɛ, Saul nɔpɔɔr la zugʋ kɛ ka ba zɔ dabiem.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Amaa Jonatan da pʋ wʋm ye o saam Saul pɔ ye sɔ' da lɛm si'ela, ka zaŋ balakanɛ ka o zanl la tʋm siindin la yisi niŋ o nɔɔrin ka o nini nie.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Ka soogianam la yinne yɛl o ye, “Fʋ saam pɔnɛ nɔɔrɛ zi'el ye, ‘Onɛ wʋsa di si'el zina, nɔpɔɔr bɛɛ o zug.’ Linɛ kɛ ka li wʋm nidib la ka ba tadig hali la.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan lɛbis ye, “M saam bɔ yɛlli tisi ti teŋgbauŋ la. Man lɛm siind la ka m nini yʋ'ʋn pilig nyain si'em la,

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Daakan la Israel dim la da kʋ Filistia dim la yi Mikmas hali ti paae Aijalon teŋin la, ba da gɛnnɛ.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Ba da faaɛn pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi nɛ na'abibisi kʋʋ ba yɔɔg-yɔɔg n ɔnbid nɛ ziim la wʋsa.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Sɔ' da yʋ'ʋn yɛl Saul ye, “Gɔsima nidib la tʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon! Ba ɔnbidi ni'im kanɛ nam mɔr ziim.” Ka Saul yɛl ye, “Ya san'am zi'elʋg la! Biligim kugtita'ar tɔ'ɔtɔ digil kpɛla na.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Ka ye, “Kem nidibin la yɛli ba ye, ‘Sɔ' wʋsa mɔr o naaf bɛɛ pɛ'og naa kʋ kpɛla ɔnb. Da ɔnbi ni'im linɛ ka li ziim nam pʋ yuoe, ka li kɛ ka ya tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la san'anɛ. Lin zugɔ sɔ' wʋsa da mɔr o bʋnkɔnbʋg yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ keŋ kʋʋ ani.’”

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Saul da mɛ' maan bimbimi tis Zugsɔb la anina. O da nan zi' mɛɛ li buudii, o yiiga bimbimi la.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Saul ye, “Kɛlli ka ti kadi Filistia dim la yʋ'ʋŋa kʋʋ ba wʋsa ka da bas baa nid yinne ka o tiligɛ.” Ka ba lɛbis o ye, “Maalim linɛ na an sʋm tisif.” Amaa maanmaan kpɛɛm da ye, “Kɛl ka ti bu'os Zugsɔb la kpɛla.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Alazug Saul da bu'os Wina'am, ye, “M zɔm dɔl Filistia dim la gbine kʋʋ? Fʋ na sʋŋ ka ti nyaŋi baa?” Amaa Zugsɔb la da pʋ lɛbis si'el daakanɛ.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Saul da lɛn yɛl ye, “Yanam banɛ an kpɛɛmnam nɛ soogianam la wʋsa la'asimi na, ka ti gɔs ye tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɔ ka ti tʋm zina?

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ vʋe ka faaɛn Israel dim la yʋ'ʋr zug, onɛ tʋm taal nwa', asɛɛ o kpi; baa li ya'a anɛ man biig Jonatan n tʋmi li.” Amaa nidib la sɔ' da pʋ ya'ae nɔɔrɛ.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Saul da yɛl Israel dim la wʋsa ye, “Yanam zi'enim kpɛ'ɛsa ka mam nɛ Jonatan mɛ zi'en kpɛla.” Ka nidib lɛbis ye, “Maalim linɛ na an sʋm tisif.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Saul daa sɔs Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la, ye, “Gandigim tisim nyain!” Ka ba maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm ka li gaŋ Saul nɛ Jonatan ka kɛ nidib la.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛl ye, “Bʋgʋlimi mam nɛ Jonatan onɛ aan m biig la!” Ka li gaŋ Jonatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛl Jonatan ye, “Yɛlimim fʋn tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛsi'a.” Ka Jonatan lɛbis o ye, “Man zaŋi m balaari tin'e siind bi'ela lɛm la siak mam na kpii?”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Saul yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la kɛl ka tɔɔg paae man bɛdegʋ, fʋn Jonatan ya'a pʋ kpii.”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Amaa nidib la yɛl Saul ye, “Jonatan ka' onɛ na kpii, ka' onɛ zi yɔlisim tita'ari kɛn Israel la naa? Ayei! Zugsɔb onɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zugɔ, hali o zuobʋg baa yinne kʋ li teŋa, bɔzugɔ on tʋm si'el wʋsa zina la, li anɛ Wina'am sʋŋir.” Ka nidib la da faaɛn Jonatan ka o pʋ kpii.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Ka Saul bas ka pʋ lɛn kad Filistia dim la, ka ba wʋsa lɛbi ba teŋin.

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: O da zab nɛ hali nɛ kpi'euŋʋ nyaŋ Amalek dim la banɛ da wɛbigidi ba la, ka faaɛn Israel dim la ba nu'usin. Saul yidim yɛla

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Saul na'am saŋa la wʋsa da anɛ zaba ban nɛ Filistia dim la. Ka Saul ya'a da baŋ ye sɔ' mɔr paŋ ka o sʋnf mɛ kpi'em, o zaŋid o nɛ ka o lieb zabzabid.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Ka Samuel yɛl Saul ye, “Man ka Zugsɔb la daa tʋm ka m kena bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋif ka fʋ lieb na'ab ka gaad o nidib Israel dim la tuon; dinzugɔ kɛlisim dinɛ yit Zugsɔb la san'an nannanna.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Onɛ an Paŋ Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa', ‘M na tɛɛg Amalek dim la tʋbir ban da tʋm Israel dim tʋʋm si'a ka la'am gu' ba ban da yi Egipt teŋin na la.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Nannanna kem tʋ'ʋs Amalek dim la ka san'am bam mɔr la'asi'a wʋsa. Kʋʋm dap nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis nɛ bilies nɛ niigi nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ yʋgʋma nɛ bʋmis wʋsa.’”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Alazug, Saul da buol dap la la'asi ba Telaim soogianam tusa kɔbisyi' nɛ soogianam tusa piiga banɛ yi Juda na.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da pian' tis Samuel ye,

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Saul da keŋ paae Amalek teŋin kɛ ka ninsieba keŋ gilig teŋ la su'a bɔn'ɔgin sa.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Ka o da yɛl Keen dim la ye, “Yimi kpɛla; basimi Amalek dim la gʋllim ka m da ti kpanbi san'am yanam nɛ banɛ. Bɔzugɔ yanam da pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛdi tis Israel dim la ban da yi Egipt teŋin na la.” Keen dim la sid da yi teŋin la ka bas Amalek dim la.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ka Saul tʋ'ʋs Amalek dim la nɛ zaba lin pin'il Havila ken paae Sur lɛbisid ya-nya'aŋ Egipt baba.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Amaa Saul nɛ o soogianam la da pʋ kʋ na'ab la nɛ bʋnkɔnbsʋma laa, ba mɛ da pʋ siak ye ba san'am linɛ an la'asʋma la wʋsaa. Amaa linɛ wʋsa da ka' sʋ'ʋm ka mɛ pʋ nie nif la ma'aa ka ba da san'am.

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “M sʋnf san'amnɛ man kɛ ka Saul di na'am la, bɔzugɔ o tiaki tʋm nɛ on mi' si'el ka ka' mam Zugsɔb la pa'al o ye o niŋ si'em laa.” Li da daam Samuel, ka o kum yʋ'ʋŋ kan wʋsa.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Bɛkɛung asuba Samuel da isigi keŋ Saul san'an, amaa ba da yɛl o ye Saul keŋ Kaamel. Anina ka o kpi'e kugwɔkʋ zi'el ye li an yʋ'ʋri tis o, ka gaadi keŋ sig Gilgal.

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Samuel n da keŋ paae nyɛ Saul la, ka Saul yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la na niŋi fʋ zug bareka! M tʋm Zugsɔb la yɛl ye m tʋm si'el la wʋsa.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Amaa Samuel lɛbis o ye, “Ka pɛbama yi yaanɛ kaasidi m tʋba ni? Bɛɛ bʋʋn nwɛnɛ niigi m tʋba ni?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Soogianam la gban'e ba yi Amalek dimin la na; bʋnkɔnbid banɛ ka ba gaans bʋnsʋma ye ba maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la, amaa ti san'am banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbis o ye, “Kɛl ala! Kɛl ka m yɛlif Zugsɔb la sa yɛlim si'el yʋ'ʋŋ.” Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “O sa yɛlif ye bɔ?”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel yɛl o ye, “Zugsɔb la da diisif Israel na'ab la'an nɛ fʋn da gɔsi fʋ mɛŋ ye fʋ ka' sɔ' la. Fʋ da pʋ lieb Israel buudi la wʋsa tuongataa?

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: Ka o tʋmif ye fʋ keŋ tʋm tʋʋm si'a ka yɛlif ye, ‘Kem san'am Amalek dim banɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la wʋsa; zam nɛ ba hali nɛ fʋn na ti nyaŋi kʋʋ ba wʋsa.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Tɔ'! Ka wala ka fʋ pʋ tʋm nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛlif si'em la? Wala ka fʋ zɔ tɔ'ɔtɔ faaɛn la'ad la ka tʋm linɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm Zugsɔb la tuonnɛ?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Saul lɛbis ye, “Amaa man siak Zugsɔb la nɔɔr. M keŋ Zugsɔb la titʋmis la. M kʋ Amalek dim la ka gban'e ba na'ab Agag n mɔri kena.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Soogianam la nɔk pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi banɛ ka ba faaɛn la, gaans bʋnsʋma la ye ba nɔki ba maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la Gilgal teŋin.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Amaa Samuel lɛbis o ye, “Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye Zugsɔb sʋnf malis nɛ nyu'or maana nɛ maan banɛ wʋsa bɛɛ gaad fʋn na siak o nɔɔrɛɛ? Siakir gat maan, ka onɛ tʋbiri wʋm gat pɛrabanɛ mɔr kpaam.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Ki'isʋg anɛ bɛ'ɛd wʋʋ ba'ad bʋgʋb nɛ, ka tita'alim an bɛ'ɛd wʋʋ teŋgbana maalʋg nɛ. Ka fʋn zan'as Zugsɔb la pian'ad la zugɔɔ, o mɛ zan'as ye fʋ kʋ lɛn an na'aba.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Ka Saul yʋ'ʋn yɛl Samuel ye, “Alaa m tʋm taal, man ki'is Zugsɔb la zi'elʋg nɛ fʋ pa'ala la. M daa zɔti nidib la dabiem ka gʋ'ʋŋi siaki tisi ba.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nannanna, m bɛlimnɛ, kɛlli m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd taali bas ka dɔllim ka ti lɛbi dʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr.”

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Amaa Samuel lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Mam kʋ dɔlli fʋ lɛbɛ. Fʋ zan'as Zugsɔb la nɔɔr ka o mɛ zan'asif ye fʋ kʋ lɛn an Israel dim na'aba!”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Samuel n fɛndig ye o keŋ ka bas o la, ka Saul gban'e o fuug nɔɔr ka li aaɛn.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Samuel yɛl o ye, “Tɔ'! Zugsɔb la aaɛn Israel sʋ'ʋlim la yii fʋ san'an zina zaŋi tisi fʋ tiraan onɛ an sʋm gatif.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Wina'am onɛ an Israel dim girima la pʋ ma'ad bɛɛ tiakid o pʋtɛn'ɛrɛ; bɔzugɔ o ka' ninsaal ka na tiak o pʋtɛn'ɛrɛ.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “M sid tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. Amaa tisimim girima m nidib la kpɛɛmnam nɛ Israel dim la wʋsa tuon. Maalim suguru ka dɔllim ka ti lɛb ka m dʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Samuel da dɔl Saul n lɛb ka o dʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Ka Samuel yɛl ye, “Yisim Agag onɛ an Amalek dim na'ab la na!” Agag da yina nɛ sʋnkpi'euŋʋ, tɛn'ɛsid ye bi'esʋg kae, ba kʋ lɛn kʋʋ o ya'asɛ.

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Amaa Samuel yɛl ye, “Fʋ zaba sʋ'ʋgʋ sadigim daa kɛ ka bimanam kpɛlim zaalim la, ala mɛn ka fʋ ma mɛ ye o kpɛlim zaalim o pu'a taaba sʋʋgin ka ka' biiga.” Ka Samuel kʋ Agag Zugsɔb la tuon Gilgal teŋin ka kie o zɔra-zɔra.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel nyaan yii ani keŋ Rama, amaa Saul da lɛb o yin, Gibea linɛ an o mɛŋ teŋ.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Hali nɛ Samuel nyɔvʋr bɛn wʋsa, o pʋ lɛn keŋ nyɛ Saul ya'asɛ, la'an nɛ Samuel n da kum o yɛla la. Ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf san'amnɛ on kɛ ka Saul lieb Israel na'ab la.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl Samuel ye, “Fʋ ye fʋ nɔk saŋa wala kummi tisid Saul kanɛ ka mam pʋn zan'as ye o kʋ an Israel dim na'ab la? Liem kpaam pɛ'ɛli fʋ iil la ka duoe gban'e suor, ka m ye m tʋmif nɛ Jese onɛ bɛ Betilehem la yin. M gaŋ o biis la yinne ye o di na'am.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbis ye, “M ye m niŋ wala keŋɛ? Saul ya'a wʋm ala, o na kʋʋm.” Ka Zugsɔb la ye, “Nɔkim na'asa'a keŋ ka yɛl ye, ‘M kennɛ na ye m maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la.’

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Buolim Jese ka o kɛn malʋŋ la ye di maal zin'isi'a la na, ka m na pa'alif fʋn na niŋ si'em. Fʋ na nɔk malʋŋ kpaam la bu'oe niŋ onɛ wʋsa ka m pa'alif la zug.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Samuel da tʋm nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. On da paae Betilehem la, bʋnkʋd la da tʋ'ʋs o nɛ ka kirid. Ba da bu'os o ye, “Fʋ kɛn nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm naa?”
