english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, li anɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm ken; m kennɛ na ye m maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la. Maalimi ya mɛŋ nyain ka kɛn maannin la na.” Ka o maal Jese nɛ o biis la nyain ka ba zemis nɛ ban na keŋ maannin la; ka yʋ'ʋn kaanbi ba.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: Ban da paae la, Samuel da nyɛ Eliab ka tɛn'ɛs o sʋnfʋn ye, bi'esʋg kae, onɛ ka Zugsɔb la gaŋ la zi'e o tuon la.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la yɛl Samuel ye, “Da gi'en o niŋgbiŋ nɛ o wa'alim laa, ka mam zan'as o nɛ. Zugsɔb la pʋ gɔt ninsaali gɔt si'el la. Ninsaal gɔtnɛ yiŋ vɛnlim, amaa Zugsɔb la gɔtnɛ sʋʋnr.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ka Jese buol Abinadab. Ka o kena gaad Samuel tuon, amaa ka Samuel yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la mɛ pʋ gaŋ oŋa.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Ka Jese lɛn kɛ ka Siama kena gaad Samuel tuon, amaa Samuel yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la mɛ pʋ gaŋ oŋa.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Jese da kɛ ka o biis ayɔpɔi kena gaad Samuel tuon. Amaa ka Samuel yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la mɛ pʋ gaŋ bama.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os Jese ye, “Fʋ biis wʋsa nwaa?” Ka Jese lɛbis o ye, “Kpaanr la kpɛlim, amaa on kemnɛ kɔnbid.” Ka Samuel yɛl o ye o tʋm ka ba keŋ buol o na. Ka ye, “Ti kʋ zin'inɛ asɛɛ o ti paae na.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Ka o sid tʋm ka ba keŋ buol o na. O da anɛ na'akimbil vɛnliŋ ka o nini an wisi, ka mɔr laafi sʋ'ʋŋa, ka o zi'esim mɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa. Ka Zugsɔb la ye, “Duom nɔk kpaam la bu'oe niŋ o zugin ka onɛ la.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Ka Samuel nɔk iil la nɛ malʋŋ kpaam la bu'oe niŋ o zugin, o bieya la tuon. Ka lin da pin'il daakan la, Zugsɔb la Siig la da sig o zugin na nɛ paŋ. Ka Samuel nyaan lɛb Rama. David tʋmmi tisid Saul

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa Zugsɔb la Siig la da yi ka bas Saul, ka sibɛ'ɛd yi Zugsɔb la san'an na daamid o.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Saul tʋmtʋmnib la da yɛl o ye, “Gɔsima sibɛ'ɛd yi Zugsɔb la ni na daamidif.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Ti zugsɔba, kɛl ka tinam banɛ aan fʋ yammis la ie onɛ na nyaŋi nwɛ' kɔn na. O na nwɛ' saŋkanɛ wʋsa ka sibɛ'ɛdnam la ti naam Zugsɔb la san'anɛ kena, ka li kɛ ka fʋ paam yɔlisim.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul da yɛli ba ye, ba ieem onɛ mi' nwɛ'ɛb sʋ'ʋŋa dɔl o na.

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Yammis la yinne da lɛbis ye, “Mam mi' Jese onɛ yi Betilehem la biig onɛ mi' kɔn nwɛ'ɛb. O anɛ sʋnkpi'euŋ sɔb, ka mɛ lɛn an zabzabid. O mi' pian'ad sʋ'ʋŋa ka mɛ vɛnl, ka Zugsɔb la bɛɛ o ni.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Saul da tʋm nidib Jese san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Kɛl ka fʋ biig onɛ kem kɔnbid la kɛɛn m san'an na.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Jese da nɔknɛ bʋŋ ka lɔ diib, nɛ daam nɛ gan'ar, ka gban'e bʋpɔlli mɔri ba nɛ o biig David n keŋ Saul san'an.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: David da kena paas banɛ tʋmmi tisid Saul la. Saul da nɔŋ o yɛla hali, ka David paas banɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la nid yinne.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul tʋm yɛl Jese ye, “Kɛl ka David kpɛlimmi m yin kpɛla liebi m tʋmtʋmnib la yinne, ka m sʋnf malis o yɛla.”

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ wʋsa ka siig la yi Wina'am san'anɛ sig Saul ni na, David nɔkidnɛ kɔn la nwɛ', hali ka Saul ti nyɛɛ o mɛŋ ka paam laafi ka sibɛ'ɛd la yi ka bas o.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa Filistia dim la da la'as zabzabidib Soko linɛ bɛ Juda teŋin la ye ba zab. Ban da la'asi naae la ba da keŋ digin Efes-Damim, ka li anɛ teŋ kanɛ bɛ Soko nɛ Azeka teŋsʋk.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da la'as nɛ kʋkʋn zug, ka Israel dim mɛ bɛ kʋkʋn yinne zug ka bɔn'ɔg yʋ'ʋn bɛɛ ba teŋsʋk.

english_verse: The Philistine army had a hero named Goliath who was from the town of Gath and was about three meters tall.
translation_verse: Filistia dau sɔ' da yi Gaf teŋin na ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Goliyaf. O da anɛ ba zaba gandaug, ka o wa'alim gat ninsaali nar ye o wa'am si'em.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: Ba da zan'anɛ kʋntzɛn'ug la maal wʋʋ ta'ada ka o pid ka sieba mɛ ligil o gbɛya. Ka o kpan da ya'ae o nya'aŋ ka mɛ an kʋntzɛn'ug.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: David n da kʋ Filistia nid la naae ka lɛb na la, ka Abner dɔl o kɛn Saul san'an na ka David nan zanl Filistia dau la zug.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: O kpandaug la da wa'am nɛ hali, ka li kpanbiel la tɛbisim an kʋnt gbila kɔbisyuobʋ. Ka onɛ ziid o gbanti'edʋg la bɛɛ o tuon.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Goliyaf da duoe zi'en ka tansi tʋ Israel dim la ye, “Bɔ ka ya yina zi'e tuunl taaba ye ya zabɛ? Mam ka'anɛ Filistia nid ka yanam mɛ an Saul yammisɛ? Gaŋimi dau yinne ka o kɛɛn m san'an na.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: O ya'a nyaŋi zabi kʋ mam, ti na liebi ya yammis; amaa mam mɛ ya'a nyaŋi kʋʋ o, yanam mɛ na liebi ti yammis ka tʋmmi tisidi ti.”

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Filistia dau la da lɛn yɛl ye, “Nannanna mam gban'e ye m zab nɛ Israel dim gandaug. Gaŋimi sɔ' ka mam nɛ on tʋ'ʋs taaba.”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Ban wʋm Filistia dau la pian'ad la, dabiem da kpɛn' banɛ hali ka ba sʋnf san'am.

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: David da anɛ Jese onɛ an Efirata nid la biig, ka da yi Juda, Betilehem sʋ'ʋlim. Jese da mɔr biribis anii. Saul saŋa la o da anɛ ninkʋdʋg ka di yʋma bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: Amaa David da ɛɛn kennɛ Saul san'an ka lɛbid yinne gur o saam kɔnbid Betilehem teŋin

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Bɛogʋn nɛ zaam wʋsa Filistia dau la da ɛɛn yinɛ na zi'en ka pian' o ya'amin, hali ti paae dabisa pisnaasi daar.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: O da nɔk o balaar, ka yii sig kɔlʋgin pi'is kugsaliba anu su o kɔnbkem buorigin la, ka zanl o luobigi gaad ye o tʋ'ʋs Filistia dau la.

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Jese da yɛl David ye, “Nɔkim kawɛnsɛn'ɛda nɛ bodobodo gbila piiga paasi keŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ tisi fʋ bieya la ban la'as zin'isi'a la.

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: Nɔkim waagazi nam nwa' piiga pɛ'ɛsi keŋ tisi ba kpɛɛm la. Kem gɔsi ba ka lɛb na ka m wʋmi ba labaar.

english_verse: They're with Saul's army, fighting the Philistines in Elah Valley.”
translation_verse: Ban nɛ Israel dim la wʋsa bɛ Saul san'an Ela bɔn'ɔgin la zabid nɛ Filistia dim la.”

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la, ka David dɛŋi isigi gu'ul kɔnbid la nɛ kɔnbkem yinne, ka lɔ la'ad la nwɛnɛ Jese pa'al o si'em la. O da keŋ paae bam bɛ zin'isi'a la ka soogianam la mɛ maal siri yit ye ba keŋ zaba zin'igin la, ka pɔɔd zaba pɔɔr.

english_verse: The army of Israel and the Philistine army stood there facing each other.
translation_verse: Israel dim la nɛ Filistia dim la da tuunl fɔɔli ka zi'enɛ kpa' taaba.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: David da bas la'ad la tis soogianam la la'agur la ka zɔɔ keŋ zaba zin'igin la pʋ'ʋs o bieya la.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: On da nam pian'ad nɛ ba la, ka Goliyaf onɛ an Filistia dim gandaug la ya'an yina tʋ'ʋd Israel dim la, ka David wʋm.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da nyɛ dau la, ba wʋsa da zɔɔ lɛb nya'aŋ nɛ dabiem

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl ye, “Ya nyɛ dau kaŋa yit daar wʋsa si'em laa? Ala ka o tʋ'ʋdi ti daar wʋsa bɔɔdi ti nɔɔrin. Na'ab la yɛl ye o na tis onɛ nyaŋi kʋ dau la kpan'am, ka na lɛn nɔk o pu'ayua tis o sɔba ka o di. Ka on sɔb yidim wʋsa kʋ lɛn yɔ lampɔɔ.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: David da bu'os dap banɛ zi'e kpi'e nɛ o la ye, “Ba ye bɔ ka ba na nɔki tis onɛ nyaŋi kʋ Filistia dau nwa' ka yis Israel dim nyan kaŋa pʋʋginɛ? Filistia dau kaŋa aan anɔ'ɔnɛ, mɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋʋ ka tɛn'ɛs ye o na nyaŋi zab nɛ Wina'am kanɛ vʋe la soogianama?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Ba da tuunsi tis o ban pʋn yɛt si'em la ye, “Nɛ' ka ba na nɔki tis onɛ wʋsa nyaŋi kʋʋ o.”

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Eliab onɛ an David bier kpɛɛm la da wʋm ka o pian'ad nɛ dap la, o sʋnf da duonɛ nɛ o hali ka o bu'os o ye, “Bɔzug ka fʋ kɛn kpɛla na? Ka anɔ'ɔn ka fʋ nɔk kɔnbid banɛ an bi'ela la gu'ul sian'arin la? Mam mi' fʋ pa'alim-mɛŋ nɛ fʋ sʋnkpi'euŋʋ an si'em. Fʋ kʋdim kennɛ na ye fʋ gɔs zaba la!”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbis ye, “M maal bɔ? M la'am da ya'ae m nɔɔrɛɛ?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn fɛndigi lɛb sɔ' san'an ya'asi lɛm pian' pian'akan nɔɔ, ka dap la lɛbisi yɛl o wʋʋ bam pʋn yɛl o si'em la.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: David n da pian'ad si'el la, nidib da wʋmya, ka keŋ yɛl Saul, ka Saul tʋm ye ba buol o na.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: David da yɛl Saul ye, “Da kɛ ka Filistia nid la yɛla kpɛn'ɛs sɔ' dabiem; man onɛ an fʋ sankpan'as la na keŋ zab nɛ o.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul da lɛbis o ye, “Fʋ kʋ nyaŋi keŋ zab nɛ dau kaŋa; fʋ anɛ biig, amaa oŋa pʋn anɛ zabzabid o biilimin sa.”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Amaa David da yɛl Saul ye, “Mam anɛ onɛ guri m saam pɛ'ɛs. Ka saŋa kanɛ wʋsa ka gbigim bɛɛ kunduŋ kena gban'e pɛbil pɛ'ɛsin la gaadɛ,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: m ɛɛnti zɔnɛ dɔl o keŋ nwɛ' o ka kpidig pɛbil la o nɔɔrin. O ya'a zan'as ken ka fɛndig ye o zab nɛ mam, m ɛɛnti gban'e nɛ o yier baba la ka nwɛ' o kʋ.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: Man kʋ gbigima nɛ kunduna; Filistia dau kanɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋ nwa' nwɛnɛ bʋnkɔnbban yinne nɛ, bɔzugɔ o bɔɔdnɛ ye o zab nɛ Wina'am kanɛ vʋe la soogianam.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb kanɛ faaɛn mam yi gbigima nɛ kunduna nu'u-ɛɛnsin la na nyaŋi faaɛn mam yi Filistia dau kaŋa nu'usin.” Saul da yɛl David ye, “Kem ka Zugsɔb la na bɛ nɛf.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Saul da yɛɛgi o mɛŋ zaba fuugʋ yɛɛl David ka nɔk gbian'anʋ yɛɛl o, ka nɔk kʋntzɛn'ug zupibigi pid o.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: David da nɔk o sʋ'ʋgi kɔri pa'al fuug la zug, ka yʋ'ʋn duoe makid ye o keŋ giligi gɔs bɔzugɔ o pʋ miilim la'aban yɛɛbɔ. David da yɛl Saul ye, “M kʋ nyaŋi yɛ la'abama, bɔzugɔ m pʋ miilimi ba yɛɛbɔ.” Ka yɛɛsi ba digil.

english_verse: Goliath came toward David, walking behind the soldier who was carrying his shield.
translation_verse: Ka Filistia dau la kennɛ li'en David ka onɛ ziid o gbanti'edʋg la gaad o tuon.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: O da ʋk o nindaa gɔsi nyɛ David ka o an bizi'an ka vɛnl, ka o nɛ'ɛs o

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: ka bu'os o ye, “Mam anɛ baa, ka fʋ zanl balaari kennɛ m san'an naa?” Ka Filistia dau la kan'a ba teŋgbana ziil David.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o ye, “Kem kpɛla na, ka m na nɔki fʋ ni'imi tis baas nɛ zʋʋnd!”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl o ye, “Fʋ kennɛ na ye fʋ zab nɛ mam nɛ sʋ'ʋs nɛ kpana nɛ piema, amaa man tʋ'ʋsidif nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yʋ'ʋr, ka an Israel soogianam Wina'am onɛ ka fʋ pɔ'ɔgidi o yʋ'ʋr la.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Zina, Zugsɔb la na nɔki fʋ niŋi m nu'usin ka m nwɛ' fʋ digil ka fi'igi fʋ zug. Zina m na nɔk Filistia soogianam niŋgbina la tis baas nɛ zʋʋnd, ka dunia wʋsa na baŋ ye Israel dim mɔr Wina'am.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Banɛ la'as kpɛla wʋsa na baŋ ye li ka' sʋ'ʋs nɛ kpana ka Zugsɔb la zaŋidi faand o nidiba; zaba la anɛ Zugsɔb la din, ka dinzug o na nɔki ya wʋsa niŋi ti nu'usin.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Ka tʋm o buorigin la yis kugir yinne niŋ luobigin la yuulim-yuulim vɛnlig, ka kugir la keŋ nwɛ' Filistia dau la gbɛ'og ka vʋdigi kpɛn' pʋʋgin, ka o luu avanba.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: David da nyaŋ Filistia dau la nɛ luobig nɛ kugir; ka pʋ zanl sʋ'ʋgʋ o nu'uginɛ.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: David da zɔɔ keŋ zi'en o zugin ka fuoe Goliyaf mɛŋ sʋ'ʋgʋ yisi li tɛɛngʋn. On kʋʋ o la nya'aŋ, o da nɔk sʋ'ʋg la fi'ig o zug. Filistia dim la da baŋ ye ba gandaug la kpiya la, ba da fɛndigi gban'e zɔɔg.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ka Israel nɛ Juda dim da mɛ niŋi ba kadib diin ka kaasid kuŋʋ dɔlli ba hali ti paae Gaf sʋ'ʋlim ti paae Ekron yaŋirin la. Banɛ ka ba kʋʋ ba la da dig nɛ gbandaa Siaaram suorin la ti paae Gaf nɛ Ekron.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ban da kadi ba naae ka lɛb na la, ba da keŋ Filistia dim la'asʋg zin'igin la vaae ba la'ad la wʋsa.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: David da nɔk Filistia dau la zug la mɔri kɛn Jerusalem na, ka nɔk Filistia dau zaba la'ad la digil o mɛŋ sʋgʋrin.

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Saul n da gɔt David ka o yit ye o tʋ'ʋs Filistia dau la, o bu'os Abner, onɛ an soogianam la kpɛɛm la ye, “Abner, anɔ'ɔn biigi an dasaŋ kaŋa?” Ka Abner lɛbis o ye, “Naa, Na'aba, ya'a an sida mam zi'.”

english_verse: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da lɛbis ye, “Mɔɔm baŋ dasaŋ la an sɔ' biig.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul da bu'os o ye, “Dasaŋa, fʋ aan anɔ'ɔn biiga?” Ka David lɛbis ye, “Mam anɛ fʋ sankpan'as Jese onɛ yi Betilehem la biig.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Lin da yi daakan la, Saul da kɛ ka David kpɛlim o san'an ka pʋ lɛn kul o saam yin ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Jonatan da naal nɔɔr nɛ David bɔzugɔ o da nɔŋ o nɛ wʋʋ o mɛŋ nɛ.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Jonatan da yɛɛg o dansik linɛ ka o yɛ la tis David, nɛ o pʋʋgin fubil hali nɛ o sʋ'ʋg nɛ tiraug nɛ sɛnbidiŋ.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Tʋʋm kanɛ wʋsa ka Saul da ɛɛn tis David ye o tʋm, o da tʋmmi li nɛ sʋ'ʋŋa hali, linzug da kɛ ka Saul nɔk o diis o soogianam la kpɛɛm yinne. Ka li malis nidib la wʋsa, nɛ Saul mɛŋ kpɛɛmnam la gba.

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: David n da kʋ Filistia dau la naae ka nidib la lɛbid yin la, pu'ab da yi Israel tɛɛns la wʋsa ni la'as ye ba tʋ'ʋs Na'ab Saul ka yʋ'ʋm yʋʋma ka wa'ad nɛ sumalisim nɛ siyada nɛ wiis.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Ban da wa'ad la ba da yʋ'ʋm nɛ yɛt ye, “Saul kʋ nɛ tusir ka David on kʋ tusa piiga”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Saul sʋnf da san'amnɛ hali, ban da yʋ'ʋmmi pɛndigid la ka li daam Saul. Ka o yʋ'ʋn tɛn'ɛsid o sʋʋnrin ye, “Gɔsim ban dʋ'ʋsid David yʋ'ʋr ye o kʋ tusa piiga! Amaa mam kʋ nɛ tusir ma'aa. Bɔɔ yʋ'ʋn kpɛlim, li ka' on na di'e m na'am sʋ'ʋlim laa?”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la sibɛ'ɛd da yi Wina'am san'an na nɛ paŋi kpɛn' Saul. O da bɛnɛ o yinne tansid ka wa'ad wʋʋ nɔdi'es nɛ, ka David zin' nwɛ'ɛd kɔn la nwɛnɛ on ɛɛnti pʋn nwɛ'ɛd si'em la. Saul mɛ da zanl kpanni o nu'ugin.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Ka tɔn nɛ paŋ, ka tɛn'ɛsid ye, “M na vʋdig David n tabil dɔkpin.” Amaa David da nyaŋi li'iŋ nɔɔra ayi'.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Saul da zɔt David nɛ, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la da bɛ David san'an ka lɛɛ bas Saul.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: On da tʋm tʋʋm si'a wʋsa nyaŋir da bɛnɛ bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la da bɛɛ o san'an.

english_verse: But everyone else in Judah and Israel was loyal to David, because he led the army in battle.
translation_verse: Amaa Israel nɛ Juda dim wʋsa da nɔŋ o nɛ hali bɔzugɔ onɛ gati ba tuon ka ba maan si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Saul da yɛl David ye, “M bipuŋ kpɛɛm Merab nwana, m na nɔk o tisif ka fʋ di. Mɔɔm tʋm tis mam nɛ sʋnkpi'euŋ. Ka zab Zugsɔb la zaba la.” Saul da tɛn'ɛs nɛ ye, “M kʋ nɔki m nu'ugʋ si'is oo. M na kɛ ka Filistia dim la lɛɛ niŋ ala.”

english_verse: David answered, “How could I possibly marry your daughter? I'm not very important, and neither is my family.”
translation_verse: Amaa David lɛbisi yɛl Saul ye, “Ka mam aan anɔ'ɔnɛ? M yidim nɛ m saam dɔɔg nidib la wʋsa mɛ aan anɔ'ɔnam ka man ti nar ye m an na'ab diema?”

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Alazug saŋaa da paae ye ba zaŋ Saul bipuŋ Merab n tis David la, ba da zaŋ o tis Adriel onɛ yi Mehola la.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Amaa Saul bipuŋ Mikal ya'am da kpɛn' nɛ David, ka ban da yɛl Saul la, o sʋnf da ma'ae nɛ hali,

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: ka o tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “M na nɔk o tis o ka o lieb bɛndig linɛ na kɛ ka Filistia dim la kʋʋ o.” Alazug Saul da yɛl David ye, “Nannanna suor yinne lɛn yɔ'ɔg ya'asi tisif ka fʋ na nyaŋi liebi m diem.”

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛt David nɛ'ɛnam saŋa wʋsa. Amaa David da lɛbis ye, “Ya tɛn'ɛs ye li anɛ na'ana nɛ mam na lieb Na'ab diemaa? Mam anɛ nɔŋdaan ka sɔ' zi' ma.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Saul yammis la da yɛl o David n lɛbis si'em la,

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: o da yɛl ye, “Yɛlimi David ye, ‘Na'ab la pʋ bɔɔd pu'asʋlli fʋ san'anɛ. On bɔɔd si'el anɛ ye fʋ kʋ Filistia dim kɔbiga ka nwaasi ba yu'ogbana mɔr na tis o, ka li pa'al ye fʋ yɔɔ o dataas sam.’” Saul gban'ar la wʋsa da anɛ ye David kpɛn' Filistia dim la nu'usin.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Sankpan'asnam la da lɛbi yɛl David ala la, o sʋnf da ma'ae nɛ on bɔɔdi kilim Na'ab diem la zug. Saŋa da nam pʋ paae la

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Saul n da baŋ ye Zugsɔb la bɛ nɛ David, ka o bipuŋ Mikal mɛ bɔɔd David la,

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: Saul da maligim zɔɔ o nɛ dabiem hali, ka o lieb o dataa nɛ o nyɔvʋr bɛn.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Filistia soogia kpɛɛmnam la da yit nɛ saŋa wʋsa zabid, ban da ɛɛnti pɛndigid si'em la zug David da paamid nyaŋir nɛ ya'an saŋa wʋsa gat Saul kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa, ka o yʋ'ʋr tiig zin'ig wʋsa.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Saul da yɛl Jonatan nɛ banɛ tʋmmi tisid o la wʋsa ye, ba kʋʋm David. Amaa Jonatan da nɔŋ David nɛ hali.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: M na yii zi'enɛ m saam san'an paalʋ kanɛ ka fʋ su'a la baba. M na pian' fʋ yɛla tis o, ka yɛlif on yɛl si'el wʋsa.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ, o da kuos o nyɔvʋri zab nɛ Filistia dau la kʋʋ o. Zugsɔb la da di nyaŋ tita'ari tis Israel ka fʋ da nyɛɛ li ka mɔr sumalisim. Bɔzug ka fʋ na kʋ dau onɛ ka' taal wʋʋ David ka li gbin kae?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Saul da di'e Jonatan sa'alʋg la ka pɔ ye, “Nɛ Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zugɔɔ, m kʋ kɛ ka ba kʋ David ya'asɛ.”

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Jonatan da buol David ka yɛl o sɔnsig la ken naae si'em wʋsa. O da zii o kɛn Saul san'an na ka o bɛ nɛ o wʋʋ on daa pʋn bɛnɛ o si'em la.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Zaba da lɛn kɔ' ya'as ka David yii zab nɛ Filistia dim la. O da tʋ'ʋsi ba nɛ paŋ hali ka ba gʋ'ʋŋi zɔ ka bas o.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: ka Saul da bɔɔd ye o nwɛ' o nɛ kpan la tabil dɔkpin, amaa David da nyaŋi li'iŋ ka Saul nwɛ' kpan la ka li keŋ kpɛn' dɔkpinnin. Yʋ'ʋŋ kan, David da zɔnɛ su'a.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Saul da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ David yinne su'a gur ka bɛog ya'a nie ka ba kʋʋ o. Amaa Mikal, David pu'a la, da sa'al o ye, “Fʋ ya'a pʋ zɔ yʋ'ʋŋa faaɛn fʋ mɛŋa bɛog ya'a nie ba na kʋʋf.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Alazug, Mikal da yis David n tud takoro sigis ka o zɔɔ su'a.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Ka Mikal da nɔk bʋnsi'a linɛ nwɛnɛ nid nɛ pa'al David gadʋg la zug, ka pili li nɛ fuug ka vʋns bʋʋg kɔnbidi vili niŋi li zug baba la.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Saul n da tʋm nidib la ye ba keŋ gban'e David la, Mikal da yɛl ye, “O bɛn'ɛdnɛ.”

english_verse: Saul sent the guards back and told them, “Bring David to me—bed and all—so I can kill him.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul lɛn lɛbisi ba ye ba kem nyɛ David mɛŋ ka yɛli ba ye, “Ʋkimini o nɛ gadʋg la wʋsa kɛɛn m san'an na ka m kʋʋ o.”

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Amaa nidib la da kpɛn' gɔsi nyɛ ka bʋn la pa'ae gadʋg la zug, ka li zug baba la an bʋʋg kɔnbid.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Saul da bu'os Mikal ye, “Fʋ niŋ wala ma' mam wala ka kɛ ka m dataa zɔɔ bɔdigɛ?” Ka Mikal lɛbis o ye o yɛlim ye, “Kɛl ka m gaad, ya'a ka' alaa m na kʋʋf.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
translation_verse: David n da nyaŋi zɔɔ pɔns la, o da keŋ Samuel san'an Rama teŋin yɛl o Saul n maal o si'el wʋsa. Ka on nɛ Samuel keŋ Nayof n zin'inɛ ani.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Saul n daa wʋm labaar ye David bɛ Nayof, Rama sʋ'ʋlim la,

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: o da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ gban'e o na. Amaa ba da nyɛ nɔdi'esidib ka ba la'as bɛdegʋ di'esid Wina'am pian'adi tisid nidib nwɛnɛ ban ɛɛnti niŋid si'em la, ka Samuel paasi ba aan ba tuongat, ka Wina'am Siig la sig Saul nidib la zugin na ka ba mɛ pin'ili di'esid Wina'am pian'adi tisid nidib la.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Ba da keŋ yɛl Saul linɛ maan la, ka o lɛn tʋm nidib bɛdegʋ ya'as. Ka ban mɛ pin'ili di'esid Wina'am pian'ad. Saul da lɛn tʋm nidibi paas nɔɔra atan'. Ka ban mɛ maan wʋʋ nɔdi'esidib la nɛ.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Ka Saul mɛ yʋ'ʋn duoe keŋ Rama paae Seku bultita'ar la ni bu'os ye, “Samuel nɛ David bɛ yaanɛ?” Ka ba lɛbis o ye, “Ba bɛnɛ Nayof linɛ bɛ Rama la.”

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Ka Saul keŋ Nayof linɛ bɛ Rama la. Amaa Wina'am Siig mɛ da sig o zugin na, ka o pin'ili di'esid Wina'am pian'ad hali ti paae Nayof.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: O da yɛɛsi o fuud ka li Samuel tuonnɛ tansid wʋʋ nɔdi'esidib la. O da dig suokan zug dabiskan nɛ li yʋ'ʋŋ la wʋsa. Linɛ kɛ ka nidib yɛl ye, “Saul mɛ paas nɔdi'esidibin la nɛɛ?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: David da zɔɔ yi Nayof Rama sʋ'ʋlim keŋ Jonatan san'an bu'os o ye, “M maal bɔ? Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɔ ka m tʋm? M tʋmi fʋ saam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɔ kimm ka o mɔɔd ye o yisi m nyɔvʋrɛ?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Ayei, fʋ kʋ kpii! Gɔsima m saam nan zi' tʋm si'el ka li an bʋntita'ar bɛɛ bʋmbil ka pʋ nwɛ' mam sɔɔraa. O na niŋ walaa su'a mam nɛ'? Li ka' ala!”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Amaa David da pɔya ka yɛl ye, “Fʋ saam mi' ye fʋ pʋ di'em mam yɛlaa, alazug o gban'anɛ o sʋʋnrin ye, ‘M kʋ kɛ ka Jonatan baŋ nɛ', ka li na daam o.’ Amaa nɛ Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zug, nɛ man nɛ fʋnɛ zi'e kpɛla la, li kpɛlimnɛ fiin nɛ man naan kpiin.”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Jonatan yɛl David ye, “Fʋn bɔɔd ye m tʋm si'el wʋsa tisif, m na tʋm.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbis ye, “Gɔsima, bɛogʋ an nwadpaalig di'ema, ka li sʋ'ʋm ye man nɛ na'ab la la'am di; amaa kɛl ka m keŋ su'a pɔɔgin la ka dabisir la gaadi yi bɛogʋn ka zaam ma'ae.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Fʋ saam ya'a pʋ nyɛɛ ma, fʋn on yɛl o ye, David sɔsnɛ suor man san'an ye o niŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ Betilehem o mɛŋ teŋin, ka ba tuŋ la mɔri yʋʋm-yʋʋm maan.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: O ya'a yɛl ye li an sʋm alaa, mam onɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as la paam yɔlisim. Amaa o sʋnf ya'a duoe, fʋn baŋim ye o gban'anɛ ye o mugusim.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Maalim sʋm tis mam onɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as la, bɔzugɔ fʋ da kɛ ka ti naal nɔɔri lieb yinne Zugsɔb la tuon. M ya'a tʋm taal, fʋ mɛŋ kʋʋmim! Bɔ ka fʋ na zaŋimi tisi fʋ saam la?”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan lɛbis ye, “Ayei! Mam ya'a mi'in ye m saam mɔɔdnɛ ye o san'amif, m naan kʋ yɛli nɛ fɔɔ?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Jonatan yɛl o ye, “Kem na! Kɛl ka ti yii keŋ pɔɔgin la.” Ka babayi' la da dɔl taaba yi.

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: Jonatan da yɛl David ye, “Mam pɔ nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la ye daar anwa win, m na pian' tisim saam, ka li ya'a malis o ye fʋ lɛb na, m na tɔlim labaar na ka fʋ wʋm.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Amaa o ya'a gban'anɛ ye o san'amif Zugsɔb la on kɛl ka li wʋm mam sʋ'ʋŋa m ya'a pʋ kɛ ka fʋ baŋ ka mɔri fʋ yi nɛ laafii. Zugsɔb la na bɛ nɛf wʋʋ on da bɛnɛ m saam si'em la.

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: Mɛ da kɛ ka fʋ zuod la naae nɛ man yidima hali baa Zugsɔb la ya'a ti yis David dataas wʋsa dunia kaŋa ni.”

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: Alazug Jonatan da maal nɔnaar nɛ David yidim ka kaanbi yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la na bu'os David dataas bu'osa.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Jonatan da kɛ ka David maligim tɛndig o kaanbʋg la pa'an on nɔŋ o si'em, bɔzugɔ o nɔŋ o wʋʋ on nɔŋ o mɛŋ si'em la.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan yɛl David ye, “Bɛog anɛ nwadpaalig di'ema; fʋ ka'alim la na pak bɔzugɔ fʋ zin'isir la na dig zaalim.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Di'ema la yimbɛogʋ zaŋi ken zaam la, yim keŋ zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ daa dɛŋi su'a yɛl kaŋa daa pin'il la, zi'enɛ kpi'en Ezel kugir la.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: M na tɔn piema atan' ani baba, ka li nwɛnɛ m nyɛnɛ si'el ka tɔɔnd nɛ.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: M na tʋm biig ka yɛl o ye, ‘Kem iee piema la na!’ M ya'a yɛl o ye, ‘Gɔsima, piema la kpi'enɛ fʋn zi'e zin'isi'a la, pi'isimi baa mɔr kpɛla na’, fʋn kem na ka Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zug, fʋ nyɛ yɔlisim; dabiem kae.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Amaa m ya'a yɛl biig la ye, ‘Gɔsima, piema la digi fʋ tuon la!’ Li anɛ tilas ye fʋ gaad, bɔzugɔ li pa'al ye fʋ gaadim.

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Yɛl kanɛ ka fʋn nɛ mam pian' li yɛla la tiɛnm, ka Zugsɔb la aan ti kasɛt saŋa linɛ ka' naarɛ.”

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: David sid da su'a pɔɔgin la, ka nwadpaal di'ema la da paae la, Na'ab la da zin' ye o di.

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: O da zin'inɛ on ɛɛn zin' zin'isi'a saŋa wʋsa kpi'e dɔkpin la kpa' Jonatan, ka Abner tia'al Saul, amaa David zin'ig la da anɛ zaalim.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Saul da pʋ yɛl si'el daakanɛ, bɔzugɔ o da tɛn'ɛsi ye, “Daasi'erɛɛ si'eli kɛ ka David kae nyain nɛ ka li kɛ ka o pʋ kɛn malʋŋ la naa. Asida o ka' nyain nɛ.”

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: Amaa bɛogʋ da nie la, nwadig la dabisa ayi' daar, David zin'ig la da anɛ zaalim ya'as. Ka Saul bu'os o biig Jonatan ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka Jese biig la pʋ kenaa di su'os nɛ zina wʋsa?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: O yɛl ye, ‘Kɛl ka m keŋ, bɔzugɔ ti yidim mɔri maan ye ba maal, ka m bier ye li anɛ tilas ye m bɛɛ ani. Man ya'a sid an onɛ ka fʋ nɔŋim, fʋn on kɛl ka m keŋ nyɛɛ ba.’ Linɛ kɛ ka o pʋ nyaŋi kena zin'in nɛ fʋ di la.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Saul sʋnf da duoe nɛ Jonatan hali, ka o yɛl o ye, “Fʋn kanɛ an pu'a kanɛ ki'isid ka tʋm linɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm biiga! Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye m zi' ye fʋ niŋ nɛ nɔɔr yinne nɛ Jese biig la? Fʋ zi' ye li anɛ nyannɛ tis fʋn nɛ fʋ ma kanɛ du'af laa?

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Jese biig la nam bɛ dunia la, fʋn nɛ fʋ sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa kʋ zi'enɛ. Nannanna tʋm ka ba mɔr o na, ka asɛɛ o kpi!”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Ka Jonatan lɛbisi bu'os o saam ye, “Bɔzugʋ kɛ ka li nar ye o kpi? O maal bɔ?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Ka Saul tɔn Jonatan nɛ kpan ye o kʋʋ o. Ani ka Jonatan baŋ ye o saam gban'anɛ ye o kʋ David.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Jonatan da duoe kʋk la zug nɛ ɛndʋg; nwadig la dabisa ayi' la daar la o da pʋ dii, bɔzugɔ o sʋnf da san'amnɛ, nɛ nyan tʋʋma linɛ ka o saam maan David la.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Bɛkɛung Jonatan da yii keŋ pɔɔgin la wʋʋ on nɛ David n pʋn gban'e si'em la. O da ken ka dɔl biribiŋ bil,

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Zɔm keŋ iee piim banɛ ka m tɔn la.” Biig la zɔt la, ka o tɔn piim yinne ka li gaŋ o.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Biig la da paae zin'ikanɛ ka Jonatan piema la lu la, ka Jonatan buol o ye, “Piim la pʋ lu nɛ fʋ tuonnɛɛ?”

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Ka o tans ye, “Niŋim tɔ'ɔtɔ! Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ! Da zi'enɛ!” Ka biig la pi'ig piim la lɛb o zugdaan la san'an.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Jonatan da nɔk o zaba la'ad la tis biig la, ka yɛl o ye, “Ziimi ba lɛb tempʋʋgin la.”

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Biig la gaad la, David yi dagɔbʋg baba kena igin Jonatan tuon nɔɔra atan' ka su'uni o nindaa teŋin. Ka ba kuak taaba ka ba wʋsa kaas, amaa David daa kaas bɛdegʋ gat o tiraan la.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Jonatan da yɛl David ye, “Kem nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm, bɔzugɔ ti pɔɔ tis taaba nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr ye, ti ye ti anɛ zuod. Ka ye, ‘Zugsɔb la an kasɛta sɔb man nɛ fʋ teŋsʋk, fʋ yaas nɛ man yaas saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ!’” Ka David gaad ka Jonatan lɛb tempʋʋgin la.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: David da keŋ Nob, Ahimelek onɛ an maanmaan la san'an. Dabiem da kpɛn' Ahimelek on nyɛɛ o ka o aan o kɔn'ɔkɔn' la, ka o bu'os o ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka fʋ kennɛ fʋ kɔn'ɔkɔn'? Bɔɔ kɛ ka sɔ' pʋ dɔlli fɔ?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbisi yɛl Ahimelek onɛ an maanmaan la ye, “Na'abi tisim tʋʋm si'a ka yɛlim ye, ‘Li pʋ sʋ'ʋm ye sɔ' baŋi fʋ ken la gbin nɛ man yɛlif ye fʋ maal si'ela.’ Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ man nidib la m yɛli ba ban na sia'alim zin'isi'a.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Nannanna, dibɔ ka fʋ mɔri fʋ nu'uginɛ? Tisimim bodobodo gbila anu, bɛɛ fʋn nyɛ si'el wʋsa.”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Amaa maanmaan kpɛɛm la lɛbisi yɛl David ye, “Mam pʋ mɔr bodobodo zaal kpɛla, m mɔri bodobodo kanɛ an Zugsɔb la din. Fʋn nɛ fʋ nidib la ya'a sa pʋ digin nɛ pu'aba, ya na tun'e ɔnbi li.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbis ye, “Da kɛ ka li paki fɔ; hali ti ya'a ken, ken kanɛ pʋ tɛbisa ti pʋ li'en pu'aba, ka li kɛ ka ti an kasi. Ka kɛl dabiskaŋa an nimmua dabisirɛ. Nidib la anɛ kasi.”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Ka maanmaan kpɛɛm la nɔk bodobodo linɛ an Wina'am din la tis o, bodobodo si'a da lɛn kae anii asɛɛ linɛ ka ba digil Zugsɔb tuon la ma'aa, ka ba yis ka lɛdig bodobodo tʋʋl daakan la.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Saul yammis yinne da bɛɛ ani daakan la, ka ba gban'e o zin'il Zugsɔb la tuon. O da anɛ Doyig onɛ an Edom buudi la nid, ka an Saul kɔnbkemnib la kpɛɛm.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: David bu'os Ahimelek ye, “Fʋ pʋ mɔr kpan bɛɛ zaba sʋ'ʋg kpɛlaa? M pʋ mɔri m sʋ'ʋg bɛɛ zaba lauk si'a naa, bɔzugɔ Na'ab la titʋmis la anɛ gbirigir.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Ka maanmaan la lɛbis ye, “Goliyaf onɛ an Filistia nid, ka fʋ daa kʋʋ o Ela bɔn'ɔgin la, o sʋ'ʋg la bɛ kpɛla ka ba kpilim nɛ fuug ka li bɛ dansik la nya'aŋ. Fʋ ya'a bɔɔdaa fʋn nɔkimi li, ka sʋ'ʋg lɛn kae kpɛla ya'a ka' linɛ.” Ka David lɛbis ye, “Sʋ'ʋg lɛn kae nwɛnɛ lii, nɔkim tisim na!” David bɛ Gaf

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Daakan la David da zɔɔ yi Saul san'anɛ keŋ Akis onɛ an Gaf na'ab la san'an.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Amaa Akis yammis la da bu'os ye, “Ka' David n nwaa, ka' onɛ aan o teŋ na'ab laa? Ka' on ka ba mɔri yʋ'ʋm ka wa'ad laa? Ba yɛt ye, ‘Saul kʋ tusir, ka David kʋ tusa piiga’”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Nɛ' da iank David ya'am ka o pin'ili zɔt Akis onɛ an Gaf na'ab la dabiem.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: O da ma'anɛ maal o mɛŋ wʋʋ o zugʋ fɛndignɛ ba tuon; ka on bɛɛ ba nu'usin la zug o niŋidi nwɛnɛ gɛɛŋ nɛ, ka mɔr si'elnamɛ bɔɔnd za'anɔɔr dalamma la zug ka kɛ ka nintɔɔnd sɔnnɛ dɔlisid o tieŋi sigid teŋin.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Akis bu'os o yammis la ye, “Gɔsim dau la! O anɛ gɛɛŋ! Bɔ ka ya zii o kɛɛn m san'an na?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Man kɔ'ɔŋ nɛ gɛɛmis ka ya ziid oŋa ken kpɛla na ka o niŋid nɛ'ɛnamɛ m tuonnɛɛ? Li anɛ tilas ye dau kaŋa kpɛn' m yin naa?”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: David da bas Gaf ka zɔɔ keŋ Adullam teŋinɛ su'a tampinyɔkin. O bieyanam nɛ o sizuop nɛ o saam nidib la da wʋmi li la, ba da keŋ o san'an.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Banɛ wʋsa da mɔr sʋnsa'aŋ, bɛɛ sama, bɛɛ yɛla la da la'as o san'an. Ka o liebi ba tuongat. Dap nwɛnɛ kɔbisnaasi da bɛɛ o san'an.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: David da yii ani keŋ Misipa linɛ bɛ Moab sʋ'ʋlimin la, ka yɛl Moab Na'ab ye, “Kɛl ka m ma nɛ m saam kena bɛɛ fʋ san'an hali nɛ mam na ti baŋ Zugsɔb la bɔɔd ye o maal si'eli tisim.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Alazug o da basi ba ka ba bɛ Moab Na'ab la san'an, saŋa kan wʋsa ka David bɛɛ o kpi'euŋ zin'ig la.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Amaa Gad onɛ an Zugsɔb nɔdi'es la yɛl David ye, “Da bɛ kpi'euŋ zin'igin la, kem Juda teŋin.” Alazug David da yii ani keŋ Heref sian'arin.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Ka Saul wʋm ye ba nyɛ David nɛ o nidib la, li saŋa la ka o mɔr kpan o nu'ugin, zin' tisi'a linɛ bɛ Gibea kʋkʋn zug la gbinnin, ka o ninkpi'ema la wʋsa gilig o.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛli ba ye, “Kɛlisimi, Benjamin nidiba! Jese biig la na nyaŋi tisi ya pɔɔd nɛ tibanɛ wan lɔmbɔn'ɔdɛɛ? O na kɛ ka ya lieb soogianam tusir-tusir nɛ kɔbig-kɔbig tuongatiba?

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Linzug ka ya la'asi su'a gban'e bɛ'ɛd man yɛlaa? Hali ya sɔ' pʋ yɛl mam saŋkan ka m biig la maal nɔnaar nɛ Jese biig la. Ya'a an sida, ya ba'a kae nɛ mam, ka ya nid baa yinne pʋ tɛn'ɛsi yɛlim ye m biig la naal nɛ man sankpan'as ka ba ieed mam suoya wʋʋ on niŋ si'em zina laa.”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Ka Doyig onɛ an Edom buudi dau la da zi'e nɛ Saul kpi'emnam la, ka yɛl ye, “Man nyɛ Jese biig la ka o keŋ Ahimelek san'an, onɛ an Ahitub biig ka bɛ Nob teŋin la.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Ahimelek bu'os Zugsɔb la lin nar ye David tʋm si'em. Ka mɛ tis o diib, nɛ Goliyaf onɛ an Filistia nid la zaba sʋ'ʋg.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tʋm buol maanmaan Ahimelek onɛ an Ahitub biig la nɛ o saam yidim wʋsa banɛ daa an maanmaannibi bɛ Nob teŋin la, ka ba kena.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Saul yɛl ye, “Fʋn kanɛ an Ahitub biiga, kɛlisim!” Ka o siak ye, “Naa, m zugdaana!”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛl o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋn nɛ Jese biig la su'a gban'e gban'abɛ'ɛdi m yɛla, ka fʋ tis o bodobodo nɛ sʋ'ʋg, ka bu'os Zugsɔb la tis o? Ka li kɛ ka o zana'si m nɔɔr ka yʋ'ʋn digi pigidim anwa?”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Ka Ahimelek lɛbis o ye, “Naa, fʋ yammis la wʋsa ni, anɔ'ɔnɛ an sida sɔb wʋʋ David onɛ aan fʋ diem la? Ka' o anɛ banɛ gurif la tuongat, ka fʋ yidim tisid o girima hali?

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa an yiiga ka mam bu'os Wina'am tis oo? Ayei! Na'aba, da mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd nɛ man kanɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as la, bɛɛ m saam yidima, ka mam zi' yɛlbanɛ maan la yɛla baa bi'elaa.”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab la daa lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Ahimelek, li anɛ tilas ye fʋ kpi, fʋn nɛ fʋ saam yidim la wʋsa.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl banɛ gur o ka zi'e kpi'e o la ye, “Fɛndigim kʋʋe Zugsɔb maanmaannib la, ka ba mɛ niŋ nɛ nɔɔr yinne nɛ David. Ba daa mi' ye o zɔtnɛ yit man san'an, ka pʋ yɛli ma.” Amaa o kpi'emnam la daa pʋ siak ye ba si'is Zugsɔb maanmaannib la.

english_verse: Saul turned to Doeg, who was from Edom, and said, “Kill the priests!” On that same day, Doeg killed
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Doyig ye, “Alaa fʋn fɛndigim nwɛ' maanmaannib la kʋ.” Doyig onɛ an Edom dau la da fɛndigi nwɛ' baa kʋ. Daakan la o kʋ dap pisnii nɛ anu banɛ da yɛ maanmaannib dansikanam la.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: O mɛ da san'am Nob linɛ an maanmaannib teŋ la, nɛ dap nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis nɛ bilies nɛ niigi nɛ bʋmis nɛ pɛ'ɛs.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Amaa Abiata onɛ an Ahimelek biig la da nyaŋi su'a zɔɔ keŋ David san'an.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: O da yɛl David ye Saul kʋ Zugsɔb maanmaannib la.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl Abiata ye, “M daa nyɛ Doyig onɛ an Edom dau la anina ka pʋn baŋ ye o na yɛl Saul. Man zug ka ba kʋʋ fʋ saam yidim la wʋsa!

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Kpɛlim kpɛla nɛ man; da zɔt dabiem; dau kanɛ ieedi fʋ nyɔvʋr la mɛ ieednɛ man din mɛn. Fʋ na paam yɔlisim mam san'an.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl David ye, “Gɔsima, Filistia dim la zabid nɛ Kiela teŋ ka faandi ba ki zieŋin la.”

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: O da keŋ Zugsɔb la tuonnɛ bu'os o ye, “M kem zab nɛ Filistia dim la faaɛn Kiela dim laa?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Kem zab nɛ ba ka faaɛn ba.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Amaa David nidib la da yɛl o ye, “Hali Juda teŋin kpɛla nwa' tinam zɔti dabiem, li yʋ'ʋn na an wala ti ya'a keŋ Kiela ye ti zab nɛ Filistia zabzabidib la?”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Ka David lɛn lɛb Zugsɔb la san'an ya'as ye o bu'os o, ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis o ye, “Kemi, ka m na kɛ ka fʋ nyaŋ Filistia dim la.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Alazug David nɛ o nidib la da keŋ Kiela teŋin zab nɛ Filistia dim la nyaŋi ba ka faaɛn ba bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa gaad. Ala ka David da faaɛn Kiela teŋ dim la.

english_verse: David heard about Saul's plan to capture him, and he told Abiathar, “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: David n da baŋ ye Saul gban'adi gban'abɛ'ɛd o yɛla la, o yɛl Abiata onɛ an maanmaan la ye, “Mɔr dansik la na!”

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os ye, “Ti Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am, man onɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as la wʋm ya nyain ye Saul gban'e nɛ ye o kena san'am Kiela man zug.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Kiela teŋ dim na gban'ami tis oo? Saul na kena wʋʋ man wʋm si'em laa? M Zugsɔba, fʋn onɛ an Israel Wina'am la, gandigim ka pa'alim.” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis o ye, “O na kena.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛm bu'os ye, “Kiela teŋ dim la na gban'e mam nɛ m nidib la tis Saul bɛɛ?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis o ye, “Ba na niŋ ala.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: David da su'a bɛ Zif teŋ sian'arin la, nɛ kʋkʋna la ni. Daar wʋsa Saul da ieed o nɛ, amaa Wina'am da pʋ kɛ ka Saul nyɛɛ o.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: David n da nam bɛ Hores linɛ bɛ Zif sian'arin la, o da wʋm ye Saul yina mɔɔd ye o kʋʋ o.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Saul biig Jonatan da keŋ David san'an Hores ye o kpɛmis o yadda Wina'am san'an.

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: O yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem. M saam Saul kʋ nyaŋi niŋif si'ela. Asɛɛ fʋ ba'asi lieb Israel Na'ab, ka man tia'ali fʋ zug. Hali m saam mɛŋ mi' ye li anɛ ala.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Babayi' la da pɔya ka naal taaba nɔɔr Zugsɔb la tuon. Ka Jonatan lɛbi kul yin, amaa David da kpɛlim Hores.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Zif dim la da keŋ Saul san'an Gibea teŋin yɛl o ye, “Fʋ zi' ye David su'a nɛ tinam san'anɛ? Ɛɛn! O bɛ Hores sian'anr sʋʋgin la, Hakila kʋkʋnin la, lɛbisid dagɔbʋg baba Jesimon teŋin la.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Ka Saul lɛbisi ba ye, “Zugsɔb la na niŋi ya zug bareka, ya ba'a bɛ nɛ mam la zug.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: Lɛm maligim vɛɛnsi baŋi on bɛ zin'isi'a nɛ onɛ nyɛɛ o la. Ka ba yɛlim ye o anɛ bibia hali.

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Mɔɔmi ka baŋ o suak zin'ibanɛ ka o mɔr la wʋsa, ka lɛbi na tisim labaar kanɛ an viki. Ka m dɔlli ya ka ti keŋ iee o. Hali baa ti ya'a na iee o Juda sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa ka paam o gban'e, ti na niŋ ala.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Dinzug ba da yii gaad Saul tuonnɛ keŋ Zif. Saŋkan la David nɛ o nidib la da keŋ Maon sian'arin linɛ bɛ Araba lɛbisid Jesimon teŋ dagɔbʋg la.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Saul nɛ o nidib la da pin'il ieeb. David n da wʋm la, o keŋ nɛ Maon sian'arin kpɛn' tampinsi'a lɛuŋʋn su'a. Ka Saul wʋm ka keŋ Maon sian'arin la ieed David.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Saul da dɔlisid nɛ zuor la lʋgir yinne, ka David nɛ o nidib la mɛ dɔl lʋgkaŋa la, mɔɔd ye ba niŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ zɔ ka bas Saul bɔzugɔ, Saul nɛ o nidib la da mirid David nɛ o nidib la ye ba gban'e ba.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Ka ninsɔ' mɔr labaar na yɛl Saul ye, “Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ na! Filistia dim la kena bɔɔdi zabi faaɛn teŋ la.”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul bas David kadib ka keŋ ye o tʋ'ʋs Filistia dim la. Linzugʋ kɛ ka ba buon zin'ikan la ye Sela-Hammalekof.

english_verse: David left and went to live in the hideouts at En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Ka David yii anina keŋ zin'ikpi'euŋ dinɛ bɛ Engedi la.

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Saul n da kad Filistia dim la naae ka lɛb na la, ba da yɛl o ye, “David bɛ Engedi sian'arin.”

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: O da paae kɔnbid dɔɔd banɛ kpi'e suor baba ka tampinyɔk bɛɛ ani ka kpɛn' ye o nyɛ' bin; zi' ka David nɛ o nidib la pʋn dɛŋin kpɛn' tampinyɔkin la bɛ pʋʋgin-pʋʋgin sa.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Ka David dap la yɛl ye, “Dabis bamanam buudi la ka Zugsɔb la da pian' tisif ye, ‘M na nɔki fʋ dataas la niŋi fʋ nu'usin, ka fʋ maali ba fʋn bɔɔd si'em.’” Ka David duoe baanlimm ka Saul pʋ baŋɛ, ka o nwaae Saul fuug nɔɔr.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ, David sʋnf da san'amnɛ, on nwaae fuug la nɔɔr la,

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: David da nɔk nɛ pian'abama diin o nidib la ka ba pʋ zab nɛ Saul. Ka Saul ti yi tampinyɔkin la gaad.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: Ka David mɛ yi naa buol Saul ye, “M zugdaan Na'aba!” Ka Saul gi'e, ka David su'un nɛ o nindaa teŋin

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka fʋ kɛlisid nimbanɛ ma'adif ye David bɔɔdi fʋ bɔɔb la?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Zina fʋ mɛŋ nyɛ Zugsɔb la nɔki fʋ niŋi m nu'usin tampinyɔk la pʋʋgin si'em. Sieba muk nɛ ye m kʋʋmif ka m zan'as; m yɛli ba ye, ‘Mam kʋ ʋki m nu'ugʋ si'isi m zugdaana, bɔzugɔ o anɛ onɛ ka Zugsɔb la gaŋ ka bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zugin.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, m Saamma, fʋ fuug nɔɔri nwa' ka m zanli m nu'ugin! M nwaae li nɛ yis ka lɛɛ pʋ kʋʋ fɔ. Nannanna tɛn'ɛsim ka baŋ ye mam pʋ gban'e bɛ'ɛdɛ ka mɛ ka' onɛ na yii fʋ nya'aŋa. Mam pʋ tʋm taal si'a tisi fɔ, amaa fʋ ieedim nɛ ye fʋ kʋʋ m.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na yɔ taal kanɛ ka fʋ tʋm tis mam la, amaa man nu'ug kʋ si'isi fɔ.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Wʋʋ kpɛɛmnam mɔri ba yɛlsim ye, ‘Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim san'an ka bɛ'ɛd tʋmid.’ Alazugɔ man nu'ug kʋ si'isi fɔ.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Mam aan anɔ'ɔn ka Israel dim na'ab la yina kati ma? Man kanɛ nwɛnɛ bakpiilʋŋ bɛɛ silinsauk laa?

english_verse: I pray that the Lord will help me escape and show that I am in the right.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na kad mam nɛ fʋn saria, ka tɛk onɛ ka' bʋʋd la tʋbir. O mɛŋ na niŋ dinɛ nari tis mam, ka faanmi yisi fʋ nu'ugin.”

english_verse: “David, my son—is that you?” Saul asked. Then he started crying
translation_verse: David n da yɛl nɛ' naae la, ka Saul bu'os ye, “Fʋ kʋkɔri laa, m biig David?” Ka kum agɔla gɔla.

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: Ka yɛl o ye, “Fʋ mɔr pʋpielim gaad mam, fʋ maal mam sʋ'ʋŋa, ka man lɛɛ maalif bɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Fʋ yɛlim nannanna tʋʋm sʋŋ kanɛ ka fʋ tʋm tis mam; Zugsɔb la nɔkimi niŋi fʋ nu'ugin, amaa fʋ pʋ kʋʋ ma.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Nid ya'a paam o dataa, o na bas o ka o gaad yɔlim nɛɛ? Zugsɔb la na yɔɔf sʋ'ʋŋa fʋn maal sʋ'ʋm si'a tis mam zina la.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: M mi' ye fʋ sid na lieb Israel na'ab, ka sʋ'ʋlim la na paam yaligiri fʋ nu'usin.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Nannanna pɔɔm nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr ye fʋ kʋ kɛnsigi m yaas tuŋ, bɛɛ yisi m yʋ'ʋri m yidiminɛ.”

english_verse: So David promised, and Saul went home. David and his men returned to their hideout.
translation_verse: David da pɔɔ tis Saul. Ka Saul lɛbi kul amaa David nɛ o nidib la da duoe paae zin'ikpi'euŋ la.

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Yɛlimi nɛ o ye, ‘Win na pɛligi fʋ zug! Wina'am mɛ na yaligi fʋ zak nɛ fʋ mɔrim wʋsa!

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: Tɔ', di nwɛnɛ m wʋm ye fʋ kiesidi fʋ pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid, ka fʋ kɔnbkemnibi daa bɛ nɛ ti la, ti daa pʋ maannɛ ba bɛ'ɛdɛ. Ka saŋa kanɛ ka ba daa bɛ Kaamel la wʋsa ba si'el pʋ bɔdigɛ.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Bu'osimi fʋ yammis la ka ba na yɛlif sida. Alazugɔ gɔsim maal si'eli tisim dasam nwa', lin maal sʋ'ʋm sia'ali ya dabisir daar la. M bɛlimnɛ, tisimi ti fʋn mɔr si'el wʋsa.’”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: David nidib la paae la, ba yɛl Nabal labaar linɛ yi David san'an na. Ka yʋ'ʋn gu'usid.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os yammis la ye, “David kaŋa aan anɔ'ɔnɛ? Anɔ'ɔnɛ an Jese bikaŋa? Nannanna yammis pamm yʋ'ʋn zɔtnɛ ka basidi ba zugdaannam.

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Bɔ ka m nɔkidi m diib nɛ ku'om nɛ m ni'im kanɛ ka m kʋ ye m tis banɛ kiesi m pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid la tisid nimbanɛ ka sɔ' zi' ban yi zin'isi'a na?”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: David nidib la da fɛndigi lɛb. Ba da paae yɛl David on pian' si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbisi yɛli ba ye, “Zaŋiminɛ ya zaba sʋ'ʋs!” Ka ba zaŋ ka David mɛ zaŋ o din. Dap la da paae kɔbisnaasi dɔl David n keŋ, ka kɔbisyi' kpɛlim gur la'ad la.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Nannanna tɛn'ɛsim gɔs fʋn na niŋ si'em ka tɔɔg da paae ti zugdaan la nɛ o yidima. O anɛ nimbɛ'og hali ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi pian' tis o.”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Ka yɛl yammis la ye, “Gaadimi tuon, ka m na dɔlli ya nya'aŋ.” Amaa o da pʋ yɛl o sid Nabal.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: O da ban'a o bʋŋ la paae zuor teŋsʋk linɛ an bɔn'ɔfalig la, ka David nɛ o nidib la mɛ zuligidi kpa'ad o ka o tʋ'ʋsi ba.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: David da tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “Alaa, man daa gur dau kaŋa arezak la sian'arin ka o si'el pʋ bɔdig la wʋsa anɛ zaalim? O nɔknɛ bɛ'ɛdi yɔɔd man tʋʋm sʋŋ la.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Tan', bɛog bɛkɛunga anwa win, m ya'a pʋ mɛlis dau kaŋa nɛ o dap la wʋsaa, Wina'am on bu'osim!”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Abigel n da nyɛ David la o da sig o bʋŋ la zug tɔ'ɔtɔ igin David tuon ka su'uni o nindaa teŋin

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: M bɛlimnɛ kɛlli m taali bas, ka m anɛ fʋ sankpan'as asida sida. Zugsɔb la na kɛ ka fʋ sʋ'ʋlim yalig ka yuug, bɔzugɔ fʋ zabidnɛ Zugsɔb la mɛŋ zaba, m zugdaana. Da kɛ ka sɔ' nyɛ yɛlbɛ'ɛdi fʋ nii, hali nɛ fʋ nyɔvʋr bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: M zugdaana, la'an nɛ sɔ' duoe zi'e ye o yisi fʋ nyɔvʋr la, fʋ nyɔvʋr su'anɛ Zugsɔb Wina'am nu'usin. Amaa fʋ dataas la nyɔvʋr na yii keŋ lu nwɛnɛ ban yuligid kugiri yisid luobigin si'em la.
