english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: M zugdaana, Zugsɔb la ya'a ti tʋm tisif wʋʋ on kaanb si'em la, o na gaŋif ka fʋ an Israel tuongat.

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: M zugdaana, da lɛm mɔri li fʋ sʋnfʋn ye fʋ yis ziim bɛɛ yɔ bɛ'ɛd san'ami fʋ mɛŋa. Ka Zugsɔb la ya'a tisif nyaŋir fʋn tiɛnmi m yɛla ka da tam.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl Abigel ye, “Na'asi anɛ Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la din! Onɛ tʋmif zina ye fʋ kena sia'alim.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Albareka anɛ fʋ din, fʋn mɔr ya'am si'em la zug. Fʋ gu'um ka m pʋ yis ziim zinaa ka mɛ pʋ yɔ bɛ'ɛd sam nɛ m mɛŋ nu'ugɔ.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Li ya'a ka' Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la vʋe ka gu'um la zugɔ, m naan san'amini ya. Fʋ ya'a pʋ kɛɛn tɔ'ɔtɔ na sia'alini ma, Nabal nɛ o tʋmtʋm la baa yinne kʋ vʋe bɛog bɛkɛunga nwa' winnɛ.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Ka David siaki di'e la'abanɛ ka o mɔr la wʋsa ka yɛl o ye, “Lɛm kul nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm. M wʋmi fʋ pian'ad la, ka siaki fʋ sɔsʋg la.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Abigel da lɛbi paae nyɛ ka Nabal buol nidibi la'as ka maal diib ka ba dit ka nuud nwɛnɛ o anɛ na'ab nɛ. O sʋnf daa malis nɛ hali ka o nuu kʋʋl. Alazug Abigel da pʋ yɛl o si'ela, hali ka bɛog ti nie.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie ka Nabal nini yʋ'ʋn pilig la, ka o pu'a yɛl o si'el wʋsa, ka o sʋnf san'am ka o ga'aŋ wʋʋ kugir nɛ.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Di dabpiiga nya'aŋ la, Zugsɔb la da nwɛ' Nabal ka o kpi.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: O da su'uni o nindaa teŋin ka ye, “Mam anɛ ya tʋmtʋm pu'ak, ka ti'eb ye m tʋm tisi ya, hali ka pie yanam banɛ an m zugdaan la yammis la nɔba.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Abigel da duoe tɔ'ɔtɔ ti'ebi ban' bʋŋ, ka o zak bipumis anu dɔl o, ka ban nɛ ban tʋm ninsieba la dɔl taaba keŋ David san'an ka o lieb o pu'a.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: David mɛ da dii Ahinoam onɛ yi Jezireel na la ka ba wʋsa aan o pu'ab.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Amaa Saul da pʋn nɔk o bipuŋ Mikal, onɛ an David pu'a la, tis Paltiel onɛ an Lais biig onɛ da yi Gallim na la.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Zif dim la da lɛn keŋ Saul san'an Gibea teŋin yɛl o ye, “Fʋ zi' ye David su'a nɛ tinam san'anɛɛ? Ɛɛn! O bɛ Hakila kʋkʋnin la, kpa' Jesimon teŋ la.”

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Saul da maali ba gbɛɛnb zin'ig la kpi'el suor linɛ bɛ Hakila kʋkʋnin kpi'e Jesimon la. Amaa on da baŋ ye Saul dɔlis o nɔba paae anina na la,

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ka David yii keŋ zin'ikanɛ ka Saul kenna ye o diginɛ gu' la. O da nyɛ Saul nɛ Abner onɛ an Nier biig ka an soogianam la kpɛɛm la gu' zin'isi'a. Saul da dignɛ teŋsʋk ka soogianam la diginɛ gilig o.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: David da bu'os Ahimelek onɛ an Hitti dau la nɛ Abisai, onɛ an Zeruyia biig ka an Joab pitʋ la ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ na dɔl mam ka ti keŋ Saul gbɛɛnb zin'igin la?” Ka Abisai da lɛbis ye, “Man! M na dɔlli fʋ keŋ.”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: David nɛ Abisai da keŋ soogianam la san'an yʋ'ʋŋ, ka Saul bɛɛ ani digi gbisid nidib la teŋsʋk ka o kpan ba' teŋi kpi'e o zug baba. Abner nɛ soogianam la daa dig nɛ gilig o.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Abisai da yɛl David ye, “Zina Zugsɔb la nɔki fʋ dataa la niŋi fʋ nu'ugin. Nannanna kɛl ka m kʋns o ta'al nɛ teŋ la nɛ m kpan la vuguri. M kʋ kʋns o nɔɔra ayi'.”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛl ye, “Asida sida, m bas o nɛ Wina'am, o saŋa na paae ka o kpi, ya'a ka ala o na keŋ nɛ zaba nii kpɛlim anina.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Amaa win na yis ka mam nɔki m nu'ugʋ si'is onɛ ka Zugsɔb la gaŋ ka bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zugin la. Nannanna, nɔkim o kpan la nɛ ku'om gan'ar la kpi'e o zugin la, ka ti keŋ.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ka David sid da nɔk kpan la, nɛ ku'om gan'ar linɛ kpi'e Saul zugin la, ka ba gaad. Sɔ' da pʋ nyɛ bɛɛ baŋi li yɛla bɛɛ nie gbɛɛminɛ. Ba wʋsa da gbis nɛ bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka ba gbis gbɛnkan buudi.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: David da lɔ'ɔŋ gbɛogʋ lalig bi'ela dʋ kʋkʋn zug. Paalʋ kanɛ da bɛɛ ba teŋsʋk la da pʋ pɔɔda.

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: Ka o kaas kuŋi buol soogianam la nɛ Abner onɛ an Nier biig la ye, “Abner! Fʋ kʋ siaki m buolʋg laa?” Ka Abner lɛbis ye, “Fʋ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ buon Na'aba?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbis o ye, “Mɛ fʋ ye fʋ anɛ dau, bɛɛ ka' ala? Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwɛnɛ fʋ Israel teŋinɛ? Bɔ ka fʋ pʋ guri fʋ zugdaan onɛ an Na'ab la? Sɔ' pa'a kena ye o kʋʋ ya zugdaan onɛ an Na'ab la.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Fʋn maal si'el la ka' sʋ'ʋm. Nɛ Wina'am onɛ bɛ saazug nwa', fʋn nɛ fʋ nidib la nari kum, bɔzugɔ ya pʋ guri ya zugdaan onɛ ka Zugsɔb gaŋ ka bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zugin la. Gɔsim giligi ye Na'ab kpan la nɛ o ku'om gan'ar linɛ pa'a dig o zug baba la bɛ yaanɛ?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Saul da baŋ David ka bu'os o ye, “Fʋ kʋkɔri laa, m biig David?” Ka David lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, m zugdaan Na'aba.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Ka bu'os ye, “M zugdaana, m anɛ fʋ sankpan'as, bɔ ka fʋ kati m bugirɛ? M maalif bɔ, bɛɛ taal bɔ ka m tʋm?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Naa, m zugdaana, kɛlisimi fʋ sankpan'as la pian'ʋk. Li ya'a anɛ Zugsɔb la kɛ ka fʋ kisig man, on di'em maan. Amaa li ya'a anɛ saalibi tuguli ti, ba na paam nɔpɔɔr Zugsɔb la tuon! Ba kad mam m pʋʋr linɛ bɛ Zugsɔb la teŋin la, ka yɛt ye, ‘Kem dɔl bada.’

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Nannanna, da kɛ ka m kpi teŋ zʋŋ kanɛ ka' Zugsɔb la teŋa. Naa, bɔ ka Israel Na'ab la yina ieed silinsaukɔ? Li nwɛnɛ sɔ' na ieed kunduŋ zuoya ni.”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Man tʋm taal. Lɛm na, m biig David, bɔzugɔ fʋ gɔs ka m nyɔvʋr mɔr nyɔɔd zina, m kʋ lɛm mɔ ye m san'amif ya'asɛ. Sida m tʋm nɛ nwɛnɛ zɔlʋg nɛ ka yidig bɛdegʋ.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbis ye, “Naa, gɔsima, fʋ kpan la nwa'. Kɛl ka fʋ dasam la yinne kena di'e li.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɔɔd nɛ onɛ wʋsa mɔr pʋpielim ka an sida sɔb. Zugsɔb nɔki fʋ niŋi m nu'ugin zina, amaa mam pʋ siak ye m nɔki m nu'ugʋ si'is onɛ ka Zugsɔb gaŋ ka bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zugin la.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ man sid nyɛ ka fʋ vʋm la mɔr nyɔɔd zina la, ala mɛn ka Zugsɔb la mɛ nyɛ mam din mɛn ka yisim yɛla wʋsa pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Ka Saul yɛl David ye, “M biig David, fʋ na paam albareka. Fʋ na tʋm nyalima ka sid nyaŋ.” Ka David daa keŋ o ken, ka Saul mɛ lɛbi kul.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: David daa tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “Dabisbama ni Saul ya'a paamim, o kʋ basi ma. Man na niŋ si'em anɛ m zɔɔ keŋ Filistia dim la san'an. Lin na kɛ ka Saul basim ieeb Israel teŋin wʋsa, ka m da luu o nu'uginɛ.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl Saul ye David zɔɔ keŋ Gaf la, o da bas David ieeb.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl Akis ye Naa, Na'aba, “Fʋ sʋnf ya'a malis nɛ mam, fʋn bɔɔm teŋi fʋ sʋ'ʋlimin la tisim ka m zin'in. Li pʋ nar ye mam nɛ fʋ la'am bɛ na'ateŋin kpɛla.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Daakan la Akis da tis o Ziklag, ka dinzug ka li lieb Juda na'anam sʋ'ʋlim hali nɛ zina.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: David da zin' Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋlimin la nɛ yʋʋm nɛ nwadis anaasi.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: David nɛ o nidib la da keŋ zabi faaɛn Gesur dim nɛ Giriz nɛ Amalek dim la.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Saŋa kanɛ wʋsa ka David zab nɛ zin'isi'a o da ɛɛn pʋ kɛt ka dau bɛɛ pu'a kpɛlim vʋeya amaa ka lɛɛ nɔk pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi nɛ bʋmis nɛ yʋgʋma nɛ fuud ka nyaan lɛb Akis san'an.

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: Akis ya'a da bu'os ye, “Ya ka ya keŋ faaɛn zina?” David na lɛbis ye, “Ti keŋ nɛ Negef linɛ bɛ Juda”, bɛɛ, “Negef linɛ bɛ Jerameel” bɛɛ, “Negef linɛ an Keen dim teŋ la.”

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: O da kʋʋd dap nɛ pu'ab wʋsa, ya'a ka' alaa ba na lɛb Gaf teŋin yɛl Na'ab Akis on tʋm si'el. On da tʋm si'em nwa', saŋkanɛ ka ba da bɛ Filistia dim sʋ'ʋlimin la wʋsa.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Akis da niŋ David yadda ka tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “O nidib Israel dim la kisi o nɛ, alazugɔ o na aan m sankpan'as saŋa wʋsa.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da la'as taaba tiinsim zin' Seunim teŋin. Ka Saul nɛ Israel dim la mɛ la'asi tiinsim Giliboa kʋkʋna baba.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Saul n da nyɛ Filistia soogianam la, dabiem da gban'e o nɛ ka o sʋnf wʋsa san'am.

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: O da bu'os Zugsɔb la ye o baŋ yɛl la an si'em, amaa Zugsɔb la da pʋ gandigi yi zaansʋŋin bɛɛ maanmaan kpɛɛm bɛɛ nɔdi'esidib san'anɛ.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Saul yʋ'ʋn da yɛl banɛ tʋmmi tisid o la ye, “Ieemi pu'a kanɛ an ba'abʋgʋd la tisim, ka m keŋ o san'anɛ m bu'osi gɔs.” Ka ba yɛl o ye, “Pu'a yinne bɛ Endo.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Ka Saul tiak o mɛŋi yɛ kparikɛɛnd. Ka yʋ'ʋŋ sisɔbir ka on nɛ dapa ayi' da duoe keŋ pu'a la san'an yɛl o ye, “Bʋgʋm ba'adi tisim, ka buol dau onɛ ka m pʋdig o yʋ'ʋr la siig ka o yina.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Amaa pu'a la lɛbis ye, “Sida fʋ mi' ye Saul kad sɔɔnb nɛ ba'akɔn dim wʋsa yis, ka bɔ ka ya bɔɔd ye ya bɛndim ka zi kum kɛɛn m zugin na?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Ka Saul pɔ ye, “Sida ka m yɛtif, si'el kʋ niŋif tʋʋm kaŋa zugɔ.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la bu'os Saul ye, “Anɔ'ɔn ka m na buol ka o yina ka fʋ bu'osɛ?” Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Buolim Samuel na!”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Pu'a la da nyɛ Samuel la, o da kaas kuŋ agɔla ka yɛl Saul ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka fʋ ma'ama? Fʋ anɛ Saul!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem. Fʋ nyɛ bɔ?” Ka pu'a la lɛbis ye, “M nyɛnɛ kpi'im ka o yit teŋin dʋt na.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os o ye, “O nwɛnɛ anɔ'ɔnɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “O anɛ bʋnkʋdʋgʋ yɛ fuwɔk.” Ka Saul baŋ ye li anɛ Samuel, ka o digin avanba ka o nindaa kpa' teŋ.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Ka Samuel bu'os Saul ye, “Bɔzug kimm ka fʋ daamim hali kɛ ka m yina?” Ka Saul lɛbis ye, “Yɛlpakiri paam hali: Filistia dim la zabid nɛ mam ka Wina'am fɛndig ka basim. O pʋ lɛn gandigidimi yit nɔdi'esidibin bɛɛ zaansʋŋinɛ. Linzug ka m buolif ye fʋ yɛlim mam na niŋ si'em.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Ka Samuel lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Nannanna Zugsɔb la sadigim fɛndig ka basif ka liebi fʋ dataa, ka bɔ ka fʋ bu'osid mam?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tʋmnɛ wʋʋ on daa dɔlis mam ni yɛl si'em la. Zugsɔb la aaɛn sʋ'ʋlim la yisi fʋ nu'ugin zaŋi tisi fʋ kpi'es la yinne. Ɛɛn, o zaŋi tis David.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Fʋn pʋ siak Zugsɔb nɔɔr ka pʋ san'am Amalek dim la wʋʋ on daa ye fʋ niŋ si'em la, dinzug ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka lina paaf zina.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na nɔk fʋn nɛ Israel wʋsa niŋ Filistia dim la nu'usin, bɛog fʋn nɛ fʋ biis la wʋsa na kpi. Zugsɔb la mɛ na kɛ ka Filistia dim na nyaŋi fʋ soogianam la.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Ka Saul kpɛn gbirigi lu avanba, ka dabiem kpɛn' o, Samuel pian'ad la zug. O paŋ wʋsa da naae nɛ, bɔzugɔ yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ la wʋsa o da pʋ di si'ela.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Pu'a la da kɛn Saul san'an na nyɛ ka o kirid la, o yɛl o ye, “Naa, gɔsima! Man kanɛ aan fʋ sankpan'as pu'ak la siaki fʋ nɔɔr ka kuosi m nyɔvʋri tʋm fʋn yɛl ye m tʋm si'el la.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Nannanna, m bɛlimnɛ wʋm tisim ka m tisif diib ka fʋ di ka paam paŋi gaadi fʋ gaadʋg.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: O da zan'as ya ka ye, “M kʋ dii.” Amaa o nidib la la'as nɛ pu'a la ka ba pian' tis o, ka o wʋm tisi ba, ka duoe teŋin la zin'in kʋk zug.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Pu'a la da mɔr na'abilpɔl yin la, ka zaŋi kɔdig, ka nɔk zɔ'ɔm maal bodobodo linɛ ka' danbinnɛ.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Ka zaŋi li tis Saul nɛ o nidib la, ka ba di. Yʋ'ʋŋ kan nɔɔ ka ba duoe gaad.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Amaa Filistia kpɛɛmnam la sʋnf daa duoe nɛ o ka ba lɛbis ye, “Kɛl ka dau la lɛbi keŋ zin'ikanɛ ka fʋ daa tis o la! Li ka' tilas ye o dɔlli ti keŋ zabaa, ka o na ti tuligi zabid nɛ ti. Fʋ zi' ye o na tun'e dɔl suokaŋa kʋʋ ti nidib la ka li ma'ae o zugdaan la sʋnfɔɔ?”

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Ka' David kanɛ ka ba mɔri yʋ'ʋmmi wa'adi yɛt ye, “‘Saul kʋʋ o tusir, ka David kʋ tusa piiga laa?’”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Dinzug Akis da buol David ka yɛl o ye, “Nɛ Wina'am onɛ vʋe la mɛnɛ, fʋ anɛ onɛ ka ti tis sida. Fʋ ya'a dɔlli m soogianam la li naan malisi nɛ m bɔzugɔ, lin pin'il daakanɛ ka fʋ kɛɛn m san'an na la ti paae zina, m pʋ nyɛ taal si'a fʋ san'anɛ. Amaa teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la pʋ siak ye fʋ pɛ'ɛsɛ.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Fɛndigim lɛbi kul nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm; da maal si'el linɛ na daam Filistia teŋ sʋ'ʋdib la sʋʋnrɛ.”

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os ye, “M maal taal bɔ ka fʋ nyɛ? Mam aan fʋ sankpan'asi bɛɛ fʋ san'an hali ti paae zina la, fʋ nyɛ taal bɔɔ m san'anɛ? Ka bɔ ka m kʋ nyaŋi keŋ zab nɛ fʋn onɛ aan m zugdaan la dataasɛ?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Ka Akis lɛbis ye, “M mi' ye fʋ an sʋm m nini ni nwɛnɛ Wina'am maliak nɛ. La'an nɛ wala, Filistia kpɛɛmnam la ye, ‘O pʋ sʋ'ʋm ye o dɔlli ti keŋ zabirin la.’

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Dinzug David nɛ o nidib la da isig bɛogʋn lɛb Filistia dim teŋin la, ka Filistia dim la keŋ dʋ Jezireel.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: David nɛ o nidib la da paae Ziklag daba atan' daar, zi' ka Amalek dim la da keŋ gbirigi zab nɛ Negef nɛ Ziklag n faaɛn ba ka nyu'oe teŋ la nɛ bugum.

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: David nɛ o nidib la da paae Ziklag na la, ba da nyɛ zin'ig la nyu'oe nɛ bugum, ka ba gban'e ba pu'ab nɛ ba biribis nɛ ba bipumisi mɔri ba gaad.

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: Li da kɛ ka David nɛ o nidib la kum hali ka paŋ ti lɛn ka' kumma.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da gban'e David pu'aba ayi' la, banɛ da an Ahinoam onɛ yi Jezireel nɛ Abigel, Nabal onɛ yi Kaamel na la pʋkɔɔnr.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: David sʋnf da san'amnɛ hali, bɔzugɔ nidib la da gban'ad nɛ ye ba lɔb o nɛ kuga. Sɔ' wʋsa sʋnf da duoe nɛ, o biribis nɛ bipumis yɛla. Amaa ka David paam kpɛmisʋg Zugsɔb onɛ aan o Wina'am la san'an.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl Abiata onɛ an maanmaan kpɛɛm ka an Ahimelek biig la ye, “Mɔr dansik la na!” Abiata da mɔri li kɛɛn o san'an na.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os Zugsɔb la ye, “M kadim banɛ kena faaɛn ti la bugirɛɛ? M na paae baa?” Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Kadimi ba bugir, ka fʋ sid na paae ba.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Ba da nyɛ Egipt nid pɔɔgin ka mɔr o kɛn David san'an na. Ba da tis o ku'om ka o nu ka tis o diib

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: linɛ da an kekama ka ba gbilim nɛ tiwala nu'ukukudis ayi' ka o di. Dau la da diya ka paŋ yʋ'ʋn kena, bɔzugɔ o da pʋ di bɛɛ nuu, daba atan' yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ wʋsa.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Ka David da bu'os o ye, “Fʋ dɔl anɔ'ɔnama, ka yaanɛ ka fʋ yina?” Ka o gandig o ye, “Mam anɛ Egipt nid, Amalek dau sɔ' yammʋg. Ban'a daa gba'am ka m zugdaan la kɛɛsimi bas daba atan' zina.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Tinamɛ daa keŋ Negef sʋ'ʋlim la zabi faaɛn Juda dim sieba banɛ an Keret nɛ Kaleb teŋ dim, ka nyaan nyu'oe Ziklag nɛ bugum la.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os o ye, “Fʋ na nyaŋi dɔllimi keŋ banɛ daa keŋ faaɛn la zin'iginɛɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Pɔɔm Wina'am ye fʋ kʋ kʋʋm bɛɛ nɔkimi tisim zugdaan la, ka m na dɔlli fʋ keŋi ba san'an.”

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: O da gaad tuonnɛ dɔl David n keŋ paae Amalek dim la, ka ba di'e zin'ig la wʋsa, dit ka nuud ka di'emid, ban nyaŋi vaae disieba yi Filistia dim teŋin nɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlimin la zug.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: David da zab nɛ ba yi bɛogʋn ti ma'ae zaam ka sɔ' pʋ pɔnsɛ, asɛɛ dasam kɔbisnaasi banɛ nyaŋi ban' yʋgʋma zɔ la ma'aa.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: David da nyaŋi di'e Amalek dim la vaae si'el la wʋsa, la'an nɛ o pu'aba ayi' la.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: David da faaɛn bʋnkʋd nɛ dasam, biribis nɛ bipumis, hali nɛ la'abanɛ ka ba nɔk la wʋsa, mɔri lɛb. Baa si'el-si'el da pʋ bɔdigɛ.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: O da faaɛn Amalek dim kɔnbid nɛ niigi la wʋsa, ka o nidib la kadi gaad tuon ka yɛt ye, “David la'adi nwa'.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Amaa nimbɛ'ɛdnam banɛ daa gɛndig David nidib la ka ieed yɛla la da yɛl ye, “Bam pʋ nyaŋi keŋ nɛ tinam la, ti kʋ pʋdig la'abanɛ ka ti di'e la sieba tisi ba, amaa sɔ' wʋsa lɛɛ tun'e nɔk o mɛŋ pu'a nɛ o biisi keŋ.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛbisi yɛl ye, “Ayei, da maalinɛ ala nɛ bʋnkanɛ ka Zugsɔb la tisi ti la. Onɛ nɔk banɛ kena zab nɛ ti la niŋi ti nu'usin ka ti nyaŋi ba.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Anɔ'ɔnɛ na kɛlis yanamɛ yɛt si'el la? Onɛ kpɛlim gur la'ad la nɛ onɛ keŋ zabir la pʋʋr na an yinne. Ba zan' na pʋdig azinzema.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: David da yɛl nɔɔrɛ digil, ka li an malʋŋʋ tis Israel hali ti paae zina.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: David n da paae Ziklag na la, o da yis la'ad la sieba tis Juda kpɛɛmnam banɛ da aan o zuanam la ka yɛl ye, “Ya piini nwa' la'abama yinɛ Zugsɔb dataasin la na.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Filistia dim da zab nɛ Israel dim la Giliboa zuor la zugʋ nyaŋi kʋʋ ba pamm, ka banɛ kpɛlim la zɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da mu'oe nini hali Saul nɛ o biis la yɛla; ba da kʋʋ o biis Jonatan nɛ Abinadab nɛ Malikisua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Zaba la da ɔnsig nɛ hali gɛɛl Saul, ka tiratɔɔndib la da nyaŋi tɔn Saul n pu'alim o bɛ'ɛd bɛ'ɛdi.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Saul da yɛl onɛ ziid o zaba la'ad la ye, “Fuomi fʋ sʋ'ʋg la kunsimi kʋ, ya'a ka' ala nimbanɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋ nwa' na kena n kunsimi kʋ ka li lieb nyannɛ tisim.” Amaa o zaba la'aziid la da zɔt dabiem ka pʋ siaki niŋ ala. Ka Saul fuoe o mɛŋ sʋ'ʋgʋ ba'a teŋin ka bas o mɛŋi lii li zugʋ kpi.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Zaba la'aziid la nyɛ ka Saul kpi la, ka on mɛ fuoe o sʋ'ʋgʋ ba', ka mɛ bas o mɛŋi li zug ka ba wʋsa la'am kpi daar yinne.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Saul nɛ o biis atan' la nɛ onɛ ziid o zaba la'ad, nɛ o nidib la wʋsa da la'am kpinɛ daar yinne.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Israel dim banɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔfaligin nɛ banɛ lɔ'ɔŋi bɛ Joodan baba la, nyɛ Israel soogianam la zɔ ka Saul nɛ o biis la wʋsa kpi la, ba da duoe zɔ ka basi ba tɛɛns la. Ka Filistia dim la di'e lii zin'in.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ nie ka Filistia dim la kena ye ba yɛɛs banɛ kpi la fuud la, ka nyɛ Saul nɛ o biis atan' la dig Giliboa zuor la zug.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Jabis Gilead nidib la da wʋm Filistia dim la maal Saul niŋgbiŋ la si'em la,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: ba nimbanɛ sʋnfʋ kpi'em ka ba pʋ lɛbid nya'aŋ zaba ni la da duoe keŋ Betsean yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ yak Saul nɛ o biis la niŋgbina lɛb Jabis n nyu'oe ba.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Ka nɔki ba kɔnba la pin' tisi'a gbinnin Jabis teŋin, ka lɔ nɔɔr daba ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Na'ab Saul kum la nya'aŋ, David da nyaŋ Amalek dim ka lɛb Ziklag teŋin na, ka kpɛlim ani daba ayi'.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Daba atan' la daar ka dau sɔ' yi Saul nɛ o nidibi la'as zin'isi'a zaba ni la kena, ka o fuud aans ka o zug wʋsa an uusʋg ka li pa'al o sʋnsa'aŋ. On da paae David san'an na la ka igin teŋin na'as o.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os o ye, “Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Man yinɛ Israel dim la'asʋg la zin'igini su'a zɔɔ kena.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os o ya'as ye, “Yɛlimim, bɔɔ maalɛ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Nidib la zɔɔ widig zabbɔn'ɔgin la ka nidib bɛdegʋ kpi. Saul nɛ o biig Jonatan mɛ kpiya.”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Man bɛɛn nɛ Giliboa zuorin la ka Saul mɛ bɛɛ anina ka nɔk o kpan nɛ ti'il ka dɛlli li, ka zabzabidib nɛ ba zaba tɛrekonam la'asi gilig o.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Ka on gi'e gɔsi nyɛɛm la ka buolim, ka m bu'os o ye, ‘Fʋ bɔɔd ye m maal bɔɔ tisi fɔ?’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'osim ye, ‘Fʋ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ?’ Ka m lɛbis o ye, ‘Amalek nid.’

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, ‘Li'elim na kʋʋ m, ka mam pu'alim si'em la m pʋ lɛn lal nɛ kum amaa ka lɛɛ nan vʋe.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Ka m li'el o san'ani kʋʋ o bɔzugɔ, m mi' ye on sadigim pu'alim dig si'em la o kʋ nyaŋi vʋ'ʋgɛ. Din ka man nɔk na'am zupibig la o zugin, nɛ baŋ kanɛ bɛɛ o nu'ugin la mɔri kena ye m tisi m zugdaan.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ka David nɛ banɛ bɛɛ anina la wʋsa yɛɛsi ba fuud la aans sʋnsa'aŋ zug.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Ka ba kum ka lɔ nɔɔr Saul nɛ o biig Jonatan yɛla ti paae zaam, nɛ Zugsɔb nimbanɛ an Israel dim la yɛla, ban kʋʋ ba wʋsa zaba ni la zug.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os dau kanɛ yɛl o Saul kum la ye, “Fʋ yi ya na?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Man anɛ Amalek nid.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl ye, “Fʋ ziim na kpɛlimmi fʋ mɛŋ zugin, lin sadigim yii fʋ mɛŋ nɔɔrin na di kasɛt ye fʋnɛ kʋ onɛ ka Zugsɔb gaŋ ka bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zug la.” David sʋnsa'aŋ yʋʋm

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: David da yʋ'ʋm yʋʋm kaŋa Na'ab Saul nɛ o biig Jonatan yɛla.

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: Ka tis nɔɔr ye ba pa'alim Juda dim yʋʋm kaŋa, ka ba buoli li ye, Tuk Yʋʋm, ka ba sɔbi li Jaser gbauŋʋn la, ye,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “Ya girima dim la kpii dig la, Giliboa zuoya la zug ka ya kpi'euŋ la naae.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Da yɛli li yɛla Gaf teŋinɛ, mɛ da mɔɔnnɛ li yɛla Askɛlon suoya la nii. Ka Filistia dim pu'ayuos sʋnf na ma'ae ka banɛ pʋ kpɛn' baŋʋ la pu'asada maal sumalisim.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Kai! Giliboa zuorɛ, mɛligim kʋ luu fʋ zugin bɛɛ saa nii, bɛɛ pɔɔd banɛ maan zʋʋd la lɛn du'a ya'asɛ! Bɔzugɔ ani ka ba san'am kpi'euŋ sɔb la gbanti'edʋg, Ba kʋ lɛn suoɛn Saul zaba gbanti'edʋg la nɛ kpaam.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Saul nɛ Jonatan da nyaŋidi ba dataas, Ba da kʋʋd kpi'emnam saŋa wʋsa: Jonatan tiraug la nan zi' lɛb zaalim, Saul sʋ'ʋraug la nan zi' lɛb ka o sʋnf pʋ ma'ae.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Saul nɛ Jonatan daa nɔŋ taaba ban daa vʋe la, la'an nɛ kum zin'igin ba pʋ wɛligɛ. Ba daa zɔti gat siligʋ na ian'ad ka mɔr paŋi gat gbigim.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: Yanam Israel pu'ayuosɛ, kummi Saul yɛla onɛ nɔk na'abiis fuudi yɛɛli ya ka pili ya nɛ sanlima la'avɛnla la.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Israel dima wʋmmiya, ya kpi'euŋ la naae ya; Jonatan n kpii dig Giliboa zuoya zug la.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: M ba'abiig Jonatan, m sʋnf san'ami fʋ yɛla; fʋ daa anɛ onɛ paae m ya'am. Fʋn daa nɔŋim si'em la anɛ nyalima, li daa anɛ nyalima hali gat pu'ab nɔŋilim.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Israel dima, ya kpi'euŋ la naae ya! Zaba la'ad la wʋsa bɔdig ya!”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Li da paae saŋsi'a ka David bu'os Zugsɔb la ye, “M kem Juda tɛɛns la yinne ni zin'inɛɛ?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, o kem. Ka David lɛm bu'os ye, “Yaanɛ ka m na keŋɛ?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Kem Hebron teŋin.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Alazug David da duoe nɛ o pu'aba ayi', Ahinoam onɛ yi Jezireel na la nɛ Abigel onɛ an Nabal pʋkɔɔnr ka yi Kaamel na la.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: David mɛ da nɔk dap banɛ bɛɛ o san'an la ban nɛ ba yidimi mɔri ba keŋ zin'in Hebron nɛ tembanɛ bɛɛ anina la.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Juda dim da kenɛ Hebron na nɔk malʋŋ kpaam bu'oe niŋ David zug, ka diis o na'am, ye o an Juda dim na'ab. David n pian' tis Jabis Gilead dim la yɛla Ban daa yɛl Na'ab David ye Jabis Gilead dimi mum Saul la,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: o da tʋm nidibi yɛli ba ye, “Zugsɔb albareka na bɛ nɛ ya. Yanamɛ maal sʋm ka mum Saul onɛ aan ya zugdaan la.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la mɛ na maali ya sʋm ka pa'ali ya o sida an si'em ka mam mɛ na maali ya ala, yanamɛ tʋm tʋʋm sʋŋ si'a la zug.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Nannanna kpɛ'ɛŋimini ya mɛŋ, ka kpɛ'ɛŋi ya sʋnf, ka ya zugdaan Saul kpiya, ka Juda dim diis man na'am ye m aan ba na'ab.” Isibosef n di Israel na'am la yɛla

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Abner onɛ an Nier biig ka an Saul zabzabidib kpɛɛm la da nɔk Isibosef onɛ an Saul biig la mɔr o kɛn Mahanam teŋin na,

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: ka diis o na'am anina, ye o sʋ'oe Gilead nɛ Aser nɛ Jezireel la'an nɛ Efiram nɛ Benjamin nɛ Israel wʋsa.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: David mɛ da bɛ nɛ Hebron teŋin ka di Juda na'am yʋma ayɔpɔi nɛ nwadis ayuobʋ. Tanp nwɛ'ɛb yɛla

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Abner onɛ an Nier biig la da la'as nɛ Isibosef onɛ an Saul biig la nidib ka yi Mahanam keŋ Gibeon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Ka Joab onɛ an Zeruyia biig la nɛ David nidib da yii tʋ'ʋsi ba Gibeon bɛuŋin la. Ka bama zi'e bɛuŋ la nɔɔrin ka bama la mɛ bɛ gbɛkaŋa la sa.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Ka Abner yɛl Joab ye, “Ti kɛl ka na'akim la sieba duoe zab taaba ka ti gɔs.” Ka Joab lɛbis ye, “Li anɛ sida; kɛl ka ba zab.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Ka ba duoe zi'en ka ba kaal Benjamin nɛ Isibosef onɛ an Saul biig la nidib pii nɛ ayi', ka mɛ kaal David nidib pii nɛ ayi'.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Ka sɔ' wʋsa gban'e o bi'em zug, ka nɔk zaba sʋ'ʋgʋ kʋns o lʋgiri vɛ'ɛg o lɛbis o tuon, ka ba la'am lu teŋin. Dinzug ka ba buon Gibeon teŋ la zin'ikan ye, Helkaf Hazzurim.

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Daakan la zaba la da mu'oe nɛ galis ka David nidib la zabi nyaŋ Abner nɛ Israel dim la wʋsa.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Zeruyia biribis atan' la mɛ da bɛɛ ani: Joab nɛ Abisai nɛ Asahel. Asahel nɔba da kpi'em nɛ zɔɔgʋ nwɛnɛ walig nɛ.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Ka Abner zɔt ka gi'e nya'aŋi gɔs ka bu'os ye, “Fʋnɛ laa, Asahel?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, manɛ la!”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Ka Abner yɛl o ye, “Fɛndigimi fʋ dagɔbʋg bɛɛ fʋ datiuŋʋ gban'e na'akim la yinne faaɛn o zaba la'ad la wʋsa.” Ka Asahel zan'as ka kpɛn kad o.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abner da lɛn sa'al Asahel ye, “Basim ka da kati ma; bɔɔ na kɛ ka man nwɛ' fʋ basɛ? Ka m ya'a niŋ ala m na niŋ wala gɔsi fʋ bier Joab nindaanɛ?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Amaa Asahel da zan'as ka kpɛn dɔl o. Alazug Abner da lɛbis o kpan la nya'aŋi kʋns Asahel pʋʋr ka li tɔligi yii o nya'aŋ. Ka o kpɛn lii anina kpi. Ka onɛ wʋsa gat ka paae zin'ikanɛ ka Asahel lii kpi la, asɛɛ ka o zi'en.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Amaa Joab nɛ Abisai da kpɛn kad Abner, winnigi ti bɔɔd kpɛn'ɛb la, ka ba paae Amma kʋkʋn kanɛ kpi'e teŋ kanɛ buon Gia, ka ba dɔl anina ken Gibeon teŋ sian'arin la.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Benjamin nidib la da zi'en Abner nya'aŋ ka ba la'as gumm zi'e kʋkʋn la zug.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Ka Abner buol Joab ye, “Ti na kpɛn kʋʋd taaba saŋa wʋsaa? Fʋ zi' ye din na zi dataadʋg naa? Bʋndaar ka fʋ na kɛ ka ba basi ba ba'abiis la kadibɔ?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Ka Joab lɛbis ye, “Wina'am ma'aa mi' dinɛ naan niŋin fʋ ya'a pʋ pian'anɛ, nidib la naan kpɛn katinɛ ba ba'abiis la hali ka bɛog ti nie.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Alazug ka Joab pieb na'atan, ka nidib la wʋsa gu'oe ka pʋ lɛn kad Israel dim la, ka mɛ pʋ lɛn zabɛ.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan wʋsa Abner nɛ o nidib la da keŋ paae Araba. Ba da lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la, dɔlisi yi Bitron teŋin paae Mahanam teŋin.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Ani ka Joab lɛb ka pʋ lɛn kad Abner ya'asɛ, ka buol o nidib la wʋsa la'as. David nidib la pii nɛ awai da kpi ka Asahel pʋ paasi.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Ba da mum Asahel nɛ o saam yaʋgʋn Betilehem teŋin. Ka Joab nɛ o nidib la keŋ yʋ'ʋŋ la wʋsa nie bɛogʋ paae Hebron teŋin na.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Saul nɛ David yidimi da zabid nɛ taaba saŋa si'a la, Abner da kpɛ'ɛŋid ye o nyɛ zi'esim Saul yin la.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Saul da mɔr pu'abil ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Rizipa, o da anɛ Aya pu'ayua. Isibosef da yɛl Abner ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ digin nɛ m saam pu'abila?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Abner sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ hali Isibosef n yɛl si'el la zug, ka o lɛbis ye, “Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye m anɛ yalim Juda dɔɔg la nii? Man zi'enɛ fʋ saam nɛ o yidim nɛ o zuanam yɛla hali ti paae zina, ka pʋ nɔki ya niŋ David nu'uginɛ. La'an nɛ wala fʋ yɛlim ye m tʋm bɛ'ɛd nɛ pu'a kaŋa!

english_verse: I ask God to punish me if I don't help David get what the Lord promised him!
translation_verse: M pɔya! Zugsɔb maalimim on bɔɔd si'em man Abner ya'a pʋ tʋm tis David wʋʋ Zugsɔb la zi'el o si'em,

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: ka tiak Saul na'am la diis David ka o sʋ'oe Israel nɛ Juda tɛɛns wʋsa din yi Dan hali ti paae Beerseba teŋin la!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Isibosef da pʋ lɛn ya'ae nɔɔri yɛl Abner si'ela bɔzugɔ o da zɔt o nɛ dabiem.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Abner da tʋm nidib David san'an yɛl o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ sʋ'oe teŋ la? Maalim nɔɔr yinne nɛ man ka m na sʋŋi mɔr Israel wʋsa lɛbi fʋ san'an na.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: David da lɛbis o ye, “Li an sʋ'ʋŋa. M na maal nɔɔr yinne nɛf. Amaa bʋn yinne ka m bɔɔd ye fʋ maal. Da kɛɛn m san'an naa, asɛɛ ka fʋ mɔr Mikal onɛ an Saul pu'ayua la kɛn na tisim.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: David da tʋm yɛl Isibosef onɛ an Saul biig la ye, “M bɔɔdi m pu'a Mikal onɛ ka m da di ka kʋ Filistia dim kɔbiga ka nwaasi ba yu'ogbana kena tis ka li an pu'asʋl la.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Isibosef da tʋm faaɛn pu'a la o sid la san'an onɛ an Paltiel ka an Lais biig la.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Ka o sid la dɔl o nya'aŋi kaasid hali ti paae Bahurim. Ka Abner yɛl o ye, “Lɛm kul,” ka o lɛbi kul.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Abner da nwɛ' Israel dim kpɛɛmnam la sɔɔra ka yɛl ye, “Ya daa pʋn bɔɔd ye ya diis David na'am.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Nannanna niŋimin ala! Zugsɔb la da zi'el David nɔɔr ye, ‘M tʋmtʋm David zug, m na faaɛn Israel nidib Filistia dim nɛ ba bi'emnam wʋsa nu'usin.’”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abner mɛŋ da pian' tis Benjamin dɔɔg la dim. Ka keŋ Hebron David san'ani tu'as o Israel dim nɛ Benjamin nidib la wʋsa bɔɔd ye ba niŋ si'em.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Abner onɛ mɔr nidib pisi la da keŋ David san'an Hebron teŋin, ka David maal on nɛ o nidib la saauŋ.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Abner da yɛl David ye, “M zugdaan na'aba, kɛl ka m keŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ la'as Israel dim la naa tisif, ka ba na la'asi fʋ san'an na niŋ nɔɔr yinne. Ka fʋ na sʋ'oe ba paae fʋn bɔɔd si'em bɛn nɛ sumalisim.” David da kɛɛs Abner ka o lɛb nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la nɔɔ ka Joab dɔl David nidib la yi zaba la ni lɛb Hebron teŋin na nɛ ya'an, ban nyaŋ zaba la ka faaɛn la'ad bɛdegʋ la zug. Amaa Abner da pʋ lɛm bɛɛ ani bɔzugɔ David da kɛɛs o ka o keŋ nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Joab nɛ o zabzabidib la da paae na la, ka yɛl o ye Abner onɛ an Nier biig la kɛn Na'ab la san'an na ka lɛb nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Ka Joab keŋ na'ab la san'ani yɛl o ye, “Bɔɔ nwa' ka fʋ maalɛ? Gɔsima! Abner kɛɛn fʋ san'an na la, bɔ ka fʋ bas o? Nannanna o gaadya.

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Fʋ mi' ye Abner onɛ an Nier biig la kenɛ na ye o ma'aa fʋ kpansi baŋi fʋ ken zin'ig nɛ fʋn tʋm si'em wʋsa.” Joab n kʋ Abner si'em

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Ka Joab bas David ka tʋm buol Abner, ka ba buol o Sira buligin la lɛb na. Amaa David da pʋ baŋɛ.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Abner n da lɛb Hebron na la, ka Joab dɔl o yi za'anɔɔr la baba ka niŋ wʋʋ o bɔɔdi ye o pian' si'eli tis on ma'aa amaa ka kpɛn kʋns o pʋʋri kʋʋ o yɔɔ o pitʋ Asahel sam.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Li nya'aŋ ka David ti wʋmi li yɛla ka yɛl ye, “Man nɛ m sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa kʋdim zi' Abner onɛ an Nier biig la kum la yɛla baa bi'ela.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: O ziim na kpɛlim Joab zugin, on nɛ o saam yidim la wʋsa. Joab nɛ o yidim la wʋsa na mɔr fɛn'ɛdi ba niŋgbina ni, bɛɛ kʋkɔm ban'as na mɔri ba, ka sieba na an tadimbʋʋs, ka sieba na kpi tanpin ka sieba kɔ'ɔŋ diibi di.”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Joab nɛ o ba'abiig Abisai da kʋ Abner, on da kʋʋ ba pitʋ Asahel zabbɔn'ɔgin Gibeon teŋin la zug.

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl Joab nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ anina la ye, “Aansimi ya fuud ka yɛ bɔto fuudi pa'ali ya sʋnsa'aŋ, ka kum dɔl Abner tuonnɛ gaad.” Na'ab David mɛŋ da dɔl sɔnduoya la baba gaad.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Ba da mum Abner nɛ Hebron teŋin, ka na'ab la mɛŋ kaasid agɔla gɔla. Ka nidib la wʋsa mɛ kum.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la yʋ'ʋm yʋʋm kaŋa tis Abner, ye, “Li nar ye Abner kpi wʋʋ yalimm?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Ba pʋ lɔɔ fʋ nu'usɛ, ka fʋ nɔba mɛ pʋ lɔ nɛ baansɛ. Fʋ kpinɛ wʋʋ nimbɛ'ɛdnamɛ gu' fʋ kʋnɛ.” Ka nidib la lɛn kum o yɛla ya'as.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la wʋsa la'as na bɛllim David ye o di diib ka li nam pʋ sɔbɛ. Amaa ka David pɔ ye, “M pɔya ye, man ya'a di si'el ka winnig nam pʋ lii Wina'am kʋʋmim, asɛɛ ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb.”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Nidib la wʋsa da kpansi li ka ba sʋnf ma'ae li yɛla. Sida, na'ab la maal si'em la wʋsa da ma'ae ba sʋʋnr.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Daakan la ka nidib la nɛ Israel dim wʋsa baŋ ye na'ab la nu'ug kae Abner onɛ an Nier biig la kuminɛ.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la yɛl o nidib la ye, “Ya pʋ baŋ ye tuongat nɛ nintita'ar kpi Israel teŋin zinaa?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Zina nwa', la'an nɛ ban bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋim zug ka diisim na'am la m tadig nɛ, ka Zeruyia biis la kpi'emi gati m. Zugsɔb la na yɔ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb wʋʋ o tʋʋma an si'em.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Isibosef onɛ an Saul biig la da wʋm ye Abner kpi Hebron la, o giinla da siɛnnɛ, ka Israel dim wʋsa ya'am iank.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: Dapa ayi' nwa' da yii keŋ Isibosef yin, paae anina nintaŋ ka o digi vʋ'ʋsid. Ka ba kpɛn' zakin wʋʋ ba bɔɔdi ki nɛ, ka o nam bɛɛ o dɔɔgin la dig gadʋg zug. Ka ba kpɛn kʋns o pʋʋri tabil teŋin. Ban da kʋns o kʋʋ naae la, ka fi'ig o zugʋ su'a mɔri gaad.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Ba da mɔr Isibosef zugʋ keŋ Hebron n tis Na'ab David ka yɛl o ye, “Na'aba, fʋ dataa Isibosef onɛ an Saul biig la zugʋ nwa'. Fʋ dataa onɛ daa mɔɔd ye o kʋʋf la. Zina Zugsɔb la yɔ Saul nɛ o biis la samme tis fʋn onɛ aan ti zugdaan la.”

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Ala ka dau sɔ' daa kena yɛlim ye, ‘Saul kpiya,’ ka tɛn'ɛs ye o mɔri labasʋŋʋ kena yɛlim ka m kɛ ka ba kʋʋ o Ziklag teŋin,

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: ka kɛl nimbɛ'ɛdnamɛ na keŋ sɔ' yinnɛ kʋ o, o mɛŋ gadʋg zugɔ? Li nar ye m kʋʋ ya yɔ o sam ka kɛ ka teŋ la digin baanlimm.”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: David da tis o nidib la nɔɔr ka ba kʋʋ ba, ka fi'isi ba nu'us nɛ ba nɔba ka nɔki ba niŋgbina ya'al Hebron bɛuŋ baba. Amaa ka nɔk Isibosef zugʋ mum Abner yaʋgʋn Hebron teŋin.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Taya Na'ab Hiram da tʋm nidib Na'ab David san'an ka tis o na'aziinr daad nɛ kampintanam nɛ banɛ mi' kuga mɛɛb ka ba mɛ' na'ayiri tis David.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Hebron teŋin ka o da bɛ ka sʋ'oe Juda yʋma ayɔpɔi nɛ nwadis ayuobʋ, ka zin'in Jerusalem teŋin sʋ'oe Israel nɛ Juda wʋsa yʋma pistan' nɛ atan'. Jerusalem da lieb David teŋ tita'ar la yɛla

english_verse: David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.” That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.” David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east.
translation_verse: David da keŋ zin'in teŋ la kpi'euŋ zin'ikanɛ ka o zabi nyaŋ la ni, ka ba buonnɛ li ye, David Tempʋʋg la. Ka o mɛ' zaŋguom kanɛ mɔr paŋi giligi li ka yʋ'ʋn mɛ' ya' bɛdegʋ ka li kilim tempʋʋg.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Na'ab la nɛ o nidib da duoe keŋ Jerusalem tempʋʋgin ye ba zab nɛ Jebus dim banɛ bɛɛ anina la. Jebus dim la da yɛl David ye, “Fʋ kʋ nyaŋi kpɛn' kpɛla naa, hali zʋnzɔɔs nɛ pɔnda na zabi kadi fʋ yis.” Ban da tɛn'ɛs ye, “David kʋ nyaŋi kpɛn' naa.”

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Ka o kpi'euŋ la yʋ'ʋn maligim zu'oe hali, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la da bɛ nɛ o. David nɛ Hiram dim naal nɔɔr

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: David da baŋ ye Zugsɔb la kɛ ka o na'am la zi'en kiŋ-kiŋ Israel sʋ'ʋlimin, ka dʋ'ʋsi li o nidib Israel dim yɛla. David n du'a biis Jerusalem teŋin

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: David n da duoe yi Hebron teŋin la nya'aŋ, o da di pu'ab Jerusalem teŋinɛ paas. Ka du'a biribis nɛ bipumisi paas.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: Ibiha nɛ Elisua nɛ Nefeg nɛ Jafia nɛ

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: Elisama nɛ Eliada nɛ Elifelet. David n nyaŋ Filistia dim la yɛla (

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da wʋm ye David di Israel na'am la, ka duoe nɛ ba zabzabidibi keŋ ieed o. Amaa David n da wʋm la ka duoe sigi kpɛn' zin'ikanɛ ka ba mɛ' ka li aan ba kpi'euŋ zin'ig la.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Ka Filistia dim la kena yadig Refa Dim Bɔn'ɔgin la wʋsa.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os Zugsɔb la ye, “M kem zab nɛ Filistia dim laa? Fʋ na zaŋi ba niŋi m nu'usinɛɛ?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Kem, ka m sid na zaŋ Filistia dim la niŋi fʋ nu'usin.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Ka David keŋ Baal Perazim, anina ka o nyaŋi ba. O da yɛl ye, “Nwɛnɛ ku'om tansid si'em la, ala ka Zugsɔb la mɛ tans na nyaŋi m dataas.” Dinzug ka ba buon anina ye Baal Perazim ka li gbin pa'al ye, Zugsɔb la Tans Na.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da basi ba bada anina, ka David nɛ o nidib la vaae ba gaad.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Saŋa yinne ya'as ka Filistia dim la kena yadig Refa Dim Bɔn'ɔgin la wʋsa.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os Zugsɔb la ka o lɛbis ye, “Da kpa' keŋ zab nɛ ba, amaa kem gaadi giligi ba nya'aŋi paae tibanɛ zi'e anina la baba pin'ili zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a ti wʋm ka li nwɛnɛ nidib nɔba nɔɔdi dammid tiis la zugin, fʋn duom tɔ'ɔtɔ bʋʋli ba. Bɔzugɔ li pa'al ye mam Zugsɔb la gaadi fʋ tuon ye m zab nɛ Filistia dim zabzabidib la.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ka David maal wʋʋ Zugsɔb la yɛl o si'em la, ka kʋ Filistia dim la wʋsa din yi Gibeon paae Giza.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Banɛ da ziid Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la ya'a yak nɔba ayuobʋ, o kʋʋdnɛ lɔlig nɛ na'apɔlli maal maan.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: David da yɛnɛ dansik ma'aa wa'ad Zugsɔb la tuon nɛ o sʋnf wʋsa.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Ka on nɛ Israel dim wʋsa mɔr Zugsɔb daka la kena ka tansid agɔl gɔla ka piebid na'atana.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb daka la ti kpɛn'ɛd David teŋin la, ka Mikal onɛ an Saul pu'ayua la gɔsid takoro ni. Ka on nyɛ David n wa'ad Zugsɔb la tuon si'em la o nɛ'ɛs o, o sʋʋnrin.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Ka ba nɔk Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la niŋ tɛreko paallin, mɔri yi Abinadab yin dinɛ bɛ kʋkʋn zug la. Uzaa nɛ Ahio banɛ an Abinadab biis la da dɔlisid tɛreko la

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: ka on nɛ o nidib la da naam Baala teŋ kanɛ bɛ Juda teŋgbauŋʋn la ye ba mɔr Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la lɛb Jerusalem na. Ba da buon Daka la nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr ye, Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb. Onɛ bɛ Kerubnam la zugin ka Wina'am girima nɛ o paŋ bɛɛ ba teŋsʋk.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: ka Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la bɛɛ li zug, ka Ahio gaadi li tuon.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: David nɛ Israel nidib la wʋsa da maannɛ sumalisim nɛ ba sʋʋnr wʋsa Zugsɔb la tuon. Ba da yʋ'ʋmnɛ ka piebid wiis ka nwɛ'ɛd googinam nɛ siyada.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Ban da paae Nakon zieŋin la, Uzaa da gban'e Wina'am daka la bɔzugɔ niigi la da tu'ug nɛ ka daka la bɔɔd liib.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋnf da duoe nɛ Uzaa, on pʋ tis Zugsɔb daka la na'asi la zug. Wina'am da nwɛ' o bas ka o kpi Zugsɔb daka la baba,

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Ka David sʋnf pɛlig bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la sʋnpɛɛn da lu Uzaa zug. Ka din yi saŋkanɛ paae zina ba buon zin'ikan la ye Perez Uzaa.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: David da zɔ Zugsɔb la dabiem daakan la, ka yɛl ye, “M ye m niŋ wala ka mɔr Zugsɔb daka la kuli m san'an na?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: O da pʋ bɔɔd ye o siaki di'e Zugsɔb daka la ka li keŋ David Teŋinɛ. Ka lɛɛ mɔri li keŋ Obededom onɛ an Gaf nid la yin.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl na'ab David ye, “Zugsɔb la niŋ Obededom nɛ o yidim nɛ on mɔr si'el wʋsa albareka, ka li anɛ Zugsɔb daka la zug.” Ka David keŋ Obededom yinnɛ nɔk Zugsɔb daka la mɔri keŋ David Teŋin ka maal sumalisim.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Ka ba mɔr Zugsɔb daka la na kpɛn'ɛs Fuug Sʋgʋr kanɛ ka David ti' li yɛla la. Ka David maal maana linɛ nyu'od nɛ bugum nɛ taaba la'asʋg maana Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Ka nɔk bodobodo nɛ tiwala pʋdig Israel dim la wʋsa pu'ab nɛ dap. Ka nidib la wʋsa lɛbi kuli ba yaan.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ David da lɛb yin ye o niŋ o yidim albareka, ka Mikal onɛ an Saul pu'ayua la yina tʋ'ʋs o ka yɛl ye, “Zina Israel na'ab la maal o mɛŋi bɛɛ o kɔn'! O yaal o mɛŋ sankpan'asnam nɛ pu'asada tuon nwɛnɛ ninyɔɔdi niŋid si'em.”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: David da yɛl Mikal ye, “Li anɛ Zugsɔb la tuon ka m wa'ad. Onɛ gaŋim ka basi fʋ saam nɛ o yidim wʋsa, ka zaŋimi zi'el ye m gur o nidib Israel dim la. M na maal sumalisim Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: M na maligim maali m mɛŋ ninyaalig ka diisi m mɛŋ nyan hali gaad ala. Amaa li ya'a anɛ sankpan'asnam nɛ pu'asada la yɛla, man nan kpɛm mɔri m na'asi la!”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: amaa m nɔŋilim la kʋ yii o san'an wʋʋ man yisi li Saul onɛ daa bɛɛ fʋ tuon la san'an si'em la.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: o da yɛl Natan onɛ an nɔdi'es la ye, “Man na niŋ wala bɛ na'ayin ka ba maali li nɛ na'aziinr vɛnliŋa, ka Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la gbɛɛnd sʋgʋrinɛ?”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Ka Natan lɛbis ye, “Fʋn mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛsi'a fʋ sʋnfʋn la an sʋm. Kem tuonnɛ tʋmi li, ka Zugsɔb la na bɛ nɛf!”

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: Kem yɛli m tʋmtʋm David ye man Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, Li anɛ fʋnɛ na mɛ' yiri tis mam ka m kpɛn'ɛ?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Din yi man da yis Israel dim Egipt teŋin paae zina, mam pʋ gbɛn yinnɛ. Mam da bɛ nɛ sʋgʋrin yanamɛ da paae teŋ si'a wʋsa.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Man ken nɛ Israel dim la, m nam zi' bu'os banɛ aan ba tuongatib ka m gaŋ ye ba guri m nidib Israel la ye, “Bɔ ka ya pʋ nɔk na'aziinr daadi mɛ' yiri tisi ma?”

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛn yɛl ye, “Tɔ', nannanna, yɛlimi m tʋmtʋm David ye man Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛt si'eli nwa' ye, ‘M zaŋif nɛ yi kɔnbkemmin na n kɛ ka fʋ lieb na'abi guri m nidib Israel dim la.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: M dɔlli fʋ ken, fʋn keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa, ka kadi fʋ dataasi yisi fʋ tuon. Nannanna m na maalif nintita'ar, nwɛnɛ nintitada banɛ bɛ dunia nwa' nii an si'em la.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: M na tis Israel dim banɛ aan m nidib la zin'ig, ka na zin'ili ba ka ba na mɔri ba mɛŋ teŋ ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn daami ba ya'asɛ. Nimbɛ'ɛdnam kʋ lɛm mugusi ba wʋʋ ban da niŋid si'em pin'ilʋgʋn la.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Fʋ dabisa la bɛn ya'a ti paae, ka fʋ tig sa'ab, m na kɛ ka fʋ biig yinne duoe naa di'e fʋ zi'esim. O na yinɛ fʋ mɛŋ niŋgbiŋin na. M na kɛ ka o na'am la zi'en.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Oŋa an onɛ na mɛ' yir man yʋ'ʋr zug. M na kɛ ka o na'am saŋa kʋ mɔr bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Man na aan o saam ka o mɛ aan m biig. O ya'a tʋm bɛ'ɛd m na kɛ ka nidib tɛk o tʋbir,

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am, fʋ nie nɛ'ɛŋa tis man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la yɛl ye, ‘M na mɛ' yiri tisif.’ Alazug ka m kpɛ'ɛŋi m mɛŋi zaŋid winsɔsʋg nwaa tisidif.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab David duoe kpɛn' zin'in Zugsɔb la tuon ka yɛl ye, “Man aan anɔ'ɔnɛ, Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔba, ka man yin la mɛ an bɔ ka fʋ dʋ'ʋsim ka mɔrim hali paae zina?

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Man David na lɛn yɛlif ye bɔ? Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔba, bɔzugɔ fʋ mi'im, ka m aan fʋ tʋmtʋm.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Fʋn zi'el si'em nɛ fʋ bɔɔdim la zug, fʋ maal bʋntita'akaŋa ka nie li pa'al man onɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la.
