english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: “M Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔba! Sɔ' lɛn kae nwɛnɛ fɔ. Win si'a mɛ lɛn kae asɛɛ fʋn ma'aa. Ti wʋm ya nɛ ti mɛŋ tʋba ka li an sida.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Anɔ'ɔnɛ lɛn nwɛnɛ fʋ nidib Israel dima? Fʋnɛ da faaɛn ba yis ban da an yammis Egipt teŋin la, ye ba aan fʋ din. Fʋ da tʋm bʋnnyalima ka kadi ba dataas nɛ ba wina yis ka tisi ba teŋ sʋŋ ka fʋ yʋ'ʋr paam girima.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, fʋnɛ zin'ili fʋ nidib Israel dim ka ba aan fʋ mɛŋ din, saŋa dinɛ ka' bɛnnɛ, ka liebi ba Wina'am.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Ala ka fʋ na mɔr yʋ'ʋtita'ar saŋa wʋsa. Ka nidib na yɛl ye, Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la anɛ Israel Wina'am; ka man David yir la na zi'enɛ fʋ tuon, man aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la zug.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔba, fʋ anɛ Wina'am. Fʋ pian'ad wʋsa anɛ sida gʋllim, ka fʋ zi'el nɔsʋŋʋ tisim.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Nannanna li ya'a pie fʋ pʋʋg, fʋ niŋim man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la yir albareka ka kɛ ka li kpɛn yaligidi ken tuon saŋa wʋsa. Fʋn Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian' li, ka fʋ bareka tisib pʋʋginɛ, man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la na mɔri fʋ albareka saŋa wʋsa.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Benaya onɛ an Jehoyada biig la da sʋ'oe Keret dim nɛ Pelet dim. Ka David biis la an o na'ayikpɛm.

english_verse: David also defeated the Moabites. Then he made their soldiers lie down on the ground, and he measured them off with a rope. He would measure off two lengths of the rope and have those men killed, then he would measure off one length and let those men live. The people of Moab had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him.
translation_verse: David mɛ da nyaŋ Moab dim la. On da nyaŋi ba naae la, o da kɛ ka ba digin teŋin tʋn taaba ka o nɔk nwiigi maki ba. O ya'a mak nwiig la zin'isa ayi', o kʋʋdi ba nɛ, amaa makir kanɛ paas atan' la o basidi ba nɛ. Alazugʋ da kɛ ka Moab dim la siaki dɔl David ka yɔɔd lampɔ tisid o.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Dinɛ paas la, David da zab nɛ Na'ab Hadadeze onɛ an Rehob biig ka an Zoba na'ab la nyaŋ o, on da lɛbid ye o di'e o sʋ'ʋlim dinɛ dɛn'ɛd Efiritis kɔldaug saŋsi'a la.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Aram dim banɛ bɛ Damaskus la da wʋmya, ka kena ye ba sʋŋ Hadadeze onɛ an Zoba na'ab la. David da kʋʋ ba nidib tusa pisi nɛ ayi',

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: ka gaŋ o zabzabidib tuongatib sieba niŋ Aram dim sʋ'ʋlimin dinɛ bɛ Damaskus la. Li da kɛ ka Aram dim la lieb o sʋ'ʋlim nidib ka yɔɔd lampɔ tisid o. Zugsɔb la da tis David paŋ ka o nyaŋid on keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David da faaɛn Hadadeze zabzabidib tuongatib la zaba la'asʋma mɔri kul Jerusalem. Li da anɛ gbanti'edis ka ba nɔk sanlima m bulig.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: O mɛ da faaɛn kʋntzɛn'ug bɛdegʋ Teba nɛ Berota tɛɛnsin la, linɛ an Hadadeze sʋ'ʋlim la din.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: o tʋm o biig Joram Na'ab David san'an na ye o pʋ'ʋs o nɛ o zusʋŋ, nɛ on zabi nyaŋ Hadadeze onɛ da zabid nɛ on Tou la. Joram da mɔr sanlima nɛ anzurifa nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug na tis o.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Na'ab David da pɛsig la'ad linɛ an sanlima, nɛ anzurifa nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug la tis Zugsɔb la, wʋʋ on da maal si'em nɛ sanlima nɛ anzurifa banɛ ka o zab nɛ teŋ sieba nyaŋ ka vaae li kul na la wʋsa.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Zadok onɛ an Ahitub biig la nɛ Ahimelek onɛ an Abiata biig la da an maanmaannib; ka Seraya mɛ an gbansɔbid;

english_verse: David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
translation_verse: David da sʋ'ʋg Israel wʋsa, ka tʋm dinɛ an sʋm nɛ sida tisid o nidib.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Joab onɛ an Zeruyia biig la da sʋ'oe zabzabidib la; Jehosafat onɛ an Ahilud biig la da sʋ'oe gbana yɛla;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os ye, “Sɔ' nan kpɛlim Saul yin la ka m na pa'al o m pʋpielim Jonatan zugɔ?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Saul tʋmtʋm yinne da bɛ ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Ziba. Ka ba buol o kɛn David san'an na ka na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Fʋnɛ an Ziba laa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Naa, Ɛɛn; m anɛ fʋ tʋmtʋm.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Sɔ' pʋ kpɛlim Saul yin ka m pa'al Wina'am pʋpielim tis oo?” Ka Ziba lɛbis na'ab la ye, “Jonatan biribiŋ yinne nan kpɛm bɛ, ka pɔn'ɔlim.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” David asked. Ziba replied, “He lives in Lo-Debar with Machir the son of Ammiel.”
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la bu'os ye, “O bɛ yaanɛ?” Ka Ziba lɛbis o ye, “O bɛ Lodebaa teŋin, Ammiel biig Makir yin.”

english_verse: David sent some servants to bring Jonathan's son from Lo-Debar. His name was Mephibosheth, and he was the grandson of Saul. He came to David and knelt down. David asked, “Are you Mephibosheth?” “Yes, I am, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Mefibosef onɛ an Jonatan biig ka an Saul yaaŋ la da paae David san'an na la, o da su'un teŋin ye o na'as o. Ka David buol o ye, “Mefibosef!” Ka o siak ye, “Naa, man onɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la nwa'.”

english_verse: David said, “Don't be afraid. I'll be kind to you because Jonathan was your father. I'm going to give you back the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul. Besides that, you will always eat with me at my table.”
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem,” ka m sid na pa'ali fʋ m pʋpielim, fʋ saam Jonatan zug. M na lɛbis paalʋ kanɛ wʋsa aan fʋ yaab Saul paalʋ la tisif. Man nɛ fʋ na la'asidi diti m diib zin'igin.

english_verse: Mephibosheth knelt down again and said, “Why should you care about me? I'm worth no more than a dead dog.”
translation_verse: Ka Mefibosef su'un teŋin ka yɛl ye, “Naa, m an bɔ ka fʋ tɛnri m yɛla, man onɛ nwɛnɛ bakpiilʋŋ la?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, Saul's chief servant, and told him, “Since Mephibosheth is Saul's grandson, I've given him back everything that belonged to your master Saul and his family.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la buol Ziba, onɛ an Saul tʋmtʋm la yɛl o ye, “M nɔk dinɛ wʋsa aan fʋ zugdaan Saul nɛ o yidimi sʋ'oe si'el la wʋsa tis o yaaŋ nwa'.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had beaten them, they made peace with Israel and accepted David as their ruler. The Arameans were afraid to help Ammon any more.
translation_verse: Na'anam banɛ wʋsa da la'as nɛ Hadadeze la nyɛ ka Israel dim nyaŋi ba la, ba mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm nɛ Israel dim ka liebi ba tʋmtʋmnib. Dinzug, Aram dim la da zɔ dabiem ka pʋ lɛn sʋŋ Ammon dim la ya'asɛ.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, and I will be kind to his son.” So he sent some officials to the country of Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab David tɛn'ɛs ye, “M na maal Hanun onɛ an Nahas biig la pʋpielim wʋʋ o saamme da maalim pʋpielim si'em la.” Dinzug, o da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ pʋ'ʋs Hanun saam la kʋʋr. David nidib la paae Ammon dim teŋin la,

english_verse: But Hanun's officials told him, “Do you really believe David is honoring your father by sending these people to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our city, so he can destroy it.”
translation_verse: ka Ammon dim kpɛɛmnam la yɛl Hanun onɛ aan ba zugdaan la ye, “Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye David na'as nɛ fʋ saam la ka tʋm nidib na ye ba pʋ'ʋsɛɛ? Ayei, fʋ zi' ye David tʋm o nidib la nɛ na ye ba kena labisi gɔs teŋ la ka o ti kena zabi faaɛn lii?”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off on one side of their faces. He had their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Ala ka Hanun gban'e David nidib la pʋni ba tiemis la pʋsʋk-pʋsʋk ka maki ba gbina zinzema nwaasi ba fuud la bas ka kadi ba yis.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message and told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl David yɛl kaŋa la, o da tʋm o tʋmtʋmnib ka ba tʋ'ʋsi ba nɛ labakaŋa ye, “Kpɛlimmi Jeriko teŋin ka ya tiemis la bus ka ya nyaan kul na” bɔzugɔ ba da diisi banɛ nyan hali.

english_verse: The Ammonites realized that they had made David very angry, so they hired more foreign soldiers. Twenty thousand of them were foot soldiers from the Aramean cities of Beth-Rehob and Zobah,
translation_verse: Ammon dim la baŋ ye ba pɔ'ɔg David la, ba keŋ da' zabzabidibi paasi ba mɛŋ. Ba da da'anɛ zabzabidib tusa pisi banɛ yi Befirehob nɛ Zoba dinɛ bɛ Aram sʋ'ʋlimin la, la'an nɛ Maaka na'ab nɛ o nidib tusir, nɛ nidib tusa pii nɛ ayi' banɛ yi Tob sʋ'ʋlimin na.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the cities of our God. I pray that the Lord will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Zi'enim sʋ'ʋŋa ka kpɛ'ɛŋi fʋ sʋnf ka ti zabi ti nidib nɛ ti Wina'am teŋ la yɛla. Zugsɔb la na maal linɛ ka o mɛŋ bɔɔd.”

english_verse: David heard what they had done, and he sent out Joab with all of his well-trained soldiers.
translation_verse: David n da wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la, o da tʋm Joab nɛ zabzabidib la wʋsa.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops came out and got ready to fight in front of the gate to their city. The Arameans from Zobah and Rehob and the soldiers from Tob and Maacah formed a separate group in the nearby fields.
translation_verse: Ka Ammon dim la yina ka ti'eb zaba ti'ebʋgʋ ba teŋ la za'anɔɔrin. Ka Aram dim banɛ yi Zoba na nɛ Rehob la'an nɛ Tob nɛ Maaka nidib wʋsa la'as sian'arin zin'ig yinne.

english_verse: Joab saw that he had to fight in front and behind at the same time, and he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Arameans.
translation_verse: Joab da nyɛya ka zabzabidib la tʋ'ʋsid o tuon nɛ o nya'aŋ wʋsa la o gaans Israel zabzabidib banɛ an ninkpi'ema ka mi' zaba sʋ'ʋŋa la zi'eli ba gu' Aram dim la.

english_verse: He put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and gave them orders to fight the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ka zaŋ banɛ kpɛlim la niŋ Abisai onɛ aan o pitʋ la nu'ugin ka kɛ ka ba gu' Ammon dim la.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Arameans are too much for me to handle, you can come and help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Joab da yɛl o ye, “Aram dim la ya'a kpi'emi gaadi m paŋ, fʋn kena sʋŋim, ka Ammon dim la mɛ ya'a kpi'em gaadi fʋ paŋ, mam mɛ na kena sʋ'ʋŋif.

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Arameans, and the Arameans ran from them.
translation_verse: Ka Joab nɛ o nidib la keŋ tuonnɛ zab nɛ Aram dim la, ka ba zɔɔ widig.

english_verse: When the Ammonite soldiers saw that the Arameans had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab stopped fighting the Ammonites and returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ammon dimi nyɛ ka Aram dim la zɔt la ka ba mɛ zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' tempʋʋgin la ka bas Abisai. Ka Joab bas Ammon dim la zaba ka lɛb Jerusalem na.

english_verse: The Arameans realized they had lost the battle, so they brought all their troops together again.
translation_verse: Aram dimi baŋ ye Israel dim nyaŋi ba la, ka ba lɛn keŋ la'as taaba.

english_verse: Hadadezer sent messengers to call in the Arameans who were on the other side of the Euphrates River. Then Shobach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them to the town of Helam.
translation_verse: Hadadeze da kɛ ka Aram dim sieba lɔ'ɔŋ kɔldaug la na, ka ba keŋ Helam teŋin, ka Siobak onɛ an Hadadeze zabzabidib kpɛɛm la gaadi ba tuon.

english_verse: David found out what the Arameans were doing, and he brought Israel's whole army together. They crossed the Jordan River and went to Helam, where the Arameans were ready to meet them.

translation_verse: Ka o buol o mɛŋ tʋmtʋmi yɛl o ye, “Vɛ'ɛgim pu'a kaŋa yis ka kpar dɔɔg la lɛbis.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Ka o tʋmtʋm la yis o yiŋ ka kpar dɔɔg la. Tama da yɛnɛ fukanɛ ligidi zu'oe. Li da anɛ ba malʋŋ ye na'abikanɛ nan zi' dau yɛɛd fuban la buudi.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: O da nɔk tampɛligim bugi o zugʋ pa'an o sʋnsa'aŋi an si'em, ka aaɛn fukanɛ ka o yɛ la, ka nɔk o nu'ugʋ kʋk zugʋ kaasidi ken.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Ka o taʋn Absalom bu'os o ye, “Fʋ taʋn Amnon digin nɛf nɛ bɛɛ? M taʋn, kɛl tʋkpiidʋg, da kɛ ka li daami fɔ, ka o anɛ fʋ taʋn.” Ka Tama kpɛlim o taʋn Absalom yin nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ ka bɛɛ o kɔn'ɔkɔn'.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Ka Absalom kisig Amnon hali on diis o taʋn Tama nyan la zug; amaa ka pʋ ya'ae o nɔɔri yɛl o si'el, si'ela. Absalom kʋ Amnon

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Yʋma ayi' nya'aŋ, ka banɛ kiesid Absalom pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid la bɛ Baal Hazo linɛ kpi'e Efiram la, ka o buol na'abiis la wʋsa ye ba kena maal sumalisim nɛ o.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom keŋ na'ab la san'an yɛl o ye, “Banɛ kiesidi m pɛ'ɛs kɔnbid la kena. Naa, fʋn nɛ fʋ na'ayikpɛm la na kena la'as nɛ tii?”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ayei, m biiga, ti wʋsa kʋ la'asi keŋɛ. Li na an ziidi tisif.” La'an nɛ Absalom da mɔ nɛ nimmua ye o keŋ la, o zan'as nɛ ka lɛɛ niŋ o zug albareka.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom yɛl o ye, “Ya'a aan ala fʋn kɛ ka Amnon onɛ aan m bier la dɔlli ti keŋ.” Ka na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye Amnon dɔlli keŋɛ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Amaa Absalom da sin'ig o galis, ka o siak ye Amnon nɛ na'abiis la wʋsa kem.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Absalom da yɛl o nidib la ye, “Kɛlisimi! Amnon ya'a ti nu daam tig hali, ka m yɛl ye, ‘Nwɛ'ɛmin o,’ yanam kʋʋm o. Da zɔti dabiem, kpɛ'ɛŋimini ya sʋnf, ka manɛ tisi ya nɔɔr.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Absalom nidib la da niŋ Amnon wʋʋ on yɛli ba si'em la, ka na'abiis la duoe ban'a ba widi zɔ.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Ban nam bɛ suor la, ka labaar paae Na'ab David san'an na ye, “Absalom kʋ na'abiis la, baa yinne pʋ kpɛlim.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la duoe zi'en, ka aaɛn o fuug sʋnsa'aŋ zug ka lɛbi digin teŋin. Ka o yammis la mɛ duoe aansi ba fuud.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Amaa Semea onɛ an David bier la biig Jonadab da yɛl ye, “M zugdaana, da tɛn'ɛs ye ba kʋnɛ na'abiis la wʋsa, Amnon ma'aa kpi. Nɛ' anɛ dinɛ pʋn dɛŋi bɛ Absalom sʋnfʋn, din yi daakanɛ ka Amnon bibig o taʋn Tama la.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Naa, m zugdaana, da kɛ ka fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛr an wʋʋ fʋn wʋm si'em ye na'abiis la wʋsa kpinɛ la. Ka Amnon ma'aa kpi.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Saŋkan ka Absalom pʋn zɔ. Ka dau kanɛ zi'e gur la gɔs suorin la nyɛ nidib bɛdegʋ ka ba bɛɛ o tuonnɛ yi kʋkʋn la baba sigid na, ka o keŋ yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Man nyɛ nidib ka ba yi Horonam kʋkʋn la baba kenna.”

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Ka Jonadab yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Naa, m pʋ yɛlɛɛ, ka' na'abiis la nwaa?”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: On pian' naae la, ka na'abiis la kpɛn' na kaasidi agɔla gɔla. Ka Na'ab la nɛ o yammis la mɛ kum hali nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ. Absalom n zɔɔ keŋ Gesur la yɛla

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la bɔɔd nɛ o sʋnf wʋsa ye o keŋ Absalom san'an bɔzugɔ, o sʋnf da bʋk Amnon kum la yɛla.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Joab onɛ an Zeruyia biig la da baŋ ye Na'ab la mɔr Absalom ya'amlɛog la,

english_verse: and he sent someone to bring in the wise woman who lived in Tekoa. Joab told her, “Put on funeral clothes and don't use any makeup. Go to the king and pretend you have spent a long time mourning the death of a loved one.” Then he told her what to say.
translation_verse: o da tʋm sɔ' Tekoa teŋin ye o dɔl pu'a kanɛ an ya'am sɔbi bɛɛ anina la na. On paae na la, ka o yɛl o ye, “Yɛɛm kʋʋr fuud, ka da suoɛn kpaam, ka keŋ Na'ab la san'ani ma'aa ye fʋ kaasid nɛ kʋʋr. Maalimi fʋ mɛŋ wʋʋ pu'a kanɛ zaŋ dabisa bɛdegʋ maal sʋnsa'aŋ onɛ kpi yɛla.” Joab da pa'al o on na keŋ Na'ab la san'ani yɛl o si'em.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Ka Tekoa dim pu'a la paae Na'ab la san'an la, o iginnɛ ka o nindaa kpa' teŋ ye o tis o na'asi, ka yɛl ye, “Na'aba, sʋŋim!”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Bɔɔ daamidi fɔ?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Man sid kpinɛ ka m kilim pʋkɔɔnr.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la mɔri biis ayi', ka ba keŋ pɔɔgine zab ka sɔ' kae anina na pansigi baa. Ka m biig yinne nwɛ' o tiraan la kʋ.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Nannanna, m sid nidib la wʋsa duoe nɛ zi'e m yɛla. Ba yɛl ye, ‘Tisimi ti bikanɛ kʋʋ o tiraan la ka ti mɛ kʋʋ o, o ba'abiig la nyɔvʋr yɛla! Ka o yi buudi la ni ka kʋ lɛn di faarɛ.’ M ya'a siak ka ba kʋʋ m biyimmir nwa', sɔ' lɛn kae na zi'eni m sid la nɛ o yidim zi'esiminɛ. Ti yʋ'ʋr na bɔdig dunia nwa' zug.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la lɛbis ye, “Kulim, ka m na maali fʋ yɛl la tisif.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Amaa pu'a la yɛl o ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, fʋ ya'a sʋŋi maal yɛl nwa' ka ba ye ba zɛrigif, mam na siaki di'e li, man nɛ m nidib la, ka li kʋ kɛɛn fʋ san'an na, Na'aba.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la lɛbis o ye, “Ayei, da kɛ ka lin paki fɔ! Ninkanɛ daamif, fʋn mɔr o na, ka m na kɛ ka o kʋ maligim daamif ya'asɛ.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “Alaa, Na'aba, pɔɔm nɛ fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr ye fʋ kʋ kɛ ka sɔ' kʋʋ m biyimmir la yɔ sam, ka li kilim tukɔ.” Ka o yɛl ye, “Asida ka m yɛtif, nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr, hali fʋ biig la zuobʋg baa yinne kʋ li teŋa.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la lɛn yɛl ye, “Naa, dim suguru ka m lɛm bu'osif pian'ad yinne ya'as!” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Bu'osim!”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la yɛl ye, Ka bɔzug ka fʋ siak ye fʋ na tʋm nɛ'ɛŋa tis mam, ka lɛɛ kʋ tʋm ala tis Wina'am nidib wʋsa? Na'aba, fʋ pian'ad la gban'anɛ fʋ mɛŋ! Bɔzugɔ fʋ kadi fʋ biigi kpɛn'ɛs mɔɔg ka pʋ siak ye o kul naa.

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Ti wʋsa na ba'asi kpi. Ti nyɔvʋya la nwɛnɛ ku'om na kpa'ae teŋin ka ti kʋ tun'e vaae la nɛ. Alazug ka ti ya'a tʋm linɛ ka' sʋm, Wina'am bɔɔdnɛ suokanɛ ka o na kɛ ka ti lɛb o san'an na.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Nannanna m kena ye m yɛlif nɛ'ɛŋa, m zugdaan onɛ aan m Na'aba, bɔzugɔ nidib la kɛnɛ ka dabiem mɔrim, ka m tɛn'ɛs ye, M na pian' tis Na'ab la, ka daasi'erɛɛ o na maali m yɛl la tisim.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Daasi'erɛɛ Na'ab na siak ka faaɛn man nɛ m biig la dau kanɛ bɔɔd ye o kɛ ka ti kʋ nyaŋi di faar linɛ ka Wina'am maali tisi ti la nu'ugin.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: “Nannanna man yɛt si'eli nwa', ‘M zugdaan onɛ aan m Na'aba, fʋ pian'ad na tisim yɔlisim, bɔzugɔ fʋ nwɛnɛ Wina'am maliak nɛ, ka mi' dinɛ an sʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛdi bakid. Fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am la na bɛ nɛf!’”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl pu'a la ye, “M ye m bu'osif nɛ bu'osʋg, amaa da su'a si'ela.” Ka pu'a la lɛbis ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, bu'osim!”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Joab nu'ug bɛɛ fʋ yɛl nwa' wʋsa pʋʋgin, bɛɛ m ma'aanɛɛ?” Ka pu'a la lɛbis ye, “Li anɛ sida, zugdaana, sɔ' kae na ki'is fʋn yɛl si'el la wʋsaa. Ɛɛn, li anɛ fʋ tʋmtʋm Joab n pa'alim ye m niŋi li. Onɛ pian' pian'abama wʋsa tisim.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Fʋ tʋmtʋm Joab n niŋ nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ ye o tiak yɛlbanɛ bɛ nannanna la. M zugdaana, fʋ mɔr ya'am nwɛnɛ Wina'am maliak nɛ. Fʋ mi' dinɛ wʋsa maan teŋ la zug wʋsa.” David n kɛ Absalom taali bas la yɛla

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Joab ye, “Li an sʋm, m na tʋmi li. Kem mɔr m biig Absalom n lɛb na.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Ka Joab vanbin ka nɔk o nindaa kpa' teŋi tis o na'asi, ka kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis o ka yɛl ye, “Na'ab onɛ an m zugdaana, nannanna m baŋ ye m paae fʋ ya'am, bɔzugɔ fʋ maal man sɔs si'el la tisim.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Ani ka Joab keŋ Gesur n dɔl Absalom lɛb Jerusalem na.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab la da yɛl ye, “Asɛɛ ka o keŋ o mɛŋ yin. O kʋ nyɛ man nindaa.” Absalom da kuli o yin ka pʋ nyɛ Na'ab la nindaa.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: O zuobid la ya'a da ɛɛnti nɔbigi zu'oe ka yʋ'ʋn tɛbis la, o kiesidi li nɛ. O da kiesid o zuobid la yʋʋm wʋsa nɔɔr yinne. O da ɛɛnti vaae mak ka li tɛbisim zu'oe.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalom da du'a biribis atan' nɛ bipuŋ yinne. Bipuŋ la yʋ'ʋri da buon Tama. O da anɛ pu'a vɛnliŋ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalom da bɛ nɛ Jerusalem yʋma ayi' ka pʋ nyɛ Na'ab la nindaa,

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: ka tʋm buol Joab ye o kena ka o tʋm o Na'ab la san'an. Amaa Joab da zan'as ka pʋ keŋɛ. Ka o lɛn tʋm paas nɔɔra ayi' ka o zan'as ka pʋ kenaa.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Absalom da yɛl o yammis la ye, “Gɔsimi ya, Joab pɔɔgʋ bɛ man pɔɔg la zugin la; kem nyu'oe li nɛ bugum!” Absalom yammis la sid da nyu'oe pɔɔg la nɛ bugum.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Ka Joab keŋ Absalom yinnɛ bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ yammis la nyu'oe m pɔɔg la?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom lɛbis o ye, “Gɔsima, m tʋmi fʋ san'an na ye fʋ kena ka m tʋmif na'ab la san'an ka fʋ bu'os o ye, ‘Bɔzug ka fʋ buolim ka m yi Gesur lɛb na? M ya'a kpɛn bɛɛn anina li naan sɔn'ɔn.’ Tɔ', m bɔɔd ye m nyɛ Na'ab la, ka m ya'a ka' bʋʋdɛ, on kʋʋmim.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Joab da keŋ yɛl Na'ab la, ka Na'ab la buol Absalom, ka o kpɛn' na vanbin ka o nindaa kpa' teŋ Na'ab la tuon. Ka Na'ab la pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Li da paae saŋa si'a ka Absalom da' zaba tɛreko nɛ widi ka bɔ nidib pisnu ka ba bɛɛ o tuon.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: O da ɛɛnti duoe nɛ bɛogʋn keŋ zi'en suor kanɛ kpɛn'ɛd tempʋʋgin la kpikpɛŋ. Sɔ' ya'a mɔr o antu'a ken na'ayin ye o maal, Absalom na buol o sɔba bu'os ye, “Fʋ yi teŋ kanɛ na?” Ka o sɔb na yɛl o ye, “Na'abiiga, m yinɛ Israel dɔɔd la yinne ni na.”

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: Absalom na yɛl o ye, “Gɔsima, fʋ pian'ad la an sʋm ka dɔl suor, amaa sɔ' kae na'ayinne na kɛlisi fʋ pian'ad la tisi fɔ.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Ka onɛ wʋsa daa li'el o igin o tuonnɛ pʋ'ʋs o nɛ girima, Absalom na tiɛn o nu'ugʋ gban'e o ka pʋ'ʋs o sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Absalom da niŋidnɛ anwana tisid Israel dim wʋsa banɛ ken na'ab la yinnɛ bɔɔd antu'a maalʋg. Ala ka o da fɛndig Israel dim ya'am lɛb o san'an na.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Lin ti paae yʋma anaasi naar saŋa la, Absalom da yɛl na'ab la ye, “Naa, kɛl ka m keŋ Hebron n lɛbisi m nɔzi'elʋg.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Ka man da bɛ Gesur Aram teŋin la, m da zi'el nɔɔr ye, Zugsɔb la ya'a mɔrimi lɛb Jerusalem na, m na keŋ Hebron n wɔ'ɔg o.”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl o ye, “Kem nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.” Ka o duoe keŋ Hebron.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Sɔ' da kena yɛl David ye, “Nidib la ya'am lɛb nɛ Absalom san'an.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl o na'ayikpɛm banɛ da la'am bɛ nɛ o Jerusalem la ye, “Asɛɛ ka ti zɔ! Ya'a ka' ala Absalom kʋ kɛ ka ti sɔ'ɔsɔ yii. Asɛɛ ka ti yi nannanna; ya'a ka' ala, o ya'a paae ti kpɛla, tinam nɛ teŋ la wʋsa kʋ pɔnsɛ.”

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Naa, ti anɛ fʋ yammis, ti ti'eb nɛ ye ti tʋm wʋʋ fʋn gban'e si'em la.”

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ka nidib la wʋsa kena gaadi o tuon, la'an nɛ Keret dim nɛ Pelet dim wʋsa, nɛ nidib kɔbisyuobʋ banɛ an Gaf dim ka da dɔl o yi Gaf na la.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Ittai onɛ an Gaf nid la ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ dɔlli ti? Kem lɛb Na'ab Absalom san'an. Fʋ anɛ saan ka yii fʋ mɛŋ teŋin zɔɔ kpɛn' na.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Su'os ma'aa ka fʋ sa kena, li pʋ nar ye m kɛ ka fʋ dɔlli ti zɔti giligida. Mam mɛŋ zi' man ken zin'isi'a. Nɔkim nidib la lɛb, pʋpielim nɛ sida na dɔlli fʋ nya'aŋ.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Amaa Ittai da lɛbis Na'ab la ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, ya'a an sida, fʋn bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa, li ya'a anɛ kum bɛɛ vʋm, man onɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la na bɛ.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: David da yɛl Ittai ye, “Tɔ', ka kem tuon!” Ka Ittai onɛ an Gaf nid la dɔl o nidib la keŋ tuonnɛ gaad, nɛ ba yidim la wʋsa.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Na'ab la nɛ o nidib la daa yit teŋin la, teŋ la nidib wʋsa daa kaas agɔla, gɔla pamm. Ka na'ab la lɔ'ɔŋ Kidron bɔn'ɔg la nɛ o nidib la wʋsa kennɛ kpa'ad sian'arin la. Ban lɛbis Wina'am Daka la Jerusalem la yɛla

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Zadok nɛ Abiata banɛ an maanmaannib la, nɛ Levi dim banɛ ziid Wina'am daka la, da la'am bɛɛ ani. Ka ba zi'el Wina'am daka la teŋin, ka Abiata maal maana hali ka nidib la wʋsa ti yi teŋin la naae.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Zadok ye, “Nɔkim Wina'am daka la zii lɛb tempʋʋgin la; ka li ya'a an Wina'am bɔɔdim, o na mɔrimi lɛb na ka m nyɛɛ li nɛ o bɛllim zin'ig la ya'as.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Amaa o ya'a yɛl ye, o sʋnf pʋ malis nɛ mam, man ti'eb ya. Kɛl ka o tʋm dinɛ an sʋm tis o.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da lɛn yɛl Zadok onɛ an maanmaan la ye, “Ka' fʋnɛ an onɛ mi' dinɛ saa na maal bɛog saa? Lɛm tempʋʋgin la nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm, fʋn nɛ fʋ biig Ahimaaz nɛ Jonatan onɛ an Abiata biig la. Ka kɛ ka Abiata mɛ dɔlli ya lɛb.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Man na guri ya kɔldaug kanɛ bɛ sian'arin, zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om pʋ zulim la, ka ya ti tisim labaar.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ka Zadok nɛ Abiata nɔk Wina'am daka la lɛb Jerusalem zin'inɛ anina.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Amaa David da kpɛn ken nɛ dʋt Olif Zuor la zug ka kum. O da nɔk si'eli lus o zug ka ken nɔbteŋ. Nidib banɛ da dɔl o la wʋsa da lusi ba zut ka ken nɔbteŋi dɔl o ka kum.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Ba yʋ'ʋn da yɛl David ye, “Ahitofel paas banɛ gban'e pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd nɛ Absalom la.” David da sɔs Wina'am ye, “M Zugsɔba, kɛl ka Ahitofel sa'alʋg lieb zɔlim.” Husai lɛbig la yɛla

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: David da paae kʋkʋn zug, zin'ikanɛ ka ba pʋ'ʋsid Wina'am la, ka Husai onɛ an Arik nid la tʋ'ʋs o ka o fuud aans ka o zug an uusʋg.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Ka David yɛl o ye, “Fʋ ya'a dɔllim, fʋ na an ziidi tisim,

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: amaa fʋ ya'a lɛb tempʋʋgin ka yɛl Absalom ye, ‘Na'aba, m na aan fʋ tʋmtʋm. Saŋa kanɛ gaad la m daa anɛ fʋ saam tʋmtʋm, amaa nannanna m na aan fʋ tʋmtʋm.’ Ala ka fʋ na sʋŋim ka nyaŋi san'am Ahitofel sa'alʋg la.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Zadok nɛ Abiata pʋn dɛŋi bɛɛ anina na paasi fʋ zug. Yɛlimi ba dinɛ wʋsa ka fʋ wʋm na'ayin la.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Ahimaaz onɛ an Zadok biig la nɛ Abiata biig Jonatan bɛɛ ba san'an. Tʋmmi ba na nɛ fʋn wʋm labasi'a wʋsa.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: David zua Husai da lɛbi paae Jerusalem saŋa kanɛ ka Absalom kpɛn'ɛd tempʋʋgin la.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Na'ab David n da keŋ lalig bi'ela tʋʋgi paae kʋkʋn la zug la, o da nyɛ Ziba onɛ an Mefibosef tʋmtʋm la, ka o zi'e gur o ka mɔr bʋmis ayi' ka ba ziid bodobodo gbila kɔbisyi', nɛ tiis wala ka ba gbilim ban kɔbiga, nɛ kekamgbila kɔbiga, nɛ daam gan'ar.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os Ziba ye, “Fʋ mɔr nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa kena ye fʋ niŋ bɔ?” Ka Ziba lɛbis ye, “M mɔr bʋmis la kena ye na'ayidim mɔri ban'ad. Bodobodo nɛ bʋnwanna la anɛ na'ayidim diib, ka daam la mɛ an banɛ keŋ sian'arin gɛn la din ye ba nɔki nuu tɔ'ɔŋi ba giinla.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Fʋ zugdaan Saul yaaŋ la bɛ ya?” Ka Ziba lɛbis ye, “O bɛ Jerusalem, bɔzugɔ o tɛn'ɛs ye, ‘Zina Israel dim na nɔki m yaab na'am lɛbisi tisim’”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Ziba ye, “Dinɛ wʋsa an Mefibosef bʋn la anɛ fʋ din yʋ'ʋs.” Ka Ziba yɛl ye, “Naa, m pʋ'ʋsif bareka ka igin teŋin! Win na kɛ ka fʋ na'am la keŋ tuon! Kɛl ka m paae fʋ ya'am, m zugdaana.” Simie pɔ nɔɔri tis David la yɛla

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Na'ab David n da li'en Bahurim teŋin la ka dau sɔ' onɛ an Saul tuŋ nid yina; o yʋ'ʋri da buon Simie ka o saam an Gera. Ka on yit na la ka pɔɔd nɔɔri tit David,

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: ka lɔbid on nɛ o na'ayikpɛm la wʋsa nɛ kuga, hali la'an nɛ banɛ an zabzabidib ka mi' zaba sʋ'ʋŋa bɛ David datiuŋ nɛ o dagɔbʋg la.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Simie da pɔɔd nɔɔr la ka yɛt ye, “Isigim sa, isigim! Gɔsim tuksɔb! Fʋ anɛ nimbɛ'og!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Zikanɛ ka fʋ kpa'ae Saul yin ka di'e o zin'ig la samme la ka Zugsɔb la yɔɔd. Zugsɔb la nɔk na'am la niŋi fʋ biig Absalom nu'ugin. Fʋ kennɛ san'auŋ bɔzugɔ fʋ anɛ ninkʋʋd!”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Abisai onɛ an Zeruyia biig la yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Bɔzug ka bakpiilʋŋ kaŋa pɔɔdi m zugdaan onɛ aan m Na'ab la nɔɔrɛ? Kɛl ka m keŋ fi'ig o zug!”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab la da yɛl ye, “Nɔɔr yinne bɔ bɛ man nɛ yanam Zeruyia biis sʋʋginɛ? O ya'a pɔɔd nɔɔr ka li anɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye o pɔɔm David nɔɔr, anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi bu'os o ye, ‘Bɔ ka fʋ maan nɛ'?’”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Ka David lɛn yɛl Abisai nɛ kpɛɛmnam la ye, “Mam mɛŋ biig onɛ an m niŋgbiŋ la ya'a mɔɔd ye o yis man nyɔvʋrɛ, onɛ an Benjamin dɔɔg nid na niŋ wala? Basimin o. Kɛlli ka o pɔɔe. Li anɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye o niŋim.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Daasi'erɛ Zugsɔb la na nyɛ m sʋnsa'aŋ la ka lɛbis sʋm tisim, man di'e nɔpɔkaŋa zaalim-zaalim la.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: David nɛ o nidib la da kpɛn dɔl suor la ken, ka Simie mɛ dɛn'ɛd kʋkʋn la baba dɔl o ka lɔbid o nɛ kuga ka fɛn'ɛd o titan.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Na'ab la nɛ o nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la da paae ba ken zin'ig la, ba gɛnnɛ hali. Ka zin'in anina vʋ'ʋs. Absalom n kpɛn' Jerusalem la yɛla

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalom nɛ Israel nidib wʋsa da paae Jerusalem na, ka Ahitofel paasi dɔlli ba.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Ka Husai onɛ an Arik nid ka an David zua la kɛn Absalom san'an na ka yɛl o ye, “Na'aba, Wina'am na tisif nyɔvʋr wɔk! Naa, Wina'am na tisif nyɔvʋr wɔk!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom bu'os Husai ye, “Fʋ sid daa nɔŋi fʋ zua laa? Bɔ ka fʋ pʋ dɔl o keŋɛ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Husai da yɛl Absalom ye, “Ayei, onɛ ka Zugsɔb la nɛ Israel dim wʋsa gaŋ la, on ka mam mi' ka na dɔl.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Dinɛ lɛm paas anɛ, anɔ'ɔn ka m na tʋm tisɛ? Li pʋ sʋm ye m tʋm tisif wʋʋ man daa tʋmmi tisidi fʋ saam si'em laa? Alazug, m na tʋm tisif.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Ka Absalom yɛl Ahitofel ye, “Sa'alimi ti, ti na niŋ wala?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ka Ahitofel yɛl o ye, “Gbɛɛm nɛ fʋ saam pu'abibis banɛ ka o bas ye ba gur na'ayir la. Ka Israel dim wʋsa na wʋm ye, fʋ kpɛn' fʋ saam nyɔnya ni galis, ka ya kʋ nyaŋi naal nɛ taaba ya'asɛ. Ka banɛ wʋsa dɔllif la na zi'en kiŋ-kiŋ.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Ka ba ti' sʋgʋr na'ayir la dɔɔg zugʋ tis Absalom, ka o digin nɛ o saam pu'abibis la, Israel dim wʋsa nini ni.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la nidib la wʋsa da gɔs Ahitofel sa'alʋg ka li nwɛnɛ Wina'am mɛŋ-mɛŋ yɛlʋg. Alazug, David nɛ Absalom da pʋ di'emid nɛ dau nwa' sa'alʋgɔ.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Ala ka ti ya'a nyɛɛ o zin'isi'a wʋsa ti na zab nɛ o, ti na lii o zugin nwɛnɛ mɛligim lit teŋin si'em la. On nɛ o nidib la baa yinne kʋ yii.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: M na zab nɛ o saŋkan ka o ti gɛn ka paŋ kae la. M na kpɛn'ɛs o dabiem ka nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la zɔ. M na nwɛ' nɛ na'ab la ma'aa kʋ o,

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: ka mɔr nimbanɛ kpɛlim la lɛb na tisif. Fʋn bɔɔd ye fʋ kʋ dau sɔ' la ya'a kpi, li na kɛ ka nidib la wʋsa na lɛbi fʋ san'an na wʋʋ pu'a-ɛliŋi kunnɛ o sid yir nɛ sumalisim si'em la. Nid baa yinne kʋ paam dɛŋŋa.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Absalom nɛ Israel kpɛɛmnam la da nyɛ ka gban'akaŋa nwɛnɛ li an sʋm tisi ba.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Amaa Absalom da yɛl ye, “Buolim Husai onɛ an Arik nid la ka ti wʋm on mɔr si'el ye o yɛl.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Ka Husai n paae na la ka Absalom yɛl o ye, “Ahitofel n tisi ti sa'al kaŋa, ti niŋim wʋʋ on yɛl si'em laa? Ya'a ka' ala, fʋn tisimi ti fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛre gban'e si'em.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Ka Husai lɛbis Absalom ye, “Sa'al kanɛ ka Ahitofel tis la ka' sʋm saŋa kaŋaa.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Fʋ mi' ye fʋ saam la nɛ o nidib la anɛ zabzabidib amɛŋa. Ba nwɛnɛ mɔɔgin bʋnyua kanɛ ka ba gban'e o biis nɛ. Fʋ mi' ye fʋ saam la mi' zaba hali. O kʋ siaki la'as nɛ o zabzabidib la gbɛɛn.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Hali anwaa o su'anɛ tampinlɛma ni, bɛɛ o tɔɔm keŋ bɛ zin'isi'a. O ya'a pin'ili zab nɛ fʋ zabzabidib la yiiga ka kʋʋ ba sieba, nidib la wʋsa na wʋm ka yɛl ye ba kʋ Absalom zabzabidib la bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Li ya'a niŋ ala, hali baa zabzabid kanɛ sʋnfʋ kpi'em wʋʋ gbigim la, dabiem na kpɛn' o ka o ya'am wʋsa bɔdig. Bɔzugɔ Israel dim wʋsa mi' ye fʋ saam la anɛ zabzabid, ka banɛ bɛɛ o san'an la mɛ an sʋnkpi'euŋ dim.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Man sa'alʋg anɛ nwa': Kɛl ka Israel dim wʋsa la'asi fʋ san'an na, din yi Dan keŋ paae Beerseba, ka ba na zu'oe nwɛnɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin titanbin'isʋg nɛ. Ka fʋ mɛŋ na gaad tuon zaba la ni.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: O ya'a lɛn zɔ nɛ keŋ kpɛn' tempʋkanɛ ka ba mɛ' zaŋguommi gilig la, Israel dim wʋsa na mɔr nwiisi kena vɛ'ɛgi li sigis bɔn'ɔgin, hali ka sɔ' kʋ nyɛɛ li yaama baa bi'elaa.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Absalom nɛ Israel dim la wʋsa da yɛl ye, “Husai onɛ an Arik nid la sa'alʋg la an sʋm gat Ahitofel sa'alʋg la.” Zugsɔb la mɛŋi da gban'e ye o san'am sa'al sʋŋ dinɛ ka Ahitofel sa'al la, ka kɛ ka yɛltɔɔg li Absalom zugin. Husai sa'alʋg la da faaɛn David si'em

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Husai da yɛl Zadok nɛ Abiata banɛ an maanmaannib la, Ahitofel n sa'al Absalom nɛ Israel kpɛɛmnam la ban na niŋ si'em, ka lɛn yɛli ba on mɛŋi tiaki sa'ali ba si'em.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Ka yɛli ba ye, “Nannanna tʋm tɔ'ɔtɔ yɛl Na'ab David ye o da gbɛn kɔlig la zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om pʋ zulim laa. O lɔ'ɔŋim ka da gʋ'ʋŋɛ. Ya'a ka' ala, na'ab nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la ba na kʋʋ ba wʋsa.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Jonatan nɛ Ahimaaz da bɛ nɛ Enrogel teŋin. Ba da tʋm tʋmtʋm pu'ak wʋʋ ban pʋn gban'e si'em la, ye o keŋ yɛli ba, ka ban mɛ keŋ yɛl Na'ab David. Ba da pʋ bɔɔd ye ba kuosi ba mɛŋi kpɛn'ɛd tempʋʋgin la ka nidib nyɛti baa.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Amaa na'akimbil sɔ' da nyɛ babayi' la ka keŋ yɛl Absalom, ka ba baŋ ka yi tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ dau sɔ' yin Bahurim teŋin. O da mɔr bulig zakin la, ka ba sigi li pʋʋgin.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: O pu'a da nɔk bulig la liŋe pibil bulig la nɔɔr, ka yadig kibielim li zug, ka sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ baŋɛ.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Absalom nidib la paae pu'a la yin na la ba bu'os o ye, “Ahimaaz nɛ Jonatan bɛ yaanɛ?” Ka pu'a la lɛbisi ba ye, “Ba lɔ'ɔŋ kɔlig la.” Ka dap la iee ba zin'igi gʋ'ʋŋ, ka lɛb Jerusalem.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Dap la lɛb la nya'aŋ, ka babayi' la dʋ na keŋ yɛl Na'ab David. Ba da yɛl o ye, “Duom lɔ'ɔŋ kɔldaug la tɔ'ɔtɔ. Ahitofel sa'al Absalom nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la ban na niŋ si'em ka nyaŋi gban'af.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Ka David nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ o san'an la duoe lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la. Bɛogʋ ti nie la ka ba wʋsa pʋn gaad Joodan kɔldaug la ka sɔ' pʋ lɛn kpɛlim.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ahitofel n nyɛ ka ba pʋ dɔl o sa'alʋg la, ka o bɔb o buŋi ban'a kul o mɛŋ teŋin. On paae la, o maal o yir la sʋ'ʋŋa ka yʋ'ʋn yul o mɛŋi kpi, ka ba mum o, o saam yaʋgʋn. Absalom n kad David la yɛla

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: David da keŋ nɛ Mahanam teŋin, ka Absalom lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan n kad o bugir, on nɛ Israel dim wʋsa.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Absalom da gaŋnɛ Amasa o zabzabidib la ni ye o di'e Joab zin'ig. Amasa da anɛ dau kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Jeta la biig. Jeta da anɛ Isimael nid ka o pu'a yʋ'ʋr buon Abigel onɛ an Nahas pu'ayua. Abigel da anɛ Zeruyia pitʋ, Zeruyia mɛ da anɛ Joab ma.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Israel dim nɛ Absalom da la'as nɛ Gilead teŋgbauŋʋn. Ban maal zuod nɛ David la yɛla

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: David n da paae Mahanam la, Soobi nɛ Makir nɛ Barizila da bɛɛ ani. Soobi da anɛ Nahas biig ka yi Rabba teŋin na ka an Ammon nid, ka Makir mɛ an Ammiel biig ka yi Lodebaa teŋin na, Barizila da anɛ Gilead nid ka yi Rogelim teŋin na.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: Ka mɔr siind nɛ bin'iskpaam nɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ bin'isgbisidim wʋsa na tis David nɛ o nidib la ye ba di. Bɔzugɔ ba da mi' ye nidib la gɛnnɛ ka kɔ'ɔm nɛ ku'onuud mɔri ba.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: David da pʋdig zabzabidib la zin'isa atan' ka ba tuongatib an Joab, nɛ o pitʋ Abisai onɛ an Zeruyia biig la, nɛ Ittai onɛ an Gaf nid la. Ka Na'ab la yɛl zabzabidib la ye, “Bi'esʋg kae, asɛɛ man dɔlli ya keŋ.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Amaa nidib la da yɛl ye, “Li pʋ nar ye fʋ yii; ba ya'a ti kadi ti ka ti zɔt, ba ba'a kʋ bɛ nɛ tinama, hali baa ti pʋsʋk ya'a kpii ba ba'a kʋ bɛɛ, amaa fʋn gat tinam tusa piiga. Li na an sʋm nɛ fʋn na bɛ tempʋʋgin la ka sʋŋidi ti.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la yinne nyɛ la, o yɛl Joab ye, “Mam nyɛ Absalom ka o ya'ae tiig zug.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Zaba da yadig teŋ la wʋsa, ka nimbanɛ zɔɔ kpɛn' sian'akʋdigin la kpi, da gaad banɛ ka ba zabi kʋʋ ba la. Joab n kʋ Absalom la yɛla

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Absalom da keŋ di'ig David nidib la. O da ban'adnɛ wief, ka zɔ nɛ wief la keŋ kpɛn' titita'ar gbinnin, ka tiig la wila gban'e Absalom zug, ka o ya'ae tiig la zugʋ yuulim ka wief la kpɛm bɛ zɔɔgin.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Ka Joab bu'os o ye, “Fʋ ye fʋ nyɛɛ o? Bɔ ka fʋ pʋ kpɛn kʋns o anina tabil teŋinɛ kʋʋ o? Mam naan tisi nɛf yɔɔd anzurifa piiga ka lɛn tisif zabzabid sɛnbidiŋ.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: M ya'a kuosini m nyɔvʋri kʋ Absalom ka Na'ab la wʋm ka di lieb yɛl, fʋ kʋ siaki zi'enɛ m nya'aŋa.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Ka Joab lɛbis o ye, “M kʋ san'am saŋa zi'e kɛlisid dabiem pian'adɛ!” Ka nɔk kpana atan' keŋ ka o nan vʋe ka ya'ae tiig la zug, ka o kʋns Absalom nyɔ'ɔg.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Ka nidib piiga banɛ ziid Joab zaba la'ad la zɔɔ gilig Absalom nwɛ' o kʋ.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Ka Joab pieb na'atan ka zabzabidib la bas ka pʋ lɛn kad Israel dim la, Joab n da buoli ba la zug.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Ka ba nɔk Absalom lɔb bʋmbɔk tita'ar pʋʋg sian'arin la, ka vaae kuga lɔbi bʋʋl o, ka Israel dim la zɔɔ kuli ba yaan.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Absalom nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa la o da kpi'e kugiri zi'el Na'ab Bɔn'ɔgin la. O da tɛn'ɛs ye, “Mam pʋ mɔr biribis ka ba na pʋdigi m yʋ'ʋr bɛogɔ.” Ka nɔk kugir la zi'el ka pʋd o li o mɛŋ yʋ'ʋr, ka ba buon ani ye, Absalom Tiɛnr Zin'ig hali paae zina. David sʋnsa'aŋ yɛla

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Zadok biig Ahimaaz da yɛl ye, “Kɛl ka m zɔɔ keŋ yɛl Na'ab la ye, Zugsɔb la yis o, o dataas la nu'usin.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Ka Joab yɛl o ye, “Ka' fʋnɛ na mɔr labakaŋa zina keŋɛ: fʋ na tun'e mɔr labaari keŋ saŋa si'a amaa ka' zina, bɔzugɔ Na'ab la biig kpiya.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Joab da yɛl dau sɔ' onɛ yi Kus na ye, “Kem yɛl Na'ab la fʋn nyɛ si'el.” Ka dau la igin Joab tuon ka zɔɔ keŋ.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Ahimaaz da lɛn yɛl Joab ye, “M bɛlimnɛ, li ya'a an si'em wʋsa kɛl ka m zɔɔ dɔl Kus dim dau la nya'aŋ.” Ka Joab lɛbis o ye, “M dakɔɔnrɛ, bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye fʋ keŋɛ? Labakaŋa ka' dinɛ na tisif yɔɔdɛ.”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “La'an nɛ lin wʋsa, kɛl ka m zɔɔ keŋ.” Joab da lɛbis ye, “Ka zɔm!” Ka Ahimaaz zɔɔ dɔl zin'ikanɛ an paalʋ la gaad Kus dim dau la tuon.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: David da yina zin' za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ pʋʋgin la nɛ za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ yiŋ la teŋsʋk ka onɛ gur la dɔlis zaŋguom za'anɔɔr la baba dʋ dɔɔg la zug. Ka gɔsi nyɛ dau sɔ' ka o zɔt o kɔn'ɔkɔn'.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Ka onɛ gur la buol Na'ab la yɛl o. Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye, “O ya'a aan o kɔn'ɔkɔn' alaa o mɔri labasʋŋʋ kenna.” Ka dau la zɔti li'en na.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Ka onɛ gur la lɛn nyɛ dau sɔ' ka o zɔti kenna ya'as. Ka o buol onɛ gur za'anɔɔr la ye, “Gɔsima, dau sɔ' zɔt o kɔn'ɔkɔn' ya'as!” Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye, “On mɛ na mɔr nɛ labasʋŋʋ kenna.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Ka onɛ gur la yɛl ye, “Man gɔs ka onɛ gaad tuon la zɔɔg la nwɛnɛ Ahimaaz onɛ an Zadok biig la nɛ.” Ka Na'ab la lɛbis ye, “O anɛ ninsʋŋ. O na mɔr labasʋŋ na.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ka Ahimaaz paae na buol Na'ab la yɛl ye, “Si'el wʋsa an sʋ'ʋŋa!” Ka igin Na'ab la tuon ka su'uni o nindaa teŋin ka yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb Wina'am yʋ'ʋr paamim zʋn'or, o yis nimbanɛ duoe zi'e m zugdaan onɛ aan m Na'ab yɛla la.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la bu'os ye, “Ka m biig Absalom, o yi laafii?” Ka Ahimaaz lɛbis ye, “Joab n pa'a tʋmim saŋsi'a la, zin'ig la pa'a dammidnɛ, amaa man zi' dinɛ maalɛ.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl o ye, “Zi'enim kpikpɛŋ ka gu'us.” Ka o lɛb kpikpɛŋi zi'en.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Ka Kus nid la paae na yɛl ye, “M Zugdaan onɛ an Na'aba, kɛlisim labasʋŋ! Fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am yisif zina nimbanɛ duoe zi'e fʋ yɛla la nu'usin.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os Kus dim dau la ye, “Ka m biig Absalom, o yi laafii?” Ka Kus dim dau la lɛbis ye, “Naa, li an sʋm ka banɛ wʋsa duoe zi'e bɔɔd ye ba san'amif la naae nwɛnɛ na'akimbil nwa' nɛ!”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la kirid, ka dɔl za'anɔɔr la kpɛn' dɔɔgin kum. On ken la, ka yɛt ye, “O, m biig Absalom! M biigaa, m biig Absalom, man ya'a pʋn kpiin ka fʋn lɛɛ kpɛlim li naan kʋ sɔn'ɔnɛɛ, Absalom m biiga! M biigaa!”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl Joab ye, “Na'ab la kummi ka fabinnɛ o biig la yɛla.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Daakan la zabzabidib la sumalisim la da lieb nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ, bɔzugɔ ban da wʋm ka ba yɛl ye, “Na'ab la maan nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ o biig la yɛla la.”

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Nidib la da lɛb tempʋʋgin nwɛnɛ nimbanɛ keŋ zaba ka ba kadi ba ka ba di nyan ka zɔnɛ.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da lus o nindaa ka kaasidi agɔla gɔla ye, “Oi, m biig Absalom! Oi, m biig Absalom! Oi, m biigaa!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Joab da duoe keŋ Na'ab la san'an ka yɛl ye, “Zina fʋ diisi fʋ nidib la wʋsa nyan, banɛ zabɛ faaɛn fʋ nyɔvʋr nɛ fʋ biis nɛ fʋ pu'ab nɛ fʋ pu'abibis nyɔvʋr la.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Fʋ nɔŋ nɛ banɛ kisif ka yaae banɛ nɔŋif. Zina fʋ pa'alya nyain ye fʋ zabzabidib nɛ tuongatib nɛ ba nidib la anɛ zaalim fʋ tuon. Fʋ gɔs ka Absalom ya'a vʋe ka tinam wʋsa kpi zina li an sʋm.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Duom nannanna yi kpɛmisi fʋ nidib la. M pɔya nɛ Zugsɔb la ye zina fʋ ya'a pʋ duoe yii, sɔ' kʋ lɛn kpɛlimmi fʋ san'an paae yʋ'ʋŋɔ. Ka tɔɔg kanɛ ka fʋ na nyɛ la na gaad dinɛ ka fʋ nyɛ fʋ na'akinnim saŋa hali ti paae zina.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab David duoe keŋ zin' o zin'isirin za'anɔɔrin la. Ban da yɛl nidib la ye, “Na'ab la zin' za'anɔɔrin la,” ba wʋsa da la'asi kɛɛn o san'an na. David lɛbi di'e o na'am Saŋkan la Israel dim banɛ da dɔl Absalom la da pʋn zɔɔ kuli ba yaan.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Absalom onɛ ka ba daa bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zugʋ diis o na'am ye o guri ti la kpi zaba la ni: bɔɔ na kɛ ka ti kʋ lɛm mɔr Na'ab la lɛbis na?”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Na'ab David mɛ da tʋm yɛl Zadok nɛ Abiata banɛ an maanmaannib la ye, “Yɛlim Juda kpɛɛmnam la ye, ‘Bɔzug ka hali nɛ nwa' ka yanam pʋ siak ye man onɛ aan ya Na'ab la lɛb na? Man wʋm ye Israel dim pʋn siak ye m lɛb na ka yanam ma'aa zan'as.

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Ya anɛ m ba'abiis, mam mɛŋ ziim, ka bɔzug ka ya nam pʋ siak ye m lɛb na?’

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Ka yɛl Amasa ye, ‘Fʋ ka'anɛ mam mɛŋ ziim? M ya'a pʋ di'e zabzabidib kpɛɛm la Joab san'ani tisi fɔ, Wina'am on bu'osim.’”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ban da wʋm ala la Juda dim wʋsa ya'am da fɛndig ya ka li nwɛnɛ nid yinne nɛ, ka ba tʋm yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Fʋn nɛ fʋ nidib la wʋsa lɛm na.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Simie, onɛ an Gera biig ka an Benjamin nid ka yi Bahurim teŋin na la da duoe tɔ'ɔtɔ dɔl Juda dim ye ba tʋ'ʋs Na'ab David.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: Na'aba, mam baŋ ye m tʋm bɛ'ɛd, din ka man dɛŋi gaad Josef yidim la wʋsa tuonnɛ kena ye m tʋ'ʋsif, m zugdaana.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Ba da lɔ'ɔŋ kɔldaug la zin'ikanɛ pʋ zulim la ye ba nɔk Na'ab la nɛ o yidim wʋsa, ka maal linɛ wʋsa ka o bɔɔd. Simie onɛ an Gera biig la mɛ da lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan la ka igin teŋin Na'ab la tuon

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, kɛlli m taali bas, ka da tɛn'ɛsid bɛ'ɛd linɛ ka man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm daa tʋm, daakanɛ ka fʋ yit Jerusalem la! Na'aba, yisimi li fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛrin!

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Na'ab David da lɛbis ye, “Man nɛ yanam nɔɔr yinne an bɔ, yanam banɛ an Zeruyia biisɛ? Ya bɔɔd ye ya ienɛ yɛla tisim! Li sʋm ye ba kʋ sɔ' Israel teŋin zinaa? Man mi' ye zina m anɛ Israel wʋsa Na'ab.”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la lɛn yɛl Simie ye, “Fʋ kʋ kpii.” Ka yɛl nɔɔri zi'el ye sɔ' da si'is oo.

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: On yi Jerusalem kena ye o tʋ'ʋs Na'ab la, Ka na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ daa pʋ dɔllimi keŋɛ, Mefibosef?”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Ayei, m zugdaan onɛ an m Na'aba, man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la anɛ pɔn'ɔr, ka m gban'e m pʋtɛn'ɛrin ye m na gban'e m buŋi ban'a dɔllif, amaa Ziba onɛ aan m tʋmtʋm la ma'am,

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: ka kena gbi'i m yɛla fʋ san'an, m zugdaana. Na'aba, fʋ nwɛnɛ Wina'am maliak nɛ; alazugɔ tʋm linɛ an sʋm tisif, m zugdaana.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Naa, tinam banɛ an Saul biis nɛ o yaas la wʋsa narin nɛ fʋn na kʋʋ ti, amaa fʋ gaŋ mam tisim suor ye m dit nɛ banɛ diti fʋ diib zin'igin la, m zugdaana. Alazug suobɔ ka man mɔri na lɛn sɔs si'el fʋn kanɛ an na'ab la san'anɛ?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ pian'ad bɛdegʋ? M yɛl fʋn nɛ Ziba ye ya pʋdigim pɔɔd la.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Mefibosef da yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, kɛl ka o nɔk si'el wʋsa, fʋn sadigim kul nɛ laafi la na.”

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Barizila onɛ an Gilead nid la mɛ da yi Rogelim na, ye o dɔl Na'ab David n lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la zi'el o suor.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Barizila ye, “Lɔ'ɔŋim na dɔllim ka ti keŋ Jerusalem ka m na mɔrif.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Amaa Barizila da lɛbis Na'ab la ye, “Naa, mam na lɛn vʋe yʋma ala, ka li nar ye m dɔlli fʋ keŋ Jerusalem?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: M na dɔlli fʋ lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la lalig bi'ela: bɔ ka li nar ye fʋ yɔ man anwana wʋsa?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka m lɛb ka kpii m mɛŋ teŋin, zin'ikanɛ kpi'e m ba' nɛ m ma yaad la. Amaa m biig Kimham nwa', kɛl ka o lɔ'ɔŋi dɔlli fʋ keŋ, ti zugdaan onɛ an Na'aba. Naa, maalim dinɛ wʋsa ka fʋ tɛn'ɛs ka li na an sʋm la tis o.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab lɛn yɛl ye, “Tɔ', m siakya! Kimham na dɔllimi lɔ'ɔŋ, ka m na maal dinɛ na malisi fʋ tis o. Ka fʋn bɔɔd si'el wʋsa m san'an, m na maali tisif.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Ka nidib la wʋsa lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan, ka Na'ab la mɛ lɔ'ɔŋ. Ka Na'ab la pʋ'ʋs Barizila sʋ'ʋŋa ka niŋ o zug bareka, ka Barizila lɛbi kul.

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Na'ab la lɔ'ɔŋi paae Gilgal la, Kimham da dɔlli lɔ'ɔŋ. Juda zabzabidib la wʋsa nɛ Israel zabzabidib la pʋsʋk da dɔl Na'ab la lɔ'ɔŋ. Juda nɛ Israel dim nwa'as David yɛla

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Li da pʋ yuugɛ ka Israel dim la ken David san'an na ka yɛt o ye, “Naa, bɔ ka ti ba'abiis Juda dim la nɔkif nɛ fʋ yidim wʋsa nɛ fʋ nidib la lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la, ka pʋ yɛli ti?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Ka Juda dim wʋsa lɛbis Israel dim la ye, “Linɛ kɛ ka ti tʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la anɛ ye, tinam nɛ Na'ab la kpin nɛ taaba. Bɔ ka ya sʋnya pɛlig nɛ'ɛŋa yɛla? Ti di nɛ Na'ab si'el bɛɛ? Bɛɛ ti nɔknɛ si'el ye ti sʋ'oe ya?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim la lɛbis Juda nidib la ye, “Ya mɛŋ mi' ye tinam mɔr dɔɔd piiga Israel buudi la ni, ka li nar ye ti sʋ'oe Na'ab David n gati ya, ka bɔzug ka ya nɛ'ɛsidi ti wala? Ka' tinamɛ daa dɛŋi pian' yiiga ye ti na mɔr Na'ab la lɛb naa?” Amaa Juda dim la daa maligim pian'ad pian'ayaalisi tisid Israel dim la.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Dau sɔ' da bɛ ani an onɛ ieed yɛla ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Seeba, o da anɛ Bikir biig ka an Benjamin dɔɔg la nid. O da pieb na'atan ka kie kuŋ ye, “Tinam pʋ mɔr pʋʋr David san'anɛ, ti pʋ mɔr pʋʋr Jese biig la san'anɛ! Israel dima, sɔ' wʋsa lɛm kul!”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Israel dim wʋsa da bas David ka dɔl Seeba onɛ an Bikir biig la, amaa Juda dim la da kpɛm bɛɛ ba Na'ab la san'an hali lin yi Joodan n ti paae Jerusalem.
