english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Na'ab David da lɛb o yin Jerusalem, ka zaŋ o pu'abibis piiga banɛ ka o daa bas ye ba gur na'ayir la niŋi ba yin ka kɛ ka ba guri ba. O da tisidi ba diib amaa ka pʋ gbɛɛnd nɛ ba. Ba da guri ba nɛ zin'ig yinne ka ba bɛ nwɛnɛ pʋkɔnya nɛ ti paae ba kum daar. Joab n kʋ Amasa la yɛla

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Amasa ye, “Buolim Juda nidib la wʋsa daba atan' nwa' pʋʋgin la'as ka dɔlli ba fʋ mɛŋi lɛb na.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Amaa Amasa n da keŋ ye o buol Juda dim na la o da yuugi gaad Na'ab la zi'el o saŋa si'a la.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: David da yɛl Abisai ye, “Nannanna Seeba onɛ an Bikir biig la na tʋmi ti bɛ'ɛdi gaad Absalom. Duom nɛ m mɛŋ zabzabidib la kad o bugir: ya'a ka' ala, o na zɔɔ kpɛn' su'a tempʋkanɛ ka ba mɛ' zaŋguom kpi'ema giligi li ka ti kʋ paae o.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Alazug Joab zabzabidib la, nɛ Keret dim nɛ Pelet dim, nɛ zabzabidib banɛ kpi'em la wʋsa da yina ka Abisai aan ba tuongat. Ka ba naam Jerusalem kad Seeba onɛ an Bikir biig la bugir.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Ban da nam bɛ Gibeon tampintita'arin la, ka Amasa kena sia'ali ba. Joab da yɛnɛ o zaba fuug. Ka zaba sʋ'ʋg bɛɛ o sien la li tɛɛngʋn ga'al nɛ sɛnbidiŋ la. Ka on keŋ tuon la, ka li yi tɛɛngʋn la li na.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ka Joab yɛl Amasa ye, “Fʋ niŋgbina an wala, m ba'abiiga?” Ka gban'e o tieŋ nɛ o datiuŋ nu'ug wʋʋ o ye o kuak o nɛ.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Amasa da pʋ gu'usid nɛ sʋ'ʋg la bɛ Joab nu'ugin la, ka Joab kʋns o pʋʋr ka o nyɔɔd wʋsa yii li teŋin, ka o pʋ lɛn kʋns o ya'asɛ, ka Amasa kpi. Ka Joab nɛ o ba'abiig Abisai bas o ka kad Seeba Bikir biig la bugir.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Joab nidib la yinne da zi'e kpi'e Amasa ka yɛl ye, “Onɛ bɔɔd Joab nɛ David, on gaadim dɔl Joab!”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ka Amasa dig o ziimin la bilim suor teŋsʋk. Dau la nyɛ ka zabzabidib la wʋsa ɛɛnti kena kpɛlim anina la, ka o baŋ ye onɛ wʋsa paae Amasa san'an o zi'enid nɛ la, ka o vuug o kpɛn'ɛs sian'arin ka nɔk fuugʋ pil o.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Ka ban yis Amasa suorin la naae la, nidib la wʋsa da dɔl Joab ka ba kad Seeba onɛ an Bikir biig la bugir. Ban kʋ Seeba la yɛla

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Seeba da gilig Israel buudi la wʋsa paae Abɛl-Bet-Maaka ka dɔl Beer dim sʋ'ʋlimin la wʋsa, ka ba la'as taaba dɔl o.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Zabzabidib banɛ da bɛ Joab san'an la wʋsa da kena gilig Seeba nɛ Abɛl-Bet-Maaka. Ka vaae tanni pɛ'ɛl bʋmbɔk kanɛ gilig teŋ la zaŋguom la, ka yʋ'ʋn pin'ili nwɛ'ɛd zaŋguom la ye ba da'ae li bas.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Pu'a kanɛ an ya'am sɔb da naam tempʋʋgin la buol ye, “Kɛlisimi, kɛlisimi! Yɛlimi Joab ye o kem kpɛla na ka m pian' tis o.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Ka o kena kpa'ad pu'a la ka o bu'os ye, “Fʋnɛ an Joab laa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Manɛ la.” Ka o yɛl ye, “Kɛlisim! Man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la mɔr si'el ye m yɛlif.” Ka o lɛbis ye, “M kɛlisid.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Ka o keŋ tuonnɛ yɛl ye, “Yʋʋmpʋkʋda saŋa la ba da yɛl ye, fʋ ya'a bɔɔd ye fʋ gban'e fʋ pian'ad gbin, fʋn kem Abɛl teŋin ka li na maal.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Tinamɛ an sumbʋgʋsʋm nɛ sida dim Israel pʋʋgin. Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye fʋ san'am teŋ kanɛ nwɛnɛ Israel dim wʋsa ma la? Bɔ ka fʋ mɔɔd ye fʋ faaɛn teŋ kanɛ an Zugsɔb la dinnɛ?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Ka Joab lɛbis ye, “Wina'am da kɛɛ! Waii, Win da kɛ ka m san'ami lii!

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Li ka' alaa, amaa dau sɔ' ki'is Na'ab David nɔɔr ka zɔɔ kpɛn' ya teŋin la, o yʋ'ʋri buon Seeba ka o saam an Bikir onɛ yi Efiram dinɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la: zaŋimi dau yinne kaŋa tisim ka m na bas teŋ la.” Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Dim suguru ka ba na fi'ig o zugʋ lɔb ka li gaŋ zaŋguom la tisif.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Ka pu'a la keŋ nidib la wʋsa san'an nɛ o ya'am sa'alʋg la, ka ba fi'ig Seeba onɛ an Bikir biig la zugʋ lɔbigi tis Joab. Ka o pieb na'atan ka o nidib la wʋsa widig ka bas teŋ la ka ba wʋsa lɛbi kuli ba yaan, ka Joab mɛ lɛb Na'ab la san'an Jerusalem. David ninkpi'ema la yɛla

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Joab n da sʋ'oe Israel wʋsa zabzabidib la, ka Benaya onɛ an Jehoyada biig la sʋ'oe Keret dim nɛ Pelet dim.

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adoniram da sʋ'oe tʋmtʋmnib la, ka Jehosafat onɛ an Ahilud biig la sʋŋid gbauŋ sɔbid la.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Seeva da anɛ gbauŋ sɔbid, ka Zadok nɛ Abiata an maanmaannib.

english_verse: Ira from Jair was David's priest.
translation_verse: Ira onɛ an Jair nid la da an David mɛŋ maanmaan.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: David da bu'os Gibeon dim la ye, “M na maal bɔɔ tisi ya ka ya ti kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis Zugsɔb nidib la?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis na'ab la ye, “Ya'a kpɛlim dau kanɛ gban'e suobɛ'ɛdi ti yɛla ka kʋʋ ti san'ami ti ka ti pʋ lɛm mɔr zin'ig Israel la,

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: kɛl ka ti di'e o sɔb biribis ayɔpɔi kʋʋ ba paalʋ Zugsɔb la tuon Gibeon teŋin, onɛ an Saul onɛ ka Zugsɔb da gaŋ la.” Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye, “M na nɔki ba tisi ya.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Na'ab David da pʋ siak ye o kɛ ka ba kʋ Mefibosef onɛ an Jonatan biig ka mɛ an Saul yaaŋ la, bɔzugɔ on nɛ Jonatan da maal nɔnaar Zugsɔb la tuon.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: O da zaŋi ba tis Gibeon dim la ka ba kʋʋ ba paalʋ kʋkʋn zug Zugsɔb la tuon. Ba da la'asi kʋ nidiba ayɔpɔi la wʋsa ba teŋin mui bunib saŋa linɛ an sapal.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Rizipa onɛ an Aya pu'ayua la da nɔk nɛ bɔto maal digisig tampiing zugʋ gbɛɛnd, din yi bunib saŋa ti paae saŋkanɛ ka saa ni banɛ kpi la zug la, o da pʋ kɛ ka niis si'isi ba nintaŋ, bɛɛ sian'anr bʋnkɔnbid si'isi ba yʋ'ʋŋʋ.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: ka ba mum Saul nɛ o biig Jonatan kɔnba la Saul saam Kis yaʋgʋn, Zela teŋin linɛ bɛ Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin la. Ka maal si'el wʋsa wʋʋ Na'ab la yɛl si'em la. Din nya'aŋ ka Wina'am di'e ba sɔsʋg teŋ la yɛla. Israel nɛ Filistia dimi lɛn zab la yɛla (

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Zabsi'a da bɛ Gaf ya'as, ka dau tita'ar bɛ ani mɔr nu'ubibis ayuob, yuob nɛ nɔbibis ayuob, yuob. O nu'ubibis nɛ nɔbibis la da la'as nɛ pisi nɛ anaasi. O mɛ da anɛ Refa nid.

english_verse: One time David got very tired when he and his soldiers were fighting the Philistines.
translation_verse: Saŋa yinne ka Filistia dim nɛ Israel dim da lɛn zab nɛ taaba ya'as. David da dɔl o nidib la keŋ ye ba zab, ka gɛɛnlis gban'e o.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Ka Isbi-Benob, onɛ yaanamɛ da an Refa dim la, da bɛɛ ani, ka o kpan tɛbis hali ka o mɔr zaba sʋ'ʋtita'ar. O da bɔɔd ye o kʋ David,

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: amaa Zeruyia biig Abisai da zɔɔ kena faaɛn David. O da nwɛ' Filistia nid la bas teŋin ka kʋʋ o. Ka David nidib la pɔɔ zi'el ye, “Fʋ kʋ lɛn dɔlli ti keŋ zaba ya'asɛ. Bɔzugɔ fʋ anɛ fitiri tis Israel dim ka fʋ ya'a kpi fitir la na kpiig.”

english_verse: There was another battle with the Philistines at Gob, where Sibbecai from Hushah killed a descendant of the Rephaim named Saph.
translation_verse: Li da paae saŋsi'a ka zabsi'a lɛm bɛ nɛ Filistia dim la Gob teŋin. Saŋkan la Sibɛkai onɛ an Husea nid la da kʋ Saf, o mɛ da anɛ Refa nid.

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Zabir yinne da lɛn zab nɛ Filistia dim Gob teŋin. Elhanan onɛ an Jair biig ka an Betilehem nid la da kʋ Lahmi onɛ an Gaf nid ka an Goliyaf ba'abiig la, o da mɔr kpan ka kpandaug la mugumi nwɛnɛ yu'adir nɛ.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: O da nɛ'ɛs Israel dim la, ka Jonatan kʋʋ o. Jonatan ba' da anɛ David bier Simie.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Bama anaasi la wʋsa da anɛ Refa dim banɛ yi Gaf teŋin na, ka David nɛ o nidib la da kʋʋ ba.

english_verse: You rescued me from enemies who were hateful and too powerful for me.
translation_verse: O faanmi yisi m dataas banɛ mɔr paŋ hali la ni, banɛ kisim ka mɔr paŋi gatim la.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Na'ab David da yʋ'ʋm yʋʋm kaŋa tis Zugsɔb la on faaɛn o yis o dataas nɛ Saul nu'usin la.

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Alazug, Zugsɔba, m na na'asif buudi wʋsa sʋʋgin, m na yʋʋm wɔ'ɔgi fʋ yʋ'ʋr la.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: O da yʋ'ʋm ye, “Zugsɔb la aan m tampiing, m suak zin'ikpi'euŋ nɛ m faangid.

english_verse: You are the rock where I am safe. You are my shield, my powerful weapon, and my place of shelter. You rescue me and keep me safe from violence.
translation_verse: M Wina'am la aan m tampiing, o san'an ka m su'ad. Onɛ lusidim ka aan m vʋm la paŋ. O anɛ m kpi'euŋ zin'ig nɛ m faangid. O faanmi yi zabbɔɔdib la nu'usin.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: M buol Zugsɔb onɛ nar nɛ zʋn'or la, ka paam yɔlisim yii m dataas nu'usin.

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Kum lɔbi giligimi nwɛnɛ nwiis nɛ, ka kum ku'onwiis pilim yɔɔg-yɔɔg.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: M mugusʋg pʋʋgin m daa buolnɛ Zugsɔb la; m daa kaasi buoli m Wina'am la. Ka o naanɛ o Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la ka wʋm tisim, m kukuma la daa paae o san'an ka kpɛn' o tʋba ni.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Teŋgbauŋ la damnɛ ka mi'im zika-zika, hali ka saŋgbana la gbina dam, ka kirid o sʋnfʋ duoe la zug.

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Nyɔ'ɔs daa naanɛ o nyɔnya nii yina; ka bugum linɛ kanbid yii o nɔɔrin na, ka bugumsaana linɛ dit yii li pʋʋgin na.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: O da buak agɔla ka sig na, ka saŋgbansabilig bɛɛ o nɔba teŋir.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: O da ban' Kerub la iank. Ka sisi'em da'ad o ken tɔ'ɔtɔ wʋʋ niiŋ nɛ.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: O da nɔk liki su'a o mɛŋ, ka kɛ ka saa saŋgbansabilig gilig o.

english_verse: Fiery coals lit up the sky in front of you.
translation_verse: Ka bugum naan sa-ian'asʋg nɛ nɛɛsim linɛ bɛɛ o san'an la yina.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tans wʋʋ satansʋg nɛ arezana ni. Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la lɛn vu ya'as.

english_verse: You scattered your enemies with arrows of lightning.
translation_verse: O da tɔn piema la widig o bi'emnam la, ka kadi ba nɛ sa-ian'astita'ar.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, fʋ tansʋg nɛ pɛbistita'ar kanɛ yii fʋ nyɔnya ni na la kɛ ka Atɛuk ku'osuoya nɛ teŋgbauŋ la ɛɛnbir nie paalʋ.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: O naan nɛ agɔlli su'uni gban'e m nu'ugʋ yaami yis ku'ozuluŋ pʋʋgin.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Ba daa kena ludimi m dabisbɛ'og daar, amaa ka Zugsɔb la sʋŋim.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: O daa mɔrimi yii keŋ zin'ikanɛ an yaliŋa. O daa faanm on nɔŋim la zug.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tʋmnɛ tisim wʋʋ man an pʋpiel si'em la. M nu'usi an nyain la zug ka fʋ tisim piini.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Man dɔlis Zugsɔb suoya la wʋsa; m pʋ tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi fɛndig ka basi m Wina'am.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: M dɔlisid o wada la wʋsa, m pʋ fɛndig ka bas o zi'ela la.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: O pʋ nyɛ gba'ar si'a m san'anɛ, m mɔɔ gban'e m mɛŋ ka pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: M pʋpielim la zug ka Zugsɔb la niŋim zug bareka. M nu'usi an nyain la zug ka o tisim piini.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
translation_verse: Banɛ an sida dim la fʋ pa'annɛ ba ye fʋ anɛ sida sɔb, banɛ ka' gba'ar la fʋ pa'annɛ ba ye fʋn mɛ ka' gba'arɛ.

english_verse: With all who are sincere you are sincere, but you treat the unfaithful as their deeds deserve.
translation_verse: Banɛ an nyain la fʋ pa'annɛ ba ye fʋ anɛ nyain. Amaa banɛ bɛllim pʋ dɔl suor la, fʋ mɛ pa'annɛ ba ye fʋ mi' ba gbin.

english_verse: You rescue the humble, but you look for ways to put down the proud.
translation_verse: Fʋ faand banɛ siedi ba mɛŋ la, amaa fʋ kpansid nyɛɛsim dim la ka na sigisi ba teŋin.

english_verse: Our Lord and God, you are my lamp. You turn darkness to light.
translation_verse: M Zugsɔba, fʋnɛ aan m fitir, Zugsɔb la kɛ ka lik lieb nɛɛsim tisim.

english_verse: Your way is perfect, Lord, and your word is correct. You are a shield for those who run to you for help.
translation_verse: Ya'a an sida, Wina'am suoya la an sʋ'ʋŋa. Zugsɔb la pian'ad pʋ mɔr zirii; onɛ lusid banɛ wʋsa su'a o san'an.

english_verse: You are my strong fortress, and you set me free.
translation_verse: Li anɛ Wina'am la tisidim paŋ, ka maannɛ m suor sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: You make my feet run as fast as those of a deer, and you help me stand on the mountains.
translation_verse: O maali m nɔba wʋʋ walig nɔba nɛ, ka dʋ'ʋsimi zi'el zuor zug.

english_verse: You teach my hands to fight and my arms to use a bow of bronze.
translation_verse: O pa'alim mam na zab si'em, m nu'us tun'e pɔnd kʋntzɛn'ug tiraug.

english_verse: You alone are my shield, and by coming to help me, you have made me famous.
translation_verse: Fʋ zaŋ nɛ zaba gbanti'edʋgʋ lusim ka m nyaŋi m dataas. Fʋ sʋŋir kɛ ka m an nintita'ar.

english_verse: You clear the way for me, and now I won't stumble.
translation_verse: Fʋ yalig suokanɛ bɛɛ m tuon la, ka m nɔba kʋ sadigɛ.

english_verse: I kept chasing my enemies until I caught them and destroyed them.
translation_verse: M kadi m dataasi nyaŋi ba, ka pʋ fɛndig nya'aŋa, hali nɛ mam ti san'ami ba wʋsa.

english_verse: I destroyed them! I stuck my sword through my enemies, and they were crushed under my feet.
translation_verse: M san'ami ba nyain ka ba kʋ lɛn nyaŋi duoe. Ba lii m nɔba teŋir.

english_verse: You helped me win victories and forced my attackers to fall victim to me.
translation_verse: Fʋ tisim paŋ ye m zab, ka kɛ ka m dataas igini m tuon.

english_verse: You made my enemies run, and I killed them.
translation_verse: Fʋnɛ kɛ ka m dataas fɛndigi zɔ ka basim, ka m kʋ banɛ kisim la wʋsa.

english_verse: They cried out for help, but no one saved them; they called out to you, but there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ka ba kaasi bɔɔd sʋŋir, amaa sɔ' kae na faaɛn ba. Ba kaasi tis Zugsɔb la ka o pʋ gi'e gɔsi ba.

english_verse: I ground them to dust, and I squashed them like mud in the streets.
translation_verse: M bʋ' ba hali ka ba ti nwɛnɛ uusʋg nɛ. M tuo ba ka nɔɔ ba mɛdig nwɛnɛ bian'ar dinɛ bɛ suorinɛ.

english_verse: You rescued me from my stubborn people and made me the leader of foreign nations, who are now my slaves.
translation_verse: Fʋ faanmi yis nimbanɛ kisim la nu'usin, ka kɛ ka m lieb tɛɛns la zugdaan; ka sʋ'oe nimbanɛ ka m zi' ba.

english_verse: They have lost all courage and from their fortresses they come trembling.
translation_verse: Ba wʋsa giinla kɛns nɛ, ka ba kiridi yiti ba kpi'euŋ zin'isin kenna.

english_verse: You are the living Lord! I will praise you! You are a mighty rock. I will honor you for keeping me safe.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sid bɛ! Zun'or anɛ m Tampiing la din! Wina'am onɛ aan m tampiing ka aan m Faangid la yʋ'ʋr na nyɛ dʋ'ʋsʋg.

english_verse: You took revenge for me, and you put nations in my power.
translation_verse: O anɛ Wina'am onɛ yɔɔd banɛ tummim bɛ'ɛd la sam, ka kɛt ka m nyaŋ tɛɛns banɛ giligim la ka sʋ'ʋgi ba,

english_verse: You protected me from violent enemies, and you made me much greater than all of them.
translation_verse: ka faanmi m dataas san'ani bas. Fʋ dʋ'ʋsimi gaadi m dataas, ka faanmi yis banɛ bɔɔd zaba la ni.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord has told me what to say.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Siig la pian' yii m san'an na, o pian'ad la da bɛ nɛ m zilimin.

english_verse: Our Mighty Rock, the God of Jacob, told me, “A ruler who obeys God and does right
translation_verse: Israel Wina'am la pian' ya. Israel Tampiing la yɛlim ye, “Sɔ' ya'a sʋ'oe nidib ka guri ba nɛ pʋpielim, o ya'a guri ba nɛ Wina'am zɔtim,

english_verse: is like the sunrise on a cloudless day, or like rain that sparkles on the grass.”
translation_verse: o nwɛnɛ winnigi na tans bɛogʋn ka li nie nɛ, bɛkɛung kanɛ ka saŋgbana kae, ka nwɛnɛ saa na nii nie ka mɔɔd yit teŋin na nɛ.”

english_verse: I have ruled this way, and God will never break his promise to me. God's promise is complete and unchanging; he will always help me and give me what I hope for.
translation_verse: “Man yir an sʋ'ʋŋa tis Wina'am. O pʋ maal o nɔnaar dinɛ ka' naar la nɛ mam? Ka mɛ gu' si'el wʋsa ka li an sʋ'ʋŋaa? O kʋ maali m yɛla wʋsa hali, ka faaɛn maa? O na tisim man bɔɔd si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: But evil people are pulled up like thornbushes. They are not dug up by hand,
translation_verse: Amaa nimbɛ'ɛdnam la, ba na lɔbi ba kpikpɛŋ sa wʋʋ gɔn'ɔs dinɛ ka ba kʋ siaki zaŋ nu'usi ku'olɛ.

english_verse: but with a sharp spear and are burned on the spot. The Three Warriors (
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋsa ye o si'is gɔn'ɔs zaŋid nɛ kʋnt daug bɛɛ kpandaug. Ba na nyu'oe ba nɛ bugum, ban dig zin'isi'a la.” David zabzabidib banɛ da kpi'em la (

english_verse: except Eleazar. He killed Philistines until his hand was cramped, and he couldn't let go of his sword. When Eleazar finished, all the Israelite troops had to do was come back and take the enemies' weapons and armor. The Lord gave Israel a great victory that day.
translation_verse: amaa Eleazar da zi'en ka kʋ Filistia dim la hali ka o nu'ug ti kena gɛn ka ga'aŋi tabinɛ o sʋ'ʋg la. Zugsɔb la da tisi ba nyaŋir dabiskan la daar. Zabzabidib la da lɛb Eleazar san'an na amaa ba da yɛɛsnɛ kpi'imnam la la'ad ma'aa.

english_verse: and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. He was the commander of the Thirty Warriors, but he still did not become one of the Three Warriors.
translation_verse: O da di'e na'asi gaad nidib pistan' la, hali ka liebi ba tuongat, la'an nɛ ban da pʋ kaal o paas nimbɛda atan' la sʋʋgin la.

english_verse: These are the names of David's warriors: Ishbosheth the son of Hachmon was the leader of the Three Warriors. In one battle, he killed
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋbama anɛ nintitada banɛ da an Na'ab David nidib la: Joseb Basibef onɛ da an Takɛmon nid la da an nimbɛda atan' la kpɛɛm. O da nɔk kpan nɛ kʋ nidib kɔbisnii zabir yinne ma'aa ni.

english_verse: The next one of the Three Warriors was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite. One time when the Philistines were at war with Israel, he and David dared the Philistines to fight them. Every one of the Israelite soldiers turned and ran,
translation_verse: Onɛ tia'al anɛ Eleazar onɛ an Dodai biig ka an Ahoohi nid la. O anɛ onɛ da paas nimbɛda atan' la ni. Li da paae saŋa si'a ka Filistia dim la'as Pas-Damim ye ba zab, ka Eleazar nɛ David tʋ'ʋdi ba. Ka dabiem kpɛn' Israel dim zabzabidib la ka ba zɔ,

english_verse: but Shammah stood in the middle of the field and killed the Philistines. The crops were saved, and the Lord gave Israel a great victory.
translation_verse: amaa Seamma da zi'en pɔɔg la teŋsʋkʋ zab. O da zab nɛ Filistia dim la, ka Zugsɔb tis o paŋ ka o nyaŋi ba hali.

english_verse: One year at harvest time, the Three Warriors went to meet David at Adullam Cave. The Philistine army had set up camp in Rephaim Valley
translation_verse: Li da anɛ Bunib saŋa ya'as ka nidib atan' banɛ an nidib pistan' la kpɛɛmnam la kɛn David san'an na, tampinyɔkin dinɛ bɛ Adullam la. Ka Filistia dim la mɛ la'as Refa Dim Bɔn'ɔgin la zi'e ye ba zab.

english_verse: and had taken over Bethlehem. David was in his fortress,
translation_verse: Saŋkan la David da bɛ nɛ o zin'ikpi'euŋin la, ka Filistia zabzabidib la bɛ Betilehem.

english_verse: and he was very thirsty. He said, “I wish I had a drink from the well by the gate at Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ku'onuud da mɔr David ka o yɛl ye, “O! M bɔɔd ye sɔ' gbin'e ku'om bulig kanɛ kpi'e Betilehem za'anɔɔrin la na tisinim!”

english_verse: The Three Warriors sneaked into the Philistine camp and got some water from the well near Bethlehem's gate. But after they brought the water back to David, he refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as a sacrifice
translation_verse: Ka o nimbɛda atan' la bʋŋ Filistia dim la teŋsʋkʋ gaadi keŋ paae bulig kanɛ kpi'e Betilehem za'anɔɔrin la gbin'e ku'om la zii lɛb na tis David. Amaa o da zan'as ya ka pʋ nu ku'om la, ka kpa'ae li bas Zugsɔb la tuon,

english_verse: and said to the Lord, “I can't drink this water! It's like the blood of these men who risked their lives to get it for me.” The Three Warriors did these brave deeds. The Thirty Warriors (
translation_verse: ka yɛl ye, “Win da kɛ ka m tʋm nɛ'ɛŋaa, m Zugsɔba! Li na nwɛnɛ nimbanɛ kuosi ba nyɔvʋri keŋ la ziim ka m nu.” Alazug ka o zan'as ka pʋ nuu. Tʋʋm kpi'ema banɛ ka nimbɛda atan' nwa' da tʋm nwana.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did some amazing things. He killed two of Moab's best fighters, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.
translation_verse: Benaya, onɛ an Jehoyada biig la, da anɛ zabzabid hali, ka yi Kabziel teŋin na. O da mɔya hali. O da kʋ Moab nimbɛda ayi'. O da lɛn sig bʋmbɔkin kʋ gbigim, daar kanɛ ka sisalig da bɛ ka ku'om ga'aŋi nwɛnɛ sakuga la.

english_verse: Another time, he killed an Egyptian, as big as a giant. The Egyptian was armed with a spear, but Benaiah only had a club. Benaiah grabbed the spear from the Egyptian and killed him with it.
translation_verse: O mɛ da kʋ Egipt dau tita'ar la'an nɛ on da zanl kpan o nu'ugin la. Benaya da keŋ o san'an nɛ balaar ka zɛ kpan la Egipt dim dau la nu'ugin faaɛn ka nɔk o mɛŋ kpan nɛ kʋʋ o.

english_verse: Benaiah did these things. He never became one of the Three Warriors, but he was just as famous as they were and certainly just as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. David made him the leader of his bodyguard.
translation_verse: O da di'e na'asi gaad nidib pistan' la, amaa o da pʋ paas nimbɛda atan' la nii. Ka David da kɛ ka o sʋ'oe banɛ gur on mɛŋ la.

english_verse: and said, “Your Majesty! Why have you come to see me?” David answered, “I've come to buy your threshing place. I have to build the Lord an altar here, so this disease will stop killing the people.”
translation_verse: Ka yɛl ye, “Bɔ ka m zugdaan onɛ an m Na'ab la, kɛn man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la san'an na?” Ka Na'ab David lɛbis o ye, “M ye m da' nɛ fʋ zieŋ nwa' mɛ' maan bimbimi tis Zugsɔb la, ka daasi'erɛɛ tɔɔg dinɛ paae nidib la na gu'oe.”

english_verse: They went to Gilead and to Kadesh in Syria. Then they went to Dan, Ijon, and on toward Sidon.
translation_verse: Ba da keŋ Gilead nɛ Tatim-Hodis sʋ'ʋlimin paae Dan-Jaan kaae Sidon baba.

english_verse: So David told Joab and the army officers, “Go to every tribe in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north all the way south to Beersheba, and count everyone who can serve in the army. I want to know how many there are.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Joab nɛ zaba tuongatib banɛ bɛɛ o san'an la ye, “Kemi Israel buudi la wʋsa ni, din yi Dan n paae Beerseba, kaalimini ba ka m baŋ ban zem si'em.”

english_verse: But when David refused to change his mind, Joab and the army officers went out and started counting the people.
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab la daa pian' kad Joab nɛ tuongatib la ka ba gʋ'ʋŋi keŋ kaal Israel zabzabidib la.

english_verse: They crossed the Jordan River and began with Aroer and the town in the middle of the river valley. From there they went toward Gad and on as far as Jazer.
translation_verse: Ban da lɔ'ɔŋ Joodan kɔldaug la, ba da la'as nɛ zin'ikanɛ kpi'e Aroa tempʋʋg la dagɔbʋg bɔn'ɔgin la. Ba da dɔlli yi Gad n paae Jaza.

english_verse: After they had gone through the whole land, they went back to Jerusalem. It had taken them
translation_verse: Ban da gilig teŋ la wʋsa naae la, ba da lɛb Jerusalem na nwadis awai nɛ dabpisi daar.

english_verse: Araunah looked and saw David and his soldiers coming up toward him. He went over to David, bowed down low,
translation_verse: Arauna n da ʋk o nindaa gɔsi nyɛ ka Na'ab la nɛ o nidib kennɛ o san'an na la, o da yina igin ka o nindaa kpa' teŋin.

english_verse: David saw the angel killing everyone and told the Lord, “These people are like sheep with me as their shepherd. I have sinned terribly, but they have done nothing wrong. Please, punish me and my family instead of them!” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: David n da nyɛ maliak kanɛ nwɛ'ɛd nidib la kʋʋd la, o da yɛl Zugsɔb la ye, “Manɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛd nɛ dinɛ ka' sʋm. Bama nwɛnɛ pɛ'ɛs nɛ, ba maal bɔ? Kɛl ka tɔɔg la li man nɛ m yidim zugin.” Na'ab David n maal maannɛ gu'oe yɛltɔɔd la yɛla

english_verse: After everyone had been counted, David realized he had done wrong. He told the Lord, “What I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Lord, please forgive me.”
translation_verse: On da kaal nidib la naae la, David ya'am da lɛb na ka o yɛl Zugsɔb la ye, “M tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɛdegʋ nɛ man maal si'el la. Nannanna, Zugsɔba, m bɛlimnɛ, yisimi, fʋ tʋmtʋm la, tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi bas, ka m tʋm zɔlim tʋʋma.”

english_verse: Before David even got up the next morning, the Lord had told David's prophet Gad
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nied ka Na'ab David nam pʋ duoe gbɛɛmin la ka Zugsɔb pian'ad paae Gad onɛ an Wina'am nɔdi'es ka an onɛ tu'asid David bɛog sa yɛla la ye,

english_verse: to take a message to David. Gad went to David and told him: You must choose one of three ways for the Lord to punish you: Will there be seven years when the land won't grow enough food for your people? english_verse: When Bathsheba went to see Solomon, he stood up to meet her, then bowed low. He sat back down and had another throne brought in, so his mother could sit at his right side.
translation_verse: Ka Batsieba kpɛn' Na'ab Solomon san'an ye o pian' Adonija yɛla la, ka Na'ab la duoe tʋ'ʋs o, vanbin o tuonnɛ na'as o, ka lɛbi zin'in o na'am gbauŋ zug. Ka o kɛ ka ba mɔr kʋk na tis Na'ab ma la ka o zin'in o datiuŋ.

english_verse: Bathsheba sat down and then asked, “Would you do me a small favor?” Solomon replied, “Mother, just tell me what you want, and I will do it.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o ye, “Naa m bɔɔd ye m sɔs nɛ si'el bi'ela fʋ ni, amaa da mɔŋi ma!” Ka Na'ab la ye, “M maa, yɛlim ka m kʋ mɔŋi fɔ!”

english_verse: Solomon said: What? Let my older brother marry Abishag? You may as well ask me to let him rule the kingdom! And why don't you ask such favors for Abiathar and Joab?
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Solomon lɛbis o ma ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ sɔsid Abisag onɛ an Seunim nid la ye fʋ tisi Adonija? Fʋ na ba'asi sɔs na'am la tis o! M mi' ye o anɛ m bier. Ɛɛn, fʋ sɔsid na'am la nɛ ye fʋ tis on nɛ Abiata onɛ an maanmaan la nɛ Joab Zeruyia biig la.”

english_verse: I swear in the name of the Lord that Adonijah will die because he asked for this! If he doesn't, I pray that God will severely punish me.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Solomon pɔ nɛ Zugsɔb la ye, “Wina'am kɛl ka tɔɔg kɛɛn m san'an na li ya'a bɔɔd din an si'em Adonija ya'a pʋ zaŋ o nyɔvʋri yɔ on sɔsid si'el la yɛlɛ!

english_verse: The Lord made me king in my father's place and promised that the kings of Israel would come from my family. Yes, I swear by the living Lord that Adonijah will die today.
translation_verse: M pɔya nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ diisimi m saam David na'am ka dabiem kae, ka zi'el na'am la tinam zakin kpɛla nwɛnɛ on da pɔ nɔɔri zi'el si'em la, asɛɛ Adonija kpi zina!”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “go kill Adonijah.” So Adonijah died. Abiathar Is Sent Back Home
translation_verse: Na'ab Solomon da tis Benaya onɛ an Jehoyada biig la nɔɔr ka o keŋ nwɛ' Adonija bas teŋin ka o kpi. Ba yis Abiata maanmaan tʋʋma ni

english_verse: Solomon sent for Abiathar the priest and said: Abiathar, go back home to Anathoth! You ought to be killed too, but I won't do it now. When my father David was king, you were in charge of the sacred chest, and you went through a lot of hard times with my father.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Abiata onɛ an maanmaan la ye, “Lɛm Anatof linɛ aan fʋ mɛŋ teŋin la zin'in! Fʋ nar nɛ fʋn na kpi, amaa m kʋ kʋʋf nannannaa, bɔzugɔ fʋ da zi Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la Nɔnaar Daka la dɔlli m saam David, ka mɛ di namiskan ka m saam da namis la.”

english_verse: But I won't let you be a priest of the Lord anymore. And so the promise that the Lord had made at Shiloh about the family of Eli came true. Joab Is Killed
translation_verse: Dinzug, Solomon da yisi Abiata Zugsɔb maanmaan tʋʋma la ni, ka kɛ ka Zugsɔb pian'ad la liebi amɛŋa, on da yɛl si'el Eli yir yɛla Siilo teŋin la. Joab kum yɛla

english_verse: Joab had not helped Absalom try to become king, but he had helped Adonijah. So when Joab learned that Adonijah had been killed, he ran to the sacred tent and grabbed hold of the corners of the altar for protection.
translation_verse: Labaari da paae Joab onɛ naal nɔɔr nɛ Adonija la, la'an nɛ on da pʋ dɔl Absalom la, o da zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' Zugsɔb Sʋgʋrin la, ka gban'e maan daka la iila zi'e.

english_verse: When Solomon heard about this, he sent someone to ask Joab, “Why did you run to the altar?” Joab sent back his answer, “I was afraid of you, and I ran to the Lord for protection.” Then Solomon shouted, “Benaiah, go kill Joab!”
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl Na'ab Solomon ye, Joab zɔɔ kpɛn' Zugsɔb sʋgʋrin zi'e maan daka la ni la, Solomon da tis Benaya onɛ an Jehoyada biig la nɔɔr ye, “Kem nwɛ' o kʋ!”

english_verse: Benaiah went to the sacred tent and yelled, “Joab, the king orders you to come out!” “No!” Joab answered. “Kill me right here.” Benaiah went back and told Solomon what Joab had said.
translation_verse: Benaya da kpɛn' Zugsɔb sʋgʋrin la yɛl Joab ye, “Na'ab ye fʋ yina!” Amaa ka o lɛbis o ye, “Ayei, mam na kpi kpɛla!” Ka Benaya lɛbi yɛl Na'ab la Joab n lɛbis o si'em la.

english_verse: Solomon replied: Do what Joab said. Kill him and bury him! Then my family and I won't be responsible for what he did to Abner the commander of Israel's army and to Amasa the commander of Judah's army. He killed those innocent men without my father knowing about it. Both of them were better men than Joab. Now the Lord will make him pay for those murders.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na yɔɔ o sam ziim kanɛ ka o yis la yɛla, bɔzugɔ, o kʋ dapa ayi' ka m saam zi' ti'irɛ; ba da anɛ Abner onɛ an Nier biig ka an Israel zabzabidib tuongat la, nɛ Amasa onɛ an Jeta biig ka an Juda zabzabidib tuongat la. Nidiba ayi' nwa' da anɛ ninsʋma ka an sida dimi gat o.

english_verse: Benaiah went back and killed Joab. His body was taken away and buried near his home in the desert.
translation_verse: Ka Benaya keŋ nwɛ' Joab n kʋʋ o: ka ba mum o, o mɛŋ yin mɔɔgin sa.

english_verse: Solomon put Benaiah in Joab's place as army commander, and he put Zadok in Abiathar's place as priest. Shimei Is Killed
translation_verse: Na'ab la da kɛ ka Benaya an soogianam kpɛɛm n di'e Joab zin'ig, ka Zadok mɛ di'e Abiata zin'igi an maanmaan. Simie kum yɛla

english_verse: Solomon sent for Shimei and said, “Build a house here in Jerusalem and live in it. But whatever you do, don't leave the city!
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tʋm buol Simie ka yɛl o ye, “Mɛɛmi fʋ yir Jerusalem tempʋʋgini bɛɛ ani, amaa da keŋ zin'isi'a.

english_verse: If you ever cross Kidron Valley and leave Jerusalem, you will be killed. And it will be your own fault.”
translation_verse: Daar kanɛ ka fʋ ti yii lɔ'ɔŋ Kidron bɔn'ɔg la, baŋim ye fʋ na kpi, ka fʋ ziim na kpɛlimmi fʋ mɛŋ zugin.”

english_verse: “That's fair, Your Majesty,” Shimei answered. “I'll do that.” So Shimei lived in Jerusalem from then on.
translation_verse: Simie da lɛbis Na'ab la ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, fʋn yɛl si'em la an sʋ'ʋŋa, m na niŋ ala!” Simie da zin'in Jerusalem ka li yuug.

english_verse: About three years later, two of Shimei's servants ran off to King Achish in Gath. When Shimei found out where they were,
translation_verse: Amaa yʋma atan' nya'aŋ ka o sankpan'asnam ayi' zɔɔ keŋ Akis onɛ an Maaka biig ka an Gaf na'ab la san'an. Ka ba yɛl Simie ye, “Fʋ sankpan'asnam la bɛ Gaf teŋin.”

english_verse: Someone told Solomon that Shimei had gone to Gath and was back.
translation_verse: Solomon n da wʋm ye, Simie yi Jerusalem keŋ Gaf ka lɛb na la,

english_verse: Solomon sent for him and said: Shimei, you promised in the name of the Lord that you would never leave Jerusalem. I warned you that you would die if you did. You agreed that this was fair, didn't you?
translation_verse: o da buol Simie yɛl o ye, “M da kɛ ka fʋ pɔ Zugsɔb la tuon ka sa'alif ye, daar kanɛ ka fʋ ti yi Jerusalem keŋ zin'isi'a, baŋim ye daakan la fʋ na kpi, bɛɛ ka' ala? Saŋkan la fʋ da yɛlim ye, li an sʋ'ʋŋa, ye fʋ na siaki li!

english_verse: You have disobeyed me and have broken the promise you made to the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ pʋ dɔlli fʋ nɔzi'elʋg kanɛ ka fʋ zi'el Zugsɔb la tuon, ka dɔlis man tisif nɔsi'a la?”

english_verse: I know you remember all the cruel things you did to my father David. Now the Lord is going to punish you for what you did.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da lɛn yɛl Simie ye, “Fʋ mi' fʋ sʋnfʋn tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka fʋ tʋm tisim saam David la. Baŋim ye Zugsɔb la na yɔɔ fʋ li sam.

english_verse: But the Lord will bless me and make my father's kingdom strong forever.
translation_verse: Amaa man Solomon na mɔr albareka, ka David na'am la na kpɛm bɛ Zugsɔb la tuon saŋa wʋsa.”

english_verse: “Benaiah,” Solomon shouted, “kill Shimei.” So Shimei died. Solomon was now in complete control of his kingdom.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis Benaya onɛ an Jehoyada biig la nɔɔr, ka o yii keŋ nwɛ' Simie kʋ. Solomon na'am la yʋ'ʋn da zi'e kiŋ-kiŋ.

english_verse: At that time, there was no temple for worshiping the Lord, and everyone offered sacrifices at the local shrines.
translation_verse: Nidib la da nan kpɛm maan maana nɛ zuoya ni bɔzugɔ, saŋkan la ba da nam pʋ mɛ Zugsɔb la yirɛ. Solomon maal maan ka sɔs ya'am

english_verse: I'll also give you what you didn't ask for. You'll be rich and respected as long as you live, and you'll be greater than any other king.
translation_verse: Dinɛ lɛm pɛ'ɛs, m na tisif dinɛ ka fʋ pʋ sɔsɛ. M na tisif kpan'am nɛ girima wʋsa; ka fʋ nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa, na'ab kʋ bɛɛ zem nɛ fɔ.

english_verse: Solomon loved the Lord and followed his father David's instructions, but Solomon also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the shrines.
translation_verse: Solomon da pa'annɛ o nɔŋilim nɛ Zugsɔb la ka dɔlisid o saam David wada, ya'a ka' on da maan maana ka nyu'od tudaar zuoya ni la ma'aanɛɛ.

english_verse: One night while Solomon was in Gibeon, the Lord God appeared to him in a dream and said, “Solomon, ask for anything you want, and I will give it to you.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da nie o mɛŋ Solomon san'an zaansʋŋin Gibeon teŋin ka yɛl o ye, “Sɔsim fʋn bɔɔd ye m tisif si'el wʋsa.”

english_verse: Solomon answered: My father David, your servant, was honest and did what you commanded. You were always loyal to him, and you gave him a son who is now king.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Solomon lɛbis ye, “Fʋ pa'ali fʋ nɔŋilim nɛ fʋ tʋmtʋm David onɛ an m saam la, bɔzugɔ, o da tisif sida nɛ pʋpielim ka zi'e sʋ'ʋŋa nɛ o sʋʋnr wʋsa. Fʋ nan kpɛn ken tuon nɛ nɔŋilim tita'ar o san'an ka tis o biribiŋ ye o zin'in o na'am gbauŋ la zug zina.

english_verse: Lord God, I'm your servant, and you've made me king in my father's place. But I'm very young and know so little about being a leader.
translation_verse: “Nannanna, m Zugsɔb Wina'am, fʋ kɛya ka m di'e m saam David zin'igi di na'am, amaa m anɛ biig ka zi' mam na tʋmmi m na'am tʋʋma wʋsa si'em.

english_verse: And now I must rule your chosen people, even though there are too many of them to count.
translation_verse: M bɛ nɛ nimbanɛ ka fʋ gaŋ la sʋʋgin ye m tʋmmi tisidif. Ba anɛ nimbɛda ka zu'oe ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kaal bɛɛ gɛligi baa.

english_verse: Please make me wise and teach me the difference between right and wrong. Then I will know how to rule your people. If you don't, there is no way I could rule this great nation of yours.
translation_verse: Alazug, tisim ya'am ka m na guri fʋ nidib la ka mi' sʋ'ʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛdi bakid. Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi gɔsi fʋ nimbama wʋsa?” Solomon winsɔsʋg gandigir

english_verse: God said: Solomon, I'm pleased that you asked for this. You could have asked to live a long time or to be rich. Or you could have asked for your enemies to be destroyed. Instead, you asked for wisdom to make right decisions.
translation_verse: Wina'am da yɛl o ye, “Fʋn sadigim sɔs nɛ', ka pʋ sɔs nyɔvʋwɔk bɛɛ kpan'am fʋ mɛŋ yɛlɛ, bɛɛ sɔs ye fʋ dataas kpii, amaa ka sɔs ya'am ye fʋ gur nidib la nɛ sida la,

english_verse: So I'll make you wiser than anyone who has ever lived or ever will live.
translation_verse: m na maal fʋn sɔs si'el la, ka na tisif ya'am nɛ baŋir linɛ ka sɔ' nam zi' mɔra, ka sɔ' mɛ kʋ lɛm maligim mɔri li buudii.

english_verse: If you obey me and follow my commands, as your father David did, I'll let you live a long time.
translation_verse: Ka fʋ ya'a dɔlli m suoya la nɛ m nɔzi'elʋg nɛ m wada la wʋʋ fʋ saam David n da dɔl si'em la, m na tisif nyɔvʋwɔk.”

english_verse: Solomon woke up and realized that God had spoken to him in the dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the sacred chest, where he offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. Then Solomon gave a feast for his officials. Solomon Makes a Difficult Decision
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Solomon nie ka yʋ'ʋn baŋ ye li anɛ zaansʋŋ. O da lɛb Jerusalem zi'en Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la tuonnɛ maal maan dinɛ an nyu'or maan nɛ taaba la'asʋg maan. Ka maal diib nɛ bʋnnuuda tis o nidib la wʋsa. Na'ab Solomon kad saria nɛ ya'am

english_verse: One day two women came to King Solomon,
translation_verse: Lin nya'aŋ ka pu'agɔɔnda ayi' mɔri ba antu'a kɛn Na'ab Solomon san'an na.

english_verse: and one of them said: Your Majesty, this woman and I live in the same house. Not long ago my baby was born at home,
translation_verse: Ka yinne yɛl o ye, “M zugdaana, man nɛ pu'a kaŋa la'am bɛ nɛ yir yinne. Man daa du'a biig la ka o bɛ.

english_verse: and three days later her baby was born. Nobody else was there with us.
translation_verse: Man du'a la daba atan' daar ka pu'a nwa' mɛ du'a. Tinam ma'aa bɛ yin la, sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ bɛ yin la paas tinamɛ ti babayi' la zugɔ.

english_verse: One night while we were all asleep, she rolled over on her baby, and he died.
translation_verse: “Ka pu'a kaŋa sa gbisi biligi diinli o biig la ka o kpi,

english_verse: Then while I was still asleep, she got up and took my son out of my bed. She put him in her bed, then she put her dead baby next to me.
translation_verse: ka o duoe yʋ'ʋŋ tisʋʋsi keŋ nɔk man biig la saŋkanɛ ka m sa gbisid la. Ka zaŋ man biribiŋ la digil o tuon ka zaŋ o bikpiilʋŋ la digil man tuon.

english_verse: In the morning when I got up to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him in the light, I knew he wasn't my son.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ bɔɔd nier la ka man duoe ye m mu'asi m biig la nyɛ ka o kpi! Amaa bɛogʋ nie naae nyain ka mam gɔs o kii la, li ka' bikanɛ ka man du'a la laa.”

english_verse: “No!” the other woman shouted. “He was your son. My baby is alive!” “The dead baby is yours,” the first woman yelled. “Mine is alive!” They argued back and forth in front of Solomon,
translation_verse: Ka pu'a kaŋa la mɛ yɛl ye, “Ayei, biribiŋ kanɛ vʋe la anɛ mam biig, bikpiilʋŋ la aan fʋ din!” Amaa pu'a kanɛ dɛŋ tuon la zan'as ka ye, “Ayei, bikpiilʋŋ la aan fʋ din, ka onɛ vʋe la an man biig!” Ka ba nwa'as taaba Na'ab la tuon.

english_verse: Someone bring me a sword.” A sword was brought, and Solomon ordered,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye ba tisim o sʋ'ʋraug, ka ba mɔr sʋ'ʋraug na tis o.

english_verse: “Cut the baby in half! That way each of you can have part of him.”
translation_verse: Ka o tis nɔɔr ye, “Buakimi bivʋr la pʋsʋk; tisimi oŋa pʋsʋk ka mɛ tis oŋa la pʋsʋk!”

english_verse: “Please don't kill my son,” the baby's mother screamed. “Your Majesty, I love him very much, but give him to her. Just don't kill him.” The other woman shouted, “Go ahead and cut him in half. Then neither of us will have the baby.”
translation_verse: Amaa pu'a kanɛ biigi vʋe la da zɔɔ o biig la nimbaanlig ka yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Naa, m zugdaana, tisim o bivʋr la ka da kʋʋ o!” Amaa oŋa la yɛl ye, “Man nɛ fʋ wʋsa kʋ nyɛ biig la, buakim o zin'is ayi'!”

english_verse: Solomon said, “Don't kill the baby.” Then he pointed to the first woman, “She is his real mother. Give the baby to her.”
translation_verse: Ani ka Na'ab la kʋ pian'ad la ye, “Nɔkimi biig la tis pu'a kanɛ kɛn yiiga na la, da kʋʋ o; ka li anɛ o maa la.”

english_verse: Everyone in Israel was amazed when they heard how Solomon had made his decision. They realized that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
translation_verse: Israel dim wʋsa wʋm Na'ab la vɛɛns si'em ka naan kʋ antu'a la li lidigi ba nɛ, bɔzugɔ ba baŋ ye o nyɛ ya'am la nɛ Wina'am san'an ka tu'ad linɛ an sida.

english_verse: Solomon chose twelve regional officers, who took turns bringing food for him and his household. Each officer provided food from his region for one month of the year.
translation_verse: Solomon mɛ da mɔr kpɛɛmnam pii nɛ ayi', banɛ an sʋ'ʋlim kpɛɛmnam ka bɛ Israel tɛɛnsin la, banɛ da la'asid diibi tisid Na'ab nɛ o yidim la wʋsa. Sɔ' wʋsa da tisid nɛ nwadig yinne yʋʋm wʋsa pʋʋgin.

english_verse: These were the twelve officers: The son of Hur was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ba yʋda nwa': Benhur da sʋ'oe Efiram dinɛ an kʋkʋna teŋ la;

english_verse: The son of Deker was in charge of the towns of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-Shemesh, and Elon-Beth-Hanan.
translation_verse: ka Bendeka sʋ'oe Makas nɛ Saalibim nɛ Befisemes nɛ Elon nɛ Befihanan tɛɛns la;

english_verse: The son of Geber was in charge of the town of Ramoth in Gilead and the villages in Gilead belonging to the family of Jair, a descendant of Manasseh. He was also in charge of the region of Argob in Bashan, which had
translation_verse: Bengeba da sʋ'oe Ramot linɛ bɛ Gilead teŋin la, ka lɛn sʋ'oe teŋkpɛmis linɛ ka Manase biig Jair da zin' Gilead sʋ'ʋlimin la, nɛ Agob sʋ'ʋlim dinɛ bɛ Basan la, o tempʋʋs da anɛ pisyuobʋ banɛ ka ba mɛ' zaŋguommi gilig, ka zaŋ kʋntzɛn'ug daadi kpari li za'anɔɔr la;

english_verse: Ahinadab son of Iddo was in charge of the territory of Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Ahinadab onɛ an Iddo biig la da sʋ'oe Mahanam teŋ la;

english_verse: Baana son of Hushai was in charge of the territory of Asher and the town of Bealoth.
translation_verse: Baana onɛ an Husai biig la, da sʋ'oe Aser dɔɔg sʋ'ʋlim, nɛ Alof teŋ;

english_verse: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was in charge of the territory of Issachar.
translation_verse: Jehosafat onɛ an Parua biig la da sʋ'oe Isaka dɔɔg sʋ'ʋlim;

english_verse: Shimei son of Ela was in charge of the territory of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Simie onɛ an Ela biig la da sʋ'oe Benjamin dɔɔg sʋ'ʋlim;

english_verse: Geber son of Uri was in charge of Gilead, where King Sihon of the Amorites and King Og of Bashan had lived. And one officer was in charge of the territory of Judah. The Size of Solomon's Kingdom
translation_verse: Geber onɛ an Uri biig la da sʋ'oe Gilead teŋgbauŋ, Amor dim na'ab Sihon nɛ Basan teŋ na'ab Og n da bɛ si'el la. Diisi yinne da bɛ sʋ'oe tɛɛns la wʋsa. Na'ab Solomon mɔrim nɛ o ya'am yɛla

english_verse: Solomon ruled every kingdom between the Euphrates River and the land of the Philistines down to Egypt. These kingdoms paid him taxes as long as he lived.
translation_verse: Solomon da sʋ'ʋg tɛɛns la wʋsa, din yi Efiritis kɔldaug la keŋ paae Filistia teŋin keŋ paae Egipt teŋ titɔndig. Tembama dim da tʋmnɛ ka yɔɔd lampɔ tisid Solomon o nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa la wʋsa.

english_verse: Solomon ruled the whole region west of the Euphrates River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, and he was at peace with all of the countries around him.
translation_verse: O da sʋ'oe tɛɛns banɛ bɛ kɔldaug la tuon la nɛ li na'anam, din yi Tifsa m paae Gaza la, ka mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm zin'is wʋsa ka zaba kae.

english_verse: Everyone living in Israel, from the town of Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south, was safe as long as Solomon lived. Each family sat undisturbed beneath its own grape vines and fig trees.
translation_verse: Solomon nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa la, Juda nɛ Israel dim wʋsa da bɛnɛ nɛ sumalisim ka dabiem kae, din yi Dan hali keŋ paae Beerseba teŋin. Sɔ' wʋsa da mɔr o pɔɔg nɛ o lɔmbɔn'ɔg.

english_verse: Each of the twelve regional officers brought food to Solomon and his household for one month of the year. They provided everything he needed,
translation_verse: Diisinam la da mɔr sɔ' wʋsa nɛ o nwadig ka o ziid diibi kenna tisid Na'ab Solomon nɛ banɛ wʋsa ken na'ayin na ye ba di la; si'el-si'el da pʋ pansigidi baa.

english_verse: Solomon was brilliant. God had blessed him with insight and understanding.
translation_verse: Wina'am da tis Solomon ya'am nɛ baŋir nɛ pʋtɛn'ɛsʋŋ ka li galis wʋʋ atɛuk titanbin'isi an si'em la.

english_verse: He was wiser than anyone else in the world, including the wisest people of the east and of Egypt. He was even wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Mahol's three sons, Heman, Calcol, and Darda. Solomon became famous in every country around Judah and Israel.
translation_verse: O da mɔr ya'am gat sɔ' wʋsa, la'an nɛ Etan onɛ da an Ezrak teŋ nid la, o da mɔr ya'am gat Heman nɛ Kalkol nɛ Daada banɛ da an Mahol biis la. Ka o yʋ'ʋr tiig tembanɛ gilig la wʋsa.

english_verse: He could talk about all kinds of plants, from large trees to small bushes, and he taught about animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.

english_verse: This is the temple where you have chosen to be worshiped. Please watch over it day and night and listen when I turn toward it and pray.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka fʋ nindaa kpa' yikaŋa nwa' yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ wʋsa, zin'ikaŋa ka fʋ yɛl ye fʋ yʋ'ʋr na bɛ anina la, ka wʋm sɔsʋg kanɛ ka fʋ sankpan'as na kpa' yikaŋa nwa' sɔs la.

english_verse: Our Lord, sometimes you will order your people to attack their enemies. Then your people will turn toward this temple I have built for you in your chosen city, and they will pray to you.

translation_verse: On da bu'os ka ba sa'al o naae la, Na'ab la da maal sanlima na'abibis ayi'. O da yɛl nidib la ye, “Li lalli galis nɛ yanamɛ na ken Jerusalem; ya teŋgban banɛ da mɔri ya yi Egipt na la nwa'!”

english_verse: Then he put one of the gold calves in the town of Bethel and the other in the town of Dan.
translation_verse: O da nɔk yinne zi'el Betel teŋin, ka mɛ zi'el yinne Dan teŋin.

english_verse: The people sinned because they started going to these places to worship.
translation_verse: Ka nɛ' lieb tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd hali, nidib la da keŋ hali paae Dan teŋin maan ba'ar kanɛ bɛɛ anina la.

english_verse: Jeroboam built small places of worship at the shrines and appointed men who were not from the tribe of Levi to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Jeroboam da mɛ' teŋgbana dɔɔd kʋkʋna wʋsa zug. Ka bɔ nidibi diis maanmaannib dɔɔg wʋsa ni, la'an nɛ ban da ka' Levi dim la.

english_verse: He also decided to start a new festival for the Israelites on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, just like the one in Judah. On that day, Jeroboam went to Bethel and offered sacrifices on the altar to the gold calf he had put there. Then he assigned the priests their duties.
translation_verse: Nwadkanɛ paas anii la, li dabpii nɛ anu daar, nwadkanɛ ka o mɛŋ gaŋ la, o da maal maana bimbim kanɛ ka o mɛ Betel teŋin la. O da zi'el malʋŋʋ tis Israel dim la, ka dʋ bimbim la zugʋ maal maana.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. Suddenly one of God's prophets arrived from Judah and shouted: The Lord sent me with a message about this altar. A child named Josiah will be born into David's family. He will sacrifice on this altar the priests who make offerings here, and human bones will be burned on it.
translation_verse: O da di'e Zugsɔb la pian'ad ka kaas agɔla zɛrig maan bimbim la ye, “Fʋn bimbim nwa', bimbim nwa'! Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ba na du'a biribiŋ David yin, ka o yʋ'ʋr na buon Josia. Fʋn bimbim kaŋa zug ka o na kɔdig maanmaannib banɛ maan maana kʋkʋna zug teŋgbana nwa' ni. Ba na nyu'oe ninsaal kɔnba fʋ zug!”

english_verse: You will know that the Lord has said these things when the altar splits in half, and the ashes on it fall to the ground.
translation_verse: Daakan la yim ka Wina'am nid la da tis zanbin ka yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la zi'el zanbin si'a nwa': bimbim la na buak ka li tampɛligim na widig teŋin la!” Jeroboam nu'ugʋ kpi la yɛla

english_verse: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
translation_verse: Ka bimbim la mɛ buak ka li tampɛligim la widig, nwɛnɛ Wina'am nid la yɛl Zugsɔb la pian'ad si'em la.

english_verse: “Please pray to the Lord your God and ask him to heal my hand,” Jeroboam begged. The prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed.
translation_verse: Ani ka Na'ab la yɛl Wina'am nid la ye, “Sɔsimi fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am la tisim, ka m nu'ug la lɛbi li zin'igin!” Wina'am nid la da sɔs Zugsɔb la o yɛla, ka Na'ab la nu'ug lɛbi li zin'igin an wʋʋ din ɛɛnti an si'em la.

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Wina'am nid la ye, “Kemi m yin na paam si'eli di, ka m na tisif piini.”

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.
translation_verse: Amaa Wina'am nid la da lɛbis o ye, “Hali fʋ ya'a tisim fʋn mɔr si'el wʋsa pʋsʋk m kʋ dɔllif bɛɛ m di diib ka nu ku'om kpɛla.

english_verse: The Lord said I can't eat or drink anything and that I can't go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Li anɛ Zugsɔb la tisim nɔɔr ye m da di diib bɛɛ nu ku'om bɛɛ dɔl suokanɛ ka m kena la lɛbɛ.”

english_verse: Then he started home down a different road. An Old Prophet from Bethel
translation_verse: Ka o tɔɔm suor ka pʋ dɔl suokanɛ ka o dɔlli keŋ Betel la lɛbɛ. Betel nɔdi'es kʋdiri niŋ si'em

english_verse: At that time an old prophet lived in Bethel, and one of his sons told him what the prophet from Judah had said and done.
translation_verse: Wina'am nɔdi'es kʋdig da bɛ Betel tempʋʋgin, ka o biis kena yɛl o Wina'am nid la kena tʋm si'em daakan la. Ba la'am yɛli ba saam on pian' si'em tis Na'ab la.

english_verse: “Show me which way he went,” the old prophet said, and his sons pointed out the road.
translation_verse: Ka ba saam la bu'osi ba ye, “O dɔl suokanɛ keŋɛ?” Ka biis la pa'al Wina'am nid onɛ yi Juda na la dɔl suosi'a.

english_verse: “Put a saddle on my donkey,” he told them. After they did, he got on the donkey
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl o biis la ye, “Li'emi bʋŋ la tisim!” Ban li'a bʋŋ la tis o la ka o ban'a

english_verse: and rode off to look for the prophet from Judah. The old prophet found him sitting under an oak tree and asked, “Are you the prophet from Judah?” “Yes, I am.”
translation_verse: bʋŋ la kad Wina'am nid la bugir, ka nyɛɛ o ka o zin' titita'ar gbinnin. Ka o bu'os o ye, “Fʋnɛ an Wina'am nid onɛ yi Juda na laa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Manɛ la.”

english_verse: “Come home with me,” the old prophet said, “and have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ka nɔdi'es kʋdig la yɛl o ye, “Dɔllim ka ti kul ka fʋ di!”

english_verse: “I can't go back with you,” the prophet replied, “and I can't eat or drink anything with you.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am nid la yɛl ye, “M kʋ nyaŋi dɔlli fʋ lɛbɛ, ka mɛ kʋ la'as nɛ fʋ di diib bɛɛ nu ku'om zin'ikaŋa.

english_verse: The Lord warned me not to eat or drink or to go home the same way I came.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛlim ye, ‘Da di diib bɛɛ nu ku'om anina, bɛɛ fʋ lɛn dɔl suokanɛ ka fʋ dɔlli kena la.’”

english_verse: The old prophet said, “I'm a prophet too. One of the Lord's angels told me to take you to my house and give you something to eat and drink.” The prophet from Judah did not know that the old prophet was lying,
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am nɔdi'es kʋdig la yɛl ye, “Mam anɛ nɔdi'es wʋʋ fʋn an si'em la. Zugsɔb la pian'ad yi maliak san'an yɛlim ye, ‘Dɔl o lɛbi fʋ yin na ka o di diib ka nu ku'om.’”

english_verse: so he went home with him and ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am nid la dɔl o lɛbi di ka nuu o yin la. Wina'am nid kum yɛla

english_verse: a message for the prophet from Judah: Listen to the Lord's message. You have disobeyed the Lord your God.
translation_verse: ka o kaasi yɛl Wina'am nid onɛ yi Juda la na ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ye, fʋ san'am Zugsɔb la pian'ad, ka pʋ dɔlli fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am nɔzi'elʋg dinɛ ka o tisif la!

english_verse: He told you not to eat or drink anything here, but you came home and ate with me. And so, when you die, your body won't be buried in your family tomb.
translation_verse: Fʋ lɛb na di diib ka nu ku'om zin'ikanɛ ka o yɛlif ye fʋ da di bɛɛ nuu. Alazugɔ, fʋ niŋgbiŋ kʋ mumi fʋ saamnam yaadin la.”

english_verse: and the prophet from Judah left. Along the way, a lion attacked and killed him, and the donkey and the lion stood there beside his dead body.
translation_verse: On da di'e o suori ken la, ka gbigim sia'al o suorin la kʋʋ o lɔb o niŋgbiŋ la bas suorin la, ka bʋŋ la nɛ gbigim la la'am zi'e kpi'e nɛ o.

english_verse: Some people walked by and saw the body with the lion standing there. They ran into Bethel, telling everyone what they had seen.
translation_verse: Ninsieba da dɔl anina gat ka nyɛɛ o niŋgbiŋ la dig teŋin, ka gbigim la mɛ zi'e kpi'e anina, ka ba lɛb tempʋʋgin nɔdi'es kʋdig la bɛ zin'isi'a la yɛl o.

english_verse: When the old prophet heard the news, he said, “That must be the prophet from Judah. The Lord warned him, but he disobeyed. So the Lord sent a lion to kill him.”
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es kanɛ mɔr o suorinɛ lɛb na la wʋmi li la o yɛl ye, “Li anɛ Wina'am nid onɛ ki'is Zugsɔb pian'ad la, la. Zugsɔb la zaŋ o tis gbigim la, ka o gban'e o kʋʋ o, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb pian'ad la dɛŋi sa'al o si'em la.”

english_verse: The old prophet told his sons to saddle his donkey, and when it was ready,
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es la da yɛl o biis la ye, “Li'emi bʋŋ la tisim.” Ka ba niŋ ala.

english_verse: he left. He found the body lying on the road, with the donkey and lion standing there. The lion had not eaten the body or attacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Ka o yii keŋ nyɛ niŋgbiŋ la ka li dig suorin ka bʋŋ la nɛ gbigim la la'am zi'e kpi'e. Gbigim la da pʋ ɔnb niŋgbiŋ la bɛɛ pu'alim bʋŋ la.

english_verse: The old prophet picked up the body, put it on his own donkey, and took it back to Bethel, so he could bury it and mourn for the prophet from Judah.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es la da nɔk Wina'am nid la ban'al o bʋŋ zugʋ mɔr o lɛb o mɛŋ teŋinɛ kaas o kʋʋr ka mum o.

english_verse: He buried the body in his own family tomb and cried for the prophet.
translation_verse: O da mum o nɛ o mɛŋ yaʋgʋn ka kaas o kʋʋri yɛt ye, “Oi! M ba'abiiga!”

english_verse: I'm sure that everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the shrines in Samaria will happen.”
translation_verse: Wina'am labaar kanɛ ka o di'e pian' Betel bimbim la yɛla nɛ teŋgbana nɛ kʋkʋna zug teŋgbana banɛ bɛ Samaria tempʋʋdin la niŋ amɛŋa.” Teŋgbana maalʋg la yɛla

english_verse: But Jeroboam kept on doing evil things. He appointed men to be priests at the local shrines, even if they were not Levites. In fact, anyone who wanted to be a priest could be one.
translation_verse: Hali nɛ'ɛŋa nya'aŋ la, Jeroboam da pʋ tiak o suobɛ'ɛdnam la, ka lɛn gaans maanmaannib buudi wʋsa ni, onɛ wʋsa kʋdim bɔɔd ye o lieb maanmaan la o da diis o ye o maal kʋkʋna zug teŋgbana la.

english_verse: About the same time, Abijah son of Jeroboam got sick.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Jeroboam biig Abija bɛn'ɛd,

english_verse: She got ready and left for Ahijah's house in Shiloh. Ahijah was now old and blind,
translation_verse: Jeroboam pu'a la da keŋ Ahija yin Siilo teŋin niŋ wʋʋ on yɛl o ye o niŋ si'em la. Ahija da kʋdignɛ ka pʋ lɛn nyɛta,

english_verse: But when Ahijah heard her walking up to the door, he said: Come in! I know you're Jeroboam's wife—why are you pretending to be someone else? I have some bad news for you.
translation_verse: On da paae za'anɔɔrin ka Ahija wʋm o nɔbkida la, o yɛl ye, “Kpɛn'ɛm na Jeroboam pu'a, bɔ ka fʋ tiakidi fʋ mɛŋa? Ba tʋm man nɛ fʋ san'an na nɛ lababɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: Give your husband this message from the Lord God of Israel: “Jeroboam, you know that I, the Lord, chose you over anyone else to be the leader of my people Israel.
translation_verse: Kem yɛl Jeroboam ye Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, ‘M dʋ'ʋsif nɛ nidib la sʋʋgin, ka kɛ ka fʋ aan m nidib Israel tuongat.

english_verse: I even took David's kingdom away from his family and gave it to you. But you are not like my servant David. He always obeyed me and did what was right.
translation_verse: M aaɛn sʋ'ʋlim la nɛ David yinne tisif, amaa fʋ ka' wʋʋ m tʋmtʋm David, onɛ di'e m nɔzi'elʋg nɛ o sʋnf wʋsa, ka tʋm dinɛ an sʋm ma'aa man tuon la.

english_verse: “You have made me very angry by rejecting me and making idols out of gold. Jeroboam, you have done more evil things than any king before you.
translation_verse: Fʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛdi gaad banɛ da dɛŋi fʋ tuon la wʋsa. Fʋ maal teŋgban sieba tisi fʋ mɛŋ nɛ bada banɛ ka ba maal nɛ kʋnt. Fʋ kɛya ka m sʋnf duoe, ka fʋ lɛm bidi m kʋdig.

english_verse: “Because of this, I will destroy your family by killing every man and boy in it, whether slave or free. I will wipe out your family, just as fire burns up trash.
translation_verse: “‘Nɛ'ɛŋa zug m na mɔr tɔɔg Jeroboam yin na. M na nwaae o yir la biribiŋ kpaanr wʋsa bas Israel teŋin, banɛ an yammis nɛ banɛ ka' yammis wʋsa. M na nyu'oe Jeroboam yir la wʋʋ sɔ' na nyu'oe na'ambin, ka li dii nug si'em la.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel will mourn at his funeral. But he will be the last one from Jeroboam's family to receive a proper burial, because he's the only one the Lord God of Israel is pleased with.
translation_verse: Israel dim wʋsa na kum o yɛla ka mum o. On ma'aa na an Jeroboam yir la nid ka ba na mum o, bɔzugɔ on ma'aa bɛ Jeroboam yin la ka Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la nyɛ ka o an sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: The Lord will soon choose a new king of Israel, who will destroy Jeroboam's family. And I mean very soon.
translation_verse: “Ka dinɛ lɛn paas, Zugsɔb la na gaŋ o mɛŋ na'ab Israel sʋ'ʋlimin, ka o na li' Jeroboam gbin la. Dabisir anɛ zina! Ɛɛn, li anɛ nannanna nwa'!

english_verse: years from Jerusalem, the city where the Lord had chosen to be worshiped. His mother Naamah was from Ammon.
translation_verse: Ani ka Jeroboam pu'a duoe kul Tiza. On ti yak o nɔbiri zi'el yaŋirin la ka biig la kpi.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel came and mourned at his funeral, just as the Lord's servant Ahijah had said. Jeroboam Dies
translation_verse: Ka ba mum o, ka Israel dim wʋsa kum o yɛla, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl o tʋmtʋm Ahija onɛ an nɔdi'es si'em la. Nadab di'e Jeroboam zin'ig

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including the battles he won, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Na'ab Jeroboam da tʋm tʋʋm sieba wʋsa nɛ on da zab, zab sieba nɛ on da mɔr teŋ la si'em la, ba sɔbi kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Tʋʋma gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: The people of Judah disobeyed the Lord and made him even angrier than their ancestors had.
translation_verse: Juda da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon. Ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ba da tʋm la zug da kɛ ka o sʋnf duoe ka li gaadi ba yaanamɛ da tʋm si'em la.

english_verse: They also built their own local shrines and stone images of foreign gods, and they set up sacred poles for worshiping the goddess Asherah on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ba da sɛ teŋgban kuga kʋkʋna zut, ka maal Asera dinɛ an teŋgban la kʋkʋna wʋsa zug nɛ titita'ar wʋsa gbinnin.

english_verse: Even worse, they allowed prostitutes at the shrines, and followed the disgusting customs of the foreign nations that the Lord had forced out of Canaan.
translation_verse: Hali dap mɛ da tʋmnɛ dapgɔɔnda tʋʋma ba teŋgbana ni. Israel nidib la da tʋmnɛ bʋn linɛ kis nwɛnɛ nimbanɛ da bɛ teŋin la da tʋm si'em ka Zugsɔb la da kadi ba yis saŋkanɛ ka Israel dim da kpɛn'ɛd teŋin la.

english_verse: After Rehoboam had been king for four years, King Shishak of Egypt attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na'ab Rehoboam da di na'am la, li yʋma anu saŋa, Egipt na'ab Sisiak da kena zab nɛ Jerusalem.

english_verse: He took everything of value from the temple and the palace, including Solomon's gold shields.
translation_verse: O da vaae Zugsɔb Yir la kpan'am wʋsa nɛ na'ayir kpan'am la wʋsa. O da vaae si'el wʋsa la'an nɛ sanlima zaba gbanti'edis linɛ ka Solomon da maal la.

english_verse: Rehoboam had bronze shields made to replace the gold ones, and he ordered the guards at the city gates to keep them safe.
translation_verse: Alazug Na'ab Rehoboam da maal kʋntzɛn'ug gbanti'edisi lɛbis, ka nɔki ba gu'ul banɛ gur na'ayir la kpɛɛmnam.

english_verse: Whenever Rehoboam went to the Lord's temple, the guards carried the shields. But they always took them back to the guardroom as soon as he was finished.
translation_verse: Na'ab la ya'a ɛɛnti kpɛn' Zugsɔb yin la, banɛ gur la na mɔr gbanti'edis nwa' dɔl o keŋ, ka li nya'aŋ ka ba lɛbisi li dɔkanɛ ka ba gur la ni. Na'ab Rehoboam kum

english_verse: Everything else Rehoboam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Na'ab Rehoboam na'am diib saŋa nɛ on da tʋm si'el wʋsa, ba sɔbi niŋ Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: He and Jeroboam were constantly at war.
translation_verse: Rehoboam nɛ Jeroboam da zabidi nɛ taaba saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: Rehoboam's mother Naamah was from Ammon, but when Rehoboam died, he was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Abijam then became king.
translation_verse: Na'ab Rehoboam da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o David tempʋʋgin. O ma yʋ'ʋri da an Naama; o da anɛ Ammon nid. Ka o biig Abija di'e o zin'igi di na'am.

english_verse: His own grandmother Maacah had made an idol of Asherah, and Asa took it and burned it in Kidron Valley. Then he removed Maacah from her position as queen mother.
translation_verse: Hali ka pidig o yaapu'a Maaka onɛ da an pu'ana'ab la na'am bɔzugɔ, o da sɛ teŋgban Asera dazi'edir la pʋ'ʋsid. Asa da kie dazi'edir la lɔbi bas Kidron bɔn'ɔgin ka nyu'oe li nɛ bugum.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Nebat biig Na'ab Jeroboam na'am diib yʋma pii nɛ anii saŋa la, Abija da di Juda na'am,

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Asa tis nɔɔr ye ba giligim Juda wʋsa mɔɔl ye sɔ' wʋsa yim ka baa nid yinne da kpɛlim, ka ba keŋ fuoe kuga nɛ dabanɛ ka Baasa da mɔri mɛɛd Rama la. Na'ab Asa da nɔki lii mɛ' Geba teŋ kanɛ bɛ Benjamin nɛ Misipa teŋin la.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: O da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd banɛ wʋsa ka o saam da dɛŋi tʋm la. O da pʋ pɛsig o sʋnf wʋsa tis o Zugsɔb Wina'am wʋʋ o yaab Na'ab David n da pɛsig o sʋnf si'em laa.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: David da tʋm dinɛ an sʋm Zugsɔb la tuon, ka pʋ gɛsig Zugsɔb la da zi'el o nɔɔr si'em la baa yinne o nyɔvʋr bɛllim pʋʋginɛ, asɛɛ Uria onɛ an Hitti nid la yɛla la ma'aa.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Abija na'am diib saŋa la, ba sɔbi kpɛn'ɛs Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la. Abija nɛ Jeroboam da zabidnɛ saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Na'ab Abija da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o David tempʋʋgin ka o biig Asa di'e o zin'igi di na'am. Asa di Juda Na'am (

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: O da mɔr sanlima nɛ anzurifa nɛ la'abanɛ ka on nɛ o saam da pɛsigi tis Zugsɔb la kpɛn'ɛs Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la. Na'ab Asa maal nɔɔr yinne nɛ Aram sʋ'ʋlim Na'ab

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Zaba da bɛ Na'ab Asa nɛ Israel Na'ab Baasa sʋʋgin ba na'am diib saŋa la wʋsa.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Jeroboam da an Israel Na'ab la li yʋma pisi saŋa ka Asa da di Juda na'am.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: O da kad dap banɛ tʋm dapgɔɔnda tʋʋma teŋgbana ni yis teŋin la ka yis bada banɛ ka o saam da ba' la wʋsa bas.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Hali la'an nɛ on da pʋ yis teŋgbana banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna zut la, Na'ab Asa da kpɛm pɛsig o sʋnf wʋsa tis o Zugsɔb Wina'am.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab Baasa da duoe zabid nɛ Juda, ka keŋ Rama teŋin mɛ' kpi'euŋ zin'igi gu' ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kpɛn' bɛɛ yi Juda Na'ab Asa sʋ'ʋlim la nii.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Asa da nɔk anzurifa nɛ sanlima linɛ da kpɛlim Zugsɔb Yir suak dɔɔdin la, nɛ linɛ bɛɛ o mɛŋ na'ayin la niŋ o na'ayikpɛm la nu'usin. Ka kɛ ka ba mɔri keŋ Aram Na'ab Ben-Hadad onɛ da an Tabirimon biig ka an Hezion yaaŋ ka sʋ'oe Damaskus tempʋʋg la.

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: O da ye ba yɛl o ye, “Kɛl ka man nɛ fʋn maal nɔnaar, nwɛnɛ m saam nɛ fʋ saamme da mɔr nɔɔr yinne si'em la. Gɔsima, anzurifa nɛ sanlima ka m nɔki tisidif ka li an piini. Nannanna basim nɔnaar kanɛ ka fʋn nɛ Israel Na'ab Baasa maal la ka li kɛ ka o yii m teŋin la ka basim.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad da siak Na'ab Asa nɔɔr ka tʋm o zabzabidib tuongatib ka ba keŋ zab nɛ Israel tɛɛns la. O da nyaŋ Iyon teŋ nɛ Dan teŋ, nɛ Abɛl-Bet-Maaka teŋ, la'an nɛ Kenɛref baba, la'am kpanb nɛ Naftali dɔɔg sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Baasa n da wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la, o da bas Rama mɛɛb, ka lɛb Tiza tempʋʋgin bɛɛ anina.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Na'ab Asa na'am diib saŋa, on da nyaŋi maal si'el nɛ on tʋm si'el, nɛ tempʋʋd banɛ ka o mɛ' la, ba da sɔbi lii niŋ Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la. On da kʋdig saŋa si'a la, ban'as da gban'e o nɔba.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Na'ab Asa da di Juda na'am la, li yʋma ayi' saŋa ka Na'ab Jeroboam biig Nadab da di Israel na'am. O da di na'am Israel teŋin yʋma ayi'.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon, ka dɔl o saam suoya nɛ o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dinɛ ka o da kɛ ka Israel dim tʋm la.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Baasa da di na'am la, o da kʋ Na'ab Jeroboam yidim la wʋsa ka pʋ bas nid baa yinne. O da san'ami ba wʋsa, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka o nɔdi'es Ahija onɛ an Siilo nid la yɛl si'em la,

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: bɔzugɔ Jeroboam da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd ka mɛ kɛ ka Israel dim wʋsa tʋm, ka Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la sʋnf pɛlig.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Na'ab Nadab na'am diib saŋa la, ba da sɔbi kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la. Baasa nɛ Juda Na'ab Asa zaba yɛla

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Zaba da bɛ Juda Na'ab Asa nɛ Israel Na'ab Baasa sʋʋgin ba na'am diib saŋa la wʋsa.

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Asa da di na'am la yʋma atan' saŋa la, ba da diis Ahija biig Baasa Israel wʋsa na'am Tiza teŋin. O da di na'am la nɛ yʋma pisi nɛ anaasi.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon, ka dɔl na'ab Jeroboam suoya nɛ o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd banɛ ka da o kɛ ka Israel dim wʋsa tʋm la.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la pian'ad da kɛn Jehu onɛ an Hanani biig la san'an na tis Na'ab Baasa

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: ye, “M ʋki fʋ agɔla yis titanin na, ka gaŋi fʋ niŋi m nidib Israel dim tuongat, amaa fʋ dɔl Jeroboam suoya ka kɛ ka m nidib Israel dim la tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi kɛ ka m sʋnf pɛlig nɛ ba.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Dinzug m na kanbis fʋn Baasa, nɛ fʋ yir la wʋsa. M na kɛ ka fʋ yir nwɛnɛ Nebat biig Jeroboam yir nɛ.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Baas na ɔnbi fʋ nimbanɛ kpi tempʋʋgin la, ka niis banɛ ian'ad agɔla la mɛ na di banɛ kpi tempʋʋg la yiŋ!”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Dinɛ lɛm paas la, Wina'am labaar da kɛn Wina'am nɔdi'es Jehu onɛ an Hanani biig la san'an na ka li anɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd banɛ ka Baasa da tʋm la zug. O da kɛ ka Zugsɔb la sʋnf duoe ka li ka' nɛ on da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd ban ka Jeroboam tʋm la buudi ma'aanɛ amaa on da kʋ Jeroboam yidim wʋsa la zug. Ela nɛ Zimiri Na'am diib

english_verse: Elah son of Baasha became king of Israel after Asa had been king of Judah for
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Asa n da di na'am la li yʋma pisi nɛ ayuobʋ saŋa la, Baasa biig Ela da di Israel na'am zin'in Tiza teŋin yʋma ayi'.

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab Omir da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuonnɛ gaad banɛ dɛŋ o tuon la wʋsa.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
