translation_verse: Zimiri onɛ aan o na'ayikpɛɛm ka gɔsid Na'ab la zaba tɛrekonam pʋsʋk la da duoe gban'e pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd Na'ab la yɛla. Saŋkan la Na'ab Ela da bɛ nɛ Ariza onɛ gɔsid na'ayir Tiza teŋin la yinnɛ nu daam kʋʋl.

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Zimiri da kpɛn' na nwɛ' Na'ab la bas ka kʋʋ o, Juda Na'ab Asa da di na'am la li yʋma pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi saŋa la. Ani ka o da di'e na'am la di.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: On da di na'am ka zin'in o na'am gbauŋ zugʋ naae la, o da kʋ Na'ab Baasa yidim wʋsa. O da pʋ bas dau baa yinne, hali la'an nɛ o du'adib nɛ o zuanam wʋsa.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Alazug, Zimiri da san'am Baasa yidim wʋsa wʋʋ Zugsɔb la da zan'as on nɛ o yidim ka pian' tis o nɔdi'es Jehu si'em la.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim linɛ da maal Na'ab Ela na'am diib saŋa la nɛ on tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi ba kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Israel dimi da wʋm ba la'asʋg zin'igin la ye, Zimiri duoe zi'en na'ab la yɛla ka ba'asi kʋʋ o la, ba da nɔk Omir, onɛ an Israel soogianam tuongat la, diis o na'am daakan nɔɔ, ba la'asʋg la zin'igin.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Omir nɛ Israel dim la wʋsa da yi Gibɛton keŋ gilig Tiza teŋ la.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Zimiri da nyɛ ka ba nyaŋ tempʋʋg la, o zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' na'ayir zɔŋŋin ka nyu'oe li nɛ bugum kpii anina.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Li anɛ on tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd, ka maan dinɛ ka' sʋm Zugsɔb la tuon, ka dɔl Na'ab Jeroboam suoya, nɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka o tʋm ka kɛ ka Israel dim mɛ tʋm la zug ka o niŋ ala.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Zimiri na'am diib saŋa nɛ on da zan'as Zugsɔb nɔɔr la, ba da sɔbi li kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la. Israel Na'ab Omir nɛ Tibin dataadʋg yɛla

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Israel nidib la da pʋdig nɛ zin'isa ayi'. Nidib la pʋsʋk da dɔl Ginaf biig Tibin bɔɔd ye o di na'am, ka pʋsʋk kanɛ kpɛlim la sʋŋid Omir.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Asa n da di na'am la li yʋma pistan' nɛ yinne saŋa la, Omir da di Israel na'am. O da di na'am la nɛ yʋma pii nɛ ayi', ka zin'in Tiza tempʋʋgin yʋma ayuobʋ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: O da dɔl Jeroboam onɛ an Nebat biig la suoya nɛ o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dinɛ ka o da kɛ ka Israel dim wʋsa tʋm, ka kɛ ka Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la sʋnf pɛlig nɛ ba bada banɛ ka' suor la.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Na'ab Omir na'am diib saŋa la, ba da sɔbi kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Na'ab Omir da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o Samaria teŋin, ka o biig Ahab di'e o zin'igi di na'am. Ahab di na'am

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Asa n da di na'am la li yʋma pistan' nɛ anii saŋa la, Omir biig Ahab da di Israel na'am. O da zin'in nɛ Samaria teŋin yʋma pisi nɛ ayi'.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Omir biig Na'ab Ahab da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon hali gaad banɛ da dɛŋ o tuon la.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Li ka' on da dɔl Jeroboam onɛ an Nebat biig la suoya la ma'aanɛ, amaa o da di Jezebɛl onɛ an Sidon na'ab Efiba'al pu'ayua ka tʋmmi tisid Baal onɛ an teŋgban ka wɔ'ɔgid o la.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: O da mɛ' dɔɔgʋ tis Baal, Samaria tempʋʋgin, ka mɛ' maan bimbimi li pʋʋgin.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahab da lɛn sɛ teŋgban Asera dazi'edir la, ka tʋm linɛ duoe Zugsɔb la sʋnf hali. O da kɛ ka Israel Wina'am la sʋnf pɛligi gaad na'anam banɛ dɛŋ o tuon la wʋsa.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahab saŋa la, Hiel onɛ yi Betel teŋin na la da lɛbisi mɛ' Jeriko teŋ la. On da ɛɛnb ɛɛnbir la ka o biribiŋ kpɛɛm Abiram kpi, ka on ti mɛɛ naad la ka o bikpaanr Segub kpi. Li da maal nɛ wʋʋ Zugsɔb pian'ad la da yɛl si'em tis Josua onɛ an Nun biig la.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Elaja onɛ an Tisibi nid ka yi Tisibi teŋ kanɛ bɛ Gilead sʋ'ʋlimin la da yɛl Ahab ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am ka m pʋ'ʋsid o la sadigim vʋe la, mɛligim kʋ lii, ka yɛti saa, yʋma bi'ela banɛ kena la, ya'a ka' li ti yi man nɔɔrin naa. Wina'am diis Elaja diib

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb labaar da kɛn Elaja san'an na yɛl o ye,

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Yim kpɛla lɛb ya-nya'aŋ, keŋ su'a Kerif bɔn'ɔfaligin linɛ bɛ Joodan nya'aŋ la.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Fʋ na nuud ku'om ku'osuorin la, m na kɛ ka agaand mɔr diibi kenna tisidif anina.”

english_verse: Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Elaja da niŋ Zugsɔb la yɛl o si'em la ka keŋ Kerif bɔn'ɔfaligin la, Joodan nya'aŋi bɛɛ anina.

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Agaand la da mɔr bodobodo nɛ ni'imi ken bɛogʋn-bɛogʋn nɛ zaam-zaam tisid o ka o dit, ka nuud ku'om ku'osuorin la. Wina'am diis Elaja Zarefat teŋin

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Ka li ti kena ka ku'osuor la kpiɛn kʋdig bɔzugɔ, saa da pʋ niid teŋin laa.

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Duom tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ Zarefat teŋin dinɛ bɛ Sidon sʋ'ʋlimin la zin'in ani. M yɛl pu'a sɔ' anina ye o tisif diib.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: O da duoe keŋ Zarefat, on da paae tempʋʋg la za'anɔɔrin la, pʋkɔɔnr sɔ' da bɛɛ ani kɔɔd daad. Ka o buol pu'a la yɛl o ye, “Kpɛn'ɛm gbin'e ku'om bi'ela tisim ka m nu”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: On da duoe wa'ae ye o mɔr ku'om la na la, ka o lɛm buol o ye, “M bɛlimnɛ, ka mɔr bodobodo bi'ela na tisim!”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Nɛ Zugsɔb Wina'am kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋr zugɔ, mam pʋ mɔr bodobodo! M mɔri zɔ'ɔm nu'ukukudugin nɛ kpaam bi'ela ka li bɛ laa gbinnin sa; din ka m la'asid daad ye m keŋ maal diib bi'ela ka man nɛ m biribiŋ la dii ti dikɛuu ka kpi.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Ka Elaja yɛl o ye, “Da zɔt dabiem! Kem maal wʋʋ fʋn yɛl si'em la, amaa dɛŋim maal bodobodo fiinf na tisim, ka maal linɛ kpɛlim la ka fʋn nɛ fʋ biig la di.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, fʋ zɔ'ɔm la kʋ naae ka kpaam la mɛ kʋ naae, hali nɛ Wina'am na ti tis saa teŋgbauŋ la zug na.”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Pu'a la da kpɛn' maal wʋʋ Elaja yɛl o si'em la. Diib da bɛ ka Elaja nɛ pu'a la nɛ o yidim wʋsa dit daar wʋsa.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Zɔm la da pʋ naae ka kpaam la mɛ pʋ pɔ'ɔgɛ, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la da pian' tis Elaja si'em la. Elaja vʋ'ʋg pʋkɔɔnr la biribiŋ

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Li da paae saŋsi'a ka pu'a kanɛ sʋ'oe yir la biribiŋ la bɛn'ɛd. Ban'a la da wʋm o hali ka o ti ba'asi kpi.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Pu'a la da yɛl Elaja ye, “Mam nɛ fʋ bɔ ni, Wina'am nida? Fʋ kenɛ na ye fʋ tiɛn manɛ m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yɛla ka kʋʋ m biigaa?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Ka Elaja yɛl o ye, “Mɔri fʋ biig la na!” Ka di'e o pu'a la nu'usin mɔr o dʋ dɔkanɛ ka o gbɛɛnd, ka ba mɛɛ li sʋn'ʋl zugin la, digil biig la o gadʋg zug.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Ka kaasi tis Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “M Zugsɔb Wina'am, fʋ mɔri zutɔɔgʋ kɛn pu'a kanɛ ka man nɛ on bɛ la zugin na ka kɛ ka o biig la kpii?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Ka tiɛn o mɛŋi pa'al biig la zug nɔɔr atan' ka kaasi tis Zugsɔb la ye, “M Zugsɔb Wina'am, kɛl ka biig la nyɔvʋr lɛb o san'an na!”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da wʋm Elaja kaasig ka kɛ ka biig la vʋ'ʋsʋm lɛb na ka o vʋ'ʋg.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Ka Elaja mɔr biig la sig teŋin na kpɛn' zakin tis o ma ka ye, “Gɔsima, fʋ biig la vʋ'ʋg ya!”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ani ka pu'a la yɛl Elaja ye, “Nannanna m sid baŋ ye fʋ anɛ Wina'am nid, ka Zugsɔb pian'ad linɛ yiti fʋ nɔɔrin na la an sida.”

english_verse: For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
translation_verse: Alazug Elaja da duoe wa'ae Ahab san'an ye o pa'al o mɛŋ. Saŋkan la kɔ'ɔm da wʋm Samaria teŋ dim hali,

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Jezebɛl da kʋʋd Zugsɔb nɔdi'esidib la, Obadia da nɔk nɔdi'esidib kɔbiga su'a tampinlɛma ni zin'is ayi', zin'ig yinne wʋsa da anɛ nidib pisnu. Ka mɔr diib nɛ ku'om kennɛ tisidi ba.)

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Ahab da yɛl Obadia ye, “Giligim gɔs zin'ibanɛ ka ku'om miid saŋa wʋsa, nɛ bɔn'ɔdin, ka daasi'erɛɛ ti na paam mɔma'asa tisi ti widi la ka ba ɔnb ka vʋe ka ti bʋnkɔnbid la wʋsa da kpii.”

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Dinzug ba da pʋdig teŋ la ban na iee paae si'em bɛn. Ahab da lɛb zin'ig yinne ka Obadia mɛ lɛb zin'ig yinne.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Obadia da keŋ sia'al Elaja. O da baŋ o ka su'un teŋinɛ na'as o ka yɛl ye, “Li sid anɛ fʋnɛɛ, m zugdaan Elaja?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Obadia da bu'os o ye, “M zugdaana, m taal an bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye fʋ zaŋimi niŋ Na'ab Ahab nu'ugin ka o kʋʋ ma?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Hali nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr zugɔ, teŋ bɛɛ na'am sʋ'ʋlim kae ka m zugdaan pʋ tʋm sɔ' ye o iee fɔ. Ka ba ya'a lɛb na ka ye ba pʋ nyɛɛ fɔ, o na kɛ ka ba pɔ ye ba sid pʋ nyɛɛ fɔ.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Amaa nannanna fʋ yɛlim ye m kem yɛli m zugdaan la ye, ‘Elaja bɛ kpɛla.’

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Lin an si'em la, m ya'a basif kpɛla ka keŋ daasi'erɛ Zugsɔb la Siig na zii fʋ keŋ zin'isi'a. M ya'a keŋ yɛl Na'ab Ahab, ka o kena iee fʋ pʋ nyɛɛ, o na kʋʋm. Tɛnr ye m biilimin sa ka m pʋ'ʋsid Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Ka Elaja lɛbis o ye, “Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb onɛ ka m pʋ'ʋsid la sadigim vʋe la, m na zaŋi m mɛŋi pa'al Ahab zina.” Elaja nɛ Na'ab Ahab

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Obadia da keŋ Na'ab Ahab san'anɛ yɛl o. Ka Ahab keŋ Elaja san'an.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: On da nyɛ Elaja la ka yɛl o ye, “Fʋn kanɛ ieed yɛla Israel teŋin la nwaa?”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Elaja da lɛbis o ye, “Mam pʋ ieed yɛla Israel teŋinɛ, amaa li anɛ fʋn nɛ fʋ saam yidim. Fʋ bas Zugsɔb zi'ela la ka dɔl Baal teŋgbana la.

english_verse: Call together everyone from Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. Be sure to bring along the
translation_verse: Nannanna, la'asim Israel nidib wʋsa ka ya sia'alim Kaamel zuorin la. Dɔl Baal nɔdi'esidib kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu la na, nɛ Asera nɔdi'esidib kɔbisnaasi banɛ la'am dit nɛ Jezebɛl la.” Kaamel zuor zug Makir

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahab sid da tʋm buol Israel dim wʋsa nɛ nɔdi'esidib la Kaamel zuorin.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Elaja da gaad nidib la tuonnɛ yɛli ba ye, “Ya bɔɔd ye li yuugi paae wala ka ya fɛndigi ya pʋtɛnda ayi', yi' la ni? Ya ya'a baŋ ye Zugsɔb la an Wina'am yanam dɔl o, amaa li ya'a lɛn anɛ Baal yanam dɔl o.” Amaa ka nidib la pʋ yɛl si'ela.

english_verse: Then Elijah continued: I am the Lord's only prophet, but Baal has
translation_verse: Elaja da lɛn yɛli ba ye, “Mam ma'aa an Zugsɔb la nɔdi'esi kpɛlim, amaa Baal mɔr nɔdi'esidib kɔbisnaasi nɛ pisnu.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Bɔɔm na'araad ayi' tisi ti. Ka kɛ ka ba mɛŋ gaŋ ban bɔɔd sɔ' kɔdigi bɛs o pa'al daad zug, amaa ba da nyu'oe bugum. Mam mɛ na maal onɛ kpɛlim la pa'al daad zug ka kʋ nyu'oe bugum mɛnɛ.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Ya na buoli ya teŋgban la yʋ'ʋr, ka mam mɛ buol Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr. Win kanɛ ka ba na buol ka o siak nɛ bugum la anɛ Wina'am asida.” Ka nidib la wʋsa yɛl ye, “Fʋn yɛl si'el la an sʋm!”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Elaja da yɛl Baal nɔdi'esidib la ye, “Gaŋimi na'araad la yinne maal yiiga, yanamɛ sadigim zu'oe la. Buolimi ya teŋgban la yʋ'ʋr, amaa da nyu'oe bugum!”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Ka ba nɔk na'araug kanɛ ka ba di'e la maal. Ka ba buol Baal yʋ'ʋr bɛogʋn tat-tat-tat hali ti paae nintaŋ tisʋʋs, ye, “Baal, siakimi ti buolʋg!” Ka ba tansid agɔla gɔla amaa sɔ' pʋ siakɛ, ka li fɔn baanlimm. Ka ba wa'a gilig bimbim kanɛ ka ba maal la.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Ka li ti paae nintaŋ tisʋʋs ka Elaja pin'ili la'adi ba ye, “Tansimi bɛdegʋ, ye bi'esʋg kae o anɛ win! Daasi'erɛɛ o nan ka'anɛ ya'a bɛɛ o nan tɛn'ɛsid nɛ, ya'a ka' ala o keŋi ye o dʋ'ʋn bɛɛ o nwienɛ, ya'a ka' ala o gbisid nɛ, asɛɛ ka ya nie o!”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Ka ba tansid agɔla gɔla, ka mɔr sʋ'ʋs nɛ kpana nwaadi ba mɛŋ wʋʋ ba malima da an si'em la ka ziim ti kena yit.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Winnig da buli kena gbɛlig ka ba nan kpɛn tansidi pian'ad hali ti paae zaam maan saŋa. Amaa sɔ' pʋ siakɛ, ka li fɔn baanlimm, ka sɔ' mɛ pʋ kɛlisɛ.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: O da nɔk kuga la mɛ' bimbim nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr zug. Ka tu bʋmbɔki giligi li ka li yalim ka ku'om galamnama anaasi na nyaŋi niŋ anina.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: Ka o maal daad la pa'al, ka kɔdig na'araug la bɛsi pa'al daad la zug. Ani ka o yʋ'ʋn yɛli ba ye, “Pɛ'ɛlimi yʋya anaasi nɛ ku'om ka kpa'ae niŋ maan la nɛ daad la zug!”

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Ka ku'om la pʋbigi sig bimbim la teŋiri pɛ'ɛl bʋmbɔk la.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Maan la saŋaa da paae la, ka Wina'am nɔdi'es Elaja li'el na ka sɔs Wina'am ye, “Zugsɔba, Abraham Wina'am, Isaak Wina'am, Israel Wina'am, kɛl ka sɔ' wʋsa baŋ zina ye fʋ sid anɛ Israel Wina'am ka mam mɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm, ka tʋm nɛ' wʋsa ka li anɛ fʋnɛ tisim nɔɔr.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Siakimi m sɔsʋg Zugsɔba, siakimi m sɔsʋg, ka din ka nimbama na baŋ ye fʋ anɛ Zugsɔb Wina'am, ka na fɛndigi ba sʋnya lɛbi fʋ san'an na ya'as!”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Ani ka Zugsɔb bugum la li na di maan la nɛ daad nɛ kuga la la'an nɛ teŋ la hali ka lɛlig ku'om linɛ bɛ bʋmbɔkin la.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Nidib la wʋsa nyɛ nwa' la, ka lii avanba ka kaas ye, “Zugsɔb la anɛ Wina'am, Zugsɔb la anɛ Wina'am!”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Ka Elaja tansi ba ye, “Gban'ami Baal nɔdi'esidib la, da kɛ ka nid baa yinne zɔɔ!” Ka ba gban'e ba, ka Elaja mɔri ba sig Kison bɔn'ɔgin la kʋʋ ba wʋsa ani. Elaja di'e Wina'am pian'ad ye saa na ni

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Elaja da yɛl Na'ab Ahab ye, “Kulim yinne di ka nu, ka sakʋdʋg damya!”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ahab da keŋ di ka nu, amaa Elaja da duoe keŋ dʋ Kaamel zuor zugʋ igin teŋin ka o nindaa bɛɛ o duma teŋsʋk.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: O da yɛl o sankpan'as ye, “Kem gɔsi atɛuk la baba!” O da keŋ gɔs ka yɛl ye, “Si'el kae!” Nɔɔra ayɔpɔi ka Elaja yɛl o ye, “Lɛm gɔs!”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Ka dinɛ pɛ'ɛsi ayɔpɔi la sankpan'as la lɛb na yɛl ye, “Saŋgbanbili zem wʋʋ ninsaal nu'ug nɛ dʋt atɛukʋn la na.” Ka Elaja tansi yɛl o ye, “Kem yɛl Na'ab Ahab ye o kpɛn'ɛmi o tɛreko la ni kul tɔ'ɔtɔ ka saa la da paae o suorɛ!”

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Wina'am paŋ da sig Elaja san'an na ka o nɔk sɛnbidiŋi sɛnbi o fuug ka zɔɔ gaad Ahab tuonnɛ paae Jezireel.

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahab da yɛl o pu'a Jezebɛl Elaja tʋm si'em, nɛ on kʋ nɔdi'esidib la si'em.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Jezebɛl da tʋm yɛl Elaja ye, “M pɔya mɛnɛ! Bɛog anwa win, m ya'a pʋ kʋʋf nwɛnɛ fʋn sa kʋ sieba si'em la, wina la on kʋʋmim.” Elaja zɔɔ keŋ Horeb zuorin

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Dabiem da gban'e Elaja ka o zɔ ye o faaɛn o nyɔvʋr. On da paae Beerseba Juda sʋ'ʋlimin la, o da bas o sankpan'as anina.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: On mɛŋ da keŋ dabismum kennɛ kpɛn' sian'arin. O da paae saad tiigin zin'in tiig la gbinnin ka sɔs Wina'am bɔɔd ye o kpi. O da yɛl ye, “Zugsɔba, li siak ala, di'emi m nyɔvʋr, ka mam pʋ gati m yaanama,”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: ka diginɛ gbis. Zugsɔb maliak da kɛn vuguri na si'is o ka yɛl ye, “Duom di!”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Ka o gɔsi o zug baba nyɛ ka ba sɛn'ɛl bodobodo bugumin, ka ku'om nɛ gan'ar zi'e. Ka o di ka nu ka lɛbi diginɛ gbis.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: O da duoe di ka nu, ka diib la tis o paŋ ka o duoe keŋ dabpisnaasi, yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ wʋsa, ti paae Horeb linɛ an Wina'am zuorin la.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Anina ka o kpɛn' tampinlɛuŋʋn gbɛn yʋ'ʋŋ kan la. Wina'am sa'al Elaja Zugsɔb labaar da kɛɛn o san'an na bu'os o ye, “Elaja, fʋ tʋm bɔ kpɛla?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M sʋnf gban'anɛ, ye m tʋm Zugsɔb Wina'am Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la tʋʋma, amaa Israel dim zan'asi fʋ nɔnaar la, ka nwa'ae fʋ bimbima la bas, ka kʋʋ fʋ nɔdi'esidib la. Mam ma'aa kpɛlim ka ba mɛ mɔɔd ye ba kʋ mam!”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl o ye, “Yim keŋ zuorin la zi'en Zugsɔb la tuon ka Zugsɔb la bɔɔd ye o gaad.” Sisi'etita'ar da dam nwɛ' zuor la buak ka widig tampiins Zugsɔb la tuon; amaa Zugsɔb la da pʋ bɛ sisi'em la nii. Sisi'em la nya'aŋ ka teŋ dammid hali mi'im, amaa Zugsɔb la da ka' anina.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Teŋ la dammʋg nya'aŋ ka bugum yina, amaa Zugsɔb la da ka' bugum la nii. Ka bugum la nya'aŋ ka kʋkɔbaanlig nyaan pian'.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Elaja wʋmi li la, o tɛk o fuugʋ lus o nindaa yina zi'en tampinlɛuŋ la nɔɔrin. Ka kʋkɔr la bu'os o ye, “Fʋ tʋm bɔ kpɛla, Elaja?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M sʋnf gban'anɛ, ye m tʋm Zugsɔb Wina'am Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la tʋʋma, amaa Israel dim zan'asi fʋ nɔnaar la nɛ, ka nwa'ae fʋ bimbima la bas, ka kʋʋ fʋ nɔdi'esidib la. Mam ma'aa kpɛlim ka ba mɛ mɔɔd ye ba kʋ mam.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da yɛl o ye, “Lɛm dɔl fʋn dɔl suosi'a kena la, ka keŋ Damaskus sian'arin la. Fʋ ya'a paae anina, fʋn nɔkim malʋŋ kpaam bu'oe niŋ Hazael zugʋ diis o Aram na'am.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: Ka mɛ bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ Nimsi biig Jehu zugʋ diis o Israel na'am, ka keŋ Elasia onɛ an Safat biig ka yi Abɛl Mehola teŋin la bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ o zug ka o zi'enɛ fʋ nɔba zugʋ an nɔdi'es.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Jehu na kʋ onɛ wʋsa zɔɔ yi Hazael san'an, ka Elasia mɛ na kʋ onɛ wʋsa zɔɔ yi Jehu san'an.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Elaja da yii anina keŋ nyɛ Safat biig Elasia, ka on nɛ o nidib mɔr na'akunya pii nɛ ayi' kuod, ka o mɛŋ gban'e niigi kʋʋnr kanɛ paas pii nɛ ayi' la. Elaja da keŋ paae o san'an ka nɔk o fuugʋ lɔbi gɛɛl o.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Elasia da bas niigi la kuob ka zɔti dɔl Elaja ka ye, “Kɛl ka m lɛbi kɛɛsi m ba' nɛ m ma ka lɛb na!” Ka Elaja yɛl o ye, “Lɛm! M maalif bɔ?”

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Elasia da bas o ka lɛb. O da zaŋ o lɔlis la kʋ ka kɔ' yɔksin daad la nyu'oe bugum dʋg ni'im la tis nidib la ka ba ɔnb. Ka o yʋ'ʋn yii keŋ dɔl Elaja tʋmmi tisid o.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Ba da vili ba sies nɛ bɔto fuud ka vili ba zut nɛ nwiisi keŋ Israel Na'ab san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Naa, fʋ sankpan'as Ben-Hadad ye fʋ di suguru ka da kʋʋ o.” Ka Na'ab la bu'os ye, “O nan vʋeyaa? O anɛ m ba'abiig!”

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛn tʋm nidib na yɛl ye, “Ben-Hadad n yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘M pa'a tʋm na yɛl ye m bɔɔdi fʋ anzurifa nɛ sanlima nɛ fʋ pu'ab nɛ fʋ biis.

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: Amaa bɛogʋ anwa saŋa m na tʋm m na'ayikpɛm ka ba kpɛn' fʋ yin la, nɛ fʋ na'ayikpɛm la yaan, yis dinɛ wʋsa ka ya gɔs ka li an bʋnsʋma hali la faaɛn li wʋsa mɔri keŋ.’”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛmnam la nɛ nidib la wʋsa yɛl ye, “Da kɛlis on yɛl si'el la, bɛɛ fʋ siak o bɔɔdim la tis o!”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: O da lɛbisi yɛl Ben-Hadad nidib la ye, “Yɛlimi m zugdaan Na'ab la ye, on dɛŋi yɛl si'el la m siakya, amaa dinɛ ka o yuolim yɛl la m kʋ nyaŋɛ.” Ba da lɛbi yɛl Ben-Hadad ban lɛbisi ba si'em la.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad da lɛn tʋm ninsieba Na'ab Ahab san'an ye, “M pɔya ye li ya'a bɔɔd lin an si'em titan kʋ lɛn kpɛlim Samaria teŋin m pɛ'ɛl man nidib la yinne nu'ukukudugɔ!”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab da lɛbisi yɛli ba ye, “Yɛlimini o ye onɛ nan yɛɛd zaba la'ad da dʋ'ʋs o mɛŋ wʋʋ onɛ pʋn zabi nyaŋ ka yɛɛgid o la'adɛ!”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad da wʋm labakaŋa nɛ saŋa kanɛ ka on nɛ o na'anam bɛɛ ba sʋga la ni nuud daam. O da tans o nidib la ye, “Ti'ebimi zaba!” Ka ba ti'eb ye ba keŋ zab nɛ tempʋʋg la. Ahab zabi nyaŋ

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es da kɛn Israel Na'ab Ahab san'an na yɛl o ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Fʋ nyɛ soogianam banɛ ka' bɛn laa? Zina m na zaŋi ba niŋi fʋ nu'ugin ka fʋ na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.’”

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Amaa Ahab da bu'os o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ ye o tʋmi li?” Nɔdi'es la da lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Na'akim sieba banɛ sʋŋid sʋ'ʋlim gɔmenanam la na tʋmi li.’” Ka o lɛm bu'os ye, “Ka anɔ'ɔn na pin'il zaba la?” Ka Nɔdi'es la lɛbis o ye, “Fʋnɛ na pin'il.”

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Na'akim sieba banɛ sʋŋid sʋ'ʋlim gɔmenanam la dɛŋi yi yiiga. Ben-Hadad da dɛŋi yis o soogia baanlʋg ye ba gur, ka ba lɛb na yɛl o ye, “Dap sieba yi Samaria tʋ'ʋsid na.”

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Ka o ye, “Ba ya'a yina nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm, yanam gban'ami ba vʋt na, ba ya'a lɛn yinɛ na nɛ zaba yanam gban'aminɛ ba vʋt na!”

english_verse: The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle,
translation_verse: Ka gɔmenanam na'akim la yi tempʋʋgin la na, ka soogianam la bɛɛ ba nya'aŋ.

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: Ka sɔ' wʋsa gban'e o dataa. Saŋkan la ka Aram dim la yʋ'ʋn zɔt ka Israel dim la kati dɔlli ba. Amaa Ben-Hadad da ban' wiefʋ zɔ nɛ o nimbanɛ ban'ad widi la.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab la da keŋ tuonnɛ zabi nyaŋ zaba tɛrekonam nɛ widi la, ka kʋ Aram dim la hali ka li ka' na'anaa. Ben-Hadad zab nɛ Samaria ya'as

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Din nya'aŋ la, nɔdi'es la da lɛb Israel Na'ab san'an na yɛl o ye, “Zi'enim sʋ'ʋŋa ka gɔs fʋn na maal si'em, bɔzugɔ sapal saŋa Aram Na'ab na lɛn kena zab nɛf.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Aram na'ab na'ayikpɛm la da sa'al o ye, “Israel dim teŋgbana la anɛ kʋkʋna ni teŋgbana, dinɛ kɛ ka ba daa nyaŋi ti la. Amaa ti ya'a zab nɛ ba teŋ kanɛ an sassi la ni, ti na nyaŋi ba.

english_verse: Here's what you should do. First, get rid of those
translation_verse: Niŋim anwa: Yisim na'anam la ba zin'igin ka tiak ninsieba banɛ an zaba tuongatibi lɛbisi ba zin'isin la.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: Asɛɛ ka fʋ lɛm bɔ soogianam bɛdegʋ ka ba zem wʋʋ banɛ daa kpi la nɛ widi nɛ zaba tɛrekonam, ka ba wʋsa kal zem wʋʋ bama la kiapi. Ti na zab nɛ Israel dim la zin'ikanɛ an sassi la. Nɛ'ɛŋa bi'esʋg kae, ti na nyaŋi ba.” Ka o siaki ba sa'alʋg ka tʋm wʋʋ ban yɛl o si'em la.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Sapalli da paae la, Na'ab Ben-Hadad da la'as Aram dimi keŋ Afek teŋin ye o zab nɛ Israel dim.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Wina'am nid la da kena yɛl Israel Na'ab la ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Aram dim la tɛn'ɛs ye, Zugsɔb la anɛ kʋkʋna Wina'am ka ka' bɔn'ɔdin Wina'am, dinzugɔ m na zaŋ soogianam banɛ ka' bɛn nwa' niŋi fʋ nu'usin ka ya baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.’”

english_verse: For seven days the two armies stayed in their camps, facing each other. Then on the seventh day the fighting broke out, and before sunset the Israelites had killed
translation_verse: Daba ayɔpɔi ka ba zi'e kpi'e taaba. Daba ayɔpɔi la daar ka ba paae taaba. Israel dim la da kʋ Aram dim soogianam banɛ ken nɔba la tusa kɔbiga daar yinne.

english_verse: The rest of the Syrian army ran back to Aphek, but the town wall fell and crushed
translation_verse: Banɛ kpɛlim la da su'a Afek tempʋʋgin ka zaŋguom lii kʋʋ ba nidib tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi. Na'ab Ben-Hadad da zɔɔ kpɛn' tempʋʋgin su'a dɔkanɛ bɛ pʋʋgin la. Ahab bas Ben-Hadad

english_verse: His officials said, “Your Majesty, we've heard that Israel's kings keep their agreements. We will wrap sackcloth around our waists, put ropes around our heads, and ask Ahab to let you live.”
translation_verse: O na'ayikpɛm la da yɛl o ye, “Gɔsima, ti wʋm ye Israel na'anam la anɛ nimbaanlzɔtib. Kɛl ka ti sie ti mɛŋi sɔn bɔto fuudi ti siesin ka nɔk nwiisi viligi ti zuti keŋ o san'an bɛllim o, ka daasi'erɛɛ o kʋ kʋʋ fɔ.”

english_verse: Benhadad's officials were trying to figure out what Ahab was thinking, and when he said “brother,” they quickly replied, “You're right! You and Benhadad are like brothers.” “Go get him,” Ahab said. When Benhadad came out, Ahab had him climb up into his chariot.
translation_verse: Nidib la da nɔki li ka li anɛ zanbin sʋŋʋ tisi ba ka siak tɔ'ɔtɔ ye, “Ɛɛn, fʋ ba'abiig Ben-Hadad.” Ka Na'ab la ye, “Kem mɔr o na!” Ben-Hadad n da yina la, Ahab da kɛ ka o kpɛn' o tɛreko la ni.

english_verse: Benhadad said, “I'll give back the towns my father took from your father. And you can have shops in Damascus, just as my father had in Samaria.” Ahab replied, “If you do these things, I'll let you go free.” Then they signed a peace treaty, and Ahab let Benhadad go. A Prophet Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Ben-Hadad da yɛl ye, “M na lɛbis tɛɛns banɛ ka m saam da faaɛn fʋ saam san'an la. Fʋ na mɛɛ fʋ da' zin'is Damaskus tempʋʋgin wʋʋ m saamme da mɛ Samaria tempʋʋgin si'em la.” Ahab da yɛl o ye, “Fʋn sadigim zi'el nɔɔr si'em la, m na basif ka fʋ keŋ.” O da kɛ ka o zi'el nɔɔr ka o bas o ka o kul.

english_verse: About this time the Lord commanded a prophet to say to a friend, “Hit me!” But the friend refused,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la labaar da yi nɔdi'esidib la biig yinne ni na yɛl o tiraan ye, “Nwɛ'ɛmim!” Ka o zan'as.

english_verse: and the prophet told him, “You disobeyed the Lord, and as soon as you walk away, a lion will kill you.” The friend left, and suddenly a lion killed him.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es la da yɛl ye, “Fʋn zan'as ka pʋ siak Zugsɔb nɔɔr la, fʋ ya'a basim, gbigim na kʋʋf.” Dau la da gaad la, gbigim da sia'al o kpɛn kʋʋ o.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es la da nyɛ dau sɔ' ya'as ka yɛl o ye, “M bɛlimnɛ nwɛ'ɛmim.” Ka dau la nwɛ' o pu'alim o.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Ka nɔdi'es la keŋ zi'en suor kpikpɛŋ gur na'ab la ka nɔk pienni vilig o zug nɛ o nindaa tiak o mɛŋ.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Na'ab la ti gat la ka o buol o ye, “Naa! M keŋ nɛ zaba la ni, ka lin ti mu'oe la ka sɔ' mɔr ninkanɛ ka ba zabi gban'e o na ka yɛl ye, ‘Gur dau kaŋa, o ya'a bɔdig fʋ nyɔvʋri la ka fʋ tiak, ya'a ka' ala fʋ na yɔ anzurifa gbila pisyuobʋ nɛ anii.’

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Ka m nini mu'oe ka m bɛ kpɛ' ka bɛ kpɛ' la ka dau la zɔɔ bɔdig.” Ka Israel Na'ab la yɛl ye, “Fʋn yɛl si'em la, fʋ kadi fʋ mɛŋ saria.”

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es la da tabinɛ yis pien la o nindaan tɔ'ɔtɔ, ka Israel Na'ab la baŋ ye o anɛ nɔdi'es.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Fʋ bas ninkanɛ ka m gban'e ye o kpi. Dinzugɔ, fʋ nyɔvʋr ka fʋ tiak o nyɔvʋr, ka nɔki fʋ nidibi tiak nɛ o nidib.’”

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Ka Israel Na'ab la kul Samaria nɛ sʋnpɛɛn.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Ahab da yɛl Nabof ye, “Fʋn vain tiis pɔɔg la sadigim kpi'e nɛ m yin la, kɛl ka m di'e li maali m zɛnma'asa bɔn'ɔg. M na tisif vain tiis pɔɔg kanɛ an sʋ'ʋŋa gaad ala, bɛɛ fʋ ya'a lɛm bɔɔd, m na yɔɔf ka li sia'al fʋn naan kuosin ka li ligidi an si'em.”

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Amaa Nabof da lɛbis ye, “Wina'am da kɛ ka m nɔki m yaanam faari tisi fɔ!”

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Ahab da kul o yin nɛ ɛndʋg nɛ sʋnpɛɛn, bɔzugɔ Nabof onɛ an Jezireel nid la yɛl ye o kʋ nɔki m yaanam faari tis o la zug. O da paae yinne dig gadʋg zugʋ nɔk o nindaa kpa' dɔkpin ka zan'as diib. Jezebɛl ninkʋʋr la yɛla

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: O pu'a Jezebɛl da kpɛn' na bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ sʋnf san'am ka fʋ zan'as diibɔ?”

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M yɛl nɛ Nabof onɛ an Jezireel nid la ye o kuos o vain tiis pɔɔg la tisim, bɛɛ o ya'a bɔɔd m na tiaki m vain tiis pɔɔgʋ tis o, ka o zan'as, ka yɛl ye, ‘M kʋ tisi fʋ m pɔɔg la.’”

english_verse: “Aren't you the king of Israel?” Jezebel asked. “Get out of bed and eat something! Don't worry, I'll get Naboth's vineyard for you.”
translation_verse: Ka o pu'a Jezebɛl yɛl o ye, “Israel Na'abi niŋid si'em nwaa? Duom di, ka maal sumalisim, ka mam na di'e Nabof onɛ an Jezireel nid la pɔɔg la tisif.”

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Ka biriku'an dima ayi' kena zin'inɛ o tuon, ka ma'aa tis Nabof nidib la tuon ye, “Nabof pian' pɔ'ɔg Wina'am nɛ Na'ab la.” Ka ba duoe mɔr Nabof n yi yiŋi lɔb o nɛ kuga kʋ.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: Ba da tʋm yɛl Jezebɛl ye, “Ba lɔb Nabof nɛ kuga ka o kpi.”

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Jezebɛl n kpɛn wʋm ye, ba lɔb Nabof nɛ kuga kʋ la, ka yɛl Ahab ye, “Duom keŋ sʋ'ʋg Nabof onɛ an Jezireel nid la pɔkanɛ ka o daa zan'as ye o kʋ kuosi tisif la! O kpiya.”

english_verse: Ahab got up and went to take over the vineyard. Elijah Condemns Ahab
translation_verse: Ahab n da wʋm ye Nabof kpiya la, o da duoe keŋ sʋ'ʋg Nabof vain tiis pʋʋg la. Elaja zɛrig Ahab nɛ Jezebɛl

english_verse: “King Ahab of Israel is in Naboth's vineyard right now, taking it over.
translation_verse: “Duom sigi tʋ'ʋs Israel Na'ab Ahab onɛ sʋ'oe Samaria la. Nannanna o bɛ Nabof vain tiis pɔɔgin la. O keŋnɛ ye o sʋ'ʋgi li.

english_verse: Go tell him that I say, ‘Ahab, you murdered Naboth and took his property. And so, in the very spot where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they will lick up your blood.’ ” When Elijah found him,
translation_verse: Yɛlim o ye, ‘Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': Fʋ pʋ kʋ nɛ dau sɔ' ka faaɛn o faarɛ?’” Yɛlim o ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'el nwa': ‘Zin'ikanɛ ka baas liel Nabof ziim la, ani ka baas mɛ na lieli fʋ ziim; ɛɛn fʋ mɛŋ ziim!’”

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Ahab n da nyɛ Elaja la, o da bu'os o ye, “Fʋ nyɛɛ maa, m dataa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, m nyɛɛf! Fʋn gban'e fʋ sʋʋnrin ye fʋ tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb tuon la zug ka m nyɛɛf la.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: ‘M na kɛ ka tɔɔg luu fʋ zugin na. M na kanbisi fʋ yaas ka nwaae biribiŋ kpaanr wʋsa banɛ bɛ Ahab yin; banɛ an yammis nɛ banɛ ka' yammis wʋsa Israel teŋin.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: M na maali fʋ yir wʋʋ Nebat biig Jeroboam nɛ Ahija biig Baasa ya' la an si'em la, bɔzugɔ fʋ kɛya ka m sʋnf pɛlig ka mɛ kɛ ka Israel tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.’

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb la mɛ yɛl Jezebɛl yɛla ye, ‘Baas na ɔnb Jezebɛl Jezireel teŋ zaŋguomin la.

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: “‘Baas na ɔnb Ahab nimbanɛ kpi tempʋʋgin la ka niis di banɛ kpi tempʋʋg la yiŋ la.’”

english_verse: Tell them to put him in prison and to give him nothing but bread and water until I come back safely.”
translation_verse: ka yɛli ba ye na'ab la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Yɔɔmi ninkaŋa sanrega ni, da tis o si'el si'ela asɛɛ bodobodo nɛ ku'om ma'aa paae mam na ti lɛb laafi na.’”

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab da yɛl o na'ayikpɛm ye, “Ya mi' ye Ramot teŋ dinɛ bɛ Gilead sʋ'ʋlimin la anɛ tinamɛ sʋ'oe, amaa ti pʋ maal si'el-si'el ye ti di'e li yis Aram na'ab nu'usinɛ!”

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os Na'ab Jehosafat ye, “Fʋ na dɔllim ka ti keŋ zab nɛ Ramot dinɛ bɛ Gilead laa?” Ka o da lɛbis Israel Na'ab ye, “Mam nɛ fʋ anɛ yinne, m nidib anɛ fʋ nidib ka m widi aan fʋ widi.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Amaa Na'ab Jehosafat da bu'os ye, “Ka Zugsɔb la nɔdi'es lɛn ka' kpɛla ka ti na bu'osɛɛ?”

english_verse: Then Ahab sent someone to bring Micaiah as soon as possible.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab la da yɛl o na'ayikpɛm la yinne ye, “Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ buol Mikaya, Imla biig la, na!”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab nɛ Jehosafat onɛ an Juda Na'ab la da yɛnɛ ba na'am fuudi zin' ba na'am gbana zut zieŋ dinɛ bɛ Samaria yaŋir la kpikpɛŋ, ka nɔdi'esidib la bɛɛ ba tuonnɛ pian'adi ba nɔdi'esʋg pian'ad.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Zedekaya onɛ an Kenaana biig la da maal kʋnt iila ka kʋʋs ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Fʋ na nɔk nɛ'ɛŋa zɛ Aram dim la, hali nɛ fʋn na ti san'ami ba wʋsa!’”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'esidib banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa mɛ da yɛl ala ye, “Naa! Zam nɛ Ramot dinɛ bɛ Gilead la ka fʋ na nyaŋ! Zugsɔb la na nɔki li niŋi fʋ nu'usin.” Mikaya pian' ye ba na zabi gʋ'ʋŋ

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Onɛ ka ba tʋm ye o keŋ buol Mikaya na la yɛl o ye, “Gɔsima, ba la'as nɛ pian'ad wʋʋ ba maalnɛ nɔɔr yinne nɛ, ye Na'ab la na nyaŋ. Siakim tisi ba ka pian' dinɛ na malis Na'ab la!”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Amaa Mikaya yɛl ye, “Nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ vʋe la zugɔɔ, mam ye m yɛl o nɛ Zugsɔb la yɛlim si'el ma'aa.”

english_verse: Then Micaiah went to Ahab, and Ahab asked, “Micaiah, should I attack the Syrians at Ramoth?” “Yes!” Micaiah answered. “The Lord will help you defeat them.”
translation_verse: On paae na la ka Na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Mikaya, ti kem zab nɛ Ramot teŋ dinɛ bɛ Gilead sʋ'ʋlimin la bɛɛ ti kɛla?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Naa! Zam ka fʋ na nyaŋ! Zugsɔb na nɔki li niŋi fʋ nu'usin!”

english_verse: “Micaiah, I've told you over and over to tell me the truth!” Ahab shouted. “What does the Lord really say?”
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Nɔɔr ala ka m na yɛlif nɛ nimmua ye fʋ pian' dinɛ an sida ma'aa nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋrɛ?”

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Mikaya da lɛbis o ye, “Man nyɛ ka Israel dim wʋsa zɔɔ widig kʋkʋna ni nwɛnɛ pɛ'ɛs banɛ ka' kɔnbkemnib nɛ. Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, ‘Nimbama pʋ mɔr zugdaana, kɛl ka sɔ' wʋsa lɛbi kul o yin nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm!’”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Mikaya da lɛn yɛli ba ye, “Dinzugɔ kɛlisimi Zugsɔb la labaar: m nyɛ ka Zugsɔb la zin' o na'am gbauŋ zug ka banɛ bɛ arezana ni la wʋsa la'asi zi'e gilig o datiuŋ nɛ o dagɔbʋg.

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: “Alazug Zugsɔb la nɔk dama'am siigi niŋi fʋ nɔdi'esidib la wʋsa nɔɔrin. Zugsɔb la gban'e fʋ yɛla nɛ bɛ'ɛd.”

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ani ka Zedekaya onɛ an Kenaana biig la keŋ nwɛ' Mikaya nindaa nɛ tampiank ka ye, “Zugsɔb Siig la dɔl suokanɛ yi mam san'anɛ kena pian' tisi fɔ?”

english_verse: Ahab shouted, “Arrest Micaiah! Take him to Prince Joash and Governor Amon of Samaria.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab da tis nɔɔr ye, “Gban'ami Mikaya mɔr o lɛb Ammon onɛ an tempʋʋg la zugdaan nɛ Joab onɛ an na'abiig la san'an,

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka Aram nid tɛk o tiraugʋ tɔn yɔɔgʋ ka li keŋ gban'e Israel Na'ab la, piim la da wiee nɛ o zaba la'ad la sʋʋginɛ kʋns o. Na'ab la da yɛl onɛ dɔribidi o zaba tɛreko la ye, “Fɛndigim tɛreko la ka ti yi zaba la yiŋ, ka m pu'alim nɛ.”

english_verse: Ahab and Jehoshaphat led their armies to Ramoth in Gilead.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab nɛ Jehosafat onɛ an Juda Na'ab la da duoe keŋ Ramot Gilead teŋin.

english_verse: Before they went into battle, Ahab said, “Jehoshaphat, I'll disguise myself, but you wear your royal robe.” Then Ahab disguised himself and went into battle.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab da yɛl Na'ab Jehosafat ye, “Man na tiaki m mɛŋi kpɛn' zaba la pʋʋgin, amaa fʋn yɛɛmi fʋ na'am fuud.” Ka sid tiak o mɛŋi kpɛn' zaba la ni.

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Tɛrekonam zabzabidib tuongatib la nyɛ Na'ab Jehosafat la, ba da tɛn'ɛs ye, “Bi'esʋg kae, Israel Na'ab la nwa'!” Ka ba fɛndig ye ba zab nɛ o, amaa Jehosafat da nwɛ' kuŋ,

english_verse: they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
translation_verse: ka tɛrekonam la tuongatib la gɔs ka li ka' Israel Na'ab laa, ka ba bas ka pʋ lɛn kad o.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Winnigi ti kpɛn'ɛd la ka kikaasig taae soogianam la bɛ zin'isi'a la wʋsa ye, “Dau wʋsa kulim o tempʋʋgin, ka sɔ' wʋsa lɛb o mɛŋ teŋin!”

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da kpiya ka ba mɔr o keŋ Samaria tempʋʋgin mum o ani.

english_verse: Some workers washed his chariot near a spring in Samaria, and prostitutes washed themselves in his blood. Dogs licked Ahab's blood off the ground, just as the Lord had warned.
translation_verse: Ba da pie tɛreko la nɛ Samaria bɛuŋin ka baas kena liel o ziim la nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb labaar la yɛl si'em nyain la.

english_verse: Everything else Ahab did while he was king, including the towns he strengthened and the palace he built and furnished with ivory, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Ahab na'am diib saŋa, la'an nɛ on da tʋm si'el, nɛ on da mɛ' na'ayir ka pi'e li nɛ wabʋg nyina la, nɛ tempʋʋd banɛ ka o da mɛ' ka li mɔr kpi'euŋ la; ba da sɔbi ba kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

translation_verse: Israel na'ab Ahab n da di na'am yʋma anaasi la, ka Asa biig Jehosafat da di Juda na'am.

english_verse: The country of Edom had no king at the time, so a lower official ruled the land.

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab offered to let his sailors go with Jehoshaphat's sailors, but Jehoshaphat refused.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Ahab biig Ahazaya da yɛl Na'ab Jehosafat ye, “Kɛl ka m nidib la dɔlli fʋ nimbanɛ ken nɛ anrima la.” Amaa ka Jehosafat zan'as.

english_verse: Jehoshaphat died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king. King Ahaziah of Israel
translation_verse: Jehosafat da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o, o yaab David tempʋʋgin. O biig Jehoram da di'e o zin'igi di na'am. Ahazaya di Israel na'am

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Ahab became king of Israel in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Juda na'ab Jehosafat n di na'am yʋma pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ka Ahab biig Ahazaya da di Israel na'am Samaria teŋin. O da di Israel na'am la nɛ yʋma ayi'.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon bɔzugɔ, o da dɔlisid o ba' nɛ o ma nɔba, nɛ Jeroboam onɛ an Nebat biig ka da kɛ ka Israel dim tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la nɔba.

english_verse: Ahaziah worshiped Baal and made the Lord God of Israel very angry, just as his father had done.
translation_verse: O da pʋ'ʋsid nɛ Baal ka kɛ ka Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la sʋnf duoe, nwɛnɛ o saamme da tʋm si'em la.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Ahazaya da naanɛ o girimbisa zug Samaria teŋin lu naa pu'alim. Dinzug o da tʋm nidib ka yɛli ba ye, “Kemi Ekron teŋgban kanɛ buon Baal-Zebub la san'anɛ bu'osi gɔs ye m na paam laafi m pu'alʋŋ nwa' nii?”

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb maliak da yɛl Elaja onɛ an Tisibi nid la ye, “Kem tʋ'ʋs Samaria na'abi tʋm ninsieba la na ka bu'osi ba ye, ‘Li pa'al ye Wina'am ka' Israel teŋin bɛɛ wala ka ya ken Baal-Zebub Ekron teŋgban la san'anɛ?’

english_verse: Tell him that because he has done this, he's on his deathbed!” And Elijah did what he was told.
translation_verse: Alazug, Zugsɔb la yɛl si'el na'ab la yɛla nwa' ye: ‘Fʋn dig digsi'a la, fʋ kʋ duoe. Asɛɛ ka fʋ kpi.’” Ka Elaja sid keŋ.

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Nimbanɛ ka na'ab la da tʋm la lɛb o sa'an la, ka o bu'osi ba ye, “Bɔɔ kɛ ka ya lɛb na?”

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Dau sɔ' sia'ali ti, ka yɛli ti ye, ‘Lɛm yɛli Na'akanɛ tʋmi ya la ye Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye: li pa'al ye Wina'am ka' Israel teŋin bɛɛ wala, ka fʋ tʋm nidib Baal-Zebub kanɛ an Ekron dim teŋgban la san'anɛ? Dinzug fʋn dig digsi'a la fʋ kʋ duoe. Asɛɛ fʋ kpi.’”

english_verse: “What did the man look like?” Ahaziah asked.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'osi ba ye, “Nimbɔ buudi ka yanam sia'al ka o yɛli ya nɛ'?”

english_verse: “He was hairy and had a leather belt around his waist,” they answered. “It must be Elijah!” replied Ahaziah.
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis o ye, “O anɛ kɔnbilʋg sɔb, ka lɔɔ o siaa nɛ gbauŋ sɛnbidiŋ.” Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye, “Elaja onɛ yi Tisibi teŋin la, la.”

english_verse: Fire has already wiped out the other officers and their soldiers. Please don't let it happen to me.”
translation_verse: Gɔsima, bugum pʋn yi arezana ni na kanb soogiakpɛɛmnam ayi' nɛ ba nidib la, amaa nannanna zɔmim nyɔɔg!”

english_verse: The angel from the Lord said to Elijah, “Go with him and don't be afraid.” So Elijah got up and went with the officer.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb maliak yʋ'ʋn da pian' tis Elaja ye, “Sigim dɔl o; da zɔt dabiem!” Ka Elaja sid duoe sigi dɔl o ka ba keŋ na'ab la san'an

english_verse: When Elijah arrived, he told Ahaziah, “The Lord wants to know why you sent messengers to Ekron to ask Baalzebub about your injury. Don't you believe there's a God in Israel? Ahaziah, because you did that, the Lord says you will die.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': Li pa'al ye Wina'am ka' Israel teŋin ka fʋ na bu'osɛ, ka gʋ'ʋŋi tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ bu'os Baal-Zebub kanɛ an Ekron teŋgban laa? Fʋn maal nɛ' la zug, fʋ kʋ vʋ'ʋg ka duoe fʋn dig gadsi'a la zugɔ. Asɛɛ fʋ kpi!”

english_verse: Ahaziah died, just as the Lord had said. But since Ahaziah had no sons, Joram his brother then became king. This happened in the second year that Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
translation_verse: Ka na'ab la daa sid kpi nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl Elaja ye o pian' si'em la. Ahazaya da ka' biig la zug, o pitʋ Joram da di Israel na'am, ka li anɛ Jehosafat biig Jehoram n da di Juda na'am la li yʋma ayi' la nya'aŋ.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaziah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim linɛ wʋsa n tʋm Ahazaya na'am saŋa la, nɛ on tʋm si'el wʋsa la, ba da sɔbi li kpɛn'ɛs Israel na'anam gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Not long before the Lord took Elijah up into heaven in a strong wind, Elijah and Elisha were leaving Gilgal.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da bɔɔd ye o nɔk Elaja keŋ arezana nɛ sisi'epiliŋ la, Elaja nɛ Elasia da yinɛ Gilgal teŋin ken.

english_verse: Elijah said to Elisha, “The Lord wants me to go to Bethel, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Bethel.
translation_verse: Ka Elaja yɛl Elasia ye, “Kpɛlim kpɛla; Zugsɔb la tʋmim ye m keŋ Betel teŋin.” Amaa Elasia da lɛbis o ye, “Asida ka m yɛtif, nɛ Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋrɛ, m kʋ basi fʋ dɔllimm!” Alazug ba wʋsa da keŋ paae Betel teŋin.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Nɔdi'esidib banɛ da la'asi bɛ Betel la da yii kɛn Elasia san'an na bu'os o ye, “Fʋ mi' ye Zugsɔb la na nɔki fʋ zugdaan la zina yii fʋ san'an ka basi fɔɔ?” Ka Elasia lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn m mi', amaa da pian'adi nɛ li yɛlaa!”

english_verse: Elijah then said, “Elisha, now the Lord wants me to go to Jericho, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life, that I will stay with you no matter what!” And he went with Elijah to Jericho.
translation_verse: Ka Elaja yɛl Elasia ye, “M biig Elasia, kpɛlim kpɛla: ka Zugsɔb la tʋmim ye m tɔlisi keŋ Jeriko teŋin.” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Asida ka m yɛtif, nɛ Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋrɛ, mam kʋ basi fʋ dɔllimm!” Alazug ba da tɔlisi keŋ paae Jeriko teŋin.

english_verse: A group of prophets who lived there asked Elisha, “Do you know that today the Lord is going to take away your master?” “Yes, I do,” Elisha answered. “But don't remind me of it.”
translation_verse: Nɔdi'esidib banɛ da la'asi bɛ Jeriko la da keŋ Elasia san'an bu'os o ye, “Fʋ mi' ye Zugsɔb la na nɔki fʋ zugdaan la yii fʋ san'an zina ka basi fɔɔ?” Ka o lɛbisi ba ye, “Ɛɛn m mi', amaa da pian'adi nɛ li yɛlaa!”

english_verse: Elijah then said to Elisha, “Now the Lord wants me to go to the Jordan River, but you must stay here.” Elisha replied, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I will never leave you!” So the two of them walked on together.
translation_verse: Ka Elaja yɛl o ye, “Kpɛlim kpɛla; ka Zugsɔb la tʋmim ye m keŋ Joodan mu'arin.” Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Asida ka m yɛtif, nɛ Zugsɔb kanɛ vʋe la yʋ'ʋrɛ, mam pʋ ye m basi fʋ dɔllimm!” Alazug babayi' la daa dɔl taaba keŋ.

english_verse: Fifty prophets followed Elijah and Elisha from Jericho, then stood at a distance and watched as the two men walked toward the river.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'esidib la ban pisnu, da la'as taaba keŋ zi'e lallisa, gɔsid zin'ikanɛ ka Elaja nɛ Elasia zi'e Joodan mu'ar nɔɔrin la.

english_verse: When they got there, Elijah took off his coat, then he rolled it up and struck the water with it. At once a path opened up through the river, and the two of them walked across on dry ground.
translation_verse: Elaja da yɛɛg o fuugʋ kpilim ka ʋki nwɛ' ku'om la. Ka ku'om la da duoe zi'enɛ nwɛnɛ zaŋguom nɛ lɛbis datiuŋ nɛ dagɔbʋg wʋsa. Ka babayi' la nɔ teŋ kpi'emisi lɔ'ɔŋ.

english_verse: After they had reached the other side, Elijah said, “Elisha, the Lord will soon take me away. What can I do for you before that happens?” Elisha answered, “Please give me twice as much of your power as you give the other prophets, so I can be the one who takes your place as their leader.”
translation_verse: Ban daa lɔ'ɔŋi naae la ka Elaja bu'os Elasia ye, “Yɛlimim, bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye m maali tisif ka ba nyaan nɔkimi fʋ san'anɛ?” Ka Elasia lɛbis ye, “Kɛl ka m paami fʋ paŋ la buudi zin'isa ayi'.”

english_verse: “It won't be easy,” Elijah answered. “It can happen only if you see me as I am being taken away.”
translation_verse: Elaja da lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Fʋ sɔs nɛ linɛ yɛla tɔi;” la'an nɛ wala fʋ ya'a ti nyɛ ka ba nɔkimi yii fʋ san'an, li na aan fʋ din; ya'a ka' ala, fʋ kʋ nyɛɛ.

english_verse: Elijah and Elisha were walking along and talking, when suddenly there appeared between them a flaming chariot pulled by fiery horses. At once, a strong wind took Elijah up into heaven.
translation_verse: Ban daa dɔl taaba ken ka sɔnsid la, tɔ'ɔtɔ ka widi tɛreko nɛ widi yina nwɛnɛ bugum nɛ kpɛn' ba teŋsʋkʋ baki ba, ka nɔk Elaja nwɛnɛ sisi'epiliŋ nɛ dʋ arezana.

english_verse: Elisha saw this and shouted, “Israel's cavalry and chariots have taken my master away!” After Elijah had gone, Elisha tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Elasia da nyɛ nɛ' la ka nwɛ' kuŋ ye, “M Saamma, m Saamma, widi tɛrekonam nɛ Israel wiedban'adiba!” Ka o da pʋ lɛn nyɛɛ o ya'asa. Elasia da gban'e o mɛŋ fuugʋ pʋdig ayi' sʋnsa'aŋ zug,

english_verse: Elijah's coat had fallen off, so Elisha picked it up and walked back to the Jordan River.
translation_verse: ka pi'ig fukanɛ naam Elaja san'an lu la lɛbi keŋ zi'en Joodan mu'ar la nɔɔrin,

english_verse: When the prophets from Jericho saw what happened, they said to each other, “Elisha now has Elijah's power.” They walked over to him, bowed down,
translation_verse: Nɔdi'esidib banɛ yi Jeriko na zi'e gɔsid la da yɛl ye, Elaja siig la yʋ'ʋn bɛ nɛ Elasia zug. Ka ba keŋ tʋ'ʋs o ka igin o tuonnɛ na'as o,

english_verse: They kept begging until he was embarrassed to say no. He finally agreed, and the prophets sent the men out. They looked three days for Elijah but never found him.
translation_verse: Amaa ba da dɔl o li yɛla, hali ka nyan ti gban'e o ka o gʋ'ʋŋ zan'asʋg. Alazug o da yɛl ye, “Tɔ', ka tʋmmini ba!” Ka ba tʋm nidib pisnu la, ka ba iee o zin'ig daba atan' ka pʋ nyɛɛ o.

translation_verse: Ban da lɛb Elasia san'an Jeriko teŋin na la, o da yɛli ba ye, “M daa pʋn pʋ yɛli ya ye ya da keŋɛ?” Elasia kɛ ka ku'om lieb sʋ'ʋm la yɛla

english_verse: One day the people of Jericho said, “Elisha, you can see that our city is in a good spot. But the water from our spring is so bad that it even keeps our crops from growing.”
translation_verse: Teŋ la dap da yɛl Elasia ye, “Ti zugdaana, gɔsima! Teŋ kaŋa bɛ nɛ zin'isʋŋin nwɛnɛ fʋn pʋn nyɛɛ li si'em la, amaa ku'om la ka' sʋ'ʋm, ka teŋgbauŋ la mɛ pʋ du'ad zʋʋdɛ.”

english_verse: He replied, “Put some salt in a new bowl and bring it to me.” They brought him the bowl of salt,
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl ye, “Mɔri lapaalig na, ka niŋi yaarim li pʋʋgin!” Ka ba sid mɔr na tis o.

english_verse: and he carried it to the spring. He threw the salt into the water and said, “The Lord has made this water pure again. From now on you'll be able to grow crops, and no one will starve.”
translation_verse: Ka o yii mɔri li keŋ ku'om la bʋn zin'isi'a la nɔk yaarim la lɔsi li pʋʋgin, ka yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘M tiak ku'okaŋa ka li lieb sʋm. Li kʋ lɛn zi kum na bɛɛ kɛ ka teŋ la zʋʋd kʋ du'aa.’”

english_verse: The water has been fine ever since, just as Elisha said. Some Boys Make Fun of Elisha
translation_verse: Ka ku'om la sid lieb sʋ'ʋŋa ti paae zina, nwɛnɛ Elasia da pian' si'em la. Bibanɛ la' Elasia la yɛla

english_verse: Elisha left and headed toward Bethel. Along the way some boys started making fun of him by shouting, “Go away, baldy! Get out of here!”
translation_verse: Elasia da yii ani keŋ Betel teŋin, ka on daa dɔl suori ken la, bisieba daa naam tempʋʋgin la yina la'ad o ka yɛl o ye, “Zupieŋaa kem sa! Zupieŋaa kem sa!”

english_verse: Elisha turned around and stared at the boys. Then he cursed them in the name of the Lord. At once two bears ran out of the woods and ripped to pieces
translation_verse: Ka o fɛndigi gɔsi ba ka pɔ nɔɔri niŋi ba nɛ Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr. Ka zɔta ayi' yi sian'arin la naa gban'e dasam la ban pisnaasi nɛ ayi' aansi ba niŋgbina la zɔrisi zɔris.

english_verse: Elisha went up to Mount Carmel, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: Ka o gaadi keŋ Kaamel zuorin la ka yii ani lɛb Samaria teŋin.

english_verse: Joram son of Ahab became king of Israel in Jehoshaphat's eighteenth year as king of Judah. Joram ruled twelve years from Samaria
translation_verse: Jehosafat n da di Juda na'am yʋma pii nɛ anii la nya'aŋ la, Ahab biig Joram da di Israel na'am n bɛ Samaria tempʋʋgin. Joram da anɛ Israel na'ab yʋʋm pii nɛ ayi'.

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He tore down the stone image his father had made to honor Baal, and so he wasn't as sinful as his parents.
translation_verse: O da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la nini ni ka lɛɛ pʋ paae o saam nɛ o ma da tʋm si'em la. O da vuoɛn kugir kanɛ da an Baal teŋgban ka o saam da maal la bas.

english_verse: But he kept doing the sinful things that Jeroboam son of Nebat had led Israel to do. The Country of Moab Rebels against Israel
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, o mɛ da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd wʋʋ Jeroboam onɛ an Nebat biig la da tʋm si'em ka pan'as Israel dim ka ba mɛ tʋmi li la. O da pʋ basi li. Moab nɛ Israel dim zaba la yɛla

english_verse: For many years the country of Moab had been controlled by Israel and was forced to pay taxes to the kings of Israel. King Mesha of Moab raised sheep, so he paid the king of Israel
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa Mesea onɛ an Moab Na'ab la da gʋ'ʋl pɛ'ɛs, ka li an ye o tisid Israel Na'ab la pɛbibis tusa kɔbiga nɛ pɛraad tusa kɔbiga kɔnbid yʋʋm wʋsa.

english_verse: But soon after the death of Ahab, Mesha rebelled against Israel.
translation_verse: Amaa Ahab n da kpi la, Moab Na'ab la da ki'is Israel Na'ab la nɔɔr.

english_verse: One day, Joram left Samaria and called together Israel's army.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Na'ab Joram da yi Samaria tempʋʋgin keŋ la'as Israel dim wʋsa.

english_verse: He sent this message to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “The king of Moab has rebelled. Will you go with me to attack him?” “Yes, I will,” Jehoshaphat answered. “I'm on your side, and my soldiers and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: O mɛ da tɔlim labakaŋa yɛl Jehosafat onɛ an Juda Na'ab la ye, “Moab Na'ab la ki'isi m nɔɔr. Fʋ na sʋŋim ka ti keŋ zab nɛ Moab dimaa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Man nɛ fʋ na keŋ. Man nɛ fʋn anɛ yinne, man nidib la anɛ fʋ nidib, ka m widi la mɛ aan fʋ widi.”

english_verse: But which way should we go?” “We will march through Edom Desert,” Joram replied.
translation_verse: Ka o bu'os ye, “Suokanɛ ka ti na dɔlli keŋ zab nɛ ba?” Ka o lɛbis o ye, “Ti ye ti dɔlnɛ yi Edom sian'arin la.”

english_verse: So Joram, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom led their troops out. But seven days later, there was no drinking water left for them or their animals.
translation_verse: Dinzug Israel Na'ab la da yi ya, nɛ Juda Na'ab la nɛ Edom Na'ab. Ban gilig daba ayɔpɔi naae la, soogianam la daa lɛn ka' ku'om na nuu ba mɛŋ, bɛɛ ba bʋnkɔnbid banɛ bɛ nɛ ba la.

english_verse: Joram cried out, “This is terrible! The Lord must have led us out here to be captured by Moab's army.”
translation_verse: Ka Israel Na'ab la kaas kuŋ ye, “Mbaye! Zugsɔb la la'as tinam na'anama atan' nwa' nɛ kpɛla na ye o zaŋi ti niŋ Moab Na'ab la nu'uginɛɛ?”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat said, “Which of the Lord's prophets is with us? We can find out from him what the Lord wants us to do.” One of Joram's officers answered, “Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He was one of Elijah's closest followers.”
translation_verse: Amaa Jehosafat da bu'os ye, “Zugsɔb nɔdi'es ka' kpɛla ka ti bu'os Zugsɔb la yii o san'anɛɛ?” Israel Na'ab la kpɛɛm yinne da lɛbis ye, “Elasia onɛ an Safat biig ka daa sʋŋid Elaja la bɛ kpɛla.”

english_verse: Jehoshaphat replied, “He can give us the Lord's message.” The three kings went over to Elisha,
translation_verse: Ka Jehosafat yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛlʋg sid bɛɛ o ni.” Alazug Israel Na'ab, nɛ Jehosafat nɛ Edom Na'ab la da keŋ o san'an.

english_verse: and he asked Joram, “Why did you come to me? Go talk to the prophets of the foreign gods your parents worshiped.” “No,” Joram answered. “It was the Lord who led us out here, so that Moab's army could capture us.”
translation_verse: Elasia da yɛl Israel Na'ab la ye, “Bɔɔ bɛ man nɛ fʋn san'anɛ? Kemi fʋ saam nɛ fʋ ma nɔdi'esidib la san'an!” Ka Israel Na'ab la lɛbis ye, “Ayei! Li anɛ Zugsɔb la buol tinam na'anama atan' la'as ye o nɔki ti niŋ Moab Na'ab nu'usin.”

english_verse: Elisha said to him, “I serve the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as he lives, I swear I wouldn't even look at you if I didn't respect King Jehoshaphat.”
translation_verse: Elasia da yɛl ye, “Asida ka m yɛtif nɛ Zugsɔb onɛ ka m dɔl la yʋ'ʋr ye, li ya'a ka' man tisid Juda Na'ab la na'asi zugɔ m kʋ gi'e gɔsini ya baa bi'elaa.

english_verse: Then Elisha said, “Send for someone who can play the harp.” The harpist began playing, and the Lord gave Elisha this message for Joram:
translation_verse: Amaa nannanna mɔri onɛ an kɔnnwɛ'ɛd na!” Ka ba mɔr o na, ka kɔnnwɛ'ɛd la nam bɛ nwɛ'ɛbin la, ka Zugsɔb paŋ sig Elasia zugin na

english_verse: The Lord says that this dry riverbed will be filled with water.
translation_verse: ka o yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Tuumi bʋmbu'ad bɔn'ɔfaligin la wʋsa!’

english_verse: You won't feel any wind or see any rain, but there will be plenty of water for you and your animals.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛn yɛl si'eli nwa' ye: ‘Ya kʋ nyɛ sisi'em bɛɛ saa, amaa bɔn'ɔg la na pɛ'ɛl nɛ ku'om, ka yanam nɛ ya niigi nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ kpɛlim la na nu.’

english_verse: That simple thing isn't all the Lord is going to do. He will also help you defeat Moab's army.
translation_verse: Nɛ' anɛ na'ana Zugsɔb la nini ni. O mɛ na lɛn kɛ ka ya nyaŋ Moab dim.

english_verse: You will capture all their walled cities and important towns. You will chop down every good tree and stop up every spring of water, then ruin their fertile fields by covering them with rocks.
translation_verse: Ya mɛ na nyaŋi ba tɛɛns banɛ kpi'em nɛ ba tembɛda la wʋsa. Ya na nwa' tisʋma la wʋsa, ka gu'oe ku'om bun zin'isi'a la wʋsa ka nɔk kugaa san'ami ba pɔsʋma la wʋsa.”

english_verse: The next morning, while the sacrifice was being offered, water suddenly started flowing from the direction of Edom, and it flooded the land.
translation_verse: Li yimbɛog asuba ti paad saŋa kanɛ ka ba ye ba maal malʋŋ la, ba nyɛ ka ku'om kpɛn pʋbidi yit Edom baba kenna, ka teŋ la wʋsa pɛ'ɛl nɛ ku'om.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the people of Moab had heard that the three kings were coming to attack them. They had called together all of their fighting men, from the youngest to the oldest, and these troops were now standing at their border, ready for battle.
translation_verse: Moab dim la wʋsa da la'as teŋ la titɔndigin bɔzugɔ ba da wʋm ye na'anam la kenna ye ba zab nɛ ba, ka ba buol dau wʋsa, bʋnkʋdʋg bɛɛ dasaŋ, onɛ na nyaŋi zanl zaba la'ad la, ye ba yina zab.

english_verse: When they got up that morning, the sun was shining across the water, making it look red. The Moabite troops took one look
translation_verse: Ban daa duoe bɛogʋn asuba la, ka winnig tu'al ku'om la, Moab dim la da bɛ zin'isi'a la ba da nyɛti li ka li nwɛnɛ ziim nɛ.

english_verse: and shouted, “Look at that blood! The armies of those kings must have fought and killed each other. Come on, let's go take what's left in their camp.”
translation_verse: Ka ba ye, “Lina anɛ ziim. Na'anam la tulignɛ zabi kʋ taaba. Moab dima, ti kem faaɛn ba la'ad la!”

english_verse: But when they arrived at Israel's camp, the Israelite soldiers came out and attacked them, until they turned and ran away. Israel's army chased them all the way back to Moab, and even there they kept up the attack.
translation_verse: Amaa Moab dim la da keŋ Israel dim la'asʋg zin'igin la, Israel dim la da duoe zab nɛ ba hali ka ba ti gʋ'ʋŋi zɔ ka Israel dim la faaɛn teŋ la ka kʋ Moab dim la.

english_verse: The Israelites destroyed the Moabite towns. They chopped down the good trees and stopped up the springs of water, then covered the fertile fields with rocks. Finally, the only city left standing was Kir-Hareseth, but soldiers armed with slings surrounded and attacked it.
translation_verse: Ba da san'am tempʋʋd la, ka dau wʋsa pi'ig kugiri lɔb pɔɔd banɛ an sʋm la wʋsa ka li ti ligil nɛ kuga. Ba da vi' ku'om dinɛ pʋbid la wʋsa, ka nwa' tisʋma la wʋsa; Kir-Haresef teŋ ma'aa kuga da kpɛlim digi li zin'igin, amaa dap banɛ da mɔr luobis la da giligi zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Ka o yʋ'ʋn da nɔk o bikpɛŋ onɛ na ti di'e o na'am la maal maan teŋ la zaŋguom la zug. Lina da kɛya ka ba sʋʋnr duoe nɛ Israel dim la hali ka ba fɛndigi lɛbi ba mɛŋ teŋin.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
