english_verse: and said, “Open the window facing east.” When it was open, Elisha shouted, “Now shoot!” Jehoash shot an arrow and Elisha said, “That arrow is a sign that the Lord will help you completely defeat the Syrian army at Aphek.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Yɔ'ɔgim nya'aŋ takoro la,” ka o yɔ'ɔg. Ka Elasia yɛl o ye, “Tɔɔnm!” Ka o tɔn ka Elasia ye, “Zugsɔb la nyaŋir piim la, piim kanɛ na nyaŋ Aram dim la! Fʋ na nyaŋ Aram dim la Afek teŋin.”

english_verse: and disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He never stopped following the example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon, ka li dɔlnɛ Nebat biig Jeroboam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la buudi nɔɔ, ka kɛ ka Israel dim mɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛd. O da pʋ fɛndig ka bas o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with the Israelites, so he let King Hazael of Syria and his son Benhadad rule over them for a long time.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb sʋnf da duoe nɛ Israel dim, ka o kɛ ka ba bɛ Aram dim Na'ab Hazael nɛ o biig Ben-Hadad nu'usin, ba na'am la bɛn wʋsa.

english_verse: Jehoahaz prayed to the Lord for help, and the Lord saw how terribly Hazael was treating the Israelites. He answered Jehoahaz
translation_verse: Jehoahas da sɔs Zugsɔb la bɔɔd sʋŋir, ka o wʋm tis o bɔzugɔ o da nyɛ Aram Na'ab la wɛbigidi ba si'em.

english_verse: by sending Israel a leader who rescued them from the Syrians, and the Israelites lived in peace as they had before.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da bɔ sɔ' onɛ na faaɛn Israel ka ba nyaŋi yi Aram dim nu'usin. Li da kɛ ka Israel dim nyaŋi lɛbi zin'ini ba mɛŋ yaan wʋʋ ban da pʋn zin' si'em la.

english_verse: Jehoash became king of Israel in the thirty-seventh year of Joash's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Juda na'ab Joas da di na'am la yʋma pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi, ka Jehoas onɛ an Jehoahas biig la da di Israel na'am Samaria tempʋʋgin. O da di na'am la nɛ yʋma pii nɛ ayuobʋ.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoahaz did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Jehoahas na'am diib saŋa la, nɛ on da tʋm si'el nɛ on da nyaŋi maal si'el la, ba da sɔbi li kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Jehoahaz died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoash became king. King Jehoash of Israel
translation_verse: Jehoahas da kpiya ka ba mum o bam mum o yaanam zin'isi'a Samaria tempʋʋgin, ka o biig Jehoas lɛdigi di na'am la. Jehoas n di Israel na'am la

english_verse: “Grab a bow and some arrows,” Elisha told him, “and hold them in your hand.” Jehoash grabbed the bow and arrows and held them. Elisha placed his hand on the king's hand
translation_verse: Ka o yɛl Israel Na'ab la ye, “Nɔkim tiraug la zanl!” On nɔk la ka Elasia mɛ ʋk o nu'ugʋ pa'al Na'ab la nu'ug zug

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his war against King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ bʋmbanɛ da maal Jehoas na'am diib saŋa la, on da tʋm si'el nɛ on da nyaŋi maal si'el la, nɛ on zabid nɛ Amazaya, Juda Na'ab la si'em la, ba da sɔbi li kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria beside the other Israelite kings. His son Jeroboam then became king. Elisha the Prophet Dies
translation_verse: Jehoas da kpiya ka o biig Jeroboam lɛdigi dii o saam na'am la. Ba da mum Jehoas Samaria tempʋʋgin, bam mum Israel na'anam zin'isi'a la. Elasia kum yɛla

english_verse: Some time before the death of King Jehoash, Elisha the prophet was very sick and about to die. Jehoash went in and stood beside him, crying. He said, “Master, what will Israel's chariots and cavalry be able to do without you?”
translation_verse: Ban'asi'a da gban'e Elasia hali ti kʋʋ o. On da nam pʋ kpi la Jehoas onɛ da an Israel Na'ab la da keŋ ye o kaae o ka kum o ban'as la yɛla. Ka ye, “M Saama, m Saama, Israel dim zaba tɛrekonam nɛ ba wiedban'adiba!”

english_verse: Elisha said, “Pick up the arrows and hit the ground with them.” Jehoash grabbed the arrows and hit the ground three times, then stopped.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛl o ye, “Nɔkim piema la!”, Ka Na'ab la nɔk. Ka Elasia yɛl o ye, “Tɔɔnm teŋ!” Ka o tɔn nɔɔr atan' ka gu'oe.

english_verse: Elisha became angry with the king and exclaimed, “If you had struck it five or six times, you would completely wipe out the Syrians. Now you will defeat them only three times.”
translation_verse: Wina'am tʋmtʋm la sʋnf da duoe nɛ Na'ab la ka o yɛl o ye, “Li sʋm aannɛ ye fʋ tɔn teŋ la nɔɔr anu bɛɛ ayuobʋ; lin ka fʋ naan nyaŋin Aram dim la li' ba wʋsa. Amaa nannanna fʋ na nyaŋi ba nɛ nɔɔr atan' ma'aa!”

english_verse: Elisha died and was buried. Every year in the spring, Moab's leaders sent raiding parties into Israel.
translation_verse: Elasia da kpiya ka ba mum o. Saŋkan la Moab dim da kennɛ faand ki, bunib saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: Once, while some Israelites were burying a man's body, they saw a group of Moabites. The Israelites quickly threw the body into Elisha's tomb and ran away. As soon as the man's body touched the bones of Elisha, the man came back to life and stood up. Israel Defeats Syria
translation_verse: Israel dau da kpiya ka ba bɛɛ ani ye ba mum o ka ʋk zugʋ nyɛ ka faandib la ya'an kenna, ka ba nɔk kum la bas Elasia yaʋg la pʋʋg. Ka kum la lu yaʋgʋn la si'is Elasia kɔnba la ka vʋ'ʋgi duoe zi'e.

english_verse: Israel was under the power of King Hazael of Syria during the entire rule of Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Aram Na'ab Hazael da wɛbid Israel dim hali Jehoahas na'am diib saŋa la wʋsa.

english_verse: But the Lord was kind to the Israelites and showed them mercy because of his solemn agreement with their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. In fact, he has never turned his back on them or let them be completely destroyed.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la da mi' ba yɛla ka zɔɔ ba nimbaanlig ka pa'al ye o ba'a bɛ nɛ ba, on naal nɔɔr nɛ Abraham nɛ Isaak nɛ Jakob la zug. Hali ti paae zina o pʋ siak ye o san'ami ba bɛɛ yisi ba o tuonnɛ.

english_verse: Hazael died, and his son Benhadad then became king of Syria.
translation_verse: Aram Na'ab Hazael da kpiya ka Ben-Hadad onɛ an o biig la lɛdigi di na'am la.

english_verse: King Jehoash of Israel attacked and defeated the Syrian army three times. He took back from Benhadad all the towns Hazael had captured in battle from his father Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Ka Jehoahas biig Jehoas lɛn lɛb tembanɛ ka Hazael da nyaŋ o saam Jehoahas zaba ni ka di'e la faaɛn yi Hazael biig Ben-Hadad san'an. Nɔɔr atan' ka Jehoas nyaŋ o, ka faaɛn tɛɛns la wʋsa lɛbis.

english_verse: Jeroboam extended the boundaries of Israel from Lebo-Hamath in the north to the Dead Sea in the south, just as the Lord had promised his servant Jonah son of Amittai, who was a prophet from Gath-Hepher.
translation_verse: O da nyaŋi lɛn di'e Israel titɔndis lin yi Lebo-Hamat ti paae Atɛuk linɛ bɛ Araba la, nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb Israel Wina'am la da pʋn dɛŋi yɛl si'em la. O da pian' yii o tʋmtʋm Jona san'an, onɛ an Amitai biig, ka an nɔdi'es onɛ yi Gaf Hefe teŋin la.

english_verse: Amaziah son of Joash became king of Judah in the second year of Jehoash's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Jehoahas biig Jehoas n da di Israel na'am yʋma ayi' nya'aŋ la ni, Joas biig Amazaya mɛ da di Juda na'am mɛn.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon hali, ka pʋ siaki fɛndig ka bas Nebat biig Jeroboam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka o da kɛ ka Israel dim tʋm la.

english_verse: Jeroboam died and was buried, and his son Zechariah became king.
translation_verse: Jeroboam da maal ka'alim, ka ba mum o ban mum Israel na'anam zin'isi'a la.

english_verse: Amaziah followed the example of his father Joash by obeying the Lord and doing right. But he was not as faithful as his ancestor David.
translation_verse: O da tʋm linɛ an sʋm Zugsɔb la san'an, amaa ka' wʋʋ o yaab David n da tʋm si'em la. Si'el wʋsa ni o da dɔlisid nɛ o saam Joas nɔba,

english_verse: Amaziah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: amaa o da pʋ yis teŋgbana banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna zut la, ka nidib la kpɛm maan maana nyu'od bʋnnyubisa ani.

english_verse: As soon as Amaziah had control of Judah, he arrested and killed the officers who had murdered his father.
translation_verse: Amazaya yʋ'ʋn da baŋ ye sʋ'ʋlim la bɛ nɛ o nu'ugin kiŋ-kiŋ la, o da kʋ kpɛɛm banɛ da kʋʋ o saam onɛ da an na'ab la

english_verse: But the children of those officers were not killed. The Lord had commanded in the Law of Moses that only the people who sinned were to be punished, not their parents or children.
translation_verse: ka lɛɛ pʋ kʋʋ ba biisɛ. On da niŋ si'em la da dɔlnɛ linɛ ka Zugsɔb da kɛ ka Moses sɔb zi'ela gbana la ni ye, “Ba kʋ kʋ sɔ' o biig yɛla bɛɛ ba kʋ sɔ' o ba' yɛla la. Sɔ' wʋsa ye o kpinɛ o mɛŋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yɛla.”

english_verse: Amaziah, you think you're so powerful because you defeated Edom. Go ahead and celebrate—but stay at home. If you cause any trouble, both you and your kingdom of Judah will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Fʋ sid nyaŋ Edom ka yʋ'ʋn mɔr tita'alim. Mɔr sumalisim fʋn nyaŋ la, amaa bɛɛ fʋ yin baanlimm. Bɔ ka fʋ ieed yɛla ye fʋ lugi fʋ mɛŋi kpanb nɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa?”

english_verse: One day, Amaziah sent a message to King Jehoash of Israel: “Come out and face me in battle!”
translation_verse: Amazaya da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ Jehoas onɛ an Jehoahas biig ka an Jehu yaaŋ onɛ an Israel Na'ab la san'an yɛl o ye, “Kem na ka man nɛ fʋ kpa' taaba.”

english_verse: Jehoash sent back this reply: Once upon a time, a small thornbush in Lebanon announced that his son was going to marry the daughter of a large cedar tree. But a wild animal came along and trampled the small bush.
translation_verse: Amaa Israel Na'ab Jehoas da lɛbisi yɛl Juda Na'ab Amazaya ye, “Tituugi da bɛ Lebanon teŋin tʋm yɛl na'aziinr ye, ‘Nɔkimi fʋ bipuŋ la tisim ka m tisim biig ka o di.’ Ka Lebanon sian'anrin bʋnkɔnbʋg kena nɔ tituug la mɛdig.

english_verse: But Amaziah refused to listen. So Jehoash and his troops marched to the town of Beth-Shemesh in Judah to attack Amaziah and his troops.
translation_verse: Amazaya da pʋ kɛlisɛ, alazug Israel Na'ab Jehoas da tʋ'ʋs o nɛ zaba. On nɛ Amazaya onɛ an Juda Na'ab la da tʋ'ʋs taab Befisemes teŋin linɛ bɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: During the battle, Judah's army was crushed. Every soldier from Judah ran back home,
translation_verse: Israel da nyaŋ Juda dim ka sɔ' wʋsa zɔɔ kul o yin.

english_verse: He took the gold and silver, as well as everything of value from the Lord's temple and the king's treasury. He took hostages, then returned to Samaria.
translation_verse: O da vaae sanlima nɛ anzurifa nɛ laas banɛ bɛ Zugsɔb la Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la wʋsa nɛ na'ayir la la'ad la wʋsa. O mɛ da gban'e nidibi mɔri lɛb Samaria.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoash did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he defeated King Amaziah of Judah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Jehoas na'am diib saŋa la, on da tʋm si'el nɛ on da nyaŋi maal si'el la, nɛ on zab nɛ Amazaya, Juda Na'ab la si'em la, ba da sɔbi li kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: After his death the people of Judah made his son Azariah king, even though he was only
translation_verse: Ka Juda nidib la'as taaba diis Azaria na'am ka o nan an yʋma pii nɛ ayuobʋ. Ka o di'e o saam Amazaya zin'ig.

english_verse: Azariah was the one who later recaptured and rebuilt the town of Elath. King Jeroboam the Second of Israel
translation_verse: Onɛ da maligim mɛ' Elaf teŋ zaŋguoma lɛbis teŋ la tis Juda, o saam Amazaya kum nya'aŋ. Israel na'ab Jeroboam onɛ paas ayi' la yɛl

english_verse: Jeroboam son of Jehoash became king of Israel in the fifteenth year of Amaziah's rule in Judah. Jeroboam ruled
translation_verse: Amazaya onɛ an Joas biig la di Juda na'am la li yʋʋm pii nɛ anu saŋa, ka Jehoas biig Jeroboam da di Israel na'am Samaria tempʋʋgin ka kpɛn zin' na'am gbauŋ la zug yʋma pisnaasi nɛ yinne.

english_verse: The Lord helped Jeroboam do this because he had seen how terribly the Israelites were suffering, whether slave or free, and no one was left to help them.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da nyɛ Israel dimi da di namisʋg si'em. Ba sɔ' wʋsa da namisidnɛ, ka sɔ' kae na nyaŋi sʋŋi ba.

english_verse: And since the Lord had promised that he would not let Israel be completely destroyed, he helped Jeroboam rescue them.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la da pʋn gban'e ye o kʋ kpiis Israel yʋ'ʋr dunia nwa' la zug, o da dɔlis nɛ Jehoas biig Jeroboam nii faaɛn ba.

english_verse: Everything else Jeroboam did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he recaptured the towns of Damascus and Hamath, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yɛla banɛ da maal Jeroboam na'am diib saŋa la, on da tʋm si'el nɛ on da nyaŋi maal si'el la, nɛ on da zabi nyaŋ si'em, nɛ on da nyaŋi faaɛn Damaskus nɛ Hamat tɛɛns linɛ da an Juda dim sʋ'ʋlimin la lɛbisi tis Israel si'em la, ba da sɔbi li kpɛn'ɛs Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Everything else Pekahiah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Pekah of Israel
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Pekahaya na'am saŋa nɛ on da tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi niŋ Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la. Peka di Israel na'am la yɛla

english_verse: Pekahiah became king of Israel in the fiftieth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, and he ruled two years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Azaria da dii o na'am la li yʋma pisnu saŋa ka Menahem biig Pekahaya di Israel na'am Samaria tempʋʋgin ka zin'in na'am gbauŋ la zug yʋma ayi'.

english_verse: Azariah obeyed the Lord by doing right, as his father Amaziah had done.
translation_verse: O da tʋm linɛ an sʋm Zugsɔb la tuon nwɛnɛ o saam Amazaya da tʋm si'em la.

english_verse: But Azariah did not destroy the local shrines, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amaa o da pʋ yis teŋgbana banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna la zut la, ka nidib la kpɛm maan maana nyu'od bʋnnyubisa ani.

english_verse: The Lord punished Azariah with leprosy for the rest of his life. He wasn't allowed to live in the royal palace, so his son Jotham lived there and ruled in his place.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da kɛ ka kʋkɔm ban'as gban'e Na'ab la, hali ka o ti kpi. O da bɛ nɛ o yiri o kɔn'. Na'ab la biig Jotam da lieb gbandaani bɛ na'ayin la ka gɔt nimbanɛ bɛ teŋin la.

english_verse: Everything else Azariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Azaria na'am saŋa, nɛ on da tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi niŋ Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Azariah died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Jotham then became king. King Zechariah of Israel
translation_verse: Azaria da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o David tempʋʋgin. Ka o biig Jotam da lɛdigi di na'am la. Sallum n da di Israel na'am si'em

english_verse: Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's rule in Judah, but he ruled only six months from Samaria.
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Azaria da dii o na'am la li yʋʋm pistan' nɛ anii ka Jeroboam biig Zakaria mɛ da di Israel na'am Samaria tempʋʋgin, o da zin'in na'am gbauŋ la zug nɛ nwadis ayuobʋ.

english_verse: Shallum son of Jabesh plotted against Zechariah and killed him in public. Shallum then became king.
translation_verse: Jabis biig Sallum da su'a gban'e bɛ'ɛd Zakaria yɛla. O da gban'e o nidib la tuonnɛ kʋʋ o ka di'e na'am la di.

english_verse: So the Lord had kept his promise to Jehu that the next four kings of Israel would come from his family. Everything else Zechariah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Shallum of Israel
translation_verse: Alazug, Zugsɔb la da pian' si'em tis Jehu la da lieb amɛŋa ye, “Fʋ yaas na zin'in na'am gbauŋ la zugʋ ti paae yaan-naas.”

english_verse: Shallum became king of Israel in the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's rule in Judah. But only one month after Shallum became king,
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Uzia da dii o na'am la yʋʋm pistan' nɛ awai saŋa la ka Jabis biig Sallum di Israel na'am mɛn. O da zin' na'am gbauŋ la zug Samaria tempʋʋgin nwadig yinne.

english_verse: Menahem became king of Israel in Azariah's thirty-ninth year as king of Judah, and he ruled Israel ten years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Juda Na'ab Azaria na'am da paae yʋma pistan' nɛ awai la, Gadi biig Menahem da di Israel na'am Samaria tempʋʋgin ka da zin'in na'am gbauŋ la zug yʋʋm piiga.

english_verse: He constantly disobeyed the Lord by following the example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon. O na'am saŋa la wʋsa o da pʋ bas Nebat biig Jeroboam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka o da kɛ ka Israel dim mɛ tʋm la.

english_verse: During Menahem's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria invaded Israel. He agreed to help Menahem keep control of his kingdom, if Menahem would pay him over
translation_verse: Asiria Na'akanɛ buon Pul la da nyaŋ teŋ la di'e, ka Menahem tis o anzurifa tusir ye o sʋŋ o ka li kɛ ka o nyaŋi mɔr o sʋ'ʋlim la.

english_verse: Jotham followed the example of his father by obeying the Lord and doing right.
translation_verse: O da tʋm linɛ tig Zugsɔb la nini nwɛnɛ o saam Uzia da tʋm si'em la.

english_verse: Everything else Menahem did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Menahem na'am saŋa nɛ on da tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi niŋ Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and caused the Israelites to sin, just as Jeroboam son of Nebat had done.
translation_verse: Pekahaya da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon. O da pʋ bas Nebat biig Jeroboam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka o da kɛ ka Israel dim tʋm la.

english_verse: He disobeyed the Lord and followed the evil example of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: O da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon. O da pʋ bas Nebat biig Jeroboam tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka o da kɛ ka Israel dim tʋm la.

english_verse: During Pekah's rule, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria marched into Israel. He captured the territories of Gilead and Galilee, including the towns of Ijon, Abel-Bethmaacah, Janoah, Kedesh, and Hazor, as well as the entire territory of Naphtali. Then he took Israelites from those regions to Assyria as prisoners.
translation_verse: Israel Na'ab Peka zʋmaʋŋ la, Asiria Na'ab Tigilaf-Pilesa da kena gban'e Iyon nɛ Abɛl-Bet-Maaka nɛ Yanoa nɛ Kedes nɛ Hazo. O da nyaŋ Gilead nɛ Galile pɛ'ɛs nɛ Naftali sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa vaae nidib la mɔri lɛb Asiria.

english_verse: In the twentieth year of Jotham's rule in Judah, Hoshea son of Elah plotted against Pekah and murdered him. Hoshea then became king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ka Ela biig Hosea da gban'e bɛ'ɛd Remalaya biig Peka yɛla. O da zab nɛ o ka kʋʋ o ka di'e na'am la di. Saŋkan la ka Uzia biig Jotam na'am la da paae yʋʋm pisi la.

english_verse: Everything else Pekah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Jotham of Judah (
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Peka na'am saŋa nɛ on da tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi niŋ Israel Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la. Jotam di Juda na'am la yɛla (

english_verse: Jotham son of Azariah became king of Judah in the second year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Remalaya biig Peka da di Israel na'am la, li yʋma ayi' saŋa ka Uzia biig Jotam mɛ da di Juda na'am.

english_verse: It was Jotham who rebuilt the Upper Gate that led into the court around the Lord's temple. But the local shrines were not destroyed, and they were still used as places for offering sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amaa o da pʋ yis teŋgbana banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna la zut la, ka nidib la kpɛm maan maana nyu'od bʋnnyubisa ani. Jotam da maligim mɛ yaŋir linɛ bɛ zugin ka bɛ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsʋg Zin'igin la.

english_verse: Everything else Jotham did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Jotam na'am saŋa nɛ on da tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi niŋ Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: During his rule, the Lord let King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel start attacking Judah.
translation_verse: Dabisban la Zugsɔb la da dɛŋi tʋm Aram Na'ab Rezin nɛ Remalaya biig Peka ye ba zab nɛ Juda.

english_verse: Jotham died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Ahaz became king.
translation_verse: Jotam da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o, o yaanam yaadin, David tempʋʋgin. Ka o biig Ahaz lɛdigi di na'am la.

english_verse: Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah in the seventeenth year of Pekah's rule in Israel.
translation_verse: Remalaya biig Peka da di na'am yʋma pii nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni ka Jotam biig Ahaz da di Israel na'am.

english_verse: Ahaz died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem, and his son Hezekiah became king.
translation_verse: Ahaz da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o kpi'el nɛ o yaanam, David tempʋʋgin. Ka o biig Hezekia lɛdigi di na'am la.

english_verse: and was even more sinful than the kings of Israel. He sacrificed his own son, which was a disgusting custom of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel.
translation_verse: O da dɔlnɛ suobanɛ ka Israel na'anam da dɔl la, hali ka nɔk o biigi maal maannɛ nyu'oe bugum. Tʋʋmkisa bama zug ka Zugsɔb la da yis kʋdimin dim ka nɔk teŋ la tis Israel dim la.

english_verse: Ahaz offered sacrifices at the local shrines, as well as on every hill and in the shade of large trees.
translation_verse: Ahaz da maan maana ka nyu'od bʋnnyubisa maana zin'isin nɛ kʋkʋna zug nɛ tibɛda wʋsa gbinnin.

english_verse: While Ahaz was ruling Judah, the king of Edom recaptured the town of Elath from Judah and forced out the people of Judah. Edomites then moved into Elath, and they still live there. About the same time, King Rezin of Syria and King Pekah of Israel marched to Jerusalem and attacked, but they could not capture it.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Aram Na'ab Rezin da nyaŋi kad Juda nidib la yis Elaf teŋin ka di'e lɛbisi tis Aram. Ka Edom dim la keŋ zin'in Elaf teŋin ti paae zina.

english_verse: Ahaz sent a message to King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria that said, “Your Majesty, King Rezin and King Pekah are attacking me, your loyal servant. Please come and rescue me.”
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahaz da tʋm ye ba yɛl Asiria Na'ab Tigilaf-Pilesa ye, “Man anɛ fʋ sankpan'as nɛ fʋ zabzabid. Kem na faanmi yis Aram nɛ Israel Na'abanɛ zabid nɛ mam la nu'usin,.”

english_verse: Along with the message, Ahaz sent silver and gold from the Lord's temple and from the palace treasury as a gift for the Assyrian king.
translation_verse: Ahaz da nɔk anzurifa nɛ sanlima linɛ bɛ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la, nɛ la'ad linɛ bɛ suak zin'igin na'ayin la, mɔri keŋ tis Asiria Na'ab la piini.

english_verse: As soon as Tiglath Pileser received the message, he and his troops marched to Syria. He captured the capital city of Damascus, then he took the people living there to the town of Kir as prisoners and killed King Rezin.
translation_verse: Asiria Na'ab la da siakya ka keŋ zab nɛ Damaskus dimi nyaŋi ba. O da gban'e teŋ la nidibi keŋ Kir ka kʋ Rezin onɛ aan ba Na'ab la.

english_verse: Later, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser. And while Ahaz was there, he saw an altar and sent a model of it back to Uriah the priest, along with the plans for building one.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahaz da keŋ Damaskus ye o pʋ'ʋs Asiria Na'ab Tigilaf-Pilesa. O da nyɛ maan bimbim Damaskus tempʋʋgin ka maki li ka kɛ ka ba keŋ pa'al Uria onɛ an maanmaan la suobanɛ ka ba na dɔlisi maali li buudi.

english_verse: Uriah followed the plans and built an altar exactly like the one in Damascus, finishing it just before Ahaz came back.
translation_verse: Alazug Uria onɛ an maanmaan la da mɛ' bimbim la wʋʋ Na'ab la maki li Damaskus si'em pa'al la. O da mɛnɛ naae ka Na'ab Ahaz nyaan lɛbi kul.

english_verse: When Ahaz returned, he went to see the altar and to offer sacrifices on it. He walked up to the altar
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yi Damaskus n lɛb na ka nyɛ maan bimbim la, o da keŋi li tuon ka maal maana li zug.

english_verse: and poured wine over it. Then he offered sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessings.
translation_verse: O da maal nyu'or maan nɛ zʋʋd maan, ka kpa'ae bʋnnuuda maan la li zug ka nɔk maan linɛ an taaba la'asʋg maan ziim la misig bimbim la.

english_verse: After that, he had the bronze altar moved aside, so his new altar would be right in front of the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Kʋntzɛn'ug maan daka kanɛ an Zugsɔb la din la da zi'enɛ bimbim paal la nɛ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsʋg Dɔɔg la teŋsʋk, ka Ahaz nɔki li lɛbisi zi'el bimbim paal la datiuŋ baba.

english_verse: He told Uriah the priest: From now on, the morning and evening sacrifices as well as all gifts of grain and wine are to be offered on this altar. The sacrifices for the people and for the king must also be offered here. Sprinkle the blood from all the sacrifices on it, but leave the bronze altar for me to use for prayer and finding out what God wants me to do.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahaz yʋ'ʋn da tis Maanmaan Uria nɔɔr ye, “Maan bimbim tita'ar paal la zug ka fʋ na maal bɛogʋn nyu'or maan nɛ zaam zʋʋd maan nɛ na'ab la nyu'or maan nɛ o zʋʋd maan nɛ nidib la wʋsa nyu'or maan nɛ ba zʋʋd maan nɛ ba bʋnnuuda maan la. Nɔkim nyu'or maan nɛ maan bama la ziim misig bimbim nwa'. Amaa kʋntzɛn'ug maan daka la na an man mɛŋ-mɛŋ din. Ani ka m na bʋgʋd ka baŋid linɛ na niŋ.”

english_verse: Ahaz also had the side panels and the small bowls taken off the movable stands in the Lord's temple. He had the large bronze bowl, called the Sea, removed from the bronze bulls on which it rested and had it placed on a stand made of stone.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahaz da nɔk tɛrekonam linɛ mɔr ku'om zi'esa li zug la ka yisi li bʋnlamma nɛ ku'om laas la. O da yis Atɛuk laa dinɛ sʋn'e kʋntzɛn'ug na'araad la zugin la digil kuga zug.

english_verse: He took down the special tent that was used for worship on the Sabbath and closed up the private entrance that the kings of Judah used for going into the temple. He did all these things to please Tiglath Pileser.
translation_verse: O da nɔk Vʋ'ʋsʋm Daar fuug linɛ ka ba da nɔki maal Pʋ'ʋsʋg Zin'igin la yis, ka yɔ' na'ayir suor linɛ kpɛn'ɛd Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la baba. O da niŋi linɛ ye li ma'ae Asiria Na'ab la sʋʋnr.

english_verse: Everything else Ahaz did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim yɛla banɛ da maal Ahaz na'am saŋa nɛ on da tʋm si'el la, ba da sɔbi niŋ Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Hoshea son of Elah became king of Israel in the twelfth year of Ahaz's rule in Judah, and he ruled nine years from Samaria.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ahaz n da di Juda na'am la yʋʋm pii nɛ ayi' la, Ela biig Hosea da di Israel na'am Samaria tempʋʋgin, ka zin'in na'am gbauŋ la zug yʋma awai.

english_verse: Hoshea disobeyed the Lord and sinned, but not as much as the earlier Israelite kings had done.
translation_verse: O da tʋm bɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon, amaa li da pʋ paae Israel na'abanɛ gaad la.

english_verse: During Hoshea's rule, King Shalmaneser of Assyria invaded Israel; he took control of the country and made Hoshea pay taxes.
translation_verse: Asiria Na'ab Salmanɛser da keŋ ye o zab nɛ Hosea, ka o da sie o mɛŋi lieb Salmanɛser tʋmtʋm ka la'asid la'adi yɔɔd o yʋʋm wʋsa.

english_verse: But later, Hoshea refused to pay the taxes and asked King So of Egypt to help him rebel. When Shalmaneser found out, he arrested Hoshea and put him in prison. Samaria Is Destroyed and the Israelites Are Taken to Assyria
translation_verse: Amaa Asiria Na'ab la da baŋ ye Hosea ka' sida sɔba, bɔzugɔ o da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ maal zuod nɛ Soo onɛ an Egipt Na'ab la, ka pʋ lɛn la'asid yʋʋm-yʋʋm yɔɔd la tisid Asiria Na'ab la ya'asɛ. Alazug Salmanɛser da gban'e o niŋ sanrega ni.

english_verse: Shalmaneser invaded Israel and attacked the city of Samaria for three years,
translation_verse: Asiria Na'ab da keŋ kpɛn' Israel teŋin la wʋsa lɔbi gilig Samaria tempʋʋgʋ digi guri li yʋma atan'.

english_verse: before capturing it in the ninth year of Hoshea's rule. The Assyrian king took the Israelites away to Assyria as prisoners. He forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Hosea na'am la yʋma awai saŋa, Asiria Na'ab la da nyaŋ Samaria ka gban'e Israel dim la mɔri keŋ Asiria teŋin. O da paae zin'ili ba nɛ Hala teŋ kanɛ kpi'e Habor kɔldaug ka bɛ Gozan sʋ'ʋlimin la nɛ Media dim tempʋʋdin la.

english_verse: All of this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God, who had rescued them from Egypt, where they had been slaves. They worshiped foreign gods,
translation_verse: Nɛ' wʋsa da niŋnɛ Israel dimi da tʋm bɛ'ɛdi tisi ba Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba Wina'am la, onɛ da yisi ba Egipt teŋin na ka faaɛn ba yi Na'ab Faaro nu'ugin la. Ba da dɔlnɛ winsieba,

english_verse: followed the customs of the nations that the Lord had forced out of Israel, and were just as sinful as the Israelite kings.
translation_verse: ka dɔl buudbanɛ ka Zugsɔb da kadi baa yis ka di'e teŋ la tisi ba la malima nɛ malimbanɛ ka Israel na'anam da pin'il la.

english_verse: Even worse, the Israelites tried to hide their sins from the Lord their God. They built their own local shrines everywhere in Israel—from small towns to large, walled cities.
translation_verse: Israel dim la da su'adi maan linɛ ka' sʋ'ʋm tisidi ba Zugsɔb Wina'am la, ka li pʋ dɔl suorɛ. Lin da yi dɔwɔk kanɛ ka ba zin' gur la, ti paae tembanɛ kpi'em la ba da mɛ' teŋgbana nɛ maana zin'isi ba tɛɛnsin la wʋsa.

english_verse: They also built stone images of foreign gods and set up sacred poles for the worship of Asherah on every hill and under every shady tree.
translation_verse: Ba da kpi'e kuga zi'el nɛ Asera dazi'eda ba' kʋkʋna wʋsa zug nɛ tibɛda wʋsa gbina ni.

english_verse: They offered sacrifices at the shrines, just as the foreign nations had done before the Lord forced them out of Israel. They did sinful things that made the Lord very angry.
translation_verse: Ba da nyu'od bʋnnyubisa maana zin'ig wʋsa nwɛnɛ nimbanɛ da bɛɛ anina tʋm si'em ka Zugsɔb la da kadi ba yis la. Ba da tʋm bɛ'ɛd hali, ka li daam Zugsɔb la ka o sʋʋnr duoe.

english_verse: Even though the Lord had commanded the Israelites not to worship idols, they did it anyway.
translation_verse: Ba da maan nɛ bada, la'an nɛ Zugsɔb la da yɛl ye, “Li pʋ nar ye ya tʋm nɛ' la.”

english_verse: So the Lord made sure that every prophet warned Israel and Judah with these words: “I, the Lord, command you to stop doing sinful things and start obeying my laws and teachings! I gave them to your ancestors, and I told my servants the prophets to repeat them to you.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb da pʋn kɛ ka o nɔdi'esidib nɛ banɛ nyɛt la sa'al Israel nɛ Juda dim ye, “Fɛndigimi ka basi ya suobɛ'ɛd la, ka dɔllini m nɔzi'ela nɛ m gban'ar la, ka li dɔl nɛ wadbanɛ ka m yammis banɛ aan m nɔdi'esidib la da tu'asi tisi ya yaanam la wʋsa.”

english_verse: But the Israelites would not listen; they were as stubborn as their ancestors who had refused to worship the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Amaa ba kʋ kɛlisɛ ka ba zug mɛ kpi'em wʋʋ ba yaanam banɛ da pʋ niŋi ba Zugsɔb Wina'am yadda la.

english_verse: They ignored the Lord's warnings and commands, and they rejected the solemn agreement he had made with their ancestors. They worshiped worthless idols and became worthless themselves. The Lord had told the Israelites not to do the things that the foreign nations around them were doing, but Israel became just like them.
translation_verse: Ba da zan'as o gban'ar nɛ o nɔnaar linɛ ka o naal nɛ ba yaanam nɛ nimmua sa'al banɛ ka o da tisi ba la. Ba da dɔl ba'ayɔɔd hali ti kɛ ka ba mɛŋ lieb ninyɔɔd. Ba da tu'as ninsieba banɛ da bɛ tembanɛ da giligi ba la, la'an nɛ Zugsɔb la da pʋn yɛli ba ye ba da tʋm wʋʋ temban nidibi tʋm si'em la. La'an nɛ wala, ba da tʋm wʋʋ nimbama tʋm bɛ'ɛd si'em la.

english_verse: The people of Israel disobeyed all the commands of the Lord their God. They made two gold statues of calves and set up a sacred pole for Asherah; they also worshiped the stars and the god Baal.
translation_verse: Ba da zan'as Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba Wina'am zi'ela la wʋsa ka ya'abi ba mɛŋ bada ayi' wʋʋ na'apɔla ka mɛ maal Asera dazi'eda. Ba da igini zun'od nwadbibis wʋsa ka wɔ'ɔgid Baal.

english_verse: They used magic and witchcraft and even sacrificed their own children. The Israelites were determined to do whatever the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Ba da kɔtidnɛ ba biribis nɛ bipumisi maan maana nyu'od bugum. Ba da tʋmnɛ sɔnpʋt tʋʋma ka bʋgʋd ba'ad ka pɛsigi ba mɛŋi tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la tuon ka li daam Zugsɔb la ka o sʋnf duoe.

english_verse: The Lord became so furious with the people of Israel that he allowed them to be carried away as prisoners. Only the people living in Judah were left,
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb la sʋnf da duoe nɛ Israel dim hali, ka o yisi ba o san'an. Juda dɔɔg la ma'aa da kpɛlim.

english_verse: but they also disobeyed the Lord's commands and acted like the Israelites.
translation_verse: Hali Juda da pʋ dɔlli ba Zugsɔb Wina'am zi'ela laa. Ba da dɔlnɛ tʋʋm banɛ ka Israel dim mɔri kpɛn' ba sʋʋgin na la.

english_verse: So the Lord turned his back on everyone in Israel and let them be punished and defeated until no one was left.
translation_verse: Dinzug Zugsɔb la da zan'as Israel dim wʋsa: o da kɛ ka tɔɔg paae ba, ka basi ba niŋ banɛ na san'ami ba la nu'usin ti paae saŋkanɛ ka o yisi ba o san'an.

english_verse: Earlier, when the Lord took the northern tribes away from David's family, the people living in northern Israel chose Jeroboam son of Nebat as their king. Jeroboam caused the Israelites to sin and to stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: On da wɛlig Israel n yis David zakin la, ba da kɛ ka Nebat biig Jeroboam liebi ba Na'ab. Ka Jeroboam da kɛ ka Israel dim bas Zugsɔb la dɔllim ka tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛtita'ar.

english_verse: until the Lord got rid of them, just as he had warned his servants the prophets. That's why the people of Israel were taken away as prisoners to Assyria, and that's where they remained. Foreigners Are Resettled in Israel
translation_verse: Hali ka Zugsɔb la ti yisi ba o tuon nwɛnɛ on da sa'ali ba si'em yit o yammis banɛ aan o nɔdi'esidibin la. Dinzug ba da gban'e Israel dimi yisi ba, ba mɛŋ teŋin mɔri ba keŋ Asiria ka ba nam kpɛm bɛɛ anina. Samaria maligim zin'in si'em

english_verse: The king of Assyria took people who were living in the cities of Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath, and Sepharvaim, and forced them to move to Israel. They took over the towns where the Israelites had lived, including the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Asiria Na'ab da mɔr nidibi yi Babilon nɛ Kuta nɛ Ava nɛ Hamat nɛ Sefaavam tɛɛnsin na zin'ili ba Samaria sʋ'ʋlim tempʋʋdin ka ba lɛdig Israel dim zin'ig. Ba da sʋ'ʋg Samaria nɛ li tɛɛns wʋsa.

english_verse: At first these people did not worship the Lord, so he sent lions to attack them, and the lions killed some of them.
translation_verse: Ban da dɛŋin zin'in ani la, ba da pʋ dɔl Zugsɔb la; alazug o da kɛ ka gbigima keŋ nidib la sʋʋgin kʋʋ ba sieba.

english_verse: A messenger told the king of Assyria, “The people you moved to Israel don't know how to worship the god of that country. So he sent lions that have attacked and killed some of them.”
translation_verse: Labaar da paae Asiria Na'ab ye, “Nidib la ka fʋ lɛbisi ba na ka maligim bɔ zin'ig Samaria sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛnsin zin'ili ba la, ba zi' teŋ la teŋgban la bɔɔd si'ela. Din ka o kɛ ka gbigima keŋ ban bɛ zin'isi'a la kʋ nidib la.”

english_verse: The king replied, “Get one of the Israelite priests we brought here and send him back to Israel. He can live there and teach them about the god of that country.”
translation_verse: Li da kɛ ka Asiria Na'ab la tis nɔɔr ye, “Kɛlli ka maanmaannib banɛ ka ya gban'e yi Samaria la na yinne lɛbi zin'in ani pa'al nidib la teŋgban la bɔɔd si'el.”

english_verse: One of the Israelite priests was chosen to go back to Israel. He lived in Bethel and taught the people how to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Dinzug maanmaan yinne onɛ ka ba da gban'e o yi Samaria na la da keŋ zin'in Betel teŋin pa'an nidib la ban na dɔl Zugsɔb la si'em.

english_verse: But in towns all over Israel, the different groups of people made statues of their own gods, then they placed these idols in local Israelite shrines.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, buudi wʋsa da maali ba teŋgbana tempʋbanɛ wʋsa ka ba zin' la ni n ba' teŋgban banɛ ka Samaria dim da pʋn maan maana kʋkʋna zug la.

english_verse: The people from Babylonia made the god Succoth-Benoth; those from Cuthah made the god Nergal; those from Hamath made Ashima;
translation_verse: Babilon dim la da maal nɛ Sukof-Benof, ka banɛ yi Kuta maal Negal, ka banɛ yi Hamat la maal Asiima.

english_verse: those from Avva made Nibhaz and Tartak; and the people from Sepharvaim sacrificed their children to their own gods Adrammelech and Anammelech.
translation_verse: Ava dim da maal Nibihas nɛ Tatak, ka Sefaavam dim la kʋʋ ba biisi nyu'oe maal maana tis Adramelek nɛ Anamelek banɛ an Sefaavam teŋgbana la.

english_verse: They worshiped their own gods, just as they had before they were taken away to Israel. They also worshiped the Lord, but they chose their own people to be priests at the shrines.
translation_verse: Ba da dɔl Zugsɔb la, amaa ba mɛ da lɛn dɔlli ba mɛŋ teŋgbana nwɛnɛ tembanɛ ka ba yina la malʋŋʋ an si'em la.

english_verse: Everyone followed their old customs. None of them worshiped only the Lord, and they refused to obey the laws and commands that the Lord had given to the descendants of Jacob, the man he named Israel.
translation_verse: Din yi saŋkanɛ ti paae zina ba nam kpɛn dɔlli ba malimkʋda la. Ba pʋ dɔl Zugsɔb, bɛɛ o gban'ar nɛ o dɔlisʋg nɛ wada nɛ nɔzi'ela linɛ ka o tis Jakob onɛ ka o pʋd o, o yʋ'ʋr ye Israel la yaas la.

english_verse: At the time when the Lord had made his solemn agreement with the people of Israel, he told them: Do not worship any other gods! Do not bow down to them or offer them a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da naal nɔɔr nɛ Israel dim la O da tisi ba zi'elʋg ye, “Da wɔ'ɔgi teŋgban si'a bɛɛ igini li tuonnɛ; da siaki ba nɔɔr bɛɛ maal maannɛ tisi ba.

english_verse: Worship only me! I am the one who rescued you from Egypt with my mighty power. Bow down to me and offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb onɛ mɔri ya yi Egipt na nɛ o paŋ tita'ar nɛ o nu'ukpi'euŋ la, on ma'aa ka li an tilas ye ya dɔl. On ka ya na igin o tuon ka maal maana tis o.

english_verse: and remember the solemn agreement between us. I will say it again: Do not worship any god
translation_verse: Da tami nɔnaar linɛ ka m naal nɛ ya la, ka mɛ da dɔlli win siebaa,

english_verse: except me. I am the Lord your God, and I will rescue you from all your enemies.
translation_verse: lɛɛ dɔlli Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la, bɔzugɔ, onɛ na faaɛn ya yisi ya dataas nu'usin.”

english_verse: But the people living in Israel ignored that command and kept on following their old customs.
translation_verse: Ba da pʋ siak ye ba kɛlis baa bi'elaa, amaa ka kpɛn ken tuon nɛ ba malimkʋda la.

english_verse: They did worship the Lord, but they also worshiped their own idols. Their descendants did the same thing.
translation_verse: Tembama nidib da dɔl Zugsɔb la ka da lɛm maan teŋgbana hali ti paae zina, ba biis nɛ ba yaas nam kpɛn tʋmnɛ wʋʋ ba yaanamɛ da tʋm si'em la.

english_verse: Stop listening to Hezekiah! Pay attention to my king. Surrender to him. He will let you keep your own vineyards, fig trees, and cisterns
translation_verse: “Ayei, da kɛlisidi Hezekia pian'adɛ! Asiria Na'ab la yɛl si'eli nwa': Mɔri sumbʋgʋsʋm nɛ mam ka yisi ya mɛŋi kɛn man san'an na. Ala ka sɔ' wʋsa na dii o mɛŋ tiis wala ka nuu o mɛŋ buligin ku'om,

english_verse: Don't forget that it was the Lord who sent me here with orders to destroy your nation!
translation_verse: Linɛ lɛm paas, fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye man kenna ye m zab nɛ ya ka pʋ di'e nɔɔr Zugsɔb la san'anɛ? Zugsɔb la mɛŋi yɛlim ye m kem na zab nɛ teŋ kaŋa san'ami li.”

english_verse: Hezekiah obeyed the Lord, just as his ancestor David had done.
translation_verse: O da tʋm sʋ'ʋm hali Zugsɔb la san'an nwɛnɛ o yaab David n da tʋm sʋ'ʋm si'em la.

english_verse: He destroyed the local shrines, then tore down the images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. He also smashed the bronze snake Moses had made. The people had named it Nehushtan and had been offering sacrifices to it.
translation_verse: O da vɔn' teŋgbana zin'is la, ka nwa'a teŋgban kuga la ka kɔ' Asera dazi'eda la bas. O da kɔ'ɔsi kɔ'ɔs kʋntzɛn'ug waaf linɛ ka Moses da maal la, bɔzugɔ, hali ti paae saŋkan la Israel dim da nyu'od nɛ bʋnnyubisa tisidi li .

english_verse: Hezekiah trusted the Lord God of Israel. No other king of Judah was like Hezekiah, either before or after him.
translation_verse: Hezekia da niŋ Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yadda. Juda na'anam la wʋsa sʋʋgin sɔ' da kae nwɛnɛ o, banɛ gaad o tuon bɛɛ kpɛlim o nya'aŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: He was completely faithful to the Lord and obeyed the laws the Lord had given to Moses for the people.
translation_verse: O da gban'e Zugsɔb la nɛ kiŋ-kiŋ ka pʋ siaki bas o dɔllimm. O da dɔl zi'ela banɛ ka Zugsɔb la da tis Moses la.

english_verse: The Lord helped Hezekiah, so he was successful in everything he did. He even rebelled against the king of Assyria, refusing to be his servant.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da bɛ nɛ o; o ya'a da maal si'el wʋsa li da anɛ sʋ'ʋŋa. O da zan'as Asiria Na'ab nɔɔr ka pʋ lɛn dɔl oo.

english_verse: Hezekiah defeated the Philistine towns as far away as Gaza—from the smallest towns to the large, walled cities.
translation_verse: O da nyaŋ Filistia dim la hali ti paae Gaza teŋ nɛ ba sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa, lin yi dɔwɔk kanɛ ka ba zin' gur la, ti paae ba kpi'euŋ zin'ig la wʋsa.

english_verse: During the fourth year of Hezekiah's rule, which was the seventh year of Hoshea's rule in Israel, King Shalmaneser of Assyria led his troops to Samaria, the capital city of Israel. They attacked
translation_verse: Hezekia da di na'am yʋma anaasi saŋa la, ka Ela biig Hosea onɛ an Israel Na'ab la da pʋn zin' o na'am gbauŋ zug yʋma ayɔpɔi. Yʋʋm kan la, Asiria Na'ab Salmanɛser da keŋ nɛ nidibi lud Samaria lɔbi gilig teŋ la.

english_verse: The king of Assyria took the Israelites away as prisoners; he forced some of them to live in the town of Halah, others to live near the Habor River in the territory of Gozan, and still others to live in towns where the Median people lived.
translation_verse: Asiria Na'ab da gban'e Israel dimi mɔri lɔ'ɔŋ Asiria zin'ili ba Hala teŋ kanɛ kpi'e Habor kɔldaug ka bɛ Gozan sʋ'ʋlimin la nɛ Media dim tempʋʋdin la.

english_verse: All of that happened because the people of Israel had not obeyed the Lord their God. They rejected the solemn agreement he had made with them, and they ignored everything that the Lord's servant Moses had told them. King Sennacherib of Assyria Invades Judah (
translation_verse: Dinɛ kɛ ka nɛ'ɛŋa da niŋ la anɛ ban da pʋ siaki ba Zugsɔb Wina'am, ka zan'as o nɔnaar la zug, nɛ linɛ wʋsa ka Moses onɛ an Zugsɔb sankpan'as da tis nɔɔr la. Ba da pʋ kɛlis o nɔɔr bɛɛ tʋm on yɛl si'el la.

english_verse: for a while. Then he will come and take you away to a country just like yours, where you can plant vineyards, raise your own grain, and have plenty of olive oil and honey. Believe me, you won't starve there. Hezekiah claims the Lord will save you. But don't be fooled by him.
translation_verse: hali nɛ mam na ti kena nɔki ya keŋ teŋ kanɛ nwɛnɛ ya din la, teŋ kanɛ ka ki bɛ, ka bodobodo bɛ, nɛ tiwanna pɔɔd, nɛ teŋ kanɛ ka olif tiis bɛ, nɛ siind. Gaŋimi vʋm ka basi kum! “Da kɛlisidi Hezekia ma'adi ya ye, ‘Zugsɔb la na faaɛn ti la.’

english_verse: One of the Assyrian commanders told them: I have a message for Hezekiah from the great king of Assyria. Ask Hezekiah why he feels so sure of himself.
translation_verse: Asiria na'ayikpɛɛm yinne da yɛli ba ye, Yɛlimi Hezekia ye, Asiria Na'atita'ar la yɛl si'eli nwa': Fʋ ti'e bɔ ka lɛɛ mɔr sʋnkpi'euŋ kanɛ?

english_verse: Is Hezekiah now depending on the Lord your God? Didn't Hezekiah tear down all except one of the Lord's altars and places of worship? Didn't he tell the people of Jerusalem and Judah to worship at that one place?
translation_verse: Ka fʋ ya'a yɛl mam ye, Tinam ti'enɛ ti Zugsɔb Wina'am, ka' o maana zin'is nɛ o bimbima ka Hezekia san'am ka yɛt Juda nɛ Jerusalem dim ye, “sɛɛ ka ya pʋ'ʋs bimbim kanɛ bɛ Jerusalem tuon laa?”

english_verse: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah's rule in Judah, King Sennacherib of Assyria invaded the country and captured every walled city, except Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Hezekia na'am la da paae yʋʋm pii nɛ anaasi la, Asiria Na'ab Senakɛrib da zab nɛ Juda teŋ kpi'ema la nyaŋi gban'e ba.

english_verse: Hezekiah sent this message to Sennacherib, who was in the town of Lachish: “I know I am guilty of rebellion. But I will pay you whatever you want, if you stop your attack.” Sennacherib told Hezekiah to pay ten tons of silver and one ton of gold.
translation_verse: Alazug Juda Na'ab Hezekia da tɔlim labakaŋa tis Asiria Na'ab Lakis teŋin ye, “Man tʋm taal, dɔlli fʋ nidib la ka ya lɛb, ka m na yɔ fʋn bɔɔd ye m yɔ si'el wʋsa.” Asiria Na'ab da yɛl Juda Na'ab Hezekia ye asɛɛ ka o tis o anzurifa gbila tusa ayi' nɛ sanlimgbila kɔbiga nɛ anaasi.

english_verse: So Hezekiah collected all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.
translation_verse: Alazug Hezekia da tis o anzurifa linɛ ka ba nyɛ Zugsɔb la Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la nɛ na'ayir la'ad suak zin'ig la wʋsa.

english_verse: He even stripped the gold that he had used to cover the doors and doorposts in the temple. He gave it all to Sennacherib.
translation_verse: Saŋkaŋa Hezekia onɛ an Juda Na'ab la da la'as sanlim kanɛ ka o da nɔki bulig kʋlis nɛ kʋlis dazi'eda Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la tis Asiria Na'ab.

english_verse: The king of Assyria ordered his three highest military officers to leave Lachish and take a large army to Jerusalem. When they arrived, the officers stood on the road near the cloth makers' shops along the canal from the upper pool.
translation_verse: Asiria Na'ab da tʋm o kpɛɛmnam atan' banɛ sʋ'oe zaba yɛla la nɛ soogianam bɛdegʋ ka ba naan Lakis teŋin keŋ Jerusalem, Na'ab Hezekia san'an. Ba da paae Jerusalem keŋ zi'en ku'osuokanɛ ka ba wɛdig ka li kpɛn'ɛd bɛuŋ kanɛ bɛ zuginɛ kpi'e zin'ikanɛ ka ba maan fuudi dɛligid la.

english_verse: They called out to Hezekiah, and three of his highest officials came out to meet them. One of them was Hilkiah's son Eliakim, who was the prime minister. The other two were Shebna, assistant to the prime minister, and Joah son of Asaph, keeper of the government records.
translation_verse: Ba da tʋm buol Na'ab la; ka Hilkia biig Eliakim onɛ an na'ayikpɛɛm nɛ Siebna onɛ an gbansɔbid la, nɛ Joa onɛ saamme an Asaf ka o sɔbid yɛla digin la ka ba yii keŋ tʋ'ʋsi ba.

english_verse: Does he think he can plan and win a war with nothing but words? Who is going to help him, now that he has turned against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Fʋ ye fʋ mɔr suoya nɛ soogianam paŋ, amaa fʋ pian'adi pian'azaal. Anɔ'ɔn ka fʋ ti'e ka ki'isid man nɔɔrɛ?

english_verse: Is he depending on Egypt and its king? That's the same as leaning on a broken stick, and it will go right through his hand.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, nannanna fʋ ti'enɛ Egipt kanɛ nwɛnɛ balaari ɛɛn buak bɛɛ tuoɛn ka sɔ' ya'a zanl ka dɛlli li ka li kʋns o nu'ugʋ pu'alim o si'em la. Ala ka Egipt Na'ab Faaro aan tis onɛ wʋsa dɛllim o.

english_verse: The king of Assyria wants to make a bet with you people. He will give you
translation_verse: “Kem na! Kɛl ka fʋn nɛ m zugdaan Asiria Na'ab la di da'. M na tisif widi tusa ayi', fʋ ya'a na nyɛ banɛ na ban'a ba!

english_verse: How could you even defeat our lowest ranking officer, when you have to depend on Egypt for chariots and cavalry?
translation_verse: Fʋ ye fʋ niŋ wala nyaŋ hali baa man kpɛɛmnam la yinne, baa onɛ an biigi ba san'an la? La'an nɛ fʋn ti'e Egipt zaba widi tɛrekonam nɛ wiedban'adib la!

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said, “Sir, we don't want the people listening from the city wall to understand what you are saying. So please speak to us in Aramaic instead of Hebrew.”
translation_verse: Ka Hilkia biig Eliakim nɛ Siebna nɛ Joa da lɛbis o ye, “Naa, mɔɔm pian' tisi ti Aram buudi pian'ad bɔzugɔ ti wʋmmi li, amaa da pian'adi ti nɛ Hibiru pian'ad la ka nimbanɛ bɛ zaŋguom la zug wʋmma.”

english_verse: The Assyrian army commander answered, “My king sent me to speak to everyone, not just to you leaders. These people will soon have to eat their own body waste and drink their own urine! And so will the three of you.”
translation_verse: Amaa kpɛɛm la da lɛbis ye, “Li anɛ yanam nɛ ya zugdaan la yɛla ma'aa ka m zugdaan tʋmim ye m kenna yɛli ya pian'akaŋa ka ka' dap banɛ zin' zaŋguom zug la mɛnɛɛ? Ban nɛ yanam wʋsa na dii ya mɛŋ bina ka nu ya mɛŋ dʋ'ʋnim!”

english_verse: Then, in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he shouted in Hebrew: Listen to what the great king of Assyria says!
translation_verse: Ka o duoe zi'en ka tansi buol nɛ Hibiru pian'ad ye, “Kɛlisimini Asiria na'atita'ar la yɛl si'em!

english_verse: Don't trust him when he tells you that the Lord will protect you from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Da siaki ka Hezekia bɛlisi ya ye ya niŋim Zugsɔb la yaddaa! Bɔzugɔ o yɛti ya ye, ‘Zugsɔb la sid na nyaŋi faaɛn ti, tempʋkaŋa kʋ nyaŋi kpɛn' Asiria dim Na'ab la nu'uginɛ.’

english_verse: Were any other gods able to defend their land against the king of Assyria?
translation_verse: Teŋgban si'a nam mi' faaɛn o teŋ man Asiria Na'ab nu'uginɛɛ?

english_verse: What happened to the gods of Hamath and Arpad? What about the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Were the gods of Samaria able to protect their land against the Assyrian forces?
translation_verse: Hamat nɛ Apad teŋgbana la bɛ yaanɛ? Sefaavam nɛ Hena nɛ Iva teŋgbana la bɛ yaanɛ? Ba nyaŋi faaɛn Samaria yisi m nu'uginɛɛ?

english_verse: None of these gods kept their people safe from the king of Assyria. Do you think the Lord your God can do any better?
translation_verse: Tembama teŋgbana la wʋsa sʋʋgin, teŋgban kanɛ nyaŋi faaɛn o teŋi yi man nu'uginɛ? Zugsɔb la ye o niŋ wala faaɛn Jerusalem yi man nu'uginɛ?”

english_verse: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah had been warned by King Hezekiah not to answer the Assyrian commander. So they tore their clothes in sorrow and reported to Hezekiah everything the commander had said.
translation_verse: Ka Hilkia biig Eliakim onɛ an na'ayikpɛɛm nɛ Siebna onɛ an gbansɔbid nɛ Joa onɛ saamme an Asaf onɛ sɔbid yɛla digin la, yɛ fu-aanlima keŋ Hezekia san'an yɛl o Asiria na'ayikpɛɛm la yɛl si'em.

english_verse: One day he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, when his sons, Adrammelech and Sharezer, killed him with their swords. They escaped to the land of Ararat, and his son Esarhaddon became king.
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka o bɛɛ o teŋgban kanɛ buon Nisirok la dɔɔgin maan malʋŋ ka o biis Adiramelek nɛ Siareza ki'e o nɛ sʋ'ʋgʋ kʋ ka zɔɔ keŋ Ararat teŋin. Ka Esaraddon onɛ aan o biig la di na'am.

english_verse: As soon as Hezekiah heard the news, he tore off his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he went into the temple of the Lord.
translation_verse: Na'ab Hezekia da wʋm ala la, o da aans o fuud ka yɛ bɔto fuugʋ keŋ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin.

english_verse: The kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah have all disappeared. Hezekiah Prays (Isaiah
translation_verse: Hamat Na'ab la bɛɛ Apad Na'ab bɛɛ na'ab onɛ an Sefaavam tempʋʋg Na'ab la bɛɛ banɛ an Hena bɛɛ Iva Na'anam la bɛ yaanɛ?”

english_verse: He told Prime Minister Eliakim, Assistant Prime Minister Shebna, and the senior priests to dress in sackcloth and tell the prophet Isaiah:
translation_verse: O da tʋm Eliakim onɛ an na'ayikpɛɛm la nɛ Siebna onɛ an gbansɔbid la nɛ maanmaannib kpɛɛmnam la ka ba wʋsa yɛ bɔto fuudi keŋ nɔdi'es Azaya onɛ an Amoz biig la san'an.

english_verse: These are difficult and disgraceful times. Our nation is like a woman too weak to give birth, when it's time for her baby to be born.
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl o ye, “Na'ab Hezekia yɛl si'eli nwa': zina anɛ tɔɔg nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ nɛ nyan dabisir, nwɛnɛ pu'a na sa'ae ka biig zug tʋm na ka paŋ lɛn kae na uns ka o yina la.

english_verse: Please pray for those of us who are left alive. The king of Assyria sent his army commander to insult the living God. Perhaps the Lord heard what he said and will do something, if you will pray.
translation_verse: Daasi'erɛɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la wʋm Asiria na'ayikpɛɛm onɛ ka o zugdaan Asiria Na'ab tʋm ye o tʋ' Wina'am Kanɛ Vʋe la pian' si'em; ka na zɛrig o zaŋi ken pian'akanɛ ka Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am wʋm la. Alazugɔ sɔsim Wina'am tis banɛ kpɛlim bi'ela ka nan vʋe la!”

english_verse: When these leaders went to Isaiah,
translation_verse: Na'ab Hezekia kpi'emnam la da kɛn Azaya san'an na la,

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had this message for Hezekiah: I am the Lord. Don't worry about the insulting things that have been said about me by these messengers from the king of Assyria.
translation_verse: Azaya da yɛli ba ye, “Yɛlimini ya zugdaan la ye, ‘Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': Da zɔti dabiem nɛ yanamɛ wʋm pian'abanɛ ka Asiria na'ab biis la kena pian' pɔ'ɔg man la zugɔ.

english_verse: I will upset him with rumors about what's happening in his own country. He will go back, and there I will make him die a violent death.
translation_verse: Kɛlisimi! M na fɛndig o ya'am ka o ya'a wʋm labasi'a o na lɛb o mɛŋ teŋin, ani ka m na kɛ ka ba ki'e o nɛ sʋ'ʋgʋ kʋ.’”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the commander of the Assyrian forces heard that his king had left the town of Lachish and was now attacking Libnah. So he went there.
translation_verse: Asiria kpɛɛm la da wʋm ye Asiria Na'ab yi Lakis la, o da yii keŋ nyɛ ka Na'ab la zabid nɛ Libna teŋ dim.

english_verse: About this same time the king of Assyria learned that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was on his way to attack him. Then the king of Assyria sent some messengers with this note for Hezekiah:
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Senakɛrib da wʋm labaar ye Tirhaka onɛ an Kus Na'ab la yit ye o zab nɛ o la, o da lɛn tɔlim labaari yɛl Hezekia ye,

english_verse: Don't trust your God or be fooled by his promise to defend Jerusalem against me.
translation_verse: “Yɛlim Hezekia onɛ an Juda Na'ab la ye, da kɛ ka teŋgban kanɛ ka fʋ dɛl la ma'af ye, ‘Ba kʋ nyaŋi di'e Jerusalem tis Asiria Na'ab laa.’

english_verse: You have heard how we Assyrian kings have completely wiped out other nations. What makes you feel so safe?
translation_verse: Gɔsima, fʋ mɛŋ pʋn wʋm Asiria Na'abi tʋm si'el tembama la ni; o san'ami ba nyain-nyain. Ka fʋn tɛn'ɛs ka fʋ na paam faangirɛɛ?

english_verse: The Assyrian kings before me destroyed the towns of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and everyone from Eden who lived in Telassar. What good did their gods do them?
translation_verse: Tembanɛ ka m yaanam da zabi nyaŋi san'am la teŋgbana da nyaŋi faaɛn baa? Tembanɛ an: Gozan nɛ Haran nɛ Rezef teŋgbana la nɛ Eden nimbanɛ da bɛ Telasa la. Ba teŋgban baa yinne da pʋ nyaŋi faaɛn baa!

english_verse: After Hezekiah had read the note from the king of Assyria, he took it to the temple and spread it out for the Lord to see.
translation_verse: Hezekia da di'e gbauŋ la ban tʋm sieba o san'an na la nu'ugin karim. Ka duoe keŋ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yinnɛ fuoe gbauŋ la digil Zugsɔb la tuon,

english_verse: Isaiah went to Hezekiah and told him that the Lord God of Israel had said: Hezekiah, I heard your prayer about King Sennacherib of Assyria.
translation_verse: Azaya onɛ an Amoz biig la da tɔlim labaari tis Na'ab Hezekia ye, “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, ‘Mam wʋmi fʋ sɔsʋg Asiria Na'ab Senakɛrib yɛla.’

english_verse: He prayed: Lord God of Israel, your throne is above the winged creatures. You created the heavens and the earth, and you alone rule the kingdoms of this world.
translation_verse: ka sɔs Zugsɔb la ye, “M Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am, fʋnɛ zin' Kerubnam teŋsʋk. Fʋn ma'aa an Wina'am sʋ'oe sʋ'ʋlim banɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa. Fʋnɛ maal agɔl nɛ teŋ.

english_verse: It is true, our Lord, that Assyrian kings have turned nations into deserts.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, li anɛ sida ye Asiria na'anam san'am tembama nɛ li teŋgbana wʋsa.

english_verse: They destroyed the idols of wood and stone that the people of those nations had made and worshiped.
translation_verse: Ba nɔki ba bada la wʋsa lɔb bugumini san'ami ba. Bɔzugɔ ba daa ka' winaa, amaa daad nɛ kuga linɛ ka nidib maali kpi'a nɛ ba nu'us la.

english_verse: But you are our Lord and our God! We ask you to keep us safe from the Assyrian king. Then everyone in every kingdom on earth will know that you are the only God. The Lord's Answer to Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: M Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am, faanmi ti yii o nu'ugin, ka sʋ'ʋlim linɛ bɛ dunia kaŋa wʋsa baŋ ye fʋn ma'aa an Wina'am, m Zugsɔba.” Azaya da tu'as Senakɛrib luus yɛla (Aza

english_verse: Now this is what I say to that king: The people of Jerusalem hate and make fun of you; they laugh behind your back.
translation_verse: Pian'akanɛ ka Zugsɔb la pian' zɛrig o nwa': “‘Zion pu'asadir onɛ nan zi' dau nɛ'ɛsif ka la'adif. Jerusalem pu'ayua lɔbid o zugʋ fʋ zɔɔg la yɛla.

english_verse: That same night the Lord sent an angel to the camp of the Assyrians, and he killed
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la Zugsɔb maliak da keŋ kʋ dap tusa kɔbiga nɛ pisnii nɛ anu Asiria dim la'asʋgʋn la. Bɛog da nie ya, ka nidib la duoe nyɛ nidibi kpii digi dig.

english_verse: Sennacherib, you cursed, shouted, and sneered at me, the holy God of Israel.
translation_verse: Anɔ'ɔn ka fʋ tʋ'ʋd ka nɛ'ɛsida? Anɔ'ɔn ka fʋ tansid nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ka midigid nini nɛ nyɛɛsim? Ka'anɛ Israel Dim Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi laa?

english_verse: You let your officials insult me, the Lord. And this is how you bragged about yourself: “I led my chariots to the highest heights of Lebanon's mountains. I went deep into its forest, cutting down the best cedar and cypress trees.
translation_verse: Fʋ bas nɛ banɛ ziidi fʋ labaya ken la na nɔɔr ye ba kena tʋ' Zugsɔb la bam bɔɔd si'em. Ka yɛl ye, “Mam mɔr zaba tɛrekonam bɛdegʋ la zug ka m nyaŋi dʋ zuor zug zin'ikanɛ dʋʋ gaad zin'is wʋsa Lebanon teŋin. Man nwa' na'aziinr tiwa'a la wʋsa digil teŋin nɛ tibanɛ ka li daad wa'am la. Man keŋi paae teŋ la nɛ sian'anr la bɛn.”

english_verse: I dried up every stream in the land of Egypt, and I drank water from wells I had dug.”
translation_verse: Ka ye, “Man tu bulis teŋ zʋna ni ka nuu li ku'om, Ka mam mɛŋ nɔbpansimpana ka m nɔki kɛ ka Egipt ku'osuoya kpiɛn.”

english_verse: Sennacherib, now listen to me, the Lord. I planned all this long ago. And you don't even realize that I alone am the one who decided that you would do these things. I let you make ruins of fortified cities.
translation_verse: Fʋ pʋ wʋm ye kʋdimin sa ka m gban'e lii? Ɛɛn, yʋʋm pʋkʋdʋgin sa ka mam da pʋn gban'e li yɛla! Nannanna ka m yʋ'ʋn kɛ ka li maal. Ka fʋ nɔk tɛɛns banɛ da mɔr kpi'euŋ la ka kɛ ka li lieb zin'ikanɛ ka kuga dig kuda-kuda.

english_verse: Their people became weak, terribly confused. They were like wild flowers or tender young grass growing on a flat roof, scorched before it matures.
translation_verse: Ba nimbanɛ paŋi naae la lidig nɛ ka di nyan. Ba nwɛnɛ bʋmbʋta linɛ nam bun pɔɔgin ka nwɛnɛ mɔbiili linɛ nan tansid. Ka lɛn nwɛnɛ mɔɔdi naanɛ tansid mɔpil zug, ka nintaŋ tʋʋlʋg nyaŋi ba ka ba pʋ nyaŋi nɔbigɛ.

english_verse: I know all about you, even how fiercely angry you are with me.
translation_verse: Amaa mam mi' fʋn bɛ zin'isi'a, nɛ fʋn ken ka lɛbid suosi'a; nɛ fʋn kis man si'em la.

english_verse: I have seen your pride and the tremendous hatred you have for me. Now I will put a hook in your nose, a bit in your mouth, then I will send you back to where you came from.
translation_verse: Fʋn kisim si'em la, nɛ fʋ tʋ'ʋd la kpɛn' m tʋba ni, alazug, m na nɔki m gu'a la ga' fʋ nyɔnya, ka li'a fʋ nɔɔr nɛ salibir, ka kɛ ka fʋ lɛb wʋʋ fʋn kɛn si'em la na.’

english_verse: Hezekiah, I will tell you what's going to happen. This year you will eat crops that grow on their own, and the next year you will eat whatever springs up where those crops grew. But the third year you will plant grain and vineyards, and you will eat what you harvest.
translation_verse: Na'ab Hezekia, zanbin kanɛ ka m na tisi fʋ nwa': dʋnna ya ye ya dinɛ ki linɛ yi ka sɔ' pʋ bʋdɛ. Ka yʋʋm kanɛ pɛ'ɛs ayi' la ya na di linɛ yii li mɛŋ. Amaa yʋʋm kanɛ paasida atan' la bʋdim ka bʋn. Bʋdim tiis pɔɔd ka dii li wala.

english_verse: Those who survive in Judah will be like a vine that puts down deep roots and bears fruit.
translation_verse: Linɛ paas la, nimbanɛ kpɛlim Juda dɔɔgin la na ba'a nya'a teŋin yina wal wala agɔl.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will see to it that some who live in Jerusalem will survive.
translation_verse: Jerusalem pʋʋgin nidib bi'ela na kpɛlim ka Zion zuor zug banɛ kpɛlim ka pʋ kpi la na la'as na. Zugsɔb la nyɛlʋg na kɛ ka nɛ' maal.

english_verse: I promise that the king of Assyria won't get into Jerusalem, or shoot an arrow into the city, or even surround it and prepare to attack.
translation_verse: Alazug, Zugsɔb la yɛt si'eli nwa' zaŋi ken Asiria Na'ab la yɛla ye, ‘O kʋ kpɛn' teŋ kaŋa pʋʋga, bɛɛ tɔn piim kpɛla. O kʋ nyaŋi kpɛn' ani ka zanl gbanti'edʋg bɛɛ nyaŋi mɛ' gu'ub zaŋguommi giŋi li.

english_verse: As surely as I am the Lord, he will return by the way he came and will never enter Jerusalem.
translation_verse: On dɔl suosi'a kena la o na dɔl anii lɛb, o kʋ kpɛn' teŋ kaŋa pʋʋginɛ.’ Zugsɔb la yɛl ala.

english_verse: I will protect it for myself and for my servant David. The Death of King Sennacherib (Isaiah
translation_verse: Ka ye ‘Man na sʋŋ teŋ kaŋa ka faaɛn li bas mam mɛŋ yɛla, nɛ David onɛ an man tʋmtʋm la yɛla.’”

english_verse: After this King Sennacherib went back to Assyria and lived in the city of Nineveh.
translation_verse: Dinzug Na'ab Senakɛrib da basi ba gu'ub zin'ig la ka duoe tɔɔm ka lɛb Ninive tempʋʋgin zin'inɛ ani.

english_verse: Hezekiah died, and his son Manasseh became king.
translation_verse: Hezekia da kpiya ka o biig Manase lɛdigi di na'am la.

english_verse: “Don't forget that I have been faithful to you, Lord. I have obeyed you with all my heart, and I do whatever you say is right.” After this, he cried bitterly.
translation_verse: “M Zugsɔba, tiɛnm man dɔllif nɛ sida si'em nɛ m sʋnf wʋsa, m pɛsigi m mɛŋ ka tʋm si'el wʋsa ka li an sʋ'ʋŋa fʋ nini ni!” Ka Hezekia kaas nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.

english_verse: Before Isaiah got to the middle court of the palace,
translation_verse: Azaya da yit zakin la, ka Zugsɔb lɛm pian' tis o ye,

english_verse: the Lord sent him back to Hezekiah with this message: Hezekiah, you are the ruler of my people, and I am the Lord God, who was worshiped by your ancestor David. I heard you pray, and I saw you cry. I will heal you, so that three days from now you will be able to worship in my temple.
translation_verse: “Lɛm yɛl Hezekia onɛ aan m nidib tuongat la ye, ‘Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ yaab David Wina'am la yɛl ye: m wʋmi fʋ sɔsʋg, ka mɛ nyɛɛ fʋ ninta'am; m na kɛ ka fʋ paam laafi. Daba atan' zina fʋ na keŋ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin.

english_verse: “What did you show them?” Isaiah asked. Hezekiah answered, “I showed them everything in my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ka nɔdi'es la bu'os o ye, “Ba nyɛ bɔɔ fʋ yin la?” Ka Hezekia lɛbis ye, “Ba nyɛ si'el wʋsa. Si'el pʋ kpɛlim suak dɔɔgin la ka m pʋ pa'ali baa.”

english_verse: Then Isaiah said to the king's servants, “Bring some mashed figs and place them on the king's open sore. He will then get well.”
translation_verse: Azaya da yɛl sankpan'asnam la ye ba yisim kekama kpaam suoɛn o natiŋkpi'eŋ la. Ka ba niŋ ala ka Hezekia paam laafi.

english_verse: Isaiah replied, “The Lord will prove to you that he will keep his promise. Will the shadow made by the setting sun on the stairway go forward ten steps or back ten steps?”
translation_verse: Ka Azaya lɛbis ye, “Nɛ' na an Zugsɔb la zanbinnɛ pa'anif ye Zugsɔb na maal on kaanb si'el wʋsa: ma'asim na vurigi keŋ tuon nɔba yakir piiga bɛɛ lɛb nya'aŋ nɔba yakir piigaa?”

english_verse: “It's normal for the sun to go forward,” Hezekiah answered. “But how can it go back?”
translation_verse: Hezekia da lɛbis o ye, “Li anɛ na'ana ka ma'asim vurigi keŋ tuon nɔba yakir piiga, lɛɛ kɛl ka li lɛb nya'aŋ nɔba yakir piiga!”

english_verse: Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow go back ten steps on the stairway built for King Ahaz. The Lord Is Still with Hezekiah (Isaiah
translation_verse: Ka nɔdi'es Azaya sɔs Zugsɔb la, ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka ma'asim la lɛb nya'aŋ nɔba yakir piiga wʋʋ lin da sig Ahaz ma'asim makir zin'igin si'em la. Babilon na'ab tʋm nidib na'ab Hezekia san'an (Aza

english_verse: Merodach Baladan, the son of Baladan, was now king of Babylonia. And when he learned that Hezekiah had been sick, he sent messengers with letters and a gift for him.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la Merodak-Baladan onɛ saamme an Babilon na'ab ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Baladan la da tɔlim gbana nɛ piini ye ba tis Hezekia bɔzugɔ o da wʋm o ban'as la yɛla.

english_verse: Hezekiah welcomed the messengers and showed them all the silver, the gold, the spices, and the fine oils that were in his storehouse. He even showed them where he kept his weapons. Nothing in his palace or in his entire kingdom was kept hidden from them.
translation_verse: Hezekia da di'e saam la ka pa'ali ba linɛ wʋsa bɛɛ o la'ad dɔɔgin la. Linɛ an; anzurifa nɛ sanlima nɛ tudaar nɛ kpasʋma. O zaba la'ad zin'ig nɛ la'abanɛ wʋsa bɛ la'ad suak dɔɔgin la ka o da pa'ali ba. Si'el da pʋ kpɛlim na'ayin la bɛɛ o sʋ'ʋlim la ni ka o pʋ pa'alɛ.

english_verse: Isaiah asked Hezekiah, “Where did these men come from? What did they want?” “They came all the way from Babylonia,” Hezekiah answered.
translation_verse: Azaya onɛ da an nɔdi'es la da keŋ Na'ab Hezekia san'an bu'os o ye, “Nimbanɛ kena la yɛl ye bɔ, ka ba yi yaanɛ na?” Ka Hezekia lɛbis ye, “Ba yinɛ lallisa, hali Babilon teŋin na.”

english_verse: Then Isaiah told Hezekiah: I have a message for you from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka Azaya yɛl Hezekia ye, “Tɔ'! Kɛlisim Zugsɔb la yɛl si'el:

english_verse: One day everything you and your ancestors have stored up will be taken to Babylonia. The Lord has promised that nothing will be left.
translation_verse: ‘Saŋa kenna ka la'abanɛ bɛ na'ayin nwa' wʋsa nɛ fʋ yaanamɛ da su'a la'asieba ba saŋa ti paae zina la wʋsa, ba na vaae li wʋsa lɛb Babilon teŋin ka si'el-si'el kʋ kpɛlim!’ Zugsɔb la yɛl ala.”

english_verse: Some of your own sons will be taken to Babylonia, where they will be disgraced and made to serve in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Fʋ yaas la sieba, banɛ aan fʋ mɛŋ ziim la, ba na gban'e ba mɔri keŋi zan' ba ka ba lieb Babilon Na'ab yin tʋmtʋmnib.

translation_verse: Ka Hezekia lɛbis ye, “Zugsɔb pian'akanɛ ka fʋ pian' la an sʋm!” Bɔzugɔ, o tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “sumbʋgʋsʋm ya'a sadigim bɛ man nyɔvʋr bɛllim saŋa, li ka' yɛllɛ.”

english_verse: Everything else Hezekiah did while he was king, including his brave deeds and how he made the upper pool and tunnel bring water into Jerusalem, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim bʋn linɛ maal Hezekia na'am saŋa la nɛ on nyaŋi maal si'el, nɛ on nyaŋi tu bɛuŋ ka wɛdig ku'osuori kɛ ka ku'om nyaŋi kpɛn' tempʋʋgin la na si'em la, ba sɔbi li niŋ Juda Na'anam Gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Amon disobeyed the Lord, just as his father Manasseh had done.
translation_verse: O da tʋm bɛ'ɛd bɛdegʋ Zugsɔb la tuon wʋʋ o saam Manase da tʋm si'em la.

english_verse: Now I, the Lord God of Israel, will destroy both Jerusalem and Judah! People will hear about it but won't believe it.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, ‘M ye m kɛnɛ ka san'auŋ kɛn Jerusalem nɛ Juda dim zugin na hali ka onɛ tʋbiri wʋmi li yɛla la, o niŋgbiŋ na dam.

english_verse: He rebuilt the local shrines that his father Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for the god Baal and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah, just as King Ahab of Israel had done. And he faithfully worshiped the stars in heaven.
translation_verse: O da lɛm mɛ' teŋgbana zin'ibanɛ ka o saam Hezekia da san'am bas la. O mɛ da lɛm mɛ' Baal maan bimbima la, ka zi'el daugʋ tis teŋgban Asera la nwɛnɛ Israel na'ab Ahab n da tʋm si'em la. O da iginid nwadbibis tuonnɛ wɔ'ɔgidi ba.

english_verse: In the temple, where only the Lord was supposed to be worshiped, Manasseh built altars for the worship of pagan gods
translation_verse: O da mɛ' maan bimbima Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin linɛ ka Zugsɔb yɛl ye, “Jerusalem pʋʋgin ka m na niŋi m yʋ'ʋr la.”

english_verse: and the stars. He placed these altars in both courts of the temple,
translation_verse: Pʋ'ʋsim Yir za'as ayi' la pʋʋgin wʋsa o da mɛ' nɛ bimbima tis nwadbibis la wʋsa.

english_verse: and even set up the pole for Asherah there. Manasseh practiced magic and witchcraft; he asked fortunetellers for advice and sacrificed his own son. He did many sinful things and made the Lord very angry. Years ago the Lord had told David and his son Solomon: Jerusalem is the place I prefer above all others in Israel. It belongs to me, and there I will be worshiped forever.
translation_verse: Manase da zaŋ daugʋ kpi'e maal Asera ba'ar la niŋ Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la, zin'ikanɛ ka Zugsɔb da yɛl David nɛ o biig Solomon ye, “Pʋ'ʋsim Yikaŋa pʋʋg, nɛ Jerusalem tempʋʋg linɛ ka man gaŋi yi Israel buudi tɛɛns wʋsa ni la, ka m na niŋi m yʋ'ʋr ani yʋma linɛ ka' bɛn la.

english_verse: If my people will faithfully obey all the commands in the Law of my servant Moses, I will never make them leave the land I gave to their ancestors.
translation_verse: Ba ya'a gu'us ka tʋmmi m nɔzi'elʋg kanɛ ka m yɛli ba ye ba tʋm la, ka dɔlli m wada linɛ ka m sankpan'as Moses da tisi ba la, m kʋ lɛn kɛ ka Israel dim yiridi yit teŋ kanɛ ka m da tisi ba yaanam la.”

english_verse: But the people of Judah disobeyed the Lord. They listened to Manasseh and did even more sinful things than the nations the Lord had wiped out.
translation_verse: Amaa nidib la da pʋ siakɛ. Manase da pan'asi ba kpɛn'ɛs mɔɔg, ka li kɛ ka ba maligim tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd hali gat buudbanɛ ka Zugsɔb da san'am ka Israel dim nyaan paae na la.

english_verse: One day the Lord said to some of his prophets:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da pʋn kɛ ka yammis banɛ an o nɔdi'esidib la yɛl

english_verse: King Manasseh has done more disgusting things than the Amorites, and he has led my people to sin by forcing them to worship his idols.
translation_verse: ye, “Juda Na'ab Manase tʋm tʋʋmkisa. O tʋm bɛ'ɛdi gaad Amor dim banɛ da gaad o tuon la, ka kɛ ka Juda dim dɔl o bada la ka tʋm bɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: Jerusalem is as sinful as Ahab and the people of Samaria were. So I will wipe out Jerusalem and be done with it, just as someone wipes water off a plate and turns it over to dry.
translation_verse: M na tiɛn linɛ ka ba mɔri makid la Jerusalem pʋʋgin nwɛnɛ man da nɔki lii mak Samaria tempʋʋg nɛ Ahab zak si'em la. M na pie Jerusalem ka pibili li wʋʋ ban ɛɛnti pie laa si'em ka liebi pibil la.

english_verse: I will even get rid of my people who survive. They will be defeated and robbed by their enemies.
translation_verse: M na zan'asi m nimbanɛ kpɛlim la, ka basi ba tisi ba dataas la ka ba faaɛn ba ka san'ami ba la'asʋma wʋsa.

english_verse: My people have done what I hate and have not stopped making me angry since their ancestors left Egypt.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ ba tʋm nɛ bɛ'ɛdi m san'an ka kɛ ka li daamim ka m sʋnf duoe, lin pin'il daakanɛ ka ba yaanam naan Egipt n yina la ti paae zina.’”

english_verse: Manasseh was guilty of causing the people of Judah to sin and disobey the Lord. He also refused to protect innocent people—he even let so many of them be killed that their blood filled the streets of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dinɛ lɛm pɛ'ɛs la, Manase da kʋ nidib bɛdegʋ banɛ pʋ tʋm taalɛ, ka ziim pɛ'ɛli pʋbid Jerusalem teŋin zin'is wʋsa, hali lin pʋ pɛ'ɛs tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka o da kɛ ka Juda dim tʋm, ka li kɛ ka ba tʋm bɛ'ɛd hali Zugsɔb tuon la.

english_verse: Everything else Manasseh did while he was king, including his terrible sins, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Ya'a kpɛlim linɛ wʋsa maal Manase na'am saŋa la, la'am pɛ'ɛs tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka o tʋm la, ba sɔbi li Juda Na'anam Gbana la ni.

english_verse: He died and was buried in Uzza Garden near his palace, and his son Amon became king. King Amon of Judah (
translation_verse: Manase da maal ka'alim ka ba mum o, o pɔkanɛ bɛ na'ayir samannin la, linɛ an Uzaa pɔɔg la. Ka o biig Ammon lɛdigi di na'am la. Ammon n di Juda na'am la yɛla (

english_verse: refused to be faithful to the Lord, the God his ancestors had worshiped.
translation_verse: Na'ab Ammon da ki'is Zugsɔb onɛ aan o yaanam Wina'am la, ka pʋ dɔl Zugsɔb la bɔɔd si'em.

english_verse: Some of Amon's officials plotted against him and killed him in his palace.
translation_verse: Ammon na'ayikpɛm la da yii o nya'aŋ ka kʋʋ o na'ayir la pʋʋg.

english_verse: While Shaphan was at the temple, Hilkiah handed him a book and said, “Look what I found here in the temple—The Book of God's Law.” Shaphan read it,
translation_verse: Hilkia onɛ an Maanmaan la da yɛl Safan onɛ an gbansɔbid la ye, “Man nyɛ wada Gbauŋ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la.” O da nɔki tis Safan ka o karimi li.

english_verse: and ask Hilkiah the high priest to collect from the guards all the money that the people have donated.
translation_verse: “Kem maanmaan kpɛɛm Hilkia san'an yɛl o ka o la'as ligidbanɛ ka ba la'asi mɔri ken Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin na la, linɛ ka banɛ gur za'anɔya la di'es nidibin la.

english_verse: Tell Hilkiah to give it to the men supervising the repairs to the temple. They can use some of the money to pay
translation_verse: Nɔkimi lii niŋ banɛ ka ba gaŋ ye ba gɔs Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la nu'usin ka kɛ ka ba yɔ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yir tʋmtʋmnib la ka ba maligim maal Yir la zin'ikanɛ san'am la wʋsa.

english_verse: the workers, and with the rest of it they can buy wood and stone for the repair work.
