english_verse: They are honest, so we won't ask them to keep track of the money.
translation_verse: Amaa li ka' tilas ye ba pa'al ban nɔk ligidi la tʋm si'em bɔzugɔ ba tʋmnɛ nɛ sida.” Hilkia da nyɛ Zugsɔb zi'elʋg gbauŋ la yɛla

english_verse: then went back to Josiah and reported, “Your officials collected the money in the temple and gave it to the men supervising the repairs.
translation_verse: Safan onɛ an gbansɔbid la da lɛb Na'ab la san'an yɛl o ye, “Naa, ti nyɛ ligidkanɛ bɛ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la, ka nɔki tis tʋmtʋmnib banɛ gɔt Pʋ'ʋsim Yir tʋʋma la.”

english_verse: But there's something else, Your Majesty. The priest Hilkiah gave me this book.” Then Shaphan read it out loud.
translation_verse: O mɛ da lɛn yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Hilkia onɛ an Maanmaan la nɔk gbauŋ la tisim.” Ka Safan karimi li Na'ab la tuon.

english_verse: When Josiah heard what was in The Book of God's Law, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da wʋm pian'abanɛ sɔb wada Gbauŋʋn la, o da aans o fuud.

english_verse: At once he called together Hilkiah, Shaphan, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Achbor son of Micaiah, and his own servant Asaiah. He said,
translation_verse: O da tis Hilkia, onɛ an Maanmaan la, nɛ Safan biig Ahikam nɛ Mikaya biig Akibo nɛ Safan onɛ an gbansɔbid la nɛ Asaya onɛ tʋmmi tisid Na'ab la nɔɔr ye,

english_verse: “The Lord must be furious with me and everyone else in Judah, because our ancestors did not obey the laws written in this book. Go find out what the Lord wants us to do.”
translation_verse: “Kem bu'osi baŋi linɛ bɛ Zugsɔb la san'an, man nɛ m nidib la nɛ Juda dim wʋsa, zaŋi keŋ linɛ sɔb gbauŋ kanɛ ka ti nyɛ la pʋʋgin. Zugsɔb la sʋnf duoe nɛ ti hali, ka li anɛ ti yaanamɛ pʋ siak pian'ad linɛ bɛ gbauŋ kaŋa ni la ka mɛ pʋ tʋm nwɛnɛ lin sɔb gbauŋ kaŋa ni ye ti tʋm si'em la zug.”

english_verse: The five men left at once and went to talk with Huldah the prophet. Her husband was Shallum, who was in charge of the king's clothes. Huldah lived in the northern part of Jerusalem, and when they met in her home,
translation_verse: Hilkia onɛ an Maanmaan la nɛ Ahikam nɛ Safan nɛ Asaya da keŋ ye ba pian' tis nɔdi'es pu'ak onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Hulda ka da an Sallum pu'a la. Sallum da anɛ onɛ gur fuud suak dɔɔg la, ka an Tikiva biig onɛ mɛ an Haras biig. O da bɛ nɛ Jerusalem teŋ yapaala la ni.

english_verse: she said: You were sent here by King Josiah, and this is what the Lord God of Israel says to him:
translation_verse: Pu'a la da yɛli ba ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa': Yɛlimi dau kanɛ tʋmi ya man san'an la na ye,

english_verse: “Josiah, I am the Lord! And I will see to it that this country and everyone living in it will be destroyed. It will happen just as this book says.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Mam ye m kɛnɛ ka tɔɔg lu teŋ kaŋa nɛ li nidib la zug, ka li dɔl wʋʋ lin sɔb gbauŋ kanɛ ka Juda Na'ab karim la.

english_verse: The people of Judah have rejected me. They have offered sacrifices to foreign gods and have worshiped their own idols. I cannot stand it any longer. I am furious.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ ba bas man, ka maan maana ka nyu'od bʋnnyubisa tisid bada banɛ ka ba maal nɛ ba nu'us la ka li kɛ ka m sʋnf duoe nɛ ba. M sʋʋnr duonɛ hali dit wʋʋ bugum nɛ, ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kpiisi lii!’”

english_verse: I noticed how sad you were when you read that this country and its people would be completely wiped out. You even tore your clothes in sorrow, and I heard you cry.
translation_verse: ‘Fʋn wʋm mam pian' pian'asi'a zɛrig teŋ kaŋa nɛ li nidib la ye, ba na paam nɔpɔɔr ka lieb zaalim ka fʋ sʋʋnr san'am ka fʋ sigisi fʋ mɛŋ si'em man Zugsɔb la san'an ka aansi fʋ fuud ka kaas man tuon la zug, m wʋmi fʋ sɔsʋg.’ Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: So I will let you die in peace, before I destroy this place.” The men left and took Huldah's answer back to Josiah.
translation_verse: Fʋ kʋ nyɛ tɔkanɛ ka m ye m kɛ ka li kɛn teŋ kaŋa ni na laa, ka fʋ na ti kpi ka ba mumif nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.” Ba da mɔr pu'a la gandig si'em la wʋsa lɛbi yɛl Na'ab la.

english_verse: Neco appointed Josiah's son Eliakim king of Judah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. He took Jehoahaz as a prisoner to Egypt, where he died.
translation_verse: Faaro Neko da diis Josia biig Eliakim o saam na'am, ka tiak Eliakim yʋ'ʋr ye Jehoyakim. Amaa o da mɔr Jehoahas n keŋ Egipt teŋin, ka o da kpii ani.

english_verse: During Josiah's rule, King Neco of Egypt led his army north to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. Josiah led his troops north to fight Neco, but when they met in battle at Megiddo, Josiah was killed.
translation_verse: Josia n da nan an Na'ab la, Egipt Na'ab Faaro Neko da keŋ Efiritis kɔldaugin ye o sʋŋi Asiria Na'ab. Na'ab Josia da yi ye o tʋ'ʋsi zab nɛ o, amaa Neko da tʋ'ʋs o kʋʋ o Megido teŋin.

english_verse: King Neco of Egypt had Jehoahaz arrested and put in prison at Riblah near Hamath. Then he forced the people of Judah to pay him
translation_verse: Faaro Neko da mɔr o keŋ Dibila linɛ bɛ Hamat teŋin lɔɔ o nɛ bana linɛ kɛ ka o kʋ nyaŋi sʋ'oe Jerusalem. Ka yʋ'ʋn muk Juda ye ba yɔ anzurifa ligidi kɔbiga nɛ sanlima yinne.

english_verse: He had the buildings torn down where the male prostitutes lived next to the temple, and where the women wove sacred robes for the idol of Asherah.
translation_verse: Josia mɛ da nwa'ae yir kanɛ ka dapgɔɔnda banɛ tʋmmi tisid teŋgbana la da bɛ ka nidib kennɛ dig nɛ ba la, yir kanɛ da kpi'e Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin, zin'ikanɛ ka pu'ab da ʋgʋd piena tisid Asera la.

english_verse: Josiah had the sacred pole for Asherah brought out of the temple and taken to Kidron Valley, where it was burned. He then had its ashes ground into dust and scattered over the public cemetery there.
translation_verse: Josia da nɔk Asera dazi'edir la yis Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la keŋ Kidron bɔn'ɔg linɛ bɛ Jerusalem yiŋ la nyu'oe li ani. O da nɛɛmi li ka li kilim zɔ'ɔm ka nɔki yugus tadimnam yaadin la.

english_verse: Those local priests could not serve at the Lord's altar in Jerusalem, but they were allowed to eat sacred bread, just like the priests from Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ba da pʋ kɛ ka maanmaannib banɛ da maan maana tisid kʋkʋna zut teŋgbana la maal maana Zugsɔb bimbim linɛ bɛ Jerusalem teŋin la, amaa ba da la'asid nɛ ba maanmaan taaba la ɔnbid bodobodo linɛ ka' dabinnɛ.

english_verse: Josiah sent some men to Hinnom Valley just outside Jerusalem with orders to make the altar there unfit for worship. That way, people could no longer use it for sacrificing their children to the god Molech.
translation_verse: O da san'am Tofet teŋgban linɛ da bɛ Ben Hinnom Biis bɔn'ɔgin la, ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn nyaŋi nɔk o biribiŋ bɛɛ bipuŋi maal maan Molek bugum la nii.

english_verse: Some of the kings of Judah, especially Manasseh, had built altars in the two courts of the temple and in the room that Ahaz had built on the palace roof. Josiah had these altars torn down and smashed to pieces, and he had the pieces thrown into Kidron Valley, just outside Jerusalem.
translation_verse: O da nwa'ae maana bimbim banɛ ka Juda Na'anam da mɛ' Ahaz dɔkanɛ bɛɛ agɔl dɔɔg la zug, nɛ bimbim banɛ ka Manase da mɛ' Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yir za'as ayi' la ni la. O da yisi ba ani nwa'asi bugusi bugus ka vaae lɔbi bas Kidron bɔn'ɔgin.

english_verse: After that, he closed down the shrines that Solomon had built east of Jerusalem and south of Spoil Hill to honor Astarte the disgusting goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Na'ab la mɛ da san'am maana zin'ig linɛ bɛ Jerusalem ya-nya'aŋ la lɛbid Zam Kʋkʋn linɛ ka Israel Na'ab Solomon da mɛɛ tis Asitoref dinɛ an teŋgban bɛ'ɛd ka an Sidon dim teŋgban la, nɛ Kemos linɛ an Moab dim teŋgban bɛ'ɛd la, nɛ Molek dinɛ an Ammon dim teŋgban kanɛ an kisʋg la.

english_verse: He tore down the stone images of foreign gods and cut down the sacred pole used in the worship of Asherah. Then he had the whole area covered with human bones.
translation_verse: Josia da nwa' ba'ar kuga la ka kɔ' Asera dazi'eda la digil teŋin, ka nɔk ninsaalib kɔnba yadigi pɛ'ɛl zin'ig la.

english_verse: But Josiah was not finished yet. At Bethel he destroyed the shrine and the altar that Jeroboam son of Nebat had built and that had caused the Israelites to sin. Josiah had the shrine and the Asherah pole burned and ground into dust.
translation_verse: Ka dinɛ lɛm paas anɛ ye, Josia da lɛn nwa' kʋkʋna zug teŋgban bimbim linɛ bɛ Betel teŋin ka Nebat biig Jeroboam da maal ka li kɛ ka Israel dim tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la. O da nyu'oe kʋkʋna zug teŋgbana la nɛ daad la nɛɛm ka li kilim zɔ'ɔm, ka kanbis Asera dazi'edir la mɛn.

english_verse: As he looked around, he saw graves on the hillside. He had the bones in them dug up and burned on the altar, so that it could no longer be used. This happened just as God's prophet had said when Jeroboam was standing at the altar, celebrating a festival. Then Josiah saw the grave of the prophet who had said this would happen
translation_verse: Na'ab Josia da gɔsi giligi nyɛ yaad banɛ da gilig kʋkʋna dɛn'ɛr la, ka kɛ ka ba yis kɔnba yaadin la nyu'oe maan daka la zugʋ san'ami li, ka li dɔl nɛ Zugsɔb labaar linɛ ka o Wina'am tʋmtʋm la da pʋn dɛŋi yɛl la.

english_verse: and he asked, “Whose grave is that?” Some people who lived nearby answered, “It belongs to the prophet from Judah who told what would happen to this altar.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os ye, “Yaʋg kugir bɔɔ nwa' ka m nyɛt la?” Ka teŋ la nidib lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Li anɛ zanbinnɛ pa'an Wina'am tʋmtʋm onɛ daa yi Juda na yɛl fʋn maal Betel maan bimbim si'em la yaʋg.”

english_verse: Josiah replied, “Then leave it alone. Don't dig up his bones.” So they did not disturb his bones or the bones of the old prophet from Israel who had also been buried there.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Basimini li baanlimm, da kɛ ka sɔ' daami lii.” Dinzug ka ba da pʋ lɛɛg on nɛ nɔdi'es onɛ da yi Samaria teŋin na la kɔnba la.

english_verse: Josiah got rid of every disgusting person and thing in Judah and Jerusalem—including magicians, fortunetellers, and idols. He did his best to obey every law written in the book that the priest Hilkiah found in the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Linɛ lɛm pɛ'ɛs la Josia da kad ba'akɔn dim nɛ sɔnpʋttib la wʋsa, nɛ bada banɛ bɛ yaan la, nɛ wina nɛ yɛlkisa banɛ wʋsa da bɛ Juda nɛ Jerusalem teŋin la. O da niŋ nɛ' ye linɛ sɔb wada gbauŋ kanɛ ka Hilkia onɛ an Maanmaan la da nyɛ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la niŋ amɛŋa.

english_verse: But the Lord was still furious with the people of Judah because Manasseh had done so many things to make him angry.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala Zugsɔb la da pʋ bas o sʋnpɛɛn linɛ ka o mɔr nɛ Juda, ka li anɛ Na'ab Manase da tʋm si'el ka o sʋnf duoe la zugɔ.

english_verse: About a month later, in Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year as king, Nebuzaradan, who was his official in charge of the guards, arrived in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nebukadnɛza onɛ an Babilon Na'ab la da di na'am la yʋma pii nɛ awai saŋa nwadig kanɛ paas anu la daba ayɔpɔi daar la, Nebuzaradan onɛ an soogianam kpɛɛm ka an na'ayikpɛɛm Babilon na'ayin la da kɛn Jerusalem na.

english_verse: Then he ordered the Babylonian soldiers to break down the walls around Jerusalem.
translation_verse: O soogianam la da la'asi nwa'a zaŋguoma la wʋsa gilig Jerusalem.

english_verse: He led away as prisoners the people left in the city, including those who had become loyal to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan onɛ an soogianam tuongat la da zi nimbanɛ kpɛlim tempʋʋgin la nɛ banɛ da nɔki ba mɛŋi niŋ Babilon Na'ab la nu'ugin la nɛ nimbanɛ kpɛlim wʋsa lɛb o teŋin.

english_verse: Only some of the poorest people were left behind to work the vineyards and the fields.
translation_verse: Amaa o da bas banɛ an nɔŋ dim hali la ye ba kpɛlim tʋm vain tiis pɔɔdin nɛ pɔɔd tʋʋma wʋsa.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers took the two bronze columns that stood in front of the temple, the ten movable bronze stands, and the large bronze bowl called the Sea. They broke them into pieces so they could take the bronze to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Babilon dim la da nwa'ae kʋntzɛn'ug buos la nɛ tɛrekonam linɛ mɔr ku'om zi'esa la nɛ latita'ar dinɛ ka ba nɔk kʋntzɛn'ugʋ maal ka li bɛ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la. Ba da zi kʋntzɛn'ug la lɛb Babilon teŋin.

english_verse: They carried off the bronze things used for worship at the temple, including the pans for hot ashes, and the shovels, snuffers, and also the dishes for incense,

translation_verse: Soogiakpɛɛm la da nɔk tudaar nyu'or dʋgid nɛ laas banɛ ka ba mɔri zu'asid ku'om ka ba nɔk sanlima nɛ anzurifa maali ba la mɔri keŋ.

english_verse: The pile of bronze from the columns, the stands, and the large bowl that Solomon had made for the temple was too large to be weighed.
translation_verse: Buos ayi' banɛ ka ba maal nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug la, nɛ latita'ar nɛ tɛrekonam linɛ mɔr ku'om zi'esa ka Solomon da maali niŋ Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la da anɛ kʋntzɛn'ug linɛ zu'oe galis, ka ba kʋ nyaŋi maki li tɛbisim.

translation_verse: Azuba da kpi la, Kaleb da di Efirata du'a Hur.

english_verse: was the father of Uri and the grandfather of Bezalel.
translation_verse: Hur da du'a Uri, ka Uri du'a Bezalel.

english_verse: was the father of Jair, who ruled
translation_verse: Segub da du'a Jair ka o sʋ'oe tɛɛns pisi nɛ atan' Gilead teŋgbauŋʋn.

english_verse: Some time later the nations of Geshur and Aram captured
translation_verse: Bama wʋsa da anɛ Makir onɛ an Gilead la yaas.

english_verse: After the death of Hezron, Caleb married Ephrath, his father's wife. Their son was Ashhur, who later settled the town of Tekoa. The Descendants of Jerahmeel
translation_verse: Heziron da kpi Efirata teŋin, linɛ an Kaleb sʋ'ʋlim la. On da kpii naae la, o pu'a Abija da du'a Asur ka Asur mɛ du'a Tekoa. Jerameel yaas yʋda nwa'

english_verse: Jerahmeel, Hezron's oldest son, was the father of Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
translation_verse: Heziron bikpɛɛm da anɛ Jerameel, ka Jerameel bikpɛɛm an Ram, ka banɛ tia'al an Buuna nɛ Orem nɛ Ozem nɛ Ahija.

english_verse: Jerahmeel had a second wife, Atarah, who gave birth to Onam.
translation_verse: Ka o pu'abil Atara biig mɛ an Onam.

english_verse: Ram was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
translation_verse: Jerameel bikpɛɛm Ram biribis da anɛ Maaz nɛ Jamin nɛ Eker.

english_verse: Onam was the father of Shammai and Jada. Shammai was the father of Nadab and Abishur.
translation_verse: Ka Onam biribis da an Seamaae nɛ Jada. Ka Seamaae biribis da an Nadab nɛ Abisuor.

english_verse: Abishur married Abihail, and their two sons were Ahban and Molid.
translation_verse: Abisuor pu'a yʋ'ʋri da buon Abihel, ka o biribis da anɛ Aban nɛ Moolid.

english_verse: Nadab was the father of Seled and Appaim. Seled had no children;
translation_verse: Nadab biribis da anɛ Seled nɛ Apayim. Seled da kpiya ka pʋ du'a biisɛ.

english_verse: Appaim's son was Ishi, the father of Sheshan and the grandfather of Ahlai.
translation_verse: Apayim biig da anɛ Isi, ka on biig mɛ an Siesan, ka Siesan biig an Alai.

english_verse: Jada was the father of Jether and Jonathan. Jether had no children,
translation_verse: Jada onɛ an Seamaae pitʋ la biribis da anɛ Jeta nɛ Jonatan. Jeta da kpiya ka pʋ du'a biisɛ.

english_verse: but Jonathan had two sons: Peleth and Zaza.
translation_verse: Jonatan biribis da anɛ Pelef nɛ Zaza. Bama wʋsa da anɛ Jerameel yaas.

english_verse: Sheshan had no sons, and so he let one of his daughters marry Jarha, his Egyptian slave. Their son was Attai,
translation_verse: O da nɔk o bipuŋi tis Jaha ka o kul o, du'a Atai tis o.

english_verse: the father of Nathan and the grandfather of Zabad.
translation_verse: Atai da du'a Natan, ka Natan du'a Zabad

english_verse: Zabad's descendants included Ephlal, Obed, Jehu, Azariah, Helez, Eleasah, Sismai, Shallum, Jekamiah, and Elishama. The Descendants of Caleb
translation_verse: Ka Sallum da du'a Jekamiya, ka Jekamiya du'a Elisama. Kaleb dɔɔg dimi nwa'

english_verse: and Hebron's four sons, Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
translation_verse: Hebron biribis da anɛ Kora nɛ Tapua nɛ Rekem nɛ Sema.

english_verse: Shema was the father of Raham and the grandfather of Jorkeam. Rekem was the father of Shammai,
translation_verse: Sema da du'a Raham ka Raham du'a Jokiam. Ka Rekem mɛ du'a Seamaae

english_verse: the grandfather of Maon, and the great-grandfather of Bethzur.
translation_verse: ka Seamaae da du'a Maon ka Maon du'a Bet Zur.

english_verse: Ephah was one of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran named his son after his brother Gazez.
translation_verse: Kaleb pu'abil Efa da du'a Haran nɛ Mooza nɛ Gaziis. Haran mɛ da mɔr biig ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Gaziis.

english_verse: Ephah was the daughter of Jahdai, who was also the father of Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph.
translation_verse: Jadaae biribis da anɛ Regem nɛ Jotam nɛ Gesean nɛ Pelet nɛ Efa nɛ Saaf.

english_verse: Maacah was another of Caleb's wives, and their sons were Sheber and Tirhanah.
translation_verse: Kaleb pu'abil Maaka da du'a Siebɛr nɛ Tirana.

english_verse: Later, they had two more sons: Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Achsah.
translation_verse: O da lɛn du'a biribis ayi', ka banɛ an Saaf nɛ Siiva. Saaf da sʋ'oe Madmana teŋ ka Siiva sʋ'oe Makbina nɛ Gibea tɛɛns. Kaleb pu'ayua da an Akisa.

english_verse: Shobal, who settled the town of Kiriath-Jearim, was the ancestor of Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth clan,
translation_verse: Soobal onɛ da an Kiriaf Jiarim saam la yaas da anɛ Haroi nɛ Manahaf dim la pʋsʋk,

english_verse: and the clans that lived near Kiriath-Jearim; they were the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. The Zorathites and the Eshtaolites were descendants of the Mishraites.
translation_verse: nɛ Kiriaf Jiarim dɔɔd la wʋsa; banɛ da an Yitir nɛ Puf nɛ Seuma nɛ Misira dim. Ka ba yaas da an Zora nɛ Esitaol dim.

english_verse: Salma settled the town of Bethlehem and was the ancestor of the Netophathites, the people of Atroth-Bethjoab, half of the Manahathite clan, and the Zorites.
translation_verse: Sanlima yaas da anɛ Betilehem nɛ Netofa nɛ Atirof Bet Joab dim, nɛ Manahaf dim la pʋsʋk ya'as nɛ Zoor dim,

english_verse: Salma was also the ancestor of the clans in Jabez that kept the court and government records; they were the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These clans were the descendants of Hammath the Kenite, who was also the ancestor of the Rechabites.
translation_verse: nɛ gbauŋmi'idib dɔɔd banɛ bɛ Jabes teŋin la. Banɛ da an Tiira nɛ Simeaf nɛ Sueka dim. Bama da anɛ Ken dim ka ba yaab an Hammaf onɛ biisi da an Rekab yidim la.

english_verse: more sons. His wife Bathsheba daughter of Ammiel gave birth to Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon.
translation_verse: ka on biig mɛ an Na'ab Ahaz, ka on biig mɛ an Na'ab Hezekia, ka on biig mɛ an Na'ab Manase,

english_verse: David's other wives also gave birth to sons. Tamar was his daughter. The Descendants of King Solomon
translation_verse: Bama wʋsa da anɛ Na'ab David biribis, ka o pu'abibis la biribis pʋ paasɛ. Ka Tamar aan ba taʋn. Juda sʋ'ʋlim na'anam yʋda nwa'

english_verse: Solomon's descendants included the following kings: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah, Azariah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, and Josiah and his four sons, Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Jehoahaz.
translation_verse: Na'ab Josia biribisi da an Johanan, onɛ aan o bikpɛɛm la, ka onɛ tia'al ayi' an Na'ab Jehoyakim, ka onɛ tia'al atan' an Na'ab Zedekaya, ka onɛ tia'al anaasi an Sallum.

english_verse: Jehoiachin, who was taken to Babylon as a prisoner, had seven sons: Shealtiel,
translation_verse: Na'ab Jehoyakim yaas banɛ ka ba da gban'e keŋ Babilon la anɛ o biig Sealtiel,

english_verse: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
translation_verse: nɛ Malikiram nɛ Pedaya nɛ Sienaza nɛ Jekamiya nɛ Hosiama nɛ Nedabaya.

english_verse: Pedaiah had two sons: Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel was the father of Meshullam, Hananiah, and Shelomith their sister.
translation_verse: Pedaya biribis da anɛ Zerubabɛl nɛ Simie. Zerubabɛl biribis da anɛ Mesulam nɛ Hanania, ka ba taʋn da an Sielomif.

english_verse: He also had five other sons: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed.
translation_verse: O mɛ da lɛn mɔr biribis anu, ka banɛ an Hasuba nɛ Ohel nɛ Berekaya nɛ Hasadaya nɛ Jusab-Hesed.

english_verse: the father of Shemaiah and the grandfather of Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.
translation_verse: Siekania yaas yʋda anɛ Semaya nɛ o biribis Hatus nɛ Igal nɛ Baraya nɛ Nearaya nɛ Safat; ba wʋsa anɛ nidib ayuobʋ.

english_verse: Neariah was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam.
translation_verse: Nearaya biribis yʋda anɛ Eloanai nɛ Hizikaya nɛ Azirikam; ba wʋsa anɛ nidib atan'.

english_verse: Elioenai was the father of Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.
translation_verse: Eloanai biribis yʋda anɛ Hodavia nɛ Eliyaasib nɛ Pelaya nɛ Akub nɛ Johanan nɛ Delaya nɛ Anani; ba wʋsa anɛ nidib ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: Judah was the father of five sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
translation_verse: Juda yaas da anɛ Perez nɛ Heziron nɛ Karmi nɛ Hur nɛ Soobal.

english_verse: Shobal was the father of Reaiah, the grandfather of Jahath, and the great-grandfather of Ahumai and Lahad. These men all belonged to the Zorathite clan.
translation_verse: Ka Soobal biig Riaya da du'a Jahaf, ka Jahaf du'a Ahumai nɛ Lahad. Zora dɔɔg dimi la.

english_verse: Hur was the oldest son of Caleb and Ephrath. Some of his descendants settled the town of Bethlehem. Hur's other descendants included Etam, Penuel, and Ezer. Etam's sons were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, and his daughter was Hazzelelponi. Penuel settled the town of Gedor, and Ezer settled the town of Hushah.
translation_verse: Penuel da anɛ Geduor saam, ka Eza mɛ an Husea saam. Ba da anɛ Hur onɛ da an Efirata bikpɛɛm la yaas. Hur da an Betilehem dim wʋsa yaab.

english_verse: Ashhur, who settled the town of Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.
translation_verse: Asur biigi da an Tekoa. Asur pu'ab da anɛ ayi', ka ba yʋda an Hela nɛ Naara.

english_verse: daughters. But his brothers did not have as many children, so the Simeon tribe was smaller than the Judah tribe.
translation_verse: Naara biribis da anɛ Ahuzam nɛ Hifa nɛ Temeni nɛ Hahasitari.

english_verse: Ashhur and Helah were the parents of Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan.
translation_verse: Hela biribis da anɛ Zeref nɛ Zohar nɛ Efinan

english_verse: Koz, the father of Anub and Zobebah, was also the ancestor of the clans of Aharhel, the son of Harum.
translation_verse: nɛ Kos. Ka Kos biis mɛ da an Anub nɛ Hazobeba nɛ Harum nɛ o biig Ahahel yaas.

english_verse: Jabez was a man who got his name because of the pain he caused his mother during birth. But he was still the most respected son in his family.
translation_verse: Jabes yʋ'ʋr da dʋʋ gaad o mabiis la wʋsa. O ma da pʋd o yʋ'ʋr ye, Jabes, ka yɛl ye, “M da du'a o nɛ ka li zabid hali!”

english_verse: One day he prayed to Israel's God, “Please bless me and give me a lot of land. Be with me so I will be safe from harm.” And God did just what Jabez had asked.
translation_verse: Jabes da kaasi buol Israel Wina'am ka sɔs o ye, “Niŋimi m zug bareka ka kɛ ka m sʋ'ʋlim yalig! Sʋŋimim ka gɔsim ka m da nyɛ tɔɔgɔ!” Ka Wina'am wʋm o sɔsʋg la.

english_verse: Chelub was the brother of Shuhah and the father of Mehir. Later, Mehir had a son, Eshton,
translation_verse: Kɛlub da anɛ Suha mabiig, ka o biig da an Mehir, ka Mehir biig da an Esiton.

english_verse: whose three sons were Bethrapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah. It was Tehinnah who settled the town of Nahash. These men and their families lived in the town of Recah.
translation_verse: Ka Esiton biis an Bet Rafa nɛ Pasia nɛ Tehina. Ka Tehina biig an Yir-Nahas. Ban da anɛ Reka dap.

english_verse: Kenaz was the father of Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had two sons: Hathath and Meonothai,
translation_verse: Kenas biribis da anɛ Ofniel nɛ Seraya. Ka Ofniel biribis an Hataf nɛ Meonotai.

english_verse: who was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, who settled a place called “Valley of Crafts” because the people who lived there were experts in making things.
translation_verse: Ka Meonotai biig an Ofra. Seraya biig da anɛ Joab. Ka Joab biig an Ge-Haharasim. Linɛ kɛ ka ba da buonnɛ ba anwa la anɛ ye, nimbanɛ da bɛɛ anina la nu'ug tʋʋm da anɛ la'ad maalʋg.

english_verse: Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah was the father of Kenaz.
translation_verse: Jefune biig Kaleb biribis da anɛ Iru nɛ Ela nɛ Na'am. Ela biig da anɛ Kenas.

english_verse: Ezrah was the father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered was married to Bithiah the daughter of the king of Egypt. They had a daughter named Miriam and two sons: Shammai and Ishbah. It was Ishbah who settled the town of Eshtemoa. Mered was also married to a woman from the tribe of Judah, and their sons were Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel. Jered settled the town of Gedor; Heber settled the town of Soco; and Jekuthiel settled the town of Zanoah.
translation_verse: Ezira biribis da anɛ Jeta nɛ Mered nɛ Efer nɛ Jalon. Mered da di Na'ab Faaro biig ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Bitiya. O bipuŋ yʋ'ʋri da an Miriam ka o biribis an Seamaae nɛ Isiba. Ka Isiba biig an Estemoa. Mered pu'a kanɛ da an Juda nid la biribis da anɛ Jered nɛ Heber nɛ Jekutiel. Jered biig yʋ'ʋri da buon Geduor. Heber biigi da an Soko. Jekutiel biigi da an Zanoak.

english_verse: A man named Hodiah was married to the sister of Naham. Hodiah's descendants included Keilah of the Garmite clan and Eshtemoa of the Maacathite clan.
translation_verse: Hodaya da di Naham taʋn, ka ba yaasi an Kiela nɛ Estemoa. Kiela da anɛ Gerem nid, ka Estemoa mɛ an Maaka nid.

english_verse: Shimon was the father of Amnon, Rinnah, Benhanan, and Tilon. Ishi was the father of Zoheth and Benzoheth.
translation_verse: Siimon biribis da anɛ Amnon nɛ Arina nɛ Ben-Hanan nɛ Tiiloon. Isi yaas da anɛ Zohef nɛ Ben-Zohef.

english_verse: The members of these clans were the potters who lived in the towns of Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king. The Descendants of Simeon
translation_verse: Nimbama da anɛ banɛ ya'abid ka zin' Netayin nɛ Gedera tɛɛnsin ka tʋmmi tisid Na'ab la. Simeon yaas yʋda nwa'

english_verse: The descendants of Shaul included his son Shallum, his grandson Mibsam, and his great-grandson Mishma.
translation_verse: Simeon biribis da anɛ Nemuel nɛ Jamin nɛ Jarib nɛ Zera nɛ Sauul. Sauul da du'a Sallum, ka Sallum du'a Mibsam, ka Mibsam mɛ du'a Misima.

english_verse: The descendants of Mishma included his son Hammuel, his grandson Zaccur, and his great-grandson Shimei.
translation_verse: Misima da du'a Hamuel, ka Hamuel du'a Zakur, ka Zakur mɛ du'a Simie.

english_verse: Before David became king, the people of the Simeon tribe lived in the following towns: Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar-Shual, Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth-Marcaboth, Hazarsusim, Bethbiri, and Shaaraim.
translation_verse: nɛ Bet Maakabof nɛ Hazasusim nɛ Befibiri nɛ Siaaram tɛɛnsin. Tembama da aan ba tɛɛns hali ti paae Na'ab David na'am saŋa.

english_verse: They also lived in the five villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan,
translation_verse: Ba teŋkpɛmis la anɛ: Etam nɛ Ɛɛn nɛ Rimmon nɛ Token nɛ Asean. Ba da anɛ tɛɛns anu.

english_verse: as well as in the nearby villages as far as the town of Baal. These are the places where Simeon's descendants had settled, according to their own family records.
translation_verse: Nɛ tembibis banɛ giligi ba la wʋsa, hali ti paae Baalaf. Ban da zin' teŋ sieba la. Ba da sɔbi ba dɔɔg la nidib yʋda digil.

english_verse: When the people needed more pastureland for their flocks and herds, they looked as far as the eastern side of the valley where the town of Gerar is located,
translation_verse: ba da yii yadig teŋ la ieed yaama ye ba tisi ba bʋnkɔnbid, hali ti paae Geduor teŋ bɛn, linɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ bɔn'ɔfaligin la.

english_verse: and they found a lot of good pastureland that was quiet and undisturbed. This had once belonged to the Hamites,
translation_verse: Ba da nyɛ mɔsʋma ani, ka paalʋ la yalim bɛdegʋ, ka teŋ la wʋsa dig baanlimm. Ham buudi la sieba da dɛŋi zin'inɛ ani kʋdimin sa ka duoe tɔɔm.

english_verse: They killed the last of the Amalekites and lived there from then on.
translation_verse: Ba da kʋ Amalek dim banɛ da nyaŋi zɔɔ pɔns Seir teŋin la ka zin'in teŋin la hali ti paae zina.

english_verse: Reuben was the oldest son of Jacob, but he lost his rights as the first-born son because he slept with one of his father's wives. The honor of the first-born son was then given to Joseph,
translation_verse: Reuben da anɛ Israel bikpɛɛm, amaa on da digin nɛ o saam pu'a la zug, ba da faaɛn dinɛ an bikpɛɛm faar la tis Josef onɛ mɛ da an Israel biribiŋ la. Alazug, ba da pʋ sɔb Reuben yʋ'ʋri pɛ'ɛs banɛ nar ye ba di Israel faar la nii.

english_verse: Reuben had four sons: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Reuben onɛ da an Israel bikpɛɛm la biribis da anɛ Hanok nɛ Pallu nɛ Heziron nɛ Karmi.

english_verse: The descendants of Joel included Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, Micah, Reaiah, Baal, and Beerah, a leader of the Reuben tribe. Later, King Tiglath Pileser of Assyria took Beerah away as prisoner.
translation_verse: ka Baal du'a Beera onɛ ka Asiria Na'ab Tigilaf-Pilesa da gban'e o keŋ ka o lieb yammʋg la. Beera da anɛ Reuben dɔɔg la tuongat.

english_verse: The family records also include Jeiel, who was a clan leader, Zechariah, and Bela son of Azaz and grandson of Shema of the Joel clan. They lived in the territory around the town of Aroer, as far north as Nebo and Baal-Meon,
translation_verse: ka Azas da du'a Bela, ka Azas saam an Sema ka on saam mɛ an Joel. Joel nɛ o nidib la da zin'inɛ Aroa hali ti paae Nebo nɛ Baal Meon tɛɛnsin.

english_verse: and as far east as the desert just west of the Euphrates River. They needed this much land because they owned too many cattle to keep them all in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da zin'in ya-nya'aŋ baba yadig hali paae sian'anr la nɔɔrin nɛ Efiritis kɔldaug la, bɔzugɔ ba bʋnkɔnbid la da wiak bɛdegʋ Gilead teŋin.

english_verse: When Saul was king, the Reuben tribe attacked and defeated the Hagrites, then took over their land east of Gilead. The Descendants of Gad
translation_verse: Saŋkanɛ ka Saul da zin' na'am gbauŋ zug la, ba da zab nɛ Haga buudi la nyaŋi ba ka di'e ba teŋ la zin'inɛ tiig Gilead teŋ la zin'ikanɛ lɛbid ya-nya'aŋ la wʋsa. Gad yaas yʋda nwa'

english_verse: The tribe of Gad lived in the region of Bashan, north of the Reuben tribe. Gad's territory extended all the way to the town of Salecah.
translation_verse: Gad dɔɔg la da tʋgisnɛ Reuben dɔɔg la tuonnɛ zin'in Basan teŋin hali ti paae Saleka.

english_verse: Some of the clan leaders were Joel, Shapham, Janai, and Shaphat.
translation_verse: Joel n da an zugdaan Basan teŋin la ka Safam tia'al ayi', ka banɛ paas an Janai nɛ Safat.

english_verse: Ahi, the son of Abdiel and the grandson of Guni, was the leader of their clan.
translation_verse: Abdiel biig Ahi onɛ yaabi da an Guni la da aan ba tuŋ la tuongat.

english_verse: The people of Gad lived in the towns in the regions of Bashan and Gilead, as well as in the pastureland of Sharon.
translation_verse: Gad dɔɔg la da zin'inɛ Gilead linɛ bɛ Basan teŋgbauŋʋn nɛ li teŋkpɛmis la, nɛ Saron mɔma'asa zin'is la nɛ li yalʋŋ la bɛn wʋsa.

english_verse: Their family records were written when Jotham was king of Judah and Jeroboam was king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ba da sɔb nɛ' wʋsa niŋi ba tuŋ gbana la ni, Juda Na'ab Jotam na'am saŋa la, nɛ Na'ab Jeroboam da an Israel na'ab saŋa si'a la. Zaba yɛla

english_verse: They fought against the Hagrites and the tribes of Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.
translation_verse: Ba da zab nɛ Haga buudi la, nɛ Jetur dim, nɛ Nafis dim, nɛ Nodab dim la wʋsa.

english_verse: Whenever these soldiers went to war against their enemies, they prayed to God and trusted him to help. That's why the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh defeated the Hagrites and their allies.
translation_verse: Ba da sɔs Wina'am zaba la saŋa, ka o sʋŋi ba ka ba zabi nyaŋ Haga dim nɛ banɛ zi'e ba nya'aŋ la wʋsa. Wina'am da wʋm tisi ba, ban da niŋ o yadda la zug.

english_verse: Many of the Hagrites died in battle, because God was fighting this battle against them. The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh lived in that territory until they were taken as prisoners to Assyria. The Tribe of East Manasseh
translation_verse: ka kʋ nidib la bɛdegʋ bɔzugɔ Wina'am mɛŋi da sʋ'oe zaba la. Ka ba zin'in teŋ la ni hali nɛ Asiria dimi ti gban'e ba keŋ ka ba lieb yammis. Manase dɔɔg pʋsʋk dim la yʋda nwa'

english_verse: East Manasseh was a large tribe, so its people settled in the northern region of Bashan, as far north as Baal-Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon.
translation_verse: Manase dɔɔg pʋsʋk la da zu'onɛ. Ba da zin'inɛ Basan keŋ paae Baal Hemon nɛ Senir .

english_verse: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel were their clan leaders; they were well-known leaders and brave soldiers. The Tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh Are Defeated
translation_verse: Ba dɔɔg la tuŋ-tuŋ tuongatib da anɛ Efer nɛ Isi nɛ Eliel nɛ Aziriel nɛ Jeremia nɛ Hodavia nɛ Jadiel. Ba da anɛ banɛ sʋnfʋ kpi'em zaba ni, ka an yʋ'ʋr dim ka aan ba tuŋ la tuongatib.

english_verse: The people of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh were unfaithful to the God their ancestors had worshiped, and they started worshiping the gods of the nations that God had forced out of Canaan.

english_verse: even though he never became one of them. And he was certainly as famous as the rest of the Thirty Warriors. So David made him the leader of his own bodyguard.

english_verse: Several of these warriors were from King Saul's own tribe of Benjamin. They were experts at using a bow and arrows, and they could shoot an arrow or sling a stone with either hand.
translation_verse: Ba da mɔri ba zaba la'ad, ka mɛ mi' tiraug tɔɔnb hali bɛɛ tun'e vɛnligid luobig datiuŋ nɛ adagɔbʋg wʋsa; ba da anɛ banɛ kpin nɛ Saul ka yi Benjamin dɔɔg la ni na, ba yʋda da anɛ:

english_verse: Men from the tribe of Gad also joined David at his fortress in the desert and served as his warriors. They were also brave soldiers—fierce as lions and quick as gazelles. They were always prepared to fight with shields and spears.
translation_verse: Gad teŋ nidib sieba da buaki keŋ sian'arin David san'an, zin'ikanɛ ka o maal ka li aan o kpi'euŋ zin'ig la. Ba da anɛ zabzabidib amɛŋa banɛ ti'eb ka gur zaba ka nyaŋidi zanl zaba la'ad nɛ li buudi wʋsa. Ba nindaas da nwɛnɛ gbigima nindaas nɛ, ka ba tun'e zɔɔg hali wʋʋ walig kanɛ bɛ kʋkʋna ni nɛ.

english_verse: All these men were army officers; some were high-ranking officers over a thousand troops, and others were officers over a hundred troops.
translation_verse: Gad dɔɔg dim nwa' da anɛ zabzabidib tuongatib; ka banɛ pʋ paae kpɛɛmnam la gɔt zabzabidib kɔbig-kɔbig, ka kpɛɛmnam la gɔt tusir-tusir.

english_verse: Earlier, they had crossed the Jordan River when it flooded, and they chased out the people who lived in the valleys on each side of the river. Warriors from the Benjamin and Judah tribes
translation_verse: Nidib nwa' da mɔya hali: nwadkanɛ pin'in yiiga yʋʋm la pʋʋgin la, saŋa kan ka Joodan kɔldaug pɛ'ɛli badig la, ba da lɔ'ɔŋi zab nɛ banɛ bɛ bɔn'ɔdin la kad nimbanɛ bɛ kɔldaug la nya'aŋ nɛ li tuon la widigi ba wʋsa.

english_verse: One time a group of men from the tribes of Benjamin and Judah went to the fortress where David was staying.
translation_verse: Ninsieba mɛ da yi Benjamin nɛ Juda dɔɔdin kɛn David kpi'euŋ zin'igin la na.

english_verse: David met them outside and said, “If you are coming as friends to fight on my side, then stay and join us. But if you try to turn me over to my enemies, the God our ancestors worshiped will punish you, because I have done nothing wrong.”
translation_verse: David da yii tʋ'ʋsi ba, ka yɛli ba ye, “Ya ya'a kennɛ m san'an na nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm ye ya sʋŋim, m na siak ka mam nɛ yanam niŋ nɔɔr yinne. Amaa ya ya'a kena ye ya gbi' mam tisim dataas, la'an nɛ mam pʋ maal si'el la, ti yaanam Wina'am la na kadi ya saria.”

english_verse: Some of the warriors who joined David were from the tribe of Manasseh. They had earlier gone with David when he agreed to fight on the side of the Philistines against King Saul. But as soon as the Philistine rulers realized that David might turn against them and rejoin Saul, they sent David away to the town of Ziklag.
translation_verse: Manase dɔɔg la ni sieba mɛ da aaɛn kɛn David san'an na, saŋa kanɛ ka on nɛ Filistia dim da keŋ ye ba zab nɛ Saul la. Amaa on nɛ o nidib la da pʋ sʋŋ Filistia dim la bɔzugɔ Filistia tuongatib la da nwɛ' taab sɔɔra ka kadi ba ye ba lɛm kul. Ba da yɛl ye, “O pa'a ti lɛbi kuosi ti tis Saul onɛ aan o zugdaan kʋdig la.”

english_verse: and brave soldiers, and so David made them officers in his army. They fought on his side when enemy troops attacked.
translation_verse: Ba da anɛ zabzabidib banɛ sʋnfʋ kpi'em, alazug ba da gaad David zabzabidib la tuonnɛ zabid nɛ banɛ da ginnɛ faand la. Lin nya'aŋ la, ba da anɛ Israel zabzabidib kpɛɛmnam.

english_verse: of his relatives, who were also officers;
translation_verse: ) yii o nidibin na;

english_verse: leaders from Issachar, along with troops under their command—these leaders knew the right time to do what needed to be done;
translation_verse: ) nɛ ba dɔɔg dim banɛ ka ba gaadi ba tuonnɛ pa'annɛ ba ban na maal si'em la;

english_verse: Other Israelites from as far away as the territories of Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali brought cattle and sheep to slaughter for food. They also brought donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen that were loaded down with flour, dried figs and raisins, wine, and olive oil. Everyone in Israel was very happy.
translation_verse: Ala mɛn ba taaba banɛ bɛ lalli la wʋsa, wʋʋ Isaka nɛ Zebulun nɛ Naftali dɔɔd dim la, da nɔk bʋmis nɛ yʋgʋma nɛ widi nɛ niigi zi diibi kena tisi ba. Ba da mɔr zɔ'ɔm nɛ tiis wala kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb nɛ daam nɛ kpaam nɛ niigi nɛ pɛ'ɛs bɛdegʋ na. Nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa da pa'annɛ Israel dim sʋnfʋ ma'ae si'em.

english_verse: All of these soldiers voluntarily came to Hebron because they wanted David to become king of Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel wanted the same thing.
translation_verse: Bama wʋsa da anɛ zabzabidib banɛ gban'e nɛ ba sʋʋnr wʋsa ye ba keŋ Hebron teŋin diis David na'am. Israel dim banɛ paas la da gban'e nɛ nɔɔr yinne ye ba diis David Israel na'am.

english_verse: The soldiers stayed in Hebron three days, eating and drinking what their relatives had prepared for them.
translation_verse: Dap la da bɛ nɛ David san'an daba atan', ka dit ka nuud, bɔzugɔ ba yidim da tisi ba linɛ ka ba na dit.

english_verse: Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
translation_verse: David nɛ Israel nidib la wʋsa da keŋ Baal teŋin linɛ bɛ Juda teŋgbauŋʋn ka ba buonnɛ li ye, Kiriaf Jiarim la, ye ba nɔk Wina'am Daka dinɛ ka Kerubnam bɛɛ li zug ka Wina'am girima nɛ o paŋ bɛɛ ba teŋsʋk, ka Zugsɔb yʋ'ʋr bɛɛ ani la.

english_verse: Some time later, David talked with his army commanders,
translation_verse: David da nwɛ' sɔɔra nɛ o zabzabidib tuongatib banɛ sʋ'oe nidib tusir-tusir nɛ kɔbig-kɔbig la.

english_verse: David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?”
translation_verse: David da zɔ Wina'am dabiem daakan la, ka yɛl ye, “Mam ye m niŋ wala lɛn siak ka Wina'am Daka la kɛɛn m san'an na?”

english_verse: The people agreed this was the right thing to do.
translation_verse: Nidib la wʋsa da siak on yɛl si'el la, bɔzugɔ ba da gɔs ka li dɔl suor.

english_verse: The sacred chest was still at Abinadab's house, and when David and the crowd arrived there, they brought the chest outside and placed it on a new ox cart. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart,
translation_verse: Ka ba nɔk Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la niŋ tɛreko paallin, mɔri yi Abinadab yin na, ka Uzaa nɛ Ahio banɛ an Abinadab biribis la dɔlisidi kad na'abanɛ vɛ'ɛd tɛreko la.

english_verse: while David and the crowd danced and sang praises to the Lord with all their might. They played music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
translation_verse: David nɛ Israel nidib la wʋsa da maannɛ sumalisim nɛ ba paŋ wʋsa Wina'am tuon. Ba da yʋ'ʋmnɛ ka piebid wiis ka nwɛ'ɛd googinam nɛ siyada nɛ na'atana.

english_verse: But when they came to Chidon's threshing place, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the chest to stop it from falling.
translation_verse: Ban da paae Kidon teŋin zieŋ kanɛ ka ba bʋ'ʋd ki la, niigi la da tu'ug ka Daka la bik ka Uzaa zɔɔ ti'e ye li da luu.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋnf da duoe nɛ Uzaa, ka o nwɛ' o bas ka o kpi, on nɔk o nu'ugʋ si'is Daka la zug. O da kpi Wina'am tuon,

english_verse: David then got angry with God for killing Uzzah. So he named that place “Attack on Uzzah,” and it's been called that ever since.
translation_verse: David sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ Zugsɔb la sʋnfʋ pɛlig nɛ Uzaa la zug. Ka lin yi saŋkan la paae zina ba buon zin'ig kan la ye, Perez Uzaa.

english_verse: So instead of taking it to Jerusalem, David decided to take it to the home of Obed-Edom, who lived in the town of Gath.
translation_verse: O da pʋ bɔɔd ye o siaki di'e Wina'am Daka la ka li keŋ David Teŋin bɛɛ o san'anɛ. Ka lɛɛ mɔri li keŋ Obededom onɛ an Gaf nid la yin.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom, his family, and everything he owned.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Daka la da kpɛm bɛ nɛ Obededom onɛ an Gaf nid la yinne paae nwadis atan', ka Zugsɔb la niŋ on nɛ o yidim nɛ on mɔr si'el wʋsa zug bareka.

english_verse: David and his army marched to Baal-Perazim, where they attacked and defeated the Philistines. He said, “I defeated my enemies because God broke through them like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Ka David nɛ o nidib la keŋ Baal Perazim, anina ka o nyaŋi ba. Ka yɛl ye, “Nwɛnɛ ku'om tansidi yit si'em la, ala ka Wina'am mɛ tans na nyaŋi m dataas.” Dinzug ka ba buon anina ye, “Baal Perazim”.

english_verse: David obeyed God and he defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Gibeon to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ka David maal wʋʋ Wina'am yɛl o si'em la, ka kʋ Filistia zabzabidib la wʋsa din yi Gibeon ti paae Giza teŋin.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. They brought along carpenters and stone workers, and enough cedar logs to build David a palace.
translation_verse: Taya Na'ab Hiram da tʋm nidib Na'ab David san'an ka tis o na'aziinr daad nɛ kampintanam nɛ banɛ mi' kuga mɛɛb ka ba mɛ' na'ayiri tis o.

english_verse: After David moved to Jerusalem, he married more women and had more sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Jerusalem teŋin la David da di pu'abi paas. Ka du'a biribis nɛ bipumis bɛdegʋ paas.

english_verse: His children born there were Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet. David Defeats the Philistines (
translation_verse: Elisama nɛ Eliada nɛ Elifelet. David n nyaŋ Filistia dim la (

english_verse: From then on, David became even more famous, and the Lord made all the nations afraid of him.
translation_verse: Dinzug David yʋ'ʋr da tiig teŋ la wʋsa, ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka tɛɛns la wʋsa zɔt David.

english_verse: When the Philistines heard that David had become king of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard about their plan and marched out to meet them in battle.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da wʋm ye ba bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋ David zug ka diis o Israel na'am la, ba da duoe nɛ ba zabzabidibi keŋ ieed o. Amaa David da wʋmi ba yɛla ka yi ye o tʋ'ʋsi ba.

english_verse: The Philistines had already camped in Rephaim Valley and were raiding the nearby villages.
translation_verse: Ka Filistia dim la da kena paae Refa Dim Bɔn'ɔgin la pin'ili san'amid la'ad.

english_verse: David asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help me win?” The Lord told David, “Yes, attack them! I will give you victory.”
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os Wina'am ye, “M kem zab nɛ Filistia dim laa? Fʋ na zaŋi ba niŋi m nu'usinɛɛ?” Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Kem ka m sid na zaŋ Filistia dim la niŋi fʋ nu'usin.”

english_verse: Then David ordered his troops to burn the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filistia dim la da lɔbi ba bada bas ani ka zɔ, ka David tis nɔɔr ye ba nyu'om bada la nɛ bugum.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Saŋa si'a ya'as ka Filistia dim la daa kena paae bɔn'ɔgin la ka pin'ili san'amid la'ad.

english_verse: David asked God what he should do, and God answered, “Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind them where the balsam trees are.
translation_verse: Ka David bu'os Wina'am ya'as ka o lɛbis ye, “Da kpa' keŋ zab nɛ ba, amaa kem kaae giligi ba nya'aŋi paae tibanɛ zi'e anina la baba pin'ili zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: Wait there until you hear the treetops making the sound of marching troops. That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army. So you must then attack quickly!”
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a ti wʋm ka li nwɛnɛ nidib nɔba nɔɔdi dammid tiis la zugin, fʋn yim zab nɛ ba. Bɔzugɔ din na pa'al ye mam Wina'am la gaadi fʋ tuon ye m zab nɛ Filistia dim zabzabidib la.”

english_verse: David had several buildings built in Jerusalem, and he had a tent set up where the sacred chest would be kept.
translation_verse: David n da mɛ dɔɔdi naae zin'ikanɛ ka ba buon ye David Teŋ la, o da bɔ zin'igi maali ti' fuug sʋgʋri niŋ Wina'am Daka la ani.

english_verse: Next, David invited everyone to come to Jerusalem and watch the sacred chest being carried to the place he had set up for it.
translation_verse: David da la'as Israel dim wʋsa Jerusalem teŋin ye ba mɔr Zugsɔb Daka la kɛn zin'ikanɛ ka o maal ye li bɛ la.

english_verse: He also sent for Aaron's descendants and for the Levites. The Levites that came were:
translation_verse: O da buol Aaron nɛ Levi yaas la la'as na. Ba da anɛ:

english_verse: Uriel, the leader of the Kohath clan, and
translation_verse: Kohat tuŋ la ni: Uriel da aan ba tuongat nɛ o nidib kɔbiga nɛ pisi (

english_verse: Joel, the leader of the Gershon clan, and
translation_verse: Gerson tuŋ la ni: Joel da aan ba tuongat nɛ o nidib kɔbiga nɛ pistan' (

english_verse: Shemaiah, the leader of the Elizaphan clan, and
translation_verse: Elizafan tuŋ la ni: Semaya da aan ba tuongat nɛ o nidib kɔbisyi' (

english_verse: Eliel, the leader of the Hebron clan, and
translation_verse: Hebron tuŋ la ni: Eliel onɛ an tuongat la nɛ o nidib pisnii (

english_verse: The first time we tried to bring the chest to Jerusalem, we didn't ask the Lord what he wanted us to do. He was angry with us, because you Levites weren't there to carry the chest.”
translation_verse: Li anɛ yanam Levi dɔɔg dim la daa pʋ bɛ nɛ ti li pin'ilʋgʋn la kɛ ka Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am la sʋnf daa pɛlig nɛ ti. Ti daa pʋ bu'os o baŋ din nar ye ti zii li si'em.”

english_verse: The priests and the Levites made themselves clean. They were now ready to carry the sacred chest
translation_verse: Alazug maanmaannib la nɛ Levi dɔɔg dim la da maali ba mɛŋ nyain linɛ na kɛ ka ba nyaŋi zi Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am Daka la na.

english_verse: on poles that rested on their shoulders, just as the Lord had told Moses to do.
translation_verse: Levi dim la da zi Wina'am Daka la nɛ li dapuuda la ba biankimpiind zug, wʋʋ Zugsɔb la da tis Moses nɔɔr ka pa'al si'em la.

english_verse: David then told the leaders to choose some Levites to sing and play music on small harps, other stringed instruments, and cymbals.
translation_verse: David da yɛl Levi dɔɔg tuongatib la ye ba gaŋimi ba ba'abiis banɛ na yʋ'ʋmid, ka ba nwɛ'ɛd kɔna nɛ siyaaris nɛ galana ka piebid wiisi yʋ'ʋm sumalisim yʋʋma.

english_verse: Four Levites were then appointed to guard the sacred chest. They were Berechiah, Elkanah, Obed-Edom, and Jehiah. Finally, David chose priests to walk in front of the sacred chest and blow trumpets. They were Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer. The Sacred Chest Is Brought to Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Siebanaya nɛ Joseafat nɛ Netanɛl nɛ Amasai nɛ Zakaria nɛ Banaya nɛ Elieza da anɛ maanmaannib, ba tʋʋm da anɛ ye ba pieb na'atana Wina'am Daka la tuon. Obededom nɛ Jehel mɛ da guri Daka la dɔɔg za'anɔɔr. Ban nɔk Nɔnaar Daka la lɛbid Jerusalem la yɛla (

english_verse: David, the leaders of Israel, and the army commanders were very happy as they went to Obed-Edom's house to get the sacred chest.
translation_verse: David nɛ Israel kpɛɛmnam nɛ banɛ gat zabzabidib tusir tuon la da keŋ ye ba nɔk Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la yi Obededom yin nɛ sumalisim.

english_verse: God gave the Levites the strength they needed to carry the chest, and so they sacrificed seven bulls and seven rams.
translation_verse: Wina'am da sʋŋ Levi dim banɛ da ziid Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la zug, ba da kʋ na'araad ayɔpɔi nɛ pɛraad ayɔpɔi.

english_verse: David, the Levites, Chenaniah the music director, and all the musicians were wearing linen robes, and David was also wearing a linen cloth.
translation_verse: David da yɛnɛ fuwɔk linɛ pɛlig wʋʋ Levi dim banɛ ziid Daka la fuud la, nɛ banɛ da an yʋʋmyʋ'ʋmnib la, nɛ Kanania onɛ pa'an yʋʋmyʋ'ʋmnib la. David mɛ da yɛ dansika paas.

english_verse: While the sacred chest was being carried into Jerusalem, everyone was celebrating by shouting and playing music on horns, trumpets, cymbals, harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Alazug Israel dim wʋsa da zi Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la kena ka tansid agɔla gɔla ka piebid na'atana nɛ wiis, ka nwɛ'ɛd galana nɛ googinam nɛ siyaaris.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing in honor of the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la ti kpɛn'ɛd David teŋin la, ka Mikal onɛ an Saul pu'ayua la gɔsid takoro ni. Ka on nyɛ David n wa'ad Zugsɔb la tuon si'em la ka o nɛ'ɛs o, o sʋʋnrin.

english_verse: After David had finished, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord
translation_verse: On da maal nyu'or maan nɛ taaba la'asʋg maan la naae la, o da kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis nidib la Wina'am yʋ'ʋr zug.

english_verse: and gave every person in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins.
translation_verse: Ka nɔk diibi pʋdig Israel dim la, pu'ab nɛ dap wʋsa.

english_verse: David appointed some of the Levites to serve at the sacred chest; they were to play music and sing praises to the Lord God of Israel.
translation_verse: O da gaŋ Levi dim la sieba ye ba tʋm Daka la tʋʋma Zugsɔb la tuon, ka an nu'unwɛ'ɛdib, ka maan bareka pʋ'ʋsim, ka wɔ'ɔgid Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la.

english_verse: Asaph was their leader, and Zechariah was his assistant. Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and another man named Jeiel were appointed to play small harps and stringed instruments. Asaph himself played the cymbals,
translation_verse: Ba tuongat da anɛ Asaf, ka Zakaria tia'al, nɛ Jeyel nɛ Siemiramof nɛ Jehel nɛ Matitia nɛ Eliab nɛ Benaya nɛ Obededom nɛ Jeyel. Ban tʋʋm da anɛ ba nwɛ' kɔna ka pieb wiis, Asaf tʋʋm da anɛ ye o nwɛ'ɛd siyada.

english_verse: and the two priests Benaiah and Jahaziel were to blow trumpets every day in front of the sacred chest. David's Song of Praise (Psalms
translation_verse: Ka Benaya nɛ Jahaziel banɛ da an maanmaannib la tʋʋm da anɛ ye ba piebid na'atana saŋa wʋsa Wina'am Nɔnaar Daka la tuon. David yʋʋm kanɛ pian'ad Wina'am yʋ'ʋr la

english_verse: We must never forget his agreement and his promises, not in thousands of years. *
translation_verse: O tɛnri o nɔnaar la yɛla saŋa wʋsa, nɛ o pian'ʋk linɛ ka o tis zʋmaana tusir la,

english_verse: You belong to the family of Israel, his servant; you are his chosen ones, the descendants of Jacob.
translation_verse: Yanam Israel yaas banɛ aan o tʋmtʋmnib, nɛ Jakob biribis banɛ ka o gaŋ la, tɛnri nyalima banɛ ka o maal la nɛ tʋʋm kilima banɛ ka o tʋm la nɛ on kad saria si'em yɛla.

english_verse: That same day, David instructed Asaph and his relatives for the first time to sing these praises to the Lord:
translation_verse: Daakan la David da tis Asaf nɛ banɛ dɔl o nya'aŋ la yʋʋm kaŋa ye ba yʋ'ʋm pʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb la:

english_verse: Praise the Lord and pray in his name! Tell everyone what he has done.
translation_verse: Pʋ'ʋsimi Zugsɔb la bareka, buolim o yʋ'ʋr; kɛl ka tɛɛns la wʋsa baŋ on maal si'el.

english_verse: Sing praises to the Lord! Tell about his miracles.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋm tis o, yʋ'ʋm zun'e o; mɔɔlim o tʋʋmnyalima la wʋsa.

english_verse: Celebrate and worship his holy name with all your heart.
translation_verse: Maalim sumalisim Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋri an kasi la zug; kɛl ka banɛ ieed Zugsɔb la wʋsa maal sumalisim.

english_verse: Trust the Lord and his mighty power. Worship him always.
translation_verse: Gɔsimi Zugsɔb nɛ o paŋ la; ieminɛ o zin'ig saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: The Lord is our God, bringing justice everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Onɛ aan ti Zugsɔb Wina'am; ka o sariakadib bɛ dunia wʋsa ni.

english_verse: when he said, “I'll give you the land of Canaan.”
translation_verse: O da yɛl ye, “Fʋn ka m ye m nɔk Keenan teŋ la tis ka li liebi fʋ faar.”

english_verse: At the time there were only a few of us, and we were homeless.
translation_verse: Saŋa kan ka ba kal da nam pʋ zu'oe la; sida, ba da pɔɔd ka mɛ an saam teŋin la.

english_verse: We wandered from nation to nation, from one country to another.
translation_verse: Ba da gɔɔndi giligid teŋ-teŋ yit sʋ'ʋlim yinne ken sʋ'ʋlim yinne ni.

english_verse: God did not let anyone mistreat our people. Instead he protected us by punishing rulers
translation_verse: O da pʋ kɛ ka sɔ' mugusi baa; ba yɛla ka o da zɛrig na'anam ka yɛli ba ye,

english_verse: and telling them, “Don't touch my chosen leaders or harm my prophets!”
translation_verse: “Mid ka ya si'is onɛ ka man gaŋ la; da niŋi m nɔdi'esidib la si'ela.”

english_verse: Everyone on this earth, sing praises to the Lord. Day after day announce, “The Lord has saved us!”
translation_verse: Dunia wʋsa yʋ'ʋm yʋʋma pian' Zugsɔb la, yɛlimini o faangir kanɛ ka' naar la yɛla daar wʋsa.

english_verse: Tell every nation on earth, “The Lord is wonderful and does marvelous things!
translation_verse: Kɛlli ka dunia wʋsa wʋm o girima la yɛla, ka kɛ ka nidib la baŋ o tʋʋmnyalima la yɛla.

english_verse: The Lord is great and deserves our greatest praise! He is the only God worthy of our worship.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la anɛ kpi'euŋ sɔb ka nar nɛ wɔ'ɔgir, onɛ nar ye ti zɔɔ o gaad wina wʋsa.

english_verse: Other nations worship idols, but the Lord created the heavens.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ tɛɛns la wina la wʋsa anɛ bada amaa Zugsɔb la maal saŋgbana.

english_verse: Give honor and praise to the Lord, whose power and beauty fill his holy temple.”
translation_verse: Vɛnlim nɛ kpi'euŋ ma'aa bɛɛ o san'an, paŋ nɛ sumalisim mɛ bɛ on bɛ si'el la.

english_verse: Tell everyone of every nation, “Praise the glorious power of the Lord.
translation_verse: Yanam nimbanɛ bɛ tɛɛsin la wʋsa pian'am Zugsɔb la, pian'ami Zugsɔb la, o girima nɛ o paŋ la zug.

english_verse: He is wonderful! Praise him and bring an offering into his temple. Worship the Lord, majestic and holy.
translation_verse: Zun'omi Zugsɔb la wʋʋ o yʋ'ʋr la nar si'em. Mɔri piini kɛɛn o san'an na; zun'omi Zugsɔb la, o girima nɛ o kasi bɛllim la zug.

english_verse: Everyone on earth, now tremble!” The world stands firm, never to be shaken.
translation_verse: Dunia wʋsa zɔm o dabiem. Dunia la zi'enɛ kiŋ-kiŋ; li ka' linɛ vurigida.

english_verse: Tell the heavens and the earth to be glad and celebrate! And announce to the nations, “The Lord is King!”
translation_verse: Kɛl ka agɔl maal sumalisim ka dunia maal sumpielim. Kɛl ka ba yɛl dunia wʋsa sʋʋgin ye, “Zugsɔb la an Na'ab!”

english_verse: Command the ocean to roar with all of its creatures and the fields to rejoice with all of their crops.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka atɛuk maligim maal tʋkpiidʋg, nɛ teŋgbauŋ la, nɛ linɛ bɛɛ li ni wʋsa.

english_verse: Then every tree in the forest will sing joyful songs to the Lord. He is coming to judge all people on earth.
translation_verse: Tibanɛ bɛ sian'arin la na yʋʋm; ba na yʋʋm nɛ sumalisim, on kenna ye o kad dunia saria la zug.

english_verse: Praise the Lord because he is good to us, and his love never fails.
translation_verse: Pʋ'ʋsimi Zugsɔb la bareka on an sʋm la zug; o nɔŋilim la bɛ nɛ saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: Say to him, “Save us, Lord God! Bring us back from among the nations. Let us celebrate and shout in praise of your holy name.
translation_verse: “Kaasimi kuŋ ye, ‘O Zugsɔba, fʋnɛ aan ti faangid, faanmi ti; la'asimi ti ka faaɛn ti yis teŋ zʋŋ dim la ni, ka ti na pʋ'ʋsi fʋ yʋ'ʋr linɛ an kasi la bareka, ka ti na paam girima fʋ wɔ'ɔgir la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you deserve to be praised forever and ever.” After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!” David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
translation_verse: Zun'or anɛ Zugsɔb la din, onɛ an Israel Wina'am la, lin yi nannanna nɛ saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.’” Ka nidib la wʋsa yɛl ye, “Ami! Zun'omi Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept.
translation_verse: David da bas Asaf nɛ o taaba la Zugsɔb Nɔnaar Daka la zin'igin ye ba maan maana saŋa wʋsa wʋʋ dabisir wʋsa nar ye li maan an si'em.

english_verse: David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon.
translation_verse: David da kɛ ka Zadok onɛ an maanmaan la nɛ o taaba la kpɛn tʋm Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Fuug Sʋgʋrin la, maan zin'ig linɛ bɛ Gibeon teŋin la.

english_verse: They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel.
translation_verse: Ba da maan nyu'or maana tisid Zugsɔb la maan daka la zug saŋa wʋsa, bɛogʋn nɛ zaam wʋʋ lin sɔb si'em Zugsɔb zi'elʋgin linɛ ka o da zi'eli tis Israel dim la.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Banɛ da paas da anɛ Heman nɛ Jedutun nɛ banɛ ka ba gaans ka buoli ba yʋda ye ba tis Zugsɔb la bareka pʋ'ʋsim la, “Bɔzugɔ o nɔŋilim la bɛ nɛ saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.”

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were also responsible for blowing the trumpets, and for playing the cymbals and other instruments during worship at the tent. The Levites in Jeduthun's clan were the guards at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Heman nɛ Jedutun tʋʋm da anɛ ba piebid na'atana ka nwɛ'ɛd siyada nɛ bʋnnwɛ'ɛda banɛ kpɛlim la ka yʋ'ʋm yʋʋm sʋma. Jedutun tuŋ dimi mɛ da gur teŋ la yaŋir.

english_verse: After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_verse: Ka nidib la wʋsa lɛbi kul, sɔ' wʋsa nɛ o yin, ka David lɛb ye o kaanb, kaanb sʋŋʋ tis o yidim.

english_verse: Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
translation_verse: Na'ab David yʋ'ʋn da bɛɛ o na'ayin la, o da yɛl Natan onɛ an nɔdi'es la ye, “Man na niŋ wala bɛ na'ayin ka ba maali li nɛ na'aziinr davɛnla, ka Zugsɔb nɔnaar Daka la gbɛɛnd sʋgʋrinɛ?”

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person.
translation_verse: Li nwɛnɛ nɛ'ɛŋa nam pʋ paae fʋ ya'am, m Wina'am, ka fʋ lɛn yɛl ye fʋ na tʋm gaad ala tisim yidim bɛog sa. Fʋ lɛn gɔsim ka li nwɛnɛ manɛ gat ninsʋma dunia nwa' ni nɛ, m Zugsɔb Wina'am.

english_verse: to go to David and tell him: David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: “Kem yɛli m tʋmtʋm David ye, Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, ‘Li ka' fʋnɛ na mɛ' yiri tis mam ka m kpɛn'ɛ.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Lin yi man da yis Israel dim Egipt teŋin la paae zina. Mam da bɛ nɛ sʋgʋrin yanamɛ da paae teŋ si'a wʋsa, ka naanɛ ya bɛllim zin'ig yinne ti tɔlis zin'ig yinne ni.

english_verse: I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Man ken nɛ Israel dim la, m nam zi' bu'os banɛ aan ba tuongatib ka m gaŋ ye ba guri m nidib Israel dim la ye bɔ ka ya pʋ nɔk na'aziinr daadi mɛ' yiri tisi ma?’”

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: M dɔlli fʋ ken, fʋn keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa, ka kadi fʋ dataasi yisi fʋ tuon. Nannanna m na maalif nintita'ar, nwɛnɛ nintitada banɛ bɛ dunia nwa' nii an si'em la.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace. They will no longer have to tremble with fear—evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: M na tis Israel dim banɛ aan m nidib la zin'ig, ka na zin'ili ba ka ba mɔri ba mɛŋ teŋ ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn daami ba ya'asɛ. Nimbɛ'ɛdnam kʋ lɛm mugusi ba wʋʋ ban da niŋid si'em pin'ilʋgʋn laa.

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people, and I will keep your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that like you, your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: M pʋn dɛŋi maal nɛ'ɛŋa nɛ saŋa kanɛ ka m da pin'ili gaans tuongatibi tisim nidib Israel dim la. M mɛ na nyaŋi fʋ dataas wʋsa tisif. Mam Zugsɔb la mɛŋ na mɛ' yiri tisif.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Fʋ dabisa la bɛn ya'a ti paae, ka fʋ tig sa'ab, m na kɛ ka fʋ biig yinne duoe na di'e fʋ zin'ig. M na kɛ ka o na'am la zi'en.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Oŋa an onɛ na mɛ' yir man yʋ'ʋr zug. M na kɛ ka o na'am saŋa kʋ mɔr bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Man na aan o saam ka on mɛ na aan m biig. M nɔŋilim la kʋ yi o san'an wʋʋ man yisi li nimbanɛ daa bɛɛ fʋ tuon la si'em laa.

english_verse: I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka o guri m yir la nɛ m sʋ'ʋlim la saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ, o na'am na bɛ saŋa wʋsa ka kʋ mɔr bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: Nathan told David exactly what the Lord had said. David Gives Thanks to the Lord (
translation_verse: Natan da keŋ tu'as David Wina'am nie si'eli pa'al o la wʋsa.’” David winsɔsʋg (

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts. What else can I say, except that you have honored me?
translation_verse: Man David na lɛn yɛlif ye bɔ? M Zugsɔba, bɔ ya'as ka David na yɛllɛ, fʋn tis o na'asi si'a la? Bɔzugɔ fʋ mi'im, ka m aan fʋ tʋmtʋm.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed: Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab David duoe kpɛn' zin'in Zugsɔb la tuon ka yɛl ye, “M Zugsɔb Wina'am, man aan anɔ'ɔnɛ, ka man yin la mɛ an bɔ ka fʋ dʋ'ʋsim ka mɔrim hali paae zina?

english_verse: It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, fʋn zi'el si'em nɛ fʋ bɔɔdim la zug, nɛ man aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la zug, fʋ maal bʋntita'ar kaŋa ka nie kaanbʋg la pa'alim.

english_verse: No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Sɔ' lɛn kae nwɛnɛ fʋ Zugsɔba. Win si'a mɛ lɛn kae asɛɛ fʋn ma'aa. Ti wʋm ya nɛ ti mɛŋ tʋba ka li an sida.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here.
translation_verse: Anɔ'ɔnɛ lɛn nwɛnɛ fʋ nidib Israel dima? Fʋnɛ da faaɛn ba yis yammid pʋʋgin Egipt teŋin, ye ba aan fʋ din. Fʋ da tʋm bʋnnyalima ka kadi ba dataasi yis ka tisi ba teŋ sʋŋ ka fʋ yʋ'ʋr paam girima. Fʋ da tʋm nɛ'ɛŋa tis Israel ma'aa.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, fʋnɛ nɔki fʋ nidib Israel dim ka ba aan fʋ mɛŋ din, saŋa dinɛ ka' bɛnnɛ, fʋn onɛ an Zugsɔb la liebi ba Wina'am.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.” My kingdom will be strong,
translation_verse: Ala ka fʋ sid na mɔr yʋ'ʋtita'ar saŋa wʋsa. Ka nidib na yɛl ye, Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la anɛ Israel Wina'am; ka man David yir la na zi'enɛ fʋ tuon, man aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la zug.

english_verse: because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Fʋn onɛ an Wina'am la, fʋ nie nɛ'ɛŋa tis man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la, ye fʋ na mɛ' yiri tisim, alazug ka li kpɛ'ɛŋi m ka m sɔsid Winsɔsʋg kaŋa tisidif.

english_verse: You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, fʋ anɛ Wina'am! Fʋnɛ kaanb, kaanb sʋŋ bama tisi fʋ tʋmtʋm.

english_verse: Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_verse: Nannanna li tigi fʋ nini ye fʋ niŋ man kanɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋm la yir bareka ka kɛ ka di kpɛn yaligidi ken tuon saŋa wʋsa. Fʋn Zugsɔb la niŋi li bareka, ka ti na nyɛɛ fʋ bareka hali saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.”

english_verse: While King Hadadezer of Zobah was trying to gain control of the territory near the Euphrates River, David met him in battle at Hamath and defeated him.
translation_verse: Dinɛ paas la, David da zab nɛ Na'ab Hadadeze onɛ an Zoba na'ab la nyaŋ o, on da lɛbid ye o di'e o sʋ'ʋlim linɛ dɛn'ɛd Efiritis kɔldaug la, ka kad o hali ti paae Hamat tempʋʋgin.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: David da faaɛn Hadadeze zabzabidib tuongatib la zaba la'asʋma mɔri kul. Li da anɛ gbanti'edis ka ba nɔk sanlima bulig.

english_verse: Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: O da gaŋ o zabzabidib tuongatib sieba niŋ Aram dim sʋ'ʋlimin linɛ bɛ Damaskus la. Nɛ'ɛŋa da kɛ ka Aram dim la lieb o sʋ'ʋlim nidib ka yɔɔd lampɔ tisid o. Zugsɔb la da tis David paŋ ka o nyaŋid on keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa.

english_verse: King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze.
translation_verse: o da tʋm o biig Hadoram Na'ab David san'an na ye o pʋ'ʋs o nɛ o zusʋŋ, nɛ on zabi nyaŋ Hadadeze onɛ da zabid nɛ on Tou la. Hadoram da mɔr sanlima nɛ anzurifa nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug na tis o.

english_verse: Abishai the son of Zeruiah defeated the Edomite army in Salt Valley and killed
translation_verse: Abisai onɛ an Zeruyia biig la da kʋ Edom nidib tusa pii nɛ anii Yaarim Bɔn'ɔgin la.

english_verse: Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler. Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war. A List of David's Officials (
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab David zaŋ zabzabidib tuongatibi gu'ul Edom teŋ la wʋsa. Ka Edom nidib la lieb o sʋ'ʋlim nidib. Zugsɔb la da tis David paŋ, ka on keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa o nyaŋid nɛ. Na'ab David ninkpi'ema la yɛla

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Joab onɛ an Zeruyia biig la da sʋ'oe zabzabidib la; Jehosafat onɛ an Ahilud biig la da sʋ'oe gbana yɛla;

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
translation_verse: Zadok onɛ an Ahitub biig la nɛ Abimelek onɛ an Abiata biig la da an maanmaannib; ka Seraya mɛ an gbansɔbid;

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_verse: Benaya onɛ an Jehoyada biig la da sʋ'oe Keret dim nɛ Pelet dim. Ka David biribis la aan o na'ayikpɛm.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died. But when David's officials arrived at Ammon,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab David tɛn'ɛs ye, “M na maal Hanun onɛ an Nahas biig la pʋpielim wʋʋ o saamme mɛ da maalim pʋpielim si'em la.” Dinzug, o da tʋm nidib ye ba keŋ pʋ'ʋs Hanun saam kʋʋr la. David nidib la paae Ammon dim teŋin la ka keŋ Hanun san'an ye ba pʋ'ʋs o kʋʋr la.

english_verse: Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians.
translation_verse: Joab n da nyɛ ka zabzabidib la gilig o tuon nɛ o nya'aŋ wʋsa la, o gaans Israel zabzabidib banɛ an ninkpi'ema ka mi' zaba sʋ'ʋŋa la zi'eli ba gu' Aram dim la.

english_verse: Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king.
translation_verse: Li da paae saŋa si'a ka Ammon na'ab Nahas kpi, ka o biig Hanun dii o saam na'am.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_verse: Nidib banɛ wʋsa da la'as nɛ Hadadeze ka nyɛ ka Israel dim nyaŋi ba la, ba da mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm nɛ Israel dim ka liebi ba tʋmtʋmnib. Dinzug, Aram dim la da zɔ dabiem ka pʋ lɛn sʋŋ Ammon dim la ya'asɛ.

english_verse: the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
translation_verse: Ka Ammon dim kpɛɛmnam la yɛl Hanun onɛ aan ba zugdaan la ye, “Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye David na'as nɛ fʋ saam la ka tʋm nidib na ye ba pʋ'ʋsɛɛ? Ayei, fʋ zi' ye David tʋm o nidib la nɛ ye ba kena labisi gɔs teŋ la ka o ti kena zabi faaɛn lii?”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Alazug Hanun da gban'e David nidib la pʋni ba tiemis la ka maki ba gbina zinzema nwaasi ba fuud la bas ka kadi ba yis.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Ban da yɛl David yɛl kaŋa yɛla la, o da tʋm o tʋmtʋmnib ka ba tʋ'ʋsi ba, ban daa diisi ba nyan la zug. Ka ba yɛli ba ye, “Kpɛlimmi Jeriko teŋin ka ya tiemis la bus ka ya nyaan kul na.”

english_verse: David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army.
translation_verse: David n da wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la, o da tʋm Joab nɛ zabzabidib la wʋsa.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
translation_verse: Ka Ammon dim la yina, ti'eb zaba ti'ebʋgʋ ba teŋ la za'anɔɔrin, ka na'anam banɛ kena la la'asi zi'e sian'arin zin'ig yinne.

english_verse: Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites.
translation_verse: Ka zaŋ banɛ kpɛlim la niŋ Abisai onɛ aan o pitʋ la nu'ugin ka kɛ ka ba gu' Ammon dim la.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Joab da yɛl o ye, “Aram dim la ya'a kpi'emi gaadi m paŋ, li anɛ ye fʋ kena sʋŋim, amaa Ammon dim la ya'a kpi'emi gaadi fʋ paŋ, mam mɛ na kena sʋ'ʋŋif.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Zi'enim sʋ'ʋŋa ka kpɛ'ɛŋi fʋ sʋnf ka ti zabi ti nidib nɛ ti Wina'am teŋ la yɛla. Zugsɔb la na maal linɛ ka o mɛŋ bɔɔd.”

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them.
translation_verse: Ka Joab nɛ o nidib la keŋ tuonnɛ zab nɛ Aram dim la, ka ba zɔɔ widig.

english_verse: When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ammon dimi nyɛ ka Aram dim la zɔt la ka ba mɛ zɔɔ keŋ kpɛn' tempʋʋgin la ka bas Abisai. Ka Joab bas Ammon dim la zaba ka lɛb Jerusalem na.

english_verse: As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.
