translation_verse: Zina nɔɔ pu'ab banɛ an burikinnam ka bɛ Pesia nɛ Media sʋ'ʋlim la na wʋm Na'apu'a la maal si'el la, ka ba mɛ na niŋ ala tisi ba sidib banɛ an burikinnam la. Li na kɛ ka na'asi nɛ nɔɔr yinne naae teŋgbauŋ kaŋa ni.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: “Alazug, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siak, fʋn sɔm gbauŋ ka tik nu'ug ka kɛ ka li lieb wada Pesia nɛ Media teŋin ye, Vasiti kʋ lɛn kɛn Na'ab tuon naa, ka faaɛn o na'am la tis onɛ sɔn'ɔ o.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Na'aba, fʋn ya'a niŋ ala ka li tiigi fʋ teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa, pu'ab la na tisi ba sidib girima lin pin'il tadimnamin ti keŋ paae kpi'emnamin la.”

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: O da sɔb gbana tis o sʋ'ʋlim la bɛn wʋsa, ka tɛɛns wʋsa di'e li ka li sɔbi ba mɛŋ buudi pian'adin, yɛti ba ye dau wʋsa na sʋ'ʋg o mɛŋ yidim.

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Lina nya'aŋ, Na'ab Zeesis sʋnfʋ yʋ'ʋn da ma'ae la, o da tiɛn Vasiti n da maal si'el nɛ on gban'e si'el o yɛla.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: O na'ayikpɛm banɛ da sa'an o la da yɛl ye, “Naa, kɛl ka ba iee paam pu'asadbanɛ zi' dau na tisif.

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka Na'ab gaans kpɛɛmnam zin'ig wʋsa ka ba zi'en o nɔba zugʋ gaans pu'asadvɛnla mɔri kɛn Susa teŋin na. Naa, kɛl ka fʋ tʋmtʋm onɛ ka ba fuo o ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Hegai ka o gur pu'ab la sʋ'oe ba ka gɔti ba vɛnlim yɛla.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Ka kɛ ka pu'asadir kanɛ ka Na'ab ya'am kpɛn' la di'e Vasiti zin'igi lieb na'apu'a.” Sa'al kaŋa da malis Na'ab la ka o sid da niŋ ala.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka Jew nid da bɛ Susa teŋin, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Modekaya, ka o saam yʋ'ʋr buon Jair ka o yaanam an Simie nɛ Kis. O da anɛ Benjamin dɔɔg nid.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Babilon Na'ab Nebukadnɛza da gban'e Juda Na'ab Jehoyakim nɛ o nidibi yi Jerusalem kena maali ba yammis la, o da anɛ ba nid yinne.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Ban da mɔɔl Na'ab la tɔlʋŋ zin'ig wʋsa la, ba da mɔr pu'asada bɛdegʋ kɛn Susa teŋin na ka Hegai guri ba. Ba mɛ da mɔr Esta n kɛn Na'ab la yin na mɛ gu'ul Hegai onɛ da gur zin'ikanɛ ka pu'ab la'asi bɛ la.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: O nini da tig Esta ka o bɔɔd o yɛla hali. Linzug o da bɔ duorim la'adi tis o, nɛ disʋma linɛ bɛɛ li kɔn'. O da gaans bipumis ayɔpɔi yi na'ayin la ye ba gɔsid o yɛla, ka nɔk on nɛ o tʋmtʋm bipumis la bɛ zin'isi'a la tɔɔm niŋ zin'isʋŋin.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Esta da pʋ pa'al o buudi nɛ o tuŋʋ bɔzugɔ, Modekaya da pʋ siak ye o niŋ alaa.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Daar wʋsa Modekaya da kaalim pu'ab la bɛ zin'isi'a la gɔsid Esta an si'em nɛ ban maan o si'em.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Pu'asadir ya'a na kpɛn' Na'ab Zeesis san'an, asɛɛ ka ba dɛŋin nɔk nwadis pii nɛ ayi' maal o ka o vɛnl wʋʋ ban pa'al si'em la. Ba na zaŋ nwadis ayuobʋ suoɛn o kpaam nɛ tiim linɛ ka ba buon mir la, ka lɛn nɔk nwadis ayuobʋ kanɛ kpɛlim la niŋ o tudaari nɛ li buudi wʋsa.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Pu'asadir ya'a da ye o yi pu'asada la bɛ zin'isi'a la kpɛn' Na'ab la san'an ka yɛl ye o bɔɔd si'el wʋsa, ba nɔkid nɛ tisid o ka o mɔri ken Na'ab la dɔɔgin.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: O ɛɛnti kpɛn' nɛ Na'ab la san'an zaam, ka lɛb bɛkɛung na tɔɔm zin'isi'a pu'ab la zin'igin la, ka kpɛm bɛ Saasgas onɛ ka ba fuo o ka o gɔt pu'abibis la nu'ugin. Pu'asadir la kʋ lɛn lɛb Na'ab la san'anɛ ya'a ka' o ya'am ti lɛb o san'an ka o buol o yʋ'ʋr ye ba mɔr o naa.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Na'ab la ya'am da kpɛn' Esta gaad pu'ab la wʋsa, ka o zug di Na'ab la gat pu'asada banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa. Ka o nɔk na'am zupibigi pid o zug ka faaɛn Vasiti na'am la diis o.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la maal diib bɛdegʋ Esta na'am diib yɛla tis nidib la wʋsa, la'an nɛ o ya'am dim nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa. O da mɔɔl vʋ'ʋsʋm dabisire tis o sʋ'ʋlim nidib la wʋsa ka tis nidib la piinsʋma bɛdegʋ. Modekaya tilig na'ab la nyɔɔr

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Ban da lɛn la'as pu'asada la, Modekaya da zin'inɛ Na'ab la zɔŋŋin.

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: Amaa Esta da pʋ pa'al o buudi nɛ o tuŋ yɛla wʋʋ Modekaya da sa'al o si'em la, bɔzugɔ o da nan kpɛm mɔr sa'al kanɛ ka Modekaya da sa'al o wʋʋ on da nan ugus o saŋsi'a la.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Bigitana nɛ Teris da bɛɛ ani, ka an Na'ab la kpɛɛmnam banɛ gur za'anɔɔr linɛ kpɛn'ɛd la. Saŋa kanɛ ka Modekaya da zin' Na'ab la zɔŋŋin la, ba sʋnf da duoe hali ka ba gban'e ye ba kʋ Na'ab Zeesis.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Modekaya da wʋm ban gban'e si'em la ka yɛl Esta, ka on mɛ nɔki yɛl Na'ab la, ka li kɛ ka Modekaya paam yʋ'ʋr.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Ka ban da vɛɛnsi nyɛ ka li an sida la, ba da yul nidib ayi' la nɛ nwiisi kʋ. Nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa da sɔbi niŋ Na'anam Labaya Gbana la ni Na'ab la nini ni.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Nɛ' wʋsa nya'aŋ la Na'ab Zeesis da na'as Haman onɛ an Hamedata biig ka an Agag buudi la ka tis o kpɛŋ ka li gaad kpɛɛm banɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye banɛ bɛ zɔŋŋin la wʋsa iginim o tuon ka tis o girima. Ba wʋsa da niŋid ala, amaa Modekaya ma'aa da zan'as ka pʋ iginidi tisid o girimaa.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Ka o taaba la da bu'os o ye, “Bɔzugʋ kɛ ka fʋ pʋ siak ye fʋ dɔl Na'ab la tis nɔsi'a la?”

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ ban da pian'adi tisid Modekaya li yɛla la daar wʋsa la, o da pʋ tiak o pʋtɛn'ɛrɛ. Alazug, ba da yɛl Haman li yɛla ye ba gɔs ye o na siaki bas Modekaya ka o kpɛm bɛ ala bɛɛ o kʋ siakɛ? Bɔzugɔ o da yɛli ba ye o anɛ Jew.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Haman da baŋ ye Modekaya pʋ bɔɔd ye o igin o tuon bɛɛ tis o girima la, o sʋnf da duoe nɛ hali.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: On da baŋ Modekaya nidib la an ninsieba buudi la o da pʋ siak ye o kʋ Modekaya ma'aanɛ, amaa ka ieed suokanɛ na kʋ on nɛ o nimbanɛ an Jew dim la wʋsa, Na'ab Zeesis sʋ'ʋlimin la wʋsa.

english_verse: It was now the twelfth year of the rule of King Xerxes. During Nisan, the first month of the year, Haman said, “Find out the best time for me to do this.” The time chosen was Adar, the twelfth month.
translation_verse: Zeesis na'am la yʋma pii nɛ ayi' saŋa, nwadig kanɛ an yiiga ka ba buonnɛ li Nisan la ni, ka ba da maal pur Haman tuon ye ba gaŋ dabisir nɛ nwadig kanɛ ka ba na kʋ Jew dim la, ka li keŋ lu nwadig pii nɛ ayi' linɛ ka ba buon Ada la zug, li dabpiiga nɛ atan' daar.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Haman da yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Naa, ninsieba bɛ kpɛla ka ba malima bɛɛ li kɔn', ka ba gɛndig nɛ fʋ nidib sʋ'ʋlimin la wʋsa; ba anɛ banɛ pʋ siaki dɔlli fʋ wada laa. Na'aba, li pʋ sʋm ye fʋ kɛ ka nimbama bɛ teŋ kaŋa nii.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'a na siak, fʋn tisim nɔɔr ka ba kʋʋ ba, ka m na nɔk anzurifa ligidi bɛdegʋ niŋ na'am ligidi suak zin'igi tis banɛ yii kʋʋ ba la.”

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Na'ab la da fuoe o nu'ubil tikir baŋi yis o nu'ugin tis Haman onɛ da an Jew dim dataa la. O da anɛ Hamedata biig ka an Agag buudi.

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Haman ye, o kɛl ligidi la, ka lɛɛ maal nidib la wʋʋ on gban'e ye o niŋi ba si'em la.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Yiiga nwadig la ni, li dabpiiga nɛ atan' la daar, ba da la'as teŋ la gbansɔbidib la wʋsa. Ba da sɔb gbana tis o sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa, nɛ Gɔmenanam nɛ tɛɛns la tuongatib nɛ kpɛɛmnam wʋsa, ka tɛɛns wʋsa di'e li ka li sɔbi ba mɛŋ sɔbirin, nɛ buudi la wʋsa mɛŋ pian'adin, ka li pa'al Haman n gban'e ye ba tʋm si'em. Ba da sɔb nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa nɛ Na'ab Zeesis yʋ'ʋr ka nɔk o mɛŋ nu'ug baŋ la tiki li zug.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Ba da tʋm nidib ka ba mɔri keŋ tis sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa. Pian'akanɛ da bɛ gbauŋʋn la da yɛti ba ye nwadkanɛ paas pii nɛ ayi' la ni, li dabpiiga nɛ atan' daar, ba kʋʋm Jew dim la na'akim nɛ pu'asada nɛ ninkʋda, la'an nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis wʋsa ka faaɛn ba la'ad la wʋsa.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Labaya dim la da zi Na'ab la wada la keŋ mɔɔl Susa tempʋʋgin mɔɔli gilig. Din saŋa la, Na'ab la nɛ Haman da zin'inɛ nuud daam, amaa Susa teŋ la da pɛ'ɛl nɛ tʋkpiidʋg.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Modekaya wʋm ban gban'e si'em la, o sʋnf san'amnɛ hali ka o aans o fuud ka yɛ bɔtkɛɛnd ka nɔk tampɛligim bug, sʋnsa'aŋ la zug, ka kpɛn' teŋ la pʋʋgini kaasid agɔla gɔla nɛ nimmua.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: Amaa o da paae Na'ab la yaŋirini tir, bɔzugɔ sɔ' ya'a yɛ bɔtkɛɛnd fuud, ba pʋ siakid ka o kpɛn'ɛda.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Zin'ikanɛ wʋsa ka Na'ab la tik gbauŋ si'a la paae, Jew dim la da kpɛn' nɛ kukuma ka lɔ nɔɔr ka kaasid ka ki'ed kuŋ. Ba bɛdegʋ da yɛnɛ bɔtkɛɛnd ka nɔk tampɛligim bugi ba mɛŋ.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Esta zak biis la nɛ dap banɛ da gur o la da kena yɛl o Modekaya yɛla la ka o sʋnf da san'am hali. Ka o tis fuud ye ba keŋ tis Modekaya ka o yɛ ka bas bɔtkɛɛnd la, amaa o da zan'as nɛ ka pʋ di'e fuud laa.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Esta da buol Hatak onɛ ka Na'ab la gaŋ ye o gur o la, ka tʋm o ye o kem bu'os Modekaya linɛ daamid o, nɛ linɛ niŋ.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatak da yii keŋ Modekaya san'an Na'ab la yaŋir la tuon.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Ka Modekaya yɛl o linɛ maal la wʋsa, la'an nɛ Haman n gban'e ye ba ya'a sid nyaŋi kʋ Jew dim la wʋsa o na yɔ ligidi niŋ ban su'ad Na'ab la ligidi zin'isi'a la.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Modekaya mɛ da nɔk gbauŋ kanɛ ka ba sɔb Jew dim la yɛla ka ba karimi li Susa teŋin la tis Hatak ye o keŋ pa'al Esta, ka yɛl o ye o mɔɔm ka yɛl Esta ka o keŋ Na'ab la san'ani bɛllim o ye o zɔmi o nidib la nimbaanlig.

english_verse: Hathach went back to Esther and told her what Mordecai had said.
translation_verse: Hatak da lɛbi yɛl Esta Modekaya yɛl si'el la.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: “Na'ayikpɛm la nɛ nimbanɛ wʋsa bɛ teŋ la sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa mi' ye dau bɛɛ pu'a pʋ kpɛn'ɛd Na'ab la zɔŋŋin ka li ya'a ka' ye o buol o nɛ. Onɛ niŋ ala, asɛɛ ka ba kʋʋ o. Linɛ na faanf anɛ Na'ab la na ʋk o sanlima dansaar la tiel ka fʋ gban'e. Amaa dabpistan' linɛ gaad la wʋsa, Na'ab la pʋ buolim ka m kpɛn' o san'anɛ.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Ban da nɔk Esta labaar la yɛl Modekaya la,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Modekaya da lɛbis ye ba kem yɛl o ye, “Da tɛn'ɛs ye fʋn bɛ na'ayin la zug, ba na kʋ Jew dim la wʋsa ka fʋn pɔnsɛ.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Nannanna fʋ ya'a sin, Jew dim la yɔlisim tun'e yi zin'isi'a na, amaa fʋn nɛ fʋ saam yidim na san'am. Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ mi' linɛ zugʋ kɛ ka fʋ bɛ na'am zin'igin saŋa kaŋa?”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ka Esta lɛbis labaar ye ba kem yɛl Modekaya ye,

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Kem la'as Jew dim banɛ bɛ Susa teŋin wʋsa ka ya lɔ nɔɔri sɔsi m yɛla. Da di bɛɛ nu si'el yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ wʋsa daba atan'. Man nɛ m zak biis la mɛ na lɔ nɔɔr nɛ ya. Ti ya'a niŋ ala naae, m na keŋ Na'ab la san'an la'an nɛ lin pʋ dɔl suor la. Ka m ya'a lɛn kpi li naanɛ.”

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Modekaya da keŋ niŋ wʋʋ Esta pa'al o si'em la.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Daba atan' la nya'aŋ, Esta da yɛɛ o na'am fuugʋ kpɛn' na'ayir la pʋʋgʋ zi'en Na'ab la zɔŋ za'anɔɔr tuon. Na'ab la da zin' nɛ o na'am gbauŋ zug dɔɔg la pʋʋgin ka o nindaa kpa' zɔŋ la za'anɔɔr la.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: On da nyɛ Esta ka o zi'e zakin la, Na'ab la ya'am da kpɛn' o ka o ziank o sanlima dansaar linɛ ka o zanl la tiel o san'an na. Ka Esta paae o tuonnɛ si'isi li zug la.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da bu'os ye, “Esta, yɛlim fʋn bɔɔd si'el? Hali baa li zem nɛ m sʋ'ʋlim la pʋsʋkɔ, m na tisif.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ka Esta lɛbis o ye, “Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siakin, fʋn nɛ Haman naan kɛɛn na di dikanɛ ka m maal ye m tisif la.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl ye, “Mɔri Haman tɔ'ɔtɔ na ka ti niŋ Esta bɔɔd si'el la.” Dinzug Na'ab la nɛ Haman da keŋ ye ba di dikanɛ ka Esta maal la.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Ban da bɛɛ ani nuud daam la, ka Na'ab la maligim yɛl Esta ye, “Yʋ'ʋn yɛlimim fʋn bɔɔd ye m maal si'eli tisif, ka m na maal. Bɔ kimm ka fʋ bɔɔda? Hali baa fʋn bɔɔd si'el la ya'a zem nɛ m sʋ'ʋlim la pʋsʋk m na tisif.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a sid nɔŋim yɛla ka mɛ sid na maal man bɔɔd si'eli tisim, fʋn nɛ Haman kem bɛog na di dikanɛ ka m ye m maali tisi ya la. Ka m saa na gandig fʋn bu'osid man bɔɔd si'el la yɛla.” Haman sʋnf duoe nɛ Modekaya

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Haman da yina ka o sʋnf ma'ae nɛ hali. Amaa on da nyɛ Modekaya ka o zi'e Na'ab la za'anɔɔrin ka pʋ duoe zi'en ka kirid nɛ dabiem on Haman tuon la, o sʋnf da duoe nɛ Modekaya hali pamm.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, Haman da nyaŋi gban'e o mɛŋ ka yii kul. Ka buol o zuanamɛ la'as nɛ o pu'a onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Zeres la,

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: ka nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg nɛ on mɔr arezak si'em nɛ o biisi zem si'em nɛ Na'ab la na'asid o si'em ka tis o kpɛuŋʋ gaad o taaba banɛ wʋsa bɛ na'ayin la.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Haman da lɛn yɛli ba ye, “Ka' lin ma'aanɛ, man ma'aa ka Na'ab pu'a Esta buoli paas Na'ab la zug ka ti keŋ di dikanɛ ka o maali tis Na'ab la, ka lɛm buol man nɛ Na'ab la bɛog ya'as.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Amaa nɛ' wʋsa pʋ niŋim malisim, man nyɛ ka Modekaya zin' Na'ab la za'anɔɔr tuon la.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la Na'ab la da pʋ gbisɛ, ka kɛ ka ba nɔk gbambanɛ ka ba sɔbid yɛla digin ka ba buon Na'anam Tiɛnr Gbana la, ye ba mɔr na karim ka o wʋm.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os ye, “Modekaya da niŋ anwana la, yɔɔd bɛɛ girimbɔ ka ba tis o?” Ka o na'ayikpɛm la lɛbis ye, “Ba da pʋ maal si'eli tis oo.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la bu'os ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ bɛ zakin la?” Saŋkan mɛn ka Haman mɛ kpɛn' ye o yɛl Na'ab la ka o kɛ ka ba yul Modekaya dawa'ama banɛ ka o ba' la zugʋ kʋʋ o.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Na'ab nidib la da lɛbis o ye, “Li anɛ Haman n zi'e zakin la.” Ka Na'ab yɛl ye, “Kɛlli ka o kpɛn' na.”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Ka Haman kpɛn' na ka Na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka ti na maali tis onɛ ka Na'ab gban'e ye o tis o girima la?” Haman da tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, “Anɔ'ɔn ka Na'ab nɔŋi paae mam, ka bɔɔd ye o tisi o sɔb girima ka li ya'a ka' manɛ?”

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,
translation_verse: O da lɛbis Na'ab la ye, “Onɛ ka Na'ab bɔɔd ye o tis o girima la,

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: ba nɔkim na'am fukanɛ ka Na'ab mi' yɛ nɛ wiedkanɛ ka o mi' ban', ka na'am baŋ bɛɛ o zugin la.

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la yɛl Haman ye, “Tɔ'! Kem tɔ'ɔtɔ nɔk na'am fuug nɛ wief la niŋ wʋʋ fʋn yɛl si'em la nɔɔ tis Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid ka zin' m zɔŋŋin la. Bʋmbanɛ ka fʋ kaal la wʋsa mid ka fʋ bas baa yinne.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Haman sid da nɔk fuug la ka lɔ wief la. O da bɔb Modekaya nɛ fuug la ka ban'al o wief la zugʋ giligid teŋ la ka kɛ ka ba yɛt nidib la ye, “Na'abi maal si'eli nwa' tis onɛ ka o gban'e ye o tis o girima la!”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Modekaya da giligi naae ka lɛb Na'ab la zɔŋŋin na. Amaa Haman da zaŋ si'eli lus o nindaa lɛb tɔ'ɔtɔ kul nɛ nyan,

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: ka yɛl o pu'a Zeres nɛ o zuanam la linɛ wʋsa maal o. Banɛ sa'an o la nɛ o pu'a Zeres da yɛl o ye, “Fʋn nɛ Modekaya onɛ kpa' taab la an Jew nid la zug, fʋ ye fʋ ba'asi lu nɛ. Fʋ lɛn ka' onɛ na nyaŋ o, asɛɛ fʋ ba'asi san'am!”

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Ban da nan pian'ad nɛ o la, Na'ab la sankpan'asnam da kena ye ba dɔl Haman tɔ'ɔtɔ kɛn dikanɛ ka Esta maal ka buon o la zin'igin na.

english_verse: The king and Haman were dining with Esther
translation_verse: Na'ab la nɛ Haman da keŋ ye ba la'am di nɛ Esta.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Ban da nan bɛɛ ani nuud daam la, Na'ab la da lɛm bu'os Na'apu'a Esta ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔda? Yɛlim ka m na tisif, hali baa li ya'a zem wʋʋ man sʋ'ʋlim la pʋsʋk gba fʋ na nyɛ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Na'apu'a Esta da lɛbis ye, “Naa, fʋ ya'a sid siak ye fʋ na tisim man sɔs si'eli fʋ san'an, alaa mam bɔɔd si'el anɛ ye fʋ sʋŋim ka m nyɔvʋr da san'am ka mɛ faanm nidib la bas.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ ba kuos man nɛ m nidib la tis ye ba mugusi ti ka kʋʋ ti wʋsa. Ba ya'a kuosini ti wʋʋ yammis, m sinnin nɛ, bɔzugɔ lin pʋ siak ye m daam Na'aba.”

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Na'ab Zeesis da bu'os o ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ la? Dau kanɛ ye o tʋm tʋʋm kan la bɛ yaanɛ?”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Ka Esta lɛbis ye, “Nimbɛ'og onɛ kisi ti ka mɔɔdi ti yɛla anɛ Haman, onɛ zin' nwa'.” Ka dabiem kpɛn' Haman, Na'ab la nɛ Esta tuon.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da sʋnf da duoe hali ka o duoe ka bas o daam la ka keŋ kpɛn' na'ayir lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la. Amaa Haman n da baŋ ye Na'ab la pʋn kʋʋs o yɛla bɛ'ɛd la, ka kpɛm bɛllim Esta o nyɔvʋr yɛla.

english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da naan lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la lɛbi kpɛn' on pa'a zin' si'eli nuud daam la ka nyɛ ka Haman bilim Esta nɔba ni on dig sɔŋ si'a zug la. Na'ab la da tans nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, “Fʋ maan pu'ana'ab la nɛ anwaa, la'an nɛ man bɛ yin kpɛla laa?” Na'ab la ti ye o pian' naae la, ka ba pʋn pin' Haman nindaa ka li pa'al ye ba kʋʋs o bɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Dinzug ba da nɔk Haman n keŋ yul dakanɛ ka o da ba'a zi'el ye o yul Modekaya la. Ka Na'ab la sʋnf nyaan niŋ lamm.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Daakan nɔɔ Na'ab la da nɔk Haman onɛ an Jew dim dataa la sʋ'oe zin'isi'a teŋin la tis Esta. Ka Modekaya paae Na'ab la tuon, bɔzugɔ Esta da pa'al ban kpin si'em.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da pʋn dɛŋim pidig o nu'ug tikir baŋ la yis Haman san'an, ka yʋ'ʋn nɔki li tis Modekaya. Ka Esta kɛ ka o sʋ'ʋg zin'ikanɛ ka Haman da sʋ'oe la wʋsa.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Esta da lɛn vanbin Na'ab la nɔba nii kum ka bɛllim o ye gban'abɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka Haman onɛ an Agag buudi la gban'e zaŋi keŋ Jew dim la yɛla la, kɛl ka li kpi.

english_verse: King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther,
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tiɛn o sanlima dansaar la ka Esta si'isi li ka duoe zi'en o tuon.

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: O da ye, “Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siak, ka gɔs ka li nar, ka fʋ sʋnf mɛ sid malis nɛ mam, fʋn sɔm ka tiki fʋ nu'ug ka li kpiis gban'ar kanɛ ka Haman onɛ an Hamedata biig ka an Agag buudi gban'e ka sɔb ye o san'am Jew dim banɛ bɛ sʋ'ʋlim kaŋa ni wʋsa la.

english_verse: and I can't bear to see my people and my own relatives destroyed.”
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ man ye m niŋ wala bɛ ka gɔti m nidib nɛ m du'adib ka ba san'amida?”

english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Na'ab Zeesis da yɛl Na'apu'a Esta nɛ Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la ye, “Haman n zabid nɛ Jew dim la zug, m nɔk o zin'ig la tis Esta ka kɛ ka ba yul o daug zugʋ kʋ.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Amaa linɛ sɔb nɛ Na'ab la yʋ'ʋr ka tik nɛ o nu'ug baŋ zanbin la, si'el kae na tiaki lii. Tɔ', nannanna maligim sɔb wada si'a ya'as nɛ man Na'ab la yʋ'ʋr ka tiki li nɛ m nu'ug tikir baŋ la, ka zi'el yanamɛ bɔɔd si'em zaŋi ken Jew dim la yɛla.”

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Modekaya da nɔk nɛ Na'ab la yʋ'ʋri sɔb ka nɔk o nu'ug tikir baŋi tik, ka nɔki tis banɛ ban'ad na'am widi banɛ ka ba zamisi ba ka mi' zɔɔb sʋ'ʋŋa la ye mɔr gbana la keŋi tɔd.

english_verse: In these letters the king said: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies. A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis nɔsi'a la da lieb nɛ zi'elʋg sʋ'ʋlim la wʋsa ni, ka ba kɛ ka li paae nidib la ka buudi wʋsa baŋ, ka li kɛ ka Jew dim la wʋsa ti'eb dabiskan daare yɔɔ ba bi'emnam sam.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Modekaya da yi Na'ab la san'an ka yɛ na'am fuug linɛ an bʋlʋ nɛ bʋmpielig, ka sanlima baŋ tita'ar pil o zugin, ka o nɔk pien zɛn'ug linɛ ʋg nɛ gum sʋŋʋ vil o mɛŋ. Ka Susa teŋ nidib la da di'em nɛ sumalisim.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Jew dim la san'an li da anɛ sumalisim nɛ sumpielim nɛ zusʋŋ nɛ girimtita'ari tisi ba.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Teŋ la sʋ'ʋlim nɛ li tempʋʋs la, zin'ikanɛ wʋsa ka Na'ab la nɔzi'elʋg la paae, Jew dim la wʋsa da mɔr nɛ sumalisim ka ba maan diib nɛ di'ema. Ka buudi bɛdegʋ banɛ ka' Jew dim la muki ba mɛŋi lieb Jew dim buudi bɔzugɔ Jew dim la yɛla da kpɛn'ɛsi ba nɛ dabiem.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Nwadkanɛ paasid pii nɛ ayi' ka ba buon Ada la, li dabis pii nɛ atan' la daar, ka ba da ye ba nɔk Na'ab la tis nɔsi'a la tʋm. Daakan la Jew dim la dataas la da tɛn'ɛs ye ba na nyaŋi ba, amaa li da tulig nɛ ka Jew dim la lɛɛ nyaŋi ba dataas la.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Jew dim la da la'as taaba ban bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa Na'ab Zeesis sʋ'ʋlimin la ye ba zab nɛ banɛ mɔɔdi ba san'auŋ yɛla la, sɔ' kae da nyaŋi zi'en nɛ ba, bɔzugɔ buudi la wʋsa da zɔti ba nɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Nimbɛda banɛ da bɛ teŋin la wʋsa, nɛ Gɔmenanam nɛ tuongatib nɛ na'ayir kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa da kpɛn'ɛd nɛ Jew dim la zug, bɔzugɔ ba wʋsa da zɔti Modekaya dabiem.

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.
translation_verse: Modekaya yʋ'ʋn da lieb nintita'ar na'ayin la, ka o yʋ'ʋr tiig teŋ la wʋsa, ka o paŋ paasid daar wʋsa.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Jew dim la da san'am ka kʋʋ ba dataas la wʋsa nɛ sʋ'ʋg, ka maal banɛ kisi ba la wʋsa ban bɔɔd si'em.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Banɛ da kpi Susa tempʋʋgin la, ba da yɛl Na'ab la daakan nɔɔ.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Na'apu'a Esta ye, “Jew dim la kʋ dap kɔbisnu nɛ Haman biis piiga Susa tempʋʋgin la. Ka ba yʋ'ʋn maal wala sʋ'ʋlim bama la ni? Nannanna fʋ bɔɔdim an bɔ? Sɔsim ka fʋ na nyɛ. Bɔ ka fʋ bɔɔd ye m lɛm maali tisi fɔ? Yɛlim ka m na maali tisif.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Esta da lɛbis ye, “Naa, Na'aba, fʋ ya'a na siak, fʋn tisim Jew dim banɛ bɛ Susa la nɔɔr ka bɛog ba saa na tʋm wʋʋ ban pa'a tʋm kpɛla zina si'em la, ka yul Haman biis piiga la daba'ada la zug.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye ba sid niŋ ala, ka ba da bas nɔɔr la Susa teŋin. Ka ba ya'al Haman biis piiga la daba'ada la zug.

english_verse: Then on the fourteenth day of Adar the Jews of the city got together and killed
translation_verse: Jew dim banɛ bɛ Susa teŋin la da la'as Ada nwadig la dabis pii nɛ anaasi daare kʋ dap kɔbistan' amaa ka pʋ nɔki ba nu'ugi si'isi ba laukɔ.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa da niŋnɛ Ada nwadig la dabis pii nɛ atan' daar, ka dabis pii nɛ anaasi daar la ka ba nɔki vʋ'ʋs ka li an diib nɛ di'ema dabisir. Purim Di'ema Malʋŋ

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Jew dim banɛ da bɛ Susa la on da la'as taaba nɛ dabis pii nɛ atan' nɛ pii nɛ anaasi la daar ka nɔk dabis pii nɛ anu daar la vʋ'ʋs ka li an diib nɛ di'ema daar.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Linɛ kɛ ka Jew dim banɛ bɛ teŋkpɛmis la nɔk Ada nwadig la dabis pii nɛ anaasi daar ka li an sumalisim nɛ diib dabisir nɛ dabiskanɛ ka ba tisid taaba piini.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Modekaya da sɔb bʋmbama digil ka tɔlim gbana tis Jew dim banɛ bɛ Na'ab Zeesis teŋin la wʋsa, banɛ bɛ yamma bɛɛ lalli,

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: ye o kɛ ka ba nɔk Ada nwadig dabis pii nɛ anaasi nɛ pii nɛ anu daar la wʋsa ka li an di'ema dabisa tisi ba,

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: pa'an saŋa kanɛ ka Jew dim la paam yɔlisim yii ba dataas nu'usin la, nɛ nwadkanɛ ka ba sʋnsa'aŋ lieb sumalisim, ka ba kukuma lieb la'ad. O da sɔbi tisi ba ye ba mɔ ka dabisban la, ba na dit ka maan sumalisim ka tisid taaba diib ka tisid nɔŋ dim piini.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Jew dim la siak ye ba na maan ala saŋa wʋsa wʋʋ ban pin'il si'em la, ka tʋm wʋʋ Modekaya n sɔb si'em tisi ba la.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ Haman onɛ saamme an Hamedata ka o an Agag buudi ka an Jew dim dataa la da gban'e bɛ'ɛd ka maal pur linɛ an bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm ye o baŋ dabiskanɛ ka o na san'am Jew dim la.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Amaa Esta da keŋ Na'ab la san'an la, Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye gban'abɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka Haman gban'e Jew dim la yɛla la na lɛb o mɛŋ zugin, ka ye on nɛ o biis la, ba na yuli ba nɛ dabanɛ ka o ba'a la zug.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Dinzug ba da buon dabisban ye, Purim ka li yinɛ pian'ʋk kanɛ ka ba buon pur la ni na. Bʋn linɛ wʋsa sɔb gbauŋʋn la nɛ ban nyɛ si'el nɛ linɛ maal la zug

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Alazug Na'apu'a Esta onɛ an Abihel biig la nɛ Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la da sɔb nɛ kpi'euŋʋ paas gbauŋ kanɛ paasida ayi' la zaŋi ken Purim la yɛla.

english_verse: Copies of this letter were sent to Jews in the
translation_verse: Modekaya da tɔlim gbana la tis Jew dim banɛ bɛ Na'ab Zeesis sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛns kɔbiga nɛ pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (

english_verse: provinces of King Xerxes. In the letter they said: We pray that all of you will live in peace and safety.
translation_verse: ) la ni wʋsa. Linɛ da sɔb gbauŋʋn la da anɛ pian'asʋma ka yɛt ye ba zi'e ba nya'aŋ.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: Ka ye ba mɔɔm ka Purim dabisa la zi'en wʋʋ lin nar si'em ka dɔl wʋʋ Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la nɛ Na'apu'a Esta gban'e si'em tisi ba la, nɛ ban zi'eli li si'em tisi ba mɛŋ nɛ ba yaas dɔl wʋʋ saŋa kanɛ ka ba lɔɔd nɔɔr ka maan sʋnsa'aŋ la.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Esta gban'ar la da kɛ ka Purim malima la zi'en, ka ba sɔbi li niŋ gbana nii digil.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Na'ab Zeesis da tis nɔɔr ye teŋ la nidib wʋsa yɔ lampɔ keŋ paae teŋ la wʋsa bɛn.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: O paŋ nɛ kpi'euŋ tʋʋma linɛ tʋm wʋsa la'an nɛ kpi'euŋ kanɛ wʋsa ka Modekaya da mɔr ka li anɛ Na'ab la ziank o paae ani la, ba mɛ da sɔbi li wʋsa niŋ Media nɛ Pesia na'anam la gbana la ni.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Modekaya onɛ an Jew nid la da tia'al Na'ab Zeesis nya'aŋ, ka gat Jew dim la wʋsa, ka o taaba banɛ an Jew dim la tisid o girima bɛdegʋ, bɔzugɔ o da tʋm sʋ'ʋm tis o nidib la, ka pian'adi bɔɔd sʋ'ʋm ba bɛog yɛla.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Dau sɔ' da bɛ Uz teŋin ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Job. Dau nwa' da anɛ ninvʋsʋŋ ka ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, ka mɛ an pʋʋg yinne sɔb. O da anɛ onɛ zɔt Wina'am ka kis dinɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la bu'os Sʋntaana ye, “Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?” Ka o gandig ye, “Man yinɛ teŋgbauŋʋn la na, ka bɛɛ anina giligid zin'is wʋsa.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: O biribis la da ɛɛnti maannɛ di'ema ba yaan la ti kaligi ba ya' la wʋsa; ka buoli ba tanp la ka ba kena di ka nu nɛ ba.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Ba di'ema dabisa la ya'a gaad, Job na tʋm buoli ba ka maali ba nyain. O da ɛɛn tɛn'ɛs o sʋʋnrin ye, daasi'erɛɛ o biis la pa'ati tɛn'ɛs pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd Wina'am yɛla. Dinzug, o da ɛɛn duonɛ bɛkɛungʋ maal maan linɛ nyu'od bugum o biis la yinne-yinne zug. Sʋntaana dɛŋi mak Job la yɛla

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka Wina'am biis la'as ye ba zaŋi ba mɛŋi pa'al Wina'am, ka Sʋntaana mɛ paasi ba zug.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am bu'os o ye, “Fʋ tiɛn m tʋmtʋm Job yɛlaa? Ninsaal ka' teŋgbauŋ nwa' zugʋ nwɛnɛ o. O anɛ ninvʋsʋŋ ka ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, ka mɛ an pʋʋg yinne sɔb. O anɛ onɛ zɔt mam Wina'am ka kis dinɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.”

english_verse: “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked.
translation_verse: Ka Sʋntaana lɛbis Wina'am ye, “Di anɛ zaalim ka Job zɔt fʋn Na'awinnɛɛ?

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Mɛ fʋ zaŋi gu'udi gu' on nɛ o yidim nɛ on mɔr si'el wʋsa? Fʋ mɛ niŋ o zug bareka ka o pɛ'ɛs nɛ niigi du'a pɛ'ɛl teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Tiɛnmi fʋ nu'ugʋ san'am o mɔrim la wʋsa ka fʋ na nyɛ ka o ki'isi fʋ, fʋ nifin.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Sʋntaana ye, “Tɔ', on mɔr si'el wʋsa la bɛɛ fʋ nu'ugin, amaa mid ka fʋ si'is o mɛŋ.”

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Daar yinne ka Job biribis nɛ o bipumis mɔri ba di'ema o bikpɛɛm la yinne dit ka nuud,

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: ka sɔ' kɛn Job san'an na yɛl o ye, “Na'akuoda la bɛɛn nɛ anina kuod ka bʋmis la ɔnbid mɔɔd anina baba

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: ka Seba dim libigi ba kadi ba wʋsa keŋ. Ba kʋ tʋmtʋmnib la wʋsa, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: On nan bɛɛ anina pian'ad la ka nid yinne lɛm paae na ye, “Bugum naan agɔla li na kanb pɛ'ɛs la nɛ fʋ tʋmtʋmnib la wʋsa, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: On nan bɛɛ anina pian'ad la ka yinne mɛ zɔɔ paae na ye, “Kaldea dimi la'as taab zin'is atan' kpɛm bʋʋl na kadi fʋ yʋgʋma la wʋsa keŋ ka kʋʋ fʋ tʋmtʋmnib la wʋsa, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: On nan bɛɛ anina pian'ad la ka nid yinne lɛm paae na yɛl ye, “Fʋ na'akim nɛ fʋ bipumis la bɛ nɛ fʋ bikpɛɛm la yinnɛ maan di'ema dit ka nuud,

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: ka sisi'etita'ar naam pipirigin na kpɛn gubil yir la ka li luu bʋʋli ba ka ba kpi, ka mam ma'aa pɔns ka kena ye m yɛlif!”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Ka Job duoe aans o fuud ka pʋn o zug ye o pa'al o sʋnsa'aŋi an si'em, ka vanbin teŋin sɔs Wina'am

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: yɛt ye, “M da naani m ma pʋʋgin yinɛ zaalim na, zaalim mɛn ka m na lɛb. Zugsɔb la tisim, onɛ lɛn di'e ya'as; Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr nar nɛ girima.”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ linɛ niŋ la wʋsa, Job da pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛd bɛɛ nyɔl Wina'am ye o tʋm o bɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Daar yinne ya'as ka Wina'am biis la'as ye ba zaŋi ba mɛŋi pa'al Wina'am, ka Sʋntaana mɛ paasi dɔlli kena.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la bu'os Sʋntaana ye, “Fʋ yi yaanɛ na?” Ka Sʋntaana gandig Zugsɔb la ye, “Man yinɛ teŋgbauŋʋn la na, ka bɛɛ anina giligid zin'is wʋsa.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Ka Wina'am bu'os o ye, “Fʋ tiɛn m tʋmtʋm Job yɛlaa? Ninsaal kae teŋgbauŋ nwa' zugʋ nwɛn o. O anɛ ninvʋsʋŋ ka ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ, ka mɛ an pʋʋg yinne sɔb. O anɛ onɛ zɔt mam Wina'am ka kis dinɛ wʋsa an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. Hali baa fʋn zaŋimi tugul nɛ o ka san'am o zaalim-zaalim la, o nan kpɛn zi'enɛ o burikinnim la pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Ka Sʋntaana lɛbis ye, “Mɛ vʋm an si'el wʋsa, ninsaal kʋ maligim siaki zaŋ o vʋm tiak nɛ si'ela.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Kɛl ka tɔɔg paae o mɛŋ niŋgbina ka fʋ na nyɛ ka o ki'isif.”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la yɛl Sʋntaana ye, “Tɔ', gɔsima, m zaŋ o si'el wʋsa niŋi fʋ nu'ugin, ya'a ka' o vʋm ma'aanɛ. Da si'is o vʋm la.”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Ka Sʋntaana yi Wina'am tuon ka kɛ ka sankpangbiriba gban'e Job niŋgbina hali yii o nɔba ni paae o zupaasʋʋg

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Ka Job nɔk sɛwia ɛnbisid o mɛŋ ka keŋ zin' tampʋʋr zug.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Ka o pu'a yɛl o ye, “Fʋ nan kpɛn zi'enɛ fʋ burikinnimin laa? Fʋ ya'a ki'is Wina'am ka kpi, di pʋ sɔn'oe yaa?”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Fʋ pian'ad la nwɛnɛ pu'a kanɛ ka' ya'am nɛ. Bʋnsʋma ma'aa ka ti di'esid Zugsɔb la san'an ka lɛɛ kʋ di'e bʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ?” Yɛlbama wʋsa pʋʋgin, Job pʋ ya'ae o nɔɔri pian' Wina'am bɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Job zuanam atan' da bɛ; ba da anɛ Elifaz onɛ an Teman nid la, nɛ Bilidad onɛ an Suh nid, nɛ Zofar onɛ mɛ an Naama nid la. Ban da wʋm yɛltɔɔg dinɛ paae o la, ba da la'as taaba ye ba keŋ bɛlis o.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Ban da nam bɛ lalli ka nyɛ o la, ba da pʋ baŋ ye onɛ la. Ba sʋnya da san'amnɛ hali ka ba pin'ili kaasid ka aansidi ba fuud ka nɔk tampɛligim niŋi ba zut ye li pa'ali ba sʋnsa'aŋ.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Ka ba paae na la'am zin'in teŋin nɛ o daba ayɔpɔi nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ. Ka ba sɔ'ɔsɔ pʋ ya'ae o nɔɔri yɛl o si'ela bɔzugɔ ba da nyɛ ka o namisʋg la galis hali.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Ka Job yʋ'ʋn ya'ae o nɔɔri pɔɔ zɛrig o du'am dabisir.

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: O da yɛl ye,

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “Kɛl ka m du'am dabisir la ba'as yɔri, hali nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ ka ba yɛl ye, ‘Ba tʋk biribiŋ pʋʋg la!’

english_verse: and send thick, gloomy shadows to fill it with dread.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka dabisir la kilim lik biridi; kɛl ka saŋgbansabilig ligili li, ka lik nyaŋ nintaŋ dabiskaŋa nwa' ni.

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Pʋn da kɛ ka pu'a nɔk pʋʋg yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ; kɛl ka sɔ' da wʋm sumalisim tʋkpiidʋgɔ.

english_verse: Let those with magic powers place a curse on that day.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka banɛ mɔr nɔtɔɔd pɔ nɔɔri niŋ dabisir nwa', ka teŋgban kpɛn'ɛdib bɔ bɔɔb dabisir nwa' zug.

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Kɛl ka li bɛkɛung nwadbibis lieb lik; kɛl ka li gu'us nintaŋi gʋ'ʋŋ ka kʋ nyɛ bɛogʋn sɔɔnrim,

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: bɔzugɔ li sʋm ye li li'inimi m ma pʋʋgin ka o da du'am ka m nyɛ yɛltɔɔd bamaa.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Bɔzug ka pu'adu'as la da du'asi m ma, ka bɔ ka m ma da tisim bin'isim ka m mu'a?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Anwaa m digin nɛ baanlimm nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm. Anwaa m gbisidin nɛ ka vʋ'ʋsid.

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: Anwaa m vʋ'ʋsidin nɛ ninvʋsʋma banɛ mɔr sanlima, ka pɛ'ɛli ba ya' nɛ anzurifa la.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Bɔzug ka ba da pʋ pin'im wʋʋ pu'a ɛɛn du'a bikpi'im ka ba pin' o si'em la, bɛɛ bilia kanɛ pʋ nyɛ nɛɛsim ka lɛb si'em la?

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Kpi'im teŋ ka bugusnam pʋ lɛn tʋm bugisim tʋʋmaa, ka banɛ tadig nyɛt vʋ'ʋsʋm.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Tadimnam nɛ kpi'emnam wʋsa bɛɛ anina, ka yammis nyɛ yɔlisim ba dima nu'usin.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: Kassa! Nɛɛsim an bɔɔ tis sʋnsa'aŋ daana? Ka vʋm an bɔɔ tis onɛ bɛ tɔɔg pʋʋginɛ?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Ba ieed kum ka kum pʋ kennaa, ba ieed kum hali nɛ nimmua gat ban na ieed la'asʋŋ dinɛ su'a.

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: Ba mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm bɛdegʋ ka maan sumalisim ban paae yaʋgʋn la zug.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Bɔzug ka ba tisid onɛ ka' bɛog nyɔvʋrɛ; ka Wina'am gan'al ye ba na namis hali la?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: M sin'uŋ lieb diibi tisim, ka m ʋʋnsʋg nwɛnɛ ku'om kpa'adnɛ.

english_verse: and my worst fears have all come true.
translation_verse: Gbaagba man zɔt si'el la, linɛ paam! Linɛ ka m sid zɔt amɛŋa mɛŋa la paam.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Ayei, m pʋ mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm, li ka' m sʋ'ʋm. M ka' vʋ'ʋsʋm, li anɛ daauŋ ma'aa.”

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Nid ya'a lɛbis o nɔɔrɛ, li na daami fɔɔ? Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi gban'e o mɛŋ ka da pian' si'ela?

english_verse: have guided and encouraged many in need.
translation_verse: Fʋ sa'alʋg da sʋŋ banɛ bɔɔd liig, ka kpɛmis banɛ giinla kɛns la.

english_verse: But now you feel discouraged when struck by trouble.
translation_verse: Ka yɛltɔɔg yʋ'ʋn paae fʋ mɛŋ ka fʋ tadig, li di'igif nɛ ka fʋ sʋʋnr wʋsa san'am.

english_verse: You respect God and live right, so don't lose hope!
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ fʋ Wina'am zɔtim la kʋ tisif kpi'euŋɔɔ? Ka fʋ sida bɛllim la kʋ tisif ti'irɛɛ?

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ kpansi gɔs ka banɛ wʋsa kuod bɛ'ɛd ka bʋt yɛla mɛ bunnɛ bɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Wina'am ya'a vʋ'ʋs fɛɛn, ba san'amidnɛ; o sʋnf ya'a duoe, ba mɛlimidnɛ.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Gbigim tun'e nwa'am ka nyuul hali, amaa la'an nɛ wala o nyina kɔya.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Gbigimnya'aŋ pʋ nyaŋi gban'e bʋnkɔnbʋgɔ ka li nyaŋ o, ka o biis widig yaaŋ-yaaŋ.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: Kɛlisima, labaar kɛn man san'an na, ka m tʋba wʋm ka li nya'amid.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: Li kena nwɛnɛ zaansʋŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ saŋa ka nidib wʋsa gbisid.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Ka pɛbisim nwɛ'ɛmi gaad ka li kpɛn'ɛsim waad ka m niŋgbina wʋsa kpɛn' waki.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Ka li fɔn baanlimm, amaa ka m zi' lin an si'ela. Ka di nwɛnɛ si'el nɛ zi'e m tuon, ka m wʋm ka li yɛt ye,

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: ‘Ninvʋsaal na tun'e an pʋpiel sɔbi gaad Wina'am? Ninsaal na tun'e an nyain gaad onɛ maal oo?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Wina'am ya'a ye o mɛŋ-mɛŋ tʋmtʋmnib pʋʋg pʋ paada, hali ka ye o maliaknam tʋm dinɛ pʋ nara,

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: ka ninsaalib banɛ ka o nɔk ya'adi maal ka ba na tun'e san'ami ba hali gaad ban san'amid zʋnzʋnr si'em la!

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ba tun'e kpi bɛogʋn bɛɛ zaamnɔɔr. Ba tun'e kpi, hali ka sɔ' ba'a kae.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Ba ya'a yisi ba vʋm, ba kpiidnɛ yɔɔg-yɔɔg.’”

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Asida, sʋntɔɔg kʋʋd zɔlʋg, ka fufum kʋʋd zi'ilim daan.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ nyɛ ka zɔlʋg ba'a nya'a, ka li pʋ yuugɛ ka o yir ba'as yɔri.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Namisʋg pʋ naanid teŋinɛ yit naa, ka yɛla mɛ pʋ bun teŋin naa.

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: Saalib wʋsa du'anɛ nɛ yɛla nwɛnɛ nyɔ'ɔsi yit bugumin si'em la.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: Ya'a aan mam, man naan ieen Wina'am zin'ig; mam na zaŋi m yɛla wʋsa paae o tuon na.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Onɛ kɛt ka saa niid teŋgbauŋ zug, ka kɛt ka ku'om bɛ pɔɔdin.

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Onɛ dʋ'ʋsid tadimnam saazug, ka bɛlisid banɛ kaasid kʋʋr.

english_verse: in their own evil schemes, and their wisdom fails.
translation_verse: O bɛnd ya'am dimnɛ gban'adi ba nɛ ba mi'ilim pʋʋgin, ka ba bɔɔdim wʋsa lieb yɔri.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Onɛ gur tadimnam ka gu'udi baa yisid banɛ nɔya tɔi wʋʋ yabid la san'an, ka faandi ba paŋ dim nu'usin basid.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Alazug tadimnam yʋ'ʋn mɔr ti'ir ka banɛ tʋm dinɛ pʋ nar la pʋ lɛm mɔr nɔɔr ya'asɛ.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Onɛ pu'alimid, onɛ mɛ lɛn ti'ebid; onɛ tisid dɛmis, onɛ mɛ ma'ad dɛmis la.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: O na yisif yɛltɔɔd ayuobʋ pʋʋgin; hali baa li ya'a paaf nɔɔr ayɔpɔi, o na yisif.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Kɔ'ɔm ya'a li na, o na gurif ka fʋ kʋ kpii, hali zaba pʋʋgin, o na lusif ka sʋ'ʋg kʋ kʋʋ fɔ.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: O na gurif ka saalib nɔya kʋ niŋif si'ela. San'auŋ ya'a paae na fʋ kʋ zɔ dabiem.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: San'auŋ nɛ kɔ'ɔm saŋa fʋn la'adnɛ, fʋ pʋ zɔt mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbbɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Kugbanɛ bɛɛ fʋ pɔɔdin la kʋ lɛn san'ami fʋ zʋʋdɛ, ka mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbid na bɛ nɛf nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Fʋ mɛŋ na baŋ ye nimma'asim bɛɛ fʋ yin, ka fʋ bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa na bɛ, ka baa yinne kʋ kpii.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, fʋ biis na zu'oe, ka fʋ tuŋ tiɛn wʋʋ mɔɔdi galis teŋ zug si'em la.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Fʋ na kʋdigi paae fʋ bɛn ka nyaan kpi, nwɛnɛ ki ɛɛn bi'ig si'em ka ba nyaan bun la.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Ti kpans ya, ka baŋ ye nɛ' anɛ sida. Dinzug, wʋm sʋ'ʋŋa ka zaŋi lii tʋm tʋʋma fʋ bɛllimin.”

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: Di tɛbisim na gaad titanbin'isʋg linɛ dig atɛuk gbɛog la. Linɛ kɛ ka m pian'ad yɔɔg-yɔɔg la.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la tɔn mam nɛ o piema, Ka piema la yabid kpɛn' m siigin. Wina'am kɛnɛ ka o sʋnpɛɛn kpɛn'ɛsim dabiem.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Mɔɔgin bʋŋ ya'a nyɛ yaama ɔnbida, o na kaasidaa, bɛɛ lɔlig na ɔnbid yam ka lɛm bʋʋnna?

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Ba dit dikanɛ ka yaarim kae, bɛɛ ya nam mi' nyɛ ka gɛlpielim mɔr mimilim?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Man diibi an si'em la, ka m ya'amlɛog ka' li ni baa bi'elaa.

english_verse: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
translation_verse: Mam ya'a sɔs si'ela, Wina'am na gandigi maa? O na siaki maali m sʋʋnr bɔɔdim?

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Amaa linɛ tisidim sumbʋgʋsʋm anɛ ye, la'an nɛ tɔɔg la wʋmim si'em la, m pʋ ki'is Onɛ an Kasi la yɛlʋgɔ.

english_verse: Why should I patiently hope when my strength is gone?
translation_verse: Paŋ bɔ ka m mɔr ka li na tisim ti'irɛ? Bʋnsʋŋ bɔɔ bɛ tuon ka m na maal suguru gura?

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: M paŋ paae kugirɛɛ? Ka m niŋgbiŋ anɛ kʋntzɛn'ugɔ?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: Ya'a an sida, m pʋ lɛm mɔr paŋ kanɛ ka m na sʋŋi m mɛŋa, ka linɛ naan kɛɛn ka m nyaŋ la mɛ lɛn kae.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: Di nar ye ninkanɛ bɛ yɛltɔɔgin nyɛ sʋŋiri o zuanam san'an, hali baa o ya'a pʋ lɛn zɔt Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la dabiem.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: Sɛɛung ka saa niid hali ka sakuga lii pɛ'ɛli li ka li badigid;

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Kpikpinkpinnib banɛ ban'adi ba yʋgʋma ya'a kena ka bie ye ba nu ku'om, ba kennɛ hali kpɛn' pipirigin ti bɔdig.

english_verse: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
translation_verse: ba sʋnya san'amidnɛ bɔzugɔ ba na nyɛ ka ku'om kae.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Yanam mɛ anɛ ala, ya kʋ tun'e sʋŋi ma; ya nyɛɛm namisʋg la ka dabiem gban'e ya.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: M nam mi' sɔsi ya ye, ‘Tisiminim piini, bɛɛ zaŋiminɛ ya mɔrim yɔ man yɛla,

english_verse: or to purchase my freedom from brutal enemies?
translation_verse: bɛɛ faanminimɛ yisi m dataas nu'usin, bɛɛ, faanminim nimbɛ'ɛdnam mugusʋginɛ’?

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: Tɔ', pa'aliminim ka m na an baanlimm ka kɛlis, yɛliminim man gbɛlig si'el.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Ya'a an sida, yɛlmɛŋir tɔi, amaa ya zɛrigir la wʋsa nyɔɔd an bɔ?

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Ya bɔɔdi yɛl ye m pian'ad la mɔri gbɛlʋŋ, ka gɔs man yɛl si'el la wʋsa ka li an pɛbisim?

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: Amaa dimi suguru ka gɔsinim. Ya gɔs ka m anɛ onɛ na zi'eni ya tuonnɛ ma' dama'am?

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Basimi yanamɛ yɛt si'el la. Maligim tɛn'ɛsi sʋ'ʋŋa ka da mɔŋinim bʋʋdɛ.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Ya tɛn'ɛs ye m ma'adnɛɛ? Ya gɔs ka m zi' sida nɛ ziri bakidaa?”

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Ka nwɛnɛ sankpan'asi tʋm tadig ka bɔɔd ye winnig li tɔ'ɔtɔ si'em la, bɛɛ nwɛnɛ onɛ kuod baadi gur o yɔɔd si'em la,

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: ala ka ba kɛ ka m bɛ yɔri bɛllim nwadis wʋsa, ka dig yʋ'ʋŋ wʋsa liebid ka pʋ tun'e gbisida.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: M ya'a kpɛn' yʋ'ʋŋ ye m gbis, m tɛn'ɛsidnɛ ye, ‘Saŋkanɛ ka m na nie?’ Ka bɛog mɛ pʋ nieda, ka m digi liebid bɛog nyain.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Zunzunya nɛ dian'ad ma'aa pɛ'ɛli m niŋgbina; m niŋgbauŋ la anɛ fɛn'ɛdi nyuusid.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: M dabisa zɔtnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ hali gat onɛ ʋgʋd pienni lɔbid sʋlʋg ʋgʋb daug si'em la, ka li ba'asʋg wʋsa anɛ yɔri, ka ti'ir kae.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: M Wina'am, tɛnr ye m vʋm anɛ giŋa nwa'; ka m nif kʋ lɛn nyɛ bʋnsʋŋ linɛ na tisim sumalisim ya'asɛ.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Nini banɛ gɔsidim la kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ ma; fʋ na ieedi m zin'ig, ka m kʋ lɛm bɛɛ.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ saŋgbana ɛɛnti gaad tɔ'ɔtɔ si'em la, ala mɛn ka onɛ kpii keŋ kpi'im teŋ kʋ lɛn lɛb naa.

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: O kʋ lɛn lɛb o yin na ya'asɛ, ba mɛ kʋ lɛn tɛnri o yɛla ya'asɛ.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ m kʋ sinni m nɔɔrɛ; m na tu'as lin mugusim si'em; m na nyɔl hali pa'alim sʋnpɛɛnni zem si'em.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: M anɛ atɛuk ku'om bɛɛ ku'omin bʋnyua, ka fʋ kɛ ka ba guri maa?

english_verse: I'd rather choke to death than live in this body.
translation_verse: Li kɛ ka m siak nɛ ban na yulim ka m kpi gaad mam bɛ bɛllim si'a nwa'.

english_verse: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
translation_verse: M vʋm la ka' vɔɔnrɛ, m pʋ bɔɔd ye m vʋe saŋa wʋsaa; basim mam baanlimm ka m bɛllim nwa' ka' vɔɔnrɛ.

english_verse: What makes you so concerned about us humans?
translation_verse: Ninsaal an bɔ ka o yɛla paki fɔ, o an bɔ ka fʋ tɛn'ɛsid o yɛla?

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: O an bɔ ka fʋ kpansid o daar woo, ka makid o saŋa wʋsa?

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Fʋ kʋ di suguru ka fɛndigi fʋ nindaa m san'anɛɛ, bɛɛ kɛ ka m paam vʋ'ʋsʋm bi'elaa vɔli m nintɔɔndɛ?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Fʋn kanɛ gɔsid ninsaalib wʋsa la, taal bɔ kimm ka m tʋm tisi fɔ? Bɔ ka fʋ maalim bʋmbʋ'ʋdir ka bʋ'ʋdim saŋa wʋsa? Man lieb nɛ ziidi tisi fɔɔ?

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Fʋ ye fʋ zaŋ saŋa wala pian'? Fʋ pian'ad la nwɛnɛ sisi'em nɛ.

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Wina'am na mɔŋ bʋʋd sɔb bʋʋdɛɛ? Wina'am Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar sɔb la na zan'as linɛ an sidaa?

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: fʋ ya'a an pʋʋg yinne sɔb ka pʋ mɔr gba'arɛ, hali baa di ya'a an si'em wʋsa Wina'am mɛŋ na lɛbisi fʋ zi'eli fʋ zi'esimin.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: Fʋn daa pin'il si'em bi'ela la, fʋ mɔrim na galis hali saŋa kanɛ kenna la.

english_verse: Our ancestors were wise, so learn from them.
translation_verse: Bu'osim zʋmaana banɛ gaad la yɛla, ka fʋ na zamis ya'am ti yaanam san'an.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ tinam anɛ bɛɛga-bɛɛga biis ka zi' si'el si'ela, ka ti dabisa mɛ pʋ zem si'el dunia nwa' nii.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Ba ya'a nan nɔbigid ka pʋ siak ki'ebɔ, ba zɛndigidnɛ kʋdigid tɔ'ɔtɔ nwɛnɛ mɔɔd nɛ.

english_verse: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
translation_verse: Ala ka li aɛn nɛ banɛ tam Wina'am yɛla la. Banɛ ba'a kae nɛ Wina'am la ti'ir na ba'as yɔri.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: On zaŋ o ti'iri niŋ si'el la ka' paŋa, on ti'e si'el la nwɛnɛ silinsi'ipaanlʋŋ nɛ.

english_verse: they take hold and fall because it's so flimsy.
translation_verse: O dɛlnɛ o silinsi'ipaanlʋŋ la ka li kɛnsig ka o mak ye o gammi li ka li tɔnsig.

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: O nwɛnɛ mɔɔdi na bɛ nintaŋin ka ba dɔn'ɔsid ka ku'om wʋm, ka li tɛɛn gilig lɔmbɔn'ɔg;

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: ka li nya'a tɔɔn gilig tampiins nɛ kuga ye li nyɛ zin'isʋŋ.

english_verse: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
translation_verse: Amaa ba ya'a vuoɛn li, hali sɔ' pʋ lɛn tɛnr on bɛɛn zin'isi'a ya'asɛ.

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Fʋ nyɛ yaa, banɛ pʋ zɔt Wina'am la nyɔɔdi la, sieba na kena n di'e ba zin'ig.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: Amaa gɔsima Wina'am kʋ maligim bas sida sɔba; o mɛ kʋ sʋŋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dima.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: O na lɛn kɛ ka fʋ la'ad nɛ sumalisim, hali fʋ na la' kaas kuŋ nɛ sumalisim ya'as.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: O na kɛ ka nyan di banɛ kisif la, ka san'am pitɔɔg dim la ya'.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Ɛɛn, m mi' ye li anɛ ala yim. Ka ninsaal ye o niŋ wala kilim pʋpiel sɔb Wina'am tuonnɛ?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Nid ya'a bɔɔd ye o nwa'as nɛ o, o sɔb kʋ nyaŋi gandig o bu'osʋg yinne bu'osa tusir pʋʋginɛ.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: O ya'am la ka' makirɛ ka o paŋ ka' bɛnnɛ. Anɔ'ɔn nam mi' mak o mɛŋ nɛ Wina'am ka di ya'annɛ?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: O sʋʋnr ɛɛn duoe ka o vɔn' zuoya lɔb, hali ka zuoya la zi' onɛ niŋida.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: Onɛ dammid teŋgbauŋ la, ka li mi'im zin'ig wʋsa.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: O ya'a bɔɔd, o tun'e kɛ ka nintaŋ da yii; o mɛ tun'e kɛ ka nwadbibis kʋ nie.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: On ma'aa yadig saŋgbana la ka kennɛ atɛuk ku'onwiis zug.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Onɛ maal nwadbibis buudi wʋsa zin'is atan' ka sieba bɛ dagɔbʋg ka sieba bɛ teŋsʋk ka sieba mɛ bɛ datiuŋ; o mɛ la'as Nɔnya'aŋ-nɛ-o-biis nɛ A-kidigim-bu'osnam.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: O tʋm nɛ tʋʋmnyalima banɛ ka ninsaal kʋ gban'e li gbinnɛ, o kilima la ka' bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Kassa, o dɔlli m san'anɛ gat, amaa m pʋ nyɛt oo; o ya'a gat, m kʋ baŋ oo.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: O ya'a faaɛn si'eli gaadɛ, anɔ'ɔn na nyaŋi gu' o? Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi bu'os o ye, ‘Bɔ ka fʋ niŋid ala?’

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Wina'am pʋ gu'ud o sʋnpɛɛnnɛ; hali baa bʋnzɔtir linɛ bɛ ku'otita'arin buon Arahab la, o sʋŋidib dig nɛ o nɔba teŋir.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: M ye m niŋ wala zab nɛ Wina'am? M ye m nyɛ nɔɔr ya nwa'as nɛ o?

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Hali man ya'a buol o ka o siak, mam pʋ tɛn'ɛs ye o na kɛligi m pian'adɛ.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: O na kɛ ka sisi'etita'ar nwɛ'ɛmi yutim ka kɛ ka m fɛn'ɛd la maligim paas zaalim-zaalim.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: O kʋ kɛ ka m vʋ'ʋs baa bi'elaa amaa ka kpɛm paasidim tɔɔg.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Li ya'a anɛ paŋaa, onɛ an paŋ tita'ar sɔb; bɛɛ li ya'a anɛ sariakadib, anɔ'ɔnɛ pa'an o sida suorɛ?

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ man ka' gbɛlʋŋ la, m ba'a ka' nɛ m mɛŋ-mɛŋ yɛllɛ, m mɛŋ gɔs ka m vʋm la anɛ yɔri.

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: Man gɔs ka li wʋsa anɛ yinne, lin ka m ye, ‘O san'amid banɛ ka' gbɛlʋŋɔ nɛ banɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim wʋsa.’

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Yɛlmugusa ya'a ti kʋ ninkanɛ ka' taalɛ, Wina'am la'ad o nɛ.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Teŋ si'a ya'a li pitɔɔg dim nu'usin, Wina'am lusid nɛ banɛ kad saria la nini. Ya'a ka' onɛ, ka anɔ'ɔnɛ?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: Dunia nwa' pʋʋgin, m yʋma zɔt tɔ'ɔtɔ gat zɔzɔt, ba zɔtnɛ tɔ'ɔtɔ gat ka sumalisim kae.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Dabisa la zɔtnɛ nwɛnɛ anrʋŋ kanɛ gat tɔ'ɔtɔ nɛ, ka nwɛnɛ silʋgʋ na naan agɔlli zuligid ye o gban'e nɔbil nɛ.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: M ya'a ye, ‘M na bas nyɔnyɔlʋg la wala, ka basim nindalɔɔr la ka maal sumalisim.’

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala m namisʋg la kpɛn'ɛsidim nɛ dabiem, bɔzugɔ m mi' ye fʋ kʋ tisim bʋʋdɛ.

english_verse: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
