english_verse: You will turn back to me and ask for help, and I will answer your prayers.
translation_verse: ‘Ala ka ya na buolim ka sɔsim, ka m na wʋmi ya sɔsʋg.

english_verse: You will worship me with all your heart, and I will be with you
translation_verse: Ya na ieem ka nyɛɛm, ya ya'a sid ieem nɛ ya sʋnya wʋsa.’

english_verse: You feel secure, because you think I have sent prophets to speak for me in Babylonia.
translation_verse: Daasi'erɛɛ ya na yɛl ye, ‘Zugsɔb la tisi ti nɔdi'esidib Babilon teŋin.’

english_verse: I had you taken from Jerusalem to Babylonia. But you had better listen to me now.
translation_verse: ‘Dinzugɔ, wʋmi man Zugsɔb la pian'ad, yanam banɛ ka m kɛ ka ba gban'e ya mɔri keŋ Babilon teŋin la.’

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me what would happen to Shemaiah, who was one of our people in Babylonia. After my letter reached Babylonia, Shemaiah wrote letters to the people of Jerusalem, including the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, and the other priests. The letter to Zephaniah said:
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, Fʋ sɔb gbana nɛ fʋ mɛŋ yʋ'ʋri tis nimbanɛ bɛ Jerusalem wʋsa, nɛ Maaseya biig Zefanaya onɛ an maanmaan la nɛ maanmaannib banɛ kpɛlim la. Fʋ yɛl Zefanaya ye,

english_verse: After the death of Jehoiada the priest, the Lord chose you to be the priest in charge of the temple security force. You know that anyone who acts crazy and pretends to be a prophet should be arrested and put in chains and iron collars.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la gaŋif ye fʋ an maanmaanni di'e Jehoyada zin'igi sʋ'oe Zugsɔb Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la. Gban'am onɛ wʋsa gɛɛm ka niŋid wʋʋ o anɛ nɔdi'esi ba'a o nɛ kʋnt ba'an.

english_verse: Jeremiah from the town of Anathoth is pretending to be a prophet there in Jerusalem, so why haven't you punished him?
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ pʋ gban'e Jeremia onɛ an Anatof teŋin nid ka niŋid wʋʋ o anɛ nɔdi'esi ya sʋʋgin la?

english_verse: He even wrote a letter to the people here in Babylonia, saying we would be here a long time. He told us to build homes and to plant gardens and grow our own food.
translation_verse: O tis tinam banɛ bɛ Babilon teŋin la labakaŋa na ye, Li na yuug hali, dinzugɔ mɛɛmi ya' n bɛɛ ani, maalimi lɔmbɔn'ɔd ka di linɛ wʋsa maal ani.”

english_verse: When Zephaniah received Shemaiah's letter, he read it to me.
translation_verse: Zefanaya onɛ an maanmaan la da karim gbauŋ la tis nɔdi'es Jeremia.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me what to write in a second letter
translation_verse: Ani ka labakaŋa kɛn Jeremia san'an na ye,

english_verse: to the people of Judah who had been taken to Babylonia. In this letter, I wrote that the Lord had said: I, the Lord, have not chosen Shemaiah to be one of my prophets, and he has misled you by telling lies in my name.
translation_verse: “Mɔɔlim labakaŋa tis nimbanɛ ka ba gban'e ba lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ la ye, Zugsɔb la yɛl Semaya onɛ an Nehelam nid la yɛla si'em nwa ye: Semaya sadigim pian' tisi ya la'an nɛ mam pʋ tʋm o, ka kɛ ka ya niŋ yadda nɛ linɛ ka' sida la,

english_verse: He has even talked you into disobeying me. So I will punish Shemaiah. He and his descendants won't live to see the good things I will do for my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye: M sid na namis Semaya onɛ an Nehelam nid la nɛ o yaas. O kʋ lɛm mɔr sɔ' ka o kpɛlim nimbama sʋʋgin bɛɛ o nyɛ bʋnsʋma banɛ ka m na tʋm tisim nidib la, on pian' si'em zan'as man la zug.”

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel said, “Jeremiah, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Sɔm man yɛlif pian'asieba la wʋsa niŋ gbauŋʋn.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to Israel and Judah: Screams of terror are heard, with no word of peace.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, “M wʋmnɛ dabiem nɛ sʋnsan'aŋ kuŋ kaasig, li anɛ dabiem ka ka' sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: Can men give birth? Then why do I see them looking so pale and clutching their stomachs like women in labor?
translation_verse: Bu'osim ka gɔs: dau na nyaŋi du'a biisɛɛ? Ka bɔ ka m nyɛ ka dau kanɛ mɔr paŋ wʋsa zin' ka o nu'us bɛɛ o pɔɔrin wʋʋ pu'a sa'ae, ka ba nindaas wʋsa nwɛɛgida?

english_verse: My people, soon you will suffer worse than ever before, but I will save you.
translation_verse: Dabiskan la tɔɔgʋ na an si'em la! Dabisir kʋ lɛm bɛɛ nwɛnɛ li ya'asɛ. Li na anɛ yɛla saŋa tis Jakob nidib, amaa m na faaɛn ba li pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: Now you are slaves of other nations, but I will break the chains and smash the yokes that keep you in slavery.
translation_verse: “Dabiskan la daar,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la, “m na kɔ'ɔg yu'asindaug linɛ bɛɛ ba niŋgɔnya ni la ka na kɛns bana linɛ lɔɔ ba la; saam kʋ lɛn kɛ ka ba an yammis ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Then you will be my servants, and I will choose a king for you from the family of David. *
translation_verse: Ka ba yʋ'ʋn na tʋm tisi ba Zugsɔb nɛ ba Wina'am nɛ David onɛ aan ba na'ab onɛ ka m na tisi ba la.

english_verse: Israel, you belong to me, so don't be afraid. You deserved to be punished; that's why I scattered you in distant nations. But I am with you, and someday I will destroy those nations.
translation_verse: Alazugɔ, m tʋmtʋm Jakob nidibaa, da zɔti dabiem; da kɛ ka li paki ya, Israel dima.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “M sid na faaɛn ya tɛɛns banɛ lal la ni na, nɛ ya yaas banɛ ka ba mɔri lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ la. Jakob nidib la yʋ'ʋn na mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm ka zin' baanlimm, ka sɔ' kʋ lɛm kpɛn'ɛsi ba dabiem ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Then I will bring you and your descendants back to your land, where I will protect you and give you peace. Then your fears will be gone. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Heal Israel and Judah
translation_verse: M bɛ nɛ ya ka na faaɛn ya.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “La'an nɛ man san'am buudi wʋsa banɛ ka m widigi ya kpɛn'ɛs la, m kʋ san'am yanam nyainnɛ. M na namisi ya amaa ka kɛ ka li dɔlli li suor; ka kʋ kɛ ka ya keŋ zaalim-zaalim ka pʋ di'e namisʋg baa bi'elaa.”

english_verse: The Lord said: My people, you are wounded and near death.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, “fʋ sapu'ad la ka' ti'ebʋgɔ, fʋn pu'alim si'em la ka' bɔdigirɛ.

english_verse: You are accused of a crime with no one to defend you, and you are covered with sores that no medicine can cure. *
translation_verse: Sɔ' kae na nwɛ' nu'ugʋ fʋ yɛlaa, fʋ fɛn'ʋg la ka' tiim, fʋ ka' laafi nyɛɛbɔ.

english_verse: Your friends have forgotten you; they don't care anymore. Even I have acted like an enemy. And because your sins are horrible and countless, I will be cruel as I punish you.
translation_verse: Fʋ taaba la wʋsa tami fʋ yɛla; ba ba'a ka' nɛ fɔ. M nwɛ'ɛf wʋʋ dataa na nwɛ'ɛf si'em ka namisif wʋʋ bugusim sɔb nɛ, fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi zu'oe ka ka' bɛn la zug.

english_verse: But if your enemies try to rob or destroy you, I will rob and destroy them, and they will be led as captives to foreign lands.
translation_verse: Amaa onɛ mɔɔd ye o san'amif la mɛ na san'am; fʋ bi'emnam la wʋsa na lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ zʋŋ. Banɛ faandif la wʋsa ba na faaɛn ba; banɛ zabid nɛ ya la mam mɛ na zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: No one wants you as a friend or cares what happens to you. But I will heal your injuries, and you will get well. The Lord Will Rescue Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Amaa m na kɛ ka fʋ nyɛ laafi ya'as ka ti'ebi fʋ dɛmis la,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “Bɔzugɔ ba buonif ye, ‘Onɛ ka ba kadi bas’ nɛ ‘Zion onɛ ka sɔ' ba'a ka' nɛ o.’”

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I will be kind to you and let you come home. Jerusalem now lies in ruins, but you will rebuild it, complete with a new palace.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye: “M na lɛbis Jakob yidim zusʋŋ la na ka zɔɔ o nidib nimbaanlig ban bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa. Tempʋʋg linɛ an dabɔɔg la, ba na lɛbisi mɛɛ li, ka na'ayir la na lɛbi zi'enɛ li zin'igin.

english_verse: Other nations will respect and honor you. Your homes will be filled with children, and you will celebrate, singing praises to me.
translation_verse: Ba san'an ka bareka pʋ'ʋsim yʋʋma na yina ka ba maan sumalisim tansid agɔla gɔla. M na paasi ba kal, ka ba kʋ sie; M na kɛ ka ba nyɛ na'asi, ka ba kʋ lɛn ziemi ba ya'asɛ.

english_verse: It will be just like old times. Your nation will worship me, and I will punish anyone who abuses you.
translation_verse: Ba biis na nwɛnɛ kʋdimin dimi mɔr paŋ si'em la, ba teŋ la na zi'en sʋ'ʋŋa; m na namis banɛ wʋsa mugusidi ba.

english_verse: One of your own people will become your ruler. And when I invite him to come near me at the place of worship, he will do so. No one would dare to come near without being invited.
translation_verse: Ba tuongat la na anɛ ba mɛŋ nid; ka ba na'ab la na yinɛ ba sʋʋgin na. M na kɛ ka o li'elim ka bɛ m san'an yammin, ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na li'eli m san'an na ka mam pʋ buol o?” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: You will be my people, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Ala ka ya na aan m nidib ka mam mɛ na aan ya Wina'am.

english_verse: I am furious! And like a violent storm I will strike those who do wrong.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, Zugsɔb la sʋnpɛɛn nwɛnɛ sisi'em nɛ, o na nwɛnɛ sisi'epiliŋi da'ad na sigid bugusim dim zutin.

english_verse: I won't calm down until I have finished what I have decided to do. Someday, you will understand what I mean.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋnpɛɛn linɛ mɔr dabiem la kʋ lɛbɛ, asɛɛ o ti tʋm o sʋnfʋ gban'e si'el la naae. Dabisa kenna ka ya na gban'e li gbin sʋ'ʋŋa.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Israel, I promise that someday all your tribes will again be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Li saŋa ya'a ti paae, M na an Israel dɔɔd la wʋsa Wina'am, ka ban na aan m nidib.”

english_verse: In the desert I was kind to those who escaped death. I gave them peace, and when the time is right, I'll do the same for you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Rebuild Israel
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye: “Nidib banɛ vʋ'ʋg ka pʋ kpi zaba ni la na nyɛ nimbaanlzɔɔr sian'arin la. M na kena tis Israel dim vʋ'ʋsʋm.”

english_verse: You will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria and enjoy the grapes.
translation_verse: Ya na lɛn sɛ vain tiis Samaria zuoya la ni; kpaadib la na sɛɛ ba ka dii ba wala.

english_verse: Someday those who guard the hill country of Ephraim will shout, “Let's go to Zion and worship the Lord our God.” Israel Will Return to Its Own Land
translation_verse: Dabisir kenna ka banɛ gur la na kaas kuŋ Efiram kʋkʋna la ni ye, ‘Kemi na, kɛlli ka ti keŋ Zion, ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la san'an!’”

english_verse: The Lord says: Celebrate and sing for Israel, the greatest of nations. Offer praises and shout, “Come and rescue your people, Lord! Save what's left of Israel.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa: “Yʋ'ʋmmi nɛ sumalisim tis Jakob; tansimi bɛdegʋ tis sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ gat sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa la. Kɛl ka ba wʋmi ya zʋn'or ka yɛl ye, ‘O Zugsɔba, faanmi fʋ nidib, Israel dim banɛ kpɛlim la.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, will bring my people back from Babylonia and everywhere else on earth. The blind and the lame will be there. Expectant mothers and women about to give birth will come and be part of that great crowd.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, m na mɔri ba yi ya-datiuŋ na ka la'as banɛ bɛ dunia kpikpɛmis la na. Ba sʋʋgin la zʋnzɔɔs nɛ pɔnda na bɛ, pu'apʋʋs nɛ banɛ sa'ae; ba na lɛb na lieb buudi bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: They will weep and pray as I bring them home. I will lead them to streams of water. They will walk on a level road and not stumble. I am a father to Israel, my favorite children.
translation_verse: Ba na kena nɛ kukuma; m ya'a mɔri ba lɛbid na ba na sɔsid man Wina'am suguru. M na mɔri ba dɔlis ku'om zin'ig, zin'ikanɛ an sassi ka ba kʋ tu'ugi ba nɔbirɛ, bɔzugɔ man anɛ Israel dim saam ka Efiram aan m bikpɛɛm.”

english_verse: Listen to me, you nations nearby or across the sea. I scattered the people of Israel, but I will gather them again. I will protect them like a shepherd guarding a flock;
translation_verse: Buudi wʋsa, wʋmmi Zugsɔb la labaar; mɔɔlim tisi tɛɛns banɛ lal ka bɛɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la: “Onɛ widig Israel dim la na lɛn la'asi ba na ka na guri ba wʋʋ kɔnbkemmi gur o kɔnbid si'em la.

english_verse: I will rescue them from enemies who could overpower them.
translation_verse: Man Zugsɔb la na tis Jakob nidib la yɔlisim ka faaɛn ba yis banɛ paŋi zu'oe gaadi ba la nu'usin.

english_verse: My people will come to Mount Zion and celebrate; their faces will glow because of my blessings. I'll give them grain, grapes, and olive oil, as well as sheep and cattle. Israel will be prosperous and grow like a garden with plenty of water.
translation_verse: Ba na kena yʋ'ʋm nɛ sumalisim Zion zuor la zug; ba na maal sumalisim Zugsɔb la tisi ba piini linɛ an zʋʋd nɛ danpaalig nɛ kpaam nɛ kɔnbid nɛ na'abibis la zug. Ba na nwɛnɛ lɔmbɔn'ɔg kanɛ ka ba dɔn'ɔsid sʋ'ʋŋa, ka ba kʋ mɔr sʋnsa'aŋ ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Young women and young men, together with the elderly, will celebrate and dance, because I will comfort them and turn their sorrow into happiness.
translation_verse: Pu'asada la na wa'ad nɛ sumalisim, la'an nɛ na'akim nɛ bʋnkʋd wʋsa. M na tiaki ba kukuma ka li lieb sumalisim; M na yisi ba sʋnsa'aŋ la ka bʋgʋli ba sʋnya.

english_verse: I will bless my people with more food than they need, and the priests will enjoy the choice cuts of meat. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Offers Hope
translation_verse: M na tis maanmaannib la diib bɛdegʋ, ka m nidib la na nyɛ m piini bɛdegʋ,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: In Ramah a voice is heard, crying and weeping loudly. Rachel mourns for her children and refuses to be comforted, because they are dead. *
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, “Ba wʋm sɔ' kʋkɔr Rama teŋin ka o kaasid ka fabin ka kum kʋʋr kukuma, Ka li anɛ Rakɛl n kaasid o biis la yɛla ka pʋ siakid bɛliŋɔ, bɔzugɔ o biis la kae.”

english_verse: But I, the Lord, say to dry your tears. Someday your children will come home from the enemy's land. Then all you have done for them will be greatly rewarded.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye: “Gu'om ka da kaasida ka duusi fʋ ninta'am, ka ba na yɔɔ fʋ, fʋ tʋʋma la yɛla,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “Ba na yii ba dataas teŋin lɛb na.

english_verse: The people of Israel moan and say to me, “We were like wild bulls, but you, Lord, broke us, and we learned to obey. You are our God— please let us come home.
translation_verse: “M sid wʋm Efiram fabinnɛ yɛt ye, ‘Fʋ namisim wʋʋ na'abil kanɛ gɛɛm nɛ, ka m sid siaki li. Lɛbisimim na, ka m na lɛb, bɔzugɔ, fʋnɛ aan m Zugsɔb Wina'am.

english_verse: When we were young, we strayed and sinned, but then we realized what we had done. We are ashamed and disgraced and want to return to you.”
translation_verse: Man daa yidig la nya'aŋ m daa tiak ka lɛb na. Man yʋ'ʋn daa gban'e li gbin la, ka bibigi m nyɔ'ɔg m daa di nyan hali ka m zug zi bɔzugɔ m biilimin nyan la daa paae m.’

english_verse: People of Israel, you are my own dear children. Don't I love you best of all? Though I often make threats, I want you to be near me, so I will have mercy on you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Efiram ka'anɛ mam mɛŋ biig ka an bikanɛ ka m nɔŋaa? La'an nɛ mam pian'ad o yɛla bɛ'ɛd la, m nan kpɛn tɛnr o yɛla. Dinzugɔ m sʋnf nan bɔɔd o yɛla; m zɔt o nimbaanlig hali.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: With rock piles and signposts, mark the road well, my dear people. The road by which you left by will now lead you home.
translation_verse: “Sɛɛm zanbina suorin la! Zi'elim linɛ pa'an suor! Kpansim suoraug la, suokanɛ ka fʋ dɔl la. Lɛm na, O Israel onɛ nwɛnɛ pu'asadirɛ, lɛmmi fʋ tempʋʋsin la na.

english_verse: Will you ever decide to be faithful? I will make sure that someday things will be different, as different as a woman protecting a man. The Lord Will Bring Judah Home
translation_verse: Bʋndaar ka fʋ na bas giligirɛ, fʋn bipuŋ kanɛ ka' sida sɔba? Zugsɔb la na maal bʋmpaal teŋgbauŋ la zug, ka pu'a yʋ'ʋn na gu'ud dau.”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, said: I promise to set the people of Judah free and to lead them back to their hometowns. And when I do, they will once again say, “We pray that the Lord will bless his home, the sacred hill in Jerusalem where his temple stands.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb, ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, “M ya'a ti yisi ba sankpan'asim la ni lɛbis na, ka lɛbisi ba zusʋŋ la na, nimbanɛ bɛ Juda teŋin nɛ li tempʋʋsin la na lɛm pian' pian'abama ya'as ye, “Zugsɔb na niŋif bareka, zuokanɛ an kasi, ka an pʋpielim sɔbaa!

english_verse: The people will live in Jerusalem and in the towns of Judah. Some will be farmers, and others will be shepherds.
translation_verse: Nidib na la'asi bɛ Juda nɛ li tempʋʋsin la, kpaadib nɛ banɛ kemmi ba kɔnbidi giligid la na bɛ.

english_verse: Those who feel tired and worn out will find new life and energy,
translation_verse: M na kpɛ'ɛŋ banɛ tadig la ka diis banɛ vibid kɔ'ɔm la ka ba tig.”

english_verse: and when they sleep, they will wake up refreshed.
translation_verse: Man wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la, ka duoe gɔsi gilig, ka gbɛɛm la malisi tisim.

english_verse: Someday, Israel and Judah will be my field where my people and their livestock will grow.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la daa yɛl ye, “Dabisa kenna, ka m na kɛ ka Israel nɛ Juda zi'en sʋ'ʋŋa, ka nidib nɛ bʋnkɔnbid na bɛɛ ba tɛɛnsin la.

english_verse: In the past, I took care to uproot them, to tear them down, and to destroy them. But when that day comes, I will take care to plant them and help them grow.
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ m vɔɔn ba nɛ ka nwa'a ba bas, ka san'ami ba ka mɔr tɔɔgʋ kɛɛn ba zugin na la, ala ka m na guri ba ka lɛbisi baa mɛ' ka sɛɛ ba.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: No longer will anyone go around saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Dabisban la ni nidib kʋ lɛn siilim ye, “Ba'anam ɔnb kekama, ka li nwɛlig biis sʋnfɔ.

english_verse: When that day comes, only those who eat sour grapes will get the sour taste, and only those who sin will be put to death. The New Agreement with Israel and Judah
translation_verse: Sɔ' wʋsa lɛɛ na kpiid nɛ o mɛŋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yɛla; onɛ wʋsa ɔnb kekammi'isa na kpinɛ o mɛŋ kum.”

english_verse: The Lord said: The time will surely come when I will make a new agreement with the people of Israel and Judah.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye “Dabisa kenna, ka m na maal nɔnapaal nɛ Israel dim nɛ Juda dim la.

english_verse: It will be different from the agreement I made with their ancestors when I led them out of Egypt. Although I was their God, they broke that agreement.
translation_verse: Li kʋ nwɛnɛ nɔnaar kanɛ ka m da maal nɛ ba yaanam man da gban'e ba nu'ug ka mɔri ba yi Egipt teŋin la baa bi'elaa, bɔzugɔ, ba da san'ami m nɔnaar la, la'an nɛ man da mɔri ba, wʋʋ dau mɔr o pu'a si'em la.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Here is the new agreement that I, the Lord, will make with the people of Israel: “I will write my laws on their hearts and minds. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
translation_verse: “Nɛ'ɛŋa an nɔnaar kanɛ ka m na maal nɛ Israel dim la, li nya'aŋ m na nɔki m wada la niŋi ba sʋnya ni wʋʋ ban sɔbidi niŋid gbauŋʋn si'em la. “M na aan ba Wina'am ka ba mɛ na aan m nidib.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: “No longer will they have to teach one another to obey me. I, the Lord, promise that all of them will obey me, ordinary people and rulers alike. I will forgive their sins and forget the evil things they have done.”
translation_verse: “Sɔ' kʋ lɛm pa'al o tiraan bɛɛ o ba'abiig ye, ‘Baŋim Zugsɔb la!’ Bɔzugɔ ba wʋsa na baŋim, lin yii ba biisin paae ba kpɛɛmnamin, bɔzugɔ m na kɛɛ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la wʋsa bas ka kʋ lɛn tiɛn li yɛla ya'as baa bi'elaa.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful. I command the sun to give light each day, the moon and stars to shine at night, and ocean waves to roar.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, onɛ maal winnig ka li nie nintaŋ la, onɛ pian' ka nwadig nɛ nwadbibis zi'en ka tisid nɛɛsim yʋ'ʋŋ, onɛ gudigid Atɛuk ka li ku'onwiis dammid la o yʋ'ʋri buon Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb.

english_verse: I will never forget to give those commands, and I will never let Israel stop being a nation. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ya ye, “Bama nwa ya'a ti pʋ lɛm bɛ nwɛnɛ din nar si'em, Israel yaas la mɛ na bɔdig ka kʋ lɛn an buudi m san'anɛ.”

english_verse: Can you measure the heavens? Can you explore the depths of the earth? That's how hard it would be for me to reject Israel forever, even though they have sinned. I, the Lord, have spoken. Jerusalem Will Be Rebuilt
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, “fʋ ya'a na nyaŋi mak saŋgbana la ka kpɛn' teŋ teŋir vɛɛns teŋgbauŋ ɛɛnbir la, ala ka mam mɛ na zan'as Israel yaas ban maal si'el wʋsa la zug.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: The Lord said: Someday, Jerusalem will truly belong to me. It will be rebuilt with a boundary line running from Hananel Tower to Corner Gate.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Dabisa kenna, ka ba na lɛbisi mɛ' tempʋkaŋa tisim, lin yi Hananɛl Girimbisa la ni keŋ paae Gɔnligir Zin'ig Za'anɔɔr la.

english_verse: From there, the boundary will go in a straight line to Gareb Hill, then turn toward Goah.
translation_verse: Nwiig kanɛ ka ba mɔri makid la na pin'il anina tiɛn paae Gareb zuorin la gɔnligi keŋ Goa.

english_verse: Even that disgusting Hinnom Valley will be sacred to me, and so will the eastern slopes that go down from Horse Gate into Kidron Valley. Jerusalem will never again be destroyed.
translation_verse: Bɔn'ɔg la wʋsa, zin'ikanɛ ka ba lɔbid ninkpiilima nɛ tampɛligim la, nɛ linɛ dɛn'ɛni keŋ Kidron bɔn'ɔg nya'aŋ la, keŋ paae Widi Za'anɔɔr gɔnligirin la, na anɛ kasi tis Zugsɔb la. Tempʋʋg la kʋ lɛn san'am bɛɛ ba nwa'ae li basɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to me in the tenth year that Zedekiah was king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa an labakanɛ yi Zugsɔb la san'anɛ kɛn Jeremia ni na, Zedekaya da di o na'am la li yʋʋm piiga saŋa la, mɛ da anɛ Nebukadnɛza n da dii o na'am la li yʋʋm pii nɛ anii saŋa.

english_verse: At that time, the Babylonian army had surrounded Jerusalem, and I was in the prison at the courtyard of the palace guards.
translation_verse: Lin saŋa ka Babilon na'ab zabzabidib la da kena gilig Jerusalem, ka vi' Nɔdi'es Jeremia lɛbis banɛ gur Juda na'ayir la zakin.

english_verse: Zedekiah had ordered me to be held there because I told everyone that the Lord had said: I am the Lord, and I am about to let the king of Babylonia conquer Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Juda na'ab Zedekaya da kpɛn'ɛs o sanrega anina ka ye, “Bɔzug ka fʋ di'esid Wina'am pian'adi yɛt ala? Fʋ yɛl ye, Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, M na kɛ ka Babilon na'ab faaɛn tempʋkaŋa.

english_verse: King Zedekiah will be captured and taken to King Nebuchadnezzar, who will speak with him face to face.
translation_verse: Juda na'ab Zedekaya kʋ nyaŋi yi Babilon dim nu'usinɛ, amaa ba na gban'e o tis Babilon na'ab ka o na nyɛɛ o nɛ o mɛŋ nini, ka ba nindaa kpa' taaba ka o pian' tis o.

english_verse: Then Zedekiah will be led away to Babylonia, where he will stay until I am finished with him. So, if you people of Judah fight against the Babylonians, you will lose. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: O na mɔr Zedekaya keŋ Babilon teŋin, ka o na kpɛlim anina hali ka m maal o mam bɔɔd si'em paae li bɛn. Fʋ ya'a zab nɛ Babilon dim la fʋ kʋ nyaŋi baa.” Zugsɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Later, when I was in prison, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Jeremia da yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb labaar kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Jeremiah, your cousin Hanamel, the son of your uncle Shallum, will visit you. He must sell his field near the town of Anathoth, and because you are his nearest relative, you have the right and the responsibility to buy it and keep it in the family.
translation_verse: Hanamel onɛ an Sallum biig ka aan fʋ ba'apit biig la na kɛɛn fʋ san'an na yɛl ye, Da'ami m pɔɔg kanɛ bɛ Anatof teŋin la, bɔzugɔ fʋn kpin nɛ man la fʋ mɔr suokanɛ na da' li.”

english_verse: Hanamel came, just as the Lord had promised. And he said, “Please buy my field near Anathoth in the territory of the Benjamin tribe. You have the right to buy it, and if you do, it will stay in our family.” The Lord had told me to buy it
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la, m ba'apit biig Hanamel sid kɛɛn m san'an na zakin la ka yɛl ye, Da'ami m pɔɔg linɛ bɛ Anatof teŋin, Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin la. Fʋn sadigim mɔr suori na da' li sʋ'oe la, da'ami lii fʋ mɛŋ. Ani ka m baŋ ye li anɛ labaar kanɛ yi Zugsɔb la san'an na;

english_verse: Lord God, you stretched out your mighty arm and made the sky and the earth. You can do anything.
translation_verse: “Aa, m Zugsɔb Wina'am, fʋnɛ maal saŋgbana nɛ teŋgbauŋ nɛ fʋ mɛŋ paŋ tita'ar nɛ fʋ nu'ug kanɛ wa'am la. Si'el kae tɔi tisi fɔ.

english_verse: And while he, the witnesses, and all the other Jews sitting in the courtyard were still watching, I gave both copies to Baruch son of Neriah.
translation_verse: ka zaŋi li tis Baruk onɛ an Neraya biig ka an Mahiseya yaaŋ la, ka m ba'apit biig Hanamel bɛɛ ani nɛ kasɛtib banɛ tiki ba nu'us gbauŋʋn la, nɛ Juda dim wʋsa ka ba zin' banɛ gur la zakin.

english_verse: I told Baruch that the Lord had said: Take both copies of this bill of sale, one sealed shut and the other open, and put them in a clay jar so they will last a long time.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, ‘Nɔkim pɔɔg la da'ab gbana, linɛ tabil la nɛ linɛ pʋ tabil la, su yʋʋrin ka li na bɛɛ ani yuug.’

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I promise you that people will once again buy and sell houses, farms, and vineyards in this country. Jeremiah Questions the Lord
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, ‘Ba na lɛn da' ya' nɛ pɔɔd nɛ tiis pɔɔd teŋ kaŋa ni.’”

english_verse: You show kindness for a thousand generations, but you also punish people for the sins of their parents. You are the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Fʋ pa'annɛ fʋ nɔŋilim nɛ nidib tusa-tusa, amaa ka lɛɛ namisid tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim banɛ kpi la biisi ba saamnam yɛla. O Wina'am kanɛ zu'oe ka mɔr paŋ hali, fʋn ka fʋ yʋ'ʋr an, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la,

english_verse: With great wisdom you make plans, and with your great power you do all the mighty things you planned. Nothing we do is hidden from your eyes, and you reward or punish us as we deserve.
translation_verse: fʋ gban'ar zu'oya, ka fʋ tʋʋma an tʋʋm bɛda. Fʋ nini laki gɔsid ninsaalib wʋsa suoya; fʋ yɔɔd sɔ' wʋsa nɛ o itʋŋ nɛ o tʋʋma nar ye o di'e si'em.

english_verse: You are famous because you worked miracles in Egypt, and you are still working them in Israel and in the rest of the world as well.
translation_verse: Fʋ da tʋm nyalima nɛ zanbina Egipt teŋin ka nan kpɛn tʋmmi li paae zina, fʋ tʋmmi li Israel dim nɛ nidib wʋsa sʋʋgin, ka di'e yʋ'ʋr linɛ nam kpɛn aan fʋ din.

english_verse: You terrified the Egyptians with your miracles, and you reached out your mighty arm and rescued your people Israel from Egypt.
translation_verse: Fʋ tʋm zanbina nɛ tʋʋmnyalima mɔri fʋ nidib Israel dimi yi Egipt teŋin na, fʋ da tiɛn fʋ nu'ug kpi'euŋ nɛ nu'ug kanɛ mɔr paŋ hali ka mɔr dabiem la.

english_verse: Then you gave Israel this land rich with milk and honey, just as you had promised our ancestors.
translation_verse: Fʋ da pɔɔ zi'eli ba yaanam la ye fʋ na tisi ba teŋ kanɛ pʋbid bin'isim nɛ siind, ka sid tisi ba.

english_verse: But when our ancestors took over the land, they did not obey you. And now you have punished Israel with disaster.
translation_verse: Ba kena kpɛn' sʋ'ʋgi li, amaa ba pʋ siaki fʋ nɔɔr bɛɛ dɔlisi fʋ wada laa; ba pʋ maal fʋn yɛli ba ye ba maal si'el laa, ala ka fʋ kɛ ka tɔɔg kaŋa wʋsa paae ba.

english_verse: Jerusalem is under attack, and we suffer from hunger and disease. The Babylonians have already built dirt ramps up to the walls of our city, and you can see that Jerusalem will be captured just as you said.
translation_verse: Gɔsim ban mɛɛ gilig tempʋʋg la si'em bɔɔd ye ba faaɛn li. Li anɛ zaba nɛ kɔ'ɔm nɛ ban'as zug ka Babilon dim banɛ zabid la sid na faaɛn li. Fʋn yɛl si'el la sid maal ya, wʋʋ fʋn nyɛɛ li si'em nannanna la.

english_verse: So why did you tell me to get some witnesses and buy a field with my silver, when Jerusalem is about to be captured by the Babylonians? The Lord Explains about the Field
translation_verse: La'an nɛ Babilon dimi na faaɛn teŋ la, fʋn onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛlim ye, ‘Da'am pɔɔg la nɛ anzurifa ka kɛ ka nidib dii li kasɛt.’”

english_verse: Jeremiah, I am the Lord God. I rule the world, and I can do anything!
translation_verse: Manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ an nidib wʋsa Wina'am la. Si'el bɛɛ tɔi tis mam?

english_verse: It is true that I am going to let King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, M na nɔk teŋ kaŋa tis Babilon dim nɛ Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza ka o sʋ'ʋgi li.

english_verse: The Babylonian army is already attacking, and they will capture the city and set it on fire. The people of Jerusalem have made me angry by going up to the flat roofs of their houses and burning incense to Baal and offering wine sacrifices to other gods. Now these houses will be burned to the ground!
translation_verse: Babilon dim banɛ zabid nɛ tempʋkaŋa la na kpɛn' na nyu'oe li nɛ bugum; la'an nɛ ya' banɛ ka nidib nyɔ'ɔd bʋnnyubisa dɔɔd zugʋ tisid Baal ka basid ku'om tisid winsieba ka li duodi m sʋʋnr la.

english_verse: They have set up repulsive idols in my temple, and now it isn't a fit place to worship me.
translation_verse: Ba ba'a ba bada linɛ an bʋnkisa la yikanɛ ka man Yʋ'ʋr bɛ la ni, kɛ ka li lieb dian'ad.

english_verse: And they led Judah into sin by building places to worship Baal in Hinnom Valley, where they also sacrificed their sons and daughters to the god Molech. I have never even imagined they would commit such disgusting sins.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ' Baal teŋgbana zin'ig Ben Hinnom Biis Bɔn'ɔgin la, ye ba mɔri ba biribis nɛ ba bipumisi maan maana nyu'od bugum tisid win Molek, mam mɛŋ pʋ tisi ba nɔɔr bɛɛ li bɛɛ m pʋtɛn'ɛrin ye ba na maal yɛlkisʋg kaŋa buudi kɛ ka Juda tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ.

english_verse: Jeremiah, what you said is true. The people of Jerusalem are suffering from hunger and disease, and so the king of Babylonia will be able to capture Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ya yɛt tempʋkaŋa yɛla ye, “Li anɛ zaba nɛ kɔ'ɔm nɛ ban'as zug ka Babilon dim banɛ zabid la na faaɛn li.” Amaa Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye,

english_verse: I am angry with the people of Jerusalem, and I will scatter them in foreign countries. But someday I will bring them back here and let them live in safety.
translation_verse: M sid na la'asi ba tembanɛ ka m sʋnpɛɛn kɛ ka m widigi ba kpɛn'ɛs la ka na mɔri ba lɛb kpɛla na ka ba bɛ nɛ yɔlisim.

english_verse: They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Ba na aan m nidib ka mam mɛ na aan ba Wina'am.

english_verse: Even though I have brought disaster on the people, I will someday do all these good things for them.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Nwɛnɛ mam mɔr tɔɔgʋ kɛn bama zugin na si'em la, ala ka m na maal yɛlsʋma banɛ ka m zi'el nɔɔr ye m na tisi ba la.

english_verse: Jeremiah, when you bought the field, you showed that fields will someday be bought and sold again. You say that this land has been conquered by the Babylonians and has become a desert, emptied of people and animals.
translation_verse: Ba na lɛn da'ad pɔɔd teŋ kaŋa ni, zin'ikanɛ ka ya yɛl ye, “Teŋ la san'amnɛ ka nidib nɛ bʋnkɔnbid lɛn kae, Babilon dimi faaɛn li la zug.”

english_verse: But someday, people will again spend their silver to buy fields everywhere—in the territory of Benjamin, the region around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah, and in the hill country, the foothills to the west, and the Southern Desert. Buyers and sellers and witnesses will sign and seal the bills of sale for the fields. It will happen, because I will give this land back to my people. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ba na nɔk anzurifa ligidi da' pɔɔd, ka ba na tik nu'ug, ka kasɛtib na bɛ Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin nɛ teŋkpɛmis banɛ gilig Jerusalem la, Juda tempʋʋsin nɛ tempʋbanɛ bɛ Sefela nɛ linɛ bɛ Negef la, bɔzugɔ m yisi ba zutɔɔg la, ka yisi ba sankpan'asim pʋʋgin lɛbis na. Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: I was still being held prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guards when the Lord told me: I am the Lord, and I created the whole world.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Zugsɔb onɛ maal teŋgbauŋ wʋsa, ka ya'abi li zi'el la, o yʋ'ʋri an Zugsɔb:

english_verse: Ask me, and I will tell you things that you don't know and can't find out.
translation_verse: ‘Buolimi ka m na siak ka yɛli ya yɛlsu'ada linɛ ka ya zi'isigɛ.’”

english_verse: Many of the houses in Jerusalem and some of the buildings at the royal palace have been torn down to be used in repairing the walls to keep out the Babylonian attackers. Now there are empty spaces where the buildings once stood. But I am furious, and these spaces will be filled with the bodies of the people I kill. The people of Jerusalem will cry out to me for help, but they are evil, and I will ignore their prayers.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Gɔsima, ba da'ae ya' banɛ bɛ tempʋʋgin la nɛ na'ayir linɛ bɛ Juda la bas ye ba nɔki gu' Babilon dim ka ba da nyaŋi kpɛn' na zab nɛ ba. Amaa m sʋnpɛɛn la pʋʋgin nimbanɛ ka m na kʋ la na yadigi pɛ'ɛl ya' la nɛ zin'ig la wʋsa. M na bid tempʋkaŋa kudugʋ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la zug.

english_verse: Then someday, I will heal this place and my people as well, and let them enjoy unending peace.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, m na mɔr ti'ebʋg nɛ laafi kenna; m na ti'ebi m nidib ka kɛ ka ba nyɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm nɛ yɔlisim bɛdegʋ ka na zin' ka dabiem kae.

english_verse: I will give this land to Israel and Judah once again, and I will make them as strong as they were before.
translation_verse: M na yis Juda nɛ Israel dim sankpan'asim pʋʋgin mɔri ba lɛb na, ka na kɛ ka ba lɛm mɔr kpi'euŋ wʋʋ ban daa an si'em la.

english_verse: They sinned and rebelled against me, but I will forgive them and take away their guilt.
translation_verse: Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka ba tʋm pɔ'ɔgim la wʋsa m na pie li ka ba an nyain, ka kɛɛ ba taali bas.

english_verse: When that happens, all nations on earth will see the good things I have done for Jerusalem, and how I have given it complete peace. The nations will celebrate and praise and honor me, but they will also tremble with fear because of the powerful things I have done.
translation_verse: Ala ka tempʋkaŋa na kɛ ka m yʋ'ʋr dʋ, m na mɔr sumalisim nɛ na'asi buudi wʋsa san'an, banɛ wʋsa wʋm tʋʋm sʋma linɛ ka m ye m maali tis teŋ kaŋa la; li na paki ba, ka ba na kirid nɛ dabiem mam maali ba sʋ'ʋm nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm linɛ ka m tisi ba la yɛla.

english_verse: Jeremiah, you say that this land is a desert without people or animals, and for now, you are right. The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are deserted, and people and animals are nowhere to be seen. But someday you will hear
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, ya yɛt teŋ kaŋa yɛla ye, teŋ la san'amnɛ ka nidib bɛɛ bʋnkɔnbid lɛn kae. La'an nɛ wala Juda tempʋʋsin nɛ Jerusalem suoraad banɛ ka ba bas ka nid bɛɛ bʋnkɔnbid pʋ lɛn dɔl la, ba na lɛn wʋm tʋkpiidʋgʋ li pʋʋgin ya'as.

english_verse: happy voices and the sounds of parties and wedding celebrations. And when people come to my temple to offer sacrifices to thank me, you will hear them say: “We praise you, Lord All-Powerful! You are good to us, and your love never fails.” The land will once again be productive.
translation_verse: Ya na wʋm ka pu'apaala nɛ ba sidib maan sumalisim nɛ banɛ mɔr bareka pʋ'ʋsim piini ken Zugsɔb la Yin na yɛt ye, “Pʋ'ʋsimi Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la bareka on an sʋm la zug; o nɔŋilim la bɛ nɛ saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.” M na lɛbis zusʋŋ kanɛ ka teŋ la daa pʋn mɔr la. Zugsɔb la pian' li.

english_verse: Now it is empty, without people or animals. But when that time comes, shepherds will take care of their flocks in pastures near every town in the hill country, in the foothills to the west, in the Southern Desert, in the land of the Benjamin tribe, and around Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord's Wonderful Promise
translation_verse: Tempʋbanɛ bɛ kʋkʋna teŋ, linɛ bɛ Sefela nɛ linɛ bɛ Negef nɛ Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin la nɛ teŋkpɛmis banɛ gilig Jerusalem nɛ tempʋbanɛ bɛ Juda la, ani ka kɔnbid na lɛn gaad onɛ kaannɛ ba la nu'usin.” Zugsɔb la pian' li.

english_verse: The Lord said: I made a wonderful promise to Israel and Judah, and the days are coming when I will keep it.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Dabisa kenna,” ka m na maal nɔsʋŋ kanɛ ka m kaanbi zi'el Israel nɛ Juda dim la.

english_verse: I promise that the time will come when I will appoint a king from the family of David, a king who will be honest and rule with justice.
translation_verse: “Dabisban la ni, nɛ saŋa kan la, m na kɛ ka pʋpiel duoe David yaasin la na; O na tʋm linɛ an sʋm nɛ sida teŋ la zug.

english_verse: In those days, Judah will be safe; Jerusalem will have peace and will be named, “The Lord Gives Justice.”
translation_verse: Dabisbama ni ka Juda na paam yɔlisim ka Israel na bɛ nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm. Ban na buon o yʋ'ʋsi'a nwa, Zugsɔb Onɛ aan Ti Pʋpielim Sɔb la.”

english_verse: and there will always be priests from the Levi tribe serving at my altar and offering sacrifices to please me and to give thanks.
translation_verse: bɛɛ Levi dim banɛ an maanmaannib la kɔ'ɔŋ biribiŋ ka o na zi'enɛ m tuon saŋa wʋsa maal nyu'or maan nɛ zʋʋd maan nɛ maana wʋsa.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la labaar kɛn Jeremia san'an na ye,

english_verse: I, the Lord, have an agreement with day and night, so they always come at the right time. You can't break the agreement I made with them,
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa, ‘Ya ya'a na nyaŋi san'am nɔnaar kanɛ ka m kɛ ka yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ bɛ la ka kɛ ka li kʋ lɛn nyaŋi bɛɛ li saŋaa,

english_verse: and you can't break the agreements I have made with David's family and with the priests from the Levi tribe who serve at my altar. A descendant of David will always rule as king of Israel,
translation_verse: ala ka m nɔnaar kanɛ ka m maal nɛ m tʋmtʋm David nɛ nɔnaar kanɛ ka m maal nɛ Levi dim ka ba an maanmaannibi bɛɛ m tuonnɛ tʋm la na san'am, ka David mɛ kʋ lɛm mɔr yaaŋ ka o na zin'inɛ o na'am gbauŋ la zugɔ.

english_verse: and there will be more descendants of David and of the priests from the Levi tribe than stars in the sky or grains of sand on the beach.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka m tʋmtʋm David yaas nɛ Levi dim banɛ tʋmmi tisidi m la yaas kʋ mɔr kallɛ, ba na nwɛnɛ nwadbibis banɛ bɛ saŋgbauŋin la ka nwɛnɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin titanbin'isi an si'em la.’”

english_verse: You've heard foreigners insult my people by saying, “The Lord chose Israel and Judah, but now he has rejected them, and they are no longer a nation.”
translation_verse: “Fʋ pʋ baŋ ye nimbama nwa yɛt ye, ‘Zugsɔb la zan'as sʋ'ʋlim ayi' banɛ ka o gaŋ nwaa?’ Ala ka ba nɛ'ɛsidi m nidib la ye ba ka' buudi, ka pʋ nannɛ baa.

english_verse: Jeremiah, I will never break my agreement with the day and the night or let the sky and the earth stop obeying my commands.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, ‘M ya'a pʋ maalinɛ m nɔnaar nɛ nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ ka zi'el wada tis agɔla nɛ teŋgbauŋɔ,

english_verse: In the same way, I will never reject the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob or break my promise that they will always have a descendant of David as their king. I will be kind to my people Israel, and they will be successful again.
translation_verse: alazug m naanɛ zan'as Jakob yaas nɛ m tʋmtʋm David, ka kʋ gaŋ o yaas la yinne ka o an Abraham nɛ Isaak nɛ Jakob yaas la na'aba. M na lɛbisi ba zusʋŋ la ka yisi ba sankpan'asim pʋʋginɛ lɛbis na ka zɔɔ ba nimbaanlig.’”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar had a large army made up of people from every kingdom in his empire. He and his army were attacking Jerusalem and all the nearby towns, when the Lord told me
translation_verse: Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza nɛ o soogianam la wʋsa nɛ o sʋ'ʋlim la, nɛ o nimbanɛ ka o sʋ'oe la da zabid nɛ Jerusalem nɛ tempʋbanɛ giligi li la, labakaŋa da yi Zugsɔb la san'anɛ kɛn Jeremia san'an na ye,

english_verse: to say to King Zedekiah: I am the Lord, and I am going to let Nebuchadnezzar capture this city and burn it down.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Kem Juda na'ab Zedekaya san'anɛ yɛl o ye, Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, M bɔɔd ye m nɔk tempʋkaŋa tis Babilon na'ab ka o nyu'oe li.

english_verse: You will be taken prisoner and brought to Nebuchadnezzar, and he will speak with you face to face. Then you will be led away to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Fʋ kʋ nyaŋi zɔɔ yi ka o da gban'e fɔ amaa ba na ba'asi gban'e fʋ tis o. Fʋ na nyɛ Babilon na'ab nɛ fʋ mɛŋ nini. Fʋn nɛ on na kpa' taaba ka o pian' tisif, ka fʋ na keŋ Babilon.”

english_verse: Zedekiah, I promise that you won't die in battle.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, kɛlisim, Zugsɔb la kaanb si'em ye fʋ Juda na'ab Zedekaya kʋ kpi zaba la nii.

english_verse: You will die a peaceful death. People will mourn when you die, and they will light bonfires in your honor, just as they did for your ancestors, the kings who ruled before you.
translation_verse: Fʋ na kpinɛ baanlimm, wʋʋ fʋ yaanam banɛ da an na'anam ka kpi ka ba nyu'oe bugum na'asidi ba, ba kʋya ni si'em la, ala ka ba na nyu'oe fʋ kʋʋrin na'asif ka kaasi fʋ kʋʋr ye, “Oi, ti zugdaan gaad ya!” Mam mɛŋi kaanb nɔkaŋa. Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: I went to Zedekiah and told him what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es Jeremia da yɛl Juda na'ab Zedekaya lina wʋsa Jerusalem tempʋʋgin,

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king of Babylonia was trying to break through the walls of Lachish, Azekah, and Jerusalem, the only three towns of Judah that had not been captured. The People Break a Promise
translation_verse: saŋkan ka Babilon na'ab soogianam la da nam bɛɛ ani zabid nɛ Lakis nɛ Azeka tempʋkpi'ema banɛ da nam kpɛlim Juda la. Yammis nyɛ yɔlisim

english_verse: King Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Jerusalem made an agreement to free all Hebrew men and women who were slaves. No Jew would keep another as a slave. And so, all the Jewish slaves were given their freedom.
translation_verse: Na'ayikpɛm la nɛ banɛ wʋsa da kpɛn'ɛsi ba mɛŋ nɔnaar nwa pʋʋgin la da siak ye ba na basi ba yamdaad nɛ ba yampu'ab la, ka kʋ lɛm mɔri ba ka ba an yammisɛ. Ba da siakya ka basi ba.

english_verse: But those slave owners changed their minds and forced their former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Amaa li nya'aŋ ka ba tiaki ba pʋtɛnda ka lɛm gban'e ba ya'as.

english_verse: That's when the Lord told me to say to the people:
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb labaar kɛn Jeremia san'an na ye,

english_verse: I am the Lord God of Israel, and I made an agreement with your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, where they had been slaves.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, M da maal nɔnaar nɛ ya yaanam man da mɔri ba yi Egipt na, ya sankpan'asim pʋʋgin la. Ka yɛl ye,

english_verse: As part of this agreement, you must let a Hebrew slave go free after six years of service. Your ancestors did not obey me,
translation_verse: “Yʋma ayɔpɔi wʋsa ya na basi ya Hibiru tiraan onɛ kuos o mɛŋi tisi ya. O ya'a tʋm tisif yʋma ayuobʋ, asɛɛ ka fʋ kɛ ka o keŋ.” Ya yaanam da pʋ kɛlisid bɛɛ wʋmmi m pian'adɛ.

english_verse: but you decided to obey me and do the right thing by setting your Hebrew slaves completely free. You even went to my temple, and in my name you made an agreement to set them free. But you have abused my name, because you broke that agreement and forced your former slaves back into slavery.
translation_verse: Amaa ya lɛn fɛndigi san'amidi m yʋ'ʋr; ya wʋsa yinne-yinne lɛn lɛbi gban'e ya yamdaad nɛ yampu'ab banɛ ka ya daa bas ye ba kem ban bɔɔd zin'isi'a la. Ya mugusi ba ka ba lɛn aan ya yammis ya'as.

english_verse: You have disobeyed me by not giving your slaves their freedom. So I will give you freedom—the freedom to die in battle or from disease or hunger. I will make you disgusting to all other nations on earth.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye: Ya pʋ siaki m nɔɔrɛ; ya zan'as ya ka pʋ mɔɔl yɔlisim yɛla tisi ya taaba la. Alazugɔ, m na mɔɔl “yɔlisim” yɛla tisi ya, Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la, yɔlisim linɛ ka ya na kpi zaba ni, nɛ ban'abɛ'ɛd, nɛ kɔ'ɔm. M na kɛ ka dunia sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nyɛɛ ya nyan.

english_verse: You asked me to be a witness when you made the agreement to set your slaves free. And as part of the ceremony you cut a calf into two parts, then walked between the parts. But you people of Jerusalem have broken that agreement as well as my agreement with Israel. So I will do to you what you did to that calf.
translation_verse: Nidib banɛ san'ami m nɔnaar ka pʋ dɔlisid zi'ela banɛ ka m tisi ya la, m na buaki ya zin'isa ayi' wʋʋ na'abil ka ba ɛɛn buak zin'isa ayi' ka dɔlli li sʋʋginɛ gaad si'em la.

english_verse: I will let your enemies take all of you prisoner, including the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, the royal officials, the priests, and everyone else who walked between the two parts of the calf. These enemies will kill you and leave your bodies lying on the ground as food for birds and wild animals.
translation_verse: m na nɔki ba tisi ba dataas banɛ mɔɔd ye ba kʋʋ ba la. Ba niŋgbina la na kilim diibi tis niis banɛ ian'ad agɔla nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ bɛ teŋgbauŋ la zug la.

english_verse: These enemies are King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia and his army. They have stopped attacking Jerusalem, but they want to kill King Zedekiah and his high officials. So I will command them to return and attack again. This time they will conquer the city and burn it down, and they will capture Zedekiah and his officials. I will also let them destroy the towns of Judah, so that no one can live there any longer.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, M bɔɔd ye m tis nɛ nɔɔr, ka mɔri ba lɛb teŋ kaŋa ni na. Ba na zab nɛ teŋ la faaɛn li, ka nyu'oe li. M na kɛ ka Juda tempʋʋs la lieb dabɔɔd ka sɔ' kʋ lɛm bɛɛ ani ya'asɛ.

english_verse: “Go to the Rechabite clan and invite them to meet you in one of the side rooms of the temple. When they arrive, offer them a drink of wine.”
translation_verse: “Kem buol Rekab yidimin la ka ba kɛn Zugsɔb la Yin na kpɛn' dɔbanɛ bɛ lʋga ni la yinne, ka tisi ba daam ka ba nu.”

english_verse: So I went to Jaazaniah, the leader of the clan, and I invited him and all the men of his clan.
translation_verse: Alazug ka m keŋ buol Jaazanaya onɛ an Jeremia biig ka an Habaziniya yaaŋ, nɛ o ba'abiis nɛ o biis nɛ Rekab yidim la wʋsa.

english_verse: I brought them into the temple courtyard and took them upstairs to a room belonging to the prophets who were followers of Hanan son of Igdaliah. It was next to a room belonging to some of the officials, and that room was over the one belonging to Maaseiah, a priest who was one of the high officials in the temple.
translation_verse: Ka m mɔri ba kɛn Zugsɔb pʋ'ʋsim Yin la na, kpɛn'ɛsi ba nɔdi'es Hanan onɛ an Igdalaya biig nɛ o nya'andɔlib la dɔɔgin. Li da kpi'enɛ kpɛɛmnam la dɔɔg, linɛ bɛ Sallum biig Maaseya onɛ an za'anɔgur la dɔɔg la zugin.

english_verse: I set out some large bowls full of wine together with some cups, and then I said to the Rechabites, “Have some wine!”
translation_verse: Ka m nɔk latitada ka li pɛ'ɛl nɛ daam ka nɔk nwama nɛ bʋtiisi zi'el Rekab yidim la tuon ka yɛli ba ye, “Numi daam nwa!”

english_verse: But they answered: No! The ancestor of our clan, Jonadab son of Rechab, made a rule that we must obey. He said, “Don't ever drink wine
translation_verse: Amaa ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ti pʋ nuud daam bɔzugɔ, ti yaab Jonadab onɛ an Rekab biig la da zi'eli ti nɔkaŋa ye, ‘Yanam bɛɛ ya yaas da nu daam.’

english_verse: or build houses or plant crops and vineyards. Instead, you must always live in tents and move from place to place. If you obey this command, you will live a long time.”
translation_verse: Ka lɛn yɛl ye, ‘Da mɛɛi, bɛɛ bʋdi, bɛɛ sɛ daam tiisɛ; da mɔri nɛ'ɛnama, amaa bɛɛi sʋga ni. Ala ka ya na vʋe yuug zin'ikanɛ ka ya bɛ wʋsa guri ya bʋnkɔnbid la.’

english_verse: except now we have to live inside Jerusalem because Nebuchadnezzar has taken over the countryside with his army from Babylonia and Syria.
translation_verse: Amaa Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza daa kena faaɛn teŋ la ka ti yɛl ye, ‘Kemi na ka ti keŋ Jerusalem ka nyaŋi yi ka bas Babilon nɛ Aram dim soogianam la.’ Ala ka ti kpɛlim Jerusalem.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the people of Judah and Jerusalem: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, want you to learn a lesson
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Kem yɛl Juda dim nɛ Jerusalem nidib ye, “Ya kʋ zamis ya'am ka siaki m nɔɔr yɛlʋgɔɔ?” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: from the Rechabite clan. Their ancestor Jonadab told his descendants never to drink wine, and to this very day they have obeyed him. But I have spoken to you over and over, and you haven't obeyed me!
translation_verse: Jonadab onɛ da an Rekab biig la zi'el o yaas nɔɔr ye ba da nu daam, ka ba siak ka dɔlli li, ban siaki ba yaab nɔɔr la zug. Amaa man pian' nɔɔr bɛdegʋ tisi ya ka ya pʋ siaki m nɔɔrɛ.

english_verse: You refused to listen to my prophets, who kept telling you, “Stop doing evil and worshiping other gods! Start obeying the Lord, and he will let you live in this land he gave your ancestors.”
translation_verse: M lɛn tʋmi m tʋmtʋmnib banɛ an nɔdi'esidib la nɔɔr babiga. Ba yɛli ya ye, “Ya wʋsa yinne-yinne fɛndigimi ya suobɛ'ɛdnamin la ka tiaki ya tʋʋma; da dɔlli winsieba na'asidi baa. Lin ka ya na vʋe teŋ kanɛ ka m tis yanam nɛ ya yaanam la ni.” Amaa ya pʋ kɛlis bɛɛ wʋm tisi ma.

english_verse: The Rechabites have obeyed the command of their ancestor Jonadab, but you have not obeyed me,
translation_verse: Jonadab yaas la dɔlisi ba yaab Rekab n zi'eli ba nɔsi'a la, amaa nimbama pʋ siaki m nɔɔrɛ.

english_verse: your God. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and I warned you about the terrible things that would happen to you if you did not listen to me. But you have ignored me, so now disaster will strike you. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to the Rechabites
translation_verse: “Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, ‘Kɛlisimi! M na kɛ ka tɔɔg kanɛ ka m yɛli zi'el la paae Juda nɛ Jerusalem dim wʋsa. M pian' tisi ba amaa ba pʋ kɛlisɛ; m buoli ba amaa ba pʋ siakɛ.’”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to say to the Rechabite clan: “I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You have obeyed your ancestor Jonadab,
translation_verse: Jeremia da yɛl Rekab yidim la ye, “Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa, ‘Ya siaki ya yaab Jonadab ka siak o nɔzi'ela ka maal on yɛli ya si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: so I promise that your clan will be my servants and will never die out.”
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye Jonadab onɛ an Rekab biig la kʋ kɔ'ɔŋ biribis banɛ na tʋmmi tisid mam.’”

english_verse: During the fourth year that Jehoiakim son of Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah,
translation_verse: Juda na'ab Jehoyakim onɛ an Josia biig la da di o na'am la li yʋma anaasi saŋa, labakaŋa da yi Zugsɔb la san'anɛ kɛn Jeremia ni na ye,

english_verse: since the time Josiah was king, I have been speaking to you about Israel, Judah, and the other nations. Now, get a scroll and write down everything I have told you,
translation_verse: “Nɔkim gbauŋʋ sɔb pian'abanɛ ka m pian'adi tisidif Israel yɛla, nɛ Juda nɛ tɛɛns banɛ bɛ la, mam pin'il Josia na'am diib saŋa pian'adi tisidif hali ti paae nannanna la.

english_verse: then read it to the people of Judah. Maybe they will stop sinning when they hear what terrible things I plan for them. And if they turn back to me, I will forgive them.”
translation_verse: Daasi'erɛɛ Juda nidib ya'a wʋm tɔɔg banɛ wʋsa ka m ye m mɔri kɛɛn ba zugin na la, ba wʋsa yinne-yinne na fɛndig ka basi ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la ka m na kɛɛ ba bɛ'ɛd la nɛ ba taali bas.”

english_verse: I sent for Baruch son of Neriah and asked him to help me. I repeated everything the Lord had told me, and Baruch wrote it all down on a scroll.
translation_verse: Alazug Jeremia da buol Baruk onɛ an Neraya biig la tu'as o; Jeremia bɛɛ ani tu'asid Zugsɔb pian'ad la, ka Baruk sɔbidi li gbauŋʋn.

english_verse: Then I said, Baruch, the officials refuse to let me go into the Lord's temple,
translation_verse: Ban sɔbi naae la ka Jeremia yɛl Baruk ye, “Ba vi' m suor; m kʋ nyaŋi keŋ Zugsɔb pʋ'ʋsim Yinnɛ.

english_verse: so you must go instead. Wait for the next holy day when the people of Judah come to the temple to pray and to go without eating. Then take this scroll to the temple and read it aloud.
translation_verse: Dinzug fʋn kem Zugsɔb pʋ'ʋsim Yin dabiskanɛ ka ba lɔ nɔɔr la, ka karim gbauŋ kanɛ ka fʋ sɔb la tis nidib la. Karim tis Juda nidib wʋsa banɛ yii ba tɛɛnsin kena la.

english_verse: The Lord is furious, and if the people hear how he is going to punish them, maybe they will ask to be forgiven.
translation_verse: Daasi'erɛɛ ba na mɔri ba winsɔsʋgʋ kɛn Zugsɔb san'an na, ka sɔ' wʋsa na fɛndig ka bas o suobɛ'ɛd la, ka Zugsɔb la sʋnpɛɛn linɛ ka o yɛl la zu'onɛ galis.”

english_verse: In the ninth month of the fifth year that Jehoiakim was king, the leaders set a day when everyone who lived in Jerusalem or who was visiting there had to pray and go without eating. So Baruch took the scroll to the upper courtyard of the temple. He went over to the side of the courtyard and stood in a covered area near New Gate, where he read the scroll aloud. This covered area belonged to Gemariah, one of the king's highest officials.
translation_verse: Lin saŋa ka Baruk da bɛ Safan biig Gemaraya onɛ an gbansɔbid la dɔɔgin, linɛ bɛ zak kanɛ bɛ zugin Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yir Za'anɔpaallin la, ka o karim tis nimbanɛ bɛ Zugsɔb pʋ'ʋsim Yin la wʋsa Jeremia pian'ad linɛ bɛ gbauŋʋn la.

english_verse: Gemariah's son Micaiah was there and heard Baruch read what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Mikaya onɛ an Gemaraya biig ka an Safan yaaŋ la da wʋm Zugsɔb la pian'ad linɛ bɛ gbauŋʋn la,

english_verse: When Baruch finished reading, Micaiah went down to the palace. His father Gemariah was in the officials' room, meeting with the rest of the king's officials, including Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, and Zedekiah.
translation_verse: o da sigi kpɛn' gbansɔbid la dɔɔgin linɛ bɛ na'ayin la, zin'ikanɛ ka kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa zin' la, ba da anɛ Elisama onɛ an gbansɔbid la nɛ Delaya onɛ an Semaya biig la nɛ Elinatan onɛ an Akibo biig la nɛ Gemaraya onɛ an Safan biig la nɛ Zedekaya onɛ an Hanania biig la nɛ kpɛɛm banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa.

english_verse: Micaiah told them what he had heard Baruch read to the people.
translation_verse: Mikaya da yɛli ba Baruk n karim si'el gbauŋʋn la tis nidib la ka ba wʋm la nya'aŋ,

english_verse: the officials said, “Please sit down and read it to us,” which he did.
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl o ye, “Zin'inim, ka karim tisi ti!” Ka Baruk karim tisi ba.

english_verse: After they heard what was written on the scroll, they were worried and said to each other, “The king needs to hear this!” Turning to Baruch, they asked,
translation_verse: Ban wʋm pian'abama wʋsa la dabiem da gban'e ba, ka ba gɔsid taaba ka yɛl Baruk ye, “Asɛɛ ti yɛl Na'ab la pian'abama wʋsa.”

english_verse: “Did someone tell you what to write on this scroll?”
translation_verse: Ani ka ba yɛl Baruk ye, “Yɛlimi ti, fʋ niŋ wala sɔb nɛ' wʋsa? Jeremia pian' li tisi fɔɔ?”

english_verse: “Yes, Jeremiah did,” Baruch replied. “I wrote down just what he told me.”
translation_verse: Ka Baruk lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, onɛ pian' tisim ka m sɔb gbauŋʋn la.”

english_verse: The officials said, “You and Jeremiah must go into hiding, and don't tell anyone where you are going.”
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛmnam la yɛl Baruk ye, “Fʋn nɛ Jeremia kem su'a, da kɛ ka sɔ' baŋ yanamɛ bɛ zin'isi'aa.”

english_verse: The king told his son Jerahmeel to take Seraiah and Shelemiah and to go arrest Baruch and me. But the Lord kept them from finding us. Jeremiah's Second Scroll
translation_verse: Na'ab la lɛɛ da tisnɛ nɔɔr ye Jerameel onɛ an Na'ab biig la, nɛ Seraya onɛ an Aziriel biig la nɛ Sielemaya onɛ an Abidel biig la, kem gban'e Baruk onɛ an gbansɔbid la nɛ Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la na. Amaa ka Zugsɔb la su'a ba.

english_verse: I had told Baruch what to write on that first scroll, but King Jehoiakim had burned it. So the Lord told me
translation_verse: Na'ab la daa nyu'oe gbambanɛ ka Jeremia pian' ka Baruk sɔb la nya'aŋ la, Zugsɔb labaar da kɛn Jeremia san'an na ye,

english_verse: to get another scroll and write down everything that had been on the first one.
translation_verse: Nɔkim gbauŋ yinne ya'asi sɔb pian'ad linɛ bɛ gbauŋ kanɛ ka Na'ab Jehoyakim nyu'oe la ni.

english_verse: Then he told me to say to King Jehoiakim: Not only did you burn Jeremiah's scroll, you had the nerve to ask why he had written that the king of Babylonia would attack and ruin the land, killing all the people and even the animals.
translation_verse: Mɛ yɛlim Juda na'ab Jehoyakim ye Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, Fʋ nyu'oe gbauŋ la ka yɛl ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ sɔbi ani ye Babilon na'ab na kena san'am teŋ kaŋa ka nidib nɛ bʋnkɔnbid kʋ lɛm bɛ?”

english_verse: So I, the Lord, promise that you will be killed and your body thrown out on the ground. The sun will beat down on it during the day, and the frost will settle on it at night. And none of your descendants will ever be king of Judah.
translation_verse: Dinzug, Zugsɔb la yɛl Juda na'ab Jehoyakim yɛla si'em nwa, O kʋ nyɛ biig kanɛ na zin'in Na'ab David na'am gbauŋ la zugɔ; ba na lɔb o niŋgbina bas ka nintaŋ tʋʋlʋg nwɛ'ɛdi li nintaŋ ka wama'asim na ga'aŋi li yʋ'ʋŋ.

english_verse: You, your children, and your servants are evil, and I will punish everyone of you. I warned you and the people of Judah and Jerusalem that I would bring disaster, but none of you have listened. So now you are doomed!
translation_verse: M na namis on nɛ o biis nɛ o tʋmtʋmnib la ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la zug; banɛ bɛ Jerusalem nɛ banɛ bɛ Juda la, tɔɔg kanɛ ka m gban'e ye li na kena la, m na mɔri li ba zugin na bɔzugɔ ba pʋ kɛlisida.

english_verse: After the Lord finished speaking to me, I got another scroll and gave it to Baruch. Then I told him what to write, so this second scroll would contain even more than was on the scroll Jehoiakim had burned.
translation_verse: Ala ka Jeremia lɛn nɔk gbansi'a tis gbansɔbid Baruk onɛ an Neraya biig la, ka Jeremia lɛm pian'ad ka Baruk sɔbid pian'abanɛ bɛ gbauŋ kanɛ ka Juda na'ab Jehoyakim nyu'oe la. Ka lɛm paas pian'asieba li zug banɛ nwɛnɛ ala.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia had removed Jehoiachin son of Jehoiakim from being the king of Judah and had made Josiah's son Zedekiah king instead.
translation_verse: Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza da diis Zedekaya onɛ an Josia biig la Juda na'am, ka o di'e Jehoyakin onɛ an Jehoyakim biig la zin'ig.

english_verse: But Zedekiah, his officials, and everyone else in Judah ignored everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: On bɛɛ o tʋmtʋmnib la bɛɛ nimbanɛ bɛ teŋin la da pʋ kɛlis Zugsɔb la pian' si'eli tis Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la.

english_verse: Then the Lord told me to send them back to Zedekiah with this message: Zedekiah, you wanted Jeremiah to ask me, the Lord God of Israel, what is going to happen. So I will tell you. The king of Egypt and his army came to your rescue, but soon they will go back to Egypt.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa, “Yɛlim Juda na'ab onɛ tʋmi ya na ye ya bu'osim la ye, ‘Faaro soogianam banɛ kena ye ba sʋ'ʋŋif la na lɛbi ba mɛŋ teŋin Egipt,

english_verse: Then the Babylonians will return and attack Jerusalem, and this time they will capture the city and set it on fire.
translation_verse: ka Babilon dim la lɛb na zab nɛ tempʋkaŋa. Ba na faaɛn li ka nyu'oe li nɛ bugum.’

english_verse: Don't fool yourselves into thinking that the Babylonians will leave as they did before.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa ye, ‘Da ma'aa ya mɛŋ ka tɛn'ɛsid ye, “Babilon dim la na basi tii.” Ba kʋ basɛ!

english_verse: Even if you could defeat their entire army, their wounded survivors would still be able to leave their tents and set Jerusalem on fire. Jeremiah Is Put in Prison
translation_verse: Hali baa ya ya'a nyaŋ Babilon soogianam banɛ zabid nɛ ya la ka li kpɛlim nɛ ba nimbanɛ pu'alim la ma'aa bɛɛ ba sʋga la ni, ba na yina nyu'oe tempʋkaŋa.’”

english_verse: The Babylonian army had left because the Egyptian army was on its way to help us.
translation_verse: Babilon soogianam la da fɔnrigi lɛb nya'aŋ Faaro soogianam la zug,

english_verse: So I decided to leave Jerusalem and go to the territory of the Benjamin tribe to claim my share of my family's land.
translation_verse: Jeremia da duoe ye o yi tempʋʋgin la ka keŋ Benjamin sʋ'ʋlimin ye o di'e o pʋʋr linɛ aan o faar o nidibin la.

english_verse: I was leaving Jerusalem through Benjamin Gate, when I was stopped by Irijah, the officer in charge of the soldiers at the gate. He said, “Jeremiah, you're under arrest for trying to join the Babylonians.”
translation_verse: Amaa on da paae Benjamin Za'anɔɔrin la, banɛ gur za'anɔɔr la kpɛɛm onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Irija ka o saam an Sielemaya ka o yaab an Hanania la da gban'e o ka yɛl ye, “Fʋ pʋ bas teŋ la nɛ ka keŋ la'as nɛ Babilon dim laa?”

english_verse: “I'm not trying to join them!” I answered. But Irijah wouldn't listen, and he took me to the king's officials.
translation_verse: Jeremia da lɛbis ye, “Li ka' sidaa, m pʋ bas teŋ la ka keŋ la'as nɛ Babilon dima.” Amaa Irija da pʋ kɛlis o pian'ad la, ka gban'e o mɔri keŋ tis kpɛɛmnam la.

english_verse: King Zedekiah secretly had me brought to his palace, where he asked, “Is there any message for us from the Lord?” “Yes, there is, Your Majesty,” I replied. “The Lord is going to let the king of Babylonia capture you.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Zedekaya tʋm ka ba mɔr o kɛn na'ayin la na, ka o su'a bu'os o ye, “Labaar pʋ yi Zugsɔb la san'an naa?” Ka Jeremia lɛbis ye, “Sida, Zugsɔb la na nɔki fʋ tis Babilon na'ab.”

english_verse: Then I continued, “Your Majesty, why have you put me in prison? Have I committed a crime against you or your officials or the nation?
translation_verse: Jeremia da lɛm bu'os Na'ab Zedekaya ye, “Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd bɔ ka m tʋm tisif bɛɛ fʋ na'ayikpɛm la bɛɛ nimbama ka ya kpɛn'ɛsim sanrega ni?

english_verse: Have you locked up the prophets who lied to you and said that the king of Babylonia would never attack Jerusalem?
translation_verse: Fʋ nɔdi'esidib banɛ pian' ziri tisif la bɛ yaanɛ, banɛ yɛl ye Babilon dim kʋ zab nɛ teŋ kaŋa la?

english_verse: Please, don't send me back to that prison at Jonathan's house. If you do, I will die there.”
translation_verse: Amaa nannanna, m zugdaan Na'aba, Naa, kɛlisim ka m mɔri m sɔsʋgʋ kɛɛn fʋ tuon na. Da lɛbisim Jonatan onɛ an gbansɔbid la yinnɛ, ya'a ka' ala m na kpii ani.”

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me taken to the prison cells in the courtyard of the palace guards. He told the soldiers to give me a loaf of bread from one of the bakeries every day until the city ran out of grain.
translation_verse: Na'ab Zedekaya da tis nɔɔr ye ba niŋim Jeremia banɛ gur la zakin ka tisid o bodobodo gbil yinne daar wʋsa ti paae diibi na naae tempʋʋgin la nyain. Ala ka Jeremia da kpɛlim banɛ gur la zakin.

english_verse: So the four of them went to the king and said, “You should put Jeremiah to death, because he is making the soldiers and everyone else lose hope. He isn't trying to help our people; he's trying to harm them.”
translation_verse: Kpɛɛmnam la da yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Dau kaŋa sʋ'ʋm ye ba kʋʋ o. On yɛt si'el la pu'asidnɛ soogianam banɛ kpɛlim tempʋʋgin la nɛ nidib la wʋsa giinla. Dau kaŋa pʋ bɔɔd nidib la sʋ'ʋm amaa o mɔɔdnɛ ba san'auŋ.”

english_verse: Zedekiah replied, “Do what you want with him. I can't stop you.”
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Zedekaya lɛbis ye, “O bɛ nɛ ya nu'usin, man kanɛ an na'ab la kʋ nyaŋi ki'isi ya nɔɔrɛ.”

english_verse: Then they took me back to the courtyard of the palace guards and let me down with ropes into the well that belonged to Malchiah, the king's son. There was no water in the well, but I sank down in the mud.
translation_verse: Alazug ba da nɔk Jeremia sigis Malkija onɛ an Na'ab biig la buligin, linɛ da bɛ banɛ gur la zakin la. Ka ba nɔk nwiisi sigis Jeremia buligin la. Ku'om da ka' li pʋʋginɛ li lɛɛ da anɛ bian'ar ma'aa, ka Jeremia fir bian'arin la.

english_verse: Ebedmelech said, “Your Majesty, Jeremiah is a prophet, and those men were wrong to throw him into a well. And when Jerusalem runs out of food, Jeremiah will starve to death down there.”
translation_verse: “M zugdaan Na'aba, nimbama maal Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la si'em la anɛ bugusim tʋʋma. Ba lɔs o nɛ buligin, ka o na namis ka kpi kɔ'ɔm bɔzugɔ, diib lɛn kae tempʋʋginɛ.”

english_verse: Ebedmelech and the soldiers went to the palace and got some rags from the room under the treasury. He used ropes to lower them into the well.
translation_verse: Alazug Ebɛd-Melek da buol nidib la ka keŋ ban su'ad la'ad dɔsi'a na'ayin la teŋir la nɔk kparikɛɛnd nɛ fukʋda ani lɔ nɛ nwiisi sigisi tis Jeremia buligin la.

english_verse: Then he said, “Put these rags under your arms so the ropes won't hurt you.” After I did,
translation_verse: Ebɛd-Melek da yɛl Jeremia ye, “Nɔkim kparikɛɛnd nɛ fukʋda nwa' vili fʋ nu'us ka nwiis la da pu'alimi fɔ.” Ka Jeremia niŋ ala,

english_verse: the men pulled me out. And from then on, I was kept in the courtyard of the palace guards. King Zedekiah Questions Jeremiah
translation_verse: ka ba vɛ'ɛg o nɛ nwiis buligin la dʋ'ʋs o na. Ka Jeremia da kpɛlim banɛ gur la zakin. Zedekaya sɔs Jeremia ye o sa'al o

english_verse: King Zedekiah had me brought to his private entrance to the temple, and he said, “I'm going to ask you something, and I want to know the truth.”
translation_verse: Na'ab Zedekaya da lɛn tʋm buol Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la na, Pʋ'ʋsim Yir za'anɔɔr kanɛ paas atan' la ni, ka yɛl o ye, “M bɔɔd ye m bu'osif nɛ si'el, da su'am si'el si'ela.”

english_verse: “Why?” I replied. “You won't listen, and you might even have me killed!”
translation_verse: Jeremia da yɛl Zedekaya ye, “M ya'a tisif lɛbisʋg fʋ kʋ kʋʋ maa? Baa man ya'a tisif sa'alʋg fʋ kʋ kɛlisɛ.”

english_verse: He said, “I swear in the name of the living Lord our Creator that I won't have you killed. No one else can hear what we say, and I won't let anyone kill you.”
translation_verse: Amaa Zedekaya da su'a pɔɔ tis Jeremia ye, “M pɔya nɛ Wina'am kanɛ vʋe ka tisidi ti pɛbisim la, m kʋ kʋʋf bɛɛ nɔki fɔ tis banɛ bɔɔd ye ba kʋʋf la.”

english_verse: Then I told him that the Lord had said: “Zedekiah, I am the Lord God All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I promise that if you surrender to King Nebuchadnezzar's officers, you and your family won't be killed, and Jerusalem won't be burned down.
translation_verse: Ani ka Jeremia yɛl Zedekaya ye, “Wina'am onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa': ‘Fʋ ya'a nɔki fʋ mɛŋi tis Babilon na'ayikpɛm la, ba kʋ kʋʋ fɔ, ka mɛ kʋ nyu'oe tempʋkaŋa; fʋn nɛ fʋ yidim wʋsa na vʋe.

english_verse: But if you don't surrender, I will let the Babylonian army capture Jerusalem and burn it down, and you will be taken prisoner.”
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ ya'a kʋ siaki nɔki fʋ mɛŋi tis Babilon na'ab na'ayikpɛm la, Babilon dim na faaɛn li ka nyu'oe li nɛ bugum; fʋ mɛ kʋ nyaŋi zɔɔ yii ba nu'usinɛ.’”

english_verse: Zedekiah answered, “I can't surrender to the Babylonians. I'm too afraid of the people of Judah who have already joined them. The Babylonians might hand me over to them, and they would torture me.”
translation_verse: Zedekaya da yɛl Jeremia ye, “M zɔtnɛ Jew dim banɛ aaɛn lɛb Babilon dimin la dabiem, Babilon dim la pa'ati nɔkimi tisi ba ka ba niŋim yɔri-yɔri.”

english_verse: I said, “If you will just obey the Lord, the Babylonians won't hand you over to those Jews. You will be allowed to live, and all will go well for you.
translation_verse: Jeremia da lɛbis o ye, “Ba kʋ nɔki fʋ tisɛ!” Siakim Zugsɔb la nɔɔr ka niŋ wʋʋ man yɛlif si'em la, ba na basif ka kʋ kʋʋ fɔ.

english_verse: But the Lord has shown me that if you refuse to obey,
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ ya'a zan'as ka pʋ nɔki fʋ mɛŋi tisɛ, Zugsɔb la nie si'eli tisimi nwa',

english_verse: then the women of your palace will be taken prisoner by Nebuchadnezzar's officials. And those women will say to you: Friends you trusted led you astray. Now you're trapped in mud, and those friends you trusted have all turned away.
translation_verse: Pu'a banɛ kpɛlim Juda na'ayin la, ba na mɔri ba yii keŋ Babilon na'ab na'ayikpɛm la san'an. Pu'a ban la na ti yɛl ye, “Fʋ zuanam banɛ ka fʋ niŋi ba yadda la ma'af ka nyaŋif, fʋ nɔba fir bian'arin; ka fʋ zuanam zɔ ka basif.”

english_verse: The Babylonian army will take your wives and children captive, you will be taken as a prisoner to the King of Babylonia, and Jerusalem will be burned down.”
translation_verse: “Babilon dim la na faaɛn fʋ pu'ab nɛ fʋ biis la wʋsa. Fʋ mɛ kʋ nyaŋi zɔɔ yii ba nu'usinɛ amaa Babilon na'ab na gban'af; ka ba na nyu'oe tempʋkaŋa.”

english_verse: Zedekiah said, “Jeremiah, if you tell anyone what we have talked about, you might lose your life.
translation_verse: Zedekaya da yɛl Jeremia ye, “Da kɛ ka sɔ' baŋi ti sɔnsig nwa' yɛllɛ, ya'a ka' ala fʋ na kpi.

english_verse: And I'm sure that if my officials hear about our meeting, they will ask you what we said to each other. They might even threaten to kill you if you don't tell them.
translation_verse: Na'ayikpɛm la ya'a ti wʋm ye fʋ kena sɔns nɛ m ka kena yɛlif ye, ‘Yɛlimi ti fʋn yɛl Na'ab si'el la nɛ Na'abi yɛlif si'el la, ya'a ka' ala ti na kʋʋf.’

english_verse: So if they question you, tell them you were begging me not to send you back to the prison at Jonathan's house, because going back there would kill you.”
translation_verse: Fʋn yɛlim ye, ‘M pa'a sɔsidnɛ Na'ab la suguru ye o da lɛbisim Jonatan yin ka m kpii ani.’”

english_verse: The officials did come and question me about my meeting with the king, and I told them exactly what he had ordered me to say. They never spoke to me about the meeting again, since no one had heard us talking.
translation_verse: Na'ayikpɛm la wʋsa sid da kɛn Jeremia san'an na bu'os o, ka o lɛbisi ba Na'ab la yɛl o ye o yɛl si'el la wʋsa. Ka ba pʋ lɛn yɛl o si'ela, sɔ' pʋ wʋm on sɔns si'el nɛ Na'ab la zug.

english_verse: I was held in the courtyard of the palace guards until the day Jerusalem was captured.
translation_verse: Jeremia da kpɛm bɛ banɛ gur la zakin hali ti paae saŋa kanɛ ka Babilon dim faaɛn Jerusalem la.

english_verse: When King Zedekiah and his troops saw that Jerusalem had been captured, they tried to escape from the city that same night. They went to the king's garden, where they slipped through the gate between the two city walls and headed toward the Jordan River valley.
translation_verse: Juda na'ab nɛ o soogianamɛ nyɛɛ ba la, ba da yi yʋ'ʋŋʋ dɔl na'ab lɔmbɔn'ɔg suor la zɔɔ dɔl za'anɔɔr linɛ bɛ zaŋguoma ayi' sʋʋgin la, zɔti kpa'ad Araba linɛ an Joodan bɔn'ɔgin la.

english_verse: to Ebedmelech from Ethiopia: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. I warned everyone that I would bring disaster, not prosperity, to this city. Now very soon I will do what I said, and you will see it happen.
translation_verse: “Kem yɛl Ebɛd-Melek onɛ an Kus nid la ye Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, ‘M bɔɔd ye m kɛ ka man zi'el nɔɔr teŋ kaŋa yɛla si'em la niŋ amɛŋa, li na anɛ tɔɔgʋ tisi ba. Li saŋa ya'a paae li na niŋi fʋ nini ni.

english_verse: “Find Jeremiah and keep him safe. Take good care of him and do whatever he asks.”
translation_verse: “Nɔkim o gur o; da daam o, amaa tisim o on sɔs si'el wʋsa.”

english_verse: But the Babylonian troops caught up with them near Jericho. They arrested Zedekiah and took him to the town of Riblah in the land of Hamath, where Nebuchadnezzar put him on trial, then found him guilty,
translation_verse: Amaa ka Babilon zabzabidib la kadi ba paae Jeriko zin'ikanɛ an sassi la nii gban'e ba mɔri keŋ Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza san'an Dibila linɛ bɛ Hamat teŋin la, ka Na'ab la da kadi ba saria ani.

english_verse: and gave orders for him to be punished. Zedekiah's sons were killed there in front of him, and so were the leaders of Judah's ruling families.
translation_verse: Babilon na'ab da kɛ ka ba kʋ Zedekaya biis o nini ni ka kʋʋ o na'ayikpɛm la wʋsa.

english_verse: Then his eyes were poked out, and he was put in chains, so he could be dragged off to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ani ka o kpig Zedekaya nini ka lɔɔ o nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug bana mɔr o keŋ Babilon teŋin.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Babylonian army had burned the houses in Jerusalem, including the royal palace, and they had broken down the city walls.
translation_verse: Babilon dim la da nyu'oe na'ayir la nɛ bugum nɛ nidib la ya' wʋsa, ka da'ae Jerusalem zaŋguoma la wʋsa bas.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guards, led away everyone from the city as prisoners, even those who had deserted to Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan onɛ an soogianam kpɛɛm la da gban'e nimbanɛ kpɛlim tempʋʋgin la nɛ banɛ da dɛŋi zɔ ka bas Zedekaya la wʋsa mɔri keŋ Babilon.

english_verse: Only the poorest people who owned no land were left behind in Judah, and Nebuzaradan gave them fields and vineyards.
translation_verse: Amaa o da bas banɛ an nɔŋ dim ka pʋ mɔr si'el la Juda teŋin ka tisi ba vain tiis pɔɔd nɛ pɔɔd.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar had given the following orders to Nebuzaradan:
translation_verse: Babilon na'ab da pʋn tis Nebuzaradan onɛ an soogianam kpɛɛm la nɔɔr Jeremia yɛla ye,

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, Nebushazban, Nergal Sharezer, and the other officers of King Nebuchadnezzar
translation_verse: Ala ka Nebuzaradan nɛ o kpɛɛm taaba Nebusiasiban nɛ Negal-Siareza nɛ banɛ an Babilon na'ab na'ayikpɛm la wʋsa

english_verse: sent some of their troops to bring me from the courtyard of the royal palace guards. They put me in the care of Gedaliah son of Ahikam and told him to take me to my home. And so I was allowed to stay with the people who remained in Judah. The Lord Promises To Protect Ebedmelech
translation_verse: da tʋm ka ba yis Jeremia banɛ gur la zakin na ka nɔk o tis Gedalaya onɛ an Ahikam biig ka an Safan yaaŋ la ka o mɔr o kul, ka o kpɛlim ani nɛ o nidib.

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Ban da nan gur Jeremia zakin la, Zugsɔb la labaar da kɛɛn o san'an na ye,

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M na faanf ka ba kʋ kʋʋf zaba nii, amaa fʋ na zɔɔ faaɛn fʋ nyɔvʋr, fʋn tisim sida la zug.’” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Ban da gban'e nidib Jerusalem nɛ Juda tɛɛnsin ye ba zii ba keŋ Babilon la, ba mɛ da lɔ Jeremia nɛ bana ka kɛ ka o bɛɛ ba sʋʋgin. Amaa Nebuzaradan onɛ an banɛ gur Babilon tuongat la da nyɛɛ o ka yis o bas Rama teŋin. Lin nya'aŋ ka Zugsɔb labaar da kɛn Jeremia san'an na.

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: Amaa zina m yis bana la fʋ nu'usin. Fʋ ya'a bɔɔd, fʋn dɔllimi keŋ Babilon teŋin ka m na gɔsif sʋ'ʋŋa; fʋ ya'a pʋ lɛm bɔɔda, fʋn kɛl, ka kpɛlim kpɛla. Gɔsima, teŋ la dig la, fʋn bɔɔd zin'isi'a wʋsa fʋn kem.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar has chosen Gedaliah to rule Judah. You can live near Gedaliah, and he will provide for you, or you can live anywhere else you choose. Nebuzaradan gave me a supply of food, then let me leave.
translation_verse: Jeremia n da nam pʋ fɛndig ye o keŋ bɛɛ o lɛbis o la, ka Nebuzaradan lɛn yɛl ye, “Lɛm Gedalaya onɛ an Ahikam biig ka an Safan yaaŋ la san'an, on ka Babilon na'ab gaŋ ye o sʋ'oe Juda tɛɛns la, ka fʋn nɛ on nɛ nidib la la'am bɛ; bɛɛ fʋ keŋ fʋn bɔɔd si'el.” Tuongat la da tis o diib nɛ piini ka naan kɛ ka o keŋ.

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Ala ka Jeremia da duoe keŋ Gedalaya san'an Misipa teŋinɛ bɛ nɛ nimbanɛ da kpɛlim teŋin la. Gedalaya lieb gɔmena sʋ'oe Juda (

english_verse: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, together with Johanan and Jonathan, the two sons of Kareah, had been officers in Judah's army. And so had Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah from Maacah. They and their troops had been stationed outside Jerusalem and had not been captured. They heard that Gedaliah had been chosen to rule Judah, and that the poorest men, women, and children had not been taken away to Babylonia. So they went to Mizpah and met with their new ruler.
translation_verse: Ani ka ba kɛn Gedalaya san'an na Misipa teŋin. Tuongatib la da anɛ Isimael onɛ an Netanaya biig la nɛ Johanan nɛ Jonatan banɛ da an Karea biis la nɛ Seraya onɛ an Tanhumef biig la nɛ Efai onɛ an Netofa nid la biis nɛ Jaazanaya onɛ yi Maaka la, ka ba dɔlli ba nidib la kena.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ na kpɛlim Misipa zi'enɛ ya nɔba zug Babilon dim la ya'a ti kennɛ ti san'an na, amaa yanam na kpɛlim tempʋbanɛ ka ya di'e la ni, ka bun zʋʋd la ka maal tiis daam la nɛ kpaam su yʋya la ni ka yadig tiwala la.”

english_verse: Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year. Gedaliah Is Murdered
translation_verse: ba wʋsa da lɛb Juda teŋgbauŋʋn Gedalaya san'an Misipa teŋin na. Ba da yinɛ tɛɛns banɛ ka ba widigi kpɛn' la wʋsa ni. Ba da nyɛ daam bɛdegʋ nɛ tiis wala. Ban kʋ Gedalaya la yɛla (

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Karea biig Johanan nɛ soogianam tuongatib banɛ da bɛ paalʋ la wʋsa da kɛn Gedalaya san'an na Misipa teŋin

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: ka yɛl o ye, “Fʋ zi' ye Ammon na'ab Baalis n tʋm Netanaya biig Isimael na ye o kʋʋ fɔɔ?” Amaa Gedalaya da pʋ niŋi ba yadda.
