english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Karea biig Johanan da yɛl Gedalaya o kɔn'ɔkɔn' Misipa teŋin ye, “Kɛl ka m keŋ kʋ Isimael ka sɔ' da baŋɛ. Bɔ ka o bɔɔd ye o kʋʋf ka kɛ ka Israel dim banɛ la'asi giligif la widig ka Juda dim banɛ kpɛlim la mɛ widigi ti ba'asi bɔdigɛ?”

english_verse: Gedaliah answered, “Don't kill Ishmael! What you've said about him can't be true.”
translation_verse: Amaa Gedalaya da lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Da tʋm tʋʋm kanɛ! Fʋn yɛt Isimael yɛla si'em la ka' sidaa.”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Nwadis ayɔpɔi la ni ka Isimael onɛ an Netanaya biig ka an Elisama yaaŋ ka an na'ayikpɛɛm la da dɔl dap piiga kɛn Ahikam biig Gedalaya san'an Misipa teŋin na. Ban da la'asi dit la,

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Isimael nɛ o dap piiga la da duoe nɔk sʋ'ʋgʋ kʋ Gedalaya. Ala ka ba da kʋ ninkanɛ ka Babilon na'ab gaŋ ye o an gɔmena teŋin la.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Isimael mɛ da kʋ Juda dim banɛ da bɛ Gedalaya san'an la wʋsa, la'an nɛ Babilon soogianam banɛ da bɛ ani la.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Ban da kʋ Gedalaya yimbɛog ka sɔ' nam pʋ baŋi li yɛl la,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Netanaya biig Isimael da yi Misipa na tʋ'ʋsi ba. O da kennɛ ka kum, ka yɛli ba ye, “Kemi Ahikam biig Gedalaya san'an na.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: Ban kpɛn' tempʋʋgin la, Isimael nɛ dap banɛ da bɛɛ o san'an la da kʋʋ baa lɔs buligin.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Amaa ba nidib piiga da yɛl Isimael ye, “Da kʋʋ ti! Tinam mɔr ki nɛ mui nɛ kpaam nɛ siind ka nɔki li su'a.” Ka o basi ba ka pʋ la'asi ba nɛ bama la kʋʋ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Isimael da gban'e Na'ab la pu'ayuos nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ Misipa la wʋsa nɛ banɛ da kpɛlim ani ka Nebuzaradan da gaŋ Gedalaya ye o guri ba la wʋsa. O da gban'e ba mɔri lɔ'ɔŋi keŋ Ammon dim teŋin.

english_verse: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
translation_verse: Karea biig Johanan nɛ soogianam tuongatib la wʋsa da wʋm bɛ'ɛd linɛ ka Isimael tʋm la,

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: ba da duoe nɔki ba nidib wʋsa keŋ zab nɛ Isimael. Ba da kad o keŋ gban'e nɛ bɛuŋ tita'ar la baba linɛ bɛ Gibeon la.

english_verse: When Ishmael's prisoners saw Johanan and the officers, they were happy
translation_verse: Nidib banɛ wʋsa ka Isimael mɔr la da nyɛ Johanan nɛ soogianam tuongatib la, ba sʋnf da ma'ae ya.

english_verse: and turned around and ran toward Johanan.
translation_verse: Isimael da gban'e ninsieba Misipa teŋin la wʋsa da fɛndigi lɛb Johanan san'an.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Amaa Isimael nɛ o nidiba anii da zɔɔ bɔdigi keŋ Ammon dim san'an. Ban zɔɔ keŋ Egipt la yɛla

english_verse: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_verse: ye ba su'a ka Babilon dim da nyɛɛ ba. Ba da zɔti ba nɛ dabiem bɔzugɔ Netanaya biig Isimael da kʋ Gedalaya onɛ ka Babilon na'ab da gaŋ ye o an gɔmena teŋin la.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Ka soogianam tuongatib la wʋsa, la'an nɛ Karea biig Johanan nɛ Hosiaya biig Jaazanaya nɛ nidib la wʋsa; lin yii ba tadimnamini ti paae ba kpi'emnam la wʋsa da keŋ

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Naa, wʋmi ti fabʋlʋg ka sɔsi fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am la nimbanɛ kpɛlim la yɛla. Fʋn nyɛ la, ti daa anɛ bɛdegʋ amaa nannanna ti yʋ'ʋn anɛ bi'ela.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Sɔsim ka fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am la yɛli ti tinamɛ na keŋ si'el nɛ tinamɛ na niŋ si'em.”

english_verse: “All right,” I answered, “I will pray to the Lord your God, and I will tell you everything he says.”
translation_verse: Nɔdi'es Jeremia da lɛbis ye, “M wʋm ya. M na sɔs Zugsɔb onɛ aan ya Wina'am la wʋʋ yanamɛ yɛl si'em la. M na kɛlis Zugsɔb la yɛl si'el wʋsa ka kena yɛli ya, m kʋ su'a ya si'el si'ela.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord himself will be our witness that we promise to do whatever he says,
translation_verse: Ani ka ba yʋ'ʋn yɛl Jeremia ye, “Ti ya'a pʋ tʋm wʋʋ fʋ Zugsɔb Wina'am la yɛlif ye ti tʋm si'em la wʋsa, Zugsɔb onɛ an sida sɔb la na di kasɛti gɛɛnsi ti.

english_verse: even if it isn't what we want to do. We will obey the Lord so that all will go well for us.”
translation_verse: Li ya'a na an sʋm woo, li ya'a lɛn anɛ bɛ'ɛd woo, ti na siaki ti Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ ka ti tʋmmi fʋ o san'an la nɔɔr. ka si'el wʋsa na niŋ sʋ'ʋŋa tisi ti, tinam lɛɛ na siaki ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la nɔɔr.”

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord gave me an answer for
translation_verse: Dabpiiga nya'aŋ ka Zugsɔb labaar kɛn Jeremia san'an na.

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: Ka yɛli ba ye, “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am ka ya daa tʋmim ye m mɔri ya fabʋlʋgʋ keŋ o san'an la yɛl ye,

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: Ya ya'a bɛ teŋ kaŋa ni, m na kɛ ka ya nyɛ zi'esim sʋŋ ka m kʋ lɛn da'ae ya basɛ. M na sɛɛ ya ka kʋ lɛn vuoɛn ya ya'asɛ. M sʋʋnr san'am ya nɛ namisʋg kanɛ ka m kɛ ka li paae ya la.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Da zɔti Babilon na'ab onɛ mɔri ya dabiem la. Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. M na bɛ nɛ ya ka na faaɛn ya yis o nu'usin.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: M na zɔɔ ya nimbaanlig ka kɛ ka on mɛ zɔɔ ya nimbaanlig ka kɛ ka ya lɛbi zin'inɛ ya teŋin la.”

english_verse: But you might keep on saying, “We won't stay here in Judah, and we won't obey the Lord our God.
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a yɛl ye ya kʋ kpɛlim teŋ kaŋa nii, ka zan'asi ya Zugsɔb Wina'am nɔɔr,

english_verse: We are going to Egypt, where there is plenty of food and no danger of war.”
translation_verse: ka ye ya na keŋ zin'in Egipt, zin'ikanɛ ka ya kʋ nyɛt zaba bɛɛ wʋm tanp na'atan piebʋg bɛɛ kɔ'ɔm yɛlaa,

english_verse: People of Judah, you survived when the Babylonian army attacked. Now you are planning to move to Egypt, and if you do go, this is what will happen.
translation_verse: dinzugɔ kɛlisimi Zugsɔb la labaar yanam Juda dim banɛ kpɛlim la. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye ya ya'a mɔɔd ye ya keŋ Egipt, ka sid keŋ zin'inɛ ani,

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Sida, banɛ wʋsa mɔɔd ye ba keŋ Egipt teŋin zin'in la wʋsa na kpi zaba ni, la'an nɛ kɔ'ɔm nɛ ban'abɛ'ɛd; ba nid baa yinne kʋ vʋ'ʋg bɛɛ nyaŋi yi tɔɔg kanɛ ka m na kɛ ka li kɛɛn ba zugin na la.

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye ya ya'a lɛb Egipt teŋin, m sʋnpɛɛnni sadigim kpa'ae yɛɛl banɛ bɛ Jerusalem la, ala ka m sʋnpɛɛn mɛ na kpa'ae yɛɛli ya. Ya na anɛ banɛ ka ba na mɔri ya yʋ'ʋri pɔɔdi tisid nidib ka li na paki ya. Ya na nyɛ kʋʋsbɛ'ɛd nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ, ka kʋ lɛn nyɛ zin'ikaŋa ya'asɛ.

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: “Yanam Juda dim banɛ kpɛlim la, Zugsɔb la yɛli ya ye, ‘Da keŋi Egipt teŋinɛ.’ Baŋimi nɛ' sʋ'ʋŋa; m sa'ali ya zina nwa' ye,

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: Li daa anɛ yidig tita'ar nɛ yanamɛ daa tʋmim Zugsɔb Wina'am la san'an ka yɛl ye, ‘Sɔsimi ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la tisi ti ka on yɛl si'el wʋsa ti na tʋmi li la.’

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Zina nwa' m yɛli ya on yɛl si'el la wʋsa amaa ya nam kpɛn zan'asnɛ ka pʋ siaki ya Zugsɔb Wina'am la nɔɔrɛ.

english_verse: And so, you will die in Egypt from war, hunger, and disease.
translation_verse: Alazugɔ baŋimi ye yanamɛ bɔɔd ye ya keŋ zin'isi'a zin'in la, ya na kpi zaba ni ka kɔ'ɔm nɛ ban'abɛ'ɛd mɛ na kʋʋ ya.”

english_verse: I told the people everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Jeremia da yɛl nidib la ba Zugsɔb Wina'am yɛl o si'el ye o yɛli ba la wʋsa.

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: Amaa Azaria onɛ an Hosiaya biig la nɛ Karea biig Johanan nɛ banɛ dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋ la wʋsa da yɛl Jeremia ye, “Fʋ fanɛ! Ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la pʋ yɛlif ye, ‘Da keŋi Egipt teŋinɛ zin'in ani.’

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Amaa Neraya biig Baruk dɔlli fʋ nɔɔri bɔɔd ye o nɔki ti tis Babilon dim ka ba kʋʋ ti bɛɛ ba mɔri ti keŋ Babilon teŋin.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Karea biig Johanan nɛ soogianam tuongatib nɛ nidib la wʋsa da zan'as Zugsɔb la nɔɔr ka pʋ kpɛlim Juda teŋinɛ.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Ka lɛɛ la'as nimbanɛ kpɛlim ka yi sʋ'ʋlim banɛ ka ba da widigi kpɛn' ka lɛb na la wʋsa mɔri ba keŋ.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ da mɔr Misipa dim la, dap nɛ pu'ab nɛ biis nɛ na'ab pu'ayuos banɛ ka Nebuzaradan onɛ an banɛ gur la kpɛɛm la, da gu'ul Ahikam biig Gedalaya onɛ an Safan yaaŋ la, ka lɛm pɛ'ɛs nɔdi'es Jeremia nɛ Neraya biig Baruk la mɔri ba keŋ.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: Ba da zan'as Zugsɔb la nɔɔr ka kpɛn' Egipt teŋin hali ti paae Tapanes.

english_verse: Jeremiah, carry some large stones to the entrance of the government building in Tahpanhes. Bury the stones underneath the brick pavement and be sure the Jews are watching.
translation_verse: “Nɔkim kugbɛda m pin' ya'adin ka Juda dim la nini nyɛ, zin'ikanɛ ka ba maal tampiga digil ka ba dɔlli ani gat ka li bɛ Na'ab Faaro na'ayir za'anɔɔr Tapanes teŋin la.”

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Yɛlimi ba ye Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, M na tʋm buoli m tʋmtʋm Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza, ka o na nɔk o na'am kʋk la zi'el kuga banɛ ka fʋ pin' kpɛla la zug; o na ti' o na'am sʋk ka kuga la bɛɛ li ma'asimin.

english_verse: I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_verse: O na nyu'oe Winnig pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔg linɛ bɛ Heliopolis teŋin Egipt teŋgbauŋʋn la, o na san'am teŋgban kuga linɛ bɛ ani la ka nyu'oe Egipt dim wina pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔd la.

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Labakaŋa da kɛn Jeremia san'an na yɛt Juda dim banɛ bɛ Migdol nɛ Tapanes nɛ Memfis tɛɛnsin, nɛ banɛ bɛ Egipt ya-dagɔbʋg baba la wʋsa yɛla ye

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb, ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Ya nyɛ man kɛ ka yɛltɔɔg paae Jerusalem nɛ Juda nɛ tɛɛns banɛ bɛ Juda wʋsa la si'em. Zina ba dignɛ zaalim ka an dabɔɔd

english_verse: because the people of Judah made me angry by worshiping gods that had never helped them or their ancestors.
translation_verse: ka li anɛ bɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ba tʋm la zug. Ba nyu'od maana ka pʋ'ʋsid winsieba ka ban bɛɛ yanam bɛɛ ya yaanam zi', ka duoe m sʋʋnr.

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: M tʋmi m nɔdi'esidib nɔɔrin babiga ye ba yɛli ba ye, ‘Da tʋmmi yɛlkisa banɛ ka man kis la!’

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Amaa ba pʋ wʋm bɛɛ kɛlisɛ; ba pʋ fɛndig ka basi ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la, bɛɛ bas maana linɛ ka ba nyu'odi tisid winsieba la.

english_verse: Finally, my anger struck like a raging flood, and today Jerusalem and the towns of Judah are nothing but empty ruins.
translation_verse: Alazug ka m sʋnpɛɛn kpa'ae yɛɛl Juda tɛɛns nɛ Jerusalem suoraad la, ka san'ami ba ka ba lieb dabɔɔd wʋʋ yanamɛ nyɛɛ li si'em zina la.”

english_verse: Why do you now insist on heading for another disaster? A disaster that will destroy not only you, but also your children and babies.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb, ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, “Bɔ ka ya mɔr yɛltɔɔg kaŋa buudi kɛɛn ya zugin na, ya bɔɔd ye ya li'inɛ Juda dim nɛ ya biis nɛ ya bilies ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn kpɛlim?

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka ya mɔri ya nu'usi maan linɛ kɛt ka m sʋʋnr pɛligida? Bɔ ka ya nyu'od tudaari tisid Egipt teŋ kanɛ ka ya kena zin' la wina? Ya na san'ami ya mɛŋ ka kɛ ka ba mɔri ya yʋ'ʋri pɔɔdi tisid nidib ka li na paki ya buudbanɛ ka ya bɛɛ ba sʋʋgin dunia nwa' ni la wʋsa.

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Ya tam bɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ya yaanam nɛ na'anam nɛ pu'ana'anam tʋm Juda teŋin la nɛɛ? Ka ya tam yanam nɛ ya pu'abi tʋm bɛ'ɛd si'a Juda nɛ Jerusalem suoraadin la nɛɛ?

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Lin keŋ paae zina, ba pʋ sie ba mɛŋ bɛɛ pa'al na'asi, bɛɛ dɔlis wada nɛ nɔzi'ela banɛ ka m tis ban nɛ ba yaanam la.”

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: M na yis Juda dim banɛ kpɛlim ka mɔɔd ye ba keŋ Egipt teŋin na zin'in anina la. Ba wʋsa na bɔdig Egipt teŋin la; ba na kpi zaba ni, bɛɛ kɔ'ɔm kʋʋ ba. Lin yii ba tadimnamin ti paae ba kpi'emnam wʋsa na kpi zaba ni, bɛɛ kɔ'ɔm kʋʋ ba. Ba na mɔri ba yʋ'ʋri pɔɔdi tisid nidib ka li an pakir nɛ kʋʋsbɛ'ɛd nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: M na namis banɛ bɛ Egipt la nɛ zaba nɛ kɔ'ɔm nɛ ban'abɛ'ɛd wʋʋ man namis Jerusalem dim si'em la.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Juda dim banɛ kpɛlim ka kena bɛ Egipt la baa yinne kʋ nyaŋi yi bɛɛ tilig ka lɛb Juda teŋin, zin'ikanɛ ka ba ya'am bɔɔd ye ba lɛb la; ba sɔ' kʋ lɛb anii, asɛɛ ba bi'ela ma'aa na lɛb.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Ka dap banɛ wʋsa mi' ye ba pu'ab nyu'od maana tisid winsieba la, la'an nɛ pu'ab la, nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ Egipt ya-datiuŋ nɛ ya-dagɔbʋg baba la wʋsa yɛl Jeremia ye,

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “Ti kʋ kɛlis labakanɛ ka fʋ yɛti ti Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋr zug laa!

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Ti na ba'asi maal tinamɛ yɛl ye ti na maal si'el la wʋsa. Ti na nyu'oe tudaari tis win kanɛ an Agɔla Pu'ana'ab la, ka tis o daam wʋʋ tinam nɛ ti yaanam nɛ ti na'anamɛ da niŋid si'em Juda tɛɛns nɛ Jerusalem suoraadin la. Hali saŋkan la ti da mɔr diib bɛdegʋ ka mugusʋg si'a pʋ paae tii.

english_verse: But since the time we stopped burning incense and offering wine sacrifices to her, we have been dying from war and hunger.
translation_verse: Amaa lin yi saŋa kanɛ ka ti bas ka pʋ lɛn nyu'od tudaari tisid Agɔla Pu'ana'ab la ka mɛ pʋ tisid o daam la, ti pʋ lɛm mɔr si'ela; ka kɔ'ɔm nɛ zaba ma'aa yʋ'ʋn kʋʋdi ti.”

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Ka pu'ab la mɛ yɛl ye, “Tinamɛ da nyu'od tudaari tisid Agɔla Pu'ana'ab la ka tisid o bʋnnuuda maana la, ti sidib da baŋ ye ti maan ma'asa ka li nwɛnɛ win la nɛ, ka maan maana tisid o.”

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Ya zi' ye Zugsɔb la tɛnr ka nan kpɛn tɛn'ɛsid maana banɛ ka yanam nɛ ya yaanam nɛ ya na'anam nɛ ya kpɛɛmnam da nyu'od Juda tɛɛnsin nɛ Jerusalem suoraadin laa?

english_verse: And when he could no longer put up with your disgusting sins, he placed a curse on your land and turned it into a desert, as it is today.
translation_verse: Hali Zugsɔb la daa pʋ lɛn nyaŋi mɔdig nɛ ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nɛ yɛlkisa banɛ ka ya maal la, li kɛ ka nɔpɔɔr yʋ'ʋn bɛ teŋ la zug ka li lieb dabɔɔd ka nidib kae li pʋʋgin nwɛnɛ lin an si'em zina la.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Yanamɛ sadigim nyu'od maana nɛ bʋnnyubisa ka tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔg Zugsɔb la ka pʋ siak o nɔɔr bɛɛ dɔl o wada la nɛ o zi'ela la, linɛ kɛ ka tɔɔg paae ya, ka ya nyɛti li nannanna la.”

english_verse: Then I told the men and their wives, that the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, had said: Here in Egypt you still keep your promises to burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to the so-called Queen of Heaven.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa: Yanam nɛ ya pu'ab la tʋʋma pa'al ye ya nɔɔri yɛl si'el la niŋ asida. Ya yɛl ye, “Ti na ba'asi maal tinamɛ zi'el nɔɔr si'em la, ti na maal maana ka nyu'oe bʋnnyubisa ka nɔk bʋnnuuda tis Agɔla Pu'ana'ab la.” Alazugɔɔ, kemi tuon! Maalimi yanamɛ zi'el nɔɔr ye ya na tʋm si'el la!

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Amaa kɛl ka Zugsɔb labaar la kpɛm bɛɛ ya san'an, Zugsɔb la yɛli tis yanam Juda dim banɛ bɛ Egipt la ye, “M pɔya nɛ m yʋ'ʋtita'ar la ye yanam banɛ an Juda dim ka bɛ Egipt zin'isi'a wʋsa kʋ lɛm buoli m yʋ'ʋr bɛɛ pɔ nɛ man Zugsɔb la yʋ'ʋrɛ.

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: M gɔsidi ba nɛ ye ba nyɛ bɛ'ɛd, ba kʋ nyɛ linɛ an sʋm; zaba nɛ kɔ'ɔm na kʋ Juda dim banɛ bɛ Egipt teŋin la ka ba wʋsa ti kpii naae.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Banɛ na nyaŋi yi zaba la ni naan Egipt n lɛb Juda teŋin na la na anɛ bi'ela. Ala ka Juda nimbanɛ kpɛlim ka kena bɛ Egipt teŋin la na baŋ onɛ pian'adi na zi'en. Ba na baŋ ye man pian'adi zi'en bɛɛ ban din la zi'enɛ.”

english_verse: And here is how you will know that I will keep my threats to punish you in Egypt.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Nɛ'ɛŋa na an zanbinnɛ pa'al ye m na namisi ya kpɛla, ala ka ya na baŋ ye man yɛl ye yɛltɔɔg na paae ya la anɛ linɛ zi'e.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa'. ‘M bɔɔd ye m nɔk Egipt na'ab Faaro Hofira niŋ o bi'emnam banɛ ieed o nyɔvʋr la nu'usin, nwɛnɛ man daa nɔk Juda na'ab Zedekaya niŋ o bi'em Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza nu'usin si'em la.’”

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ an Israel Wina'am la yɛlif si'em nwa', Baruk:

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: ‘Fʋ yɛl ye tɔɔg yʋ'ʋn paae mam! Zugsɔb la paas sʋnsa'aŋi m niŋgbina zabir la zug; m yʋ'ʋn ʋʋnsi gɛnnɛ ka vʋ'ʋsʋm kae.’”

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛlim ye, “Yɛlim o ye Zugsɔb la yɛl o si'eli nwa': M na da'ae man mɛ' si'el la bas ka vɔn' man sɛ si'el teŋ la wʋsa ni.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Li nar ye fʋ ieed bʋmbɛda tisidi fʋ mɛŋaa? Da ieeda. M na mɔr tɔɔg nidib wʋsa zugin na,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la, “amaa fʋn keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa m na kɛ ka fʋ su'a gaad ka kʋ kpii.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa an Zugsɔb la labaari yi Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la san'an na tɛɛns sʋ'ʋlim yɛla:

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Egipt yɛla: Labakaŋa anɛ Egipt na'ab Faaro Neko soogianam yɛla, banɛ ka Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza da nyaŋi ba Kakimis Efiritis Kɔldaugin la, Josia biig Jehoyakim da di na'am la li yʋma anaasi saŋa:

english_verse: It's time to go into battle! So grab your shields,
translation_verse: “Ti'ebimi ya gbanti'edis, banɛ an bʋmbibis nɛ bʋmbɛda la wʋsa, ka yii keŋ zaba!

english_verse: saddle your horses, and polish your spears. Put on your helmets and armor, then take your positions.
translation_verse: Li'emi widi la nɛ salibir, ban'ami widi la! Zi'enimi ya zi'esa ni pidimi kʋnt zupibis! Saasimi ya kpana la nɔya, ka bɔbi ya zaba la'ad!

english_verse: I can see the battle now— you are defeated and running away, never once looking back. Terror is all around.
translation_verse: M nyɛ bɔ? Dabiem kpɛn' ba nɛ, ba lɛbidnɛ nya'aŋ, ba nyaŋi ba zabzabidib la. Ba zɔti tɔ'ɔtɔ ka pʋ lɛn gi'ed nya'aŋa, ka dabiem gilig zin'ig wʋsa. Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: You are strong and run fast, but you can't escape. You fall in battle near the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Banɛ mi' zɔɔg hali la kʋ nyaŋi zɔɔ bɛɛ banɛ mɔr paŋ la nyaŋi pɔnsɛ. Ya-datiuŋ linɛ kpi'e Efiritis kɔldaug la baba, ka ba tu'usidi lit.

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwa' duod wʋʋ Nail kɔldaugɔ, ka nwɛnɛ mu'ar ku'om pɛ'ɛli badigida?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Egipt duosid nɛ wʋʋ Nail kɔldaug nɛ, nwɛnɛ ku'om pʋbid kɔldaadin nɛ paŋ. O yɛl ye, ‘M na duoe pil teŋgbauŋ la; m na san'am tempʋʋs nɛ ba nidib la,’

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Widii, kemi tuon! Kemi nɛ sʋnpɛɛn, yanam banɛ dɔribid zaba tɛrekonam la! Kemi, zabzabidibaa. Kus nɛ Put dim banɛ ziid gbanti'edis la, yanam Libiya dim banɛ tɛk tiraug la.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Amaa dabiskan la anɛ Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la din; li anɛ sam yɔɔb dabisir, ka o na yɔ o dataas sam. Zaba sʋ'ʋg la na kʋ hali ti tig, li na kʋ hali ka ziim la ti yisi li ku'onuud. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la na maal maan teŋ kanɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ ka kpi'e nɛ Efiritis kɔldaug la.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Buudi wʋsa na wʋm pu'asadir la di nyan la yɛla; o kaasig la na pɛ'ɛl dunia. Zabzabid na tu'ug o tiraan; ka ba wʋsa na la'asi li teŋin.”

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: Mɔɔlim nɛ'ɛŋa Egipt teŋin, ka yɛli li Migdol, ka mɛ mɔɔli li Memfis nɛ Tapanes. Ti'ebim ka zi'eni ya zi'esa ni, bɔzugɔ zaba sʋ'ʋg la na kʋʋd banɛ kpi'e nɛ ya la.

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka ya zabzabidib la lit teŋinɛ? Ba kʋ nyaŋi zi'enɛ bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la na da'ae ba bas teŋin.

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Ba na tu'usidi takid; ba na lit taaba zug. Ba na yɛl ye, Duomi, kɛlli ka ti lɛb! Ti kulimi ti mɛŋ nidibin nɛ ti mɛŋ teŋin! Zɔmi ka bas dataa kanɛ zabid nɛ sʋ'ʋg ka mugusidi ti la.

english_verse: Give the king of Egypt this new name, “Talks-Big-Does-Nothing.”
translation_verse: Ani ka ba na yɛl ye, Aa, Egipt na'ab Faaro maannɛ tʋkpiidʋg zaalim; o san'am o suori bas.

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: “Asida mɛnɛ”, Na'akanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la, Sɔ' na kena an onɛ bɛ zuoya la sʋʋgin nwɛnɛ Tabo zuor la, ka nwɛnɛ Kamel zuor kanɛ bɛɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Vaami ya la'adi lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ, yanam banɛ bɛ Egipt la, bɔzugɔ Memfis na san'am ka lieb dabɔɔd ka nidib kʋ bɛɛ ani.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: “Egipt nwɛnɛ na'asa'a vɛnliŋ, amaa pɔ'ɔg na yi ya-datiuŋʋ kena zab nɛ o.

english_verse: The foreign soldiers you hired will turn and run. But they are doomed, like well-fed calves being led to the butcher. *
translation_verse: Soogianam banɛ ka o da' la anɛ o taaba ka nwɛnɛ na'abibis banɛ nɔb nɛ. Ban mɛ na fɛndig ka ba la'am zɔ, ba kʋ zi'enɛ, bɔzugɔ dabisbɛ'og paae ba, ba namisʋg saŋa paae ya.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Egipt na vʋ'ʋsidi nwɛnɛ waafʋ zɔt ka fʋʋsid nɛ, dataa la zabidi kenna nɛ paŋ la; ba na la'asi gilig o nɛ liemis, wʋʋ nidibi na nwaad tiisi lugid.”

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: Ba na nwaa o tiis la, “hali ba ya'a bɔɔd ban zu'oe si'em. Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. Ba zu'oe gaad na'azɔmnam, sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi kaali ba.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Egipt pu'asadir la na di nyan, ba na nɔk o tis nimbanɛ yi ya-datiuŋ la na.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl ye, “M bɔɔd ye m mɔr nɛ namisʋgʋ kɛn Ammon onɛ an Tebɛs teŋ win la zugin na, nɛ Na'ab Faaro, nɛ Egipt dim wina nɛ ba na'anam nɛ banɛ ti'e Faaro la zugin na.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: M na nɔki ba tis banɛ ieedi ba nyɔvʋr la, m na nɔki ba tis Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la. Amaa li nya'aŋ Egipt na lɛm mɔr nidib wʋʋ lin da an si'em la.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M tʋmtʋmnib Jakob nidiba, da zɔti dabiem, ka m bɛ nɛ ya,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “La'an nɛ man san'am tɛɛns banɛ ka m da widigi ya kpɛn'ɛsi ba sʋʋgin la, m kʋ san'ami ya nyainnɛ. M na tɛki ya tʋbir ka li dɔl sida suor; m kʋ kɛ ka ya keŋ zaalim ka pʋ di'e tʋbtɛɛgirɛ.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la labaari nwa' kɛn Jeremia onɛ an nɔdi'es la ni na Filisitia dim yɛla saŋa kanɛ ka Faaro nam pʋ keŋ zab nɛ Gaza dima.

english_verse: I, the Lord, tell you that your land will be flooded with an army from the north. It will destroy your towns and sweep you away, moaning and screaming.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Gɔsim ku'om la dʋt ya-datiuŋ si'em; li na zɔt nɛ paŋ wʋʋ kɔldaug ku'om nɛ. Li na pɛ'ɛl teŋ ka lim linɛ bɛɛ ani wʋsa, nɛ tempʋʋs la nɛ nimbanɛ zin' ani la. Nidib la na kaas agɔla; banɛ bɛ teŋin la wʋsa na kaasid.

english_verse: When you hear the thunder of horses and chariots, your courage will vanish, and parents will even abandon their own children.
translation_verse: Widi nɔba ya'a ti vuudi ian'adi kenna dataa la zaba tɛrekonam la ya'a ti vuud ka ba nɔba la ian'asid. Ba'anam kʋ gi'e ye ba sʋŋi ba biisɛ; ba na zɔt ka ba nu'us kpi.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Dabisir paae ya ka ba na san'am Filisitia dim ka li' banɛ kpɛlim ka na sʋŋ Taya nɛ Sidon. Zugsɔb la bɔɔd ye o san'am Filisitia dim, banɛ da kpɛlim ka dɔl atɛukʋ yi Kafitor teŋin la.

english_verse: The Anakim who survive in Gaza and Ashkelon will mourn for you by shaving their heads and sitting in silence.
translation_verse: Gaza na kum ka pʋn o zug sʋnsa'aŋ yɛla; Askɛlon na an baanlimm. Yanam banɛ kpɛlim ka bɛ paalʋ la, bʋndaar ka ya na bas kʋʋr kaasig nɛ ya mɛŋ niŋgbina nwaabɔ?

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Ya fabinnɛ yɛt ye, ‘Aa, Zugsɔb zaba sʋ'ʋgɔ, bʋndaar ka fʋ na vʋ'ʋsɛ? Lɛmmi fʋ tɛɛngʋn la; gu'om ka an baanlimm.’

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Amaa li na niŋ wala vʋ'ʋs Zugsɔb la tisi li nɔɔr la? On yɛli li ye li zam nɛ Askɛlon nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin wʋsa la?”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel dim Wina'am la yɛl Moab dim yɛla si'em nwa': “Tɔɔg na paae Nebo teŋ, bɔzugɔ li na san'am. Ba na gban'e Kiriafaim teŋ ka diisi li nyan; ba na diis kpi'euŋ zin'ig la nyan ka widigi li.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Ba kʋ lɛn zun'e Moab ya'asɛ; nidib na bɛ Hesbon teŋinɛ gban'e gban'ar ye, ‘Kemi na ka ti li' teŋ kan la nyain.’ Hali Madmen teŋ la na lɛbi fɔn baanlimm; zaba sʋ'ʋg la mɛ na katif.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Kɛlisim kaasig linɛ yit Horonam na, san'auŋ nɛ kaasig nɛ ya'am fɛndigir na bɛ.

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Moab teŋ la na nwa'; ka bibibis la na kaasid.

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: Ba na dɔl suor kanɛ dʋt Luhif la, kaasid hali ken; ka suor kanɛ sigid Horonam la ka ba wʋm sʋnsa'aŋ kaasig.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Zɔmi! Zɔm faaɛn ya nyɔvʋr; niŋimi wʋʋ sian'arin waligi bɛ mɔɔgin nɛ.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Yanamɛ sadigim ti'e ya mɛŋ tʋʋma nɛ ya kpan'am la, ba na gban'e ya ka ya na an yammis mɛn, Kemos onɛ aan ya win la mɛ na lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ, la'an nɛ o maanmaannib nɛ ba kpɛɛmnam la.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Onɛ san'amid la na kena san'am tɛɛns la wʋsa, ka teŋ baa yinne kʋ kpɛlim. Bɔn'ɔg la na san'am ka kukuos la wʋsa birigi san'am, bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb la pian' ya.

english_verse: Spread salt on the ground to kill the crops. Leave its towns in ruins, with no one living there.
translation_verse: Zu'asim yaarim Moab teŋin, bɔzugɔ teŋ la na san'am wʋsa; tempʋʋs la na kpɛlim zaalim ka sɔ' kʋ bɛɛ ba nii.

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: Nɔpɔɔr bɛ onɛ pʋ tʋm Zugsɔb la yɛl ye o niŋ si'el la! Nɔpɔɔr bɛ onɛ zan'as ka pʋ kʋ nidib la!

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ani ka nyan na kpɛn' Moab dimi ba win Kemos yɛla, wʋʋ Israel dimi daa niŋ Betel win la yadda ka di nyan si'em la.”

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: Ya na niŋ wala yɛl ye, “Tinam anɛ zabzabidib, ka mɔr sʋnkpi'euŋ zaba ni?

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Ba na kpɛn' Moab sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛns la wʋsa san'ami li; na'akimsʋma la wʋsa na kpi zaba la ni. Man onɛ an Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian' la.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: Moab liig la li'el ya; yɛlbɛ'ɛd na li o zugin tɔ'ɔtɔ.

english_verse: I will order the nearby nations to mourn for you and say, “Isn't it sad? Moab ruled others, but now its glorious power has been shattered.”
translation_verse: Yanam banɛ kpi'e nɛ o la, kaasim tis o, banɛ mi' on daa an si'em la wʋsa; yɛlimi ye, Gɔsim zan'an kanɛ mɔr paŋ la kɔ'ɔg si'em; gɔsim na'am dansaar la kɔ'ɔg si'em!

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Sigimi ya na'am gbauŋ la zugʋ zin'in teŋ kpi'emisin, yanam Dibon teŋ dima. Onɛ san'am Moab la na kena zab nɛ ya san'ami ya tempʋbanɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ la.

english_verse: You people of Aroer, go wait beside the road, and when refugees run by, ask them, “What happened?”
translation_verse: Zi'enimi suor kpikpɛŋ ka gɔsid, yanam banɛ bɛ Aroa teŋin la. Bu'osimi dau kanɛ zɔt la nɛ pu'a kanɛ bɔdigid la, bu'osimi ba ye, ‘Bɔɔ maalɛ?’

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Moab dim di nyan, bɔzugɔ ba widig ya. Kummi ka kaasidi! Mɔɔlimi Aanon kɔlʋgin la ye Moab san'am ya.

english_verse: I will punish every town that belongs to Moab, but especially Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,
translation_verse: Sariakadib paae tɛɛns banɛ bɛ kʋkʋna zug la, li paae Holon nɛ Yahaza nɛ Mefaaf

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Moab iil linɛ pa'annɛ o paŋ la kɔya; o nu'ug mɛ kɔ'ɔg ya,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: People of Moab, you claim to be stronger than I am. Now I will tell other nations to make you drunk and to laugh while you collapse in your own vomit.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka o nuu kʋʋl, bɔzugɔ o zan'as Zugsɔb la nɔɔr. Kɛl ka Moab bilim o mɛŋ tiindin la; ka lieb onɛ ka ba na la'ad o.

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Li ka' Israel n da aan ya bʋnla'adir laa? Ba da gban'e o na'ayiis sʋʋginɛɛ? Ya lɔbidi ya zut ka la'ad o saŋa kanɛ ka ya pian'ad o yɛla.

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: Yanam banɛ bɛ Moab la, basimini ya tempʋʋs la ka keŋ bɛ tampiinsin. Bɛɛi wʋʋ dawana ka maali ya tɛɛd tampinyɔ'ɔdin.

english_verse: So I will cry and mourn for Moab and its town of Kir-Heres.
translation_verse: Dinzug m na kaas Moab yɛla, Moab yɛla ma'aa ka m kaasid, M kumnɛ Kir Haresef yɛla.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Yanam vain tiis banɛ bɛ Sibma teŋin la, m na kaasi tisi ya, wʋʋ Jaza kum si'em la. Ya wila la yaadim paae atɛuk la; hali ba paae Jaza Tɛukʋn la. San'auŋ sɔb la lii fʋ wala banɛ bi'ig la zug.

english_verse: Weeping from Heshbon can be heard as far as Elealeh and Jahaz; cries from Zoar are heard in Horonaim and Eglath-Shelishiyah. And Nimrim Creek has run dry.
translation_verse: “Ba kaasig la dʋtnɛ Hesbon n paae Eleale nɛ Jahaz, ka yi Zoar hali paae Horonam nɛ Egilaf Sielisiya, hali Nimirim ku'om la kʋdig nɛ.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka banɛ bɛ Moab teŋin la kpi'ilim; banɛ maan teŋgbana kukuosin ka nyu'od bʋnnyubisa tisi ba wina la.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: “M kaasidi m sʋnfʋn tisid Moab wʋʋ na'akpak nɛ; ka kaasidi tisid Kir Haresef. Kpan'am kanɛ ka ba nyɛ la wʋsa gaad ya.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Moab sʋ'ʋlim tɛɛnsin la dɔɔd wʋsa zut, nɛ nidibi la'as zin'isi'a wʋsa, si'el-si'el kae asɛɛ kukuma ma'aa, bɔzugɔ m nwa'ae Moab nɛ wʋʋ gan'ar nɛ ka sɔ' pʋ lɛm bɔɔdi lii.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: “Gɔsim Moab teŋi nwa'ae si'em! Moab yʋ'ʋn fɛndignɛ bid kʋdig nɛ nyan! Moab yʋ'ʋn lieb nɛ bʋnla'adir, ka an pakiri tis banɛ gilig o la wʋsa.”

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye: “Gɔsima! Silʋg zuligid na, o yadig o kpʋkpama Moab zugin.

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Ba na nyaŋ tempʋʋs la ka faaɛn kpi'euŋ zin'is la. Daakan la Moab zabzabidib la sʋnya yʋ'ʋn na nwɛnɛ pu'a sa'ae bɔɔd du'ab nɛ.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Moab teŋ la na san'am bɔzugɔ ba zan'as Zugsɔb la nɔɔr.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Banɛ wʋsa nyɛ dabiem la ka zɔt na li bʋmbɔkin la, onɛ wʋsa naan bʋmbɔkin dʋt na, baŋ la na gban'e o; m na kɛ ka yʋʋm kanɛ an namisʋg saŋa la paae Moab dim la wʋsa.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: “Hesbon teŋ la ma'asim ka zɔɔma la zi'e bʋra. Bɔzugɔ, bugum naam Hesbon n yina, bugum pielim yi Sihon teŋin; li ditnɛ Moab gbɛ'og, nɛ banɛ dʋ'ʋsidi ba mɛŋ la zunwana.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Tɔɔg paae ya, Moab dima! San'auŋ paae Kemos win nidib la; ba gban'e ya biribis la lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ ka kɛ ka ya bipumis la lieb yammis.”

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “La'an nɛ wala, dabisa kenna ka m na kɛ ka Moab zusʋŋ la lɛb na.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. Moab sariakadib yɛla la naari la.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa anɛ Ammon dim yɛla: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Israel pʋ mɔr biribisɛɛ? O pʋ mɔr faditibaa? Ka bɔ ka yanam Molek win nidib la kena ye ya di'e Gad teŋ la sʋ'oe ya? Bɔ ka ya bɛɛ li tempʋʋsin la?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Amaa dabisa kenna,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la, “Ka m na kɛ ka zaba kuŋ kaasi keŋ Rabba linɛ an Ammon dim teŋ tita'arin la; li na lieb dabɔɔd, ka ba na nyu'oe tembibis banɛ kpi'e la nɛ bugum. Ka banɛ daa kad Israel dimi yis la Israel mɛ yʋ'ʋn na kadi ba yis.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: “Kaasimi, Hesbon dima, ka Ai teŋ la san'am ya! Kaasimi, Rabba dima! Yɛɛmi bɔto fuud ka kumi; zɔm lɛbi kpɛ' ka lɛb kpɛ' zaŋguoma la pʋʋgin: ba na kɛ ka ya Molek win la lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ la'an nɛ o maanmaannib nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ dʋ'ʋsidi fʋ mɛŋi fʋ bɔn'ɔd la yɛla? Fʋ dʋ'ʋsidi fʋ mɛŋ ye fʋ bɔn'ɔd la du'ad zʋʋd sʋ'ʋŋa. Fʋn kanɛ ka' sida sɔba, fʋ ti'enɛ fʋ kpan'am la ka yɛt ye, ‘Anɔ'ɔn na zab nɛ mam’

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka banɛ giligif la wʋsa kpɛn'ɛsif dabiem,” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ nwa'. “Ba na kadi ya wʋsa, ka sɔ' kae na nyaŋi la'as zɔɔma la.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, li nya'aŋ m na lɛbis Ammon dim zusʋŋ la.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. Edom dim labaar

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Fɛndigim zɔ, yanam banɛ bɛ Dedan teŋin la su'ami tampinyɔ'ɔd banɛ zulim la ni, bɔzugɔ m na kɛ ka tɔɔg paae Esau li saŋa la m na namis o.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Banɛ pɔn'ɔd tiis wala la ya'a pɔn', ba kʋ nya'al bi'elaa? Na'ayiis ya'a kpɛn' yisi'a ni yʋ'ʋŋɔ, ba kʋ zunɛ ban bɔɔd si'el bɛn ma'aanɛ?

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Amaa m na yɛɛs Esau ka kɛɛ o biel; M na pilig zin'ibanɛ ka o su'ad la, ka o kʋ lɛn nyaŋi lus o mɛŋa. O biis nɛ o nidib nɛ o kpi'es wʋsa na kpi, ka sɔ' kʋ lɛm bɛ ya'asɛ.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Basimi fʋ kpiibis la ka m na guri ba nyɔvʋya. Pʋkɔnya la mɛ nɔkimi ba ti'iri niŋi m san'an.”

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Banɛ pʋ nar ye ba nyɛ namisʋg la ya'a paam namisʋgɔ, ya tɛn'ɛs ye ya na keŋ zaalim ka da nyɛ namisʋgɔ? Ya kʋ keŋ zaalim, asɛɛ ka ya nu nwam linɛ aan m sʋnpɛɛn la.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “M pɔya ye Bozira teŋ na lieb dabɔɔg, ka an bʋnzɔtir, ka lɛn an bʋnla'adir onɛ ka ba na mɔri pɔɔd nɔɔri tisid nidib; ka li tempʋʋs la wʋsa na lieb dabɔɔd, saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.”

english_verse: I have sent a messenger to command the nations to prepare for war against you people of Edom.
translation_verse: M wʋm labaar ka li yi Zugsɔb la san'an na ye, “Ba tʋm nidib tɛɛns sʋ'ʋlim ni ye ba yɛl ye, ‘La'asimi taaba! Duom yii zaba!’

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Nannanna m na kɛ ka fʋ lieb tembil tɛɛns la sʋʋgin, ka nidib na nɛ'ɛsidif.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Fʋn kpɛn'ɛsid nidib dabiem la, nɛ nyɛɛsim kanɛ ka fʋ mɔri fʋ sʋnfʋn la ma'adif. Fʋ bɛ nɛ tampiins linɛ bɛ zuoya zug la, ka bɛ kukuos zug agɔla. La'an nɛ fʋn maali fʋ tɛɛd ka li bɛ agɔla lalli wʋʋ fʋ anɛ silʋg la, ani ka m na vɛ'ɛgi fʋ sigis na.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: People passing by your country will be shocked and horrified to see a disaster
translation_verse: “Edom na lieb bʋnzɔtir; banɛ wʋsa dɔl ani gaad, li na aan ba pakir ka ba wʋsa na kɛɛnd o, o sapu'ad la yɛla.

english_verse: as bad as the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah and towns nearby. The towns of Edom will be empty.
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ Sodom nɛ Gomora da san'am la'an nɛ tɛɛns banɛ da kpi'e ba la.” Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “ala mɛn ka sɔ' kʋ bɛ Edom sʋ'ʋliminɛ, nid kʋ bɛɛ ani ya'asɛ.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ gbigimi na yi Joodan gɔn'ɔsin na wa'ae yaama zin'igin ye o gban'e kɔnbʋg si'em la, ala ka m na kad Edom yis o teŋin la tɔ'ɔtɔ. Anɔ'ɔn ka m na gaŋ ka o tʋmi li? Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwɛnɛ mam ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na mak o mɛŋ nɛ mam? Kɔnbkem bɛ ya na zab nɛ mam?

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Edom. Your children will be dragged off and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, kɛlisim Zugsɔb la gban'e Edom yɛla si'em, on gban'e ye o niŋ banɛ bɛ Teman teŋin la yɛla si'em. Ba na gban'e pɛbibis la mɔri keŋ; o na san'ami ba kariyauŋ la wʋsa ban zug.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will reach the Red Sea and cause the earth to shake.
translation_verse: Ba liig la vuud na kɛ ka teŋ dam; ba na maligim kaas ka li paae Atɛuk Zɛn'ugʋn.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Gɔsima! Silʋg bɛɛ ani laan ka na zulig na, yadig o kpʋkpama Bozira zugin. Daakan la ya'a paae Edom zabzabidib la sʋnya na nwɛnɛ pu'a na sa'ae bɔɔd du'ab.” Damaskus dim labaar

english_verse: The Lord says about Damascus: The towns of Hamath and Arpad have heard your bad news. They have lost hope, and worries roll over them like ocean waves.
translation_verse: Damaskus dim yɛla: “Li pak Hamat nɛ Apad dim ban wʋm lababɛ'ɛd la zug. Ba sʋnya san'am ya, ka li daami ba ka ba zɔti tuulim wʋʋ atɛuk ku'om nɛ.

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damaskus tadig ya, dabiem gban'e ba, ka ba fɛndigi zɔt; tɔɔg nɛ zabir yʋ'ʋn gban'e ba, ka li zabir nwɛnɛ pu'a na sa'ae.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Sida ba na bas teŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋri daa yit hali la, teŋ kanɛ ka ba ya'am kpɛn' hali la!

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Sida, na'akim la na kpi suoraadin; ka soogianam la na an baanlimm dabiskan la ni.” Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ nwa'

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: “M na nyu'oe Damaskus zaŋguoma la bugum; li na di Na'ab Ben Hadad kpi'euŋ zin'is la wʋsa.” Kedar nɛ Hazo dim labaar

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Kedar nɛ Hazo sʋ'ʋlim labaar, banɛ ka Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza da kena zab nɛ ba la: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Duom, zam nɛ Kedar dim ka kʋ nimbanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la!

english_verse: Run and hide, you people of the desert who live in villages! Nebuchadnezzar has big plans for you.
translation_verse: “Zɔmi tɔ'ɔtɔ, yanam banɛ bɛ Hazo la! Kpɛn'ɛm su'a tampinyɔ'ɔd banɛ zulim ni.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza duoe zi'enɛ ya yɛla; o gban'e ya yɛla bɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: Duom zab nɛ sʋ'ʋlim banɛ bɛ nɛ ba mɛŋ ti'ir la,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “Sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ pʋ mɔr za'anɔya bɛɛ gammɛ; nidib la bɛ nɛ ba kɔn'ɔkɔn'.

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Ba na zabi faaɛn ba yʋgʋma, ba bi'emnam na vaae ba niigi mɔri keŋ. M na widigi ba kpɛn'ɛs zin'ibanɛ lal; tɔɔg na yi zin'ig wʋsa paae ba.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: “Hazo na lieb wɛbaas zin'ig, li na dig zaalim ka nidib kae saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ. Sɔ' kʋ lɛm bɛɛ ani; nid kʋ lɛn zin'inɛ ani ya'asɛ.” Elam dim labaar

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Gɔsima, M na kɔ'ɔg Elam dim tiraug, linɛ aan ba paŋ la.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M na zi'eli m na'am gbauŋ Elam sʋ'ʋlimin ka san'am o na'anam nɛ kpɛɛmnam la wʋsa.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: “La'an nɛ wala, dabisa kenna ka m na lɛbis Elam zusʋŋ la na.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Labaar la nwa' ka Zugsɔb la pian' dɔlis Jeremia onɛ an Wina'am nɔdi'es la ni Babilon dim nɛ Babilon teŋgbauŋ la yɛla:

english_verse: Raise the signal flags; shout so all nations can hear— Babylon will be captured! Marduk, Babylon's god, will be ashamed and terrified, and his idols broken.
translation_verse: “Mɔɔlimi li tɛɛns la sʋʋgin, ʋkim tuuta la agɔla mɔɔli li; da basi si'ela amaa yɛlimi li wʋsa ye, ‘Ba na nyaŋ Babilon; ka diis ba'ar Bel nyan, ka dabiem na kpɛn' ba'ar Marduk. Banɛ ka ba ya'abi zi'el la na di nyan ka dabiem kpɛn' bada nɛ wina la wʋsa.’

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Sʋ'ʋlim na yi ya-datiuŋ na zab nɛ o ka san'am o teŋ la bas. Sɔ' kʋ lɛn bɛɛ ani, nidib nɛ bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa na zɔɔ lalig.

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Li saŋa nɛ li dabisa ya'a paae, Israel dim nɛ Juda dim na la'as taaba ba na kummi ieedi ba Zugsɔb Wina'am la,” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Ba na bu'osid Zion suor ka fɛndigi ba nindaasi kpa'adi ani. Ba na kena zaŋi ba mɛŋi naal nɛ Zugsɔb la li na anɛ nɔnaar linɛ ka' naarɛ ka ba kʋ tami li yɛlaa.

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: M nidib la da nwɛnɛ pɛ'ɛs banɛ bɔdig; banɛ kemi ba la kɛ ka ba bɔdig ka bɛ zuoya la ni gɔɔnd. Ba bɛ nɛ zuoya nɛ kukuosinɛ giilim ka tami ba mɛŋ vʋ'ʋsʋm zin'ig.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋsa nyɛɛ ba, kʋʋdi ba nɛ; ba dataas la da yɛl ye, Tinam pʋ tʋm taalɛ, banɛ tʋm bɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔgi ba Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba kɔnbkem amɛŋa la, onɛ ka ba yaanam da mɔr ti'ir la kɛ ka li aan ala.

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: “Zɔm yii Babilon; basimi Babilon dim teŋ la, ka nwɛnɛ bʋʋs banɛ gaadi ba taaba tuonnɛ.

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka buudbɛda banɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la la'as taaba, m na kɛ ka ba la'as taaba zab nɛ Babilon. Ba na zi'enɛ ba zi'esa ni zab nɛ o, anina ka ba na gban'e o. Ba piema la na nwɛnɛ zabzabidib banɛ mi' zaba hali ka yit ka pʋ lɛbid zaalim.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ala ka ba na nyaŋ Babilon dim; banɛ zabid nɛ Babilon la na faaɛn ban bɔɔd si'el.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Fʋ sʋnfʋ ma'ae ka fʋ maan sumalisim, fʋn kanɛ faandi m nidib la; fʋ ian'adi nwɛnɛ na'asa'a bʋ'ʋd ki ka kaasid wʋʋ wieddaad nɛ.

english_verse: The city of Babylon was like a mother to you. But it will be disgraced and become nothing but a barren desert.
translation_verse: Nyan tita'ar na dii fʋ ma; onɛ du'af la na di nyan hali. Babilon na pɔɔd tɛɛns wʋsa sʋʋgin, li na anɛ sian'atita'ar, ka an pipiris nɛ zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om kae.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋnpɛɛn zugɔ, nidib kʋ bɛ ani amaa li na bɛ nɛ li kɔn'ɔkɔn'. Banɛ wʋsa dɔl Babilon n gat li na paki ba ka ba kɛɛnd o, san'auŋ kanɛ paae o la yɛla.

english_verse: Babylon has rebelled against me. Archers, take your places. Shoot all your arrows at Babylon.
translation_verse: Maalim zi'enɛ giligi Babilon, yanam banɛ mi' tiraad tɔɔnb la wʋsa. Tɔɔnmi nɛ o! Da kɛ ka piim kpɛlim, ka o tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi pɔ'ɔg Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Kaasimi kuŋ zin'ig wʋsa gilig o! O siakya, o dɔɔd banɛ wa'am hali la liya, o zaŋguom la aaɛn li. Nɛ'ɛŋa sadigim an Zugsɔb sam yɔɔb la, yɔɔmi sam la; niŋimi nɛ o wʋʋ on niŋ bam si'em la.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Da kɛ ka ba lɛm bʋd Babilon teŋin bɛɛ ba nɔk gɔn'ɔgʋ bunɛ. Dataa kanɛ kʋʋd la zug kɛl ka sɔ' wʋsa lɛb o mɛŋ nidibin, kɛl ka sɔ' wʋsa zɔɔ lɛb o mɛŋ teŋin.

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: “Israel dim nwɛnɛ kɔnbid banɛ ka gbigima kadi ba ka ba widig. Onɛ dɛŋi gban'e ba yiiga da anɛ Asiria na'ab. Ka Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza ba'asi kɔɔ ba kɔnba naae la.”

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb ka an Israel Wina'am la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye: “M na namis Babilon na'ab nɛ o teŋ la wʋsa wʋʋ man daa namisi Asiria na'ab si'em la.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Amaa m na mɔr Israel banɛ nwɛnɛ kɔnbid la lɛbi ba mɛŋ teŋin na, ka ba na ɔnbid yaama Kaamel nɛ Basan zuoya la ni; Efiram nɛ Gilead zuoya la ni ka ba na di linɛ malisi ba tig.”

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Dabisban la ni nɛ saŋkan la, Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la, “ba na ieed Israel gbɛlʋŋ amaa ka kʋ nyɛ si'ela, ba mɛ na ieed Juda dim tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd amaa ka kʋ nyɛ si'ela, bɔzugɔ banɛ kpɛlim bi'ela la m na kɛɛ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi bas.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Kem zabi nɛ Meratam teŋ la nɛ banɛ bɛ Pekod la. Kadiminɛ ba kʋʋ ba ka san'ami ba nyain!” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la. “Maalim si'el wʋsa wʋʋ man yɛlif si'em la.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Zaba vuud bɛ teŋin la, vuud la anɛ san'auŋ tita'ar!

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Babilon da nwɛnɛ hamma nɛ nwɛ'ɛd tɛɛns sʋ'ʋlim buasid, amaa gɔsim on widigi dig yaama-yaama tɛɛns la sʋʋgin si'em!

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babilon teŋa, m bɛndif nɛ baŋ, baŋ la gban'af nɛ ka fʋ naan baŋi li. Ba daa nyɛɛf ka gban'af bɔzugɔ fʋ zan'as Zugsɔb la nɔɔr.

english_verse: I've brought out my weapons, and with them I will put a curse on Babylonia.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɔ'ɔg o zaba la'ad suak zin'ig la ka yis o sʋnpɛɛn zaba la'ad la na. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la mɔr tʋʋma na tʋmi li Babilon teŋin.

english_verse: Come from far away, you enemies of Babylon! Pile up the grain from its storehouses, and destroy it completely, along with everything else.
translation_verse: Yimi lalli kena zab nɛ o. Yɔ'ɔgim o bʋya la; la'asimi ba wʋʋ ki nɛ. San'ami ba wʋsa nyain ka da kɛ ka sɔ' kpɛlim.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Kʋʋm o na'aribpaalis la wʋsa; mɔri ba keŋ kʋʋb zin'igin! Tɔɔg na paae ba! Bɔzugɔ ba dabisir paae ya, ba namisʋg la saŋa paae ya.

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Kɛlisim zɔɔma banɛ yi Babilon n kul Zion na la yɛt si'em ye, ‘Gɔsimi ti Zugsɔb Wina'am la yɔ sam si'em! O sid yɔ o Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la sam.’

english_verse: Attack Babylon, enemy archers; set up camp around the city, and don't let anyone escape. It challenged me, the holy God, so do to it what it did to other cities. Proud Babylon Will Fall
translation_verse: La'asim tɔn'ɔsnam na ka ba zab nɛ Babilon, banɛ tɔɔnd tiraad la wʋsa! La'asim giligi teŋ la; da kɛ ka sɔ' zɔɔ pɔnsɛ! Yɔɔm o sam on maal si'el la; niŋim o wʋʋ on niŋ si'em la. Bɔzugɔ o mak o mɛŋ nɛ Zugsɔb la, Israel dim Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi la.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, na'akim la na kpi suoraadin; daakan la, soogianam la wʋsa na an baanlimm.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: “Gɔsima, fʋn kanɛ an nyɛɛsim sɔba, m duoe zi'enɛ fʋ yɛla.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em la. O yɛl ye, “Fʋ daar paae ya, fʋ namisʋg la saŋa paae ya.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛsim sɔb na tu'ugi li ka sɔ' kae na sʋŋ o ka o duoe. M na nyu'oe fʋ tempʋʋs la wʋsa nɛ bugum ka li na kanb banɛ wʋsa bɛɛ o san'an la.”

english_verse: You Babylonians were cruel to Israel and Judah. You took them captive, and now you refuse to let them go.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Israel nidib la nyɛ mugusʋg, ban nɛ Juda nidib la wʋsa. Banɛ gban'e ba la wʋsa mɔri ba nɛ kiŋ-kiŋ, ka zan'as ye ba kʋ kɛ ka ba keŋɛ.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, will rescue and protect them. I will bring peace to their land and trouble to yours.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala ba Faangid la mɔr paŋ; o yʋ'ʋri buon Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb. O na zi'enɛ zabi ba yɛla ka mɔr vʋ'ʋsʋm kɛɛn ba teŋin la na, amaa banɛ bɛ Babilon la kʋ nyɛ vʋ'ʋsʋm.

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Ba na zab nɛ ziri nɔdi'esidib la! Ba na lieb zɔn. Ba na zab nɛ zabzabidib la! Dabiem na kpɛn' ba.

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Ba na zab nɛ ba widi nɛ zaba tɛrekonam la nɛ saam banɛ zabidi sʋŋidi ba la wʋsa! Ba na lieb wʋʋ pu'ab nɛ. Ba na zab nɛ ba, ka faaɛn ba kpan'am la mɔri keŋ.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Sawak na li teŋ la zug ka kɔldaad la wʋsa na kʋdig! Teŋ la pɛ'ɛli nɛ bada, ka ba bada la kpɛn'ɛsidi ba dabiem.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ Wina'am da san'am Sodom nɛ Gomora nɛ tɛɛns banɛ kpi'e ani si'em la, ala ka sɔ' mɛ kʋ bɛ Babilon teŋinɛ; sɔ' kʋ zin'inɛ ani.” Zugsɔb la yɛl si'em la.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: Gɔsima! Dataas yi ya-datiuŋʋ kena; sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ labis ka li na'anam mɛ zu'oe ba duoe nɛ paŋtita'ari kenna.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: Ba bɔbnɛ nɛ tiraad nɛ kpana; ba anɛ bugusnam ka pʋ zɔt nimbaanliga. Ban ban'adi ba widi ken la, ba vuudi nwɛnɛ atɛuk ku'om vuud nɛ. Ba kennɛ nwɛnɛ banɛ ti'eb zaba ye ba zab nɛ Babilon teŋ la.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Babilon na'ab wʋmi ba labaar, ka o giinla kɛns. Sʋnsa'aŋ paae o, ka li zabid o wʋʋ pu'a na sa'ae ka li zabid si'em la.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ gbigimi na yi Joodan gɔn'ɔsin na, wa'ae yaama zin'igin ye o gban'e kɔnbʋg si'em la, ala ka m na kad Babilon n yis teŋin la tɔ'ɔtɔ. Anɔ'ɔn ka m na gaŋ ka o tʋmi li? Anɔ'ɔnɛ nwɛnɛ mam ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na mak nɛ mam? Kɔnbkem bɛ ya na zi'enɛ zab nɛ mam?

english_verse: Listen to my plans for you, people of Babylonia. Your children will be dragged off, and your country destroyed.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, kɛlisim Zugsɔb la gban'e Babilon yɛla si'em, on gban'e Babilon teŋ la yɛla si'em nwa': Ba na gban'e pɛbibis la mɔri keŋ; ka san'ami ba kariyauŋ la wʋsa ban zug.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Ba ya'a ti gban'e Babilon teŋ la li dammir na kɛ ka teŋgbauŋ la kirid; kikaasig la na maligim kaas buudi la wʋsa sʋʋgin.

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Gɔsima, m na kɛ ka san'auŋ sɔb la sʋnf duoe nɛ Babilon nɛ Lɛb-Kama teŋgbauŋʋn nidib la wʋsa, li na nwɛnɛ sisi'etita'ar nɛ da'adi ba.

english_verse: Foreign soldiers will come from every direction, and when the disaster is over, Babylonia will be empty and worthless.
translation_verse: M na tʋm teŋ zʋŋ nidib Babilon teŋin ka ba yɛligi li wʋʋ ki bielim nɛ ka san'am teŋ la; o dabisbɛ'og la daar ya'a ti paae ba na gilig o zin'ig wʋsa zab nɛ o.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Da kɛ ka Babilon tɔn'ɔsnam la tɛki ba tiraad la, bɛɛ ba ti'ebi ba zaba la'adɛ. Da basi ba na'akim la, kʋʋmi ba soogianam la wʋsa.

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Ba na pu'alim bɛ'ɛd bɛ'ɛdi ka lii dig Babilon suoraadin la.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pʋ tam Israel dim nɛ Juda yaas la yɛlaa, la'an nɛ ba teŋ la pɛ'ɛl nɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la Israel Wina'am Onɛ An Kasi la tuon la.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Zɔm yi Babilon! Zɔm faaɛn ya nyɔvʋr! Da kɛ ka ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la namisʋg paae ya. Zugsɔb la sam yɔɔb paae ya; o na yɔ Babilon dim linɛ nar nɛ ba.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilon da nwɛnɛ sanlim bʋtiŋ nɛ Zugsɔb la nu'ugin; o kɛ ka teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa nuu kʋʋl. Sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nuu o daam la linzugʋ kɛ ka ba gɛɛm.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Babilon na gbirigi lii kɔ'. Kaasim tisi nɛ o! Bɔɔm kpaam suoɛn o zin'ibanɛ zabid la; ka daasi'erɛɛ o na paam laafi.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛbis ye, ‘Ti naan ti'ebin Babilon, amaa o kʋ nyaŋi paam laafi; kɛlli ka ti bas o ka sɔ' wʋsa lɛb o mɛŋ teŋin, ka o sariakadib la paae saŋgbana, li dʋnɛ paae saŋgbana.

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: Saasimi piema la, nɔkimi ya gbanti'edis! Zugsɔb la kɛ ka Media na'anam sʋnf duoe, bɔzugɔ on gban'e si'el anɛ o san'am Babilon. Zugsɔb la na yɔ sam, o na yɔ o Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la sam.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Yanam banɛ bɛ kɔldaad bɛdegʋ ni ka mɔr kpan'am linɛ zu'oe la, ya bɛn paae ya, ya saŋa paae ya, ka ya na kpi.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pɔya nɛ o mɛŋ ye, ‘M na kɛ ka nidib lɛbi pɛ'ɛl, nwɛnɛ na'azɔmnam nɛ ka ba na tansid agɔla fʋ san'an ban nyaŋ la zug.’

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: O ya'a tans, ku'om linɛ bɛɛ agɔl la ɛɛnti gudig nɛ; o kɛt ka saŋgbana naanid teŋgbauŋʋn la dʋt na. Onɛ kɛt ka saa nɛ sa-ian'asʋg kenna ka yisid sisi'em o suak dɔɔdin na.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: O mɛŋ paŋ ka o maal teŋgbauŋ la; ya'am ka o nɔki maal dunia la on gban'e li gbin si'em la ka o tiɛn saŋgbana la.

english_verse: People who make idols are stupid! They will be disappointed, because their false gods cannot breathe.
translation_verse: Ninsaal wʋsa anɛ zɔlʋg ka mɛ pʋ mɔr baŋirɛ; banɛ kʋnt sanlima wina la wʋsa di nyan. Ban kpi'ed ka ya'abid si'el la ka' sidaa; li pʋ mɔr vʋm.

english_verse: Idols are merely a joke, and when the time is right, they will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ba ka' vɔɔnrɛ, ba anɛ linɛ mɔr la'adi tis nidib. Ba sariakadib saŋa ya'a ti paae, ba na bɔdig.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Onɛ an Jakob yaas Wina'am la pʋ nwɛnɛ bama, onɛ maal si'el wʋsa, la'an nɛ Israel buudbanɛ aan o faar la. O yʋ'ʋri buon Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb.”

english_verse: as well as men and women, young and old,
translation_verse: kʋ dau nɛ pu'a, ka kʋ na'akin nɛ pu'asadir,

translation_verse: nɛ kɔnbkem nɛ kɔnbid, nɛ kpaad nɛ na'akuoda, fʋn ka m nɔki widig gɔmenanam nɛ kpɛɛmnam.

english_verse: But now, my people will watch, while I repay you for what you did to Zion.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.

english_verse: Signal the nations to get ready to attack. Raise a flag and blow a trumpet. Send for the armies of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Choose a commander; let the cavalry attack like a swarm of locusts.

translation_verse: Ti'ebim buudbama ka ba zab nɛ o; Media na'anam, nɛ ba gɔmenanam nɛ ba kpɛɛmnam, nɛ tɛɛns banɛ ka ba sʋ'oe la wʋsa.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babilon zabzabidib la gu'oe zaba; ba kpɛlim nɛ ba kpi'euŋ zin'isin la. Ba paŋ naae ya; ba yʋ'ʋn nwɛnɛ pu'ab nɛ. Ba nyu'oe o nidib la ya' nɛ bugum; dabanɛ yɔɔd o za'anɔɔr la kɔya.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
