english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, m ti'ebidnɛ ye m nɔk onɛ ka fʋ sʋnf nɔŋ ka fʋ ya'am kpɛn' o hali la. La'an nɛ wala da fabil bɛɛ kum bɛɛ kɛ ka ninta'am yii fʋ nini nii.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: Fabilim baanlimm; da kum onɛ kpi la yɛllɛ. Da basi fʋ zug zaalim bɛɛ keŋ nɔbteŋa; da ligili fʋ nindaa, bɛɛ di malʋŋ dikanɛ ka onɛ ɛɛn paam kʋʋr dit la.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Dinzug m da pian' tis nidib la bɛogʋn, ka zaam ka m pu'a kpi. Bɛogʋ da nie la m da maal wʋʋ on da pʋn yɛlim ye m niŋ si'em la.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la bu'osim ye, “Fʋ kʋ kɛ ka ti baŋ linɛ zugʋ kɛ ka fʋ maan na anwaa?”

english_verse: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
translation_verse: Yɛlim Israel dim la ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa': “M gban'anɛ ye m san'ami m Pʋ'ʋsim Yir kpi'euŋ zin'ikanɛ ka ya mɔr nyɛɛsim li yɛla, ka ya nini tig ka ya ya'am nɔŋ hali la. Ya biribis nɛ ya bipumis banɛ ka ya bas nya'aŋ la, ba na kʋʋ ba wʋsa.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Ka ya na niŋ wʋʋ man niŋ si'em la. Ya kʋ ligili ya nindaa bɛɛ di dikanɛ ka banɛ ɛɛn paam kʋʋr dit la.

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Ya kʋ basi ya zug zaalim bɛɛ keŋ nɔbteŋa. Ya kʋ fabil bɛɛ kumm, amaa ya na tadigi ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la zug ka fabinnɛ tisid taaba.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Ezikil na an zanbinnɛ tisi ya; ya na niŋ wʋʋ on niŋ si'em la nɔɔ. Nɛ'ɛŋa ya'a sid niŋ, ya na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: Ka fʋn, Ninsaal biiga, daakanɛ ka m ye m san'ami ba kpi'euŋ zin'ig la, ba sumalisim nɛ ba girima, linɛ ka ba nini kpɛn' la, linɛ ka ba ya'am bɔɔd la, ba biribis nɛ bipumis wʋsa mɛ na san'am.

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: Daakan la, onɛ nyaŋi zɔɔ pɔns la na kena tisif labaar la.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Saŋkan la fʋ zilim na lak; ka fʋn nɛ on na sɔns ka fʋ kʋ lɛn an gika. Dinzug fʋ na an zanbinnɛ tisi ba, ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb labaar da kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Ammon
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, zaŋimi fʋ nini kpa Ammon dim baba ka di'e m nɔɔr pian'adi zɛrigi ba.

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: m na kɛ ka nimbanɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la kena gban'e ya, ba na la'asi ya teŋ la pʋʋgin ka ti' ba sʋga kpɛlim ani; ba na dii ya tiis la wala ka nuu ya bin'isim la.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka Rabba teŋ lieb zin'ikanɛ ka yʋgʋma na ɔnbid yaama ka Ammon lieb zin'ikanɛ ka kɔnbid na digi vʋ'ʋsid. Ka ya na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.’”

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: Dinzug m na basi ya, ka sʋ'ʋlimnam la faaɛn ya. M na yisi ya nyain tɛɛns la ni, ka san'ami ya, ka ya baŋ ye manɛ sid an Zugsɔb la.” Zɛrigir linɛ ken Moab dim san'an

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Moab nɛ Seir dimi sadigim yɛl ye, ‘Gɔsimi Juda yʋ'ʋn nwɛnɛ sʋ'ʋlim banɛ kpɛlim la wʋsa,’

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: alazug m na bas suori tis dataas ka ba kpɛn' Moab teŋ titɔndigin la, lin yii li tempʋʋs la tuon Befijesimof nɛ Baal Meon nɛ Kiriafaim linɛ an teŋ la girima zin'ig la.

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: M na nɔk Moab nɛ Ammon dim la tis ya-nya'aŋ dim, ka ba nyaŋ nidib la ka sʋ'ʋgi ba, ka li kɛ ka sʋ'ʋlimnam la kʋ lɛn tiɛn Ammon yɛla ya'asɛ;

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: ka m kɛ ka tɔɔg lu Moab dim zug. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.” Labaar linɛ zɛrigid Edom dimin la

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “Edom dim daa yɔ Juda dim sam ka li kɛ ka ba lieb tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim ban niŋ ala la zug.

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, ‘M na namis Edom dim ka kʋʋ ba nidib nɛ ba bʋnkɔnbid. M na kɛ ka li kpɛlim zaalim, ka kʋ nidib la lin yi Teman teŋin hali ti paae Dedan teŋin.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka Israel dim yɔ Edom dim samme tisim, ka ba na tʋm Edom dim nyɔnbid wʋʋ m sʋnf duor nɛ m tʋbtɛɛgiri an si'em la; ba na baŋi m sam yɔɔbi an si'em.’ Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.” Labaar linɛ zɛrigid Filistia dim la

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “Filistia dim la yɔ sam, ka niŋ linɛ dɔl gban'abɛ'ɛd linɛ bɛɛ ba sʋnfʋn nɛ kʋdimin sa dataadʋg linɛ ka ba ye ba dɔlisi san'am Juda la zug.

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, ‘M na zab nɛ Filistia dim la, ka yis Keret dim la nyain ka san'am banɛ kpɛlim atɛuk nɔɔrin la.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: M na yɔɔ ba sam bɛdegʋ ka tɛɛgi ba tʋbiri m sʋnf duor la pʋʋgin. M ya'a kɛ ka tɔɔg luu ba zugin na ala ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.’”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Tinamɛ da an yammisi bɛ teŋ zʋŋ la yʋʋm pii nɛ yinne saŋa, nwadig la pin'ilʋg daar, ka Zugsɔb labaar la kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, Taya la'ad Jerusalem ye, ‘Hahaa! Yaŋir kanɛ ka ba dɔlli kpɛn'ɛd sʋ'ʋlimnamin la kɔ' ya, ka li kʋlis gbɛlli kpa' mam. Nannanna on yʋ'ʋn dig si'em wʋʋ dabɔɔd la, m na paam kpan'am.’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: Alazugɔ Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, ‘Taya, fʋ anɛ m dataa, ka m na kɛ ka sʋ'ʋlim bɛdegʋ la'asi kena giligif wʋʋ atɛukʋ duosidi li ku'opila si'em la.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Ba na nwa'ae Taya zaŋguoma ka da'ae zin'ibanɛ ka ba dʋti gur teŋ la bas; m na kɔɔns titan la wʋsa ka kɛ tampinzaal.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Atɛuk la pʋʋgin o na an zin'ikanɛ ka ba na dɛligid zulis’ Man Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la. Sʋ'ʋlimnam la na kenna faand o la'ad,

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: ka ba na zabi kʋʋ o nimbanɛ bɛɛ o teŋkpɛmis linɛ bɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “Man na kɛ ka sɔ' yi ya-datiuŋ baba na ka o na zab nɛ Taya; on sɔb anɛ Nebukadnɛza, onɛ an Babilon na'ab nɛ na'anam na'ab la, o na mɔr o widi nɛ zaba tɛrekonam nɛ wiedban'adib nɛ zabzabidib bɛdegʋ kena.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: O na kʋ banɛ wʋsa zin' teŋ la gʋʋr la. O na maali gu' gilig teŋ la, ka digil tanni maal zaba dʋʋsa ka li dʋ hali ti paae zaŋguoma la bɛn, ka nɔk o gbanti'edis la gu' gilig ka zab nɛf.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: O na kɛ ka ba nɔk gulungun'udi nwɛ' fʋ zaŋguoma la, ka nɔk o zaba la'adi nwa'a zin'ibanɛ ka ba dʋt ani gu'ud teŋ la.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: O widi la na zu'oe galis ka ba uusʋg ma'aa ligilif. Zaba widi la dammir ma'aa na kɛ ka zaŋguoma la mi'im. O la'ad tɛrekonam nɛ zaba tɛrekonam na dɔlli kpɛn' teŋ la pʋʋg wʋʋ nidibi na dɔlli kpɛn' teŋ kanɛ ka li zaŋguoma lu si'em la.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: O widi la na gilig teŋ la suoya la wʋsa, o na kʋʋ fʋ nidib la wʋsa, ka fʋ zaŋguom kpi'ema la lu teŋin.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: O na faaɛn fʋ areza'as ka zuu fʋ kpikpinkpinnib la la'ad; ba na da'ae ya zaŋguoma la bas ka nwa'ae ya ya' vɛnla la, ka lɔb kuga la nɛ daad nɛ tan la wʋsa bas atɛukʋn.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka yʋʋm kanɛ ka ya yʋ'ʋmmi maan tʋkpiidʋg la gu'oe, ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn wʋmi ya bʋnnwɛ'ɛda la yʋʋma ya'asɛ.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka fʋ lieb tampiing kanɛ dig paalʋ, ka an zin'ig kanɛ ka ba dɛligid zulis. Ba kʋ lɛm maligim mɛɛf ya'asɛ, bɔzugɔ man kanɛ an Zugsɔb la pian'.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' zaŋi keŋ Taya yɛla: “Ba ya'a ti zabi nyaŋif ka nimbanɛ bɛ ku'om nɔɔrin la wʋm ka banɛ pu'alim la ʋʋnsid, dabiem na kpɛn' ba fʋ luug la yɛla.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Ani ka tɛɛns banɛ bɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la na'anam wʋsa na sigi ba na'am gbana zug ka yidigi ba sialɔɔdis ka yɛɛsi ba na'am fuudi digil kpikpɛŋ. Dabiem ya'a kpɛn' ba, ba na zin'in teŋin kirid saŋa wʋsa, ka gigilim gɔsidif.

english_verse: and sing this funeral song: “The great city beside the sea is destroyed! Its people once ruled the coast and terrified everyone there.
translation_verse: Ba na yʋ'ʋm kʋʋr yʋʋma fʋ yɛla yɛtif ye, “Gɔsim ban san'amif si'em, tempʋkanɛ da ka' tiraana, ka nidib keŋ zin'in ani kpi'en atɛuk nɔɔrin la! Fʋn nɛ fʋ nidib la da mɔr paŋ atɛukʋn la, fʋ da kpɛn'ɛsid banɛ wʋsa da bɛ ani la dabiem.”

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Nannanna tembanɛ bɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la kiridnɛ lin pin'il daakanɛ ka fʋ lu la; tembanɛ bɛ atɛuk teŋsʋk la dabiem gban'e ba nɛ fʋn lu nyain si'em la.

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la ka m na sigisi fʋ paas banɛ kpi ka bɛ kpi'im teŋ la, ka kɛ ka fʋ paae nimbanɛ da gaad kʋdim-kʋdim sa la. M na kɛ ka fʋ sig teŋ la teŋir, nwɛnɛ kʋdimin dabɔɔd la bɛ teŋin si'em la, paas nɛ banɛ bɛ yaʋgʋn la, ka fʋ kʋ lɛn lɛb na bɛɛ nyaŋi zin'in nɛ banɛ vʋe dunia la.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka fʋ naar an bɛ'ɛd bɛ'ɛdi ka fʋ kʋ lɛn vʋe ya'asɛ. Ba na ieef amaa ba kʋ maligim nyɛɛf ya'asɛ.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, yʋ'ʋmim kʋʋr yʋʋma Taya yɛla.

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: Yɛlim Taya linɛ bɛ suor nɔɔrin ka ba dɔlli ken atɛukʋn la, ka yɛl kpikpinkpinnib bɛdegʋ banɛ bɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, Taya teŋa, fʋ yɛt ye, “Man vɛnlim la tiraan kae.”

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Fʋ sʋ'ʋlim da bɛ nɛ atɛuk teŋsʋk; banɛ da mɛɛf la da kɛ ka fʋ vɛnlim la aan amɛŋa.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Fʋ nwɛnɛ anrintita'ar nɛ. Ba da bɔ dasʋma maalif, daad banɛ bɛ Hemon zuorin la; ba da nɔk na'aziinr daadi yi Lebanon teŋin na ye ba maal tuuta dawɔkʋ tisif.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Ka lɛn nɔk tikpi'ema daad Basan teŋin tisif ka fʋ maal anrʋŋ dabanɛ ka ba mɔri gaad ku'omin la; ka nɔk dakpi'ema linɛ yi Saipuros teŋin linɛ bɛɛ atɛuk sʋʋgin la na maali fʋ teŋir la ka zaŋ wabʋg nyina niŋi li zug.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Pien sʋŋ ka ba da' yi Egipt na sɛɛn li ya'al anrʋŋ dawɔk la zug ka sisi'em da'adi li ka anrʋŋ la ken, ka lin lɛn aan fʋ tuuta. Fʋ fuud linɛ ligin nintaŋ nɛ saa la anɛ bʋlʋ nɛ pipɛl-zɛn'ug ka li yinɛ Elisea teŋ kanɛ bɛɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Sidon nɛ Arivad tɛɛns dap la an banɛ dɔribidi fʋ anrʋŋ la. Taya, fʋ dap banɛ mi' tʋʋma kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb la da bɛ anrʋŋ la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: Dap banɛ yi Pesia nɛ Lidia nɛ Put la da bɛɛ fʋ zabzabidib la sʋʋgin. Ba nɔk gbanti'edis la nɛ kʋnt zupibis la ya'ali fʋ zaŋguoma la zug, ka fan' la'ad bɛdegʋ mɔri kena tisif.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Arivad nɛ Helek zabzabidib la'asi giligi fʋ zaŋguoma la zin'ig wʋsa. Gammad dap da dʋ yanamɛ dʋt si'eli gu'ud teŋ la. Ba da nɔk gbanti'edis la ya'ali gilig zaŋguoma la; ka kɛ ka fʋ vɛnlim la nie paalʋ.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Fʋn nɛ Girik nɛ Tubal nɛ Mesek tɛɛns la da da'ad taaba la'ad; ba nɔkid yammis nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug la'adi tiakidi fʋ la'ad la.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Bet Togama dap da mɔr widi banɛ tʋm tʋʋma, nɛ zaba widi, nɛ wiedbʋmisi kpiisid nɛ fʋ nidib la.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Roda dim da kpiisid nɛf, ka tɛɛns bɛdegʋ banɛ bɛɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la nidib aan ya da'adis, ba da mɔri wabʋg nyina nɛ dasabila banɛ kpi'em.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Juda nɛ Israel n da kpiisid nɛf la; ba da nɔk ki linɛ yit Minnif teŋin nɛ disʋma nɛ siind nɛ kpaam nɛ kpasɔɔndim tiakid nɛ la'abanɛ ka fʋ mɔr la.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Fʋn mɔr la'ad nɛ arezak bɛdegʋ la zug ka Damaskus dim kpiisid nɛ fʋ ziid daam yit Helbon teŋin na ka ziid pɛ'ɛs kɔnbidi yit Zaha teŋin na.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Dedan dim da kpiisid nɛ ya nɛ pien banɛ ka ba mɔri pa'an wief zug ka ban'ad la.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Arabia nɛ Kedar tuongatib la wʋsa da anɛ fʋ da'adis; ba da mɔri pɛbibis nɛ pɛraad nɛ bʋʋsi kuosid.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Seeba nɛ Raama da'abiis da kpiisid nɛ ya, ba da mɔri zɛɛnd nɛ li buudi wʋsa nɛ kugvɛnla nɛ sanlima ti'ad nɛ ya.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Haran nɛ Kannɛ nɛ Eden nɛ Seeba kpikpinkpinnib nɛ Asuor nɛ Kilimad dim da tɔlim nɛ fʋ.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Fʋ da' la ni ba mɔr fusʋma nɛ pien linɛ an bʋlʋ nɛ fuud linɛ ka ba ʋg sʋ'ʋŋa kuoɛn li nɔɔr la nɛ futusa linɛ pɔnri vɛnl la kenna kuosid.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Anrima banɛ yi Tarsis la tʋʋm anɛ ba ziidi fʋ la'ad la. Fʋ ziidi la'atɛbisa bɛdegʋ atɛuk la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Banɛ mi' anrʋŋ gaab la da nɔki fʋ keŋ atɛuk teŋsʋk. Amaa ka ya-nya'aŋ sisi'em kena aansif zɔra-zɔra ani.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Atɛuk la nɔɔrin teŋgbauŋ na dam ka fʋ nimbanɛ tʋmm atɛukʋn la kaas kuŋ.

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: Banɛ gaad anrima la wʋsa na basi ba anrima la; banɛ maan anrima nɛ banɛ tʋm atɛukʋn la na zi'en atɛuk la nɔɔrin.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Ba na dʋ'ʋsi ba kʋkɔya agɔla kaas nɛ sʋnsa'aŋi fʋ yɛla. Ba na bugi ba zut nɛ titan sʋnsa'aŋ zug ka bilim tampɛligimin.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Ba na pʋni ba zuti fʋ yɛla ka na yɛ bɔtkɛnda. Ba na kummi fʋ yɛla nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ tita'ar hali ka maal sʋnsa'aŋ bɛdegʋ.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Ka ban kaasid kuŋ ka fabinnɛ fʋ yɛla la, ba na kaasid kʋʋr kaasʋgʋ fʋ yɛla ye, “Anɔ'ɔnɛ da an wʋʋ Taya, onɛ ka atɛuk ku'om giligɛ? Amaa nannanna li fɔnnɛ baanlimm.”

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Fʋ da'abiis la da yii atɛukʋn la, fʋ da kɛ ka sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nyɛ on bɔɔd si'el; nɛ fʋ arezak tita'ar nɛ fʋ la'ad la kɛ ka dunia na'anam kilim bʋndaannam.

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Nannanna atɛuk la aansif zɔra-zɔra; fʋ tʋmtʋmnib la nɛ fʋ la'ad la wʋsa la'as nɛ fʋ sim ku'ozulʋŋ la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: “Banɛ bɛɛ atɛuk nɔɔrin la wʋsa gigilimnɛ gɔsidif. Dabiem gban'e ba na'anam la nɛ, ka ba sʋnf san'am ka dabiem kɛ ka ba nindaa wʋsa san'am.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Da'abiis banɛ bɛ teŋin la maannif nɛ siaa ye fʋ ba'asnɛ yɔri ka kʋ lɛm bɛ baa bi'elaa.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la da pian' tisim ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, yɛlim Taya tuongat la ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, Nyɛɛsim linɛ bɛɛ fʋ sʋnfʋn la zug ka fʋ ye, “Mam anɛ win; m zin'inɛ win na'am kʋk zug atɛuk la teŋsʋk.” Amaa fʋ anɛ ninsaal ka ka' win nɛ, la'an nɛ fʋn tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ mɔri ya'am nwɛnɛ win la.

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: Fʋ ya'am gat Daniel nɛ bɛɛ? Ka yɛlsu'adir kae na nyaŋi su'a nɛ fɔɔ?

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Ya'am nɛ yɛla gbin gban'ar kanɛ ka fʋ mɔr la kɛnɛ ka fʋ paam kpan'am tisi fʋ mɛŋ ka la'as sanlima nɛ anzurifa su'a fʋ la'ad dɔɔdin la.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Fʋ mi'ilim linɛ ka fʋ mɔri zaŋi ken kpiisʋg zin'igin la kɛ ka fʋ arezak la nɔbig, ka fʋ arezak la zug kɛ ka fʋ yʋ'ʋn lieb nyɛɛsim sɔb.

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, Fʋn tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ mɔri ya'am wʋʋ winne mɔr ya'am si'em la zug,

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: m ye m kɛnɛ ka saam kena zab nɛf, sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ nidibi tɔi gat sɔ' wʋsa. Ba na fuoe ba zaba sʋ'ʋgʋ san'ami fʋ vɛnlim nɛ baŋir la ka kʋnsi fʋ vɛnlim linɛ nyɛɛn pil-pil la.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Fʋ na kpi kum kpi'euŋ atɛuk ku'om la teŋsʋk, ka ba na mɔri fʋ sig yaʋgʋn.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Fʋ na lɛn yɛl ye, “Man anɛ win,” nimbanɛ kʋʋf la san'anɛɛ? Ayei, fʋ na anɛ ninsaal, ka ka' win, nimbanɛ kʋʋf la tuonnɛ.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Fʋ na kpi nwɛnɛ baa nɛ banɛ an saam la nu'usin. Man Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, kaasim kʋʋr Taya na'ab yɛla ka yɛl o ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “Fʋ da anɛ onɛ ka sɔ' ya'a bɔɔd ye o nyaŋi maal si'el asɛɛ ka o paaf; fʋnɛ mɛ da gat sɔ' wʋsa nɛ ya'am nɛ vɛnlim.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: Fʋ da bɛ nɛ Eden linɛ an Wina'am lɔmbɔn'ɔg la ni; kugvɛnliŋ banɛ da nyɛɛn wʋʋ gɔtiŋ ka an bʋmpielis nɛ bʋnzɛn'is nɛ bʋnsabilis ka ba ligidi zu'oe hali la wʋsa, da paasidi fʋ vɛnlim. Li wʋsa ba da nɔknɛ sanlima maali li; daakanɛ ka ba da maalif la ka ba da pʋn la'asi ba digil.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Ba da bu'oe malʋŋ kpaam niŋif ka fʋ an Kerub kanɛ gur, ala ka m gaŋi fʋ zi'el. Fʋ da bɛ nɛ Wina'am zuor linɛ an kasi la ni ka ken kugbanɛ nyɛɛn pil-pil la teŋsʋkʋ giligid.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Linɛ ka fʋ da maan wʋsa gba'ar da kae; lin pin'il daakanɛ ka ba da maalif la ti paae saŋa kanɛ ka ba yʋ'ʋn nyɛt bɛ'ɛdi fʋ san'an la.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Fʋ da kpimisi gilig zin'ig wʋsa ka li da kɛ ka zaba ma'aa pɛ'ɛlif, ka fʋ tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. Ka m kadi fʋ yis Wina'am zuorin la nɛ nyan, fʋn Kerub onɛ gur la, ka m da kadi fʋ yis kugbanɛ nyɛɛn pil-pil la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛsim ma'aa da pɛ'ɛli fʋ sʋnf fʋ vɛnlim la yɛla. Ala ka m lɔbi fʋ bas teŋin ka li pa'al na'anam la ya'am.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: Fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nɛ fʋ zam kpikpiŋ la kɛ ka fʋ san'ami fʋ winpʋ'ʋsʋm dɔɔd la, lin ka m kɛ ka bugum yii fʋ mɛŋ san'an naa kanbif, ka m sief hali ka fʋ ti lieb wʋʋ tampɛligim dig teŋin nimbanɛ da gɔtif la wʋsa nini ni.

english_verse: and the people of other nations are shocked. Your punishment was horrible, and you are gone forever. Judgment on Sidon and Peace for Israel
translation_verse: Tembanɛ wʋsa da mi'if la maannif nɛ siaa. Fʋ ye fʋ ba'asnɛ yɔri ka kʋ lɛm bɛ baa bi'elaa.” Sidon labaar linɛ zɛrigid o la yɛla

english_verse: and tell its people: I, the Lord God, am your enemy! People will praise me when I punish you, and they will see that I am holy.
translation_verse: ka yɛl ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “Sidon, m na zab nɛf ka paam yʋ'ʋri li ni. M ya'a kɛ ka tɔɔg luu fʋ zugin ka pa'alim mɛŋi fʋ san'an ye m anɛ kasi li na kɛ ka ba baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M na tʋm ban'asi fʋ san'an ka kɛ ka ziim pʋbigi fʋ pala la zug. Banɛ ka ba kʋ la na digi fʋ teŋsʋk, ba na yi zin'is wʋsa kena giligif. Ala ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: “Israel nidib la kʋ lɛm mɔr kpi'es banɛ an nimbɛ'ɛdnam banɛ tɔi wʋʋ gɛnda banɛ mɔr gɔn'ɔs, nɛ gɔn'ɔs banɛ pʋlim hali ka kunsid la. Ani ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la.”

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “M ya'a la'as Israel nidib la yi sʋ'ʋlim banɛ wʋsa ni ka ba da widigi bɛ la, m na pa'alim mɛŋ ye m anɛ kasi ba san'an sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nini ni. Ka ba na bɛɛ ba mɛŋ teŋin, zin'ikanɛ ka m da nɔki tisim tʋmtʋm Jakob la.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Ba na bɛɛ ani nɛ laafi ka mɛɛ ba mɛŋ ya', ka sɛ tiwanna ba pɔɔdin; m ya'a kɛ ka tɔɔg paae ba kpi'es banɛ da namisidi ba la ba na bɛ nɛ laafi. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ aan ba Wina'am la.”

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: Tinamɛ da an yammisi bɛ teŋ zʋŋ yʋma piiga la saŋa, li nwadis piiga la dabis pii nɛ ayi' daar, ka Zugsɔb labaar la kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, zan'asim Faaro onɛ an Egipt na'ab la, ka di'em m nɔɔr pian'ad linɛ ka m zɛrig o la tis o, on nɛ Egipt teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Pian'am tis o ka yɛl o ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “Faaro onɛ an Egipt na'aba, manɛ zan'asif, fʋn kanɛ an bandatita'ari digi fʋ kɔlisin la. Fʋ yɛl ye, ‘Nail kɔldaug la anɛ man din; Manɛ maali li tisim mɛŋ.’

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: Amaa m na nɔk gu'osi gban'e fʋ yiebaŋ la ka kɛ ka zimbanɛ bɛɛ ani la ga' kpɛlimmi fʋ ni. M na vɛ'ɛgi fʋ yis kɔlʋgin la na, la'an nɛ zimbanɛ ga'af la wʋsa.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: M na basif pipirigin la, fʋn nɛ zimbanɛ yit kɔlʋgin la wʋsa. Fʋ na lu paalʋ teŋ la zug ka ba kʋ nɔki fʋ mumm. M na nɔkif ka fʋ an diibi tis sian'arin bʋnkɔnbid nɛ niimis banɛ ian'ad agɔla la.

english_verse: Then everyone in Egypt will know that I am the Lord. You and your nation refused to help the people of Israel and were nothing more than a broken stick.
translation_verse: Ani ka banɛ bɛ Egipt teŋin la wʋsa na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la. “Fʋ anɛ balapɔn'ɔsiri tis Israel nidib.

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: Ba da gban'af nɛ ba nu'us ka fʋ kɔ'ɔgi tuoɛn kʋnsi ba biankimpiindi aans; ka ba dɛllimif, ka fʋ kɔ' ka kɛ ka ba sies tɛnrig.”

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, M na kɛ ka ba kena zab nɛf ka kʋʋ fʋ nidib nɛ fʋ bʋnkɔnbid la.

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: Egipt ye li liebnɛ dabɔɔd ka ba baŋ ye manɛ sid an Zugsɔb la. Fʋ yɛl ye, “Nail la anɛ man din; manɛ maali li.”

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Alazug m zan'asif ka zan'asi fʋ kɔlis la, ka na kɛ ka Egipt san'am ka lieb dabɔɔdi dig zaalim, lin pin'il Migdol n keŋ paae Ason hali ti paae Kus titɔndig bɛn.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Ninsaal bɛɛ bʋnkɔnbʋg nɔba kʋ lɛn dɔl ani gaadɛ, sɔ' mɛ kʋ bɛɛ ani hali ti paae yʋma pisnaasi.

english_verse: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
translation_verse: M na mɔri ba yi teŋ zʋŋ la nii lɛb naa zin'il Egipt Teŋin Linɛ bɛ zugin la, ba yaanam teŋin la. Ani ba na an sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ ka' kpi'euŋɔ.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Egipt kʋ lɛn an teŋ kanɛ ka Israel nidib na nɔki ba mɛŋi dɛlla, amaa li na anɛ zin'ikanɛ na tɛɛnsidi ba, ban da tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd ka fɛndigi lɛb o san'anɛ bɔɔd sʋŋir la. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la.”

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Yʋma pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi la ni, nwadkanɛ pin'in yiiga la dabisir yinne daar, Zugsɔb labaar la da kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza da nɔk o zabzabidibi keŋ zab nɛ Taya teŋ; ka ba zi la'ad hali ka ba zut kɔn ka ba biankimpiind wʋsa pie ka kɛ kɔnba. La'an nɛ wala on nɛ o nidib la wʋsa pʋ nyɛ nyɔɔd zabkanɛ ka ba keŋ zab nɛ Taya la.

english_verse: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, ‘M ye m kɛnɛ ka Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza na sʋ'ʋg Egipt, ka zii ba arezak la wʋsa keŋ. O na fan' ka sʋ'ʋg teŋ la ka li an yɔɔdi tis o zabzabidib la.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: M na nɔk Egipt n tis o ka li an o yɔɔd on mɔ si'em la zug, bɔzugɔ on nɛ o zabzabidib la tʋmi lii tisim. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: “‘Daakan la m na kɛ ka iil busi tis Israel dim, linɛ pa'an paŋ, ka kɛ ka fʋn Ezikil pian' ka sɔ' wʋsa wʋm. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.’”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga,” di'emi m nɔɔr pian'ad ka yɛl ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, Kaasim kuŋ ka yɛl ye, “Kaasimi dabiskan la yɛla!”

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ dabisir la mirnɛ, Zugsɔb dabisir la li'el ya. Dabisir la na anɛ zibisʋg dabisir, saŋa linɛ an yɛla tis sʋ'ʋlimnam la.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Zaba na bɛ Egipt teŋgbauŋʋn, ka yɛla bɛdegʋ na kɛn Kus teŋin na. Ba ya'a kʋ nidib Egipt teŋin, ba na zii li arezak la gaad ka nwa'a li ɛɛnbir la wʋsa bas.

english_verse: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
translation_verse: “Kus nɛ Put nɛ Lidia nɛ Arabia teŋ la wʋsa, nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ Nɔnaar Teŋin la, ba wʋsa na la'am kpi nɛ Egipt dim la.”

english_verse: All of your allies will be killed, and your proud strength will crumble. People will die from Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛt si'eli nwa' ye, “Banɛ ti'e Egipt la wʋsa na kpi ka ba paŋ nɛ ba nyɛɛsim na ba'as yɔri lin pin'il Migdol n ti paae Ason la ba na kʋʋ ba digil ani.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: “Ba na kpɛlim zaalim tɛɛns banɛ kpɛlim zaalim la sʋʋgin, ka ba tɛɛns la na digi paas tempʋbanɛ an dabɔɔd la.

english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M ya'a ti nyu'oe Egipt nɛ bugum ka kʋ banɛ sʋŋid o la wʋsa ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: “Daakan la, nidib na yii m san'anɛ anrima keŋ vɔlis Kus nimbanɛ pʋ zɔt si'el la. Egipt san'auŋ daar la dabiem na gban'e ba, bɔzugɔ li anɛ tilas ye li kena.”

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “M na kɛ ka Egipt dim banɛ zu'oe la naae ka li na yinɛ Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza paŋin.

english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka Nail kɔlis ku'om la kpiɛn ka m kuos teŋ la tis nimbɛ'ɛdnam; m ye m kɛnɛ ka saam kena zab nɛ teŋ la ka teŋ la nɛ bʋn linɛ bɛɛ li ni wʋsa san'am.” Man kanɛ an Zugsɔb la pian'.

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “M na san'am bada la ka kɛ ka ba'ar kʋ lɛm bɛ Memfis teŋinɛ. Tuongat mɛ kʋ lɛm bɛ Egipt teŋin ya'asɛ; m na kɛ ka dabiem giligi paae teŋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: The city of Pathros will be left in ruins, and Zoan will be burned to the ground. Thebes, your capital city, will also be destroyed!
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka Egipt Teŋ Linɛ Bɛ Zugin la kpɛlim zaalim, ka nyu'oe Zoan tempʋʋg nɛ bugum ka kɛ ka tɔɔg paae Tebɛs teŋ la.

english_verse: The fortress city of Pelusium will feel my fierce anger, and all the troops stationed at Thebes will be slaughtered.
translation_verse: M na kpa'ae m sʋntɔɔgʋ niŋ Pelusium, Egipt teŋkpi'euŋ la, ka kɛ ka Tebɛs arezak linɛ zu'oe la naae.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: M na nyu'oe Egipt nɛ bugum; Pelusium na nwɛɛlim nɛ tɔɔg. Ba na zabi nyaŋ Tebɛs tempʋʋg la; Memfis na paam yɛla saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: Heliopolis nɛ Bubastis dasam na kpi zaba ni, ka tɛɛns la wʋsa lieb yammis.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: M ya'a san'am Egipt dim paŋ la lik na lu Tapenɛs teŋ la zug nintaŋ; ani ka paŋ linɛ tisid o nyɛɛsim la na naae. Saŋgbana na ligil o, ka o teŋkpɛmis la nidib na lieb yammis.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka tɔɔg paae Egipt, ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: Tinamɛ da an yammisi bɛ teŋ zʋŋ la yʋma pii nɛ yinne la ni nwadkanɛ pin'in la daba ayɔpɔi daar, Zugsɔb la labaar da kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I, the Lord, have defeated the king of Egypt! I broke his arm, and no one has wrapped it or put it in a sling, so that it could heal and get strong enough to hold a sword.
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, m kɔ'ɔg Faaro onɛ an Egipt na'ab la nu'ug. Ba pʋ lɔɔ li ye li tug bɛɛ bɔ si'elnamɛ bɔb ye li paam paŋi nyaŋi zanl sʋ'ʋgɔ.”

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “M zan'as Faaro onɛ an Egipt na'ab la. M na kɔɔ o nu'us ayi' la wʋsa, linɛ nam pʋ kɔ' la nɛ linɛ pʋn kɔ' sa la wʋsa, ka kɛ ka sʋ'ʋg la naan o nu'ugin la lu teŋin.

english_verse: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
translation_verse: M na widig Egipt dim la kpɛn'ɛs tɛɛns la wʋsa ni.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka Babilon na'ab paam paŋ, amaa Faaro nu'us na nwɛlig. M na nɔk sʋ'ʋg la niŋ Babilon na'ab la nu'ugin ka o nɔki zab nɛ Egipt. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: M na widig Egipt dimi kpɛn'ɛs tɛɛnsin la wʋsa. Ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: Tinamɛ da an yammisi bɛ teŋ zʋŋ la yʋma pii nɛ yinne la ni, nwadis atan' la dabisir yinne la daar ka Zugsɔb la labaar kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: Yɛlim Faaro onɛ an Egipt na'ab la nɛ o nimbanɛ zu'oe hali la ye, Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi mak o mɛŋ nɛ fʋ na'am pʋʋginɛ?

english_verse: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
translation_verse: Ku'om da kɛ ka li nɔbig, ka ku'okanɛ bɛ teŋin la kɛ ka o wa'am; kɔlis la da pʋbidnɛ giligid o gbin, ka maal ku'osuoya ka li kennɛ paad tibanɛ bɛ la wʋsa.

english_verse: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
translation_verse: Linzug li da nɔbigi wa'am hali gat tibanɛ wʋsa bɛ la. Li wila da maligim paas bɛdegʋ ka wa'am hali, ka tɔɔndi yadigid, ku'om bɛ bɛdegʋ la zug.

english_verse: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
translation_verse: Niimis banɛ bɛ wʋsa da maal tɛɛd wila la ni, ka bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa banɛ bɛ teŋ la zug kena du'a li gbinnin. Sʋ'ʋlim titada la wʋsa da bɛ nɛ li ma'asim.

english_verse: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
translation_verse: Li vɛnlim la da ka' tiraana, nɛ li wila linɛ yaarim-yaarim la, bɔzugɔ li nya'a la da signɛ teŋin hali ti paae ku'okanɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: None of the cedar trees in my garden of Eden were as beautiful as this tree; no tree of any kind had such long branches.
translation_verse: Na'aziinr linɛ bɛ Wina'am lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la da kʋ nyaŋi mak nɛ li, bɛɛ tibɛda banɛ bɛ tempʋʋsin la nyaŋi mak nɛ li wila la. Tiig da kae Wina'am lɔmbɔn'ɔgin la mɔr vɛnlim nwɛnɛ li.

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: Manɛ da maali li ka li vɛnl ka mɔr wila bɛdegʋ. Tikanɛ wʋsa da bɛ Eden Wina'am lɔmbɔn'ɔg la pʋʋgin la da bɛn'ɛd o nɛ fufum.

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, Lin da wa'am hali ka li vaand wa'ami gat si'el wʋsa ka mɔr nyɛɛsim li wa'alim la zug la,

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: m nɔki li tis tɛɛns la tuongat la, ye o tɛɛgi li tʋbir wʋʋ li bugusim tʋʋma kanɛ ka li tʋm la nar si'em. M yisi li m san'an,

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: ka teŋ zʋŋ sʋ'ʋlim linɛ mɔr pʋtɔɔgʋ gat sɔ' wʋsa la na nwaae lii bas ka li vaand la sʋʋgi lu zuoya zug nɛ bɔn'ɔdin; ka li wila la kɔɔ dig bɔn'ɔfalis banɛ bɛ teŋin la.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Niimis banɛ bɛ la wʋsa da ya'an tiliilʋŋ la zug, ka bʋnkɔnbid la wʋsa mɛ da bɛɛ li wila linɛ li la sʋʋgin.

english_verse: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Alazug tisi'a kʋ lɛn duoe agɔla nɛ nyɛɛsim kɔlʋg la nɔɔrin, ka wa'ami gat tiis wʋsa nɛ li vaandɛ. Tiig kae na lɛm paam ku'om bɛdegʋ ka duoe wɔkʋʋ. Li zi'eli tisi ba wʋsa ye ba kpii sig teŋin wʋʋ ninsaal nɛ, ka la'as nɛ banɛ bɛ yaʋgʋn la.

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, Daakanɛ ka tiig la da sig kpi'im teŋ la, ku'otitada linɛ bɛ teŋin la da maal sʋnsa'aŋ, ka m da giŋi li ku'osuoya la, ka li ku'otita'ar la wʋsa kpiɛn. Linzug ka m pil Lebanon nɛ lik, ka tiis banɛ bɛ teŋ la zug la wʋsa kʋdig.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Sʋ'ʋlimnam la da wʋm ka o lu ka li dam si'em la, m da kɛ ka ba kiridi li dammir la zug, saŋkan ka m da sigis o yaʋgʋn nɛ banɛ pʋn dɛŋi sig teŋin la. Ka tiis banɛ bɛ Eden la wʋsa nɛ tisʋma nɛ tivɛnla banɛ bɛ Lebanon la wʋsa, tibanɛ da paam ku'om sʋ'ʋŋa ka pʋn dɛŋi sig teŋ la teŋir la na paam sumalisim o liig la zug.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: Banɛ da bɛɛ o ma'asim nɛ banɛ da la'as o sʋ'ʋlimin la, da dɔl o sig yaʋgʋn la'an nɛ banɛ ka ba kʋʋ ba zaba ni la.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: “Tiig kae Eden nii na nyaŋi mak nɛ fʋ vɛnlim nɛ fʋ na'am la. La'an nɛ wala fʋn mɛ na la'am lu teŋin nɛ Eden tiis la, fʋ na la'asi digin nɛ banɛ zi' Wina'am la, nɛ banɛ kpi zaba ni la. “Nɛ'ɛŋa anɛ Na'ab Faaro nɛ o nimbanɛ kalli ka' bɛn la.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: Tinamɛ da an yammisi bɛ teŋ zʋŋ la saŋa, li yʋʋm pii nɛ ayi' la ni, nwadis pii nɛ ayi' la ni, dabisir yinne daar ka Zugsɔb labaar kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, kaasim kʋʋr Faaro onɛ an Egipt na'ab la yɛla ka yɛl o ye, Fʋ nwɛnɛ gbigim nɛ sʋ'ʋlimnam la sʋʋgin; fʋ nwɛnɛ bandatita'ari bɛ kɔlisin lugidi giligid kɔldaugin la, gudigid ku'om la nɛ fʋ nɔba ka ku'om la wʋsa an bian'ar.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, M ye m nɔknɛ nidib bɛdegʋ, ka nɔki m zulis la lɔbi gɛɛlif, ka ba tɛɛgi fʋ dʋ'ʋs na.

english_verse: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
translation_verse: Man na yisi fʋ lɔb gbɛog ka dɛligif paalʋ. M na kɛ ka dunia niimis wʋsa la'as na diif ka bʋnkɔnbid banɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa kena ɔnbif.

english_verse: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
translation_verse: M na nɔki fʋ ni'imi yadig tampiing zug ka kɛ ka fʋ niŋgbina la pɛ'ɛl bɔn'ɔd la.

english_verse: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka fʋ ziim pʋbigi pɛ'ɛl teŋgbauŋ la hali ti paae zuoya la, ka fʋ niŋgbina la pɛ'ɛl bɛɛnna la.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: M ya'a fɛɛnsi fʋ yis, m na pil saŋgbana la ka kɛ ka nwadbibis la lieb lik. M na nɔk saŋgbauŋʋ pil winnig ka nwadig la kʋ lɛn tis o nɛɛsim ya'asɛ.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Linɛ wʋsa bɛɛ agɔlli tisid nɛɛsim la m na kɛ ka li lieb liki fʋ san'an; m na kɛ ka lik kɛɛn fʋ teŋin la na. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
translation_verse: M ya'a tɛɛgi ya tʋbir tɛɛns la sʋʋgin, ka zii ya keŋ teŋ zʋŋ zin'ikanɛ ka ya nan zi' keŋɛ, li na pak nidib bɛdegʋ ka kɛ ka ba sʋnf san'am.

english_verse: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
translation_verse: M ya'a ʋki m zaba sʋ'ʋg la ba tuon li na kɛ ka nidib bɛdegʋ lidigi fʋ yɛla ka dabiem na kɛ ka ba na'anam gigilimi fʋ yɛla. Daakanɛ ka fʋ na lu la sɔ' wʋsa niŋgbina na dammid saŋa wʋsa o nyɔvʋr yɛla.

english_verse: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, Babilon na'ab la na kena zab nɛf.

english_verse: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka fʋ nidib bɛdegʋ kpi; banɛ an dapkpi'ema ka tɔi hali gat sɔ' wʋsa tɛɛnsin la na zabi kʋʋ ba. Ba na kɛ ka Egipt nyɛɛsim la wʋsa naae, ka nyaŋ o nimbanɛ an bɛdegʋ la wʋsa.

english_verse: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
translation_verse: M na kʋʋ o niigi la wʋsa banɛ dɛn'ɛd ku'om bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa. Nid kʋ lɛn nɔk o nɔbiri gbɛndigi li ya'asɛ bɛɛ niigi la nɔki ba nɔba gudig ka li kilim bian'arɛ.

english_verse: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ka m yʋ'ʋn na kɛ ka o ku'om la tisig ka kɛ ka o bɛɛnna la pʋbid wʋʋ kpaam nɛ. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M ya'a kɛ ka Egipt kilim dabɔɔd ka yis linɛ wʋsa bɛɛ ba teŋ la zug, m mɛ ya'a ti kʋ onɛ wʋsa bɛɛ ani ba na baŋ ye manɛ sid an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: “Kʋʋr kukuma kaŋa ka ba na kum tis o. Tɛɛns la pu'ab na kum Egipt nɛ o nidib bɛdegʋ la yɛla; ba na kumi ba yɛla. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, kaasim kuŋ Egipt nimbanɛ an bɛdegʋ la yɛla. Sigisimi ba wʋsa teŋin nɛ teŋ titada dim la, ye ba la'as nɛ banɛ bɛ yaʋgʋn la wʋsa.

english_verse: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
translation_verse: Bu'osimi ba ye, “Ya mɔr vɛnlim gati ya taabaa? Sigimi yaʋgʋn la'as nɛ banɛ zi' Wina'am la.

english_verse: You cannot escape! The enemy's sword is ready to slaughter every one of you.
translation_verse: Ba na la'as nɛ banɛ kpi zaba ni la kpi. Sʋ'ʋg la fuoe ya, kɛl ka ba tɛɛg Egipt nɛ o nimbanɛ an bɛdegʋ la wʋsa gaadi keŋ.

english_verse: Brave military leaders killed in battle will gladly welcome you and your allies into the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Yaʋg la pʋʋgin tuongatib banɛ an kpi'emnam la na yɛl Egipt dim nɛ banɛ paasi ba zug la ye, Ba sigim na la'am dig nɛ Wina'am, nɛ banɛ kpi zaba ni la!”

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Ba yaad la bɛ nɛ teŋin sa ka o zabzabidib la digi gilig o yaʋg la. Banɛ wʋsa da kpɛn'ɛsid banɛ vʋe teŋ la ni dabiem la kpiya, ba kʋʋ ba zaba ni.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: Ba maalnɛ gadʋgʋ digil o ka li bɛ nimbanɛ kpi la teŋsʋk, ka o nimbanɛ an bɛdegʋ la wʋsa digi gilig o yaʋg la, ba wʋsa zi' Wina'am, ka ba kʋʋ ba zaba ni, bɔzugɔ ba daamʋg da tiig teŋ la zug. Ba di nyan ka kpii la'as nɛ banɛ bɛ yaʋgʋn la.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Mesek nɛ Tubal bɛɛ ani nɛ ba nimbanɛ an bɛdegʋ la wʋsa ka ba giligi ba yaad la. Ba wʋsa zi' Wina'am, ka ba kʋʋ ba zaba ni, bɔzugɔ ba da mugusid nidib dunia zug.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ dig nɛ zabzabidib banɛ kpi ka zi' Wina'am, ka sig yaʋgʋn nɛ ba zaba la'ad, ka ba nɔki ba zaba la'ad la kʋki ba zut yaʋgʋn la. Ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yɔɔd la bɛɛ ba kɔnba ni, bɔzugɔ ba mugusʋg la da tiig dunia zug.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: “Na'ab Faaro, fʋ mɛ na kpi keŋ la'as nɛ banɛ zi' Wina'am la, nɛ banɛ kpi zaba ni la.

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Edom bɛɛ ani nɛ o na'anam nɛ o tuongatib. La'an nɛ ban da mɔr paŋ la, ba la'asi ba digil yaʋgʋn nɛ banɛ zi' Wina'am ka kpi zaba ni la.

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: “Tuongatib banɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la wʋsa nɛ Sidon dim la mɛ bɛɛ ani; ba kpi nɛ nyan, ka ba la'asi ba nɛ banɛ ka ba kʋ la, la'an nɛ ban da mɔri ba paŋ la vɔlisid nidib si'em la. Ba dig nɛ banɛ zi' Wina'am la zaba ni, ka mɛ di nyan nɛ banɛ bɛ yaʋgʋn la.

english_verse: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
translation_verse: “Na'ab Faaro nɛ o zabzabidib la wʋsa na nyɛɛ ba, ka li bʋgʋl o sʋnf nɛ o nimbanɛ an bɛdegʋ ka ba da kʋʋ ba zaba ni la.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: “La'an nɛ man da kɛ ka o kpɛn'ɛs nidib la dabiem la, Faaro nɛ o nidib la wʋsa na la'as nɛ banɛ zi' Wina'am ka kpi zaba ni la.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: ka o nyɛ ka tanp ken teŋ la zug na, ka pieb na'atan ye nidib la baŋ,

english_verse: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
translation_verse: Tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd banɛ ka o dɛŋi tʋm la wʋsa la kʋ lɛn nɔki ziil oo. O ya'a tʋm linɛ an sʋm ka nar, o sid na vʋe.

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Tinamɛ da an yammisi bɛ teŋ zʋŋ la, yʋʋm pii nɛ ayi' saŋa, nwadis piiga la dabisa anu la daar, ka dau sɔ' onɛ da zɔɔ pɔns Jerusalem teŋin la kena yɛlim ye, “Tempʋʋg la luya!”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, pian'am tisi fʋ teŋ dim la ka yɛli ba ye, “Man ya'a ti kɛ ka tanp lu teŋ si'a, ka teŋ la nidib gaŋi ba dap la yinne ye o an onɛ guri ba;

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: On sadigim wʋm ka na'atan la pieb ka o pʋ sa'al o mɛŋ nɛ nimmua la, o ziim ye li bɛ nɛ o mɛŋ zug. O ya'a sa'alin o mɛŋ nɛ nimmua, o naan faaɛn o mɛŋi bas.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Amaa onɛ gur la ya'a nyɛ ka zaba kenna ka o pʋ pieb na'atan la kɛ ka nidib la baŋɛ ka zaba la paae na ka sɔ' kpi, o sɔba na ba'asi kpi o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdin, amaa m na kɛ ka o ziim ziil onɛ gur la zug.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: Tɔ', “Ninsaal biiga, man maalif nɛ teŋ gur ye fʋ gur Israel nidib la; alazug kɛlisim man pian'ad si'el la, ka yɛli ba sa'alʋg kanɛ yiti m san'an na la.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: M ya'a yɛl bugus ye, ‘Bugusim sɔba, fʋ sid na kpi,’ ka fʋ pʋ sa'al o sɔb nɛ nimmua ye o basim o suoyɔɔd la, bugusim sɔb la na kpi o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la yɛla, ka m na kɛ ka o ziim ziilif.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ ya'a sa'al bugusim sɔb la ye o basim o suoyɔɔd la, ka o ya'a pʋ tiakɛ, o na kpi o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdin la, amaa fʋn na yisi fʋ mɛŋ yɛla ni.

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Pʋpielim sɔb ya'a bas pʋpielim tʋʋma, ka tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd, o na kpii li yɛla.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, ya'a kpɛlim nɛ fʋ, fʋ teŋ nidib la pian'adi fʋ yɛla dɔkpina ni nɛ ya' za'anɔya nii yɛt taaba ye, “Kemi na ka ti wʋm labaar linɛ yi Zugsɔb la san'an na.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: “Ninsaal biiga, yɛlim Israel nidib la ye, ‘Ya yɛt ye, Ti yidigir nɛ ti tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la diinli ti nɛ, ka ti kpiidi li yɛla. Ti ye ti niŋ wala vʋ'ʋgɛ?’”

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: Yɛlimi ba ye, Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, Sida-sida ka m yɛti ya ye, bugusim sɔb ya'a kpi li pʋ malisi ma, man bɔɔd si'el anɛ ba bas bugusim tʋʋma ka vʋe. Fɛndigimi! Fɛndigim yii ya suobɛ'ɛdin la! Israel nidiba, bɔ ka ya ieed kum?

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: Alazug, Ninsaal biiga, yɛlimi fʋ teŋ nidib la ye, Pʋpielim sɔb ya'a ti pin'ili ki'isid, o pʋpielim kanɛ ka o dɛŋi tʋm la kʋ faaɛn o, ka bugusim sɔb ya'a tiak ka pʋ lɛn tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ, o tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka o dɛŋi tʋm la mɛ kʋ lɛn kɛ ka o luu. Pʋpiel ya'a tʋm bɛ'ɛd, ba kʋ kɛ ka o vʋe on da tʋm tʋʋm sʋŋ sieba la zugɔ.

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: M ya'a yɛl pʋpielim sɔb ye o sid na vʋe ka o ti'e o pʋpielim linɛ ka o pʋn dɛŋi tʋm la zug ka pin'ili tʋm bɛ'ɛd, tʋʋm sʋma banɛ ka o pʋn tʋm la wʋsa sɔ' kʋ lɛn tiɛn lii, o na kpi tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd linɛ ka o tʋm la zug.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: M mɛ ya'a yɛl bugus ye, “Fʋ sid na kpi,” daasi'erɛɛ o na bas bugusim tʋʋma ka tʋm linɛ nar.

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: O ya'a lɛbis linɛ ka sɔ' nɔki digil o san'an ka pɛ'ɛŋ ligidi, ka lɛbis linɛ ka o zu, ka dɔlis suobanɛ tisid vʋm ka pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛdɛ, o na vʋe ka kʋ kpii.

english_verse: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
translation_verse: Amaa fʋ nidib la yɛt ye, “Sida kae Zugsɔb la suoya la anii!” Amaa li lɛɛ anɛ ban suoya la ni ka sida kae.

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb ya'a bas tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd ka tʋm tʋʋm sʋma nɛ linɛ dɔl suor, o na vʋe on tʋm ala la zug.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, Israel dima, ya yɛt ye Zugsɔb la suoya pʋ dɔl sidaa. Amaa m na kad sɔ' wʋsa saria ka li dɔl nɛ on tʋm si'em. O pa'al Jerusalem na lu si'em

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Dau la saa na kɛn wʋʋ bɛog na la, li zaam ka Zugsɔb la paŋ da kɛɛn m san'an na, ka m zilim lak, ka dau la nyaan kɛɛn m san'an bɛkɛung na. Ka m lɛn ka' gika ka ya'ae m nɔɔr ka pian'ad.

english_verse: Then the Lord said:
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb labaar kɛɛn m san'an na ye,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, nimbanɛ bɛ teŋ kanɛ lu la ni yɛt ye, “Abraham da anɛ dau yinne, la'an nɛ wala o da sʋ'ʋg teŋ la. Amaa tinam zu'oya, li anɛ sida ye ba pʋn nɔk teŋ la tisi ti ye li aan ti faar.”

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: Dinzug yɛlimi ba ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la ye, “Yanamɛ sadigim nan ɔnbid ni'im linɛ mɔr ziim ka ti'e ya bada, ka kʋʋd nidib la; li sʋm ye ya sʋ'ʋg teŋ laa?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Ya ti'enɛ ya paŋ, ka tʋm tʋʋmkisa, ka dig nɛ taaba pu'ab. Li sʋm ye ya sid sʋ'ʋg teŋ laa?”

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Yɛlimi ba ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “Sida-sida ka m yɛti ya ye, banɛ kpɛlim tɛɛns banɛ ka ba nwa' ba la ni na kpi zaba ni; banɛ zɔɔ kpɛn' mɔɔgin la, m na kɛ ka wɛog bʋnkɔnbid gban'e ba; banɛ bɛ teŋ kpi'ema ni nɛ tampinyɔ'ɔdin la, ban'as na kʋʋ ba.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka teŋ la kpɛlim dabɔɔd, ka paŋ kanɛ ka ba mɔr nyɛɛsim li yɛla la kilim zaalim, ka Israel zuoya la na kpɛlim zaalim ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn dɔl ani gaadɛ.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ka m ya'a kɛ ka teŋ la kpɛlim dabɔɔd ka li anɛ tʋʋmkisa banɛ ka ba tʋm la zug, ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.”

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Man nidib la kennɛ fʋ san'an na wʋʋ ban ɛɛn pʋn niŋid si'em la. Ba na zin'ini fʋ tuon ye ba kɛlisi fʋ pian'ad, amaa ba pʋ tʋm wʋʋ fʋn yɛt si'em laa. Ba nɔkidi ba nɔɔri pian'ad wʋʋ ba pɛsigi ba mɛŋi tis mam nɛ, amaa ba sʋnf la pɛ'ɛl nɛ filʋŋ ka ba bɔɔd ye ba paam linɛ ka' ba dinnɛ.

english_verse: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
translation_verse: Nɛ lin wʋsa ba gɔsidifnɛ nwɛnɛ onɛ yʋ'ʋmmi sɛnlimmi ba nɛ nɔmalisiŋ ka nwɛ'ɛd bʋnnwɛ'ɛda sʋ'ʋŋa, bɔzugɔ ba wʋmmi fʋ pian'ad ka pʋ maan fʋn yɛt si'el laa.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: “Nɛ'ɛnam wʋsa ya'a sid ti niŋ; li mɛ sid na niŋ ka ba na baŋ ye nɔdi'es sid mi' bɛɛ ba san'an.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: Ninsaal biiga, di'emi m nɔɔr pian'ad linɛ ka m zɛrigid Israel kɔnbkemnib la tisi ba; pian'am yɛli ba ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa' ye, “Tɔɔg bɛɛ tis Israel kɔnbkemnib, banɛ ba'a bɛ nɛ ban mɛŋ yɛla ma'aa la! Kɔnbkemnib tʋʋm ka'anɛ ba gur kɔnbidɛɛ?

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Ya dit ka nuud, ka mɔr bʋnkɔnbid la kɔnbidi maan fusʋma yɛɛd, ka kʋʋd bʋnkɔnbsʋma la ɔnbid, amaa ya lɛɛ pʋ gɔsid kɔnbid laa.

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Ya ba'a ka' nɛ banɛ tadig la bɛɛ ya ti'eb banɛ bɛn'ɛd la bɛɛ pies banɛ pu'alim la fɛn'ɛdɛ. Banɛ bak la ya pʋ mɔri ba lɛb naa, bɛɛ iee banɛ bɔdig laa; ya mɔri banɛ nɛ bugusim ka maannɛ ba bɛ'ɛd hali.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka ba da widig, bɔzugɔ onɛ na kemi ba kae, ka ban da widig la ba da kilim diibi tis sian'arin bʋnkɔnbid.

english_verse: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
translation_verse: M kɔnbid la da giligi keŋ zuoya nɛ kʋkʋna wʋsa ni. Ba da widigi gilig dunia wʋsa, ka sɔ' pʋ iee ba, bɛɛ gɔs ye ba bɛ yaanɛ.”

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: “Asida sida ka m yɛti ya,” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la, “Man pɛ'ɛs la ka' onɛ kemmi baa, ka ba gban'e ba nɛ paŋ ka ba kilim sian'arin bʋnkɔnbid diib, ka kɔnbkemnib la pʋ iee kɔnbid la, amaa ba ba'a bɛ nɛ ba mɛŋ yɛla ma'aa ka ka' kɔnbid la yɛlaa.”

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'eli nwa' ye, “M zan'as kɔnbkemnib la ka mɛ kɛ ka m kɔnbid la yɛla ziili ba zugin. M na kadi ba ka ba kʋ lɛn kemi m kɔnbid laa, ka li kɛ ka kɔnbkemnib la kʋ lɛn nyaŋi diisidi ba mɛŋa. M na faanm kɔnbid la yisi ba nɔɔrin, ka ba kʋ lɛn an diibi tisi baa.”

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “Mam mɛŋ na iee m kɔnbid la ka guri ba.

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: Wʋʋ kɔnbkemmi na nyɛɛ o kɔnbid banɛ widig ka guri ba si'em la, ala ka m na gɔsi m pɛ'ɛs la. M na faaɛn ba ka mɔri ba yi zin'ikanɛ wʋsa ka ba da widigi kpɛn' dabisbɛ'og daar linɛ da an lik ma'aa la.

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: M na yisi ba tɛɛnsin la na, ka la'asi ba mɔri kɛɛn ba mɛŋ teŋin na. M na kemi ba Israel zuoya la nɛ bɔn'ɔfalisin nɛ zin'ig wʋsa linɛ bɛ teŋin la.

english_verse: I promise to take care of them and keep them safe,
translation_verse: Mam mɛŋ na kemi m kɔnbid la ka guri ba ka ba dig baanlimm.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: “M na ie banɛ bɔdig la ka mɔr banɛ bak la lɛb na. Banɛ pu'alim la m na ti'ebi ba, ka gɔs banɛ tadig la, amaa banɛ nɔb ka kpi'em la m na kʋʋ ba. M na kemmi ba nɛ sida.”

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: “Ya'a kpɛlim nɛ yanam banɛ aan m kɔnbid la,” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl si'em nwa', “M na bak pɛ'ɛs la nɛ pɛraad la nɛ bʋʋs la yinne-yinne.

english_verse: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
translation_verse: Li pʋ sia'ali ya nɛ yanamɛ ɔnbid yam sʋma laa? Ka li lɛn anɛ tilas ye ya nɔ yaama banɛ kpɛlim la nɛ nɔbaa? Ya ya'a nu ku'okanɛ an nyain, li pʋ sia'ali yaa? Li nar ye ya nɔki ya nɔba gbɛndig ku'okanɛ kpɛlim la ka li kilim bian'arɛɛ?

english_verse: That means my other sheep have nothing fit to eat or drink.
translation_verse: Li nar ye m kɔnbid la ɔnb yaama banɛ nɔ nɛ nɔba la, ka nu ku'okanɛ gbɛndigi kilim bian'arɛɛ?”

english_verse: You strong ones have used your powerful horns to chase off those that are weak,
translation_verse: Yanamɛ zaŋi ya biankimpiind nɛ ya nyɔ'ɔd nɛ ya iila tuo pɛbanɛ ka' paŋ la hali ti nyaŋi kadi ba wʋsa la zug,

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: m na faanm pɛ'ɛs la ka ba kʋ lɛm gban'e baa. M na kad pɛ'ɛs la saria yinne-yinne ka bak pɛ'ɛsʋma la yis pɛbɛ'ɛdnam la ni.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka kɔnbkem yinne guri ba, ka on na anɛ m tʋmtʋm David, ka onɛ na kemi ba, ka an ba kɔnbkem.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Man onɛ an Zugsɔb la na aan ba Wina'am, ka m tʋmtʋm David na an tuongati ba san'an.” Man kanɛ an Zugsɔb la pian'.

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: M na maal nɔnaar nɛ ba linɛ na an laafi nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm, ka yis wɛog bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa ka ba na bɛ pipirigin la, ka gbis sian'arin la ka dabiem kae.

english_verse: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka ba zin'ini giligi m zuor la, ka niŋi ba zug albareka. M na kɛ ka saa niid din nar ye di niid saŋa si'a. Di ye li anɛ bareka saa.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Tiis banɛ bɛ teŋin la na wali ba wala, ka teŋgbauŋ la na du'a zʋʋd; nidib la na bɛ nɛ laafi teŋ la zug. Ba na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la, m ya'a kɔ'ɔgi ba yɔksin daug la, ka yisi ba banɛ gban'e ba maal yammis la nu'usin.

english_verse: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Tɛɛns la nidib la kʋ lɛn faaɛn baa, bɛɛ wɛog bʋnkɔnbidi gban'e baa. Ba na bɛ nɛ laafi, ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn kɛ ka dabiem mɔri ba.

english_verse: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
translation_verse: M na tisi ba teŋ kanɛ sid du'ad zʋʋd, ka kʋ kɛ ka kɔ'ɔm bɛɛ ba teŋinɛ. Tɛɛns la nidib mɛ kʋ la'adi ba ka diisidi ba nyannɛ.

english_verse: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ala ka ba na baŋ ye manɛ aan ba Zugsɔb Wina'am la, ka bɛ nɛ ba; ba mɛ na baŋ ye, ban Israel nidib la wʋsa anɛ m nidib.

english_verse: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_verse: “Yanam banɛ aan m pɛ'ɛsi bɛɛ m bʋlʋʋgin la, anɛ m nidib, ka man aan ya Wina'am.” Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
translation_verse: ka yɛli ba ye, Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “M zan'asif, Seir zuorɛ, m na tiɛn m nu'ugʋ zab nɛf ka kɛ ka fʋ kilim dabɔɔd.

english_verse: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka fʋ tempʋʋs la lieb dabɔɔd, lin ka ya na baŋ ye manɛ an Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
