english_verse: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
translation_verse: O na tis zʋʋd maan taslaa yinne na'araug wʋsa zugin nɛ pɛraug wʋsa zugin nɛ kpaam kɔliba anu.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “Za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ zak la pʋʋginɛ kpa' ya-nya'aŋ la, ba na yɔɔ li daba ayuobʋ linɛ an tʋʋma dabisa la wʋsa pʋʋgin, amaa Vʋ'ʋsʋm Daar nɛ nwadpaalig daar wʋsa ba na yɔ'ɔgi li.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Na'ab la na yi yiŋi dɔl za'anɔɔr la kpɛn' dɔl za'anɔɔr linɛ bɛ za'ambɛŋin la keŋ zi'en za'anɔɔr la baba. Maanmaan la na maal o nyu'or maan nɛ o taaba la'asʋg maan la. Ani ka Na'ab la na zi'en maal za'anɔɔrin la ka yi, amaa ba kʋ yɔ' za'anɔɔr laa, ka li ti paae zaam.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Vʋ'ʋsʋm Daar nɛ nwadpaalig malʋŋ saŋa, teŋ la nidib wʋsa na la'asi zun'e Zugsɔb la za'anɔɔr la kpɛn'ɛb zin'igin la.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Nyu'or maan linɛ ka Na'ab la na mɔri kena la na anɛ pɛribis ayuobʋ nɛ pɛraug banɛ wʋsa pʋ mɔr dɛŋŋa.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Zʋʋd maan linɛ ka ba na tisi paas pɛraug la zug la na anɛ taslaa, zʋʋd maan la nɛ pɛribis la o na mɔri li nɛ o ya'am gban'e si'em, ka la'am mɔr kpaam kɔliba anu paas zʋʋd taslaa wʋsa zug.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Nwadpaalig la daar o na tis na'arapɔl, nɛ pɛbibis ayuobʋ nɛ pɛraug, ka ba wʋsa da mɔr dɛŋŋa.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: O na tis zʋʋd maan la taslaa yinne paas na'araug la zug, nɛ taslaa yinne paas pɛraug la zug, nɛ pɛbibis la zug wʋʋ o ya'am gban'e si'em bɛn, ka la'am mak kpaam galam anu paas taslaa wʋsa zugin.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: Na'ab la ya'a kpɛn', asɛɛ ka o dɔl za'ambɛŋin za'anɔɔr la kpɛn', ka na lɛn dɔl zin'ikan la yi.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: “Teŋ la nidib ya'a ti kɛn Zugsɔb la san'an na, malima banɛ ka ba zi'el la saŋa, onɛ wʋsa na dɔl za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la kpɛn', na dɔlnɛ za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ ya-dagɔbʋg la yi. Sɔ' da dɔl on dɔl za'anɔsi'a kpɛn' la yii, amaa sɔ' wʋsa na dɔl za'anɔkanɛ kpa' o la yi.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Na'ab la na bɛɛ ba sʋʋgin, ba ya'a kpɛn'ɛd on dɔlli kpɛn', ba ya'a yit on dɔlli yi.

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. translation_verse: “Malʋŋ tiɛnr saŋa nɛ malima banɛ ka ba zi'el la saŋa, zʋʋd piini la na anɛ taslaa paas na'araug zug, nɛ zʋʋd taslaa paas pɛraug zug, nɛ pɛbibis zug wʋsa wʋʋ na'ab la paŋi na tun'e si'em, ka ba na mak kpaam galam anu paas taslaa wʋsa zugin.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: Na'ab la ya'a tis Zugsɔb la ya'amlɛog piini, li ya'a na an nyu'or maan bɛɛ taaba la'asʋg maan, ba na yɔ'ɔg za'anɔɔr kanɛ kpa' ya-nya'aŋ la tis o. O na maal nyu'or maan bɛɛ taaba la'asʋg maan wʋʋ on maan Vʋ'ʋsʋm Daar si'em la. O ya'a maali naae ka yi, ba na yɔ' za'anɔɔr la.

english_verse: Each morning a year-old lamb that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to please me.
translation_verse: “Daar wʋsa ya na tis pɛ'og kanɛ an yʋʋm yinne ka pʋ mɔr dɛŋŋa maal nyu'or maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la; bɛkɛung wʋsa asɛɛ ka ya maali li.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: O ya'a lɛn zaŋi lii tis o yammis la yinne, yammʋg la na sʋ'oe li ti paae vʋ'ʋsʋm yʋʋm kanɛ ka ba na tisi ba yɔlisim, saŋkan ka o na lɛbisi tis na'ab la. O faar la anɛ na'abiis la din, ban ma'aa sʋ'oe li.

english_verse: The ruler must never abuse my people by taking land from them. Any land he gives his children must already belong to him. The Sacred Kitchens
translation_verse: Li pʋ sʋm ye na'ab la faaɛn paalʋ linɛ an nidib la din ka kadi baa yis linɛ aan ba faari nɛ. O mɛŋ faar ma'aa ka o na tis o biis. Ala ka ba kʋ faanm nidib la faar ka kadi ba basɛ.”

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Ani ka dau la mɔrimi kpɛn' za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ lʋgirin la kpɛn' dɔbanɛ an kasi kpa' ya-datiuŋ, linɛ an maanmaannib dɔɔd la. Ani ka o pa'alim paalʋ linɛ bɛ ya-tuona la.

english_verse: We went back to the outer courtyard and walked past the four corners.
translation_verse: Ani ka o dɔllimi yi zak kanɛ bɛ yiŋ la na dɔllimi giligi li lɔdis anaasi la, ka m nyɛ ka lɔdig wʋsa mɔr zak ya'as.

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: Ka ba nɔk kuga mɛɛ gilig za'as anaasi la ka dan'amis bɛɛ li pʋʋgin la kpi'e nɛ zaŋguom la.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Ka o yɛlim ye, “Za'abibis bama ni ka Pʋ'ʋsim Yir la tʋmtʋmnib na dʋgid maana banɛ ka nidib kena maal la.”

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛm mɔrimi dɔl za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la yi yiŋ la na ka dɔlli mɛ giligi paae za'anɔɔr kanɛ bɛ yiŋi kpa' ya-nya'aŋ la, ka ku'om la pʋbidi dɔlli li dagɔbʋg baba.

english_verse: The man walked east, then took out his measuring stick and measured
translation_verse: Dau la da lɛb ya-nya'aŋ baba la, ka mɔr nwiig kanɛ makid o nu'ugin. Ka o mak nɔba tusir nɛ kɔbisnu (

english_verse: meters downstream, the stream had become a river that could be crossed only by swimming.
translation_verse: ) ya'as, amaa li da anɛ kɔldaug ka m kʋ nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋɛ, bɔzugɔ ku'om la da zu'onɛ ka zulim ka li ya'a ka' lugibɔ, sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi lɔ'ɔŋɛ.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: O da yɛlim ye, “Ninsaal biiga, fʋ nyɛ nɛ'?” Ka mɔrimi keŋ kɔldaug la nɔɔrin.

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: Man paae ani la, m nyɛ tiis bɛdegʋ ka ba bɛ kɔldaug la nɔɔrin zin'is ayi' la wʋsa.

english_verse: The man said: This water flows eastward to the Jordan River valley and empties into the Dead Sea, where it turns the salt water into fresh water.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛlim ye, “Ku'okaŋa pʋbidnɛ lɛbid ya-nya'aŋi sigid Joodan bɔn'ɔgin la ken atɛukʋn, tiakidi atɛuk ku'om linɛ an yaarim la ka li lieb ku'osʋŋ.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Kɔldaug la ku'om pʋbigi keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa, bʋnvʋya nɛ li buudi na bɛɛ ani bɛdegʋ. Zimi na bɛɛ ani bɛdegʋ, bɔzugɔ ku'om la pʋbidi ken zin'isi'a la na kɛ ka ku'om linɛ an yaarim la tiaki an ku'osʋŋ; alazug ku'om la pʋbigi keŋ zin'isi'a wʋsa si'el wʋsa na vʋe.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ziiŋgban'adib na kena zi'en kɔldaug la nɔɔrin; ba na zi'en Engedi teŋin hali ti paae Eneglam. Zin'ibanɛ ka ba na dɛligid asau na bɛɛ ani. Zimi nɛ li buudi wʋsa na bɛ wʋʋ atɛuk tita'ar la zimi an si'em la.

english_verse: But the marshes along the shore will remain salty, so that people can use the salt from them.
translation_verse: Amaa bɛɛnna nɛ zin'ibanɛ ka ku'om giisi digi dig la kʋ an ku'osʋŋɔ, zin'iban la na kpɛm bɛ ala an yaarim zin'ig.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Tiwanna nɛ li buudi na yi kɔlnɔya la ni zin'is ayi' la wʋsa. Ba vaand kʋ sʋʋg bɛɛ ba gʋ'ʋŋ walibɔ. Nwadig wʋsa ba wan wala, bɔzugɔ ku'om linɛ pʋbidi yit Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la na dɔn'ɔsidi ba. Ba wala la na an diib ka ba vaand la na ti'ebid ban'as.” Teŋ la titɔndis

english_verse: The northern border will begin at the Mediterranean Sea, then continue eastward to Hethlon, to Lebo-Hamath, then across to Zedad,
translation_verse: Teŋ la titɔndigi na an si'em nwa': Ya-datiuŋ baba la na mɔri ala paae Atɛuk Tita'ar la paae Heflon suorin la gaadi paae Lebo-Hamat nɛ Zedad,

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: keŋ Berota nɛ Sibiram, linɛ bɛ Damaskus nɛ Hamat titɔndigin la, mɔri ala paae Hazer-Hatikon linɛ bɛ Hawaran teŋ titɔndigin la.

english_verse: So the northern border will run between the Mediterranean Sea and Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between Damascus and Hamath.
translation_verse: Titɔndig la na dɔlisnɛ titɔndig linɛ bɛ Damaskus teŋ la ya-datiuŋʋ tɔlisi yi atɛukʋn la paae Hazar Enan teŋin, ka Hamat teŋ titɔndig la kpɛlimmi li ya-datiuŋ. Nɛ'ɛŋa na an titɔndig linɛ bɛ ya-datiuŋ la bɛn.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: Ya-nya'aŋ la baba na dɔlisi paae Hawaran nɛ Damaskus teŋsʋk, ka dɔlisi dɛn'ɛn Joodan kɔldaug la, linɛ bɛ Gilead nɛ Israel teŋsʋk la, keŋ paae atɛuk linɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la paae Tamar. Nɛ'ɛŋa na an ya-nya'aŋ la bɛn.

english_verse: The southern border will begin at Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and will end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ya-dagɔbʋg la baba li na mɔri ala yi Tamar n gaadi keŋ Meriba-Kades ku'omin la, dɛn'ɛn Egipt titɔndiginɛ keŋ Atɛuk Tita'arin la. Nɛ'ɛŋa na an ya-dagɔbʋg la bɛn.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: Ya-tuona baba la, Atɛuk Tita'ar la na aan li titɔndigi keŋ paae zin'ikanɛ kpa' Lebo-Hamat teŋ la. Nɛ'ɛŋa na an ya-tuona la titɔndig.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Ya na pʋdig teŋ la tisi ya mɛŋ wʋʋ Israel dɔɔd la an si'em la.

english_verse: It will belong to the Israelites and to any foreigners living among them whose children were born in Israel. These foreigners must be treated like any other Israelite citizen, and they will receive
translation_verse: Ya na pʋdigi li tisi ya mɛŋ ka li an faari tisi ya nɛ saam banɛ zin' nɛ ya ka mɔr biis la. Ya na niŋi ba wʋʋ Israel dim banɛ an teŋin dim ka ba du'a ba anina la; ban bɛ nɛ ya la, ba na la'am di'e faar la nɛ Israel dim.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Saam la ya'a zin'in Israel dɔsi'a wʋsa teŋin, ani ka ya na tisi baa ba faar. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: Lin yi Juda titɔndig la ya-nya'aŋi paae ya-tuona la, ya na bɛŋi li ka li bɛɛ li kɔn', li na anɛ nɔba makir tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu (

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Zin'ikanɛ ka ya bɛŋi li ka li bɛɛ li kɔn' la na an Zugsɔb la din, li wa'alim na anɛ nɔba makir tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu (

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa na anɛ zin'ikanɛ an kasi ka an maanmaannib la din. Li ya-datiuŋ la wa'alim na anɛ nɔba makir tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu (

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Zin'ikanɛ an kasi nwa' na anɛ maanmaannib la din, banɛ yi Zadok tuŋʋn na, ka tʋmmi tisidim ka pʋ badig wʋʋ Levi dim la sieba da badigi dɔl Israel dim ka ba yirid si'em la.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: Li na anɛ piinkanɛ ka ba di'e ka li bɛɛ li kɔn' ka an kasi, paalʋ la pʋʋgin. Li anɛ zin'ikanɛ an kasi, ka li titɔndig la tɔnd nɛ Levi dim teŋ la.

english_verse: I will give the other half of my sacred land to the Levites. Their share will also be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide,
translation_verse: Linɛ kpi'e maanmaannib teŋ la na anɛ Levi dim la pʋʋr, ka li wa'alim na anɛ nɔba makir tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu (

english_verse: and they must never sell or trade any of this land—it is the best land and belongs to me.
translation_verse: Li pʋ nar ye ba kuosi li bɛɛ tiaki li zin'isi'a. Li anɛ teŋ la zin'ikaŋa an paalʋ sʋŋ, ka li pʋ sʋm ye ba tɔlisi li tis sɔ', bɔzugɔ li anɛ kasi tis Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: Li wʋsa makiri an si'em nwa', li ya-datiuŋ baba la na anɛ nɔba makir tusa ayuobʋ nɛ kɔbisyɔpɔi nɛ pisnu (

english_verse: The land on the east and west sides of the city limits will be farmland for the people of Jerusalem; both sections will be five kilometers long and three kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Linɛ kpɛlim ka li titɔndig tɔnd nɛ zin'ikanɛ an kasi la, dɔlisi keŋi li ya-nya'aŋ la wa'alim na anɛ nɔba makir tusa pii nɛ anu (

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Tʋmtʋmnib banɛ bɛ tempʋʋgin la ka na tʋm pɔɔgin la na yinɛ Israel dɔɔd pii nɛ ayi' la wʋsa ni na.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: Paalʋ la na anɛ mauk, li nɔya la zin'ig wʋsa na anɛ nɔba makir tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu-nu (

english_verse: The regions east and west of this square of land will belong to the ruler of Israel. His property will run east to the Jordan River and west to the Mediterranean Sea. In the very center of his property will be my sacred land, as well as the temple,
translation_verse: Linɛ kpɛlimmi li lʋga ayi' la tɔ'ɔŋ zin'ikanɛ an kasi la nɛ teŋ la bʋn la na anɛ Na'ab la bʋn. Lin yi ya-nya'aŋ la nɔba makir tusa pistan' nɛ ayɔpɔi nɛ kɔbisnu (

english_verse: together with the share belonging to the Levites and the city of Jerusalem. The northern border of the ruler's property will be the land that belongs to Judah, and the southern border will be the land that belongs to Benjamin. The Division of Land among Tribes in the South The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Alazugɔ, linɛ an Levi dim la din, nɛ tempʋʋgʋ sʋ'oe si'el la na bɛ nɛ Na'ab la sʋ'oe si'el la teŋsʋk. Na'abi sʋ'oe si'el la na bɛ nɛ Juda nɛ Benjamin n sʋ'oe si'el la teŋsʋk.

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Gad titɔndig linɛ bɛ ya-dagɔbʋg la na yi Tamar linɛ bɛ ya-nya'aŋ la paae Meriba-Kades ku'om la, dɔlisi ala keŋ paae Egipt titɔndig linɛ an kɔldaug la paae Atɛuk Tita'ar la.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Paalʋ kanɛ ka ya na pʋdigi tis Israel dim dɔɔd la ka li an ba faar la nwa': nɛ'ɛŋa na aan ba pʋʋr. Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la. Tempʋʋg la za'anɔya

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Lin dɔlisi kaae gilig teŋ la wʋsa la, anɛ nɔba makir tusa pisi nɛ ayɔpɔi (

english_verse: In the third year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia attacked Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Jehoyakim da di Juda na'am la, yʋma atan' saŋa, Babilon na'ab Nebukadnɛza da kena nɛ o nidibi lɔbi gilig Jerusalem teŋ la.

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la bas suor ka o gban'e Jehoyakim onɛ an Juda na'ab la ka vaae Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la'ad la. O da zi la'abama wʋsa keŋ digil la'ad dɔɔg linɛ bɛɛ o ba'ar dɔɔgin Babilon teŋin la.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Aspenas onɛ aan o na'ayikpɛm wʋsa kpɛɛm la ye o gaansim banɛ yi na'adɔɔgin nɛ girima dim la mɔr na.

english_verse: The king said, “They must be healthy, handsome, smart, wise, educated, and fit to serve in the royal palace. Teach them how to speak and write our language
translation_verse: Di nar ye ba an dasam banɛ ka' dɛŋŋa ka vɛnl, ka ba zug tʋm, ka ba nyɛ sa'alʋg, ka an banɛ na tun'e zamis ka gban'e si'el gbin tɔ'ɔtɔ, ka nar ye ba tʋm na'ayin la. O da ye o pa'ali ba Babilon dim pian'ad nɛ ba ya'am gbana nɛ ba malima yɛla.

english_verse: and give them the same food and wine that I am served. Train them for three years, and then they can become court officials.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da maknɛ dikanɛ ka ba na di nɛ dankanɛ ka ba na nu daar wʋsa o diib zin'igin la. Li da anɛ ye ba zamisi ba yʋma atan', ka lin nya'aŋ ka ba keŋ tʋm tis Na'ab la.

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Banɛ da yi Juda ka ba gaŋi ba la da anɛ Daniel nɛ Hanania nɛ Misael nɛ Azaria.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Na'ayir kpɛɛm la da tisi ba yʋ'ʋpaala. Ba da buon Daniel ye Belteseaza, ka buon Hanania ye Siadirak, ka buon Misael ye Mesiak, ka buon Azaria ye Abɛdnɛgo.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Amaa Daniel da gban'e ye o kʋ di na'ayir la diib bɛɛ o nu daam la dian'a o mɛŋa, ka da sɔs suor kpɛɛm la san'an ye o pʋ bɔɔd ye o niŋ ala dian'a o mɛŋa.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Wina'am da kɛ ka kpɛɛm la ya'am kpɛn' Daniel ka o zɔɔ o nimbaanlig.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: Amaa kpɛɛm la lɛɛ da zɔtnɛ dabiem ka yɛl Daniel ye, “Na'ab la, pʋm pa'alim yanamɛ na di ka nu si'el. O ya'a ti nyɛ ka ya niŋgbina pʋ saalim wʋʋ ya dasam taaba la, o na kʋʋm.”

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: Na'ayir kpɛɛm la da bɔ sɔ' ka o gur Daniel nɛ o zuanam atan' la. Daniel da yɛl onɛ ka kpɛɛm la gaŋ ka o guri ba la ye,

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: “M zugdaana, m bɛlimnɛ, nɔkim dabisa piiga ma'aa kpansi ti gɔs. Da tisi ti si'eli gaad zɛnvaand nɛ ku'om ma'aanɛ.

english_verse: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
translation_verse: Ka yʋ'ʋn mak tinam nɛ ti taaba banɛ dit Na'ab la disʋma la gɔs tinamɛ na an si'em, ka lin nya'aŋ fʋ tun'e maali ti fʋn bɔɔd ye fʋ maal si'em wʋsa.”

english_verse: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
translation_verse: O da siak ala tisi ba ka kpansi ba dabisa piiga.

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Dabisa piiga la nya'aŋ, ba laafi nɛ ba vɛnlim da gaadi ba taaba banɛ da dit disʋma la.

english_verse: After this, the guard let them eat vegetables instead of the rich food and wine.
translation_verse: Ka onɛ guri ba la da nɔk diib nɛ dansʋma linɛ ka na'ab la tis la ka lɛdig zɛnvaand.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Wina'am da tis nidiba anaasi bama mi'ilim ka ba gban'ad ban zamisid si'el la gbin sʋ'ʋŋa. Ka Daniel baŋid nier nɛ zaansʋŋ wʋsa gbinnɛ pa'an.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Saŋa kanɛ ka Na'ab la da zi'el ye ba mɔri ba lɛb o san'an na la da paae la, kpɛɛm la da mɔri ba keŋ Na'ab Nebukadnɛza san'an.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la sɔns nɛ ba ka nyɛ ka dasam la wʋsa sʋʋgin sɔ' kae nwɛnɛ Daniel nɛ Hanania nɛ Misael nɛ Azaria. Dinzug Na'ab la da kɛ ka ba kpɛlim o yin la tʋmmi tisid o.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Na'ab la ya'a da bɔɔd ya'am bɛɛ sa'alʋg o bu'osidnɛ ban, bɔzugɔ, o da nyɛ ka ba sɔn'oe o tima dim nɛ banɛ maan nyalima o sʋ'ʋlim la ni wʋsa nɔɔr piiga.

english_verse: Daniel served there until the first year of King Cyrus.
translation_verse: Daniel da bɛɛ ani, hali ka Na'ab Sarus ti di na'am.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Na'ab Nebukadnɛza n da di na'am gɔnlig yʋma ayi' la, o da zaansim ya, ka o sʋnf san'am hali ka o mak ye o gbisi gʋ'ʋŋ.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: o da yɛli ba ye, “M zaansim nɛ zaansʋŋ si'a ka li daamim hali, ka m bɔɔd ye m baŋi li gbin.”

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Banɛ nyɛt yɛla yɛt la da lɛbis Na'ab la nɛ Aram buudi pian'ad ye, “Naa Na'aba, yɛlimi tii fʋ zaansʋŋ la ka ti yɛli fʋ li gbin.”

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da lɛbisi ba ye, “Man gban'e si'em nwa': ya ya'a pʋ yɛl zaansʋŋ la an si'em ka mɛ pa'alimi li gbinnɛ, m na kʋʋ ya ka fi'isi-fi'isi ya zɔra-zɔra, ka ya ya' la kpɛlim dabɔɔd.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Amaa ya ya'a nyaŋi yɛlim zaansʋŋ la nɛ li gbin, ya na di'e piini nɛ yɔɔd nɛ na'asi bɛdegʋ m san'an. Dinzugɔ, yɛliminim zaansʋŋ la nɛ li gbin.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Ka ba lɛn lɛbisi yɛl o ye, “Naa, Na'aba, kʋdim yɛlimi ti fʋ zaansʋŋ la, ka ti yɛli fʋ li gbin.”

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: Ya ya'a kʋ yɛlim zaansʋŋ la, namisʋg yinne ka m ye m tisi ya. Li pa'ali ye Ya gban'anɛ ye ya ma'aa ziri tisim, ka tɛn'ɛs ye yɛla na tiak. Linzug yɛliminim zaansʋŋ la ka ala ka m na baŋ ye ya na nyaŋi yɛlimi li gbin.”

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Tima dim la da yɛl o ye, “Naa, Na'aba, hali na'abanɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ nɛ paŋ ka li galisi gaad sɔ' wʋsa dunia nwa' nan zi' yɛli o ya'am bɛɛ tima dim ye ba maal fʋn yɛl si'el la!

english_verse: It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
translation_verse: Na'abi bɔɔd si'el la tɔinɛ galis. Sɔ' kae na nyaŋi yɛl Na'ab nɛ'ɛŋa asɛɛ teŋgbana la, ka ban mɛ pʋ la'am bɛ nɛ ninsaaliba.”

english_verse: This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends. God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
translation_verse: Ka ba sid sɔb gbauŋ ye ba kʋ ya'am dim banɛ bɛ Babilon la wʋsa. Ba da tʋm ninsieba ye ba yii ie Daniel nɛ o zuanam la kʋʋ ba.

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Ariok onɛ an banɛ gur Na'ab la tuongat la da yi ye o kʋ ya'am dim Babilon pʋʋgin la, Daniel da pian' tis o nɛ ya'am nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm.

english_verse: and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened,
translation_verse: O da bu'os Na'ab soogia kpɛɛm la ye, “Bɔ yɛla kimm ka Na'ab tis nɔkpi'euŋ kaŋa?” Ka Ariok nɔk yɛl la pa'al Daniel.

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa da kɛ ka Daniel keŋ Na'ab la san'an sɔs ye o tisim o saŋa bi'ela ka o na pa'al o zaansʋŋ la gbin.

english_verse: Daniel returned home and told his three friends.
translation_verse: Ka Daniel yʋ'ʋn lɛb yinne yɛl o zuanam Hanania nɛ Misael nɛ Azaria.

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: Daniel da yɛli ba ye ba sɔsim Wina'am onɛ bɛ arezana ni la ka o zɔɔ ba nimbaanlig yɛl kaŋa pʋʋgin; linɛ na kɛ ka ba da la'as on nɛ o taaba la nɛ ya'am dim banɛ bɛ Babilon la kʋʋ.

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Li da nie pa'al Daniel zaansʋŋ pʋʋgin yʋ'ʋŋ kan la ka o baŋ Na'ab la zaansʋŋ la gbin. Ka Daniel pian' zun'e Wina'am onɛ bɛ arezana ni la yʋ'ʋr,

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: ka ye, “Wina'am yʋ'ʋr paamim zʋn'or saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ! Ya'am nɛ paŋ anɛ o din.

english_verse: You control human events— you give rulers their power and take it away, and you are the source of wisdom and knowledge.
translation_verse: Onɛ tia'asid saŋa nɛ sigir; onɛ diisid nidib na'am ka lɛn yisidi ba na'amin. Onɛ tisid ya'am dim mi'ilim ka tisid banɛ tɛn'ɛsid la baŋir.

english_verse: “You explain deep mysteries, because even the dark is light to you.
translation_verse: Onɛ nied yɛlsu'ada pa'an; o mi' linɛ bɛ likin ka nɛɛsim bɛɛ o san'an.

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: M pʋ'ʋs bareka ka zʋn'ʋf, m yaanam Wina'am. Fʋ tisim ya'am nɛ paŋ, fʋ nie pa'alim tinamɛ sɔsif si'el yɛla la, fʋ pa'ali ti Na'ab zaansʋŋ la gbin.” Daniel n pa'al zaansʋŋ la gbin si'em

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: Daniel da keŋ Ariok san'an, onɛ ka Na'ab la da gaŋ ye o kʋ ya'am dim Babilon teŋin la, ka yɛl o ye, “Da kʋ ya'am dim banɛ bɛ Babilon teŋin laa. Dɔllimi keŋ Na'ab la san'an ka m yɛl o zaansʋŋ la gbin.”

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Ariok da dɔl Daniel n keŋ Na'ab la san'an tɔ'ɔtɔ kpɛn' ka yɛl o ye, “Naa, Na'aba, m nyɛnɛ dau yinne ka o bɛ yammis banɛ yi Juda teŋin na la san'an, onɛ na nyaŋi yɛlif zaansʋŋ la gbin.”

english_verse: The king asked Daniel, “Can you tell me my dream and what it means?”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da bu'os Daniel ye, “Fʋ sid na nyaŋi yɛlim man zaansim nyɛ si'el la nɛ li gbinnɛɛ?”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Ka Daniel lɛbis ye, “Naa, Na'aba, ya'am sɔb bɛɛ tiim sɔb bɛɛ ba'akɔlʋg sɔb kae na nyaŋi yɛlif fʋn bɔɔd ye fʋ baŋ si'el la,

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: “Fʋn sa dig la, naa Na'aba, fʋ ya'am la sa fɛndigi lɛb nɛ bʋmbanɛ na ti maal la ni, ka Onɛ nied yɛlsu'ada pa'an la nie pa'alif linɛ na ti maal.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Ya'a an mam, bʋn kaŋa nie pa'al man ka li ka'anɛ man mɔr ya'am gati m ninsaal taaba laa, amaa, Na'aba, li na sʋŋ ka fʋ baŋ zaansʋŋ la gbin, nɛ linɛ sa bɛɛ fʋ pʋtɛn'ɛrin la.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: “Na'aba, fʋ sa zaansimnɛ nyɛ si'el ka li zi'e fʋ tuon nwɛnɛ ninsaal nɛ; li sa zu'onɛ hali nyɛɛn, ka fʋ gɔt ka li mɔr dabiem.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Linɛ sa zi'e la zug anɛ sanlim ma'aa, ka li nyɔ'ɔg nɛ nu'us an anzurifa, ka li pʋʋr nɛ gbɛya an kʋntzɛn'ug,

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: ka li nɔba an kʋnt, ka li nɔbibis la an kʋnt ka gɛndig ya'ad.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: Fʋn sa nan gɔti li la ka tampiing buak ka li ka' ninsaali nɔk nu'ugʋ buaki lii. Li sa luu nwɛ' linɛ zi'e la nɔbibis linɛ an kʋnt ka gɛndig ya'ad la nwa'ae.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Ka saŋkan la mɛn ka kʋnt nɛ ya'ad, nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug, nɛ anzurifa, nɛ sanlima la wʋsa sa nwa'ae bugusi bugus nwɛnɛ udugi dig zieŋin nɛ. Ka sisi'em kena kanligi li gaad ka fʋ kʋ nyaŋi baŋ lin kpɛn' si'ela. Amaa tampiing kanɛ sa nwa'ae li la sa kilim zuori pɛ'ɛl dunia wʋsa.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: “Na'aba, zaansʋŋ la sa an si'em nwa'. M yʋ'ʋn na pa'alif zaansʋŋ la gbin.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Na'aba, fʋ anɛ na'anam wʋsa na'ab. Wina'am onɛ bɛ arezana ni la tisif sʋ'ʋlim nɛ paŋ nɛ kpi'euŋ nɛ girima;

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: “Fʋn ya'a gaad, sʋ'ʋlim yinne na kena tɔi gaadi fʋ din la. Linɛ tia'al atan' na kena na an kʋntzɛn'ug, ka na sʋ'ʋg dunia wʋsa.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Nɔbibis la bɛŋi an kʋnt nɛ ya'ad la, ala ka sʋ'ʋlim la na bɛŋi kpi'em ka zin'isi'a pʋ kpi'ema.

english_verse: This kingdom will be the result of a marriage between kingdoms, but it will crumble, just as iron and clay don't stick together.
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ fʋn nyɛ ka kʋnt naal nɛ ya'ad si'em la, ala mɛn ka nidib la na la'as taaba ka kʋ nyaŋi niŋ nɔɔr yinne, wʋʋ kʋnti pʋ naan nɛ ya'ad sʋ'ʋŋa si'em la.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Fʋn nyɛ tampiing la ka li buaki yi zuorin na la gbinnɛ la, amaa li ka' ninsaal nu'ugʋ kɛ ka tampiing la kɔ'ɔg kʋnt la, nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug la nɛ ya'ad la nɛ anzurifa la nɛ sanlim la wʋsa bur-bur. “Tɔ', Na'aba, Wina'am Tita'ar la sa pa'alif linɛ na niŋ bɛog sa. Zaansʋŋ la anɛ yɛlsida, ka li gbinnɛ pa'al si'em la anɛ sida, ka ka' bi'esʋgɔ.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab Nebukadnɛza vanbin Daniel tuonnɛ na'as o ka tis nɔɔr ye ba tisim o piini nɛ tudaar linɛ nyuusid hali.

english_verse: The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da yɛl Daniel ye, “Sida, fʋ Wina'am la sid anɛ teŋgbana wʋsa Wina'am, nɛ na'anam wʋsa Zugsɔb, nɛ onɛ nied yɛlsu'ada pa'an, bɔzugɔ fʋ nyaŋi nie yɛlsu'adkaŋa.”

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis Daniel kpi'euŋ ka tis o piini bɛdegʋ. O da kɛ ka o sʋ'ʋg Babilon teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa ka maal o ya'am dim la wʋsa kpɛɛm.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Linɛ pɛ'ɛs la Daniel da sɔs Na'ab la ye o gaŋ Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo ka ba sʋŋi gɔsid Babilon yɛla, ka Daniel lɛɛ kpɛlim na'ayin la.

english_verse: and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke.
translation_verse: ka kpi'emnam banɛ da la'as la wʋsa kena giligi ba. Ba da nyɛya ka bugum la pʋ vʋnligi ba niŋgbiŋ, bɛɛ ba zuobid nyuusid kaanlʋgɔ; bugum la daa pʋ si'isi ba fuudɛ, ka bugum nyuug mɛ kae ba niŋgbiŋinɛ.

english_verse: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
translation_verse: O da la'as o gɔmenanam la nɛ ya'am dim nɛ sa'ansa'annib nɛ tuongatib nɛ banɛ su'ad ligidi nɛ banɛ kad saria nɛ lɔyanam nɛ kpɛɛmnam banɛ bɛɛ o sʋ'ʋlimin la wʋsa ye ba la'as na ka ba zaŋ bʋn linɛ ka o ya'abi zi'el la pɛsig.

english_verse: Then an official stood up and announced: People of every nation and race, now listen to the king's command!
translation_verse: Ba da mɔɔl nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, “Nidib nɛ sʋ'ʋlim nɛ buudi wʋsa,

english_verse: Trumpets, flutes, harps, and all other kinds of musical instruments will soon start playing. When you hear the music, you must bow down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
translation_verse: ya ya'a wʋm ka na'atana, nɛ wiis, nɛ bʋnnwɛ'ɛda la wʋsa dam, li anɛ tilas ye sɔ' wʋsa igin linɛ ka Na'ab Nebukadnɛza nɔk sanlimaa ya'abi zi'el la tuon ka wɔ'ɔgi li.

english_verse: Anyone who refuses will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Onɛ wʋsa kʋ igini li tuon ka wɔ'ɔgi li, ba na ʋk o tɔ'ɔtɔ lɔs bugum tita'ar pʋʋgin.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard the music, they bowed down and worshiped the gold statue that the king had set up.
translation_verse: Alazug ban da wʋm ka bʋnnwɛ'ɛda la nɛ li buudi wʋsa nwɛ'ɛd la, nidib la nɛ sʋ'ʋlim la dim wʋsa nɛ buudi wʋsa da igin bʋn linɛ ka Na'ab Nebukadnɛza nɔk sanlime ya'abi zi'el la tuonnɛ wɔ'ɔgi li.

english_verse: Some Babylonians used this as a chance to accuse the Jews to King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Li da anɛ saŋa kaŋa ka Babilon nidib la sieba paam suori yi paalʋ naa gbi' Jew dim la.

english_verse: They said, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Ba da yɛl Na'ab Nebukadnɛza ye, “Naa, Na'aba!

english_verse: You commanded everyone to bow down and worship the gold statue when the music played.
translation_verse: Fʋ tis nɔɔr ye onɛ wʋsaa wʋm ka bʋnnwɛ'ɛda la nwɛ' on iginim fʋn nɔk sanlima kud si'eli zi'el la tuon,

english_verse: And you said that anyone who did not bow down and worship it would be thrown into a flaming furnace.
translation_verse: ka onɛ wʋsa kʋ igini wɔ'ɔgi lii, li anɛ ba lɔb o bas bugum tita'ar la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: Sir, you appointed three men to high positions in Babylon Province, but they have disobeyed you. Those Jews, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, refuse to worship your gods and the statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Naa na'aba, Jew dim sieba banɛ ka fʋ tisi ba kpi'euŋ ka ba gɔsid yɛlsieba Babilon teŋ kaŋa ni la pʋ gi'igidi fɔ. Ba pʋ dɔlli fʋ bada la, ka mɛ pʋ siak ye ba igin linɛ ka fʋ nɔk sanlima ya'abi zi'el la tuonnɛ. Banɛ an; Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar was furious. So he sent for the three young men and said,
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la sʋnf duo nɛ ba hali, ka o tʋm buol dasam atan' la ka bu'osi ba ye,

english_verse: Now I am going to give you one more chance. If you bow down and worship the statue when you hear the music, everything will be all right. But if you don't, you will at once be thrown into a flaming furnace. No god can save you from me.”
translation_verse: Nannanna m ye m tisi ya nɛ suor ya'as ka ya igini wɔ'ɔg bʋn la yʋ'ʋs. Ya ya'a wʋm ka bʋnnwɛ'ɛda la nwɛ' ka ya igini wɔ'ɔgi li, yɛla naae ya. Amaa ya ya'a wʋm ka pʋ iginɛ, m na gban'e ya lɔs bugumin. Ba'asi'a kae na nyaŋi faaɛn ya yii m nu'uginɛ.”

english_verse: The three men replied, “Your Majesty, we don't need to defend ourselves.
translation_verse: Ka dasam atan' la lɛbisi yɛl ye, “Naa, li ka' ye ti bɔɔdi ye ti pian' tisi ti mɛŋ bʋʋd yɛl kaŋa nii.

english_verse: The God we worship can save us from you and your flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Wina'am kanɛ ka ti dɔl la na nyaŋi faaɛn ti yii fʋ nu'ugin nɛ bugum la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: But even if he doesn't, we still won't worship your gods and the gold statue you have set up.”
translation_verse: Amaa hali baa o ya'a kʋ faaɛn ti, baŋim, Na'aba, ye tinam kʋ wɔ'ɔgi fʋ bada la bɛɛ igin bʋn linɛ ka fʋ nɔk sanlimaa maali zi'el la tuonnɛ.”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
translation_verse: Nebukadnɛza sʋnf daa duoe nɛ hali ka o nindaa tiak nidiba atan' nwa' yɛla. Ka o tis nɔɔr ye ba maalim bugum la ka li zu'oe gaad lin aan si'em la zin'is ayɔpɔi,

english_verse: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
translation_verse: ka tis o soogia banɛ kpi'em la nɔɔr ye ba lɔ Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo lɔs bugumin la.

english_verse: Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?” “Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
translation_verse: Saŋkan la li da pak Na'ab Nebukadnɛza ka o vaae duoe zi'en ka bu'os banɛ san'an o la ye, “Ka' nidiba atan' ka ti lɔɔ lɔs bugumin laa?” Ka ba lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn, Na'aba, ala yim.”

english_verse: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ka gɔsimiya! Man nyɛti nidib anaasi ka ba bɛ bugumin la ken, ka si'el pʋ lɔɔ ba bɛɛ maali ba niŋgbinaa; ka onɛ paas anaasi la nwɛnɛ maliak nɛ.”

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
translation_verse: Nebukadnɛza da ɛnrigi li'el bugum la ka tans nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, “Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo, Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la sankpan'asnama, yim kɛɛn kpɛla na!” Ka Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo da naan bugumin la yina,

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar said: Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own.
translation_verse: Ka Nebukadnɛza yɛl ye, “Wina'am onɛ an Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo Wina'am la yʋ'ʋr paamim zʋn'or! O tʋm o maliak ka o kena faaɛn o yammis! Ba da niŋ o yadda ka zan'as man Na'ab la nɔɔr ka siak ye ba ya'a kpi sɔn'oe ban na pʋ'ʋs bɛɛ wɔ'ɔg man ba'ar bɛɛ teŋgban si'a ka ya'a ka' ba Wina'am la ma'aanɛ.

english_verse: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
translation_verse: Alazug m tisidnɛ nɔɔr ye nidib wʋsa nɛ sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nɛ buudi wʋsa banɛ pian' zɛrig Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo Wina'am la, ba na ki'e o sɔba zɔrisi zɔris ka o yir la lieb dabɔɔg, bɔzugɔ ba'asi'a kae na nyaŋi faaɛn sɔ' anwana.”

english_verse: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis Siadirak nɛ Mesiak nɛ Abɛdnɛgo kpɛuŋ Babilon sʋ'ʋlim la ni.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar sent the following letter to the people of all nations and races on the earth: Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Man Na'ab Nebukadnɛza sɔb gbauŋ kaŋa tisid nidib nɛ sʋ'ʋlimnam nɛ buudi wʋsa banɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa ni yɛt ye, Ya na paam yɛlsʋm bɛdegʋ!

english_verse: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
translation_verse: M mɔr sumalisim ye m yɛli ya tʋʋmnyalima banɛ ka Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la tʋm tisim.

english_verse: His miracles are mighty and marvelous. He will rule forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: O tʋʋmnyalima la zu'onɛ hali, o tʋʋm titada la kpi'emnɛ galis! O sʋ'ʋlim la ka' bɛnnɛ; o kpi'euŋ la bɛ nɛ saŋa linɛ ka' naarɛ.

english_verse: I was enjoying a time of peace and prosperity,
translation_verse: Man, Nebukadnɛza daa bɛnɛ m mɛŋ yin linɛ an na'ayir la mɔri m arezak ka li siakim.

english_verse: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
translation_verse: Ka m tis nɔɔr ye ba la'asim ya'am dim banɛ bɛ Babilon teŋin wʋsa na ka ba yɛlim zaansʋŋ la gbin.

english_verse: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
translation_verse: Tima dim nɛ ya'am dim la daa la'as na ka m yɛli ba zaansʋŋ la, ba daa pʋ nyaŋi yɛlimi li gbinnɛ.

english_verse: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
translation_verse: Ka m yɛl ye, “Belteseaza, fʋn onɛ sʋ'oe banɛ nyɛt yɛla yɛt la wʋsa, man mi' ye wina banɛ an kasi la siig bɛɛ fʋ ni, ka si'el kae tɔi tisif nɛ fʋn na baŋɛ. Tɔ', m zaansʋŋ la nwa', pa'alim mɛ li gbin:

english_verse: In my sleep I saw a very tall tree in the center of the world.
translation_verse: Man digi m gadʋg zugʋ gbisid ka nyɛ si'eli nwa': m nyɛnɛ ka tiig zi'e m tuon, teŋ la teŋsʋkʋ, wa'am hali.

english_verse: It grew stronger and higher, until it reached to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Tiig la daa nɔbignɛ zu'oe ka mɔr paŋ ka li wa'alim keŋ tʋn saŋgbauŋ, ka dunia wʋsa nyɛti li.

english_verse: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
translation_verse: Li vaand la daa vɛnlnɛ hali, ka li wala la zu'oe hali, ka dunia wʋsa na nyaŋi di. Niimis wʋsa daa nyaŋi ya'anɛ li zug, ka tɛɛ ba tɛɛdi li zug, ka bʋnvʋr linɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa dii li wala.

english_verse: “While I was in bed, having this vision, a holy angel came down from heaven
translation_verse: Zaansʋŋ la pʋʋgin man nan dig la, ka m nyɛ maliak ka o naan arezana ni sigid na.

english_verse: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
translation_verse: O daa tans nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, ‘Nwaam tiig la ka pɛsi li wila la; fanrisimi li vaand la ka widigi li wala la. Kɛl ka bʋnkɔnbid la zɔɔ yii li gbinnin, ka niimis la mɛ iank ka bas wila la.

english_verse: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, surrounded by grass and held by chains of iron and bronze. ‘Make sure that this ruler lives like the animals out in the open fields, unprotected from the dew.
translation_verse: Amaa kɛl ka li til la nɛ nya'a la kpɛlim teŋgbauŋʋn la mɔɔd sʋʋgin, ka nɔki kʋnt nɛ kʋntzɛn'ugʋ viligi li. Kɛl ka o gɛndig nɛ bʋnkɔnbidi bɛ mɔɔgin ka mɛligim kanɛ yit agɔl na la lit o zugini madigid o.

english_verse: Give him the mind of a wild animal for seven long years.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka o ninsaal ya'am la tiaki lieb bʋnkɔnbʋg ya'am ka li ti paae yʋma ayɔpɔi saŋa.

english_verse: This punishment is given at the command of the holy angels. It will show to all who live that God Most High controls all kingdoms and chooses for their rulers persons of humble birth.’
translation_verse: Banɛ ka ba tʋm nɛ labaya la da kɛ ka li nie paalʋ, maliaknam la da kɛ ka gban'ar la nie nyain, ka li kɛ ka banɛ vʋe la baŋ ye Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la sʋ'oe ninsaal sʋ'ʋlim ka na tun'e nɔki li tis on gaŋ sɔ' wʋsa, la'an nɛ banɛ ka nidib gɔs ka nɛ'ɛs la.’

english_verse: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
translation_verse: Tɔ': nɛ'ɛŋa an zaansʋŋ kanɛ ka man Na'ab Nebukadnɛza zaansim. Alazug, Belteseaza, yɛlimim zaansʋŋ la gbin, bɔzugɔ ya'am sɔb kae man teŋgbauŋ nwa' nii na nyaŋi yɛlim zaansʋŋ kaŋa gbinnɛ. Amaa fʋn na nyaŋ, bɔzugɔ wina banɛ an kasi la siig bɛɛ fʋ ni.” Daniel yɛl zaansʋŋ la gbin

english_verse: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.
translation_verse: Daniel da anɛ ki' ka pʋ pian'aa, ka li pak o hali. Ka man Na'ab la yɛl o ye, “Belteseaza, da kɛ ka zaansʋŋ la bɛɛ li gbin daami fɔ.” Ka Belteseaza lɛbis ye, “M zugdaana, zaansʋŋ la ya'a aannɛ fʋ dataas la yɛla, ka li gbin pa'an banɛ kisif la yɛla li naan sɔn'ɔn!

english_verse: You saw a tree that grew so big and strong that it reached up to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Tiig kanɛ ka fʋ nyɛ ka li nɔbigi lieb titita'ar ka li wa'alim tʋn saŋgbauŋ, ka dunia wʋsa nyɛti li,

english_verse: Its leaves were beautiful, and it produced enough fruit for all living creatures; animals lived in its shade, and birds nested in its branches.
translation_verse: ka li vaand vɛnl ka li wala zu'oe ka sɔ' wʋsa dit, ka bʋnkɔnbid wʋsa digi li ma'asimin, ka zin'is bɛ ka niis na nyaŋi tɛɛ ba tɛɛdi li wila ni.

english_verse: Your Majesty, that tree is you. Your glorious reputation has reached heaven, and your kingdom covers the earth.
translation_verse: Naa, Na'aba, fʋnɛ an tiig la! Fʋ lieb nintita'ar ka mɔr kpi'euŋ; fʋ kpi'euŋ la nɔbignɛ hali keŋ tʋn saŋgbauŋ, ka fʋ sʋ'ʋlim la yadigi paae dunia wʋsa.

english_verse: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
translation_verse: Naa, Na'aba, fʋ nyɛ sɔ' ka ba tʋm o, ka o an kasi naan arezana ni sigid na ka yɛt ye, ‘Nwaamɛ tiig la san'ami li, amaa basimi gbi'ir linɛ vilig nɛ kʋnt nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug la ka li bɛ mɔɔg la teŋsʋk, ka li nya'a la bɛ teŋin. Kɛl ka mɛligim linɛ yit agɔl la lii o zug; kɛl ka o lieb wʋʋ sian'arin bʋnkɔnbʋgʋ ti paae yʋma ayɔpɔi bɛn.’

english_verse: Your Majesty, God Most High has sent you this message, and it means
translation_verse: Na'aba, zaansʋŋ la gbinnɛ nwa', ka Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la gban'e si'em nwa' zaŋi kennɛ fʋ yɛla, m zugdaan onɛ an Na'aba.

english_verse: that you will be forced to live with the wild animals, far away from humans. You will eat grass like a wild animal and live outdoors for seven years, until you learn that God Most High controls all earthly kingdoms and chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Ba na kadi fʋ yis nidib teŋsʋk ka fʋ keŋ bɛ nɛ bʋnkɔnbid; fʋ na ɔnbid yaama wʋʋ niigi ka mɛligim kanɛ yit agɔl la na madigif. Yʋma ayɔpɔi nya'aŋ ka fʋ na baŋ ye Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la mɔr kpi'euŋ ka sʋ'oe ninsaal sʋ'ʋlim, ka na tun'e nɔki lii tis on bɔɔd sɔ' wʋsa.

english_verse: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
translation_verse: On tis nɔsi'a ye ba basim tigbi'ir la gbin pa'annɛ ye fʋ na lɛn sʋ'oe sʋ'ʋlim la ya'as, fʋ ya'a ti baŋ ye Arezana Wina'am sʋ'oe si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
translation_verse: Alazugɔ, naa, Na'aba, niŋim suguru ka siaki m sa'alʋg la: pin'ilim tʋm linɛ nar ka bas tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nɛ fʋ bugusim la, ka tʋm sʋ'ʋm tis banɛ bɛ mugusʋgin. Ka daasi'erɛɛ linɛ na sʋŋ ka fʋn bɛ ka si'el wʋsa an sʋ'ʋŋa si'em la na keŋ tuon.” Zaansʋŋ la niŋ amɛŋa la yɛla

english_verse: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. I was saying to myself, “Just look at this wonderful capital city that I have built by my own power and for my own glory!”
translation_verse: ka yɛl ye, “Babilon teŋ tita'ar kaŋa, ka' manɛ mɛ' ka li an m na'am zin'ig nɛ m paŋ nɛ m kpi'euŋ ye li tisim yʋ'ʋr girimaa?”

english_verse: But before I could finish speaking, a voice from heaven interrupted: King Nebuchadnezzar, this kingdom is no longer yours.
translation_verse: O nɔɔr da nam pʋ li teŋa, ka kʋkɔr naan agɔlli pian' ye, “Gban'e kanɛ gban'e fʋ yɛla nwa', Na'ab Nebukadnɛza: fʋ na'am kpi'euŋ la yii fʋ san'an.

english_verse: You will be forced to live with the wild animals, away from people. For seven years you will eat grass, as though you were an ox, until you learn that God Most High is in control of all earthly kingdoms and that he is the one who chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Fʋ na yi nidib teŋsʋk ka keŋ bɛ mɔɔgin nɛ bʋnkɔnbid; fʋ na ɔnbid mɔɔd wʋʋ sian'arin niigi nɛ. Yʋma ayɔpɔi ya'a ti gaad ka fʋ yʋ'ʋn na baŋ ye Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la mɔr kpi'euŋʋ sʋ'oe ninsaal sʋ'ʋlim ka nɔkidi tisid on bɔɔd sɔ' wʋsa.”

english_verse: This was no sooner said than done—I was forced to live like a wild animal; I ate grass and was unprotected from the dew. As time went by, my hair grew longer than eagle feathers, and my fingernails looked like the claws of a bird.
translation_verse: Li pʋ yuugɛ ka ban daa yɛl ye si'el na maal Na'ab Nebukadnɛza la sid maal o. Ba da kad o yis nidib sʋʋgin ka o ɔnbid mɔɔd wʋʋ naaf nɛ. Mɛligim da yit agɔlli lit o niŋgbina zug, hali ka o niŋgbiŋ kɔnbilʋg ti yii nwɛnɛ bʋnyua kɔnbid nɛ ka o nu'u-ɛɛns nɛ o nɔb-ɛɛns yii nwɛnɛ viiug nɔb-ɛɛns nɛ.

english_verse: Finally, I prayed to God in heaven, and my mind was healed. Then I said: “I praise and honor God Most High. God lives forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: “Saŋa la bɛnnɛ ti paae la, ka mam Nebukadnɛza ʋki m nindaa gɔs arezana ka m ya'am lɛb na. Ka m zun'e Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la, m da na'as o ka dʋ'ʋs o yʋ'ʋr, on onɛ vʋe saŋa linɛ ka' bɛn la. O kpi'euŋ la bɛ nɛ yʋma linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ; o sʋ'ʋlim la bɛnɛ nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ zʋmaana wʋsa.

english_verse: To him the nations are far less than nothing; God controls the stars in the sky and everyone on this earth. When God does something, we cannot change it or even ask why.”
translation_verse: Nidib banɛ bɛ dunia wʋsa o gɔsid ka ba anɛ zaalim. O tʋmnɛ on bɔɔd si'el nɛ paŋ kanɛ bɛ arezana ni la nɛ nimbanɛ bɛ dunia la. Sɔ' kae na nyaŋi gu'oe o nu'ug ye o da tʋm bɛɛ bu'os o ye, ‘Bɔ ka fʋ maan nɛ'?’

english_verse: At that time my mind was healed, and once again I became the ruler of my glorious kingdom. My advisors and officials returned to me, and I had greater power than ever before.
translation_verse: Saŋa kanɛ ka m ya'am daa lɛb na la, m girima nɛ m kpi'euŋ la da lɛbi m san'an na. Banɛ sa'annim nɛ m ninsʋma la da iee m zin'ig, ka m lɛbi m na'am gbauŋ la zug, hali ka paam kpi'euŋʋ gaad man da mɔr si'em yiiga la.

english_verse: That's why I say: “Praise and honor the King who rules from heaven! Everything he does is honest and fair, and he can shatter the power of those who are proud.”
translation_verse: “Nannanna, man Nebukadnɛza wɔ'ɔg ka zun'e ka na'as Na'ab kanɛ bɛ arezana la, bɔzugɔ linɛ ka o maan wʋsa anɛ sʋ'ʋŋa, ka o suoya wʋsa dɔl sida suor. Ka banɛ ken nɛ nyɛɛsim la o nyaŋidi kɛt ka ba siedi ba mɛŋ.”

english_verse: One evening, King Belshazzar gave a great banquet for a thousand of his highest officials, and he drank wine with them.
translation_verse: Beliseaza onɛ an na'ab la da maal diibi tis o kpɛɛmnam la ban tusir, ka on nɛ ban la'an zin' nuud daam.

english_verse: He got drunk and ordered his servants to bring in the gold and silver cups his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem. Belshazzar wanted the cups, so that he and all his wives and officials could drink from them.
translation_verse: Ban da nuud daam la, o da tʋm ye ba kem vaae sanlima nɛ anzurifa bʋtiis linɛ ka o yaab Na'ab Nebukadnɛza da vaae Pʋ'ʋsim Yin linɛ bɛ Jerusalem teŋin la na ka on nɛ o na'ayikpɛm la nɛ o pu'ab nɛ o pu'abibis la nɔki nu daam.

english_verse: When the gold cups were brought in, everyone at the banquet drank from them and praised their idols made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
translation_verse: Ban da nan nuud daam la, ba da wɔ'ɔgidi ba bada banɛ ka ba kud nɛ sanlima nɛ anzurifa nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug nɛ kʋnt nɛ daad nɛ kuga la.

english_verse: Suddenly a human hand was seen writing on the plaster wall of the palace. The hand was just behind the lampstand, and the king could see it writing.
translation_verse: Li pʋ yuugɛ ka ninsaal nu'ubil nie na ka pin'ili sɔbid dɔkpin zugʋ, kpi'e zin'ikanɛ ka ba nyu'oe fitiri zi'el na'ayin la. Na'ab la gɔsid nu'ubil la ka li sɔbid la,

english_verse: He was so frightened that his face turned pale, his knees started shaking, and his legs became weak.
translation_verse: o nindaa daa tiak nɛ ka dabiem kpɛn' o ka o duma pin'ili nwɛ'ɛd taaba ka o nɔba kpi.

english_verse: The king called in his advisors, who claimed they could talk with the spirits of the dead and understand the meanings found in the stars. He told them, “The man who can read this writing and tell me what it means will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. He will wear robes of royal purple and a gold chain around his neck.”
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tʋm buol tiim dim nɛ banɛ tʋm nyalima nɛ banɛ nyɛt yɛla yɛt, ka bɛ Babilon la ye ba kena; ka ba paae na ka o yɛli ba ye, “Sɔ' ya'a nyaŋi karim sɔb la ka yɛlimi li gbin, m na yɛɛl o na'am fuug ka nɔk sanlima niŋgɔnkɔrigi kɔl o, ka onɛ na an onɛ tia'al atan' gat sɔ' wʋsa m sʋ'ʋlim nwa' ni.”

english_verse: All of King Belshazzar's highest officials came in, but not one of them could read the writing or tell what it meant,
translation_verse: Ya'am dim banɛ an na'ab la nidib la wʋsa da kpɛn' na, amaa ba da pʋ nyaŋi karim sɔb la, bɛɛ yɛl Na'ab la li gbinnɛ.

english_verse: and they were completely puzzled. Now the king was more afraid than ever before, and his face turned white as a ghost.
translation_verse: Dabiem da maligim kpɛn' Na'ab Beliseaza ka o sʋnf san'am hali. O ya'am dim la sʋnf mɛ da san'amya hali.

english_verse: When the queen heard the king and his officials talking, she came in and said: Your Majesty, I hope you live forever! Don't be afraid or look so pale.
translation_verse: Pu'ana'ab la da wʋm Na'ab nɛ o na'ayikpɛm la pian'ad la, ka yii kpɛn' diib zin'igin la ka ye, “Naa, Na'aba, da zɔt dabiem, mɛ da kɛ ka fʋ sʋnf san'am!

english_verse: In your kingdom there is a man who has been given special powers by the holy gods. When your father Nebuchadnezzar was king, this man was known to be as smart, intelligent, and wise as the gods themselves. Your father put him in charge of all who claimed they could talk with the spirits or understand the meanings in the stars or tell about the future.
translation_verse: Dau sɔ' bɛɛ fʋ sʋ'ʋlim nwa' ni ka wina banɛ an kasi la siig bɛɛ o ni. Fʋ saam saŋa la ba da nyɛ ka o anɛ onɛ mɔr mi'ilim nɛ ya'am nɛ baŋir wʋʋ wina la nɛ. Fʋ saam Na'ab Nebukadnɛza da gaŋ o ka o an tiim dim nɛ banɛ tʋm nyalima nɛ banɛ ye ban nyɛt yɛla yɛt la wʋsa kpɛɛm.

english_verse: He also changed the man's name from Daniel to Belteshazzar. Not only is he wise and intelligent, but he can explain dreams and riddles and solve difficult problems. Send for Daniel, and he will tell you what the writing means.
translation_verse: Daniel kaŋa onɛ ka ba lɛm buon ye Belteseaza la, ba da nyɛ ka o ya'am vʋe ka o mɔr baŋir ka gban'ad pian'ad gbin, ka lɛn nyaŋidi pa'an zaansʋŋ gbin, ka bʋkid bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm, ka tun'e wɛligid yɛl kpi'ema. Buolim Daniel na, ka o na yɛli ya sɔb la gbin.”

english_verse: When Daniel was brought in, the king said: So you are Daniel, one of the captives my father brought back from Judah!
translation_verse: Dinzug ba da mɔr Daniel n kɛn Na'ab la san'an na, ka Na'ab la bu'os o ye, “Fʋ anɛ Daniel, nimbanɛ ka Na'ab, onɛ aan m saam la, da gban'e Juda n mɔri kena la yinnee?

english_verse: I was told that the gods have given you special powers and that you are intelligent and very wise.
translation_verse: M wʋm ye wina siig bɛɛ fʋ ni ka fʋ mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr nɛ baŋir ka fʋ ya'am la bɛɛ li kɔn'.

english_verse: Neither my advisors nor the men who talk with the spirits of the dead could read this writing or tell me what it means.
translation_verse: Ba mɔr ya'am dim nɛ tiim dimi kena ye ba karim sɔb nwa' ka yɛlimi li gbin, amaa ba pʋ nyaŋi yɛlimi li gbinnɛ.

english_verse: But I have been told that you understand everything and that you can solve difficult problems. Now then, if you can read this writing and tell me what it means, you will become the third most powerful man in my kingdom. You will wear royal purple robes and have a gold chain around your neck.
translation_verse: M wʋm ye fʋ na nyaŋi yɛl yɛlsu'ada gbin ka sʋŋi maal yɛlmugusa, hali baa li ya'a kpi'em si'em. Tɔ'; fʋ ya'a nyaŋi karim sɔb nwa' ka yɛlimi li gbin, m na yɛɛlif na'am fuug ka kɔllif sanlim niŋgɔnkɔrig, ka kɛ ka fʋ na an onɛ tia'al atan' gat sɔ' wʋsa m sʋ'ʋlim nwa' ni.”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, I will read the writing and tell you what it means. But you may keep your gifts or give them to someone else.
translation_verse: Daniel da lɛbis Na'ab la ye, “Kɛlli fʋ piini la ka li aan fʋ mɛŋ din, ka nɔk yɔɔd la tis fʋn bɔɔd sɔ' wʋsa. La'an nɛ wala, Na'aba, mam na karim sɔb la tisif ka yɛli fʋ li gbin.

english_verse: Sir, the Most High God made your father a great and powerful man and brought him much honor and glory.
translation_verse: “Naa, Na'aba, Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la da tisi fʋ saam Nebukadnɛza dunia paŋ nɛ kpi'euŋ nɛ girima nɛ yʋ'ʋr.

english_verse: God did such great things for him that people of all nations and races shook with fear. Your father had the power of life or death over everyone, and he could honor or ruin anyone he chose.
translation_verse: On da tis o kpi'euŋ si'a la, nidib nɛ sʋ'ʋlim nɛ buudi wʋsa da kiridnɛ ka zɔt o dabiem. Banɛ ka o da gban'e ye o kʋ o kʋʋdnɛ; banɛ ka o gban'e ye o tis yɔlisim o tisidnɛ yɔlisim; banɛ ka o bɔɔd ye o paasi ba kpɛuŋ o paasidnɛ kpɛuŋ; ka banɛ ka o bɔɔd ye o sigis o sigisidnɛ.

english_verse: But when he became proud and stubborn, his glorious kingdom was taken from him.
translation_verse: Amaa o sʋnfʋ da digilim ka nyɛɛsim kɛ ka o lieb tita'al la, ba da sigis o, o na'amin la ka yis o girima la.

english_verse: His mind became like that of an animal, and he was forced to stay away from people and live with wild donkeys. Your father ate grass like an ox, and he slept outside where his body was soaked with dew. He was forced to do this until he learned that the Most High God rules all kingdoms on earth and chooses their kings.
translation_verse: Ba da kad o yis o nidib sʋʋgin, ka nɔk bʋnkɔnbʋg ya'am kpɛn'ɛs o; o da la'am bɛnɛ nɛ wɛogʋn bʋmis ka ɔnbid yaama wʋʋ niigi nɛ; ka mɛligim naamid agɔlli lut o niŋgbina la zug, hali ka o nyaan ti siak ye Wina'am Onɛ Gaad Si'el Wʋsa la sʋ'oe ninsaalib sʋ'ʋlim, ka on bɔɔd sɔ' ka o diisid o na'am.

english_verse: King Belshazzar, you knew all of this, but you still refused to honor the Lord who rules from heaven.
translation_verse: “Amaa Beliseaza, fʋn onɛ aan o biribiŋ la pʋ sie fʋ mɛŋa la'an nɛ fʋn mi' nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa la.

english_verse: Instead, you turned against him and ordered the cups from his temple to be brought here, so that you and your wives and officials could drink wine from them. You praised idols made of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, even though they cannot see or hear or think. You refused to worship the God who gives you breath and controls everything you do.
translation_verse: Fʋ lɛɛ nɔknɛ fʋ zugʋ kpa'anɛ Zugsɔb onɛ sʋ'oe Arezana la. Fʋ kɛ ka ba nɔk o Pʋ'ʋsim Yin bʋtiis la tisif ka fʋn nɛ fʋ kpɛɛmnam nɛ fʋ pu'ab nɛ pu'abibis nɔki li nu daam. Fʋ wɔ'ɔgid wina banɛ ka fʋ kud nɛ anzurifa nɛ sanlima nɛ kʋntzɛn'ug nɛ kʋnt nɛ daad nɛ kuga la, banɛ kʋ nyaŋi nyɛ, bɛɛ wʋm, bɛɛ gban'e pian'ad gbin la. Amaa fʋ pʋ na'as Wina'am kanɛ mɔri fʋ nyɔvʋr nɛ fʋ suoya wʋsa o nu'ugin laa.

english_verse: That's why he sent the hand to write this message on the wall.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka o tʋm nu'ug la ka li kena sɔb labakaŋa.

english_verse: Belshazzar gave a command for Daniel to be made the third most powerful man in his kingdom and to be given a purple robe and a gold chain.
translation_verse: Ka nwɛnɛ Beliseaza pʋn dɛŋi digil nɔsi'a la, ba sid da nɔk na'am fuugʋ yɛɛl Daniel ka nɔk sanlima niŋgɔnkɔrigi kɔl o ka mɔɔl ye onɛ tia'al kpɛɛmnama atan' sʋ'ʋlim la ni.

english_verse: That same night, the king was killed.
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la ba da kʋ Beliseaza onɛ an Babilon dim na'ab la,

english_verse: In order to make sure that his government was run properly, Darius put three other officials in charge of the governors. One of these officials was Daniel.
translation_verse: ka lɛn gaŋ Daniel nɛ kpɛɛmnam ayi' banɛ na pa'an nidib kɔbiga nɛ pisi la na tʋm si'em. Kpɛɛmnam atan' nwa' tʋʋm da anɛ ye ba gɔs ka sɔ' da zam Na'ab la ka o na'am nyɛ pɔ'ɔgirɛ.

english_verse: And he did his work so much better than the other governors and officials that the king decided to let him govern the whole kingdom.
translation_verse: Daniel da tʋm hali gaad o taaba la wʋsa ka li pie Na'ab la pʋʋg, ka o gban'e ye o gaŋ Daniel ka o an kpɛɛm kanɛ na gɔt si'el wʋsa o sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: The other men tried to find something wrong with the way Daniel did his work for the king. But they could not accuse him of anything wrong, because he was honest and faithful and did everything he was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa zug da kɛnɛ ka o taaba la ie suokanɛ ka ba na paam si'eli ma'aa tabil Daniel zaŋi ken sʋ'ʋlim la yɛla, amaa ba da pʋ nyɛ suorɛ. Ba da pʋ nyɛ zam si'a o san'anɛ, bɔzugɔ o da anɛ pʋpiel ka zam bɛɛ gbɛlʋŋ ka' o san'anɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they said to one another, “We will never be able to bring any charge against Daniel, unless it has to do with his religion.”
translation_verse: Ba da maki gʋ'ʋŋ ka yɛl taaba ye, “Ti kʋ nyɛ suosi'a ma'aa ziil Daniel, ka li ya'a ka' li lɛb nɛ o Wina'am la wada babaa.”

english_verse: They all went to the king and said: “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Alazug kpɛɛm bama da la'as taaba gumm keŋ Na'ab la san'anɛ yɛl o ye, “Naa, Na'ab Darius!

english_verse: All of your officials, leaders, advisors, and governors agree that you should make a law forbidding anyone to pray to any god or human except you for the next
translation_verse: Fʋ na'ayikpɛm nɛ teŋ la kpɛɛmnam nɛ banɛ san'an banɛ sʋŋidif ka fʋ gur teŋ la gban'e ka siak ye fʋ tikim nu'ug ye sɔ' da sɔs si'el wina bɛɛ teŋgban si'a bɛɛ ninsaal sɔ' san'an dabisa pistan' pʋʋginɛ, asɛɛ fʋn ma'aa. Ka onɛ ki'is zi'elkaŋa, ba na lɔb o bas gbigima bɔkin.

english_verse: Order this to be written and then sign it, so it cannot be changed, just as no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed.”
translation_verse: Nannanna, Na'aba, sɔm ka tik nu'ug linɛ na kɛ ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi tiaki lii; ka li dɔl Media nɛ Pesia dim wada linɛ ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi tiakɛ.”

english_verse: So King Darius made the law and had it written down.
translation_verse: Na'ab Darius sid da sɔb wada la ka tik nu'ug.

english_verse: Daniel heard about the law, but when he returned home, he went upstairs and prayed in front of the window that faced Jerusalem. In the same way that he had always done, he knelt down in prayer three times a day, giving thanks to God.
translation_verse: Daniel n da wʋm ye Na'ab la sɔbi tik nu'ug ka li yi paalʋ la, o da kul yinne kpɛn' o dɔkanɛ bɛ girimbisa zug la yɔ'ɔg o takoronamɛ kpa' Jerusalem teŋ. Daar wʋsa o da iginid o duma zug nɔɔr atan' pʋ'ʋs Wina'am wʋʋ on daa ɛɛn pʋn maan si'em la.

english_verse: The men who had spoken to the king watched Daniel and saw him praying to his God for help.
translation_verse: Dap bama da la'as taabaa keŋ nyɛ ka Daniel sɔsid Wina'am bɔɔd sʋŋir.

english_verse: The men then told the king, “That Jew named Daniel, who was brought here as a captive, refuses to obey you or the law that you ordered to be written. And he still prays to his god three times a day.”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Naa, Na'aba, Daniel, onɛ yi Juda na ka an yammis la nid yinne la, ki'isi fʋ nɔɔr nɛ fʋ wada linɛ ka fʋ sɔb ka tik nu'ug la. O nan sin ka pʋ'ʋsidnɛ nɔɔr atan' daar yinne.”

english_verse: The king was really upset to hear about this, and for the rest of the day he tried to think how he could save Daniel.
translation_verse: Na'ab la wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la ka li daam o hali, ka o mɔ on na niŋ si'em yis Daniel n bas, ka mɔ hali gʋ'ʋŋ ka winnig ti li.

english_verse: At sunset the men returned and said, “Your Majesty, remember that no written law of the Medes and Persians can be changed, not even by the king.”
translation_verse: Nidib la da la'as taaba gumm keŋ yɛl Na'ab la ye, “Naa, Na'aba, da tam ye Media nɛ Pesia dim wada la kʋ nyaŋi tiakɛ.”

english_verse: So Darius ordered Daniel to be brought out and thrown into a pit of lions. But he said to Daniel, “You have been faithful to your God, and I pray that he will rescue you.”
translation_verse: Alazug Na'ab la da bas nɔɔr, ka ba mɔr Daniel na lɔb o bas gbigima buugin la. Na'ab la da yɛl Daniel ye, “Wina'am kanɛ ka fʋ pʋ'ʋsid o saŋa wʋsa la na faaɛn fʋ bas!”

english_verse: A stone was rolled over the pit, and it was sealed. Then Darius and his officials stamped the seal to show that no one should let Daniel out.
translation_verse: Ba da bilig kugtita'ari kena diinl buug la nɔɔr, ka Na'ab la tik nɛ o mɛŋ baŋ zanbin nɛ o kpɛɛmnam la zanbina mɛn, pa'al ye Daniel n bɛ yɛlsi'a pʋʋgin la kʋ maligin tiakɛ.

english_verse: All night long the king could not sleep. He did not eat anything, and he would not let anyone come in to entertain him.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la lɛbi kul o yin ka pʋ di bɛɛ kɛ ka ba nwɛ' kɔna wʋʋ ban ɛɛnti niŋid si'em la. O da pʋ nyaŋi gbisɛ.

english_verse: At daybreak the king got up and ran to the pit.
translation_verse: Bɛogʋ da nie la, Na'ab la da isig asuba zɔ tɔ'ɔtɔ keŋ gbigima buugin la.

english_verse: He was anxious and shouted, “Daniel, you were faithful and served your God. Was he able to save you from the lions?”
translation_verse: On da li'el la, o da tansi buol Daniel nɛ kʋkɔtita'ar ye, “Daniel, Wina'am Onɛ Vʋe la tʋmtʋmma, fʋ Wina'am kanɛ ka fʋ pʋ'ʋsid saŋa wʋsa la nyaŋi faaɛn fʋ yis gbigima la nii?”

english_verse: Daniel answered, “Your Majesty, I hope you live forever!
translation_verse: Ka Daniel lɛbis ye, “Naa, Na'aba!

english_verse: My God knew that I was innocent, and he sent an angel to keep the lions from eating me. Your Majesty, I have never done anything to hurt you.”
translation_verse: M Wina'am la tʋmnɛ o maliak ka o kena kpar gbigima la nɔya. Ba pʋ maalim si'ela, bɔzugɔ o nyɛ ka m pʋ mɔr taal si'aa. M mɛ nan zi' tʋm si'eli gɛsigi fɔ, naa Na'aba.”

english_verse: The king was relieved to hear Daniel's voice, and he gave orders for him to be taken out of the pit. Daniel's faith in his God had kept him from being harmed.
translation_verse: Na'ab la sʋnf da ma'ae hali ka o tans ye ba yisim Daniel gbigima la san'an na tɔ'ɔtɔ. Ka ban da yis Daniel na la, si'el-si'el da pʋ ɛnbig oo bɔzugɔ o da niŋ o Wina'am yadda.

english_verse: And the king ordered the men who had brought charges against Daniel to be thrown into the pit, together with their wives and children. But before they even reached the bottom, the lions ripped them to pieces.
translation_verse: Na'ab la da tis nɔɔr ye ba gban'am banɛ faa tis Daniel zaalim-zaalim la na lɔb gbigima buugin la, ban nɛ ba biis nɛ ba pu'ab wʋsa. Ban da lɔbi ba la, ba da nam pʋ paae teŋa ka gbigima la pʋn gban'e ba ɔnb ka kɔɔ ba kɔnba bugusi bugus.

english_verse: King Darius then sent this message to all people of every nation and race in the world: “Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Na'ab Darius da sɔbi tis nidib wʋsa nɛ sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nɛ buudi wʋsa teŋ la wʋsa zug ye; “Wina'am na tisi ya yɛlsʋm bɛdegʋ!

english_verse: I command everyone in my kingdom to worship and honor the God of Daniel. He is the living God, the one who lives forever. His power and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: M sɔbid gbauŋ kaŋa tisid sɔ' wʋsa: tisimi Daniel Wina'am la girima ka na'as o. Bɔzugɔ o anɛ Wina'am Kanɛ Vʋe ka bɛ saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ. O sʋ'ʋlim ka' san'auŋʋ, o paŋ la ka' naarɛ.

english_verse: He rescues people and sets them free by working great miracles. Daniel's God has rescued him from the power of the lions.”
translation_verse: Onɛ nyaŋidi faand ka tisid yɔlisim; onɛ maan nyalima nɛ kilima arezana nɛ dunia wʋsa ni. Onɛ mɛ faaɛn Daniel n yis gbigima la ni.”

english_verse: All went well for Daniel while Darius was king, and even when Cyrus the Persian ruled.
translation_verse: Alazug Daniel da lieb nintita'ar Na'ab Darius nɛ Na'ab Sarus onɛ da an Pesia teŋ nid la na'am saŋa.

english_verse: Daniel wrote: In the first year of King Belshazzar of Babylonia, I had some dreams and visions while I was asleep one night, and I wrote them down. The four winds were stirring up the mighty sea,
translation_verse: O da yɛl ye, “Zaansʋŋ la pʋʋgin ka m nyɛ sisi'etita'ar ka li da'adi yit lʋga anaasi dammid atɛuk ku'om la.

english_verse: when suddenly four powerful beasts came out of the sea. Each beast was different.
translation_verse: Ka bʋnkɔnbkpi'ema anaasi banɛ pʋ nwɛn taaba da naan atɛuk la pʋʋginɛ dʋ na.

english_verse: The first was like a lion with the wings of an eagle. As I watched, its wings were pulled off. Then it was lifted to an upright position and made to stand on two feet, just like a human, and it was given a human mind.
translation_verse: “Yiiga sɔb la da nwɛnɛ gbigim, ka mɔr kpʋkpama ka li nwɛnɛ abaar kpʋkpama nɛ. Ka m gɔsid o hali ka o kpʋkpama la ti vuoɛn ka ba ʋk o teŋin la duoe zi'el o nɔba zug wʋʋ ninsaal nɛ, ka nɔk ninsaal ya'am tis o.

english_verse: The second beast looked like a bear standing on its hind legs. It held three ribs in its teeth, and it was told, “Attack! Eat all the flesh you want.”
translation_verse: “M da nyɛ bʋnkɔnbkanɛ paas ayi' la ka o nwɛnɛ bʋnyua, ka zi'e nɔbyiuŋ, ka ga' sapiris atan' o nyina ni, ka ba yɛl o ye, ‘Duom ka ɔnb ni'im linɛ aan fʋ din la tig.’

english_verse: The third beast was like a leopard—except that it had four wings and four heads. It was given authority to rule.
translation_verse: “Lin nya'aŋ ka m lɛn gɔsi nyɛ yinne ya'as ka on nwɛnɛ wɛbaa nɛ. Ka kpʋkpama anaasi bɛɛ o nya'aŋ nwɛnɛ niiŋ kpʋkpama. Bʋnkɔnbkaŋa daa mɔri zut anaasi, ka ba tis o kpi'euŋ ye o sʋ'ʋg nidib.

english_verse: The fourth beast was stronger and more terrifying than the others. Its huge teeth were made of iron, and what it didn't grind with its teeth, it smashed with its feet. It was different from the others, and it had horns on its head—ten of them.
translation_verse: “Lin nya'aŋ la ka yʋ'ʋŋ sɔb ka m zaansim nyɛ bʋnkɔnbʋg kanɛ paas anaasi la ka o an bʋnzɔtir ka mɔr dabiem ka mɛ mɔr paŋ hali. O nyina la da anɛ bɛda-bɛda ka an kʋnt; ka o mɔri ɔnbid ka san'amid o dataas, ka linɛ wʋsa kpɛlim ka pʋ san'am la ka o nɔɔd nɛ o nɔba. On da bɛ nɛ o kɔn' nɛ bʋnkɔnbid banɛ ka m pʋn dɛŋi nyɛ la wʋsa, ka mɔr iila piiga.

english_verse: Just as I was thinking about these horns, a smaller horn appeared, and three of the other horns were pulled up by the roots to make room for it. This horn had the eyes of a human and a mouth that spoke with great arrogance. Judgment Daniel wrote:
translation_verse: Man da nan tɛn'ɛsid iila la yɛla la, ka iil yinne lɛm busi yi bama la teŋsʋk na, ka nan an bʋmbil. Ka yiiga iila atan' vɔn'. Onɛ yuolim yina la daa mɔri nini ka li nwɛnɛ ninsaal nini nɛ, ka mɔr nɔɔri pian'adi dʋ'ʋsid o mɛŋ.

english_verse: Thrones were set up while I was watching, and the Eternal God took his place. His clothing and his hair were white as snow. His throne was a blazing fire with fiery wheels,
translation_verse: “Man daa gɔsid la, “ka nyɛ ka ba yis na'am gbana na digil, ka onɛ da pʋn bɛ yʋʋmpʋkʋda saŋa la lɛb na zin'in o na'am gbauŋ zug. O fuug da pɛlignɛ wʋʋ sakuga nɛ, ka o zug zuobid pɛlig wʋʋ gungum. O na'am gbauŋ la da ian'adnɛ pil-pil wʋʋ bugum, ka bugum diti li lɛuŋʋn la yit na.

english_verse: and flames were dashing out from all around him. Countless thousands were standing there to serve him. The time of judgment began, and the books were opened.
translation_verse: Bugum da naanɛ o tuonnɛ, pʋbigidi yit na wʋʋ kɔldaug ku'om nɛ. Maliaknam tusa-tusa da bɛɛ o san'anɛ tʋmmi tisid o ka tusa piiga zin'is tusa piiga zi'e o tuon. Ka ba zin' sariakadib zin'igin la, ka lak gbana la.

english_verse: I watched closely to see what would happen to this smaller horn because of the arrogant things it was saying. Then before my very eyes, the fourth beast was killed and its body destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: “Ka m kpɛn gɔsid iil la pian'adi dʋ'ʋsid o mɛŋ si'em la. M da gɔsid o ala ka ba ti kʋ bʋnkɔnbʋg la ka san'am o niŋgbiŋ la ka lɔb o bas bugumin.

english_verse: The other three beasts had their authority taken from them, but they were allowed to live a while longer.
translation_verse: Bʋnkɔnbbama la, ba daa faaɛn ba kpi'euŋ la, amaa ka siak ye ba kpɛn vʋe saŋa bi'ela.

english_verse: As I continued to watch the vision that night, I saw what looked like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven, and he was presented to the Eternal God.
translation_verse: “Ka m nyɛ sɔ' m zaansʋŋ la pʋʋgin yʋ'ʋŋ kan la, ka o zi'e m tuonnɛ nwɛnɛ ninsaal biig la, naan arezana kenna nɛ saŋgbana. O da li'el onɛ da pʋn bɛ yʋʋmpʋkʋda saŋa la ka ba biel oo kɛɛn o san'an na.

english_verse: He was crowned king and given power and glory, so that all people of every nation and race would serve him. He will rule forever, and his kingdom is eternal, never to be destroyed. The Meaning of Daniel's Vision
