english_verse: I saw a vision of the Lord standing by the temple altar, and he said, “Shake the columns until the tops fall loose, and the doorposts crumble. Then make the pieces fall on the people below. I will take a sword and kill anyone who escapes.
translation_verse: Ka m daa nyɛ Zugsɔb la ka o zi'e bimbim la baba, ka yɛl ye, “Nwɛ'ɛm bʋmbuos la zug nɛ paŋ, ka li kɛ ka za'anɔɔr la ɛɛnbir dam. Kɛl ka li lu nidib la wʋsa zug; ka banɛ kpɛlim la, m na kɛ ka ba kpi zaba ni. Ba wʋsa na kpi. Ba sɔ'ɔsɔ kʋ yii.

english_verse: “If they dig deep into the earth or climb to the sky, I'll reach out and get them.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ ban na tuu kpɛn' teŋ teŋir la, m nu'ug na paae ba ani yisi ba na. La'an nɛ ban na dʋʋ bɛ saŋgbana ni la, m na sigisi ba na.

english_verse: If they escape to the peaks of Mount Carmel, I'll search and find them. And if they hide from me at the bottom of the ocean, I'll command a sea monster to bite them.
translation_verse: Ba ya'a dʋ Kaamel zuor zugʋ su'a, m na kadi ba sigis teŋin na gban'e ba. Ba ya'a su'a atɛuk teŋir, m na kɛ ka wa'atita'ar kanɛ bɛɛ ani la dumi ba.

english_verse: I'll send a sword to kill them, wherever their enemies drag them off as captives. I'm determined to hurt them, not to help them.” His Name Is the Lord
translation_verse: La'an nɛ dataasi na gban'e ba keŋ teŋ zʋŋ la, hali anina ka m na kɛ ka ba kʋʋ ba zaba ni M na laki m nini kpa' gɔsidi ba ka li na anɛ gɔs bɛ'ɛd ka ka' gɔs sʋŋɔ.

english_verse: When the Lord God All-Powerful touches the earth, it melts, and its people mourn. God makes the earth rise and then fall, just like the Nile River.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la ya'a nɔ teŋ la zin'isi'a li mɛdigidnɛ, ka banɛ bɛɛ ani la wʋsa kaasid kʋʋr, Teŋ la mɛŋ na duosid wʋʋ Nail kɔldaug ku'om; ka lɛn lɛbid teŋin wʋʋ Egipt kɔldaug nɛ.

english_verse: He built his palace in the heavens and let its foundations rest on the earth. He scoops up the ocean and empties it on the earth. His name is the Lord. The Lord Is God
translation_verse: O mɛɛ o na'am yir saŋgbana ni ka o yir la ɛɛnbir bɛ teŋgbauŋ zug, on kanɛ buon atɛuk ku'om la la'asid ka nɔkidi li dɔn'ɔsid teŋgbauŋ la, o yʋ'ʋri buon Zugsɔb.

english_verse: Israel, I am the Lord God, and the Ethiopians are no less important to me than you are. I brought you out of Egypt, but I also brought the Philistines from Crete and the Arameans from Kir.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb onɛ an paŋ tita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, ‘Yanam Israel dim nɛ Kus dim la, ya ka'anɛ yinne man san'anɛɛ? Ka' manɛ mɔr Israel dim la yi Egipt naa? Ka' manɛ yis Filistia dim Kafitor teŋin na, ka mɛ yis Aram dim la Kir teŋinɛɛ?

english_verse: My eyes have seen what a sinful nation you are, and I'll wipe you out. But I will leave a few of Jacob's descendants. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: Sida, mam Zugsɔb Onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la nini laknɛ gɔsid sʋ'ʋlim kanɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim teŋ la. M na san'ami ba wʋsa teŋgbauŋ nwa' zug. La'an nɛ wala m kʋ san'am Jakob yidim la nyainnɛ’” Zugsɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: At my command, all of you will be sifted like grain. Israelites who remain faithful will be scattered among the nations. And the others will be trapped like trash in a sifter.
translation_verse: M na tis nɔɔr, ka na yɛlig Israel dim tɛɛns la wʋsa sʋʋgin wʋʋ ki ka ba yɛligid si'em la, ka kugir baa yinne kʋ lu teŋa.

english_verse: Some of you are evil, and you deny that you will ever get caught. But you will be killed. The Lord's Promise to Israel
translation_verse: Banɛ an tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dimi bɛɛ m nidib sʋʋgin la wʋsa na kpi zaba ni, nɛ banɛ wʋsa yɛt ye, “Tɔɔg kʋ paae ti la.” Israel na lɛn nyɛ zi'esim ya'as

english_verse: In the future, I will rebuild David's fallen kingdom. I will build it from its ruins and set it up again, just as it used to be.
translation_verse: “Li saŋa ya'a ti paae m na duoe David Fuug Sʋgʋr linɛ li teŋin la. M na lɛbisi maal zin'ibanɛ san'am la, ka mɛɛ li zi'el, ka li an wʋʋ lin da an si'em la.

english_verse: Then you will capture Edom and the other nations that are mine. I, the Lord, have spoken, and my words will come true.
translation_verse: Ala ka ba na sʋ'oe Edom nimbanɛ kpɛlim la, nɛ tɛɛns banɛ wʋsa ka ba da pʋd o ba nɛ m yʋ'ʋr la.” Zugsɔb onɛ yɛl nɛ'ɛŋa ka na tʋmmi li la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: You will have such a harvest that you won't be able to bring in all of your wheat before plowing time. You will have grapes left over from season to season; your fruitful vineyards will cover the mountains.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔb onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye ‘Daakan la ya'a ti paae, onɛ nwɛ'ɛd vugus la na gaad onɛ bʋn la ka onɛ bʋ'ʋd ki la mɛ na gaad onɛ bʋn la. Damalisiŋ na naan zuoya la ni tu'asidi sigid kʋkʋna la wʋsa zug.

english_verse: I'll make Israel prosper again. You will rebuild your towns and live in them. You will drink wine from your own vineyards and eat the fruit you grow.
translation_verse: M na mɔr zɔɔma la lɛbis na; ba na lɛbisi mɛ' tempʋbanɛ an dabɔɔd la zin'in. Ba na sɛ vain tiis pɔɔdin ka pɔn' tiis la wala ka nuu li daam; ba na maal lɔmbɔn'ɔd ka dii li nyɔɔd.

english_verse: I'll plant your roots deep in the land I have given you, and you won't ever be uprooted again. I, the Lord God, have spoken!
translation_verse: M na zin'il Israel dimi ba mɛŋ teŋin ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn duoe ba teŋ kanɛ ka m tisi ba la nii.’ Ya Zugsɔb Wina'am la pian' li.”

english_verse: The Lord God gave Obadiah a message about Edom, and this is what we heard: “I, the Lord, have sent a messenger with orders for the nations to attack Edom.”
translation_verse: Obadia n da zaansim ka Zugsɔb onɛ an paŋ tita'ar sɔb la nie pa'al o Edom dim yɛla si'em nwa'. Ti wʋm labaar ka li yi Zugsɔb la san'an na yɛt ye o tʋm o tʋmtʋm buudi wʋsa ni, ye ba yɛl ye, “Duomi ka ti ti'ebi keŋ zab nɛ Edom dim la!

english_verse: The Lord said to Edom: I will make you the weakest and most despised nation.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, m na kɛ ka fʋ an tembil tɛɛns la wʋsa ni ka ba na ziemif hali.

english_verse: You live in a mountain fortress, because your pride makes you feel safe from attack, but you are mistaken.
translation_verse: Fʋn kanɛ bɛ tampiins linɛ bɛ zuoya zug, ka bɛ kukuos zug agɔla la, nyɛɛsim kanɛ ka fʋ mɔri fʋ sʋnfʋn la ma'adif. Fʋ nwɛ'ɛdi fʋ nyɔ'ɔg ye, ‘Anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi sigisim teŋinɛ?’

english_verse: I will still bring you down, even if you fly higher than an eagle or nest among the stars. I, the Lord, have spoken!
translation_verse: La'an nɛ fʋn ianki dʋ agɔl wʋʋ silʋg ka tɛɛdi fʋ tɛog nwadbibis la teŋsʋk la, ani ka m na vɛ'ɛgi fʋ sigis na.” Zugsɔb la pian'ʋkʋ la.

english_verse: If thieves break in at night, they steal only what they want. And people who harvest grapes always leave some unpicked. But, Edom, you are doomed!
translation_verse: “Na'ayiis ya'a kɛɛn ya yin na bɛɛ faandib ya'a libigi ya yʋ'ʋŋ, ba kʋ zuu ya la'ad la wʋsaa, asɛɛ ban ieed si'el la ma'aa. Bunnib la ya'a bun pɔɔdinɛ, ba kʋ bas sieba ka banɛ wi'isid la mɛ paam?

english_verse: Your allies can't be trusted. They will force you out of your own country. And your best friends will trick and trap you, even before you know it.
translation_verse: Banɛ sʋŋidif la na kadi fʋ ta'as teŋ titɔndigin; nimbanɛ aan fʋ zuanam la na pan'asif ka bɛndi nyaŋif. Banɛ diti fʋ diib la bɛnd baansi fʋ tuon amaa ka fʋ kʋ baŋɛ.”

english_verse: Edom, when this happens, I, the Lord, will destroy all your marvelous wisdom.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Daakan la bi'esʋg kae, m na kʋ Edom nimbanɛ mɔr ya'am nɛ banɛ an baŋir dim Esau zuoya ni la.

english_verse: Warriors from the city of Teman will be terrified, and you descendants of Esau will be wiped out. The Lord Condemns Edom's Cruelty
translation_verse: Yanam Teman dima, dabiem na kpɛn' ya zabzabidib la, ka onɛ wʋsa bɛ Esau zuoya la ni ba na kɔdig o.

english_verse: You were cruel to your relatives, the descendants of Jacob. Now you will be destroyed, disgraced forever.
translation_verse: Yanamɛ da kisi ya pitʋ Jakob la zug, ya na di nyan ka nyɛ san'auŋ saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ.

english_verse: You stood there and watched as foreigners entered Jerusalem and took what they wanted. In fact, you were no better than those foreigners.
translation_verse: Daakanɛ ka saam da vaae o la'ad wʋsa la ya da zi'enɛ gɔsid. Hali ka teŋ zʋŋ dim la kpɛn' o tempʋʋgin la ka maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm Jerusalem yɛla, ya da anɛ wʋʋ ba bi'emnam la yinne.

english_verse: Why did you celebrate when such a dreadful disaster struck your relatives? Why were you so pleased when everyone in Judah was suffering?
translation_verse: Li da pʋ dɔl suor ye ya sʋnf malisi ya ba'abiig la'ad san'auŋ la saŋa, bɛɛ maan sumalisim Juda san'auŋ dabisir la daarɛ, bɛɛ nwɛ'ɛd nyɔ'ɔg daakanɛ ka ba paam yɛla laa.

english_verse: In their time of torment, you ambushed refugees and handed them over to their attackers. The Lord Will Judge the Nations
translation_verse: Li mɛ pʋ dɔl suor ye ya zi'e suokita ni kʋʋdi ba nimbanɛ zɔti yit la, bɛɛ ya lɛm gban'ad banɛ kpɛlim vʋe la tisidi ba dataas, ba san'auŋ dabisir la daarɛ.

english_verse: The day is coming when I, the Lord, will judge the nations. And, Edom, you will pay in full for what you have done.
translation_verse: Daakanɛ ka Zugsɔb na kad buudi wʋsa saria la li'el ya. Yanam Edom dimi maal Israel dim si'em la ya bɛ'ɛd kanɛ ka ya maal la, li lɛbi ya mɛŋ zugin.

english_verse: I forced the people of Judah to drink the wine of my anger on my sacred mountain. Soon the neighboring nations must drink their fill— then vanish without a trace. Victory for Israel
translation_verse: Nwɛnɛ yanam banɛ aan m nidib la da nu tʋbtɛɛgir daam m zuokanɛ an kasi la zug la, ala mɛn ka tɛɛns la wʋsa na nuudi li saŋa wʋsa, ba na nu hali, ka lɛm maligin nuu ti bʋg ka bɔdig nwɛnɛ ba nan zi' bɛ dunia kaŋa nwa' ni nɛ.

english_verse: The Lord's people who escape will go to Mount Zion, and it will be holy. Then Jacob's descendants will capture the land of those who took their land.
translation_verse: Amaa Zion Zuor na an zin'ikanɛ ka onɛ wʋsa bɛ na paam faangir: li na an zin'ikanɛ an kasi. Ka Jakob yidim wʋsa na lɛb na dii ba faar.

english_verse: The people of Israel who live in the Southern Desert will take the land of Edom. Those who live in the hills will capture Philistia, Ephraim, and Samaria. And the tribe of Benjamin will conquer Gilead.
translation_verse: M nimbanɛ bɛ Negef la na di'e Edom zuoya la wʋsa bɛɛ anina. Ka banɛ bɛ Sefela teŋgbauŋʋn la mɛ na sʋ'oe Filistia teŋ la. Ba na sʋ'ʋgi li mɔri paae Efiram sʋ'ʋlim nɛ Samaria teŋgbauŋ la wʋsa, ka Benjamin yaas la mɛ na sʋ'oe Gilead sʋ'ʋlim la.

english_verse: Those who return from captivity will control Phoenicia as far as Zarephath. Captives from Jerusalem who were taken to Sepharad will capture the towns of the Southern Desert.
translation_verse: Ka Israel dim banɛ nam bɛ Keenan teŋin la na kul na ka sʋ'ʋg teŋ la wʋsa mɔri keŋ paae Zarefat; ka banɛ mɛ yi Jerusalem teŋin bɛɛ Sefarad teŋgbauŋʋn la na lɛb na sʋ'oe Negef teŋkpɛmis la wʋsa.

english_verse: Those the Lord has saved will live on Mount Zion and rule over Edom. Then the kingdom will belong to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ka banɛ nyɛ faangir la na dʋ Zion Zuor zuginɛ sʋ'oe Edom zuoya sʋ'ʋlim la. Ka Zugsɔb yʋ'ʋn na an Na'ab ka sʋ'oe na'am sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa.

english_verse: One day the Lord told Jonah, the son of Amittai,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la pian'ʋk da kɛn Jona onɛ an Amitai biig la san'an na ye,

english_verse: to go to the great city of Nineveh and say to the people, “The Lord has seen your terrible sins. You are doomed!”
translation_verse: “Kem Ninive linɛ an teŋ tita'ar la nii mɔɔli tisi ba ye, ‘Man nyɛti ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la wʋsa.’”

english_verse: Instead, Jonah ran from the Lord. He went to the seaport of Joppa and found a ship that was going to Spain. So he paid his fare, then got on the ship and sailed away to escape.
translation_verse: Amaa Jona da duoe zɔti ken Tarsis teŋin ye o zɔɔ yi ka bas Zugsɔb la. O da zɔɔ sig Joppa tempʋʋgin linɛ bɛ Atɛuk nɔɔrin la ka nyɛ anrʋŋ linɛ wa'ae Tarsis. Ka o yɔ ka kpɛn' ye o dɔlli ba keŋ Tarsis teŋin, dinɛ na kɛ ka o zɔɔ yi ka bas Zugsɔb la.

english_verse: But the Lord made a strong wind blow, and such a bad storm came up that the ship was about to be broken to pieces.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb kɛ ka sisi'etita'ar kɛɛn Atɛukʋn la na. Sisi'em la da mɔri paŋ hali da'adi Atɛuk ku'om la ka anrʋŋ la bɔɔd ye li kɔ'.

english_verse: The sailors were frightened, and they all started praying to their gods. They even threw the ship's cargo overboard to make the ship lighter. All this time, Jonah was down below deck, sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ka dabiem kpɛn' nimbanɛ tʋm anrʋŋ tʋʋma la ka sɔ' wʋsa nwɛ'ɛd kuŋi buon o win. Ka ba vaae anrʋŋ la la'adi lɔbi bas Atɛuk la pʋʋgin ye li faki tisi ba. Amaa ka Jona on gaadi sig anrʋŋ la teŋiri digi gbisid.

english_verse: The ship's captain went to him and said, “How can you sleep at a time like this? Get up and pray to your God! Maybe he will have pity on us and keep us from drowning.”
translation_verse: Ala ka anrʋŋ la kpɛɛm keŋ o san'anɛ bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋn digi gbisida? Duom ka buoli fʋ win, ka daasi'erɛ o na zɔɔ ti nimbaanlig ka faaɛn ti bas.”

english_verse: Finally, the sailors got together and said, “Let's ask our gods to show us who caused all this trouble.” It turned out to be Jonah.
translation_verse: Ka banɛ gɔsid anrʋŋ la yɛl taaba ye, “Kɛlli ka ti maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm baŋ onɛ zug ka yɛltɔɔg kaŋa paadi ti!” Ka ba maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm ka li gban'e Jona.

english_verse: They started asking him, “Are you the one who brought all this trouble on us? What business are you in? Where do you come from? What is your country? Who are your people?”
translation_verse: Ka ba bu'os o ye, “Yɛlimi ti, anɔ'ɔn zug ka yɛlbama nwa' paadi ti? Fʋ tʋʋma an bɔ? Fʋ yi yaanɛ? Fʋ teŋ yʋ'ʋrɛ? Fʋ an buudkanɛ nida?”

english_verse: Jonah answered, “I'm a Hebrew, and I worship the Lord God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbisi ba ye, “M anɛ Hibiru nid, ka pʋ'ʋsid Zugsɔb onɛ an Arezana Wina'am ka maal Atɛuk nɛ teŋgbauŋ la.”

english_verse: When the sailors heard this, they were frightened, because Jonah had already told them he was running from the Lord. Then they said, “Do you know what you have done?”
translation_verse: Ka nɛ'ɛŋa kpɛn'ɛs nidib la dabiem pamm ka ba bu'os ye, “Bɔɔ nwa' ka fʋ niŋɛ?”

english_verse: The storm kept getting worse, until finally the sailors asked him, “What should we do with you to make the sea calm down?”
translation_verse: Ka Atɛuk la zan'as ka gudigid, ka ba bu'os o ye, “Ti na niŋif wala ka Atɛuk nwa' ma'ae tisi ti?”

english_verse: Jonah told them, “Throw me into the sea, and it will calm down. I'm the cause of this terrible storm.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbisi ba ye, “Ʋkiminimɛ lɔbi bas Atɛuk la pʋʋgin ka li na ma'ae tisi ya. M mi' ye li anɛ m taal, linɛ kɛ ka pɛbistita'ar nwa' da'ad.”

english_verse: The sailors tried their best to row to the shore. But they could not do it, and the storm kept getting worse every minute.
translation_verse: Amaa nidib la da kpɛ'ɛŋidi ba mɛŋ ye ba mɔr anrʋŋ la lɛb gʋʋr ka pʋ nyaŋɛ, bɔzugɔ Atɛuk la maligim zan'as nɛ ka mɔɔd nɛ paŋ.

english_verse: So they prayed to the Lord, “Please don't let us drown for taking this man's life. Don't hold us guilty for killing an innocent man. All of this happened because you wanted it to.”
translation_verse: Ka ba nwɛ' kuŋi tis Zugsɔb la ye, “Zugsɔba, da kɛ ka ti kpi dau nwa' nyɔvʋr yɛlaa! Dau nwa' ya'a ka' taalɛ, da kɛ ka o ziim yɛla dɔlli tii, ka li anɛ fʋn Zugsɔb bɔɔdim ye li aan ala.”

english_verse: Then they threw Jonah overboard, and the sea calmed down.
translation_verse: Ka ba ʋk Jona lɔb o Atɛuk la pʋʋgin ka Atɛuk la nyaan lɛbi ma'ae baanlimm.

english_verse: The sailors were so terrified that they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made all kinds of promises.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa da kɛ ka dabiem kpɛn' nidib la, Zugsɔb la yɛla. Ka ba maal maannɛ tis Zugsɔb la, ka pɔɔ zi'el o.

english_verse: The Lord sent a big fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was inside the fish for three days and three nights.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la da tʋm ziiŋ tita'ar na ka o vɔl Jona. Daba atan', yʋ'ʋŋ nɛ nintaŋ wʋsa, ka o bɛ ziiŋ la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: From inside the fish, Jonah prayed to the Lord his God:
translation_verse: Ka Jona naam ziiŋ la pʋʋgin ka sɔs Zugsɔb Wina'am ye,

english_verse: When I was in trouble, Lord, I prayed to you, and you listened to me. From deep in the world of the dead, I begged for your help, and you answered my prayer.
translation_verse: “M yɛlpakir pʋʋgin ka m kaasi buol Zugsɔb la ka o wʋmi m sɔsʋg. Yaʋg pʋʋgin ka m buol ye fʋ sʋŋim, ka fʋ wʋmi m kaasig.

english_verse: You threw me down to the bottom of the sea. The water was churning all around; I was completely covered by your mighty waves.
translation_verse: Fʋ nɔkimi lɔb Atɛuk ku'ozuluŋin pʋʋgin, zin'ikan ka ku'onwiis la giligim ka ku'opila la pilim.

english_verse: I thought I was swept away from your sight, never again to see your holy temple.
translation_verse: Ka m tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ kadim nɛ yisi fʋ san'an, amaa m na lɛn gɔsi kpa' fʋ Pʋ'ʋsim Yir kanɛ an kasi la.

english_verse: I was almost drowned by the swirling waters that surrounded me. Seaweed had wrapped around my head.
translation_verse: Ku'om la paae m niŋgɔɔnr bɛn, ka m sim ku'ozuluŋin ka kɔlgʋʋma vili m zug.

english_verse: I had sunk down deep below the mountains beneath the sea. I knew that forever, I would be a prisoner there. But, you, Lord God, rescued me from that pit.
translation_verse: M sim nɛ sigi paae zuoya teŋir. Ka teŋ la yɔɔ m, saŋa linɛ ka' bɛnnɛ, Amaa, m Zugsɔb Wina'am, Fʋ yisi m nyɔvʋr bʋmbɔkin la na.

english_verse: When my life was slipping away, I remembered you— and in your holy temple you heard my prayer.
translation_verse: Zugsɔba, din daa kpɛlim bi'ela ka m kpi la, M daa tiɛn fʋ yɛla; Ka m winsɔsʋg dʋ fʋ san'an na; Ti paae fʋ Yikanɛ an Kasi pʋʋgin.

english_verse: All who worship worthless idols turn from the God who offers them mercy.
translation_verse: Banɛ dɔl bada dinɛ ka' nyɔɔd la kɔ'ɔŋ yɛlsʋm linɛ aan ba din la.

english_verse: But with shouts of praise, I will offer a sacrifice to you, my Lord. I will keep my promise, because you are the one with power to save.
translation_verse: Amaa mam na yʋ'ʋm bareka pʋ'ʋsʋg yʋʋma, Ka maal maannɛ tisif. Mam pɔ nɔɔri zi'el si'em la, Ka sid na maali li. Faangir yit nɛ Zugsɔb la san'an na.”

english_verse: The Lord commanded the fish to vomit up Jonah on the shore. And it did.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la kɛ ka ziiŋ la tin Jona basi Atɛuk la gbɛog.

english_verse: Once again the Lord told Jonah
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la pian'ʋk da kɛn Jona san'an na ya'as

english_verse: to go to that great city of Nineveh and preach his message of doom.
translation_verse: ye, “Kem Ninive teŋ tita'ar la nii mɔɔl labakan ka m tisif la.”

english_verse: Jonah obeyed the Lord and went to Nineveh. The city was so big that it took three days just to walk through it.
translation_verse: Jona yʋ'ʋn da siak Zugsɔb la nɔɔr ka keŋ Ninive. Ninive da anɛ teŋ tita'ar, ka li na nɔk wʋʋ daba atan' ka nid na keŋ paae li bɛn.

english_verse: After walking for a day, Jonah warned the people, “Forty days from now, Nineveh will be destroyed!”
translation_verse: Dabismum ka Jona zaŋi tu'as labaar la ye, “Li kpɛlim dabpisnaasi ma'aa ka Ninive na san'am.”

english_verse: They believed God's message and set a time when they would go without eating to show their sorrow. Then everyone in the city, no matter who they were, dressed in sackcloth.
translation_verse: Ninive dim la da niŋ Wina'am yadda. Ka sɔ' wʋsa lɔ nɔɔr. Ba biis nɛ ba kpɛɛmnam wʋsa, ka ba yɛ bɔto fuud linɛ pa'an ye ba tiakya.

english_verse: When the king of Nineveh heard what was happening, he also dressed in sackcloth; he left the royal palace and sat in dust.
translation_verse: Ninive Na'ab la da wʋm labaar la, o duoe o na'am gbauŋ zug ka yɛɛg o na'am kparib ka yɛ bɔto fuugʋ zin' tampɛligimin ye o pa'al o sʋnfʋ san'am si'em ban tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la zug.

english_verse: When God saw that the people had stopped doing evil things, he had pity and did not destroy them as he had planned.
translation_verse: Wina'am da nyɛ ban niŋ si'em la, nɛ ban tiak ka basi ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la, o da zɔɔ ba nimbaanlig ka pʋ kɛ ka san'auŋ la kena wʋʋ on dɛŋi gban'e si'em la.

english_verse: Jonah was really upset and angry.
translation_verse: Amaa Jona sʋnf da san'amnɛ hali ka o gɛn',

english_verse: So he prayed: Our Lord, I knew from the very beginning that you wouldn't destroy Nineveh. That's why I left my own country and headed for Spain. You are a kind and merciful God, and you are very patient. You always show love, and you don't like to punish anyone.
translation_verse: ka sɔs Zugsɔb ye, “Zugsɔba, ka' man daa pʋn bɛ yin ka yɛl si'em la nwaa? Nwa' zug ka m daa zɔti wa'ae Tarsis teŋin la. M pʋn mi' fʋ yɛla, ye fʋ anɛ Wina'am kanɛ zɔt nimbaanlig ka dit suguru, fʋ sʋʋnr pʋ duod tɔ'ɔtɔɔ, ka fʋ nɔŋilim bɛ saŋa wʋsa; fʋ anɛ Wina'am onɛ pʋ bɔɔd ye fʋ san'am nida.

english_verse: Now let me die! I'd be better off dead.
translation_verse: Alazug Zugsɔba, di'emi m nyɔvʋr, bɔzugɔ, m kum sɔn'oe m vʋm!”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “What right do you have to be angry?”
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Fʋ mɔr suor kanɛ ka fʋ sʋʋnr na pɛligɛɛ?”

english_verse: Jonah then left through the east gate of the city and made a shelter to protect himself from the sun. He sat under the shelter, waiting to see what would happen to Nineveh.
translation_verse: Ka Jona yʋ'ʋn yi kpikpɛŋ, teŋ la ya-nya'aŋi ti' sʋgʋri zin' ani gur ye o gɔs linɛ na maal teŋ la.

english_verse: The Lord made a vine grow up to shade Jonah's head and protect him from the sun. Jonah was very happy to have the vine,
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb Wina'am kɛ ka tuŋ yii nɔbigi lus sʋgʋr la tis Jona ma'asim. Ka o niŋgbina ma'ae ka o sʋnf ma'ae tuŋ la yɛla.

english_verse: but early the next morning the Lord sent a worm to chew on the vine, and the vine dried up.
translation_verse: Amaa bɛogʋ nie la ka Wina'am kɛ ka zʋnzʋnr kena ɔnb tuŋ la nya'a ka li zɛndigi kʋdig.

english_verse: During the day the Lord sent a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, making him feel faint. Jonah was ready to die, and he shouted, “I wish I were dead!”
translation_verse: Ka nintaŋ dʋ ka Wina'am kɛ ka sisi'etʋʋlʋg yi ya-nya'aŋ na da'ad, ka nintaŋ tʋʋlʋg nwɛ' Jona zupaasʋʋg, ka o ligi bɔɔd kum, ka yɛl ye, “M ya'a kpi li sɔn'oe mam vʋe nwa'!”

english_verse: But the Lord asked, “Jonah, do you have the right to be angry about the vine?” “Yes, I do,” he answered, “and I'm angry enough to die.”
translation_verse: Amaa Wina'am yɛl Jona ye, “Fʋ mɔr suor, ka fʋ gɛn' tuŋ la kum yɛlaa?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn m mɔr suor, m sʋnf pɛlig nɛ hali ka li siak mam na kpi.”

english_verse: But the Lord said: You are concerned about a vine that you did not plant or take care of, a vine that grew up in one night and died the next.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Zugsɔb lɛbis ye, “Tuŋ la yɛla pakif hali, la'an nɛ fʋn pʋ bʋdi li ka mɛ pʋ gɔsi li ka li nɔbig la. Li yinɛ nɔbig yʋ'ʋŋ yinne ka lɛn kpi yʋ'ʋŋ yinne.

english_verse: I am Micah from Moresheth. And this is the message about Samaria and Jerusalem that the Lord gave to me when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were the kings of Judah. Judgment on Samaria
translation_verse: Zugsɔb da tu'asi tis Maika onɛ yi Moreset la na, saŋa kanɛ ka Jotam nɛ Ahaz nɛ Hezekia da di Juda sʋ'ʋlim na'am tuunl taaba la. O da nie pa'al o labaar dinɛ an Samaria nɛ Jerusalem yɛla. Ba kʋʋs Samaria nɛ Jerusalem bɛ'ɛd

english_verse: Listen, all of you! Earth and everything on it, pay close attention. The Lord God accuses you from his holy temple.
translation_verse: Nidiba, ya wʋsa kɛlisimi; teŋgbauŋ nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ fʋ ni la wʋsa, wʋmmi, ka Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la na di kasɛti zɛrigi ya. Zugsɔb onɛ bɛɛ o Dɔɔg kanɛ an Kasi pʋʋgin la.

english_verse: And he will come down to crush underfoot every pagan altar.
translation_verse: Gɔsimi! Zugsɔb la yii o bɛllim zin'ig la kenna, o sigid na ka ken zuoya la zut.

english_verse: Mountains will melt beneath his feet like wax beside a fire. Valleys will vanish like water rushing down a ravine.
translation_verse: Zuoya nyɛligid o nɔba teŋir, ka bɔn'ɔfalis buakid nwɛnɛ bugum nyɛligid kpaam nɛ, bɛɛ ku'om suud susuudin nɛ.

english_verse: This will happen because of the terrible sins of Israel, the descendants of Jacob. Samaria has led Israel to sin, and pagan altars at Jerusalem have made Judah sin.
translation_verse: Nɛ' wʋsa anɛ Jakob n ki'is Wina'am nɔɔr la zug, li anɛ Israel yidim tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la zug. Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ kɛ ka Jakob ki'is Wina'am nɔɔrɛ? Li ka' Samaria tempʋʋg nidibaa? Ka Juda dim maannɛ ba bada yaanɛ? Li ka' Jerusalem tempʋʋginɛɛ?

english_verse: So the Lord will leave Samaria in ruins— merely an empty field where vineyards are planted. He will scatter its stones and destroy its foundations.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb yɛl ye, “Dinzugɔ, m na kɛ ka Samaria lieb dabɔɔg, ka an zin'ikanɛ ka ba bʋt ka kuod vain tiis pɔɔg. M na kpa'ae li kuga la wʋsa bas bɔn'ɔgin; ka basi li ɛɛnbir la zaalim.

english_verse: Samaria's idols will be smashed, and the wages of temple prostitutes will be destroyed by fire. Silver and gold from those idols will then be used by foreigners as payment for prostitutes. Judah Is Doomed
translation_verse: Ba bada la wʋsa na nwa'a lieb sɛya, ka bugum di piini linɛ ka ba mɔri kennɛ ba pʋ'ʋsim dɔɔgin la. M na san'ami ba maana bimbima la wʋsa. Ban tʋm pu'agɔɔnda tʋʋma paam la'abama la, ba dataas mɛ na faaɛn li nɔki yɔ pu'agɔɔnda.” Kaasig nɛ kukuma

english_verse: Because of this tragedy, I go barefoot and naked. My crying and weeping sound like howling wolves or ostriches.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa zugɔ m na kaasid ka kum, ka ken nɔbteŋ nɛ biel sʋnsa'aŋ zug. M na kaas wʋʋ mɔɔgin baa nɛ, ka kum nwɛnɛ viiug nɛ.

english_verse: The nation is fatally wounded. Judah is doomed. Jerusalem will fall.
translation_verse: Samaria fɛn'ɛd la ka' tiim; li yʋ'ʋn paae Juda. Li paae m nidib za'anɔɔrin hali nɛ Jerusalem tempʋʋgin na.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath! Don't even cry. Instead, roll in the dust at Beth-Leaphrah.
translation_verse: Da yɛl nɛ' Gaf teŋinɛ, da kaasi baa bi'elaa. Bet Ofira teŋ dima, bilimmi uusʋg la ni.

english_verse: Depart naked and ashamed, you people of Shaphir. The town of Bethezel mourns because no one from Zaanan went out to help.
translation_verse: Yanam banɛ bɛ Safir teŋin la, gaadimi biel nɛ nyan. Yanam banɛ bɛ Zaanan teŋin la, da yii yiŋ naa. Betezel dim mɛ kaasidnɛ, ba kʋ lɛn sʋŋi ya kɔtaa nɛ.

english_verse: Everyone in Maroth hoped for the best, but the Lord sent disaster down on Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Banɛ bɛ Marot paam tɔɔg ka gu'usidi bɔɔd sʋŋir, bɔzugɔ namisʋg yi Zugsɔb la san'an na hali paae Jerusalem teŋ za'anɔɔrin.

english_verse: Now you will have to give a going-away gift to Moresheth. Israel's kings will discover that they cannot trust the town of Achzib.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, ya tisim Moreset-Gaf dim piini ka kɛɛsi ba ka ba keŋ. Israel na'anam na gɔsid ye Akizib teŋinɛ bɔɔd sʋŋir, amaa ba ye ba pan'asi ba nɛ.

english_verse: People of Mareshah, the Lord will send someone to capture your town. Then Israel's glorious king will be forced to hide in Adullam Cave.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka onɛ zabidi nyaŋid kena nyaŋ yanam banɛ bɛ Maresa teŋin la. Banɛ an Israel tuongatib la na lɛbi keŋ Adullam.

english_verse: Judah, shave your head as bald as a vulture and start mourning. Your precious children will be dragged off to a foreign country.
translation_verse: Pʋnimi ya zut nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ, ya biis banɛ ka ya nɔŋ la zug. Maalimi ya zut wʋʋ zuung zug nɛ, bɔzugɔ ba na mɔri ba keŋ ka ba an yammis teŋzʋŋin.

english_verse: Doomed! You're doomed! At night you lie in bed, making evil plans. And when morning comes, you do what you've planned because you have the power.
translation_verse: Yɛltɔɔg bɛ banɛ gban'e ye ba maal bɛ'ɛd, nɛ banɛ tɛn'ɛsid bɛ'ɛdi ba gadʋg zug! Ka bɛog nie ka ba sid tʋmi li la, bɔzugɔ ban mɔr paŋ kanɛ na nyaŋi tʋmi li la zug.

english_verse: You grab any field or house that you want; you cheat families out of homes and land.
translation_verse: Ba mɔr fufum nɛ ba taaba pɔɔd nɛ ya' ka faandi ba sʋ'oe. Ba filim yidaan ka faaɛn o yir, hali ka diti ba taaba faar.

english_verse: But here is what the Lord says: “I am planning trouble for you. Your necks will be caught in a noose, and you will be disgraced in this time of disaster.”
translation_verse: Dinzug ka Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “M gban'e ye m kɛ ka bʋmbɛ'ɛd lii ya zug, hali ka ya kʋ nyaŋi faaɛn ya mɛŋ baa bi'elaa. Ya kʋ lɛn kennɛ dʋ'ʋsidi ya mɛŋa, bɔzugɔ, li na an yɛltɔɔg amɛŋa.

english_verse: When that happens, this sorrowful song will be sung about you: “Ruined! Completely ruined! The Lord has taken our land and given it to traitors.”
translation_verse: Daakan la ya dataas na yʋ'ʋm sʋnsa'aŋ yʋʋm kaŋa la'adi yaa yɛt ye, ‘Ti ba'as yɔri, ba faanm nidib la faari pʋdig! O faaɛn li ti san'an, ka nɔki ti pɔɔd la tis banɛ gbi'i ti.’

english_verse: “Enough of your preaching!” That's what you tell me. “We won't be disgraced, so stop preaching!”
translation_verse: Nidib la yɛt ye, “Da pian'ad nɔdi'esʋg pian'adɛ.” “Da pian'ad nɔdi'esʋg pian'akaŋa tisi tii! Bɔzugɔ nyan kʋdim kʋ dii tii.”

english_verse: Descendants of Jacob, is it right for you to claim that the Lord did what he did because he was angry? Doesn't he always bless those who do right?
translation_verse: Jakob yidima, li nar ye ya yɛt ye, “Zugsɔb pʋ lɛn zɔt o nidib la nimbaanligaa? O sid na tʋm wʋʋ yanamɛ yɛt si'em laa?” Yanamɛ yɛt si'el la an sʋ'ʋŋaa? Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Mam pian'ad la ka' sʋ'ʋm tis banɛ an sida dimaa?

english_verse: My people, you have turned against one another! You have even stolen clothes right off the backs of innocent neighbors who pass by in peace.
translation_verse: Amaa m nidib la yʋ'ʋn duoe nɛ kis mam wʋʋ m anɛ ba dataa nɛ. Ya faand banɛ an suokennib la fusʋma, ka pʋ zɔti ba nimbaanlig wʋʋ banɛ yi zaba ni lɛbidnɛ.

english_verse: You take over lovely homes that belong to the women of my nation. Then you cheat their children out of the inheritance that comes from the Lord.
translation_verse: Ya kadi m nidib la pu'abi yisi ba ya' vɛnla ni ka faaɛn albareka linɛ ka m tisi ba biis la ka ba kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ li.

english_verse: Get out of here, you crooks! You'll find no rest here. You're not fit to belong to the Lord's people, and you will be destroyed.
translation_verse: Duom, gaadimi tɔ'ɔtɔ! Teŋ kaŋa nwa' ka' ya vʋ'ʋsʋm zin'ig ya'asɛ. Ya kɛ ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dian'a zin'ig la ka li san'am hali lɛn ka' maalʋgɔ.”

english_verse: The only prophet you want is a liar who will say, “Drink and get drunk!” A Promise of Hope
translation_verse: Ziri nɛ faad sɔb ya'a kena giligidi ma'adi ya ye, “M ye m tisi ya nɛ nɔdi'esʋg pian'ad linɛ an ye daam nɛ bʋnnuudkpi'ema an sʋm,” nɔdi'es kan la ka ya bɔɔd! Wina'am kaanb yɛlsʋmmi tis Israel dim

english_verse: I, the Lord, promise to bring together the people of Israel who have survived. I will gather them, just as a shepherd brings sheep together, and there will be many.
translation_verse: Jakob yidima, m sid na la'asi ya wʋsa, m sid na la'as Israel dim banɛ kpɛlim la. M na la'asi ya wʋʋ pɛ'ɛse bɛ bʋlʋʋgin si'em la. Sida ya teŋ la na lɛm pɛ'ɛl nɛ nidib tʋkpiidʋg wʋʋ bʋnkɔnbidi pɛ'ɛl zɔŋŋin nɛ.

english_verse: I will break down the gate and lead them out— then I will be their king.
translation_verse: Wina'am na yɔ'ɔg za'anɔɔr ka gaadi ba tuon, ba na da'ae za'anɔɔr la bas ka yi. Ba Na'ab la na dɔlli ba ken, Zugsɔb la mɛŋ na gaadi ba tuon.

english_verse: but you prefer to do evil instead of what is right. You skin my people alive. You strip off their flesh,
translation_verse: Ka ya lɛɛ kis linɛ an sʋ'ʋm ka nɔŋ linɛ an bɛ'ɛd. Ya siidi m nidib la niŋgbina ka waligi ba niŋgbina ni'im la ka kɛ kɔnba;

english_verse: Someday you will beg the Lord to help you, but he will turn away because of your sins.
translation_verse: Saŋa kenna ka ba na ti kaasidi buon Zugsɔb la amaa ka o kʋ lɛbisi baa. O na su'a o nindaa saŋa kan la, ka kʋ wʋmi ba winsɔsʋgɔ, ban tʋm bɛ'ɛd la zug.

english_verse: You lying prophets promise security for anyone who gives you food, but disaster for anyone who refuses to feed you. Here is what the Lord says to you prophets:
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Nɔdi'esidib la pan'asidi m nidib la nɛ kpɛn'ɛsid wɛog, Ba kaanbidnɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm tisid banɛ tisidi ba diib, ka lɛɛ kaanbid bɛ'ɛdi tisid banɛ pʋ tisidi baa.

english_verse: You prophets and fortunetellers will all be disgraced, with no message from me.”
translation_verse: Ba'abʋgʋdib la na di nyan, ka banɛ nyɛt la zug fak. Ba na pin' ba nindaa nɛ nyan, bɔzugɔ, Wina'am kʋ ti lɛn gandigi ba ya'asɛ.’”

english_verse: But the Lord has filled me with power and his Spirit. I have been given the courage to speak about justice and to tell you people of Israel that you have sinned.
translation_verse: Amaa ya'a anɛ mam, Zugsɔb Siig nɛ o paŋ la pɛ'ɛlim, ka tisidim sida nɛ ya'am linɛ mɔr kpi'euŋ, ka m na yɛl Jakob nidib la nɛ sʋnkpi'euŋʋ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la yɛla, ka pa'al Israel dimi ba taali an si'em.

english_verse: So listen to my message, you rulers of Israel! You hate justice and twist the truth.
translation_verse: Kɛlisimi, yanam banɛ an Jakob tuongatib la, nɛ banɛ an Israel kpɛɛmnam la, yanam banɛ kis sida sariakadib ka tiakid sida ka li liebid ziri la.

english_verse: You make cruelty and murder a way of life in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ya nɔk ziim mɛɛd Zion teŋ la, ka kɛ ka Jerusalem pɛ'ɛl nɛ bugusim.

english_verse: You leaders accept bribes for dishonest decisions. You priests and prophets teach and preach, but only for money. Then you say, “The Lord is on our side. No harm will come to us.”
translation_verse: Teŋ la tuongatib di'esidnɛ si'elnam nidibin ka kad saria, ka maanmaannib mɛ di'esid si'elnam ka pa'an Wina'am zi'ela gbinnɛ tisid nidib la, ka nɔdi'esidib di'esid ligidi ka yɛt ban nyɛt si'eli tisid nidib la. Nɛ wala wʋsa ba yɛt ye, “Mɛ Zugsɔb la bɛ nɛ ti? Yɛlbɛ'ɛd kʋ paae ti wae!”

english_verse: And so, because of you, Jerusalem will be plowed under and left in ruins. Thorns will cover the mountain where the temple now stands.
translation_verse: Yanam zug, Zion na lieb pɔɔg ka ba kuod, ka Jerusalem lieb tandia'ana dʋʋr, ka Pʋ'ʋsim Yir zuor la lieb sian'anr.

english_verse: In the future, the mountain with the Lord's temple will be the highest of all. It will reach above the hills, and every nation will rush to it.
translation_verse: Naar saŋa la Zuokanɛ ka Zugsɔb Yir zi'e li zug la na zi'en kiŋ-kiŋ. Li na ti wa'ami gaad zuoya la wʋsa; ka dunia nidib wʋsa na la'as anina pʋ'ʋs.

english_verse: People of many nations will come and say, “Let's go up to the mountain of the Lord God of Jacob and worship in his temple.” The Lord will teach us his Law from Jerusalem, and we will obey him.
translation_verse: Tɛɛns bɛdegʋ na la'as taaba ka yɛl ye, “Kemi na ka ti keŋ Zugsɔb zuorin la, Israel Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la. O na pa'ali ti o suori an si'em ka ti siak ka dɔlli li sʋ'ʋŋa.” Wina'am wada na yit Zion zuorin, ka Zugsɔb la pian'ad na yi Jerusalem teŋin na.

english_verse: He will settle arguments between distant and powerful nations. They will pound their swords and their spears into rakes and shovels; they will never again make war or attack one another.
translation_verse: O na an tɛɛns wʋsa sariakat ka na maal tembanɛ kpi'em ka bɛ lalli nɛ yammin la wʋsa pian'adi tisi ba. Ba na zan' ba tanp sʋ'ʋsi maal kʋnya, ka nɔki ba kpana maal gɔn'ɔd. Tɛɛns kʋ lɛn tʋ'ʋsid tanp nɛ taaba, bɛɛ ba zamisid zabaa zabid si'em ya'asɛ.

english_verse: Everyone will find rest beneath their own fig trees or grape vines, and they will live in peace. This is a solemn promise of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Sɔ' wʋsa na zin'in o tiig gbinnin baanlimm nɛ sumalisim ka sɔ' kʋ lɛn kpɛn'ɛs o dabiem. Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la kaanb nwa' zi'el, ala ka o tis nɔɔr.

english_verse: Others may follow their gods, but we will always follow the Lord our God. The Lord Will Lead His People Home
translation_verse: Tɛɛns wʋsa ya'a bɔɔd ban dɔlli ba bada amaa tinam na dɔlli ti Zugsɔb onɛ aan ti Wina'am la saŋa wʋsa. Zugsɔb la na la'as Israel dim na ya'as

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will gather my people— the lame and the outcasts, and all others into whose lives I have brought sorrow.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ya ye, “Daakan la,” m na la'asi m nimbanɛ an pɔnda, ka la'as banɛ zɔɔ lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ sieba la, nɛ banɛ ka m kɛ ka sʋnsa'aŋ paae ba la.

english_verse: Then the lame and the outcasts will belong to my people and become a strong nation. I, the Lord, will rule them from Mount Zion forever.
translation_verse: Ba anɛ pɔnda ka lal nɛ yir, amaa m na la'asi ba na ka kɛ ka ba paam paŋ. Mam Zugsɔb na bɛ Jerusalem tempʋʋgin ka aan ba Na'ab saŋa wʋsa.

english_verse: Jerusalem, why are you crying? Don't you have a king? Have your advisors gone? Are you suffering like a woman in childbirth?
translation_verse: Amaa nannanna bɔ ka ya kaasid agɔla gɔla? Ya ka' na'ab ka o na gaadi ya tuonnɛɛ? Ya ya'am dim banɛ san'anɛ ya kpinɛ naae nyain nɛɛ? Ka tɔɔg yʋ'ʋn paae ya wʋʋ pu'a na sa'ae?

english_verse: Keep on groaning with pain, you people of Jerusalem! If you escape from your city to the countryside, you will still be taken as prisoners to Babylonia. But later I will rescue you from your enemies.
translation_verse: Jerusalem nidiba, liebimi ka ʋʋnsidi wʋʋ pu'a kanɛ sa'ae nɛ. Amaa nannanna nwa', asɛɛ ka ya yi tempʋkaŋa ni keŋ gbɛn mɔɔgin. Ba na mɔri ya keŋ Babilon ka ya lieb yammis. Amaa Zugsɔb la na faaɛn ya, anina ka o na yisi yaa ya dataas la nu'usin.

english_verse: Zion, because of your sins you are surrounded by many nations who say, “We can hardly wait to see you disgraced.”
translation_verse: Amaa nannanna tɛɛns bɛdegʋ la'as ye ba zab nɛ ya, ka yɛt ye, “Kɛlli ka ti diis Jerusalem dim la dian'ad! Kɛlli ka ba di namisʋgʋ ti nini ni!”

english_verse: But they don't know that I, the Lord, have gathered them here to grind them like grain.
translation_verse: Amaa ba zi' Zugsɔb la tɛn'ɛsa an si'em ka mɛ kʋ nyaŋi baŋ o gban'arɛ. O la'asidi ba nɛ ye o bʋ' ba wʋʋ ki ka ba bʋ'ʋd zieŋin si'em la.

english_verse: Smash them to pieces, Zion! I'll let you be like a bull with iron horns and bronze hoofs. Crush those nations and bring their wealth to me, the Lord of the earth.
translation_verse: “Jerusalem dima, duomi ka bʋ' tɛɛns la wʋʋ ki nɛ. M na tisi ya paŋ ka ya nwɛnɛ na'araug kanɛ iila an kʋnt ka o nɔba an kʋntzɛn'ug. Ka ya na bʋ' tɛɛns bɛdegʋ wʋʋ ki, ka faaɛn ba areza'as linɛ ka ba filim paam la tis mam Zugsɔb onɛ sʋ'oe dunia wʋsa la.”

english_verse: Jerusalem, enemy troops have surrounded you; they have struck Israel's ruler in the face with a stick.
translation_verse: Jerusalem dima, la'asimi ya zabzabidib, ka ya bi'emnam lɔbi giligi ya teŋ la. Ba na nɔk daugʋ nwɛ' Israel tuongat. Tuongat na yi Betilehem na

english_verse: Bethlehem Ephrath, you are one of the smallest towns in the nation of Judah. But the Lord will choose one of your people to rule the nation— someone whose family goes back to ancient times.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb lɛn yɛl ye, “Amaa fʋn Betilehem Efirata kɛlisim! Fʋ anɛ tembil Juda tɛɛns wʋsa sʋʋgin, amaa fʋ ni ka m ye m gaŋ sɔ' ka o na gɔs Israel teŋ la ka sʋ'oe li. O tuŋ dɔlnɛ ya yaanam saŋa linɛ pin'il kʋdimin sa la.”

english_verse: Like a shepherd taking care of his sheep, this ruler will lead and care for his people by the power and glorious name of the Lord his God. His people will live securely, and the whole earth will know his true greatness,
translation_verse: O ya'a kena o na gɔs o nidib nɛ paŋ kanɛ yit Zugsɔb san'an na la, nɛ na'am na'asi kanɛ an on Zugsɔb Wina'am din la, wʋʋ kɔnbkemmi gɔsid o kɔnbid si'em la. Ka o nidib yʋ'ʋn na bɛ baanlimm ka dabiem kae, bɔzugɔ dunia wʋsa na baŋ o paŋi an si'em,

english_verse: because he will bring peace. Assyria Will Be Defeated Let Assyria attack our country and our palaces. We will counterattack, led by a number of rulers
translation_verse: ka o na mɔr sumbʋgʋsʋm na. Asiria zaba nɛ tʋbir tɛkir yɛla Asiria dim ya'a kpɛn' ti teŋin la na ka paae ti ya-vɛnla la ni na, ti na gaŋi ti tuongatib ayɔpɔi bɛɛ anii ka ba sʋ'oe sʋ'ʋlim la ka zab nɛ ba.

english_verse: whose strong army will defeat the nation of Assyria. Yes, our leaders will rescue us, if those Assyrians dare to invade our land. The Survivors Will Be Safe
translation_verse: Soogianam la na ti zabi nyaŋ Asiria linɛ an Nimrod teŋ la, ka na sʋ'oe li wʋsa nɛ paŋ. Asiria dim la ya'a lɔ'ɔŋi ti titɔndis ye ba san'ami ti teŋ la ba na faaɛn tii yisi ba nu'usin.

english_verse: A few of Jacob's descendants survived and are scattered among the nations. But the Lord will let them cover the earth like dew and rain that refreshes the soil.
translation_verse: Jakob nimbanɛ kpɛlim la na bɛ nidib bɛdegʋ sʋʋgin nwɛnɛ mɛligim yit Zugsɔb la san'an na, ka lɛn nwɛnɛ saa misid mɔɔd nɛ ka pʋ ti'e ninsaala.

english_verse: At present they are scattered, but later they will attack, as though they were fierce lions pouncing on sheep. Their enemies will be torn to shreds, with no one to save them;
translation_verse: Jakob nimbanɛ kpɛlim la na bɛ tɛɛns wʋsa nɛ nidib bɛdegʋ sʋʋgin nwɛnɛ gbigimi na bɛ mɔɔgin bʋnkɔnbid sʋʋgin si'em la, bɛɛ gbigimbili na bɛ pɛ'ɛsini gban'adi ba aansid ka sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi faaɛn ba basɛ.

english_verse: they will be helpless, completely destroyed. Idols Will Be Destroyed in Israel
translation_verse: Ya nu'us na ʋk agɔla nɛ paŋ, ka ya nyaŋi ya dataas nɛ banɛ kisi ya, ka na san'ami ba wʋsa.

english_verse: The Lord said: At that time I will wipe out your cavalry and chariots,
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “Daakan la, m na kʋʋ ya widi la ka kɔɔ ya tɛrekonam la bas.

english_verse: as well as your cities and your fortresses.
translation_verse: M na san'ami ya tɛɛns la wʋsa ka nwa'a ya kpi'euŋ zin'is la bas.

english_verse: I will stop you from telling fortunes and practicing witchcraft.
translation_verse: M na san'ami ya sɔɔng la, ka ya kʋ lɛn mɔri ya ba'akɔn la bugida.

english_verse: You will no longer worship the idols or stone images you have made— I will destroy them,
translation_verse: M na nwa'a ya wina nɛ ya teŋgban kuga la, ka ya kʋ lɛm pʋ'ʋsid dinɛ ka ya nu'us maalɛ.

english_verse: together with the sacred poles and even your towns.
translation_verse: M na vɔɔn ya teŋgban Asera daad la ka san'ami ya maan bimbima la wʋsa.

english_verse: I will become furious and take revenge on the nations that refuse to obey me.
translation_verse: M sʋʋnr na pɛlig, ka m na yɔɔ ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la sam; ka san'am tɛɛns banɛ pʋ siak mam nɔɔr la.”

english_verse: The Lord said to his people: Come and present your case to the hills and mountains.
translation_verse: Kɛlisimi Zugsɔb la yɛt si'el: “Duomini agɔl ka tu'a ya antu'a ka zuoya la wʋm. Kɛlli ka kʋkʋna kɛlis yanamɛ bɔɔd ye ya yɛl si'el.

english_verse: Israel, I am bringing charges against you— I call upon the mountains and the earth's firm foundation to be my witnesses.
translation_verse: Zuoya, wʋmmi Zugsɔb la zɛrigir nwa'; dunia ɛɛnb kʋda, kɛlisimi! Zugsɔb la mɔr pian'ad nɛ o nidib. O mɔr antu'a nɛ Israel dim:

english_verse: My people, have I wronged you in any way at all? Please tell me.
translation_verse: O yɛl ye, ‘M nidiba, m maali ya bɔ? Bɔ ziid ka m ziili ya? Lɛbisiminim!

english_verse: I rescued you from Egypt, where you were slaves. I sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Manɛ da mɔri ya yi Egipt na, ka faaɛn ya yammid pʋʋgin. M da tʋm Moses nɛ Aaron nɛ Miriam ye ba gaadi ya tuonnɛ dɔlli ya yi.

english_verse: Don't forget the evil plans of King Balak of Moab or what Balaam son of Beor said to him. Remember how I, the Lord, saved you many times on your way from Acacia to Gilgal. True Obedience
translation_verse: M nidiba, tɛn'ɛsimi Balak onɛ da an Moab Na'ab la da gban'e ya yɛla si'em ka Beor biig Balaam mɛ lɛbis o si'em. Tɛn'ɛsimi yanamɛ da yi Sittim hali keŋ Gilgal la, ka baŋi Zugsɔb pʋpielim tʋʋmaa an si'em.’” Wina'am bɔɔd si'el

english_verse: What offering should I bring when I bow down to worship the Lord God Most High? Should I try to please him by sacrificing calves a year old?
translation_verse: M ye m mɔr bɔ kimm kɛn Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ bɛɛ agɔl la tuon na tis o nɛ girima? M na mɔri na'apɔla banɛ an yʋʋm yinne kena maal nyu'or maana o san'anɛɛ?

english_verse: Will thousands of sheep or rivers of olive oil make God satisfied with me? Should I sacrifice to the Lord my first-born child as payment for my terrible sins?
translation_verse: Wina'am sʋʋnr na malis nɛ pɛraad tusir bɛɛ o bɔɔdnɛ kpaam nɛ dʋgid linɛ ka' kallɛ? Bɛɛ m nɔkimi m bikpɛɛm onɛ aan m mɛŋ-mɛŋ ziim, yɔɔ m pɔ'ɔgir nɛ m tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la yɛla?

english_verse: The Lord God has told us what is right and what he demands: “See that justice is done, let mercy be your first concern, and humbly obey your God.” Cheating and Violence
translation_verse: M dau, o pʋn pa'alif linɛ an sʋm. Ka bɔ kimm ka Zugsɔb la lɛɛ bɔɔd ye fʋ tʋm? O bɔɔd ye fʋ tʋm linɛ an sida ka mɔr nimbaanlzɔɔr nɛ nɔŋilim, ka sigisi fʋ mɛŋi ken nɛ Wina'am. Israel taal nɛ ba tʋbtɛɛgir yɛla

english_verse: I am the Lord, and you are wise to respect my power to punish. So listen to my message for the city of Jerusalem:
translation_verse: Kɛlisimi! Zugsɔb la yɛt teŋ nwa' dim ye, “Onɛ zɔti m yʋ'ʋr la anɛ ya'am sɔb.” Kɛlisimi onɛ mɔr paŋ la nɛ onɛ tisi li la.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, will punish you for cheating with weights and with measures.
translation_verse: M bas zam sɔb onɛ mɔr laas nɛ bɔtbanɛ pʋ paae ma'ad la'adi kuosid ka o keŋ zaalim?

english_verse: You rich people are violent, and everyone tells lies.
translation_verse: Ba areza'as dim la anɛ faandib, ka ba teŋin dim la an ziri dim ka pian'ad ziri pian'ad.

english_verse: Because of your sins, I will wound you and leave you ruined and defenseless.
translation_verse: M pʋn pin'ili san'ami ya ka namisi ya, ka li anɛ ya tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd nwa' zug.

english_verse: You will eat, but still be hungry; you will store up goods, but lose everything— I, the Lord, will let it all be captured in war.
translation_verse: Ya na dit ka pʋ tigida, ka kɔ'ɔm nan mɔri ya. Ya na su bʋya ni, amaa ka zi' lin di'e si'ela; ka lin ka ya su la wʋsa na gaad zaba ni.

english_verse: You won't harvest what you plant or use the oil from your olive trees or drink the wine from grapes you grow.
translation_verse: Ya na bʋd ka kʋ bunɛ, ka nwiak olif ka kʋ dii li kpaam, ka kuan' daam ka lɛɛ kʋ nuu.

english_verse: Jerusalem, this will happen because you followed the sinful example of kings Omri and Ahab. Now I will destroy you and your property. Then the people of every nation will make fun and insult you.
translation_verse: Ya siaki dɔl na'ab Omir malima, nɛ Ahab yidim tʋʋma wʋsa; Ya dɔlli ba suoya wʋsa. Alazug, m na kɛ ka ya paam san'auŋ. Sɔ' wʋsa na gɔsi ya zaalim, ka na la'adi ya ka kisi ya.”

english_verse: I feel so empty inside— like someone starving for grapes or figs, after the vines and trees have all been picked clean.
translation_verse: Abɔ nimbaanligi nwa' paae mam! M nwɛnɛ onɛ paae na ka ba pʋn pɔn' tiwala vain tiis pɔɔgin naae, ka ki'e ki ka diib lɛn kae ya'asɛ. Bʋnwanna kae ka m na di bɛɛ kekama wala banɛ dɛŋid bi'igir ka m bɔɔd la kae.

english_verse: No one is loyal to God; no one does right. Everyone is brutal and eager to deceive everyone else.
translation_verse: Wina'am nidib la wʋsa widignɛ, ninsʋŋ nɛ yadda sɔb lɛn kae; ba sɔ' pʋ lɛn kpɛlim teŋ nwa' nii. Ba wʋsa anɛ ninkʋʋdib, ka bɛnti ba mɛŋ ba'abiis.

english_verse: Don't trust anyone, not even your best friend, and be careful what you say to the one you love.
translation_verse: Da niŋi ya tiraan yaddaa, hali baa ya zuanam bɛɛ ya pu'aba; da yɛli ba linɛ bɛɛ ya sʋnfʋnɛ.

english_verse: Sons refuse to respect their own fathers, daughters rebel against their own mothers, and daughters-in-law despise their mothers-in-law. Your family is now your enemy.
translation_verse: Biribis pʋ tisidi ba saamnam girimaa, ka bipumis mɛ zabid nɛ ba manam, ka bipu'ab mɛ zabid nɛ ba dayaamnam. Ya na nyɛ ka ya dataas aan ya mɛŋ yidim.

english_verse: But I trust the Lord God to save me, and I will wait for him to answer my prayer. The Nation Turns to God
translation_verse: Amaa, ya'a anɛ mam, man gɔtnɛ Zugsɔb onɛ aan m ti'ir la; M gurnɛ Wina'am onɛ aan m faangid la. Wina'am la na wʋmi m sɔsʋg. Israel dim na lɛm duoe ya'as

english_verse: My enemies, don't be glad because of my troubles! I may have fallen, but I will get up; I may be sitting in the dark, but the Lord is my light.
translation_verse: Da gɔs mam zaalim, m dataa! Baa mam lu la, m na lɛn duoe. La'an nɛ man zi'e likin la, Zugsɔb mɛŋi aan m nɛɛsim.

english_verse: I have sinned against the Lord. And so I must endure his anger, until he comes to my defense. But I know that I will see him making things right for me and leading me to the light.
translation_verse: M na an baanlimm ka Zugsɔb la tɛɛgi m tʋbir bɔzugɔ m tʋm o bɛ'ɛd, hali ti paae saŋkan ka o na tu'a m antu'a ka tisim bʋʋd ka sɔ' wʋsa nyɛ. Zugsɔb na mɔrimi yis likin la na, ka m nyɛɛ o pʋpielim la.

english_verse: You, my enemies, said, “The Lord God is helpless.” Now each of you will be disgraced and put to shame. I will see you trampled like mud in the street. A Bright Future
translation_verse: Anina ka m dataas na baŋ ye Zugsɔb la bɛɛ m san'an; ka nyan na dii ba, banɛ daa kisim ka yɛt ye, “Fʋ Zugsɔb onɛ aan fʋ Wina'am la bɛ yaanɛ la?”. M nini ni ka m na nyɛ ka ba nɔɔ ba wʋʋ ban nɔɔd bian'ar linɛ bɛ suorin si'em la.

english_verse: Towns of Judah, the day is coming when your walls will be rebuilt, and your boundaries enlarged.
translation_verse: Daakan la Israel tempʋʋs na lɛbi mɛ', ka ya titɔndis yalig.

english_verse: Those nations will suffer disaster because of what they did. Micah's Prayer and the Lord's Answer
translation_verse: Amaa teŋ la na lɛn kpɛlim nɛɛm, ka li anɛ banɛ bɛ anina la tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd zug. Wina'am nimbaanlzɔɔr nɛ o nɔŋilim yɛla

english_verse: Lead your people, Lord! Come and be our shepherd. Grasslands surround us, but we live in a forest. So lead us to Bashan and Gilead, and let us find pasture as we did long ago.
translation_verse: Ti Zugsɔba, kem na guri fʋ nidib, mɔri fʋ pɛ'ɛs la keŋ yamma'asa zin'ig. Nannanna ba bɛ sian'arini ba kɔn'ɔkɔn', la'an nɛ yam sʋma zin'isi giligi ba la. Kɛl ka ba na paam yam sʋŋ kanɛ bɛ Basan nɛ Gilead tɛɛnsin la wʋʋ ban da paamid kʋdimin si'em la.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will work miracles just as I did when I led you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: “M na tʋm nyalima linɛ an bʋntitada tisi ya, nwɛnɛ mam da tʋm nyalima si'em ka yisi ya Egipt teŋgbauŋʋn na la.”

english_verse: Nations will see this and be ashamed because of their helpless armies. They will be in shock, unable to speak or hear,
translation_verse: Dunia nwa' wʋsa nidib na nyɛɛ li ka nyan dii ba ka ba paŋ la wʋsa naae. Ba na zaŋi ba nu'usi pin' ba nɔya, ka ba tʋba kpid.

english_verse: because of their fear of me, your Lord and God. Then they will come trembling, crawling out of their fortresses like insects or snakes, lapping up the dust. No One Is Like God The people said:
translation_verse: Ba na dit titan nwɛnɛ wiigi nɛ, ka nwɛnɛ bʋnvʋya banɛ vuud teŋin. Ba na fɛndigi lɛbi ti Zugsɔb Wina'am san'an na nɛ dabiem, ka na zɔti ya ka kirid.

english_verse: Our God, no one is like you. We are all that is left of your chosen people, and you freely forgive our sin and guilt. You don't stay angry forever; you're glad to have pity
translation_verse: Wina'am lɛm bɛ yaanɛ nwɛnɛ fʋ: fʋ kɛti fʋ nimbanɛ kpɛlim la taali basid. Fʋ pʋ kɛt ka fʋ sʋʋnr pɛligid nɛ fʋ nidib la saŋa wʋsaa, fʋ anɛ onɛ pa'an nimbaanlzɔɔr.

english_verse: and pleased to be merciful. You will trample on our sins and throw them in the sea.
translation_verse: Fʋ na lɛn dii ti suguru, ka nɔɔ ti tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd la teŋin, ka zaŋi lɔbi basi atɛukʋn la.

english_verse: You will keep your word and be faithful to Jacob and to Abraham, as you promised our ancestors many years ago.
translation_verse: Fʋ na pa'ali fʋ sida an si'em nɛ Jakob ka pa'ali fʋ nimbaanlzɔɔr nɛ Abraham nwɛnɛ fʋn da kaanb si'em zi'eli ti yaanam, saŋa linɛ ka' naar la.

english_verse: I am Nahum from Elkosh. And this is the message that I wrote down about Nineveh. The Fierce Anger of the Lord
translation_verse: Labakaŋa anɛ Ninive yɛla ka Wina'am nie pa'al Nahum onɛ yi Elikos teŋin na la ka o sɔb. Zugsɔb sʋnf pɛlig Ninive yɛla

english_verse: The Lord God demands loyalty. In his anger, he takes revenge on his enemies.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la anɛ Wina'am onɛ nyuun, ka an onɛ yɔɔd sam nɛ o sʋʋnr wʋsa: Zugsɔb yɔɔd o dataas wʋsa sam, ka o sʋnf pɛligid nɛ o bi'emnam.

english_verse: The Lord is powerful, yet patient; he makes sure that the guilty are always punished. He can be seen in storms and in whirlwinds; clouds are the dust from his feet.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la sʋʋnr pʋ duod tɔ'ɔtɔɔ amaa o lɛɛ mɔr paŋ; ka lɛɛ kʋ bas tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd sɔb ka o keŋ zaalim-zaalim, asɛɛ o tɛɛg o tʋbir. O suor bɛ nɛ sisi'etita'ar nɛ sisi'epiliŋin, ka saŋgbana la aan o nɔba uusʋg.

english_verse: At the Lord's command, oceans and rivers dry up. Bashan, Mount Carmel, and Lebanon wither, and their flowers fade.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tisid nɔɔr ka Atɛuk kpiɛnd, onɛ kɛt ka kɔlis la wʋsa kʋdigid; Basan nɛ Kaamel zuoya mɔɔd la zɛndig nɛ, ka Lebanon tiis puum linɛ vɛnl la wʋsa sʋʋg.

english_verse: At the sight of the Lord, mountains and hills tremble and melt; the earth and its people shudder and shake.
translation_verse: Zuoya la na dam, ka zuobibis nyɛlig. Teŋ la mi'im o tuon, nɛ dunia la zin'ikanɛ ka nidib bɛ wʋsa.

english_verse: Who can stand the heat of his furious anger? It flashes out like fire and shatters stones. The Power of Assyria Will Be Broken
translation_verse: O sʋʋnr ya'a duoe, anɔ'ɔnɛ na nyaŋi zi'enɛ o tuon bɛɛ kpɛm bɛɛ o ni, o sʋnpɛɛn la saŋa? O sʋnpɛɛn la kpa'adnɛ nwɛnɛ bugum nɛ, ka tampiins wʋsa nwa'adi widigid o tuon.

english_verse: The Lord is good. He protects those who trust him in times of trouble.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la an sʋ'ʋŋa, fʋ ya'a ti bɛ yɛllin, onɛ aan fʋ suak zin'ig; o sʋŋid banɛ niŋ o yadda la.

english_verse: But like a roaring flood, the Lord chases his enemies into dark places and destroys them.
translation_verse: Amaa Ninive tempʋʋg la wʋsa, o na kɛ ka ku'om dii li ka li naae, ka kad o dataas wʋsa kpɛn'ɛs likin.

english_verse: So don't plot against the Lord! He wipes out his enemies, and they never revive.
translation_verse: Bɔɔ kɛ ka ya gban'e pʋtɛn'ɛbɛ'ɛd Zugsɔb la yɛla? O na li' ya wʋsa vuguri ka li naae.

english_verse: They are like drunkards overcome by wine, or like twisted thornbushes burning in a fire.
translation_verse: Ba na tʋ'ʋsid wʋʋ banɛ bug daam nɛ, ka bugum na dii ba nwɛnɛ gɔn'ɔs nɛ mɔkpi'emis nɛ.

english_verse: Assyria, one of your rulers has made evil plans against the Lord.
translation_verse: Ninive, sɔ' nam mi' yii fʋ san'an na tɛn'ɛsid bɛ'ɛdi tisid Zugsɔb la, ka sa'an nidib sa'al bɛ'ɛdɛɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord says, “Assyria, no matter how strong you are, you will be cut down! My people Judah, I have troubled you before, but I won't do it again.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb la yɛl ye, “La'an nɛ ban mɔr sʋŋidib ka ba an bɛdegʋ la, ba na kɛnsigi ba bɛn la ka li naae. Amaa namiskanɛ daa paae yanam Juda dim la, m kʋ lɛn namisi ya ala ya'asɛ.

english_verse: I'll snap your chains and set you free from the Assyrians.”
translation_verse: Nannanna m na yis yu'asin la ya niŋgɔnya ni ka san'am bana banɛ lɔɔ ya nu'us wʋsa.”

english_verse: Assyria, this is what else the Lord says to you: “Your name will be forgotten. I will destroy every idol in your temple, and I will send you to the grave, because you are worthless.”
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la tis nɔɔr Ninive dim yɛla, ye, “Ya kʋ mɔr yaas ka ba pʋdigi ya yʋ'ʋrɛ. M na san'ami ya bada banɛ ka ya mɛɛ zi'el la wʋsa. M na tuu ya yaad, bɔzugɔ ya ka' vɔɔnrɛ ka li pʋ nar ye ya vʋeya.”

english_verse: Look toward the mountains, people of Judah! Here comes a messenger with good news of peace. Celebrate your festivals. Keep your promises to God. Your evil enemies are destroyed and will never again invade your country.
translation_verse: Gɔsima, sɔ' mɔr labasʋŋʋ yit zuoya ni kenna, O pian'ad anɛ suguru nɛ sumbʋgʋsʋm. O yɛt ye, “Yanam Juda dima, maalimi ya malima la di'ema, ka yɔ yanamɛ kaanb si'eli zi'el la. Bɔzugɔ nimbɛ'ɛdnam kʋ lɛn nyaŋi yaa, ba na paam san'auŋ.”

english_verse: Nineveh, someone is coming to attack and scatter you. Guard your fortresses! Watch the road! Be brave! Prepare for battle!
translation_verse: Ninive dima, ya dataas kenna ye ba san'ami ya. Gu'umi ya teŋ la zaŋguoma la! Gɔsimi suoraad la ni! Ka ti'ebi ya mɛŋ nɛ zaba la'ad wʋsa.

english_verse: Judah and Israel are like trees with branches broken by their enemies. But the Lord is going to restore their power and glory. *
translation_verse: Zugsɔb la na lɛbis Jakob girima la ya'as ka li nwɛnɛ Israel dim girima la, la'an nɛ san'auŋ dimi da kena san'ami ya tɛɛns nɛ ya pɔɔd wʋsa la.

english_verse: Their horses prance, and their armored chariots dart around like lightning or flaming torches.
translation_verse: Tɛrekonam la widignɛ dɔl teŋ la suoya wʋsa, ba zɔtnɛ ken tuon ka lɛbid nya'aŋ zin'ig wʋsa. Ba nwɛnɛ bugum pielim nɛ ka ian'ad wʋʋ saa nɛ.

english_verse: An officer gives a command. But his soldiers stumble, as they hasten to build a shelter to protect themselves against rocks thrown down from the city wall.
translation_verse: Ka Na'ab la tansi buol o zabzabidib tuongatib, ka ba zɔti kenna ka tu'usid. Ba dataas la zɔɔ paae teŋ la zaŋguomin ka mɔr gbanti'edis ye ba lusi ba mɛŋ.

english_verse: The river gates fly open, and panic floods the palace.
translation_verse: Ka za'anɔya banɛ kpi'e kɔldaug la yɔ'ɔs ka na'ayir la wʋsa li.

english_verse: Nineveh is disgraced. The queen is dragged off. Her servant women mourn; they moan like doves, and they beat their breasts in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ba nyaŋ teŋ la dim wʋsa ka mɔri baa kul ka ba liebi ba yammis. Ba pu'asada la wʋsa bibigi ba nyɔ'ɔg nɛ sʋnsa'aŋ ka kaasidi limisid taaba wʋʋ dawana nɛ.

english_verse: Nineveh is like a pond with leaking water. Shouts of “Stop! Don't go!” can be heard everywhere. But everyone is leaving.
translation_verse: Ninive nidib la nwɛnɛ mu'ar ka li zaŋguom aaɛn, ka li ku'om wʋsa pʋbidi gat, ka nidib la kaasid nɛ kʋkɔtitada yɛt ye, “Zi'enimi! Zi'enimi!” Amaa sɔ' pʋ gi'e gɔs bɛɛ zi'enɛ.

english_verse: Enemy soldiers shout, “The city is full of treasure and all kinds of wealth. Steal her silver! Grab her gold!”
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛt ye, “Faanmi anzurifa nɛ sanlima la'ad la!” Bɔzugɔ teŋ la kpan'am ka' naarɛ, li arezak la bɛ zin'isi'a wʋsa.

english_verse: What happened to this city? They were safer there than powerful lions in a den, with no one to disturb them.
translation_verse: Nannanna ya tempʋkanɛ da nwɛnɛ gbigima bʋʋg la bɛ yaanɛ? Zin'ikanɛ ka ba da diisidi ba gbigimbibis ka gbigim nya'aŋ nɛ gbigimdaug nɛ ba biis gɔɔnd ka dabiem kae la bɛ yaanɛ?

english_verse: These are the same lions that ferociously attacked their victims, then dragged away the flesh to feed their young.
translation_verse: Gbigimdaug la daa gban'ad ni'im buudi wʋsa ka li tigid o yidim ka kpɛlimid o gbɛɛnsirin la.

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful is against you, Nineveh. God will burn your chariots and send an army to kill those young lions of yours. You will never again make victims of others or send messengers to threaten everyone on this earth.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “Baŋim ye man anɛ fʋ dataa!” “M na nyu'oe fʋ zaba tɛrekonam la nɛ bugum, ka kɛ ka m zaba sʋ'ʋg la bɛɛns gbigimpɔla la wʋsa. M kʋ kɛ ka bʋnkɔnbid banɛ ka fʋ kʋʋd la baa yinne kpɛlim. Sɔ' kʋ lɛn wʋm banɛ aan fʋ tʋmtʋmnib la kʋkɔrɛ.”

english_verse: You were nothing more than a prostitute using your magical charms and witchcraft to attract and trap nations.
translation_verse: Nwa' wʋsa anɛ Ninive onɛ nwɛnɛ pu'agɔɔndir la kʋkɔma'asim zug; ka o zaŋ sɔɔng nɛ ba'abʋgʋsim pan'as tɛɛns la ka ba kilim yammis, ka nyaŋ buudi la wʋsa nɛ o sɔɔng.

english_verse: But I, the Lord All-Powerful, am now your enemy. I will pull up your skirt and let nations and kingdoms stare at your nakedness.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la yɛl ye, “Baŋim ka man anɛ fʋ dataa!”, “M na lidigi fʋ fuug la pili fʋ nindaa ka kɛɛf biel, ka dunia dim wʋsa nyɛɛ fʋ nyan paalʋ.

english_verse: I will cover you with garbage, treat you like trash, and rub you in the dirt.
translation_verse: M na kɛ ka ba nɔk bʋnfɛn'ɛsa lɔbif, ka nɛ'ɛsif ka ziemif hali, ka sɔ' wʋsa gɔsid ka la'adif.

english_verse: Everyone who sees you will turn away and shout, “Nineveh is done for! Is anyone willing to mourn or to give her comfort?” Nineveh's Fate Is Sealed
translation_verse: Sɔ' mɛkama ya'a nyɛɛf, o na zɔ ka basif, ka yɛt ye, ‘Oi, oi! Ninive san'amnɛ! Ka anɔ'ɔnɛ na fabil o yɛla? Yaanɛ ka m na nyɛ sɔ' ka o bɛlis o?’”

english_verse: Nineveh, do you feel safer than the city of Thebes? The Nile River was its wall of defense.
translation_verse: Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ anɛ sʋ'ʋm gat Tebɛs teŋ kanɛ bɛ Nail kɔldaug baba ka ku'om giligi li laa? Kɔldaug la aan o gu'ud, ka ku'om la aan o zaŋguom.

english_verse: Thebes trusted the mighty power of Ethiopia and Egypt; the nations of Put and Libya were her allies.
translation_verse: Kus teŋgbauŋ nɛ Egipt da sʋŋid Tebɛs, ka mɔr paŋ tita'ar kanɛ ka' bɛnnɛ. Put nɛ Libiya tɛɛns la da zi'e ba nya'aŋ.

english_verse: But she was captured and taken to a foreign country. Her children were murdered at every street corner. The members of her royal family were auctioned off, and her high officials were bound in chains.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala wʋsa ba da nyaŋ teŋ la ka mɔr o nidib la lɔ'ɔŋ teŋ zʋŋ ka ba lieb yammis. Ba fanbi ba biliesi kʋʋ bas suoya la ni yɔɔg-yɔɔg. Ba maal bʋgʋlʋm-bʋgʋlʋm gaans nintitada la, ka gban'e na'ayikpɛm la lɔ nɛ bana.

english_verse: Nineveh, now it's your turn! You will get drunk and try to hide from your enemy.
translation_verse: Fʋn mɛ na nyɛ namisʋg wʋʋ nidi na kʋʋlnɛ fʋ na zɔti ieed suak zin'ig ka na ieed su'asigi fʋ dataas zin'igin.

english_verse: Your fortresses are fig trees with ripe figs. Merely shake the trees, and fruit will fall into every open mouth.
translation_verse: Fʋ teŋ kpi'ema la wʋsa na nwɛnɛ kekama tibanɛ walaa bi'ig, ka ba ya'a mi'imi ba walbi'ima la na lut onɛ dit la nɔɔrin.

english_verse: Your army is weak. Fire has destroyed the crossbars on your city gates; now they stand wide open to your enemy.
translation_verse: Gɔsimi fʋ zabzabidib la, ba anɛ pu'ab! Fʋ teŋ la za'anɔya la yɔ'ɔgnɛ tisi fʋ dataas; ka bugum di dalamma banɛ puugid dɔɔd la wʋsa.

english_verse: Your city is under attack. Haul in extra water! Strengthen your defenses! Start making bricks! Stir the mortar!
translation_verse: Wikimi ku'om digili ka ti'ebi gur ka ba na ti gilig teŋ la! Maalimi fʋ zaŋguoma nɛ dalamma la ka ba mɔr paŋ! Nɔnimi ya'ad la, nɔɔmi tan la maalimi zaŋguoma la zin'ibanɛ san'am la!

english_verse: You will still go up in flames and be cut down by swords that will wipe you out like a field attacked by grasshoppers. So, go ahead and increase like a swarm of locusts!
translation_verse: Anina ka bugum la na diif. Zaba sʋ'ʋg la na ki'e fʋ kʋ nwɛnɛ sisɔma ɔnbid mɔɔd si'em la. Wiakimi nwɛnɛ sisɔma nɛ ka wiak wʋʋ na'azɔmnam nɛ.

english_verse: More merchants are in your city than there are stars in the sky— but they are like locusts that eat everything, then fly away.
translation_verse: Fʋ kpikpinkpinnib nɔbignɛ hali ka ba kal gaad nwadbibis. Amaa ba nwɛnɛ na'azɔmnamɛ na luu yadig teŋinnɛ, ɔnb si'el wʋsa ka lɛn iank.

english_verse: Your guards and your officials are swarms of locusts. On a chilly day they settle on a fence, but when the sun comes out, they take off to who-knows-where.
translation_verse: Fʋ kpɛɛmnam la nwɛnɛ na'azɔmnam nɛ, ka fʋ gbauŋmi'idib la nwɛnɛ sisɔma banɛ tab zaŋguom bɛogʋn ka winnig ya'a ti tans ka ba iank ka sɔ' zi' ban keŋ zin'isi'a.

english_verse: King of Assyria, your officials and leaders are sound asleep, while your people are scattered in the mountains. Yes, your people are sheep without a shepherd.
translation_verse: Fʋn Asiria Na'aba! Fʋ kɔnbkemnib la gbisidnɛ, ka fʋ nintitada la mɛ digi vʋ'ʋsid. Banɛ kpɛlim la widigi dʋ zuoya ni, ka sɔ' kae na la'asi baa.

english_verse: You're fatally wounded. There's no hope for you. But everyone claps when they hear this news, because your constant cruelty has caused them pain.
translation_verse: Si'el kae na nyaŋi ti'ebi fʋ fɛn'ɛd la, bɔzugɔ sapu'ad la zu'oe siak fʋn na kpi. Onɛ wʋsa wʋm labaar la, pʋ'ʋsidnɛ nu'usi fʋ luug la yɛla. Bɔzugɔ, nid kae ka fʋ pʋ namis oo?

english_verse: I am Habakkuk the prophet. And this is the message that the Lord gave me. Habakkuk Complains to the Lord
translation_verse: Wina'am n da nie labasi'a tis o nɔdi'es Habakuk la nwa': Habakuk nyɔnyɔlʋg la yɛla

english_verse: Our Lord, how long must I beg for your help before you listen? How long before you save us from all this violence?
translation_verse: M Zugsɔba, nɔɔra ala ka m buoli fʋ bɔɔd sʋŋir ka fʋ pʋ wʋm tisi ma? M kaasi tisif ye, “Zaba kɔɔd na ye!” Ka fʋ pʋ faaɛn ma.

english_verse: Why do you make me watch such terrible injustice? Why do you allow violence, lawlessness, crime, and cruelty to spread everywhere?
translation_verse: Bɔ ka fʋ kɛ ka m gɔt linɛ ka' sida? Bɔ ka fʋ siakid linɛ pʋ dɔl suorɛ? San'auŋ nɛ zaba kɔɔdi kennɛ m tuon na; ka nɔŋgbannwa'ar nɛ zabbɔɔsim bɛ zin'ig wʋsa.

english_verse: Laws cannot be enforced; justice is always the loser; criminals crowd out honest people and twist the laws around. The Lord Answers Habakkuk
translation_verse: Alazug, wada la lɛn ka' paŋa ka sida mɛ lɛn kae. Nimbɛ'ɛdnam la namisidnɛ ninsʋma la, ka dinzug sida pʋ lɛn tʋm kɔɔtʋnamin laa. Zugsɔb la lɛbisʋg

english_verse: Look and be amazed at what's happening among the nations! Even if you were told, you would never believe what's taking place now.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Gɔsimi tɛɛns la, ka kɛ ka li lidigi ya. Man onɛ aan ya Wina'am la na tʋm tʋʋm tita'ar si'a ya zʋmaana nwa' ni, ka hali baa sɔ' ya'a pɛlig o pʋʋgʋ yɛli ya, ya kʋ siak ye li sid niŋyaa.

english_verse: I am sending the Babylonians. They are fierce and cruel— marching across the land, conquering cities and towns.
translation_verse: M ye m kɛnɛ ka Babilon dim banɛ an pitɔɔg dim nɛ zabzabidib ka ginnɛ zabid tɛɛns wʋsaa faand zin'ibanɛ ka' ba din la nyɛ paŋ.

english_verse: How fearsome and frightening. Their only laws and rules are the ones they make up.
translation_verse: Ba anɛ banɛ kpɛn'ɛsid tɛɛns dabiem pamm; ka sʋ'oe ba mɛŋi tʋm ban bɔɔd si'em, ka maan linɛ na tisi ba mɛŋ girima.

english_verse: Their cavalry troops are faster than leopards, more ferocious than wolves hunting at sunset, and swifter than hungry eagles suddenly swooping down.
translation_verse: Ba zaba widi zɔti gat wɛbaas zɔɔg, ka kpɛn'ɛsid nidib dabiem wʋʋ kunduna ka kɔ'ɔm zabid zaamnɔɔr. Ba soogianam la ban'adnɛ widii dɛɛd hali, ka ba wiedban'adib la mɛ yi kateŋ na. Ba ian'adnɛ nwɛnɛ zuundi ieed ni'im nɛ.

english_verse: They make fun of rulers and laugh at fortresses, while building dirt mounds so they can capture cities.
translation_verse: Ba tʋ'ʋdnɛ na'anam, ka la'ad teŋin dim wʋsa. Tembanɛ mɛ zaŋguoma giligi ba tɛɛns la, ba la'adi ba nɛ ka vaad tanni kpa'asidi digin ka li dʋʋ gaŋ zaŋguom la ka ba kpɛn' zabi nyaŋi ba.

english_verse: Then suddenly they disappear like a gust of wind— those sinful people who worship their own strength. Habakkuk Complains Again
translation_verse: Li nya'aŋ ka ba ku'oli vaae si'el mɛkama gaad wʋʋ sisi'em nɛ. Ninvʋbɛ'ɛd bama nɔki ba mɛŋ paŋ la ka li aan ba Wina'am.” Habakuk nyɔnyɔlʋg linɛ paas ayi'

english_verse: But you can't stand sin or wrong. So don't sit by in silence while they gobble up people who are better than they are.
translation_verse: Fʋ anɛ kasi galis nɛ fʋn na gɔsid bɛ'ɛd, bɛɛ siaki tis banɛ tʋm linɛ pʋ nara. Ka bɔzug kimm ka fʋ siaki tis ninvʋbɛ'ɛdnam nwa'? Bɔzug ka fʋ sin baanlimm, ka pitɔɔg dim kʋʋd nimbanɛ zɔt fʋn Wina'am gati ba la?

english_verse: The people you put on this earth are like fish or reptiles without a leader.
translation_verse: Fʋ kɛya ka saalib nwɛnɛ zimi bɛ atɛukʋn nɛ. Ba nwɛnɛ ku'omin bʋnvʋya banɛ ka' tuongata.

english_verse: Then an enemy comes along and takes them captive with hooks and nets. It makes him so happy
translation_verse: Ka tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd dim la yʋ'ʋn tɛɛdi ba dʋ'ʋsid nɛ gu'os, ka gban'adi ba nɛ zulis ka vɛ'ɛdi ba dʋ'ʋsid gbɛog na, dinzug ka o la'ad ka maan sumalisim.

english_verse: that he offers sacrifices to his fishing nets, because they make him rich and provide choice foods.
translation_verse: Alazug ba maan maana tisidi ba zulis la, ka kaanbidi tisidi ba saunam la. Ba yɛt ye la'abama zug ka ba paam diib, ka nyɛt bʋmmalisa dit.

english_verse: Will he keep hauling in his nets and destroying nations without showing mercy?
translation_verse: Ba na kpɛn pɛ'ɛnnɛ ba saunam la ka kpa'asid saŋa wʋsa? Ba na kpɛn san'amid tɛɛns la ka pʋ zɔt nimbaanliga?”

english_verse: While standing guard on the watchtower, I waited for the Lord's answer, before explaining the reason for my complaint.
translation_verse: Habakuk da lɛn yɛl ye, “M na zi'en m zi'esigin ka gur o. M na gɔs on na yɛl si'em tisim, nɛ mam na lɛbis o si'em mɛn.”

english_verse: Then the Lord told me: “I will give you my message in the form of a vision. Write it clearly enough to be read at a glance.
translation_verse: Ka Zugsɔb la lɛbis ye, “Sɔm man nie si'eli pa'alif la sʋ'ʋŋa niŋ linɛ an lammiri ni, ka onɛ mɔɔn zaŋi li zɔt ka karimi li.”

english_verse: At the time I have decided, my words will come true. You can trust what I say about the future. It may take a long time, but keep on waiting— it will happen!
translation_verse: Bɔzugɔ linɛ ka m nie pa'alif la mɔri li saŋa. Li yɛtnɛ naar saŋa yɛla, ka ka' ziri antu'aa. Li na nwɛnɛ li yuugidnɛ, amaa gurini li, ka li sid na kena ka kʋ yuugɛ.

english_verse: “I, the Lord, refuse to accept anyone who is proud. Only those who live by faith are acceptable to me.” Trouble for Evil People
translation_verse: Gɔsim nyɛɛsim sɔb! O sʋnfʋ bɔɔd si'el la ka' sʋ'ʋm baa bi'elaa. Amaa pʋpielim sɔb na vʋenɛ o yadda niŋir zug.

english_verse: Wine is treacherous, and arrogant people are never satisfied. They are no less greedy than death itself— they open their mouths as wide as the world of the dead and swallow everyone.
translation_verse: Nyɛɛsim sɔb la kpan'am ma'ad o ka o mɔr tita'alim ka li kɛ ka o pʋ vʋ'ʋsida; O anɛ dindiis nwɛnɛ yaʋgʋ an si'em la, ka nwɛnɛ kum pʋ tigid si'em la. O la'asid tɛɛns wʋsa sʋ'oe ka kɛ ka ba nidib la wʋsa kilim o sankpan'asnam.

english_verse: But they will be mocked with these words: You're doomed! You stored up stolen goods and cheated others of what belonged to them.
translation_verse: Sɔ' mɛkama na nɛ'ɛsid nidib nwa' ka maannɛ ba siaa yɛt ye, “Yɛltɔɔg bɛ yanam banɛ zu nidib la'adi kilim bʋmmɔrnam la zug! Ya mugusi ba nɛ pitɔɔlim ka paam kpan'am. Saŋa wala ka ya na kpɛn tʋm ala?”

english_verse: You robbed cities and nations everywhere on earth and murdered their people. Now those who survived will be as cruel to you.
translation_verse: Fʋn da faand tɛɛns bɛdegʋ la zug, nimbanɛ kpɛlim la mɛ na faaɛn fʋ kpan'am la. Fʋ da kpa'ae saalib ziim hali ka san'am tɛɛns nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ anina la wʋsa.

english_verse: You're doomed! You made your family rich at the expense of others. You even said to yourself, “I'm above the law.”
translation_verse: Yɛltɔɔg bɛɛ tis onɛ dɔl suobɛ'ɛdi paam kpan'am mɛɛ o yir, fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ mɔrim la na gu' fʋn nɛ fʋ yidim, ka san'auŋ da paae yaa.

english_verse: But you will bring shame on your family and ruin to yourself for what you did to others.
translation_verse: Fʋn gban'e ye fʋ san'am nidib bɛdegʋ si'em la, fʋ na kɔ'ɔŋi fʋ nyɔvʋr ka diisi fʋ yidim nyan.

english_verse: The very stones and wood in your home will testify against you.
translation_verse: Dɔkpina la kuga na kaasid, ka daad la maan tʋkpiidʋgʋ suakid.

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful sends up in flames what nations and people work so hard to gain.
translation_verse: Li ka'anɛ Zugsɔb Wina'am onɛ an Paŋtita'ar Sɔb la kɛ ka nidib la tʋm tʋʋma ka bugum dii li wʋsa, ka buudi wʋsa namisʋg la an zaalim?

english_verse: Just as water fills the sea, the land will be filled with people who know and honor the Lord.
translation_verse: Saŋa kenna ka teŋgbauŋ wʋsa na ti pɛ'ɛl nɛ Zugsɔb girima wʋʋ ku'om pɛ'ɛl atɛuk si'em la.

english_verse: You're doomed! You get your friends drunk, just to see them naked.
translation_verse: Yɛltɔɔg bɛ ninkanɛ kɛ ka o kpi'es nu daam bug on bɔɔd ye o gɔsi ba nyan la zug.

english_verse: Now you will be disgraced instead of praised. The Lord will make you drunk, and when others see you naked, you will lose their respect.
translation_verse: Fʋn naan nyɛɛn girima la, nyannɛ ye li diif. Li mɛ paaf yʋ'ʋs! Num bug ka ba gɔsi fʋ nyan! Zugsɔb sʋnpɛɛn na paaf nwɛnɛ ban na tis danuud daam ka o nuu kʋʋl, ka nyan dii o ka o pʋ lɛm mɔr girima si'em la.

english_verse: You destroyed trees and animals on Mount Lebanon; you were ruthless to towns and people everywhere. Now you will be terrorized. Idolatry Is Foolish
translation_verse: Fʋn namis Lebanon teŋgbauŋ ka kʋ o bʋnkɔnbid si'em la, ala ka namisʋg na paaf. Fʋ da kpa'ae saalib ziim ka san'am tɛɛns nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ anina wʋsa.

english_verse: What is an idol worth? It's merely a false god. Why trust a speechless image made from wood or metal by human hands?
translation_verse: Ba'ar nyɔɔd lɛɛ an bɔ? Ka' ninsaali zaŋ o nu'ugʋ maalɛɛ? Bɛɛ bʋnkanɛ ka ba mɛɛ lii zi'el ka mɔri pan'asid nidib la? Onɛ ya'abi li la niŋ on maal si'el la yadda, o maal ba'ar ka li pʋ tun'e pian'ada.

english_verse: What can you learn from idols covered with silver or gold? They can't even breathe. Pity anyone who says to an idol of wood or stone, “Get up and do something!”
translation_verse: Yɛltɔɔg bɛ onɛ yɛl daug ye, “Paamim vʋm!” Bɛɛ yɛl kugir ye, “Duom keŋ!” Li na nyaŋi guri fɔɔ? Ba nɔknɛ sanlima nɛ anzurifa buligi li, ka nyɔvʋr ka' li nii.

english_verse: Let all the world be silent— the Lord is present in his holy temple.
translation_verse: Amaa Zugsɔb Wina'am bɛɛ o Pʋ'ʋsim Yir linɛ an kasi la ni; kɛl ka dunia wʋsa an baanlimm o tuon!

english_verse: This is my prayer:
translation_verse: Habakuk onɛ an Wina'am nɔdi'es la winsɔsʋgʋ nwana:

english_verse: I know your reputation, Lord, and I am amazed at what you have done. Please turn from your anger and be merciful; do for us what you did for our ancestors.
translation_verse: “Zugsɔba, m wʋmi fʋ yʋ'ʋr la dʋ si'em, ka fʋ tʋʋma kɛ ka dabiem gban'am. Maligim tʋmi li taaba tinam saŋa nwa', kɛl ka ba baŋi fʋ tʋʋmnyalima la zʋmaʋŋ kaŋa nwa', ka zɔɔ ti nimbaanligi fʋ sʋnpɛɛn saŋa.

english_verse: You are the same Holy God who came from Teman and Paran to help us. The brightness of your glory covered the heavens, and your praises were heard everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Wina'am nie o mɛŋi yit Teman teŋgbauŋʋn na, Kasi Sɔb la yinɛ Paran zuorin na. O girima pɛ'ɛl arezana wʋsa, ka o zʋn'or tiig dunia la.

english_verse: Your glory shone like the sun, and light flashed from your hands, hiding your mighty power.
translation_verse: O nɛɛsim nwɛnɛ winnigi na tansid nɛ, ka niedi yit o nu'usin na, anina ka o paŋ la su'a.

english_verse: Dreadful diseases and plagues marched in front and followed behind.
translation_verse: O kɛ ka ban'abɛ'ɛd bɛɛ o tuon, ka wiim dɔl o nya'aŋ.

english_verse: When you stopped, the earth shook; when you stared, nations trembled; when you walked along your ancient paths, eternal mountains and hills crumbled and collapsed.
translation_verse: O ya'a zi'en ka teŋgbauŋ wʋsa mi'im, ka o gɔs ka buudi zan' kirid; ka zuokʋda dam, ka kʋkʋn kʋda lu. O suoya wʋsa anɛ linɛ ka' naarɛ.

english_verse: The tents of desert tribes in Cushan and Midian were ripped apart.
translation_verse: Ka m nyɛ ka Kusan teŋgbauŋ sʋga san'am, ka Midian dim la wʋsa sʋnya mɛ san'am.

english_verse: Our Lord, were you angry with the monsters of the deep? You attacked in your chariot and wiped them out.
translation_verse: M Zugsɔba, fʋ sʋnf duonɛ nɛ kɔldaad laa? Bɛɛ fʋ sʋnfʋ pɛlig nɛ ku'osuoya la? Fʋ sʋʋnri daa duoe nɛ Atɛuk la zug ka fʋ ban'a fʋ widi, nɛ fʋ zaba tɛrekonamɛ zabi nyaŋɛɛ?

english_verse: Your arrows were ready and obeyed your commands. You split the earth apart with rivers and streams;
translation_verse: Fʋ yisi fʋ tiraugʋ ti'eb, ka fuoe piema bɛdegʋ. Fʋ nɔk kɔldaadi buak teŋgbauŋ la.

english_verse: mountains trembled at the sight of you; rain poured from the clouds; ocean waves roared and rose.
translation_verse: Zuoya wʋmi fʋ dammir ka mi'im, ka ku'om la pʋbid nɛ ku'onwiisi gat; ku'ozuluŋ la dammid ka li ku'opila dʋt agɔla.

english_verse: The sun and moon stood still, while your arrows and spears flashed like lightning.
translation_verse: Winnig nɛ nwadig da zi'enɛ ki' agɔla ka pʋ lɛn kenna, li anɛ fʋ piema nɛ fʋ kpan linɛ ian'ad wʋʋ sa-ian'asʋg la zug,

english_verse: to rescue your people and save your chosen one. You crushed a nation's ruler and stripped his evil kingdom of its power.
translation_verse: Fʋ yina ye fʋ faaɛn fʋ nidibi bas, nɛ fʋ Na'ab kanɛ ka fʋ gaŋ la. Fʋ nwɛ' nimbɛ'ɛdnam tuongat la, ka faaɛn o nidib la ka kɛ o zaalim.

english_verse: His troops had come like a storm, hoping to scatter us and glad to gobble us up. To them we were refugees in hiding— but you smashed their heads with their own weapons.
translation_verse: O mɛŋ kpan ka fʋ da nɔki kʋns o zug, saŋa kan ka o zabzabidib kenna nwɛnɛ sisi'etita'ari ye ba widigi ti la, ka niŋid nwɛnɛ ba ye ba vɔlnɛ nɔŋ dim banɛ zɔɔ su'a la.

english_verse: Then your chariots churned the waters of the sea. Habakkuk's Response to God's Message
translation_verse: Fʋ da kɛ ka fʋ widi la nɔ atɛuk la, ka dammid ku'ozulima wʋsa.

english_verse: When I heard this message, I felt weak from fear, and my lips quivered. My bones seemed to melt, and I stumbled around. But I will patiently wait. Someday those vicious enemies will be struck by disaster. Trust in a Time of Trouble
translation_verse: Man wʋm la m ya'am iank nɛ ka m nɔɔr kirid, ka m sʋʋnr tuod kpiu-kpiu, ka m kɔnba nwa'ad, ka m nɔba kirid. Amaa la'an nɛ wala m mɔdigid ye m nyɛ daakanɛ ka tɔɔg na paae banɛ faandi ti la.”

english_verse: Fig trees may no longer bloom, or vineyards produce grapes; olive trees may be fruitless, and harvest time a failure; sheep pens may be empty, and cattle stalls vacant—
translation_verse: Habakuk da lɛm pʋ'ʋs ye, “Hali baa kekaŋ la pʋ pu puum la, ka tiis wala mɛ nan kae la; hali baa olif tiis la pʋ walɛ, ka teŋ la zʋʋd pʋ maal la; hali baa kɔnbidi ka' bʋlʋʋginɛ, ka niigi mɛ ka' baukʋn la,

english_verse: but I will still celebrate because the Lord God is my Savior.
translation_verse: la'an nɛ wala wʋsa mam na mɔr sumalisim Zugsɔb san'an; m sʋnf na ma'ae, Wina'am onɛ aan m faangid la zug.

english_verse: The Lord gives me strength. He makes my feet as sure as those of a deer, and he helps me stand on the mountains. To the music director: Use stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Zugsɔb Wina'am aan m paŋ. O maali m nɔba ka li nwɛnɛ walig nɔba nɛ, ka m kpɛn ken tuonnɛ dʋt kʋkʋna nɛ zuoya ka pʋ tu'ugida.” Yʋʋmyʋ'ʋmnib tuongat la din. Ba yʋ'ʋmmi li nɛ googi.

english_verse: I am Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah. When Josiah son of Amon was king of Judah, the Lord gave me this message. Judgment on Judah
translation_verse: Zugsɔb da tis o nɔdi'es Zefanaya onɛ an Kus biig la labaar. Kus da anɛ Gedalaya biig ka Gedalaya mɛ an Amaraya biig ka Amaraya an Hezekia biig. Saŋkan la ka Josia onɛ da an Ammon biig la da zin' na'am gbauŋ zug, Juda teŋgbauŋʋn. San'auŋ linɛ kenna la yɛla
