translation_verse: Ka dasaŋ sɔ' onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Yutikus da bɛɛ ani ka zin' dɔɔg la takoro zug. Ka Paul kpɛm pian'adi ken tuon la, ka gbɛn'um gban'e o, ka o gbisi naam dɔkanɛ bɛɛ agɔl la zugʋ li teŋin na. Ka ba ʋk o duoe ka o pʋn kpi sa.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul sig teŋin keŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ bibig o ka ye, “Da kɛ ka li paki ya; ka o nan vʋe.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Paul daa lɛbi dʋʋ gbin'es bodobodo ɔnb ka sɔns nɛ ba yuug. Ka bɛog nie ka o basi ba ka keŋ.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Ka ba dɔl dasaŋ la kul. Ka o vʋe, ka li niŋi ba sumalisim bɛdegʋ. Paul paae Miletus teŋin

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Ka ti kpɛn' anrʋŋʋ dɛŋ Paul tuonnɛ keŋ Assos teŋin, on ye o keŋ nɛ nɔba la zug.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: On tʋ'ʋsi ti Assos teŋin la o la'am kpɛn' anrʋŋ la nɛ ti keŋ Mitilene teŋin.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka ti yi Mitilene teŋin keŋ Kios teŋ baba. Ka bɛog nie ya'as ka ti paae Samos teŋin na. Ka li yimbɛogʋn ya'as ka ti paae Miletus teŋin.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Paul n da bɔɔd ye o bɛ Jerusalem ka Pentekost daar naan paae la zug, o da kpɛn' anrʋŋʋ luak Efesus, on pʋ bɔɔd ye o yuug Asia sʋ'ʋlimin la zug. Paul pian' tis Efesus yadda niŋidib kpɛɛmnam

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Ka Paul naam Miletus teŋin tɔlim Efesus teŋin ye yadda niŋidib kpɛɛmnam la tʋ'ʋs o na.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Ka ban paae o san'an na la, o yɛli ba ye, “Ya mi' man daa bɛ bɛllim si'a nɛ ya daakanɛ ka m paae Asia sʋ'ʋlimin kpɛla hali nɛ zina.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: M daa sigisi m mɛŋi tʋm Wina'am tʋʋma nɛ ninta'am ka siaki di'e mugusʋg linɛ daa yi Jew dim makirin na.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: La'an nɛ wala, ya mi' ye m daa pʋ zan'as ye m tu'asi ya bʋn linɛ na sʋŋi yaa. Amaa m daa pa'ali ya paalʋ nɛ ya yaan,

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: ka pian' nɛ nimmua tis Jew dim nɛ banɛ ka' Jew dim la ye ba fɛndigim dɔl Wina'am ka niŋ Zugsɔb Yesu yadda.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: “Nannanna m siak Wina'am Siig Kasi nɔɔr ye m keŋ Jerusalem ka zi' linɛ na niŋim aninaa.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: M mi' ye man paae tempʋsi'a ni wʋsa, Siig Kasi la pa'annim ye ba na lɔɔm ka namisim ka kpɛn'ɛsim sanrega ani.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Amaa m gɔs ka m nyɔvʋr anɛ zaalim, man on ya'a nyaŋi zɔ zɔɔg la paae li bɛn, ka tʋm tʋʋm kanɛ ka m Zugsɔb Yesu tisim ye m mɔɔl Wina'am pʋpielim labasʋŋ la.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: “M mi' ye yanam banɛ ka m mɔɔl Wina'am na'am yɛla ya san'an la kʋ nyɛɛm ya'asɛ.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Dinzug ka m yɛti ya zin'ikaŋa ye ya yinne ya'a bɔdig m ba'a lɛn ka' o ni la.

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: M mɔɔli tisi ya Wina'am yɛla wʋsa ka pʋ su'a si'ela.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Gu'usimi ya mɛŋ ka gur nimbanɛ wʋsa ka Wina'am Siig Kasi la gu'uli ya la. Guri Wina'am nimbanɛ ka o da' nɛ o Biig la ziim la.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: M mi' ye m ya'a basi ya, nimbɛ'ɛdnam na kɛɛn ya san'an na gban'e ya wʋʋ zaŋku'ari gban'ad kɔnbid si'em la.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Hali ninsieba na yii ya sʋʋgin na tiak yɛlsida ka ma' yadda niŋidib la pi'e ba keŋi ba san'an.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ gu'usiminɛ ya mɛŋ ka tɛnr ye yʋma atan' nwa' ka m sa'annɛ ya nɛ nimmua nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ wʋsa nɛ ninta'am ka pʋ basɛ.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: “Nannanna m zaŋi ya niŋ Wina'am nu'usin nɛ o pʋpielim pian'ad linɛ na kpɛmisi ya yadda ka kɛ ka ya la'as nɛ Wina'am maal ninsieba ka ba an nyain la.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: M daa pʋ mɔr ya'amlɛog nɛ sɔ' anzurifa bɛɛ sanlima bɛɛ fuudɛ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: M tʋm nɛ m mɛŋ nu'usi diisidi m mɛŋ nɛ m dɔllim taas la.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: M pa'ali ya si'el mɛkama wʋsa ye, asɛɛ ka ya sʋŋ tadimnam nɛ ba tʋʋma pʋʋgin nwɛnɛ man daa niŋid si'em la, ka tɛnr pian'ad linɛ ka ti Zugsɔb Yesu daa yɛl la ye, ‘Albareka bɛ nɛ onɛ tisidi gat onɛ di'ed.’”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Paul n pian' nɛ'ɛŋa naae la ka igin teŋin nɛ o taaba la wʋsa pʋ'ʋs Wina'am.

english_verse: Everyone cried and hugged and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ka ba wʋsa kaasi bibid Paul ka kɛɛs o.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Ba sʋnya daa san'amnɛ hali on yɛl ye, ba kʋ lɛn nyɛɛ o la. Ka ba biel o keŋ anrʋŋʋn la.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Ka ti kɛɛsi ba ka kpɛn' anrʋŋʋ kpa' keŋ Kos teŋin paae ani. Ka bɛog nie ka ti paae Rodes teŋin ka naam anina keŋ Patara teŋin.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Ani ka ti nyɛ anrʋŋ ka li wa'ae Fonisia teŋin ka ti kpɛn' keŋ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Ka ti paae zin'isi'a ka gɔsi nyɛ Saipuros ka li bɛ tuon sa ka ti bas ka dɔl dagɔbʋg la ka luaki gaadi yi Siriya sʋ'ʋlim sig Taya teŋin, zin'ikan ka ba ye ba sigis anrʋŋ la la'ad la.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Amaa ti saŋa paae la ka ti kɛɛsi ba ka gaad. Ka ban nɛ ba pu'ab nɛ ba biis wʋsa bieli ti yi teŋ la kpikpɛŋ. Ka ti wʋsa igin teŋin atɛuk nɔɔrini pʋ'ʋs Wina'am ka kɛɛs taaba.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Ka tinam kpɛn' anrʋŋʋn, ka ba mɛ lɛbi kul.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Ka ti yi Taya teŋin keŋ Tolemais teŋin pʋ'ʋs yadda niŋidib banɛ bɛ anina la, ka gbɛɛn ba san'an daar yinne.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka ti yi anina keŋ Sizerea teŋin kpɛn' Filip yinnɛ zin'in anina. O da anɛ onɛ mɔɔn Wina'am labaar, ka an kpɛɛmnam ayɔpɔi la ni yinne, ban ka ba da gaŋ Jerusalem teŋin ye ba tɔnd diib la.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: O da mɔr pu'ayuos anaasi ka ba an yiwies ka mɛ an Wina'am nɔdi'esidib.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Ka ti da bɛɛ anina dabisa bi'ela ka Wina'am nɔdi'es onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Agabus yi Juda paae na

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: ka kɛɛn ti san'an na fuoe Paul sɛnbidiŋi lɔɔ o mɛŋ nɔba nɛ o nu'us ka yɛl ye, “Wina'am Siig Kasi la yɛl si'em nwa', ‘Jew dim na lɔ sialɔɔdiŋ kaŋa nwa' daan anwana Jerusalem teŋin nɔk o niŋ banɛ ka' Jew dim la nu'usin.’”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Tinamɛ wʋm nɛ'ɛŋa la ka tinam nɛ nimbanɛ bɛɛ anina la bɛllim Paul ye o da keŋ Jerusalem.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Amaa ka o lɛbis ye, “Bɔ ka ya kaasidi san'amidi m sʋnfɔ? M pʋ ti'eb ye ba lɔɔm Jerusalem teŋin ma'aanɛɛ, amaa m la'am na kpi ani ti Zugsɔb Yesu yʋ'ʋr zug.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Ka ti pʋ nyaŋ o ka o siaki tisi tii. Ka ti bas o ka yɛl ye, “Zugsɔb bɔɔdim niŋim.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ti da bɛ nɛ anina dabisa bi'ela ka nyaan ti'ebi keŋ Jerusalem.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Ka Sizerea teŋ nya'andɔlib sieba bieli ti mɔri ti keŋ Mason yin ye ti bɛɛ anina. Mason da anɛ Saipuros nid onɛ da an nya'andɔl pin'ilʋgʋn sa. Paul paae Jerusalem

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Ka ti paae Jerusalem na ka yadda niŋidib di'e ti nɛ sumalisim.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka Paul dɔlli ti keŋ Jemes san'an. Ka yadda niŋidib kpɛɛmnam wʋsa bɛ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ka Paul pʋ'ʋsi ba ka tu'asi ba Wina'am dɔlis o tʋʋma pʋʋgin maal si'el wʋsa tis banɛ ka' Jew dim la.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ka ban wʋm la ka dʋ'ʋs Wina'am yʋ'ʋr sʋ'ʋŋa ka yɛl Paul ye, “Ti ba'abiiga, gɔsim lin an si'em. Jew dim tusa bɛdegʋ niŋ Yesu yadda, ka mɔr wada kanɛ ka Wina'am tis Moses la sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Ti wʋm ye fʋ pa'al Jew dim wʋsa banɛ zin' nɛ banɛ ka' Jew dim la tɛɛnsin ye ba basim Moses wada, ka da kpɛn'ɛsi ba biis baŋʋ bɛɛ dɔl Jew dim malimaa.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Ba na wʋm ye fʋ kena. Bɔ ka ti na niŋɛ?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Kɛl ka ti yɛlif tinamɛ tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ niŋ si'em. Nidib anaasi bɛɛ ti san'an kpɛla pɔ ye ba na maal si'eli tis Wina'am.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Dɔlli ba keŋ ka la'as nɛ ba ka ya pie ya mɛŋi ba malʋŋ la zug, ka yɔɔ ba sama la tisi ba, ka ba nyaŋi pʋni ba zuobid. Nɛ'ɛŋa na kɛ ka sɔ' wʋsa baŋ ye linɛ ka ba pian' fʋ yɛla la ka' sidaa, amaa fʋn mɛ dɔlisidnɛ wada la yɛl ye ti niŋim si'em la.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Amaa li ya'a anɛ banɛ ka' Jew dima ka niŋ yadda la, ti daa sɔb gbauŋʋ yɛli ba ye, ‘Ba da di ba'ar diib bɛɛ di ziim. Ka da ɔnb bʋnkɔnbʋg kanɛ ka ba sianki kʋʋ. Ka dap nɛ pu'ab da san'am taabaa.’”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka Paul nɔk nidib la ka ba pie ba mɛŋ malʋŋ la yɛla. Ka lin nya'aŋ ka o keŋ Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la zi'el dabiskanɛ ka mɛŋ pier malʋŋ la na naae, ka sɔ' wʋsa na maal o maannɛ tis Wina'am. Ba gban'e Paul Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Lin da kpɛlim bi'ela ka daba ayɔpɔi la naae la, ka Jew dim banɛ yi Asia sʋ'ʋlim na nyɛ Paul Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin, ka kɛ ka nidib la sʋnya pɛlig nɛ Paul ka ba gban'e o.

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Ka tans ye, “Israel dima, sʋŋimi ti! Dau kaŋa nwa' giligid tɛɛns wʋsa pa'an nidib ye ba da dɔl Israel dim nɛ Moses wada nɛ Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yir malʋŋ laa. Hali o mɔr banɛ ka' Jew dim la kpɛn' Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la naa miligi li.”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: Ban nyɛ Trofimus onɛ yi Efesus na ka o dɔl Paul la zug, ka tɛn'ɛs ye o dɔl o nɛ kpɛn' Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Ka teŋ la dam ka nidib wʋsa zɔɔ la'as taaba gban'e Paul n tɛɛg o yis Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la. Ka yɔ za'anɔya la tɔ'ɔtɔ.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Ka bɔɔd ye ba kʋ Paul. Ka labaar paae Room soogia kpɛɛm san'an na ye Jerusalem wʋsa dam nɛ.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Ka o duoe tɔ'ɔtɔ dɔl soogianam nɛ ba kpɛɛmnam ka ba zɔɔ keŋ nidibin la. Ka ban nyɛ soogia kpɛɛm nɛ soogianam la ka bas Paul bʋ'ʋb.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Ka soogia kpɛɛm la keŋ gban'e Paul ka tis soogianam nɔɔr ye ba lɔɔm o nɛ bana ayi'. Ka bu'os on an sɔ' nɛ on niŋ si'el.

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ka nidib la daa tansidi pian'ad kɔn'ɔb-kɔn'ɔb ka tʋkpiidʋg la zu'oe hali ka kpɛɛm la daa pʋ nyaŋi wʋm linɛ maal la, o daa tis soogianam nɔɔr ye ba nɔkim o dʋʋ ba yitita'arin la.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ka ba mɔr o paae ban dʋt si'eli kpɛn'ɛd dɔɔgin la ka soogianam la zii o kpɛn', nidib la bugusim zug.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Ka ba wʋsa kenna tansid ye, “Kʋʋmi nɛ o.” Paul tu'a ye o yis o mɛŋ

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Ka ban ye ba kpɛn'ɛs Paul soogianam yin la, ka o yɛl soogia kpɛɛm la ye, “M mɔr si'el ye m yɛl.” Ka kpɛɛm la bu'os o ye, “Fʋ wʋm Girik dim pian'adɛɛ?

english_verse: “Aren't you that Egyptian who started a riot not long ago and led
translation_verse: Alaa fʋ ka' Egipt nid onɛ daa zigid ye o kad gɔmena, ka daa dɔl ninkʋʋdib tusa anaasi keŋ mɔɔgin la?”

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul lɛbis ye, “M anɛ Jew nid ka yi Tarsus teŋin linɛ bɛ Silisia teŋgbauŋʋn la. M anɛ teŋ tita'ar nid. M sɔsidif ye fʋ kɛ ka m pian' tis nidib la.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛm la bas o nɔɔr. Ka Paul zi'e ban dʋt si'eli kpɛn'ɛd dɔɔgin la zug, ka ʋk o nu'ug ka nidib la fɔn baanlimm, ka o pian' tisi ba nɛ Hibiru pian'ad ye,

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Ban wʋm ka o pian'adi tisidi ba nɛ Hibiru pian'ad la ka ba sin baanlimm, ka o ye,

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Mam anɛ Jew nid ka ba du'am Tarsus linɛ bɛ Silisia teŋgbauŋʋn la. Amaa ba ugus man nɛ teŋ kaŋa ni. Ka Gamaliel zamisim ka m zamisi ti yaanam wada la sʋ'ʋŋa. M sʋnf lɔnɛ Wina'am yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa nwɛnɛ yanamɛ niŋid si'em zina la.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: M da namis banɛ dɔl suokaŋa hali kʋʋdi ba, ka gban'ad dap nɛ pu'abi kpɛn'ɛsidi ba sanrega ni.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Wina'am maanmaan kpɛɛm nɛ kpɛɛmnam wʋsa na nyaŋi di man kasɛt ye m pian'ad la anɛ sida. M da di'e gbana ba san'anɛ tis Jew dim banɛ bɛ Damaskus, ka wa'ae anina ye m gban'e suokaŋa nya'andɔlib banɛ bɛ anina lɔɔ ba nɛ bana mɔri ba lɛb Jerusalem na namisi ba.” Paul tu'as o tiakir la yɛla (Tʋm

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Man da kennɛ paad Damaskus nintaŋ tisʋʋs saŋa la, ka nɛɛsim tita'ar yi saazug na nie nyain giligim.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Ka m li teŋin ka wʋm ka kʋkɔr buolim ye, ‘Saul, Saul, bɔ ka fʋ namisidi ma?’”

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Ka m bu'os o ye, “Naa, fʋ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ m Zugsɔba?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “M anɛ Yesu, onɛ an Nazaret nid onɛ ka fʋ namisid la.”

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Ka nimbanɛ daa bɛɛ m san'an la nyɛ nɛɛsim la, amaa ka pʋ gban'e kʋkɔr kanɛ pian'ad la gbinnɛ.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Ka m bu'os ye, “Zugsɔba, m na niŋ wala?” Ka m Zugsɔb la yɛlim ye, “Duom kpɛn' Damaskus, ka anina ka ba na yɛlif linɛ wʋsa ka Wina'am zi'eli tisif ye fʋ tʋm.”

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Ka m pʋ nyɛta, nɛɛsim la kɛ ka m zu'om la zug. Ka banɛ dɔllim la vɛ'ɛm, ka ti keŋ kpɛn' Damaskus.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Dau da bɛ anina, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Ananias. O da anɛ onɛ dɔlisidi ti wada la ka Jew dim banɛ bɛ Damaskus wʋsa pian'ad o yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Ka o kɛɛn m san'an na ka yɛl ye, ‘M ba'abiig Saul, lakim.’ Saŋkan yim ka m nini lak ka m nyɛt.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Ka o yɛlim ye, ‘Wina'am onɛ ka ti yaanam da pʋ'ʋsid la gaŋif ye fʋ baŋ o bɔɔdim ka nyɛ on an pʋpielim sɔb si'em, ka wʋm ka o pian'ad nɛ o mɛŋ kʋkɔr.

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: Fʋ na yɛl nidib wʋsa fʋn nyɛ ka wʋm si'el la.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Fʋ gur bɔ? Duom ka di'e Wina'am Ku'om sʋʋb, ka buol Yesu yʋ'ʋr ka o pie fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi bas.’”

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: “Ka m lɛbis ye, ‘M Zugsɔba, nimbama mi' sʋ'ʋŋa ye m daa ken la'asʋg dɔɔdin wʋsa gban'ad banɛ niŋif yadda la bʋ'ʋdi ba ka kpɛn'ɛsidi ba sanrega ni.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Saŋkan ka ba da kʋ Sitivin onɛ tu'asid nidibi fʋ yɛla la, m da bɛɛ anina ka tɛn'ɛsid ye ban niŋid si'el la anɛ sʋm, ka gur banɛ kʋʋ o la fuud.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: “Ka Zugsɔb yɛlim ye, ‘Kem, ka m ye m tʋmif nɛ banɛ ka' Jew dim ka bɛ lalli la san'an.’” Nidibi bɔɔd ye ba kʋ Paul la

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la kɛlis Paul hali ka o ti pian' nɛ'ɛŋa, ka ba pin'ili tansid ye, “Kʋʋminɛ o ka o pʋ nar ye o bɛ dunia nii.”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Ka ba tansid ka mɔri ba fuudi yuulim agɔla ka gbɛn'ɛsid titani yaaridi agɔla.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Ka soogia kpɛɛm la tis soogianam la nɔɔr ye ba nɔkim Paul n kpɛn'ɛsi ba yin la ka fieb o ka bu'os o baŋ linɛ kɛ ka nidib la tansid o wala la.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Amaa ban lɔɔ o ye ba fieb o la, ka o bu'os soogia kpɛɛm onɛ zi'e anina la ye, “Suor bɛɛ ya wada ni ye ya fieb Room nid ka ba nam pʋ kad o saria?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Ka soogia kpɛɛm la wʋm ala la, ka o keŋ onɛ sʋ'oe ba wʋsa la san'anɛ bu'os o ye, “Bɔ ka fʋ ye fʋ maal ala? Dau nwa' anɛ Room teŋ nid.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Ka soogianam la kpɛɛm keŋ Paul san'anɛ bu'os o ye, “Fʋ anɛ Room nida?” Ka o lɛbis ye, “Ɛɛn.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Ka soogia kpɛɛm la yɛl ye, “Mam mɛ anɛ Room nid, amaa m daa yɔnɛ ligidi bɛdegʋ ka nyaan lieb teŋ la nid.” Ka Paul ye, “Amaa ba du'a man nɛ Room teŋin ka m an Room nid.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Ka banɛ pa'a ye ba fieb o la lɛb nya'aŋ tɔ'ɔtɔ. Ka soogianam kpɛɛm la zɔ dabiem, on baŋ ye Paul anɛ Room nid ka o kɛ ka ba lɔɔ o la zug. Paul zi'e Jew dim kpɛɛmnam tuon

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka kpɛɛm la bɔɔd ye o baŋ linɛ zug kimm ka Jew dim la zi'e Paul yɛla, ka o yidig Paul, ka tis nɔɔr ye Wina'am maanmaan kpɛɛmnam nɛ teŋ kpɛɛmnam wʋsa la'asim na. Ka ba la'as. Ka o mɔr o keŋ zi'eli ba tuon.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Ka Paul gɔsid kpɛɛmnam la kii ka yɛl ye, “M ba'abiisɛ, man pʋtɛn'ɛr anɛ nyain Wina'am san'an m biilimin sa paae zina.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Ka maanmaan kpɛɛm Ananias tis nɔɔr ye banɛ zi'e kpi'e Paul la nwɛ'ɛm o nɔɔr.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul yɛl o ye, “Wina'am na nwɛ'ɛf. Fʋ nwɛnɛ zaŋguom kʋdig kanɛ ka ba taae. Ka yiŋ vɛnl, ka pʋʋgin ka' sʋm la. Fʋ zin' kad man saria, wada la yɛla, amaa fʋ san'am wada la, fʋn tis nɔɔr ye ba nwɛ' man la.”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Ka banɛ zi'e kpi'e Paul la yɛl o ye, “Fʋ tʋ'ʋdnɛ Wina'am maanmaan kpɛɛm?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “M ba'abiisɛ, m zi' ye o anɛ Wina'am maanmaan kpɛɛm. Bɔzugɔ Wina'am gbauŋʋn li sɔb ye, ‘Mid ka fʋ pɔ nɔɔri niŋ tuongat onɛ guri fʋ nidib la.’”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul baŋ ye sieba an Sadusii dim, ka sieba an Farisii dim la, ka yɛl kpɛɛmnam la'asʋgʋn la ye, “M ba'abiisɛ, mam nɛ m yaanam anɛ Farisii dim. Mam mɔr ti'ir ye banɛ kpi la na lɛn vʋ'ʋg la zug ka m bɛ yɛla ni la.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: On yɛl nɛ'ɛŋa la ka Farisii dim nɛ Sadusii dim la pin'ili nwa'asid nɛ taaba, ka nidib la wɛlig.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Sadusii dim la pʋ siak ye kum vʋ'ʋgir nɛ maliaknam nɛ siis bɛɛ, amaa Farisii dim siaki li wʋsa.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Ka tʋkpiidʋg duoe Paul yɛla. Ka gbauŋmi'idib sieba banɛ an Farisii dim duoe nwa'as nɛ paŋ ye, “Ti pʋ nyɛ dau kaŋa nwa' tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdɛ. Daasi'erɛɛ li anɛ siig bɛɛ maliaki pian' tis o.”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ka nɔŋgbannwa'ar la kena galis, ka soogia kpɛɛm la zɔ dabiem ye ba na aans Paul zɔra-zɔra, ka tis soogianam nɔɔr ye ba kem faaɛn o nidib la san'anɛ mɔr o kpɛn' soogianam yin la.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ kan la ka Zugsɔb la kɛn Paul san'an na yɛl o ye, “Kpɛ'ɛŋimi fʋ sʋnf; ka li nar ka fʋ tu'asi m yɛla Room teŋin, wʋʋ fʋn tu'asi m yɛla Jerusalem teŋin kpɛla si'em la.” Paul gban'ar la yɛla

english_verse: The next morning more than
translation_verse: Banɛ da la'asi gban'e nɛ'ɛŋa la da gaad nidib pisnaasi.

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Ka ba keŋ maanmaan kpɛɛmnam nɛ kpɛɛmnam san'anɛ yɛl ye, “Ti la'asi pɔ nɔɔr ye ti kʋ di si'ela asɛɛ tinamɛ na ti kʋ Paul.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Dinzug fʋn nɛ kpɛɛmnam la'asim ka tʋm soogia kpɛɛm la san'an ye o mɔr Paul n kɛɛn ya san'an na, ka niŋ nwɛnɛ ya bɔɔd ye ya wʋm o yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa; ka tinam ti'eb ye ti kʋ o hali ka o nam pʋ paae naa.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Ka Paul taʋn biig wʋm ban gban'e si'em la ka keŋ soogianam yin la yɛl Paul.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul buol soogia kpɛɛmnam la yinne yɛl o ye, “Dasaŋ kaŋa mɔr si'el ye o yɛli ya kpɛɛm la. Dinzugɔ dɔl o keŋ.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Ka soogia kpɛɛm la mɔr biig la keŋi ba kpɛɛm la san'anɛ yɛl ye, “Paul onɛ an sanrega nid la, buolim ye m mɔr dasaŋ kaŋa kɛɛn fʋ san'an na; ka o mɔr si'el ye o yɛlif.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛm la gban'e o nu'ugʋ mɔr o yi kpikpɛŋi bu'os o ye, “Fʋ mɔr bɔ ye fʋ yɛli ma?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Ka o lɛbis ye, “Jew dim gban'aya ye bɛog ba na sɔsif ye fʋ mɔr Paul n kɛɛn ba kpɛɛmnam la'asʋgʋn la na. Ka niŋ nwɛnɛ ba bɔɔd ye ba wʋm o yɛla sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Ka kpɛɛm la yɛl dasaŋ la ye, “Da yɛl sɔ' ye fʋ yɛlɛ m si'ela.” Ka kɛ ka o keŋ. Soogia kpɛɛm zaŋ Paul tis gɔmena Felik

english_verse: The commander called in two of his officers and told them, “By nine o'clock tonight have
translation_verse: Ka o buol o soogia kpɛɛmnama ayi' yɛli ba ye, “La'asim soogianam kɔbisyi', nɛ wiedban'adib pisyɔpɔi nɛ kpantɔɔndib kɔbisyi', ka ba ti'eb yʋ'ʋŋ kaŋa kɛrefa awai keŋ Sizerea.

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Ka tis Paul widi ka o ban', ka mɔr o baanlimm keŋ gɔmena Felik san'an.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Ka o sɔb gbauŋʋ yɛl ye,

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: Naa, gɔmena sʋŋ Felik, man Klaudius Lisias n sɔb gbauŋ kaŋa tisidif. M pʋ'ʋsidif.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Jew dim daa gban'e dau kaŋa nwa' ka bɔɔd ye ba kʋ o, ka mam wʋm ye o anɛ Room nid, ka keŋ nɛ soogianamɛ faaɛn o,

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: ka bɔɔd ye m baŋ lin yɛla ka ba tu'ad o yɛla bɛ'ɛd, ka mɔr o keŋi ba kpɛɛmnam la'asʋgʋn.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: M daa nyɛ ka ba nwa'asid o yɛla ka li anɛ Jew dim wada yɛla, ka o pʋ niŋ si'el ka li nar nɛ kum bɛɛ ba yɔɔ o sanrega nii.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛlim ye Jew dim gban'e yɛlbɛ'ɛd o yɛla la, dinzug ka m tʋm o tɔ'ɔtɔ fʋ san'an na, ka tis nɔɔr ye banɛ zi'e o yɛla la kemi fʋ san'an na yisi ba nɔɔr pian'ad.

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Ka soogianam la niŋ wʋʋ on yɛli ba si'em la, ka mɔr Paul yʋ'ʋŋ kanɛ paae Antipatris teŋin.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka soogianam banɛ ken nɛ nɔba la lɛb Jerusalem na ka wiedban'adib la dɔl Paul n keŋ.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Ka ba mɔr o paae Sizerea teŋin nɔk gbauŋ la tis gɔmena ka nɔk Paul n tis o.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Ka o karim gbauŋ la ka bu'os on yi sʋ'ʋlim si'a na. On baŋ ye o yinɛ Silisia sʋ'ʋlimin la,

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: o yɛl o ye, “Banɛ mɔri fʋ antu'a la ya'a paae na m na kɛlisi fʋ antu'a.” Ka o tis nɔɔr ye ba kpɛn'ɛs o na'ab Herod yin ka ba gur o.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Ka daba anu daar ka maanmaan kpɛɛm Ananias kena nɛ kpɛɛmnam sieba nɛ kpɛɛm kanɛ mi' antu'a, ka o yʋ'ʋr buon Tertullus. Ka ba zaŋ Paul antu'a tis gɔmena la.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Ka ba buol Tertullus. Ka o pin'ili tu'asid Paul yɛla ye, “Naa, na'asʋŋ Felik, fʋ ya'am la tisi ti sumbʋgʋsʋm, ka tiak bʋmbɛ'ɛd bɛdegʋ ka li an sʋm.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Ti siak nɛ'ɛŋa zin'is wʋsa ka pʋ'ʋsidif sʋ'ʋŋa.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Na'aba, mam pʋ bɔɔd ye m namisif la zug ka m sɔsidif ye fʋ di suguru ka kɛlisi ti antu'a giŋ nwa' Paul yɛla.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: “Ti nyɛ ninkaŋa ka o anɛ nimbɛ'og nɛ onɛ bɔɔd yɛla. O tugul Jew dim nidib dunia wʋsa, ka ba zab. O anɛ banɛ dɔl Nazaret nid la tuongat.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: ka tis nɔɔr ye banɛ mɔr antu'a nɛ o la kemi fʋ san'an na. Fʋ ya'a bu'os o, fʋ mɛŋ na wʋm o san'an lin wʋsa ka ti pian'ad o yɛla la.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Ka Jew dim mɛ paasi pian' o yɛla, ka yɛl ye, nɛ'ɛŋa wʋsa anɛ sida. Paul tu'a yis o mɛŋ Felik tuon

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Ka gɔmena la tis Paul suor ye o pian'am. Ka Paul yɛl ye, “M mi' ye fʋ niŋ sariakat sʋ'ʋlim kaŋa nwa' ni ka li yʋma lal. Alazug ka li niŋim malisim ye m pian' yisi m mɛŋi fʋ tuon kpɛla.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Li anɛ na'ana nɛ fʋn na nyaŋi baŋ ye li pʋ gaad dabis pii nɛ ayi' nwa' ka m daa keŋ Jerusalem ye m pʋ'ʋs Wina'am.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Ka Jew dim la pʋ nyɛ m ka m nwa'as nɛ sɔ' Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la. Ba mɛ pʋ nyɛ ka m tugul nidib la'asʋg dɔɔdin bɛɛ zin'isi'a.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Ba mɛ kʋ nyaŋi nie bigisi m linɛ ka ba yɛl ye m maal yaa.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Amaa m siak nɛ'ɛŋa ye m dɔlnɛ suor kanɛ ka ba ye li bɛɛ li gʋnni la, m pʋ'ʋsid Wina'am onɛ ka ti yaanam da pʋ'ʋsid la. M siak linɛ wʋsa sɔb Moses wada gbauŋʋn nɛ Wina'am nɔdi'esidib gbana ni la.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: M mɔr ti'ir Wina'am ni nwɛnɛ ban mɔr ti'ir si'em la, ye nidib wʋsa banɛ an sʋm nɛ banɛ ka' sʋm na vʋ'ʋg kumin.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka m kpɛ'ɛŋidi m mɛŋ saŋa wʋsa ye m pʋtɛn'ɛr nie Wina'am san'an nɛ nidibin.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “M yi Jerusalem ka li yʋma lal ka m mɔr ligidi lɛb ye m tisim mɛŋ nimbanɛ an tadimnam la, ka maal maana tis Wina'am.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Man daa naae pier malʋŋ la ka niŋid nɛ'ɛŋa Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yin la, ka ba nyɛɛm. Nidib bɛdegʋ daa ka' anina ka daauŋ mɛ daa kae.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Amaa Jew dim sieba banɛ yi Asia sʋ'ʋlim daa bɛɛ anina. Ba ya'a mɔrin yɛlsi'a nɛ man, ba mɛŋ naan mɔrini m antu'a kɛɛn fʋ san'an na.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Nimbama ya'a daa nyɛ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd si'a saŋkanɛ ka kpɛɛmnam la daa kati m saria la, ban yɛlimi li nannanna.

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Li ya'a ka' yɛl yinne ma'aa ka m daa zi'enɛ ba tuon ka dʋ'ʋsi m kʋkɔri yɛli baa. M daa yɛli ba ye, ‘M zi'e ya tuon zina ka ya kati m saria ka li anɛ man niŋ yadda ye kum vʋ'ʋgir bɛ la.’”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Gɔmena Felik n daa mi' labasʋŋ la suor sʋ'ʋŋa la zug, o bas pian'ad la, ka yɛli ba ye, “Soogia kpɛɛm Lisias ya'a paae na, m na gban'e ya pian'ad la yɛla.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Ka tis soogia kpɛɛm onɛ gur Paul la nɔɔr ye o gɔsim o, amaa ka tis o yɔlisim bi'ela, ka kɛ ka o zuanam tis o on bɔɔd si'el. Paul zi'e Felik nɛ Drusilla tuon

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Ka dabisa bi'ela nya'aŋ ka Felik nɛ o pu'a Drusilla onɛ an Jew nid la kena. Ka o buol Paul ka kɛ ka o pian' Yesu Kristo yadda niŋir yɛla.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul pian'ad pʋpielim nɛ mɛŋ luakir nɛ sariakadib linɛ kenna la yɛla, ka dabiem gban'e Felik, ka o yɛl Paul ye, “Kem, ka m ya'a ti nyɛ saŋa m na buolif.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: O mɛ daa mɔri ti'ir ye Paul na da' o nɛ ligidi dinzug, o daa tʋmmi buon o tu'ombi'el-tu'ombi'el ye o sɔns nɛ o.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Ka yʋma ayi' gaad ka Porsius Festus yʋ'ʋn di'e Felik zin'ig. Ka Felik bɔɔd ye o maal linɛ na malis Jew dim la zug, o kɛ ka Paul kpɛm bɛ sanrega ni.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ka Festus paae teŋ kanɛ ka o sʋ'oe la ni ka zin' anina daba atan', ka naam Sizerea teŋin keŋ Jerusalem.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Anina ka maanmaan kpɛɛmnam nɛ Jew dim tuongatib mɔr Paul na tis Festus,

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: ka sɔs o ye o sʋŋi ba yis Paul n lɛbis Jerusalem, ka ba gban'e ye ba su'a kʋ o suorin.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Ka Festus lɛbis ye, “Paul bɛ sanrega ni Sizerea teŋin. Mam mɛŋ na lɛb anina daba ayi' nwa'.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: O ya'a tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd si'a, yanam kɛl ka ya tuongatib dɔlli mɛ keŋ Sizerea ka ba pian' li yɛla.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Ka Festus zin'in nɛ ba ka li pʋ gaad dabisa piigaa, ka naan keŋ Sizerea teŋin. Ka bɛog nie ka o kpɛn' kɔɔtʋ ni zin'in, ka tis nɔɔr ye ba mɔr Paul na.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Ka Paul kpɛn' na ka Jew dim banɛ yi Jerusalem duoe zi'eni gilig o, ka pian' ye o tʋm taal bɛdegʋ, taal banɛ ka ba kʋ nyaŋi nie li gbin nyainnɛ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul tu'a ye o yis o mɛŋ ka yɛl ye, “M pʋ niŋ si'el ka li an bɛ'ɛd Jew dim wada ni bɛɛ Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yir bɛɛ pɔ'ɔg Room na'atita'ar Siiza.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Ka Festus bɔɔd ye o niŋ linɛ na malis Jew dim la zug, o bu'os Paul ye, “Fʋ siak ye fʋ na keŋ Jerusalem ka m kadi fʋ saria nɛ antu'a bama yɛlaa?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Paul lɛbis ye, “M bɛ nɛ Room na'atita'ar Siiza mɛŋ kɔɔtʋ ni; anina nar nɛ ban na kadi m saria. Fʋ mɛŋ mi' sʋ'ʋŋa ye m pʋ tʋm bɛ'ɛdi tis Jew dima.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Ka m ya'a san'amin wada ka niŋin si'el linɛ ka m narin nɛ kum, m naan kʋ zan'asinɛɛ. Amaa m antu'a linɛ ka ba mɔr na ye ba pian' la ya'a ka' sidaa, sɔ' kʋ nyaŋi nɔkimi tisi baa. M bɔɔd ye ba kadi m saria Room na'atita'ar Siiza kɔɔtʋ ni.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Ka Festus nɛ o sʋŋidib pian' gban'e, ka o lɛbis Paul ye, “Fʋ yɛl ye, fʋ bɔɔd ye ba kadi fʋ saria Room na'atita'ar kɔɔtʋ ni. Dinzugɔ na'atita'ar la san'an ka fʋ na keŋ.” Paul zi'e Agrippa nɛ Benis tuon

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Dabisa bi'ela nya'aŋ ka na'ab Agrippa nɛ o taʋn Benis kɛn Sizerea na ye ba pʋ'ʋs Festus.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Ka ba bɛɛ anina yuug bi'ela la, ka Festus tiɛn na'ab Agrippa Paul antu'a la yɛla ye, “Dau bɛ kpɛla, ka Felik bas o ka o kpɛm bɛ sanrega ni.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Ka man keŋ Jerusalem la, Jew dim maanmaan kpɛɛmnam nɛ teŋ la kpɛɛmnam mɔr o antu'a kena tiɛn m, ka sɔsi m ye, m kʋʋsim ye o tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: “Amaa ka m lɛbisi ba ye, li ka' Room dim malima ye ba kɛ ka ba mɔr ninkanɛ ka ba gban'e o la keŋ niŋ o si'el la, asɛɛ on nɛ banɛ kɛ ka ba gban'e o la kpa' taaba, ka tis o suor ka o na nyaŋi ki'is ban yɛl si'eli ziil o la.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Banɛ kɛ ka ba gban'e dau la kena la daa kɛn kpɛla na la, m daa pʋ kɛ ka li yuugɛ, amaa bɛogʋ nie la, ka m kpɛn' zin'in kɔɔtʋ ni, ka tis nɔɔr ka ba mɔr o kpɛn' na,

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: ka tɛn'ɛs ye ba na yɛl ye o tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd. Amaa ban duoe zi'en la ba pʋ nyaŋi yɛl on tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd si'aa.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Amaa ban nɛ on nwa'as taaba nɛ ba pʋ'ʋsim suor yɛla ma'aa, nɛ dau sɔ' onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Yesu, onɛ kpi ka Paul yɛl ye o vʋ'ʋg ya la yɛla.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Ka m pʋ nyaŋi gban'e mam na niŋ si'em baŋ yɛl bama gbinnɛ, ka bu'os Paul ye o bɔɔd ye o keŋ Jerusalem ka m kad o saria aninaa?

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Ka Paul yɛl ye o bɔɔd ye o kpɛlim sanrega ni, ka keŋ Room na'atita'ar Siiza kɔɔtʋ ni ka o kʋʋs o pian'ad la. Ka m tis nɔɔr ye o bɛ sanrega la ni ti paae saŋkanɛ ka m na mɔr o keŋ na'atita'ar la san'an.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ka na'ab Agrippa yɛl Festus ye, “M bɔɔd ye m mɛŋ wʋm dau kaŋa nwa' pian'ad.” Ka Festus lɛbis ye, “Bɛog ya'a nie fʋ na wʋm o pian'ad.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka Agrippa nɛ Benis kena dʋ'ʋsid na'am bɛdegʋ, ka kpɛn' antu'a dɔɔgin nɛ soogia kpɛɛmnam nɛ teŋ la tuongatib. Ka Festus tis nɔɔr ye ba mɔr Paul na,

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: ka o yɛl ye, “Naa, na'ab Agrippa, nɛ banɛ wʋsa la'as na. Ya nyɛ dau kaŋaa, Jew dim wʋsa yɛl o yɛla Jerusalem teŋin nɛ kpɛla, ka tansid ye o pʋ nar ye o kpɛn vʋeya.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Amaa mam pʋ nyɛ on niŋ si'el ka li nar nɛ on na kpii. Ka o mɛŋ yɛl ye o bɔɔd ye ba ta'as o pian'ad la na'atita'ar san'an. Ka m gban'e ye m na kɛ ka o keŋ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Amaa m pʋ mɔr antu'a zugʋ o yɛla na sɔbi tis na'atita'ar laa. Alazug ka m kɛ ka ba mɔr o ya san'an na, fʋn na'ab Agrippa mɛŋ-mɛŋ ya'a bu'os o bu'osa naae, m na nyɛ yɛl si'a o ni sɔb.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ka m tɛn'ɛs ka li ka' sʋm tisim nɛ mam na zaŋ sanrega nidi tis na'atita'ar ka pʋ pa'al sʋ'ʋŋa ban gban'e o si'el yɛlaa.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: Ka yɛl ye, “Na'ab Agrippa, m tɛn'ɛs ka li malis man ka m na tu'a yisi m mɛŋi fʋ tuon zina nwa' nɛ lin wʋsa ka Jew dim la yɛl ye m tʋm ya ka kɛ ka ba gban'e m na la.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Fʋn sadigim mi' Jew dim malima nɛ ba gban'ar sʋ'ʋŋa la zug, m sɔsidif ye fʋ maal suguru ka kɛlisi m pian'ad la.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Ba baŋ ya ka li yuug. Ba ya'a bɔɔd, ba tun'e zi'eni di kasɛt ye m anɛ Farisii dim nid yinne banɛ ti'e ba pʋ'ʋsim yɛla hali la.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Kaanb kaŋa ka ti buudi pii na ayi' banɛ pʋ'ʋsid Wina'am nintaŋ nɛ yʋ'ʋŋ la mɔr ti'ir ye ba na nyɛɛ li. Naa, li anɛ ti'ir kaŋa zug ka Jew dim kɛ ka ba gban'am.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Bɔ ka li tɔi tisi ya ye Wina'am na nyaŋi vʋ'ʋg kum?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Man tʋm nɛ'ɛŋa Jerusalem teŋin. Maanmaan kpɛɛmnam da tisim paŋ ka m gban'e Wina'am nidib bɛdegʋ kpɛn'ɛs sanrega ni. Ka banɛ ka ba da kadi ba saria ye ba nar nɛ kum la, mam mɛŋ da siaki ba kʋʋb yɛla.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: Saŋa bɛdegʋ ka m namisi ba la'asʋg dɔɔdin kpɛ'ɛŋi fɛndigi ba ka ba basi ba pʋ'ʋsim la. Ka m sʋnf da pɛlig nɛ ba hali ka m keŋ tɛɛns banɛ ka' Jew dim sʋ'ʋlim la ni, ye m namisi ba. Paul tu'as o tiakir yɛla (Tʋm

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: “Li da anɛ nɛ'ɛŋa zug ka m da di'e nɔɔr maanmaan kpɛɛmnam san'anɛ keŋ Damaskus teŋin.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Naa, ka m bɛ suor zug nintaŋ tisʋʋs ka nyɛ nɛɛsim ka li nie gaad nintaŋi yi saazug na giligim nɛ banɛ dɔllim la.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Ka ti wʋsa li teŋin ka m wʋm kʋkɔr ka li yɛlim nɛ Hibiru pian'ad ye, ‘Saul, Saul, bɔ ka fʋ namisidi ma? Li na an tɔɔgʋ tisif nwɛnɛ naafʋ na tɔn daug nɛ.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: “Ka m bu'os ye, ‘Naa, fʋ aan anɔ'ɔnɛ?’ “Ka Zugsɔb la yɛlim ye, ‘M anɛ Yesu onɛ ka fʋ namisid la.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Amaa duom zi'en ka m nie m mɛŋi fʋ san'an ka gaŋif ye fʋ liebi m tʋmtʋm. Fʋ na tu'as nidib fʋn nyɛ si'eli m san'an zina nɛ m yɛla lin ka m na ti pa'alif.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: M na sʋŋif ka fʋ yi Jew dim nu'usin nɛ banɛ ka' Jew dim buudi la nu'usin, banɛ ka m tʋmmi fʋ ba san'an la.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: M na laki ba pʋtɛnda, ka fɛndigi ba yis likinɛ lɛbisi ba nɛɛsimin, ka yisi ba Sʋntaana nu'usinɛ lɛbisi ba Wina'am san'an. M na kɛ ka ba niŋi m yadda ka Wina'am yisi ba tʋʋmbɛ'ɛdi bas, ka la'asi ba nɛ Wina'am nidib.’ Paul tu'as o tʋʋma yɛla

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: Ka m pin'il Damaskus nɛ Jerusalem nɛ Juda sʋ'ʋlim wʋsa nɛ buudbanɛ ka' Jew dim la san'anɛ mɔɔl ye ba fɛndigim keŋ Wina'am san'an, ka tʋm linɛ pa'al ye ba tiakya.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa zug ka Jew dim daa gban'am Wina'am Pʋ'ʋsim Yinnɛ zigid ye ba kʋʋm.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Amaa m paam Wina'am sʋŋir hali ti paae zina, ala ka m zi'e kpɛla tu'asid man nyɛ si'eli tisidi ya, yanam banɛ an kpi'emnam nɛ tadimnam wʋsa. Man yɛl si'el wʋsa anɛ linɛ ka Wina'am nɔdi'esidib nɛ Moses da yɛl ye li na niŋ.

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: O da yɛl ye asɛɛ ka Kristo namis ka lieb onɛ vʋ'ʋg kumin yiiga, ka mɔɔl labasʋŋ la tis Jew dim nɛ banɛ ka' Jew dim buudi la.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Paul n tu'ad ye o yis o mɛŋ nɛ'ɛŋanam ni la, ka Festus tans Paul ye, “Fʋ gɛɛmnɛ. Fʋ zamis galisʋg la kɛnɛ ka fʋ gɛɛm.”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Ka Paul lɛbis ye, “Naa, m pʋ gɛɛm. M pian'adi yɛlsida nɛ ya'am.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: “Na'ab Agrippa, m na nyaŋi pian' tisif nɛ sʋnkpi'euŋ, fʋn mi' nɛ'ɛŋanam wʋsa la zug. M baŋ ye fʋ nyɛ nɛ'ɛŋanam wʋsa lin niŋ paalʋ la zug. Li pʋ niŋ likinɛ.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Na'ab Agrippa, fʋ siak Wina'am nɔdi'esidib la yɛlaa? M mi' ye fʋ siakya.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Ka Agrippa yɛl Paul ye, “Fʋ tɛn'ɛs ye fʋ na zaŋ saŋa bi'ela kɛ ka m kilim Kristo nidaa?”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul yɛl ye, “Li ya'a yuug bɛɛ li ya'a pʋ yuugɛ, m sɔsid Wina'am ye fʋn nɛ banɛ wʋsa kɛlisid man zina la na kilim wʋʋ man an si'em la. Amaa m pʋ bɔɔd ye ba lɔɔ ya nɛ bana wʋʋ ban lɔ man si'em laa.”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Ka gɔmena Festus nɛ na'ab la nɛ Benis nɛ nidib la wʋsa duoe

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: yi ka yɛl taaba ye, “Dau kaŋa pʋ niŋ si'el ka li nar ye o kpi bɛɛ ba kpɛn'ɛs o sanrega nii.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Ka Agrippa yɛl Festus ye, “Dau kaŋa nwa' ya'a pʋ yɛlin ye o bɔɔd ye o keŋ na'atita'ar Siiza la san'anɛ, fʋ naan yisin o.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: Ka ba gban'e ye ti kpɛn' anrʋŋʋ keŋ teŋ kanɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Itali la, ka nɔk Paul nɛ sanrega nidib sieba niŋ soogia kpɛɛm yinne onɛ yʋ'ʋri buon Julius la nu'ugin, o da anɛ Ogestus soogianam kpɛɛm.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Ka ti kpɛn' anrʋŋ kanɛ yi Adramitium teŋin na ye ti keŋ Asia atɛuk gbɛog teŋ sieba ni. Ka ti kpɛn' wa'ae. Ka Aristarkus onɛ an Masedonia nid ka yi Tɛsalonika na la, dɔlli ti.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka ti paae Sidon teŋin, ka Julius maal Paul sʋ'ʋŋa bas o nɔɔr ka o keŋ o zuanam san'an ka ba tis o on bɔɔd si'el wʋsa.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: Ka ti kpɛn' anrʋŋ anina. Ka pɛbisʋgʋ tʋ'ʋsidi ti la zug ka ti dɛn'ɛd Saipuros teŋ la ka dɔl zin'ikanɛ na lus pɛbisʋg la lɛbis.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: Ka gaad atɛuk linɛ kpi'e Silisia nɛ Pamfilia tɛɛnsin la paae Mira teŋin linɛ bɛ Lisia sʋ'ʋlimin la.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Anina ka soogia kpɛɛm la nyɛ Alekzandria anrʋŋ ka li bɔɔd ye li keŋ Itali teŋin. Ka ti wʋsa kpɛn'.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Ka li ka' na'ana, ka ti ken ku'omin la bi'el-bi'el dabisa bi'ela paae Nidus teŋin na. Ka pɛbisʋg pʋ kɛ ka ti nyaŋi keŋ tuonnɛ, ka luaki dɛn'ɛn Salmone teŋ kanɛ bɛ Krete sʋ'ʋlimin la. Ka Krete teŋ lus pɛbisʋg la lɛbis.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: Ka ti kennɛ dɛn'ɛnidi atɛuk gbɛog. Ka li mu'oe ka ti paae zin'ikanɛ buon “Zin'isʋŋ, zin'ikanɛ ka Anrima Zi'enid la.” Ka li kpi'e Lasea teŋin.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: Ka dabisa la yuug ka li lieb yɛlli tisi ti nɛ tinamɛ na keŋ ku'omin la ka nɔlɔɔr linɛ an suguru sɔsʋg dabisir la gaad la zug, ka Paul sa'ali ba ye

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: “M baŋ ya ka ti ku'omin ken la na niŋ yɛlbɛ'ɛdi tisi ti. La'ad la bɛdegʋ na san'am, la'an nɛ anrʋŋ la mɛŋ nɛ nidib nyɔvʋya.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Amaa ka soogia kpɛɛm la kɛlis anrʋŋ la sɔb pian'ad, ka pʋ kɛlis Paul n yɛl si'el laa.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: Ka ti paae tembil zin'ikanɛ ka ku'om gilig ka li buon Kauda la. Ka teŋ la lusi ti sisi'emin. Ka ti kpɛ'ɛŋi ti mɛŋ ka gban'e anrimbil la sʋ'ʋŋa

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: dʋ'ʋs anrʋŋ tita'ar la zugin. Ka ba nɔk nwiisi viligi lɔɔ li kiŋ-kiŋ nɛ anrʋŋ tita'ar la tisi li paŋ. Ka ti zɔ dabiem ye ti na ti paae zin'ikanɛ ka titanbin'isʋg bɛ ka ba buon ye Sirtis ka ku'om pʋ zulim la. Linzug ka ba sigis anrʋŋ la futita'ar la ka kɛ ka sisi'em la ziidi li ken.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka sisi'em la kpɛn da'ad. Ka ba pin'ili yisid la'abanɛ bɛ anrʋŋʋn la basid ku'omin.

english_verse: Then on the third day, with their bare hands they threw overboard some of the ship's gear.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog lɛn nie ka ba mɛŋ yis anrʋŋ la mɛŋ la'adi bas ku'omin.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: Dabisa bɛdegʋ ka saŋgbana ligil winnig nɛ nwadbibis, ka sisi'em kpɛn da'ad nɛ paŋ. Ka ti pʋ lɛm mɔr pʋtɛn'ɛr nɛ vʋm.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Ka li yuug ka nidib la pʋ di diibɔ. Ka Paul zi'eni ba sʋʋgin yɛl ye, “Ya ya'a daa siakini m nɔɔr ka pʋ duon Krete teŋinɛ, ti naan yiin yɛlbama nwa' wʋsa ni.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Amaa m sɔsidi ya ye ya kpɛ'ɛŋi ya sʋnya. Ka hali baa yinne kʋ kpii ti sʋʋginɛ. Asɛɛ anrʋŋ la ma'aa na san'am.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Yʋ'ʋŋ ka Wina'am onɛ sʋ'oe man ka m pʋ'ʋsid o la maliak sa zi'enɛ m san'an ka

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: yɛlim ye, ‘Paul, da zɔt dabiem. Sida fʋ na zi'en na'atita'ar Siiza tuon, fʋ sariakadib la yɛla. Ka Wina'am na tis banɛ dɔllif la wʋsa vʋm.’

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ, kpɛ'ɛŋimi ya sʋnya; ka man niŋ Wina'am yadda ye li sid na niŋ wʋʋ maliak la yɛlim si'em la.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Amaa sisi'em na da'ae ti keŋ zin'ig kan ka ku'om gilig la fir.”

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Ka ba lɔdig anrʋŋ la kʋnti basi atɛukʋn la ka lɔdig daad banɛ kɛt ka anrʋŋ la ken ban bɔɔd zin'isi'a la, ka dʋ'ʋs fuug linɛ bɛ anrʋŋ la tuon la ye pɛbisʋg da'ae anrʋŋ la keŋ tuon.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Ka nimbanɛ tʋm anrʋŋ la tʋʋma la ma' ye ba sigisidnɛ kʋnt la ku'omin anrʋŋ la tuon, ka sigis anrimbil la ku'omin kpɛ'ɛŋid ye ba yi anrʋŋʋn la.

english_verse: The sailors were afraid that we might hit some rocks, and they let down four anchors from the back of the ship. Then they prayed for daylight.
translation_verse: Ka ba zɔ dabiem ye anrʋŋ la na tʋ'ʋs tampiins, ka sigis anrʋŋ la kʋnt linɛ kpɛn' teŋin la anaasi nɛ nwiis anrʋŋ la nya'aŋ ka sɔs Wina'am ye bɛog nie.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Ka Paul yɛl soogia kpɛɛm nɛ soogianam la ye, “Nimbama nwa' ya'a pʋ zin'in anrʋŋʋn la, ti wʋsa kʋ nyaŋi tiligɛ.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Ka soogianam la kɛnsig nwiis banɛ lɔ anrimbil la ka kɛɛ li ka li keŋ.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Dinzugɔ m bɛlimi ya nɛ ye ya di diib ka nyɛ paŋ; ka ya zuobʋg baa yinne kʋ bɔdigɛ.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: On yɛl nɛ'ɛŋa naae la, ka nɔk bodobodo pʋ'ʋs Wina'am bareka ba wʋsa tuon ka kɔ'ɔg bodobodo la di.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Ka ba wʋsa kpɛ'ɛŋi ba sʋnya di diib la.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Ban dii siak la ka nɔk linɛ kpɛlim la lɔb ku'omin, ye anrʋŋ la fak. Anrʋŋ la san'auŋ yɛla

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Ka bɛog nie ka banɛ tʋm anrʋŋ la tʋʋma pʋ baŋ teŋ laa. Amaa ka ba nyɛ zin'ikanɛ an kʋkʋn ka gban'e ye ba ya'a nyaŋ, ba na kɛ ka anrʋŋ la kpa' anina.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Ka anrʋŋ la tʋ'ʋs titanbin'isdʋʋr. Ka li tuon firi gʋ'ʋŋ ken. Ka ku'opila nwɛ'ɛdi li nya'aŋ, ka li san'am.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Ka soogianam la gban'e ye ba kʋ sanrega nidib la wʋsa ka sɔ' da nyaŋi su'a lug ku'om la dʋ gbɛogɔ.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Amaa ka soogia kpɛɛm la bɔɔd ye o yis Paul kumin ka zan'as, ka tis nɔɔr ye banɛ mi' lugub la iankim yi anrʋŋʋn la yiiga lugi dʋ gbɛog,

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: ka banɛ kpɛlim la gban'e daad nɛ anrʋŋ la dakɔɔlima lugi dʋ. Ala ka ti wʋsa daa tiligi dʋ gbɛog.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa nya'aŋ ka ti baŋ ye teŋ la yʋ'ʋri buon Malta.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Ka teŋ la nidib di'e ti sʋ'ʋŋa. Ka saa pin'ili niid ka waad bɛ ka ba nyu'oe bugum tisi ti ka ti ʋʋsid.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Ka Paul la'asid daad ye o niŋ bugumin, ka waaf bɛɛ anina ka tʋʋlʋg wʋm o ka o yina ga' o nu'ug.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Nidib la nyɛ waaf la ga' o nu'ug la ka yɛli ba taaba ye, “Bi'esʋg kae, oŋa anɛ ninkʋʋd. Yɛlsida oŋa kʋ vʋ'ʋgɛ, hali la'an nɛ on nyaŋi yi ku'omin na la.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Paul misig o nu'ug ka waaf la li bugumin ka pʋ niŋ o si'ela.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: Ka nidib la gu'usid ye ba na nyɛ ka o niŋgbina mɔd bɛɛ o na kpɛn li teŋin kpi. Amaa lin yuug ka ba pʋ nyɛ ka si'el niŋ o la ka ba tiaki ba pʋtɛnda ye o anɛ teŋgban.

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Ka pɔɔg kpi'e zin'ikanɛ ka ti bɛ la yammin ka an na'ab la pɔɔg. Ka na'ab la yʋ'ʋr buon Publius. Ka o di'e ti nɛ sumalisim. Ka ti bɛɛ o yinne aan o saam daba atan'.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Ka o saam bɛn'ɛdi digi ka o niŋ tʋl ka o saand. Ka Paul kpɛn' dɔɔgin la sɔs Wina'am ka pa'al o nu'us o ni ka o nyɛ laafi.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Nɛ'ɛŋa niŋ la ka nimbanɛ an ban'adnam wʋsa kena. Ka Paul sɔs Wina'am ka ba nyɛ laafi.

english_verse: The people were very respectful to us, and when we sailed, they gave us everything we needed. From Malta to Rome
translation_verse: Ka ba na'asi ti bɛdegʋ ka tisi ti piini, tinamɛ bɔɔd gaadʋg la, ka ba tisi ti linɛ wʋsa ka ti na bɔɔd ken la pʋʋgin. Paul naam Malta paae Room teŋin

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Ka nwadis atan' nya'aŋ ka ti kpɛn' Alekzandria teŋin anrʋŋ linɛ bɛ Malta teŋin la sisi'etita'ar saŋa, ka anrʋŋ la yʋ'ʋr buon “Win Liiba.” Ka ba niŋ anrʋŋ la pʋʋgin.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Ka ti keŋ paae Sirakus teŋin ka zin'in anina daba atan',

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: ka naanɛ anina paae Regium teŋin na. Ka bɛog nie ka sisi'em yi ti nya'aŋ na da'adi ti. Ka daba ayi' daar ka ti paae Puteoli teŋin.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: Anina ka ti nyɛ yadda niŋidib sieba, ka ba sɔsi ti ka ti zin'in nɛ ba daba ayɔpɔi, ka naan kɛn Room teŋin na.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Ka yadda niŋidib banɛ bɛ Room teŋin la wʋmi ti yɛla, ka yina. Ka sieba paae zin'ikanɛ ka ba buon ye Saam Dɔɔda Atan' teŋin na. Ka sieba paae zin'ikanɛ buon Appius Da'an la na tʋ'ʋsi ti. Ka Paul n nyɛɛ ba la ka pʋ'ʋs Wina'am ka o sʋnf kpɛ'ɛŋ. Paul bɛ Room teŋin

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: Tinamɛ kpɛn' Room teŋin na la, ka soogia kpɛɛm la kɛ ka Paul zin'in o kɔn' ka soogia gur o.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Ka daba atan' nya'aŋ ka Paul buol Jew dim kpɛɛmnam banɛ bɛ teŋin la la'as ka yɛli ba ye, “M ba'abiisɛ, hali la'an nɛ mam daa pʋ niŋ si'el linɛ an bɛ'ɛdi ti nidibin bɛɛ wada banɛ ka ti di'e ti yaanam san'an la, ba daa gban'e m Jerusalem teŋin nɔki mɛ tis Room soogianam.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Ka ba bu'osim bu'osa ka bɔɔd ye ba basim, ban daa pʋ nyɛ ka m tʋm tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd si'a linɛ nar nɛ kum la zug.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Amaa ka Jew dim zan'as. Ka man kʋ tun'e niŋ si'el la zug ka m sɔs nɔɔr soogia kpɛɛm la san'an ye o tisim suor ka m keŋ Room na'atita'ar Siiza kɔɔtʋ ni, ka li ka' ye m mɔri antu'a si'a nɛ m mɛŋ nidiba.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Dinzug ka m buoli ya ye m nyɛɛ ya ka pian' tisi ya. Nid kan yɛla ka Israel dim mɔr ti'ir la zug ka ba lɔ m nɛ bana.”

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Ka ba yɛl o ye, “Ti pʋ di'e gbana Juda teŋin ka li sɔbi fʋ yɛlaa. Jew dim banɛ kɛn kpɛla na la, ba sɔ' pʋ tisi ti fʋ labaar bɛɛ pian' fʋ tʋʋmbɛ'ɛd yɛlaa.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Amaa ti bɔɔd ye ti wʋmi fʋ san'an fʋn tɛn'ɛsid si'el pʋ'ʋsim kanɛ ka fʋ dɔl la yɛla. Ti mi' ye zin'ig wʋsa nidib pian'ad pʋ'ʋsim la pian'abɛ'ɛd.”

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Ka ba zi'el dabisir nɛ Paul. Ka li daar paae ka nidib bɛdegʋ la'as Paul zin'igin la na. Ka Paul tu'asidi bigisidi ba Wina'am na'am yɛla, yi bɛogʋn ti ma'ae zaam. Ka o kpɛ'ɛŋi nyaŋi pa'annɛ ba Yesu yɛla Moses wada gbauŋʋn nɛ Wina'am nɔdi'esidib gbana ni.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Ka o pian'ad la nyaŋi kɛ ka sieba siak ka sieba pʋ siakɛ.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Ban nwa'as taaba hali la, Paul daa tu'asi ba nwa' ka ba nyaan widig, “Wina'am Siig Kasi da dɔlis Azaya onɛ an nɔdi'es la san'an pian' yɛlsida tisi ya yaanam ye,

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: “Kem nimbama san'an yɛli ba ye, ‘Ba na wʋm ka lɛn wʋm, amaa ka kʋ gban'e li gbinnɛ. Ba na gɔs ka lɛn gɔs, amaa ka kʋ nyɛ si'ela.’”

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: Nimbama nwa', sʋnya digilimnɛ, ka ba tʋba ziank nɛ wʋm, ka umi ba nini. Ya'a ka' ala, ba naan nyɛɛn nɛ ba nini, ka wʋmin nɛ ba tʋba, ka baŋin nɛ ba pʋtɛnda, ka tiaki lɛbi m san'an na, ka m ti'ebi ba.
